title: Kimi Antonelli Won the Race - Port Hercules was the Real Spectacle
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Monaco Grand Prix 2026: Where Superyachts Stole the Show
imageCaption: Port Hercules during the 2026 Monaco Grand Prix. While Kimi Antonelli battled to victory on the streets above, Monaco's superyacht fleet hosted one of the most exclusive parties on the planet.
summary: Monaco Grand Prix 2026: Kimi Antonelli Won the Race, but the Superyachts Stole the Show
body: Kimi Antonelli took a stunning victory on the streets of Monte Carlo, but down in Port Hercules another spectacle was unfolding as Monaco's floating palace district came alive.
There are bigger motor races. There are faster circuits. There are certainly tracks where overtaking is easier. Yet there is only one Monaco Grand Prix.

Standing beside Port Hercules during the 2026 Monaco Grand Prix weekend, it quickly became clear that while the Formula One cars provided the soundtrack, the harbour itself was every bit as much a star attraction.

From my vantage point overlooking the famous harbour section of the circuit, the scene was almost surreal. Hundreds of millions of pounds worth of superyachts sat bow-to-stern along the quays, packed so tightly together that from a distance they appeared almost like floating apartment blocks. Every available berth was occupied. Radar domes, helipads, sun decks and infinity pools competed for attention while guests mingled on upper decks enjoying what has become one of the most exclusive social events on the planet.
Meanwhile, only a few metres away, Formula One machinery screamed through the harbour section of the circuit.

The contrast was extraordinary. One moment your eye was drawn to a sleek 70-metre yacht hosting a champagne reception. The next, an F1 car flashed past the barriers at astonishing speed before disappearing beneath the famous tunnel.

For sailors, Monaco Grand Prix weekend offers something no other sporting event can replicate. The harbour becomes a temporary showcase for some of the world's most impressive vessels. Feadships, Lürssens, Benettis, Oceancos and custom-built masterpieces lined the waterfront. Crew members worked tirelessly behind the scenes while owners and guests enjoyed parties that continued long after the racing had finished.

As the weekend progressed, Port Hercules became less of a marina and more of a floating city. Music drifted across the water from yacht decks. Invitations were traded like currency. Helicopters buzzed overhead carrying guests from Nice and Cannes. Luxury tenders darted between vessels carrying passengers to dinners, receptions and late-night celebrations.

The race itself produced a memorable result. Mercedes youngster Kimi Antonelli delivered one of the biggest performances of his rapidly developing Formula One career, taking victory on one of motorsport's most demanding stages. Winning in Monaco instantly places a driver into a very exclusive club, and Antonelli's triumph marked what many believe could be the beginning of a remarkable era for the young Italian.
The packed grandstands erupted as he crossed the finish line, but even then the celebrations seemed almost secondary to the spectacle unfolding throughout the harbour.
Monaco has always been different.
Elsewhere, the race is the entire show.
In Monaco, the race is merely the centrepiece of a much larger performance.

The yachts host parties attended by celebrities, business leaders, racing legends and royalty. Waterfront restaurants overflow with guests. Champagne flows freely while deals are struck and friendships renewed against a backdrop of Mediterranean sunshine and Formula One noise.
As evening descended across the Principality, the atmosphere shifted once again. The roar of engines gave way to music.

The harbour lights reflected from polished hulls and calm Mediterranean water. Guests gathered on flybridges and aft decks while conversations drifted between racing, sailing and where the next party might be. Looking across the packed marina, it was impossible not to appreciate the remarkable connection between Monaco and the sea.

Long before Formula One arrived, Monaco was a maritime destination. The harbour remains the heart of the Principality, and during Grand Prix week it becomes the world's most glamorous marina. For sailors visiting the event, that is perhaps the greatest attraction of all.

Kimi Antonelli may have taken the chequered flag, but down in Port Hercules the superyacht fleet delivered a masterclass of its own. Monaco remains one of the few places on earth where the world's fastest cars race alongside some of the world's most extraordinary yachts. And for one spectacular weekend each year, nobody seems entirely sure which attraction steals the show.
This year, it might just have been the boats.

title: Bering Yachts Dazzles with Interiors of the 33m Bering 110 Explorer Yacht, Conjuring a Calm, Composed and Pragmatic Sea Experience
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Bering Yachts Dazzles with Interiors of the 33m Bering 110 Explorer Yacht, Conjuring a Calm, Composed and Pragmatic Sea Experience
summary: Turkish shipbuilder, Bering Yachts, has released interior renderings of its sophisticated 33.1m Bering 110 explorer yacht model, designed in partnership with Red Yacht Design.
body: Bering yachts, along with Red Yacht Design, is set to redefine luxury sea exploration with the unveiling of the interior renderings of its Bering 110 (B110) explorer yacht model. Already nearing completion, the first unit of this series is poised to hit the waters by 2027. Showcasing robust and broad lines stamped by Red Yacht Design, B110 comes with a steel hull and boasts a range of over 5,000 nautical miles.

Crafted as a 'modern but true explorer', the B110 enjoys the spaciousness and features typical of larger yachts. According to the designer team, the B110 offers an immersive experience of 'gentle' and 'introspective' interiors that strikingly contrast with its machismo exterior. They envisioned an environment exuding a sense of calmness, coherence and deep composure, valuing stillness and poise over grandeur and extravagance.

Designed with long-distance expeditions in mind, practicality is a key feature of the B110. For instance, it has dedicated storage spaces, a generous pantry capacity for a month's sea journey, and an asymmetrical saloon optimising the interior width. With cabin spaces both in the deck and below, this yacht also provides the option for customisation where indoor and outdoor furniture and other amenities can be added as per the client's preferences.

title: ACO Musto Skiff World Championship 2026 Begins with Exciting Pre-Worlds Races
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: ACO Musto Skiff World Championship 2026 Begins with Exciting Pre-Worlds Races
summary: Ocean racers and sailing enthusiasts descended upon Yacht Club de Carnac for the ACO Musto Skiff World Championship 2026, kicking off with a captivating pre-worlds event.
body: The ACO Musto Skiff World Championship 2026 welcomed an array of racers to the distinguished Yacht Club de Carnac. The highly anticipated event started on a high note, with thrilling pre-worlds races that showcased both the competitive spirit and exceptional sportsmanship of participating competitors. The event was a testament to the dedication and hard work of Yacht Club de Carnac's team, which once again successfully executed a superb event. Run by committed volunteers, the club welcomed each participant warmly, setting the stage for a riveting weeklong championship. Racers encountered variable adventures merely getting to the location. They conquered everything from dodging enormous potholes to dealing with displaced axles and cancelled ferries. However, all competitors managed to make it to the starting line on time, thanks to quick updates via WhatsApp. The pre-worlds races were greeted with light wind and bright sunshine, rekindling the friendly competition amongst racers. A few recalls ensured the black flag made a timely appearance to keep overly eager competitors in check. However, once racing got underway, it was as fierce as a French trimaran sailing in full offshore conditions. The lead positions varied rapidly, much like fluctuating stock prices, proving that no racer was safe. Ultimately, Eddie Bridle, the current UK National Champion and European Champion took the pre-worlds win, reminding everyone that while form may be temporary, skill stands the test of time. He was closely followed by Alex Greil and Jamie Hilton, the latter marking a podium finish on his wedding anniversary. The pre-worlds concluded with an informal prize-giving ceremony, awarding locally sourced prizes to the top spots. Participants then gathered to celebrate the beginning of the championship week, basking in the sun, enjoying fresh oysters, and toasting with champagne. Now the stage is set for action-packed racing, promising gusty conditions, plenty of sunshine, and undoubtedly, countless thrilling moments. The ACO Musto Skiff World Championship surely promises to be an unforgettable week of racing excellence.

title: China's Historic Venture into High-End Yachting: A Groundbreaking 323m Residential Yacht - Ulyssia
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: China's Historic Venture into High-End Yachting: A Groundbreaking 323m Residential Yacht - Ulyssia
summary: Luxury and adventure unite in Ulyssia, a maiden residential yacht project set to define the future of superyachting.
body: Ulyssia Residences has emboldened China's foray into luxury shipbuilding, confirming its colossal 323-metre residential yacht Ulyssia will be constructed by China Merchants Cruise Shipbuilding (CMCS). This major development marks not only a significant stride towards Ulyssia's 2031 maiden voyage but also sets a novel precedent in high-end seafaring.

The concept of Ulyssia originated from Espen Øino, daring to blend the colossal scale of an ocean-going passenger vessel with the exclusivity and state-of-the-art amenities typical of superyacht living. This unique project will house 122 private residences and 22 guest suites, accompanied by an ambitious array of amenities boasting a yacht club and marina, medical facilities, luxury tenders, Triton submersibles, and comprehensive wellness and exploration facilities.

The news has launched waves of excitement across the industry and beyond. Espen Øino, the visionary behind Ulyssia, spoke of his pride and anticipation as the project moves into the construction phase: 'Ulyssia brings together proportions and technical complexity of a large ocean-going vessel with the character, privacy and refinement of a yacht. Transitioning to the construction phase is a profound moment indeed.'

Ulyssia Residences Chief Executive Alain Gruber further added that the agreement with CMCS has opened the doors to expansive innovation, technological advancement, and expertise in manufacturing, ushering the project into its next phase of development.

This announcement is a thrilling signal of a new era for superyachting and luxury living, embodying the spirit of high-end seafaring adventure. With the blueprint set for such a unique blend of size, scale, and sustainability, one thing is certain; Ulyssia will re-define the concept of maritime living.

title: Ylliam XII - Comptoir Immobilier Triumphs in the 87th Bol d'Or du Léman: A controversial Clubhouse Celebration Saga
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Ylliam XII - Comptoir Immobilier Triumphs in the 87th Bol d'Or du Léman: A controversial Clubhouse Celebration Saga
summary: A thrilling race to remember, as Ylliam XII - Comptoir Immobilier clinches victory at the 87th Bol d'Or du Léman in the midst of a heated controversy.
body: The 87th Bol d'Or du Léman set sail amid a flurry of suspense and anticipation. Only after 11 hours and 48 minutes of fierce racing, Bertrand Demole's team, Ylliam XII - Comptoir Immobilier, emerged ahead, graciously slicing through the finish line first. It was a feat worth celebratory fireworks and jubilation; however, instead, the air was thick with controversy.

Ylliam XII had been disqualified for changing its crew past the registration deadline. The team was left amidst uncertainty till the later morning, a technical error in the disqualification process found by the Jury led them to overturn the decision.

This abnormal blip in proceedings allowed Marco Favale's X-Wing to steal the limelight, quite unknowingly, for one tantalising moment. They savoured the victory champagne and basked in the celebratory spotlight adorning the main stage, oblivious to the impending turn of events.

The race saw a vibrant mix of weather conditions, the forecasts promising light sunshine and dominant south-westerly breezes majestically transitioning into thermal winds by nightfall. This wind direction had previously favoured the Swiss shoreline in 2018, as pointed out by Nicolas Charbonnier, the tactician aboard X-Wing.

The spirited fleet commenced the race with a marginal four knots of breeze, still havening the memory of last the windless weekend at Genève-Rolle. As the fleet approached Versoix, the winds welcomed them with an uplifting ten knots, enough to push the TF35s onto their foils, charting their course towards Saint-Prex.

The familiarity of the Swiss shore guided the trio of Ylliam XII - Comptoir Immobilier, Ylliam 17 and X-Wing led them to establish an early betting system. However, as they found their way into the Grand Lac, the rest of the fleet swiftly closed the gap.

title: Innovation Reborn: Alpha Custom Yachts Revolutionize Luxury with The Launch Of The Fourth Squalo 100 Motor Yacht
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Innovation Reborn: Alpha Custom Yachts Revolutionize Luxury with The Launch Of The Fourth Squalo 100 Motor Yacht
summary: Joining a splendid line of predecessors, the fourth Squalo 100 motor yacht, Squalo 4, makes a splash at Alpha Custom Yachts' latest launch.
body: From its base in Fano, the reputed shipyard Alpha Custom Yachts proudly unveils the fourth gem in their esteemed 29.6-metre Squalo 100 motor yacht series, aptly called Squalo 4. Designed by the creative mind of Roberto Curtó Design, this unique model not only defies but challenges conventional norms. Crafted to provide a profound experiential journey, it uniquely focuses on the genuine pleasures associated with being on board.

The Squalo 100 stands as an embodiment of Alpha's philosophy, asserting that meaningful comfort touches all five senses. Space, silence, vibrations, color, ambiance, and privacy are all seamlessly incorporated, defining the yacht's onboard experience. The vessel features structurally independent living spaces separate from the hull and superstructure, termed as 'floating' walls, floors, and ceilings. This effective separation mitigates sound and vibration transfer, subsequently ensuring an overwhelmingly serene atmosphere.

On the outside, the yacht showcases clean, bold lines complemented by a vast expanse of glazing. These external features underscore the yacht's contemporary aspect. Whereas, its internal features emphasize natural materials, soft textures, and refined details, cultivating an atmosphere of relaxation while preserving elegance. The yacht can accommodate up to 10 individuals in its five suites, with an additional provision for a crew of five.
Alpha Custom Yachts continues to solidify its position as a leading luxury yacht manufacturer, with an additional four yachts estimated to be under construction or on order.

title: Plym Yacht Club Showcases Resilience and Diversity in Successful Friday Series 1 Event
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Plym Yacht Club Showcases Resilience and Diversity in Successful Friday Series 1 Event
summary: Sailing enthusiasts were treated to a spectacle at Plym Yacht Club's Dart Sails & Covers Friday Series 1, marked by unpredictability, diversity and camaraderie.
body: If there is one place that keeps the heart of sailing beating with youthful enthusiasm, it is undoubtedly the Plym Yacht Club. Hosting the much-anticipated Dart Sails and Covers Friday Series 1, it thrust a diverse range of vessels into the limelight, from a Squib to a Corby 35. Amid an assortment of courses, every Friday evening was steeped in anticipation and thrill for each participant.

In an unpredictable British summer, the series managed to dodge the unseasonal weather for the most part, losing only one race to the whims of the wind. This unexpected pause offered the astonishing sight of the iconic Waverly paddle steamer sailing into Plymouth Sound.
In the YCT fleet, John Lewis's Squib 'Bootneck' led the rest, claiming continuous victories. The rest of the pack trailed closely behind, resulting in a gripping battle for the podium in each race.
For the IRC fleet, highlights included Mark Lewers' 'Dangerous When Wet' leading solo for substantial portions of race 6, and memorable scenes of 'Badabing's' bowman peering from the top of the mast.

After a day's sailing, Plym Yacht Club welcomed all to share tales of their oceanic adventures over sailing supper and beer. As Series 2 looms on the horizon, the infectious enthusiasm promises a bigger, more vibrant spectacle, with additions like a Cork 1720 and another Laser 28 set to join the ranks. The inclusive and jubilant spirit of Plym Yacht Club ensures a bright future for the sport, filled with challenge, diversity and delightful camaraderie.

title: Adventures on the Horizon: ISA Yachts' Third Unica 45M Steel Model is Underway
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Adventures on the Horizon: ISA Yachts' Third Unica 45M Steel Model is Underway
summary: Italian shipbuilders, ISA Yachts have commenced construction on their third Unica 45M Steel mega yacht, setting a new standard for luxury seafaring.
body: Italian masters of maritime construction, ISA Yachts, have kicked-off their latest venture: building the third yacht in their Unica 45M Steel series, scheduled for deployment in 2029. Innovatively designed for extended blue water journeys, this megayacht offers a rare mix of substantial fuel capacity, in excess of 60,000 litres, and a high-displacement, steel hull.

One of the defining attributes of this vessel is its distinctive stern design spread over three cascading levels, replete with sun lounging spaces, an infinity cockpit, and a plush pool. The highlight? Incredible ocean views through an elegant glass balustrade.

Boasting voluminous living spaces and extensive outdoor decks, this model offers large glass surfaces to amplify the synergy with the surrounding seascape. Notable features include alfresco dining on the upper aft deck, a vast bow area primed for sunbathing and socialising, and a 16-metre-long sundeck adorned with a jacuzzi, lounge, and dining area.

The main deck is a wellness and gastronomy haven, with a gymnasium and a formal dining area. In a departure from the original layout seen in the first two models, the third unit comprises a spacious VIP cabin—distinguished by a walk-in wardrobe and lavish bathroom—occupies the front section of the deck. The lower deck contains four guest cabins, all featuring ensuite bathrooms.

Providing an enviable autonomy, the yacht is powered by twin CAT C32 engines, allowing a maximum speed of 15 knots, a cruising speed of 14 knots, and an impressive range of 4,000 nautical miles at 10 knots.

According to BOATPro, ISA Yachts has distinguished itself in the maritime construction realm with 16 yachts presently ordered or under construction, including a recent unveiling of an extraordinary 70-metre superyacht design framed in an alliance with Lobanov Design.

title: Day 3 of the Santa Maria Cup 2026 Unveils Tensions and Triumphs on the Waves
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Day 3 of the Santa Maria Cup 2026 Unveils Tensions and Triumphs on the Waves
summary: Four dynamic teams have sailed straight into the semi-finals of the prestigious Santa Maria Cup following the double round robin stage. Another day of exhilarating action sees competition reaching fever pitch.
body: The tranquil seas of Annapolis offered an intense battlefield for the second stage of the 2026 Women's World Match Racing Tour. After three gruelling days of competition, four out of ten outstanding all-female teams have secured their hard-fought spots in the Santa Maria Cup's knockout rounds. Defending champion Allie Blecher from the USA, Sweden's fearsome duo Anna Östling and Martina Carlsson, and the Dutch threat Julia Aartsen have all earned their place in the semi-finals, setting the stage for the rapidly approaching Saturday showdown. Despite the tranquil seas, the third day of racing got off to a delayed start due to unusually high temperatures over Annapolis confining the sea breeze. However, soon enough the sails were full, and the fierce battle for supremacy continued as the remaining round robin matches clashed, and the final four were confirmed. A particularly enthralling performance was delivered by Olympic Gold Medallist Lily Xu Lijia of China, who proved that her prowess extended beyond Olympic arenas as she triumphed in her very first Women's World Match Racing Tour. Disrupting the status quo, Xu claimed an impressive victory over former Santa Maria Cup winner and fellow Olympian Anna Östling. Throughout, Allie Blecher and her steadfast Team BAAM held fort valiantly, topping the standings with fifteen wins and leaving no space for errors. Close on their heels, with fourteen overall victories, were Anna Östling and Team Wings. Asserting their dominance, Östling and her crew delivered one of the strongest performances of the second round robin. As the thrilling race unfolds, eyes are now set on the semi-final showdown where Blecher, Östling, Carlsson, and Aartsen will take their places at the helm.

title: Dutch Studio Vripack Unveils Striking Interiors of the Revolutionary Sustainable Yacht, Zero
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Dutch Studio Vripack Unveils Striking Interiors of the Revolutionary Sustainable Yacht, Zero
summary: Vripack, a Dutch design studio, offers an unprecedented glimpse into the interiors of the world's first 'fossil-fuel free' yacht, Zero.
body: Located in Zwartsluis, the Netherlands, a feat of innovative yachting is taking shape. The famed Dutch design studio, Vripack, is meticulously crafting the interiors of the world's first 'fossil-fuel free' sailing yacht, known as Zero. With its imminent launch set for this summer, this 69-metre marvel stands as a testament to the boundless potential of sustainable yachting, daring to reimagine traditional norms and sculpt a vision of the future.

The underpinnings of the yacht's conception hinge on revolutionary energy harvesting technologies, ranging from wind to thermal and solar power. The ultimate aim? Eradicating fossil fuel dependency, thereby setting a new standard in sustainable yachting.

The studio has gone to great lengths to make Zero 'undeniably beautiful'. From meticulously hand-carved oak corners to cambered ceiling lights, the yacht combines traditional craftsmanship with cutting-edge technologies like 3D printing, AI and VR. It lends every furnishing a purpose, integrates it into the overall design, and ensures it looks beautiful. The result? An innovative yacht that integrates sustainability into its very core, from the curved glass of the Brazilian certified teak superstructure to the liberal use of natural textures over traditional polished finishes.

Imbued with a futuristic spirit, yet firmly rooted in traditional maritime culture, Vripack's vison hints at an exhilarating future for sustainable yachting. The world watches eagerly as Zero prepares to make waves on its maiden voyage, poised to reshape the sustainable yachting landscape forever.

title: Unlock Legal Navigation Basics: Survival Tools for Skippers in a Litigious World
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unlock Legal Navigation Basics: Survival Tools for Skippers in a Litigious World
summary: Ensure your next sail isn't your last, with our boating expert's ultimate guide on skipper responsibilities and the continuous importance of logbooks.
body: Boating can be a captivating blend of adventure and tranquillity, but it is not without its share of hazards and responsibilities. Whether in the role of a weekend adventurer or a professional skipper, every voyage demands one to be prepared in all senses. Recent legal instances highlight the need for skippers to show an appropriate degree of care, whether embarking on a private or commercial trip. The notion may seem daunting, however, if you are an earnest skipper, you most likely have this covered. The real task here is to keep an accurate record of your vigilant actions.

In preparation for a trip, monitor weather patterns closely, and on the day of departure, record the forecast in your ship’s log. While it doesn’t matter if your log is papered or electronic, always ensure that your weather source is reputable. For tide tracking, consider the tidal information of any primary and secondary ports. You can manually note this or grab a screenshot of the weather and tide tables from an authentic source.

Copious attention to the boat’s engine is a must. Use the WOBBLE acronym to remember to check Water levels (both raw and coolant), Oil, Belts, Bilges, Look (for leaks or damages), and Electrics. Ensure every detail, especially any existing faults that could further compromise the vessel's integrity, are logged.

To adhere to the Merchant Shipping Act, you must plan every voyage. Use APEM (Appraise, Plan, Execute, and Monitor) as your guide. Appraise the wisdom of your trip, plan by plotting your route, and consider all critical elements such as weather, tides, vessel size, location, your expertise and your crew’s capabilities. In the end, simply setting sail without proper forethought is never an option. The sea is a visage of beauty and danger, and only the observant and prepared can truly navigate its depths and live to believe the tale.

title: From High Seas to Groundhog: The Tale of Captain Guy Booth Battling Trials, Time and Tide
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: From High Seas to Groundhog: The Tale of Captain Guy Booth Battling Trials, Time and Tide
summary: Guy Booth, a seasoned mariner recounts his years on the water, the struggles behind the scenes, and the loyalty that has anchored him through rough tides.
body: Ebb and flow - that's the life of a sailor. Captain Guy Booth knows this only too well. His life has been a symphony of highs and lows, marked by fierce loyalty and tireless endurance. The battles he has fought aren't always against the waves but often against the hands of fate itself. After four tumultuous years, Booth candidly discusses the reality of his existence, far from the idyllic sailor life, painted by the outside world. We last met Booth following a legal storm involving a ship called 'Phi'. Although 'Phi's' controversy has since faded into the sea foam, its ripples continue to churn Booth's life. When asked about his wellbeing, his answer was a sober 'bit shit, really.' This sets the tone for the kind of relentless seas Booth has been sailing. However, despite hardships, Booth personifies 'a lifer.' His life is the sea, and the sea is his life. Over thirty impressive years in yachting, countless awards, keynote orations - his resume speaks volumes. A man who has spent more time on water than land, living the mariner's dream - or so one would think. The reality of Booth's current scenario is starkly different. Dockcasts instead of broadcasts, maintenance over sailing, deathly quiet instead of a bustling inbox - these constitute his everyday. He longs for his days beneath the sun, exploring exotic locations, commanding the luxurious 'Phi.' However, the ghost of a decree haunts 'Phi', a detention order that seems to outlive its author. With no definitive end in sight, Booth pauses, taking a moment to reflect upon his life and the obstacles many others like him face. Despite the strains of trials, he stands tall. Captain Guy Booth, thus, continues his journey, sailing through the adversities life throws his way, steadfast in his dedication and loyalty to the mesmerizing high seas.

title: The Final Countdown: A Riveting Peek into Musto Skiff Class Pre-Championship Training Excursion
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Final Countdown: A Riveting Peek into Musto Skiff Class Pre-Championship Training Excursion
summary: In preparation for the World Championship in Carnac, nine committed sailors participated in an intensive training weekend at Brightlingsea Sailing Club.
body: As the World Championship in Carnac looms, a dedicated group of nine Musto Skiff sailors recently descended upon Brightlingsea Sailing Club. They convened for a rigorous training weekend, gearing up for the grand journey across the Channel and the challenges that await. The sailing club, graciously hosting these preparations, offered an impeccable setting for knowledge exchange and concentrated readiness efforts. The group comprised both seasoned campaigners and fresh faces, fostering an ideal atmosphere for collective growth and individual feedback, courtesy of a balanced fleet of seven boats each day.

The intensive weekend saw sailors tackling common issues like out-haul tension adjustments and bridle lengths, with an emphasis on reaching a 'stable groove'. This concept highlights the need for minimal corrective inputs on the mainsheet and rudder, resulting in a smooth sail. Importantly, the training sessions shed light on the intricacies of starting practices, reinforcing the notion that the best beginnings often lead to triumphant finishes. These training weekends are not just about bolstering techniques and fixing mechanical issues; they also serve as a reminder of the passion, camaraderie and commitment in competitive sailing. Together, they conquer the waves, overcome obstacles, and steadily progress towards their collective goal - The World Championship.

title: Gusty Decisions and Patient Sailing Exemplified at the ILCA Open Meeting in Bough Beech
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Gusty Decisions and Patient Sailing Exemplified at the ILCA Open Meeting in Bough Beech
summary: Bough Beech Sailing Club served as an arena for grasp of wind and wits at the annual ILCA open event, unraveling an exciting sailing encounter.
body: The annual ILCA open event at Bough Beech Sailing Club unfolded a saga of strategic sailing amid erratic wind conditions. On May 30, as the forecast promised, a sunny day offered the canvas for 21 eager sailors to unleash their skills and patience. Adding a tinge of unpredictability, the wind seemed to be playing its own metaphoric game of hide and seek.

The fleet consisted of 15 ILCA 7s and six ILCA 6s. Richard Southern along with his race team expected the wind to force a 180-degree shift during the day and, in response, came up with an uncomplicated windward leeward trajectory without any spreader for the sailing venture.

The subsequent segment of the race saw Joe Warwicker and Charlie Weatheritt steal the show. Winds had dropped even more when their competition began, requiring a metamorphosis in strategies. With their vessels crawling down what transformed from a beat to a broad reach, the sailors made calculative moves to outwit each other. What started as a dubious roll tacks, unfolded a tight race, ending with Charlie trumping over Joe.

There was a mutual consensus to take a breather hoping for a wind refill, rather than rushing for a second race before lunch. As the second race post lunch commenced, with some participants dropping, patience met strategy again. David Goddard and Robert held the lead in the 7s, while Joe and Charlie had a rematch in the 6s. The day was a blend of strategic decisions, dubious tacks and resilient perseverance, ending with Charlie the victorious one and Tessa taking a well-merited third place.

title: The Commodious Odyssey of Owning a Luxury Superyacht in South Africa
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Commodious Odyssey of Owning a Luxury Superyacht in South Africa
summary: Embarking on a quest for a superyacht in South Africa? Gird yourself for a lengthy journey marked by sparse choices, taxation hurdles, international procurement, and complex capital transfers.
body: For the luxury yacht enthusiast in South Africa, the pursuit of a grand vessel is no mere dalliance, but a journey laced with the complexity of an epic sea voyage. While South Africa enjoys a well-deserved reputation for manufacturing high-quality cruising catamarans, a prospective buyer seeking a luxury motoryacht will grapple with slim choices around the corner.

But behold, the adventure doesn't stop at the paucity of local options! The path beckons towards overseas shores, where lie a vessel befitting a seafarer’s dream. However, herein lies the hitch – steep import taxes coupled with a scant buyer pool make it financially daunting to harbour such prized assets in local waters.

Despite these seemingly arduous timelines, the global market teems with fierce competition. Premier shipyards are bustling at near-maximum capacity, straining with substantial backlogs. Remember: swift action is the name of the game in securing the coveted vessel or a prized shipyard slot.

Found your coveted ship? The next hurdle arises from issuing an international money transfer to fund your high-volume offshore purchase while maintaining total transparency and promptness, and at a rate that doesn't chip away at your deal. It's where time is truly of the essence, dictating the market dynamics.

It paints a vivid picture: a buyer in Sandton signs for a motoryacht moored in La Spezia, Italy - the deposit window being a nail-biting 72 hours. The deal is varyingly vulnerable to currency fluctuations while rivals may be circling the same proverbial hull.

But oh, the triumphant moment when your superyacht, the symbol of grandeur and adventuring spirit, finally graces the waters of Cape Town's V&A Waterfront. A testament to journeying through obstacles and prevailing - much like a thrilling sea voyage itself.

title: Loch Earn Sailing Club Will Be the Stage of the 2026 Optimists Brown Cup for 60 Young Sailors Across Scotland.
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Loch Earn Sailing Club Will Be the Stage of the 2026 Optimists Brown Cup for 60 Young Sailors Across Scotland.
summary: The legendary Loch Earn will once again host the Scottish Schools Brown Cup, welcoming around 60 young sailors raring to test their mettle on the water in 2026.
body: Loch Earn Sailing Club is braced to host the 2026 Scottish Schools Brown Cup. A fleet of young, enthusiastic sailors from different schools across Scotland are expected to partake in the event. It's no ordinary cup, but a benchmark of superiority as the organisers aim to create a congenial yet competitive atmosphere where the love for sailing blooms in each participant. The event is not just directed towards the experienced juniors, but it also encompasses the newer entrants, providing them with the opportunity to sail and compete in one of their first regattas. The event has been systematically designed to involve fleets of Topper, Optimist, RS Feva and Handicap.

This prestigious Brown Cup will be presented to the top school team comprising three boats. But that's not all! Prizes are also planned for individual and class performances. Among the variety of boats, Optimists, Toppers and handicap classes will be dominant. It's a definite spectacle to behold as the young take to the waters, setting sail for glory in Scotland's prestigious sailing event. To keep up with further information, enthusiasts are advised to follow updates on the Scottish Schools Sailing website. Unquestionably, the 2026 Brown Cup Scottish Schools Regatta is set to make a splash, bringing together the future stars of Scottish sailing.

title: Sunreef Unleashes A New Beast: The Sporty Ultima 55 Catamaran Makes Waves
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Sunreef Unleashes A New Beast: The Sporty Ultima 55 Catamaran Makes Waves
summary: Polish-based brand, Sunreef, showcases its latest marvel, the Sunreef Ultima 55, a luxury powercat equipped with innovative design elements and advanced features.
body: A new champion is making a splash in the luxury power yacht world. Polish brand Sunreef, renowned for creating spacious, luxury cruising catamarans, often with eco-friendly solar-assisted drivetrains, is now expanding its horizon with a range of sporty, sleek, and high-performing Ultima powercats. The first to seize the spotlight is the new and dashing Ultima 55.

Distinctively different from its predecessors, the Ultima 55 trades lavish indoor spaces with massive outdoor area while maintaining Sunreef's signature luxury and comfort. Streamlined with axe-head bows and a reverse-angled windscreen, this sporty yacht exudes an adventure boat vibe, perfectly suited for sun-drenched Mediterranean escapades.

Not to be outdone, comfort and efficiency go hand in hand on this vessel. Features like a fixed foil between the hulls significantly reduce resistance and pitching, ensuring a smoother, fuel-efficient ride, even in choppy waters.

Coming to the accommodation, the owner's suite is a masterstroke in space utilization. By positioning the bed on a platform spanning the deck between two hulls, it creates a larger-than-expected area, making it feel much bigger and grander. Meanwhile, the guest cabin has a cozier design, sharing the starboard hull with a crew cabin.

Granted, the external dining area has room for improvement. The vast deck could be better utilized by furnishing an outdoor dining space. But this small matter barely dents the sails of the Sunreef Ultima 55. With its innovative design, top-notch performance and unparalleled comfort, this yacht paints a promising picture of Sunreef’s future fleet.

title: Sailing Electronics Leader, B&G, Joins Forces with Renowned Skipper Francesca Clapcich on her Vendée Globe 2028 Campaign
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Sailing Electronics Leader, B&G, Joins Forces with Renowned Skipper Francesca Clapcich on her Vendée Globe 2028 Campaign
summary: B&G has set sail into a partnership with skipper Francesca Clapcich, as the official supplier for her 2028 Vendée Globe campaign.
body: B&G, the world-leading supplier in sailing electronics, has embarked on a partnership with Team Francesca Clapcich, supporting the Italian American skipper in her campaign to compete in the 2028 Vendée Globe. Clapcich's 60-foot foiling IMOCA, 11th Hour Racing, will be armored with the company's navigation systems, well-equipped for the intensities of modern offshore foiling racers. B&G, celebrating its 70th anniversary in 2026, carries with it a formidable legacy in ocean racing, experienced in steering winners to victory in both the Whitbread Round the World Race and The Ocean Race since its inception in 1973. Its systems, developed in extreme offshore environments, are designed for rapid reaction times, ensuring stability even when boat speeds cross the 30-knots threshold. For Clapcich, B&G's hardware isn't just hardware; it becomes her eyes and senses on the waters, helping her navigate wind shifts and sea conditions with ease. The comforts of technology onboard, allowing her to manage the boat's flight trim and other aspects with utmost clarity, are indeed a game-changer. With 2026 marking a pivotal turn in Clapcich's journey towards the 2028 Vendée Globe, the skipper has wasted no time in adjusting to solo racing with a fully-packed racing calendar. Her sailing season debut was the solo 1000 Race in May, scheduled to be followed by the solo Vendée Arctique on June 7 from Les Sables d'Olonne, France. Her only fully crewed race for 2026 - The Ocean Race Atlantic - will see her team race from New York, USA, to Lorient, France before she goes back to solo and ends the year with the iconic Route du Rhum race from St Malo, France to Guadeloupe in the Caribbean. B&G's systems will remain an indispensable asset on her voyage, offering her the tools needed to interpret true wind data and safely handle maneuvers at sea. Matt Eeles, Product Director for B&G, has expressed pride in the partnership with Francesca and her team, whose pioneering spirit and history of success mirrors B&G's own ambitions and values. This collaboration remains rooted in a mutual love for sailing, a sport that reinforces respect for the natural world and connects people with the elements.

title: Cayman Registry Aims to Elevate Superyacht Standards with Additional Voluntary Flag Notation
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Cayman Registry Aims to Elevate Superyacht Standards with Additional Voluntary Flag Notation
summary: The Cayman Registry's initiative to raise the superyacht industry's standards offers owners the ability to exceed the minimum requirement set by recognized yacht codes.
body: In the world of superyachts, adhering to standards is a vital aspect of safety, operation, and even prestige. The Cayman Registry, a significant player and flag for many of the world's opulent superyachts, is taking an innovative approach to further uplift these standards, setting an outstanding example for the rest of the yachting industry.

As part of the Red Ensign Group (REG), Cayman Registry is committed to hiking standards on a voluntary as well as regulatory basis. Usually, yachts comply with the minimum mandated requirements established by the REG Yacht Code, especially the ones intended for commercial use. Still, this initiative aims to go beyond that baseline. Interestingly, the same standards are also commonly implemented by those who construct or acquire yachts for personal use, thus providing a secured experience for the owner and the guests aboard while also boosting the resale value.

The new plan introduced by the Cayman Registry allows the assignment of additional voluntary flag notations. Although initial emphasis is on key safety areas, the scope of this will extend to cover other elements like crew accommodation, impacting crew welfare and turnover rates. In time, this could lead to a ranking system for yachts based on the number of additional voluntary notations achieved.

As this initiative begins to make waves, new-build projects are recommended to make potential and current owners aware of the additional notations well ahead of contract signing. This gives the yacht builder enough time to evaluate the supplementary costs involved. The current list of extra voluntary flag notations encompasses several safety areas applicable to superyachts and assures more extensive security and protection for everyone on board.

The Cayman Registry's initiative proves to be a beacon of change in the yacht industry, pushing boundaries while keeping superior service, safety, and standards at the forefront. It is not merely about exceeding standards; it's about setting new benchmarks for the industry and aspiring for even greater heights.

title: Damen Yachting's Pioneer Xplorer 60 and Yacht Support 53 Embark on Global Ventures Following a Comprehensive Refit
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Damen Yachting's Pioneer Xplorer 60 and Yacht Support 53 Embark on Global Ventures Following a Comprehensive Refit
summary: Post refit, Damen Yachting's Superyachts, the Xplorer 60 and Yacht Support 53, are set to embark on an adventurous journey traversing the globe.
body: Damen Yachting's premier Xplorer 60 superyacht, After You, and her support ship, the 53-metre vessel Emotional, recently concluded their meticulously planned refit period. The works that these yachts underwent were deeply personalised to align with the unique needs and operational requirements of their respective owners. From refits and servicing to optimising performance, preparatory operations were substantial, preparing the fleet for ambitious exploration and worldwide cruising in remote locations.

Primarily designed for extreme adventure exploits, After You is the maiden yacht from Damen Yachting's Xplorer 60 series. Yet, while its robust exterior and robust steel hull invoke strength and fearlessness, the yacht is not void of luxury. Fitted with creature comforts consistent with a luxury superyacht, After You flaunts a spacious accommodation, an observation lounge presenting stunning 270-degree sights, and a versatile certified helideck capable of accommodating an array of helicopters.

Michel Coens, head of Refit & Services at Damen Yachting, praised the completion of the refurbishment operations, stating the return of the yachts as a significant vote of confidence in his team's skill, facilities, and collaborative spirit. He notes the departure of After You and Emotional, now embarking on their next voyage, as an uplifting moment of pride and accomplishment for the entire team.

title: The Stellar Superyachts Mooring in Monaco for the Glamorous 2026 F1 Grand Prix
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Stellar Superyachts Mooring in Monaco for the Glamorous 2026 F1 Grand Prix
summary: Every year, the gleaming playground of Monaco transforms into an aquatic showcase, playing host to impressive superyachts for the F1 Grand Prix weekend.
body: Year upon year, the glitz and glamour of the Monaco Grand Prix pull some of the world's most intriguing figures and their flamboyant superyachts to the sun-soaked Côte d'Azur. This luxurious weekend event transforms the city-state into an unparalleled nautical exhibition, as superyacht owners, charter guests, and Formula 1 aficionados flock to Monte Carlo's sun-drenched shores. And what an armada they bring. This year alone, 106 magnificent yachts have dropped anchor in Port Hercule, ready to enjoy the spectacle on Sunday, 7 June 2026. Yet, another 180 yachts are strewn along the idyllic French Riviera, dotting the coastline from Roquebrune-Cap-Martin to Beaulieu-sur-Mer with their monumental silhouettes. This is the enchanting world of the Monaco Grand Prix, where power, opulence, and engineering marvels converge. Concrete proof lies in last year's record-breaking congregation of yachts for the 2025 Formula One Grand Prix. A staggering 202 yachts, with 115 of them extending beyond 24 metres, found a home in and around Monaco, displaying a remarkable growth in popularity from the 167 yachts in 2022 to 187 in 2024. Not quite in the lap of the bustle yet comfortably close, Kismet, the Motor Yacht of the Year 2025 winner, makes her acclaimed appearance. A marvel of modern design, this 122m beauty boasts an exterior designed by Italian stalwart, Nuvolari Lenard, and interiors by Reymond Langton, ensuring charter guests enjoy palatial luxury at sea. As for the audacious Breakthrough, this hydrogen fuel-cell-powered superyacht has quite literally broken through conventions. With a design inspired by sustainability and long-range cruising, she is an extraordinary testament to technology's symbiotic relationship with naval architecture. Lastly, claiming its rightful place among the glittering lineup is Renaissance, a grand structure that perfectly embodies the wise old adage, 'every ship has its own story'. The result of an owner's decades-long endeavour, this remarkable vessel truly epitomises the unending quest for aquatic perfection. And as the day of the main event nears, all eyes are on the future — of Formula 1, luxury yachting, and the extraordinary fusion of the two in the heart of Monte Carlo. As the sun sets on the French Riviera, the anticipation for the Grand Prix packs the air, humming with the promise of speed, splendour, and a weekend of unalloyed joy on board the world’s most impressive, iconic superyachts.

title: Discover how Princess Yachts Advances the Marine Industry with the Launch of its Authentic Parts Platform
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover how Princess Yachts Advances the Marine Industry with the Launch of its Authentic Parts Platform
summary: Princess Yachts brings a new era for yacht maintenance and refit through their new platform bookended by authentic, factory-supplied parts.
body: Leading British builder, Princess Yachts, has held firm a proverbial champagne bottle against the hull of an innovative venture. The endeavour? - Princess Genuine - a new platform designed to revolutionise yacht maintenance, refit, and aftersales support. This platform acts as a nexus for yacht owners, skippers, and service professionals craving reliable, direct access to factory-supplied parts and accessories.

In an industry often marked with choppy waters, Princess Yachts has consistently outpaced rival undertow, fabricating top-tier service quality to match their iconic crafts. The creation of the Princess Genuine platform amplifies this commitment. The platform offers a practical means to promote safe sailing and prolong the lifespan and performance of their yachts.

Thus, as Princess Yachts charts a new course with its Princess Genuine platform, the company not just streamlines after-sales support processes for yacht owners but also underscores its dedication to nurturing the passions sailing aficionados hold dear.

The new platform gives users free access to industry analysis and interviews with marine industry veterans alongside the freshest news in the maritime sector. Innovations such as these serve as a gentle reminder: the joys of being on water are intrinsically tied to the quality of care each yacht receives.

So, adopt the Princess Genuine platform and amplify not just the functionality of your yacht, but also the essence of your sailing memories. Because with Princess Yachts, voyages become stories and seas transform into narratives.

title: Yacht Enthusiasts Unite: The Rhody Regatta Offers Thrilling Racing and Philanthropy Under One Sail
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Yacht Enthusiasts Unite: The Rhody Regatta Offers Thrilling Racing and Philanthropy Under One Sail
summary: Thrilling races and good-natured charity collide at the Rhody Regatta, a nautical spectacle that benefits the needy while challenging skilled sailors.
body: The Rhody Regatta, an eagerly anticipated annual event, proudly organised by the International Yacht and Athletic Club (IYAC), became the talk of the town not just for its thrilling races, but for its hearty support of Meals on Wheels in Rhode Island. Demonstrating that prudent decisions on the shoreline can lead to exhilarating experiences on the waves, the fourth regatta highlighted the synergy between strategic decisions and nautical prowess.

The skippers were challenged by dramatic shifts in the wind, current events and a variety of strategic decisions. Mick Harvey, the event's Co-Chair admitted, 'we lost five or six boats to the date change.' However, the competitors understood and appreciated both the Race Committee's decision and their efforts to conduct a safe and exciting event.

Emerging victorious with the best corrected time was Joe Brito's J/121 Incognito from Bristol, R.I. The race was not easy, with winds transitioning from light, shifty breezes in Narragansett Bay's East Passage to a complex collision of north and southwest sea breezes in the West Passage. Brito led by example, masterfully navigating these changes and finishing two minutes ahead of his class competitors on corrected time.

Among the day's many dramatic stories was the performance of Moose McClintock and Jeff O'Brien's JS9000 Slim Shady. Starting first in PHRF 1, the boat initially enjoyed more breeze than later starters and built an imposing lead approaching Beavertail point. Alas, the ever-shifting winds of fate caused a turn of events, but the regatta remained a triumphant combination of skilled sailing and charitable spirit.

title: The 43-metre Christensen Motor Yacht La Sirena Sees Major Price Reduction
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The 43-metre Christensen Motor Yacht La Sirena Sees Major Price Reduction
summary: The Christensen motor yacht, La Sirena, has just seen a substantial $500,000 decrease in its asking price.
body: Luxury does not come cheap, but it just became a tad bit more affordable on the marine front. The epitome of lavishness, the 43-metre Christensen motor yacht, La Sirena, has undergone a notable price reduction. Dealing a generous cut, RJC Yachts, who listed the vessel for sale, has announced a decrease of $500,000. Now, the superyacht is available for a snip at $6,495,000.

Constructed to the unrivaled ABS class by the esteemed American superyacht yard Christensen, La Sirena boasts impressive architectural feats. The naval architecture was also crafted by Christensen, and Setzer Yacht Architects designed the exterior. The interior, meanwhile, was brought to life by K.C. Designs alongside Sarah Fahey. The luxury motor yacht, outfitted in GRP, experienced a full refit in 2024. This update coincided with the completion of her ABS 25-year inspection and survey.

Beyond its shared spaces, La Sirena offers sumptuous private accommodations. Up to nine guests can enjoy their stay in a master suite and three queen-sized cabins, all complete with en suite bathroom facilities. Meanwhile, the spacious crew quarters can comfortably accommodate seven.

Yet comfort does not stop at the cabin literally; an enclosed aft deck with air-conditioning provides a large dining and lounging area. The surroundings are encased in windows, permitting guests to savour sweeping panoramic views. Meanwhile, the foredeck, coupled with a built-in sofa and sunpads, is set for some sun-soaking and relaxation.

To cap it all off, La Sirena offers an expansive flybridge, a perfect spot for al fresco cocktails and dining. With an inbuilt bar, barbecue, and a spa pool flanked by sunpads and paired with another bar, the yacht is determined to make a mark in the leisure and luxury aspects, infusing a dash of splendor to the sea.

title: Inverting Convention, Lagaria Reveals 90m Superyacht Concept 'Platea' as an Open-Air Club at Sea
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Inverting Convention, Lagaria Reveals 90m Superyacht Concept 'Platea' as an Open-Air Club at Sea
summary: The innovative design studio Lagaria, thriving in Monaco, presents a revolutionary superyacht concept, identified as Platea, where the outdoor experience is king.
body: Monaco-based design trailblazers Lagaria has just removed the curtain from their fresh, remarkably inclusive and forward-thinking superyacht concept, fittingly named Platea. The brainchild of founders Magnus Naglestad and Adeline Lagaria, Platea impeccably encapsulates their unique belief that the most memorable yacht experiences absolutely occur on deck and in the enchanting embrace of the open sea air. Platea eschews conventional yacht designs that aim to stuff the hull with enclosed space. Instead, it boasts a disruptive inverted layout that amplifies the importance of exterior deck areas. The yacht's main deck becomes the pivotal element of its form, forming an impressive, expansive social area that imitates an over water beach club. This groundbreaking design begins at the stern with an open-plan bar, lounge, and dining area that effortlessly converges into a secluded grand terrace. The terrace continues the tale of luxury with an expansive pool, a jacuzzi, and another full bar service. The yacht also accommodate a convenient helipad on the elevated foredeck to elevate user experience and access. Designers chose to relegate all guest accommodations to the lower deck. This insightful design decision was grounded in the aim to allocate prime deck-side space for social spaces that animate the yacht throughout the day. Further thoughtful design decisions include the aft bridge placement. Drawing inspiration from Scandinavian well-boat design, the move frees up the yacht's heart for a generous social zone, which simultaneously minimizes enclosed volume and gives full operational visibility via large wing stations. The owner's quarters consist of a private balcony-holding apartment located aft. Platea's gross weight is about 20% lower than similar superyachts, achieved by prioritizing experiential quality over interior volume. The novelty of its layout combined with intelligent spatial prioritization results in a refreshingly unique concept that, according to its creators, commands a higher charter revenue per gross tonnage than others. Platea stands as an emblem of change, a symbol of what can emerge when common expectations are overturned and new questions asked. The result truly sets it apart from anything else skimming the waves. Its design efficiency speaks volumes. Despite its internal volume being less, it compensates in terms of impeccable oceanic experience. Lagaria's modernistic mould-breaking approach, previously glimpsed in their collaborative work with Turkish shipyard RMK Yachts on the highly lauded 'Orca 58', promises to continually redefine the meaning of luxury at sea, making sailing a uniquely immersive celebration of life's finest pleasures.

title: The Astounding Feadship Superyacht, Project 826, Takes Final Voyage to Amsterdam for the Last of Construction
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Astounding Feadship Superyacht, Project 826, Takes Final Voyage to Amsterdam for the Last of Construction
summary: Feadship's extraordinary 80-metre superyacht, aptly known as Project 826, sails on to its final construction phase, including sea trials now in Amsterdam.
body: Pictures released by the Dutch yard Feadship showcases the impressive and elegant 80-metre superyacht, previously known as Project Thalassa, making its way to significant facilities in Amsterdam. Here, it will commence the closing stages of construction, which involves sea trials. This massive project was initially launched in April, splashing onto the scene at Feadship's yard in Kaag. BOATPro's insider knowledge hints at a delivery date as soon as this coming summer.

Awe-inspiring exterior design by none other than Malcolm McKeon reveals a striking low, sculpted appearance for Project 826. Inspired by dynamic sailing yachts, the superyacht presents a sharp plumb bow and a widening hull. Its delicately curved windows and sleek lines round off the aesthetically pleasing finish. While the interiors, crafted by the acclaimed Milanese studio M2Atelier, remain a closely-guarded secret, their contemporary design has been hinted at with descriptions of warmth and relaxation casually tossed our way.

From the beach club, the superyacht's wanderlust inducing watersports area unfolds. There are also designated fitness spaces, including a yoga area and weight room both encompassing fold-out terraces. One enticing feature includes a main deck pool lounge boasting a glass-bottomed pool that absorbs all the natural light bathing the beach club below.

This pleasure palace on water redefines luxury with its transforming winter gardens, an open-planned sun deck with a minimal yet effective hardtop, circular bar, and comfortable seating area. Fancy a bit of sports action? Project 826 has got you covered with a touch-and-go helipad transformed into a pickleball court.

Hitting the waves at 16 knots max speed and capable of covering 5,500 nautical miles at 12 knots, Project 826 is a testament to marine engineering prowess. With an estimated summer delivery date, this magnificent creation is sure to make waves in the yachting world soon.

title: American Skipper Erica Lush Bows Out of La Solitaire Du Figaro Amidst Sailing Incident
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: American Skipper Erica Lush Bows Out of La Solitaire Du Figaro Amidst Sailing Incident
summary: American sailor Erica Lush unsuspectingly leaves the third leg of La Solitaire du Figaro Paprec following an unexpected mainsail mishap.
body: Dramatic news today from the heart of the fiercely competitive world of yacht racing: Erica Lush, the American Skipper, was forced to retire from her position in the La Solitaire du Figaro Paprec during Leg 3 of the race. Sailing off the coast of Île de Ré, Lush sat in the 36th position when disaster struck, tearing her mainsail as a weather front passed in the early hours of Tuesday morning.

The experienced sailor valiantly attempted to repair the damage, to no avail. With no other solution at hand that would allow her to continue racing with the damaged mainsail, withdrawal was the only course of action available for Lush. As a result, she did the only thing that was left for her: she notified Race Direction of her retirement at 6:49 a.m.

This incident serves as a stark reminder of just how unpredictable the world of competitive sailing can be, as sailors have to be prepared to calmly face the unpredictable tribulations of the ocean. It’s not just a test of sailing expertise, but also a test of endurance, resilience, quick thinking, and an unyielding spirit. The sea might have won this round, but rest assured, Erica Lush will return to conquer, stronger than ever before.

title: Day 2 of ILCA 6 Masters World Championships 2026 Offers Up Thrilling Sailing Conditions and Intense Competitions
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Day 2 of ILCA 6 Masters World Championships 2026 Offers Up Thrilling Sailing Conditions and Intense Competitions
summary: After a day of thrilling races, the ILCA 6 Masters World Championships 2026 further shapes up the leaderboard with sailors fighting it out in perfect sailing conditions.
body: As the second day of the 2026 ILCA 6 Masters World Championships descends, the dust settles over at the Nautical Club of Kalamaki, setting the perfect scene for adventurous tales of grit, tenacity, and skilful sailing. Warm Mediterranean waters were graced by a fleet of global sailors who went head-to-head with nature and each other, battling it out in classic Athens sea-breeze conditions. Two highly competitive races were held, successfully totalling four races thus far. This helped to clarify the positions of individuals across all divisions on the leaderboard. The day started off with a modest breeze blowing in from the South. As the afternoon took over, the wind speed bumped up to facilitate a more challenging competition. Moderate sea conditions were the perfect arena for this high stakes race. With the leadership at stake, Jon Emmett, a seasoned sailor from Great Britain, was buzzing with excitement. Jon gleefully remarked that the day's atmosphere was electric and he thoroughly enjoyed the intense sailing conditions in which one slight miscalculation could lead to irreparable damage in the race. Reflecting on days past, he fondly recollected his experiences at the Senior Europeans in 2024. Coming back to these waters again brought a rush of excitement and nostalgia, making the ILCA Masters racing all the more special. Commenting on her experience, Greece's Anna Agrafioti navigated through choppy waters in her home city. Despite the challenging wave conditions, she is determined to push harder tomorrow. With the completion of four races in the championship, patterns are beginning to emerge with consistent performance becoming a crucial determining factor. It is still early to predict the final winners as the competition stands neck-to-neck across all divisions. Eyes are now set on tomorrow's events - two more races that promise to bring more thrill and excitement to Greece's famous waters. With the first signal set for 13:00, the quest for world championship continues as sailors set sail again.

title: Yacht Tragedy in Turkey: 40-Metre Bering Familia Motor Yacht Sinks Mysteriously
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Yacht Tragedy in Turkey: 40-Metre Bering Familia Motor Yacht Sinks Mysteriously
summary: A 40-metre Bering motor yacht, Familia, has shockingly sank in Sinop, Turkey, leaving a mystery to be unraveled.
body: In the idyllic waters of Sinop, Turkey, a tragic turn of events has unfolded. The 40-metre Bering motor yacht, Familia, found herself succumbing to the waters on a fateful Saturday evening. By Sunday morning, her hull was completely submerged, leaving only her superstructure poking out from the watery abyss.

Amidst heavy rain, the ship began taking on water and eventually sank, though the exact cause of the predicament remains a mystery. The six crew members on board at the time were all evacuated in haste, but thankfully without any injuries, hinting at their preparedness and resilience in the face of adversity.

The AIS tracker confirms that the Familia arrived at the Sinop Pier on Thursday, making her stay a tragically short one before catastrophe struck two days later. Local reports now suggest that attempts have begun to salvage the sunken pride.

As the adventures at sea continue, this unfortunate episode serves as a stark reminder: for all the allure that comes with exotic yachting, the inhabitants of mother earth must always respect the depths and the secrets they hold. The maritime community will follow the subsequent developments with bated breath, hoping to unravel the mystery shrouding the sinking of the Familia.

title: The Luxurious RJ102 Explorer Yacht Mon Coeur Graces the Coastline: A Novel Offering by Cantiere delle Marche
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Luxurious RJ102 Explorer Yacht Mon Coeur Graces the Coastline: A Novel Offering by Cantiere delle Marche
summary: Cantiere delle Marche (CdM) unveils its 31-metre RJ102 explorer yacht, Mon Coeur, blending rugged performance with elegant design.
body: Consider this - a yacht that melds the rugged capability of an explorer yacht with the refined elegance of Italian craftsmanship. Introduce this paradox to the renowned shipyard - Cantiere delle Marche (CdM), and the result is the majestic 31-metre RJ102 explorer yacht, Mon Coeur. As the RJ Class explorer line's smallest addition, Mon Coeur is not lightweight on features.

Designed in collaboration with Italian designer Francesco Paszkowski, the yacht exemplifies striking lines that resonate with the RJ identity, conveying bold, purposeful profiles. Paszkowski elegantly intertwined a sinuous stern, subtly flared bow, and recessed windows that embody the yacht's distinctive avant-garde look. Mon Coeur neatly packages the same commanding presence and assured ocean-readiness typically ascribed to larger yachts.

'Understated and elegant yet richly detailed,' Mon Coeur’s overall design concept points directly at the fulfilment of the owners' visions, designed to serve as their world exploration base camp aboard. Cassetta honours the yacht's objective by extensively customising the layout to cater to a limited number of guests, thereby enriching the intimate sharing of sea conquest experiences.

The new RJ102 is powered by twin Caterpillar C18 Acert IMO TIER III engines, promising a range of 3,500 nautical miles at 10 knots, with key dimensions including a 7.3-metre beam and a full load displacement of 250t.

CdM's co-founder and CEO, Vasco Buonpensiere, underscored Mon Coeur's bespoke design, reflecting the owner's aspirations and entrepreneurial spirit. Mon Coeur, inaugurated as the RJ family's most compact design, signifies the successful actualisation of mariner's dreams into reality.

Mon Coeur's owners spoke at the launch, extolling their extraordinary journey of conceptualising and realising the yacht with the CdM team. Mon Coeur stands at the crossroads of a successful partnership and exciting seafaring ventures, delivering the wanted quality and capability.

title: Unprecedented Half-Million-Dollar Price Reduction Announced for Prestigious Sanlorenzo Motor Yacht 'Another One'
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unprecedented Half-Million-Dollar Price Reduction Announced for Prestigious Sanlorenzo Motor Yacht 'Another One'
summary: In a significant pricing update, the extraordinary 34-metre Sanlorenzo motor yacht known as 'Another One' receives a magnificent price cut of $500,000.
body: The Sanlorenzo motor yacht, 'Another One', has been relisted with a $500,000 reduction in price. This luxurious yacht is now open to buyers for an impressive $12,450,000. Featuring sleek designs by Zuccon International Project and breath-taking interiors by Lissoni & Partners, this yacht is tailor-made for opulence and comfort.

Designed with a modern and minimalistic style, the interiors of 'Another One' are truly eye-catching. One can enjoy the convenience of an open plan dining area and kitchen, alongside a saloon that boasts a large L-shaped sofa and coffee table. The dining area, situated towards the front, can accommodate six guests for a formal dining experience. Connecting all decks, an awe-inspiring spiral staircase is the central point of this yacht's design.

The guest cabins, all en suite, are located on the lower deck of the 'Another One' and include an owner's suite, two double cabins, and a twin. These spaces promise undisturbed privacy and supreme comfort for up to eight guests, along with accommodations for five crew members.

The yacht's prime feature is the atypically expansive beach club, designed in the fashion of explorer-style yachts. This area showcases a spacious 90-square-metre swim platform, extendable with fold-down terraces on both sides. Moveable furniture pieces can easily transform this space into an open-air lounge, while the indoor area also serves as a fully-equipped gym or a shaded daybed area.

Adding to its list of multitasking capabilities, the indoor beach club's interior doubles as a storage space for a tender and crane while the yacht is underway. Powered by four Volvo Penta IPS engines, each boasting a whopping 1,350hp, the 'Another One' offers an impressive maximum speed of 23 knots. With a cruising speed of 20 knots, she guarantees a pleasant journey of up to 1,600 nautical miles. This sleek marvel, now available at a reduced price, is the very definition of elegance, adventure, and sea-bound freedom.

title: Unfurling New Horizons: International Marine Management Acquires Atlantic Refit Center, Steering into European Waters
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unfurling New Horizons: International Marine Management Acquires Atlantic Refit Center, Steering into European Waters
summary: Leading Caribbean refit powerhouse, International Marine Management (IMM), purchases Atlantic Refit Center in its strategic move into Europe. The acquisition marks a significant milestone for IMM as it expands its global footprint.
body: Upon the undulating tides of the flourishing yachting industry, a Caribbean behemoth has charted its course towards European waters. International Marine Management (IMM), with its four robust decades of experience, has acquired the Atlantic Refit Center (ARC) without disclosing the investment amount. This acquisition is a milestone in IMM's journey as it extends its operations to European shores, forming a complete circle back to where it all commenced for IMM's Founder and COO, Fabrice Maitre.

Maitre's illustrious career saw its inception in France, where he was instrumental in crucial refits of distinguished yachts such as Octopus, Skat, and Kogo, with the initial turn-around involving Tatoosh in La Rochelle in 2007. This virtuosic journey has led him back to French shores with a purpose to integrate IMM’s robust work ethic and high standards at ARC, imparting a fresh perspective to the region that he knows intimately.

IMM's acquisition of ARC is a monumental move that carries forward a diverse portfolio for the largest Caribbean refit operator. The firm's 130 dedicated personnel, spread across bases including Puerto Rico, St. Maarten, Guadeloupe, and Grenada, enables comprehensive servicing of the yachting market. The new inclusion of ARC now equips IMM to handle vessels up to 150 meters in length.

Located strategically, ARC holds the distinction of being the only deep-sea port along the French Atlantic coast. Its perfect geographic location supplemented with infrastructural splendor featuring two dry docks, a 250-ton travel lift, 300-meter afloat repair docks, 2,000 square-meter hard-standing space, and cranes capable of hoisting 150 tons, enriches its capacity for large-scale refit and conversion projects.

The Atlantic Refit Center, with its impressive two-decade long operational history, avows its prowess with the past vessel projects. Particularly, the conversion of the 71-meter Enigma XK, acknowledged at the World Superyacht Awards, has reinforced ARC's reputation in the refit sector.

In the aftermath of this distinguished acquisition, IMM's experienced team will helm the shipyard operations, ensuring a smooth and seamless transition. The outgoing President of ARC, Stéphane Marcelli, although stepping back, will remain integral to the daily operations further solidifying the handover process. As the sails unfurl to this new voyage, it fittingly marks a new chapter for the yard as it reaffirms its positioning in the international yachting sector.

title: Budding Sailors Compete Fervently in Final Merlin Rocket Youth Training and Championship
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Budding Sailors Compete Fervently in Final Merlin Rocket Youth Training and Championship
summary: Emerging talents in sailing experience an exciting mixture of fervent competition and camaraderie at the final session of the Merlin Rocket youth training program.
body: Commencing at a young age, many sailors sail single-handed dinghies, gradually moving up through different fleets. Yet there is something incredibly enticing about stepping in a Merlin Rocket for the first time. It's enough to completely sweep off anyone's feet. This specific difference was discovered by several young sailors in a training session held at Fisher Green Sailing Club. Unlike any other normal day of training, May 23rd was different. It was the culmination of a series of training sessions leading up to the final Merlin Rocket youth program session. During this day, eight talented sailors took over Fishers Green Sailing Club, dividing into four teams and battling the light winds in an all-out sailing extravaganza. With the bank holiday sun beating down on them, our young sailors threw themselves into the spirit of competition with gusto, each aiming to keep their sailing boat, the beloved 'Stanley', smoothly cruising. Guided by their brilliant coach, Courtney, they mastered popping the top batten even in the lightest of breezes. The culmination of the day was a highly-anticipated round-robin race series. The stakes were higher than ever - victory meant not just glory but the prestigious Willetts Trophy. Amidst intense competition, strategies were plotted and executed meticulously, competitors forged and renewed alliances, but most importantly, they learned the joy and thrill of being on water. The brilliance of this event lies not just in creating a platform for young sailors to showcase their skills, but in forging a strong sense of camaraderie and community amongst the sailors. As they pushed their limits, battled the wind and waves, they found not just their strengths, but also friends for life. Hence, the Merlin Rocket Youth Training and Championship was more than a sailing event, it was an experience that moulded budding sailors and instilled in them a lifelong love for sailing.

title: Unleashing the Technohull Alpha 45: Awe-inspiring Speed Melded with Unrivalled Comfort
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unleashing the Technohull Alpha 45: Awe-inspiring Speed Melded with Unrivalled Comfort
summary: Discover the raw power and luxuriant comfort nestled within Technohull's outstanding new creation: the Alpha 45. Built for high-speed exhilaration without compromising on comfort.
body: Athens-based boatbuilders, Technohull, have once again shattered expectations with their latest water marvel: the Alpha 45. This stunning 13.8m motorboat, encased in a stepped Dynastream deep-vee hull, has been designed for potent performance on the water, delivering stunning speeds in excess of 85 knots. Don't be fooled though. The Alpha 45 is no bare-bones racing machine, but a decadent display of seafaring sophistication offering ample day boating comfort.

The Alpha 45 is a testament to clever engineering and design. It boasts a broad 4.3m beam, accounting for 31% of its overall length, a figure that is striking for a high-performance craft. This breadth enables a full walkaround layout, allowing easy movement fore and aft on both sides of the boat, alongside ample room for two banks of triple helm seats. Positioned dead center, the helmsman can revel in unobstructed all-around visibility.

Flexibility is integral to the Alpha 45's deck layout. Various seating options can be tailored to specific needs, ranging from a small to large sunpad coupled with forward-facing seating or an L-shaped transom bench and easy port-side access. The cabin, accessible via a push-button gull-wing door, includes not just a double berth but also a heads compartment with appreciable headroom - barring the most secluded corners of the forepeak.

In terms of propulsion, the Alpha 45 doesn't mandate 2,000hp outboards. Owners opting for a more moderate pace can choose either a triple rig or inboard diesel engines, extending cruising range while creating a larger aft sun bed and freeing swim platforms for watersports. Although, the 1,400L fuel tanks may necessitate an upgrade in the future, particularly for those thrillingly top-rated quad 500s.
The Technohull Alpha 45: a stunning exemplar of innovation, design, and performance, undoubtedly set to propel Technohull as a leading light amidst global motoryacht enthusiasts.

title: Classic Winsome`s Phenomenal Victory in RORC De Guingand Bowl Race 2026: A Seamless Display of Sailing
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Classic Winsome`s Phenomenal Victory in RORC De Guingand Bowl Race 2026: A Seamless Display of Sailing
summary: At the 2026 RORC De Guingand Bowl Race, Classic Winsome carved out a victory, showcasing extraordinary seamanship, speed, and tactical racing.
body: The 2026 RORC De Guingand Bowl Race turned out to be a vivid symphony of top-notch seamanship, admirable speed, and strategic racing. The entire racing canvas featured a formidable mix of seasoned sailors, agile speedboats, and razor-sharp decisions that made for a spectacle worth witnessing.

The classic yacht, an S&S 41 Winsome, owned by Harry Heijst, stood tall among all, striding ahead to seize the cup on IRC (International Rating Certificate) Overall after time correction. Ben Owens JPK 1010 Leonard, manned by a two-person team, trailed behind by a mere 13 minutes and 29 seconds, illustrating the cutthroat competition at hand.

Heijst highlighted a few tactical victories on the course, one of which involved a smartly executed double gybe just before a buoy and a timely tack change for the bigger breeze, essentially demonstrating the crew's years of experience and rehearsed efficiency.

A key highlight of the race was the nerve-wracking duel for Monohull Line Honours between RORC Vice Commodore Derek Shakespeare's J/122 Bulldog and Nick & Jacquetta Edmonds' J/45 Stickleback, in which the latter emerged glorious, just 73 seconds ahead. This marked the pinnacle of arduous competition, seasoned mastery, and the sheer joy of boating.

title: Foiling Fury Returned to Bermuda as SailGP’s 2026 Title Battle Tightened
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: SailGP Returned to Bermuda as the Championship Fight Intensified on the Great Sound
summary: The Rolex SailGP Championship returned to Bermuda’s Great Sound as title rivals clashed in high-speed foiling conditions, with shifting weather, crew reshuffles and championship pressure raising the stakes dramatically.
body: Few places in world sailing make high-performance racing look as outrageously fast as Bermuda Great Sound. Flat water. Clean breeze. Foiling catamarans flying at motorway speeds just metres from shore. When the Rolex SailGP Championship returned to Bermuda for the fifth event of the 2026 season, the atmosphere already felt charged before a single F50 hit the racecourse.
