The championship table had tightened. Crews had shifted. Pressure had increased. Nobody arrived in Bermuda comfortable. That was especially true for the BONDS Flying Roos, who entered the event leading the overall standings after a commanding performance in Rio. Australia held a seven-point advantage over the chasing pack, but even three-time SailGP champion Tom Slingsby knew Bermuda would be different. Because on the Great Sound, outright boat speed rarely guarantees survival. Everybody is fast there. Very fast.

Bermuda has always exposed the finer details inside SailGP. The Great Sound removes excuses. There are no massive ocean swells masking mistakes. No chaotic sea states disrupting foil stability. No hiding behind raw horsepower. The water is so flat the boats operate close to their absolute limits almost continuously. That changes everything. Tiny tactical errors become brutally expensive. Bad starts get punished instantly. One missed manoeuvre can bury an entire race. Slingsby understood that perfectly heading into the weekend, acknowledging that Bermuda would likely come down to pure racing skill rather than technical performance differences between teams. He was right. Because when every F50 is fully lit up and foiling cleanly at nearly 100 kilometres per hour, the margins become microscopic.

Few teams entered Bermuda carrying more frustration than Emirates GBR. After a disastrous last-place finish in Rio, British driver Dylan Fletcher arrived focused on restoring consistency rather than chasing heroics. That mattered. SailGP seasons are not won through occasional brilliance alone. They are built through relentless consistency across wildly different conditions and venues. Fletcher’s focus centred heavily on starts, communication and teamwork — the areas that often separate podium finishers from teams left staring angrily at the replay screen afterwards. Especially in Bermuda. Because once the fleet compresses at high speed near the boundaries, races become unforgivingly tactical.

The opening day produced exactly the kind of conditions SailGP teams dream about. Stable breeze. Dead-flat water. Perfect foiling pressure. The F50s looked completely unleashed. Phil Robertson of Red Bull Italy described the conditions as ideal for pushing the boats to their limits. And that was obvious from the shoreline. The boats spent huge periods locked fully airborne, slicing across the Great Sound with almost frightening stability. At those speeds, every crossing feels violent. Distances vanish instantly. Closing speeds become absurd. Mistakes happen faster than crews can process them. Which is why SailGP remains such compelling viewing when conditions line up like Bermuda delivered on Saturday.

Sunday changed the script entirely. The breeze softened. Pressure became patchy. The easy rhythm of high-speed foiling disappeared and the fleet suddenly found itself fighting a far more tactical racecourse. That shift mattered enormously. SailGP often looks straightforward in strong breeze because the boats remain consistently airborne. Lighter conditions create uncertainty. Foils drop. Pressure lines split. Decisions become riskier. The Great Sound stopped rewarding pure aggression and began rewarding patience, timing and adaptability. And that is where championship campaigns can quietly unravel. Because consistency becomes far harder when conditions stop behaving predictably.

The Bermuda event also arrived amid significant movement across the SailGP fleet following the absence of New Zealand SailGP Team. The Black Foils remained sidelined after suffering major damage earlier in the season, triggering a fascinating reshuffling of talent between teams. Liv Mackay once again joined DS Automobiles Team France, while legendary wing trimmer Glenn Ashby stepped in for the injured Leigh McMillan. Meanwhile Marcus Hansen joined ROCKWOOL Racing as the Danes searched for momentum in the standings. Crew continuity matters enormously in SailGP. These boats operate at such extreme speed that communication becomes almost instinctive inside successful teams. Every late reaction costs metres. Sometimes races.

More than 5,000 spectators packed the sold-out Race Stadium at Morgan’s Point across the weekend, proving once again why Bermuda remains one of SailGP’s strongest venues. The shoreline proximity transforms the racing into something uniquely visceral. Fans do not simply watch these boats. They feel them. The acceleration. The spray. The strange silence when the foils fully engage. Then the sudden roar as an F50 rips past at terrifying speed. Nathan Outteridge of Artemis SailGP Team highlighted exactly that dynamic, noting how close the boats race to shore in Bermuda. From a spectator perspective, few sailing events in the world currently match it.

One of the quieter but more interesting storylines came from Switzerland SailGP Team. Driver Sébastien Schneiter arrived in Bermuda carrying renewed optimism following the team’s new partnership with luxury travel brand Explora Journeys. After a difficult start to the season, the rebrand appeared to inject fresh confidence into the Swiss programme. Sometimes in professional sport, momentum matters psychologically as much as technically. Especially in SailGP, where confidence can directly influence how aggressively teams attack starts and crossings.

Bermuda reminded everybody why SailGP works best when the conditions let the boats fully breathe. The Great Sound turned the fleet loose. The racing became faster, tighter and more unforgiving with every heat. Some teams arrived chasing momentum. Others arrived trying to stop the bleeding. By the end of the weekend, one thing felt increasingly clear: The 2026 SailGP championship was no longer settling into a predictable hierarchy. It was becoming a fight. A proper one. Exactly what foiling catamaran racing should look like when the breeze is up and the pressure starts climbing inside the fleet. Because at 50 knots, everybody looks calm from the shore. On board is usually another story entirely.

title: Unpredictable Winds Wreak Havoc at Mubadala Sail Grand Prix: Only Four Boats Brave the Turbulence
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unpredictable Winds Wreak Havoc at Mubadala Sail Grand Prix: Only Four Boats Brave the Turbulence
summary: The Mubadala New York Sail Grand Prix was beset by chaos as swirling winds permitted only four boats to launch, further shrinking to a mere trio after an unfortunate incident.
body: The Mubadala New York Sail Grand Prix, a typically high-spirit event, was veiled in an aura of uncertainty and disarray on its opening day. The villains? Swirling, insolent winds which fiendishly caused significant deployment issues for the F50 fleet. Only a daring quadruplet of boats braved the unruly conditions and successfully launched onto the water.

Fate, however, had an even crueler trick up her sleeve. The Bonds Flying Roos, an Australian entrant, nosedived disastrously after launch, resulting in substantial damage and consequently removing them from the remaining race events. The unfortunate mishap instantly reduced the number of contenders to a minuscule trio.

In the face of such challenges, the spirit of sailors shines brightest. Now reduced to three, the competition at the New York Sail Grand Prix soldiers on, perfectly encapsulating the resilience and indomitable spirit intrinsic to the sport. Therein lies the charm of sail racing - in adversity, the true champions rise.

title: Jaw-Dropping Scenes at the Mubadala New York Sail Grand Prix as Only Four Boats Launch and Conquer Unforeseen Challenges
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Jaw-Dropping Scenes at the Mubadala New York Sail Grand Prix as Only Four Boats Launch and Conquer Unforeseen Challenges
summary: The Mubadala New York Sail Grand Prix was marked with unpredictable weather, unexpected setbacks, and intense competition.
body: Sailing is synonymous with unpredictability and the first day of the Mubadala New York Sail Grand Prix was a testament to this. With swirling winds causing havoc, only four F50s out of the entire fleet launched. The daunting conditions did not stop there. In a heart-stopping moment, the Bonds Flying Roos met with an unfortunate mishap, nosediving and suffering significant damages. This further squeezed the competition to just three boats. However, the races went forward, with the teams that could brave the weather scoring points.

The event was not devoid of unrest, as teams unable to participate due to unavoidable circumstances were left to start the second day with no points to their names. In an environment where every point matters, this situation undoubtedly aroused significant disquiet amongst those affected.

While it wasn't always smooth sailing, there was a noticeable shift in the Swiss team’s mentality. Their focus was not just on survival, but also on evolving as a more competitive and aggressive outfit. As aspiration surges in the heart of every sailor, the debacles of the New York Sail Grand Prix reminded them that the essence of sailing lies not in the tranquillity of waters but in navigating the unpredictability of the winds. This story of resilience, grit, and bravery set against the backdrop of the teeming city of New York, serves as a testament to the indomitable spirit of sailing.

title: Vital Training Camp Catapults African Sailors Toward 2026 Youth Olympics in Dakar
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Vital Training Camp Catapults African Sailors Toward 2026 Youth Olympics in Dakar
summary: At a seaside training camp in Tangier, young African sailors intensify preparations for the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympics, accelerating the pace on their Olympic voyage.
body: When adventure mingles with ambition, a compelling chapter in sailing history is written. Such a narrative is emerging on the historic coasts of Tangier, Morocco, where the third World Sailing Youth Olympic Games (YOG) training camp unfolded recently. It's here that 13 athletes and eight hardworking coaches from Africa united, driven by the wave of a shared Olympic dream. Their eyes are set on one target - the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal, expected to be held in November 2026. Sailors from nations including Algeria, Egypt, Tunisia, Madagascar, and Morocco, were further bolstered by first-time participants from Angola and South Africa. This confluence was orchestrated by World Sailing, fueled by funds from the International Olympic Committee's Olympic Solidarity initiative. The camp focused on eliminating development barriers and equipping these African athletes and trainers with elite technical acumen to compete effectively. Fiona Kidd, the Head of International Development at World Sailing, proudly acknowledged the camp's contribution in empowering both athletes and the sport's sustainability in Africa. But the camp's effects were far more sweeping, extending much beyond the waters. The camp managed to challenge and overcome one of the most daunting hurdles in African sailing - the access to equipment, thanks to a partnership with Tahe Outdoors, who loaned 10 boards to the participating nations. The boards ensured continuity in the sailors' training by enabling them to train consistently even in their local waters, and empowered the coaches to build superior local programmes. The training was characterized by thorough technical instruction and race practice. Growth metrics showed a surge in the sailors' technical skills, tactical insight and confidence. The camp’s success was built not just on water, but off it as well, with world-class support from the Royal Moroccan Sailing Federation and logistics managed by Nuno Reiss of the PROW Group, and the Secretary and Coach of the Royal Tangier Yacht Club. This not only helped in smooth execution of the event but also facilitated visas and ensured smooth local delivery.

title: The Remarkable Debut of Excess 13 Catamaran Turns Heads at APAC Boat Shows
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Remarkable Debut of Excess 13 Catamaran Turns Heads at APAC Boat Shows
summary: The Excess 13 Catamaran, a thrilling blend of sports performance and comfortable cruising, has garnered rich accolades on its Asia-Pacific foray.
body: Stealing the limelight at the Sanctuary Cove International Boat Show, the Excess 13 Catamaran made a grand entrance into the Australian nautical scene. Thanks to the concerted efforts of local dealers 38 South Yacht Sales and World Wide Boat Brokers, the sparkling debut was made possible. Throughout the four-day event, the catamaran attracted a bevy of visitors and enthusiastic admirers.

The revelries moved a notch higher when Excess hosted a press gathering. The brand's latest developments and regional growth strategies were shared. Guests were treated to a guided tour of the Excess 13, which showcased the model's impressive features. The event later morphed into a vibrant soiree. As live music wafted through the air and a gentle breeze set in, guests savoured cocktails onboard the versatile catamaran, truly soaking in the sporty yet relaxed spirit that encapsulates the Excess 13.

Following its successful Australian debut, the Excess 13 cast its spell across the Asia Pacific region. Earlier, the first Excess 13 launched in Brisbane, Australia. Subsequently, it sailed the waters of Thailand and made quite a splash at the Malaysia International Boat Show, eliciting strong interest from attendees. The Singapore Yachting Festival was another remarkable platform where the Excess 13 received glowing praise, further establishing its international reputation.

With every new launch, the Excess 13 embarks on an exhilarating voyage, delighting sailing enthusiasts across the globe with its innovative design, convenience, and sporty spirit. This lively blend of practicality and adventure underpins the appeal of the Excess 13, as it continues to make waves in the global sailing community. Its journey thus far signals a promising trajectory, fueled by a blend of innovation and passion for sailing.

title: Inkfish Partners with Vard for a Record-Breaking €700M Marine Research Vessel Construction
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Inkfish Partners with Vard for a Record-Breaking €700M Marine Research Vessel Construction
summary: Gabe Newell's ocean research organization, Inkfish, signs a historic €700M contract with the Norwegian shipyard, Vard, for a distinguished 162m research vessel.
body: In a landmark partnership, Inkfish, a marine research organization co-founded by Oceanco owner and tech visionary, Gabe Newell, has commissioned a 162-meter research vessel from Vard, a leading Norwegian shipyard. This endeavour, costing almost €700 million and named RV11000, sets both a record for Vard for the most significant contract ever secured for a single vessel and for any Norwegian shipyards for the most considerable order of its kind. Drawing on the engineering prowess of Inkfish’s 100-meter RV6000, RV11000 is a tour de force in marine research technology. Pairing Vard design with technical partner YTMC, additional support from Fincantieri Group, and Inkfish's knowledge, this vessel is specifically tailored to oceanic research activities. Its capabilities encompass seafloor mapping, handling submarines and conducting ROV operations at depths up to a staggering 11,000 meters. In order to facilitate such state-of-the-art research, the RV11000 is equipped with a gamut of onboard features. Among these are a stern-mounted A-frame system for submarine launch and recovery, a dedicated ROV hangar, and a fibre-rope lifting system with an impressive 15,000-meter capacity. Her hull has been optimized to deliver top-notch seabed mapping performance and her accommodation is set to house 130 crew members and scientists, alongside expansive facilities and working spaces tailored for marine research. The RV11000 is also fitted with a record-breaking battery installation, enabling up to 12 hours of silent scientific sub operations. As a nod to the tech-forward ethos of the organization, it meets the latest IACS cybersecurity requirements to ensure protection against digital threats. This vessel propels marine research into a new age of discovery and exploration. Inkfish’s commitment to unveiling the deep-sea mysteries aligns seamlessly with Vard’s proven shipbuilding expertise. The RV11000 encapsulates the collective vision of these pioneering entities to enable scientists to reveal previously uncharted marine terrains and usher in groundbreaking scientific discoveries. As Stu Buckle, new builds and special projects at Inkfish, affirms, this next-generation vessel offers 'greater capability, flexibility and reach to enable science,' pushing the boundaries of marine research and serving as a testament to human innovation and aspiration.

title: Hong Kong's Lai Sun Development Offloads 80% Stake in Global Superyacht Firm, Camper & Nicholsons
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Hong Kong's Lai Sun Development Offloads 80% Stake in Global Superyacht Firm, Camper & Nicholsons
summary: Hong Kong investment holding company, Lai Sun Development, has announced the sale of their 80% stake in global superyacht services provider, Camper & Nicholsons.
body: Hong Kong's investment giant, Lai Sun Development, is charting new waters with its recent announcement. The firm has decided to sell an initial 80% stake in Camper & Nicholsons, the world-renowned superyacht services provider. Valued at an impressive €40 million, the momentous deal shakes up the superyacht industry's landscape.

Camper & Nicholsons is celebrated globally for its industry-leading superyacht services. Since its inception, the firm has been at the helm of excellence, offering a top-tier roster of services to the superyacht community. This includes everything from sales, chartering and yacht management to crew placement and marketing services. With a solid reputation for delivering a comprehensive and unparalleled service offering, Camper & Nicholsons prides itself as the 'go-to' provider in the superyacht industry.

title: Experience the Thrill of Beaconing Waves: New 25m Sportfish Yacht Coming to Life at Weaver Boatworks
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Experience the Thrill of Beaconing Waves: New 25m Sportfish Yacht Coming to Life at Weaver Boatworks
summary: The esteemed American shipyard, Weaver Boatworks, is crafting another marvel - a 24.5-metre sportfish yacht, set to enhance the passions of seafarers.
body: Renowned for making tangible the nautical dreams of seafaring enthusiasts, Weaver Boatworks has embarked on another adventure. This time, the talented artisans are shaping a fully-grown beauty, a compelling 24.5-metre sportfish yacht. Set in the heart of Maryland, the project seizes the essence of all the six preceding units from the series that first hit the water back in 2008.

Based on the yard's flagship design elements, the new build will sport a planing modified deep V hull, a tumblehome transom, flared bow and hard chines, reflecting a striking silhouette on water. Using a perfect blend of wood and epoxy, this premium yacht is being crafted from design blueprints by the late naval architect, Donald L. Blount. The blend of strength, durability, and aesthetic appeal promise nothing short of a pristine piece of craftsmanship.

Appropriately armed for its challenges, the architectural marvel will bear a robust 6.5-metre beam and an impressive volume of 78GT. An unparalleled horsepower will be delivered through twin MTU 16V2000M96 engines, ensuring a swift and stable journey across the seaward expanses.

While the shipyard is known for its iconic 29.6-metre 18 Reeler, delivered in 2019 as a unique custom project, the upcoming sportfish yacht is eagerly anticipated by the maritime community and is expected to set sail in 2028. A testament to the yard's commitment to excellence, Weaver Boatworks has, to date, successfully delivered nine yachts surpassing the 24-metre mark, constantly raising the bar for marine craftsmanship.

title: Advanced Load Sensing Technology Empowering Sailors Everywhere: Meet smartlink² Atto 1.2t
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Advanced Load Sensing Technology Empowering Sailors Everywhere: Meet smartlink² Atto 1.2t
summary: The smartlink² Atto 1.2t, an achievement in affordable load sensing technology, is set to revolutionize how sailors perceive and react to load data.
body: In a major development for the sailing world, Cyclops Marine has launched the smartlink² Atto 1.2t, an innovative load sensor offering remarkable value and efficiency. Originally crafted for the 36th America's Cup, this technology has been optimized and made accessible for every type of sailing, whether it be dinghy racing or weekend cruising. This technological marvel allows sailors to hit their quickest settings consistently and offers cruisers an assured check on safe loadings.

The benefits of this device are manifold. For performance, it provides sailors with highly precise load data, allowing them to repeat their fastest settings consistently on screen. The load data can be viewed live while sailing, compatible with all major marine electronics brands, thereby allowing real-time adjustments.

The smartlink² Atto 1.2t also provides benefits for cruising. Sailors can set their rig to a known tension at the dock and monitor rig settings live while sailing. It even provides visual cues when loads begin to escalate, enabling immediate action to depower the rig and ensuring that sailors are always within safe limits. Owning to its 1.2 tonnes of max working load, assured accuracy to within 1% of the maximum working load, and superb value for money, the latest sensor from Cyclops Marine is an undeniable choice for any sailor.

Bringing performance and safety to the forefront, the smartlink² Atto 1.2t is a clear demonstration of how innovations can transform our understanding of sailing and redefine our expectations. The arrival of the smartlink² Atto 1.2t has begun a new chapter in sailing, offering solutions that combine affordability with best-in-class technological benefits.

Whether you're a sailor aiming for the podium or just embarking on a weekend sail, the smartlink² Atto 1.2t empowers you with the live data and information you need to make the most of your voyage. Speak to a Cyclops expert or explore their online store today to find out the best sensor for your boat.

title: Epic Sail Racing Unfolds Amidst Sunshine and Breeze at Salcombe Yacht Club's Stones Boatyard Yawl & ILCA Open
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Epic Sail Racing Unfolds Amidst Sunshine and Breeze at Salcombe Yacht Club's Stones Boatyard Yawl & ILCA Open
summary: The Stones Boatyard Yawl & ILCA Open at Salcombe Yacht Club saw gripping sail racing amidst a scenic Whitsun Bank Holiday weekend.
body: Unfurling in the idyllic setting of Salcombe Ria during a glorious Whitsun Bank Holiday weekend, the Stones Boatyard Yawl & ILCA Open at Salcombe Yacht Club showcased engaging sail racing action. Twenty Salcombe Yawls formed the Red fleet, bringing intense competition to the crystalline waters, far from the mainland's scorching 30-degree heat, the event unfolded amidst a tranquil climate in its mid-twenties, complemented by a satisfying breeze.

Over three days, the competitors heralded in four thrilling races. Enthusiasm mirrored the sparkling sunrays on the water as the contestants eagerly launched their boats for Race 1, leading to a general recall and subsequent relegation to the end of the start sequence. A course navigated the racers to Blackstone, staged a long run and a subsequent broad reach to Gerston, bringing an exciting spectacle for maritime enthusiasts.

Spectacular manoeuvres captured spectators' fascination as the fleet displayed outstanding skills, claiming redress, taking chances and deciding the best routes amidst an array of boats. The leaders' strategy, especially Hendersons' daring high route, revealed a masterclass in navigation and sailing tactics.

The race concluded with an exciting crescendo, transforming Gerston into a riot of sail, foam, and spirited competition, as racers sped to finish the line. A blend of thrilling racing tackled amidst balmy weather and vibrant camaraderie, the Stones Boatyard Yawl and ILCA Open at Salcombe Yacht Club created lasting memories on the waters.

title: Italian Shipyard Magnificence: Mangusta Yachts Unleashes Seventh Oceano 44 'Lulus'
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Italian Shipyard Magnificence: Mangusta Yachts Unleashes Seventh Oceano 44 'Lulus'
summary: Mangusta Yachts, Italian luxury shipyard, launches 'Lulus,' the seventh yacht in its famed Oceano 44 series, reflecting supreme mariner excellence.
body: Proudly launching from the Italian shipyard of Mangusta Yachts, Lulus sails forth as the seventh unit in the thrilling Oceano 44 series. Boasting a robust 44.5-metre frame, she was ceremoniously given to the waves from the Group's facilities in Pisa, Italy. This exciting addition to the advanced Oceano fleet encapsulates magnificence at sea, with every single design choice culminating in what the shipyard describes as 'one of the finest expressions of Mangusta’s vision for long-range cruising'.

Commissioned by experienced owners and charter enthusiasts, and gracefully sold in December 2023 through Camper & Nicholsons. Lulus' construction has been overseen by the discerning eye of the New Build Division at Camper & Nicholsons, promising impeccable quality and detail. This assures that the yacht remains with the broker even post-delivery, gliding gracefully into their charter fleet, becoming a grand testament to the prowess of Mangusta's design.

Earning remarkable praise for its beach area, which beautifully transforms into a 180-degree platform over the water due to an exceptional large opening transom and fold-down side terraces, the Oceano 44 Lulus exemplifies luxury at sea. Accelerating further than the waves it conquers, Lulus offers superior cruising capabilities, with a top speed of 15.5 knots and a stunning range of 4,500 nautical miles at a jovial cruising speed of 11 knots. Ensuring additional onboard comfort are the electric zero-speed and underway stabilisers.

Lulus joins an illustrious line of recent sisterships, including Dorsia, Eva4Eva and The Great Escape, bringing the total number of yachts on order or under construction by the yard to 25. Evidently, with the launch of Lulus, Mangusta Yachts showcases the luxurious, personal, and explorative possibilities of sea travel on a spectacular scale, raising the bar for the next phase of their remarkable journey.

title: The Amels 80 Series Continues with Project Zurich Embarking on Sea Trials
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Amels 80 Series Continues with Project Zurich Embarking on Sea Trials
summary: Damen Yachting announces the third addition to the Amels 80 series, Project Zurich, begins sea trials.
body: In the world of luxury seafaring vehicles, Project Zurich is setting sails and turning heads. The third unit from Damen Yachting's applauded Amels 80 series, this stunning superyacht, recently embarked on its sea trials after launching at the second build facility in Vlissingen East earlier this year.

The 79.8-metre new-build quickly moved onto Damen Yachting's main headquarters in Vlissingen City for final outfitting. The luxury seafarer is expected to be ready for delivery later this year, swiftly after its initial unveiling just a few months ago in March 2022. Project Zurich's quick turnaround and progress can be credited to the highly skilled teams working tirelessly on the vessel.

One can't discuss Project Zurich without mentioning the exemplary onboard amenities. The 2,175GT superyacht inculcates splendid attractions like a sundeck sprawling over 200-square-metres. The substantially sized jacuzzi only adds to the ambiance. The owner's dedicated deck and foredeck helipad add an extra layer of luxury.

Moreover, the beach club acts as a comprehensive waterfront lounge, embracing the open sea with terraces on three sides. It also offers direct access to a gym, hammam, and sauna. As if these offerings weren't enough, the space is illuminated by the 6.5-metre, glass-bottomed pool of the main aft deck.

The interior design team's identity remains a secret, but their skill is evident in the "bright [and] custom" design theme, setting it apart from the predecessors in the series. This yacht is constructed to house 14 guests in seven cabins and 21 crew members comfortably, accommodating vast storage for toys and tenders. The watercraft was first spotted on its way to outfitting in January 2025, and it has been a sight to see ever since.

As expressed by Damen Yachting project manager Sander Peeters, coordinating such a large-scale project calls for meticulous planning, craftsmanship, and teamwork. With the final stages of delivery on the horizon, an adamant sense of precision and focus is imminent.

Presently, Damen Yachting's plate is full with seven active Amels yacht constructions, including five from the Amels 80 series, making the anticipation for Project Zurich's completion even more thrilling. As the superyacht market delivers more sophisticated, detailed, and sizable vessels, the seas are sure to witness some spectacular sights.

title: Gear Up Sailors: The 2026 F4 Foils Summer Wingding U.S. Wingfoil Championship is Now Open for Registration
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Gear Up Sailors: The 2026 F4 Foils Summer Wingding U.S. Wingfoil Championship is Now Open for Registration

body: The world of sailing rings in with yet another exciting announcement - the curtain has been raised for the registration of the 2026 F4 Foils Summer Wingding U.S. Wingfoil Championship. This prestigious event will be held at the St. Francis Yacht Club in San Francisco, California, July 30 - August 2, 2026. A notable collaboration between St. Francis Yacht Club and US Sailing, this championship witnesses F4 Foils as its revered title sponsor. Entering its third year as a national championship, this event has increasingly fueled the popularity of wingfoiling.

Year on year, this incredible event has found a consistent venue thanks to the relentless effort of St. Francis Yacht Club and its earnest pool of volunteers. Felix Weidling, the Race Director of the club, proudly states their role in materially shaping the wingfoiling scene in the U.S. The club isn't just about annual events. It's a haven for foil-sailing aficionados, offering weekly wingfoil races throughout the summer and hosting special wingfoil sessions in its junior sailing program.

U.S. Sailing, a prime mover in this championship, appreciates St. Francis Yacht Club for its unwavering commitment to the sport. Betsy Alison, the Adult Sailing Program Director at U.S. Sailing, acknowledges their role in fostering innovation and expanding the reach of foiling disciplines. Together, they aim to surge ahead, fuelling the momentum of this dynamic sailing sport.

title: Enter a bold new era in superyacht design with the launch of the Superyacht Design and Naval Architecture Association (SYDNA)
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Enter a bold new era in superyacht design with the launch of the Superyacht Design and Naval Architecture Association (SYDNA)
summary: A groundbreaking association for naval architects and interior and exterior designers in the yachting world makes its grand debut.
body: The world of yacht design is set for a revolution as the budding Superyacht Design and Naval Architecture Association (SYDNA) makes its grand entrance. Unveiled at the renowned 2026 Blue Design Summit in La Spezia, Italy, SYDNA embodies the rapid evolution and growing complexity of yacht design and naval architecture over the last century.

Years ago, naval architects adhered to a simple rule of thumb – 'if it looks right, it is right.' Fast forward a century, and the game has significantly changed. Superyacht design now marries function and aesthetics, intertwining engineering marvels with unparalleled luxury expected by modern clients.

The challenge for today's boat designers is twofold: translating the lofty dreams of clients into reality while adhering to strict regulations put forth by international governing bodies. This sector, despite its significant growth over the last four decades, lacked cohesive representation until SYDNA stepped onto the scene.

One of SYDNA's core objectives is to provide a structured approach towards enhancing industry professionalism and credibility. It aims to be a loudspeaker for its members, influencing future regulations and shaping the future of yacht design by embracing innovative technologies and sustainable solutions.

SYDNA's reach extends beyond just design – it also plays a fundamental part in shaping the perception of the industry. Given that designers are often the initial point of contact for both seasoned clients and first-time owners, their role in shaping the industry's success is critical. For this reason, the association advocates a collective discourse about contracts, rules and regulations, and other facets of the industry, empowering it to speak with a unified voice towards authorities, the media, and clients. The ultimate goal is to provide a structured approach towards bolstering the industry's professionalism, credibility, and longevity.

title: Revealing the Hidden Dimensions of the Superyacht Industry's Economic Dominance
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Revealing the Hidden Dimensions of the Superyacht Industry's Economic Dominance
summary: A landmark study unveils the incredible economic force that the global superyacht industry embodies in today's world.
body: In a landscape where economic indicators are crucial, the superyacht industry emerges as an unsung titan, with recent findings highlighting its incredible economic muscle. A comprehensive study led by Deloitte and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam indicates that this flourishing sector has contributed approximately €54 billion in total economic output based on 2022 data, marking it among leading high-value maritime manufacturing ecosystems globally.

The findings serve as a vital cornerstone for the Sybass Builders Advocacy Campaign, a strategic initiative designed to lift the curtain on the significance of yacht builders within the sprawling superyacht economy. The campaign champions the critical role these manufacturers play in fortifying skilled employment, fueling industrial innovation, and propelling continuous economic activity along global coastal regions.

At the heart of this economic maelstrom lies yacht construction, identified as the most economically catalytic activity within the sector. With a multiplier effect of 2.8, yacht construction reigns supreme in advance manufacturing and maritime industries. Translating this into practical terms means that with every €1 invested in building a yacht, an additional €1.8 is born across the wider global economy – a potent testament to the industry's pivotal role.

While downstream sectors like fleet operations, charter, tourism, brokerage, marinas, and hospitality account for the substantial share of recurring annual economic activity, the study underlines that this ecosystem pivots on the ceaseless creation and refreshment of the global fleet helmed by builders and yacht owners. This operational economy hinging on superyachts exists only because yachts are continuously conceived, engineered, built, and renewed.

New vessel construction represents a titanic 37% of the industry’s total economic impact, translating into approximately €20 billion globally. The study brands new build activity as a formidable engine for lasting sector growth, as every delivered yacht propels the operational economy for decades. An additional pillar of long-term growth opportunity comes from the fleet refit and maintenance sector that contributes an additional €5.6 billion, representing roughly 11% of the total industry impact.

However, the study uncovers an imbalance within the industry; the builders shoulder most of the industrial investment, delivery risk, and long-term accountability, even though the majority of recurring economic activity springs from the downstream fleet that they create.

Lastly, the research shines a light on the industrial weight of the upstream sector, including new builds and refit activities. This sector, shouldering an estimated economic impact of €9.5 billion, forms the industry's industrial heart. Shipyards' operational expenditure is a significant driver, where new builds account for about 76% of the total turnover, and refit activities contribute the remaining 24%. The findings underline the intricate complexity and the seamless blend of engineering prowess, precision technology, complex project management, and unparalleled craftsmanship that underpin the world’s most specialised manufacturing supply chains.

title: Discover Why Zhik Is The Trusted Leader In High-Performance Dinghy Hiking Equipment
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover Why Zhik Is The Trusted Leader In High-Performance Dinghy Hiking Equipment
summary: Dedicated to water sports excellence, Zhik consistently impresses with high-performance dinghy hiking gear trusted by world champions.
body: Ending the debate on which brand rules the world of dinghy hiking performance, Zhik stands above the rest. The global brand has built its reputation through continuous innovation, creating a comprehensive range of dinghy hiking gear that's engineered for peak performance.

Zhik's range, developed through decades of close collaboration with elite sailors, offers a complete product system built around connection, support, and sustained power. Components such as footwear, hiking straps, support systems, and specially designed suits for both men and women ensure sailors retain their connection to the boat while managing loads and maintaining strong hiking positions for extended durations.

Zhik isn't just a passive provider of gear, though. The brand continues to shape the contemporary approach to dinghy hiking with athlete-led innovation and product development. Their long-running ZhikGrip II Hiking Boot, for instance, has set a new industry standard for connection and load control, proving that the company's commitment to innovation is more than just talk.

Not one to rest on its laurels, Zhik's latest offering is the Hiking X Boot, a masterclass in design progression. Launched recently, this lightweight, highly responsive boot is engineered for high-performance hiking, enriching the already high standards of the brand.

What truly distinguishes Zhik is its systems-based design philosophy. Rather than developing products in isolation, it engineers each piece in a range around the way sailors actually move, load the boat, and interact with their vessel and the water around them. Matching cutting-edge technology and design with the real-world needs of sailors, Zhik stays committed to delivering superior performance gear for sailors to achieve their best.

title: The Thrill of Sailing Underscored At The 2026 RS Aero Spring Championship
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Thrill of Sailing Underscored At The 2026 RS Aero Spring Championship
summary: Get aboard the 2026 RS Aero Spring Championship, where breezy winds, strategic races, and an indomitable spirit set an exciting tableau.
body: The RS Aero Spring Championship 2026 hosted by the Island Barn Reservoir Sailing Club was nothing short of a wind-kissed symphony of sails. Thanks to a near-perfect prediction of an 8-knot westerly, billed to escalate to 12, the racing day promised excitement. The club could unfurl all it's got—comprehensive use of the east/width spanning a full kilometre. Participants didn’t let the fatigue from the previous week’s National Champs get the better of them. From last year's 21 entries, the competition went solid with 15 entries—more to strive for in the coming years. The rectangular course with its four movable marks churned up a thrilling contest with an interconnecting reaching legs. With a clear division between the Aeros 5 and 6 from Aeros 7 and 9 based on starting times, it allowed for an orderly completion leading to a commendable finish. Traveling from places as far as Lymington and Itchenor, the participants gave life to the event. Interestingly, Sammi Isaacs-Johnson, from Claires Court School had an edge-of-seat showdown with Richard Bullock from Itchenor with Isaacs-Johnson edging the victory. The thrilling contests carried on with Tom Hire from Lymington and Andrew Barnett from Island Barn rarely separated by more than two boat lengths! The Championship was equally inclusive, encouraging youth sailors like Fergus Anderson (Thorpe Bay). The RS Aero Spring Championship 2026 was a testament to the thrill of sailing and the spirit of fair competition that characterises the sport.

title: Revolutionising Exploration: Archipelago Yachts Advances with Its Second 24 Metre Explorer Yacht
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Revolutionising Exploration: Archipelago Yachts Advances with Its Second 24 Metre Explorer Yacht
summary: UK shipbuilder Archipelago Yachts is making waves once again as they finalise the design for their second 24-metre explorer yacht.
body: Archipelago Yachts, the illustrious British shipyard, is shaping the future of sea exploration with the design contract for their second Archipelago 80 explorer yacht. Following the same hull form of the first 24-metre model, which is currently in the shipyard, this latest endeavour is poised to eclipse its predecessor's capabilities and deliver a more impressive array of on-board features. With the aim to exceed, the company envisions an elevated approach to interior design. In an innovative move, the shipyard is wielding complete creative control by handling interior designs in-house, which promises greater synergy with onboard engineering while offering a seamless process for owner customisation. This yacht is no mere upgrade – it's a leap forward in design and functionality. It has been aptly described as a 'next generation pocket superyacht'. Bounding forward with fearless inventiveness, the vehicle incorporates a multitude of enticing features: a high-capacity helipad, a dedicated gym and sauna space, and a substantially enlarged kitchen/galley area specifically designed for extended voyages. Grand spaces for dining both inside and out, along with enough accommodation for up to 16 guests, mark this yacht as the epitome of grandeur and practicality. The vessel will be powered by a hybrid diesel-electric propulsion system to offer substantial payload capacity and long-range capability. In fact, Archipelago Yachts has declared that this would make it one of the most flexible sub-24-metre explorer platforms on the market. The bespoke layout of the yacht is fully customisable in accordance with the owner's preferences, ensuring a deeply personal touch. With the company's newest production facility on Isle of Wight, inaugurated in February this year, this second Archipelago 80 series vessel will be designed and engineered using the best resources available. Taking pride in their newfound capabilities, Dr Stephen Weatherley, CEO of Archipelago Yachts, promises 'a higher standard with this second model.' The detailed design phase has already begun for the yacht, with construction envisaged to kick-off in 2027, making the future of sea exploration as alluring as ever.

While this strategic move is set to boost the company's strategic insights, it also underscores the importance Heesen puts on industry experience and the value of leveraging it for the benefit of the organisation's overall navigation. title: Surviving the Waves: The Art of Managing Medical Emergencies at Sea
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Surviving the Waves: The Art of Managing Medical Emergencies at Sea
summary: When a routine sail turns into a sudden medical disaster, surviving takes more than just grit. Learn how we braved the storm.
body: There's something awfully enchanting about the open sea with its vast expanses of water brushing against the boat's bow, an allure known quite well to sailors and nautical aficionados. Yet, this allure could take a dramatic turn in a heartbeat, when one of the crew members suddenly finds themselves in a medical pickle. Under such dire circumstances, the sea becomes a dauntingly wide chasm between life and death. Imagine a day that started off as a fairly ordinary sail training session, the weather a gentle blend of grey skies and soft winds, and the sea a muted symphony of waves. Suddenly, the harmony breaks, replaced by an abrupt singularity. A promising instructor-in-training, a strong, confident character, takes an unlucky tumble. The fall isn't particularly severe, but the aftermath is. His next words echo through the cabin with chilling calmness, 'I've broken my leg'. Responding swiftly to the unexpected crisis, the crew promptly arranges for the injured trainee to stay still and minimize further injury, while the VHF radio springs to life in the background, calling the Coastguard for help. As the vessel makes its heartbreaking turn towards home, a lesson looms ominously over the event: Medical emergencies at sea are a very real possibility, and how you respond to them could mean the difference between life and death. The key to effective crisis management lies in conducting comprehensive safety briefings before every voyage. These briefings help familiarize the crew with the location and operation of all emergency equipment onboard. In this case, it facilitated immediate access to procedure cards and the first aid kit, proving to be instrumental in mitigating the situation. In addition, active liaison with both the Coastguard and RNLI could ensure swift evacuation and medical attention upon reaching shore. The synergy between these safety authorities allowed valuable pain management and reassurances for the casualty during the ordeal. Even in situations where emergency services capacity are stretched, alternatives such as evacuation to nearby marinas may be viable. Final thought: the sea, gracious in its beauty, is equally merciless in its capacity for unexpected danger. Be sure to be prepared; it's your greatest bet against the unpredictable tide.

title: Nix the Niggles of Boat Hauling with this Revolutionary Norwegian Trailer
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Nix the Niggles of Boat Hauling with this Revolutionary Norwegian Trailer
summary: Navigating the often hair-raising task of hauling a 3.5-tonne boat and trailer with cool-headed ease becomes doable thanks to a cutting-edge Norwegian design.
body: For any proud owner of a weighty 3.5-tonne boat rig like the Iron Explorer, or indeed any cumbersome motorboat, the process of towing can be a proverbial thorn in the side. And yet, a truly ingenious Norwegian solution might just flip the script on this tale of towing tribulation.

Scratch below the surface of boating life and you'll find a world brimming with all manner of equipment, with avid enthusiasts tirelessly tracking reviews and developments. However, every so often a piece of boating gear emerges that changes the game entirely.

The crux of the issue revolves around towing a significant 3.5-tonne load while maintaining a practical, manageable speed of 80km/h. Previous attempts with various trailers have presented their own fair share of challenges. Yet all that changed upon discovering a sterling breed of trailer currently revolutionising the coast of Norway.

Below the surface of this boat hauling masterpiece, you'll find an extraordinarily long frame support cradle at the rear, armed with a rotating axle for adaptive assistance loading and unloading the boat. The real revolution, however, is the implementation of adaptive wheels, mounted in pairs on rotating axles. This allows the wheels to morph to suit the boat's precise hull shape, thus effectively distributing weight across all wheels. This means no single wheel is overburdened, as has often been the case with standard trailers. Furthermore, these trailers have a total of 28 wheels sharing the workload, making it more manageable.

Moreover, every aspect of this groundbreaking trailer is adjustable to fit the boat's specifications perfectly, ensuring a smooth journey both on, and off the water. And if all of that wasn't enough, the package also includes an aluminium box for housing the winch battery and appropriate straps for securing the boat.

The trailer, in all its elegant simplicity and high performance, is impressive. So much so that one cannot help but be drawn to this stunning example of cutting-edge innovation. So, if you're looking for a way to drastically alleviate your boat towing ordeals, the Svela B35 MAXE9 might just be your golden ticket.

title: From Fuel-Cell Yachts to Sea-Trials, Lürssen’s Groundbreaking Creations Are Redefining Sailing Experiences
author: Old Sea Dogs
