Falmouth Harbour, a renowned port in Cornwall, UK, is transforming this vision into a reality with a £50,000 investment in high-capacity mooring buoys. This initiative comes in response to the rising demand from increasingly prevalent superyachts and sizable commercial vessels seeking splendid marinas.

The augmentation of the port's capacity through the installation of these high-density buoys will not only enhance the port’s aesthetic appeal but fundamentally increase its functional capacity. This strategic move exhibits Falmouth Harbour’s commitment to adapting to accommodate 21st-century marine trends. By making these improvements, the harbour is future-proofing itself, ensuring its position as a premier stopover destination for bigshot vessels from across the globe.

The rise of superyachts and large commercial vessels represents a prominent trend in today's marine industry, a trend that requires harbours worldwide to upgrade their infrastructure such as Falmouth has done. It is this prescience and commitment to modernisation that will continue to cruise this deepwater harbour into the future, undulating on the waves of success.

title: Lithium Boat Batteries: Unlocking the Benefits, Safety, and Technological Aspects of Modern Marine Power
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Lithium Boat Batteries: Unlocking the Benefits, Safety, and Technological Aspects of Modern Marine Power
summary: An exploration into lithium boat batteries, covering their evolving nature, benefits, safety precautions, and the technological nuances of this modern marine power.
body: Boat batteries, over the years, have undergone significant changes. At the heart of these exciting transformations are the lithium boat batteries. From heavyweight lead acid batteries, they have evolved towards maintenance-free AGM and gel variants, and now, the lightweight and efficient lithium batteries.

Lithium boat batteries have several compelling advantages including lighter weight, high energy density, deeper discharge, swift charging, and remarkable longevity. They have also found their place in homes, cars, campervans, and boats due to their effectiveness.

The term 'Lithium-ion' is actually an umbrella term for rechargeable batteries that make use of lithium ions for their electrochemical activities. There are multiple chemistry types available in the market, each having its own characteristics and applications. Among various categories, Lithium Iron Phosphate (LiFePO₄) has emerged as a popular choice for boating enthusiasts due to its capacity for thousands of repeat cycles, high safety standards, stability, and economical pricing.

With the use of this exciting technology, lithium iron phosphate batteries can offer between three and five times the energy density of lead acid. This means smaller, lighter, and more compact battery banks can achieve the same power output, transforming the way marine power is perceived today. Constructing upon this trend and optimizing the use of lithium batteries in boats, can substantially contribute to the modernization of marine power, making boating safer, more efficient, and extremely enjoyable.

title: European Craftsmanship Meets American Design in Newly Launched 117m Lürssen Superyacht Boardwalk
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: European Craftsmanship Meets American Design in Newly Launched 117m Lürssen Superyacht Boardwalk
summary: The stunning 117-metre Lürssen superyacht Boardwalk, previously known as Project 13797, is ready for her maiden voyage, fresh from the yard's facilities in Germany.
body: The impressive 117-metre Lürssen superyacht Boardwalk is ready to embark on her maiden voyage. Fresh from the company's shipyard in Bremen, Germany, the yacht was commissioned in 2022 by an American owner. Throughout the build, the owner was actively involved in the design process, ensuring every element of the yacht's structure and spatial aspects were meticulously refined. The yacht's design was a collaborative work of art. Frank Woll's classically-inspired lines sculpt the exterior while the interior décor results from a team up with the late Amy Halffman, Suzanne Glover and Teresa Francis. As Woll declared, 'the finest architects are in nature.' He took inspiration from the seascape's agile marine life, crafting Boardwalk to have fluid and streamlined geometry. Luxurious living is at the heart of the Boardwalk, with 5,602GT of living space. High gloss mahogany, polished steel and complex double-convex forms give a distinguished finish to the interior. Innovative lighting extends the sensation of movement inside, magnifying its allure. Created as a familial sanctuary at sea, the expansive decks accommodate multiple entertainment areas. Two helipads, a large pool with a neighbouring Jacuzzi, and a sizeable beach club provide various spots to unwind. One of the key features is a retractable section over the stairwell, allowing it to be hermetically sealed when not in use, a first for Lürssen yachts. In terms of accommodation, the Boardwalk hosts 11 cabins. The foremost is an opulent VIP suite complete with an onyx-finished en suite and a private lounge overlooking the bow. The other cabins have direct access to wide side decks, creating large private terraces for each. Whether you want to marvel at the top-of-the-line engine room with its glass-walled catwalk or relax in a cinema or spa, there's much to be enjoyed aboard Boardwalk. Peter Lürssen comments, 'our single objective as a shipyard is to translate a vision into an operational vessel.' He believes that Boardwalk has surpassed expectations and is a true milestone for Lürssen.

title: Ferretti's Annual General Meeting Ends in Drama with New Leadership Amid Allegations of Irregularities
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Ferretti's Annual General Meeting Ends in Drama with New Leadership Amid Allegations of Irregularities
summary: Ferretti’s AGM concluded with Weichai winning key votes, ending Alberto Galassi’s tenure and raising questions of regulatory non-compliance.
body: In a turn of events as unpredictable as the high seas, yacht manufacturer Ferretti’s recent Annual General Meeting (AGM) played out like a thriller. A leadership change was the outcome, with the Weichai slate of directors narrowly edging past billionaire Karel Komárek’s KKCG Maritime, claiming 52% of votes versus 47%. This power shift subsequently ended Alberto Galassi’s distinguished twelve-year tenure as chief executive, with his successor Stassi Anastassov expected to be confirmed imminently.

However, this was no ordinary leadership transition. The process was laden with allegations of regulatory non-compliance and undisclosed shareholder coordination, with sources indicating a possible lengthy investigation. Notably, the Czech billionaire's camp is of the belief that these allegations will ultimately tip the scales in their favour.

The battleground for control extended beyond the confines of the boardroom, treading into the offices of the Presidency of the Council of Ministers, Consob, and the Hong Kong Securities and Futures Commission. KKCG views a split election result as a testament to the firm institutional support they received as opposed to the more centred voting pattern of the Chinese-led groups, inspiring a sense of optimism for the pending regulatory outcomes.

Despite the tumultuous atmosphere, the business of yachting must go on. As the dust settles, the newly selected board, under the leadership of Chairman Tan Ning, now faces the exciting challenge of steering the prestigious Ferretti brand towards prosperous shores.

title: The Glide to Top-tier Superyacht Regulations: Design, Safety and the Facilitative Roles of Leading Maritime Codes
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Glide to Top-tier Superyacht Regulations: Design, Safety and the Facilitative Roles of Leading Maritime Codes
summary: In the vibrant sphere of superyachts, laws and codes are designed not to restrict, but rather to balance scalpel-sharp innovation with robust safety standards.
body: The marriage of dashing design and safety in the realm of superyachts is a harmonious one, owing to the regulatory strides made by prominent Maritime codes. These legal manuscripts, far from being austere shackles, are the invisible hands gently guiding the sector towards higher pinnacles of advancement, steering the balance between radical creativity and rigid safety values. Rolling back to 1997, the UK Maritime and Coastguard Agency gifted the maritime world the mother of all 'yacht codes', now known affectionately as the ‘MCA Large Yacht Code (LY1)’. Its aim was to add rigour to the safety of large commercial sailing and motor vessels without compromising on innovative prowess. The Code moved through reincarnations as LY2 and LY3 before donning a new title in 2017 - the ‘Red Ensign Group (REG) Yacht Code’. This rebranding was designed to underscore the input from the wider REG, including Bermuda, the British Virgin Islands, Cayman Islands and others. Far from being unbending edicts, yacht codes, including those from Malta and The Republic of the Marshall Islands, unveiled in 2006 and 2013, respectively, are flexible frameworks aligning safety with novel yacht designs, which are often out of step with core international maritime conventions. In recent years, these leading codes have integrated provisions for more groundbreaking designs, supporting the adoption of alternative fuels. The convergence in their regulations means that for yachts larger than 500gt, their requirements are essentially harmonized. Despite these strides in standardization, there's a noteworthy anomaly for short-range yachts, strictly under the REG Code. These vessels have certain limitations due to their lower design features, but Malta and RMI Codes currently withhold an explicit wave-height limitation. In the backdrop of this convergence, some advocates suggest a harmonized international yacht code. However, this idea faces some resistance, with the common concern that a uniform code might impede the dynamic nature of the yacht industry. Instead, the current national yacht codes enable designers, builders, and classification societies to maneuver through minor differences with ease. Also, the inclusivity within the process has been an undeniable catalyst for progress. In this constant dance of design and regulation, the indisputable beneficiary is the yachting industry itself, which continues to ride on the waves of innovation without forsaking the safety of their users.

title: The High Seas Roar with Competitive Excitement: Flying 15 Fleet Engage in Riveting Palma Vela 2026 Regatta
author: Old Sea Dogs

summary: The Flying 15 fleet descended upon the waters of Mallorca for the Palma Vela 2026, stirring up a wave of exhilarating competition and cementing a stunning legacy for sailing.
body: The adrenaline-fueled spectacle of the Palma Vela 2026 was enriched by the exciting participation of the Flying 15 fleet. For the first time in years, this dynamic class graced the regatta, hosted by the Real Club Náutico Palma, earning it the reputation as one of the premier high seas events of the season. The participating teams, travelling down from Pollença, were united by their passion for sailing, excitedly welcoming the chance to compete and gain crucial experience before the upcoming European championships.

The unpredictable weather over the event's three days added an extra layer of excitement. Participants navigated shifting winds and unpredictable sea breezes, showcasing their adaptability at sea. Unfortunately, day three was cut short due to stormy conditions, but not before participants had aired their considerable tactical skills in the face of light winds and challenging waves.

A round of applause goes to the two women's teams who participated, setting a remarkable example of inclusivity at sea. Gratitude must also be extended towards both the fleet captain, Rafa, who managed logistics, and RCNP for hosting a truly remarkable event. With the Flying 15 class back in the Palma Vela, the regatta's future looks brighter than ever. They say, 'After the storm comes the calm.’ At this regatta, they’ll be saying, 'After the storm comes the exhilaration'.

Undeterred by the changing sea conditions, sailors gave their best performance at every race, delivering a series that delighted the spectators and participants alike. The competition proved that sailing isn't just about battling the ocean; it's also about harnessing its unpredictable nature, clinging to its waves, riding its winds and, in doing so, learning something profound about oneself. With an eye toward the future, the Flying 15 fleet plans to return next year in even greater numbers, ready for the challenges and excitement that the Palma Vela will undoubtedly provide.

title: Rising Star Maddalena Spanu Clinches Victory at Defi Wind; A Triumph For The Young Azzurra Programme
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Rising Star Maddalena Spanu Clinches Victory at Defi Wind; A Triumph For The Young Azzurra Programme
summary: Maddalena Spanu, a talented athlete from the Young Azzurra programme, emerges victorious at the global Defi Wind event, a crowning achievement in her flourishing career.
body: The international watersports stage echoed with a triumphant cheer as Maddalena Spanu, a young prodigy from the Young Azzurra programme, clinched a tremendous win at the Defi Wind competition. The event, which transpired in Gruissan, France, is known as the world's largest congregation dedicated to water sports. It drew in a mammoth gathering of over 2,000 athletes to the shimmering French coast.

Competing in the Wing class, Spanu battled it out with roughly 600 athletes from every corner of the globe. With her eyes firmly set on the prize, she surged ahead to seal the overall victory in the women's category. Vania Picot and Enoha Laurant, her formidable competitors, trailed behind her in second and third place.

Her stellar performance, marked by two wins, a second and a third, crowned her as the queen of the Defi Wind, where she finished 50th overall in a fleet of 595 participants. This victory marked an extra-special occasion as she shared the podium with her brother, Nicolò Spanu, who claimed the top position in the men's category. The achievement, unsurprisingly, brought forth a whirlpool of emotions for the Spanus, expressed beautifully by Maddalena at the conclusion of the prestigious event.

With the thrill of the victory still lingering in the air, the dynamic athlete prepares for her next contest—the WingFoil Racing World Cup. The leg in Urla, Turkey, is waiting for her from 19-23 May. As the Yacht Club Costa Smeralda showers their champion Spanu with congratulatory wishes, the stage is set for her next soaring achievement.

title: Luxury at Sea: Baglietto's DOM133 Superyacht Notches Sale With Flag Set for 2028 Voyage
author: Old Sea Dogs

Broker Tomaso Polli, representing the buyer, couldn't hide his admiration for the superyacht model. Its profound trans-oceanic range, opulent deck spaces and guest-focused layout all culminate into a lavish cruiser ideal for cherished moments at sea.

Renowned Italian designer, Stefano Vafiadis, lends his creative genius to the ship's picturesque profile and interiors. The grandeur of the superyacht lies in its spacious interior volumes, a two-story beach club encasing an infinity pool with a lifting floor, a sundeck Jacuzzi, and panoramic windows ushering onto terraces - attributes that have lent the semi-custom model its enduring popularity.

Expressing immense pride at reaching this milestone, Baglietto's chief commercial officer, Fabio Ermetto, emphasised the line's adaptability. Each DOM133 is moulded by its owner's vision, lifestyle, and unique interpretation of life onboard, making every yacht a distinct entity.

With Baglietto's roosta currently boasting 17 superyachts either on order or under construction, including a 56-metre custom superyacht project, the promise of future maritime luxury is palpable. The shipbuilder also surprised enthusiasts by unveiling a new flagship - the 46.4-metre DOM155 - earlier this year.

title: Croatia’s New Approach to VAT on Yacht Charters: An Epochal Change or a Warning Sign?
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Croatia’s New Approach to VAT on Yacht Charters: An Epochal Change or a Warning Sign?
summary: Shaking up the sector, Croatia is changing the way VAT is applied within yacht chartering, focusing on structural control over rate disparity.
body: For most, the VAT discourse within yacht chartering has historically revolved around rate disparities - 13% in Croatia, 22% in Italy and so on. But Croatia has decidedly steered the conversation in a new direction, highlighting the need for structural control instead of mere rate arithmetic.

Croatia's expanded fiscalisation regime paves the way for a new enforcement architecture, rather than introducing a new tax. This new governance mandates any yacht charter invoice for a venture beginning in Croatia to adhere to a fresh set of guidelines. Crucially, the invoice must be electronically transmitted to the Croatian tax administration, assigned a unique fiscal code (JIR), and be validated before its existence is deemed legally valid.

Under this new system, if the yacht is handed over in Split, the supply is Croatian; if in Genoa, it's Italian and so forth. This approach is both territorial and consistent with EU law. Croatia is not acting out of turn but instead firming up the need for correct VAT-ID usage, appropriate place-of-supply determinations and correct invoicing.

The shift is towards a real-time invoice control framework which eliminates margin for mismatch or non-compliance. For companies operating in diverse EU jurisdictions, they must adapt to this change, ensuring precise determination of physical charter commencement points.

The Croatian system, uncomfortable as it may be, forces all stakeholders to reduce sloppiness and embrace a culture of stringent compliance. The effects of Croatia's VAT-system overhaul are not limited to its own shores, serving as a compelling case study for other charter hotspots grappling with similar VAT issues. As fiscalisation becomes the order of the day, the challenge now is for individual nations and the EU at large to harmonise these procedures. As Croatia has underscored, the key is not simply in numbers– it lies in the structural underpinnings of tax regulation and compliance in the yacht charter business.

title: Eye-Catching 2018 75 Princess, ‘3BBoys’, Awaits Its Next Owner: A Blend of Supreme Performance and Elegant Design
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Eye-Catching 2018 75 Princess, ‘3BBoys’, Awaits Its Next Owner: A Blend of Supreme Performance and Elegant Design
summary: A stellar example of modern yachting manufacturing, the 3BBoys, a 2018 75 Princess, is on the market, showcasing unmatchable performance, comfort, and style.
body: Tempting all lovers of luxury and maritime excellence, the 2018 75 Princess, profoundly identified as '3BBoys', has made an alluring entrance into the yacht marketplace. Renowned for its sublime design capabilities and unrivalled sophistication, Princess Yachts has continued to exceed expectations with this spectacular specimen.

The '3BBoys' radiates an aura of unsurpassed quality, upholding a phenomenally well-preserved condition while boasting low operation hours. Commanding impressive performance figures, the yacht boasts outstanding 1800 MAN's engines which have been recently serviced by esteemed Galati Yachts, enhancing their longevity and efficiency.

Furthering the charm of the '3BBoys', it includes an Extended Range Fuel Tank and SeaKeeper Stabilization, which ensures smooth sailing even in choppy waters. An unbeatable package of top-of-the-line Garmin Electronics elevates the yacht's appeal, promising easy navigation and seamless journeys.

Mechanically, '3BBoys' demonstrates profound eminence via upgraded and redundant equipment, including twin generators and back up/inline fresh & sea water pumps. In addition, the yacht features a water maker and Spot Zero, effectively addressing every imaginable maritime need.

Sealing its mastery on all fronts, '3BBoys' flaunts an extensive list of tasteful interior refinements, offering the utmost in luxury and sophistication to its guests. Its exterior, recently ceramic coated, dazzles the eyes, further highlighting the yacht's elegance via metallic painted accents.

The sublime 3BBoys is an embodiment of contemporary maritime architecture and machinery, blending modern elegance, superb performance and practical sea marine traits into a single stunning package. It's a yacht that is indeed outstanding in all possible categories, and only a call away for interested buyers.

title: Revival at the Sea: Norfolk Punt Open Celebrates Historic Boat Design Amid Record Participation
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Revival at the Sea: Norfolk Punt Open Celebrates Historic Boat Design Amid Record Participation
summary: An exhilarating recount of the adventure and camaraderie at the first Norfolk Punt Open of 2026, a historical event celebrated with record participation.
body: The conventional sails of Norfolk Punt Club witnessed a nostalgic resurgence on 9th and 10th May 2026, with the first open event of the year attracting an impressive fleet of 19 boats, a record for the century-old community. With spectators and sailors alike bathed in gloriously sunny conditions, the weekend served as a vibrant tribute to the club's deep-rooted sailing heritage.

To kick-start the weekend festivities, a specially organised filming day took place overseeing 14 iconic punts. Showcasing an array of designs from over a century ago to more recent models, including the venerable 108-year-old 'Prawn', the day offered attendees a rare glimpse into the class's evolution. This mesmerising spectacle wasn't merely aesthetic, as crews seized the opportunity to hone their skills in race starts, tacks, gybes, and spinnaker handling under ideal weather conditions.

The second and third races were nothing short of exhilarating, with surprising upsets and fiercely contested victories. Thanks to a shift towards starboard during the start, the deck tilted in favour of the savvy crews who leveraged this advantage. The subsequent victories went to Simon Clayton's 'Decoy' and again to Charlie Stewart's 'Snow Goose' on a handicap.

As the sun set on a day of adrenaline-fuelled races, participants and spectators alike were treated to a jovial party hosted by Rupert Redington and Bridget O'Brien, where sailing tales echoed amid laughter and cheer. The following Sunday was not short of challenges, as gusty 25-knot winds tested the mettle of the crews as well as the design of the boats, reminiscent of 49ers. Not surprisingly, the day witnessed an array of capsizes amid the white-knuckle races.

All in all, the Norfolk Punt Open 2026 managed to encapsulate the beauty of the illustrious class of boats, the spirit of the community, and the thrill of racing, setting an inspiring precedent for the events to follow.

title: The Revelation of Pa’lante - The Superyacht Redefining the Golden Age of Ocean Travel
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Revelation of Pa’lante - The Superyacht Redefining the Golden Age of Ocean Travel
summary: Project Frida emerges from the shadows, christened as Pa'lante, ready to sail the seas with an aura of vintage elegance and modern engineering.
body: Emerging from the esteemed Dutch shipyard, Heesen Yachts, Project Frida is fully revealed in a grand christening ceremony as Pa’lante, subtley encouraging one to 'keep going' or 'move forward'. Set to debut at the 2026 Monaco Yacht Show, this 55-metre steel superyacht is ready to carve her signature trails across the open seas. The vessel, perfected over two years in the meticulously precise hands at Heesen Yachts, has already showcased a 'flawless performance' during her sea trials in the North Sea. Imagine stepping on to the sun deck under the serene azure sky. A splendid whirlpool awaits you alongside a welcoming bar, multiple lounge areas and a sundeck. Equipped with the yard's patented Fast Displacement Hull form, Pa'lante exhibits her prowess on the water with MTU 4000 M63 engines pushing her to a top speed of 15.5 knots and an admirable range of 4,500 nautical miles at a comfortable pace of 12 knots. Step inside and be welcomed by the extravagant interiors emulating the 'golden age of ocean travel', coupled with an advanced SCR system for full compliance with IMO Tier III emission regulations. The interiors meld a rich palette of warm materials giving radiance to the living spaces that echo natural wengé wood, meticulously planned by the Italian studio Luca Dini Design & Architecture. Picture yourselves waking up each morning in one of the six commodious cabins, designed particularly to merge luxury with cozy comfort. A private study awaits the curious minds, while a massive en suite enhances the owner's apartment, a perfect blend of comfort, elegance and utility. CEO of Heesen, Jeroen van der Meer beholds, 'We are delighted to welcome Pa'lante to the fleet and her owners to the Heesen family.' With the officially christened vessel now part of Heesen's ambitious fleet, enthusiasts await the Monaco Yacht Show with bated breath, eager to meet this architectural marvel in all her maritime splendour.

title: Fliteboard and Mercury Racing Unveil Their Fastest e-Foil Yet, Promising Unprecedented Excitement
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Fliteboard and Mercury Racing Unveil Their Fastest e-Foil Yet, Promising Unprecedented Excitement
summary: When world-leading Fliteboard merges with high-performance Mercury Racing, a high-speed aquatic marvel is born – the ultimate e-Foil for thrillseekers.
body: Out on the vast blue canvas, the Fliteboard Race emerges as an epitome of maritime innovation, an exhilarating eFoil that defies conventional speed limits. A joint venture of Fliteboard and Mercury Racing, both behemoths in their respective fields, this electronic hydrofoiler ramps up to a staggering 30 knots, taking aquatic thrill to a new level of extreme. Undoubtedly, 20 knots will seem somewhat mundane to aquatic enthusiasts once they've traded the regular for this speed trailblazer.

Add to it the aesthetic appeal shaped by a racing-inspired, sleek silhouette and carbon fibre detailing- the Fliteboard Race exudes an aura that screams speed. In terms of flexibility, the eFoil is a match for all with its compatibility with the full Flitecell battery range. Users can opt between the 16.8Ah Nano battery pack or the heavier 40Ah Explore pack, depending upon their usage and adventure goals.

Summing up, the Fliteboard Race is a fine blend of top-notch performance, versatility, and eye-catching design. Accommodating both recreational users and competitive racers, it exhibits the potential to redefine personal watercraft technology. Those with an inclination towards the motorboats, speedboats, or superyachts category, and a soft corner for exhilaration-filled sailing adventures, prepare to have a ride of a lifetime!

title: Uncover the Luxury of the 29m Blondie, One of Van der Valk’s Notable Explorer Yachts
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Uncover the Luxury of the 29m Blondie, One of Van der Valk’s Notable Explorer Yachts
summary: The 29m Van der Valk explorer yacht Blondie steals the limelight as it is now listed for sale, elegantly combining modern design with functionality.
body: In an unveiling that is set to make waves in the luxury boat sector, the third addition to the latest generation of long-range explorers from Van der Valk has been launched. And she is quite the sight to behold. Immaculately christened as 'Blondie', this 29m explorer yacht strikes a remarkable balance between contemporary design and pragmatic sea-faring capabilities. What speaks volumes about her craft is her seamless integration of modern aesthetics with the resiliency of a trawler. This is a refreshing collaboration between Guido de Groot Design, Diana Yacht Design and Ginton Naval Architects. The yacht possesses a five-cabin layout, comfortably accommodating up to 10 guests. This includes a main deck full-beam owner’s suite. She features two VIP doubles and twin cabins, all furnished with en-suites. For the supporting staff, the aft crew quarters provide a sleeping arrangement for a team of four. The main highlights of the Blondie are not limited to just her exteriors. Stepping onboard, you’re welcomed by an open-plan saloon that is the epitome of modern comfort. Crisp white soft furnishings provide a laid-back atmosphere for lounging. Right forward, inside the same space, is a dining area capable of seating all 10 guests, flanked by window panes that allow for an influx of natural light. The sundeck offers a dedicated leisure area where guests can unwind around a large dining table. Just a stone's throw away is a compact bar where guests can enjoy drinks. Further aft, a pool is flanked by sunbeds, offering room for sun-soaked relaxation. The beach club downstairs offers guests their little sanctuary, complete with a sauna and a seating area next to the swim platform for seamless sea access. The Blondie's power comes from a pair of 1,650hp MAN V12 diesel engines, boasting a top speed of 20 knots and a cruising speed of 17 knots. With its blend of style and performance, the Blondie, now set for sale at a price tag of $10,900,000, stands as a testament to Van der Valk's prowess.

title: Victory on the Waves: The All-Women Coral World Team Triumphs in Annual USVI Tourism Regatta
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Victory on the Waves: The All-Women Coral World Team Triumphs in Annual USVI Tourism Regatta
summary: The waters of the U.S. Virgin Islands bore witness to a triumphant victory, as the all-women Coral World Team aced the 7th Annual USVI Hotel & Tourism Association Regatta.
body: When the seven bells rang out on the ninth of May, five fabulously enthusiastic teams found their positions on the emerald waters of the U.S. Virgin Islands. The 7th Annual Hotel & Tourism Association Regatta, an event that fuels the spirit of competitiveness and camaraderie among the territory's hospitality and tourism industry, was in full swing, hosted by the prestigious St. Thomas Yacht Club and Sailing Center.

On this day, teams raced aboard the Center's one-design IC24s, completing a series of competitive races that tested their sailing prowess, communication, teamwork and the very essence of the territory's marine tourism product. Emerging triumphant was the Coral World's all-women team, who outshone everyone to claim first place with an impressive haul of 5 points.

Hot on the Coral World team's heels was Margaritaville team, who secured the dignified second place with a commendable 13 points. A spirited team made up of Mahlon Monsanto, Alique Briggs, Augustine Schneider, and K'Quadeem Christopher improved on their performance from the previous year.

A familiar face graced the third-place podium once again as the U.S. Virgin Islands Department of Tourism team defended their position with an earned 16 points. The team, made up of Alani Henneman-Todman, Ian Turnbull, Wilbert Smith, and Tanya Duran, raced aboard One Love, reaffirming their love and passion for sailing. This exhilarating spectacle was a testament to not only the spirit of competition but the sheer joy and unity invoked by the caress of the sea breeze and the thrill of the race.

title: M/Y Lady Luna: A Masterpiece of the Sea Now Up for Grabs, Showcasing Exceptional Volume, Unique Wellness Features and Charter Potential
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: M/Y Lady Luna: A Masterpiece of the Sea Now Up for Grabs, Showcasing Exceptional Volume, Unique Wellness Features and Charter Potential
summary: Phoenix Yacht Management announces exclusive authority for selling the M/Y Lady Luna - a luxury ocean jewel full of bonus features and amenities.
body: Phoenix Yacht Management has announced that the glorious M/Y Lady Luna has dropped anchor in the market of luxury yachts for sale. This majestic sea marvel, a 32.1-metre motoryacht constructed by Marti Yat Shipyard in Istanbul, is looking for a new owner at the asking price of €9,750,000.

Exemplifying opulence, Lady Luna is a custom-built creation that comfortably nestles in the 30 – 35-metre segment. She has been meticulously sculpted, with Mentor Yat branding her exterior design and the elegant touch of Ira Petromanolaki of IPYD marking her interiors. Accentuating spaciousness and owner's comfort as her primary attributes, Lady Luna can house up to 10 guests across its five luxurious staterooms. The jewel of these rooms is a 20-square-metre full-beam owner’s suite that screams generosity in its space.

Underpinned by a gross tonnage of 288gt, a draft of 1.75 metres, and the power of twin MAN 650hp engines, Lady Luna is no less than a sea-horse. She elegantly cruises at the speed of 11 knots with an impressive range of 1,000 nautical miles.

Bringing the perfect blend of spaciousness, expert construction, and magnificent wellness amenities to a 32-metre platform, Lady Luna is a compelling proposition. Phoenix Yachts anticipates robust attention from potential buyers looking to invest in a well-appointed yacht with plenty of scope for both private use and charter potential.

Lady Luna has also been nominated for the prestigious World Superyacht Awards 2026 in the semi-displacement or planing motoryachts, 30 – 34.9-metre category, further demonstrating her dominance and class in the marketplace. Those eyeing this floating mansion can contact Phoenix Yachts directly for a detailed specification overview and viewing requests.

title: The M/Y Persefoni Reveals What it Really Takes to Excel in the 50-55m Superyacht Charter Class
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The M/Y Persefoni Reveals What it Really Takes to Excel in the 50-55m Superyacht Charter Class
summary: Partnering with motoryacht Persefoni across seasons has unveiled key insights into running a 50 to 55-metre class charter vessel.
body: Navigating the M/Y Persefoni across multiple Greek island seasons has provided an unrivalled perspective into the 50 to 55-metre charter class. Comprehending the demands of running such a vessel, especially in the strikingly diverse and beautifully chaotic Greek islands, is no mean feat. Infused with passion and professionalism, the Persefoni not only meets these demands but handsomely exceeds them, setting a new authoritative standard.

The stability of the Persefoni is another star of the show – it goes beyond being a mere operational commitment to a feature that enhances the entire cruising experience. Particularly in the Cyclades where the summer Meltemi winds test the stability to its limits, the Persefoni's at-anchor stabilisers deliver outstanding performance, keeping the vessel composed and stable.

Thirdly, let's not underestimate the power of a thorough refit. In 2023, Persefoni underwent a comprehensive makeover under the supervision of Emperio Yachting Alliance. Not just a cosmetic process, this refit improved all aspects of the vessel, enabling the vessel to deliver consistently high standards across seasons.

Finally, one cannot overlook the role of the crew complement. Persefoni's 13 dedicated professionals ensure that every one of the 12 guests experiences unparalleled luxury and enjoyment. This level of attention is what makes the difference between a good and an exceptional charter experience.

title: A Vision in Blue: Damen Yachting Presents its 75.2-metre Hybrid Expedition Yacht, the First Ever to Cultivate Vegetables on Board
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A Vision in Blue: Damen Yachting Presents its 75.2-metre Hybrid Expedition Yacht, the First Ever to Cultivate Vegetables on Board
summary: In the Dutch city of Vlissingen, Damen Yachting has launched its 75.2-metre hybrid expedition yacht, referred to as Custom DY 75 Hybrid.
body: A new player has entered the world of superyachts - and it comes with quite a splash. Damen Yachting's Custom DY 75 Hybrid, a 75.2-metre hybrid expedition yacht, has been revealed, marking the milestone of its official launch. The project - kept remarkably private during construction - began with her keel laying in 2022, and since then, this oceanic titan has been a beacon of anticipation for maritime enthusiasts across the globe. Notably, the yacht's design was helmed by British studio Michael Leach Design alongside Damen's own naval architects. Together, they created an incredibly capable platform that goes beyond aesthetics. The Custom DY 75 Hybrid holds a hybrid propulsion system for zero-emission global cruising, bringing eco-consciousness into the realm of luxury. Accommodation for up to twelve guests ensures comfort is not compromised by capability. One key highlight of the Custom DY 75 Hybrid – a feature that sets it truly apart in the industry – is the incorporation of commercial-grade cultivation pods. This technology allows for the growth of tomatoes, lettuce, cucumbers, and other vegetables on board, presenting a level of self-sufficiency not previously seen in private yachts. This yacht proves that sustainability, innovation, and luxury are not mutually exclusive but can be gracefully intertwined. This rugged, ocean-going vessel is equipped with an efficient power and propulsion configuration. In addition to two main engines, she also features PTO/PTI hybrid electrical drives that allow running at up to eight knots for a total range of 6,200 miles when cruising at 14 knots. Onboard battery power for regular use and silent nights at anchor without generator power make her perfectly equipped for long-term exploration. For those looking forward to extended zero-emission silent cruising in fragile marine ecosystems, stored power can be increased with containerised battery packs. The Custom DY 75 Hybrid is more than a superyacht. She is a statement of what the yachting industry can achieve, breaking new ground in sustainable sea travel and setting the bar for private yachts to follow. She is expected to be ready for delivery this summer, ready to embark on her maiden voyage and set new standards for eco-conscious exploration.

title: The Highs, Lows, and Highlights of GP Watercraft’s Spring Sailing Season
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Highs, Lows, and Highlights of GP Watercraft’s Spring Sailing Season
summary: Revisit the key moments, intriguing projects, and thrilling victories of GP Watercraft during the spring sailing season.
body: Springtime saw GP Watercraft engaging in thrilling regattas, supporting aspiring athletes, and advancing sailing programs. As Europe was on the cusp of its sailing season, the company's voyage was off to a promising start with the Grand Prix held in Vilamoura, Portugal. This pre-season regatta served as a pivotal launching pad for sailors anticipating a fruitful year on the waves. With conditions light yet wavering, it demanded immense patience, assertive positioning, and wise decision-making. Athletes such as AP, Matteo, Molly, Florencia, and Finn all accumulated noteworthy racing experience in this competitive fleet.

A shift of focus back into the UK brought attention to the ILCA UK National Open events. Matteo clinched victory in the first event, whereas AP showcased her prowess, landing third amongst the females. These events acted as arenas for the sailors to gauge their readiness for the forthcoming season.

However, the accomplishments were not confined to the racecourse. Following a successful stint at the RYA Dinghy & Watersports Show, the GP Watercraft Team unveiled an expanded assortment in the Nautivela range. This initiative strengthened their backing for youth and performance sailing programs across the UK.

Simultaneously, the company maintained a rewarding partnership with Zhik, continuing to enhance its retail operations while providing sailors with technical apparel and performance equipment during the season. In association with Melges and RYA, GP Watercraft committed to supplying boats to budding and professional RYA instructors as a part of broader initiatives supporting participation and coaching within the sport.

An exemplar of their continued sponsorship efforts was at the Royal Lymington Yacht Club Optimist Open. It was rewarding to appreciate the prowess of numerous youthful sailors, defying a vast wind range over the two-day event.
As springtime makes way for summer, GP Watercraft revs up their preparation in all sectors of the organization, promising another season filled with excitement and seafaring adventures.

title: The Real Titans Speak: New Insights into Marine Market State, As Shipyard CEOs Air Their Views
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Real Titans Speak: New Insights into Marine Market State, As Shipyard CEOs Air Their Views
summary: Inside the marine industry, whose voices really matter? An exclusive look into the views of the leaders shaping today's shipyard landscape.
body: Pundits are aplenty in the marine sector, but none hold the consequential insights of those at the helm - the CEOs of the market-leading shipyards. We ask nine such leaders the critical questions, offering a collective health check and what to expect next in the industry. The conversation spans from Royal Huisman, Damen Yachting, and Feadship in the Netherlands to Italian heavyweights Palumbo, Sanlorenzo, Azimut Benetti and Ferretti, onto Abeking and Rasmussen in Germany, and finally, Bilgin in Türkiye. Their converging views provide a fascinating lense into the industry's current state and foreseeable future.

Looking to the future, our CEO panel notes a shift in customer priorities. These captains of industry find owners more thoughtfully assessing their time on board, with purpose, sustainability and adventure now impacting the design process of these vessels. The industry leaders don't foresee explosive growth but anticipate a market shaped by quality, credibility, and relevance to modern boat owner's expectations.

An interview extract with Giordano Pellacani, Chief Commercial Officer at Ferretti Group, reveals how at the Ferretti Group Superyacht Yard, the construction process has been strengthened by the evolution of integrated design systems and incorporating in-house engineering and naval architecture expertise.

title: Sailing Beyond Wins and Losses: Stories of Confidence, Progression and Emotional Evolution at Sea
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Sailing Beyond Wins and Losses: Stories of Confidence, Progression and Emotional Evolution at Sea
summary: Sailing isn’t just about crossing finish lines, it's about the challenges faced and the lessons learned along the voyage. Here're three moving tales from the deck.
body: Without a doubt, there's more to sailing than the adrenaline rush of competition and the thrill of victory. It's about the journey, the progression, the encounter with the inner self amidst the open seas. Bundled in this tale are three yarns of courage, transformation, and self-realization.

Consider Laszlo Drummond's tale; a captivating story of hope and resilience. Despite carrying two black flags at a GB selection event, he harboured an unwavering resolve to make it to the Worlds Team. Seemingly impossible odds didn't deter him; instead, they ignited a fire under his resolve, turning the impossible into the possible. His story offers a lesson in dogged determination and an unwavering spirit.

Lastly, we explore how sailing, like an artist's brush, paints broad strokes of confidence into the lives of many. How it breaks barriers, builds courage, and instils new strength is worth pondering upon. The feeling of independence, the skills acquired, the knowledge of one's capabilities – sailing often entwines these aspects into one comprehensive journey of self-confidence and empowerment.

These stories serve as reminders of the transformative power sailing can have - it's not just a sport but a convex mirror of self-inspection, self-realization and self-improvement. The voyage on the open sea is a voyage into oneself. If you are a sailor or an aspirant, there's a lot to take home from these inspirational narratives.

title: An Inside Look at the Meserret Yacht's Stunning Reinvention, Rechristened as 'Arriva'
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: An Inside Look at the Meserret Yacht's Stunning Reinvention, Rechristened as 'Arriva'
summary: The classic 39.3-metre motor yacht Meserret steps into a bold new era, sailing under a new name, Arriva, following a ground breaking sale.
body: The breathtaking, 39.3-metre motor yacht, known as Meserret, underwent a phenomenal change when it caught the eye of a buyer represented by Marcel Busse from Yachtzoo. The finality of the sale marked a significant event in the yacht's history, as she was given a new identity – 'Arriva'. This classic beauty was orchestrated into existence in 1981, by the renowned Spanish shipyard Astilleros Armón. Crafted in steel, she was moulded to a design by Paolo Scanu, with Don Francisco Diaz Madarro overseeing the naval architecture. However, Arriva’s most coveted feature remains her distinctive canoe-sterndesign. Arriva, then known as Meserret, underwent a complete transformation between 2001 and 2002, with a full interior and exterior overhaul. Fast-forwarding to 2020, she enjoyed an extensive refit including the installation of zero-speed stabilisers. She emerged from these revamps with a shroud of elegance, declared charter-ready. Last listed for €3,400,000, Arriva accommodates 12 guests within her six luxurious en suite cabins. The two most plush cabins, the master suite and VIP, are located on the main deck. The lower deck houses a second VIP and three twin cabins. Accommodations are also made for a crew of seven. Reflecting her classic exterior, Arriva's interior remains just as regal. Rich teak panelling is awakened by light fabrics and Pastel soft furnishings, the expansive spaces further punctuated by multiple wide windows across each deck. Possessing classic woodwork blended with contemporary amenities, this stunner strikes the perfect balance. Arriva's main deck hosts comfortable living areas, from the cosy sofa space of the main saloon to the large aft deck with built-in sofas that perfectly trace the curve of the stern. On the upper deck, guests can luxuriate in the U-shaped lounge and dining area beneath a large awning, while the inside houses a secondary saloon. Forward on the deck, additional seating invites passengers to soak in the views over the bow during cruising. The sundeck, proudly clinging to a Jacuzzi nestled between sun pads, provides an ideal spot for guests to bask in. The sale and transformation of the familiar favourite, Meserret, into 'Arriva' is demonstrative of the evolution, versatility, and boundless potential in the world of yachting.

title: Famed Yacht Alhambra's Price Slashed - Dive Into the World of Luxurious Sea Voyages
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Famed Yacht Alhambra's Price Slashed - Dive Into the World of Luxurious Sea Voyages
summary: Luxury sea voyage enthusiasts are in for a treat! The iconic 35.4-metre Feadship motor yacht Alhambra has had a significant price drop.
body: Standing proudly at 35.4-metres, Alhambra, an illustrious classic canoe stern Feadship motor yacht, has just become a lot more attainable by potential buyers due to a price drop of €505,000. Now listed at €4,995,000, this refined masterpiece is a symbol of true elegance and luxury. Conceived and brought to life in 1970 under renowned designer H.W. De Voogt, Alhambra has faithfully served her owners through the years and experienced frequent refits to maintain her majestic charm.

A notable technical refit in 2008 marked the start of a renovated life for Alhambra, followed by an aggressive three-year refit plan from 2019 through 2022, under her current tenure. The refit plan brought an array of swanky modifications, including a fresh paint job, engine rebuild, interior overhaul, new teak addition to the sundeck, and new exterior enhancements like sun awnings, a bar, and a tender crane on the foredeck.

Positioned ideally at the water's edge, a stern door provides guests with easy access to the water via a newly-designed passerelle swimming ladder. On top of this, a set of sun pads has been added forward of the bridge to cater to guests' sunbathing needs. Propelled by two Detroit Diesel 16V-71N 460hp engines, Alhambra can reach top speeds of 14 knots. The yacht also comes equipped with stabilisers, ensuring unruffled comfort for her guests while at anchor or on the move.

title: Charles Leclerc, known for his speed on the F1 track, takes a plunge with latest Riva Super yacht
author: Old Sea Dogs

summary: When one of the fastest men on the planet chooses the sea instead of the racetrack, the vessel better be extraordinary. Enter the 20th Riva 102' Corsaro Super yacht, the latest seafaring darling of F1 driver Charles Leclerc.
body: Speeding on the water takes a different turn when Formula 1 driver Charles Leclerc collaborates with Italian shipyard Riva, a division of Ferretti Group. The twosome launched the 20th Riva 102' Corsaro Super yacht, named Sedici, symbolising a fascinating amalgamation of speed, elegance, and seafaring beauty.

Sedici made its grand splash at the La Spezia facilities, with Leclerc, a repeat Riva owner, at the helm. Previously, he held the title deed to the Riva 82 Diva, L'As Bleu, showing the driver's loyalty to the brand. The Corsaro Super model, an evolution of the beloved 100' Corsaro, is marked by a sleek profile, open areas, and a smooth flow between interiors and decks. It also bears the personal choices of the Monegasque racer, including Minotti-designed furniture and Jim Thompson cushions.

Powering Sedici are twin MTU 16V 2000 M96L EPA Tier III engines with the freedom to cruise at 24 knots and reach a top speed of 28 knots. Advanced stabilisation solutions, including Hydrotab Interceptor trim tabs, Sleipner Vector Fins, and Seakeeper gyroscopic stabilisers minimise sway both at anchor and while cruising.

Ferretti Group CEO Alberto Galassi celebrates Leclerc’s continued patronage, appreciating hiim choosing Riva once again. In an industry where standards are soaring sky-high, this collaboration confirms the unique appeal of Riva's functional beauty and state-of-the-art technology. Looking at BOATPro's data, Riva seems to be ready to fulfil the high demand, with 20 yachts over 24 metres in various stages of construction.
As Leclerc is set to ride the ocean waves aboard Sedici, Riva continues to surge ahead, crafting superior vessels that push the envelope of nautical design and technology.

title: Armada Cup 2026: A Riveting Return to the Atlantic Calendar with Diverse Offshore Racing in the Heart of the Basque Coast
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Armada Cup 2026: A Riveting Return to the Atlantic Calendar with Diverse Offshore Racing in the Heart of the Basque Coast
summary: The highly anticipated Armada Cup 2026 re-emerges as one of the most distinctive offshore races on the Atlantic calendar, reconnecting British and Basque sailing traditions.
body: The 460-nautical-mile Armada Cup set to unfurl its sails in 2026 is no ordinary race. Originally introduced nearly four decades ago, this unique event takes competitors across breathtaking vistas that include crossing the English Channel, circling the Ouessant Island, skirting past the Chaussée de Sein, before finally making a beeline for the picturesque Basque coast. The event culminates in the famed Bay of La Concha in Donostia, San Sebastián, a finish that's deeply etched in the minds of global sailors for its unbeatable beauty. Such an exhilarating journey is made possible thanks to the collaborative efforts of the Royal Western Yacht Club (RWYC) and the Real Club Náutico de San Sebastián (RCNSS), instilling in the event an unmatched blend of British and Basque sailing traditions and sporting spirit. Welcoming monohulls and multihulls over 27 feet, the race incites keen interest from offshore racers worldwide. Already, it boasts a promising lineup of 14 boats that have officially entered the competition well ahead of commencement, and the fleet is expected to grow bigger as the event nears, with a surge in British entries anticipated over the coming month. The post-race experience is just as unforgettable as the race itself. Participants and spectators alike are encouraged to explore the rich maritime culture and captivating culinary scenes of the Basque coast. The ports of Hondarribia and Getaria beckon with their charming nautical traditions and reminiscence of bygone eras, whereas the wider stretch of coast leading to Getxo forms a haven for those enamored with the art of Atlantic seamanship and cruising. Notably, Getaria, the birthplace of the renowned seafarer Juan Sebastián Elcano, continues to carry the torch of Basque maritime history. The joy of being on the Atlantic waters amidst the spirit of friendly competition, coupled with a plethora of sights to savor, truly sets the Armada Cup 2026 apart from its peers.

title: Star Diamond, the Iconic Superyacht from Below Deck, Finds a New Owner at Auction
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Star Diamond, the Iconic Superyacht from Below Deck, Finds a New Owner at Auction
summary: The magnificent Star Diamond, a 46.9-metre motor yacht, has found a new owner courtesy of the Boathouse Auctions.
body: Boathouse Auctions has successfully auctioned off the exquisite Star Diamond to a new owner. The opulent 46.9-metre Admiral Marine motor yacht was effectively represented by Cromwell Littlejohn of Northrop & Johnson, while the buyer was introduced by Denison Yachting's Will Noftsinger.

Delivered by Admiral Marine in 1998, the Star Diamond has maintained a pristine condition, following a significant overhaul that concluded in 2024. This renovation comprised an outstanding $9 million in mechanical, structural and shipyard upgrades. The Star Diamond's elegant interiors are crafted by Donald Starkey, with the brilliant yacht’s design under the masterful eye of Lou Codega.
Audiences may recall the Star Diamond’s remarkable performance in the second season of 'Below Deck', under the yacht's previous alias, 'Ohana'.

Flexibility is key on the Star Diamond. Her decks can easily be converted to meet the owner's needs, turning into a gym, game room, or spa. There is also no shortage of entertaining spaces as the superyacht features a spacious open-air dining area, a U-shaped bar that seats twelve, a six-person Jacuzzi, and more.

A majestic pair of Caterpillar diesel engines powers this glorious yacht, providing a maximum speed of 18 knots and a leisurely cruising speed of 14 knots. The Star Diamond is also well-prepared for stability, thanks to her advanced Quantum zero-speed stabilisers.
Undoubtedly, the Star Diamond's magnificent design, luxurious features, and top-notch facilities make it a prize catch in the superyacht sphere.

These events reflect the spirit of yachting: a fusion of strategic prowess and competent seamanship set against an inspiring aquatic backdrop. Both East Kent Radio Sailing Club and Littleton Sailing Club leave fans eagerly awaiting their next maritime adventures.

As the Global Solo Challenge inches closer, several preparations are underway for a grand event. title: Five Hours Flat Out in the Trades as Antigua Racing Cup Exploded Into Life
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Antigua Racing Cup 2026: Trade Winds Delivered a Blistering Opening Day
summary: The Antigua Racing Cup roared into action off Nelson’s Dockyard, with full trade winds, technical courses and relentless racing delivering one of the most demanding and exhilarating opening days of the Caribbean season.
body: If there was any doubt about what the Antigua Racing Cup was going to be, it disappeared within the first hour.
This wasn’t a gentle warm-up.
It was straight into it.

Out off Nelson’s Dockyard, the fleet met exactly what Antigua does best — proper trade wind sailing. A gradient easterly breeze sat firmly in the high teens, with gusts pushing beyond 20 knots, and just enough variation late in the day to keep tacticians honest.
It was the kind of day that sorts boats early.
And crews even earlier.
Full Throttle from the First Gun
The Race Committee didn’t ease anyone in.

CSA 2, 3 and 4 were sent into technical, multi-leg windward-leeward courses — five legs to start, with a punishing five-mile beat straight into the trades followed by a full-blooded run back down the track.
No hiding.
No shortcuts.
Just grind, trim, and repeat.
For CSA 1, the big boats were sent offshore on a 24-nautical-mile test — long enough to stretch the legs, short enough to keep the pressure on.
Race 2 tightened the screws further.
Shorter courses. More manoeuvres. Less margin for error.
Boat handling, crew work and decision-making were under constant strain — and after nearly five hours on the water, the fleet came ashore knowing exactly where they stood.
At the sharp end, Adrian Lee’s HH66 Lee Overlay Partners III delivered one of the standout performances of the day.
Foiling appendages. Rotating wing mast. And the kind of raw pace that turns heads even in a fast fleet.
Over 20 knots through Caribbean chop — not just quick, but composed.
This wasn’t survival sailing.
This was controlled aggression.
In the big boat division, Dan Gribble’s Tripp 65 Prevail wasted no time stamping authority on the race.
A clean start, a dialled-in setup, and once she was up to speed — gone.
Line honours and corrected time victory came with an elapsed time of just over three hours, a serious statement in a fleet that doesn’t give anything away easily.
Behind, Lennart Davidsson’s Kialoa III and John McMonigal’s Zig Zag fought their own battle — separated not by miles, but by minutes on corrected time.
Close enough to keep it interesting.
Far enough to know Prevail had done it properly.
CSA 2 delivered what Antigua racing always promises when the fleet is tight — a proper scrap.
Race 1 went to Belladonna, edging out Warthog by less than two minutes after corrected time. Race 2 flipped the script, with Warthog clawing it back by just over a minute.
Two races.
Two winners.
Margins measured in seconds.
Rikki sat quietly consistent in third — exactly where smart campaigns build regattas.
If consistency wins regattas, Danish Blue had already made its point.
Two races. Two wins.
But it wasn’t easy.
Panacea X pushed hard all day, never letting the gap open too far, while the chasing pack — Team Strada Awakening, High Tension, and J-Aguar — fought over scraps measured in seconds.
This was tactical sailing at its sharpest.
Currents, pressure lines, and local knowledge all playing their part.
The kind of racing where you don’t just sail the boat — you sail the water.
In CSA 4, Ashley Rhodes’ Whiplash put together one of the cleanest performances of the day.
Two races.
Two wins.
No drama on the scoreboard — but plenty on board.
Breakages, quick fixes, and a crew that reacted fast enough to keep the momentum alive.
Behind them, The Project, Montebello Pepsi, and Caipirinha kept the pressure on, with margins tight enough to guarantee more of the same in the days ahead.
The Real Race Begins Ashore
By the time the fleet returned, sunburnt, salt-crusted and running on fumes, the racing wasn’t quite finished.
Because in Antigua, the second race of the day happens ashore.
Stories get told.
Starts get replayed — usually incorrectly.
And the cold drinks arrive just in time.
The daily prize giving did exactly what it should — brought the fleet together.
English Harbour Rum flowing. Amstel Beer disappearing quickly. Crews from all corners of the world swapping blows and laughter in equal measure.
Because that’s the thing about days like this.
You don’t just remember where you finished.
You remember how it felt.
Day one told you everything you needed to know.
This regatta wasn’t easing into life.
It arrived fully formed.
Proper breeze. Proper courses. Proper racing.
And if this is how it started — the rest of the week was never going to be quiet.

title: Maritime Experts Discourage Private Yachts from Navigating Strait of Hormuz Despite Nord's Recent Passage
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Maritime Experts Discourage Private Yachts from Navigating Strait of Hormuz Despite Nord's Recent Passage
summary: Private yachts are being ardently cautioned against attempting to cross the potentially dangerous Strait of Hormuz, irrespective of Nord's successful journey in April 2026.
body: The adventure filled world of private yachts received a potential shockwave recently. Maritime experts have sounded alarm bells cautioning all private yachts against attempting a crossing of the Strait of Hormuz. This warning comes despite the successful passage of the massive 141.6-meter Lürssen built superyacht, Nord, on the 25th of April, 2026. The Nord marked its name in the books becoming the first superyacht to traverse the strait since a temporary ceasefire was reached earlier in the month on the 8th. However, this journey is largely considered an exception rather than an emblem of improving circumstances. The consensus among the maritime professionals is the state of affairs surrounding the strait remain largely volatile and unpredictable. Despite the Nord's successful journey, the risks of such a passage for other private yachts continue to outweigh any potential benefits. Hence, the fervent advice is to steer clear of the region until further notice. This highlights the delicate balance between the thrill and inherent risks in the world of marine travel. More to come as the situation unfolds in the Strait of Hormuz and measures are taken to ensure increased safety for all mariners.
