title: Behold the Sea Raider X: ISA Yachts' Unveils Its Latest Gran Turismo 67M Masterpiece
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Behold the Sea Raider X: ISA Yachts' Unveils Its Latest Gran Turismo 67M Masterpiece
summary: The Italian boat builder ISA Yachts reveals the first megayacht from their newest Gran Turismo 67M series - the grand Sea Raider X.
body: ISA Yachts, known for its enduring commitment to luxurious nautical craftsmanship, proudly launches its first superyacht from the new ISA Gran Turismo 67M series - the Sea Raider X. As a hefty 67 meters long, this newcomer seizes the throne as the flagship of the Italian yard's esteemed fleet. An evolution of ISA's Gran Turismo line, the Sea Raider X gracefully merges sport, elegance, and cutting-edge technology, encapsulating the distinct style of the series.

Acclaimed Vallicelli Design Studio has penned the yacht's captivating exterior lines, giving Sea Raider X a monochrome skin with a stately black steel hull and a silver aluminium superstructure. Interior designs, an ultimate display of opulence, have been conceived by the brilliant minds at Team for Design, spearheaded by the notable Enrico Gobbi. The pioneering naval architecture of the yacht sprouts from the pro-level in-house team at the shipyard.

The stunningly serene Sea Raider X caters to onboard relaxation, with luxurious amenities including an aft area surrounded by a panoramic 6.5-meter pool, wide lounges equipped with side platforms that elegantly stretch the space outwards. The decadence continues to the beach club below with a Hammam, a gym, a cool bar, and direct access to the garage that accommodates a grand 7.5-meter tender. When not in use, the covered area transforms into a spacious full-beam lounge, almost doubling the beach club's size.

Comfort is paramount in the Sea Raider X, offering lavish accommodation for 14 guests in seven richly furnished cabins, including an owner's suite, all situated impressively across its main deck. The crew is equally well cared for, with eight commodious cabins accommodating up to thirteen members.

The majestic Sea Raider X, begun 'on spec' in 2023, was up for sale during its construction, fascinatingly reveals BOATPro. Now, prospective seafarers excitedly await the yacht's prominent delivery scheduled for September this year, marking a new era in nautical elegance and riveting performance.

title: Take a Detailed Look Inside the Opulent 38m Maori Motor Yacht K+, Now Up for Sale
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Take a Detailed Look Inside the Opulent 38m Maori Motor Yacht K+, Now Up for Sale
summary: The stunning 38.2-metre Maori motor yacht K+, built by the renowned Italian shipyard, hits the sales market with promises of luxury and high performance.
body: An epitome of luxurious comfort and precision engineering, the 38.2-metre Maori Yachts motor yacht K+ has sailed onto the sales front, with a prestigious tag of €14,500,000. The vessel comes under the joint central agentage of Denison Yachting and SuperYachtsMonaco, providing a backing as prominent as the yacht itself.

Built by the renowned Italian shipyard Maori Yachts and launched in 2023, the stunning exteriors of the K+ are a showcase of the architectural marvel by Marco Ciampa Architecture & Design Studio, beautifully complemented by the naval architecture designs of NavalHead. Only seen privately so far, the yacht has been nurtured in pristine 'turn-key' condition, making it primed for the next voyage.

The yacht has the potential to host 10 guests, with separate comfortable accommodation for seven crew members, including the captain. The owner's suite, on the upper deck, comes with lavish amenities such as a private terrace, a walk-in closet and an en-suite bathroom. On the lower deck, the two VIP and double cabins boast of their own en-suite bathrooms.

The ship is powered by two MAN V12 1,800 hp diesel engines, enabling it to reach a cruising speed of 13 knots, and a remarkable top speed of 18.5 knots. Compliance with RINA Commercial Comfort class testifies to the excellence of the vessel’s range, reaching up to 3,700 nautical miles at cruising speed.

A standout feature of the opulent K+ yacht is its spacious 80-square metre beach club, fitted with sun loungers and a swim platform. The yacht's roomy main deck is furnished like an outdoor lounge with chic modern seating, a large canopy, and a bar area with a fridge.

The Maori motor yacht K+, constructed with a GRP hull and superstructure, offers an extraordinary blend of luxurious comfort, modernity, and high-sea performance. With such exceptional features, it surely stands out as a vessel with excellent charter capabilities.

title: East Anglian Offshore Racing Association (EAORA) Attracts Double the Entrants following a Major Format Shake-up
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: East Anglian Offshore Racing Association (EAORA) Attracts Double the Entrants following a Major Format Shake-up
summary: In 2026, the EAORA increases its popularity dramatically, thanks to a three-day, three-race mini regatta, held during the early May Bank Holiday weekend.
body: The East Anglian Offshore Racing Association managed to turn the tide of declining interest in its traditional opening weekend event. It did so by shaking up the format in 2026 and introduced a three-day, three-race mini regatta - a move that was lauded as a resounding success. Despite light wind conditions that simultaneously tested the grit of competitors and the patience of race officials, the event enjoyed a turnout of twice as many entrants. The increased participation produces optimism around the future of EAORA.

Day Two served up Royal Burnham YC's RALPH HERRING Trophy race on a rather calm day with light southerlies. The competing boats voyaged from Medway to Burnham on Crouch. The race concluded with Hustler 32 Hullabaloo XV, helmed by David Evans, clinching the trophy. The Ralph Herring Trophy was presented to David Evans by a long-time friend, forming an endearing moment of the event.

Day 3 reeled off with the Pattinson Cup, which saw 11 yachts at the start line at the Branklet buoy on the River Crouch. This race took the participating boats back to Mersea. Winds were light, making for slow progress along the Buxey Channel. Nonetheless, it turned out to be an exhilarating end to an event that helped rejuvenate the timber of the EAORA racing scene.

The revamp proved a great success, with yachts spending three full days on the water, involved in nail-biting races. All in all, the event served as a resounding affirmation of EAORA's successful shake-up, and bore testament to the sea's unyielding allure, the joy of sailing, and the camaraderie that unites sailors across seas. The event marked a high note that it would give heart to future EAORA events.

title: Vitters Shipyard on the Verge of Making History with the In-Build 63m Sailing Yacht, Project Dreamer
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Vitters Shipyard on the Verge of Making History with the In-Build 63m Sailing Yacht, Project Dreamer
summary: Dutch yacht manufacturer, Vitters, offers a detailed update on their ambitious 63-meter sloop sailing yacht, Project Dreamer.
body: Vitters Shipyard, the famed Dutch yacht manufacturer, recently shared encouraging progress on their custom-built 63-meter sloop sailing yacht, Project Dreamer. The sailboat, which began its construction journey in Zwartsluis, the Netherlands, is six months into its initial keel laying ceremony. With an intricately designed aluminium structure, the build now stands well on its way to completion.

Owner aspirations were ambitious but clear-cut: to craft the most significant flybridge yacht possible, whilst remaining under the monolithic 500GT. The demand for a complex and sizeable build has necessitated the division of the project into several sections which were meticulously constructed in an unconventional upside-down fashion. The critical milestone set for later this year involves turning the hull of the vessel.

While exterior design details remain limited, we know that the yacht features a 'clean, timeless' aesthetic, courtesy of Malcolm McKeon, a renowned yacht designer. The design includes features such as a radiused transom, a sprawling flybridge, and a fold-down hull door for effortless water toy deployment.

Collaborative efforts remain at the heart of Dreamer's build. With Vitters Shipyard and Monks Large Yacht Consultancy uniting their expertise, the marvel of Project Dreamer is rapidly transitioning from bold concept to sailing reality.

As construction continues apace, Vitters raises the bar for what is feasible in yacht design. With the final delivery due in 2028, the yachting world waits eagerly for the day it can witness this extraordinary floating masterpiece in all its glory.

title: Revolutionising the Superyacht Scene: Aeri Studio Unveils 42-Metre 'Glide' Yacht Concept with a Freshly Bold Approach
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Revolutionising the Superyacht Scene: Aeri Studio Unveils 42-Metre 'Glide' Yacht Concept with a Freshly Bold Approach
summary: Aeri Studio, an upcoming Parisian design firm, is redefining yacht life with their avant-garde 42-metre motor yacht concept, 'Glide'.
body: A new ripple is forming on the surface of the superyacht scene with the unveiling of 'Glide', a 42-metre motor yacht concept generated from the youthful Parisian brains behind Aeri Studio. Led by studio founder Julien Cadro, this innovative design aims to shake the foundations of conventional yacht planning, promising a taste of 'radical openness and a deeply human approach' to life on board.

Constructed to bypass the customary 'compartmentalisation' that often characterises yachts of this calibre, Glide seems to paint a picture of life at sea in broad, fluid strokes—rooms no longer feel 'predictable'. The 42-metre (with a volume of sub-500GT) blueprint has been shaped around the core concept of elasticity and continuousness.

A statement from the studio says, 'The result is a space that shifts effortlessly depending on the moment: intimate over a candlelit dinner, expansive during a lazy afternoon at sea, animated when guests gather in the evening.'

Whilst heading outdoors, the yacht's unique quality is found aft, boasting a full-beam pool, the 'centrepiece' of an external wellness area. A sunbed is eased within a shallow pool, aligning the horizon views at eye level, thus extending the confluence of luxury and natural beauty.

Glide's full-beam master suite capitalises on generosity and fluidity on board. Cadro divulged that this design favours 'space and comfort throughout', from the open-plan wardrobe to the vast en suite. The proactive method of not 'maximising cabins at the expense of quality' imparts an air of extravagance and lavish sensibility.

Accommodation for guests is spread across four cabins, with four additional ones dedicated for the crew. 'This 42-metre concept signifies the studio's ambition to contribute something distinct to a market where originality is increasingly rare,' says Cadro, pointing at a clean-lined silhouette that is 'modern without chasing novelty.' A toast, then, to this revolutionising take on yacht life, brought to life by the creative minds at Aeri Studio.

title: Exploring the Thrill of Open-Air Water Adventures through Four Prized Hard Top Sports Cruisers
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Exploring the Thrill of Open-Air Water Adventures through Four Prized Hard Top Sports Cruisers
summary: Immerse yourself in an exploration of the four best second-hand hard top sports cruisers available today; their bespoke elegance, unmatched convenience, and open-air thrill promises an invigorating marine experience.
body: Imagine yourself at the helm of a 1980s-era Merc SL—lowering the soft top, inserting handles into the windscreen header rail, and releasing the front of the roof can be a tedious engagement. Fast forward a few decades—an SL experience boils down to a simple button press. This comparison isn't just with luxury cars; it's strikingly comparable with the marine world. Where boating enthusiasts once grappled with canopies, they now long for the simplicity and protection of hard top cruisers.

The valuation of a Fairline Targa 38 hard top, slid-roof version, today far outweighs an open version with a canopy. Presenting a quartet of second-hand hard top sports cruisers, these marine marvels promise not just the thrill of open waters but the ability to encapsulate oneself at the touch of a button.

Its interior has an interesting layout, boasting an owner's cabin forward, mid cabin aft, and a saloon opposite the galley. The mid cabin door in the centre coupled with the door's left alignment enables a larger cabin running lengthways under the cockpit. The smart design creates extra headroom without compromising seating space above.

This unique layout shines in the cockpit as well, housing a substantial helm seat and a smaller one facing forward with a gap for convenient movement. It also houses a sturdy sliding roof for a smaller but tougher aperture.

The cruiser comprises twin D4 engines in configurations of 260hp or 300hp, the latter being a popular choice among 70% buyers due to its size, weight advantage, and nominal additional cost. The Gran Turismo 38 boasts a performance in the low to mid 30-knot range.

The unusual facet of this cruiser is Beneteau's patented AirStep hull, ensuring smooth sea-keeping abilities. With this stellar combination of aesthetics and functionality, the Beneteau Gran Turismo 38 forms one of the triumphant hard top sports cruisers you could get cruising with right now.

title: Shaping the Next Generation of Sailing: Sunsail Continues to Fund Future Champions and Promotes Female Inclusion
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Shaping the Next Generation of Sailing: Sunsail Continues to Fund Future Champions and Promotes Female Inclusion
summary: After achieving remarkable success in their first two years, Sunsail’s Funding the Future initiative is back to support grassroots sailing clubs for a third year running.
body: For three consecutive years now, Sunsail has been steering grassroots sailing clubs towards success through its ‘Funding the Future’ initiative. Previous beneficiaries of this brilliant initiative include the West Lancashire Yacht Club (2024) and Otley Sailing Club (2025). In addition, clubs like Rudyard, Wilsonian, and Henley Sailing Club have reaped the rewards as runners-up. This initiative has proven to be a beacon of hope, whether it's been about upgrading boats to spearhead new ventures, enhancing junior facilities, or supporting the hardworking volunteers whose dedication keeps these clubs afloat.

2026 promises to be another stellar year for this initiative, with clubs across the country being given another fantastic opportunity to boost their facilities and support their sailors. The stakes are set high, with a grand prize of £6,000 up for grabs for the overall winner and £2,000 each for two deserving runner-up clubs.

To be a part of this fantastic initiative, clubs are required to submit an application detailing their vision for the future of sailing, which will be reviewed by a panel of esteemed judges. Winners will be announced at the Southampton International Boat Show 2026, marking yet another year of making waves with Sunsail's inspiring initiative.
So don't miss the boat! Join the movement and let's shape the future of sailing together, one club at a time.

title: Swoop in on a Splendid Sea Journey as Luxurious Palmer Johnson Motor Yacht Equity Is Now for Sale
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Swoop in on a Splendid Sea Journey as Luxurious Palmer Johnson Motor Yacht Equity Is Now for Sale
summary: The ravishing 45.7-metre Palmer Johnson motor yacht, Equity, is now up for sale. Ready to hit the waves in prime condition, it offers opulent interiors and an elegance that sails through time.
body: Presenting an irresistible opportunity for seafarers, the 45.7-meter-long Equity, a magnificent Palmer Johnson motor yacht, is now calling for owners. Construction in the heartlands of the United States by the reputed yacht builders, Palmer Johnson, the yacht was brought to existence in 2008. The Equity has since thrived, owing to meticulous yard work and improvements carried out punctually, to maintain it in exemplary condition. Ensuring a remarkable aesthetic appeal, the exteriors and interiors are the manifestation of artful craftsmanship by Nuvolari & Lenard.

Setting a picture perfect scene is the formal dining table, accommodating eight, poised perfectly to serve panoramic views and abundant natural light afforded by the floor-to-ceiling windows. The yacht allows for a good night’s rest for up to 12 visitors throughout the confines of five cabins. The array of rooms houses a full-beam, main deck master cabin, complemented by two doubles and two twin rooms, all of which are fully equipped with attached facilities.

The master suite is a melange of modish and contemporary elements, featuring chic interiors, personalized deck access and high-tech aspects such as integrated LED lighting. The main deck, accessible through double doors, marks the epitome of flexibility, treading the line between rejuvenating feasts and sunbathing, presenting an alfresco dining selection that is sheltered by the above sundeck. Seating seven comfortably on cushioned chairs, the round table comes with a lazy susan. Further aft, there lies a sizeable built-in sofa and coffee tables, providing utmost comfort. The rear-most part tempts visitors with a range of sun pads, unshaded to provide quintessential sun bathing amenities, adding the final touch to the well-rounded luxuries offered by the yacht.

title: Thrills, Spills, and Excitement: The Jervis Bay Classic 2026 at Vincentia Sailing Club Unveiled
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Thrills, Spills, and Excitement: The Jervis Bay Classic 2026 at Vincentia Sailing Club Unveiled
summary: Think back to the nail-biting action and the swirling, ecstatic energy of the Jervis Bay Classic 2026 at Vincentia Sailing Club.
body: One week from the third edition of the Vincentia Sailing Club's revered Jervis Bay Classic, it came as a surprise, not just the idyllic weather, but also the impressive turnout and the zealous energy encapsulating the Moona Moona over the ANZAC long weekend – announcing the conclusion of the staple sailing season. 71 distinctive boats launched over the weekend, navigate through untouched champagne sailing conditions. A congratulatory mention and heartfelt thanks are due for the unyielding volunteers from VSC, for yet again, delivering a spectacle that’s beyond comparison. The anticipation for the Nationals is sky-high. The weekend was packed with excitement and competitions. The Australian Championships for the nimble F16s, saw the participation of 11 boats racing. Coinciding with this, the NSW Hobie Cat Association culminated its 25/26 Traveller Series, a reflection of nine thunderous events spanning across the season, the opener being the WaveGP Championships at VSC back in September. As customary, the regatta kick-started on ANZAC Day with the Round the Bay Rally, a long-haul, passage-style competition around the cardinal marks within the Moona Moona. Buoyed by a tranquil nor'east sea breeze, the rally opted for the enticing "Callala Run". The adept Bryn Robinson-Mills took an early lead, followed by emerging talent, Emma Webb. The race soon transformed into a thrilling chase with Bridget Bolewski, Andrew Spinelli, and Darren Schmidt powering down to Husky. Stealing the show was Jarrod Spencer, leading the pack on the foiling A-Class, transcending others on his course towards the Callala mark. As the riveting ordeal unfolded, the adrenaline surge was equally shared by the bustling spectators, awestruck by the summer-like setting in autumn, the action-packed short courses and the fierce challenges faced by the determined contestants on the north end of the bay.

title: Learn from the Experts: Essential Strategies and Tips for the Round Britain & Ireland Race
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Learn from the Experts: Essential Strategies and Tips for the Round Britain & Ireland Race
summary: Veteran mariners share their know-how, equipping aspiring boaters for glory in the upcoming Round Britain & Ireland Race.
body: What does it take to conquer the upcoming 50th anniversary of the Round Britain & Ireland Race, one of the world's premier sailing competitions? A recent live webinar hosted by the Royal Ocean Racing Club (RORC) revealed insights from some of the sailing world's finest authorities, imparting expertise gleaned from nine successful race campaigns. From understanding the importance of early preparation to managing crew resilience, these experts laid a road map for success. This hour-long masterclass, now available for everyone, offers invaluable wisdom for sailors, supporters, and prospective entrants.

Another critical voice in the coaching session was Pip Hare, the 2022 line honours winner aboard the impressive IMOCA 60 Medallia. She designated the race track as one of the finest offshore circuits globally and shared her method for success. A detailed 'road book' or passage plan is her secret weapon, outlining potential hazards, decision points, wind farms, oil rigs, traffic separation schemes, rocks, tides, and forecast sources. Effectively, a well-prepared crew reduces the number of critical decisions that need to be made, especially when conditions are tough, and the crew's metal is tested.

RORC Commodore Deb Fish, an experienced winner of both fully crewed and double-handed categories, also shared her lessons. Reminding sailors never to underestimate the race's latter stages, she drew attention to the fact that while the finish line may seem near, fatigue, tricky tides and unexpected hazards can turn a well-sailed competition into a disaster.

Will Naylor, preparing for his fifth Round Britain & Ireland Race with the British Army Sailing Association, drove home the crucial aspect of crew management and resilience. He advised not relying on one or two individuals for all navigation knowledge and encouraged teams to double up on skills, always thinking carefully about food, water, communications and spare reserves.

A race like the Round Britain & Ireland Race is not for the faint-hearted - it requires far more than basic endurance. The sea has always been a demanding master, but with an experienced panel of experts sharing vital strategies and tips, sailors have profound insights to aid them as they plan for the challenges ahead. Good luck to all those who dare to take the leap!

title: Numarine Introduces the Future of Yachting with Sale of new 37XP, Topping their Explorer Yacht Series
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Numarine Introduces the Future of Yachting with Sale of new 37XP, Topping their Explorer Yacht Series
summary: Turkish shipyard, Numarine, has announced the sale of a new 37XP yacht, the 21st instalment in their renowned explorer series, scheduled to be delivered in 2027.
body: Emanating a vibe of modernity and sophistication, the newly sold 37XP yacht from Numarine once again stamps the Turkish yard's dominance in luxury yachting. Stepping into the spotlight as the 21st instalment in the acclaimed explorer series, this 37.1-metre new build strikes a sublime balance between performance and onboard comfort.

An all-star team chipped in to bring this digital spectacle to life. The naval architecture is handled by Umberto Tagliavini, a long-time collaborator of Numarine, who designed a full-displacement hull optimized for cruising in the most remote corners of the world. The yacht's exterior and interior aesthetic is the handiwork of Can Yalman, who elegantly emphasized the social areas of the yacht.

Beyond its lavish recreational spaces, the Numarine 37XP provides six cabins, including a master suite on the main deck and a sizeable suite on the upper deck with exclusive access to an outdoor terrace. These spaces become storage for a tender of up to nine metres when not in use.

Offering a top speed of 14 knots and a range of 6,000 nautical miles at eight knots, the Numarine 37XP firmly secures its rank among the world's leading expedition yachts of its class. Additional noteworthy specs include a 362GT volume.
The owners of this magnificent yacht will be spending their time seasonally between the Bahamas and the Mediterranean, underlining the model's flexibility for varied climates.

This great announcement comes just after Numarine revealed a new series of explorer yachts called the Classic Line. With more innovative projects waiting in the wings, Numarine is geared to enable a higher degree of personalisation in yachting.

title: Sailing Champions Sail Beyond the Wind, Navigate the Gusts at ILCA Midland Grand Prix Open 2026
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Sailing Champions Sail Beyond the Wind, Navigate the Gusts at ILCA Midland Grand Prix Open 2026
summary: Sailing enthusiasts navigated through gusty winds at the ILCA Midland Grand Prix Open 2026, held at Shustoke Sailing Club.
body: In April 2026, a thrilling event unfolded on the choppy waters off Shustoke Sailing Club. ILCA Midland Grand Prix Open became an arena for 16 Lasers who laid down a marker for the fierce competition to come throughout the Midland Grand Prix circuit. The weather wasn't an ally, with stormy winds and persistent rain possibly leading to a lower turnout than expected, but the sailors were undeterred. The day started with a crucial decision - to choose the larger, more competitive ILCA7 rig, or opt for the safer radial, ILCA6 rig. Nearly all competitors picked the latter, including the lighter-weight juniors. After a brief from the club's Rob Marlow, the sailors took to the waters, which were bustling with activity as everyone geared up for the heavy conditions. The initial race got underway at 11 am, and it was non-stop action all the way during. The port side dominated the line, with sailors battling out to reach the windward mark. Getting on the port involved some daring moves, followed by hurried manoeuvers to lay down the starboard tack and round the mark. The first part of the race saw a lull in the wind, leading to some gybing and attempts to find more wind pressure. But with a sudden gusty comeback, things quickly changed. John Ling demonstrated exceptional mastery of navigation and weather reading to finish first in what proved an enthralling bout. Corrected positions showed John Ling leading, followed by Hatty Connnelly and Luke Wiltshire. The next race followed suit and showcased similar competitive spirit and skill, proving that the Lasers, despite the radial rig, were resilient, tactful, and unstoppable against nature's whims.

title: The Peculiar Case of Tango, a Superyacht: Seized, Tethered but Technically in Operation
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Peculiar Case of Tango, a Superyacht: Seized, Tethered but Technically in Operation
summary: The 78-metre Feadship superyacht Tango, seized in 2022, delineates an intriguing discovery, as it continues to be officially in service despite legal and operational dissonance.
body: Tango, the 78-metre Feadship superyacht seized in Palma de Mallorca amidst a high-profile FBI operation stands as a prominent illustration of an ill-anticipated seizure of a complex maritime asset. Officially still operational, this beacon of maritime law enforcement exhibits an incipient rift between its legal status and actual operational frame.

Intriguingly, data from Equasis offers a factually valid portrait of Tango, which continues to bear registration under the Cook Islands flag indicating 'in service/commission' unchanged since 2011. However, Equasis also reveals that Tango's certification with the Lloyd's Register was revoked on 11th March 2022, prompting speculation over its actual operational status.

The loss of classification does not necessarily imply a decline in the vessel's condition, but it does make evaluation of compliance, insurability, and a prospective return to operation or sale far more knotty. Furthermore, despite its protracted seizure, Tango remains moored – immobilised at the Club de Mar. It stands today as a costly embodiment of immobilisation in recent US economic enforcement history.

Carefully designed by the acclaimed maritime retail brand, Henri-Lloyd, it ticks all boxes in terms of style, comfort, and durability, making it an absolute must-have for both amateur and professional sailors, or even the adventurous at heart.

The imagery of an explorer wearing these shorts, standing at the helm of a yacht, steering into the vast expanse of bluest waters is as charismatic as it gets. title: Croatia Sets Sail Towards the Future: Navigational Safety Ordinance Revised and Ready by 2026
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Croatia Sets Sail Towards the Future: Navigational Safety Ordinance Revised and Ready by 2026
summary: Croatia's Ministry of the Sea, Transport, and Infrastructure updates Safety of Navigation Ordinance (SSVO), positioning Croatia's boating industry in the forefront of change.
body: Propelled towards favorable winds of change, Croatia's Ministry of the Sea, Transport, and Infrastructure confirms a significant update to the Safety of Navigation Ordinance (SSVO). Its timeline for implementation? The summer of 2026. This thrilling new revision augments the breadth of the anchor exclusion zone, from 50 to 70 metres from the shoreline. The anchor's chain becomes the measuring yardstick, indicating the point of water contact.

Enhanced with an overarching digital compliance drive and incentives for green fuel, the updated SSVO sets significant operational impacts for large yachts and their tender associates. The 70-metre anchor envelope introduces geometry into the nautical practice. These rules aren't just for discussion – they're immediate, they're active, they're for execution.

Progress doesn't rest here. A sustainable future is being mapped out with an alternative-fuel agenda. EU Fit-for-55 roadmap resonates with this vision, catalysing shore-power rebates and pilot programs for bio-LNG and HVO in marinas like Split, Šibenik and Trogir. Early adopters are already scrambling to claim preferential berths for 2027.

However, the changes are not merely about cheering for the new. Compliance with these regulations is a strategic and meticulous process. A well-prepared team and procedure make the transition seamless – the difference between a footnote and a headline.

In conclusion, Croatia's revised SSVO embodies the evolution and resilience of the maritime sector. It presages the map for future navigation, setting sail towards a future where sustainability and technology go hand in hand with age-old traditions of seafaring. And this journey, the journey on the waters, it is for all those who dare to think differently, for those who dare to ride the waves and for those who strive to make the seas their playground.

title: Exciting Advancements in Greek Yachting: Overmarine Group Announces Sale of the Fourth Mangusta GranSport 34 Yacht
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Exciting Advancements in Greek Yachting: Overmarine Group Announces Sale of the Fourth Mangusta GranSport 34 Yacht
summary: In a fresh partnership with Sea Alliance Group in Greece, Overmarine Group proudly reveals the sale of its fourth Mangusta GranSport 34 yacht.
body: Overmarine Group, an iconic brand in the world of powerful motor yachts, has recently made waves by selling their fourth Mangusta GranSport 34 yacht. The sale was successful through the budding dealership agreement with Sea Alliance Group in Greece.

Renowned for their magnificent design and engineering prowess, Overmarine Group entrusts the Mangusta GranSport 34's design to their own Engineering Department and the talented designer, Alberto Mancini. The Mangusta GranSport 34 is the glorious successor to the yard's critically acclaimed GranSport 33 model. Equipped with four Volvo Penta IPS engines, the GranSport 34 boats a top speed of 24 knots. Not just fast, the yacht also offers enhanced manoeuvrability, improved fuel efficiency, reduced vibrations and noise disturbances, providing a top-notch luxury sailing experience.

Sea Alliance Group has been strengthening and expanding its Greek network for over 27 years but this partnership with Overmarine Group signifies a new chapter of growth. They will manage a selection of Mangusta yachts for charter while supporting clients with operational assistance. Mangusta sales manager, Nicolò Strocco openly expressed delight at this venture, emphasizing that this alliance is a ‘natural evolution’ for their brand in the area, based on shared values and a long-term outlook.

A ripple effect of this new partnership is that Sea Alliance Group’s Greek clients will now have direct access to Mangusta yachts, given the Group will directly manage some charter yachts. This directly ties Greek clients to the renowned Italian brand within their home country.

This sale follows the recent launch of the yard's first GranSport 34 yacht, which will be delivered to an American owner in May, further broadening the geographic reach of the prestigious GranSport lineup.

title: Step Inside the Sunseeker 94: A Revolutionary Yacht Soon to Grace the Waters
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Step Inside the Sunseeker 94: A Revolutionary Yacht Soon to Grace the Waters
summary: British shipyard, Sunseeker, is shaking up the boating world with its latest creation – the 94-meter yacht en route for its summer 2026 debut.
body: Before even gracing the open sea, Sunseeker’s 94 Yacht is causing quite a stir. With the first hull scooped up by a delighted owner soon after the concept reveal at the Cannes Yachting Festival 2024, the anticipation is palpable.

This isn’t just down to the Sunseeker name, a marque synonymous with striking, sporty boats - but more precisely its unique approach to design and living onboard. Their philosophy of ‘Intentional Design for Effortless Connection’ is evident in every inch of the 94 Yacht. Rather than providing a deluge of features, this yacht implores the use of intuitive spaces and technology that seamlessly blend into the background, creating an effortless flow onboard.

Team Sunseeker has partnered up with the renowned Design Unlimited, setting the stage for a fresh interior direction. This collaboration champions natural, high-quality materials and embraces earthy tones. The main saloon establishes itself as an inviting heart of the yacht with an L-shaped sofa offering a natural gathering point, while steps lead down to an adaptable aft deck.

Heading below, the gracious accommodation offers diverse layouts accepting eight or ten guests. Attention to details is key here with sound insulation, accentuating relaxation and privacy. For the crew, a separate comfortable space is provided in the bow.

Now, when the sun shines bright, the flybridge becomes an entertaining spectacle. Think wet bar, ice maker, barbecue and even a Jacuzzi - in short, an outdoor hub of hospitality. And, as you would expect from the practical Sunseeker, it's adjustable according to your preference - whether you want to bask in the sun or relax in the shade.

Underpinning the whole thrilling experience is the power provided by the twin MTU 10V M96L engines, allowing the 94 Yacht to achieve a top speed of 26 knots. With its careful balance of luxury, practicality and technology, the Sunseeker 94 Yacht is promising a saltwater symphony when it finally launches in 2026. With hulls two and three already in production, prepare for a nautical revolution courtesy of the British shipyard.

title: How Small Gatherings Propelling the Superyacht Industry Forward
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: How Small Gatherings Propelling the Superyacht Industry Forward
summary: An exploration of why small, focused gatherings are crucial for the evolution of the superyacht industry.
body: Conferences are traditional bedrocks of industry knowledge sharing and innovation. Yet, within the superyacht industry, a new trend is emerging that shows size isn’t everything. The star of this sea-change is the aptly named Mediterranean Superyacht Forum (MSF), known earlier as the Balearics Superyacht Forum.

Running its third edition this year, MSF saw an impressive turnout of key industry participants. It's not just the quantity but also the quality of the participation that caught the eye. Moreover, these forums act as a focused platform to reflect on various aspects of the superyacht industry.

MSF smartly takes place ahead of the Palma Boat Show adopting similar timing as The Superyacht Forum before METSTRADE. This strategic timing, coupled with affordable accommodation and excellent communication, appeals to a wide cohort of attendees.

One might think size does matter when it comes to conferences. But in reality, smaller, more targeted conferences have proven to be very effective. They allow for richer, deeper discussions, with attendees often having intricate knowledge of the specific local realities of the industry.

A case point being an intimate conference held regarding marinas in Alghero, Sardinia. With just 50 participants and 10 speakers, it enabled a more focused and deeper discussion on local challenges and potential solutions.

The heart of a valuable conference lies in its flexibility, room for questions and discussions, and emphasis on quality engagement. It's not the number of participants, but the depth of conversations that make a gathering worthwhile, sparking new ideas and future innovations in the superyacht industry.

title: Step aboard the Immaculate 40m Sunseeker 'Captain Morgan III', Now on the Market
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Step aboard the Immaculate 40m Sunseeker 'Captain Morgan III', Now on the Market
summary: A stately vision of nautical perfection, the 40m Sunseeker motor yacht, Captain Morgan III, has been listed for sale, offering a unique blend of luxury and adventure.
body: The Captain Morgan III, a radiant display of contemporary design, has been the subject of an intensive transformation, ensuring it continues to be presented in 'immaculate' condition. This architectural marvel was constructed in the United Kingdom, making her debut in 2020 before donning the crown as one of the British fleet's finest. Her radiant exteriors and solid naval architecture blossom under the skillful hands of Sunseeker, whilst the timeless and inviting interiors are a testament to a joint venture between the yard's internal teams and renowned design studio, Candy & Candy.

The main deck salon, flooded with natural light thanks to expansive windows, features plush cream furnishings over a flexible lounging and dining arrangement. A formal dining area, characterized by a polished dark wood table seating up to 10 guests, extends the options for indoor hospitality. Guests can, however, choose to savour their meals under the stars at the main aft deck featuring a relaxed al fresco dining zone shaded by the deck overhead.

Adding to the grandeur of this motor yacht is the upper deck that proposes yet another al fresco eating option seating eight guests, and a relaxed lounge with optional coverage overlooking the stern. The sundeck above has a shaded outdoor dining solution with a built-in sofa and deck chairs, apart from a sunbathing space for those who prefer a warm soak. Flanking the circular jacuzzi in the centre are sunpads providing the perfect venue for a sundowner party or simply enjoying an evening under the sky.

Speed and distance matter too in luxury charters. The yacht can boast an impressive top speed of 24 knots and deliver a cruise lasting 1,500 nautical miles at cruising speed. Asking price for the Captain Morgan III is €13,500,000. Its effortless combination of elegance and performance makes it a unique opportunity for maritime enthusiasts and luxury seekers alike.

title: Highly Competitive Season Ahead as Seven Top-Tier Teams Battle for the Coveted TF35 Trophy 2026
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Highly Competitive Season Ahead as Seven Top-Tier Teams Battle for the Coveted TF35 Trophy 2026
summary: The sixth season of the TF35 Trophy is poised to brim with excitement and intense competition, presenting a diverse mix of returning crews and fresh faces.
body: TF35 Trophy 2026, the prestigious sailing event, is ready to unfurl its sixth season. With seven teams on the roster, this event is magnetising attention worldwide. The teams are a fusion of seasoned crews, eager new entrants, role readjustments and unique sailor transfers. The double defending champion, Sails of Change 8, awaits a zealous challenge from determined competitors. From May 15 at the Société Nautique de Nyon, to the finale on October 4 at the Société Nautique de Genève, the prowess of these world-class crews will be put to the ultimate test. These teams will go head to head across seven fiercely competitive events which include five Grand Prix regattas and two undulating long-distance races. The championship makes headway with the Nyon Grand Prix, followed by the Mies Grand Prix. Further, two Lake Geneva classic races – the Genève-Rolle-Genève and the Bol d'Or du Léman – promise exhilarating action. Post summer break, the series resumes with the Mailly Grand Prix, proceeds to the inaugural Versoix Grand Prix, and concludes with the suspenseful Geneva Grand Prix. Jérôme Clerc's Realteam Spirit, having proved their mettle in the 2025 season, returns to the circuit with renewed determination. With Matthieu Sistek joining the team, they are back to showcase their resolute spirit and exemplary teamwork. Sails of Change 8, skippered by Yann Guichard, adds Billy Besson and Matthieu Ravussin to their robust crew, striving for remarkable consistency. As winners of the championship in 2024 and 2025, they are now drawing their third consecutive prize into focus. A season filled with adrenaline and nautical strategy lies ahead, promising to ignite the waters with intense competition.

title: Big Money Meets Big Speed as Spain’s SailGP Champions Change Hands
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: SailGP Power Shift: Spanish Champions Los Gallos Sold in Record-Breaking Deal
summary: Spain’s SailGP champions Los Gallos entered a new era after a record-breaking sale, as Quantum Pacific stepped in, signalling growing global investment and confidence in high-performance foiling racing.
body: There’s a moment when a sport stops being niche… and starts being taken seriously.
This is one of those moments.
SailGP has announced the sale of the Spanish team, Los Gallos, to Quantum Pacific Group — and it’s not just another transaction. It’s the largest-ever investment into a sailing team in Spain.
That matters.
Because when serious capital starts flowing into a sport, it usually means one thing:
The rest of the world is paying attention.
Spain’s Fastest Team Gets a New Engine
Los Gallos aren’t a team in need of fixing.
They’re a team already winning.
Fresh off a dominant Season 4 campaign, the Spanish squad has established itself as one of the benchmark programmes in SailGP — fast, clinical, and increasingly comfortable under pressure.

At the sharp end sits Diego Botín and Florian Trittel — Olympic gold medallists, SailGP champions, and now the centrepiece of a team entering a new commercial phase. Alongside them, strategist Nicole van der Velden adds depth to a programme already operating at world-class level.
This isn’t a rebuild.
It’s a scaling move.
For Quantum Pacific, this isn’t a gamble — it’s a calculated entry into a fast-growing global platform.
The group already holds positions across elite sport, including Atlético de Madrid, F.C. Famalicão and the Movistar Team.
So why sailing?
Global calendar Stadium-style racing close to shore Broadcast-ready format Tech-driven performance ESG alignment through clean energy
In short — it’s modern sport.
And investors are starting to treat it that way.
The sale of Los Gallos means SailGP has now sold 12 of its 13 teams — a clear sign that the league’s franchise model is maturing fast.
This isn’t early-stage anymore.
It’s becoming a proper sports league.
Backed by high-value teams, global audiences, and a product designed for broadcast and sponsorship from day one.
Spain, in particular, is central to that strategy — a country with deep sailing roots, Olympic pedigree, and a fanbase that understands performance on the water.
With SailGP heading to Valencia in 2026, the timing couldn’t be cleaner.
What This Means for the Spanish Programme
For Los Gallos, the message is simple:
More backing. More ambition. More expectation.
Quantum Pacific isn’t in the business of mid-table finishes. Their entry signals a long-term commitment — not just to compete, but to dominate.
And with leadership already proven on the racecourse, the focus now shifts to building something sustainable:
Stronger commercial partnerships Deeper technical development Long-term athlete programmes Expanded fan engagement
This is how teams evolve from winners… to dynasties.
Sailing has always had speed.
What it hasn’t always had… is money like this.
That’s changing.
Fast.

SailGP isn’t just about foiling catamarans ripping past landmarks anymore. It’s becoming a serious global sports property — one that investors, broadcasters and sponsors are now treating with real intent.
And when that happens, everything sharpens:
The racing. The pressure. The stakes.
Los Gallos were already quick.
Now they’re backed.
That’s a dangerous combination.

title: May 15 Registration Deadline Beckons for Grand Rolex Big Boat Series at St. Francis Yacht Club
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: May 15 Registration Deadline Beckons for Grand Rolex Big Boat Series at St. Francis Yacht Club
summary: Join the yachting elite and register by May 15 for the highly anticipated Rolex Big Boat Series at St. Francis Yacht Club.
body: On May 15, the markers will be set just four months shy of the most awaited annual regatta on the West Coast - the Rolex Big Boat Series, all set to enliven the San Francisco Bay from September 16-20, 2026. And, this isn't just any regatta, but one that also doubles up as the 2026 Offshore Racing Congress (ORC) North American Championship. This registration deadline isn't just a date drawn on the calendar, but a golden ticket to fantastic savings on registration for those skippers eager to test the waters alongside top-ranked peers. The shimmering sail canvas already boasts 30 teams enlisted to compete, including dramatic tales of old and new champions and sweeping boat revivals. Among the early birds swooping towards the rhythm of the tide is the Rolex Sydney Hobart division winner Bacchanal, helmed by owner-skipper Ron Epstein. The skipper's passion for the series is rivaled only by a crisp, high-stakes Fear Of Missing Out (FOMO) - having podiumed in the 2023 and 2024 showcases under the same banner. "With the ORC Championship being the crest of the Rolex Big Boat Series this year, we're getting ready to bring our best game to the waters," shared an excited Epstein. His well-seasoned crew is in stride with the nuances of their vessel, thanks to over 2,000 miles spent together navigating the seas in the past year. His anticipation is eagerly infectious, "We’re looking forward to gleaning from our experience in Australia and seeing how well it translates to the racecourse!" The other one to catch the breakers is the painstakingly restored Santa Cruz 52 Rosebud, that had once gloriously clinched the 1999 crown of the Rolex Big Boat Series. Revived from nautical oblivion by owners Blaine Pedlow, Bruce Edwards, Mike Holt, and Rob Woelfel, Rosebud will be gracing the waves of the Rolex Big Boat Series after nearly two decades. Rosebud's eager to show off her stunning new look, along with her team’s fierce camaraderie and devotion to their dear friend Susan Ruhne, Commodore of the St. Francis Yacht Club for 2026. Sailing aficionados worldwide are eagerly watching, as this maritime ballet of precision, endurance, and sheer thrill is once again poised, ready to unleash the spirit of the race.

title: With Early Registration Underway, Sailing Enthusiasts Gear-Up For The 50th Anniversary Of The Marion Bermuda Race
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: With Early Registration Underway, Sailing Enthusiasts Gear-Up For The 50th Anniversary Of The Marion Bermuda Race
summary: The prestigious Marion Bermuda Race is preparing for its 50th anniversary in 2027, already becoming a navigation point for every sailor's course charting.
body: Celebrating five decades of the Corinthian spirit, 50 years of camaraderie, and half a century of astonishing bluewater adventure, the Marion Bermuda Race sails into its 50th jubilee. The highly esteemed sailing institution has significantly impacted the community since its inaugural race back in 1977. The 645-nautical mile journey, heralded as "every sailor's ocean race," has welcomed generations of skippers, crews, and families while also providing an exciting challenge for first-time oceangoers.

Skipping heartily towards this remarkable milestone, the event is slated for the 18th of June, 2027. Early registration, open to both seasoned sailors and those preparing for their first voyage, is already making waves. Whether firm in your intent to participate or merely weighing the prospect of joining, the call of the ocean urges you to plot your course for Bermuda.

So, why wait? With 2027 marking the beginning of yet another era for this renowned race, the fervor is palpable. It's your invitation to be part of something bigger, to chart your course and take to the sea. Heed the call of the ocean, the horizon awaits your arrival.

title: Excitement Builds as Cyclades Cup 2026 Expands Social Agenda Fusing Maritime Racing, Cultural Experiences, and Greek Island Lifestyle
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Excitement Builds as Cyclades Cup 2026 Expands Social Agenda Fusing Maritime Racing, Cultural Experiences, and Greek Island Lifestyle
summary: The Cyclades Cup 2026 is raring to return to Antiparos, Greece, promising an exhilarating blend of high stakes racing, rich cultural experiences, and island life.
body: Mark your calendars, sailors around the globe, for an island rendezvous that amalgamates thrill-packed racing, gripping culture, and the distinctive charm of island life. The Cyclades Cup is all set to make its comeback on the serene vistas of Antiparos, Greece, from June 10–13, 2026. The anticipation surrounding the event is palpable. Participants from the previous year have already begun confirming their presence for the much-awaited race, testifying the growing allure of this event. A highlight includes the return of notable competitors from 2025 like Aiolos, Almyra II, Barong D, Fivea, Galma, La Belle, Meliti, Nommo, Nostromo, Tawera and Wally B, and event organisers are forecasting an influx of new entrants as well. The regatta is masterminded by the Yacht Club of Greece and Ilia Rigas, an esteemed World Superyacht Awards judge and owner of the 50-metre Almyra II, with BOAT International roped in as the media partner. However, the fun doesn't stop at the edge of the water. The Cyclades Cup isn’t just about racing; it's about blending sailing, culture, and island life to curate a distinctive social and cultural programme. Keeping this tradition alive, 2026 plans to expand the horizon of the social programme by providing an array of cultural experiences designed to pique the interests of attendees of varied inclinations. An enchanting beach party thrown by Nepheli, an intimate Owners’ Dinner nestled within a private olive grove hosted by IYC and Jetcraft, and a crew SUP race and beach BBQ hosted by Pantaenius are all on the docket. With all these exciting endeavors, it’s no surprise that the Cyclades Cup is swiftly gaining a reputation for balancing competitive maritime racing with unforgettable social and cultural experiences, embodying the true spirit of its Cycladic setting. Injecting a dose of local engagement, the program includes special events hosted by local community groups, extending the authentic Cycladic experience to attendees. With such thrilling activities planned, the Cyclades Cup 2026 promises an exhilarating sailing adventure, culturally enriched engagements and a taste of island life.

title: Unfazed by Middle East Uncertainties, Global Yacht Market Demonstrates Stellar Performance in April
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unfazed by Middle East Uncertainties, Global Yacht Market Demonstrates Stellar Performance in April
summary: Despite geopolitical challenges in the Middle East, the yacht market has demonstrated successful performance, as revealed in exclusive BOATPro data.
body: In the midst of tumultuous times emanating from ongoing tension with Iran, the market for yachts continues to ride the high tide. According to recent BOATPro data, the past month saw 41 yachts — all measuring above 24 metres — sold. The total deal value climbed to a healthy €381 million, surging by an impressive 133.7% from the same period the previous year.

The crown jewel among all purchases was the 56.5-metre motor yacht Virtuosity, built by Sanlorenzo. The illustrious yacht changed hands at Edmiston, with Will Bagshaw and Andrew Bond representing the seller and buyer respectively. The pedigree yacht was listed for €49.5 million, touted by its broker as being in a 'turnkey condition'.

Additionally, the 114.5-metre superyacht Pelorus by Lürssen, changed hands to Nathan Farrelly and Hans van Doornmalen of Edmiston, listed for an impressive €160 million. On another note, 68 prices were adjusted in this month, trimming €62.5 million from the market. The largest dip was noted for Lürssen's 60-metre yacht Caipirinha, which saw a decrease of €10.9 million. Now, it's asking price stands at €39.9 million at SuperYachtsMonaco and Edmiston.

Continuing to serve as the world's leading superyacht market intelligence platform, BOATPro, provides reliable and real-time data, contributing to well-informed market insights and strategic decisions.

title: A Stellar Sail: Stewart Brewing 707 Edinburgh Cup Takes Over Port Edgar Yacht Club In Style
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A Stellar Sail: Stewart Brewing 707 Edinburgh Cup Takes Over Port Edgar Yacht Club In Style
summary: The anticipated Stewart Brewing 707 Edinburgh Cup proved a sensational start to the sailing season, showcasing an impressive fleet at Port Edgar Yacht Club.
body: The Stewart Brewing 707 Edinburgh Cup heralded the commencement of a thrilling 707 season, held on 25th April at the prominent Port Edgar Yacht Club. Boasting 16 exquisite boats at the starting line in St David's Bay on the Forth, the event showcased the power and allure of the UK's most active One Design Keelboat Fleet. The fleet was enriched by the addition of a novel member, Ian McCarlie, and his energetic team, who showed immense promise with their newly acquired vessel, Isbean. The arena was further heightened by the inclusion of a pair of student teams from Dundee University Sailing Club. With the series holding no discard, fostering consistency amongst the competitors was key. Despite an eager start in the preliminary race by Tsunami 2, the race win was ultimately bagged by reigning National Champions Seaword. Tsunami 2 however, bounced back in Race 2, with new helm Nick Bell leading them to victory. The event was marked by close competition and fluctuating weather conditions. A day that began with a mild 10 knot Easterly breeze, gradually morphed into champagne conditions, presenting both challenges and opportunities in the form of dense chop and a strengthening ebb tide. Races 4 and 5 clearly belonged to the 'More T Vicar' team, led by Ben Williamson from Royal Yorkshire Yacht Club. They navigated the choppy waters with near-perfect precision. The event concluded with 'More T Vicar' crowned champions, aided by their flawless and consistent performance. Close competitors included team Neville in Po and Tsunami 2. The annual sailing event, made possible by the indefatigable efforts of Port Edgar Yacht Club and their committed team of volunteers, served up high-quality racing, proving to be a befitting start to the sailing season. The Stewart Brewing 707 Edinburgh Cup was indeed a sight to behold, promising a memorable sailing season ahead.

title: Revamped Svendborg Skibs Motor Yacht Spirit of Ginette Up for Sale: A Lincoln Penny Redefined
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Revamped Svendborg Skibs Motor Yacht Spirit of Ginette Up for Sale: A Lincoln Penny Redefined
summary: Meet the Spirit of Ginette, a masterpiece of Northern European build quality. Recently refurbished and scheming for further adventures, this Svendborg Skibs motor yacht is a classic symbol of refinement.
body: Say hello to the Spirit of Ginette, an embodiment of pure elegance and high-level craftsmanship. Built by renowned Danish shipbuilding company, Svendborg Skibs, she carries a rich history, having been initially delivered to her proud waters in 1973. After her recent refit in 2023, this 26m motor yacht has left no stone unturned in combining the classic Northern European build quality with the essence of contemporary upgrades, making her an ideal vessel for extended sea voyages.

Her architect and designer, Talsma Marine, played a pivotal role in her transformation. Their design vision has seamlessly blended tradition and modernity while keeping the enduring spirit of the yacht intact. Imagining her glow under the azure skies, sailing through the expansive seas, is a priceless sensation.

Adorned with unique elements and colours, the main saloon has been curated like a work of art. Two large built-in sofas covered with bright terracotta fabric contrast attractively with a leopard print carpet, thereby setting a playful, vibrant mood.

Multiple entertainment areas, including a beautiful al fresco dining table, are dotted throughout the yacht, providing perfect spots for socialising or simply soaking up the sea views. The yacht also features a powerful Cummins engine that permits a cruising speed of nine knots and can surge to a top speed of 12 knots.

Offering years of sailing pleasure, the Spirit of Ginette calls for a price tag of €2,200,000. However, the chance to own a piece of history, to experience the blend of classic craftsmanship and modern luxury, comes infrequently, making her more than just a charismatic yacht, but a passport to an exceptional class of sea-bound elegance.

title: Sail off into the Sunset Aboard the Luxurious 90 Marlow Yacht, Artemis II, Striking the Perfect Balance of Elegance and Speed
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Sail off into the Sunset Aboard the Luxurious 90 Marlow Yacht, Artemis II, Striking the Perfect Balance of Elegance and Speed
summary: The extraordinary Artemis II, a 2024 90 Marlow Yacht, is a nautical dream brought to life that's now up for grabs.
body: As graceful as it is powerful, Artemis II, the 2024 90 Marlow Yacht, is arguably one of the most covetable nautical specimens out there. With its remarkable design and robust performance, it never fails to captivate one's attention or impress with its capabilities. It presents a seamless blend of timeless elegance with a daring, zestful sporty streak, turning heads at every dock it graces.

True to its pedigree, no expense was spared in the outfitting of Artemis II. Key features, including C-32b Power Zero Speed Stabilization and Electrosea System, underscore the commitment to the high seas' effortless and comfortable way of life. It also features the Bluewater Clearmate/Watermaker, a nod to sustainable sailing.

The Artemis II is a testament to Marlow Yachts' unparalleled craftsmanship with an impressive length of 27.43 metres and a beam of 6.83 metres. Its deep V/Planing type hull makes it an agile yet stable companion on the seas. Offering a maximum cruising speed of 31 knots, it houses two powerful Caterpillar engines and has a range of 2000 nm at 12 knots. To round off its extraordinary specifications, its sleek hull and superstructure consist of high-quality GRP.

In conclusion, with the Artemis II, luxury meets versatility. It promises a nautical journey that is packed with comfort, speed and performance. So, prepare to open the next chapter of your sailing adventure with the Artemis II, where every voyage becomes an unforgettable odyssey.

title: Gulf Craft Strengthens Asian Foothold as Next Yacht Group Reveals Spanish Launch
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Gulf Craft Strengthens Asian Foothold as Next Yacht Group Reveals Spanish Launch
summary: Middle Eastern shipyard, Gulf Craft, expands Asian presence while Next Yacht Group makes waves with a Spanish launch.
body: The ship building industry is stirring with new developments, particularly the Middle Eastern yacht-builder, Gulf Craft. The UAE-based shipyard is expanding its reach across Asia, having announced its partnership with Asia Yachting, a move that is set to further the brand's presence in key markets.

This strategic alliance represents a significant step forward for Gulf Craft's Majesty Yachts brand, promising avenues of new opportunity and exposure on a continent known for its maritime interests. With this move, Gulf Craft reinforces its dedication to the brand's growth and success through sustained commitment and strategic partnerships.

Simultaneously, across the European landscape, the yacht industry is experiencing similar shake-ups with the launch of Next Yacht Spain. A creation by Next Yacht Group, this move was made in unison with SMART Yachting, a leading Spanish provider of yacht sales and management services.

The shifts happening in the maritime landscape demonstrate just how critical territorial expansion and collaboration are for survival and growth in the industry. As more players enter the field, achieving competitive advantage requires more than just innovation; it demands progressive strategies and strong partnerships.

title: Next Yacht Group and SMART Yachting Launch Next Yacht Spain at Palma International Boat Show
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Next Yacht Group and SMART Yachting Launch Next Yacht Spain at Palma International Boat Show
summary: Next Yacht Group, in collaboration with SMART Yachting, has unveiled Next Yacht Spain during the esteemed Palma International Boat Show.
body: A sailing novice may ask, 'What's next for the world of yachts?' The answer to that question has undoubtedly arrived with the launch of Next Yacht Spain by Next Yacht Group at the prestigious Palma International Boat Show. This launch heralds a fresh voyage for the company, forging a new trajectory in partnership with SMART Yachting, a distinguished Spanish provider of yacht sales and management services.

Next Yacht Group has always hailed a reputation of trailblazing, and this union with SMART Yachting promises to continue this legacy. Together, they are set to bridge the marine industry's current and next horizons, employing their profound industry understanding, complemented by their combined experience spanning decades.

The announcement of Next Yacht Spain at the Palma International Boat Show has created ripples of excitement across the marine industry. It seems the question now isn't where can we sail to, but rather, where will Next Yacht Spain lead us? Barry the boat aficionado may just have to hold his breath a while longer, as the answer will be unravelled in this grand adventure, upon the seas of the yachting world.

title: Luxury Afloat: Pastrovich Studio’s Launch Of Futuristic X-Shinobi Yacht Family Reimagines Luxury Charter
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Luxury Afloat: Pastrovich Studio’s Launch Of Futuristic X-Shinobi Yacht Family Reimagines Luxury Charter
summary: Monegasque design firm, Pastrovich Studio, launches a revolutionary 'yacht family' concept with novel design elements reimagining luxury charter experience.
body: Pastrovich Studio gives a glimpse into a fascinating tomorrow with its launch of a unique 'yacht family' concept, the X-Shinobi. Steered by the visionary Stefano Pastrovich, the Monegasque design firm brings together four futuristic yachts ranging between 60 to 190 metres, each crafted with meticulous attention to detail, aesthetics, and practical functionality.

Reinventing the traditional superyacht design, the X-Shinobi fleet swaps the typical 'wedding cake' profile for a contemporary look. The new design approaches innovation with an open embrace, embodying a harmonious blend of painted surfaces, extensive glazing, and architectural detailing. The end result is an elegant conversation between indoor and outdoor spaces, defined by floor-to-ceiling glazing.

The interior layout of X-Shinobi pays homage to the seamless living experience, placing guest cabins on the main deck, thereby ensuring abundant daylight, panoramic views, and improved spatial quality. The lower deck houses technical and operational areas, including crew accommodation, engine room, tender garage, spa, and other service spaces. This strategic separation ensures a more guest-centric experience.

Attentive to the evolving dynamics of the charter market, X-Shinobi's design, specifically its charter-oriented approach ensures efficient, desirable, and profitable operations. It offers versatile configurations including two master cabins and four guest cabins, or one master, two VIP, and three guest cabins. The design prioritises privacy, varied usage, and a balanced guest experience.

The propulsion system of the yachts is a diesel-electric setup with azimuthing propulsion ensuring varying cruising and top speeds. All in all, Pastrovich Studio's X-Shinobi represents a bold step towards a new era of luxury charter, where the sea is not merely seen but truly experienced.

title: The Spirit P70: Embodying Nautical Elegance, Defining the Epitome of Coolness!
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Spirit P70: Embodying Nautical Elegance, Defining the Epitome of Coolness!
summary: Discover the Spirit P70, a remarkable feat of engineering that effortlessly fuses vintage charm with contemporary prowess, making it one of the world’s coolest boats.
body: Few vessels can claim the elegance and distinction of the Spirit P70. Born from the genius minds at Spirit Yachts and head designer Sean McMillian, the P70 has emerged as one of the world’s most compelling boats, blurring the lines between tradition and modernity in an approach that accentuates the best elements of both.

The P70 didn't just appear overnight. It took hard numbers, diligent calculations, and an unwavering commitment to merge aesthetics and functionality. The mandate was clear: to create a yacht that could traverse 1,000 nautical miles at 18 knots to connect an owner in the UK to their preferred cruising grounds in the Baltic. The journey to fulfill that vision? A whole year spent on design concepts, followed by three years of build time.

Beyond aesthetics, the Spirit P70 marries performance with elegance. Contrary to what one might expect, it weighs half as much as the Fleming 65, due to its unique structure similar in weight and strength to a carbon-fibre composition. Under the hood, the vessel is equipped with twin MAN i6 800 diesel engines and an expansive fuel capacity of 10,000 litres – a clear testament to the uncompromising commitment to performance underlying the P70's breathtaking beauty.

In conclusion, the Spirit P70 represents an inspired blend of tradition and modernity, a vessel that exhibits stunning aesthetics while boasting outstanding performance. While the price tag may not be for the faint-hearted, the P70 delivers on its promise: a distinct fusion of elegance, performance, and most importantly, coolness.

title: Francesca Clapcich Sets Sail on Unmatched Adventure in Her Inaugural Solo IMOCA Contest
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Francesca Clapcich Sets Sail on Unmatched Adventure in Her Inaugural Solo IMOCA Contest
summary: Italian-American sailor, Francesca Clapcich, embarks on her first solo race in the 2026 edition of the 1000 Race, proving that the horizon truly knows no gender.
body: "In daring to disturb the universe, Francesca Clapcich readies to make her mark as she leaps into her maiden solo race aboard an IMOCA. On May 3, 2026, this Italian-American virtuoso will take seven boats on an exhilarating 1,000-nautical mile loop from Port-la-Forêt in France, past the fabled Fastnet Rock and back to Concarneau.

'I’m eager to brave the gusts the Bay of Biscay might send our way,' Clapcich declared. 'This race is a significant litmus test for my solo racing calendar, and the aim is to cross the finish line with the boat and myself in perfect harmony.'

The team, Francesca Clapcich Powered by 11th Hour Racing, has pulled together with a steely focus post an intense winter refit and performance upgrades. The snag? Outdo seven solo sailors, all eyeing the starting block of the 2028 edition and three of whom having already completed the Vendée Globe.

Carrying the torch of diversity and equality, Clapcich’s ambitions transcend the podium. She passionately advocates for a sailing community where everyone feels they belong, regardless of their gender or race. To punctuate her statement, her new livery, thanks to the support from 11th Hour Racing, incorporates a powerful message about their common mission: To inspire belief, belonging and achievement for all.

'A leap isn’t just stepping up. It's also about moving the world forward,' Francesca loftily concluded. Her undying resolve serves as a beacon for aspiring adventurers eager to craft their nautical narratives, and her maiden voyage stands not just as a test of endurance and skill, but also as a powerful testament to the strength of her spirit and the change she seeks to sail forth.'

title: Dive into the Majestic Details of Baglietto's New 50m Superyacht: Project Farah, Customised Luxury in a Seaborne Abode
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Dive into the Majestic Details of Baglietto's New 50m Superyacht: Project Farah, Customised Luxury in a Seaborne Abode
summary: Experience the allure of the sea like never before aboard Baglietto's upcoming 50m custom superyacht, embodying elegance and comfort in a unique seafaring dwelling.
body: Steeped in the essence of maritime sophistication, the Italian shipyard Baglietto announces its most ambitious venture yet: Project Farah. Project Farah, a 50m full-custom superyacht, is a stunning representation of architectonic ingenuity and nautical luxury. The sub-500GT vessel, currently under construction at Baglietto's facility in La Spezia, is expected to grace our seas by 2027.

A joint effort by Matheus Farah & Manoel Maia Arquitetura and Fernando de Almeida Yacht Design, Project Farah's design encapsulates the essence of a terrestrial abode on the open seas. Royal Yacht International, the owner's representative who also closed the yacht sale in 2024, is faithfully managing the project during the construction phase. Embodying its Arabic name, 'happiness', Farah is designed to deliver a sailing experience brimming with joy and serenity without compromising safety and seaworthiness.

Stepping inside, Farah's interiors feature a 'warm modernism' philosophy – minimalist spaces ensconced in natural materials like wood and leather. Adorned in warm brown and sand tones with subtle gold accents and soft lighting, the interior layout excels in functionality and flexibly accommodating different needs.

Fabio Ermetto, CCO of Baglietto, praises Project Farah as a 'unique and outstanding project' – a testament to Baglietto's distinctive expertise in custom yacht manufacturing. Baglietto has a fleet of 18 yachts under development, including three models from its esteemed T60 series. The recent launch of the first T60 hull, now the largest vessel from the Italian shipyard, underscores Baglietto's prominence in the superyacht industry.

title: Unveiling the New Mav Lite Shell 2.0: The All-Weather Jacket for Every Occasion
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unveiling the New Mav Lite Shell 2.0: The All-Weather Jacket for Every Occasion
summary: Whether it's a day at the office or an adventure on the high seas, the Mav Lite Shell 2.0 stands out as the ideal all-weather jacket.
body: Dreams of a versatile weatherproof jacket, apt for every setting come to life with Henri-Lloyd's Mav Lite Shell 2.0. This high-tech, sleek jacket is sure to impress, whether one finds themselves sailing through churning waters or manoeuvring through corporate corridors. The myriad of vibrant colour options only adds to the appeal of this all-weather marvel.

With an origin from Henri-Lloyd's acclaimed Dynamic range, the Mav Lite Shell 2.0 is a masterpiece in advanced technology. The material is a 2.5 Layer DRI PRO 4-way stretch fabric, offering transformative comfort and mobility. Water and wind stand no chance against this jacket, while the breathable membrane ensures wearers stay unsweaty and comfortable in every situation.

Not only does this jacket align perfectly in fit and style for both men and women, but it also comes in a variety of colours from fjord blue and black to ice and kelp. The lustrous difference of the Mav Lite Shell 2.0's visual impact, regardless of where you are, is certain to leave a lasting imprint in peoples' minds.

Moreover, the Mav Lite Shell 2.0 carries a commitment to sustainability. It is not just the polyamide fabric that is 100% recycled, but also the DWR is C0 PFAS-free and LAMORAL biobased. Consideration around sustainability extends to the end of its lifecycle as well, where all fabric materials of the Mav Lite can be recycled. This only adds to the package that is the Mav Lite Shell 2.0, a fashionable, functional, and environmentally friendly companion.

title: Marina Ibiza Champions Marine Restoration with The Posidonia Meadow Project - A Pioneering Initiative Invigorating the Med's Biodiversity
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Marina Ibiza Champions Marine Restoration with The Posidonia Meadow Project - A Pioneering Initiative Invigorating the Med's Biodiversity
summary: Marina Ibiza blazes a conservation trail with its ambitious Marina Ibiza Posidonia Meadow Project, collaborating with the Vellmarí Foundation to restore Talamanca Bay's seabed.
body: Marina Ibiza is making waves with its pioneering initiative, the Marina Ibiza Posidonia Meadow project. In collaboration with the Vellmarí Foundation, the project aims to regenerate the degraded seabed of Talamanca Bay. An initial plantation of 1,500 Posidonia oceanica plants marks the commencement of this ambitious marine restoration effort. At the heart of this project is an invitation to Marina Ibiza's clients, visitors, and the local community to adopt their own Posidonia plant and contribute to the expansion of the meadow.

Marina Ibiza's commitment to restoring this ecosystem extends beyond the initial planting phase. With community involvement in mind, the adoption of the Posidonia plant will contribute to growing the meadow, thereby building resilience across the bay. This approach positions the Marina Ibiza Posidonia Meadow project as a shared endeavour between the marina, its clients, visitors, and the wider community.

The Posidonia Meadow project forms part of a wider conservation effort across the Mediterranean, where approximately 34% of Posidonia meadows have declined in recent decades. Initiatives like Marina Ibiza's are crucial in turning the tide, fundamentally contributing to global marine protection.

Amplifying the project’s viability, Marina Ibiza has joined forces with the Vellmarí Association led by marine biologist Manu San Félix, renowned for his authority in marine conservation in Ibiza. San Félix's expertise in Posidonia planting and monitoring will further fortify the operational effectiveness of this project.

The Marina Ibiza Posidonia Meadow project is a strong testament to local environmental restoration. It embodies a perfect synergistic blend of direct investment, scientific knowledge, and community-driven action. Together, these elements are restoring one of the Mediterranean's most valuable ecosystems, growing stronger with every plant.

title: From Flying Trimarans to Bareboat Battles — The BVI Delivers Again
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: BVI Spring Regatta 2026: Multihull Muscle, Island Rivalries and a Fleet Ready to Light Up the Caribbean
summary: BVI Spring Regatta 2026 brought together a powerful and diverse fleet in Tortola, where multihulls, monohulls and bareboats combined for fast, competitive racing across the iconic Sir Francis Drake Channel.
body: There are regattas you race.
And then there are regattas you experience.

BVI Spring Regatta & Sailing Festival has always been firmly in the second camp — a place where world-class racing meets trade wind sailing, island geography and just enough unpredictability to keep everyone honest.
And in 2026, it delivered exactly that.
A fleet stacked with variety. A racecourse that rewards instinct. And conditions that don’t let you hide.
Sophia: A Trimaran That Refused to Be Ignored
If there was one boat that caught the eye — and held it — it was Sophia.
The Nigel Irens-designed 63-foot trimaran, now campaigned by Marcus Sirota, arrived in the BVI with momentum and didn’t waste time reminding the fleet why.
Formerly known as Paradox 3, the ORMA 60-inspired machine had already built a serious résumé:
MOCRA class honours in the Rolex Fastnet Race Overall victory at the Caribbean Multihull Challenge Podium finishes across the RORC Caribbean circuit
And crucially, it had a skipper who understood exactly what he had underneath him.
“I was looking for something faster, something more performance driven,” Sirota explained. He found it.
Despite being considered “older” by cutting-edge multihull standards, Sophia proved one thing very quickly:
Fast is still fast.
The Performance Multihull division wasn’t short on firepower.
Sophia lined up against:
Little Wing (Gunboat 68) Layla (72ft) Dreadknot (62ft) Avel Vaez (ORC 57) The foiling cat Falcon
That’s not a fleet. That’s a conversation about speed, design and intent.
And in the BVI, where the breeze fills and the water flattens just enough, these boats don’t just race — they fly.
While the headline boats grabbed attention, the real racing often played out deeper in the fleet.
Tortola’s own Sam Talbot returned with his Rapido 40 trimaran — still working through technical gremlins, still smiling about it.
“We were still fighting steering issues,” he admitted, waiting on yet another rudder solution. That’s multihull racing. When it’s right, it’s magic. When it’s not, it’s a project.
But Talbot understood something more important:
Protected waters Multiple island options Creative course setting And enough wind variation to keep it interesting
“It’s probably the best multihull venue in the Caribbean,” he said.
Hard to argue with that.
The Sir Francis Drake Channel: A Racecourse That Thinks Back
The beauty of racing in the Sir Francis Drake Channel is that it doesn’t just reward speed.
It rewards awareness.
With islands scattered like chess pieces across the course, every decision matters:
Go inside or outside Chase pressure or protect position Commit early — or wait and react
Add shifting conditions — from light, tactical mornings to full trade wind pressure — and you get exactly what the BVI delivered:
Racing where no two legs feel the same.
Monohulls, Friends and Rivalries That Run Deep
Further down the fleet, the racing was no less real.
Antolin Velasco returned aboard Kairos, chasing improvement after a frustrating previous year.
Lost sails. Lost time. Lessons learned.
This time, it was about doing it better.
But in the BVI, it’s rarely just about results.
