Friends racing friends Crews splitting across boats Rivalries that are competitive — but never cold
“Part of our crew from last year were on another boat,” Velasco said. That’s the BVI in one sentence.
Bareboat Racing: Where It’s Still About the People
Then there’s the bareboat fleet.
No million-pound budgets. No optimisation programmes. Just crews, boats and a willingness to get stuck in.
Charlie Garrard’s Team Merlin summed it up perfectly:
Minimal prep New crew members Long days on the water Longer nights ashore
And still — tight racing.
“Podium is the goal,” he said. “But if it doesn’t happen, it doesn’t matter.”
Because here, it’s about something else:
Racing hard — and enjoying it properly.
Local Campaigns: Racing What You Have
Scott Meyers brought a different kind of campaign.
Living aboard Dark n Stormy at Nanny Cay, his approach was less polished, more real.
Last-minute prep Equipment still being fitted Discovering sails you didn’t know you had
“I’m kind of winging it,” he admitted.
And yet — he showed up.
That’s the point.
Why the BVI Still Delivers
What the 2026 BVI Spring Regatta proved — again — is simple:
You don’t need uniform fleets. You don’t need perfect boats. You don’t need controlled conditions.
You need:
Good water Good breeze And people who want to race
Everything else falls into place.
From high-performance trimarans to bareboat crews learning as they go, the BVI delivered a regatta that felt exactly as it should:
Unpredictable. And properly alive.
Because in the end, this isn’t just racing. It’s sailing — the way it was meant to be.

title: Clipper Round the World Yacht Race Departs From Seattle, Marking Milestones and Leaving Memories Behind
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Clipper Round the World Yacht Race Departs From Seattle, Marking Milestones and Leaving Memories Behind
summary: The Clipper Round the World Yacht Race, renowned for turning everyday people into ocean racers, bid adieu to Seattle as they embarked on the penultimate leg of their thrilling global race route.
body: The world-renowned Clipper Race, famous for transforming everyday individuals into remarkable ocean racers, set sail from Seattle, commencing the thrilling next stage of their round-the-world adventure. The ten-strong fleet of identical yachts, crewed by ordinary people hailing from diverse walks of life, bid goodbye to the Bell Harbor Marina, motoring through the scenic Puget Sound towards their next destination: Panama. The Clipper Race's departure from Seattle marked a significant milestone in its history. The most recent arrival, following a challenging route across the North Pacific Ocean from Tongyeong, South Korea, celebrated a decade of partnership, five distinctive Host Port stopovers, and four editions with a team proudly representing Seattle. These achievements have seen Seattle become one of the most frequented US cities in the race's history. The Clipper Race isn't just about traversing the globe on a competitive racecourse; it's an event that thrives on its ability to inspire and ignite the adventurous spirit in many. One such adventurer is Valarie Linton, an executive director who signed up to race the entire global route aboard the Team Power of Seattle Sports. She reflects on her Seattle stayover fondly, stating her anticipation for the forthcoming Panama Canal stretch. The upcoming leg of the race will see the Clipper Race teams challenging their strategic planning skills as they proceed south along the Pacific coast to Panama. They will encounter a range of conditions, including strong breezes, coastal influences in the north, and lighter winds coupled with rising heat as they approach the equator. Successful navigation calls for a skillful balance of speed and strategy, all while accommodating the ever-changing weather patterns. The global yacht race, created by Sir Robin Knox-Johnston, the first person to sail solo non-stop around the world, stands out for its inclusivity. Anyone, regardless of previous sailing experience, is encouraged to participate, making it a unique gateway into the world of ocean racing. As a true test of physical and mental endurance, the race, featuring ten teams led by a professional Race Skipper and First Mate, poses challenges from harsh sub-zero temperatures in the North Pacific Ocean to staggering equatorial heat.

title: Emerging Challenges in the Art of Leadership in the Superyacht Arena
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Emerging Challenges in the Art of Leadership in the Superyacht Arena
summary: A fascinating exploration of the invisible curriculum, showcasing how leadership is nurtured and developed on superyachts.
body: Talk to any captain about the factors that have shaped them into potent leaders and the likelihood is that they won't refer to a certain qualification. Rather, they will mention people – mentors, trainers, leaders who have inspired and guided them. This points to the powerful and mostly unseen aspect of leadership development: the invisible curriculum.

Seamanship and leadership have traditionally been transmitted through such interpersonal, informal, and often invisible means. Today, such a model seems as prevalent as ever, yet, paradoxically, it is also becoming increasingly challenging to execute perfectly.

The superyacht industry is what brings us here. This exploration explores leadership not merely in theory, but as it is truly implemented on the high seas, often under immense pressure. It delves into the tricky areas between authority and trust, looking at how our future leaders are nurtured and sustained.

However, the invisible curriculum is not without its shortcomings. Today’s superyacht captain, much a CEO of their floating empire, is surrounded by an environment that differs drastically from the traditional settings that originally defined roles.

While the established route to command, involving graduation via a certification ladder, does produce skilled mariners, it does not necessarily equip them for the modern nuances of command. The vessel itself has evolved significantly over the years, and so there is a pressing need to address these novel realities in leadership development.
Let us raise our sails to this exciting voyage, as we delve into the depths of the invisible yet intriguing curriculum of leadership in the world of superyachts.

title: Young Sailors Show Off their Skills in the Welsh Sailing Dragon Series at Gresford SC
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Young Sailors Show Off their Skills in the Welsh Sailing Dragon Series at Gresford SC
summary: The first North Wales event of the 2026 Dragon Series saw young sailors display superior skills amid fierce competition and fluctuating weather conditions.
body: Gresford Sailing Club had the privilege of hosting the first North Wales event of the 2026 Dragon Series. An exciting day of competition ensued, with sailors from across the region showcasing their skills in challenging conditions. The weather served up unforeseen shifts and pressure changes, resulting in thrilling races in a 6-12 knot South Easterly breeze.

An action-packed schedule, replete with six handicap races, generated scintillating competition across all levels. The silver fleet accommodated the experienced sailors, while a coach-supported training fleet nurtured the less seasoned. The races presented an exciting theatre of action, with many local Gresford SC Juniors partaking in their first racing experiences in the weeks leading up to the event.

Among the winners, visiting Optimist sailor Fletcher Sheehy led the Silver Fleet, with close competition in the chasing pack. In the ten-strong Training Fleet, Harry Mitchell edged victory by a single point.

title: Turkish Shipyard Numarine Introduces Classic Line of Explorer Yachts – A Fresh Twist on Timeless Elegance
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Turkish Shipyard Numarine Introduces Classic Line of Explorer Yachts – A Fresh Twist on Timeless Elegance
summary: Numarine, the renowned Turkish shipbuilder, has introduced a stylish new range of explorer yachts - the Classic Line, with a focus on showcasing timeless elegance and harmonized design.
body: Representing a new pinnacle in the world of luxury sea travel, Turkish shipyard, Numarine, has unveiled its latest masterpiece - the Classic Line. This extraordinary new range of explorer yachts manifests an innovative step in the yard's portfolio, rooted in a profound desire to reinterpret classic yacht aesthetics through the lens of modern exploration. Conceived in partnership with long-standing Numarine collaborator, Can Yalman, the exterior design teems with characteristic Yalman style while introducing a revolutionary touch of design and lifestyle expression. The yachts are a testament to proportion, clarity, and elegance - all built upon Numarine's existing long-range platforms. These exquisite water chariots emerged from a deliberate period of reflection, as Yalman explains: 'After working with highly optimized explorer yachts, we desired to reconnect with timeless principles of naval design'. Admiral Yalman and his team sensed a rising wave of desire for such a design approach - one that deviates from excess and instead focuses on harmonious connections with nature and a more timeless, almost romantic life at sea. Nautical connoisseurs will appreciate the naval architecture developed by Umberto Tagliavini, while the initial interiors have been expertly crafted by the Viken Group's Milan-based studio, Hot Lab. Tagliavini expressed pride in maintaining the principles of efficiency, seaworthiness, stability, and autonomy for which Numarine is revered. Launching the line are the 38XPC and 39MXPC models, each presenting its own identity. The 39MXPC delights with enhanced onboard living provided by a spacious, lavishly designed aft section with a Jacuzzi and open terrace over the water, creating a more social and Mediterranean-style experience, while the 38-metre 38XPC introduces a more classic layout, harking back to traditional yachting heritage. The shift, as a statement from the yard points out, is not in capability, but rather in the experience and expression of these prestige vessels, with a greater emphasis on atmosphere, lifestyle, and timeless design. Thus, with its Classic Line, Numarine offers yacht enthusiasts an exciting, elegant journey into the essence of timeless yachting - a voyage where grandeur, class, and the finer elements of a glorious yachting heritage truly converge.

title: Up Close and Personal with 2026's Largest Superyachts on Display at Palma International Boat Show
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Up Close and Personal with 2026's Largest Superyachts on Display at Palma International Boat Show
summary: The Palma International Boat Show (PIBS) of 2026 promises a mesmerising display of the largest and most innovative superyachts.
body: The grand showcase of marine royalty, the Palma International Boat Show of 2026, beckons yacht enthusiasts and industry insiders from around the world. The event, spanning from 29th April to 2nd May, flaunts an exquisite display of fine naval craftsmanship and innovation, headlined by some of the year's biggest and most striking superyachts. Leading the roster is Ares Yachts' latest pearl, Simena. This 62m spectacle is a salute to the age of sail, inspired by the classic silhouette of the clipper ships. Just off her maiden voyage from the Turkish shipyard, Simena graces the show with her resplendent interiors designed by Design Unlimited. This elegant marvel is the epitome of a luxuriant seafaring experience. Joining the ranks is Ohana, a 49.7m high-performer from the stables of Fitzroy Yachts. Designed by Dubois, this New Zealand-built superyacht flaunts competitive hull lines and a functional layout, marked by luxuries like a secluded master cabin and an onboard cinema. However, the 47m Andromeda La Dea is the comeback story that's got everyone buzzing. After a comprehensive three-year makeover, this Perini Navi beauty stuns with modern interiors by Guillaume Rolland of Liaigre. Her nomination for a Neptune at the 2026 World Superyacht Awards adds to her appeal. Finally, the 45.3m R.R from Overmarine Group is an Italian masterpiece that merges athletic performance with lavish comfort. Leveraging the successful Mangusta GranSport 45 series, this motor yacht showcases advanced naval architecture by Pierluigi Ausonio PLANA and design work by Alberto Mancini. A gleaming example of the strategic collaboration, R.R boasts top speeds of 26 knots and extravagant features like a 75-square-metre beach club and foredeck infinity pool.

title: An Inside Look: Sunreef Yachts' Luxurious and Innovative First Ultima 88 Catamaran
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: An Inside Look: Sunreef Yachts' Luxurious and Innovative First Ultima 88 Catamaran
summary: Polish shipyard, Sunreef Yachts, unveils the lavish interiors of its first Ultima 88 catamaran, 'Wasabi', raising the bar for luxury yachting.
body: Polish shipyard, Sunreef Yachts, offers a captivating peek into the opulence of its first Ultima 88 catamaran model: Wasabi. Crafted meticulously in the shipyard's facilities in Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates, the vessel was announced as sold to powerboat racing champ Tim Ciasulli less than a year later at the 2023 Fort Lauderdale International Boat Show. This Octo-marine marvel classifies as one among the six models in the Ultima line, which ranges between 13.7 metres and 36.4 metres, with the Ultima 88 sitting as the penultimate in size. An exemplar of Sunreef's 'forward-thinking vision', the Ultima 88 blends groundbreaking 'solar skin system' technology with performance-tailored design and leading-edge aesthetics. This state-of-the-art ship is engineered with the agility and dynamics of the monohull, combined with the multihull's space, stability, and shallow draught. Moored, Wasabi's expansive bulwarks and rear garage space evolve it into a 'true waterside retreat'. The so-called 'supercat', with a 9.3-metre beam and spacious living quarters spanning 387 square metres, comfortably hosts 10 guests. With several interior layouts on offer, one of the standout choices comes with a full-beam master suite and accessible private sauna. A tour inside reveals a contemporary decor portfolio, with a neutral colour palette, light woods, marbles, and touches of black metals and rich, tan leathers. A relaxed sofa seating arrangement in the main saloon sits alongside an open galley and formal dining area, while below houses a selected full-beam master suite including a large en suite, a large double, and a twin room. Its deck comes fitted with additional lounge seating, a laid-back al fresco dining space, and an exterior helm station. Speaking about the Ultima 88, Sunreef founder and president, Francis Lapp, claims the catamaran as a testament to Sunreef's pursuit of innovation, craftsmanship, and excellence, firmly stamping a stellar new chapter for the brand. This unveiling follows news of professional tennis player Carlos Alcaraz placing an order for a yacht from the same series.

title: Discover Amico Marine: The All-in-One Game Changer in Superyacht Refit and Maintenance
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover Amico Marine: The All-in-One Game Changer in Superyacht Refit and Maintenance
summary: Amico & Co settles on a new course with the launch of Amico Marine, aiming to revitalise the superyacht refit and maintenance sector.
body: In a game-changing move for the superyacht industry, Amico & Co has announced the launch of Amico Marine. This new venture looks set to redefine the horizon for yacht refit, maintenance and services. This innovative brand intends to amalgamate all of the Group's shipyards and associated companies into a singular, more efficient entity. This consolidation marks a significant step forward in providing streamlined and cohesive services, all under the banner of this groovy new brand.

Despite the exciting new beginnings, registration is required to gain unlimited access to all BOATPro News content. For those already in the loop, logging in will reveal a new world of possibilities. With this combination of innovation and consolidation, Amico Marine is paddling towards an exciting future in the world of superyachts.

title: The 2026 RS100 Harken Sprints at Rutland: Thrilling Races Shine, Despite Lacklustre Winds
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The 2026 RS100 Harken Sprints at Rutland: Thrilling Races Shine, Despite Lacklustre Winds
summary: Competitors converged at Rutland Sailing Club on 25th April 2026 to demonstrate their sailing prowess at the esteemed RS100 Harken Sprints, where winds posed a significant challenge.
body: Imagine the exhilaration: four competitors brimming with anticipation, gathered at the Rutland Sailing Club on a sunny April day. There on 25th April 2026, they were all poised to compete in the yearly RS Sprints, a key event of the Rooster National Tour embellished with sponsorship courtesy of Harken. But Mother Nature had other plans. She unveiled a particular riddle - an undeniably sunny but teeteringly still day. The wind was nowhere in sight.

And so, they did. Fleet racing commenced right at 10:30, unfolding a day of excitement, resilience and sportsmanship. Ian Gregory, from Frensham Pond/Stokes Bay SC, made first strides, holding onto an unyielding lead in Race 1 that saw him the first to lay claim on the windward mark. Behind him, Tom Fletcher of Hunts SC segregated himself from Martyn Catlow hailing from Leigh and Lawton SC, clinching second and third places, respectively.

Race 3 saw a calm, nearly nonchalant start from Ian Gregory. A hotly contested battle for runner-up positions ensued between Darrell Sleep, Tom Fletcher, and Martyn Catlow. An eye for wind patches and an instinctive gybe-off saw Tom sprint ahead of Sleep, securing his second place behind the unshakeable Gregory. With no further shifts, Gregory bagged his third victory. Fletcher was hot on his tail taking second, and Darrell Sleep rounded up the top three, closing a day of high medium-pace exhilaration, grit and joy of mastering the waters.

title: In an Unprecedented Event, ClubSwan 28 Races on Two Continents Simultaneously
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: In an Unprecedented Event, ClubSwan 28 Races on Two Continents Simultaneously
summary: The ClubSwan 28 sailing league showcased an extraordinary feat, running parallel races on two different continents.
body: The world of sailing recently bore witness to a remarkable spectacle. The ClubSwan 28 sailing league, an international circuit that aims to unite sailors from around the globe, held two of its races simultaneously on two continents—across the serene waves of the Mediterranean and the unpredictable currents of Florida's Gulf Coast. Such a feat underlines the truly global reach of the league and is exemplary of the intertwining of competition with camaraderie that feeds its spirit.

The scene at Pensacola was not just about the competition. Nestled under the magnolia trees, enveloped by southern hospitality, a community was being formed. The American ClubSwan 28 culture had seen a fostered atmosphere of common learning and shared experiences on water since its inaugural event in Miami. Off the water, relations were built, and old friends were brought back into the mix.

The thrill of sailing was not the only thing that was celebrated at these events. The year 2026 marked a milestone for Nautor Swan—the 60th anniversary of their legacy in sailing. The races in Bonifacio and Pensacola also served to commence this celebration of six decades of master craftsmanship, path-breaking innovation, and a unique sailing philosophy.

The message emanating from these parallel races was well received. The spirit of international sailing and friendly competition transcending geographical barriers manifested as the ClubSwan 28 Nations League. This concept is now a fully functional circuit, uniting sailors worldwide and offering an innovative platform for sailing enthusiasts to come together and compete at a global level.

title: The Pulse of the Trade: Shipyard Chiefs Unearth Insights on the Current and Future Perspectives of the Market
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Pulse of the Trade: Shipyard Chiefs Unearth Insights on the Current and Future Perspectives of the Market
summary: Diverse voices are quick to predict market trends, but the ones that run the yards, shipyard executives, have unsurpassed insights often unheard in public.
body: There's never a dearth of forecasts about the direction in which the market is steering. Consultants, journalists, owner's reps, brokers - everyone has a piece or two in the prediction puzzle. But often, the most critical perspective is least audible - the shipyard CEOs who are at the helm of yard operations.

In a quest to capture their invaluable insights, we engaged in insightful conversations with nine trailblazing yard executives. They include leaders from Royal Huisman, Azimut Benetti, Damen Yachting, and Feadship in the Netherlands, Palumbo, Sanlorenzo, and Ferretti in Italy, and Abeking & Rasmussen in Germany, extending up to Bilgin in Türkiye.

Their collective thoughts offer a crystal-clear barometer of the current new-build panorama, revealing intricate details about the market's health and anticipated future. Unsurprisingly, they don't always align, but certain themes emerge vociferously.

However, hiring the right talent, transferring the time-honoured craft knowledge to the new recruits, and ensuring its continuation are persistent challenges. Even with significant facilities investments, labour remains the Achilles heel.
Supply chains for specialist components are now steady yet fragile. Quality maintenance, without bleeding margins, is frequently identified as the determining survival factor.

Orders are coming in strong, yes, but the quality of orders is changing. Today's owners exhibit a more measured approach. They are driven less by the boat's material possession and more by the experiences it shall offer. Concerns like purpose, sustainability, and a thirst for authentic adventures deeply impact design choices.

And as for the market's potential, these titans aren't expecting rapid growth. They foresee a market that prizes the quality of the produced yachts, the yards' reliability, and their relevance to a generation whose needs transcend the vessels themselves.

We kickstart this series with Massimo Perotti, the Sanlorenzo CEO's comprehensive interview. Get ready for a riveting journey into the market's heart, crafted from the perspectives of those leading the way. Stay tuned for more such stimulating discussions in the following days.

title: Becoming Sea Masters: A Tale of Rough-water Boat Handling and Competency Building on the Irish Sea
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Becoming Sea Masters: A Tale of Rough-water Boat Handling and Competency Building on the Irish Sea
summary: Witness the transformative journey from rough waters to unsurpassed confidence and skill, as adventurous sailors traverse the challenging Irish Sea.
body: There is an old proverb, 'A smooth sea never made a skilled sailor'. The inherent truth of this saying becomes clear when one braves the challenging waters of the Irish Sea. Embodied in this narrative, it serves as a testament that skill and strength are more often carved in the furnace of adversity than in the comfort of the easier route.

No one would consider themselves a master at sea, but everyone loves the process of learning which gets better with every wave they conquer. This story began when the key characters, including Annette, Joe and the author, bought the Dale Classic 37 sailor boat, Iolar. Its exceptional seakeeping, attributed largely to its underwater profile drawn from the legendary Nelson pilot boat lineage, promised exciting sailing adventures.

The journey to mastery continued through an autumnal rough-water training session off St Anne’s Head. Skilfully managing the 3-4 metre waves, their competency started to grow under Mike's guidance, as they learned to navigate Iolar through the challenging waters. Iolar proved strong, built to RCD Category A and able to navigate the steep and confused seas without slamming.

The experiences in the Irish Sea weren't always easy though. There were times when a lack of care sent the 12-tonne Iolar off the top of a large steep wave, resulting in a rough landing rather than a smooth glide. But these instances only brought more lessons and confidence for the sailors, ultimately reinforcing the truth in the proverb that had inspired their daring sea journey.

title: Antigua’s Sailing Week 2026 Unveils Thrilling Finishes, While SVG Sailing Week Wins Gold Certification for Sustainable Practices
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Antigua’s Sailing Week 2026 Unveils Thrilling Finishes, While SVG Sailing Week Wins Gold Certification for Sustainable Practices
summary: Antigua’s Sailing Week 2026 concludes with exhilarating races, while SVG Sailing Week bags Gold Certification for championing sustainability measures.
body: The annual Antigua Sailing Week revealed an extraordinary spectacle this year, with close finishes, spectacular races, and camaraderie, proving once again, that it isn't just about mastering the winds, but also about celebrating the glorious marine beauty that makes it possible. Yet, there’s more to these exciting sailing gatherings than the raw thrill of the sport. The Caribbean archipelago of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines showcased a commendable blend of sporting memorabilia and environmental responsibility.

The sound of the 2026 Antigua Sailing Week's concluding bell was still ringing in the ears when spectators watched, spellbound, heart-stopping finishes crafted by the talent and endurance showcased by the sailors. The final race kicked off at Ffryes Beach on a sunny morning, with a better than forecast, southeast breeze, leading an epic trail of sailing boats to finish back at English Harbour amid majestic swells and energizing winds.

While races concluded with a dashing spectacle, the sailing week also had an easygoing cruising fleet. Sailors aboard Mystic Lee too savored the vivacious atmosphere, leisurely circumnavigating the immaculate breadth of the island, occasionally stopping by a beach and simply basking in the paradisiacal beauty.

Switching gears from intense race results to sustainability wins, the SVG Sailing Week quickly climbed the ladder of recognitions and earned Gold Certification for Sustainability, affirming the symbiotic relationship between sailors and the sea. Guiding this achievement was Sail Green SVG, a pronounced initiative for sustainable event management. Following this successful execution, the SVG Sailing Week was recognized for its efficient blend of sport, culture, and impactful environmental stewardship.

As the closing ceremonies wrap up for these mammoth sailing events, the echo of the surf on the hulls and the promise of environmental responsibility pave the way for exciting and sustainable sailing events in the future.

title: Discover Grace III, the Formidable Cutter-rigged Sloop from the Renowned SES Yachts
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover Grace III, the Formidable Cutter-rigged Sloop from the Renowned SES Yachts
summary: Presenting the Grace III, a luxurious 39.3-meter sailing yacht from SES Yachts, now up for grabs with a new joint central agency.
body: Nestled in the tranquil waters of the Bodrum, Turkey, awaits the Grace III. This stunning 39.3-metre sailing yacht by Turkish shipyard, SES Yachts, gleams under the Mediterranean sun, inviting a new owner to embark on a nautical adventure.

Delivered in 2021 as the third hull from the 'Truly Classic 128’ series, the Grace III is the epitome of maritime sophistication. Its aluminium hull was meticulously crafted by Bloemsma of the Netherlands, while the Hoek Design Naval Architects lent their expertise to the naval architecture and the exterior and interior design.

The yacht's efficient, cutter-rigged design promises stellar performance out on the water. With a Scania engine propelling it to speeds of up to 12 knots and a sail configuration allowing for 13.5 knots upwind and 15 knots reaching, the Grace III is as much about control and handling as it is about comfort.

The practical layout of the Grace III offers something for everyone—owners and guests alike. Accommodations include a lavish owner's suite, two inviting guest cabins, and a 'flex' cabin for additional guests or crew. Overall, the yacht can comfortably sleep four crew during owner use, or serve seven guests with six crew during charter. Light from the surrounding deckhouse windows floods the split-level saloon, creating an airy and inviting space perfect for relaxation or entertainment.

The guest cockpit is thoughtfully designed for dining and relaxation, centered around a large table with seating for 10 to 12 guests. Meanwhile, the sailing cockpit is set slightly aft, ensuring the ship's hardware and sail handling operations do not disturb the tranquillity of the guest areas.

On sale for €14,250,000, the RINA class 131 GT yacht features a fin keel with a 'torpedo-style' bulb that draws 4.6 meters, and a towering mast that rises 52.9 meters above the waterline. This exquisite sailing yacht is much more than a vessel—it's the epitome of sailing elegance.

title: The 35m Sunseeker Motor Yacht, Evereast, Finds New Owners in a Sale Handled by Denison Yachting
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The 35m Sunseeker Motor Yacht, Evereast, Finds New Owners in a Sale Handled by Denison Yachting
summary: The sale of the 34.7m Sunseeker motor yacht, Evereast, has been successfully brokered and completed by Denison Yachting.
body: Marking a key milestone in the world of luxury yacht brokerage, Denison Yachting has recently completed the sale of the Sunseeker motor yacht - Evereast. This 34.7-metre long yacht was designed and constructed by Sunseeker's elite in-house team, making it a potent exemplar of the company's highly esteemed 115 Sport Yacht series. The sale was brokered internally, with professionals Pierre Badin and Andriy Petrenko representing the interests of the seller and buyer respectively.

One of the signature characteristics that set Evereast apart from the crowd is its phenomenal state in the market following a comprehensive and 'extensive' refit program spanning the length of 2021 and 2022. This refit gave the yacht a major facelift, with her hull painted afresh, the deck areas renewed, and vinyl upholstery revamped by Bentley. Due to these newest upgrades, Evereast was listed with a price tag of €5,650,000.

Built with an emphasis on comfort and space, Evereast offers accommodation for 11 guests across five cabins. There is a full-beam main deck owner's cabin, effortlessly exemplifying opulence. Additionally, it also provides cabin spaces for six crew members.

Twin MTU 16V 2000 M94 engines, with 2640hp each, power the yacht, enabling it to reach top speeds of 26 knots. On casual days, it graciously sails at a leisurely 12 knots, offering breath-taking views of the sea to its on-board guests.

The sale of Evereast is a reflection of Sunseeker's continued dominance in the world of luxury yachts, and the effective brokerage skills of Denison Yachting. This is an encouraging trajectory, heralding more successful sales in the future.

title: Paragon of Luxury on Water, the 34m Van der Valk Motor Yacht 'One', Seals a Splendid Sale
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Paragon of Luxury on Water, the 34m Van der Valk Motor Yacht 'One', Seals a Splendid Sale
summary: The magnificent 34.1-metre Van der Valk motor yacht 'One' has transitioned to proud new ownership, infusing the yachting community with renewed excitement.
body: An illustrious chapter closed with the sale of the opulent 34.1-metre Van der Valk motor yacht 'One', brilliantly mediated by Yoeri Bijker of the Van der Valk shipyard, who represented the seller, and Jorge Saca Bahaia of Maspor Marine International, who introduced the buyer. A spectacle of Dutch craftmanship, the marine marvel was launched into the waters in 2025。

The grandeur of 'One' encapsulates the aesthetic vision of Guido De Groot, whose design harmonises with the technical brilliance of Ginton Naval Architects and Diana Yacht Design. A Carla Guilhem Design masterpiece, the interior oozes sleek and contemporary charm.

Built to entertain, the motor yacht 'One' flaunts a large main deck with calming interiors highlighted by a palate of blue, cream, and salmon. The main saloon houses a welcoming seating area with plump furnishings and a dining table for eight, bordered by sweeping floor-to-ceiling windows that invite natural light and offer breathtaking views.

The bridge deck, outfitted with large windows, provides panoramic vistas. It sports an aft lounge perfect for al fresco dining and a shaded upper lounge sporting aesthetics similar to the main saloon. The lounge is strategically placed near the pilothouse for convenient access.

The yacht's sundeck stands out with its delightful décor, featuring pastel pillows and white furnishings. A jacuzzi located at the aft offers unrivalled views, placing luxury literally at fingertips. A lounge bar on the sundeck provides a great spot for hosting, promising an inimitable indoor-outdoor experience.

The exterior design of 'One' reflects unwavering faith in straight lines. Power is sourced from two Volvo Penta diesel engines, enabling this marvel to cruise at speeds of up to 14.4 knots. The motor yacht 'One', last priced at an exhilarating €17,950,000, marks a high point in luxury boating.

title: Reconceptualised Luxury Living in the Maldives: The Rise of Continuity and Customisation over Novelty
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Reconceptualised Luxury Living in the Maldives: The Rise of Continuity and Customisation over Novelty
summary: In the heart of the captivating Maldives, a paradigm shift in luxury living is emerging, spearheaded by SIX & SIX PRIVATE ISLANDS.
body: Luxury has long been a defining feature in the breathtaking Maldives, an archipelago synonymous with lush resorts and private villas. Yet, amidst this affluent landscape, an evolution is cropping up, whispering a new narrative of what luxury entails. That whisper's source? SIX & SIX PRIVATE ISLANDS, an ambitious endeavour fuelled by the vision of reimagining island living through continuity, ownership, and long-term living.

The Maldives has long been approached as a symphony of arrival, departure and return. Yet, these timeless echoes have started to evolve into a gentler cadence. To an increasing number of travellers, the islands have become more than a holiday destination; they have become an extension of their lives. And with this shift in perspective, the expectation of continuity over novelty gains prominence, ushering in an era defined by persistence, not transience.

Underneath this model lies a strong emphasis on understated service, local community collaboration, and sustainable development. Performance isn't mere formality; it's centered around the continuity of preferred experiences. And the heart of the islands beats strongly with Rayyithun (the people of the islands) driving the operations by closely aligning with the local communities. The islands function as individual systems, managing their resources in line with EarthCheck Certification, embodying the principle of sustainable luxury.

This transformative vision of SIX & SIX PRIVATE ISLANDS signifies a fresh understanding of luxury, where ownership and continuity hold the reins. As travellers adapt to the rhythm of the islands, the islands themselves evolve, ensnaring everyone in a dance of timelessness and distinct identity.

title: Foiling at Full Noise Beneath Sugarloaf as SailGP Makes Historic Rio Debut
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: SailGP Hits Rio: Guanabara Bay Set for High-Speed Showdown as Championship Arrives in Brazil
summary: SailGP arrived in Rio de Janeiro for the first time, bringing high-speed foiling action to Guanabara Bay as global teams battled in front of home crowds and iconic scenery.
body: There are race venues.
And then there are statements.
SailGP dropped anchor — briefly — in one of the most recognisable natural amphitheatres in sport: Guanabara Bay.
Sugarloaf Mountain looming. The city rising behind it. Trade winds rolling through a racecourse that has shaped Olympic champions for decades.
For the fourth stop of the 2026 season, SailGP didn’t just arrive in Brazil.
More than 8,000 spectators lined the shore, watching F50s rip across the bay at speeds approaching 100 km/h — turning one of sailing’s most historic venues into a modern, high-speed arena.
Brazil’s Moment — And the Grael Homecoming
For the Mubadala Brazil SailGP Team, this wasn’t just another event.

At the centre of it all stood Martine Grael — two-time Olympic gold medallist and SailGP’s first female driver — racing on home waters for the first time. Alongside her, brother Marco Grael. Together, they represent one of sailing’s most respected families — children of Olympic legend Torben Grael. They learned their trade here. Now they returned, not as prospects — but as professionals, with a nation watching.

It was a full-circle moment. Old Teammates, New Rivals If the backdrop wasn’t enough, the storylines added fuel. A decade after winning Olympic gold together in Rio 2016, Martine Grael lined up against Kahena Kunze — now strategist for ROCKWOOL Racing. Former teammates. Now rivals. Same water. Different boats. Same instinct to win. For those watching from the shoreline, it was more than nostalgia. It was tension.
The 2026 SailGP season has already shown one thing clearly:
There are no passengers.
Three events. Three different winners.
Emirates GBR SailGP Team leading on 28 points Australia SailGP Team close behind United States SailGP Team carrying momentum after a breakthrough win in Sydney
The Americans, led by Taylor Canfield, arrived in Rio with confidence — and something to prove. Sydney wasn’t a fluke. Rio was the confirmation test.

France Returns — Reset and Ready After a heavy crash in Auckland forced them out of contention, France SailGP Team returned to the line. Repaired. Refocused. And carrying a point to prove. For driver Quentin Delapierre, Rio wasn’t about easing back in. It was about resetting the season.
Why SailGP Works — And Why Rio Matters
It’s tighter. Faster. Less forgiving. Identical F50 foiling catamarans Stadium-style courses Close-to-shore racing Winner-takes-all finals
There’s nowhere to hide. And venues like Rio amplify everything:
Shifting breeze off the land Complex pressure patterns Tight racing boundaries This is not open-ocean sailing. This is precision under pressure.
The Enel Rio Sail Grand Prix wasn’t just a race. It was a broadcast event.
UK (TNT Sports) USA (CBS Sports Network) Europe, Asia and Australasia
SailGP continues to position itself not just as a competition — but as a global sports product. And Rio? Rio delivered the visuals to match.
This wasn’t just another stop on the calendar. It was a signal.
SailGP is expanding. The competition is tightening. And the margins are getting smaller.
Fast boats. Tight courses. Big stages.

title: The U.S. Virgin Islands’ St. Croix to Become the Center of Sailing Universe as it Plays Host to the International Sunfish Class Association World Championships
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The U.S. Virgin Islands’ St. Croix to Become the Center of Sailing Universe as it Plays Host to the International Sunfish Class Association World Championships
summary: 2026 will see the U.S. Virgin Islands' St. Croix hosting the prestigious 55th annual International Sunfish Class Association (ISCA) World Championships, showcasing its status as a leading global sailing destination.
body: Sweeping the globe with its reputation as a world-class sailing destination, St. Croix, located within the idyllic confines of the U.S. Virgin Islands, prepares itself for a significant event in its maritime calendar. The island is set to host the esteemed 55th Annual International Sunfish Class Association (ISCA) World Championships in November 2026, scheduled for November 4-14, 2026. It is an event so grand in scope that it seeks to weave St. Croix into the very tapestry of international sailing presidencies.

Further elevating the gravitas of the event, the ISCA World Championships represent the zenith of competitive class racing, attracting the crème de la crème of sailors across multiple divisions, including Youth, Women, Masters, and Open categories.

The event also serves to catalyse local economy and community engagement. In anticipation of the Championships, local businesses and community partners are cordially invited to a meet-and-greet rendezvous on May 13. It presents an incredible opportunity to learn more about the Championships, forge connections with event organizers, and explore avenues to showcase their businesses through advertising opportunities in the official ISCA World Championship publication. This high-quality book will find its way into the hands of sailors, teams, sponsors, and guests from around the world.

Certainly, St. Croix is gearing up for a grand showcase of sailing prowess and sportsmanship. With further details about the venue, the registration timelines, and community involvement opportunities set to be announced, all eyes are firmly set on St. Croix as it readies itself for the most celebrated gathering of global sailing talent.

title: Seize the Adventure: Luxury Yacht Aveline's Price Dips by $600,000, Making Immaculate Maritime Experience More Accessible
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Seize the Adventure: Luxury Yacht Aveline's Price Dips by $600,000, Making Immaculate Maritime Experience More Accessible
summary: Luxury motor yacht Aveline, acknowledged for its exceptional blend of volume and long-range capability, experiences a $600,000 price drop.
body: The illustrious Horizon motor yacht, Aveline, has recently received a dramatic price reduction of $600,000. Known for her exquisite features and exceptional performance, Aveline, initially named Tyee, was listed for sale by Carmen Lau of Camper & Nicholsons. Manufactured with precision by the reputed Taiwanese shipyard as hull 20 of the renowned Horizon FD90 series, Aveline was masterfully sculpted under the hands of the prodigious designer, Cor D. Rover.

Credit for its flawless condition is owed to its singular, highly-experienced owner who has upheld its impeccable maintenance. Aveline is emblematic of a rare coupling of substantial volume and expansive range encapsulated within a sub-30-metre yacht. The lowered asking price, which now stands at $6,800,000, broadens the accessibility to its exclusive maritime experience.

Colour, comfort, and opulence are imprinted into Aveline's elegant interiors. Natural hues of beige and cream paint the interior along with bright, open spaces effectively capturing and diffusing natural light. Its main saloon employs panoramic windows to nourish the open-plan living and dining area with wholesome daylight. The dining area can conveniently seat between eight to ten guests, offering an indoor wining and dining alternative. Adjacent to the living quarters lies a sizeable lounging area, offering respite from the sunlight under the shade of the upper deck.

A welcoming, relaxed living space is extended on the yacht's upper deck – another saloon that comes with large doors ushering towards the upper deck aft. This elegant construction provides an enticing alfresco dining setup, seconding the entertaining spaces onboard the Aveline yacht. Additionally, a segmented wheelhouse adds to the exclusivity of the yacht, ensuring privacy on prolonged voyages.

Seizing this high-sea muscle for a lowered price tag could translate to obtaining unmatched oceanic adventures and elegant living, making every voyage unforgettable. Aveline is not just a yacht; she's a floating luxury experience.

title: Excelled Performances in Port Phillip Women's Championship Series 2025-26: Revealed Drama and Achievements of Day 4
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Excelled Performances in Port Phillip Women's Championship Series 2025-26: Revealed Drama and Achievements of Day 4
summary: Unravel the thrilling experiences of the fourth race day of the Port Phillip Women's Championship Series 2025-26, held at the Royal Melbourne Yacht Squadron.
body: With a historic background and a renewed vigour, the Port Phillip Women's Championship Series (PPWCS) 2025-26 Dance Day 4, hosted by the Royal Melbourne Yacht Squadron on the 19th of April 2026, offered a compelling spectacle of seafaring skills and strategy. The day was dedicated to the annual signature female helm Jennifer Goldsmith Trophy event. Beneath Melbourne's temperate autumnal weather, a thrilling race unfurled across a two-lap, 6-nautical-mile triangular course.

The festivities continued back at the freshly refurbished clubhouse, with a hospitable full house luncheon and presentation generously supported, as every year, by the Goldsmith family in memory of their daughter Jennifer Goldsmith who passed too early from melanoma. In a touching tribute, RMYS Commodore Cherry Birch even sported a limited-edition commemorative t-shirt, highlighting Jennifer's substantial contribution to the club during her lifetime.

Fittingly, Jennifer's longtime friend and RMYS member Sabina Rosser led the helm of Flying Tiger 10 Tigris to win the Jennifer Goldsmith Trophy. Their victory was complemented by line honours winner Serious Yahoo's submariner placement in both (PHS and AMS), reinforcing their series lead.

The fifth and final PPWCS race day—with RBYC's signature female helm event, the annual BLiSS (Brighton Lady Skipper Series) Regatta—provides another exciting opportunity for all female sailors. Notably, SYC member Robyn Ragauskus leads ORC, and a significant challenge from HBYC's Sue Burke on Lanncoorie is expected. With less than a month until the 34th Australian Women's Keelboat Regatta (AWKR), the BLiSS Regatta offers an excellent warmup chance for teams to embed unity and tactics ahead of the King's Birthday weekend. The regatta also caters to all female helms, with racing divisions customised based on competing levels.

title: The Window For Early Bird Registration for the Prestigious 87th Queen's Cup is Rapidly Closing. Act promptly!
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Window For Early Bird Registration for the Prestigious 87th Queen's Cup is Rapidly Closing. Act promptly!
summary: Here is their final call to register for the coveted 87th Queen's Cup; the deadline for early bird registrations is just around the corner.
body: The 87th Queen's Cup, a cherished sailing competition, beckons sailing enthusiasts again. Organized by South Shore Yacht Club, this year's race – a highly anticipated event within the sailing community – is opening its doors for registration. The legendary race, which will host a parade of sailing boats and yachts, is mapped from Milwaukee to Grand Haven, Michigan, and is due to take place on June 26, 2026.

Registration for this enthralling contest is currently in the early bird stage, allowing eager sailors and supporters to secure berth at preferential rates. However, the window for taking advantage of these reduced fees is rapidly closing with the cut-off slated for May 1st, 2026.

In an effort to streamline safety procedures, the Safety Checklist and Crew Overboard Drill Certificate will now be managed as two digital documents. The roles and responsibilities of the Person-in-Charge (PIC) will also undergo minor adjustments, including the requirement to digitally review and sign these safety documents. The modification frees crew members from the obligation of signing the Crew Overboard Drill Certificate individually.

With dockage graciously provided by the SSYC for competitors during race week right at SSYC, reservations are not mandatory. Docking will also be accessible in Grand Haven along the seawall, with some protection offered.
Finally, certificates from rating bodies like ORC, MWPHRF, GLMRA, and One-Design will need to be uploaded to the Nautical Cloud no later than June 22, 2026.

Remember, registration fees escalate from May 2nd and late charges will be levied after June 15th, 2026. So, seize this chance, finalize your registration and prepare to set sail on an unforgettable voyage!

title: Unveiled Splendour: Frida, the 55m Heesen Steel Superyacht Embarks on North Sea Trials
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unveiled Splendour: Frida, the 55m Heesen Steel Superyacht Embarks on North Sea Trials
summary: Frida, the 55-metre Steel superyacht crafted by Heesen Yachts, has started its inaugural sea trials in the North Sea.
body: From the innovative shipyard of Heesen Yachts, headquartered in Oss, the Netherlands, comes an exciting announcement. Frida, the 55-metre Steel series superyacht, has made her first sea trials voyage in the choppy waters of the North Sea, heralding an important milestone in her journey towards delivery, expected to take place in time for the summer cruising season.

Construction of this maritime marvel began back in 2023, launching from the yard in August 2025. The distinctive 'shark tooth' superstructure is the masterwork of Omega Architects, an emblematic feature of the Heesen's Steel series. Merging seamlessly with floor-to-ceiling windows, light floods into the lavish 760GT interiors, forming an atmosphere reminiscent of the 'golden age of ocean travel'.

Silvia Margutti, lead architect of the studio, lauds the interior as a 'modern interpretation of traditional maritime heritage'. The design starkly contrasts light hues against dark woods, echoing contemporary design trends.

Accommodation is extensively planned within Frida, with six plush cabins and airy lounging spaces. The full-beam owner’s apartment boasts a generous en suite, replete with a private study and veranda. The lower deck houses four guest cabins, with an additional versatile cabin located on the bridge deck.

The exterior matches the interiors in terms of grandeur. Generous spaces befitting a 55-metre vessel include a sundeck equipped with a sizable whirlpool, bar and multiple lounging arenas. Beneath lies a skylounge connecting to an aft terrace and beach club, providing direct access to the water from a large swim platform.

Frida utilises high-performance MTU 4000 M63 engines, enabling a top speed of 15.5 knots and a range of 4,500 nautical miles at a cruising speed of 12 knots. Abiding by the 'Large Yacht Code 3', Frida complies stringently with the highest commercial standards, further enabled by a Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) system that ensures full compliance with IMO Tier III emission regulations.

title: Sailing Legend and Indomitable Spirit: Remembering the Exceptional Gordon Ingate OAM
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Sailing Legend and Indomitable Spirit: Remembering the Exceptional Gordon Ingate OAM
summary: Sailing world mourns the loss of its revered figure, the evergreen Gordon Ingate, fondly known as 'Wingy', who left a long-lasting legacy.
body: The curtains have fallen on an era in the sailing world with the passing of the legendary Gordon Ingate OAM, or 'Wingnut', later affectionately shortened to 'Wingy'. An exceptional sailor, charming and vivacious, 'Wingy' was in his element when sailing the high seas or playing croquet at the Tea Gardens. Breathing his last at the ripe age of 100, 'Wingy' remained an indefatigable spirit enamoured by the thrill and beauty of sailing.

His journey in sailing began under the tutelage of the owners of Wayfarer and Kathleen, vessels which took part in the first Sydney Hobart race in 1945. Despite bouts of seasickness, 'Wingy' bravely soldiered on to etch his name amongst the finest in the world of sailing.

His partnership with Nina Saalfeld in boat ownerships and his camaraderie with her daughter Sally added a delightful dimension to his sailing journey. His first venture as a skipper in the 1950 Hobart on Jasnar, a double-ended sloop designed by Wally Ward, saw him taking Sally along, a testament to his inclusive spirit.

In his passing, the sailing world loses not just a remarkable sailor but also a gentle,oveable figure who brought humour and charm to a demanding sport. The memory of 'Wingy' sailing buoyantly amidst the waves, with a gleam in his eyes and a ready quip on his lips, will forever hover over the waters he so dearly loved.

title: Seventy Wounded, Injured, and Sick Veterans Navigate a 2,000-Mile Expedition Around the UK in Partnered Adventure with Invictus Games
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Seventy Wounded, Injured, and Sick Veterans Navigate a 2,000-Mile Expedition Around the UK in Partnered Adventure with Invictus Games
summary: In an inspiring show of resilience and camaraderie, a group of 70 wounded, injured, and sick veterans and serving personnel have set sail on a traditional sailing yachts to navigate a 2,000-mile expedition around the UK.
body: The Full Circle Expedition, an ambitious 2,000-mile journey, is more than just a circumnavigation of the United Kingdom. It's a journey of resilience, a quest for adventure, and a resounding testament to the valor of veterans navigating barriers beyond the battleground. Seventy wounded, injured, and sick (WIS) veterans and serving personnel make up the rotating crew aboard the Spirit of Falmouth and the Pellew, respectively 28-metre and 27-metre traditionally-rigged sailing yachts.

Kick-starting their journey on 17 March from Falmouth, Cornwall, these intrepid mariners are slated to visit 22 ports scattered across England, Scotland, Ireland, Wales before the anticipated return to Falmouth on 11 June 2026. Orchestrated by veteran sailing charity Turn to Starboard, the expedition is a partnership initiative with the Invictus Games Birmingham 2027, a renowned international adaptive sporting event dedicated to the recovery and rehabilitation of WIS service personnel and veterans.

The Full Circle Expedition extends beyond a grand voyage. It is an inspiring tale of courage, resilience, and renewal that demonstrates how the magic of group adventure and the healing power of the sea can yield unity, inspire recovery, and instill a sense of purpose. As these incredible veterans sail the Invictus Games Flag around the UK, they magnify the spirit of courage, determination, and community that continues to define them long after their military service concludes.

As the Invictus Games Birmingham 2027 looms, the Full Circle Expedition sends a resounding message about the strength, resilience, and spirit of those who serve and those who have served before them. It reminds us that recovery goes beyond the field of play, extending into challenge, connection, and community.

title: Introducing the 62-metre Flagship 'Simena' by Ares Yachts and Torlak Shipyard's 45m Motor Yacht Awe-Inspired by Hot Lab
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Introducing the 62-metre Flagship 'Simena' by Ares Yachts and Torlak Shipyard's 45m Motor Yacht Awe-Inspired by Hot Lab
summary: Take a tantalising tour of the remarkably stunning 62-meter flagship 'Simena', the pride of Ares Yachts, and Torlak Shipyard’s thrilling 45m motor yacht, designed by Hot Lab.
body: Brokerage firm Northrop and Johnson have recently shared a tantalising sneak peek onboard Ares Yachts' flagship sailing yacht, 'Simena', a stunning 62-meter watercraft. As breathtaking as it is elegant, 'Simena' first graced the waters in July of 2025, departing from the Turkish shipyard's Antalya sheds. After an array of rigorous sea trials, the yacht embarked on a maiden voyage to grace the Monaco coast. It fittingly debuted as a central feature at the Explorer Dock of the Yacht Club de Monaco Marina during the Day of Exploration festivities.

Not to be outdone, the Turkish shipyard Torlak has shared renders of their latest venture, a motor yacht currently known as NB83. This 44.9-meter beauty is built in a semi-displacement hull style with a beam measuring over nine meters. Behind the design of NB83 is the Milan-based studio, Hot Lab, that chose a slender, sporty, and monochromatic profile for the vessel. The yacht lounges a total of five compartments for guests, including an owner’s cabin complete with a private office, dressing rooms, and en-suite. Despite its sporty look, this motor yacht sets a precedent for hospitality with accommodation for 11 crew.

Both the sea marvels are set to be the highlights of the forthcoming Palma International Boat Show, with 'Simena' being the biggest display this year. A perfect blend of captivating design and top-quality craftsmanship, these yachts are sure to make waves in the world of sea vessels.

title: Women's Sailing Takes Centre Stage as Elite Talent Returns for Revival of Iconic Macnamara's Bowl
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Women's Sailing Takes Centre Stage as Elite Talent Returns for Revival of Iconic Macnamara's Bowl
summary: The long-anticipated return of the Macnamara's Bowl will see elite female sailors from around the globe set sail on a historic regatta once more.
body: In a momentous display of vigor and versatility, the Macnamara's Bowl relaunches after more than three decades of abstinence, boasting a star-studded lineup of women sailors. Renowned competitors included Charlotte Borghesi, the first female to claim victory at the SB20 World Championship, on top of Vita Heathcote, the 420 World Champion recognized internationally. They share the spotlight with Phoebe Chalmers, the North American WASZP champion, and Emma McEwen, a multi-title holder in the sailing world.

Swapping tales of yore with cutting-edge athletic prowess, the competition showcases 11 club teams from all over the world in a series of races at the Royal Lymington Yacht Club. Included in the lineup are budding youth teams from Kingston Yacht Club, putting enthusiasm, vitality, and potential at the heart of this regatta revival.

The RS21 keelboat, supplied by RS Sailing, is the vessel of choice for this nautical challenge where skill, teamwork, and tactical execution reward the victors. Regattas like Macnamara's Bowl serve to refocus attention on the richness and caliber of sailing prowess this class of competition can offer.

The weekend kicks off with an induction training day, a series of seven race sessions, and an optimistic forecast for some premier Solent racing. This event, however, transcends the limits of competition. It stands as a testament to the persistent women who have left indelible marks on the sport of sailing, chronicling the voyage from the original crews of the 1970s to today's global competitors.

title: The Future of Boating Safety? WATCHIT’s AI System Brings New Level of Vigilance to the Sea
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Future of Boating Safety? WATCHIT’s AI System Brings New Level of Vigilance to the Sea
summary: In the wake of a perilous incident, WATCHIT co-founder Lawrence Nathan aims to revolutionize boating safety with artificial intelligence.
body: The serene bliss of lounging on an Azimut flybridge was abruptly destroyed for Lawrence Nathan, WATCHIT's co-founder, when the boat he was aboard abruptly crashed into a reef off the Greek isles. But from this fiasco, an elegant yet practical solution was fashioned- the WATCHIT Smart Prevention System. Lawrence and his team developed an NMEA-compatible blackbox system employing artificial intelligence. The system absorbs data from existing navigation aids like GPS, AIS receivers, electronic compasses and autopilots. It also incorporates its 'own charting software.' With this data, WATCHIT's system identifies potential sea hazards, calculates the risk, and alerts the user to take evasive action. This system heralds a leap in maritime safety. The most notable feature is the 'Dynamic Alert Zone,' unlike conventional boat warning systems that trigger alerts based on mere distance. Instead, WATCHIT's 'Dynamic Alert Zone' considers boat speed, ongoing route and operator awareness in adjusting the potential danger area. Let's say a sailing boat is casually cruising at 5 knots with an island 200m away, the island presents no immediate threat. But consider this, a jet ski and a sports cruiser are heading towards each other at a total speed of 70 knots with the same distance apart. That's a recipe for disaster mere seconds away. The ultimate goal of WATCHIT's system is to provide users with at least a 10 to 30-second buffer to act when a potential danger is detected. This AI-powered system is tireless in its vigilance, but it will only caution when there is a clear risk of collision. Whether it's a visible threat like an approaching ship or an unseen hazard like an underwater reef, the smart system exercises prudence, only issuing warnings when truly necessary. Don't be anxious about false alarms when approaching a bustling port or marina, WATCHIT is astute enough to understand the difference. In the event of an impending danger, both visual pop-ups on the boat's existing MFD and audible warnings through its Bluetooth speaker system would alert the user. The alerts start soft, with a beep and a calm voice stating the nature of the threat. If no action is taken, the alerts increase in intensity. The cherry on top of WATCHIT's AI system is the WATCHIT Eye, a recent add-on that elevates this new-age safety system. It's a high-frequency, short-range radar capable of picking up small objects, enhancing the system's efficiency in accident prevention even further. With each bobbing head in the sea now detectable, smooth sailing just might be an achievable reality!

title: Reviva Refit announces relaunch of Bering motor yacht B121 after six-month, intensive refurbishment project
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Reviva Refit announces relaunch of Bering motor yacht B121 after six-month, intensive refurbishment project
summary: Reviva Refit of Mengi Yay, the Turkish shipyard, has debuted the spruced-up Bering motor yacht B121 upon conclusion of an expansive refit.
body: The esteemed Turkish shipyard, Mengi Yay, through its refurbishment division Reviva Refit, has recently made waves in the yachting world by officially unveiling the impressively refitted 37.4-metre Bering motor yacht B121. Deemed Project R16, the comprehensive refit kicked off with its establishment in October 2025 and took around half a year to achieve its slated April launch. This revamp was not simply a cosmetic revamp, rather it aimed for a total structural and functional makeover, according to the team at the shipyard. A primary modification was the implementation of a two-metre hull extension. This significant procedure saw the yacht almost bisected at midship, a bold move aimed at enhancing operational capabilities whilst injecting stability and improved seakeeping prowess into the vessel. Further rebirth was given to the yacht's beach club. Once a leisure zone graced with a sauna and gym, the space has been reincarnated into a garage designed for storage and easy access to one large tender and a couple of jet skis. Additionally, a new petrol storage area was developed following RINA Commercial Unrestricted Navigation class rules. The ceiling crane and shell door system also experienced alterations, with a fresh starboard-side shell door and an overhead lifting solution chipping in for more efficient handling of tenders and 'toys'. The refurbishment was rounded out by a classy upper deck staircase and, not to be missed, a fresh coat of paint adorning B121's exterior. The shipyard took immense pride in the successful venture, stating 'Not many yards in the world can execute a project of this nature — structural, regulatory and mechanical — under one roof, on one timeline'. B121, originally launched in 2024 by Bering Yachts, is scheduled for imminent delivery, signalling a successful completion of one of the most ambitiously sophisticated superyacht conversion projects undertaken in Turkey so far, and adding another feather in the cap of the Mengi Yay shipyard.

title: Breathtakingly Fast AB 95S Superyacht Makes Its Debut: AB Yachts Delivers Its First 29m Model in Spectacular Style
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Breathtakingly Fast AB 95S Superyacht Makes Its Debut: AB Yachts Delivers Its First 29m Model in Spectacular Style
summary: Turning heads with its phenomenal speed, the first unit of AB Yachts’ AB 95S series has been proudly handed over to its new owner.
body: AB Yachts has raised the bar with the delivery of its first AB 95S superyacht. A marvel of the seas, the 28.5-metre vessel is the sport version of the well-received AB 95 model. The delivery was overseen by FGI Yacht Group, with broker Simon Graham representing the experienced American owner. The superyacht launched in March from the prestigious Italian yard’s facilities in Viareggio, Italy. Onlookers were treated to the first glimpse of the model's Archea Associati design, celebrated for a bold silhouette with smooth, sporty lines and a wraparound windshield. The superyacht is geared towards sporty enthusiasts with the need for unparalleled speed, featuring a high-tech helm station developed in collaboration with Italian shipyard Fincantieri. Furthermore, it maximises leisure and thrill with an open cockpit and aft beach club, accommodating various water sports equipment. The vessel can host eight guests in an atmosphere of absolute contemporary refinement, with a primary focus on noise reduction below the deck. Powering this stellar model are three robust 2,200hp MAN V12X-2200 engines, allowing for its staggering top speed. The engineering feat doesn't end there as the hull and deck are also constructed in composite materials with extensive use of carbon fibre to reduce weight. This prized gem of yachting technology stands testimony to AB Yachts' commitment to pursuing speed and technological innovation, guaranteeing to quicken the pulse of its fortunate passengers with its velocity of over an astounding 53 knots.

title: Inaugural Winds: Excitement Surges as J/70 UK Grand Slam Series Embarks
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Inaugural Winds: Excitement Surges as J/70 UK Grand Slam Series Embarks
summary: The highly-awaited UK J/70 Grand Slam Series begins, marking the stirring start of a seven-event bonanza celebrated on the water.
body: Unveiling of the UK J/70 Grand Slam Series marks the beginning of an exciting competition. The waters of the Hamble River and Cowes are playing host to this sporting spectacle, bringing more than 20 J/70s under the spotlight. As the yachts assemble on the Hill Head plateau, they pave the way for the racing season born amidst the swells of anticipation.

Prior to setting sail, some enthusiastic teams had shed the winter's lethargy and geared up for action through early training events of the year. However, it is this kick-off series that officially marks the comeback of racing since its hiatus in October. As the ripples of excitement stretch across the waters, several first-time participants have also found their way to the J/70 start line.

The commencement of the Grand Slam Series also debuts the use of advanced Vakaros Racesense technology in the UK. Already admired on the international racing circuit, the UK fleet now gets to experience the power of rapid turnarounds, cleaner starts, and less waiting time, leading to a streamlined racing experience. As thrilling as the competition stands, who doesn't appreciate a little extra time to celebrate their efforts at the bar later?

Splendidly supported by Rooster and Ocean Rope, the J/70 UK Class continues to unveil exhilarating racing experiences. As the saying goes in the sailing world - 'The racing season starts here.' Unwind, follow, and participate in the thrilling adventures of the J/70 UK Grand Slam Series!

title: Embarking on a Digital Adventure: The 2026 Offshore Championship Season Launches for an Immersive Experience
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Embarking on a Digital Adventure: The 2026 Offshore Championship Season Launches for an Immersive Experience
summary: Launching an extraordinary boating journey, the 2026 offshore virtual championships set sail, immersing sailing enthusiasts and players alike into the ocean's thrill.
body: Setting sail into digital tides, the 2026 offshore virtual championships have commenced, opening new venues for boating enthusiasts, gamers, and navigation fans to partake in the major races on the IMOCA Globe Series calendar. A brainchild of a partnership between IMOCA and Virtual Regatta, the aim is to make offshore racing accessible to everyone, everywhere. With over one million unique players already onboard and six times more finishers than previous seasons, the initiative is living up to its ambitious goal.

Among the simulated racing experiences are some exclusively virtual races, giving players more opportunities to compete within the season. Notably, the top performers will be recognised at the end of the championship, vying for the prestigious title of the '2026 IMOCA Virtual Series Champion', a distinction that has gained significant prominence within the eSailing ecosystem.

Engaging the global body of digital sailors, the offshore virtual championships have adventurously blended the thrill of seafaring with the flexibility of digital gaming; an achievement that goes beyond borders and time zones. As eSailing accelerates alongside the winds of technological change and the world grows more interconnected every day, it's evident that the future of boating is not confined to the physical realm. The vast digital expanse awaits adventurous sailors ready neither to anchor in the past nor drift in the present but to hoist the sails towards new horizons.

title: A Tradition of Tenacity, The Kitchen Maker Makes Waves at the 18ft Skiff World Championship
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A Tradition of Tenacity, The Kitchen Maker Makes Waves at the 18ft Skiff World Championship
summary: An embodiment of dedication, the team behind the long-term The Kitchen Maker sponsor's skiff reframed the narrative of determination and brought laurels with their remarkable endeavors at the 18ft Skiff World Championship.
body: Having been part and parcel of 18ft skiff racing's history for the past 91 years, tradition holds a place of reverence. Amidst this historical canvas, many daring sailors, with the aid of generous sponsors, have gloriously skimmed across the waters, captivated the spectating crowd, and written their names in the annals of the Australian 18 Footers League.

The team of Lachlan Steel, Jerome Watts and George Morton, sailing under the long-standing sponsorship of The Kitchen Maker, recently illustrated a saga of resilience and fortitude at the 18ft Skiff World Championship, the 2026 JJ Giltinan. Sailing in an intricate ballet with the winds and waves, they managed to secure a commendable 10th position in a fleet of 27 nautically proficient teams from six nations. Their journey to the championship saw them secure several top-10 finishes, including an agonizingly close second-place finish in Race 3.

George Morton, a familiar figure amongst the team, lent an invaluable amount of experience and know-how. After moving from Brisbane, he quickly clicked with the crew, adding a vibrant energy and forming a solid foundation for their campaign. A mere month was enough for the trio to gel so wonderfully and bring their A-game at the championship.

Every ripple they carved and every gust they tacked bore witness to their unwavering spirit and boundless energy. Their story serves as a testament not only to their love for the sport but also the unyielding support of their sponsors, ensuring that their legacy continues to sail through the waters of history.

title: Unveiling a New Class of Luxury: Four Seasons' 207m Yacht Liner Successfully Completes Maiden Journey
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unveiling a New Class of Luxury: Four Seasons' 207m Yacht Liner Successfully Completes Maiden Journey
summary: Four Seasons moves into the luxury yachting sector with its 207-metre yacht liner, Four Seasons I, after its dynamic maiden voyage.
body: Domineering the luxury yachting sector, the Four Seasons I, a monumental 207-metre ‘yacht liner’, has officially set sail and is setting new benchmarks in aquatic extravagance. The majestic vessel, built meticulously by Italian shipyard Fincantieri, pioneers a unique class, integrating aspects of superyacht design with the profound amenities typical of cruise liners.

First conceptualised in 2023, the distinguishing project has smoothly moved from blueprint to reality, with Mediterranean voyages already in progress. The vessel was deliberately structured to emphasise the guest experience, offering an all-suite, residential-style layout, devoid of interior-only cabins. Its many suites boast luxurious features, such as wide terraces and private plunge pools, providing an unparalleled experience.

The Four Seasons I comes equipped with 11 elegant restaurants and lounges, a wellness centre, full-service spa, including thermal suites, hydrotherapy and cryotherapy. A marina, which expands across the vessel's sides, offers an enticing platform for watersports and guest ingress when the vessel is anchored.

The management of the yacht's operations is executed deftly by Anglo-Eastern Cruise Management Inc. (AECMI), who have been an integral cog from the building phase till now. AECMI oversees every technical and regulatory facet of the yacht, including crew recruitment and training, and managing shoreside amenities like fuel procurement and voyage planning.

Embracing its hospitality roots, the Four Seasons is extending its revered land-based model to the seas, flaishing dozens of luxe sailings across the Mediterranean, Caribbean, and Bahamas in its inaugural year, introducing an all-new definition of aquatic luxury.

title: Tight Turnarounds and Global Travel Set the Stage for a Brutal Olympic Sailing Season
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Olympic Sailing 2027 Calendar Locked In as Gdynia Worlds and Lima Pan Am Clash Looms
summary: World Sailing confirmed key 2027 dates for Olympic two-person sailing classes, with Gdynia World Championships and Lima Pan American Games overlapping to create a demanding global schedule for elite sailors.
body: There are seasons in Olympic sailing — and then there are turning points.
2027 will be one of them.

With World Sailing confirming the key dates for the two-person Olympic events, the roadmap to Los Angeles 2028 has come sharply into focus. And with it, a logistical and competitive challenge that few athletes will navigate cleanly.
It’s a qualification year.
Gdynia: Where Olympic Dreams Take Shape
The centrepiece of the season will be the 2027 World Championships in Gdynia, running from 22 July to 1 August.
This is where the majority of Olympic qualification spots will be decided.
The event will bring together the full suite of Olympic two-person classes:
470 Mixed Dinghy Nacra 17 Mixed Multihull 49er (Men’s Skiff) 49erFX (Women’s Skiff)
For many crews, this will be the moment where years of preparation either convert into Olympic selection — or fall short.
A Collision Course with Lima
The Lima 2027 Pan American Games run from 23 July to 8 August — directly overlapping with the World Championships.
That creates a brutal reality for sailors competing on both circuits:
Race for Olympic qualification in Europe Then immediately relocate across the world to South America Reset, recalibrate and race again
Not optional.
The Compressed Timeline
To make it workable — just — Panam Sailing pushed its schedule as late as possible.
The final days of the Worlds look like this:
31 July – Medal Series (470 & Nacra 17) 1 August – Medal Series (49er & 49erFX)
Then the clock starts ticking.
3 August – Equipment Inspection (470 & Nacra 17) 4 August (AM) – Equipment Inspection (49er & 49erFX) 4–6 August – Elimination Series 7 August – Medal Series 8 August – Reserve Day & Closing Ceremony
That’s not a transition.
What This Means for Teams
This schedule forces hard decisions.
Prioritise Olympic qualification in Gdynia? Chase continental medals in Lima? Or attempt both — and risk underperforming in each?
For well-funded teams with depth, support staff and logistics backing, the challenge is manageable.
For others, it’s a real constraint.
Time zones, travel fatigue, equipment transport — all become performance factors.
And at this level, small margins decide everything.
Planning Becomes Performance
Panam Sailing has made one thing clear:
The schedule is now fixed.
Certainty matters — even if the conditions aren’t ideal.
Because preparation at this level isn’t just about sailing fast.
Logistics Recovery Equipment readiness And making the right calls before the first start gun The Bigger Olympic Picture
Beyond Gdynia and Lima, the wider Olympic cycle is beginning to take shape.
Olympic test events in Long Beach and San Pedro Additional Olympic class regattas Final qualification pathways
These will be announced later in 2026, adding further structure to what is already shaping up to be a compressed and high-pressure cycle.
2027 won’t reward hesitation.
It will reward:
Preparation Adaptability And the ability to perform under pressure, repeatedly, across continents
Because in Olympic sailing, it’s not just about being fast.
It’s about being ready — when it matters most.

title: Princess Yachts Achieves Impressive Reduction in Carbon Footprint Following Solar Power Integration
