Looking forward to the company’s sustainable future endeavours with anticipation.

title: A New Era for Spain's Yacht Charter System: Transitioning from Licensing to a Simpler Self-Declaration Process
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A New Era for Spain's Yacht Charter System: Transitioning from Licensing to a Simpler Self-Declaration Process
summary: Moving towards a simplified system, Spain has replaced its charter licence system for yachts with a self-declaration procedure, making it significantly easier for owners to charter in Spain.
body: In a welcome change for yacht owners, Spain has replaced its erstwhile charter licensing system with a simple self-declaration process. This move is part of an effort to simplify bureaucracy and promote chartering within the country over other popular Mediterranean destinations like France, Italy, and Croatia. The self-declaration system, a brainchild of the Spanish Yachting Association (ANEN), comes to light with the publication of the Royal Decree 186/2023 in the Official State Gazette, which approves the navigational maritime regulations. This effectively transfers the responsibility of ensuring compliance with local maritime regulations to the boat owners. While vastly reducing the wait time associated with the old licensing procedure, this measure requires captains to file and sign an 'Affidavit of Responsibility’, ensuring their possession of all requisite documents for chartering in Spain. Once presented to the Harbour Master Office, this affidavit authorises the boat to begin chartering within Spain's waters. Despite the simplification, the maritime regulations still mandate yacht owners to have valid technical certificates, crew documentation, mandatory insurances, and other certifications. Compliance with legal requirements remains stringent and maritime authorities possess the right to verify the 'Affidavit of Responsibility’ on demand. Any changes in the documented conditions or certificates must be promptly updated with the Port Authority through a new 'Affidavit of Responsibility’. This new system, however, doesn't apply to yachts applying for their first-ever authorisation. Until 2026, first-timers (regardless of whether the yacht flies the European Union or a third-country flag) will still need to follow the traditional procedure for ensuring their data is registered within the maritime administration’s systems. Post this first step, subsequent applications can utilise the new self-declaration system. This shift marks an unprecedented advantage for yachts previously engaged in charter activities within Spain. In conclusion, as intended, this new system simplifies the chartering procedure considerably, encouraging more boat owners to consider Spain as their preferred charter destination.

title: Swedish class J yachts, Svea and Rainbow, are Set to Face Off at the Superyacht Cup Palma Richard Mille in June 2026
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Swedish class J yachts, Svea and Rainbow, are Set to Face Off at the Superyacht Cup Palma Richard Mille in June 2026
summary: Witness regatta history unfold when the powerful Svea and newly tweaked Rainbow duel it out in the waters of the Superyacht Cup Palma Richard Mille.
body: Two emblematic J Class yachts, the ever-impressive Svea and the freshly spruced Rainbow, are preparing to cross swords at the milestone 30th anniversary of the Superyacht Cup Palma Richard Mille in June 2026.

Representing Sweden, Svea enters the contest as the stern favourite. This heavyweight of the yacht racing world built an impressive record, notching triple consecutive victories at the Maxi Yacht Rolex Cup between 2022 and 2024. The team also emerged victorious in the 37th America's Cup at the J Class Barcelona Regatta in 2024.

The Superyacht Cup represents a new phase for Rainbow and her new owner, Admiral's Cup victor Peter Harrison. The event marks Rainbow's first competitive race under the helm of Harrison, the CEO of Richard Mille EMEA. Richard Mille EMEA recently formed a three-year alliance with the Regatta, bolstering its position as Europe's longest-standing Superyacht Regatta.

Rainbow's Captain, Mat Sweetman, shared his enthusiasm for the upcoming contest, while emphasising the importance of preparation and reliability. The crew will conduct a comprehensive workout of the yacht's performance and systems before the race.

Svea will introduce new tactician, Tony Rey to the season’s regattas. Rey, based in Newport, is a veteran in globe-spanning yacht races and has prior experience with J-Class yachts. It all makes for a regatta event to remember, as these sailing giants get set for a battle on the blue.

title: Rare Opportunity: Baltic 77 'Black Pearl II' Ushers in a New Era of Sailing Splendour
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Rare Opportunity: Baltic 77 'Black Pearl II' Ushers in a New Era of Sailing Splendour
summary: The Baltic 77, 'Black Pearl II', presenting a meld of innovation and elegance, is set for new ownership.
body: The 'Black Pearl II' is not just any yacht; it's a statement of timeless elegance and cutting-edge performance. This Baltic 77, designed by Bill Tripp and featuring interiors by Rhoades Young, has been setting sailing standards since it was crafted in 2008. After undergoing a comprehensive refit in 2021, the sailboat is putting its best hull forward for its next custodian.

Characterized by Baltic excellence, the 'Black Pearl II' holds a pedigree that merges innovation with unrivalled luxury. Purpose-built for delivering impressive speeds, the sailing yacht is also designed for optimal cruising comfort, making it an ideal sea-going companion.

Thanks to its lifting keel, manoeuvring and anchoring the 'Black Pearl II' is a breeze. This fast cruiser is a dream vessel for experienced sailors and enthusiasts eager to explore shallow bays and coastal waters.

Designed artfully, its interiors showcase a refined, light, and contemporary style, complete with light-coloured woods, fabrics, and ambient natural light that illuminates the yacht. The accommodation can host up to six guests, each blessed with ensuite facilities, across the yacht's three spacious cabins. It also houses a handy, versatile study area that can convert into a child’s cabin.

The 'Black Pearl II' demonstrates that size doesn’t limit luxury or performance. As a yacht, it stands out as an elite example of both. Join in a new era of sailing splendour by making this high-performing, luxury Baltic 77 your own.

title: Ferrari Hypersail Unveils Livery, Merging Cutting-Edge Sailing Technology with Iconic Italian Design
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Ferrari Hypersail Unveils Livery, Merging Cutting-Edge Sailing Technology with Iconic Italian Design
summary: Milan Design Week witness to an unexpected revelation - Ferrari unveils the livery for its 100-foot ocean monohull, the Hypersail.
body: There's a new dazzler on the horizon to steal your sea-gazing attention - Ferrari Hypersail, unveiled in the pristine milieu of the Milan Design Week. Born of a creative process where the design philosophy of the Maranello based company meets cutting-edge offshore sailing technology, this breathtaking 100-foot ocean monohull is redefining the boundaries of maritime adventure.

What makes it exceptional you ask? Well, this beauty is not mere aesthetic but a direct consequence of function; a paradigm of the sublime union of design, innovation, and performance. Meticulously architected under the guidance of Matteo Lanzavecchia, Marco Guglielmo Ribigini, and naval architect Guillaume Verdier, Hypersail stands as a testament to Ferrari's unrelenting pursuit of innovation and aesthetics.

Solar panels, ingeniously blended into the deck and hull sides, represent another feather in Hypersail's hat. An advanced study of the solar exposure the Hypersail would experience during navigation determined their placement, allowing the vessel to harness renewable energy from the wind, sun, and motion. Maintaining technological and design sophistication, these integrated solar panels, walkable and grip-equipped, ensure maximum freedom of movement for the cruising crew.

In the words of Flavio Manzoni, Ferrari's Chief Design Officer, Hypersail was a complex but thrilling project that enabled the Ferrari Design Studio to step out of their comfort zone and apply their expertise in a different context. Result - a stunning convergence of style, technology, and performance, promising to transform the traditional blue-sailing experience into an amalgamation of thrill, luxury, and sustainability.

title: The Thrills of Palma de Mallorca and Its Superyacht Ecosystem: A Gathering of Luxury, Adventure, and Expertise
author: Old Sea Dogs

summary: Every year, the Western Med becomes a hotspot for superyacht enthusiasts, with Palma de Mallorca taking the lead. It's time to mark those calendars and prepare for an event like no other.
body: Every year, when the calendar turns to this particular season, the great migration to various yacht shows held across the Mediterranean region commences. From the MYBA Charter Show in San Remo to the Mediterranean Yacht Show in Nafplion, all aim to captivate the global charter market with a stunning array of yachts. However, the focus gracefully turns towards Mallorca.

Starting from the forthcoming Tuesday, a compelling itinerary of events illuminates the Western Mediterranean's popular superyacht hub – Palma de Mallorca. What sets this week in Palma apart is the readiness of everyone involved to engage, evolving one of the first real social meets on the calendar, particularly in the aftermath of the postponed Dubai Boat Show.

As the event unfurls, the highly-anticipated Mediterranean Superyacht Forum (MSF) captivates attention. Over the span of two days, a galore of closed sessions, open discussions, intriguing debates, and workshops occur. Attendees aren’t just spectators but active participants, offering their perspectives to intricate challenges and engaging in productive conversations.

After a keen deliberation at the Forum, attention shifts towards the charmingly informal Palma International Boat Show, a networking platform where stress is a foreign concept. Attendees are always seen relaxed and eager to engage in business talks. At this promising event, the most exciting part of the week, the forecast may seem unpredictable, but the mood is consistently marked by optimism and the familiar warmth of Palma.

title: Experience the Aquila 42 Coupé: An Elegant Powercat Pushing Boundaries of Speed and Efficiency
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Experience the Aquila 42 Coupé: An Elegant Powercat Pushing Boundaries of Speed and Efficiency
summary: Unveiling the Aquila 42 Coupé, a gravity-defying powercat, combining speed, efficiency, and luxury living in its innovative design and build.
body: Meet the Aquila 42 Coupé, a powercat that dares to challenge conventional boating norms with its inspired features. Born from customer demand for a boat offering shelter without the hassle of flapping canvases, this boat goes beyond expectations. Its distinguishing feature? A fixed hydrofoil system crafted from carbon-fibre, promising exhilarating speed and efficiency.

Aquila claims that pushing the boat to roughly 22 knots, then adjusting the hydrofoil angle by motor leg trimming, enables the hull to free up, thus pushing the speeds to an impressive 30-35 knots, all while reducing fuel consumption by a substantial 20% on each nautical mile.

Step inside the Aquila 42 Coupé and discover a spacious saloon that rivals the volume of a 50ft monohull. The absence of proper side decks helps accentuate the sense of space. The lounge is a generous expanse equipped with comfortable seating opposite the two-man helm. An extensive C-shaped dinette sits opposite the long L-shaped starboard galley.

Within its confines, the Aquila 42 Coupé hosts an ensuite bedroom in each hull, a squared-off forward lounge accessed through a bow door, and a three-section sliding aft patio door. This potent combination of features offers comprehensive integration of saloon and cockpit, while maintaining the boat’s inherent sense of space and luxury.

The Aquila 42 Coupé does come with a lofty price tag, mirroring its companion, Aquila 42 Fly. However, the steep cost underlines the emphasis on a robust, vinylester resin-infused structure that ensures speed without compromising on integrity or comfort. Venture into the future of sailing with the Aquila 42 Coupé - a powercat that challenges gravity and reshapes expectations.

title: The Struggles and Triumphs of the Great Boardroom Battle: KKCG Claims Ferretti's Helm
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Struggles and Triumphs of the Great Boardroom Battle: KKCG Claims Ferretti's Helm
summary: In an unprecedented battle, KKCG Maritime stands victorious at Ferretti; proposing Karel Komárek as chairman and retaining Alberto Galassi as CEO.
body: Behind the veil of corporate manoeuvring, a high-stakes powerplay unfurled at the prestigious shipyard of Ferretti. The move featured significantly when KKCG Maritime proposed a new lineup for Ferretti's board, which concluded with Karel Komárek as the proposed chairman. The climax of these strategic movements simultaneously saw the retention of Alberto Galassi as CEO. This saga comes in the wake of KKCG's voluntary partial tender offer on Ferretti, bagging just over 29.6 million shares - approximately 8.7% of Ferretti's total share capital. The penultimate result - KKCG holding around 23.248% of Ferretti's paid-in share capital. Nestled at the heart of the new board lineup is the diverse range of skills and experiences they collectively bring to the table. KKCG's nomination includes executive director Kamil Zeman and chief financial officer Katarína Kohlmayer – familiar faces from the maritime industry. Their desire for overwhelming control does not exist without reason. Ski mogul Komárek identifies Ferretti as a robust company possessing outstanding talent and a well-established management team. To his understanding, Ferretti has significant potential for strategic opportunity, long-term value generation, and improved capital allocation - only possible if the governance at the board level strengthens. Alongside him, Ferretti’s familiar faces - Piero Ferrari and Stefano Domenicali, also find their names on the KKCG slate. Eyes are also focused on the surprise appointment of Bader Al-Kharafi - The vice-chairman and group chief executive of telecom magnate Zain Group - whose involvement raises exciting possibilities for Ferretti's future. While KKCG Maritime has managed to helm the Ferretti shipyard with a hand firm on the tiller, it remains to be seen how they navigate through the storms and sunny days ahead for the company.

title: From 1920s Luxury to Electric Engine: The Incredible Transformation of an Antique Teak Canal Cruiser
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: From 1920s Luxury to Electric Engine: The Incredible Transformation of an Antique Teak Canal Cruiser
summary: A 1926 narrowboat with ties stretching to the start of the last century has been given a remarkable new lease on life, journeying from steam to electric power.
body: The saga of this remarkable narrowboat was born in the 1920s, a time when river and canal cruising were still rare indulgences. Charles Wadham Lyne, a vicar who incongruously hailed from a wealthy merchant family, discovered the joys of boating holidays while flicking through The Motor Boat magazine, a well-known periodical even in those early days of motorized nautical adventure.

As the vicar delved deeper into the world of boating, a parallel story unfolded in the life of Hugh Poths, another avid reader of The Motor Boat. Retiring from managing a rubber works company in Malaya, Poths arranged for a load of local teak to be sent back to England. His dream? To build his family a boat for cruising on their local rivers. Using his stock of teak from Malaya, Poths commissioned the construction of a boat designed for the delights and challenges of England's winding waterways.

Fast forward to the present day, and this incredible vessel is still afloat. Having swapped hands across generations, it now cruises under the power of an electric engine. This narrowboat, quite possibly the oldest surviving example of a cruiser intended as a leisure craft for the canal rather than a converted industrial barge, is testimony to the enduring appeal of leisurely waterway cruising.

As we power forward into the future, the antique narrowboat Malaya serves as a wonderful carbon-neutral nod to our nautical past. Its electric engine propelling it into a future where sustainability and tradition go hand in hand. The historical journey of Malaya from luxury indulgence of yesteryears to today's demonstration of sustainable innovation is a ride worth remembering.

title: Innovative 83-metre Feadship Superyacht Project Solent Begins Outfitting Voyage; Set for Summer 2027 Delivery
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Innovative 83-metre Feadship Superyacht Project Solent Begins Outfitting Voyage; Set for Summer 2027 Delivery
summary: Project Solent, the Feadship superyacht, embarks on an exciting journey for outfitting, marking a pivotal stage ahead of her delivery in the summer of 2027.
body: Feast your eyes on the breathtaking new images of the Feadship superyacht, Project Solent, as she bravely navigates the waters en route to outfitting. Shared by brokerage firm Cecil Wright, these captured moments mark an exhilarating milestone in her journey to becoming the crown jewel of the high seas.

From the NMC shipyard in Alblasserdam, Project Solent has sailed through Rotterdam to her next destination - the luxurious Feadship Royal Van Lent Facility in Kaag, the Netherlands. Ensuring a nod to both tradition and innovation, the yacht will undergo a meticulous process of outfitting under the watchful eyes of the industry's finest, until the eager summer of 2027 when she will be ready for delivery.

However, the creators remain tight-lipped about other specifics of this maritime marvel. What we can anticipate, though, is a positively grand volume of 2,707GT spread across four lavishly appointed decks.
As the journey towards the peak of perfection continues, we look towards the summer of 2027 with bated breath, waiting to welcome this majestic seafarer into her watery abode.

title: Diving Deep into the Yachting Industry: Exclusive Insights from Shipyard CEOs on Market Trends and Strategies
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Diving Deep into the Yachting Industry: Exclusive Insights from Shipyard CEOs on Market Trends and Strategies
summary: It's time to set a course and navigate through a sea of insights from the executives who helm the leading shipyards across Europe.
body: Who wouldn't want to know the nitty-gritty behind the yachting industry's market trends? Usually, it's brokers, project managers, consultants, or journalists who offer their predictions and analyses. But what about those who really helm the show? The shipyard CEOs? Tap into this goldmine of insights as nine CEOs from leading shipyards across Europe take us through their journey so far and the course ahead. These industry captains hail from an array of prestigious shipyards, including Royal Huisman, Damen Yachting and Feadship from the Netherlands, through to Palumbo, Sanlorenzo, Azimut Benetti, and Ferretti in Italy, and not to forget, Abeking and Rasmussen from Germany and Bilgin from Turkey. Their individual thoughts come together to provide a valuable diagnosis of the market and a clear picture of the new-build landscape. Despite some nuances, a convergence of thought is palpably evident. The past couple of years have seen a significant shift in how these yards operate. The new modus operandi features facility redesigns, digital tool incorporation, a strong collaboration between engineering and production, and a drive to eliminate late-stage revisions that would usually hobble new builds. Key constraints? Skilled labour. The challenge lies in finding the right people, training them, retaining them and ensuring the techniques that make these yachts extraordinary are passed on to the next generation. On poking and prodding about the future, these leaders reveal a market not teeming with explosive growth, but rather importance on quality, credibility and ability to meet the expectations of a new generation of owners who desire much more than the vessel itself. It's an era of experience-hungry owners whose motivations go beyond just owning a yacht to how they use it. Purpose, sustainability, and adventure are now ruling the design seas. Garnering insights straight from the horse's mouth, we delve into these market trends, challenges, and strategies which are defining the yachting industry today along with exclusive interviews by Conor Feasey, News Editor, with each shipyard CEO. Whether you're a prospective buyer, an interested observer, or just a sailing enthusiast, this comprehensive coverage of the industry is bound to hoist your knowledge and awareness to new levels.

title: The Luxurious Vintage Charm of the 35m Benetti Yacht 'Star of the Sea' Woos New Buyer
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Luxurious Vintage Charm of the 35m Benetti Yacht 'Star of the Sea' Woos New Buyer
summary: Star of the Sea, the vintage Benetti 35m motor yacht, has been sold to another poise lover of grand maritime elegance.
body: The impeccably styled, 35m vintage Benetti motor yacht, known as 'Star of the Sea,' is now in the hands of a new, fortunate owner. Replete with history, this splendid maritime masterpiece was originally built and delivered by the Italian shipyard Benetti in 1983; its design hailing from the same quarters.

Sporting a 'vintage' steel and aluminum build, Star of the Sea transformed its sheen thanks to major renovation in 2016 followed by a comprehensive $1,000,000+ revamp in 2024. Two decades under the ownership of 'Solafide', the yacht now heralds a new era under a fresh mantle.

The master cabin elegantly rests forward on the main deck, segueing into a formal dining room adjacent to the main saloon aft, perfectly partitioned with sliding doors. Gloss-varnished woodwork brightened with colorful upholstery adds a traditional spirit onboard.

The recent refit took care of installing essential plate updates, replacing through-hull valves and fresh carpeting throughout, along with a bow thruster replacement among other upgrades. The yacht further contributed to disaster relief activities during the La Soufriére volcano eruption in 2021.

Under the hood, the yacht boasts of twin 365hp Caterpillar diesel engines, supporting a top speed of 10 knots and a cruising range of 4,000 nautical miles at eight knots. The 'Star of the Sea' stands as a testament to both vintage charm and maritime elegance.

title: Sailing Sensations: Thrilling Regattas at Birkenhead and Warsash Bring Intrigue and Desirable victories
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Sailing Sensations: Thrilling Regattas at Birkenhead and Warsash Bring Intrigue and Desirable victories
summary: In the world of sailing, Birkenhead and Warsash regattas have become legendary for their thrilling races and challenging conditions.
body: Sailors all over the globe recently tuned their eyes and navigational senses towards two exciting events: the Jack Turner Trophy IOM Open 2026 at Birkenhead's renowned Radio Sailing & Power Club and the Warsash Spring Championship. Seventeen sailors competed for the illustrious Jack Turner Trophy. The day kicked off with a promising westerly breeze and sunlight glimmering on the water's surface. Racing got underway on time under the scrutiny of RO pair, Neil Westbrook and Dave Williams. The competition was intense, with Robbie Mac scoring the first victory, narrowly defeating Paul Plested and Graham Elliott. Interestingly, the start line was port biased during the day, shifting to an even field before returning. Brad Gibson shone with a remarkable run of three consecutive wins. The event also saw commendable performances from Roger Crates, Martin Roberts, Graham, and Paul Middleton, all of whom enjoyed a shot at the podium. Meanwhile, the Warsash Spring Championship Weekend on Solent's waters basked under the spring sun, where over 50 boats delighted in an outstanding weekend of racing. Saturday’s forecast of strong afternoon tide lived up to the hype and Sunday’s wind defied predictions by satisfyingly providing ideal sailing conditions with winds up to 10 knots. The competition was filled with surprises, and keen sailors navigated gusty winds with skill and sporting spirit. With these two thrilling marine events capturing the essence of adventure and seafaring, spectators and sailors alike look forward to more grand sailing tournaments.

title: Island Racing at Its Finest as Light Winds Tested the Fleet Around Tortola
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Round Tortola Delivered: Apollo and Airgasm Claimed the 2026 Nanny Cay Cup
imageCredit: © BVI Spring Regatta - Tidal Pulse - Andrea Azzopardi
summary: BVI Spring Regatta 2026 delivered a tactical Round Tortola Race, where shifting winds, course changes and tight corrected-time margins saw Apollo and Airgasm claim the coveted Nanny Cay Cup.
body: There are days in the British Virgin Islands when everything lines up.
And then there are days like this one.

The Round Tortola Race for the Nanny Cay Cup at the BVI Spring Regatta & Sailing Festival did not deliver brute-force trade wind sailing. Instead, it handed the fleet something far more demanding — light breeze, shifting pressure and decisions that actually mattered.
The race committee, reading the conditions early, adapted. Courses were shortened and reworked across classes, making full use of the islands that define racing in the BVI.
That’s the beauty of this place.
You don’t need marks when you’ve got Tortola, Peter Island and Dead Chest doing the job for you.
If there was a defining performance on the monohull side, it belonged to Apollo.
The J/121, helmed by Don Nicholson, didn’t get it right off the line — far from it.
“We were one of three boats over early,” Nicholson admitted, with the usual shrug that comes from experience. “And of course, the helmsman always gets the blame.”
But this wasn’t a start-line race.
This was a distance race, and Apollo did exactly what good boats do when things go wrong early — they reset, pushed hard, and sailed clean.

By the time they reached the closing stages, Apollo had fought back into contention, locked in a proper match-racing duel with the Club Swan 42 Lady M. Tack for tack, no room given, no mistakes tolerated.
On corrected time, Apollo edged out Panacea X by just over two minutes — a margin that tells you everything about the day.
This wasn’t dominance.
This was execution.
A Boat Rebuilt — and Now Delivering

The boat had missed the previous year’s regatta following serious damage sustained at the STIR Regatta. What followed was a near full-season rebuild — structural work, performance upgrades, and a rethink of the setup.
1,200 pounds removed Water ballast system stripped out Larger asymmetric sails added
It wasn’t just a repair job.
It was a reset.
Nicholson accepted the rating penalty that came with the changes — but out on the water, it paid back.
“The boat felt fantastic,” he said. “Upwind and downwind, the performance is there. It’s worth every bit of that penalty.”
Airgasm: Local Knowledge Meets Pure Speed
While Apollo took the monohull honours, the multihull side belonged to Airgasm.

Barney Crook’s Corsair 31-1D, sailed with the confidence that only comes from knowing these waters properly, delivered a clean and effective race to secure the Nanny Cay Cup in the Sport Multihull division.
There were faster boats on paper.
There always are.
But the Round Tortola Race has a habit of levelling that playing field.
You don’t win here on theory.
You win by:
Reading pressure Picking the right side of the islands And keeping the boat moving when others stall
Airgasm did exactly that.
Sophia: Speed in the Right Conditions
Out on the course, the Nigel Irens 63 Sophia once again showed flashes of outright pace.
Marcus Sirota’s trimaran, already one of the most talked-about boats of the regatta, pushed hard whenever the breeze allowed.
“I think we saw 24 knots on the other side of the island,” Sirota said. “Which we weren’t expecting.”
In typical Sophia fashion, the approach wasn’t rigid.
“We didn’t follow a strict plan — we just sailed the pressure.”
That’s often the difference.
Not overthinking it.
Just sailing what’s in front of you.
Sophia finished narrowly behind Ting-A-Ling II, separated by just seconds on corrected time — another reminder of how tight things had become.
Racing around Tortola isn’t just about speed.
It’s about geography.
Wind bends around headlands Pressure builds and disappears without warning Decisions made miles earlier suddenly matter
Chris Haycraft, Regatta Chairman, put it simply:
“Round Tortola has become a classic. Everyone loves it — and it’s not going anywhere.”
He wasn’t wrong.
Because races like this don’t rely on perfect conditions.
They rely on interesting ones.
Cruising and Bareboat: Close Racing, Same Story
Further down the fleet, the same pattern played out.
Tight margins. Local knowledge. And just enough chaos to keep things honest.

Libertas took the win in Performance Cruising, with a Tortola-based crew making the most of home advantage A family crew aboard a chartered IC24 delivered a standout second-place finish In the Bareboat fleet, Topaz edged out the competition in another close battle
Even here, nothing came easily.
Every class saw compression.
Every class saw opportunity.
When It Doesn’t Go Your Way
Not everyone made it.
Equipment failures claimed a handful of boats, including:
Thunder & Lightning, forced to retire after a jib failure despite a strong start Triple Jack, sidelined by structural issues Monster Project, also unable to continue
That’s offshore and coastal racing combined.
You don’t just race the fleet.
You race the boat.
The Bottom Line
No records were broken.
The benchmark set by Fujin still stood.
But that didn’t matter.
Tight racing Smart sailing And just enough unpredictability to reward the teams who stayed switched on
Apollo and Airgasm didn’t just win.
They earned it.

title: Thrilling Competitions Light Up 2026 Sailing Scene: Inside the Jack Turner Trophy and Henri-Lloyd Warsash Spring Championship
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Thrilling Competitions Light Up 2026 Sailing Scene: Inside the Jack Turner Trophy and Henri-Lloyd Warsash Spring Championship
summary: The 2026 sailing calendar sees intense competition as the Jack Turner Trophy sailed at Birkenhead and the Henri-Lloyd Warsash Spring Championship in Warsash showcase incredible talents.
body: The 2026 sailing season roars to life with the thrilling Jack Turner Trophy IOM Open at Birkenhead Radio Sailing & Power Club and the Henri-Lloyd Warsash Spring Championship. Seventeen sailors turned out for the second annual Jack Turner Trophy, greeted by a westerly breeze and intermittent sunshine. The early successes saw Robbie Mac, Paul Plested, and Graham Elliott leading the pack, while later victories belonged to Brad Gibson and Roger Crates.

A diverse event, the Jack Turner Trophy was not only about the racing. Sailors, spectators, and organizers alike enjoyed a variety of cakes and biscuits — mostly homemade — with complimentary tea and coffee in between the sprints. Thus, the event blended the competitive spirit of sailors with the cordiality of a community brought together by their shared love for the sea.

At both events, conditions varied wildly, even forcing competitors on occasion to retreat to the clubhouse when gusts became ruthless, but in the ever-shifting panorama of sailing, this is part and parcel of the excitement. In sailing, as in life, one must keep course, adjusting sails as winds dictate. This enduring lesson is beautifully underscored by the athleticism, grace, and resilience displayed across both championships.

In navigating the unpredictability of the open waters, both the Jack Turner Trophy and the Henri-Lloyd Warsash Championship have encapsulated the joy of being on the water and the thrill of competition. The victories celebrated, the friendships forged, and the stories shared have certainly set the pace for a thrilling 2026 sailing season.

title: Discover the Summer Cloud: A Caribbean Sloop That Reinforces the Essence of Sailing over Simply Being Fast
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover the Summer Cloud: A Caribbean Sloop That Reinforces the Essence of Sailing over Simply Being Fast
summary: Step into an exploration of the Summer Cloud, an iconic Carriacou sloop, where the value lies in its heritage and the emotional connections it represents, rather than just its speed.
body: The Caribbean was etched together by sail, many eons before the buzz of motorboats and aircrafts became the norm. The islands traded resources and narratives back and forth through the means of sailing crafts, their versions as unique and as characteristic as the islands themselves. The industrious sloops were vital components to island communication, effectively carrying people, goods, building materials, and stories from shore to shore. Among these deeply rooted traditions are the distinct Carriacou sloops, descendants of their tri-island namesake: the state of Grenada, comprising of Grenada, Carriacou and Petite Martinique.

Palmer's argument against a mass-produced, 'plastic boat', as he dubs them, is compelling. The depreciation and dismissive demand, he argues, is not comparable to a vessel like Summer Cloud. Its preservation is not simply a case of maintenance, it's a proactive attempt to keep a part of maritime history alive.

The Summer Cloud, for Palmer, is not just a seafaring vessel. It's an artistic impression of inheritance and responsibility. The wooden boats are pieces of art, differentiating them from plastic replicas. This sentiment resonates profoundly with Antigua Classics, where the honored vessels are never solely admired, but cared for, debated, repaired and revered.

Bryn Palmer is a man born of the sea, raised on the waves by his father – who constructed his own boat to cross the Atlantic and taught him the essentials of sailing. The Summer Cloud is not simply a boat but a testament to history, an embodiment of art, and a custodian of the seafaring spirit. This classic sloop sails not for the thrill of speed but the preservation of an inspiring maritime legacy.

title: From Gamble to Gem: The Riveting Tale of the Yawl Mah Jong
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: From Gamble to Gem: The Riveting Tale of the Yawl Mah Jong
summary: The allure of the 1957 Sparkman & Stephens 52ft yawl, Mah Jong, is astounding; it is a symbol of elegance and adventure.
body: With her perfect proportions and incredible pedigree, the Mah Jong is a yacht that commands attention. First gracing the seas in 1957, meticulously crafted by Sparkman & Stephens and brought to life by Cheoy Lee Shipyard, she sailed into the Antigua Classic Yacht Regatta in 2026, captivating lookers on with her elegance and charm.

But it was not just aesthetics that made the Mah Jong remarkable; it was also her intriguing origin story. The vessel was commissioned by three audacious American graduates, seeking to step off the beaten path and embark upon a world voyage. Notably, one of them was the grandson of the great inventor Alexander Graham Bell.

The choice of the name was also inspired by the trio's penchant for gambling. They adored poker, and true to their spirit, the yacht, like Bacharach, took on the name of a game of chance - 'Mah Jong'.

Constructed in the exotic Burmese teak, the Mah Jong exuded an effortless grace. Her interior brimmed with handcrafted details and a charm reminiscent of a bygone era. In essence, the Mah Jong was a fascinating combination of modest resources, extraordinary vision, and unyielding spirit of exploration. She was more than just a yacht; she was the embodiment of youthful audacity, chasing dreams on the endless sea.

title: High-intensity Trans-Atlantic Showdown in September to Showcase Best of Offshore Sailing World
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: High-intensity Trans-Atlantic Showdown in September to Showcase Best of Offshore Sailing World
summary: The Ocean Race Atlantic, scheduled this September, promises to spotlight the prowess of the IMOCA fleet, featuring an equal number of male and female sailors.
body: This September, the Ocean Race Atlantic is gearing up to showcase the might of the IMOCA fleet, in what is being touted as an intense transatlantic showdown. The inaugural event promises to bring together offshore sailing's finest, making their way from New York to Lorient, battling the waves and winds in a testament to seafaring agility and prowess

What sets this race apart is its gender-balanced crew format. Each crew, consisting of four members and one onboard reporter, will have equal representation of men and women, emphasizing the sporting world's gradual shift towards more gender inclusivity.

"It's a completely mixed crew race… which is really positive and I'm glad to be able to take part," says Justine Mettraux, a member of Germany's Team Malizia. The addition of more female sailors into the mix is a growing trend in recent editions of The Ocean Race.

Another significant aspect of the Race is its focus on sustainability and inclusion. Teams will contribute to ocean science and data collection. Similarly, the Ocean Live Park at Lorient will feature activities aimed at promoting youth participation and ocean literacy, demonstrating the power of diversity and opportunity.

"I'm very excited and happy to be competing in The Ocean Race Atlantic this summer. It's a format I love, as a way to really increase the opportunities for female sailors in our sport," shares Francesca Clapcich, a Team Francesca Clapcich skipper.

title: Exclusive: 50m Feadship Superyacht Koru Gets a €595,000 Price Drop
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Exclusive: 50m Feadship Superyacht Koru Gets a €595,000 Price Drop
summary: Ready to sail away at a lower price, the superyacht Koru by Feadship is now more appealing than ever after a significant price drop.
body: Big news in the superyacht world as the stunning 49.9-metre Feadship yacht, named Koru, experiences a hefty €595K markdown. This beautifully designed seafaring gem, boasting historical significance and contemporary sophistication, has received a price cut that's bound to make waves amongst discerning buyers. The brainchild of the late iconic designer Jon Bannenberg, and originally commissioned for billionaire tycoon Emilio Azcárraga, this extravagantly stylish vessel is something special indeed.

Originally built by the renowned Dutch yard Feadship, Koru emerged from an extensive two-year rebuild carried out by Ocean Technical. Delighting all who lay eyes on her with a new navy-blue hue, an extended stern, and a refreshed sundeck and interiors, this is a yacht that declares to the world its presence and poise on the azure oceans.

What's under the hood is just as impressive. Twin MTU engines, packing a combined 2950hp, give Koru a cruising speed of 19 knots, with the ability to reach a sprightly top speed of 22 knots. This is certainly an investment for anyone with a love for superyachts that combine the alluring charm of a noteworthy pedigree with the suave sophistication of modern luxury.

author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Stay Shielded from the Sun with Vaikobi's Cutting-Edge Ocean Performance Gear
summary: Introducing Vaikobi's innovative UV Ocean Tech gear - a protectants against harmful rays, designed for sailors, boat enthusiasts, and water athletes.

This line impressively models a marriage of protection from harmful ultra-violet rays and dressed-down comfort that lasts the entire day, both on and off the water. The result? A revolutionary approach to safe, sun-soaked boating adventures.

The UV Ocean Tech collection includes a long-sleeved top that offers light, moisture-wicking wear, and a long-sleeved hooded top that extends its protection to the head, neck, and body - essential against extreme heat conditions. Teleporting the sensation of having an air conditioner installed in your clothes, their UPF50+ rash top goes the extra mile in ensuring you stay cool under the scorching sun.

Vaikobi's UV Ocean Tech offers a combination of utility and comfort, reinforcing that safety doesn't compromise style - the ocean warrior's ultimate companion. This groundbreaking invention reinforces that stellar performances in extreme UV conditions are indeed possible, all while being protected and comfortable.

Whether you're a seasoned sailor, a yachting enthusiast, or a water sport athlete, Vaikobi's UV Ocean Tech collection champions a crucial message: Safety, comfort, and superior performance are essential in navigating the wide, sun-drenched seas.

title: Revolutionary Second 39m Swan 128 Maxi Yacht, Raijin, Unveiled by Nautor Swan: Ushering a New Era of Sustainable Sailing
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Revolutionary Second 39m Swan 128 Maxi Yacht, Raijin, Unveiled by Nautor Swan: Ushering a New Era of Sustainable Sailing
summary: Nautor Swan, the Finnish yard, proudly unveils Raijin, the second Swan 128 maxi yacht unit, boasting innovative energy management and unique design features.
body: Nautor Swan, a distinguished Finnish boatyard, has launched Raijin, the second yacht in the Swan 128 maxi yacht series. The 39-meter sailing yacht graced its birth waters in Pietarsaari, Finland, joining its predecessor BeCool, which saw a successful launch last year. Raijin, named after the Japanese god of thunder, lightning, and storms, showcases impressive design and technology enhancements from its predecessor.

Custom interior adaptations and an enhanced energy management system are some of the many changes seen in Raijin. Delivering on their vision of self-sufficiency at sea, Nautor Swan has developed a Dual Energy Technology in collaboration with energy technology company Danfoss. This advanced innovation optimises energy production and conservation, lowering fuel utilisation and emissions. Under sail, energy can be generated and stored for later use in electric propulsion and onboard systems, allowing a break from generator use while anchoring.

The Swan 128, according to Nautor Swan CEO Giovanni Pomati, symbolizes the pinnacle of their evolution. The model embodies the clean design lines, the comfort of its interiors and the broad application of innovative technologies. The commencement of this second hull with its Dual Energy Technology underlines their vision of completely self-sufficient sailing, and aims for an advance in nautical miles without depending on diesel engines.

Raijin is the second-largest model in Nautor Swan's range, placing just below the new 43.5-meter Alloy 44 series. It accompanies the 88, 98, 108 and 120 models in the fleet. Lucio Micheletti at Micheletti + Partners, the styling mastermind of the series, has curated a design that's lean, light and practical. Misa Poggi, who worked alongside Antonie Bertherat and Heini Gustafsson of the shipyard’s interior team on the second hull’s interiors, has chosen a polished palette of matte finish crown-cut oak.

title: A Big Surprise: Luxury Horizon Motor Yacht El Mirar II Receives a $750,000 Price Reduction
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A Big Surprise: Luxury Horizon Motor Yacht El Mirar II Receives a $750,000 Price Reduction
summary: The exclusive Horizon motor yacht El Mirar II, a 33.5-metre beauty, has received a significant $750,000 price reduction.
body: Step aboard the Horizon motor yacht El Mirar II, a vessel that pairs unmatched luxury with an impeccable pedigree - a combination that places it firmly in a class of its own. Now, this stunning yacht is making an even bigger splash as news just reached our shores that it has received a sizeable price cut. The El Mirar II, previously listed at an asking price of $3,950,000, has received a major $750k price reduction. This bold move sets the current asking price at a much more palatable $3,200,000.

El Mirar II can comfortably play host to eight guests across its four cabins, which include a full-beam master suite, a VIP cabin with a king-sized bed, a double cabin and a twin cabin, all complete with en-suite facilities. The yacht features an open-plan layout on the main deck, which flows gracefully from the main saloon into a dining area and a country-style galley. The sundeck boasts a central Jacuzzi with 360-degree views, shaded seating at the rear, and a helm station with clear sightlines.

With a cruising speed of 12 knots and a top speed of 17 knots, El Mirar II is more than a pretty face; she’s a formidable performer too. Add to this her shallower than usual 2.3 metre draught, which makes her well-suited to sailing regions such as the beautiful Bahamas, and you have a veritable sea wonder. The Horizon motor yacht El Mirar II, breathtakingly elegant and seamlessly blending technical prowess with luxury living - now available at an indeed 'un-tight-lipped' price.

title: Steeler Yachts Marks Yet Another Milestone, Announces the Sale of the Third Ocean Explorer 85 Yacht
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Steeler Yachts Marks Yet Another Milestone, Announces the Sale of the Third Ocean Explorer 85 Yacht
summary: Dutch shipyard, Steeler Yachts, has sold the third unit from its commendable Ocean Explorer 85 yacht series.
body: The renowned Dutch shipyard, Steeler Yachts, is making waves once again. It recently unveiled the third unit from its celebrated Ocean Explorer 85 yacht series. Famed as Project 511, this 26-metre prodigy is currently being expertly crafted at the company's Meppel facilities. The first yacht of the series, Aviso, became the flagship of Steeler Yachts upon its delivery last year. The second, Moss, embarked on sea trials in February and has received attention for its earthy green profile. Project 511 is being built on the foundations of its predecessors' successes, but with a wider beam of 6.9 metres for an added sense of grandeur and space. Steeler Yachts promises the same CE Category A standards, with the hull being constructed of robust steel, and a superstructure made of aluminium. The design of Project 511 has been left in the capable hands of Dutch designer Edwin van der Mark. At the helm of interior design is Kitty van der Kamp whose appointment promises sophistication and elegance. The layout of this yacht is customised to the owner's preferences, demonstrating Steeler's comittment to personalisation and luxury. Accommodation offers four lower deck suites, including a crew cabin for two, adjacent to a dedicated utility room. Meanwhile, the main deck has been cleverly designed around a convertible wheelhouse that can be opened towards the saloon, providing a seamless flow between internal spaces. Above deck, the flybridge has been built for comfort and versatility, equipped with a full wet bar, a sports area, and a lounge area at the fore. Steeler also promises to integrate its state-of-the-art high-low flybridge windows which enable the space to be either opened or enclosed depending on the desire of those onboard. The yacht is also fitted with twin MAN engines, ensuring power and reliability, allowing for a cruising speed of eight knots and a range far exceeding 4,000 nautical miles. This third 26m Ocean Explorer 85 yacht stands as a testament to Steeler Yacht's capacity for innovating unparalleled seafaring marvels.

title: Sailing Champions Take on Renowned Seas in the Next Leg of the Grand Slam Test, Riveting Hyères from Palma de Mallorca
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Sailing Champions Take on Renowned Seas in the Next Leg of the Grand Slam Test, Riveting Hyères from Palma de Mallorca
summary: The sailing Grand Slam continues in earnest as the premier 470 fleet sets sail from Palma de Mallorca, heading for the French Riviera's iconic sailing venue, Hyères.
body: The sun-kissed waters of Palma de Mallorca wave farewell as the renowned 470 fleet carves a course for the French Riviera. Their destination: Hyères, an iconic locale that has long been hailed as one of the most superb sailing venues in Europe. This Mediterranean beauty awaits them from the 18th to the 25th of April, set to host the French Olympic Week 2026 or, as it is internationally celebrated, the Semaine Olympique Française.

Defending champions, Germany's Simon Diesch and Anna Markfort maintain their formidable reputation in the sailing community. Hailing as victors from the previous year's event, their entry into Hyères brings an added edge to the competition, raising anticipation in great measures. The championship boasts 48 entries from 18 nations, presenting a global exhibition of supreme sailing prowess. Teams from Australia, China, India, among others, amplify the international echelon of the fleet, symbolising the global strength of the 470 class.

Hyères marks the second stop of the esteemed Grand Slam. With an arguably reduced but fiercely competitive fleet when compared to Palma, the athletes engage in a test of precision and performance under a spotlight of immense pressure. The Semaine Olympique Française presents a definitive challenge against the backdrop of notoriously demanding wind conditions synonymous with southern France. Undoubtedly, this will serve as the decisive test for both well-anchored leaders and up-and-coming teams eager to make an impression on the international stage.
For more details, visit their official website.

title: Discover the Sleek Baglietto Yacht 'New Master' with Exclusive Interior Upgrade Potential
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover the Sleek Baglietto Yacht 'New Master' with Exclusive Interior Upgrade Potential
summary: Step into the universe of luxurious water travel, with the Baglietto motor yacht 'New Master', now being offered for sale at a reduced price through Smart Yachts.
body: Indulge in the magnificence of Italian craftsmanship with the Baglietto motor yacht 'New Master', now available through the new central agency of Anastasiya Myslivets and Julia Skop from Smart Yachts. Originally crafted in 2001 in Baglietto's La Spezia shipyard, this beauty offers a captivating blend of aesthetic perfection and remarkable engineering.

Armed with a steel hull and an aluminium superstructure, New Master has consistently maintained an exceptional standard, thanks to the diligence of her only private owner. Owing to its never-been-chartered status, the yacht offers a certain exclusivity - a blank canvas ripe for an interior refit.

Coziness mingles with grandeur within the New Master, with interiors designed by Elisabetta Ruggiero, featuring delightful spots for relaxation and recreation. The main deck houses a stylish saloon, a dining zone, and a television area, while a skylounge sets the scene for an undisrupted view of the ocean on the upper deck.

Guests are spoilt for choice with numerous entertaining areas, including a Jacuzzi on the sundeck, sunbathing zones, and ample seating for reveling under the sky. Powered by twin Deutz TBD 620 V16 2,450hp diesel engines, New Master achieves top speeds of 17 knots, a cruising speed of 16 knots, and a travel range of 4,500 nautical miles at 12 knots. Zero-speed stabilisers ensure enhanced comfort, whether anchored or in motion.
Now offered for €7,000,000 inclusive of VAT, the charismatic New Master invites connoisseurs of luxury to indulge in a transformative water journey seldom experienced.

title: The Ultimate Brittany Adventure in a V50 – Expect Thrilling Sights, Leisurely Strolls, And Acomplex of Wonderful gastronomy
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Ultimate Brittany Adventure in a V50 – Expect Thrilling Sights, Leisurely Strolls, And Acomplex of Wonderful gastronomy
summary: Capture the essence of a thrilling journey through Southern Brittany in a Princess V50, where beguiling scenery melds with her culinary charm.
body: In a remarkable display of companionship and adventure, a group of zealous mariners on board a Princess V50 embarked on a thrilling journey from Guernsey to Morbihan. Their adventure was punctuated with visits to captivating locations, such as Vannes, Quiberon, Concarneau, Camaret and Roscoff, before making their way back to Guernsey.

Enjoying the superior thrill delivered by the V50's joystick and the impressive pull of its IPS drives and powerful bow thruster, the travelers were powered through their voyage with seamless choreography. As they proceeded, two additional sailors, David and Debra Corson, were welcomed onboard, livening up the journey with fresh perspectives and a comforting culinary touch. The V50 optimally catered to the new guests with its cosy cabins, each furnished with its individual en-suite facilities.

Dealing with a blustery gale, the team skillfully employed the V50's joystick control to exit Vannes smoothly. As the journey continued, another highlight came into view - Crouesty, an initially challenging mooring became a triumphant achievement thanks to swift complex coordination. The invigorating voyage ended with a scenic walk along the coast to Haliguen, featuring breathtaking beaches, delicious food and panoramic views of beautiful Brittany.

title: Unleash Your Nautical Longings With the Sleek and Luxurious Motor Yacht, Bise I
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unleash Your Nautical Longings With the Sleek and Luxurious Motor Yacht, Bise I
summary: The marvel of marine engineering, the 25.9-meter Delta motor yacht Bise I, has hit the brokerage market.
body: Boasting a breathtaking blend of powerful performance and luxurious design, the Delta 88 motor yacht Bise I has officially been listed on the brokerage market.\ With a length of 25.9 meters, this floating marvel was delivered by the Swedish company Delta Powerboats in 2020, and its construction was admirably handled by Luksusjaht AS in Estonia. The yacht's design features a lightweight carbon-fibre hull and superstructure, which was meticulously crafted by Lars Modin.\ Accommodation onboard the Bise I is composed of four cabins, including a full-beam master suite, a VIP cabin, and two twin cabins, providing space for up to eight guests. There are also designated areas for a crew of four, ensuring every onboard need is promptly catered to.\ The interior of the Bise I is heavily inspired by Scandinavian design, with heavy emphasis placed on natural light, visibility and high-end finishes. The main saloon is set in an open-plan layout and includes a lounge and dining area, facilitating an appealing sociable onboard environment.\ The exterior of the yacht is designed with ample opportunities for al fresco dining and relaxation, including a cockpit and deck layout suitable for entertaining and watersports.\ Powering the Bise I are triple Volvo Penta engines, delivering a combined 3000 horsepower. This impressive mechanical setup allows for a cruising speed of 26 knots, a top speed of 39 knots, and a range of approximately 300 nautical miles at 30 knots. The joystick controls provide precise manoeuvrability when docking and underway.\ Currently moored in Genoa, Italy, the Bise I is asking for €3,950,000. With its superb performance combined with its luxurious finishes and design, it stands as a testament to the adage that some dreams do come in boat form.

title: From Lake District to the High Seas: Teenager turns Parking Lot Epiphany into World Sailing Race Experience
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: From Lake District to the High Seas: Teenager turns Parking Lot Epiphany into World Sailing Race Experience
summary: An Average Tesco car park provides unlikely inspiration for a Lake District teenager's globetrotting sailing adventure in the famed Clipper Round the World Yacht Race.
body: William Wrigley, 19 years, from St Bees in Lake District, was an ordinary teenager with a big-moment dream. Now, he's fast-tracked his way from novice to ocean racer as he preps to sail from Seattle, all the way to the UK, in the final legs of the famed Clipper Round the World Yacht Race.

This race is no ordinary feat. It stands as the only event of its kind, taking people of different walks of life and transforming them into competitive ocean racers, no matter their sailing credentials. Led by experienced skippers and a competent first mate, the crews sailing 70ft purpose-built yachts around the world follow a route broken down into eight legs. Engaging as a full team or partial crew members, participants dive into an adventure that's nothing short of extraordinary.

Before setting sail, all race participants are required to complete four levels of comprehensive training, run by expert instructors from the race's headquarters in Portsmouth, UK. This intensive training equips crew members with the skills needed to weather any sea conditions, ranging from tranquillity to storm-like conditions. And it's not only the sailing part; this drill educates the participants about everything from on-board living to dealing with unlikely challenges like large-scale catering.

This gap year sailing adventure definitely proved a marked learning curve for William who, despite being far away from home and dealing with minute details, embraced the challenge with enthusiasm and was ready to embrace the rushing waves and exciting winds that came his way.

title: ISA Yachts Achieves Major Milestone with the Sale of the Third Unica 45M Steel Superyacht
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: ISA Yachts Achieves Major Milestone with the Sale of the Third Unica 45M Steel Superyacht
summary: Italian boat manufacturer ISA Yachts has confirmed the sale of its third Unica 45M Steel luxury yacht to an American client.
body: Revolutionising the world of luxury sailing, Italian shipyard ISA Yachts recently announced the sale of the third yacht in its Unica 45M Steel series to an American client. Drawing upon advanced shipbuilding techniques, the Unica 45M Steel series has been designed to cater to a new breed of modern sea adventurers seeking the perfect blend of comfort, performance, and aesthetics.

Each of the Unica 45M Steel yachts boasts of a high displacement, steel hull and a staggering fuel capacity of over 60,000 litres. The designers have prioritised luxury and convenience, seen through the careful attention to the vessel's stern designed over three descending levels, replete with sunbathing areas, a pool and an infinity cockpit.

The stand-out features of the yacht include a 16-meter-long sundeck, a lounge with sofa seating and armchairs, a dining table, a bar, a gym, formal dining area, and a stylish jacuzzi. The master suite has a private lounge, a vanity desk, a walk-in wardrobe, and a luxurious bathroom, while four other cabins are situated on the lower deck.
Equipped with twin Caterpillar C32 engines, the superyacht boasts an impressive range of 4,000 nautical miles at 10 knots, and can reach maximum speeds of 15 knots.

With this latest sale, ISA Yachts continues to be at the forefront of innovation in the yacht manufacturing industry, with an impressive 14 yachts currently under construction or on order, including the first unit in its all-new Viper 130 series. The advanced design concepts and luxurious amenities of the Unica 45M Steel series truly redefine industry standards, captivating modern yacht owners with their customisability, comfort, and powerful performance.

title: Unveiling the XF80: Voodoo Yachts Reveals Natural Evolution of Its Luxury Yacht Line
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unveiling the XF80: Voodoo Yachts Reveals Natural Evolution of Its Luxury Yacht Line
summary: Voodoo Yachts steps ahead in the yacht-making industry, announcing significant details about its newly conceived XF80 model.
body: From the thriving shipbuilding milieu of New Zealand comes an exciting revelation, the first revealing details of Voodoo Yachts' fresh in-build project: the XF80. Extending beyond the boundaries that defined its smaller XF75 platform, the XF80 presents itself as a palpable evolution, offering expansive living areas, both inside and out. Characterised by an athletic profile, a bold hull, and a more extensive deck area, the XF80 promises a refined experience at sea.

True to Voodoo Yachts' commitment to swift and efficient sailing, an essential aspect of this stunning 23.9-meter model lies in its unprecedented ability for guests to voyage both farther and faster, all while ensuring minimal environmental impact. This characteristic shines in the model's Super Sport Edition with its high top speed over 50 knots, cruising speeds up to 40 knots, enabled by powerful engines, modern hydrofoil systems, and optimised weight engineering.

The yacht's interior echoes a bright and contemporary ethos, defined by considered lines and tactile materials, encapsulating a calm, sophisticated atmosphere. Accommodation options span a full-beam master suite, with flexible arrangements for up to five ensuite guest cabins or four guest cabins supplemented by dedicated crew quarters.

Voodoo Yachts asserts that the XF80 model represents a natural progression, an elevation of the XF75's proven strengths across every dimension - space, capabilities, and refinement. The important goal - to provide yacht owners and their guests with a higher level of freedom amplified in this ultra-modern, luxurious model - appears to have been notably achieved.

title: Clean Sailors & Circular Flow Forge Alliance, United against Wetsuit Waste
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Clean Sailors & Circular Flow Forge Alliance, United against Wetsuit Waste
summary: Clean Sailors, the initiators behind the trailblazing ReSail platform, has joined forces with Circular Flow, a pioneer in neoprene reuse solutions.
body: Eradicating marine pollution is no small feat, and collaboration is the winning strategy. This belief is displayed by Clean Sailors, the force behind the pioneering ReSail platform, as they announce an exciting partnership with Circular Flow, a vanguard in the realm of neoprene reuse solutions. This association extends the ReSail platform's global reach; it provides an avenue for sailors to be accountable by not only appropriately disposing of their expired sails, but their old wetsuits and neoprene gear as well.

The innovative ReSail platform is a global digital map pinpointing locations where old sails can discover new purpose. Given the current lack of a formal recycling structure for these complex nautical textiles, this platform is a godsend, linking sailors with organisations capable of granting these materials a second wind.

Holly Manvell, the founder of Clean Sailors, expresses that collaborating with Circular Flow is a natural progression in the ReSail journey. Both groups are driven by the core objective of addressing crucial waste and pollution issues while empowering ocean lovers to make more sustainable decisions. In broadening the scope of the ReSail platform, Clean Sailors continues to make strides in promoting practical sustainability solutions within the sailing community and beyond, providing an opportunity for sailors to support the growth of circular businesses.

title: How the New Digital Schengen Immigration Entry/Exit System Impacts Non-Schengen Nationals Giving Up Manual Stamping
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: How the New Digital Schengen Immigration Entry/Exit System Impacts Non-Schengen Nationals Giving Up Manual Stamping
summary: A major digital shift tides over Europe's immigration systems as non-Schengen nationalities' passports will no longer be manually stamped.
body: April 10, 2026, marked a significant shift in the Schengen immigration system. The era of manually stamping passports was replaced by a more sophisticated, digital Entry/Exit System (EES) for non-Schengen nationals. This European database captures the border crossing data of non-EU and non-Schengen area nationals venturing into the Schengen Zone.

Since its gradual implementation from October 12, 2025, and becoming fully operational, the changes stirred waves of questions. The Professional Yachting Association (PYA) took it upon itself to clarify the situation for non-Schengen nationals joining a crew in a Schengen port. In collaboration with French immigration administration officials, they managed to chart the waters of this new technological journey.
Further, the European Travel Information and Authorization System (ETIAS) for non-visa nationals will implement towards the end of 2026.

Upon entering the Schengen area, tempering the course of the digital fog may seem intimidating due to the withdrawal of visible evidence of legality. After all, only customs, immigration, and border police have access to the digital system. Hence, it is encouraged for all non-Schengen nationals to maintain a record displaying their Schengen entry and exit dates to circumnavigate potential misunderstandings and legal hassles.

This digital uplift places increased responsibility on the individuals. Breaching the stay limit could yield serious repercussions, such as being denied re-entry or necessitation to stay outside the Schengen area for 90 days before another short stay.
Despite some apprehensions, this digital transformation aims for increased efficiency in managing immigration, sailing the waves of modernity and progress in these rapidly changing times.

title: Exploring SF Marina's Burgeoning Projects in Anguilla and Panama: An Inside Look at Port Nimara and Port Amador
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Exploring SF Marina's Burgeoning Projects in Anguilla and Panama: An Inside Look at Port Nimara and Port Amador
summary: The leading marina design company, SF Marina, is disrupting the game with new visionary projects in Anguilla and Panama.
body: SF Marina, established in 1918, is a frontrunner in marina design. Celebrated for its advanced floating breakwaters and concrete docks, the company propels its vision forward with two ambitious projects - Port Nimara in Anguilla and Port Amador in Panama.

The CEO of SF Investments and the driving force behind the development, David Mizrahi, shed light on these projects. Starting with Port Nimara, located on the beautiful island of Anguilla, Mizrahi elaborated on the strategic selection of the site. Tucked away in a secluded area, away from busy resorts, and nestled between renowned luxury resorts of Cap Juluca and Altamer Villas, Port Nimara capitalises on its prime location. It seeks to offer a unique and effortless experience for visitors.

With an uptick in yacht traffic in recent years, the Caribbean has seen an increased demand for marinas. Anguilla, lacking a marina until now, presents an ideal prospect for meeting this demand. A notable feature of Port Nimara is that it is being built on private land. This implies that berth owners can buy the berths outright, a rarity in a region where berths are usually offered as 30- to 50-year concessions that tend to depreciate over time.

Private ownership also promises long-term security and offers the potential to generate revenue through rent when not in use. The objective, Mizrahi highlights, is to link the three distinct jurisdictions of St Martin, St Barths and Anguilla - making the most of each one's diverse offerings.

Additionally, Mizrahi emphasises the importance of understanding the marine world, instead of considering marinas as mere real estate projects. Port Nimara, he assures, would feel like a lifestyle hub, offering an array of activities for guests, from hiking and tennis to golf at the nearby Greg Norman-designed course at Aurora Anguilla Resort & Golf Club. Sailboat racing - Anguilla’s national sport - will also hold a prominent place, truly heralding a new era in marina design.

title: Tideway 80th Firefly Nationals Impresses by Expanding Entries to 120 After Initial Capacity Crushed by High Demand
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Tideway 80th Firefly Nationals Impresses by Expanding Entries to 120 After Initial Capacity Crushed by High Demand
summary: Tideway 80th Firefly Nationals gears up to deliver an outstanding celebration by raising the entry limit to 120 boats, following the overwhelming demand.
body: The Tideway 80th Anniversary Firefly Nationals at Tenby Sailing Club is shaping up to be a landmark occasion. Owing to the tremendous demand, the National Firefly Association (NFA) and Tenby Sailing Club have agreed to increase the entry limit for the championships to 120 boats. This illustrates the dynamic enthusiasm around the event, with the current number of confirmed entries already at 100. With such momentum, it appears that the fleet will reach its full potential well before the commencement of the August event.

This momentous gathering of boats underscores the value and appeal of the Firefly Nationals. Tideway's combination of competitive racing and welcoming social scene nurtures a vibrant community linked by passion and shared experiences. Furthermore, the vibrant UK University Team Racing scene attests to the universal lure of these events.

To add further excitement to the anniversary event, the NFA has organized a lottery where each participant could win Firefly F4444, a race-ready boat built by Ovington Boats Ltd. On top of the boat, the prizes include Selden spars, Hyde Sails, and covers, and a Sailboat Trailers launch trolley.

Located in the picturesque Pembrokeshire coast, Tenby Sailing Club is an idyllic location for the championships. Nearby camping is also available at the Tenby Rugby Club, offering a whole experience for everyone partaking in the illustrious event. The dedication, enthusiasm, and camaraderie apparent in the Tideway 80th Firefly Nationals showcases the compelling world of sailing and promises an unprecedented event.

title: From Birmingham to the Solent: RYA Targets Untapped Talent in Bold Inclusion Drive
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: WaveMakers Expands to Portsmouth as RYA Pushes to Redefine Sailing’s Talent Pathway
summary: Royal Yachting Association launched WaveMakers in Portsmouth, expanding access to sailing’s talent pathway and opening doors for young sailors from under-represented communities to progress into elite competition.
body: For decades, the pathway into elite sailing has been clear — but not always accessible.
Now, the Royal Yachting Association is taking another step to change that.

The expansion of its WaveMakers programme into Portsmouth marks more than just a new location. It signals a deliberate shift in how talent is found, supported and developed across British sailing — with a focus on potential, not privilege.
Working in partnership with the Andrew Simpson Foundation, the programme is designed to identify young sailors who might otherwise never reach the start line — let alone the podium.
WaveMakers didn’t appear overnight.
It was born out of the RYA’s Pathway Review — a clear-eyed assessment of where talent was being missed, and why.
Too many capable young sailors were being lost before they even had a chance.
Barriers weren’t always about ability. They were about:
Cost Access to facilities Confidence Lack of exposure to the sport
The Birmingham pilot, launched in 2024 and supported by Sport England and SportsAid, proved something important.
When those barriers are removed — talent appears.
And it appears quickly.
The move to Portsmouth is not accidental.

Based at the Andrew Simpson Centres, the new site places WaveMakers at the heart of one of the UK’s most active sailing regions — with direct access to the Solent, world-class conditions, and a culture built around performance.
But this isn’t just about geography.
A stronger focus on foiling and board disciplines A pathway into Olympic classes such as iQFOiL Exposure to higher-performance sailing environments
While Birmingham continues to develop dinghy sailors and transition them into youth classes, Portsmouth pushes the next step — speed, precision and modern Olympic sailing.
More Than Talent Identification
WaveMakers is not a one-off initiative.
It’s a structured pathway.
Community outreach Talent identification Year-round coaching Financial and logistical support Transition into elite development systems
And critically — it works with families and communities, not just individuals.
Because if you don’t build trust around the sailor, you don’t keep the sailor.
A Long-Term Play — With Clear Targets
This isn’t vague ambition.
Selection into the British Sailing Youth Team within four years Podium finishes at Youth Nationals within five years Consistent progression into Talent Academies
That’s not participation.
That’s performance.
Changing What the Sport Looks Like
Nick Scott, RYA Director of Sport, put it plainly:
WaveMakers is about ensuring sailing reflects modern Britain — not just historically, but going forward.
The aim is not just to find talent.
It’s to change who sees sailing as an option in the first place.
Richard Percy of the Andrew Simpson Foundation reinforced that message: This is about creating real opportunity — not just opening the door, but helping people walk through it.
Sailing has always been a sport of skill, judgement and resilience.
But access has often been uneven.
WaveMakers is an attempt to correct that — not by lowering standards, but by expanding the pool of people who can reach them.
And if it works, the long-term impact is bigger than medals.
It’s cultural.
New pathways New role models And a sport that looks more like the society around it What Happens Next
The Portsmouth programme is expected to begin onboarding its first sailors around Easter, with recruitment focused on connecting directly with local communities.
That’s where this either succeeds or fails.
Not in press releases.
But in who turns up — and who stays.
