But in who turns up — and who stays.

title: Serena Woodall and Lena Sanderson Join Emirates Team NZ in Preparation for 38th America's Cup
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Serena Woodall and Lena Sanderson Join Emirates Team NZ in Preparation for 38th America's Cup
summary: Emirates Team NZ is bolstering its ranks with two fresh talents, Serena Woodall and Lena Sanderson, ahead of the prestigious Louis Vuitton 38th America’s Cup.
body: A force to be reckoned with on the international sailing circuit, Emirates Team NZ, is set to surge even stronger in the upcoming America's Cup. The team has drafted in two formidable talents, Serena Woodall and Lena Sanderson, both jumping ship to full-time spots in the squadron. Their skills and passion are expected to turbocharge the team’s Women’s America’s Cup campaign while infusing fresh energy into the wider sailing squad.

Andy Maloney, the team's coach, has been instrumental in this vibrant recruitment. He praises the duo's swift adaptation to the rabid learning curve of the team's training regime, including the AC40 sailing schedule - their feel onboard was 'intuitive from the get-go'.

At the heart of their training lies technical proficiency with the AC40, a specialized equipment designed to help the skilled sailors fully exploit its power. This focus on technology, and the simulator that supports it, is carving out powerful pathways for youth and women sailors leading into this exciting new era of the America’s Cup.

The transition into competitive sailing has begun, and with the wind direction looking favorable, the journey of these new integral crew members promises to inspire many more sailing stories in the days ahead.

title: Indulge in Maritime Elegance with the Resplendent 39 Metre CERVO, Ready to Conquer New Horizons
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Indulge in Maritime Elegance with the Resplendent 39 Metre CERVO, Ready to Conquer New Horizons
summary: Imbued with Dutch heritage, the 39-metre performance-focused CERVO, a brainchild of Vitters, brings new levels of luxury and performance to the sailing world.
body: Launched in 2009 by the respected Dutch shipyard, Vitters, the agile and exquisite CERVO has since undergone extensive refits as recent as 2024/25 at Pendennis Vilanova, Spain. No stranger to transformations, she has also benefited from a comprehensive overhaul at Pendennis in 2018 and Orams in 2022, upholding her status as a seaworthy marvel.

A product of the visionary minds at Tripp Design Naval Architects, this sleek vessel is constructed with a Green Marine carbon composite hull. This advanced composite construction not only ensures the delivery of robust durability but also contributes to a lighter weight build which optimises performance.

The interior, a masterstroke by Nauta Yachts Design, exudes a comforting and contemporary charm. It caters elegantly to up to 8 guests, with an accommodating crew of five set in three separate cabins. Thus, promising an intimate, yet efficiently serviced sailing journey to the sea explorers aboard.

She's further equipped with a high-performance carbon rig from Southern Spars, outfitted with future fibre's EC6 rigging. Bolstering her sailing prowess, these facets coupled with her generous beam of 8.4 m, make for spacious deck spaces conducive for outdoor lounging and social entertaining. Add to that her long-range capacity as demonstrated by her fuel capacity of 12,500 litres and water capacity of 10,000 litres, it's clear that CERVO is poised for extended sea adventures with ease and class.

Seizing the helm of CERVO and setting sail toward the endless horizons is an invitation to experience the pinnacle of nautical luxury and performance. Whether exploring untouched beaches or hosting elegant evenings under the stars, aboard CERVO, every moment is a taste of the high sea life.

title: Jack Mahoney Unveils Turbocharged Superyacht Selling Model with Boathouse Auctions
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Jack Mahoney Unveils Turbocharged Superyacht Selling Model with Boathouse Auctions
summary: In the elusive and often sluggish world of superyacht sales, a revolutionary new model is taking centre stage, spearheaded by Jack Mahoney of Boathouse Auctions.
body: Traditionally, selling a superyacht has been synonymous with a slow, expensive process. Owners often watch their prized sea vessels lingering on the market while the mounting expenses eat away at the vessel's value. However, a fresh player in the field, Boathouse Auctions, offers an excellent alternative: a streamlined and limited-time approach designed to rev up sales, cut down on carrying costs, and pave a quicker, more efficient path to immediate liquidity.

This innovative model, spearheaded by founder Jack Mahoney, is already transforming the superyacht sales landscape, redefining owner expectations, and proving that, in the current climate, auctions can actually make sound financial sense. Boathouse Auctions stands as a testament to this excellent blend of speed, efficiency, and commercial acumen.

title: Indulge Your Nautical Fantasy: Four Unbelievable Yachts That Deliver Pure Seafaring Pleasure Under £50,000
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Indulge Your Nautical Fantasy: Four Unbelievable Yachts That Deliver Pure Seafaring Pleasure Under £50,000
summary: Owning a boat doesn't have to be a flight of fancy. Discover four affordable yet substantial entry-level yachts that combine comfort with adventure.
body: Price tags often scare potential buyers away from owning a boat due to the general perception, but cost shouldn't steal your seafaring dream. On the contrary, £50,000, which wouldn't bag you a top-of-the-range Honda Civic nowadays, could be your gateway to owning a yacht. Some remarkable models available for less than this amount promise unrivalled adventure, freedom, and fun.

One of these star yachts is the Sea Ray 200 Overnighter, built in 1991 and priced at £8,950. Famed for its impressively practical and good seakeeping attributes, it offers a one-of-a-kind combination of affordability and functionality. With a large vee-shaped double bed, ample space for two, and its relatively limited headroom, it's the perfect choice for those craving the thrill of 'camping' on water. Its design optimises space in the cockpit, making it perfect for sun lounging.

These yachts grant owners a chance to navigate the water without the deep pockets that are often associated with yacht ownership. Whether you dream of tranquil moments on the water by sun-down or the exhilaration of speed sailing, affordable yachts like the Sea Ray 200 Overnighter provide opportunities for unforgettable marine adventures. Embrace boating with all its fuss and expense, for it comes with unparalleled access to freedom, joy, and escape, proving that the glass isn't half empty or half full—it's simply larger than it needs to be!

title: Trade Winds, Tight Racing and Rum on the Lawn as Antigua Launches Its New Regatta
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Antigua Racing Cup 2026: A New Chapter Begins in Nelson’s Dockyard
summary: The inaugural Antigua Racing Cup launched from historic Nelson’s Dockyard, bringing international crews, steady trade winds and four days of high-performance racing to the heart of Caribbean sailing.
body: There are places that host regattas.
And then there are places where sailing actually belongs.
Nelson’s Dockyard is firmly in the second camp — and in April 2026, it added a new story to its long, salt-stained history with the arrival of the inaugural Antigua Racing Cup.

From 9–12 April, crews from more than 15 nations gathered beneath the old stone walls and timbered galleries of this UNESCO World Heritage Site — the world’s only working Georgian dockyard — to kick off what feels less like a new event, and more like something that has simply been waiting its turn.
Because Antigua doesn’t try to be a sailing capital.
It just is.
When the Caribbean decides to turn it on, it doesn’t do things by halves.
The trade winds were in. Easterly. Reliable. Proper.

10–15 knots across the racecourse, with gusts nudging 20 — just enough to keep crews honest without turning it into survival mode. Warm water, warm air — both hovering around 28°C — meant lightweight kit, spray flying, and boats moving the way they were designed to.
Three races were scheduled to open the series — tight, technical, and run on some of the most consistent sailing water anywhere in the world.
No excuses. No hiding.
Just racing.
Back ashore, the tone was set early.

The Skippers’ Briefing, led by Racing Manager Jaime Torres at the Copper & Lumber Store Hotel, carried that familiar mix of focus and anticipation — crews half-listening, half-already racing the course in their heads.
Then the shift.
From race mode to island mode.

The Event Lawn filled quickly as the Regatta Opening Party got underway. Cold Amstel in hand. English Harbour Rum doing its job. A steel pan carrying the anthem across the harbour as the sun dropped behind the rigging.
It wasn’t forced.
It never is in Antigua.
This is how they welcome sailors.
There’s a difference between adding another regatta to the calendar… and building something that matters.
The Antigua Racing Cup sits right at the front of a carefully structured Caribbean sequence — one that now defines April sailing in the region:

Antigua Racing Cup (9–12 April) — high-performance, competitive racing Antigua Classic Yacht Regatta (15–19 April) — tradition, heritage, elegance Antigua Sailing Week (22–26 April) — reimagined, destination-driven racing
Three events. One island. Different flavours of the same obsession.
This isn’t overlap.
It’s strategy.
This first edition wasn’t about numbers.
It was about intent.
Antigua understands something many venues are still catching up with:
Sailing has changed.
Crews want:
Proper racing Proper venues And something worth staying for ashore
The Antigua Racing Cup delivers all three.
It adds energy at a key point in the season. It keeps teams on the island longer. And it strengthens Antigua’s position as the beating heart of Caribbean sailing.
The Fleet — Writing the First Chapter
That moment where the first boats cross the line, and suddenly it’s real.
The sailors who lined up for this first Antigua Racing Cup aren’t just competitors — they’re the ones who wrote the opening page.
Get off the line clean. Sail fast. Stay sharp.
And when it’s done — head ashore and do it properly.
You can tell when something is going to stick.
It’s in the way the dock feels at night. The way crews talk about the racing — not the parties. The way nobody’s in a hurry to leave.
The Antigua Racing Cup has that feel.
Not loud. Not forced.
Just right.
And if the wind keeps blowing the way it did this week — this won’t stay “new” for long.

title: Meet Toby Allies, The Man Spearheading Pendennis's Refit Strategy and Solidifying the UK's Position in Global Yachting
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Meet Toby Allies, The Man Spearheading Pendennis's Refit Strategy and Solidifying the UK's Position in Global Yachting
summary: Toby Allies, Managing Director of Pendennis Group, sheds light on the company's refit-centric strategy, workforce investment, and international growth amidst shifts in the global superyacht sector.
body: The UK’s stature in global superyacht construction is evolving. Leading the way is Pendennis, the British yard known for its refit strategy, incessant workforce investment, and international growth. Anchored by Toby Allies, the Group's Managing Director, Pendennis is shifting gears despite a softer new-build yacht output, firmly instituting its place as a refit centre of excellence. Allies accentuates the UK's enduring prowess in service, design, and OEM supply, with Pendennis ‘‘punching well above our weight.’’

Meriting its status through investment in people and facilities, Pendennis aims at strengthening its position in the long-term by responding to the increasing number of yachts requiring refits. It continues to churn out custom new-build projects as well, with notable recent additions including the 34.9-metre Fox (2024) and 39.4-metre Halekai (2020).

According to Allies, newer segments and the increasing demand for lifecycle modernisation for yachts built 20 to 30 years ago are contributing to the group's growth. Moreover, despite pressure on pricing, delivery, and labour availability, Allies is confident that Pendennis’s differentiation lies in their people. He lauds the team's proven skill on intricate, award-winning projects and the value they attach to long-term client relationships.

Investment in infrastructure remains a central theme. Allies cites recent developments such as a digital manufacturing centre that integrates 3D scanning and Computer Numerical Control (CNC), enabling them to handle up to 12 projects yearly in Falmouth.

In an increasingly competitive global refit market, the efforts of the Pendennis Group show how a focus on refit strategy, employee development, and facility advancement can navigate industry shifts and firmly establish the UK's competitive position in the world yacht domain.

title: Master the Rough Waters: Your Essential Guide to Assembling your 2026 Sailing Race Kit
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Master the Rough Waters: Your Essential Guide to Assembling your 2026 Sailing Race Kit
summary: Get set for the new sailing season with tips on assembling your race kit, tailored to your sailing preferences and various sea conditions.
body: With the sailing season around the corner, now is an ideal time to review your racing kit. Diligently checking the existing gear, understanding the roles each item plays, and replacing worn-out equipment are surefire ways to ensure a successful sailing season. To make this process less daunting, the 2026 race kit has been broken down layer-by-layer. It provides a simplified approach to selecting gear suitable for an individual's sailing preferences and the anticipated sea conditions. The choice of gear varies significantly according to the type of sailing activity. For instance, inshore and coastal sailing have its distinct set of optimal wearables, while gear differs for younger sailors and trapeze sailing activities. Other activities — hiking, standup paddleboarding (SUP), rowing — they all require equipment uniquely tailored for safety, comfort and success. Among the must-haves, the Pro Aquafleece Top 2.0 and SuperTherm 4mm LongJohn stand out when it comes to battling the sea elements. For women, the Women's Hot Top ensures optimal performance in a variety of conditions. Additionally, the Pro Race 2 Glove, the Race Armour Buoyancy Aid, and the Pro Laced Ankle Strap Boot are essential safety gear every sailor should have in their kit bag. Building the perfect race kit requires careful consideration and a balance between functionality and comfort. This guide aims to make this process simpler and more effective. Opt for a well-assembled race kit — it's built for performance, ensuring thrilling adventures ahead.

title: Understanding the Sinking of the Bayesian: How Modern Computational Techniques Could Prevent Future Yachting Disasters
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Understanding the Sinking of the Bayesian: How Modern Computational Techniques Could Prevent Future Yachting Disasters
summary: Exploring the unfortunate sinking of the sailing yacht Bayesian off Porticello, we delve into the complex dynamics of yacht behaviour and how modern technology might help avert similar calamities in the future.
body: As we often find ourselves faced with the harsh realities of the maritime world, the tragic episode of the sailing yacht Bayesian, which occurred on 19 August 2024 off the coast of Porticello, Sicilly, is nothing but a stark reminder of the mystifying force Mother Nature wields over us seafarers. It is crucial to remember the ongoing investigations and proceedings in this regard even as we eloquently avoid treading into speculative territories or comment on the devastating loss of life. However, our allegiance to the realm of the sea and those who brave its waves gives us an inherent responsibility: to dissect the mechanics of this regrettable accident and seek answers to prevent such tragedies from recurring.

The Marine Accident Investigation Branch (MAIB), a UK government organisation dealing with marine accidents involving UK-registered vessels worldwide, published an interim report in May 2025 sharing the findings of their safety investigation into the sinking of the Bayesian. The report, in accordance with The United Kingdom Merchant Shipping (Accident Reporting and Investigation) Regulations 2012, Regulation55, focused not on assigning liability or blame but on examining the causes and circumstances leading to the incident, with a firm intent to prevent future accidents. A point worth noting is that the investigation's final findings, expected to be released soon, may bring new details and insights, particularly those gleaned from the salvaged wreck of the yacht, and could modify the details presented in the interim report.

As a pressure-point focus, the interim report highlighted some revelations from a stability and windage study conducted at the University of Southampton's Wolfson Unit for Marine Technology and Industrial Aerodynamics. This involved a deep dive into Bayesian's stability information booklet and righting-lever curves - the quintessential measure of stability for all vessels. The report presented the computational study findings of the Wolfson Unit, providing valuable insights into the yacht behaviour at the time of the accident.

Through the examination of this tragic event and careful analysis conducted by various organisations, we are offered a unique opportunity to advance our understanding of yacht behaviour. Armed with modern computing techniques, we can create safer experiences for all those who dare to conquer the waters. It's a challenging expedition but well worth the journey as it represents not merely the pursuit of knowledge but the undying human spirit to learn, adapt, and overcome.

title: Yachting Enthusiasts: Vacation Dreams Materialise as 30m Sailing Yacht Antares III Hits the Market
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Yachting Enthusiasts: Vacation Dreams Materialise as 30m Sailing Yacht Antares III Hits the Market
summary: Antares III, the spectacular 30-metre sailing yacht, has been listed for sale with Wind Yachts, offering an exciting opportunity for yacht enthusiasts.
body: Elegance and unmatched performance have been artfully combined in Antares III, a 30-metre sailing yacht now listed for sale. Set sail into the vast mutable sea with this jaw-dropping vessel, due to its listing with famed yacht sellers Daniele Botticini and Marcia Lippa of Wind Yachts. The captivating sailing vessel, launched by the New Zealand-based Yachting Developments in 2011, fosters memories of sailing pleasure and enchantment.

The exquisite design of Antares III is the handiwork of Dixon Yacht Design which expertly blended the strong naval architecture and enchanting exterior. The interiors, airy and spacious, were carefully crafted by Rhoades Young Design. The luxury yacht is currently on the market for €6,850,000, a price tag that compliments her allure and prestige.

In addition, the sailing yacht accommodates a crew of four. Once aboard, guests are welcomed by comfortable seating options in the aft and foredeck. Continuity of the upper and lower saloons establishes a generous space for guests. The bar and navigation station in the upper saloon ensures guests can enjoy the outdoor area, while the lower saloon offers a more intimate atmosphere ready to be transformed for dining.

The yacht's elevated pilothouse gives guests incomparable all-around visibility, while its opening windows facilitate friendly chats with the crew. Equipped with a high-modulus 42.7-meter Southern Spar carbon mast, the rig features a furling boom and continuous carbon rigging, replaced in 2021.

Her remarkable design grants her an astonishing 4,876 square feet of sail area when sailing upwind. Even at rest, her character is evident - with her gross tonnage resting at 107GT and a 7.35-meter beam. The Antares III can reach top speeds of 12 knots, boasting a maximum range of 3,600 nautical miles at cruising speed, driven by her Scania diesel engine.
Currently anchored in the picturesque Southern Tyrrhenian, Italy, Antares III is ready to bring her owners the adventure and tranquility that only a sailing experience can offer.

title: Not a Reinvention — An Evolution of a Caribbean Legend
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Antigua Sailing Week 2026: Evolution, Energy and a New Chapter for a Caribbean Classic
summary: Antigua Sailing Week 2026 returns with a refreshed format blending racing and cruising, reflecting how modern sailors experience the sport while preserving the spirit, competition and unmistakable Caribbean atmosphere that has defined the event for over 50 years.
body: For more than half a century, Antigua Sailing Week has been part race, part pilgrimage.
Tight, tactical racing off Antigua’s south coast Hard-fought starts and marginal gains Evenings that start with analysis and end somewhere between storytelling and rum
Full anchorages and busy marinas Global crews and returning characters A spotlight on one of the most authentic sailing cultures anywhere in the world
So when whispers started circulating about changes for 2026, people paid attention.
Because you don’t casually adjust something that’s been part of the Caribbean sailing bloodstream for decades.
Change — Or Something More Measured?
This isn’t a reinvention. It’s not a reset. And it’s definitely not walking away from what made Antigua Sailing Week what it is.
What’s happening is simpler — and more important:
It’s an evolution.

Changing sailor demographics Different expectations of time on the water A broader mix of racing, cruising and lifestyle sailing And the reality that not everyone wants to race flat-out, every day, all week
The organisers haven’t guessed at this.
They’ve listened.
Listening to the Fleet — Where the Real Decisions Happen
The shift in format didn’t come from a marketing meeting.
On docks Over drinks Mid-delivery And quietly, after racing, when sailors are honest
People still want to race. But they also want to experience Antigua.
Not just blast past it at 12 knots.
Competitive racing A cruising rally spirit More engagement with the island itself
It’s a subtle shift, but a meaningful one.
The 2026 Fleet: Stories That Define the Race
If you want to understand Antigua Sailing Week, you don’t start with the format.
You start with the people.
Take Patrick Holloran, sailing Caipirinha, a Beneteau First 40.7.
At nearly 80, he’s still lining up on the start line — not because he has to, but because he wants to.
First visit inspired by family A boat that stayed in the Caribbean Years of returning, racing, and belonging
That’s the real backbone of the event.
Not just elite campaigns — but lifelong sailors, families, first-timers and seasoned returners all sharing the same water.
More Than Racing: Antigua as an Experience
One of the biggest shifts for 2026 is recognising something long obvious:
Antigua Sailing Week has always been more than racing.
Now it leans into that fully.
Reggae in the Park — A Caribbean Classic
On April 21, the rhythm shifts ashore with Reggae in the Park.
Live reggae Island culture Crews, locals and visitors all in one place
It’s not an add-on. It’s part of the experience.
Riddim & Tides — Where Sailing Meets Lifestyle
By April 25, things move fully into Caribbean mode.
Boats Music Beach culture And a proper island atmosphere
Think less “regatta schedule” — more Antigua at full volume.
For those not racing — or those wanting a different view — Antigua delivers properly.
By Air With CalvinAir Helicopters, you can:
Track the fleet from above Watch tactics unfold in real time See the racecourse in full
It’s fast, sharp, and unforgettable.
By Sea
Or stay closer to the salt.
Front-row views from the water Music, drinks and full Caribbean energy The race, without the pressure
Not a bad way to spend a day.
Still a Racer’s Regatta — Just a Smarter One
Make no mistake.
The racing still matters.
Starts will still be tight. Margins will still be small. And the competition will still bite if you get it wrong.
But now, there’s room around that intensity.
Enjoy the island Connect with crews And remember why people came here in the first place The Bigger Picture — Why This Matters
Antigua Sailing Week is doing something many events struggle with:
Adapting without losing identity.
Too much change — and you lose the core. Too little — and you lose relevance.
This sits right in the middle.
The racing The community The character
But opens the door wider.
The Bottom Line
If you’ve sailed it before — you’ll recognise it. If you haven’t — this might be the year to start.
Because Antigua hasn’t changed direction.
It’s just trimmed the sails a little differently.
And in sailing, that’s often all it takes.

title: A High-Seas Adventure: Thrilling Kick-Off for National 12 and Border Counties Midweek Sailing Series
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A High-Seas Adventure: Thrilling Kick-Off for National 12 and Border Counties Midweek Sailing Series
summary: An adventurous day unfolded as the National 12 and Border Counties Midweek Sailing Series commenced, displaying the unpredictable essence of sailing.
body: There is something intrinsically exhilarating about stepping onto a sailing boat, knowing that the calm waters can transform into turbulent waves at any moment. This vibrancy was magnified during the National 12 Sprint Series at the Burghfield Sailing Club and the Border Counties Midweek Sailing Series at the Nantwich & Border Counties Sailing Club, which tested seasoned and novice sailors alike in a thrilling, unpredictable adventure on the seas.

Simultaneously, at the Nantwich & Border Counties Sailing Club, 23 boats and 28 tough sailors embarked on their first event of 2026. The weather favored the brave, delivering a steady wind and a fleeting chance of rain, while 28 sailors displayed grit and resilience, refusing to back down. The day was as much about understanding the conditions as it was about sailing; with the course including two long beats and quick reaches back downwind, it demanded an insightful interpretation of the environment.

Both these events set the tone for an incredible season of sailing, which promises more races, more unpredictable seas, and more thrilling tales from seasoned and adrenaline-junkie sailors alike. It's a display of true sportsmanship and resilience, as keen competitors face off against not just each other but, more importantly, against the unpredictable yet beautiful nature of sailing.

title: Discover the State of the Yacht Market Through the Eyes of Industry-leading Shipyard Executives
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover the State of the Yacht Market Through the Eyes of Industry-leading Shipyard Executives
summary: Gain a unique view into the future of the yachting market directly from those at the helm of Europe's premier shipyards.
body: Steering the course of the yachting market, shipyard executives delve into the undercurrents shaping the industry. With voices ranging from the leaders of Damen Yachting and Feadship in the Netherlands, to the powerhouses of Ferretti and Azimut Benetti in Italy, a consistent narrative emerges. Over the past few years, these shipyards have seen a fundamental shift in how they operate, brought about by significant investments in digital tools, facility redesign, and closer integration between engineering and production teams.

The quest for exceptional craftsmanship is a constant thread binding these leaders' thoughts. With a focus on quality that extends far beyond the vessel itself, the ability to find, train, and retain skilled labour is acknowledged as an ongoing challenge. Navigating the complexities of supply chains and cost management, executives highlight maintaining quality without sacrificing margins as the definitive factor for future success.

In a comprehensive interview with Abeking & Rasmussen's CEO, Matthias Hellmann shares how his shipyard is leveraging technology to streamline the construction process. This transformation, enabled by digital tools, signals a new era in yacht construction. While this discussion provides a glimpse into market trends, eager minds await further insights from eight additional shipyard CEOs scheduled to share their thoughts in the coming days.

title: Majestic Lürssen Superyacht Pelorus Charges onto Sales Scene With €160 Million Asking Price
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Majestic Lürssen Superyacht Pelorus Charges onto Sales Scene With €160 Million Asking Price
summary: The majestic 114.5-metre Lürssen superyacht, Pelorus, graces the sales market with a hefty price tag of €160,000,000.
body: The magnificently designed Lürssen superyacht, Pelorus, has now been listed for sale. Renowned names in yachting such as Tim Heywood, Terence Disdale, and Lürssen are behind this 5,403GT vessel's design and construction. Delivered in 2003, it held the 11th position as the largest yacht in the world and was the flagship of the German shipyard fleet. In recent years, significant refits have induced the addition of a second helipad and regular maintenance work aligned with the American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) class survey requirements. The vessel currently enjoys a clean status with no recommendations. Following its meticulous preservation, Pelorus now awaits its new owner with an asking price of €160,000,000.

Pelorus isn't short of entertainment and recreational facilities either. From being home to four onboard pools - including a Jacuzzi - to housing a wellness centre with a steam room and plunge pool, this vessel is the embodiment of luxury. It even incorporates a dedicated cinema room complete with plush sofas and a collection of more than 120 4K films.

Pelorus's powerhouse rides on a pair of Wartsila Model 12V26 engines, bestowing it with a top speed of 20 knots. FUller still, a range of 6,000 nautical miles is achievable at 16 knots, thanks also to the stability assured by Quantum zero-speed stabilisers - two each in the aft and forward sections of the yacht - these yachts provide ultimate comfort for guests during navigation.
Pelorus opens the door to amazing ocean adventures and unparalleled sea experiences for its future owner. This beautifully designed yacht is certain to make waves in the sales market.

title: Edmiston's Nathan Farrelly and Hans van Doornmalen Assume Sale Mandate for 115m Lürssen Superyacht Pelorus
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Edmiston's Nathan Farrelly and Hans van Doornmalen Assume Sale Mandate for 115m Lürssen Superyacht Pelorus
summary: The stunning 114.5m Lürssen superyacht Pelorus has celebrated a change in central agency.
body: The lavish 114.5-metre Pelorus, a prided product of famed shipyard, Lürssen, has had a change of central agency. Now listed for sale with the Edmiston duo: Nathan Farrelly and Hans van Doornmalen, Pelorus stands as a testimonial to the grandeur of yachting. The motor yacht, weighing a considerable 5,403GT, first skimmed the ocean's surface in 2003, before commanding attention through its distinguished design and build team, including the illustrious trio: Tim Heywood, Terence Disdale and Lürssen. Strutting an unquestionable aura of class, she was the 11th largest yacht worldwide and a crown jewel of the German shipyard when first launched. In recognising her worth and upholding her legacy, multiple overhauls were conducted in both 2008 – with the introduction of a second helipad – and 2017. The meticulous care extended to the yacht guaranteed compliance with ABS class survey requirements through to 2025. Resultantly, Pelorus enjoys a clean status with no recommendations, boasting a survey cycle reaching till 2030. The motor yacht's gravity-defying pricetag of €160,000,000 complements her splendid offerings. Beyond her steel hull, an additional line arching the bow adds a unique touch, resembling the "armour belt" design of the HMS Belfast docked on the Thames. The interior oozes a beach-club charm through its use of natural materials, cleverly curated by Terence Disdale. With 12 ensuite cabins, the vessel comfortably hosts 24 guests — a number that can be stretched to accommodate 36 guests with dispensation. The architectural masterstroke, a VIP cabin, and seven guest cabins featuring innovative elements like a fold-down terrace, etch memories of pure indulgence. Ensuring a seamless experience, a readily available crew of 46 stands at the guests' disposal. A bouquet of onboard luxuries, from a wellness centre complete with a steam room and plunge pool, to the master suite offering an enchanting view of the oceanic expanse, exemplifies the divinity embodied by the Pelorus. Retaining its unquenchable allure, the superyacht Pelorus now awaits the decisive gavel strike to seal its fate under its newest central agency, Edmiston.

title: Leading Shipyard Executives Unveil a Vision for the Future of Yacht Construction Market
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Leading Shipyard Executives Unveil a Vision for the Future of Yacht Construction Market
summary: An interview series with some of the industry's top yard CEOs offers a peek into the future of yacht manufacturing.
body: There are plenty of pundits ready to predict the trajectory of the yacht market. However, the views of shipyard CEOs, the decision-makers at the heart of the industry, are heard less frequently but carry significant weight. Seeking to obtain a more precise statistical pulse of the industry, nine market-leading shipyard executives were asked about the current state and future direction of the market. These thought leaders offer a collective diagnosis that serves as a strong indicator of the new-build landscape.

The shipyards represented span the entire spectrum of the European market, from Dutch manufacturers such as Royal Huisman, Damen Yachting and Feadship, to Italian firms Palumbo, Sanlorenzo, Azimut Benetti and Ferretti. German-based Abeking and Rasmussen are also featured along with Bilgin from Turkey. While opinions naturally vary, a number of common themes crop up repeatedly.

However, despite these advancements, the shortage of skilled labour remains a problem that cannot be entirely alleviated by improving facilities. The ability to recruit, train, retain and ensure that craftsmanship knowledge is passed on, underpins the essence of what these CEOs say. Furthermore, maintaining high-quality standards without draining profitability is frequently cited as a vital factor determining which companies will prosper in the long term.

Although the order books look strong, there is a noticeable shift in demand. Buyers are now more thoughtful, driven by the experiences they want to obtain and what they intend to do once on board. Future growth will rely on the quality of what is delivered, the reputation of the shipyard doing the delivering, and the capacity to meet the evolving demands of a new generation of vessel owners.

In a proceeding interview, News Editor Conor Feasey speaks with CEO Matthias Hellmann of Abeking & Rasmussen. The discussion continues with the series as it introduces perspectives from other shipyard chiefs in the days to come.

title: A Look into the Mysterious 140m Feadship Flagship Superyacht and the Launch of the Exceptional 80m Project 826
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A Look into the Mysterious 140m Feadship Flagship Superyacht and the Launch of the Exceptional 80m Project 826
summary: The Netherlands recently became the spotlight for yacht enthusiasts as two significant superyacht projects were unveiled - the 140m flagship project and Project 826.
body: On the waterfronts of the Netherlands, something extraordinary is taking shape - the flagship superyacht project of famed shipbuilder, Feadship. Measuring a formidable 140 metres, this mysterious vessel known only as hull 831, has been spotted for the first time, eliciting much intrigue amongst onlookers. The bow alone bespeaks the magnitude of the project, and anticipation is building for its expected completion in 2029.

Alblasserdam's NMC facilities saw the first section of the yacht emerging with much aplomb. From there, the components will journey on to Greenport Rotterdam where the build will continue with steel and aluminium. Project specifics remain cloaked in secrecy, though estimates suggest an impressive interior volume of 11,025GT. Once completed, hull 831 is anticipated to exceed Feadship's current flagship, Breakthrough, by a staggering 21.2 metres.

The exterior design work of Malcolm McKeon bestows on Thalassa an appearance of high-performance sails, emphasised by a sharp plumb bow, a widened hull, gently curved windows, and slender lines that scoop the ocean waves. This yacht's interiors, construed by Milanese M2Atelier, remain undisclosed, yet whispers of a contemporary design, steeped in warmth and relaxation, are seeping through.

The highlight of Project 826 is its expansive beach club, the largest ever created by Feadship. Spreading across two tiers over 165 square meters, this open-plan design sports a chic, relaxed lounge with a bar and teak-covered hatches doubling as terraces over water. Nothing impedes the bite-sized glimpses of the passing panorama, thanks to the absence of a bulky hull structure. Feadship has pioneered a powerful new gear system for opening and closing hatches fitted within the very doors themselves.

Apart from these alluring features, touches of luxury weave their way into Project 826 with a main deck pool lounge hosting a glass-bottomed pool shining light into the beach club below. A state-of-the-art gym, a massage room with fold-out terraces, and a watersports area add to the allure of this magnificent vessel. It is no surprise then, that Feadship describes the on-board experience as one centred around 'space, light and connection'.

title: Thrilling Race Progresses at East Kent Radio Sailing Club: DF95 Spring Series Week 2 Unfolds
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Thrilling Race Progresses at East Kent Radio Sailing Club: DF95 Spring Series Week 2 Unfolds
summary: The spirited DF95 Spring Series at East Kent Radio Sailing Club moves into its second week, shaped by exciting wins, close races, and surprise upsets.
body: Week 2 of the DF95 Spring Series at East Kent Radio Sailing Club offered up a thrilling spectacle of sailing skill and competitive spirit. The event was marked by fierce winds and stormy weather, adding to the challenge faced by the participating sailors. But even as storms lashed towards South East Kent for the second Spring series event, enthusiasm remained undeterred with 12 competitors entering the fray and 13 races run in conditions that varied from a shifty 5 knots beginning, building up to a hefty 15 knots by 1 pm.

As the series developed, beloved racing duo of Dave and Adrian took over, trading top spots in the following races, while Alan persisted in the third place. Another noteworthy performance came from Rob Owens, who managed a handsome third in race 4 and a second in race 6 before eventually falling back.

As winds picked up again post lunch, the battle for supremacy took on renewed vitality. Navigating the winds became a skill-testing endeavour, shaking up the leaderboard even further. Dave revelled in the challenging conditions, snapping up top spots in subsequent races. Adrian, Peter, and Alan variously claimed the second positions, with third places being divided among Colin, Simon Thornton, Adrian, and surprise entrant Ed Coxon.

A resurgent performance from Dave saw him win the final race, but it was too little too late to surpass Adrian, who marked his stellar performance with 16.4 points against Dave's 20. At mid-fleet, an absorbing dual unfolded between Andrew Nichols and Spencer Pope, which concluded in a thrilling tie.

The second week in the DF95 Spring Series at East Kent Radio Sailing Club proved to be an adventure at sea. The thrills and spills atop the waters, coloured by unyielding competitiveness and sharp sailing skills, made for an unforgettable sailing saga.

title: Sneak Peek at the Majestic Bow of the 140m Feadship Superyacht Under Construction
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Sneak Peek at the Majestic Bow of the 140m Feadship Superyacht Under Construction
summary: The flagship 140-metre superyacht from Dutch shipbuilder Feadship reveals its bow for the first time.
body: Master shipbuilders never fail to ignite imagination and awe, and the Dutch shipyard Feadship is indisputably one of them. A glimpse of their under-construction flagship superyacht, expected to be a breathtaking 140 metres, has set the marine world abuzz.

The first sighting of this majestic beast, known only as hull 831, was recently reported in the Netherlands. The initial section of this ambitious project was rolled out of the shed at the NMC facilities in Alblasserdam. The excitement couldn't have been more palpable; the shipbuilding world is waiting with bated breath to see Feadship's unique vision come alive.

Expected to undertake the journey to Greenport Rotterdam's facilities next, the bow's journey echoes that of the superyacht's vision - moving from ambitiously imagined designs to tangible engineering marvels. Here, the construction will progress with steel and aluminium, materials renowned for their strength and durability, matching the resolute spirit the superyacht embodies.

Make no mistake; hull 831 will not just add another feather to Feadship's cap. At a staggering 140 meters, it aims to surpass their own flagship superyacht Breakthrough by an impressive 21.2 meters. It isn't just about building a bigger boat; it's about elevating shipbuilding to a level of artistry that makes waves, setting higher standards with each new venture.

Marine enthusiasts, potential yacht owners, and competitors alike are waiting to set their eyes upon this impressive creation. Feadship's upcoming superyacht is not only expected to be a masterpiece of marine engineering but also a symbol of luxury, innovation and, above all, the uncontained joy of voyaging on the seas.

title: Revolutionizing Onboard Architecture: Italian Shipyard Sanlorenzo Unveils the Bold and Innovative 74Steel Superyacht 'Virtuosity'
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Revolutionizing Onboard Architecture: Italian Shipyard Sanlorenzo Unveils the Bold and Innovative 74Steel Superyacht 'Virtuosity'
summary: Italian shipyard Sanlorenzo unveils Virtuosity - the second in-build superyacht from its flagship 74Steel line, loaded with groundbreaking features.
body: Italian shipyard Sanlorenzo has unveiled its second in-build superyacht, Virtuosity, from its flagship 74Steel line. Once launched, the feature-filled Virtuosity promises to stamp its prominence as the shipyard's largest build to date. Spanning an impressive 73 metres, this superyacht is a follow-up to the first 74Steel superyacht, the Silver Fox. The craft, designed by Zuccon International Project, saw launch in October of last year. Virtuosity will share similar infrastructural elements, such as the engineered platform and diesel-electric configuration pioneered by its predecessor. Yet, Virtuosity leaps one step ahead on the innovation scale, introducing features 'never seen before on a superyacht,' according to the yard. Some of its outstanding characteristics include a living banyan tree growing between decks, a submerged aquarium integrated into the hull, and a vast 230-square-metre 'Ocean Resort.'

Engaging in four years of robust dialogue and extensive cooperation with the yacht's owner, this bespoke masterpiece was born. Sanlorenzo embarked on this project since 2022, aiming for a release date within the same year. Sanlorenzo's CEO, Tommaso Vincenzi, emphasised the revolutionary approach to onboard architecture, with every feature conceived from a clear architectural vision that embodied coherence and balance, rather than mere excess. The Ficus Nitida tree within the main deck exemplifies this approach. This botanical masterpiece, carefully selected for its growth criteria, will rise through an oval void between decks. The carefully-designed interiors, including the main saloon and guest areas, curve around this tree, lending to a unique chunk of nature on board the superyacht.

The design flows seamlessly into other areas of the yacht with intricate details similarly found in guest rooms, lounges and the custom wine cellar. With an ability to accommodate up to 16 guests with a crew of 24, Virtuosity is indeed a grand symbol of opulence and architectural charm at sea. Painstakingly detailed and uniquely conceived, Sanlorenzo's Virtuosity stands as a testament to the shipyard’s commitment towards pushing the boundaries of superyacht design.

title: Sanlorenzo Elevates Luxury Yachting with the Reveal of its Latest 74Steel Superyacht - Virtuosity
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Sanlorenzo Elevates Luxury Yachting with the Reveal of its Latest 74Steel Superyacht - Virtuosity
summary: Sanlorenzo unveils its largest build to date, the 73-meter superyacht, Virtuosity, from the celebrated 74Steel line, challenging architectural norms.
body: Italian shipyard Sanlorenzo asserts its mastery in audacious design as it introduces Virtuosity, a groundbreaking model from its flagship 74Steel line. Continuing from the first of its line, the 72-meter Silver Fox, Virtuosity ups the extravagance stakes as it stands as Sanlorenzo's largest construction to date.

Sanlorenzo acknowledges a noteworthy shift from the Silver Fox, as Virtuosity introduces design and architectural features hitherto unseen in the yachting world. The opulent water vessel spotlights an integrated living tree that spans two decks, a submerged aquarium melded into its hull, and an expansive 230-square-meter 'Ocean Resort'.

CEO of Sanlorenzo, Tommaso Vincenzi, posits that the design of Virtuosity represents a distinct shift in onboard architecture understanding. The superyacht integrates natural elements, transforming technical volumes into luxurious experiential environments. The innovation doesn't result in excess, but rather maintains a harmonious balance.

An essential feature in Virtuosity is the Ficus Nitida, a banyan tree species, that ascends through an oval void, connecting two decks organically. Skylights at floor level channel natural light to aid the tree's growth whilst contributing to a pleasant ambiance onboard. Surprisingly, the tree was selected before the first structural block was ever assembled, highlighting its intricate role in the yacht's design. Surrounding the central tree, the main saloon exudes comfort with lounge seating and a bar area. Simultaneously, amidships, a triple-height lobby features a dark lacquered aluminum staircase, an accompanying lift, and a personalized wine cellar stationed conveniently.

As you navigate upwards, the bridge deck maintains the quintessential indoor-outdoor approach with a winter garden veranda complete with a formal dining table, bar area, and a lobby accompanied by a walk-in wine cellar. Two further guest cabins and the captain's cabin are laid out strategically on this deck. The superyacht can accommodate up to 16 guests, serviced by a crew of up to 24. The intricate layout encompasses an owners' deck that houses the second owners' suite roughly 140 square meters in size, an aft cinema lounge, and a reflective glass-bottomed pool that overlooks the bow. A multi-functional front space features removable seating and a sensory shower. The sundeck redesign showcases an indoor gym.

Through elements of design and architecture, the superyacht pushes the envelope of luxury sailing. Virtuosity triumphantly embodies Sanlorenzo's commitment to continuous innovation and customization, leading the fleet into a bold, new era of luxury yachting.

title: From Sky to Sea: Engineering the Pinnacle of Arrival Experiences on a Superyacht Helideck
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: From Sky to Sea: Engineering the Pinnacle of Arrival Experiences on a Superyacht Helideck
summary: Crafting the quintessential arrival experience on a superyacht is an art —beginning with a sleek helicopter arrival that segues seamlessly from sky to sea.
body: Few moments at sea capture the heart quite like a helicopter making a graceful landing on a superyacht's helideck. This picturesque moment, a dazzling blend of power and finesse, speaks volumes about the yacht's capabilities and heralds unparalleled freedom and luxury. But beneath this spectacular spectacle lies a skillfully engineered ecosystem. A well-designed helicopter deck is not a mere circle etched on steel; it is intricately woven into the yacht's DNA, meticulously planned from the concept stage to achieve a profound impact. As visually appealing as it may be, without careful consideration of its functional aspects, even the most stunning layout can become an operational snag. Before the design work begins, the underlying mission of the helicopter needs to be clarified. Whether it serves as a shuttle to shore, a secure link between global estates, or an agile aerial vessel for swift responses and long-range connections largely dictates its design elements. And of course, factors such as the yacht's cruising grounds, night operations, luggage profiles, and guest movement frequency also come into play. Helideck locations must satisfy not only aesthetic preferences but also comply with aerodynamic principles. Whether perched on the bow, stern or midship, each location brings its unique benefits and challenges, ranging from clean approach paths to challenges with airflow modelling. A wind-over-deck study, despite its low cost, proves priceless by transforming unpredictability into reliable, pilot-friendly handling. Design considerations must also focus on the D value (the rotor diameter or overall length of the helicopter) which determines the deck size. A well-known conundrum amongst pilots is that owners tend to upgrade helicopters more frequently than they downsize. Therefore, designing for today's aircraft could potentially lead to costly modifications tomorrow. Another critical factor is the M value — the weight the helideck can safely carry. This value, indicated on the deck in tonnes, accounts for static loads, dynamic landing/roll loads, and landing impact forces at sea. Correct estimation of the M value ensures safe operations for current and future aircraft. Protecting your investment is also critical. A well-engineered hangar or protective enclosure extends the aircraft's service life, reduces maintenance costs, and maintains reliability. Lastly, if there's even a slight possibility of night operations, it's wise to incorporate this into the initial brief, as this element can be challenging to add later. Superyacht helideck design is an intricate interplay of style, substance, and safety, providing a spectacular gateway from sky to sea, it creates an unforgettable impression for all aboard.

title: Astonishing Achievement in Yacht Servicing: VMG Astilleros Installs World’s Largest Shiplift Drydock
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Astonishing Achievement in Yacht Servicing: VMG Astilleros Installs World’s Largest Shiplift Drydock
summary: Spain-based VMG Astilleros has added a colossal shiplift drydock to their world-class maritime facility.
body: Tucked in Sagunto, Spain, lies VMG Astilleros — a name making waves in the maritime industry. The latest development for this established Mediterranean shipyard is a feather in the cap — installing the world's largest yacht-dedicated shiplift drydock. A significant extension of VMG's strategic modernisation and expansion initiative, this milestone has fundamentally elevated their capability to service the crème de la crème of water vessels — superyachts, megayachts, and gigayachts.

The imposing Pearlson Shiplift system, a masterpiece designed by Pearlson Shiplift Corporation (PSC), features a lifting platform of 102 metres length and 22 metres width, capable of taking under its wings yachts up to 125 metres long. An amalgamation of advanced structural engineering and PSC’s proprietary continuous platform structure ensures this platform operates as a single entity, demonstrating exceptional structural integrity and preciseness.

Herralding a major evolution in VMG’s shipyard infrastructure, this newly installed shiplift announces VMG’s facility as the current record-holder for the biggest yacht-dedicated shiplift drydock globally.

The power-packed, remodelled facility also boasts of considerable hardstand capacity, further solidifying VMG Astilleros de Sagunto’s dominance as a premium superyacht refit spot in the azure Mediterranean.

With this monumental move, VMG Astilleros de Sagunto cements itself into a global network encircling more than 280 shiplifts in over 70 countries, all backed by the engineering prowess and enduring service commitment from The Pearlson Group.

VMG Astilleros de Sagunto is a leading full-service re-fit and repair shipyard for superyachts. The firm offers a grand 76,800 square metres of hardstanding area, sophisticated lifting capabilities, and a geographic advantage of direct access to the Mediterranean.
This substantial investment in infrastructure and capabilities heralds a new era that underscores VMG as a significant refit hub in the picturesque Western Mediterranean.

title: Three New Teams to Kick Start their Journey in the Upcoming 52 SUPER SERIES Season
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Three New Teams to Kick Start their Journey in the Upcoming 52 SUPER SERIES Season
summary: Three fresh teams are preparing to chart their course in the upcoming 2026 52 SUPER SERIES season at Puerto Portals.
body: Just under a month before the bold regatta of the 2026 52 SUPER SERIES season thrusts its sails into action, three new teams are preparing to join the fray. The legendary Bay of Palma at Puerto Portals will host and witness teams, representing 11 nations, competing and battling the waves for the illustrious Puerto Portals 52 SUPER SERIES Sailing Week.

Joakim Sundberg, a young Swedish entrepreneur, represents a wave of newcomers who are comparatively green in the realm of grand prix racing. With barely two years of sailing experience, the aspiring sailor shares the same, sky-high ambition as Heerema: To climb to the crests of the SUPER SERIES fleet within the next few years. These fresh faces, despite harbouring contrasting skills and experiences, come together on a common horizon — to carve their identity on the challenging canvas of the 52 SUPER SERIES season.

title: Unveiling the Santasevera 42 Sport: The Sophisticated Open Day Cruiser Perfect for Weekend Adventures
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unveiling the Santasevera 42 Sport: The Sophisticated Open Day Cruiser Perfect for Weekend Adventures
summary: Meet the latest marvel from Santasevera Yachts, the 42 Sport. This 41ft open day cruiser is a weekender's dream with its smart layout and seamless spaces.
body: Introducing the Santasevera 42 Sport, the newest prodigy unveiled by the renowned boat designer Francesco Guida. This 41ft open day cruiser is a product of sheer innovation and creativity, showcasing a smart layout thoughtfully crafted for ultimate weekend adventures on the water.

This boat converges aesthetic appeal with functional design through the day spaces, which strategically flow into one another. The central island sunbed serves as a bridge between the swim platform and the aft deck, creating a vibrant and sociable environment. Ahead of this cluster of relaxing loungers, the walkway delicately guides one forward to a sheltered C-shaped dinette on the portside. This masterpiece features a cleverly designed table so adjustable it allows for movement in any direction, adding an extra touch of luxury.

Ever-conscious of space, the Santasevera 42 Sport features a one-man helm designed to take as little room as possible, allowing the party area to flourish. If you're bitten by the wanderlust bug and decide to explore further, you're welcome to ascend one of the symmetrical side decks to the raised island sunbed at the bow.

Designed primarily as a high-end day boat for weekending couples, this cruiser offers a single cabin decked with a minimalistic bed, providing ample headroom. Additional features include a comfy changing seat to starboard, and a separate heads compartment complete with a shower.

When it comes to performance, flexibility sits at the core of this cruiser's capabilities. The boat can achieve 30-knot speed with D4-320s on sterndrives and up to 45 knots with a pair of D6-480s. Also available are IPS pod drives on lengthy jackshafts and outboard propulsion. If you're into speed thrills, you will likely be tempted by the 600hp V12 outboards, which can push the boat to speeds in excess of 50 knots.

While the Sport model provides more protection with its enclosed slide windows compared to the HT and Open variants, a Coupé version is also available, boasting an extended roofline and sliding aft doors. If you fancy a unique touch, rest assured that Santasevera Yachts, who build everything in-house at their own yard, welcome custom requests.
In essence, the Santasevera 42 Sport is the idyllic boat for sea-goers looking for luxury, functionality, and a touch of adventurous spirit.

title: 87.9m Explorer Yacht Conversion Project Unveiled from Cloak of Secrecy
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: 87.9m Explorer Yacht Conversion Project Unveiled from Cloak of Secrecy
summary: An intricate re-model of an 87.9-metre offshore supply vessel into an explorer yacht is unveiled from the Stahlbau Nord shipyard, Germany.
body: Emerging from the shroud of secrecy, a remarkably hushed 87.9-metre conversion project steps into the public eye. The said yacht is yet another testament to masterful craftsmanship, initiating its journey at the Stahlbau Nord shipyard, a subsidiary of Lloyd Werft's owner, the Roenner Group.

This covert project has breathed life into what was once an offshore supply vessel known as ASL Symphony. However, the ship’s recent redux has rendered it almost unrecognisable. Its purchase in the first quarter of 2023 by an undisclosed private owner marked the beginning of her transformation into an able-bodied explorer that exudes grandeur.

Originally, ASL Symphony was birthed in the hands of the Indonesian builder, ASL Shipyard in 2015. This once vermilion workhorse, with a 21-metre beam and 4.7-metre draught, began her journey as the multi-purpose offshore tug-cum-supply ship named Energy Lindesnes.

According to data from BOATPro, prior to her conversion, this vessel had a volume of roughly 3,921GT. Post alterations, her volume is projected to increase to an approximate 5,000GT, making her not just a vessel, but a floating palace. Omnipresent are the innovative sheens on her diesel-electric propulsion system and azimuth thrusters, with the robust Dynamic Positioning 2 system effortlessly keeping pace. She holds a mighty top speed of 22 knots.

Despite being discreetly tucked into a shed in 2025, the vessel is all set for further outfitting works in Bremen her grand launch. With a repertoire of ambitious explorers such as Solaris and Luna under its belt, Lloyd Werft sails across familiar seas with this intriguing project.

title: Master the Art of Ascending Upstream Locks in Your Boating Adventures
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Master the Art of Ascending Upstream Locks in Your Boating Adventures
summary: Expand your boating prowess with expert advice from Jon Mendez on manoeuvring a lock upstream safely and smoothly.
body: Boating inland presents certain challenges unlike those found on coastal voyages. One such challenge is locks. These structures are designed to enable boats to overcome sudden changes in water height, whether on a man-made canal snaking across hilly landscapes or a river with its own natural obstacles, such as swift rapids and falls. Locks generally comprise a lock chamber that can have its water level adjusted, gates on either end, and paddles or sluices that facilitate filling and emptying of the lock.

During this filling process, the boat(s) within the chamber may also shift forward and backward slightly due to water rebounding from the bottom gates. Monitor the lines securing your boat and adjust them as necessary. Once the water has reached the correct level, prepare to exit by tying up your boat, closing all paddles, and opening the exit gates. Always allow any swirling water to settle before moving on. Lastly, remember to close the gates behind you after passing through the lock, to facilitate the process for the next vessel. Remember, mastering the art of navigating locks is a crucial skill for any dedicated boater venturing inland.

title: Classic Superyacht Gin-Tonic Arrives at Pendennis Shipyard – Undergoes Transformation
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Classic Superyacht Gin-Tonic Arrives at Pendennis Shipyard – Undergoes Transformation
summary: The legendary Feadship motor yacht Gin-Tonic embarks on a journey of significant transformation at Pendennis shipyard in Cornwall.
body: Famed British shipyard Pendennis welcomes the arrival of classic 41.7-metre Feadship motor yacht, Gin-Tonic. The elegant superyacht is poised to undergo a significant refit programme. Touted as a 'complete transformation,' the upcoming works promise radical improvements, enhancing both performance and on-board living space. The transformation won't just be cosmetic, but structural, featuring extensions to the stern and bridge deck.

Adding to the structural enhancements, Pendennis plans to install two new main engines, simultaneously restoring the exterior with a comprehensive paint application for both her hull and superstructure. Set out in multiple phases, the initial refit is expected to stretch until early 2027.

Gin-Tonic holds a rich history, having initially been delivered by Dutch shipyard Feadship in 1981. This colossal vessel was one of three commissioned by the same owner in the 1980s. Frits De Voogt was at the helm of the yacht's exterior design and naval architecture, with British designer Mark Whiteley bringing the interiors to life. The thrilling news of this extensive refit comes following Gin-Tonic's sale to new owners in December last year. This transformation promises to revive an iconic classic, ensuring she proudly continues her legacy on the open waves.

title: Chef Aaron Thomas Scoops Top Prize at Superyacht Chef Contest 2026 on-board Motor Yacht Canvas
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Chef Aaron Thomas Scoops Top Prize at Superyacht Chef Contest 2026 on-board Motor Yacht Canvas
summary: Head chef Aaron Thomas, from the motor yacht Canvas, has emerged victorious at the seventh annual Superyacht Chef Competition, held in Monaco.
body: Setting the stage for an epic culinary battle, the seventh Superyacht Chef Competition was esteemed with spectacular flair. Astonishingly, it was the head chef of motor yacht Canvas, the esteemable Aaron Thomas, who emerged triumphant in this showdown held in the yacht playground, Monaco. With nine superyacht chefs taking to the kitchen, the competition was nothing short of breathtaking. Taking their place behind their respective stoves, the chefs were tasked with the challenge of creating a recipe, preparing, and plating it, all within the constraints of a restrictive 45 minute window. Given only a basket of mystery ingredients to work with, the stress was palpable. Moving onto the final round, participants were given 80 minutes to concoct a dessert and a main course to present in front of the esteemed panel of judges. Despite the hurdles, Thomas cooked up an exquisitely delectable lobster dish that ultimately stole the show. The two parter, a centerpiece of lobster accompanied by a morel fricassee and asparagus and a follow-up of lobster bisque, was highly lauded by the jury. A former UK Master Chef, Thomas highlighted the biggest challenge of the competition as the pace, claiming that preparing several dishes in such a short time was daunting. The jury, composed of renowned chefs and celebrities included two Michelin-star chef Philippe Etchebest from Meilleur Ouvrier de France, Italian culinary icon Carlo Cracco, cofounder of Oceanwave Monaco and superyacht chef Duncan Biggs, and Latin-American cuisine promoter, Jeeny Maltese. The artful presentation aboard the 28.7-metre Shockwave (now known as Bise I) made for an even more significant occasion. Bernard d’Alessandri, YCM director and general secretary expressed great delight in seeing rising enthusiasm for the contest, praising its support of young generations in their dreams of pursuing a maritime culinary career. The victory of Aaron Thomas, on the famed 33.5-metre Mangusta motor yacht Canvas, hence sets an inspiring precedent, redefining gourmet dining out at sea.

title: Turkish Yard RMK Marine and Design Studio Hot Lab Offer Triple Treat with New Explorer Yacht Concept
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Turkish Yard RMK Marine and Design Studio Hot Lab Offer Triple Treat with New Explorer Yacht Concept
summary: Turkish shipbuilder RMK Yachts together with Hot Lab design studio unveils Petra - a flexible 50-metre expedition yacht concept, designed to adapt to diverse ocean lifestyles.
body: In a match made to navigate the high seas, Turkish yard RMK Yachts and Milan-based design studio Hot Lab have birthed a remarkable concept: the 50-metre explorer Petra. This vessel pushes the envelope, veering from the traditional monolithic ship design by offering three distinct versions, each catering to unique owner preferences. Anchoring on flexibility, Petra introduces an unprecedented era of personalised maritime adventures.

First in the trio is the Aura. Described as the 'most lifestyle-oriented' design, Aura is for the ones at sea who prize comfort, warmth, and social cohesion. It sets the stage for relaxation and features an additional guest room, increased communal spaces, and a lower deck designated for entertainment.

Last but not least on the offering lineup is Infinite. Reflecting its name, the version is designed for endless sea adventures by merging generous spatial capacity with flexibility. In its repertoire are explorer must-haves – an ice class notation, helideck, abundant tender and crane capacity, water sports storage, optional hybrid propulsion and not to mention, the potential to conquer polar regions and transoceanic routes.

Each of the Petra trio is a unique interpretation of seafaring life. As Cuneyt Okcu, director of RMK Yachts, puts it, the Petra series is a flexible platform that accommodates an array of maritime lifestyles. The goal? To enable each vessel to become a reflection of the owner's personality and preferences.

The robust Petra will flaunt a steel hull, aluminium superstructure and teak decks. Thanks to her explorer soul, she'll offer a range of around 4,000 nautical miles at a maximum speed of 16 knots. She's further designed to transport and house large tenders, with fold-down bulwarks in her tender garage morphing into a beach club. Inside, the Petra is dressed in natural woods, sophisticated stones, leathers, and textured fabrics – chosen for their lasting quality and comforting appeal.

The creation of the Petra series indeed signals a bold, personal, and flexible approach to yacht design. It represents a fresh start for explorers on the high seas and sets sail towards an intriguing horizon in yachting.

title: Thrills and Spills: A Glimpse into the Excitement of BPI Subic and Antigua Racing Cup 2026
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Thrills and Spills: A Glimpse into the Excitement of BPI Subic and Antigua Racing Cup 2026
summary: Experience the adrenaline-pumping action of the BPI Series Subic Regatta and Antigua Racing Cup 2026 as fierce competition unfolds on the open seas.
body: Nothing beats the exhilaration of witnessing a top-level regatta, and the 2026 editions of the BPI Series Subic Regatta and Antigua Racing Cup proved no exception. The smell of the sea, the feel of the wind, and the sight of sleek vessels cutting through the waves- it's indeed a spectacle to behold.

With the breeze coming out of 110 degrees, the BPI Series Subic race was nothing short of adventurous. Race Officer Simon James devised a windward/leeward course that demanded advanced sailing technology and skill. However, it wasn't all smooth sailing. One involving incident saw the Centennial III colliding with the Belatrix, resulting in a 'gentlemanly altercation' and a little bit of awkward bowsprit interaction.

Days later, in the sun-soaked corners of Antigua, racing enthusiasts congregated for the annual Antigua Racing Cup. With 'high teens' gusting breezes topping 20 knots, competitors relished phenomenal tropical racing conditions on day one. Races were physically demanding, with punishing long beats offset by thrilling full-blooded runs, testing the endurance of even the seasoned sailors.

Adrian Lee's HH66 Catamaran, Lee Overlay Partners, was the star of the show, zipping along at over 20 knots through the idyllic Caribbean surf. Tackling the big boat class, Dan Gribble's custom Tripp 65, Prevail, fired across the finish line with an elapsed time of 3 hrs, 17 mins over the 24-nautical mile race. Sailing, as these two high-octane regattas prove, is about the thrill of the chase, the challenge of the elements, and the camaraderie among those braving the high seas.

title: Exhilarating BPI Series and Antigua Race of 2026: A Tale of Power, Precision, and Pure Sailing Passion
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Exhilarating BPI Series and Antigua Race of 2026: A Tale of Power, Precision, and Pure Sailing Passion
summary: Witness the full-throttle thrills of the 2026 Subic BPI Series Regatta and the Antigua Racing Cup. This recap takes you amid the swelling sails, heroic helmsmen, and unyielding trade winds.
body: The Subic BPI Series Regatta of 2026 etched itself into the annals of sailing history for truly unconventional reasons. One unforgettable moment earmarked that balmy April day was the high-seas joust between Centennial III and Belatrix. A fierce battle of nerve and expert seamanship unfolded, leaving spectators wide-eyed as Centennial III, owned by Judes Echauz of Standard Insurance, tried to outmaneuver Belatrix but ended in a crunch. With the air ripe with heavy uncertainty, a gentlemanly altercation ensued but was swiftly resolved without any red flags.

In both races, the commitment and resilience of all participants were a sight to behold. In the end, the victorious were those who married superior boat control with daring instinct. Despite the mishaps and momentous highs, these regattas proved once again that racing is not just about speed, but also the relationships formed and the enduring spirit of man against the sea. Spectacular scenes, yacht racing at its pinnacle, and the fervour of competition, serve as timely reminders of why the world of sailing continues to captivate.
