title: A Nautical Journey on a Princess V50 to Southern Brittany: The Experiences of First-time Motor Yacht Owners
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A Nautical Journey on a Princess V50 to Southern Brittany: The Experiences of First-time Motor Yacht Owners
summary: Join us on a thrilling adventure sailing on a Princess V50 to Southern Brittany and learn about the game-changing benefits of boat shares.
body: Venture with us to an enraptured place, Southern Brittany. Uncover its quaint climate and the beauty that lies 'around the corners', revealing itself only once you reach its threshold. Southern Brittany is a tourist's paradise, a sailor's dream. But navigating its small marinas and harbours with a 15m boat? More challenging than it may seem. Yet, Colin and Linda Le Conte found it to be an ideal spot to discover onboard their newly obtained, majestic Princess V50, Echo Beach. Their voyage, however, was marked by hurdles such as fuel accessibility, with local pumps enforcing a card limit of €180.

Meanwhile, across the waters, Duncan and Sophie Fergusson embarked on a different journey, as they bought their first motor yacht. Initially overwhelmed by the decisions and substantial investment, their quest led them to discover the compelling world of boat sharing. This practice unlocked an auxiliary space for social gaits and offered respite areas to their adolescents—proving that boating should accommodate everyone's comfort and needs.

So whether you're exploring the expanses on your Princess V50 or anticipating shared laughter on your communal yacht, remember—it's the shared experience with loved ones and nature that anchors these stories of thrilling adventures and life-altering discoveries. Life at sea offers unparalleled adventures, and it's only a matter of catching fair winds and partaking in the joy of maritime journeying. Now, isn't it time for you to set sail?

title: Gulf Craft Breaks Ground With Launch of Third Majestic 32-Metre Mastery 100 Terrace Yacht
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Gulf Craft Breaks Ground With Launch of Third Majestic 32-Metre Mastery 100 Terrace Yacht
summary: Gulf Craft, the revered UAE-based shipyard, has made waves by unveiling the third unit in its new majestic 32.3-meter Majesty 100 Terrace series.
body: The glistening azure water was split by the launch of the third yacht from Gulf Craft's invigorating new Majesty 100 Terrace line. This latest addition follows closely in the triumphant wake of the celebrated global debut of the pioneer of the series, Charisma. This vessel first coursed its way through the waters at the electrifying gatherings of the Dubai International Boat Show, Cannes Yachting Festival and Monaco Yacht Show, quickly solidifying its standing as a trailblazer in Gulf Craft's illustrious line-up.

The 32.3-metre Majesty 100 Terrace is a testament to Gulf Craft's ingenuity and ambition, marking another milestone in their extraordinary journey. With this launch, the shipyard echoes the continuous demand for a yacht that impeccably melds contemporary design, detailed craftsmanship, and the unmistakable sense of owner privacy that has become a hallmark of the Majesty 100 Terrace experience.

The masterful interiors and exteriors were the creative forge of the illustrious Dutch design agency, Phathom Studio. Gulf Craft's latest unveiling also underscores their adept lesson taken from their larger 34.1-metre Majesty 111, successfully emulating and reincarnating its key virtues on the 32.3-metre model. Since its unveiling at the 2024 Cannes Yachting Festival, the Majesty 100 Terrace has proven to outshine its counterparts as the shipyard's monumental best-seller.

Not one to rest on their laurels, Gulf Craft's CEO Erwin Bamps sheds light on the company's strategic ambitions, revealing that there are currently five superyachts on order or under construction. Even as they navigate through turbulent seas amid the ongoing tensions in the Middle East, the sense of adventure and remarkable waterborne craftmanship of Gulf Craft remains unscathed.

title: Enthralling debut of the sophisticated J/36 yacht in Australia – a symbiosis of luxury comfort and legendary performance
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Enthralling debut of the sophisticated J/36 yacht in Australia – a symbiosis of luxury comfort and legendary performance
summary: Celebrating the majestic arrival of the J/36 yacht in Australia, set to illuminate the blue waters with its dynamic allure and impressive performance.
body: Ensign Yachts, a proud flag-bearer of quality and design, has recently delivered the very first J/36 in Australia to a fortunate new proprietor in Melbourne. This impressive yacht, currently braving the open seas in its preliminary trials, is making waves with its commendable performance.

Anticipation builds with a public viewing of the J/36 announced for the 19th April 2026, at the prestigious Sandringham Yacht Club in Melbourne. This event presents a golden opportunity for sailing enthusiasts and boat lovers to witness this breathtaking vessel up close.

The J/36, an evolutionary leap from the much-revered J/112E, has already etched its name in the annals of sailing fame since its maiden voyage in 2016. Its palmarès boasts double victories at the ORC World Championship and notable triumphs at both the ORC and IRC European Championships among other accolades. This record of sterling achievements speaks volumes of the yacht's performance and capability.

Embarking onto uncharted waters, the new J/36 yacht aspires to impress Australian sailing aficionados with its legendary performance and unmatched cruising comfort. Watch out for its grand reception at Sandringham Yacht Club and seize the opportunity to experience the magic of J/36!

title: Motor Yacht A (MY A)
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Motor Yacht A (MY A)
summary: Motor Yacht A: The Superyacht That Redefines Ocean Couture, a 119-meter (390-foot) masterpiece that dropped jaws when it glided out of Blohm+Voss’s HDW deepwater shipyard in Kiel, Germany, back in 2008. Commissioned by Russian billionaire Andrey Melnichenko—a man with a taste for the audacious—and sculpted by the visionary Philippe Starck with naval finesse from Martin Francis, this super yacht is a bold statement in
body: Picture this: Motor Yacht A (MY A), a 119-meter (390-foot) masterpiece that dropped jaws when it glided out of Blohm+Voss’s HDW deepwater shipyard in Kiel, Germany, back in 2008. Commissioned by Russian billionaire Andrey Melnichenko—a man with a taste for the audacious—and sculpted by the visionary Philippe Starck with naval finesse from Martin Francis, this super yacht is a bold statement in maritime luxury. With a near-6,000-ton heft and a rumoured $300 million price tag, plus a cool $30 million annual upkeep, it’s a floating testament to excess and innovation, turning heads even today.

Starck’s design is pure avant-garde genius, born from a flash of inspiration he claims took mere minutes (though he later admitted to a month of refinement). The exterior is a sleek, silver-hulled dream, its reverse bow and tumblehome silhouette echoing the stealthy lines of a US Navy Zumwalt-class destroyer. It’s less a yacht, more a futuristic cruiser, with mirrored glass panels reflecting the ocean like a high-fashion runway. At 24.5 meters wide and a draft of 5.1 meters, it cuts through the water with minimal wake—Starck’s nod to a whale-like grace—making it a standout at elite gatherings like the Monaco Grand Prix (kicking off May 23–25, 2025).

The deck layout flips the script on tradition. Forget aft-heavy designs—Motor Yacht A boasts a forward lounge exposed to the sea breeze, sheltered by a chic overhang, a throwback to Starck’s racing days on the Seine. Spanning seven decks, it hosts 14 guests and a crew of 37 to 42 with aplomb. The tender garage, dubbed “cathedral-like” by Starck, houses custom limo tenders, while a helipad and three pools—one with a glass bottom doubling as a disco ceiling—elevate the experience. It’s a playground for the jet set, spotted recently in Galle, Sri Lanka, per X buzz on May 21, 2025.

Inside, it’s minimalist luxury with a twist. White leather walls meet dark Baccarat crystal accents, crafting a stark, almost surgical chic. The main salon, a two-deck marvel, features a mirrored ceiling and oval windows framing ocean vistas, while Baccarat chandeliers add a decadent sparkle. The owner’s suite steals the show with a rotating bed facing panoramic glass, a touch of sci-fi romance. Gold-fitted bathrooms and cutting-edge entertainment systems complete the vibe, blending comfort with high-tech allure.

Power comes from twin MAN diesels, pushing a top speed of 23 knots and a cruising range over 3,000 nautical miles at 12 to 18 knots. Its efficiency-focused design aligns with Starck’s eco-conscious edge, though the yacht’s opulence—fuelled by Melnichenko’s EuroChem and SUEK billions—raises eyebrows. Delivered in 2008, it faced a $100 million paint job lawsuit against Akzo Nobel in 2013, and in 2022, sanctions saw it laid up in the UAE. Ownership rumours tied it to Masayoshi Son, though Melnichenko’s team debunked that, keeping its status enigmatic.

Motor Yacht A is a love-it-or-hate-it icon. Its stealthy, angular beauty divides critics—some call it a design triumph, others a billionaire’s folly. For the discerning Oldseadogs.com reader, it’s a pinnacle of yachting couture, where innovation meets extravagance. Whether it’s cruising the Med or docked in controversy, this yacht remains a must-watch in 2025’s maritime scene.

title: Pacifica 44 – A True Cruiser’s Classic
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Pacifica 44 - Review
summary: In the age of sleek express yachts and fast planing hulls, the Pacifica 44 stands as a proud holdout of traditional long-range cruising. With its rugged construction, classic lines, and proven trawler hull, the Pacifica 44 is a yacht built not for flash—but for distance, dependability, and the pure joy of slow travel. For those who measure their boating not in horsepower but in nautical miles, this is a vessel worth
body: Though no longer in production, the Pacifica 44 remains a highly respected and sought-after long-distance cruiser, especially among serious boaters doing the Great Loop, extended coastal voyages, or even the occasional offshore passage. Built in the 1980s and early 1990s, primarily in Taiwan for American and international buyers, the Pacifica 44 is a testament to a different era of boatbuilding—when long-term livability, seaworthiness, and simplicity took priority over trend.

The first thing that strikes you about the Pacifica 44 is its timeless trawler profile: a high bow with forward rake, a low, protected deckhouse, and a generous flybridge perched above. It’s an honest boat, built with purpose. The hull is hand-laid fiberglass, with a long, full keel that provides stability, directional tracking, and protection for the running gear.

Two common layouts exist: the classic aft-cabin configuration and the sundeck sedan version, both offering two generous cabins, two heads, and ample outdoor space. The standard model has a raised pilothouse with dual side doors—perfect for single- or short-handed handling—and a lower helm with excellent visibility.

Below deck, you’ll find a warm, wood-trimmed interior, often finished in teak or mahogany, with thoughtful use of space. The master stateroom aft features a queen berth, generous storage, and a private en suite head. The forward guest cabin typically has a V-berth or island berth, also with its own head. Between the two lies a cozy saloon and either an up or down galley, depending on the model.

Despite its vintage, the Pacifica 44’s layout still holds up well against modern trawlers. Headroom is ample, berths are adult-sized, and there’s a surprising amount of closet and locker space, making this boat truly livable for long-term voyagers.

The Pacifica 44 offers secure, walk-around side decks with high bulwarks and sturdy stainless-steel handrails—one of its great strengths for serious cruising. The aft deck is covered and often used for outdoor dining or lounging, with access to a swim platform and a ladder for water access.

Up top, the flybridge is large, with room for a helm station, seating, and dinghy storage with a crane. Visibility is panoramic, and many owners retrofit full canvas and isinglass enclosures for all-weather use. The layout promotes easy socialising and great views whether underway or at anchor.
The forward deck includes a proper anchor platform with windlass, chain locker, and twin anchor setup, built for long stays at anchor and reliable holding in variable conditions.

Powering the Pacifica 44 is typically a single or twin diesel engine setup—most often Ford Lehman 120s, Perkins 135s, or Cummins 210s. While twin engines provide better close-quarters maneuvering, the single-engine versions are more common and are prized for their simplicity, fuel economy, and long lifespan.

At a cruising speed of 7 to 9 knots, the Pacifica 44 is remarkably fuel efficient, burning as little as 3–4 gallons per hour, with a cruising range of over 1,000 nautical miles thanks to its 500–600 gallon fuel capacity. It’s the perfect pace for those not in a rush—loopers, passagemakers, and those who want to savour the journey.

Handling is gentle and predictable. The full keel gives the boat a stable ride in beam seas, and while she’s not fast, she’s tough, capable, and gives a steady motion that makes long days on board comfortable.

Given their age, many Pacifica 44s have been updated over time with new electronics, upgraded galley appliances, solar panels, inverter systems, and diesel heating or air conditioning. With good bones, these boats are highly modifiable and well-suited to off-grid cruising.
Most are equipped with:
Onan or Northern Lights generators
Pressure hot/cold water systems
Full-size refrigerators
Navigation electronics (modernised in many cases)
Large blackwater and freshwater tanks for extended stays
The engine room is spacious, well laid out, and generally allows easy access for maintenance—a key feature for those doing their own upkeep.
Excellent value on the used market
Timeless, seaworthy design
Fuel-efficient and reliable
Comfortable for long-term cruising or liveaboard
Full walk-around decks and safe offshore layout
Age-related wear: electrical rewiring, soft decks, and old plumbing are common
Fuel tank corrosion (especially steel tanks)
Some boats may need repowering or refitting
Gelcoat blistering or wood rot in older poorly maintained examples
With a good marine survey and a bit of TLC, a Pacifica 44 can become a trustworthy floating home for decades.
This boat is perfect for:
Liveaboards and retirees seeking long-term comfort
Great Loop cruisers
Coastal and intercoastal voyagers
First-time trawler buyers looking for big features at reasonable prices
It’s not for those who want to go fast or show off. It’s for those who appreciate stability, space, and simplicity—and who find joy in the slow, steady cadence of true cruising.
Length Overall (LOA) 44 ft (13.4 m)
Beam 14 ft 6 in (4.42 m)
Draft 4 ft (1.22 m)
Fuel Capacity 500–600 gallons (1,893–2,271 L)
Water Capacity 250–300 gallons (946–1,135 L)
Engines Single or twin diesel (often Lehman, Perkins, or Cummins)
Cruising Speed 7–10 knots
Top Speed 11–14 knots (semi-displacement hulls)
Range ~1,000–1,500 nautical miles
Cabins 2 (master + guest)
Heads 2 with showers
The Pacifica 44 typically features:
A raised pilothouse with excellent visibility, side deck access doors, and full instrumentation
A saloon with galley down or galley-up layout, depending on model
A master stateroom aft with private head and shower
A forward guest cabin (V-berth or island berth), also with private head
A spacious flybridge with seating, helm controls, and optional Bimini
Wide side decks with high bulwarks for safe movement around the boat
A large aft deck for entertaining or storage
The interior is traditionally finished in teak or mahogany, giving a warm, nautical feel. Most versions include air conditioning, diesel heat, a generator, and ample tankage for serious cruising.

While not a speedster, the Pacifica 44 is built for economy and range. Cruising at 7–9 knots, fuel consumption is often around 3–4 gallons per hour, making her ideal for the Great Loop, coastal cruising, or even offshore passages.

The hull offers excellent directional stability, and a full keel provides added protection for the running gear. In twin-engine versions, maneuverability is strong—even without thrusters—while single-engine setups are more fuel-efficient but benefit from a bow thruster in tight quarters.
Fuel-efficient and ocean-capable
Timeless trawler styling
Large covered decks and flybridge
Spacious interior for extended stays
Excellent value on the used market
Age-related wear: Many Pacifica 44s are 30–40 years old
Check for fuel tank corrosion, electrical system updates, and deck leaks
Many have been repowered—check engine hours and installation quality
Some interiors may need cosmetic updating depending on owner care
The Pacifica 44 is ideal for:
Liveaboards or cruising couples
Boaters doing the Great Loop
Bluewater adventurers seeking a rugged platform
Those who value slow, steady, and reliable over flash and speed

The Pacifica 44 is not just a boat—it’s a philosophy. It represents a slower, more deliberate way to travel the world’s waterways. With generous tankage, rugged construction, and all the features needed for long-term comfort, it’s a vessel built for those who value the journey over the destination.
For anyone seeking a dependable, characterful trawler at a fair price, the Pacifica 44 remains one of the finest examples of its kind—a classic cruiser that still earns its stripes, mile after mile.

title: Princess F58 made a Show-Stopping Debut at Cannes Yachting Festival 2025
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Princess F58 Debut at Cannes Yachting Festival 2025
summary: Princess Yachts, Britain’s largest luxury yacht builder and a name synonymous with craftsmanship, performance, and timeless design, has announced that the all-new Princess F58 made her world show debut at the Cannes Yachting Festival 2025
body: This striking addition to the acclaimed F Class Flybridge range slots neatly between the popular F55 and flagship F65, delivering a fresh balance of size, style, and substance. For those who demand performance and luxury in equal measure, the F58 looks set to be one of the most talked-about yachts of the season.

The Princess F Class has long been the standard-bearer of the luxury flybridge market, and the F58 embodies the essence of the range. She blends elegant lines, expansive social spaces, and cutting-edge engineering into a package that feels both timeless and distinctly forward-looking.

With a choice of MAN V8-1000 or MAN V8-1200 engines, the F58 offers exhilarating performance with top speeds of up to 34 knots – more than enough to eat up the coastline of the French Riviera. She also becomes the first Princess yacht under 80 feet to feature the innovative hotel-services battery option, enabling sustainable silent running for onboard systems. For eco-conscious owners, this is a significant leap forward in responsible luxury yachting.

The flybridge of the F58 has been carefully designed with social living at its heart. A large dining area and fully equipped wet bar with electric barbecue sit aft, creating the ultimate space for entertaining. The central helm provides superb visibility while a second companion seat ensures no skipper has to sail alone.

Sun lovers are well catered for, too – the starboard seating effortlessly converts into a generous sunpad. Whether dining, lounging, or soaking up the views of Cannes, the flybridge sets the tone for everything the F58 represents: space, comfort, and style without compromise.

The innovation continues forward with the foredeck terrace, a feature borrowed from Princess’s larger yachts. Twin sunpads with adjustable headrests can transform into aft-facing seats, creating a versatile space equally suited to private relaxation or entertaining.

At the stern, the cockpit flows seamlessly into the saloon and galley, maximising sociability. This space leads directly to the hydraulic bathing platform and transom “beach club” area. Owners can choose layouts with toy storage, a waterside barbecue with sink, and a fold-down transom seat – the perfect waterside retreat for a morning swim or sundowner drinks.

Step inside, and the Princess DNA is unmistakable. Panoramic windows flood the saloon with natural light, creating a seamless connection between indoors and out. A U-shaped sofa with a convertible coffee/dining table sits opposite an additional sofa, making this an inviting hub for entertaining or unwinding at anchor.

The aft galley is ideally positioned between cockpit and saloon, reinforcing the F58’s sociable layout. Modern yet timeless finishes run throughout, with Princess’s renowned craftsmanship on full display.
On the lower deck, accommodation is generous and flexible:
A full-beam owner’s stateroom with breakfast area, walk-in wardrobe, and a superyacht-style ensuite.
A VIP forward cabin for guests.
A twin to starboard, which converts into a double if required.
An optional aft crew cabin with ensuite completes the accommodation, ensuring practicality for longer passages or professional operation.

Princess’s introduction of the battery-powered hotel services option on the F58 is a notable milestone. Owners can enjoy silent, emission-free operation of air conditioning, refrigeration, lighting, and other amenities while at anchor – combining environmental responsibility with absolute comfort.
This move positions Princess at the forefront of the sustainable luxury yacht market, responding to growing demand for greener yachting without compromising performance or style.

The Princess F58 is already generating excitement among buyers, dealers, and enthusiasts. With her sleek profile, outstanding specification, and thoughtful innovations, she fills an important niche in the Princess lineup – offering more space and luxury than the F55, while remaining more accessible and manageable than the flagship F65.
Her debut at the Cannes Yachting Festival 2025 was a defining moment for the shipyard, as the global yachting community gathers to see what promises to be one of the standout premieres of the season.
As Princess Yachts puts it, the F58 is “a yacht without compromise” – and from her lines, features, and performance promises, it’s hard to argue otherwise.

title: A Display of Tenacity: Derbyshire Blue Conquers in High-Spirited NSSA Double Handed Team Racing Championships
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A Display of Tenacity: Derbyshire Blue Conquers in High-Spirited NSSA Double Handed Team Racing Championships
summary: A mix of intense competition, heartening camaraderie, and youthful vigor defined the NSSA Double Handed Team Racing Championships at the Yorkshire Dales Sailing Club.
body: Sailing isn't simply about traversing waters or conquering winds—it’s a thrilling adventure of speed, strategy, and camaraderie. This sentiment was evident at the National School Sailing Association (NSSA) Double Handed Team Racing Championships, held at the picturesque Yorkshire Dales Sailing Club (YDSC). The event, hosted by North East & Yorkshire Youth Sailing Association (NEYYSA), was a veritable show of grit, teamwork, and unrivaled passion for sailing.

This year's championship saw a vibrant mix of 116 sailors forming 29 teams from 15 distinct organisations nationwide. The thrilling dynamic of racing blended perfectly with the backdrop of Yorkshire Dales' stunning scenery, adding a ripple of anticipation in the air. However, what made this event truly unique was the spirit of unity and friendly competition that prevailed throughout.

NEYYSA, resolute in its zeal to promote junior and youth sailing, curated an environment for building friendships and fostering a love for the sport. In harping on the same, each event had a seasoned lead to exhibit a rotating cast of volunteers, thereby encouraging knowledge sharing and the growth of a new generation committed to the sport's continuity.

The weather, surprisingly, played a coy mistress, with wind conditions proving to be challenging. However, this did not deter the wily sailors – instead, they used this time to socialise and soak up the vibrant atmosphere. When racing finally commenced, it was a marvellous spectacle of focused minds and dexterous maneuvering, undeterred by the capricious winds.

Photographs from the event showcase a flurry of action, interspersed with hearty laughter and shared tales of the sea. These spirited snapshots, much like the event, embody a powerful testament of sailing's timeless allure.

title: Italian Marvel on Water - A Revealing First Look at the Magnificent Solaris Power 70 Long Range
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Italian Marvel on Water - A Revealing First Look at the Magnificent Solaris Power 70 Long Range
summary: Meet the new Solaris 70 LR, an exceptional flagship from Solaris, the reputable Italian yard. This is not a mere extension of its sportier brethren, but a different beast entirely, intended for long-range, liveaboard cruising.
body: Introducing the Solaris 70 Long Range, a nautical marvel from the esteemed Italian boatyards of Solaris. Celebrated for their sportier Open and Coupé models, the renowned manufacturer has shifted their helm to chart new waters, creating a vessel intended for long-range liveaboards rather than simply being a glamorous day boat. The fresh course begins with a Category A rated semi-displacement hull, engineered for comfortable and fuel-efficient voyages at speeds varying from 8-22 knots. Powered by Twin IPS pod drives along with 4,100-litre tanks, the Solaris 70 LR promises a remarkable cruising range reaching up to 900 nautical miles at a consistent speed of 12 knots. However, the Italian artistry does not wane in this pragmatic design. The Solaris 70 LR showcases numerous design frills, harking back to a Solaris hallmark. Starting with an oversized aft cockpit featuring two extravagant lounging and dining areas, onto an extended hydraulic platform granting access to capacious storage—perfect for stowing away tenders or even a pair of Seabobs. One of the optional design executions is the installation of a massive folding balcony along the starboard side connecting seamlessly to a sliding side door in the saloon. This ingenious design blurs the boundary between the indoors and the outdoors, fringing the edges of the luxurious world within and the enchanting sights of the open sea. Inside, the customization options continue to amaze. The lower deck can be tailored to suit varying needs – from having two full-beam VIP suites at either end, or opting for three ensuite doubles and a considerable twin. A compact crew cabin adds the final touch to this meticulously crafted, dream liveaboard cruiser. The Solaris Power 70 Long Range, with its captivating blend of Italian flair and robust functionality, enters the market as a disruptive entrant in the world of luxury yachts, setting a new standard for indulgence and allure.

title: Offshore fishing machines built for the bold
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Invincible Boats
summary: Salt spray in the face, throttles down, and a hard horizon ahead — if there’s a boat brand that has built its entire reputation on fearlessness offshore, it’s Invincible Boats. In the world of center console fishing, these boats are more than fiberglass and horsepower. They’re weapons.
body: Born in Miami in 2006, Invincible set out with one mission: to build the fastest, most comfortable, most reliable offshore fishing boats in the world. Not lifestyle ornaments, not marina showpieces — but serious fishing machines. And in less than two decades, they’ve carved out a cult-like following among offshore anglers who demand nothing less than bulletproof performance.
This is the Invincible story: where they came from, why they matter, and the boats that define the fleet.

Invincible’s rise begins in South Florida — the proving ground of sportfishing, speed, and saltwater endurance. Founder Alex Lipworth was a fisherman who grew frustrated with what was on the market. At the time, most centre consoles were either slow, wet rides or high-maintenance headaches. Lipworth’s idea was simple: build a hull that would crush the competition offshore, then wrap it in rugged luxury.

The key breakthrough came with the Michael Peters–designed stepped Vee Ventilated Tunnel (SVVT) hull. This hull allowed Invincible boats to run faster with less horsepower, while keeping a stable, dry, and predictable ride — something that quickly turned heads from Florida to the Gulf Coast.

Add tournament-ready decks, wide beams, and some of the largest fuel capacities in class, and Invincible became the go-to badge for offshore anglers who wanted to run further, fish harder, and come home faster.
The Invincible Philosophy: Built Without Compromise
Invincible Boats hang their hat on a few core principles:
Speed & Efficiency: Their SVVT hulls and power packages allow 65–75 mph runs depending on setup, even on 40+ foot platforms. For anglers, that means more fishing time, less travel time.
Range: With fuel capacities topping 1,000 gallons on larger models, Invincible boats can strike offshore canyons and return without refuelling.
Fishability: 360-degree walkaround decks, cavernous livewells, insulated fish boxes, and rigging stations are designed for serious crews, not cocktail parties.
Customisation: Layouts are flexible — twin rows of helm seating, coffin boxes, tower options — designed to fit owner’s fishing style.
Rugged Luxury: Not as plush as some competitors, but interiors are sleek, modern, and practical. Every surface is built to hose down after a bloody day offshore.
As one Florida captain put it: “An Invincible is a boat you drive hard, fish hard, and trust. Everything else is just marketing.”
The Invincible Fleet: Centre Consoles & Cats
Invincible’s lineup has grown from a single centre console into a complete range of monohulls and catamarans. Each model has a distinct purpose, but all share the same DNA — performance fishing.

33’ Open Fisherman The smallest in the fleet, but no less fierce. Ideal for anglers who want a tournament-ready platform that’s trailerable and fast. Twin or triple outboard setups push this hull with authority.
36’ Open Fisherman The classic. A versatile centre console that’s equally at home chasing tuna offshore or running to the Bahamas. Known for its efficiency and seaworthiness.
39’ Open Fisherman A powerhouse of a fishing boat, often rigged with triple or quad outboards. Massive deck space, larger fuel capacity, and a serious offshore pedigree.

42’ Center Cabin The “convertible” of the Invincible world. Offers the fishability of a centre console with a small cabin for overnight trips. A favourite among hardcore anglers who want a little comfort.

46’ Pilothouse The long-range weapon. Fully enclosed helm, air-conditioning, berths, and galley options. It’s a beast designed for serious expeditions where weather and distance are part of the adventure.
Invincible Catamarans

In 2017, Invincible shook up the industry again by introducing catamaran hulls. Partnering with distinguished naval architect Morrelli & Melvin, they brought speed and stability together in ways few fishing cats had before.
35’ Catamaran Compact, agile, and perfect for those stepping into cat platforms. Stable at rest, efficient on fuel, and surprisingly quick.
37’ Catamaran A proven offshore contender, ideal for anglers who want more beam and range without stepping up to the giants.
40’ Catamaran Arguably the sweet spot of the lineup. Massive deck space, long legs, and speeds over 70 mph with quad outboards. A fan favourite among hardcore offshore tournament crews.

46’ Catamaran The flagship. A 1,200-gallon fuel tank, quads or even quint outboards, and more fishing room than most sportfishermen twice its price. This is the definition of “go anywhere, catch anything.”
The centre console market is crowded, with brands like Contender, Freeman, Yellowfin, and Valhalla all vying for dominance. What sets Invincible apart?
Catamaran edge: Their cats are among the fastest and best-engineered on the market. Freeman may have pioneered the space, but Invincible has pushed it mainstream.
Performance first: Some brands lean luxury, but Invincible leans purpose. These are boats you fish hard and put away salty.
Resale value: Strong brand loyalty and demand keep values high.
Invincible owners are a tribe. From Florida tournaments to Texas rodeos, their boats show up fast, loud, and ready. Social media is full of monster tuna and swordfish hauled across their wide decks.
The company itself fosters this identity — no soft-focus marketing, just speed runs, big fish, and salt-streaked faces. They’ve built a reputation that feels authentic because it is.
Conclusion: Why Invincible Matters

Invincible Boats aren’t just another name in the endless parade of centre consoles. They are a benchmark. Whether it’s the SVVT hull monohulls or the Morrelli & Melvin cats, these boats represent the cutting edge of performance fishing design.
For anglers who demand range, speed, and fishability — and who aren’t afraid of four (or five) roaring outboards on the transom — Invincible is the dream ticket.
As one salty owner said dockside in Miami: “If you want a boat that’ll take you out there, bring you back, and beat everyone else to the fish — get an Invincible.”

title: Why Britain’s Superyacht Industry is Poised to Navigate Uncharted Waters
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Why Britain’s Superyacht Industry is Poised to Navigate Uncharted Waters
summary: As Britain's superyacht industry embarks upon its future beyond 2026, key challenges and opportunities await to redefine the nation's maritime legacy.
body: With the dawn of post-2026 era in sight, Britain's superyacht industry stands at a crossroads marked by opportunities which, if harnessed effectively, can further cement the nation's long-standing maritime legacy. Though a beacon of excellence in design, law, and insurance, it's important to recognize a critical underpinning: the industry's success is directly tied to the physical presence of large superyachts.

A notable challenge, deterring the industry's forward march, is the dearth of large-scale refit sheds and dry docks. As the global fleet of 100 metre-plus superyachts grows by leaps and bounds, the demand for maintenance, repair, and overhaul—known as MRO—has escalated. While more owners are eyeing UK as a cruising destination, the existing refit facilities are evidently struggling to match pace. Addressing this glaring disparity is vital not just for attracting vessels to British waters, but for sustaining the health of the nation's supply chain.

Indeed, the refit sector operates as a high-value fulcrum of the supply chain industry. With refit jobs stretching from three months to a year, the sector breathes life into local employment opportunities, enriching the economy. Incentives for more large superyachts to operate within British zones could be a game-changer. Increased days at sea for the global fleet within British Isles would ensure a stable demand for local services. By proactively addressing these challenges and exploiting opportunities, the British Isles can aspire to take on the role of global leaders in servicing the world’s most sophisticated vessels, anchoring a stronger, brighter future for Britain's superyacht industry.

title: The Sofia Season Kicks Off With Exceptional Sailing and Intense Competition in the 470 Class
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Sofia Season Kicks Off With Exceptional Sailing and Intense Competition in the 470 Class
summary: As northern Europe stirs from a wintry slumber, the Bay of Palma ignites with unparalleled sailing. With the launch of the Sofia season opener, the 470 Class competitions increase the thrill factor.
body: The Bay of Palma is more than just azure waters, it’s a favourite among sailors for both regattas and training. From its steady winds to the splendid sunshine, it offers conditions that make for an exhilarating sailing experience. It is the ideal setting for the Sofia Season Opener, an event that draws both seasoned and aspiring sailors to embark on an exciting nautical adventure. The event also marks the opening of the 55th Trofeo Princesa Sofia Mallorca, drawing participants from all over the world for intense racing.

Offering a unique challenge to sailors, the unusual occurrence of snow on the Serra de Tramuntana mountains doesn't dampen the spirits of the sailors, who come prepared to brave the elements. It is common to see sailors from Olympic class to Hansa classes commence the thrilling journey, yearning for victory.

The 470 Class at the 55th Trofeo Princesa Sofia was an absolute sensation. The event saw Matisse Pacaud and Lucie de Gennes (FRA) win two races in the yellow fleet, sliding into the overall lead. Newly crowned European champions Martin Wrigley and Bettine Harris (GBR), dominated their blue fleet and are moving up the ranks.

In the mix, British sailor Micky Beckett, a multi-time winner of the ILCA 7 class, is on a quest for the Princesa Sofia title. His tenacity amidst fierce competition shows why the Princesa Sofia is one of the most coveted prizes in world sailing.

The thrill of competition, the camaraderie amongst sailors and the allure of the Bay of Palma all culminate to make the Sofia Season Opener an exceptional event, a testament to the beauty and excitement of sailing.

title: All Hands on Deck: The Glory and Adventure of The 55th Trofeo Princesa Sofia Mallorca and the 470 Class
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: All Hands on Deck: The Glory and Adventure of The 55th Trofeo Princesa Sofia Mallorca and the 470 Class
summary: Immerse yourself in the captivating world of sailing as we delve into the Sofia Season Opener's spectacular launch in the mesmerising Bay of Palma.
body: The Bay of Palma, a gem for sailing enthusiasts, recently opened its waters for the Sofia Season Opener. Even as northern Europe wakes from its winter slumber, Mallorca is awash in seven hours of daily sunshine, making it an idyllic location for sailors. For those participating in the early stages of the 55th Trofeo Princesa Sofia Mallorca, the winds have been ideal, ranging between 15 to 20 knots and making for phenomenal racing.

One unusual attraction this year has been the snow-dusted peaks of Serra de Tramuntana, adding a beautiful contrast to the sunny island landscape. However, the weather remains excellent for sailing, promising ample enjoyment for sailors who've packed a few extra warm layers.

The Princesa Sofia is anything but small, boasting over 900 boats and more than 1,100 sailors from 62 different countries. It marks the grand opening of the 2026 Sailing Grand Slam, organised by a cooperative effort between Palma's major clubs, the Balearic Sailing Federation, and the Royal Spanish Sailing Federation. To promote and secure future growth, a foundation called Bahía Activa has been established to facilitate the collaboration of clubs and organisations.

Leading up to Princesa Sofia, several Olympic class sailors make Palma their base. Equipped with world-class facilities, reliable winds, and delectable Mediterranean fare, Palma becomes a beloved home away from home for countless sailors. The well-connected Palma de Mallorca Airport further bolsters the city's appeal.

title: Reimagining Britain's Superyacht Infrastructure: Bridging the Gap Between Heritage and Future
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Reimagining Britain's Superyacht Infrastructure: Bridging the Gap Between Heritage and Future
summary: Britain, a nation revered for its maritime excellence, is at a crossroads in the superyacht industry, warranting strategic evolution and enhancement.
body: The United Kingdom's substantial maritime heritage, dating back to the age-old shipyards of the South Coast to the industrious northern engineering hubs, stands as a testament to its unrivalled quality. Recognized globally for its prowess in design, law, and insurance, the UK's superyacht sector now faces a significant turning point.

At the heart of this dynamic industry lies a fundamental law: the strength of the superyacht supply chain is intrinsically linked to large superyachts' physical presence in our waters. The so-called 'dockside economy' thrives when a massive 60-metre vessel makes a port or marina its temporary home, deploying a high-demand spectrum of services, from high-end provisioning to concierge services. As these marine giants serve as floating businesses, the domestic economy witnesses a chain-reaction support surge among local SMEs.

Increasing the global fleet's days at sea within the British Isles guarantees a sturdy demand for local services. It empowers the marine sector to flourish by providing services to the sophisticated global fleet right at their own doorstep.

However, obstacles still lie ahead. The lack of dedicated, large-scale refit sheds and dry docks, that can efficiently accommodate modern large superyachts, is a significant impediment to growth. With an unprecedented boom in superyacht deliveries worldwide and a consequential rise in demands for maintenance, repair and overhaul, the UK must step up its infrastructure.

Refits play an integral role in the supply chain, being the most labour-intensive and high-value segment. Tailoring the domestic facilities to cater to this essential sector will not only retain superyachts in UK waters for their necessary winter work-list but will also secure more business for the UK from the rapidly growing global superyacht fleet.

title: Step into Maritime History with the Exquisite Schooner 'Columbia': An Icon of American Ingenuity and Heritage
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Step into Maritime History with the Exquisite Schooner 'Columbia': An Icon of American Ingenuity and Heritage
summary: Making waves in the naval world is the breathtaking American Schooner 'Columbia', a spectacle of classic design and modern engineering on the high seas.
body: There is something magically captivating about tall ships. With their towering masts extending over 30 metres and adorned with robust white sails, they represent the daring spirit of seafarers, the immense desire for discovery, and the beginnings of transoceanic exploration. Today, they are majestic reminders of our maritime history and human bravery.

One such marvel is the U.S.-built, 43-metre Schooner 'Columbia'. A classic blend of engineering genius, elegant design, and high-class performance, the 'Columbia' is a modern homage to its predecessor, the original 1923 Gloucester fishing schooner. Conceived by Brian D'Isernia, a well-reputed U.S. shipbuilder and founder of Eastern Shipbuilding Group, the 'Columbia' not only highlights the artisanal art of shipbuilding, but it also stands as an embodiment of heritage and modernity.

Now, for the first time, the 'Columbia', originally donated by D’Isernia to a maritime-focused charity, will partake in the 2026 Sail4th 250 celebrations. These celebrations comprise a flotilla of over 50 tall ships from around the globe, making it one of the most significant maritime events ever staged. Its presence at the centrepiece of the 250th anniversary of the United States' independence celebrations signify the alignment of the 'Columbia' with the spirit of Americana.

Carrying on her predecessor's legacy, the 'Columbia' beholds the grandeur of the original design, which gained renown on both the fishing grounds and the regatta circuit, even challenging the Canadian Schooner Bluenose in the International Fishermen’s Cup Races. As a testament to the historic A.D. Story shipyard where it was built, it heralds the evolution of schooner design and stands as a beacon for American shipbuilding prowess.

Stepping aboard the 'Columbia' is an invitation to travel back in time, to a period of maritime dominance and discovery. Yet, it also offers a taste of the boundless possibilities of the present. Marvel at the modern capability of this superyacht as she sails forth, a perfect example of living history on the high seas.

title: SF Group Propels Panama into the Spotlight with Landmark Superyacht Marina Project
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: SF Group Propels Panama into the Spotlight with Landmark Superyacht Marina Project
summary: Swedish dock firm, SF Group, lays out ambitious plans to transform Panama into a thriving hub for superyacht cruising with the Port Amador marina project.
body: Steering the future of superyacht cruising is the SF Group, a prominent player from Sweden known for their marina specialties. Their latest ambition is to bring about a landmark transformation in Central American waters with their Port Amador marina project unveiled in Panama. Not only does this announcement mark a sizeable enlargement into this market, but it places the project at the Pacific entrance to the vital Panama Canal. Set to revolutionise the Amador Causeway, this initiative commands attention as a burgeoning hub for Eastern Pacific superyacht ventures.

Panama is tactically placed just minutes away from Panama City, with two international airports offering private aviation access within convenient range. Port Amador will furnish yachts with direct connectivity to both the Pacific and Atlantic via the Canal - a boon to seamless voyaging between oceans from a single home port.

The blueprint of this project has been drawn out to satiate the rising demand for extensive yacht infrastructure in the region. The marina infrastructure will also accommodate high-capacity fueling, shore power, comprehensive maintenance services and on-site customs and immigration clearance. All these elements fall in line with international superyacht standards. Security measures will not be compromised either, with ISPS compliance, controlled access and round-the-clock surveillance in place.

From boutique hotels, waterfront domiciles, retail hubs, to waterfront dining, Port Amador plans to cater to the preferences of the most discerning visitors. The first Pacific outpost of the elite Beaufort Yacht Club will also grace its precincts. With convenient access to awe-inspiring locations like the Galápagos Islands, the Pacific coast of Central America and longer expedition corridors to Alaska and Patagonia, Panama is poised as the doorway to fresh and remote cruising territories.

There are no full construction timelines available at this juncture. SF Group is staying the course with their global expansion trajectory, and with this project, they are drawing the world’s attention to Panama’s emerging role in the future of superyacht cruising.

title: Unraveling Peter Burling's Pivotal Decision to Switch Sides to Luna Rossa in America's Cup
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unraveling Peter Burling's Pivotal Decision to Switch Sides to Luna Rossa in America's Cup
summary: Discover the inside story of Peter Burling's surprising move from Emirates Team New Zealand to Italian champions Luna Rossa- all over a coffee chat.
body: The grand unveiling of Luna Rossa Prada Pirelli's AC75 in Cagliari, Sardinia, in April 2024 not only marked the beginning of an exhilarating racing season but also gave an insider's look into the seamless transition of America's Cup legend Peter Burling to the Italian team.

A series of interviews with key team members of Luna Rossa, including Burling himself and the CEO, Max Sirena, throws light on the circumstances that led to Burling's bold decision to switch allegiances.

The three-time America's Cup winner opened up about what led him to break ties with his former team, Emirates Team New Zealand (ETNZ). According to Burling, he envisioned spending more time pursuing other projects. Unfortunately, he couldn't reach a mutual agreement with ETNZ, leading to a separation.

The move wasn't a hasty decision. Burling reportedly had talks with other teams, yet he felt an undeniable pull towards Luna Rossa. Familiar with several team members who formed part of the victorious 2017 ETNZ campaign in Bermuda, Burling found Luna Rossa's team structure and synergy closest to what he had been used to at ETNZ. This tale unveils the intrigues of racing dynamics, personal preferences, and team chemistry in determining the course of sailing legends!

title: Experience the All-New Luxury at Sea with the Debut of Mitan, Numarine's Second Model from the 40MXP Series
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Experience the All-New Luxury at Sea with the Debut of Mitan, Numarine's Second Model from the 40MXP Series
summary: Making quite the splash at the Palm Beach International Boat Show, the second model, Mitan, from Numarine's 40MXP series is now open for admiration.
body: Launched by the Turkish yard Numarine, the highly anticipated second hull from their flagship 40MXP series, Mitan, has finally made its grand debut at the thriving Palm Beach International Boat Show, currently taking Florida by storm. This new luxurious maritime creation was first delivered last October to its fortunate South American owners, who envisaged a family-centric yacht that perfectly balances cosy shared spaces and an 'active use' of exterior living.

This new creation can be seen as the 'natural evolution' of the company's immensely popular 37XP series, fusing an adventurous, long-range expedition spirit with a profound, inviting outdoor living aesthetic. The exterior design is credited to the celebrated Can Yalman, with naval architecture by the esteemed Umberto Tagliavini.

Mitan's main saloon exudes an airy ambiance and is bathed in natural light. With plush sofa seating and a sizeable dining table, it is the perfect place for family gatherings. The yacht sleeps up to 12 guests in six lavish cabins, including a private owner's suite on the upper deck. This suite opens directly onto the aft deck, offering sweeping views over the stern.

Mitan distinguishes herself with an expansive aft deck, facilitated by an extended hull and slightly forward-shifted saloon’s aft sliding doors. This outdoor oasis is replete with al fresco dining, a lounge that surrounds an aft pool with a glass transom, and a large bar. The yacht’s full eight-metre beam is utilised to the maximum with a hydraulic swim platform which connects to the pool, thus creating ultimate 'beach club' experience.

Covering technical aspects, Mitan boasts an impressive range of 6,000 nautical miles at eight knots, powered by twin MAN 800hp engines, with an optional Tier III-compliant 900hp configuration. Mitan’s elongated sundeck is equally captivating, fitted with additional al fresco dining, sofa seating, a bar and a grill for an exemplary experience of luxury at sea.

Mitan's sister ship and third unit of the 40MXP series is already in construction, with delivery scheduled for later this year, demonstrating the popularity and demand for this luxurious yacht series.

title: Tureddi Yachts Achieves Benchmark with First Sale of Fully Custom TD27 at Renowned Boat Show
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Tureddi Yachts Achieves Benchmark with First Sale of Fully Custom TD27 at Renowned Boat Show
summary: Innovative Italian builder, Tureddi Yachts, triumphantly announces the sale of its first fully custom TD27 at the Palm Beach International Boat Show, marking a significant milestone.
body: When it comes to crafting maritime masterpieces, Tureddi Yachts, the visionary Italian builder, constantly treads uncharted waters. In a momentous breakthrough, the yacht maker has inked the sale of its inaugural custom TD27. This wasn't just any boat show, but the globally acclaimed Palm Beach International Boat Show where this significant transaction unfolded. The deal was gracefully navigated by Richard Cottrell, the genteel face of Global Yacht Sales, representing the lucky client.

The COO of Tureddi Yachts, Alessio Marchi, was brimming with excitement over this crucial sale, stating, 'This first fully custom TD27 sale marks a significant milestone for Tureddi Yachts.' Indeed, there is much to celebrate. The TD27 exemplifies Tureddi's unyielding commitment to achieving true, no-compromise customisation, a guiding principle carved into the company's ethos.

Indeed, Tureddi Yachts' journey is a testament to their relentless pursuit of excellence and uncompromised customisation. As they continue to ride the billows higher, the horizon appears more promising than ever for this Italian innovator, defying the ordinary as they redefine yachting paradigms.

title: 49-metre Amel's Yacht Vibrance Delighted with a New Owner in a Deal Involving Top Brokers
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: 49-metre Amel's Yacht Vibrance Delighted with a New Owner in a Deal Involving Top Brokers
summary: The premium 49.3-metre Amels motor yacht Vibrance has found a new proprietor, following a vibrant deal.
body: A high-profile transaction at sea has seen the premium 49.3-metre Amels motor yacht Vibrance switch homes. The deal involved multiple significant players, including Paul Cullen and James Lloyd of Edmiston representing the seller, while the buyer was introduced by Henry Smith of Cecil Wright. Josh Gulbranson of Fraser also played a pivotal role as a joint central agent. The luxury motor yacht's selling point did not just revolve around its elegant exterior styling and interior design, undertaken by the talented hands of Donald Starkey. Vibrance was built with a robust steel and aluminium structure by the renowned Dutch yard, Amels, and initially made her sailing debut in 2004. She has since undergone major refurbishments, most notably in 2019, that took her aesthetic and functional appeal several notches up. The revamp included a full repaint, machinery and electronics upgrades, along with a 20-year survey completed in 2024. The yacht boasts a plush accommodation setup for up to 12 guests, divided between five cabins. The luxurious layout houses a main deck master suite with a private deck, a VIP suite, a double cabin, and two twins with Pullman berths. All cabins come with complete entertainment centres, television screens, and en-suite bathroom facilities. In addition, Vibrance can also accommodate 11 crew members across six cabins. The expansive saloon offers comfortable seating on sofas and upholstered armchairs, accompanying coffee tables and a stylish bar. An adjacent dining area with formal seating for 12 guests ensures a private, gourmet dining experience on prime nights. A sky lounge and outdoor dining area further enrich the living experience aboard Vibrance while the exterior impresses with ample lounging options and a beach-club-style swim platform. One notable highpoint is an extensive sundeck featuring built-in seating areas, a dining table, sun loungers, bar and a Jacuzzi all protected under a hardtop providing shade. Powered by 1,057hp twin MTU engines, Vibrance can achieve a top speed of 14.8 knots. The LR-classed, 659GT yacht offers a cruising speed of 12.5 knots with an extended range of 4,000 nautical miles. In the end, she was sold after managing to charm the buyers with her pristine condition and luxury features, to the tune of $16,900,000.

title: Uncharted Waters: A Dive into the Future of Yachting with Europe's Top Shipyards' Executives
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Uncharted Waters: A Dive into the Future of Yachting with Europe's Top Shipyards' Executives
summary: The shipyards' captains outline their views on the future; shedding light on the direction they believe the industry is headed.
body: There's no dearth of voices claiming to predict the market's future trajectory. Industry consultants, brokers, project managers, journalists, and owners' representatives, all opine freely. The perspective that tends to get lost in the noise, however ironically, is that of the very people who steer the shipyards. Therefore, nine of Europe's leading shipyard executives have been asked to cut through the noise and state their own, more rooted perspectives. The result is a collective diagnosis and a barometer for the current new-build landscape.

Their responses who represent reputed shipyards like Royal Huisman, Damen Yachting, Feadship, Palumbo, Sanlorenzo, Azimut Benetti, Ferretti, Abeking and Rasmussen, and Bilgin, converge on certain themes. The past two to three years have seen these yards reorganize and transform. Facility redesigns, digital tools, and closer integration between engineering and production, along with a strict bias against late-stage revisions – all are part of this transformation.

While orders continue to fly in, the demands of the customers have evolved. They are increasingly driven by their on-board experiences rather than just the vessel itself. Purpose, sustainability, and adventure have become more important design drivers than ever.

The leaders are not enthused about explosive growth. Instead, their focus is on delivering quality, increasing credibility, and staying relevant to a new generation of owners. In the words of Rose Damen, Managing Director of Damen Yachting, the market's future will be defined by 'what is delivered,' not by 'how much is delivered.'

Insights from other shipyard CEOs are to be published in the coming days. They promise to provide deeper insights into the future of the yachting industry, and this series of interviews is expected to serve as the guiding compass for industry stakeholders.

title: Drama Unfolds as Underdogs Sail to Prominence in Pre-Finals of 2026 Macao Match Cup
author: Old Sea Dogs

summary: Penultimate race day of the 2026 Macao Match Cup generated thrilling upsets as two French favourites bowed out, giving way to Denmark's Jeppe Borch's rise to the semi-finals.
body: The fourth-day saga of the 2026 Macao Match Cup brought about intriguing plot twists. The French skippers, Aurélien Pierroz and Ian Garreta, despite dominating the qualifying round-robin, faced unexpected defeat during the quarter-finals stage. The exciting duo was sidelined by the extraordinary tactics displayed by American Christian Prendergast and Sweden's Oscar Engström.

Prendergast, a 20-year-old Chicago skipper, reinforced by an all-star crew, effectively tamed the waves to stun Pierroz with a 1-3 win. Meanwhile, Engström showcased a similar sailing prowess, sealing a 1-3 victory over Garreta. These triumphant underdogs later clashed in a high-stakes semi-final engagement.

In the semi-final round, Denmark's Jeppe Borch, accompanied by his crew Thor Malthe Andersen, Sebastian Wright Olsen and Matias Rossing, put up a commendable fight. Starting strong, they ended the day with an assured 2-0 lead over Berntsson. Demonstrating polished boat handling, Borch's extensive experience with Far East 28 boats served the team well.

The other semi-final race was a nail-biting contest between Prendergast and Engström. Though Engström triumphed in the opening race, Prendergast hit back, evening the score. By the end of the day, Engström secured a 2-1 win, positioning himself at the verge of match point as they head into the final day.

With the race to decide the 2026 Macao Match Cup champion and 30,000 USD winner's prize resuming tomorrow, racing enthusiasts eagerly anticipate exceptional world-class match racing. As the sailing strategies progress, a thrilling final day awaits, poised to shake up the form and swing the momentum in unpredictable directions.

title: Race Around Australia 2028 Stirs Adrenalin; The Shorthanded Ocean Racing Association Calls for Interested Parties
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Race Around Australia 2028 Stirs Adrenalin; The Shorthanded Ocean Racing Association Calls for Interested Parties
summary: Whip up excitement for the 2028 Race Around Australia, as the Shorthanded Ocean Racing Association of Australia invites interested contenders to express their intentions.
body: Forty years after the exhilarating competition in 1988, the Race Around Australia is returning in 2028. Brought to fruition by the Shorthanded Ocean Racing Association of Australia, this race embraces the spirit of the Bicentennial race of '88. The uniquely doublehanded race will see participants face an exciting journey across more than 7,000 nautical miles, split into five legs with four stopovers. The promise of two sprint stages and two pit stops also await the racing teams.

Sir Peter Blake and Mike Quilter are sailing legends who emerged victorious in the 1988 Bicentennial Race, aboard the 60-foot trimaran Steinlager 1. Providing a seasoned perspective on the gruelling challenge, Quilter said, 'It's 7,000 miles, not a Sydney Hobart. It's as much an adventure as it is a race… you've got to be self-sufficient, and you're going to have a few problems.'

The Shorthanded Ocean Racing Association is committed to conducting the race with safety at its core. Safety measures are strict, including adherence to Australian Sailing's Category 1 requirements, supplementary safety equipment, crew training, and a qualifying voyage.

Showcasing inclusivity in sailing, the race is open to monohull and multihull yachts ranging from 40 to 60 feet. Smaller, swift, seaworthy monohulls could also quality for the race. Racing will fall under IRC for monohulls and OMR for multihulls, alongside PHRF handicaps. The PredictWind Navigation Challenge will also be featured, with teams predicting their finishing times prior to the start of each leg.

Expressions of interest that fulfil the eligibility requirements will receive Provisional Entrant Status, accepting entries on a first come, first served basis. This thrilling maritime journey promises teams priority access to logistics and an opportunity to contribute to race planning. Harness the excitement and savour the adventure of a lifetime in the phenomenal Race Around Australia 2028.

title: 2026 Sydney Sail Grand Prix
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: 2026 Sydney Sail Grand Prix
summary: Spain led the 2026 Sydney Sail Grand Prix after delivering a commanding performance on the opening day of racing on Sydney Harbour. Two race wins around the demanding Shark Island SailGP course had put Los Gallos firmly atop the leaderboard heading into the decisive second day.
body: Spain took Early control of the Sydney Sail Grand Prix

The Sydney Sail Grand Prix delivered the kind of racing Sydney Harbour has become famous for — tight tactical decisions, shifting winds and foiling catamarans flying across the water at nearly 60 km/h.
At the end of four fleet races it was Spain’s Los Gallos, led by driver Diego Botín, who emerged as the strongest team of the opening day.
The Spanish crew secured two wins from four races, finishing Saturday with 32 points on the event leaderboard.
Just behind them sit the home favourites, the Australia SailGP Team, on 28 points, while Artemis SailGP Team hold third with 26 points.
Still well within striking distance are Emirates GBR SailGP Team and Red Bull Italy SailGP Team, tied on 23 points.
With only the top three teams progressing to the event Final, Sunday promises a fierce showdown.
SailGP Racing on the Shark Island Course
The Shark Island course on Sydney Harbour is widely considered one of the most technical venues on the SailGP calendar.

The racecourse weaves between islands, headlands and urban shoreline, creating constantly shifting wind patterns. Crews must read gusts, pressure lines and wind shadows while keeping their F50 foiling catamarans airborne.
On Saturday the breeze proved patchy and unpredictable.
Those willing to make decisive tactical calls gained positions quickly.
Those who hesitated were swallowed by the tightly packed fleet.
Australia Opens With a Home-Waters Victory
The opening race provided an early highlight for the Sydney crowd.
The BONDS Flying Roos, driven by Tom Slingsby, surged into the lead after a close tactical duel with Denmark’s ROCKWOOL Racing.
The Australians overtook the Danish team on the first upwind leg as the two boats traded tacks in tight formation.
Emirates GBR held a steady third place as the fleet navigated unstable wind conditions.
Strategist Tash Bryant summed up the challenge of racing in Sydney.
“Today was pretty crazy and really unpredictable. Consistency was key.”
Despite several mid-fleet battles, Australia finished the day firmly in contention.
Spain’s Race-Winning Tactical Move
Spain’s breakthrough came in race two.
Early in the race it was the Switzerland SailGP Team who appeared to control the fleet after a perfectly timed start.
But the race turned dramatically at Gate 3.
Botín’s crew chose the right-hand turn, reading a wind shift that allowed them to sweep past Switzerland and take the lead.
It was a decisive move that demonstrated both confidence and tactical awareness.
Botín explained the challenge of racing on Sydney Harbour.
“You have to sail the wind you have in the moment while trying to predict what’s coming next.”
He also acknowledged the advantage of teams familiar with the venue.
“You can tell which crews have sailed here a lot. They read the land features very well.”
Race Three Delivers Starting Line Chaos
Race three began in dramatic fashion.
Germany, Australia and Denmark were all penalised for being over the start line, immediately throwing the fleet into disarray.
Moments later the United States SailGP Team crossed in front of Switzerland, delaying both boats as they fought to accelerate away from the start.
The confusion allowed Spain, Artemis Racing, and NorthStar Canada SailGP Team to break clear in clean air.
Spain once again capitalised on the opportunity and secured their second race victory of the day.
Following the race, the U.S. team received a two-point penalty after umpires ruled they had breached rule 14 following contact during the start sequence.
Driver Taylor Canfield described the incident as unavoidable.
“We got into a spot we couldn’t get out of.”
A review of the decision was scheduled overnight.
Australia Strike Back in the Final Race
The fourth and final race of the day delivered a dramatic finish.
The BONDS Flying Roos fought their way back through the fleet to claim their second win of the day.
The victory carried added significance as Olympic gold medallist Iain Jensen returned to the team after recovering from a knee injury.
For Slingsby, the moment was special.
“It was great to give Goobs a proper homecoming.”
The two sailors have been close friends for more than three decades.
“We’ve talked about sailing together for 20 years.”
Winning Jensen’s first race back — and the final race of the day — made it a memorable return.
Sydney Harbour: SailGP’s Original Stage
Thousands of spectators lined the shores of Sydney Harbour to watch the racing unfold.
Even more followed from the official spectator fleet and hospitality vessels positioned around the racecourse.
Sydney holds a unique place in SailGP history.
Often described as the birthplace of SailGP, the harbour has now hosted the event seven times, more than any other location on the championship calendar.
Spain lead the way with Australia close behind
Just nine points separate the top five teams, meaning a single race could dramatically reshape the standings.
In SailGP racing, fortunes can change quickly.
A missed shift. A slow start. A moment off the foils.
On Sydney Harbour, that is often all it takes.

title: Controversial Protest as Activist Group Targets Tech Mogul Larry Ellison's Superyacht 'Musashi'
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Controversial Protest as Activist Group Targets Tech Mogul Larry Ellison's Superyacht 'Musashi'
summary: The activist group Led By Donkeys recently executed an audacious protest against Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison.
body: March 24 saw a daring move as a group of activists from the organization Led By Donkeys staged a protest with a surprising target: Larry Ellison's superyacht, the Musashi. Approaching by speedboat while the yacht was docked and unsuspecting on the French Riviera, the audacious protesters emblazoned the hull with large lettering, effectively 'renaming' the yacht as 'The Trump Propagandist.' Quick to share their exploits with the world, Led By Donkeys filmed their actions, disseminating the footage across multiple social media platforms. Unsurprisingly, caught in the fast and furious streams of online chatter, the news of their bold demonstration quickly traveled the globe.

Ellison's rise to prominence in the world of tech and media hasn't gone unnoticed. With the wealth and influence he's accumulated, he's brokered deals and garnered positions that have stirred up controversy. The Ellison family expansion into media, their control over TikTok's American user base, and their quest to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery are all contributing factors that sparked the recent action by the activist group.

Led By Donkeys, active since 2018, are no strangers to controversy. Their oeuvre of protests includes projecting images of Trump and convicted pedophile Jeffrey Epstein onto Windsor Castle during Trump's UK state visit, a stunt that led to arrests of members of the group. With their latest audacious action against Ellison under their belt, it leaves us pondering the question - Who's next on their list?

From its robust hull featuring triple IPS pod drives and Sleipner curved fi]n stabilisers to its stunning sunken saloon and inviting beach club, everything about the BGX83 speaks volumes about its boldness and aristocracy. title: Exploring the Elegance: Top 10 Flybridge Yachts That Redefine Luxury on Water
author: Michael Hodges

summary: Picture a sun-soaked horizon where the sky kisses the sea, and luxury transforms into a lifestyle. Welcome to the world of flybridge yachts, where elegance meets innovation on the water. From their spacious upper decks offering panoramic views to luxurious interiors crafted for ultimate comfor
body: Flybridge yachts stand out in the maritime world due to their distinctive design and unparalleled luxury. The term "flybridge" refers to the elevated upper deck, which offers an expansive, unobstructed view of the surroundings. This design not only provides a commanding vantage point for navigation but also serves as a luxurious outdoor living space. Guests can enjoy the fresh sea breeze, indulge in alfresco dining, or simply relax while taking in panoramic views. This unique feature sets flybridge yachts apart from other types of yachts, making them highly sought after by those who appreciate both style and functionality. Another unique aspect of flybridge yachts is their versatile use of space. The upper deck is not just for the captain’s helm; it’s often equipped with sun loungers, dining areas, and even hot tubs, transforming it into a multifunctional leisure zone. This effective use of space maximises comfort and luxury, ensuring that every inch of the yacht is utilized to enhance the on-board experience. Whether you are cruising along the coast or anchored in a tranquil bay, the flybridge deck becomes the ultimate spot for relaxation and entertainment.

The interior of a flybridge yacht is equally impressive, often featuring opulent décor and state-of-the-art amenities. These yachts are designed with an emphasis on comfort and elegance, offering spacious living areas, gourmet kitchens, and lavish bedrooms, all meticulously crafted with high-quality materials. The seamless blend of indoor and outdoor spaces creates a harmonious environment, perfect for both leisurely cruising and hosting extravagant gatherings. It is this combination of innovative design, luxurious features, and versatile spaces that truly makes flybridge yachts unique in the world of luxury boating.

The concept of the flybridge yacht has evolved significantly over the years, driven by advancements in nautical engineering and changing consumer preferences. In the early days of yachting, the flybridge was a simple, functional space primarily used for navigation. It provided captains with a higher vantage point, improving visibility and manoeuvrability. However, as the desire for luxury and comfort grew, so did the complexity and sophistication of the flybridge design. Modern flybridge yachts now boast elaborate upper decks that rival the interiors in terms of luxury and amenities. The evolution of flybridge yachts can also be traced through advancements in materials and technology. Early yachts were constructed primarily from wood, which, while beautiful, required extensive maintenance and was limited in terms of design flexibility. The introduction of fibreglass and other composite materials allowed for more innovative designs and greater durability. These materials not only reduced the weight of the yachts, improving performance and fuel efficiency, but also enabled the creation of more spacious and elaborate flybridge areas. In recent years, the focus has shifted towards sustainability and eco-friendly technologies. Modern flybridge yachts are increasingly equipped with hybrid engines, solar panels, and advanced waste management systems, reflecting a growing awareness of environmental impact. This shift towards sustainable luxury is part of the broader evolution of the industry, ensuring that flybridge yachts remain at the forefront of innovation while also addressing the environmental concerns of today’s discerning yacht owners. The evolution of flybridge yachts is a testament to the industry’s ability to adapt and innovate, continually raising the bar for luxury and performance on the water.

When selecting a flybridge yacht, there are several key features that discerning buyers should consider to ensure they are investing in a vessel that meets their expectations for luxury, performance, and functionality. One of the most important aspects is the layout and design of the flybridge itself. A well-designed flybridge should offer ample space for relaxation and entertainment, with comfortable seating, dining areas, and possibly even a bar or hot tub. The layout should be intuitive, allowing for easy movement and access to various areas of the yacht. Another crucial feature to look for is the quality of the interior craftsmanship. The finest flybridge yachts are often adorned with high-end materials such as marble countertops, hardwood floors, and bespoke furnishings. Attention to detail in the interior design not only enhances the overall aesthetic but also contributes to the comfort and enjoyment of the yacht. Prospective buyers should pay close attention to the quality of the finishes, the ergonomics of the living spaces, and the functionality of the kitchen and bathrooms. Performance and technology are also key considerations when selecting a flybridge yacht. Modern yachts are equipped with advanced navigation systems, powerful engines, and innovative hull designs that enhance both speed and stability. Additionally, features such as gyro stabilisers can significantly reduce motion, providing a smoother and more comfortable ride. Buyers should also consider the technological amenities available, such as integrated entertainment systems, Wi-Fi connectivity, and smart home automation, all of which can enhance the onboard experience.

When comparing flybridge yachts, size and layout are critical factors that can significantly impact the overall experience. The size of the yacht often dictates the number of amenities and the level of luxury that can be incorporated. Larger yachts typically offer more space for multiple living areas, larger bedrooms, and additional features such as gyms or cinemas. However, even smaller flybridge yachts can be designed in a way that maximizes the available space, ensuring that every inch is used effectively.

The layout of a flybridge yacht is equally important, as it determines how the space is utilized and how easily guests can move around the vessel. A well-designed layout will ensure that the various areas of the yacht flow seamlessly into one another, creating a harmonious and functional living environment. For example, the placement of the kitchen in relation to the dining area can impact how convenient it is to prepare and serve meals. Similarly, the arrangement of seating and lounging areas on the flybridge can affect how comfortable and enjoyable it is to relax and entertain guests. When comparing the size and layout of different flybridge yachts, it’s important to consider your specific needs and preferences. For example, if you plan to host large gatherings, you may prioritize a yacht with ample outdoor entertainment space and a large dining area. On the other hand, if you value privacy and tranquility, you may prefer a layout that includes more secluded areas for relaxation. Ultimately, the best flybridge yacht for you will be one that aligns with your lifestyle and enhances your enjoyment of the water.

Performance and technology are critical aspects of any flybridge yacht, as they directly impact the vessel’s capabilities and the overall experience of those on board. A high-performance yacht will offer a smooth and stable ride, even in challenging conditions, ensuring that guests can enjoy their time on the water without discomfort. This is particularly important for longer voyages, where comfort and reliability are paramount. Factors such as engine power, hull design, and stabilisation systems all play a role in determining the performance of a flybridge yacht. Advanced technology is also a key consideration when selecting a flybridge yacht, as it can enhance both the safety and enjoyment of the vessel. Modern yachts are equipped with state-of-the-art navigation systems that provide accurate and reliable information, making it easier for the captain to navigate safely. Additionally, features such as integrated entertainment systems, Wi-Fi connectivity, and smart home automation can significantly enhance the onboard experience, making it more convenient and enjoyable for guests. One of the most exciting developments in the world of flybridge yachts is the integration of sustainable technologies. Hybrid engines, solar panels, and advanced waste management systems are becoming increasingly common, reflecting a growing awareness of environmental impact. These technologies not only reduce the carbon footprint of the yacht but can also enhance its performance and efficiency. As technology continues to advance, we can expect to see even more innovative solutions that improve the performance and sustainability of flybridge yachts, making them an even more attractive option for discerning buyers.

Owning a flybridge yacht is a significant investment, and proper maintenance is essential to ensure that the vessel remains in optimal condition and retains its value. Regular maintenance not only extends the lifespan of the yacht but also ensures the safety and comfort of those on board. One of the most important aspects of yacht maintenance is regular cleaning and inspection. This includes washing the exterior to remove salt and debris, cleaning the interior to maintain its appearance, and inspecting the hull, engines, and other critical systems for any signs of damage or wear. In addition to regular cleaning and inspections, it’s important to follow the manufacturer’s recommended maintenance schedule for the yacht’s various systems and components. This may include servicing the engines, checking and replacing fluids, and inspecting and maintaining the electrical and plumbing systems.
