title: Meet the Wider 42: A Sleek Combo of Power, Speed, Innovation, and Bespoke Italian Craftsmanship
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Meet the Wider 42: A Sleek Combo of Power, Speed, Innovation, and Bespoke Italian Craftsmanship
summary: Get introduced to the marvel of Italian craftsmanship, the Wider 42, featuring awe-inspiring speed, trend-setting innovations, and indulgent design aesthetics.
body: Wider's legacy in Italian yacht craftsmanship took everyone by storm with their first ever marvel, the Wider 42. Despite the deceptive name, Wider 42 comes across as a slender speed machine, well-equipped with a carbon composite stepped hull devised by offshore racing maestro, Mark Wilson. With a beam of just 11ft 6in, one would assume there isn't much to play around with, but the name Wider reaches its justified climax when overhead extensions magically create additional deck space at the touch of a button.

But wait until you unfold the Wider 42's party trick! On its command, side panels on gunwales extend outwards, while sections of the hull descend into the water functioning as stabiliser floats. The boat transfigures into an innovatively widened space, justifying its 'Wider' brand and leaving spectators in awe.

With specifications like 42ft 4in length and 11ft 6in beam, the Wider 42 was priced at €780,000 when new, a premium that is well-indexed when compared with the boat's vast array of features. Being the first of Wider's lineage, yet setting such a high standard, it's no surprise how the Wider 42 comfortably secured its spot in the pantheon of cool boats.

title: Silverado, the Icon of American Cruises, Sold - Discover the Legacy of the Prestigious Motor Yacht
author: Old Sea Dogs

summary: Silverado, the dazzling 36.6-metre motor yacht crafted by Willard Boat Works, has found a new owner.
body: Silverado, a gem in the fleet of luxury motor yachts, brought to life by the prodigious Willard Boat Works in 1974, embarked on a new voyage with her recent acquisition. Her brokers, Robert Petrina and Mike Hickey from Northrop & Johnson, announced the sale earlier this year.

Noteworthy for her long-range offshore cruising capabilities, the Silverado boasts an all-American cruising pedigree. This yacht distinguished herself among the most significant fibreglass yachts of her epoch, showcasing exquisite design both inside and out, courtesy of acclaimed designer, John Harris. The unique build of the yacht, underscored by her proven track record, elevates the Silverado as a superior choice for maritime lovers.

The yacht elevates marine exploration with an uncommon in-hull underwater viewing platform that nurtures an expedition-centric vibe. A key feature of Silverado design is the embrace of natural light, flooding in via cavernous windows and portlights enhancing the interior aesthetic. They enhance the charm of the main saloon which comprises a card and game table as well as a full-service bar, and the formal dining area that is enriched by a scale model of Silverado herself.

The Silverado truly flaunts her glamour on the exterior. This yacht is a true adventurer's paradise, boasting an enclosed covered aft deck, Portuguese bridge with observation area, integrated swim platform, and a deck space laden with all the seafaring toys and equipment. Easy offshore navigation is enabled by the dedicated navigation office and raised pilothouse.

Underpinning Silverado's powerful performance are twin Caterpillar D349 main engines, allowing the vessel to cruise at a robust speed of 14 knots and reach a maximum speed of 17 knots. Outfitted with Koopnautic stabilisers, the yacht ensures smooth sailings under any sea conditions. Its robust construction, coupled with the displacement hull, ensures tranquil cruising conditions, guaranteeing a sublime yachting experience. The Silverado was last sold for an impressive $2,499,000, reaffirming its prestigious status among motor yachts.

title: As Shareholder Response to Ferretti Takeover Proves Lacklustre, KKCG Maritime Sweetens the Deal with an Increased Bid
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: As Shareholder Response to Ferretti Takeover Proves Lacklustre, KKCG Maritime Sweetens the Deal with an Increased Bid
summary: KKCG Maritime's initial bid for Ferretti met with unenthusiastic responses from shareholders, prompting an uptick in the offer price per share.
body: The allure of yacht production company Ferretti has seemingly failed to captivate the shareholders' imaginations. Following a lacklustre response to KKCG Maritime's initial partial tender offer, expressed in negligible numbers and silence from the shareholder body, an increased bid has been tabled. In the yachting industry, few things are as exciting as a takeover, and few as intricate. The complexity of this situation lies not only in the size of the deal but in the apparent reluctance of the shareholders to embrace the change.

As a countermeasure, the launch of an increased offer price from €3.50 to €3.90 crates intrigue. This move, a considerable 35.1 per cent premium, reset the terms of the bid and took the offer above the market price. With revised terms now standing at a potential €203.3 million in max consideration, KKCG Maritime has arguably made a strategic move to win over reluctant shareholders. Whether this strategic overture will bring about a rallying response remains yet to be seen.

All in all, the waters in the yachting industry are proving anything but calm. Yet, times of high stakes and tense negotiations are as much a part of the world of yachting as the elegantly designed vessels it produces. For now, observers wait with bated breath, anticipating what might be next for KKCG's adventurous pursuit of Ferretti.

title: Discover Forever: A Unique, Custom-built Yacht Embarking Upon the Market's Stage
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover Forever: A Unique, Custom-built Yacht Embarking Upon the Market's Stage
summary: Forever, a beautifully custom-crafted 45-metre yacht, is now ready for a new voyage with its new central agency listing.
body: Stepping into the limelight is Forever, a remarkable 45-meter custom-built yacht. it's a single-piece wonder birthed by the Italian shipyard, Logica Yachts, in 2015. Its well-forged frame made of steel, adorned with an aluminium superstructure, and possessing an impressive internal volume of 478GT, enhances its allure. Under the expert craftsmanship of Studio Brenta, the yacht sports a long, sheer line that couples stylishly with generous glazing, thereby accentuating its silhouette and granting it a sleek appearance.

The elegance of Forever doesn't just lie on the surface. It has seen continual upgrades, including external modifications and a significant interior overhaul by Michael Niederer in 2018. These improvements have not only enhanced its charm but have also amplified its cruising capability. It offers a lifestyle package that combines endurance with sophistication.

In terms of accommodation, Forever is no less than a floating mansion. It houses six en-suite cabins with the capacity to lodge 12 guests. The owner's suite, positioned forward on the main deck, benefits from extensive windows that emit an expansive view of the foredeck and pool. It also includes a small private office, a marble-finished ensuite with a bath that sits under a skylight, and a large walk-in shower, enhancing the luxury quotient. Apart from this, the yacht boasts four double cabins, a twin cabin with a Pullman berth, a spacious sixth cabin aft off the swim platform, and separate crew quarters to accommodate up to 10 individuals.

Despite its opulent interiors, Forever doesn't compromise on entertainment. It is rich with amenities and offers four separate outdoor spaces for round-the-clock revelry. The 5.5-meter pool at the foredeck includes a jet system that further enlivens the bow area. Additionally, the upper deck saloon and flybridge are fitted with a walk-around bar, ice-makers, cold-pour taps, and a teppanyaki grill.

Alongside these features, Forever is also armed with a state-of-the-art entertainment system. It encompasses LED walls, a 35,000-watt sound system, laser effects, smoke machines, DJ connections, and programmable lighting. Complementing this is an array of water toys, including Jet Skis, surfboards, and fishing equipment.

Forever, currently based in Viareggio, offers unparalleled comfort while cruising and at anchorage, thanks to its zero-speed stabilisers and the painstakingly designed quiet and low-vibration provisions. With a market value of €16,500,000, this colossal sea marvel is a worthwhile investment for enthusiasts craving opulence, performance, and the thrill of owning a custom-built vessel.

title: RYA Publishes 2026 Portsmouth Yardstick List as Data-Driven Era of Club Racing Continues
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Portsmouth Yardstick 2026 Numbers Released: What Every Club Racer Needs to Know
summary: RYA Publishes 2026 Portsmouth Yardstick List as Data-Driven Era of Club Racing Continues
body: If you race dinghies in the UK — from puddle to open water — this matters.
The Royal Yachting Association has officially released the Portsmouth Yardstick (PY) Numbers for 2026, and clubs across the country are already updating their results sheets.

For most grassroots sailors, Portsmouth Yardstick isn’t theory. It’s the quiet system working behind every corrected result on a Sunday afternoon. It allows Lasers, Wayfarers, RS boats, Solos and everything in between to line up together and still produce meaningful racing.
No measurement certificates. No weigh-ins. No protest room debates over millimetres.
Just elapsed time, corrected time, and the understanding that no two boats are identical — but they can still race fairly.

The Portsmouth Yardstick system is a relative handicap framework based on real race performance data. Boats are assigned a PY number that reflects how they typically perform against others in mixed fleets.
Lower number = faster boat. Higher number = slower boat.
To calculate results, a boat’s elapsed time (the time taken to complete the course) is converted to corrected time using a simple formula based on its PY number.
It is simple. But behind that simplicity sits decades of collected race data.
Each year, the RYA publishes a national baseline list. Clubs can then adjust those numbers locally using PY Online, reflecting their own wind patterns, water type and fleet composition.
A Solo on a windy reservoir does not behave the same as one on a tidal estuary. The system recognises that.
In 2025, the Portsmouth Yardstick system underwent its most significant overhaul in three decades.
Working with Sheffield Hallam University, the RYA:
Widened the race-time threshold to incorporate more usable data
Shifted to a median-based calculation model for greater statistical stability
Strengthened data handling within PY Online
Improved submission pathways from club scoring software
This wasn’t tinkering. It was structural refinement.
The move to median-based calculations reduces volatility caused by outlier results. In plain terms: one freak race no longer skews a class number disproportionately.
For clubs, that means more reliable handicaps and tighter racing across mixed fleets.
Over the past year, the system has seen a notable increase in club data submissions. That matters.
Portsmouth Yardstick only works because clubs contribute real race results. Without ongoing input, the system stagnates.
Adam Parry, RYA Technical Manager, acknowledged the growing collaboration:

“We greatly appreciate the volume of data clubs have submitted over the past year… Uploading information has become even more straightforward thanks to expanded direct submission options through Sailing Club Manager, Hal Sail and Sailwave.”
For 2026, the message is simple: if your club uses PY, submit your data.
The 75th anniversary of the system arrives in 2027. The stronger the dataset, the better the numbers — and the better the racing.
For race officers and club handicappers, the annual PY release isn’t just an administrative update. It’s an opportunity.
Here’s the practical approach:
Review the national baseline numbers.
Check your club’s historical results through PY Online.
Compare local performance trends against national data.
Adopt class configurations listed online.
Flag missing classes via [email protected] .
The system is collaborative. It works best when clubs treat it as a living tool rather than a fixed table.
In an era of foiling cats, GPS overlays and Olympic data analytics, Portsmouth Yardstick remains one of the most democratic systems in sailing.
It enables:
Junior sailors in Toppers to race alongside experienced helms in Phantoms.
Mixed fleets at smaller clubs to remain viable.
Grassroots racing without measurement complexity.
Entry-level sailors to feel competitive from day one.
It’s not glamorous. It’s not headline-grabbing.
But it keeps club racing alive.
And that’s worth protecting.
Because long before carbon rigs and live trackers, there was a start line, a mixed fleet, and someone with a stopwatch.
The 2026 numbers are now live.
Clubs update. Sailors race. The system rolls on.

title: Forecasted Wild Weather Forces 2026 Yacht Race Postponement, Highlights Nature's Unpredictability
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Forecasted Wild Weather Forces 2026 Yacht Race Postponement, Highlights Nature's Unpredictability
summary: Unmanaged nature's power recently took the forefront when unpredictable wild weather compelled the postponement of the celebrated 2026 Pittwater to Coffs Harbour Yacht Race.
body: The raw power of the sea and weather's unpredictable nature reminded the world of their command when a vicious forecast led to the cancellation of the 2026 Pittwater to Coffs Harbour Yacht Race. The honourable 40th race, initially scheduled for 27th March, was pushed back to an unconfirmed date in March 2027 by the organizing body, Royal Prince Alfred Yacht Race's (RPAYC), prioritizing safety over competition.

RPAYC wisely decided to postpone the event due to the wild weather forecasted to barrage the NSW coast. The decision was underpinned by comprehensive forecast reviews, expert advice, and calculated appraisals of the fleet's adeptness and the race's safety category.

The nature of the 2026 fleet was another crucial factor considered before reaching the decision. The diverse mixture of entrants, comprised of double-handed contenders and crews with variable offshore experience, reaffirmed the RPAYC's responsibility to ensure the safety of all participants, not just the most seasoned.

Apart from the weather, the logistical challenges of managing this large scale race were also taken into account. The complex planning required for fleet's safe transportation along the coast incorporating numerous factors; from navigating treacherously choppy waters to ensuring the ships' safe return to their home ports, compounds the magnitude of these challenges.

The call to postpone came promptly, allowing the ships time to return safely to their ports before the impending turbulent period hit the coast. While the committee considered delaying the race, even a later start would present potential difficulties, given the residual impact of violent seas.

Ensuring the safety of all individuals involved is always at the heart of any sailing event. Guided by this principle, the committee made a unanimous decision to cancel this year's race, emphasizing that the numerous risks involved in proceeding amid such harsh conditions far outweighed any potential benefits.

title: Horizon Yachts Launches the Reimagined ES88 Superyacht, Now Christened KEΦI: A True Mix of Elegance and Adventure.

The 27.3-metre superyacht strikes a high note in the industry as a testament to Horizon's prowess in creating extraordinary sea-faring vessels. KEΦI not just refines, but entirely redefines the yard's existing E Series into a superior and personalized sports design yacht. The customization is a nod to the Australian owner, a seasoned Horizon customer, who is also an elite angler.

Long-standing Horizon contributor Cor D. Rover is the mind behind the yacht's sporty yet sophisticated all-white profile. This chic aesthetic continues throughout her interior too, where warm vinyl wood flooring and matte white and leatherette ceilings create an ambiance of modern luxury.

High-gloss Koto wood louvers and stone countertops seamlessly blend utility with unimposing elegance. At every turn, the vessel marries contemporary aesthetics with practicality.

Horizon Yachts has succeeded in blending bespoke specifications into a stylish design, resulting in an irresistible yacht that embraces the unique values and needs of the owner. As KEΦI nears delivery, she represents a remarkable example of personalized yachting excellence, setting a new benchmark for future custom builds.

title: Sailor's Phenomenal Performance at the Ovington Inland Championships Celebrates 80 Years of Firefly Racing
author: Old Sea Dogs

body: What better way to celebrate the magnificent 80th anniversary milestone of Firefly racing than with an ebullient performance at the Ovington Inland Championship? For legendary sailing, Grafham Water Sailing Club is the place to be, as the marvel of Fireflys dance across the placid lake. In this exuberant celebration of exceptional sailing craftsmanship, every race is much more than a circumnavigation of buoys and returning to the shore. It's about sailing into a cascade of memories, old friends, and the unadulterated joy derived from being in the elements. Through the years, the Firefly has remained the top choice for sailors, offering the liberating break from normal life and transforming it into exhilarating and fun-filled seafaring. As the sun paints the sky, you'll find our victorious sailor amid familiar faces, including Nick Criag and Jon Gorringe, embarking on memorable races in an OK and K1 respectively. The triumphant sailor had been away from the world of sailing due to his farming commitments but made an impressive comeback at the Ovington Spring series, an event that holds its unique charm. Racing during the weekend was no straightforward task. Despite the unpredictable wind conditions tossing from one direction to another, the race officer delivered two nail-biting races. The first race saw our champion, along with Emily, secure a phenomenal lead, only to be overtaken towards the end. In the second race, winds shifted right before the start, making it a tricky reach to the first mark. Installing their deep-seated knowledge of sailing and an instinctive connection with the wind, they carved out a new strategy during the race to battle stiff competition. Guided by light zephyrs, they raced through the course, securing victory. A salute to the indomitable spirit of the sailors aboard the Fireflys, their camaraderie, and their shared love for the sea. This event, rich in traditions and layered with adventure, welcomes all sailing aficionados to join in the joyous celebration of Firefly's admirable sailing legacy.

title: Superyachts, VIP Experiences and Billion-Dollar Deals Define Palm Beach Boat Show 2026
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Palm Beach International Boat Show 2026: Superyachts, Luxury and a Billion-Dollar Showcase on Florida’s Waterfront
summary: The Palm Beach International Boat Show 2026 returns to West Palm Beach with over $1 billion in yachts, world-class superyachts, VIP experiences and luxury showcases, cementing its position as one of the most influential marine events in the global yachting calendar.
body: If you want to understand where the global superyacht market is heading, you don’t start in a boardroom — you start dockside in West Palm Beach.
From March 25 to March 29, 2026, the Palm Beach International Boat Show returns for its 44th edition, bringing with it more than $1 billion worth of yachts, marine technology and luxury experiences.

Positioned just steps from Palm Beach’s famous “Billionaires Row,” this is not just a boat show — it is a marketplace, a networking hub and, increasingly, a global signal of where high-end yachting is heading.
Call it what it is: this is where serious money meets serious boats.
The centrepiece of the show remains the Superyacht Show Palm Beach, hosted at Palm Harbor Marina — a floating showcase of engineering, design and unapologetic luxury.
More than:
30 superyachts over 150 feet 100+ yachts exceeding 80 feet
will be on display, ranging from cutting-edge explorer vessels to floating palaces built for long-range cruising and charter.

Leading the fleet is the 256-foot Rocinante yacht, a Lürssen-built giant that defines modern superyacht luxury. With a helipad, spa, gym and ten staterooms, it’s less a boat and more a private resort that happens to float.

Close behind is the 254-foot Boardwalk yacht, delivering seven staterooms, multiple bars, a wine cellar and a 20-foot pool — the kind of specification that quietly reminds you this market operates on a different scale.
Among the standout debuts is the 247-foot Kensho yacht, already recognised globally for its design innovation.
This is where the industry is heading:
Seamless indoor-outdoor living Panoramic ocean views Minimalist, Zen-inspired interiors Owner-focused private suites
It’s not just about size anymore — it’s about experience, flow and connection to the sea.
Also drawing serious attention is Amor À Vida yacht, a new-generation yacht incorporating hybrid propulsion and energy recovery systems.
Because for the first time at scale, luxury and sustainability are no longer competing — they’re being engineered together.
Palm Beach Lifestyle: Where the Show Becomes an Experience
The Palm Beach show has always understood something many others miss:
People don’t just come to buy boats. They come to feel the lifestyle.
At the heart of that is the Windward VIP Club, a controlled slice of calm amid the noise of the docks.
Premium open bar Curated dining experiences Private access to the superyacht showcase Early entry and concierge services
This year’s experience is elevated further with appearances from chefs including Ryan O’Sullivan and Dave White.
It’s polished, it’s efficient, and it’s designed for the kind of buyer who expects things to just work.
A Marketplace, Not Just a Show
What separates Palm Beach from many global boat shows is simple:
Deals actually get done here.
According to organisers, previous editions have generated:

title: World-Class Tennis Champion Carlos Alcaraz Delights in Joining the Luxurious World of Yachting with a 27m Sunreef Ultima 88 Catamaran
author: Old Sea Dogs

summary: Acclaimed for his prowess on the court, tennis pro Carlos Alcaraz now takes to the water, becoming the latest proud owner of Sunreef Yachts’ illustrious Ultima 88 catamaran.
body: Renowned tennis player Carlos Alcaraz, revered for his spectacular performance in the tennis court, is expanding his scope to the high seas. The Spanish player, currently leading the global chart in men's singles by the Association of Tennis Professionals, has placed an order for a new 26.8-metre catamaran from Sunreef Yachts' magnificent Ultima 88 series. The move firmly situates Alcaraz among the prestigious community of Sunreef owners. This sail will not be his usual rally across the net but a journey into the world of yachting, one poised for luxury and enjoyment.

Proudly unveiling his choice, Alcaraz praised Sunreef, crediting the yacht constructor with not only being experts in luxury catamarans but also as pioneers. The world champion expressed his confidence in the yacht constructor, believing them the perfect match to create his dream yacht – a vessel to retreat and recharge in.

Inside, the catamaran, sprawling over four guest cabins and the full-beam owner's suite, promises luxury and comfort. Natural light seeps into the owner suite, abundant with such comforts as a grand bathroom and bathtub. The flybridge provides the perfect area for rest and enjoyment, invitingly designed for relaxation and al fresco dining.

Earning an impressive collection of honours including Grand Slams and ATP Tour-level singles titles throughout his career, Alcaraz is no stranger to a high-powered lifestyle. This recent shift from the tennis lawns to yachting waters sees Alcaraz join an inspiring community of visionary Sunreef owners — a group whose achievements continually inspire the world and inject fresh energy to the yachting lifestyle. This announcement comes close on the heels of football superstar Robert Lewandowski's Sunreef catamaran order, hinting at Sunreef's growing popularity amongst sports champions who seek luxurious off-court experiences.

title: The Prized Jongert Sailing Yacht Gloria Changes Hands: A Nod to the Golden Age of Sailing With Modern Acuity
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Prized Jongert Sailing Yacht Gloria Changes Hands: A Nod to the Golden Age of Sailing With Modern Acuity
summary: The sale of the celebrated 38.4-metre Gloria, a staysail schooner by Jongert, symbolises the seamless blend of classic charm and modern technology.
body: There's something captivating about the past meeting the present, and the celebrated Gloria, a 38.4-meter Jongert sailing yacht, embodies this harmonious confluence of time. Recently, this timeless icon switched hands, with Manfred Haas representing the seller and Barney Sandeman introducing the buyer.

Gloria's design earns it the distinction of being a tribute to the 1936 Mylne schooner Panda. Its steel hull, aluminium superstructure swathed in mahogany, and aluminium masts are a testament to a bygone boating era. Yet, a substantial refit between 2011 and 2012 assures that the beauty doesn't just lie in nostalgia.

The stay sail schooner has been fitted with modern sailing standards, continually upgraded to preserve its classic charm effortlessly while accommodating contemporary tech. The sweeping alterations highlight its desire to blend the old with the new while upholding its rich maritime heritage.

The accommodation on this yacht is lavish, offering room for eight guests across four ensuite cabins. The pièce de résistance is the grand owner's cabin, distinguished with elegant library walls, plush sofas, and a generously proportioned bed in the center. Additional facilities cater to a crew of six.

Gloria's deck saloon and cockpit are a sight to behold, offering expansive entertainment areas complemented by panoramic views of the open ocean. The deck saloon is home to a U-shaped sofa and a game table located adjacent to the helm. Meanwhile, the cockpit comes with an optional awning, providing seating and a table for al fresco dining. Gloria's deck ensures there's never a dull moment for the guests, furnished with an expansive space for storing the tender, water sporting equipment, loungers for sunbathing, and a versatile awning that stretches from bow to stern.

Underlining its prime readiness for chartering, Gloria is equipped with hydraulically furled sails, a steel hull, and a fully upgraded rig and deck. A Caterpillar diesel engine powers this sailing marvel, enabling top speeds of 12 knots. Finally, although Gloria's glory has been rightfully restored while preserving its classic charm, it was last asking for €2,600,000 and is now set to embark on new adventures in sailing excellence.

title: Loving Heart at Sea: Michael Green, Dedicated Mate and Beacon of Hope, Awarded as Volunteer of the Year by Ellen MacArthur Cancer Trust
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Loving Heart at Sea: Michael Green, Dedicated Mate and Beacon of Hope, Awarded as Volunteer of the Year by Ellen MacArthur Cancer Trust
summary: Ellen MacArthur Cancer Trust shines a light on Michael Green, a passionate mate, honouring his tireless dedication as Volunteer of the Year.
body: Ellen MacArthur Cancer Trust, a charity for young cancer survivors spearheaded by Dame Ellen MacArthur, recently awarded the Volunteer of the Year honour to a tenacious mate. Michael Green, a 62-year-old native of Saltcoats, North Ayrshire, received the accolade at the Trust's annual volunteer training conference held on 21st March. The Trust compliments Green’s passion for dedicating his 'whole heart' to the cause, proving that commendation and applause are not his driving forces. Green, a marine industry professional, has been making monumental strides in the lives of young people since he began his philanthropic journey with the charity back in 2017.

The resonating impact of a cancer diagnosis in young lives extends beyond the debilitating treatment. It reverberates in their education, relationships, mental health, and self-esteem. The Trust’s thrilling voyages aim to rejuvenate the spirit of these young warriors, helping them rediscover their self-worth and independence. As they discern their potential and see that they are not alone in their fight, these youngsters come out with a rejuvenated optimism for their future. This leaves an indelible imprint on their mental wellbeing, fostering improvement and resilience.

Regardless of the emotional toll it takes on him, Green finds his motivation in the possibility of a brighter future for these survivors. He likens volunteering to running a marathon – a physically draining but psychologically rewarding endeavour. His favorite part is the lead-up to the trip due to the thrilling unpredictability it brings. Green's selfless dedication to the cause encapsulates the very essence of the Ellen MacArthur Cancer Trust's mission, deeply touching the lives of young cancer survivors.

title: From Navigating Oceans to Steering Enterprises: Unveiling the Shift in the Superyacht Captain’s Role
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: From Navigating Oceans to Steering Enterprises: Unveiling the Shift in the Superyacht Captain’s Role
summary: In line with the expanding global superyacht industry, the role of the modern superyacht captain has transformed remarkably, evolving from a traditional master-at-sea to an equivalent of a chief executive officer.
body: The superyacht industry is witnessing a paradigm shift, with captains steering their roles beyond the helm of the yacht to the wheel of organisational leadership. This metamorphosis is driven by the burgeoning worldwide fleet of superyachts, emergence of novel cruising regions, and development of nascent markets. Today, these captains head intricate enterprises that represent assets worth multi-millions of euros, managing multinational crews and making headway across various jurisdictions while navigating dense regulatory waters.

As the grasp of the industry widens, so do stakeholder expectations and regulatory demands. Consequently, the role is less about traditional navigation and seamanship and more about leadership, risk management, and strategic planning. Such expanded responsibilities align the role of a modern captain with that of a CEO, responsible for the long-term safeguarding of valuable assets and overall performance.

Viewed from this lens of leadership, the modern captain is not merely a master-at-sea but rather an admired skipper of a maritime enterprise. Increased emphasis on safeguarding long-term performance and operational integrity takes precedence over mere successful trips or charter seasons. The captain's helm, as it stands today, is analogous to a CEO's boardroom, managing assets worth millions, overseeing major refits and ensuring that vessels operate within complex international regulatory landscapes.

In essence, the captains of the present day shoulder a fourfold responsibility, namely that of an operator, steward, strategist, and catalyst. While the operational command remains integral, marked emphasis is now on stewardship, managerial strategy, and cultural evolution aboard these superyachts. The captains are seen, more than ever, not just as a traditional commander of a sea vessel, but rather a CEO of a floating enterprise.

title: Unexpected Announcements Spark Market Shake-Up in Wake of Middle East Conflict
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unexpected Announcements Spark Market Shake-Up in Wake of Middle East Conflict
summary: A surprising turn of events in Middle East negotiations has ushered in a wave of relief across global markets.
body: As the world held its breath amid escalating tensions in the Middle East, an unexpected announcement brought a much-needed sigh of relief. The hint of a possible resolution to the crisis, led by none other than U.S. President Trump, created palpable relief, especially across global markets. Alongside the intricate moves in the negotiation chessboard, potential strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure were put on hold. This resulted in a significant drop in the ailing oil market, which had previously reached a concerning height of over USD 100 per barrel. The new price drop to under USD 90 per barrel was welcomed news to countless around the globe.

Just a day before this turn of events, the world was facing a severe energy crisis, amplified by the military escalation in this volatile corner of the world. Oil and gas prices had swelled, pushing Europe and Asia, regions without their own energy supplies, into the throes of vulnerability. This energy crisis had threatened to directly contribute to inflation and provoked a rise in bond yields across Europe.

Although the latest developments provide short-term relief, the lingering fear of global recession keeps commodity currencies under pressure. The world continues to anxiously watch the Middle East, with energy prices, inflation, and potential economic slowdown being of primary concern. The evolving crisis has kept every market enthusiast, industry professional, and government on their toes, waiting for the next shoe to drop.

title: Zeelander's Second Flagship Yacht, Mojo: A Whisper-Quiet Powerhouse of Personalised Luxury
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Zeelander's Second Flagship Yacht, Mojo: A Whisper-Quiet Powerhouse of Personalised Luxury
summary: The Zeelander 8, Mojo has been successfully handed to its owner. This spectacular unit stands out for its unique pearlescent white hued hull and deck.
body: Splashing the waves with grandeur, the second unit from Dutch shipyard, Zeelander's flagship yacht series, the 'Zeelander 8' was quietly handed over to an experienced owner. Named 'Mojo', it emerges as a unique member of the fleet sporting a pearlescent white hull and deck, adorned with gold and black boot stripes, while setting itself a class apart.

The luxury vessel was designed for an adept sailor who prefers to navigate the azure waters himself and yet, keeps the option to hire a captain at his discretion. Its maiden voyage is slated to cruise the resplendent maritime frontiers of the South of France.

Behind the elegant silhouette of the yacht is the mastery of Dutch designer Cor D. Rover. For Mojo, this inherent elegance was amplified with the inclusion of custom interior embellishments like gold detailing, 'glossy' teak flooring, and tasteful leather accents. The deck layout has been custom-tailored to match the lifestyle of the owner. A fundamental reshuffling includes a central island in the saloon, improved flow through repositioning of the galley, and enlarged seating and sun pad on the aft deck.

Unending views of the sea are made possible at the helm. Fitted with additional generous seating as an extra viewpoint, it allows the captain to be accompanied in comfort while voyaging. Other lavish accessories include a Williams 435 Jet Tender and a fully stocked garage of watersports gear.

Tantalising luxury below the deck includes 5 spacious cabins, sleeping up to nine guests. The lower-deck midship master suite bolsters the design with panoramic sea views and ample headroom. With a nod towards respecting nature's elements, a 'targa' sunroof and retractable aft windows effortlessly merge indoor and outdoor living spaces.

With Mojo, Zeelander has created yet another example of uncompromising craftsmanship‎. Matching bold ideas with subtle refinements and wrapping it all in a personalised luxury package, this second-in-series yacht sets a high bar.

Nestled in the seaside cities of Pisa and Viareggio, their shipyards released the fourth unit from the flagship Mangusta GranSport 54 fast displacement series and the 10th unit from the Mangusta 104 REV range.

Under the magnifying glass of luxury, GranSport 54's highlights include an expansive beach club at the stern equipped with an opening transom door and two fold-down side hatches, and interiors suffused with natural light from elongated glazed surfaces. As the cherry on top, this four-cabin beauty offers a wellness area for massages and spa treatments.

Riding on the crest of marine luxury, three days later, the 10th Mangusta 104 REV sprang into the azure waters of Viareggio. This model, from Mangusta’s Maxi Open range, penned in collaboration with Lobanov Design and the yard's Engineering Department, shone in all its sporty yet elegant splendour.

The 31.8-metre unit stands out with its slim profile, slender glazed surfaces, and a fully-opening aft cockpit door - a feature that amplifies the indoor-outdoor connection on board. Favouring the customisation route, the 10th Mangusta 104 REV features an aesthetically rich and comfortable standard configuration with individual additions developed by the Group's talented design team and architect Francesco Bortolato from Nembo Design.

Powering through the waves with twin 2,600hp Rolls-Royce MTU engines, this superyacht's maximum speed is an impressive 35 knots. It is promised to be delivered to her owner in early May. The double launch from Overmarine shipyard is indeed a marvellous feat and a great boon to the yachting world, a testament to their dedication towards providing top tier seagoing experiences.

title: RP42 Rikki Secures IRC One Victory in One of the Closest Battles of the Caribbean 600
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Rikki Wins IRC One in the 2026 RORC Caribbean 600 After a Nine-Minute Margin
summary: After nearly three days of relentless trade wind racing, the IRC One battle in the 2026 RORC Caribbean 600 came down to the final miles. RP42 Rikki prevailed by just over nine minutes on corrected time after 600 tactical miles.
body: Nine Minutes on the Clock: Rikki’s Triumph in IRC One
Few classes in the RORC Caribbean 600 were as tightly contested as IRC One in the 2026 edition.

After nearly three days and 600 miles of offshore racing through the Caribbean islands, the final standings were decided by a margin of just nine minutes and thirty-two seconds on corrected time — one of the closest class outcomes of the race.

At the centre of that battle was Bruce Chafee’s RP42 Rikki (USA), which crossed the finish line in Antigua in 2 days 21 hours 51 minutes 30 seconds elapsed time. When the IRC calculations were complete, Rikki had done enough to secure victory.
Second place went to Xavier Bellouard’s Lift 45 Maxitude (FRA), which claimed line honours for the class but fell short on corrected time.
Third place belonged to Woody Cullen’s Swan 58 WaveWalker (USA), which finished the race in 3 days 00 hours 30 minutes 11 seconds.
It was classic Caribbean 600 racing — a contest defined not only by speed, but by navigation, timing and tactical judgement around the islands.
Victory in the Caribbean 600 rarely comes easily, and for Rikki’s navigator Suzy Leech, the race carried its own psychological challenge long before the fleet left Antigua.
This was her first Caribbean 600, and one part of the course had been playing on her mind from the start.
The notorious Guadeloupe wind shadow.
“I’d heard so much about that section of the race,” Leech admitted. “The whole time I was worried about it — especially behind Guadeloupe.”
The towering volcanic island is famous for disrupting the trade winds. Boats entering its lee can find themselves slowed dramatically while competitors just miles away continue at full speed.
Many Caribbean 600 races have been decided there.
For Rikki, the moment proved decisive.
“We were able to escape on a great puff and left our competition literally miles behind us,” Leech said. “That’s when I finally took a breath and thought — we survived.”
For skipper Bruce Chafee, the victory represented the culmination of years of preparation rather than a single successful race.
“A lot of the preparation started well before this race,” Chafee explained. “Maybe even two years ago when we first came to the Caribbean 600.”
The RORC Nelson’s Cup Series, held in Antigua just days before the main race, proved a valuable final test.
“The Nelson’s Cup was a great proving ground. Everything went smoothly and it showed us that our preparation was working.”
That preparation extended beyond the water. Moving a race boat across the Atlantic is no small undertaking.
Rikki’s campaign involved shipping the yacht from Rhode Island in the middle of winter, assembling the crew in Antigua and preparing the boat for a week of high-intensity offshore racing.
The depth of the IRC One fleet added to the pressure.
“We’re fortunate that this class has a lot of boats around the 42-foot size,” Chafee said. “We came here for the competition.”
Boats like Maxitude, WaveWalker, Jackknife, and Afazik Impulse ensured that the class remained tightly contested from start to finish.
In offshore racing terms, there was no room to relax.
Every island rounding mattered.
For Leech, one of the most rewarding aspects of the race was competing against some of the sport’s most experienced navigators.
Among them was Alexis Loison, navigating aboard Maxitude.
“Every single day I learn something new,” Leech said. “If I don’t learn something new, then it’s a wasted day.”
The Nelson’s Cup series played a crucial role in refining Rikki’s performance.
“It allowed us to get our calibrations almost spot on. Being able to race properly before the Caribbean 600 was really important.”
She also admitted that sometimes the best tactical information comes from observing competitors.
“It’s not bad to glance around occasionally and see what the bigger boats ahead of you are doing.”
The Culture of Team Rikki
If one word defines the Rikki programme, Chafee says it is simple.
Team.
“My primary job is to bring the team together — the boat, the resources, the tools they need to perform.”
That culture has created a crew that thrives under pressure.
“We’re dinghy sailors at heart,” Chafee said. “We love pushing the boat and racing hard.”
The atmosphere onboard reflected that approach.
“And we never stopped laughing,” Leech added. “It was just so much fun.”
That combination of professionalism and enjoyment is often the hallmark of successful offshore teams.
A Race Won by Small Margins
The final margin of nine minutes and thirty-two seconds after 600 miles illustrates just how competitive IRC One proved in this year’s race.
In offshore racing, that margin is effectively nothing.
One missed wind shift.
One slow sail change.
One poorly timed island rounding.
Any of those moments could have changed the result.
Instead, Rikki combined preparation, precision navigation and consistent boat speed to secure the class victory.
The Caribbean 600: Still One of the World’s Great Offshore Races
For many sailors, the RORC Caribbean 600 remains one of the most compelling races in offshore sailing.
The course weaves through 11 Caribbean islands, combining high-speed trade wind sailing with complex tactical decisions around volcanic terrain and shifting wind shadows.
The result is a race that rewards both speed and judgement.
A well-prepared boat. A confident crew. And one perfectly timed puff off Guadeloupe.
After 600 miles, it was enough.

title: Bulwarks and Bulldust Features Third-Generation Boat Builder David French's Passion for Foiling
author: Old Sea Dogs

French's narrative resonates powerfully, mirroring not only his own experiences but also the emerging passion of his children for this invigorating sport. His tale convincingly asserts that the desire to take to the skies, just as much as the seas, can indeed renew sailing enthusiasts' love for their sport. His story, rooted in his deeply personal relationship with sailing and boat building, embodies a grass-roots perspective that is as authentic as it is inspiring. As a qualified engineer, French articulates the joys and challenges of designing and building the very boats used in foiling. This story serves as a stirring reminder that the spirit of innovation is never far from the world of water sports. Yet David's mission doesn't stop at his own enjoyment of foiling. He is also committed to promoting the sport among the younger generations. It is this very determination that has made the Junior Foiling Cup a global success, reflecting French’s influence in this exciting, evolving sports realm. Bulwarks and Bulldust followers are invited to join the conversation with French, hosted by Wally Tench, Adrian Finglas, and Ben Kelly. Viewers can witness firsthand French's experiences, insights, and inspirations in a compelling narrative sure to inspire sailing enthusiasts to embark on a thrilling new adventure. Bulwarks and Bulldust's enduring support from prominent sponsors like Pantaenius Sail and Motor Yacht Insurance, The Boat Works Gold Coast, GINEICO, REVO, and Big Duck Inflatables only serves to accentuate the growing appeal of French’s story and/or foiling. title: Pensacola Cup 2026 Surges Ahead with Champagne Conditions and Unrelenting Competition
author: Old Sea Dogs

summary: Unyielding competition and a spirit of true sportsmanship on display at the GL52 Pensacola Cup 2026’s third day where Wizard remains in the lead.
body: The GL52 Pensacola Cup 2026 continued to sparkle as champagne conditions paved the way for an exciting third day. The indomitable Wizard held its lead, finishing first in all four races on the day, maintaining its consistent performance, and further reinforcing its dominance in the tournament with a mere 12 points.

Showing no signs of easing off, Windquest prominently sought to dismantle Wizard's potent victory streak, throwing down the gauntlet with daring moves. Their bold endeavors yielded mixed results - while it strengthened their standing on the leaderboard with 23 points, they remain caught in a gritty pursuit, knowing the fight is far from over.

Parallelly, the ClubSwan28 fleet commanded its share of attention with the scores remaining as tight as ever. The addition of a sixth race awarded a throw out, further adding to the competition's intrigue. Al Ramadan's Play Bigger maintained their stronghold at the top. However, with the first and third positions merely a point apart, the podium finish is still anybody's game.

With conditions looking to replicate the spectacular show of the previous day, expectations are running high for another grueling day of races. The first warning is due at 12 pm CST, signaling the commencement of what promises to be another thrilling spectacle on the water.

title: Thrills and Spills on Day Three: A Look at the GL52 Pensacola Cup and the WASZP Games 2026

summary: Day three of both the GL52 Pensacola Cup and WASZP Games provided the sailing world with unanticipated turns, exciting finishes and standout performances.
body: The glittering waters of Pensacola Bay played host to an unforgettable day three of both the GL52 Pensacola Cup and the WASZP Games 2026. Sailing enthusiasts around the globe felt the adrenaline surge as unpredictable winds, riveting finishes, and the uncompromising combativeness of the competitors unfolded in front of their eyes. The GL52 Pensacola Cup bore witness to the continued dominance of Wizard, who, stamping their authority, secured four astounding first-place finishes. Their performance took racing mastery to new heights, with just a mere twelve points against them. Not far behind, Windquest remained hot on Wizard's heels, sitting comfortably with 23 points. But the day was not completely devoid of daring challenges, as the gallant Katana began closing in on Windquest by tightening its hold on 25 points. The day also witnessed fierce competition in the ClubSwan28 fleet where Al Ramadan's Play Bigger clung to the top spot, despite fierce competition from Bacio and My Sharona. One of the highlights of the day was the truly remarkable display of skill by the young competitors, Francesco de Santis, just 16 and Bodhi Rushin, only 11. These fiery young talents, products of a well-nurtured and supported sailing system, lived proof that in sailing, age is but a mere number. As another exhilarating day of sailing drew to a close, the anticipation for what the next racing day held was palpable. The stage is set for more thrills, thrilling finishes, and tests of skill and stamina as the GL52 Pensacola Cup and WASZP Games 2026 continue their exciting sailing spectacle.

title: Simultaneous Grand Superyacht Projects Unfold: German Naval Yards and Abeking & Rasmussen Join Forces
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Simultaneous Grand Superyacht Projects Unfold: German Naval Yards and Abeking & Rasmussen Join Forces
summary: In the transcendent world of luxury sea travel, grandeur and meticulous precision take centre stage as German Naval Yards embarks on a colossal superyacht project.
body: Oceanic excellence and meticulous artistry combine in enticing synchronicity as German Naval Yards (GNY) announces its new venture – the awe-inspiring construction of a 100-metre-plus superyacht hull and superstructure for the esteemed company, Abeking & Rasmussen. This project underscores not only the strength and proficiency of this astounding partnership but also elevates their global standing in the demanding realm of luxury yacht construction.

Choosing not to rest on their laurels, alongside the unnamed endeavor that boasts an impressive 4,500GT, GNY also boasts an ongoing construction - the 114-meter Project ELF. Acquiring this in 2025, GNY continues to solidify its illustrious reputation, maintaining its position at the forefront of the luxury marine sector.

Simultaneously, German shipyard Abeking & Rasmussen unfurls its dazzling superyacht vision in collaboration with British powerhouse Reymond Langton Design. Presenting the 72-metre superyacht concept 'Aruby' at the Palm Beach International Boat Show, they once again confirm their status as industry trendsetters.

Carving an innovative path in yacht design, 'Aruby' is carefully shaped from battle-tested engineering insights and precious chunks of client feedback, culminating in a sublime, ready-to-build superyacht design that gleams with promise.

Artfully designed and with a refined regard for its namesake gemstone, 'Aruby' strides forward in its bold 'New Luxury' layout that shifts focus to self-service and discretion, allowing guests the freedom to flow between fine dining, wellness activities or distance work in the onboard office.

The 'Aruby' superyacht concept aims to elegantly reflect the modern owner’s preference for uncompromised quality without the hassle of long development lead times, underscoring yet again how the Abeking & Rasmussen and Reymond Langton Design's innovative partnership is continuing to shape the future of luxury seafaring.

title: Newly Arrived Amels 80 Yacht Finds a Buyer Quickly, Demonstrating Continued Demand for the Limited Editions Series
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Newly Arrived Amels 80 Yacht Finds a Buyer Quickly, Demonstrating Continued Demand for the Limited Editions Series
summary: The fifth Amels 80, part of Damen Yachting's Limited Editions range, got snapped up shortly after reaching the yard in Vlissingen.
body: Set sail on an intriguing tale of the high seas. Demand for Damen Yachting's Amels 80 Limited Editions range yachts remains high, with the fifth unit scooped up briskly after docking at their Vlissingen yard this January. The sale, effected in strong collaboration with brokerage firm Burgess, underlines the sustained interest in the Amels 80 design. A total of five Amels 80 yachts are currently under construction, as per BOATPro data.

Burgess is supervising the build for the buyer through its in-house team. This marks the third Amels 80 the brokerage firm has facilitated for its clients. Jan van Hogerwou, commercial executive at Damen Yachting, stated that the deal 'speaks to the enduring appeal of the Amels Limited Editions approach.' This approach merges a tried-and-true design platform with the liberty to tailor a yacht per the owner's vision while enjoying the yard's dependable build quality and delivery record.

The design champions space, openness, and a strong connection to the sea. The yacht's 200-square-metre sun deck is the most spacious in its class, allowing for various relaxation and entertainment zones. A three-sided open beach club bolsters the connection to the water. The vessel also boasts a private owner's deck, a 6.5-metre glass-bottom swimming pool, ample wellness facilities including a gym, hammam and sauna, and panoramic guest accommodation on the main deck.

In an age where discerning owners understand that sustainability and smart ownership go hand in hand, the Amels 80's hybrid propulsion system and optimised hull design don't just reduce environmental impact. They provide significant fuel savings and lower operational costs while protecting long-term value. This integration of technology and design underscores Damen's focus on comfort, operational efficiency and an enhanced onboard experience. It is intelligent yacht ownership for the modern era.

Notably, exclusive data from BOATPro reveals that Amels currently has eight yachts on order or in build. The largest of which is 120-metre Project Tanzanite, the largest Dutch-built motor yacht in history, which is set for delivery this year. The five Amels 80 are just small fishes in this vast ocean of luxury and innovation.

title: German Naval Yards Build Over 100m Superstructure for Abeking & Rasmussen Superyacht
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: German Naval Yards Build Over 100m Superstructure for Abeking & Rasmussen Superyacht
summary: German Naval Yards (GNY) embarks on an exciting venture to construct the massive hull and superstructure of a new 100-meter-plus Abeking & Rasmussen superyacht.
body: German Naval Yards (GNY), the maritime giant renowned for its expertise in yacht construction, announced an electrifying new contract to build a mammoth hull and superstructure for an Abeking & Rasmussen superyacht. A testament to German precision and engineering, a 100-metre-plus super yacht is about to take shape. The steel hull and aluminium superstructure will be crafted with the utmost precision and delivered to the accomplished German shipyard, marking a significant step for new builds in the global superyacht project. The specifics of this ambitious endeavor, such as whether it will surpass Abeking & Rasmussen's current flagship, the 118.2-metre Liva O, remain a thrilling mystery. However, there is no doubt that this mammoth project will shatter previous records, with the yacht expected to exceed 4,500GT. GNY's agreement to undertake this formidable project not only underlines the strong collaboration between the two renowned companies but also puts a spotlight on their immense capabilities to successfully execute complex projects in the global yacht-building industry. In their ongoing commitment to revolutionizing maritime construction, GNY continues their work on another colossal venture - the 114-metre Project ELF, which they acquired in late 2025. The company, part of the European group CMN Naval, has made its mark in the yachting industry with iconic creations like the 142.8-metre Sailing Yacht A. Furthermore, GNY recently received a non-binding purchase offer from defense juggernaut Thyssenkrupp Marine Systems. Such is the prominence and unwavering reputation of the GNY, destined to build the marine wonders of the future. As GNY embarks on this grand new project, the entire maritime world watches with baited breath. Who knows what incredible wonders the union of these German giants will bring into the world of yachts? It promises, at least, to be a voyage worth following.

title: Athena Racing Affirms Steadfast Support for GB1, The United Kingdom's America's Cup Hopeful
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Athena Racing Affirms Steadfast Support for GB1, The United Kingdom's America's Cup Hopeful
summary: Unfazed by history, Athena Racing backs team GB1, Britain's contender in the relentless pursuit of the coveted America's Cup.
body: Standing tall on the maritime frontier, unblemished by the ebb and flow of history, Athena Racing continues its indomitable support for the British America's Cup team, GB1. A legacy that stretches back twelve impressive years since the team's establishment in 2014, Athena Racing remains committed to the cause. Despite the fact that the coveted trophy has eluded British clutches for a staggering 175 years, Athena Racing's mission remains unchanged: to claim the sporting world's most venerable prize for the nation.

The laudable sponsorship and support of Ineos have been pivotal in GB1's campaigns in the recent past. This partnership culminated in GB1's title as the most successful British challenger in six decades at the Barcelona 2024. Nevertheless, the path going forward is clear — any assets owned and possessed by Athena Racing will be employed for the AC38. A statement that should not surprise anyone, least of all Ineos. Athena Racing, it seems, has no intention of dropping-anchor on the pursuit of Britain's sailing glory.

title: Palladino Yacht Design Unveils Audacious 95m Superyacht, Merging Architecture and the Sea
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Palladino Yacht Design Unveils Audacious 95m Superyacht, Merging Architecture and the Sea
summary: Palladino Yacht Design reveals a breathtaking 95-meter superyacht concept, marrying avant-garde design with startling architectural elements.
body: In a thrilling new revelation, Palladino Yacht Design has pulled back the curtain on a pioneering 95-meter superyacht concept. This majestic design can best be described as a sea-bound homage to modern architecture, with every element meticulously crafted to not only traverse the oceans in style but also shake up the status quo in the luxury yachting scene. Strikingly spectacular, it boasts deck levels that symbolize continuity in design, a sense of depth, and an exceptional flair for architectural heights.

The yacht's exterior is a spectacle of a metallic silver hull, with decks organized in crisp, geometric horizontal lines, forming a low-profile silhouette. This geometry, however, is more than meets the eye. It integrates full-height glazing bands that sweep across the superstructure, offering an intimate rapport between interior and exterior spaces, paired with stunning panoramic views throughout the vessel.

The pièce de résistances, however, has to be the opulent owner's suite, enveloped by floor-to-ceiling glass walls giving breathtaking forward-facing views. To top it all off, a dining and outdoor patio area forward of the suite emerges from below deck level when in use, proving that the audacious and ingenious design philosophy permeates beyond just the facade. This vessel is truly the elevated experience that the superyacht space has been awaiting.

title: Nostalgia Sets Sail: Auckland Wooden Boat Festival Revives Age-Old Maritime Heritage
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Nostalgia Sets Sail: Auckland Wooden Boat Festival Revives Age-Old Maritime Heritage
summary: Merrily echoing a bygone era, the Auckland Wooden Boat Festival again whisks spectators off on a historic maritime adventure, sparking collective nostalgia.
body: Over 17,000 sailing enthusiasts congregated for the recent Auckland Wooden Boat Festival, a spellbinding showcase of Auckland's rich nautical heritage. Effortlessly curated and into its second chapter, the festival hosted an enthralling display of the city's classic fleet, all in far better shape than at their original launch. One could almost imagine they were spectators at these vessels' earliest debuts.

Jellicoe Harbour, that storied aquatic arena, housed not just one, but two excellent boat shows over successive weekends. Among them, the Wooden Boat Festival stood distinct with one of the planet's most awe-inspiring wooden boat fleets. A cordial invitation to wander back to an earlier epoch, this showcase featured a dazzling congregation of tall masts rarely seen in today's boat shows.

Raucous excitement permeated the showgrounds as boat owners and crew members shared inspiring tales of their vessels. Displaying printed historical summaries for each boat, festival organisers brought history to life, leaving no berth empty and not a fibreglass boat in sight.

The outer marina, lined with classic boats, was a sight to observe and a sterling tribute to John Street, a key person behind the return or rebuilding of these crafts to New Zealand. Meanwhile, the Viaduct Events Centre, formerly a hub of marine technology, slipped into yesteryears hosting multiple exhibits. Row upon row of wooden dinghies replaced the modern technology of the recent SailGP foiling F50 fleet, creating an authentic atmosphere reminiscent of a halcyon past.

The Auckland Wooden Boat Festival, in every way, celebrated the timeless prestige of wooden boats and the charm of a bygone era of sailing, underscoring an undeniable authenticity and nostalgia for all those fortunate to attend.

title: Revitalising Greek Sailing: Yacht Club of Greece Introduces Six University-Sourced RS21 Keelboats to Regenerate Club Fleet
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Revitalising Greek Sailing: Yacht Club of Greece Introduces Six University-Sourced RS21 Keelboats to Regenerate Club Fleet
summary: Breathing new life into Greek sailing, the Yacht Club of Greece ushers in an exciting new era with the arrival of six RS21 keelboats.
body: The Yacht Club of Greece is entering a thrilling chapter, announcing the addition of six RS21 keelboats to its rapidly growing fleet. It's the first club-owned fleet of RS21s in Greece, injecting a new level of competitiveness and dynamism into Greek sailing. This shiny fleet of boats is set to enhance the Club's mature sailing offerings and pave the way for a hopscotch of activity on the Aegean Sea.

Investments like these make the waters more inviting, bringing modern, structured training programmes and innovative, engaging racing events within reach of members and visitors. That's not all - these new boats are set to bring fresh experiences to sailors, welcoming individuals of all levels to embrace the winds and waves. The RS21 was key to realising this vision. Its modern, high-performance design ensured its selection as a versatile sailboat, adept at competitive club racing, charter use, and learn-to-sail programmes.

Michiel Geerling, Head of Commercial at RS Sailing, shared his exhilaration, 'I'm excited to see the first RS21 fleet arrive in Greece. At RS Sailing, we're all about participation, so establishing a new fleet in new waters - especially the first club fleet in the country - is a significant moment.' RS Sailing continues to anticipate the new fleet's role in training and racing while also looking forward to welcoming Greek teams at future European and International events. Sailors, start your engines - an exhilarating wave of sailing activity is surging on the Saronic Gulf.

title: Unleashing a New Chapter: Charting the Rise of Yachting Startups in 2026
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unleashing a New Chapter: Charting the Rise of Yachting Startups in 2026
summary: The yachting startup landscape is rapidly evolving, pushing past its growth obstacles and welcoming a refreshing influx of innovative ideas and burgeoning businesses.
body: The yachting startup ecosystem, once handicapped by lack of investor attention, is experiencing a dramatic reversal under the guidance of Yachting Ventures' founder and CEO, Gabbi Richardson. The company has been hard at work for years, developing the ecosystem by linking budding maritime businesses with investors and media coverage, along with curated industry ties.

Evolving from humble boat-show beginnings, Yachting Ventures has transformed into a comprehensive platform, complete with investor tools and structures for more dynamic interactions between founders and investors. The company is also gearing up for the launch of its 'Scaling Syndicate' in Q2 2026, a move targeting companies on the threshold of significant growth.

According to Gabbi Richardson, in her eyes, the most deserving of companies for investment are those that can illustrate relevance beyond just leisure marine and yachting. Richardson outlines further insights into the startup market, investor expectations, the impact of AI, and the rising stars in the yachting sector to watch out for in 2026.

Reflecting on Yachting Ventures' journey in 2025, the focus was on enhancing its platform to increase visibility and credibility for yachting startups. The firm plans to solidify its status as a central hub, connecting founders, investors, and industry stakeholders while amplifying startup success stories.

Embracing the shift towards broader growth in 2026, many of the previously supported companies are transitioning from early-stage into scale-up mode. In response, Yachting Ventures intends to establish the 'Scaling Syndicate' in Q2. This initiative aims to gather industry experts who can assist these companies in this critical growth phase.

Participation in boat shows remains a prominent avenue for startups, given diligent campaign planning. Despite the fruitful prospects, Richardson emphasizes comprehensive preparation, visual branding, proactive outreach, and coordinated communication plans as key to making the most out of these opportunities and gaining maximum traction.

As the yachting sector rides the waves towards an exciting future, it promises to uplift startups, empower investors, and challenge tradition. Indeed, the horizon is looking bright for the yachting startup ecosystem.

title: Unveiling a New Era: ISA Yachts and Lobanov Design Launch Mesmerising 70m superyacht named Blade
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unveiling a New Era: ISA Yachts and Lobanov Design Launch Mesmerising 70m superyacht named Blade
summary: In collaboration with Lobanov Design, Italian shipyard ISA Yachts introduces an elegant, fresh interpretation of superyacht design with its 70-metre Blade.
body: In a bold affirmation of the prowess of design and innovation, Italian shipyard ISA Yachts, a brand under Palumbo Superyachts, presents to the world its latest creation - the 70-metre Blade. This new superyacht design engenders the dawn of a fresh collaboration with Lobanov Design, steered by acclaimed designer Igor Lobanov.

Blade enters the yachting scene as a fresh interpretation of ISA Yachts' design language. Its creation aims at the grand sport segment, a niche that paves the way for fast, sporty yachts with vertical or near-vertical bows. This new design harbours a strong identity, combining recognisable styling influenced by the elegant vessels of the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

Envisioning a seamless sculptural form, Blade's fluid lines traverse from bow to stern—an innovative approach for a grand sports yacht. Hull graphics are cunningly integrated into the superyacht's volume. In addition, glazing infuses a unique visual identity, brilliantly merging dotted glass panels with a contrasting black insert.

The superstructure envisages a composition of dark-painted surfaces, glass panels, teak detailing and a dynamic curve that ignites a sense of motion. Notably, the yacht features a transforming aft garage door, elegantly transforming into an idyllic bench for seafarers to marvel at the ocean.

Prioritising owner's comfort, the interior arrangement includes an aft suite on the upper deck. The suite comes with a private terrace, ensuring maximal privacy and unobstructed views of the sea. Projected performance illustrates a top speed of 17.5 knots, cruising speed of 14 knots and a range of approximately 5,000 nautical miles, powered by twin MTU 12V4000 M53L engines.

Giuseppe Palumbo, sole director of Palumbo Superyachts, hasn't held back his enthusiasm. According to him, Blade represents not only a new interpretation of ISA Yachts' DNA but a project of great strategic significance. Moreover, he sees the partnership with Lobanov Design as shared pursuit of strong design and innovation. This unveiling indicates larger schemes under progress between ISA Yachts and Lobanov Design. Clearly, the future holds much in store for these collaborating giants of the yachting sphere.

title: From Nevis to St. Barts the Caribbean 600 Turns Tactical as Class Battles Intensify
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: RORC Caribbean 600 Day Two: Duels in the Trades as the Fleet Tightens Around the Northern Islands
summary: Duels in the Trades: Day Two of the Caribbean 600 By the second day of the RORC Caribbean 600, the fleet has settled into the rhythm that defines this race. Not a simple drag race through the trade winds, but a rolling series of tactical puzzles around the islands of the eastern Caribbean.
body: From Nevis to St. Barts, the race has begun to fragment into high-speed duels, tactical compression zones and developing class battles. Each island transit reshapes the leaderboard. Each pressure line rewards patience and punishes impatience.
And this year’s edition is proving especially tactical.

Instead of the classic reaching angles that often dominate the Caribbean 600, the trade winds have been sitting further south-east than usual. That subtle shift has changed the geometry of the course, forcing crews into longer periods of upwind sailing and tight reaching.
The result is a fleet that remains remarkably compressed across multiple divisions.
The race may be beginning to take shape — but it is far from settled.
The Northern Islands: Where the Race Tightens
The northern arc of the course is always a decisive phase of the Caribbean 600.

From Antigua the fleet charges north-west toward Barbuda, before threading through the chain of islands that includes Nevis, Saba, St. Barts and Anguilla. Each island produces wind shadows, acceleration zones and abrupt tactical decisions.
A crew that rounds a headland in pressure can suddenly open miles.
A crew that hesitates for even a few minutes can lose them just as quickly.
The islands are beautiful from a distance. Up close, they are unforgiving racecourse features.
By Day Two the fleet had begun to stretch out across these islands, but the corrected-time margins remain tight across most classes.
Among the larger boats, the IRC Super Zero fleet is already shaping into a tight contest.
At the Anguilla Channel, the Mills 72 Balthasar held the corrected-time advantage, with the Farr 100 Leopard 3 just four minutes and forty-one seconds behind.
In third position sat the VO65 Jajo, skippered by Tony Rey.
These large offshore yachts thrive on power reaching, but the tighter angles of this year’s race are forcing more manoeuvres and greater tactical awareness.
At speeds approaching 20 knots, even small course changes can have dramatic effects on the leaderboard.
With the southern leg still to come, the battle between Leopard 3 and Balthasar remains very much alive.
Further down the fleet, the Class40 division has begun to spread slightly.
At the St. Barts transit point, Robin Follin’s Solano (FRA) held a commanding lead on the water.
More significantly, Solano produced the fastest sector time from Saba to St. Barts, extending their margin over Mateo Calvic’s FPFP-TP (FRA) to more than 35 minutes.
In third place, Mike Hennessy’s Scow-bow Class40 Scowling Dragon continued to hold position, roughly half an hour behind FPFP-TP.
Fourth place belonged to Jean-Yves Aglae’s Martinique Horizon (FRA).
The Class40 fleet is known for relentless pace and narrow margins, but Solano’s performance through the northern islands suggests they have found the right combination of pressure and routing.
Still, the long southern leg of the Caribbean 600 has undone many Class40 leaders before.
One of the tightest contests of the race so far is unfolding in IRC One.
At the Saba transit, Bruce Chafee’s RP42 Rikki (USA) jumped two places to take the class lead after corrected time.
The margin? Just 51 seconds ahead of Sam Hall’s J/125 Jackknife (GBR).
Behind them, Yves Grosjean’s Neo 430 Afazik Impulse (FRA) advanced into third place, while Xavier Bellouard’s Lift 45 Maxitude (FRA) slipped into fourth.
The numbers illustrate how close the class remains:
Less than 30 minutes separates second from fourth
Small performance deltas define the order
One good island rounding could reshuffle everything
As offshore sailors often say, there’s still plenty of golf left to play.
In IRC Two, the fleet rounded Saba and began the push toward St. Barts with Richard Dilley’s GS46 Belladonna holding the class lead.
Behind them, Vic Cox and Peter Dunlop’s J/122 Mojito (GBR) trailed by around 12 minutes on corrected time.
Just a few minutes further back, Ray Rhinelander’s J/133 Bella J, skippered by Sarah Nicholson, remained firmly within striking distance.
Further down the order, boats like Panacea X and Whistler remained close enough that a single tactical gain could alter the standings dramatically.
Rather than sudden ranking shifts, this phase of the race has been defined by steady time deltas.
Small gains. Small losses.
But they accumulate.
While the northern islands have begun to shape the race, many experienced Caribbean 600 sailors know the real drama often unfolds further south.
The approach to Guadeloupe is notorious.

Here the towering volcanic island blocks the trade winds, creating an enormous wind shadow on its western side. Boats arriving in the lee can find themselves almost stopped while competitors just a mile away sail in full pressure.
The area has earned a reputation among sailors as the “Guadeloupe Casino.”
You make your bet — inshore or offshore — and wait to see whether the wind pays out.
Many Caribbean 600 races have been won or lost here.
And with the fleet still relatively compressed, the upcoming transition could dramatically reshape the leaderboard.
Part of what makes the Caribbean 600 so compelling is its constant variety.
In the space of a single race, crews experience:
High-speed trade wind reaching
Upwind tactical battles
Wind shadows and acceleration zones
Night navigation through island chains
Sudden weather shifts
Unlike many offshore races that follow long open-water legs, the Caribbean 600 demands constant decision-making.
Every few hours another island appears.
Another tactical puzzle begins.
As Day Two unfolds, the race has begun to reveal its structure — but not its winner.
Across multiple classes the margins remain tight. Tactical positioning continues to matter. And the trade winds are offering no easy answers.
The fleet now turns its attention south toward Guadeloupe and the long southern leg of the course.
There, stamina, navigation and patience will matter as much as raw speed.
The Caribbean 600 rarely produces a simple story.
And this year’s edition looks set to deliver another classic.
Salt in the air. Trades in the rigging. And still a long way to go.

title: Discover the Beneteau Gran Turismo 50: A Bold and Distinctive Rearrangement of Classic Sportscruiser Elements
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover the Beneteau Gran Turismo 50: A Bold and Distinctive Rearrangement of Classic Sportscruiser Elements
summary: Beneteau breaks the mould with their new Gran Turismo 50, opting for a return to classic sportscruiser features over bigger size boat.
body: Debuting at the Dusseldorf show, the Beneteau Gran Turismo 50 made a splash, showcasing a modern reinterpretation of the classic sportscruiser model. Striking a perfect balance between elegance and functionality, this new model became the showstopper, grabbing the headline as the new flagship of the Gran Turismo range.

Eschewing the majority's trend towards inflated size, the Gran Turismo 50 is a testament to Beneteau's evolutionary vision. It harkens back to the underpinnings of what made sportscruisers a beloved class - beauty, a lowered roofline and an abundance of outdoor living space. Its standout appearance, embellished further by the Alpine edition’s midnight blue hue and carbon fibre detailing, drew attention to its elegant, flowing lines and refreshed profile.

One striking feature is the recessed seating area, a welcome adornment to the foredeck sun pads, which fuels the feeling of a more sophisticated bow-rider. With an enclosed deck saloon that provides panoramic views of the cockpit from the long bar at its aft and cushioned by a compact but comfortably furnished helm, the GT50 caters to both private and social settings.

In line with the vessel’s low deck and roofline, the full-beam owner’s cabin finds itself in the foreship, providing sufficient light, space and headroom for a luxurious experience. A small single cabin is tucked to port alongside a sizeable twin/double cabin to starboard, maximizing space efficiently.

The Beneteau Gran Turismo 50's design explores a bold approach in a world where size is a significant selling point. With its contribution to the evolution of classic sportscruisers, the GT50 signifies a triumph that Beneteau deserves to revel in.

title: Turquoise Yachts Boosts its Western Presence with Appointment of Thom Conboy
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Turquoise Yachts Boosts its Western Presence with Appointment of Thom Conboy
summary: Yacht manufacturer Turquoise Yachts has recruited Thom Conboy as their Americas representative to bolster its presence in the region.
