With this significant appointment, the company aims to enhance both their sales and after-sales support for clients and bolster the presence of the Turkish Yard in America.

Conboy, who will be based in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, brings a wealth of experience and knowledge of the yachting industry to his new role. His appointment not only demonstrates Turquoise Yachts' commitment to expanding its international presence but also its dedication to providing the highest level of service to its clients.

For consumers in the Americas, the appointment of a seasoned professional like Conboy signifies an even stronger assurance of top-tier service and after-sales support. His broad industry expertise and commitment to excellence will certainly help solidify Turquoise Yachts' name as a premier brand in the Western Hemisphere.

title: Cape Town’s V&A Waterfront to Welcome €11.5 Million Superyacht Haven Amid Transformative Sea-side Development
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Cape Town’s V&A Waterfront to Welcome €11.5 Million Superyacht Haven Amid Transformative Sea-side Development
summary: The V&A Waterfront in Cape Town is set to invest about €11.5 million into a new superyacht marina, set for completion by October 2026.
body: The V&A Waterfront marina at Cape Town's harbour precinct is about to receive an impressive €11.5 million facelift. With a completion date set for October 2026, the Quay 7 Superyacht Marina will become the first Gold Anchor-accredited facility in the region – an impressive addition to the extensive €1 billion Granger Bay precinct expansion project. This move comes hot on the heels of an increasing fleet reroute away from the Red Sea and a Mediterranean berth market grappling with burgeoning capacity pressure. CEO of V&A Waterfront, Graham Wood, is optimistic about the timely investment, citing it as a response to a growing market demand.

The increasing number of superyacht visits to Cape Town have been noted since 2009, with 35 vessels welcomed in the 2024/25 season alone. Extended stays for these mega vessels have become the norm, with some spending up to a year in the harbour. Cape Town's unique blend of world-class tourism, reliable marine services and access to adventure cruising routes trump those offered by traditional yachting hubs. The new facility aims to accommodate this preference for the city among sea farers, offering eight berths for vessels measuring between 30 and 90 metres. The berths come complete with floating jetties providing electricity, water and Wi-Fi. Within the facility, Elbow Quay tenants FFS will provide bonded fuel, while access to the Syncrolift and Robinson Dry Dock ensures convenient repair and refit work. The marina is also equipped with a concierge lounge spanning around 114 square metres to cater to visiting vessels and crew.

In keeping with the marine industrial base that Cape Town is renowned for, the marina has a secondary function that supports the local manufacturing sector. Off-season, the berths will serve as commissioning and export staging areas for the city's catamaran manufacturers including Robertson and Caine, Two Oceans Marine and Balance Catamarans. These builders command strong international export markets but have been faced with limited local berthing for their finished vessels. With this new superyacht marina, Cape Town is solidifying its standing as a credible technical hub and not just a beautiful harbour. Marina official Andre Blaine hails this development as a strategic step forward, saying it generates sustained demand for fuel suppliers, marine engineers, crew training facilities, and logistics operators, while boosting local manufacturers who require berthing space for commissioning. Referring to the project as 'economic infrastructure', Blaine believes the investment will firmly position Cape Town on the global maritime circuit.

title: Mach 50 Palanad 4 Wins IRC Zero After 600 Miles of Tactical Pressure Around the Caribbean Islands
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Palanad 4 Claims IRC Zero Victory in Tactical 2026 RORC Caribbean 600
imageCredit: © 2026 Royal Ocean Racing Club - Arthur Daniel
summary: Palanad 4 Takes IRC Zero in a Hard-Fought Caribbean 600 In a race where the margins rarely stretched beyond sight of the next headland, the Mach 50 Palanad 4 – E.Leclerc emerged victorious in IRC Zero at the RORC Caribbean 600. Skippered by Antoine Magre, the French team completed the 600-mile Caribbean circuit in 2 days, 10 hours, 32 minutes and 31 seconds, securing class line honours and posting the fastest correct
body: Behind them, James Neville’s Carkeek 45 Ino Noir finished second after a bold tactical gamble on the final leg that nearly turned the race on its head. Niklas Zennström’s Carkeek 52 Rán completed the podium after a relentless week of close racing.

Throughout the race, IRC Zero delivered one of the most compelling contests in the fleet, with Palanad 4, Ino Noir, Rán, and Frederic Puzin’s Daguet 5 locked in a tactical duel that stretched from Antigua to Barbuda and down through the northern Caribbean islands.
The final result was only decided on the last miles of the final beat back to Antigua.
This year’s edition of the Caribbean 600 unfolded very differently from recent races.
Instead of the classic reaching angles associated with the trade winds, the breeze settled further to the south-east, turning much of the course into a VMG race.
Navigator Will Harris recognised the pattern early.
“Probably about 60 percent of the race was upwind or tight reaching,” he explained. “That completely changes the way you approach the course.”
For the Mach 50 Palanad 4, a boat known for its reaching speed, the conditions demanded discipline rather than outright dominance.
“It was intense,” said Magre. “Constant manoeuvres, constant sail changes. We never really settled into a normal watch rhythm.”
The race also began with an early setback. Shortly after the start, a halyard issue dropped their J1 headsail.
“It wasn’t the best beginning,” Magre admitted. “We lost over a mile.”
But offshore races of this scale are rarely decided in the opening hours. The French team recovered steadily through precise navigation and consistent boat handling across the northern island chain.
As so often happens in the Caribbean 600, the lee of Guadeloupe became the pivotal moment.
At night, with land shadows and unstable breeze bands disrupting the fleet, Ino Noir elected to diverge from the pack.
Navigator Juan Vila explained the thinking.
“We could see on the tracker that the boats ahead were going very slowly. So we made a plan.”
The decision was to sail one to two miles further offshore, seeking a different pressure band.
“In Guadeloupe you have to make your call and cross your fingers,” Vila said.
Ino Noir gained significantly through the transition, compressing the fleet and bringing the IRC Zero podium back into contention.
Downwind Speed — and Trouble Near Barbuda
From La Désirade toward Barbuda, Ino Noir found impressive downwind speed.
“We were flying 18 to 20 knots,” Neville said.
However, the breeze eased more than forecast and the boat encountered an unexpected problem.
“We got tangled in fishing gear near Barbuda which cost us time.”
Despite the setback, the British team remained firmly in the fight as the fleet approached the final leg of the race.
With roughly 35 miles remaining and the fleet approaching Redonda, Ino Noir made another aggressive tactical decision.
Rather than following the rhumb line toward Antigua, the team sailed significantly north to avoid a large squall line blocking the course.
“We weren’t planning to go that far north,” Vila explained. “But there was a big cloud on our line.”
The choice was between sailing long to the south in lighter air or detouring north to stay in pressure.
They chose north.
For a period, the decision appeared inspired. The boats ahead slowed while Ino Noir kept moving, and corrected time calculations tightened dramatically.
For a moment, IRC Zero looked within reach.
“It was a bit of a battle of the Carkeeks,” Neville said.
But ultimately the gains were not enough to overturn Palanad 4’s accumulated advantage.
Where Palanad 4 Won the Race
While Ino Noir made bold tactical moves, Palanad 4 built their victory through consistency across every leg of the course.
Certain angles proved particularly decisive.
“About 120 degrees true wind angle in 20 knots — that’s where we’re very strong,” Harris explained.
On those reaching legs the Mach 50 delivered serious pace.
“That was sublime,” Magre added.
Crucially, Palanad 4 also performed well on the heavier upwind sections late in the race.
“The windier it gets, the better we go upwind.”
Across 600 miles, the team maintained a high level of execution.
“We didn’t sail perfect,” Magre admitted. “But we were on point most of the time.”
In offshore racing, that is usually enough.
For skipper Antoine Magre, the win carried deeper significance than a class trophy.
“My father couldn’t race with us this time,” he said. “We lost my uncle last week.”
The victory in IRC Zero was dedicated to his memory.
In a race defined by relentless pressure, constant manoeuvres and tight tactical margins, Palanad 4 held their nerve.
In the Caribbean 600, that often makes all the difference.

title: Luxury Sanlorenzo Superyachts Mouchka and Piccolino Experience Financial Waves with Price Reduction and Resale
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Luxury Sanlorenzo Superyachts Mouchka and Piccolino Experience Financial Waves with Price Reduction and Resale
summary: The luxury yacht market continues to be unpredictable as superyachts Mouchka and Piccolino, both from renowned builder Sanlorenzo, face different financial tides.
body: The superyacht industry never fails to surprise. Recently, two luxury yachts from Italian shipbuilder Sanlorenzo experienced contrasting financial trajectories, reflecting the dynamic and often unpredictable nature of the yachting market. The 35.7-metre motor yacht Mouchka had a stunning €600,000 reduction to its listing, bringing its asking price down to €12,900,000. This price cut adds to the allure of the 2021-delivered yacht, which is known for its clean, elegant exterior lines and asymmetrical layout, maximizing the interior volume and connection to the sea. Its interiors, designed by Bismut & Bismut, epitomize contemporary chic, with a neutral colour palette and panoramic floor-to-ceiling windows. The yacht accommodates ten guests across five luxurious cabins, each dressed in vibrant and navy blues, reflecting a nautical theme. Mouchka's exterior spaces span three decks, each offering versatile social and entertainment hubs. Powered by twin Caterpillar engines, the yacht reaches top speeds of 18 knots. On the other hand, the 29.1-metre motor yacht Piccolino managed to find a buyer and was renamed Alein. Delivered by Sanlorenzo in 2017, Alein is a study in modern design, with interiors and exteriors by Francesco Paszkowski. The yacht underwent a refit in 2022, ensuring its continued prestige and 'immaculately maintained' status. With accommodation for eight guests across four cabins and power from two MTU diesel engines that allow her to reach speeds of up to 28 knots, Alein’s new owner certainly has a fantastic seafaring experience ahead. Both yachts testify to Sanlorenzo's commitment to superior design, engineering and craftsmanship especially in the realm of superyachts, and continue to impact the yacht market. Whether it’s a dramatic price drop or a successful resale, these sea queens once again demonstrate that in the world of grand yachting, change is the only constant.

title: A Nostalgic Voyage: Unearthing Four Defining 90s British Motor Boats Still Glittering on the Market
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A Nostalgic Voyage: Unearthing Four Defining 90s British Motor Boats Still Glittering on the Market
summary: The 90s wave saw the maritime industry take twists and turns, some boat manufacturers giving way under the crashing waves, while others, like Sunseeker and Sealine, embraced innovation to ride high. Unearth four iconic motor boats from this era that continue to charm enthusiasts.
body: A revolution rumbled through the boating industry in the '90s when manufacturers faced a stark choice: adapt or perish. The 1980s boom with lavish spending, particularly on boats, took a nosedive in the early 1990s global recession and manufacturers had to adjust their sails if they were to weather the storm.

Then came along a selection of companies that rose to the challenge. Recognising that innovation was their life raft, they focused on outshining their competitors by introducing models that were not only newer but significantly smarter. This strategic manoeuvre positioned them to successfully navigate through troubled waters and into calmer seas. The boats that emerged during this period are now recognised as classics and, due to their design and resilience, continue to make waves in the market.

One such game-changing vessel is the Sunseeker Camargue 44, launched in 1998. Initially introduced with an odd layout in the Camargue 46 a decade earlier, Sunseeker optimised the design throughout the '90s to create more appealing models. The 44, boasting two ensuite cabins, a saloon, plus a generously sized galley, was marketed as a 'sensible Sunseeker', demonstrating that practicality could indeed be stylish. The high-gloss cherry interiors may today seem retro, but they betray a quality of finish that has stood the test of time. The boat's striking exterior features voluptuous curves topped by a forward-sloping winged radar arch—an aesthetic that remains in vogue.

Matched in its design is its performance, with the powerful Caterpillar 3126 engines offering an impressive top speed of 30 knots. Despite the three-decade-old design, the Camargue 44 still stands tall as a marvel of maritime engineering, boasting an impressive single-level cockpit and a Don Shead hull that provides a solid ride.

The Sealine 330 Statesman, another iconic motor boat of the '90s era, was built when the boat building industry was far removed from today's corporate world. The age was one of incredible innovation, resilience, and defiance in the face of a crashing economy. Those that rode the wave brought forth designs that continue to inspire, awe, and navigate the seas today.

title: Historic Shake-up for the Ocean Race: Sail Newport Declines 2027 Event to Focus on Core Missions
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Historic Shake-up for the Ocean Race: Sail Newport Declines 2027 Event to Focus on Core Missions
summary: Sail Newport, renowned for hosting The Ocean Race, made a surprising decision to drop its bid for the 2027 North American Stopover in the wake of rising costs and a shift in focus towards public access and marine education.
body: The sailing universe watched with bated breath as Sail Newport, the highly esteemed organizer of the North American editions of The Ocean Race, dropped a seismic bomb: the decision not to pursue the much-anticipated 2027 event. Citing both the surge of financial demands required to host and the wish to stay true to their foundational purpose, Sail Newport has weighed anchor on what promises to be a fascinating strategic shift. The Rhode Island group, along with city, state, and marine-community advocates, convened in late 2024 to hash out the future of their ambitious endeavor. Post deliberations, the green flag went up for a surprising course correction: declining the opportunity to host the 2027 Ocean Race. The consensus emerged from an in-depth analysis of the non-profit's mission, community needs, and the financial boons necessary to play host at such scale. This historic decision opens up the pathway to refocus efforts and resources squarely on Sail Newport's core mission—fostering public access to sailing events and enhancing marine education. The organization's path is now firmly set towards cultivating maritime passions and supporting the pursuit of sustainable sailing. The director of Sail Newport, Brad Read, lauded the heritage the group has built over the years with The Ocean Race, yet underscored the need to host an event that's financially viable for the city and state. Crucially, the passing of the baton brings with it the advent of a fresh era, not just for Newport but also for St. Petersburg, Florida. The Sunshine State abode stands to benefit not merely as the next slated North American stopover of the iconic Ocean Race in 2027, but as the spotlight on a celebrated maritime community. The inhabitants of the Southeastern U.S. maritime community anticipate the event as a remarkable opportunity. Newport, from its rich Ocean Race experience, backs the St. Pete team wholeheartedly, promising to extend unflinching support towards making this event the grand spectacle it has always been.

title: Louis Tilly and Pearl Lattanzi Emerge Victorious at WASZP All-Stars Invitational; WASZP Games Kick-Off In High Gear
author: Old Sea Dogs

summary: In an electrifying competition, Australia's Louis Tilly and America's Pearl Lattanzi clinched the coveted titles at the inaugural WASZP All-Stars Invitational. Meanwhile, the kickoff of the 2026 WASZP Games unfolded with spectacular starts.
body: The exhilaration was palpable at Pensacola as sailing enthusiasts from around the globe convened for the inaugural WASZP All-Stars Invitational. The event, an elite invitation-only regatta, brought together the cream of the WASZP sailing community for high-intensity sprint races, where consistency and grit were the name of the game, with every result counting towards the final glory. On the men's side, the contest took a dramatic turn toward the end, with Australia's Louis Tilly turning the tides in his favor. Commencing his day in the waters as the Asia-Pacific Champion, Tilly showcased his strategic expertise and nerve to clinch the last two races of the regatta. His unstoppable drive delivered the ultimate triumph, securing him the overall title and a generous US$5,000 prize. On the women's side, victory was seized by the resilient American sailor Pearl Lattanzi. Successfully defending her lead, she claimed the women's crown with panache, pocketing her own US$5,000 reward.

No sooner had the echoes of cheering faded from the All-Stars Invitational than the sailing community revved up for the 2026 WASZP Games. Kicking off at the American Magic High Performance Centre, the Games gleamed with promise and potential, immediately rewarding precision and consistency among a highly charged fleet. These Games were not just about being the fastest, but also the smartest. Sailing afficionados were treated to high-performance programmes and close encounters with the sport's next generation of talent. The adrenaline continued to mount as Pearl Lattanzi, fresh off her All-Stars victory, strode onto the WASZP Games scene. Sweeping the day's races, she led the competition at the end of Day 1, setting a blistering pace for the rest of the competition. Both the WASZP All-Stars Invitational and the WASZP Games reinforced their status as major fixtures on the sailing calendar, combining high stakes with a unique convergence of talent and skill. As spectators around the globe revel in the thrill of the competition, they eagerly look forward to what the next racing days will unfurl.

title: Kiwi Sailor Among First-Timers in the Prestigious Pittwater to Coffs Harbour Yacht Race
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Kiwi Sailor Among First-Timers in the Prestigious Pittwater to Coffs Harbour Yacht Race
summary: New Zealand sailor Brian Petersen finds his place among the ambitious debutantes in the illustrious 40th Pittwater to Coffs Harbour Yacht Race.
body: There's an electrifying spark in the air on the Pacific coast, as the 40th Pittwater to Coffs Harbour Yacht Race prepares to unfurl its sails. Among the compelled competitors, New Zealand's Brian Petersen is ready to make his debut in his TP52, V5. Formerly an onlooker in the thrilling horizon-slicing event, this year will see the Kiwi sailor reposition himself at the heart of the action and the camaraderie of the Royal Prince Alfred Yacht Club's (RPAYC) annual coastal classic. Having experienced a calendar brimming over with sailing engagements in 2025, Petersen's decision to enter this high-profile race indicates his enduring enthusiasm for the sport and his engrained spirit of competition. And why wouldn't he be excited? With the promise of a pleasant 'slide up the coast', the charming satisfaction of finally docking his boat at Pittwater, and a crew comprising a blend of Kiwi and Aussie sailors, it's an adventure just waiting to happen! Following this race, Petersen reckons, his seafaring journey will navigate through other fascinating destinations. ‘The Brisbane Gladstone’, ‘Sydney Gold Coast’ and ‘Brisbane to Mackay’ form later checkpoints on Brian's route, before wrapping up at 'Sail Paradise' in Southport. Annie Stevenson, another entrant making a run at the Pittwater Coffs race for the first time, echoes Petersen's enthusiasm with her own twist. Marking her skipper debut, she'll sail double-handed on 'Employment Hero Alliance', a Dehler 30 One-Design, with co-skipper Peter Winter. A constant catalyser of sailing evolution, Stevenson brands this race as the perfect first offshore experience for double-handed sailing and an ideal gateway for novices to essentially experience offshore racing. This racing event serves as an equalising platform where small boats can win, and March's relatively tame conditions add to its appeal. Furthermore, as the duo prepares for an eventful season, the upcoming race's perfectly timed and wonderfully designed course becomes that much more significant. On the whole, the Pittwater to Coffs Harbour Yacht Race remains ever more a cherished highlight in the sailing community's calendar.

title: Complex Courts and Boating Contracts: A Tale of Navigating Legal Uncertainties in Cross-border Boat Sales
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Complex Courts and Boating Contracts: A Tale of Navigating Legal Uncertainties in Cross-border Boat Sales
summary: Exploring a case of cross-border boat transaction under Dutch law, this article delves into the complexities of civil litigation and contractual ambiguities.
body: Stepping into a skirmish of civil litigation, which stretched over eight long years, sheds brilliant light on the nature of legal complexities in international boat sales. The curtain lifts on a dispute between two German parties, embroiled over a boat sold under Dutch law, painting an illuminating picture of how a misclassification, insufficient correction on appeal and strict enforcement of limitation doctrine can become entwined.

The second episode saw a shift in perspective, from contract extinction to enforcement. The seller moved for contract performance. The action redefined the narrative, centering it around enforceability, rather than validity. The act of contract enforcement brought the statute of the limitation under Dutch law into the spotlight.

A critical focus was Article 3:317 BW, which requires a written communication wherein the creditor 'unequivocally' reserves their right to performance. According to Dutch case law, specifically that of the Hoge Raad, this communication ought to serve a sufficiently cautionary purpose and enable the debtor to identify the claim being pursued and protect their evidence.

In this convoluted legal dispute, a perfect storm of factors resulted in considerable confusion and litigation, underscoring the necessity for clarity in legal communication, careful risk allocation and mindful contractual language in international transactions involving the sale of boats.

title: The Gentle Power of Maldon’s Thames Barges
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: The Gentle Power of Maldon’s Thames Barges
summary: There’s something unmistakably cinematic about Maldon. The Essex town, poised on the edge of the River Blackwater, feels like it belongs on a leather-bound map or the pages of a travel journal from a more deliberate era. And moored proudly along its ancient quay are icons of Britain’s working-class maritime heritage—Thames sailing barges—graceful, red-sailed giants of the estuary, rich in grit, glory, and just a touc
body: Welcome to Hythe Quay, Maldon’s waterfront catwalk for the last of the barge fleet. Here, tradition hasn’t been preserved in aspic—it’s been burnished with care, rigged to sail, and given purpose again. Names like SB Centaur and SB Pudge sound like Bond villains but are, in fact, two of the most celebrated barges in the country, still cutting through water more than a century after they first launched.

Centaur, built in 1895, is an Edwardian workhorse with serious pedigree—she served through both world wars and now offers chartered cruises where you can hoist sail and sip coffee against the rustling hush of canvas overhead. Pudge, born in 1922, helped evacuate British troops from Dunkirk. Restored lovingly, she now draws admiration not just for her history, but for her enduring poise on the tide.

The charm of these vessels lies in their paradox: engineered for utility, now revered as floating sculpture. Yet they’re still very much alive. You’ll find riggers in oilskins adjusting lines, schoolchildren wide-eyed on deck tours, and weekend sailors playing out their Joseph Conrad fantasies on open water.

This is no theme park nostalgia. The Thames Sailing Barge Trust, based in Maldon, has kept these vessels running not for ceremony but for experience. Their programs train future crews, teach hands-on sailing techniques, and ensure that a new generation understands what it means to navigate with wind, tide, and instinct.

Come summer, Maldon’s barge match races are the stuff of sepia-toned adrenaline—imagine nearly 30 barges jockeying for position, their sails straining, their crews silent and focused, the wind catching and the estuary white with spray. It’s heritage, yes, but it’s also performance. Think vintage regatta meets Le Mans.

And while the barges themselves are rustic, the experience is far from basic. The town of Maldon offers all the modern comforts of a discerning weekend escape. Think riverside restaurants serving fresh oysters and crisp white wine, artisan bakeries on cobbled streets, and the quiet luxury of simply watching the tide roll in.

This maritime glamour isn’t flashy—it’s seasoned, honest, and quietly captivating. The barges moored at Hythe Quay don’t scream for your attention; they demand a moment of stillness, a step back, a deep breath.

So if your soul’s been frayed by city speed, if your calendar feels like a battleground and your inbox a storm, here’s your remedy: slip down to Maldon, take in the rigging, let the ropes creak and sails snap. Walk the quay, sign up for a day sail, toast the day with a pint at a dockside pub. The Thames barges don’t offer escape—they offer return. To craft. To quiet. To legacy.
It’s maritime style, distilled.

title: Dive into the Rush of the Waves: YC Costa Smeralda's Thrilling 2026 Season of High-Stakes Regattas and Historic Returns Awaits!
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Dive into the Rush of the Waves: YC Costa Smeralda's Thrilling 2026 Season of High-Stakes Regattas and Historic Returns Awaits!
summary: Embrace the exhilaration of top-tier regattas with YC Costa Smeralda's fantastic 2026 sailing season, bursting with prestigious events and artistic returns.
body: The year 2026 promises a storm surge of excitement for sailing aficionados. Yacht Club Costa Smeralda (YCCS) revealed its sports program in Milan to an audience of over 200 guests. Casually known as the Costa Smeralda, the deep blue waters of the Yacht Club have become a premier stage for world sailing, encompassing international projects and events that concentrate on the next wave of sailing talents.

YC Costa Smeralda's president, Princess Zahra Aga Khan, opened the proceedings, reminding us of the club's origins in 1967 under the leadership of her father, the Aga Khan IV. Zahra emphasized the YCCS's consistent representation as an international standard in sailing, honoring a path paved by shared values of innovation, excellence, sea respect, and promoting future talents.

Spring's program will usher in excitement with the Giorgio Armani Superyacht Regatta, scheduled for late May. This regatta will open the Mediterranean superyacht racing season, with several yachts and participants already expressing interest. The season will kick off in late April with the one-design Cape 31 class's debut in Porto Cervo, an event marked with anticipation and exhilaration.

The Sardinia Cup’s awaited return, on hiatus for 14 years, will occur from the end of May into early June. This event underscores team spirit and club affiliation, rejuvenating a sense of belonging preserved within every yacht club. All in all, the YCCS's 2026 season is set to make exciting waves in the world of sailing.

title: Discover the Refurbished and Luxurious 57m Feadship Yacht Solace Listed for Glorious Sailing
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover the Refurbished and Luxurious 57m Feadship Yacht Solace Listed for Glorious Sailing
summary: The refulgent and reimagined 57-metre Feadship motor yacht Solace is now on sale after an extensive refit.
body: The Feadship motor yacht Solace, a dazzling spectacle of maritime engineering, is currently listed for sale. Already renowned for her impeccable features, an extensive refurbishment between 2024 and 2025 added several exciting elements to her design. Renovations were performed at the reputable Pendennis Shipyard, maintaining Solace’s naval architecture by Feadship De Voogt. The broad-reaching changes incorporated a hull extension, increasing her length overall from 55.5 metres to 57 metres, a complete paint job, an upgraded HVAC system, and an all-encompassing mechanical refurbishment. The interior spaces were innovatively reimagined by Vickers Studio, exuding a fresh contemporary aesthetic. The refurbished Solace is presented in outstanding condition and is primed for adventurous navigation, including a possible three-year circumnavigation. The yacht's interior is bright and welcoming, enhanced by the broad windows allowing in abundant natural light. The main deck saloon flaunts two lounges and a bar, with a dining area right aft, providing a spacious area for social gatherings and delightful onboard living. Solace offers accommodation for 12 guests across five cabins, including a full-beam master suite with breathtaking ocean views and private study. Remaining cabins are located on the lower deck featuring three double cabins and a twin. The external spaces are equally versatile with a broad lounging area featuring a U-shaped sofa and alfresco dining around a table for up to 14 guests. Other delicacies include an open-air gym, sauna, beach club and a large swim platform. It also comes with an array of water toys. Capable of reaching a speed of 15.5 knots with a 5,400 nautical miles range at a cruising speed of 12.5 knots, Solace is deemed a highly capable platform for both private use and charter and is fully Polar Code compliant. On offer for €39,495,000, Solace, is aiming to grace the upcoming Palm Beach International Boat Show with her presence, offering prospective customers a firsthand look at her splendorous offerings.

title: Uncover the Authentic Culture and Laid-Back Luxury of Grenada and Carriacou with this Six-Day Superyacht Charter Itinerary
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Uncover the Authentic Culture and Laid-Back Luxury of Grenada and Carriacou with this Six-Day Superyacht Charter Itinerary
summary: Join us on a six-day superyacht journey, with an itinerary taking us far beyond typical Caribbean escapes, into the warmth and vibrancy of Grenada and Carriacou.
body: Venture with us on a six-day charter across the brilliant blue waters of Grenada and Carriacou. Far beyond the typical Caribbean retreat, this trip presents an enchanting mix of authentic island culture and the laid-back luxury of a superyacht. Experience vibrant markets, secluded waterfalls, exquisite beaches and immerse in the heartwarming Grenadian hospitality, transforming first-time visitors into lifelong supporters of these picturesque paradises.

The journey begins on Hog Island, a haven perfect for swimming, snorkelling, and unwinding. Savour a casual barbecue on the beach and mix with the locals at Prickly Bay’s marina restaurant for an authentic experience. As the night falls, head ashore to the West Indies Brewery to relish local beers and scrumptious food, topped off with live music and dancing.

Day three brings tranquillity with a yoga session at Laluna Resort or Yoga Harmony, garnished with a traditional Grenadian breakfast. Embrace the calmness of the day while sailing north to Carriacou, finding anchor in Tyrell Bay.

Day four is dedicated to island hopping around Carriacou. Enjoy a day starting at White Island moving to Saline Island, famous for its marine life, then to Sandy Island notable for its powder-soft white and pink sand.

On the fifth day, explore the rich heritage of Carriacou with visits to Windward Boat Building Yard, Ningo Well, and Windmill & Hospital Viewpoint. To complete the day, dine at Paradise Beach Club or the Slipway Restaurant.

Finally, disembark for a final on-island adventure enjoying Grenada’s lush nature and breathtaking waterfalls. A six-day charter itinerary - the epitome of luxury sailing, exploring the authentic cultural heartbeat of Grenada and Carriacou.

title: An Adventure Awaited: The Unstoppable Splendour of the Benetti Vision Superyacht, SUR LA MER
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: An Adventure Awaited: The Unstoppable Splendour of the Benetti Vision Superyacht, SUR LA MER
summary: SUR LA MER, a stunning example of Benetti's Vision Series, beautifully combines Italian shipbuilding heritage with the grandeur, comfort and functionality of a modern superyacht.
body: With its roots in the confident craftsmanship of Italian shipbuilding, the Benetti Vision Series' SUR LA MER is a sight for sore eyes. Historically celebrated for its grandeur, space-like volume, and cruising surety that could only come from a pedigree superyacht, now it is up for grabs. Crafted by Benetti, one of the industry's most respected names, SUR LA MER showcases a masterful design for both extended journeys and easy time at anchor alike.

A look at its interior reveals a refined, spacious, and inviting design. Its layout cleverly segregates common areas from the bid for privacy, facilitating a harmonious blend of social interaction and solitude. The main salon serves as the heartbeat, ushering in guests into formal and informal dining areas. The upper-deck lounge adds an extra layer of comfort, setting an idyllic scene for those delightfully mild evenings at sea.

Taking pride in its exterior design, SUR LA MER doesn’t compromise when it comes to offering luxurious outdoor living. Expansive deck areas are tailored for a gamut of experiences, from sunbathing to outdoor dining and relaxation. A carefully considered circulation system makes possible discreet crew operations, ensuring the utmost privacy while ensuring an impeccable onboard service.

Understandably, SUR LA MER's enduring design appeal, illustrious pedigree, and a layout attuned to owner comfort, make her a compelling acquisition for those on the hunt for immediate cruising capability in a vessel that promises long-term value. Should you choose to embark on this adventure, expect a light-filled interior refreshed with luminous wood, a main deck master stateroom complete with a private foredeck jacuzzi, and several magnificent double ensuite staterooms on the lower deck.

At its best, life on SUR LA MER incorporates everything from a massive sundeck with a Jacuzzi and a service bar to a large tender garage and toy storage. This luxury yacht that had its last refit in 2024 is competitively priced in US Dollars and waits for its next chapter.

title: Embrace the Unforeseen: An Epic Journey with the Unseen Purchase of a Windic SR40 Yacht
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Embrace the Unforeseen: An Epic Journey with the Unseen Purchase of a Windic SR40 Yacht
summary: Taking a leap of faith, a seasoned mariner purchases the Windy SR40, unseen and off-plan. Against all odds, the unseen risk pays off in an unexpected adventure.
body: With a rush of adrenaline, this daring maritime enthusiast took an unheard plunge. They put their unwavering faith in Windy, trading the familiar comfort of their Windy 34 Alizé for the unfamiliar confines of a Windy SR40. The decision, based on merely a 3D model, evoked scepticism among his seafaring comrades, who considered it madness to go off-plan and opt for the first yacht built.

Bracing themselves for the moment of truth, the adventurer embarked on a journey to visit Windy in Sweden. The spring morning sun rose, casting a golden glow on the day that would decide the fate of this audacious acquisition. Taking the first glance of the Windy SR40, concerns over its scale vanished, replaced by a sense of serenity. The boat was perfectly proportioned, merging practicality and performance seamlessly. Its walkaround design offered security and comfort, without compromising on expansive outdoor spaces.

True to their commitment, Windy and Merveille Nautique responded promisingly, addressing each concern with prompt and appropriate refinements. Collaboratively, they devised an innovative dropdown platform, complemented by an aesthetic blend of teak and stainless steel, for a versatile driving experience. Extra mooring cleats were installed and ways of maximising storage were explored.

By boldly stepping into the unknown, the brave seafarer introduces us to the thrilling potential of the Windy SR40. The yacht's enhanced practicality, combined with robust performance, unbeknown to many, is a testament to Windy's design prowess. This tale of unanticipated triumph proves that sometimes, the unseen and off-plan can lead to the most satisfying adventures.

title: EuroILCA Breaks New Ground With the Inauguration of Single-Gender Sailing Coaches Clinic
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: EuroILCA Breaks New Ground With the Inauguration of Single-Gender Sailing Coaches Clinic
summary: In a move that is set to advance gender equality in sailing, EuroILCA initiates its first-ever Women Sailing Coaches Clinic
body: EurILCA is poised to break new ground within the sailing world with its premiere Women Sailing Coaches Clinic. Slated for the 21st to the 22nd of November 2026 with an optional gathering and networking dinner on the twentieth, this incredible event marks an important stride for women in sailing. It's an exclusive opportunity for female sailing coaches to engage in life-changing hands-on experiences and vast knowledge-broadening encounters.

This two-day seminar, nestled within the historic city of Athens, Greece, is carefully crafted for women coaches who are actively involved in the ILCA sailing sphere. The experience promises potent blending of technical prowess, practical sessions on the water, and multiple avenues for personal and professional growth. It encompasses six carefully chosen thematic areas that include ILCA coaching methodologies and race analysis, a comprehensive look at racing rules and boat measurement, and insightful exploration of athlete psychology and physical conditioning.

EurILCA takes an extra step by committing to cover part of the costs of this dynamic journey, entailing accommodation and meals. The registration is unconditionally free, further reflecting EuroILCA’s commitment to fostering grassroots development of women in sailing. It’s not just about leveling the playing field, but more about empowering female coaches to remain steadfast and thrive in this largely male-dominated domain.

The establishment of the Women Sailing Coaches Clinic symbolizes a wave of change in the sailing world. It’s a momentous occasion that not only recognizes the often under-celebrated contribution of women coaches in sailing but more importantly, stands as a beacon of effectual gender asset in the sport. Sailing needs as many good coaches as it can get, and EurILCA is setting the compass pointing straight towards a future where gender is no longer the exception but just another element in the refined continuum of the sailing world.

title: Three Minutes After 600 Miles: Argo Edges Zoulou in Epic RORC Caribbean 600 Duel
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Argo Claims Multihull Line Honours After 600 Miles of MOD70 Warfare
summary: Argo Claims Multihull Line Honours in a Caribbean Classic After 600 miles of relentless trade-wind racing, two MOD70 trimarans arrived back in Antigua separated by barely a mile.
body: Jason Carroll’s MOD70 Argo (USA) claimed Multihull Line Honours in the RORC Caribbean 600, stopping the clock at 01 Day 12 Hours 01 Minutes 46 Seconds. Just over three minutes later, Jon Desmond’s Final Final – Zoulou crossed the line off Fort Charlotte, completing one of the closest high-speed offshore battles in the race’s history.
This was not a drag race. It was a moving chess match at 30 knots.

From the start off Antigua to the final beat home, the two MOD70s traded pressure lines, split around islands, and pushed each other into decisions that would decide the outcome by seconds — not miles.
Winning the Start, Controlling the North
Argo made the first statement at the gun, threading the needle between pin-end traffic and the cliffs near the Pillars of Hercules. Carroll described the moment clearly:
“We expected it to be crowded. We knew we’d be faster than most of the fleet and would have to make our way through.”
Argo crossed ahead by roughly a length — around 100 metres — a small advantage that translated into a narrow but meaningful lead at the first checkpoint.
At Green Island, Argo was ahead by 1 minute 24 seconds. At Barbuda, the gap stretched past eight minutes. By Nevis and Saba, it hovered around eleven.
But this edition of the Caribbean 600 was different.
Behind Nevis — typically a fast reaching leg — the boats found themselves gybing repeatedly down a narrow pressure lane. What is normally a high-speed express section became tactical and unstable.
“We probably did 20 gybes where normally we’d just reach straight to Saba,” Carroll said. “It became about finding pressure.”
Zoulou stayed within striking distance.
Zoulou Stays in the Hunt
For Jon Desmond, this was his first RORC Caribbean 600 aboard a MOD70. Chartering Zoulou for the event, he arrived with world-class inshore multihull pedigree — but offshore, this was new territory.
“Our goal was simple,” Desmond said. “Stay close to Argo and learn.”
And they did more than that.
At 30 knots, distance compresses quickly. Eleven minutes looks vast when the boat ahead is a speck on the horizon. Then one puff arrives, one hole opens, and the gap halves.
“You see them hit a hole and suddenly they’re very big again,” Desmond reflected.
The northern section became a sparring session. Offshore splits. Inshore covers. Pressure hunting around Saba and St. Maarten. The duel never broke.
The race remained alive.
The Guadeloupe Casino
The decisive swing came west of Guadeloupe — the notorious wind shadow that has undone many race leaders.
Argo entered with a solid lead and a routing plan favouring the inshore lane.
It was wrong.
Patchy breeze stalled Argo in the lee. Zoulou sailed slightly further offshore and found pressure first, surging past at speed.
“At one point they were almost parked and we were going fast,” Desmond said.
By Les Saintes, Zoulou led by more than ten minutes — their first real command of the race.
The psychological shift was enormous.
But Argo responded. Fast.
By Les Desirade, the gap was cut in half. By Barbuda on the second rounding, it was just over a minute.
Game on.
Redonda: Full Noise
From Barbuda to Redonda, both boats regularly touched 30–35 knots. Foils down. Big sails up. Spray hammering through the nets.
Desmond described it vividly:
“It was like driving across the country on a dirt road in the rain with your head out the window. Thirty knots apparent in your face. Wild.”
At Redonda, Zoulou still led by nearly three minutes.
Only 35 miles remained.
The Double Tack That Won the Race
The final beat to Antigua became a classic match-race tacking duel in 17–20 knots of breeze.
These are not casual tacks on a MOD70. Every crew member is involved. Loads are extreme. Timing matters.
Carroll had discussed a move in advance.
“We talked about doing two tacks in quick succession. Catch them off guard.”
The opportunity came. Argo tacked once, accelerated, then immediately tacked again while Zoulou was still stabilising from their cover manoeuvre.
The second tack created separation. Clear air. Momentum.
From there, Argo slowly edged ahead.
After nearly 600 miles of racing, the margin at the finish was just over three minutes.
Respect Between Rivals
Despite the intensity, both skippers were generous in praise.
Carroll acknowledged the scale of Zoulou’s performance:
“For it being their fourth or fifth day on a MOD70, that was really impressive.”
Desmond was equally direct:
“Argo is one of the best teams in the world. To be duking it out with them for the last couple hundred miles was special.”
It was not just a contest of speed. It was endurance, judgement and tactical nerve.
The Argo Crew
Argo’s winning lineup: Jason Carroll, Chad Corning, Alister Richardson, Brian Thompson, Charles Ogletree, James Dodd, Pete Cumming and Sam Goodchild.
Years together. Crisp manoeuvres. No panic at Guadeloupe. No mistakes in the final hour.
In offshore racing at this level, cohesion wins.
Why the RORC Caribbean 600 Delivers
The RORC Caribbean 600 remains one of the most compelling offshore races in the world. Eleven islands. Constant course changes. Reliable trade winds. No two legs alike.
Carroll summed it up:
“You’re on your toes the whole time. Every few hours you’re rounding an island or making a decision.”
For Desmond, it was simpler:
“I’ll always do this race again.”
After a duel like that, it’s hard not to.
Salt in the air. Foils humming. Three minutes after 600 miles.
That’s offshore racing done properly.

title: Bering Yachts Unleashes its Rebranded, Refined B88 Explorer Yacht: The Ultimate Sea Journey Beckons
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Bering Yachts Unleashes its Rebranded, Refined B88 Explorer Yacht: The Ultimate Sea Journey Beckons
summary: Turkish shipyard Bering Yachts takes a bold stride into the future with the launch of the second hull of its rebranded B88 explorer yacht.
body: Hailing from the distinguished Turkish shipyard, Bering Yachts has raised the precise balance of exploration and luxury to a whole new level with the launch of the second hull of its engineering marvel, B88 explorer yacht. Emanating deep-rooted elegance within its steel build, the all-newly rebranded B88 unfurls a lavish expanse of over 256 square metres of ingeniously utilised interior space. The yacht's primer accommodation, a magnificently portrayed full-beam master suite, graces a substantial portion of its 8.1-metre beam. Supplementary to this grandeur, the yacht also houses four lavish guest cabins and comprehensive crew quarters capable of accommodating a proficient team of five. Amid all its opulence, Bering’s B88 is a vessel ready for action, kitted out with twin Cummins QSM11 engines that generate a total power of 900hp and pack a fuel capacity of a whopping 39,000 litres. This empowers the yacht with an exceptional ability to traverse over 5,000 nautical miles at a leisurely cruising speed of 8.5 knots. The B88 leaves no stone unturned to facilitate memorable experiences at sea, offering expanded outdoor areas, perfectly suited for al fresco dining and entertaining. Alexei Mikhailov, the resourceful founder and CEO of Bering Yachts, expresses the team’s excitement on this milestone achievement, 'This boat is fully equipped for the adventure of a lifetime. Self-sufficient with everything needed for weeks of independent life at sea, it does not rely on shore infrastructure. We can scarcely wait to navigate her through her maiden sea trials and witness her remarkable performance.' Bering Yachts’ creative director, Kristina Güner, echoed this sentiment, praising the team's extraordinary effort and dedication in successfully turning this project into reality. 'We believe this to be one of the most potent explorer yachts under the 24-metre class. We've poured all our expertise into her design, striving for comfort, practicality, and sheer genius in every element, culminating in a standout yacht boasting numerous smart solutions that significantly enhance the life-at-sea experience.' This successful launch takes place hot on the heels of Bering Yachts’ initial triumph earlier this year – the delivery of the first unit from its 23.9-metre Bering 78 explorer yacht series, named Slow Ride.

title: Thrills and Spills at Lincoln Radio Sailing Club and Idyllic Racing Conditions Makeway for Signature Zenith Open at Burton SC
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Thrills and Spills at Lincoln Radio Sailing Club and Idyllic Racing Conditions Makeway for Signature Zenith Open at Burton SC
summary: Covering the captivating world of radio sailing, this piece bears witness to the enthralling 12th round of the I.O.M Winter Series at Lincoln Radio Sailing Club and the commencing of the Zenith Open at Burton Sailing Club.
body: The winter, when assumed to be a dormant season in sailing, sees a captivating form of the sport come alive at Lincoln Radio Sailing Club. Radio sailing, an engaging blend of advanced technology and sailing skills, proves to be a spectacular sight on offer. At the 12th round of the I.O.M Winter Series, the thrill was palpable as 18 skippers jostled for top positions in increasingly challenging breezy conditions. The day unfolded with intriguing tactical choices, an adrenaline-filled shift from A to B rig conditions and local battles that had the observers' attention riveted.

Both events share a common undercurrent— the unfiltered joy of sailing, crackling with competitive energy and camaraderie. Sweeping across different forms and settings, it serves as a testament to the passion of the sailing community.

title: Luxury Redefined: Heesen's 50m Superyacht Project Sophia Sets Sail
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Luxury Redefined: Heesen's 50m Superyacht Project Sophia Sets Sail
summary: Setting sail into the seas of decadence, Heesen's 50m superyacht, Project Sophia, embodies a dynamic marvel of naval excellence.
body: There's something magical brewing in the waters. Heesen Superyachts, a Netherlands-based yacht maker, merges the quintessential visual aesthetics with state-of-the-art technology to redefine the yachting experience in its latest offering, Project Sophia. This superyacht perfectly encapsulates Heesen's history of expertise and technological excellence by offering features that directly translate into reduced fuel consumption and a smoother, quieter experience at sea. This 50-meter vessel hit the water on 14th March 2026, perfectly adhering to the delivery schedule of June 2026. Built with an aluminium hull, this is the fourth product of Heesen's 50-meter class series, pushing innovation further with enhanced hull efficiency and reduced transom depth. The efficiency of this marine marvel doesn't stop here, Project Sophia has the distinction of being the first yacht of its kind under 500GT to comply with IMO Tier-III regulations. Frank Laupman, a seasoned architect known for his unique styles, designed Project Sophia's remarkable exterior, boasting optimised, low-drag hull design and a streamlined, sporty profile. Inside, five luxurious cabins designed by Cristiano Gatto, offer ultra-modern comforts accompanied by a warm color palette giving it a homely touch. The notable features that make Project Sophia truly remarkable include a suave dining area on the bridge deck terrace and sundeck, a quaint pool housed on the main deck aft and a generous seating arrangement with loose furniture for a great outdoorsy, airy feel. Added to it are the custom elevated aft deck and the lofty tender garage that create spaces with multifunctionality and elegance. With its MTU 16V 4000 M65L engines, Project Sophia offers an impressive top speed of 23 knots and a seemingly endless range of 3100 nautical miles at 11 knots, making the voyages even more tranquil and enjoyable. Drawing upon the rich lineage of aquatic luxury and technological excellence, Heesen's Project Sophia sets new milestones, offering an elegant blend of performance, style, and sustainability in luxury yacht building.

title: 2026 WWT 5-Star Major Windsurf World Cup heads for Gran Canaria, marking an evolution in windsurfing competition
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: 2026 WWT 5-Star Major Windsurf World Cup heads for Gran Canaria, marking an evolution in windsurfing competition
summary: The Gran Canaria GLORIA Windsurf World Cup has been confirmed as a 2026 WWT 5-Star Major event, ushering in a new age of high-performance competition.
body: The announcement making Gran Canaria GLORIA Windsurf World Cup an adorned destination in the 2026 WWT 5-Star Major carousel of events is indeed a watershed moment in the world of windsurfing. Among the international windsurfing community, Gran Canaria is the undisputed leader in providing extreme big-air challenges, setting the benchmark high for performance wave and jumping competition. In 2026, this accolade lifts it to the zenith of the World Wave Tour 5-Star Pyramid.

The event hosted in Pozo Izquierdo, an area recognized universally for its formidable winds, and world-class waves, serves as the ultimate trial by fire for windsurfing professionals. Windsurfing legend and event organizer, Bjorn Dunkerbeck noted the importance of such strong partnerships in enhancing commercial opportunities for these iconic events, and in forging a path to drive the sport into the future.

A critical aspect of the 2026 season is the introduction of a new commercial model. Designed to bolster the financial stability of professional windsurfing events, this model is geared to bring long-term value to athletes, organizers, brands, and partners. This includes a structured, co-produced global live broadcast, guaranteeing 60% ad revenue to athletes, and incorporating the use of the Windsurf Ai-supported media distribution. This synergizes event economics with modern sports media, providing a scalable commercial framework crucial for the evolution of the sport.

Interestingly, this new approach comes on the back of a successful 2025 season, where live broadcast audiences had a striking increment across key events, indicative of windsurfing’s growing popularity and engagement.

So, mark the dates, from the 4th to 12th of July 2026, the windsurfing world will descend upon Pozo Izquierdo, in Gran Canaria, for an event filled with masterful displays of finesse, agility, and sheer power on the waves, cementing its status as a WWT 5-Star Major Event with a liberating 100% world ranking points.

title: New Commodore at the Helm of Royal Southampton Yacht Club with an Eco-Friendly Vision
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: New Commodore at the Helm of Royal Southampton Yacht Club with an Eco-Friendly Vision
summary: The Royal Southampton Yacht Club welcomes Karen Baker as their new Commodore. An accomplished leader, Karen carries an environmental mission to the esteemed yachting club.
body: The prestigious and historical institution of sailing, the Royal Southampton Yacht Club (RSYC), is embracing new leadership and inviting a breath of fresh air. Gone are the cliche expectations of rigidity and tradition alone. Here to stay is an era of transformation under the guidance of the newly appointed Commodore, Karen Baker, only the third woman to hold such a distinguished position in the club's 150-year history. Baker, coming from a strong background in leadership, plans to lead this venerable institution with a strategic vision and a firm hand. A veteran yachtsman and an accomplished senior leader with a background in the National Health Service, Baker brings a wealth of experience to the table. Her unique blend of skills promises to inject vitality, governance expertise, and strategic direction into the club's trajectory. Committed to preserving and enhancing the RSYC's proud traditions, Baker expresses a strong ambition to introduce fresh ideas whilst bolstering the overall member experience. Key to her strategy is engagement - expanding the club's membership and encouraging participation in a variety of sailing and water-based activities, thereby, ensuring RSYC's vibrancy, relevance, and longevity within the sailing community. Importantly, her vision also extends to the ecological responsibility of the esteemed club. With plans to improve the 'green footprint,' Baker aims to project a commitment to the environment, acknowledging the unique position of RSYC being located in an area of outstanding natural beauty. Under her environmental initiative, thousands of saplings have been planted, river clean-up operations are in progress, and exploration of solar energy for sustainable water taxi services is underway. The aim? An environmentally aware club that takes pride in its surroundings and its role in preserving them. As the club prepares for this new era under Baker's leadership, optimism and excitement sail on the horizon. The RSYC welcomes prospective members to join them on this exciting journey, with an open invitation extended for the upcoming Open Day on Monday, 6th April 2026.

title: MA Financial Group Strengthens Its Boating Service Offering with the Acquisition of Gold Coast City Marina & Shipyard
author: Old Sea Dogs
