summary: MA Financial Group is set to augment its existing portfolio of d'Albora marinas with the acquisition of Gold Coast City Marina & Shipyard in Queensland, Australia.
body: In an exhilarating development for the maritime sector, MA Financial Group has contracted to acquire the prime Gold Coast City Marina & Shipyard. Situated in the boating hub of Coomera, Queensland, this acquisition journey entails a significant outreach to the portfolio of d'Albora marinas owned by the company.

This move specifically targets strengthening the extensive service offering that the MA Financial Group extends to the passionate boat owners who populate the East Coast of Australia, including yachts, motorboats, and superyachts. Given the strategic location and the proven reputation Gold Coast City Marina & Shipyard holds, it only bolsters the potential for providing unparalleled maritime experiences.

MA Financial Group's pivotal acquisition not only underscores its growth strategy but, more fundamentally, reflects its ambitious dedication to enhancing the boating journey for maritime enthusiasts across Australia's East Coast. This bold move reaffirms the importance of innovation and ambition in the continuously evolving boating industry.

title: Experience Unrivalled Comfort at Sea with the Majestic Heesen Superyacht Laurentia, Now for Sale
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Experience Unrivalled Comfort at Sea with the Majestic Heesen Superyacht Laurentia, Now for Sale
summary: The exhilarating world of luxury yachting welcomes a fresh entrant–the 55m Heesen superyacht Laurentia, now listed for sale.
body: Ahoy, sea lovers! The charming lure of the ocean is now more irresistible with the luxurious 55-meter Heesen motor yacht Laurentia making its way to the market. Built in 2017 under the stalwart mastery of Heesen Yachts, Laurentia's alluring appeal comes as no surprise. A finalist at the World Superyacht Awards in 2018, this dutch marvel showcases a commercially registered vessel with an exceptional charter pedigree.

Stepping inside Laurentia, passengers are greeted by a bright, contemporary haven designed by Radyca. This luxurious motor yacht focuses on delivering an immersive indoor-outdoor experience, courtesy of sliding glass doors and floor-to-ceiling windows. A wall of mirrors adorns its interiors, further amplifying the illusion of a larger space.

What makes Laurentia stand out from other superyachts is its impressive accommodation capacity. The yacht comfortably houses up to 12 guests across six splendid cabins, including a full-beam owner's suite situated forward on the main deck. This suite boasts a private office, a plush walk-in closet, and an en suite bathroom, offering occupants a superior level of privacy and comfort. Additional luxury suites include a full-beam VIP suite, two double cabins, and two twins equipped with extra Pullman berths.

Qed swiftly onto outdoor fun, guests can lounge on the U-shaped lounge area on the main deck. In the delightful twilight, this area magically transforms into an open-air cinema flaunting a sizeable retractable screen. The sundeck, at the yacht's top level, serves as an exclusive social hub with a hot tub, sunbathing pads, and a dining area.
The yacht, currently docked in Palm Beach, FL, USA, is available for purchase at €45,000,000. The beckoning call of the sea and this embodiment of nautical elegance–Laurentia–await their new owner.

title: Crowning Achievement: Northampton Sailing Club Soars to Victory as RYA’s 2026 Active Club of the Year
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Crowning Achievement: Northampton Sailing Club Soars to Victory as RYA’s 2026 Active Club of the Year
summary: Northampton Sailing Club, a welcoming community situated at Pitsford Reservoir, has been distinguished as the Royal Yachting Association's (RYA) Active Club of the Year 2026.
body: Nestled on the serene shores of Pitsford Reservoir, Northampton Sailing Club proudly hoists its victory flag, earning the prestigious title of RYA's Active Club of the Year 2026. Furthermore, the club was a strong contender in the Young Person's Award 2026, a testament to its commitment to foster young talent.

As a beacon of inclusivity, Northampton Sailing Club extends a warm welcome to sailors, windsurfers, wingfoilers and paddleboarders of all calibres. In an era where many clubs face dwindling memberships, Northampton's dynamic membership has seen an exhilarating surge, doubling in recent years thanks to a concerted drive to entice more sailors to embrace the thrill of the water.

Emphasizing a cooperative spirit, the seasoned sailors of Northampton Sailing Club volunteered to offer guidance and tutelage, creating stepping stones for those seeking to ace their RYA Level 1 sailing course or join the Sunday racing. The eco-system of giving back fosters harmony amongst members while augmenting the thrill of sailing.

With a focus on integrating different age groups, winter training brought together the Pirates (8-16 year-olds), the Northampton Race Group youth team, and adults. Meanwhile, members interested in picking up windsurfing or rekindling a past passion found support in six members of the windsurf club, who've enlightened a diverse age group of wind enthusiasts.

In nurturing promising young talent, Northampton has enabled a thriving Pirates club with 65 eager 8-16 year-olds learning to sail or windsurf. The club earned the coveted RYA Pathway Club status and excitedly set up the Northampton Race Group team to partake in racing events. The club's commitment to fostering growth and inclusivity amongst its members cements its position within the local sailing community, growing from a club set for collapse to one of the region's largest in terms of membership and participation.
Northampton Sailing Club stands today as a shining testament to the power of community, philanthropy, and an undying love for sailing, setting sail towards an even brighter future.

title: Where Sailors go when they need to relax
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: The Old Sea Dogs Global Club Directory
summary: At OldSeaDogs.com, we believe every sailor is part of a bigger story — one that’s written in salt spray, wind shifts, and club burgee traditions. Whether you’re crossing oceans, dodging buoys in a frostbite series, or tying up for a pint after a Wednesday evening race, it’s the clubs that anchor us.
body: That's why we’ve built the definitive Sailing Clubs Directory — a hand-picked global collection of the finest yacht and sailing clubs from across the seven seas. From Cowes to Cascais, San Diego to Saint-Tropez, each club on our list brings together heritage, hospitality, and serious time on the water.
Here’s a closer look at some of the legends on the list.

Home to Cowes Week, the Admiral’s Cup, and some of the oldest clubs in the world, the UK section reads like a who's who of British yachting royalty. The Royal Yacht Squadron (RYS) in Cowes is the apex — 200 years of prestige and still firing the starting cannon for the world’s most competitive fleets.

Alongside it, the Royal Ocean Racing Club (RORC) powers global offshore competition, while Island Sailing Club, Warsash SC, Itchenor SC, and Royal Lymington YC keep the Solent scene vibrant year-round. These aren’t just clubs — they’re institutions, each with their own bar tales, regatta lore, and weathered locals who’ve seen it all.

The Société Nautique de Saint-Tropez (SNST) hosts one of Europe’s most glamorous regattas, Les Voiles de Saint-Tropez. Wooden classics, maxi racers, and champagne moments line the quay, but don’t let the glitz fool you — the competition is fierce, and the club is a keystone of Mediterranean sailing culture.

Northern Italy’s Yacht Club Como offers a more relaxed freshwater flavor, but it’s no less passionate. Set against the mountainous backdrop of Lake Como, it’s a haven for keelboats, dinghies, and espresso-fueled sailors who take their racing seriously — just not without lunch.

The Yacht Club of Greece (also known as the Nautical Club of Greece) is anchored in Athens, with views across the Saronic Gulf. It’s the pinnacle of Hellenic sailing culture — offering a mix of history, modern racing, and a membership that includes Olympians and offshore veterans alike.

No list would be complete without the Royal Cork Yacht Club (RCYC) — officially the oldest yacht club in the world, founded in 1720. Based in Crosshaven, County Cork, RCYC pairs historic prestige with cutting-edge competition, from youth programs to offshore challenges in the Celtic Sea.

Portugal’s Clube Naval de Cascais (CNC) sits just west of Lisbon, where the Tagus meets the Atlantic. It’s a strategic training ground for Olympic hopefuls and a wind-blasted paradise for sailors who like it breezy and brisk.

In Spain, Real Club Náutico de Barcelona (RCNB) and Club Náutico Santa Pola balance cosmopolitan flair with strong racing fleets. Barcelona plays host to global events (including the America’s Cup), while Santa Pola is the sailor’s sailor club — authentic, active, and always close to the water.

The Royal Swedish Yacht Club (KSSS) is among the most respected clubs in the world. With a base near Stockholm and a calendar full of serious racing and youth training, KSSS blends Scandinavian design sensibility with no-nonsense seamanship.

Yacht Club de Monaco is the crown jewel of the Med’s jet-set sailing scene. Designed by Norman Foster and backed by Prince Albert II, the club’s marina, regattas, and social events place it at the apex of luxury and performance yachting.

Royal Cape Yacht Club in Cape Town is a beacon of offshore excellence. Sitting at the foot of Table Mountain, it’s a launchpad for transatlantic challenges and a home base for the Cape to Rio Race. If you want to feel the pulse of Southern Ocean sailors, this is your stop.

Royal Hong Kong Yacht Club (RHKYC) offers high-end facilities and storied tradition in the heart of Victoria Harbour. With one-design and offshore fleets, plus the legendary China Sea Race, RHKYC is where serious sailors and social yachtsmen mingle.
Also noted is Sanya Serenity Marina in China, a stopover for round-the-world events and a growing hub of Asian ocean racing.

The Royal Canadian Yacht Club (RCYC), based in Toronto, combines lakeside beauty with deep racing credentials. From youth dinghies to keelboats on Lake Ontario, RCYC keeps Canadian sailing strong and stylish.

The U.S. fleet on our list covers both coasts and every flavor of American sailing. From Balboa Yacht Club in California to Edgartown Yacht Club in Martha’s Vineyard, from Golden Gate YC (home of America’s Cup history) to New York YC (birthplace of the Cup), it’s a powerhouse lineup.
Chicago YC, San Diego YC, Indian Harbor YC, and St. Francis YC round out the roster with serious regattas and waterfront swagger.

Royal Sydney Yacht Squadron (RSYS) and Royal New Zealand Yacht Squadron (RNZYS) are leaders not just down under, but worldwide. From the America’s Cup to the Sydney–Hobart and beyond, these clubs define excellence in racing, training, and seamanship.

Whether you're looking to raft up in Cowes, sip champagne in Monaco, or plot a Fastnet campaign from Cork, there's a club on the list that speaks your language. The Old Sea Dogs Club Directory is more than a list — it’s a sailor’s passport to the world.

title: Emirates Team NZ Offers First Look at Reimagined AC75, Unveiling their Sailing Strategy
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Emirates Team NZ Offers First Look at Reimagined AC75, Unveiling their Sailing Strategy
summary: AC75, a revamped sailing vessel by Emirates Team NZ, emerges more than 500 days after its last appearance in Barcelona at the 37th America's Cup.
body: Emirates Team New Zealand had gone silent for a significant hiatus, more than 500 days to be exact, following their participation in the 37th America's Cup in Barcelona. Sailors and enthusiasts alike were finally delighted as the sound of the sea was broken with the splashing of the Team's reimagined sailing vessel, the AC75, setting off on its maiden voyage in Auckland.

The revamped AC75 emerged resplendent with a new look and feel that promises to elevate future races. The revelation was a first peek into the innovative deck design, developed for a leaner crew of five sailors and one beholder. The interesting part is the strategic reduction in crew fox-holes from four to three, rousing curiosity about the Team's revamped strategy.

The unveiling was also an occasion for the Team to put the AC75 through a series of dockside checks before towing it to the eastern side of Auckland's scenic Browns Island. This is the 'Paddock,' the Team's routine training field, where they can anticipate the AC75's performance in mixed weather conditions, with both clear and overcast skies, and moderate easterly winds.

While the upcoming races await in apprehension, the reimagined AC75 signals a glorious return for the Emirates Team NZ, inspiring others to innovate and constantly raise the bar in the thrilling world of boat racing.

title: Sunreef Yachts' Ambitious Billion-Euro Target Amidst Middle East Disruptions: An Exclusive Insight
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Sunreef Yachts' Ambitious Billion-Euro Target Amidst Middle East Disruptions: An Exclusive Insight
summary: Unveiling Sunreef Yachts' audacious growth plan and the strategies leading to a revenue boost amidst Middle East disruptions.
body: Sunreef Yachts' founder and CEO, Francis Lapp, presents the yard's audacious billion-euro growth plan. Amidst navigational uncertainties in the Middle East, the firm plots a new course aimed at breaking through previous limitations. With the introduction of an innovative sales strategy, Sunreef has seen a 10 per cent upsurge in its yearly revenue. Despite production disruptions stemming from the Middle East, the company has displayed an incredible ability to adapt and innovate.

Meanwhile, another insightful discussion centers around marina acquisitions. BOATPro assembles an elite roundtable featuring Dean Smith, Chief Commercial Officer at D-Marin, and others. They delve into the present business landscape of marinas, the hurdles this sector faces, and the potential in revitalizing defunct properties into advanced marina infrastructure. This discourse highlights not only the challenges but the tremendous opportunities that lie in the transformation of outdated harbors into cutting-edge marine facilities.

title: New Era In Oceanic Racing Trimarans Erupts As Gitana 18 Takes Its First Successful Sail
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: New Era In Oceanic Racing Trimarans Erupts As Gitana 18 Takes Its First Successful Sail
summary: Offshore racing trimaran, Gitana 18, has successfully completed her maiden sail marking a significant stride in her evolution.
body: An exciting chapter unfolded for maritime innovation as the revolutionary 32m Maxi Edmond de Rothschild offshore racing trimaran Gitana 18 makes a successful first sail. This triumphant sail, which followed her initial launch, sets the stage for a promising next phase in the development of this unprecedented vessel. The trimaran was first introduced to the world in early December 2025 in the craftsmen's shed in Lorient, Brittany. She was unveiled in all her splendour for the first time on 14 February 2026, and has since been the captivating subject of the technical team's tireless efforts to perfect the mechanical systems, onboard hydraulics, and electronics.

What sets Gitana 18 apart from all its predecessors is its capability to transit from hybrid mode to full-fledged flight. Standing at the vanguard of next-generation, high-performance, oceanic trimarans, Gitana 18 further enhances her performance with a wide spectrum of adjustable elements. Detailed characteristics include a 23-metre beam, a nine square metre cockpit floor, a living area of 4.8m2 and an aerodynamic surface of 73m2. A noteworthy characteristic is her retractable Y-shaped foils, starkly reminiscent of the flying monohulls of the America's Cup. They are the foundation of an optimised flight for all points of sail. One would also notice revolutionary rudders, a redesigned central daggerboard on the central hull, and a reimagined rig with adjustable spreaders enabling the mast to bend and modify mainsail power — a first on the world stage for trimarans of this scale.

Simulator prognostics foretell that Gitana 18 could out-speed its precursor, Gitana 17, by a thrilling 10 to 15 per cent. 'Gitana 18' is her christened name, while its racing name is 'Maxi Edmond de Rothschild.' This maiden sail marks a significant milestone that testifies to the hard work and ambitious vision of the dedicated team. A palpable sense of expectation now surrounds this innovative vessel, with maritime enthusiasts keen to see her in full flight, realising her immense potential.

title: Experience the Doorway to Luxury: The Impressive 49m Compass Rose Motor Yacht Listed for Sale
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Experience the Doorway to Luxury: The Impressive 49m Compass Rose Motor Yacht Listed for Sale
summary: The meticulously crafted 48.7-metre Compass Rose, a motor yacht by C. & G. Boatworks, surfaces in the market, offering a unique opportunity for global cruising enthusiasts.
body: The realm of elite yachting is being swept by yet another wave of luxury. The aesthetically compelling Compass Rose, a 48.7-metre motor yacht by C. & G. Boatworks, has been put up for sale. Thanks to Alex Rogers of Northrop & Johnson, the admirers of fine seafaring vessels now have a chance to acquire this paragon of beauty and performance. Delivered in 2011 and subsequently refitted in 2015, the Compass Rose has proved its mettle in traversing the magnificent and often challenging seascape. Conceived as an aluminium long-range displacement yacht, the Compass Rose caters to owners desiring a vessel that is both a captivating home away from home and a vehicle capable of steady, global cruising. A brainchild of masterminds at D. Marine Design, this yacht boasts a wide silhouette contributing to an imposing 621GT. This impressive figure is on par with larger explorer yachts, thereby offering facilities and space often desired by the modern sailor. The asking price for Compass Rose is an imposing $25,950,000. But what does one get for this sum? Beneath her sumptuous exterior lies generously spacious and comfortable living areas, thanks to her 12-metre beam. The rich, dark woods used in the main saloon are beautifully complemented by contrasting pale textiles. The main lounge is expansive, designed for both relaxation and entertainment. A formal dining area and a full-service bar are added draws, making the yacht an ideal space for socialising, be it casual get-togethers or formal meet-ups. Lastly, the practical and commodious galley comes with a sit-up breakfast bar, ensuring culinary journeys are as thrilling as nautical ones.

title: Italian Shipyard Wally Redefines the Boating Experience with its Compact yet Futuristic Wallytender48
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Italian Shipyard Wally Redefines the Boating Experience with its Compact yet Futuristic Wallytender48
summary: Italian shipyard Wally has embarked on a new sea venture with its compact, 14.5m Wallytender48 weekender, a versatile boat that boasts powerful performance and an innovative design.
body: The launch of the wallypower118, or Galeocerdo, established Wally as a pioneer in the yachting world, thanks to its futuristic and unique design. Decades later, Wally continues to embody a daring, innovative spirit, most recently evident in the launch of the wallytender48. This compact, versatile dayboat is a testament to Wally's philosophy, combining cutting-edge technology, seamless design, and practical functionality for a closer proximity to the sea.

Easily boarded via a retractable passerelle, the wallytender48 continues to impress with the excellent utilisation of space. Its 4.4-meter beam is cleverly expanded at anchor by the fold-down bulwarks. A highlight is the swim platform’s ability to transform into a spacious floating terrace, making it the ideal social hub. Be it as a superyacht tender or a standalone dayboat, the wallytender48 encourages barefoot living, easy swims and endless oceanic pleasures.

Wowing furthermore with its smart engineering, the wallytender48 hosts a concealed anchoring system, maintaining the yacht's clean, sculptural profile. Performance, true to Wally's spirit, remains crucial. The twin Volvo Penta IPS 650 engines offer a top speed of 38 knots and a cruising range of 300 nautical miles at a steady 32 knots. The deep-V hull ensures stability at speed, while joystick controls allow intuitive manoeuvring. Clearly, with the Wallytender48, the future of sea outings is here.

title: A Season of Surprises: Tom Dolan's Stirring Start and the Emergence of International Talents in Offshore Racing
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A Season of Surprises: Tom Dolan's Stirring Start and the Emergence of International Talents in Offshore Racing
summary: The irrepressible Tom Dolan starts the 2026 Figaro season with an electrifying performance, while a wave of international skippers breaks onto the scene, eager to upset the sport's established norms.
body: In Concarneau, France, a season of sailing began that promised as much charm as it did challenge. This tale begins with Kingspan skipper Tom Dolan jumping headlong into the opening race of the 2026 Figaro season, despite having to withdraw from the previous year's Figaro. Displaying a mastery over the demanding mix of conditions, Dolan's performance was an impressive cocktail of skill, poise, and consistency, which saw him sail into a top-ten finish.

During the first overnight leg, Dolan tackled an unexpected speed issue. Only later, at sunrise, did Dolan discover a plastic block on the keel that caused the slowdown. Despite these minor setbacks, Dolan was able to maintain his standing and strategic edge. Brimming with joy to be back on the circuit and pleased with his performance, he now looks ahead to the next calendar event — the Trophée Banque Populaire Grand Ouest.

In related news, an undercurrent of change is sweeping across the offshore racing landscape. The 2026 La Solitaire du Figaro Paprec is poised to welcome a rising tide of international skippers who are challenging the long-standing dominance of the French. The conviction of these English-speaking skippers to overcome the odds and establish a place on the world's most demanding platform for solo sailors, is rippling through the sport. Among such warriors, Tom Dolan stands out; a beacon of hope that inspires other international talents and disrupts traditional stereotypes in offshore racing.

title: Boero Yacht Coatings Joins Forces with Ferrari Hypersail to Revamp High-Performance Sailing Through Research and Innovation
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Boero Yacht Coatings Joins Forces with Ferrari Hypersail to Revamp High-Performance Sailing Through Research and Innovation
summary: Boero Yacht Coatings announces a partnership with Ferrari Hypersail, a research platform dedicated to outsizing high-performance sailing capabilities.
body: The sailing world is set for a shake-up, as two titans in their respective fields, Boero Yacht Coatings and Ferrari Hypersail, have recently announced a ground-breaking collaboration.

The partnership was unveiled at an institutional event in Maranello, and its aim is anything but mundane. These companies, glowing beacons of Italian excellence on the global stage, are uniting their efforts in an audacious pledge to break the barriers of high-performance sailing. Both Boero and Ferrari are famed for their persistent pursuit of excellence, and this project embodies their shared ethos of innovation, meticulous due diligence, and ceaseless research.

Their common vision of performance hinges on method, discipline, and the courage to challenge established practices. In their world-view, every choice must be nuanced, every detail scrutinised, and each outcome becomes the stepping stone for the next evolution phase.

The partners bring together complementary industrial domains, aiming to generate value miles beyond a single race. It's this convergence of ambition and method that marks the setting sail for a new development phase focused on continuous research and shared expertise. Together, Boero Yacht Coatings and Ferrari Hypersail are ready to redefine the limits of sailing.

title: Dubai's Premier Boating Event Pushed to November 2026 for Alignment with Prime Boating Season
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Dubai's Premier Boating Event Pushed to November 2026 for Alignment with Prime Boating Season
summary: Permanently rescheduled, the Dubai International Boat Show now gears up to sail in November 2026, to better align with the Middle East's peak boating season.
body: The seafaring horizon has a new date to look forward to as the Dubai International Boat Show unfurls its sails for a permanent shift in schedule. Now set to take place from 25 to 29 November 2026 at the opulent Dubai Harbour, the illustrious event will no longer berth in April.

The main objective behind this repositioning is to align the coveted meeting of maritime minds with the Middle East's prime boating season. This strategic move is anticipated to create thriving market conditions, boosting launches, sales and fostering international involvement.

The not-to-be-missed collection of marine mavens will now take place a week after METSTRADE (17 to 19 November) and a week before the anticipated Abu Dhabi Boat Show, projected to run from 19th to 22nd November 2026.

In a bid to keep yacht enthusiasts in the loop with the latest developments, news, insights, and market analyses, The Superyacht Group is offering a weekly sign-up for SuperyachtNewsweek. As part of the community, access to the superyacht industry’s most comprehensive and longstanding archive of crucial business information, including a real-time superyacht fleet database, is offered at a nominal rate of £10 per month.

The move proves beneficial not just for the individual attendees but for the prosperity of the maritime industry as a whole. Boating aficionados, make a note of the new date; the Dubai International Boat Show promises an experience that's worth waiting for.

title: Edge Sailing Team Set to Ride the Waves at the Pallas Capital Gold Cup: A New Journey Begins
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Edge Sailing Team Set to Ride the Waves at the Pallas Capital Gold Cup: A New Journey Begins
summary: John Bacon's Edge is the latest entrant for the fast-growing fleet of the Pallas Capital Gold Cup, promising high adrenaline adventure.
body: Setting a thrilling stage, John Bacon's Edge has arrived in Australia to become part of the emerging Pallas Capital Gold Cup fleet. The Dunning 44, in her adventurous journey, brings with it a skilled crew which includes several top-flight sailors from previous TP52 programs, promising intense competition among the Super40 ensemble.

Katie Spithill, who previously helmed the Hooligan program at the final event of the LGT Wealth Management Australia Cup last season, has joined Bacon's team as a strategist. Keen to get started, she mentioned that the boat was constructed locally at McConaghy's in Mona Vale before setting sail for the United States.

In an ebullient statement, she commented on the boat's return to its birthplace following Bacon's overseas regatta expedition. She also highlighted her curiosity and anticipation to understand the boat better and commended the continued growth of the Pallas Capital Gold Cup.

The yacht, Edge, is a specialised Dunning 44, constructed by the renowned McConaghy Yachts in 2020 for a US owner. Bacon acquired the boat in 2022, with Edge's maiden event being the New York Yacht Club Race Week during the same year. Now residing in Australia, the yacht is all set to showcase its prowess on home waters leading up to the Pallas Capital Gold Cup.

The team's tactician, Darren 'Twirler' Jones, remarked the boat's freshness to the Australian circuit and hinted at an exciting learning curve owing to some modifications made since its last race. He believes preparation has gone well but admitted they're entering uncharted waters. Jones concluded by stating that 'time will tell' regarding the yacht's performance at the cup. The Edge certainly looks sharp and ready to cut through the waves and expectations at the Pallas Capital Gold Cup.

title: Unveiling A New Era: Sunseeker’s Milestone of First 40-metre Post Takeover
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unveiling A New Era: Sunseeker’s Milestone of First 40-metre Post Takeover
summary: Heralding a new phase in superyacht manufacturing, Sunseeker's lauded Osprey Quay facility marks the construction of its first 40-metre superyacht following a crucial takeover.
body: Heralding a new era in the competitive world of luxury yacht manufacturing, esteemed brand Sunseeker is set to charter a fresh course. Following its acquisition by a consortium led by KCP Holdings and Lionheart Capital, the ship-building giant is marking a significant milestone by constructing its first 40-metre superyacht.

The prestigious production is taking place at Sunseeker's acclaimed facility in Osprey Quay, Dorset. The crafting of this 134 Superyacht signifies Sunseeker's triumphant return to the 40-metre-plus market, a realm it has sidestepped in recent years. The venture is helmed by new leadership in the form of CEO Andrés Rubio, a seasoned stalwart with an admirable record in commercial leadership and business transformation.

Under the prudent new ownership and committed leadership team, the consortium is keen on investing in Sunseeker's brand, operations, products, customer experience, and people with the ambitious goal of establishing it as the 'best producer of yachts in the world.'

Bringing to life this vision, Sunseeker is already on its path to breaking its 40-metre market hiatus. Indicative of its commitment to growth and innovation, the company has revamped the 27,000 sq ft facilities at Osprey Quay to ensure they can sustain the scale and expectations of the evolving market. Refurbishment ensures enhanced infrastructure, optimal capability, and efficient workflow to cater to the newfound interest in this segment.

The first of the 134 Superyachts symbolises this bold new direction. This sizable superyacht marks the first of its kind rising from Sunseeker's lofts after half a decade, embodying the company's new route and marking a promising path toward future transformation and development.

The maiden 134 Superyacht is slated to undergo testing in April 2027 before gracing the West Coast of the US as the proud possession of a repeat Sunseeker patron. As this venture unfolds with buoyant expectation, the shipbuilding maestro will amalgamate creativity, intuition, and skill to bring forth unmatched design, performance, and on-board experience in the modern superyacht industry.

title: Titans of the Sea: Top GL52 Teams Ready for Clash at the 2026 Southern Series
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Titans of the Sea: Top GL52 Teams Ready for Clash at the 2026 Southern Series
summary: The ultra-competitive world of the GL52 fleet turns its eyes towards Pensacola for a thrilling regatta set to make waves in the 2026 Southern Series.
body: As the nautical world counts down to the start of the 2026 GL52 Southern Series, there's palpable anticipation for the glittering jewel in the crown - the Pensacola Cup. This first of two regattas has become a battleground for gladiators of the sailing universe, a place where the best of the best vie for the illustrious bespoke Kraken trophy, a creation of renowned Pensacola artist Joe Hobbs.

The event marks an enthusiastic return of the GL52 fleet for these giants of the ocean to their adopted US winter home in Pensacola. Located at the scenic Palafox Marina, just a stone's throw away from Jaco's Restaurant and the American Magic High Performance Training facility, the marina offers teams an unparallel combination of convenience and functionality.

Moreover, the GL52 fleet continues its admirable collaboration with the Satori Foundation to foster youth sailing opportunities in underprivileged communities. These initiatives have cultivated a sense of camaraderie, allowing Satori Foundation members privileged insights into the stunning boats, advanced technology, and the men and women who bring these magnificent vessels to life.

But it's on the open waters of Pensacola Bay, a stretch of more than 13 miles long and 2.5 miles wide where the real action lies. The bay offers the fleet a challenging yet rewarding sailing landscape, with its 20'+ depth, few obstacles, and consistent afternoon breezes between 12-20 knots. Accessible, and spectator-friendly, it has all the ingredients to ensure a thrilling spectacle for all sailing enthusiasts.

Accompanying the GL52 fleet, the ClubSwan 28 Fleet, a product of the successful collaboration between American Magic and Nautor Swan, also graces the event. Their boat, designed by the talented Juan Kouyoumdjian, stands as a testament of technical excellence meeting conceptual simplicity, from its carbon mast to the lifting keel.

As Pensacola gears up to host this captivating event, the 2026 GL52 Southern Series promises to unleash a battle of titans, a testament to human skill, innovation, and the enduring allure of the open sea.

title: Intriguing Collaboration between ISA Yachts and Luca Dini Leads to New 'Timeless' Superyacht Line
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Intriguing Collaboration between ISA Yachts and Luca Dini Leads to New 'Timeless' Superyacht Line
summary: ISA Yachts has partnered with Luca Dini Design & Architecture to present a new line of superyachts, aptly named 'Timeless'.
body: In a brilliant display of innovation and elegance, Italian shipbuilding powerhouse, ISA Yachts, a division of Palumbo Superyachts, teamed up with Luca Dini Design & Architecture to produce a new line of superyachts designated 'Timeless'. Spanning from 42 to 82 meters, the 'Timeless' line consists of five distinct yachts, each boasting a sleek, horizontal exterior silhouette and perfectly balanced proportions.

The initial model to grace the seas is the Timeless 52, embodying the very essence of customisation, according to ISA Yachts. This 52-meter yacht, constructed from aluminium and steel, offers an expansive nine-meter beam complemented by a generous volume of 499GT. Using flexible outdoor living as its anchor, the yacht features expansive walk-around areas, promoting smooth circulation and copious areas for luxurious relaxation.

Providing the opportunity for an integrated indoor and outdoor experience, the lower deck can be revamped into five or six guest cabins, with options for an additional spa or gym area and a garage space. The detailed focus on interior design allows natural light to flow freely through expansive glazed windows, enhancing the spatial perception with generous floor-to-ceiling heights and removal of any obstruction. As the marine industry advances, vessels like the 'Timeless' range are taking center stage in defining a new era of luxury sailing.

title: Renewed Efforts Needed: Yacht Safety and Crew Wellbeing Falling Short in Industry Survey
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Renewed Efforts Needed: Yacht Safety and Crew Wellbeing Falling Short in Industry Survey
summary: A sector-wide survey assesses current safety culture, mental wellbeing in yachting, highlighting pressing issues, areas for improvement.
body: In an extensive sector-wide survey, the myriad challenges faced by the yachting workforce have been rolled into focus. The study sought to establish a baseline for safety culture and mental health within the industry. With over 75% of respondents belonging to yacht crew and nearly 80% navigating yachts of 500gt or more, the survey offers a robust look at the operational landscape.

Interestingly, this snapshot of the industry reveals a workforce composed largely of established professionals with a tenure of more than ten years. This pool of experienced respondents indicates an in-depth understanding of the industry's depths, both the successes and the challenges. And challenges, it would seem, are not in short supply.

A shockingly deep-seated ignorance and disregard for safety protocols are rampant, with 40% of respondents admitting to bending rules in daily operations. The ‘owner priority’ dynamic, where commercial pressures and guest expectations often sabotage established safety procedures, fuels this unfortunate pattern. The resulting operational environment is a dangerous cocktail, paving the way for preventable accidents.

Adding salt to the wound is the nebulous supervisory structure onboard. Flat crewing arrangements and poorly defined roles leave crew members scratching their heads, uncertain of who holds the reins. Consequently, operational performance often trumps safety.

In a compelling case study of a superyacht undergoing refitting, a surprising case of hull corrosion offers a stark reminder of the systemic issues often overlooked. A hole in the hull plating, a result of unsealed anchor pockets, was discovered only during routine paint and repair works, proving that attention to safety details can prevent considerable harm.

While the survey results can seem grim, they serve an essential purpose - a clarion call for reevaluating and bolstering safety protocols. For the yachting industry, the voyage towards safer waters and stronger wellbeing anchors has only just begun.

title: Sunseeker's Remarkable 41m Superyacht Achieves Significant Construction Milestone
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Sunseeker's Remarkable 41m Superyacht Achieves Significant Construction Milestone

The construction of this compelling 40.5-metre superyacht is currently ongoing at the builder's yard in the scenic locale of Dorset, UK, where it recently underwent initial lamination. The announcement comes as a cause for celebration, as it rapidly follows just two months post the sale disclosure of the first hull during the prestigious boot Düsseldorf in January, to a maritime enthusiast from America's West Coast.
Notably, the Sunseeker 134 is the buyer's third commissioned Sunseeker yacht. With anticipation running high, the delivery of this impressive build is slated for the year 2027.

The pioneering Sunseeker 134 is the first launched from the rejuvenated Sunseeker Superyacht Range. It first broke cover at the 2025 Cannes Yachting Festival signifying a 'bold step forward' in Sunseeker's reimagined portfolio of superyachts. The yacht catches the eye with its elongated lines, reflective hull window graphics, and an innovatively designed forward window arrangement sporting reverse-angle glazing for an ultra-modern identity. As Foster illustrated at the January announcement, the Sunseeker 134 superyacht presents an intelligent blend of 'quiet power and uncompromising elegance.' A commanding silhouette and confident presence on the water veil an interior world characterized by elevated comfort, convenience, and sophisticated style.

title: Prometheus Sailing Champions Henri-Lloyd as Official Clothing Partner: A Voyage Towards Equity and Excellence on the High Seas
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Prometheus Sailing Champions Henri-Lloyd as Official Clothing Partner: A Voyage Towards Equity and Excellence on the High Seas
summary: Henri-Lloyd is confirmed as the Official Performance Clothing Partner to Prometheus Sailing, paving a way for accessible sailing and seal-worthy experiences.
body: The British sailing school frontrunner, Prometheus Sailing, warmly welcomes Henri-Lloyd as their Official Performance Clothing Partner. This beacon of boating education operates out of Port Solent, boasting a substantial fleet of charter yachts and an array of sea exploration activities. Their offerings cover everything from landlubber-friendly RYA training and yacht charters to adventurous flotilla sailing and exhilarating corporate race events. The core of Prometheus's approach is pervasive accessibility, making the high-sea adventures possible for groups of mates, solo sailors, or teams of co-workers. As part of this multi-year partnership, Henri-Lloyd, a pioneer in high-performance technical apparel, will outfit Prometheus’s sea and shore personnel. The brand's advanced gear will ensure the team stays dry, warm, and safe across every oceanic condition.

Prometheus Sailing is particularly celebrated for making yacht racing accessible through its 'Rock Up and Race' programme. It allows sailing enthusiasts to join a race crew or charter an entire yacht, with varying levels of coaching and support, and engage in remarkable events like Cowes Week or the Round the Island Race. Adding more excitement, Henri-Lloyd will conduct competitions offering winning spots to participate in prominent events as part of the partnership.

Prometheus's popular annual race series is rebirthed as the 'Henri-Lloyd Racing Series'. The series consists of five thrilling weekend regattas from March through October, sited at Port Solent. The leading teams across the series will compete head-to-head in a nail-biting final race, vying for prizes sourced from Henri-Lloyd. One of Prometheus's fleet, a Jeanneau Sun Odyssey 41ft yacht, will be proudly branded as the Henri-Lloyd vessel.

The alliance between Prometheus Sailing and Henri-Lloyd mirrors a shared commitment to encouraging more individuals to enjoy the thrill of the sea. It promises an added value, pairing accessible high-seas thrills with premium performance apparel.

title: Superyacht Eco Association Rolls Out Innovative Air Quality Certification for Luxury Vessels
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Superyacht Eco Association Rolls Out Innovative Air Quality Certification for Luxury Vessels
summary: The Superyacht Eco Association spearheads a new initiative toward environmental sustainability with the introduction of an Air Quality Certification for superyachts.

The Air Quality Certification not only pushes the envelope of environmental responsibility within the maritime industry but also sets a new benchmark for luxury vessels. title: Trade Winds and Tactical Nerve Hand Leopard 3 the IMA Maxi Crown in Antigua
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Leopard 3 Seals Come-From-Behind Victory at the 2026 RORC Nelson’s Cup
summary: Leopard 3 Delivers When It Mattered Most Antigua saved its sharpest conditions for the final act. On the third and decisive day of racing for the IMA Maxi Class at the RORC Nelson’s Cup Series, the trade winds built into the high teens off English Harbour, delivering exactly the sort of pressure-cooker environment that defines Caribbean maxi racing.
body: Two final coastal races — one of 20 nautical miles, the second 10 — were set against the dramatic backdrop of Fort Charlotte, perched high above the leeward end of the starting line. From there, race officer Nigel Biggs and his team oversaw a start sequence that has quickly become one of the most distinctive in international maxi racing: sheer cliffs, narrow tactical margins, and 100-foot yachts tacking within metres of each other.
By the end of the day, it was Leopard 3 that stood tallest — claiming a hard-fought, come-from-behind victory in the IMA Maxi division.
Race One: Margins Measured in Seconds

The first race of the day began with Karel Komárek’s 100-footer V winning the pin, Chris Flowers’ Galateia pressing above her, and Joost Schuijff’s Leopard 3 positioned one boat down from the top end.
The start mattered. On this course, control of the “cliff end” often dictates the opening phase of the beat. Captain Jack Bouttell aboard V described it clearly:
“If you win the cliff end, you can basically call water on the fleet. You’re in a land-favoured beat and can control the return to shore.”

V converted that advantage into her first race win of the series — but only just. Under IRC corrected time, she edged Leopard 3 by a mere 19 seconds. Balthasar recovered strongly after previous day boom issues to claim third.
The result compressed the leaderboard dramatically. Overall leader Deep Blue posted a fifth, leaving just one point separating Deep Blue, Leopard 3 and V heading into the final race.
The Nelson’s Cup was suddenly wide open.
Race Two: Pressure, Squalls and Precision

Before the start of the second race, a rain squall loomed south of the course — a reminder of the chaos earlier in the week when sudden shifts and torrential downpours had reshuffled positions in minutes. But this time the weather held its nerve. The squall line passed clear, leaving steady breeze building to 18–19 knots.
At the line, Galateia won the pin with Leopard 3 positioned above and V squeezed between.
Leopard 3 tactician Chris Nicholson explained the split-second decision that shaped the race:

“We wanted the left, but so did V. It became too congested. Galateia were ripping in on starboard, so we changed plan, hitched up windward and timed it right. They called water — we simu-tacked with them — and slowly ground out from underneath.”
Three 100-footers tacking within three boat lengths is not theatre. It is high-end execution under load.
Leopard 3 found her rhythm and controlled the race from there, stretching out to win by more than two and a half minutes under IRC corrected time. Galateia finished second, Balthasar third.
That 2–1 scoreline on the final day was enough to overturn the standings and hand Leopard 3 the overall IMA Maxi victory by two points from Deep Blue, with Galateia third.
Training, Youth and Momentum
For owner Joost Schuijff, the win was both tactical and cultural.
“It was very tight going into the last race. I told the crew we’ve done this before — winning the last race — and not making mistakes. The training paid off.”
He emphasised the steady progression of the programme:
“We’re still improving different things. We’re getting better and better. We’re constantly close with the other 100s now.”
Laura Schuijff highlighted another dynamic shaping Leopard 3’s resurgence:
“The young guys are really stepping up. We’ve got excellent young sailors — including an Antiguan on board — who are owning their roles.”
Nicholson was equally candid:
“Today was our best day — a 2–1. The margins are tiny. On board it feels intense. We’re still finding our feet against Galateia and V. They push harder in manoeuvres. We’re learning.”
That honesty perhaps explains the result more than anything else. Leopard 3 did not dominate the series. She refined, adjusted, and delivered under maximum pressure.
What It Means

The IMA Maxi Class at the RORC Nelson’s Cup has evolved into one of the most competitive high-performance arenas in the Caribbean. The fleet is technically sophisticated. The owners are deeply engaged. The conditions are uncompromising.
Antigua does not reward reputation.
It rewards execution.
On the final afternoon, with the breeze in the high teens and the cliff face watching over the line, Leopard 3 executed when it mattered most.
Salt in the air. Loads on the rig. Margins in seconds.

title: Experience Seafaring Elegance Aboard the Sophisticated Benetti Motopanfilo 37M, EH²
author: Old Sea Dogs

The beautifully designed EH² is a triple-deck beauty that is reminiscent of classic navetta yachts from a bygone era, yet boasts the modern amenities of today. Its sleek exterior, abundant outdoor areas, and smooth silhouette radiate a vintage magnetism that is simply irresistible. The onboard facilities are second to none, with the yacht offering copious space both inside and out for entertainment or relaxation. The EH² comfortably accommodates up to 10 guests across five opulent cabins. Every single feature of the yacht has been meticulously created for sheer relaxation and indulgence. Adding to the yacht’s appeal are top-notch amenities and state-of-the-art stabilization mechanisms, making it suitable for anything, from tranquil coastal cruising to adventurous long-distance voyages. Much of the yacht's allure comes from its stunning exterior. The curvaceous charm of the exterior along with the expansive deck areas make for a fantastic open-air experience, whether at anchor or on the move. The generously sized beach club, which is seamlessly integrated with a stern platform, offers effortless access to the sea, enhancing your marine connection. The main saloon and dining area exude contemporary chic while maintaining a warm and inviting atmosphere. The master suite and guest cabins are the epitome of luxury, finished with exquisite materials that prioritize style and privacy. The yacht is also fully equipped for charter, boasting an impressive collection of water toys. Thanks to zero-speed stabilisers, the EH² ensures smooth sailing and unmatched comfort in the seas. This 2022 Benetti Motopanfilo 37M is a captivating vessel, entwining a rich nautical heritage with leading-edge shipbuilding technology to provide an unrivalled seafaring experience.

title: Innovative Utilization of Glass Transforms Superyacht Design and Engineering - The New Horizon of Maritime Luxury
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Innovative Utilization of Glass Transforms Superyacht Design and Engineering - The New Horizon of Maritime Luxury
summary: Architectural and engineering visions are fundamentally being reshaped by the groundbreaking utilization of glass in superyacht designs.
body: In the realm of superyacht creation, the role of glass has transformed from a passive element to an essential aesthetic and engineering facet. This striking metamorphosis is reshaping the very essence of superyacht design, allowing for innovative implementations that elevate the vessel's identity, performance and comfort from the outset of its existence.

Unlike refurbishment works that often confine design possibilities within the parameters of existing structures, new-build projects gift the designer an unparalleled freedom: the power to implement sophisticated glazing systems as a core part of the yacht's architecture. This innovative approach has unlocked the gateway to advanced technologies, vast surfaces, and superior configurations, unlocking the untapped potential of yacht glazing.

Unleashing the full potential of contemporary glazing technologies in new builds can prove challenging in retrofit situations. However, development in chemically strengthened glass, structural interlayers, and optimized insulating glazing units (IGUs) have revolutionized the capabilities of superyacht glazing. Superyacht glazing now goes beyond basic architectural expectations, requiring tailored engineering approaches to fulfill the unique demands of the maritime environment, namely minimal distortion, controlled reflectivity, and consistent color perception across extensive surfaces.

Another exciting frontier is the evolution of glazed deadlights. Once solely conceived for safety and regulatory obligations, glazed deadlights are now being reimagined, retiring opaque, metallic designs in favor of enlightened, transparent concepts that revolutionize the visual and aesthetic experiences on board.

title: The Often-Overlooked but Crucial Step in Sailing Preparations: Rig Checks
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Often-Overlooked but Crucial Step in Sailing Preparations: Rig Checks
summary: Many sailors overlook a crucial aspect of pre-departure checks: the rig check. These can prevent accidents and expensive repairs while sailing.
body: Every sailing adventure should commence with a meticulous pre-departure checklist. From ensuring all safety equipment is in place, checking the weather forecasts, to examining the charts, these steps are undeniably important. Nevertheless, one check seems to be more important than the rest, yet often overlooked by sailors - the rig check.

Many sailors might believe they can avoid potential accidents by just having safety equipment onboard and a functioning engine. However, ignoring rig checks can create dangerous situations, leading to rig failures that put everyone onboard in immediate danger. Rig failures are not only risky but also astronomically expensive to repair.

The importance of rigging checks got highlighted by John Keane of Oyster 595 Alpenglow, currently on the Oyster World Rally. He confirmed that knowing their dock tune was accurate took a great deal of stress off their preparation for the rally.

One such innovation is the digital dock tune using Cyclops load monitoring system. Directly purchasing a boat from the manufacturer usually means it comes tuned to the recommended settings. But, the rig tune will inevitably change, especially after its maiden voyage. This is where the digital dock tune proves its worth. It allows sailors to quickly return the rig to the manufacturer's recommended settings by adjusting it while monitoring the tension through their onboard screens.
The system also functions through a smartphone app, transforming a potentially hours-long manual check into a quick, easy yet thorough check.

Although everything may seem ideal at the dock, conditions often change once the sails go up, especially on brand new yachts. Implementing a digital dock tune using Cyclops load monitoring system significantly reduces the frequency of problems, ensuring a safe, enjoyable, and adventurous experience for all onboard.

title: Gentle Yet Impactful Modifications in Sunseeker Manhattan 56 and Emergence of Leisure-centric Saxdor 460 GTC: A Comprehensive Review
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Gentle Yet Impactful Modifications in Sunseeker Manhattan 56 and Emergence of Leisure-centric Saxdor 460 GTC: A Comprehensive Review
summary: Details unfold as new modifications in Sunseeker Manhattan 56 and Saxdor 460 GTC promise to redefine maritime voyages with enhanced aesthetics and comfort.
body: Sunseeker Manhattan 56, graced the Düsseldorf boat show with subtle yet productive adjustments from its previous version. With a hint of mystery around its transformation from the 55, unveiled alterations leaned more towards refinement rather than a complete overhaul. To provide an improved sailing experience, changes involved parts like the stern. Smooth GRP shark fin mouldings replaced the existing cumbersome design, offering an enhanced view from the flybridge dinette. A modified transom area accommodates a new cockpit dinette/sunpad, embodying an aesthetic upgrade alongside amplifying comfort. Direct benefits of minimalistic changes include an expanded glass area and improved visibility, all thanks to the removal of the GRP 'spear'. The extended aft dinette converts into an extra sunpad promising unaltered relaxation. Designers ingeniously included a teak-topped bench underneath, a pop-up shower, and improved access to the crew cabin. Amid such alterations, the large flybridge and foredeck lounges continue to reign supreme. This refurbished version from Sunseeker, undoubtedly remains set to sail the high seas with class and convenience.

On the other hand, the Saxdor 460 GTC emerged as a promising addition in the realm of leisure boating. While Saxdor and Axopar potentially rival each other, their distinct capabilities set them apart. The new Saxdor 460 GTC is not merely a yacht but a holistic experience. Integrated features like folding balconies and a hammock set the tone for leisure and relaxation. With its fully open wheelhouse, it transcends conventional perceptions of maritime voyaging. This adventurous boat encapsulates an ideal blend of style without compromising on functionality. It represents a vision targeted to make boating more accessible with an emphasis on catering to diverse boating needs and making each voyage a memorable adventure.

title: Debra One Luxury Yacht Sees Spectacular €700,000 Price Reduction, a Must-See for Any Aspiring Sea Captain

summary: An amazing opportunity to own the 29.6-metre motor yacht Debra One arises as it undergoes a lining price reduction of €700,000.
body: The opulent world of the 29.6-metre Amer Yachts motor yacht Debra One has just become more accessible, thanks to a €700,000 price reduction. This coveted boat, which has never seen charted service, is acknowledged to have been meticulously maintained and continuously updated to the highest standards by its passionate owner. It was delivered in 2013 and now has a reduced asking price of €2,200,000 with EU VAT exclusive.

This boat offers the epitome of affluence, with its hull and superstructure crafted in GRP. Stefano Tini has wonderfully designed the interiors with high-gloss wood and natural tones against a backdrop of panoramic windows ensuring that the yacht remains bright and inviting. These details elevate the overall aesthetic of Debra One, proving that every penny of the investment is well worth it.

Onboard, guests can enjoy al fresco dining on the main deck aft, while the flybridge offers a second helm forward, a hot tub and lounges aft with an additional dining table in between. The bow area offers sun pads, ideal for lounging under the Mediterranean sun, along with a smaller table perfect for a intimate gathering.

Propelling this yacht across the waters is the power sourced from its twin V12 CAT engines, taking the yacht to top speeds of 25 knots, promising swift travels. Trading hands with Remy Becquet of Fraser, this luxury yacht now rests at a reduced price in Sanremo, Italy, making it an enticing opportunity for yacht enthusiasts and prospective buyers.

title: Dutch Shipyards Invite the Ninth Mulder ThirtySix Luxury Yacht to Hit the Open Waters
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Dutch Shipyards Invite the Ninth Mulder ThirtySix Luxury Yacht to Hit the Open Waters
summary: Following a successful launch, the ninth unit of the Mulder ThirtySix yacht series sets to the sea, confirming delivery by spring 2026.
body: The waterways of Zoeterwoude, the Netherlands, recently witnessed the spectacular launch of the ninth unit in the Mulder ThirtySix yacht series. Ready to conquer the nautical charts, this 36-metre new build will be undergoing final outfitting and commissioning, as well as rigorous sea trials, before reaching its delivery due date in the spring of 2026.

The latest maritime offspring of the Mulder shipyard was announced in September 2025, finally coming to fruition in a deal with Alex Lees-Buckley of Camper and Nicholsons. Built for seasoned, passionate yacht owners who advocate long-range cruising and a sophisticated living experience on board, this yacht is an epitome of bespoke elegance. Featuring a low-profile exterior design by Claydon Reeves Design Studio, the vessel echoes strength and stealth.

The Dutch shipyard has incorporated features from its predecessors in the ThirtySix series, taking the opulent open flybridge from Seaflower. This admirable feature was lauded by the judges of the 2024 World Superyacht Awards. Added to this is a new Seakeeper 40 gyro to complement the model's electric stabiliser fins. The interior design, a delicate blend of elegance, comfort, and functionality, will be curated by the time-honoured collaborator Vickers Studio. However, the finer details remain undisclosed.

This ThirtySix model will be equipped with Van Oossanen's patented Fast Displacement Hull Form (FDHF), a design benchmark that ensures smooth sailing, fuel efficiency, and stability even at a maximum speed of 17 knots. The build promises a distinct 'second master suite' on the lower deck, providing a private, luxurious retreat for its owners. This launch comes on the heels of the sale of 'Delta One', 'Mana I', and 'Castlefinn' last year, adding another gleaming feather to Mulder's cap.

title: Daring Evolution in the New Sunseeker Manhattan 56: A Dream Blend of Subtlety And Productive Alterations Unveiled
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Daring Evolution in the New Sunseeker Manhattan 56: A Dream Blend of Subtlety And Productive Alterations Unveiled
summary: Explore the new Sunseeker Manhattan 56 - a perfect sea vessel, blending subtle enhancements with its predecessor's unbeatable design.
body: Cloaked in mystery prior to its Düsseldorf boat show debut, the Sunseeker Manhattan 56 unveiled nuanced alterations rather than massive revamps, suggesting that perfection warrants preservation, not transformation. The key changes primarily orbit the stern of the vessel. The somewhat convoluted GRP shark fin mouldings along the trailing edge of the flybridge, replaced with a lower, more streamlined alternative, offers an unobstructed view from the elevated outdoor diner. Similar efforts transformed the transom area, making room for a freshly designed cockpit dinette/sunpad. Further modifications include the removal of the GRP 'spear' from the expansive side windows, enabling more light, a larger viewing area, and improved helm visibility. However, the new and improved cockpit dinette could well be the vessel's crowning glory. Extended out over the bathing platform and furnished with a sliding backrest, it provides ample space for both a forward- and aft-facing bench—proving an excellent selling point. An innovative design tweak allows the dinette to convert into a full-length sunpad, adding luxury and ultimate sunbathing comfort on sunny days out at sea. While these changes take centerstage, the designers ingeniously included additional smaller modifications such as a tiny teak bench underneath the sunpad, a pop-up shower to the starboard, and better access to the portside crew cabin. For the first time, the cockpit now offers an option for an aft-facing corner seat in place of the traditional bar stools. Added to this is an extra window within the moulding, adding an additional layer of detail. Business remains as usual beyond these changes, albeit with a touch of gloss, thanks to Design Unlimited's revamped finishes. The features that made the predecessor a favourite among yacht enthusiasts—a spacious aft galley fitted with a wine cooler and four fridge/freezer drawers, a luminous saloon, three substantial cabins, luxurious bathrooms, and one of the most spacious flybridges and foredeck lounges in the category—are still very much a part of this yacht's charm. The Sunseeker Manhattan 56 is not just a pristine sea vessel; it’s a subtle, yet powerful assertion of understated luxury and comfort that inspires the joy of sailing.

title: The Fifth Edition of The Grand Tour Sailing: Unwrapping the Mystery of Time
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Fifth Edition of The Grand Tour Sailing: Unwrapping the Mystery of Time
summary: Embarking on a novel expedition that connects exploration, scientific research, promotion of culture and land, the fifth edition of The Grand Tour Sailing is an adventurous journey through the essence of time.
body: Unveiling the intricacies of time's ebb and flow, the fifth edition of The Grand Tour Sailing charts a riveting course full of exploration, research, and cultural enrichment. The athletes, Manuel Vlacich and Franco Deganutti, have tacked their thematic voyage to culturally pivotal locations such as Varanasi in India, Greenwich in England, and the Diomede Islands, where each bears a unique relationship with time. Not just showcasing their outstanding sailing skills, Vlacich and Deganutti are also acting as ambassadors for the 'Io sono Friuli Venezia Giulia' brand. Their boats display the region's official branding, promoting awareness and appreciation of the region's unique identity and values globally. The pilots launched the 2026 edition with an inaugural visit to Varanasi, one of the oldest inhabited centres globally. Facing challenging conditions, they completed a seven-kilometre voyage along the heavily polluted Ganges River, negotiating local river traffic, dealing with intense weather, and managing delicate local sensibilities. Undertaking the expedition required advanced logistical planning. They had to coordinate the transport of two sailing boats, navigational equipment, and personal luggage, totalling 140 kg across multiple flights and ground transfers independently. They chose the Tiwal 3 inflatable boats that are convenient to transport and handle, highlighting the importance of practicality and adaptability in such ventures. Apart from the exploration, this journey had a scientific agenda as well. Vlacich and Deganutti collected four water samples from the Ganges for the University of Udine. These samples will further the university's ongoing project to study and protect inland waters. This one-of-a-kind voyage, connecting exploration, sustainability, sports, and science, highlights the multi-dimensional possibilities of sailing as a medium of learning and discovery.

title: Grandeur On Water: German-Built Amaral, A 58m Abeking & Rasmussen Motor Yacht, Delights A New Owner

As Amaral embarks on a new chapter, she reveals the sheer magnitude of luxury and efficiency that's possible on the open seas. With her new owner, this yacht is set to continue shaping unique, memorable voyages.

title: A Change in Tides: The 27m Posillipo-Rizzardi Motor Yacht 'This is Mine' Finds New Owners and a New Name, 'Seas The Day'
author: Old Sea Dogs

summary: The sophisticated 27.1-metre Posillipo-Rizzardi motor yacht 'This is Mine' embarks on a new adventure with new owners and a new name, 'Seas The Day'.

Beyond her technical prowess, 'Seas The Day' is an enchanting testament to the limitless potential of luxury yachting.

title: Construction Begins on Major South Marina Expansion at Nanny Cay, Tortola
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Nanny Cay Expands: $30 Million Marina Development Reshapes the BVI’s South Coast
summary: Nanny Cay Resort & Marina: Building the Next Chapter in the BVI On the south coast of Tortola, diggers are moving and steel is rising. Construction has officially begun on a major expansion at Nanny Cay Resort & Marina, marking the start of a $30+ million development designed to reposition the property as one of the Caribbean’s most capable full-service marina resorts.
body: For decades, Nanny Cay has been a working marina first and a resort second — practical, well-placed, and respected by cruising sailors and charter fleets alike. This new development signals something bigger: a response to the rapid evolution of the Caribbean fleet itself.
Catamarans are getting wider. Multihulls are getting heavier. Megayachts are getting more complex. And the infrastructure required to support them has to evolve.

At the heart of the expansion is a new 112-slip South Marina, engineered to accommodate the latest generation of performance catamarans and large sailing yachts now arriving in the region. With beam allowances designed for 60, 70 and even 80-foot multihulls, the facility reflects a simple truth: the Caribbean charter and private ownership markets have shifted decisively toward larger platforms.

To support that growth, Nanny Cay is installing a custom 150-ton travel lift, one of the widest in the region at 44 feet. The lift is specifically configured for wide-beam catamarans, complementing the existing 50-ton and 70-ton Marine Travelifts already operating in the boatyard.

The existing marina currently accommodates 302 yachts, with 110 monohulls in the Outer Marina and 192 vessels in the Inner Marina (or catamaran equivalents). The expanded yard and marina will increase both flexibility and throughput — critical in a region where hurricane season preparation and post-season recommissioning define the calendar.
To minimise disruption to ongoing operations, construction has been divided into two overlapping phases, scheduled for completion by the end of 2028.
Phase I focuses on maritime infrastructure:
Construction of a new breakwater (armour wall) to protect the South Marina
Land reclamation
Expansion of the existing boatyard
Installation of the 150-ton haul-out facility
Phase II shifts attention landside:
A new beach and beach bar
Two-level restaurant with panoramic views across the Sir Francis Drake Channel
Regatta and event village with stage and dining areas
Retail and commercial spaces
A Marine Hub incorporating the Royal BVI Yacht Club youth programme and the HLSCC Marine Training Centre
Concierge facilities, gardens, walkways, and expanded parking
This is not simply a marina extension. It is a mixed-use waterfront redevelopment aimed at strengthening Nanny Cay’s role as a regional hub.
The resort already includes a 52-bed hotel, 32 waterfront townhouses, retail outlets, chandlery, and multiple dining venues. The expansion builds on that base — not replacing it, but scaling it.

The addition of marine training facilities and youth sailing infrastructure signals long-term thinking. The Royal BVI Yacht Club’s youth programme will gain improved storage and launch facilities, reinforcing the development’s integration into the local sailing ecosystem rather than isolating it as a standalone luxury enclave.

The official groundbreaking ceremony took place on 31 October 2025, attended by senior government officials including Premier and Minister of Finance Dr. Natalio D. Wheatley, Governor Daniel Pruce, and Deputy Premier Julian Fraser. Their presence underscored the project’s economic significance to the British Virgin Islands, where marine tourism remains a cornerstone of the economy.

The Caribbean marina landscape is becoming increasingly competitive. Facilities that once comfortably handled 45-foot monohulls are now being asked to service 70-foot catamarans with complex systems and serious displacement.
Nanny Cay’s expansion is a strategic answer to that shift.
The breakwater will shelter more tonnage. The yard will lift heavier boats. The marina will berth wider beams.
And if the plans are executed as drawn, Tortola’s south coast will host one of the most technically capable marina complexes in the region.
For cruising sailors, charter operators, and megayacht programmes alike, that matters.
Salt in the air. Steel in the water. The next phase begins.

title: Ready, Set, Sail: Rhody Regatta Sets the Course for Narragansett Bay's Eagerly Anticipated 2026 Racing Season
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Ready, Set, Sail: Rhody Regatta Sets the Course for Narragansett Bay's Eagerly Anticipated 2026 Racing Season
summary: The prestigious Rhody Regatta is ready to launch Narragansett Bay's 2026 sailing season, promising a cocktail of competition and community spirit.
body: With an electrifying energy that can only signal the beginning of a new spring, the fourth annual Rhody Regatta is gearing up to launch the 2026 sailing season on Narragansett Bay. Hosted by the International Yacht and Athletic Club (IYAC), the regatta is set to take place on the last Saturday of May, offering sailors a thrilling canvas for sporting prowess, while also making a significant impact on the wider community. This year, the event will be supporting the indispensable work of Meals on Wheels of Rhode Island, an organization providing vital meals and much-needed support to homebound seniors and persons in need across the region.

The regatta's course is a single, adrenaline-boosting 18-mile lap around Conanicut Island, known by locals as Jamestown. Combining wide-open water stretches and more strategic shoreline sailing, it provides a varied and hence captivating challenge for all participants. Set near Fort Adams, the start and finish line places racers right into the beating heart of Newport's illustrious sailing history.

Open to all Cruising/Racing Yachts, whether or not they possess a 2026 PHRF of Narragansett Bay handicap, the event promises a wide field of contestants. The fleet will be split into handicap and one-design classes, the balancing act decided by IYAC's experienced Race Management.

As an official US SAILING-affiliated club, IYAC has a well-established reputation for serving as the locals' favorite sailors' bar. It is renowned for hosting several area regattas for a wide sweep of boats, from nimble sport boats to commanding Maxi yachts, thereby enriching the regional racing calendar. The NOR and registration links are expected to be released on yachtscoring.com shortly. For more information, stay tuned to iyacnewport.com.

title: The Competing Giants of the Sea: The Yachts for the 2026 St Barths Bucket
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Competing Giants of the Sea: The Yachts for the 2026 St Barths Bucket
summary: Excitement heightens as the 2026 St Barths Bucket competition looms, with a line-up of sailing magnates set to race.
body: As the 2026 St Barths Bucket approaches, a thrilling display of sail competition is dominating the chatter of the sailing community. The competition, slated to occur from the 12th-15th March, confirms a line-up of competing yachts, all vying for the highly coveted regatta title.

An interesting trend notices a growing presence of larger yachts taking up the challenge. A medley of sailing giants, each impressive in their own right, is set to grace the grand stage. The year's regatta celebrates 31 years of sailing tradition, attracting the presence of social non-racing entries as well.

Key among these entries is Burger Boat's 46.7-meter Ingot and 46-meter Nadan, bringing the rich pedigree of their makers to the front; along with Royal Huisman's 42.1-meter Hanuman, Palmer Johnson's 37.4-meter Temptation and Baltic Yacht's 34.1-meter Liara among others, shaping up a varied and quality fleet.

Also on the racing canvas is the giant Atlantic, measuring 69m. This steel-built Dutch wonder is a meticulous replica of the 1905 transatlantic Kaiser's Cup winner. The original symbolizes the zenith of early 20th-century yacht designs. Atlantic, painstakingly crafted under the watchful survey of naval architect Doug Peterson, revives that racing legacy.

Another yacht steeped in prestige is Hetairos. Measuring a staggering 66.9m, its all-carbon design and comprehensive sail area make it an eye-catching entry. The yacht is veteran of the Bucket competition and is touted as one of the most sought-after sailing superyachts, boasting of an unrivalled blend of classic aesthetics and revolutionary hull design and construction.

The anticipation for Royal Huisman's Aquarius is also palpable. Recently launched in Spring 2025, this 65.2m yacht constitutes a significant upgrade from its 56-meter predecessor. With a tall and formidable carbon rig, Aquarius promises a more capacious, modern, and efficient sailing experience.

The 60m Perseus3 by Perini Navi brings a modern touch to this line-up. With its sloop rig, the yacht marries Perini's traditional comfort with state-of-the-art systems and a tremendous downwind sail area.
All in all, the upcoming St Barths Bucket competition promises a grand spectacle of maritime feats as it continues to showcase the best in the world of yachts and sailing.

With continued growth and a vibrant atmosphere in the industry, who knew that floating palaces would become such lucrative investments? The wind is in the sails of the yacht market, and there's a highly promising horizon ahead.

title: Exploring the Competing Yachts and Sailing Greats at the 2026 St Barths Bucket Regatta
author: Old Sea Dogs

summary: As the 2026 St Barths Bucket approaches, we delve into the increasingly larger yachts preparing to compete for the prestigious regatta title.
body: The eagerly awaited 2026 St Barths Bucket, scheduled for 12th-15th March 2026, promises to be a thrilling sailing race attracting a large array of yachts ready to vie for the top spot. This regatta, with its rich 31-year history, has confirmed the entrants, which notably include several massive sailboats.

Among these impressive entrants are Burger Boat's 46.7-metre Ingot and 46-metre Nadan, Royal Huisman's 42.1-metre Hanuman, Palmer Johnson's 37.4-metre Temptation and Baltic Yachts' 34.1-metre Liara. But the participating list goes beyond purely racing vessels. Indeed, the event also welcomes numerous social non-racing entries, adding further to its festive atmosphere.

Van der Graaf's Atlantic, a replica of the 1905 transatlantic Kaiser's Cup-winning yacht, is also a sight to behold. Then there's Baltic Yachts' Hetairos, an all-carbon ketch that remains one of the most desirable sailing superyachts existing today. Her fusion of traditional aesthetics and cutting-edge hull construction make her an aesthetic and technical marvel.

Another competitor joining in 2026 is the 65.2m Aquarius from Royal Huisman, a new launch that has had the sailing world buzzing. She promises new levels of elegance and performance. Also participating is Adix, the flagship of the Spanish yard, which underwent a significant refit in 2019, and Perseus3 from Perini Navi, which beautifully combines classic comfort with modern sailing technology. The list continues with Vitters' latest modern classic, the glossy black ketch Maximus.
