title: Embracing Change in Sailing: Musto Skiff Class Votes Overwhelmingly for Further Integration of the Mainsail X
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Embracing Change in Sailing: Musto Skiff Class Votes Overwhelmingly for Further Integration of the Mainsail X
summary: Musto Skiff class members have confidently cast their ballots for the embraced inclusion of the Mainsail X, heralding an exhilarating new era for sailing.
body: A memorable milestone in sailing history has just been marked; the Musto Skiff class members in the 2025 season have cast an emphatic vote favoring the expanded use of the Mainsail X at organised events. According to the International Committee, the majority of votes landed on the 'Lighter Restrictions - Lower Penalty' option, accounting for 36% of the total vote. A significant display of confidence in this innovative mainsail offering greater flexibility in their sailing adventures.

Brennan Robinson, the Musto Skiff class International Chairman, articulates the palpable excitement regarding this pioneering step towards a more inclusive racing environment. In his view, the integration of the Mainsail X into fleet racing is no longer a mere experiment or flirtation with innovation. It has now been fully embraced, concluded from the dozens of Mainsail X's currently in circulation.

To elaborate, all sailors must nominate a primary sail size before the first race. Following that, sailors can switch sail sizes with prior notice, wherein a reduced scoring penalty applies. Notably, Grand Master and Legend sailors (anyone aged 55 and over) are exempt from the penalty and enjoy the leverage to change sail size. However, sailors who switch sail sizes cannot vie for a top three overall result. These balanced measures ensure a fair and thrilling competition amidst the fresh winds brought by the Mainsail X.

title: Fairline Squadron 58 – A Timeless Classic in Flybridge Luxury
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Fairline Squadron 58 - Flybridge
summary: There are motor yachts that try to impress with bells and whistles, and then there are those that quietly command admiration by doing everything right. The Fairline Squadron 58 is firmly in the latter category—a masterclass in British marine design that delivers confident performance, understated elegance, and practical luxury in equal measure.
body: First launched in the early 2000s, the Squadron 58 became a defining model for Fairline Yachts and remains one of the most respected vessels in the 55–60 foot class. It set a benchmark for what a flybridge cruiser could be: not just a vessel for bluewater passages, but a floating home with long-range comfort, timeless lines, and an interior that wears its age with pride.

At nearly 59 feet overall, the Squadron 58 has genuine presence on the water. Her sweeping hull windows, soft bow flare, and graceful superstructure create a profile that’s muscular without being aggressive. She’s neither loud nor flashy—just effortlessly elegant.

The beam, just shy of 16 feet, allows for generous internal volume, especially in the salon and master stateroom. The deep-V hull provides solid, confidence-inspiring performance offshore, and thanks to a well-balanced weight distribution, she rides smooth and true even in less-than-ideal conditions.
The design team clearly understood that luxury is not just about materials—it’s about how space is used. Every corner of this yacht has a purpose, and every movement feels considered.

The Fairline Squadron 58 typically comes equipped with twin diesel engines from manufacturers like Volvo Penta, MAN, or Caterpillar, ranging from 775 HP to 900 HP each. Top speed hovers around 30 knots, with a comfortable cruising speed between 22 and 26 knots.

But raw speed isn't the point. What impresses is the ease and balance with which the boat handles. Hydraulic steering is light and responsive, the ride is composed, and the boat planes smoothly. She's quiet at cruise, and despite her size, easy to manoeuvre in close quarters—especially with bow and stern thrusters or optional joystick controls.
Whether you’re island-hopping in the Med or taking a weekend run down the south coast of England, the Squadron 58 feels like a willing, capable partner.

One of the defining features of the Squadron 58 is its massive flybridge—a sun-drenched space designed for entertainment and relaxation. It’s accessed by a wide staircase from the cockpit, making it safe and easy to move between levels even underway.
A U-shaped dinette with a large teak table
A full wet bar with grill, fridge, sink, and icemaker
Dual helm seats and a full complement of navigation gear
Expansive sunpads aft, ideal for lounging or sunbathing

There’s room for a dozen guests without feeling cramped, and the view is spectacular whether you're at anchor or underway. Many owners describe the flybridge as their favourite "room" on board—and for good reason.

Step into the main salon through curved glass sliding doors, and you’re greeted by a space that balances classic marine craftsmanship with homey comfort. High-gloss cherrywood cabinetry, cream leather upholstery, and soft carpeting create a warm and inviting atmosphere.

The layout is split-level, with a generous U-shaped sofa aft, a formal dining area forward to port, and a lower helm station to starboard with two commanding leather captain’s chairs. The galley sits on the lower deck landing, amidships for reduced motion, and is fully equipped with a ceramic cooktop, full-height fridge-freezer, microwave, and ample storage.
Large windows allow for exceptional natural light, and many boats are fitted with air conditioning and entertainment systems for extended comfort on board.
Below deck, the Squadron 58 offers a three-cabin, two- or three-head layout that feels more like a luxury apartment than a boat:
Master Stateroom (midship, full-beam): A true retreat, with a queen berth, en suite bathroom with separate shower, vanity area, and large hull windows.
VIP Cabin (forward): An island double berth, hanging lockers, and en suite access to the second head.
Twin Guest Cabin (starboard): Two single berths, suitable for children or guests.
There’s also an optional crew cabin at the stern with its own head—ideal for crew, kids, or extra guests.

Storage is generous throughout, with deep lockers, full-height wardrobes, and hidden compartments. Whether you're aboard for a weekend or an entire summer, the Squadron 58 feels more than capable of meeting your needs.
Expansive flybridge with full entertaining amenities
Rich, high-quality interior joinery
True full-beam master suite
Excellent offshore performance with refined handling
Top-quality systems and engineering
Strong resale value and broker support
Check condition of flybridge canvas, upholstery, and teak decking
Inspect engine hours, servicing logs, and any updates to electronics
Ensure air conditioning, hydraulics, and generators are in good working order
Galley and head systems should be tested—especially in older models

The Squadron 58 is a true bluewater cruiser, designed to handle extended voyages and luxurious weekend escapes alike. With a solid deep-V hull, twin diesel engines, and superb stability, it combines serious offshore chops with a beautifully appointed interior and a flybridge that rivals larger yachts.
It’s ideal for families or groups who want three-cabin liveaboard space, a vast flybridge for socialising, and elegant, understated styling.
Length Overall (LOA) 58 ft 11 in (17.96 m)
Beam 15 ft 10 in (4.83 m)
Draft 4 ft 6 in (1.37 m)
Displacement ~27 tonnes (lightship)
Fuel Capacity 2,728 L (720 US gallons)
Water Capacity 1,140 L (301 US gallons)
Engines Twin Volvo Penta D12 / Caterpillar / MAN
Horsepower Typically 775–900 HP per engine
Top Speed ~30 knots
Cruising Speed 22–26 knots
Cabins 3 + crew (optional)
Heads 2 or 3, depending on layout

The Squadron 58 is no slouch on the water. With twin diesels, the yacht cruises comfortably in the mid-20 knot range and can reach 30 knots at full throttle—impressive for a boat of its size and weight. The deep-V hull ensures a soft ride, even in moderate chop, and electronic throttles and bow/stern thrusters make docking and close-quarters handling intuitive and easy, especially with the upper and lower helm stations.
This yacht is equally at home island-hopping in the Med or cruising through northern waters with a bit more bite.
The flybridge is one of the Squadron 58’s greatest assets. Accessed via a wide teak staircase from the aft deck, it’s expansive and well-configured for entertaining:
Full wet bar with grill, fridge, and sink
Large U-shaped seating area with teak table
Multiple lounging zones with sunpads
Second fully equipped helm station

On the main deck, the aft cockpit features a dining table and seating for al fresco meals, with wide side decks leading to the foredeck sunpad—perfect for sunbathing or watching the anchorage roll by.
A hydraulic swim platform is often fitted (standard on later models), making tender launching or sea access effortless.
Fairline’s craftsmanship shines below deck. The interior feels timeless, luxurious, and welcoming:
Salon: Enter through sliding glass doors into a spacious salon with plush seating, coffee table, and entertainment centre. Large windows flood the space with natural light.
Lower helm: Forward of the salon, with excellent visibility, two leather captain’s chairs, full electronics, and side-deck access via a sliding door.
Dining area: Elevated dinette opposite the galley offers indoor mealtime elegance.
Galley: Fully equipped with fridge/freezer, ceramic cooktop, microwave, dishwasher (in some), and abundant storage. Located amidships for reduced motion when underway.
The standard layout features three spacious cabins:
Owner’s Stateroom (midship, full beam): Queen berth, dressing area, vanity, ample storage, large hull windows, and en suite with separate shower.
VIP Cabin (forward): Island berth, hanging lockers, overhead hatch, and direct access to a second head (shared).
Twin Guest Cabin (starboard): Two single berths, ideal for children or guests.
Many Squadron 58s also feature a crew cabin aft, accessible from the transom, with its own small head—handy for crew, kids, or overflow guests.
Hydraulic passerelle and swim platform
Crew cabin with AC
Teak decking throughout
Onboard generator and inverter
Washer/dryer unit
Air conditioning and diesel heating
Raymarine or Garmin nav systems
Stabilisers (optional aftermarket)
Excellent long-range cruising ability
Top-quality joinery and fittings throughout
Large flybridge and expansive social spaces
Strong secondhand market presence
Feels like a 65-footer in many respects
Flybridge upholstery and bimini/canvas wear
Engine hours and service history (especially MAN/Caterpillar models)
Electronics—many older boats benefit from modernisation
Teak decking condition
Aircon, genset, and hydraulics
The Fairline Squadron 58 is perfect for:
Families or couples looking for a serious liveaboard yacht
Owners upgrading from a 40–50 ft flybridge boat
Mediterranean and UK cruising (with equal ease)
Entertainers who love open-air dining and flybridge living

The Fairline Squadron 58 has earned its reputation not just through brand recognition, but through delivering what owners truly value: quality, practicality, and quiet luxury. It’s not flashy for the sake of it—it’s considered, elegant, and built for those who understand that true luxury is effortless.

In today’s secondhand market, the Squadron 58 remains a standout. She holds her value well, has a strong support network, and—most importantly—still delivers that commanding, reassuring experience that made her a star from the start.
For those ready to graduate from mid-sized cruisers to a serious, world-class motor yacht without stepping into superyacht territory, the Fairline Squadron 58 may be exactly what you’re looking for.

title: Sailors Cayard and Kleen Dominate Day 4 of the 99th Bacardi Cup: A Battle Among Champions

body: At the prestigious 99th Bacardi Cup, an elite sailing event, spectators witnessed the continued dominance by acclaimed sailors Paul Cayard and Frithjof Kleen. Held amidst swirling winds and crystalline waters, the event marked the pivotal fourth day with pulsating moments and fierce, competitive spirit.

Yet, their momentary glory did not loosen the vice-like grip Cayard and Kleen held tight on the overall regatta. Cayard and Kleen demonstrated unwavering performance in a fleet that comprised 17 Olympians, six Olympic medalists, three Olympic champions, and 14 Star World Champions. Yet, against these odds, Cayard and his teammate posted an extraordinary near-perfect 1-1-1-2 score.

Renowned sailor Scheidt commented on Cayard's impressive performance, stating that 'Paul is on fire,' and he 'is having a super great regatta.' Echoing similar sentiments, Cayard revealed an understanding of the heightened competition, recognising the presence of top-quality sailors marking a battle at every turn.

The success of the dynamic duo, Cayard and Kleen, is attributed to their straightforward approach on the boat: a clean start, focused navigation, and an unwavering passion for riding the waves, shaping an exciting unfolding of the 99th Bacardi Cup.

title: Embrace Luxury and History with Superyacht Christina O, Now Available for a Reduced Price of €52M
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Embrace Luxury and History with Superyacht Christina O, Now Available for a Reduced Price of €52M
summary: Thriving on unparalleled glamour and power, the iconic superyacht Christina O is now on the market, priced at a reduced €52 million.
body: Steeped in luxury and commanding unparalleled status, the spectacular superyacht Christina O, known for its history of political and Hollywood royalty, is now available at a reduced price of €52 million on the brokerage market. Few seafaring vessels can mirror the prestige and commercial charter success of the amazing 99.1-metre Christina O. Originally commissioned in 1943 as an anti-submarine escort during World War II, it later underwent an awe-inspiring transformation into a floating palace. This remarkable change represents one of the notable reinventions in yachting history.

The guests aboard the Christina O form a who's who of cultural and political icons, such as Maria Callas, John Wayne, Grace Kelly, Frank Sinatra, Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis, and Elizabeth Taylor. Post-Onassis' death in 1975, despite briefly falling into decline, the yacht was later saved and revived by a family friend. A $50 million restoration was completed in 2001, and the yacht’s allure remains intact, touting preserved history and original features which have stayed unchanged since 1956!

title: Step Aboard the Swan 80: Nautor Swan's Newest Maxi Yacht Approaching Official Launch
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Step Aboard the Swan 80: Nautor Swan's Newest Maxi Yacht Approaching Official Launch
summary: As May draws closer, Nautor Swan has released updates on its first Swan 80 unit, heralding revolutionised luxury sailing with this true maxi yacht.
body: The Finnish shipyard Nautor Swan, a beacon of luxury yachts for decades, is nearing the completion of its first-ever Swan 80, a yacht unit that promises to redefine luxury sailing. This summer is pencilled for the delivery following a scheduled launch in May.

The Swan 80, with its hull numbered 80.301, was announced in April 2024. Not long after the company's new model was unveiled at the Cannes Yachting Festival 2023. The new arrival is an evolution of the Swan 78, an addition to their range of Maxi sailing yachts that ensures the same lineage of superior design and cutting-edge architecture.

Despite maintaining a hull length just under 24 metres, the Swan 80 cleverly maximises the advantages of its size and design, making it exempt from EC regulations and limitations. Starting from the mast, a minimalist and level wooden deck runs to the aft, leading seamlessly into a low-profile coach roof. The cockpit area is flat, enabling endless seating and storage configurations and an open aft deck perfect for swimming and sunbathing when cruising.

Owners can opt for different keel settings, choosing between a fixed deep, fixed shallow, and a deep telescopic lifting keel. The Swan 80's rudders are packed with sacrificial tips for directional stability and encased with sealed compartments to reduce the impact of a collision with a submerged item. Additionally, hull entrance and powerful aft section are tapered for stability.

The yacht continues Nautor's commitment to luxury and comfort indoors. It can accommodate up to 10 guests, with flexible layouts. Alternatives include converting a guest cabin for crew usage or a reading nook or dining area.

As part of the internationally expanded operations of Nautor Swan, following their 2024 acquisition by Sanlorenzo Group, the Swan 80 is set for debut at the upcoming Cannes Yachting Festival in 2026. This unveiling will add another milestone to the brand's journey and secure a prominent place in their lineup of acclaimed Maxi yachts - a lineage that includes Swan 88, Swan 98, Swan 108, and Swan 128.

title: Round the Island Race 2026: One Race, One Thousand Stories
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Round the Island Race 2026 dates released
summary: On Saturday 11 July 2026, the unmistakable spectacle returns as the Island Sailing Club once again stages one of the world’s largest and most iconic mass-participation sailing events. For thousands of sailors, the date is already inked into diaries, with race entries opening on 23 January 2026, including a limited early-bird entry period running until 13 February.
body: There are yacht races — and then there is the Round the Island Race.

Few events capture the spirit of British sailing quite like this 50-nautical-mile lap of the Isle of Wight. From professional race teams and offshore campaigners to family crews and first-time competitors, the Round the Island Race is where experience, ambition and adventure all share the same start line.

The announcement follows a stand-out 2025 race, widely regarded as one of the most successful editions in recent years. Despite cautious forecasts in the build-up, sailors were rewarded with fast, enjoyable conditions, packed start lines and an atmosphere that spread well beyond the water.

Cowes came alive. From the Royal Yacht Squadron start line watched by crowds along the seafront, to the hum of activity around Cowes Parade and the Island Sailing Club itself, the event once again proved its unique ability to unite sailors and spectators alike.
For many crews, 2025 was a reminder of why they keep coming back — and for others, a nudge to finally commit to the challenge in 2026.
Race Director Dave Atkinson reflected on the scale and energy of the event as preparations begin for next summer.
“It’s hard to believe that in just five weeks’ time we’ll be opening registrations for the 2026 Round the Island Race,” he said. “Time flies, and next year’s race will be here before we know it.”

“The last few months have given the Race Team time to reflect on what was a really special day. The weather turned out far better than expected, and while the forecast may have put some sailors off, it was a fantastic race and a huge improvement on 2024.”

“Every year, seeing all those boats lining up at the Royal Yacht Squadron, with crowds watching from the shore, is incredibly special. I never tire of the buzz race day brings. Cowes comes alive — from the Race Village on the Parade to the Island Sailing Club, where we manage the race and welcome sailors throughout the weekend.”
While competition is fierce on the water, the Round the Island Race has always been about more than results.
“Whether you’re racing, cruising, or cheering from the shoreline, Round the Island is about bringing people together,” Atkinson added.

That ethos extends to the event’s charitable partnerships. In 2025, the race proudly supported Wetwheels Hamble, a charity providing life-changing on-water experiences for people with disabilities. The Island Sailing Club has confirmed its continued support of Wetwheels into 2026, reinforcing the event’s commitment to accessibility and inclusion within sailing.

With demand consistently high, sailors are encouraged to mark 23 January in their calendars. The early-bird entry rate, available until 13 February, offers a significant saving and is expected to sell quickly.

From classic yachts and performance cruisers to cutting-edge race machines, the Round the Island Race remains one of the most exhilarating and democratic sporting events in the UK — a rare occasion where thousands of sailors share the same course, same tide and same ambition.
For veterans, it’s a tradition. For newcomers, it’s a rite of passage. For everyone involved, it’s a day that lingers long after the finish gun.
Fifty miles. One island. Thousands of stories — waiting to be written.
Sailors can register their interest now to receive updates and reminders ahead of entry opening by visiting www.roundtheisland.org.uk .
tags: Round the Island early bird entry

title: The Ocean Race 2027 — Where Offshore Sailing Meets Its Ultimate Reckoning
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: The Ocean Race 2027
summary: A 14,000-Mile Opening Statement: The Ocean Race 2027 Raises the Bar from Alicante to Auckland With less than a year to go, The Ocean Race has fired a clear warning shot across the bows of the offshore world. When the fleet leaves Alicante on 17 January 2027, crews won’t be easing into the race — they’ll be thrown straight into the longest opening leg in the event’s 53-year history.
body: The distance: 14,000 nautical miles. The message: this is not a warm-up — this is the real thing.

From the Mediterranean start line, the fully-crewed IMOCA fleet will race south through the Atlantic, round the Cape of Good Hope, across the Southern Ocean, and into the Pacific — all in one colossal opening leg. It is a passage that will test navigation, engineering, psychology and teamwork long before the race rhythm has a chance to settle.

“As it has for more than 50 years, The Ocean Race represents the pinnacle of professional offshore sailing,” said Richard Brisius, Race Chairman. “The 2027 edition raises the bar once again. The opening leg to Auckland is a statement of intent — this is offshore racing at its most extreme and most thrilling.”
The opening leg alone would stand as a lifetime achievement for most sailors. For The Ocean Race, it is merely the beginning.

Team Malizia skipper Boris Herrmann captured the sentiment felt across the fleet. “This is an amazing way to start The Ocean Race — an epic leg that takes us halfway around the world. This is what we love: time at sea, racing against the best, taking on big challenges. This is where you learn about yourself and your teammates, and forge bonds that last a lifetime.”

Alicante once again serves as the Puerto de Salida, hosting the start for the sixth consecutive edition — more than any other city in race history. For the Valencian Community, the connection runs deeper than sport.

“It is very exciting to see the fleet set sail from Alicante once again,” said Marián Cano, Regional Minister for Innovation, Industry, Trade and Tourism. “As the Puerto de Salida for this monumental leg, we will showcase our maritime heritage, our international outlook, and our commitment to ocean health and education.”

Alicante Mayor Luis Barcala echoed that pride: “The Ocean Race gives our city enormous international visibility and economic impact. But it also carries a social and educational mission that reaches far beyond the finish line.”

For the sailors, there are few arrivals that carry the weight of Auckland. Known worldwide as the City of Sails, it will host the race for the 12th time, welcoming the fleet to a place steeped in offshore legend — from Sir Peter Blake to Grant Dalton, Mike ‘Moose’ Sanderson, and Peter Burling.

“This leg between Alicante and Auckland is going to be incredible,” said Kojiro Shiraishi, skipper of DMG MORI Sailing Team. “Crossing the Equator, entering the Southern Ocean, all in a single fully-crewed leg — it’s hugely challenging and dynamic. With a new boat, experience and preparation will be everything.”
Former race winner Mike Sanderson summed up the emotional pull: “Racing into New Zealand was always a highlight. You knew you were arriving somewhere with a deep connection to the sport.”

New Zealand’s leaders are equally enthusiastic. Tourism Minister Louise Upston promised “a warm Kiwi welcome after an epic leg,” while Auckland Mayor Wayne Brown highlighted the lasting benefits of hosting one of sailing’s greatest spectacles.

From Auckland, the fleet will head to Itajaí, one of the race’s most passionate stopover ports, before returning to the Northern Hemisphere. Further stopovers in the United States and Europe will be confirmed, before a dramatic Mediterranean phase, transit through the Suez Canal, and a Grand Finale sprint to AMAALA on the Red Sea — a bold new finishing destination that underscores the race’s global ambition.

Sailed aboard the world’s fastest fully-crewed offshore boats — the IMOCA class — The Ocean Race remains the most physically and mentally demanding team event in sport. Weeks at sea, relentless competition, and conditions ranging from equatorial calms to Southern Ocean violence leave no hiding place.

“There is no racing quite like The Ocean Race,” said Rosalin Kuiper. “You’re racing with and against the best sailors in the world, on the best boats, in the hardest conditions imaginable. It’s the absolute pinnacle of offshore sailing.”

The 2027 edition reinforces the race’s commitment to mixed-gender crews, with every team carrying at least one female sailor at all times — not as a gesture, but as a statement about performance at the highest level.

Technological advances will bring fans closer to the action than ever. The OnboardLive system, trialled during The Ocean Race Europe, will provide near-constant connectivity between boats, race HQ and audiences worldwide — delivering raw, unfiltered insight into life on board.

Beyond the competition, The Ocean Race continues to lead on sustainability through its Racing for the Ocean programme. As teams circle the planet, they also act as ambassadors and data collectors, carrying scientific instruments to measure ocean health, microplastics and climate indicators in some of the world’s most remote waters.
The Race’s global ocean education programme — already active in 90 countries — will expand further ahead of 2027, translated into 18 languages, reaching millions of young people worldwide.

“We race on the ocean, but we also race for the ocean,” said Lucy Hunt, Ocean Impact Director. “Our sailors witness the ocean’s beauty and fragility firsthand. That gives our platform real power — and real responsibility.”
With the start now less than a year away, anticipation is building fast. Teams are training, boats are evolving, and the route is sharpening into focus.
Fourteen thousand miles. One opening leg. No easing in.
The Ocean Race 2027 is coming — and it will ask everything.

For the sailors, there are few arrivals that carry the weight of Auckland. Known worldwide as the City of Sails, it will host the race for the 12th time, welcoming the fleet to a place steeped in offshore legend — from Sir Peter Blake to Grant Dalton, Mike ‘Moose’ Sanderson, and Peter Burling.

“This leg between Alicante and Auckland is going to be incredible,” said Kojiro Shiraishi, skipper of DMG MORI Sailing Team. “Crossing the Equator, entering the Southern Ocean, all in a single fully-crewed leg — it’s hugely challenging and dynamic. With a new boat, experience and preparation will be everything.”
Former race winner Mike Sanderson summed up the emotional pull: “Racing into New Zealand was always a highlight. You knew you were arriving somewhere with a deep connection to the sport.”

New Zealand’s leaders are equally enthusiastic. Tourism Minister Louise Upston promised “a warm Kiwi welcome after an epic leg,” while Auckland Mayor Wayne Brown highlighted the lasting benefits of hosting one of sailing’s greatest spectacles.

From Auckland, the fleet will head to Itajaí, one of the race’s most passionate stopover ports, before returning to the Northern Hemisphere. Further stopovers in the United States and Europe will be confirmed, before a dramatic Mediterranean phase, transit through the Suez Canal, and a Grand Finale sprint to AMAALA on the Red Sea — a bold new finishing destination that underscores the race’s global ambition.

Sailed aboard the world’s fastest fully-crewed offshore boats — the IMOCA class — The Ocean Race remains the most physically and mentally demanding team event in sport. Weeks at sea, relentless competition, and conditions ranging from equatorial calms to Southern Ocean violence leave no hiding place.

“There is no racing quite like The Ocean Race,” said Rosalin Kuiper. “You’re racing with and against the best sailors in the world, on the best boats, in the hardest conditions imaginable. It’s the absolute pinnacle of offshore sailing.”

The 2027 edition reinforces the race’s commitment to mixed-gender crews, with every team carrying at least one female sailor at all times — not as a gesture, but as a statement about performance at the highest level.

Technological advances will bring fans closer to the action than ever. The OnboardLive system, trialled during The Ocean Race Europe, will provide near-constant connectivity between boats, race HQ and audiences worldwide — delivering raw, unfiltered insight into life on board.

Beyond the competition, The Ocean Race continues to lead on sustainability through its Racing for the Ocean programme. As teams circle the planet, they also act as ambassadors and data collectors, carrying scientific instruments to measure ocean health, microplastics and climate indicators in some of the world’s most remote waters.
The Race’s global ocean education programme — already active in 90 countries — will expand further ahead of 2027, translated into 18 languages, reaching millions of young people worldwide.

“We race on the ocean, but we also race for the ocean,” said Lucy Hunt, Ocean Impact Director. “Our sailors witness the ocean’s beauty and fragility firsthand. That gives our platform real power — and real responsibility.”
With the start now less than a year away, anticipation is building fast. Teams are training, boats are evolving, and the route is sharpening into focus.
Fourteen thousand miles. One opening leg. No easing in.
The Ocean Race 2027 is coming — and it will ask everything.

title: Corsair Trimarans Converge on San Francisco Bay for the Thrills of the 2026 Corsair National Championship
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Corsair Trimarans Converge on San Francisco Bay for the Thrills of the 2026 Corsair National Championship
summary: Welcoming competitors from around the globe, the 2026 Corsair National Championship promises a thrilling set of races in the iconic San Francisco Bay.
body: Mark your calendars, sailors, for the 2026 Corsair National Championship is making a splash on San Francisco Bay. Organised by Corsair Marine International along with Encinal Yacht Club and the Bay Area Multihull Association, this premier sailing event is expected to churn the waters between July 17 to 19 in 2026. Encapsulating one of the most vibrant communities of trimaran enthusiasts globally, the championship is a riveting rendezvous point where efficient design, lightweight construction, and performance mesh together for a spectacle of competitive sailing. This year's edition promises no less, with its iconic venue taking centre stage. San Francisco Bay, with its steady summer breeze, strong tidal currents, and shrewd racecourses across the South and Central Bay, is a sailing arena that calls for excellent preparation, precision, and confident helming. As a highlight, the three-day program will include a long-distance race along with multiple buoy races, all set in classic July Bay conditions. An opportunity stands for everyone in this championship, with separate competitions designated for Corsair-manufactured trimarans, including Farrier-designed models, and non-Corsair multihulls, all of them racing under PHRF or one-design scoring. Yet, the Corsair National Championship is more than a fiery race. It's a symphony of camaraderie, an intersection of likeminded sailing aficionados - all passionate about harmony between design and performance. The fleet's diversity, spanning from long-standing Farrier-designed trimarans to the latest Corsair models, echoes years of arduous development centered on sailing efficiency and practical capability. Speaking of the latest models, the championship welcomes Corsair and Farrier-designed trimarans across all classes, flaunting the brand's evolving performance heritage. Models such as the accessible yet fast Corsair 760, the modern agile Corsair 880 and the versatile Corsair 970, capable of both offshore passages and competitive races, epitomise the spirit of Corsair trimarans - unyielding tenacity and a deep commitment to sailing excellence.

title: Exciting news in the yachting world: there's a significant price decrease for the impressive 44m Pendennis catamaran, Hemisphere!
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Exciting news in the yachting world: there's a significant price decrease for the impressive 44m Pendennis catamaran, Hemisphere!
summary: The exhilarating sailing catamaran, Hemisphere, has undergone a notable price reduction of €7,500,000, stirring waves in the industry.
body: Propelling ripples of anticipation across the nautical market is the news of an attractive price adjustment on the 44.2 metre long 'Hemisphere', a stunning sailing catamaran sculpted by masterful boat builders at Pendennis. This sailing sensation, now available for the corrected price of €38,500,000, emanates luxury and adventure, promising voyages of unparalleled comfort and excitement, under the captivating charm of Michael Leach's interior design.

Designed by the illustrious Marc Van Peteghem and Vincent Lauriot Prévost of VPLP Design, Hemisphere brings new meaning to the phrase 'off-the-beaten-track exploration'. It offers spacious accommodation for up to 12 guests across its two 'principal suites', two double rooms and a twin room replete with additional Pullman berths. The boat's extensive saloon and deck areas are as wide and welcoming as those of a 70-metre monohull, and provide lodgings for up to 10 staff, facilitating a voyage of utter relaxation and joy.

The Hemisphere, known for its successful charter history, also comes well-stocked with a plethora of watersports gear to entertain its guests. Below the cantilevered overhang, deck dining and relaxation spaces offer a calming retreat, while the beckoning trampoline at the bow promises adventurous guests an exhilarating sensation of speed over the water.

With a cruising range of 3,850 nautical miles, Hemisphere's dual 490hp Caterpillar engines provide it with a top speed of 13 knots and cruising speed of 11 knots. Combine this with its shallow draught of 3.1 meters, this vessel opens up a world of sailing possibilities, especially in regions with reefs and atolls. Not forgetting, a custom 16.4-metre sports fishing tender for additional shore excursions and fishing ventures can be opened for discussion during the negotiation.

Proudly displayed in the British Virgin Isles, Hemisphere, the world's largest catamaran, stands eager and ready for its next journey. This is an opportune moment for yacht lovers to consider this great investment, designed for thrill-seekers and luxury lovers alike. As a durable, sophisticated, and awe-inspiring vessel, Hemisphere offers a passport to a whole new world of maritime exploration.

title: Embrace the Sea: Second and Third Flexplorer 165 Hulls Head to Outfitting, Promising Customized Luxury at Its Finest
author: Old Sea Dogs

summary: The second and third hulls of Cantiere delle Marche's venerable 50.3-metre Flexplorer 165 series are now headed for outfitting, promising bespoke features and unmatched sea-going opulence.
body: The allure of the open sea beckons as Italian shipyard Cantiere delle Marche (CdM) pushes the limits of luxury with the second and third hulls from its eminent Flexplorer 165 series. Now entering the outfitting phase, these releases promise unique, owner-specific features, encapsulating premier seafaring opulence.

Equally impressive is the yacht's reinforced upper deck, which stands ready to accommodate an EC130 helicopter. Inside, British studio Design Unlimited infuses the interior with refined elegance, ensuring an equally high level of attention to detail.

The third Flexplorer 165 hull showcases equal levels of customization, accommodating an owner's passion for fishing. To cater to this unique need, the yacht will carry a large Dual Console tender, effectively launched by an upgraded 4.5-ton capacity crane. Additional modifications include two other tenders and a flexible interior layout, perfect for a large family. Standout features include a convertible skylounge, an extra cabin, and a lower deck cabin that can transform into a private lounge. This striking degree of personalization encapsulates the spirit of these remarkable sea vessels, setting a new benchmark in yachting luxury and bespoke preferences.
As they undertake their outfitting journey, these exceptional Flexplorer 165 hulls promise to be the embodiment of the CdM brand - bold, innovative, and redefining the boundaries of seafaring luxury.

title: Brave the Elements: A Comparative Review of 2026's Best Waterproof Boating Jackets Exposed to Rigorous Testing
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Brave the Elements: A Comparative Review of 2026's Best Waterproof Boating Jackets Exposed to Rigorous Testing
summary: Seeking the best maritime armour for those wild, wet weather adventures? The best new waterproof boating jackets of 2026, tried and tested here for you.
body: The editor of MBY, Hugo Andreae, along with a few brave souls, ditched the lab and picked up a pressure washer to put six offshore jackets under a literal splash test. This approach originated from the old maritime adage: “There is no such thing as bad weather, only the wrong clothes.” It’s all about getting hands-on and empathy-driven – replacing tidy spec sheets and lab tests with real-world conditions and user experiences.

A day of ruthless hosing resulted in a deeply insightful selection of the best waterproof jackets available today. The stellar four included Gill's OS2 Offshore Jacket, hailed for its perfect blend of snugness and efficiency, the Lomo Coriolis Sailing Jacket, the envy-inspiring budget option, Musto’s BR3 Pertex Offshore Jacket, the fashion-forward performer, and lastly, the tech-centric Helly Hansen Aegir Race Jacket.
The Scotland based Lomo's Coriolis Sailing Jacket offered unbeatable value for money, delivering a 20,000mm waterproof rating and reinforced elbows at a surprisingly affordable price.
Musto's BR3 Pertex Offshore Jacket blended style and functionality. It offered lightweight mobility with soft, breathable fabric but fell slightly short in extreme spray tests’ neck protection.

The Helly Hansen Aegir Race Jacket, crafted for professional racers, used a heavy-duty waterproof zip instead of traditional storm flaps and a seamless shoulder design, a common leakage hotspot, rendering it water-solid.

These jackets offer a blend of comfort, style, and technology. Remember, when it comes to maritime adventures, it's not just about whether the jacket can withstand rough weather – it's about how it makes you feel when the storm finally settles.

title: Aquila 45 Sport Makes Waves in Marine Industry: Distinctive SUV-Influenced Styling Meets Supercraft Functionality
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Aquila 45 Sport Makes Waves in Marine Industry: Distinctive SUV-Influenced Styling Meets Supercraft Functionality
summary: Channeling the worldwide command of SUVs to the seas, the Aquila 45 Sport powercat debuts with unrivaled focus on an appealing blend of design and performance.
body: Meet Aquila 45 Sport, the new gem in the marine world. Setting its global debut at the Miami International Boat Show, this powercat is the first in a unique series created by Sino Eagle-owned Aquila Catamarans, developed in confluence with Yacht Design Works.

Taking a page from the edgy styling of contemporary SUVs, this new design is a wave of fresh air in the world of powercat standards. Beyond aesthetics, the vessel is geared towards open-air entertainment with a keen emphasis on both design and utility. Adorned with a lateral galley, a quartet of seats at the helm, and dual C-shaped dinettes that transform into sunbeds, the Aquila 45 Sport doesn't just take passengers on a ride, but an experience.

A spacious owner’s cabin awaits, boasting a plush king-sized bed, a private wet-room style heads compartment, and novel skylights for abundant natural light. While the vessel seems to lean towards couples given the layout, it's performance won't disappoint. Fitted with stepped hulls and dual 600hp Mercury Verado V12 outboards, Aquila speaks of a top speed climbing to a dizzying 45 knots, an adrenaline rush fused with a luxurious comfort.
The Aquila 45 Sport remains a visionary example of the marine industry's future, where the aesthetic allure of land's best vehicles meets the thrill and functionality of seafaring crafts.

title: Unleashing the Lion: Admiral's Cup Teams Join Pallas Capital Gold Cup, Star Sailors on the Horizon of the SSL Gold Cup Qualifying Series.
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unleashing the Lion: Admiral's Cup Teams Join Pallas Capital Gold Cup, Star Sailors on the Horizon of the SSL Gold Cup Qualifying Series.
summary: As sailing expands its horizons, the Pallas Capital Gold Cup gains an international edge with Admiral's Cup contenders and Star Sailors preparing for the upcoming SSL Gold Cup line-up.
body: The winds of change are blowing. The renowned Pallas Capital Gold Cup is set to become even more captivating this year with the inclusion of several teams from the much-acclaimed Admiral's Cup. These teams will breathe fresh international experience into the race, lending it a higher degree of prominence. One of these is the TP52 Zen, steered by Gordon Ketelby, making a triumphant return to Australian waters after what many thought was a permanent relocation to Europe. Ketelby's decision to bring Zen back down under was primarily influenced by his attraction to the Pallas Capital Gold Cup. His anticipation of the race, he said, hinged on the fact that it currently hosts some of the world's best racing competitions. He was willing to take Zen back home for just that reason. Notably, Zen comes packed with vast international experience which is expected to significantly color the Pallas Capital Gold Cup. Another expectedly exciting development is the growing connection between the TP52 and Super 40 fleets being noticed by many, including Zen's Campaign Manager, Shane Guanaria.

Parallel to these developing events is the gearing up of the Star Sailors League (SSL) for its 2026 Gold Cup. The qualification series for the competition are now coming together, with the second edition of the SSL Gold Cup due to kick off in a little over 255 days. The stage for the Grand Final, Rio de Janeiro in Brazil, will be graced by sixty-six national teams, forty of which qualify. The excitement rides high as teams continue to battle for the remaining nine spots in the upcoming qualification events.

Combined, these developments indicate a major shift in global sailing competitions. The intertwining of teams and fleets in different tournaments signifies an increasing crossover of talent and indeed, a globalization of the sailing world. One thing is certain: this infusion of international dynamism into sailing will lead to increasingly thrilling and unpredictable sea races. Bring on the races, and let's set sail.

title: Sir Francis Chichester's Gypsy Moth IV
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Gypsy Moth IV - An Iconic British Yacht
imageCaption: Gypsy Moth IV, Cowes, Isle of wight,
summary: Gypsy Moth IV is one of the most iconic yachts in British maritime history, known for her association with legendary sailor Sir Francis Chichester. Built in 1966 by Camper and Nicholsons, the 53-foot ketch was purpose-designed to help Sir Francis Chichester to attempt a remarkable feat, to sail solo around the world with just one stop. Which had never before been accomplished. Constructed using cold-moulded Honduras
body: He navigated alone through the Southern Ocean, Cape Horn, and across vast, often treacherous waters. His successful circumnavigation made Gypsy Moth IV a national treasure and Chichester a knight, knighted by Queen Elizabeth II using the very sword of Sir Francis Drake. The yacht instantly became a symbol of resilience, daring, and British seafaring excellence.

Following years of neglect, Gypsy Moth IV was eventually restored in the early 2000s thanks to a major conservation effort. She now serves both as a historic vessel and as a tool for education and youth sailing programmes. Her legacy continues to inspire generations of sailors and adventurers. Gypsy Moth IV is not only a feat of nautical design and endurance, but also a testament to the human spirit’s capacity for challenge, solitude, and discovery. For sailing enthusiasts and maritime historians alike, she represents a pivotal moment in modern ocean racing and solo navigation. Her journey marked a turning point in what individuals could achieve alone at sea, and her sleek silhouette remains a lasting tribute to one of the greatest sailing voyages of the 20th century. This photo of Gypsy Moth IV was taken while she was near Cowes, on the Isle of Wight, UK.

title: Bid Now for 2030-2031 World Sailing Championships – Showcasing Olympic Class Sailing at its Best
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Bid Now for 2030-2031 World Sailing Championships – Showcasing Olympic Class Sailing at its Best
summary: World Sailing invites all interested cities, venues, and organizations to submit their bids for the 2030-2031 World Sailing Championships, a significant Olympic qualification event.
body: World Sailing has sounded the klaxon for preliminary invites to the 2030-2031 World Sailing Championships, presenting a golden opportunity for international member national authorities, cities, and venues. The call is out to submit bids for hosting the monumental event, casting an exhilarating stage for sailors attempting to secure their position for the Brisbane 2032 Olympic Games. As The World Sailing Championships is the main qualification event for the Olympic Games, it represents the biggest gathering of Olympic-class and Para inclusive sailors globally.

The Championship events are planned to be scheduled between July 2030 and February 2031, or alternatively, between July and September 2031. By securing the bid to host this esteemed event, Cities or regions will avail the opportunity to endorse themselves to a worldwide audience while aligning with World Sailing's sustainability and gender equity goals.

The bidding process is welcoming hosts who can demonstrate a commitment to sporting excellence and state-of-the-art facilities while envisaging a sustainable event legacy. Total dedication to the detailing of the events, the state of readiness of the venue, and tangible planning for a sustainable legacy are all components of a winning bid. The deadline for expressions of interest and preliminary bids is slated for 24th April 2026, with final bid documentation due by 10th September 2026. The sailing community anticipates a thrilling countdown to what promises to be a momentous global event on the sporting calendar.

title: Project Zurich Splashes into Scene: Damen Yachting's Third Amels 80 Superyacht Sets Sail
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Project Zurich Splashes into Scene: Damen Yachting's Third Amels 80 Superyacht Sets Sail
summary: Project Zurich, the third unit in the Amels 80 series by Damen Yachting, has hit the water, bringing a wave of unique features that make her stand out in the luxury yachting arena.
body: Dutch shipyard Damen Yachting has introduced the third of its prestigious Amels 80 series, dubbed Project Zurich. This 80-meter marvel has taken her maiden voyage from the yard's secondary construction facility at Vlissingen-East. She will now proceed to the Damen Yachting headquarters in Vlissingen City to receive the finishing outfitting touches, with delivery expected later in the year.

Project Zurich, which was sold just months after its initial debut in March 2022, boasts a series of impressive and unique features, ensuring a distinguished position alongside her two sister yachts. The second unit of the series, the dolphin-blue hued Netto II, took her plunge two weeks prior to Project Zurich. The inaugural yacht of the series, Pangea, was successfully delivered last year.

Project Zurich outshines with a bright and custom interior design, a stark and refreshing contrast from the Sinot Yacht Architecture & Design themes of the first two hulls. She will accommodate up to 14 guests alongside her 21 crew members, providing ample space for recreational gets and tender storage areas. Delivering such grandeur requires precision and focus from all parties involved, as expressed by Sander Peeters, project manager at Damen Yachting.

Amid the high-stakes orchestration of large-scale yachting projects, it was reported that Damen Yachting is currently juggling eight yachts that are either on order or under active construction, five of which belong to the Amels 80 series.

title: Intense Final Races Decided Winners at Howth Yacht Club Dinghy Frostbites Spring Series
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Intense Final Races Decided Winners at Howth Yacht Club Dinghy Frostbites Spring Series
summary: The Howth Yacht Club Dinghy Frostbites Spring Series ended with tense competition and thrilling racing, deciding final standings across multiple fleets.
body: The curtain fell upon the Howth Yacht Club Dinghy Frostbites Spring Series on the 1st March 2026, with a heart-stopping finish that saw final standings determined in various fleets. The series, consisting of 14 races over seven weekends, saw sailors fight off challenging weather conditions and strong rivals to claim their respective victories.

After a fierce competition and tense anticipation, series leader Daragh Sheridan outshone his competition with two captivating race victories using his RS Aero. His closest competition played out a gritty performance, holding down the fort with consistent second-place finishes, reinforcing the intense competition the series brought this year. Notably, the PY Fleet displayed a spectrum of various boat types, each punctuating the races with their unique strength and strategy. It was a testament to the range and diversity of the fleet, confirming that no single design could dominate the waters.

title: Infinite Voyage III: Italian Elegance Meets Modern Performance in the 32m Azimut Motor Yacht Now Seeking New Owner
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Infinite Voyage III: Italian Elegance Meets Modern Performance in the 32m Azimut Motor Yacht Now Seeking New Owner
summary: The 32-metre Azimut Grande motor yacht, Infinite Voyage III, radiates Italian craftsmanship paired with contemporary innovations and is now listed for sale.
body: Raise the anchor, set the sails - an incredible seafaring adventure awaits the new owner of the Infinite Voyage III. This magnificent 32-metre Azimut Grande motor yacht, delivered in 2022 by the venerable Italian yard, blends contemporary design and elite Italian craftsmanship against a backdrop of unyielding performance.

Designed by Pierluigi Ausonio PLANA, the yacht displays a wide-body design, complete with a sharp carbon fibre superstructure that bolsters interior volume without compromising an iota on performance. Outfitted by Stefano Righini, her exterior design is streamlined, elegant and sleek. Step inside and marvel at the Salvagni Architetti interior; it’s a grand display of Italian style, featuring curved forms and warm tones offset by the yacht's generous 7.3-metre beam and full-height windows that allow for abundant natural light.

The lower deck houses two VIP cabins furnished with queen-sized beds alongside two twin cabins endowed with additional Pullman berths. Each cabin comes with bespoke entertainment systems and ensuite facilities.

Infinite Voyage III boasts a spacious main saloon, with cream sofas arranged in an inviting U-formation and a progressive entertainment system featuring a large retractable television. Forwards, guests may dine on a glossy oval table, comfortably seating 10.

The yacht shines in its ability to socialise and entertain. With its expansive flybridge, azimut yacht offers alfresco dining for 10, a BBQ module and a bar with integrated refrigeration. Disco lights have been artfully installed in the hardtop for those who love basks in moonlight parties.

Complementing her entertainment offerings, the yacht accommodated a side garage with a tender garage and ample space for a collection of water toys. Twin MTU engines provide a speed of 12 knots with twin electric fin stabilisers to assure comfort during voyages.
Currently moored in the idyllic waters of Phuket, Thailand, Infinite Voyage III lists at a selling price of €8,500,000, offering luxury, elegance and performance for the discerning seafarer.

title: Dutch Yard Moonen Yachts Celebrate Milestone with Ninth 122 Martinique Model, YN207, Entering Outfitting Stage
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Dutch Yard Moonen Yachts Celebrate Milestone with Ninth 122 Martinique Model, YN207, Entering Outfitting Stage
summary: Moonen Yachts announces a major milestone with its 122 Martinique model – the hull and superstructure of the ninth unit, YN207, have been joined.
body: Moonen Yachts, a highly respected Dutch yard, continues to make waves in the yacht-making industry with the joining of the hull and superstructure on its ninth 122 Martinique model – YN207. This significant milestone marks a new phase for the 37.4-metre build, pushing it one step further into the realms of the sea.

The grand moment was celebrated at a ceremony hosted by Moonen's facilities, nestled in North Brabant in the serene southern part of the Netherlands. The pairing of the hull and superstructure indicates the vessel's move into the outfitting phase. This important stage involves the installation of all the technical systems, along with the distinctive interior design elements, before the yacht moves into the final commissioning and sea trial phase. The build's delivery, eagerly awaited, is scheduled for January 2027.

The new-build sparked intrigue only three months ago when Moonen confirmed its sale to American owners. Matthew Stone and Richard Gray, Moonen's dedicated global sales representatives, stood for the yard in this significant deal. Meanwhile, Alex G. Clarke from the esteemed Denison Yachting, deftly introduced the buyer.

The emblematic exterior design of the yacht is masterly crafted by René Van Der Velden, while Diana Yacht Design is responsible for the completion of the naval architecture. This exclusive unit will be the second in the series to showcase an interior by Vripack, a design that promises to deliver a serene and light-filled environment, as per the yard's vision. This yacht is expected to include several custom additions, including a Jacuzzi on the sundeck and a full-beam owner's suite with forward-facing windows, delivering a unique connection to the sea.

It's clear as to why the Martinique model is hugely popular amongst yacht enthusiasts, with its flexible layouts and luxurious arrangements. The king of the seas, YN207, is set to join its series sister, the seventh unit 'Ad Astra,' delivered in October of the previous year, making for a family of truly grand, marine automobiles.

title: Elevating the Superyacht Industry: The Make Your Mark Marketing retreat sparks conversation on enhancing brand image
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Elevating the Superyacht Industry: The Make Your Mark Marketing retreat sparks conversation on enhancing brand image
summary: Amidst a bustling agenda of events, a unique ‘Superyacht Marketing Retreat’ is set to take place, offering industry marketing leaders an innovative platform for engagement and growth.
body: Beneath the buzz of forthcoming boat shows and industry forums, a distinctive experience emerges for those invested in the world of superyachts. The event, metaphorically christened as the 'Make Your Mark Superyacht Marketing Retreat', invites busy marketing forerunners from the industry to immerse themselves in a serene setting, collaboratively navigating the choppy waters of branding, strategy, digital reach, and luxury experiences. Make Your Mark has been meticulously crafted with the intent of fostering not just engagement, but also stimulating fresh ideas and innovative approaches to market the intricate industry of superyachts.

Highlighting the retreat’s agenda is a keynote session and workshop run by Thomas Kolster of the Goodvertising Agency, focusing on the craft of communicating to the uninitiated. Another notable initiative is the team-building effort helmed by the Superyacht Life Foundation and the Water Revolution Foundation, urging participants to explore intelligent and creative communication methods.

The day concludes with a keynote delivered by Bas Maase and Camilo Simöes from The Ocean Clean Up, an organization that has garnered global attention with its initiatives to clean and preserve ocean spaces. Their powerful storytelling, coupled with authenticity and originality, has pinpointed them as an inspiring model for shaping effective marketing strategies that transcend the yachts themselves and touch upon broader narratives, thus creating a stronger connect with audiences.

There are still opportunities to be part of this game-changing venture and contribute to the future of superyacht industry marketing. This inspiring and thought-provoking experience also promises fun and camaraderie, creating a synergy of industry experts keen to dismantle the status quo and make braver strides in marketing. In the navigation of the superyacht industry, this is indeed a marker buoy of change.

title: Amsterdam's 'Make Your Mark': A Pivotal Gathering to Reframe the Superyacht Industry’s Narrative
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Amsterdam's 'Make Your Mark': A Pivotal Gathering to Reframe the Superyacht Industry’s Narrative
summary: Amidst a bustling calendar of events, a groundbreaking superyacht experience, dubbed 'Make Your Mark', is set to occur in Amsterdam. This is not merely a gathering—it's a marketing symposium for leaders in the superyacht sector.
body: In the heart of Amsterdam, thought leaders and mavens of the superyacht industry are set to converge for a distinctive experience. Bearing the promising title 'Make Your Mark', this strategic symposium is far from your average boat show. Instead, it is a carefully curated marketing and branding retreat, designed for those at the forefront of our industry.

This retreat seeks to create an atmosphere conducive to exchanging ideas, voicing concerns, and building a vibrant network amongst peers. It serves as a platform to engage with luminaries from diverse fields including branding, digital marketing, luxury goods, content creation, and experiential marketing.

Superyacht Life Foundation and the Water Revolution Foundation will spearhead a dynamic team-building workshop at the event. This strategic forum lays the groundwork for future dialogue about how we communicate the value we offer to future clients and the world at large.

Equally noteworthy is the engagement with The Ocean Clean Up, a global initiative aimed at sanitising the world's oceans and reducing floating waste—extremely relevant to our superyacht playgrounds. Representatives from the initiative will provide unique insights on their marketing strategies and success stories, embodying an invaluable learning opportunity.

'Make Your Mark' goes beyond showcasing the yachts and their exotic locations—it pushes for authentic storytelling that dives deeper and resonates more strongly. The mission here is to challenge the status quo, incite change and embrace a marketing approach that aligns with the vibrant ethos of the superyacht community.

With a few seats still available, there's a chance to be part of this transformative gathering. Designed to be equal parts inspiring and insightful, it is an opportunity to immerse oneself in a dynamic community that wholeheartedly aims to uplift the image and future of the superyacht industry.

title: Nana II: The Gem of Overmarine Yachts Finds a New Owner in An Off-market Deal
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Nana II: The Gem of Overmarine Yachts Finds a New Owner in An Off-market Deal
summary: The formidable 45.3-metre Overmarine motor yacht Nana II has been sold in an exclusive deal, with the buyer represented by renowned brokers.
body: In the world of luxury yachts, very few names garner as much respect and admiration as Overmarine. Marking another milestone in their illustrious journey, they recently announced the sale of their 45.3-metre motor yacht, Nana II, in an off-market deal. The buyer was represented by renowned brokers Crispin Baynes and Thibault Roi of Burgess, with special acknowledgement going to Stefano Arlunno and Ivan Adzic from Overmarine for their unwavering support.

Delivered by the esteemed Italian yard in 2023, Nana II boasts being one of the exclusive quartet of Mangusta GranSport 45 yachts. She's a stunning marvel of naval architecture, developed by Pierluigi Ausonio PLANA, and thoughtfully designed by Alberto Mancini. Her accommodation provides a luxurious experience, housing 10 guests across five bright and spacious cabins. The master suite is exceptional, built around the theme of natural light and connection with the sea, and even features a fully automated foldable terrace.

Nana II also features a beach club that can be opened up in place of the garage, moved forward to provide guests a dedicated area for relaxation at sea-level. Backed by the power of three MTU diesel engines, she stands her ground with a top speed of 26 knots and a cruising range of a whopping 3,000 nautical miles.

Well-known in the yachting circles for their exquisite creations, Overmarine Group once again proves their mettle with the sale of Nana II, cementing their position at the pinnacle of luxury marine craft.

title: Sanctuary Cove International Boat Show 2026: Australia’s Ultimate On-Water Showcase Returns
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Sanctuary Cove International Boat Show 2026
imageCredit: © The Sanctuary Cove International Boat Show
imageCaption: The Sanctuary Cove International Boat Show
summary: From 21–24 May 2026, the Sanctuary Cove International Boat Show returns to Australia’s Gold Coast for its 37th edition, transforming the iconic marina village into four days of world-class boating, luxury lifestyle and waterfront celebration.
body: SCIBS has long been the Southern Hemisphere’s most influential on-water boat show — and 2026 promises to raise the bar again. Across the precincts, visitors can expect the latest marine innovation, premium yachts and powerboats, cutting-edge technology, gourmet food, live entertainment and a festival atmosphere designed for seasoned boat owners, first-time buyers and families alike.
With tickets going on sale in February 2026, demand is expected to be strong. Subscribers will receive early alerts and access to exclusive offers, making it worth getting on the list early.
Sanctuary Cove Marina: the beating heart of SCIBS

At the centre of the show sits the spectacular Sanctuary Cove Marina, where hundreds of vessels line the pontoons in one of the most impressive in-water displays anywhere in the world. Luxury motor yachts, sailing yachts, performance craft and trailer boats sit side by side, offering a rare opportunity to step aboard, compare designs and speak directly with global marine brands and industry experts.
This is where craftsmanship meets scale — where innovation is tangible and Australia’s boating industry puts its best foot forward.

For those looking to experience SCIBS in style, the Lagoon Beach Club delivers an elevated social escape. Set against the shimmering lagoon pool at the InterContinental Sanctuary Cove Resort, this premium precinct blends all-day gourmet grazing, handcrafted cocktails and live entertainment with full access to the show.
Palm trees sway, glasses clink, and conversations flow — making it the undisputed social hub of the event and a favourite among exhibitors, owners and lifestyle-led visitors.
Sanctuary Cove Village: luxury, leisure and atmosphere

Beyond the pontoons, Sanctuary Cove Village brings a different rhythm to the show. Boutique shopping, fine dining, pop-up activations and live performances spill through the village streets, offering a place to pause, indulge and soak up the SCIBS atmosphere.
It’s where boating culture meets luxury living — and where many visitors find themselves lingering longer than planned.

SCIBS isn’t just about big boats. The Sports, Leisure & Fishing precincts are a magnet for anglers, adventurers and outdoor enthusiasts, showcasing the latest gear, tackle, watersports equipment, accessories and apparel.

With live demonstrations, expert advice and hands-on product launches, these areas bring the thrill of on-water adventure ashore — and often send visitors home with new plans, new kit and new ambitions.
Whether you’re buying, browsing, dreaming or simply enjoying the spectacle, Sanctuary Cove International Boat Show 2026 is more than an exhibition — it’s a celebration of life on the water.
Four days. One iconic marina. And a showcase that defines boating in Australia.
