title: Damen Yachting launches its third Amels 80 series superyacht, Project Zurich
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Damen Yachting launches its third Amels 80 series superyacht, Project Zurich
summary: The Dutch shipyard, Damen Yachting, has announced the launch of its third 80-metre superyacht in the Amels 80 series, fondly known as the Project Zurich.
body: Dutch shipyard Damen Yachting is celebrating the successful launch of its third superyacht in the Amels 80 series, referred to as Project Zurich. The 80-metre new build made its debut in Vlissingen-East, one of Damen Yachting's construction facilities, before being transported to their main headquarters in Vlissingen City for final outfitting. There's already much excitement about its scheduled delivery later this year.

Once mere blueprints, Project Zurich is now a reality after only a few months since it was first announced in March 2022. It boasts unique features that distinguish it from its sisterships, setting a new standard in yacht design and luxury.

Project Zurich follows closely on the heels of the second unit, the exquisite 'dolphin blue' Netto II, which made its first splash just a fortnight ago. The premier unit of the series, Pangea, was delivered in October last year.

Project Zurich also introduces a new direction in interior design, departing from the Sinot Yacht Architecture & Design interiors of the first two hulls. An award-winning design team has crafted unique, custom interiors, though their identity remains confidential. They've planned spacious accommodation for 14 guests in seven cabins and 21 crew, and lots of storage for toys and tenders.

Sander Peeters, project manager at Damen Yachting, acknowledged the skills and the meticulous planning that goes into managing a project of this magnitude: 'Launching our third Amels 80 marks an important milestone for everyone involved alike,' he said. 'Yachts of this scale require meticulous planning, craftsmanship and close coordination across our teams, together with the owner’s representative.' He emphasized the importance of precision and focus in managing multiple projects of this size.

Damen Yachting has eight yachts on order or actively under construction, with five from the Amels 80 builds. The launch of Project Zurich marks another impressive achievement for Damen Yachting and an exciting addition to the luxury yachting scene.

title: Navigating the Waves: Vaikobi's Deep Dive into the Thrilling World of 18ft Skiff Racing
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Navigating the Waves: Vaikobi's Deep Dive into the Thrilling World of 18ft Skiff Racing
summary: Unveiling the engaging saga of Vaikobi's dedicated partnership with Australia's iconic 18ft Skiff Racing Championship, highlighting a transcendent relationship beyond mere sponsorship.
body: From the adrenaline pumping starting lines to the white-knuckled finish, the 18ft Skiff Racing World Championship has seen a fascinating relationship flourish with Vaikobi, a pioneering water sports apparel organisation. The sails of the impressive 27-boat fleet carry the Vaikobi crest into the marine battleground as teams dash towards the coveted title.

In the ever-evolving domain of Australian 18ft Skiff Racing, sponsorships have crucially shaped the class since the mid-1960s. However, Vaikobi's involvement transcends conventional sponsorships. They're not just a logo on the fleet. Vaikobi, under the stewardship of their charismatic CEO, Pat Langley, has embarked on a journey of deep-seated passion for the sport, earning respect far and wide.

The standout achievement came when Pat Langley took Vaikobi's involvement to a whole new helm, sponsoring Kirk Mitchell and his team for the 2023-24 season. The same triumvirate will sail under the Vaikobi banner in the much-anticipated 2026 Giltinan World Championship.

Their commitment is echoed by five-time Giltinan World 18ft Skiff champion, Trent Barnabas, who praises Langley's passionate involvement. Vaikobi's commitment does not stop at the racing waters. They actively collaborate with teams to trial and refine their top-grade sailing gear.

Beyond the roaring waters, Pat Langley's engagement extends to commentary stints for SailMedia, further highlighting his passion for sailing. It offers a transparent glimpse into Vaikobi's deep-seated love for sailing and their ambitions of remaining a valued partner of the racing world.

title: Hercules, a 1907 Steam Tugboat
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Hercules, a 1907 Steam Tugboat
summary: If you have some time to spend in San Francisco its worth visiting the pier to see Hercules, a 1907 Steam Tugboat. Step off San Francisco’s buzzing Embarcadero and head toward Hyde Street Pier. Between artisan coffee stands and tech millionaires in Allbirds, there lies a different world entirely — quieter, riveted in steel, and powered not by code but by coal and willpower. Moored against the salty breeze is Hercules
body: You can smell the history in her hull — iron, oil, and a touch of varnished mahogany. Once the hardest-working tug on the West Coast, Hercules was never built to be beautiful, but beauty is often found in purpose. And this 151-foot icon is overflowing with it.

Hercules was born in Camden, New Jersey, crafted by John H. Dialogue & Sons — think of it as the Rolls-Royce of American tugboat builders. She was no dainty harbor taxi. She was built for the open ocean, towing full-rigged sailing ships, barges, and log rafts through swells and storms. Her first act? Towing her sister ship Goliah 14,000 miles around Cape Horn to San Francisco. A flex, by any standard.
With her triple-expansion steam engine, riveted steel hull, and minimalist profile, Hercules was a fusion of raw utility and industrial grace. She didn’t shout. She thrummed.

After arriving in California, Hercules quickly became the Pacific’s power broker. She towed caissons for the Panama Canal, sailed under military service during wartime, and later moonlighted as a workhorse for the Western Pacific Railroad — ferrying rail cars across the Bay when bridges were fantasy and ferries ruled logistics.
Her power was unmatched. Her reputation, unchallenged. When you needed something moved that couldn’t move itself — you called Hercules.

Retired in 1962, Hercules could have faded into history — dismantled, forgotten, written off as industrial detritus. But like the best legends, she was rescued in the nick of time. In 1975, she was acquired by California’s State Park Foundation and later transferred to the National Park Service, who treated her not as salvage but as sculpture.
Painstakingly restored, she became a National Historic Landmark in 1986 — a title she wears like a well-cut naval coat. And these days, you can step aboard.

Strolling her teak deck feels like stepping into a Scorsese flashback — all clanking pistons and polished brass. Below deck, her engine room looks like the cover of a Tom Waits album. Gleaming pressure gauges. Endless piping. The hypnotic rhythm of steam and steel. It’s a visceral experience, deeply analog, deliciously unhurried.
In a world of sleek megayachts and sterile, silent electric motors, Hercules is something else: timeless, tactile, unfiltered. She’s a gentleman’s machine — made not for comfort, but for command.

And while you’re sipping espresso in the Marina or heading to a tasting menu in SoMa, Hercules remains tethered to the pier — a patient reminder of San Francisco’s tougher, bolder past. She doesn’t ask for attention. She earns it. She’s grit in a tailored coat. Industrial poetry.

So next time you’re in the city, skip the obvious. Wander to the waterfront. Look for the mast, the black funnel, the red trim. Climb aboard Hercules — where the stories are real, the iron is hot, and the past doesn’t whisper. It thunders.

title: The Pascoe Duo's Epic Journey Through the Winds: Seldén Sailjuice Winter Series 2025-26 Uncovered
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Pascoe Duo's Epic Journey Through the Winds: Seldén Sailjuice Winter Series 2025-26 Uncovered
summary: Benjamin and Sam Pascoe conquer the waves and weather in the thrilling Seldén Sailjuice Winter Series 2025-26, proving teamwork makes the dream work.
body: Join us as we unravel the enchanting tale of Benjamin and Sam Pascoe in last year's Seldén Sailjuice Winter Series, a stirring saga of brotherly camaraderie and not to mention, an absolute thrill ride. With the cold gusts of the Datchet Flyer serving as their first challenge in months, the duo smartly maneuvered their hefty 2000, only to experience a couple of capsizes due to rusty skills. Yet, as they say, every stumble is a step forward. And onward they went, their spirits unbroken. The young Benjamin, at helm, learning the art of efficient sailing in every fall and rise. While the light winds at the Sailjuice events proved to be a difficult adversary, with Benjamin laboring significantly to gain speed, the lack of strong winds was indeed a blessing in disguise. Their fast competitors were hampered by the conditions, and the Pasco duo managed to pull themselves up to joint-second overall. The Bloody Mary hurdle saw Sam making a mess of the start, causing a collision with the pin-end buoy. However, their determination never faltered. Displaying an exhilarating comeback, they led their category halfway through, proving yet again their competence and resilence. The Seldén Sailjuice Winter Series 2025-26 wasn't just a racing event for the Pascoe brothers, but a winter of learning, growth, and most importantly, fun-filled adventure.

title: The Seldén Sailjuice Winter Series: An Engaging Tale of Two Brothers and a Captivating Account of the DF95 Winter Series
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Seldén Sailjuice Winter Series: An Engaging Tale of Two Brothers and a Captivating Account of the DF95 Winter Series
summary: Immerse into a riveting account of brotherly sailing camaraderie in the Seldén Sailjuice Winter Series and an exciting chronicle of the DF95 Winter Series at East Kent Radio Sailing Club.
body: In the exhilarating world of sailing, the winter season has brought with it an exciting series of competitions. A tale of two siblings, Benjamin and Sam Pascoe, stands out as they bravely faced the challenges of the Seldén Sailjuice Winter Series 2025-26. Their journey was a blend of skills, strategy, and kinship, overriding the adversities thrown their way, with the Datchet Flyer being their first real challenge. Despite a few setbacks due to inexperience and stormy weathers, the brothers managed to make a comeback, turning these obstacles into stepping stones for victory.

Meanwhile, the DF95 Winter Series at East Kent Radio Sailing Club saw an amalgamation of fierce rivalry and camaraderie amongst seasoned sailors. The competition was stiff with numerous race wins shared among the top half of the fleet. Mike Brand started powerfully; however, Jim La Roche soon caught up, led at lunch, and went on to secure his event lead. A stellar moment belonged to novice John Barker, who bagged a leading position, signifying how the sport continues to inspire and induce thrill and excitement among its practitioners and followers.

Culminating on a high, the event saw Mike narrowly snatch victory from Jim in an exhilarating showdown that will be remembered for times to come. These winter series races serve to remind us how sailing is not just about boats and winds. It's about the relentless spirit, the thrill of competition, the joy of camaraderie, the tactful handling of nature's unpredictability, and the stories woven through each of these elements making every sail more than just a race.

title: Finnish Brand Saxdor Yachts Acquired by Malibu Boats, Laying Groundwork for a US Expansion
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Finnish Brand Saxdor Yachts Acquired by Malibu Boats, Laying Groundwork for a US Expansion
summary: US company Malibu Boats Inc. recently acquired Finnish brand Saxdor Yachts in a deal believed to be worth around €150 million.
body: In a thrilling crossover of brands and nations, Finnish sportsboat heavyweight Saxdor Yachts has been purchased by Malibu Boats Inc. The acquisition, worth an estimated €150 million, not only cements Malibu's presence in the global boat market but also forges an exciting new avenue for the adventurous, outboard powered boats created by Saxdor.

Established in 2019 by entrepreneurial mastermind Sakari Mattila, Saxdor Yachts fast rose to fame as Europe's rapid-growth boat brand. With a contagious infusion of innovative design and value for money, its day boats and weekenders quickly became the go-to choice for those seeking practical yet stylish marine adventure.

On the other side of the Atlantic, Malibu Boats, a distinguished boat builder, boasts an impressive and diverse portfolio of brands, including Cobalt and Pursuit. With Saxdor under its umbrella, the US company now holds a significant stake in the rapidly expanding market for outboard powered Adventure Boats.

In an exclusive exchange with Motor Boat & Yachting, a reflective Mattila confessed mixed feelings about his decision. While the company continues to stay financially robust, the time seemed right, given Mattila's age and personal circumstances, to pass the torch. The transition allows him to focus his genius on boat design, as opposed to company administration.
The industry watches with eager anticipation to see the evolution of Saxdor Yachts in the American market and the creative influence of Mattila in the years to come.

title: Ralph Hadley: A Bright Star Emerging on the Sailing Horizon Gears Up for an Eventful New Year
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Ralph Hadley: A Bright Star Emerging on the Sailing Horizon Gears Up for an Eventful New Year
summary: Riding on the wave of an amazing 2025 season, young sailor Ralph Hadley shares his aspirations for the year 2026.
body: Ralph Hadley is not just another young sailor. Having proven himself as a rising star in the 2025 season with commendable performances in the Topper class, Hadley is poised to make 2026 another year to remember. Passionate about sailing, he sails from Whitstable Yacht Club and Tankerton Bay Sailing Club when home in Kent, both being in close proximity to the Barton factory. His diligent preparation for the year ahead has already begun, undeterred by the uncooperative weather. Hadley's name is inscribed with the elite National Performance Squad and the Regional London and South East Performance Squad, which ensures that he rubs shoulders with the best in the country regularly. In 2025, he narrowly missed the podium at the World Championship event held in Medemblik, Netherlands. Reflecting back on the event, he remembers how he maintained the third position for the majority of the week, just to finish in the fourth place. But instead of letting it dampen his spirits, it has become the fuel that drives his goal in 2026 - to improve his World Championship standing. As Hadley navigates his career, he has several role models to look up to, but Micky Beckett, who started in Toppers like Hadley and eventually climbed to the top, holds a special place. Hadley's aspirations are clear, 'work his way through the ILCA rigs and maybe make it to the British Sailing Team.' As a Barton Rising Star, Hadley takes advantage of the Barton kicker, mainsheet ratchet block, downhaul and outhaul, attributing them for their durability and performance impact to his sailing career. In the end, 2026 promises to be a year filled with challenges and opportunities for Ralph Hadley, and the sails are set for his journey towards the coveted podium.

title: Introducing Tykun X: A Glorious Blend of Military Grit and Superyacht Style
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Introducing Tykun X: A Glorious Blend of Military Grit and Superyacht Style
summary: Straddling the terrain between robustness and sophistication, the Tykun X, a bespoke 10-meter chase boat, epitomises high-performance practicality.
body: Those yearning for a chase boat that skilfully straddles the rugged and refined need look no further than the Tykun X. Born from Italian parent company MED Group’s extensive military background, the Tykun X oozes suave superyacht style whilst boasting hardcore strength.

This 10-meter chase boat delivers a knockout performance, offering a steady cruising range between 25 and 40 knots, and hurtling to a claimed top speed of 55 knots, aided by a pair of 400hp, Mercury outboards.

The commercial hull, proven and robust, ensures composed and serene handling. The Tykun X champions a practical design with its single-level walkaround decks, elevated freeboard, and closed transom, while the thick foam rubbing strake, reverse screen, and optional canvases enclosing the helm solidify the craft's workmanlike charm.

As a chase boat, the Tykun X strikes a favorable balance between a large RIB and a sportsboat. Its specifications include a LOA of 34ft 5in (10.50m), a beam of 9ft 6in (2.90m), twin Mercury Verado 400hp outboards, and a maximum speed of 55 knots.
The Tykun X is an inspired choice for those who want a blend of top-notch performance, military-grade durability, and superyacht-style luxury.

title: Relishing the Rich Diversity of UK Dinghy Classes at the RYA Dinghy & Watersports Show 2026
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Relishing the Rich Diversity of UK Dinghy Classes at the RYA Dinghy & Watersports Show 2026
summary: The RYA Dinghy & Watersports Show 2026 marked a significant year for the distinct variety of anniversary classes on display for over 9,000 attendees.
body: The RYA Dinghy & Watersports Show 2026, held at the Farnborough International Exhibition & Conference Centre over the February 21 - 22 weekend, drew in upwards of 9,000 visitors from across the globe. The event presented a vast feast of maritime intrigue, with a unique mosaic of dinghy sailing classes highlighted.

In the UK, the diversity among dinghy sailing classes is both a blessing and a challenge for the sport. It offers enthusiasts a rich pick of options suited to their personal tastes and skills. However, there's a downside — diminished 'One Design' racing opportunities at club level due to a focus on the Portsmouth Yardstick (PY) or the Great Lakes handicap systems.

As the event illustrated, changes within dinghy categories vary. Some classes allow slight developments over the years, while others retain a virtually unchanged design. Meanwhile, Strict One Design classes resist alterations entirely. Evolutionary modifications, where applied, help extend a class's relevance and longevity or ease sailing without rendering existing models obsolete. Thus, the RYA Dinghy & Watersports Show acted as a fascinating study of sea sport evolution over time.

For more information about these spectacular classes, visit www.yachtsandyachting.com/class . There, you can dive into numerous reports and photographs, and find links to the respective class association websites.

title: Founder and CEO of The Italian Sea Group, Giovanni Costantino, Assumes the Title of Board’s Chairman
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Founder and CEO of The Italian Sea Group, Giovanni Costantino, Assumes the Title of Board’s Chairman
summary: The Italian Sea Group (TISG) is shifting its leadership line-up, as founder and CEO Giovanni Costantino takes on a new role.
body: The winds of change are once again filling the sails at The Italian Sea Group. The company has announced that its founder and CEO, Giovanni Costantino, is donning a new captain's cap as he takes on the role of Chairman of the Board of Directors. The move, effective immediately, is a testament to Constantino's expansive vision and expert steerage which have navigated The Italian Sea Group through the rocky waters of the boating industry.

While the dust is settling at The Italian Sea Group after the leadership shuffle, one fact remains crystal clear: Constantino's presence at the helm ensures a confident course set, an experienced hand at the tiller, and a bright future for the renowned company. With this leadership change, both adherents and critics will watch to see if the wily CEO and now Chairman can navigate the company into even more successful waters.

title: Competitive Tides in Globe40 Race as Teams Overcome Challenges of Cape Horn and Windy Southern Atlantic.
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Competitive Tides in Globe40 Race as Teams Overcome Challenges of Cape Horn and Windy Southern Atlantic.
summary: The Globe40 sailing race gets increasingly thrilling as competitors cross major milestones, notably Cape Horn, battling unpredictable and harsh weather conditions and keeping the nautical community on the edge of their seats.
body: On February 28, 2026, the sailing world watched with bated breath as the Globe40 sailing race escalated in intensity with the competitors rounding Cape Horn. This iconic landmark, infamous for its hazardous sailing conditions, marks a significant milestone in the race. The first boat to round this symbolically significant landmark was CREDIT MUTUEL, doing so on February 26, at a spell-binding 13:03 UTC.

Throughout the day, a tense procession of six crews coursed past the lonely shores of Chile's pride - Cape Horn. This included BARCO BRASIL (14:26 UTC), FREE DOM (10 minutes after BARCO BRASIL), then BELGIUM OCEAN RACING (15:51 UTC) and WILSON AROUND THE WORLD (17:04 UTC), creating a riveting spectacle for sailing enthusiasts.

The skippers of the Globe40 second edition found the journey around Cape Horn emotionally charged due to the landmark's historic implications - the end of the Pacific Ocean leg and the return to the South Atlantic. Pointing their boats towards this clear milestone on their route back to Europe, the competitors felt a sense of achievement that was shared openly and warmly amongst each other and their respective support teams.

However, relief and a sense of achievement was short-lived. Rounding Cape Horn was followed by challenging conditions in the South Atlantic – regions of whimsical calm, sudden blows from low-pressure systems of the Andes Mountains, and volatile weather that keeps even the most seasoned sailors on their toes. The fleet is currently facing a relentless low-pressure system from the southern parts, enduring wind speeds that test the mettle of the very best.

The spectacle of Globe40 continues to unfold, turning pages that only the sea knows. The drama brings with it great uncertainty, much like the unpredictable tides themselves, keeping various sailing fans around the world hooked, waiting to see what the ocean will toss up next.

title: Sirena Yachts Embarks on Exciting New Chapter with Two Majestic Premieres - Sirena 118 and Superyachts 42m
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Sirena Yachts Embarks on Exciting New Chapter with Two Majestic Premieres - Sirena 118 and Superyachts 42m
summary: Sirena Yachts, the Turkish shipyard, renowned for luxurious sailing experiences prepares to mark its 20th anniversary with two world premieres scheduled for late summer.
body: The seafaring world eagerly anticipates a milestone year for Sirena Yachts, the prestigious Turkish shipyard, setting sail into its 20th anniversary year. It delineates an exciting chapter in its illustrious history. Two grand premieres, the Sirena 118 and the Sirena Superyachts 42m, are scheduled for late summer launches, underlining Sirena's embarkation into the world of larger yachts. Initially focused on composite construction, fundamentally practical materials for building performance-oriented vessels, the brand now boldly sails into the steel and aluminium future.

The Superyachts 42m, on the other hand, mirrors a classic design bolstered by contemporary thought. The vessel embarks on a different endeavour, standing as the cornerstone for Sirena’s new steel and aluminium range. Unlike the composite centric Sirena 118, the Superyachts 42m underpins a different paradigm of luxurious seafaring experiences.

Together, these premieres spotlight Sirena's evolution and decisive movement into the fraternity of larger yachts. With an impressive portfolio consisting of Sirena 48, 60, 68, 78 and 88, it's a natural transition for the brand. As Sirena Yachts crews up for this new challenge, their voyage marks the intersection of technology, craftsmanship and luxury, making waves in the yachting world.

title: The World’s Largest Sailing Ship
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: The World’s Largest Sailing Ship
summary: Step aboard the Golden Horizon, the planet’s most majestic square-rigged sailing ship, a 2021 masterpiece that marries vintage nautical swagger with cutting-edge sophistication. Crafted by Croatia’s Brodosplit Shipyard under the visionary eye of Polish naval architect Zygmunt Choreń, this five-masted barque stretches an impressive 162 meters, with an 18.5-meter beam and a robust 8,770 gross tonnage.
body: A near-replica of the legendary 1913 France II windjammer, it was originally envisioned as Flying Clipper for Star Clippers, but a legal tussle handed it to Tradewind Voyages, who christened it with a name as bold as its silhouette. Launched into a world still reeling from COVID-19 delays, it’s a statement in steel and sail—90% of its 4,500-tonne frame sourced from Ukraine’s Metinvest, built to conquer Arctic chills or Caribbean heatwaves.

The design is a triumph of form and function. Its high-strength steel hull, forged with computer-cut precision and coated in anti-corrosive paint, supports 36 cross sails spanning 6,345 square meters—enough to blanket a football pitch. The tallest mast soars 63 meters, a 24-ton colossus, propelling the ship to a breezy 20 knots under wind power, outpacing its 16-knot engine cruise. Sustainability is the chic new black here: Golden Horizon aims to sail engine-free for 70% of its voyages, slashing fuel use with dual electric systems and a 800-cubic-meter diesel reserve for those 2,000-nautical-mile safety nets. It’s luxury with a conscience, a nod to the eco-warriors who still crave the high life.

Inside, it’s a love letter to the Golden Age of clippers, reimagined for the Instagram era. With 140 cabins across four decks—think porthole nooks to deluxe suites with balconies, fireplaces, and butler service—it sleeps 272 passengers and 159 crew in polished wood and brass elegance, accented by smart HDTVs and Wi-Fi. The two-deck dining room serves buffet breakfasts and lunches, with waiter-served dinners featuring vegan options, while the Horizon Bar offers al fresco vibes. Three pools, including a PADI-certified diving pool, a spa with a snow room and jacuzzi, and a water-sports marina for kayaking, cater to the jet-set adventurer. It’s a floating playground where relaxation meets adrenaline.

The itineraries are as curated as a fashion week runway, tracing historic trade routes from the UK’s Harwich and Glasgow to Iceland’s fjords, Jakarta’s Silk Route, and the Caribbean’s sun-kissed shores. Yet, its journey hasn’t been smooth—financial storms, a £100 million sale listing in 2022, and sanctions on a Russian-linked bank tied to Brodosplit have rocked its course. A 2021 Dover seizure over Star Clippers’ claims added drama, but its allure persists.

Sadly the Golden Horizon’s future teeters on negotiations, yet its promise endures. This isn’t just a ship—it’s a statement, blending the romance of tall ships with a sustainable edge. For the discerning traveler, it’s the ultimate voyage where luxury and legacy set sail together.

title: Invincible Mari-Cha III Yacht Breaks Waves and Records: Now Available for Purchase
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Invincible Mari-Cha III Yacht Breaks Waves and Records: Now Available for Purchase
summary: The daringly innovative, 44.7-metre Mari-Cha III Sailing Yacht is now up for sale, looking for a buyer seeking an unparalleled sailing experience.
body: Engaging the senses and evoking unparalleled expansiveness, the 44.7-metre Sensation sailing yacht Mari-Cha III is on the market. Back in 1997, this high-performance ketch splashed onto the scene, earning rave reviews for its cutting-edge technology and a 49-metre main mast from Southern Spars. It wasn't long before its fame rose like its huge mast.\

Delivered to legendary acclaim and refitted in 2010, every inch of Mari-Cha III exudes the charm harnessed by Bernard Gallay of BGYB. As the vessel beckons prospective buyers, its current asking price stands at a cool €8,500,000.\

Mari-Cha III refuses to compromise on aesthetics. Its interiors are a nod to the Edwardian style; rich, elegant fabrics and marble finishings set it apart from the competition. The main saloon and formal dining area, spacious and swathed in white panelling in the opulent interiors, bring a sense of brightness and openness to the space.\

Giving a warm welcome to its guests, the yacht's four cabins, including an indulgent full-beam master suite with private deck access, are designed for uncompromising comfort. They carry just the right hint of drama; they reflect the sea's infiniteness and the endless skies, making it a home away from home on the ocean wave.\

What makes Mari-Cha III truly unforgettable is its legacy of peak performance. Back in 1998, it stunned the sailing world by breaking the Atlantic crossing record, achieving a thrilling 17 knots in a mere 14 knots of true wind. This racing history is palpable in every inch of the yacht, marking it as an embodiment of sailing prowess and strength.\

Aside from the yacht's near-legendary status, the new owner can look forward to the luxury of a Kevlar tender and the reliable power of twin Northern Lights generators. Currently lying in Villanova Marina, Spain, stepping onboard Mari-Cha III means stepping into a grand history of sailing excellence. This ship is ready to sail new waters, looking for its next great voyage.

title: In an Exciting Move, Cork Week Expands Race Eligibility, Welcoming More Coastal Fleet Competitors
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: In an Exciting Move, Cork Week Expands Race Eligibility, Welcoming More Coastal Fleet Competitors
summary: Cork Week 2026 coasts towards expansion, allowing larger fleet participation in its celebrated Coastal Fleet race.
body: In a thrilling move, the Royal Cork Yacht Club has announced an expansion in the entry eligibility for the Coastal Fleet race at the much-anticipated Cork Week 2026, set to take place between 6th and 10th July. This pioneering decision is a direct response to a chorus of competitor feedback, widening the playing field to accommodate all boats measuring 30ft and longer. The significant change caters precisely to those owners yearning to race with spinnakers, while nurturing a preference for longer, offshore-style courses over resource-heavy, 'round-the-cans' racing found on shorter, multi-mark courses. This sweeping wave of change has brought forth a slew of key updates for 2026's Coastal Fleet race. Dedicated Corinthian Prizes will be presented to the top amateur crews sailing within the fleet, a move that will indeed bring a new dimension of competition and camaraderie to the event. Moreover, the race will now implement flexible course designs. Depending on the final roster of participants, the class may be split to offer tailored courses that align with the performance profiles of the swelling fleet. Already, organisers report a robust interest in this year's renewal, with a rising tide of 58 entries confirmed already, a number that significantly outpaces previous years. Among noteworthy participants is none other than seasoned sailor John Treanor, returning with the NMD 43 'Cristina', and another previous French Admiral's cup yacht, 'Albator'. Fans will no doubt remember John from his victorious campaign with the J/112e 'Valentina' at Cork Week 2024. The current roster of entrants is available for yacht enthusiasts and fascinated spectators alike on the official Cork Week 2026 Entries Page. As the wind billows and the tides turn, we wait with eager anticipation to see how these changes will shape the much-loved, high-seas adventure that is Cork Week.

title: Custom Line Shakes the Yachting World with Navetta 35: First of its Kind in Modern Yachting Universe
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Custom Line Shakes the Yachting World with Navetta 35: First of its Kind in Modern Yachting Universe
summary: Italian shipyard, Custom Line, unveils the Navetta 35, pushing the boundaries of the modern yachting experience and style.
body: Italian shipyard, a brand of the revered Ferretti Group, Custom Line, has pioneered a fascinating leap in the world of yachting with the introduction of its latest addition—the Navetta 35. This showstopper is pegged as a 'natural evolution' of its predecessor, the Nautika 33 model, albeit with a notable surge in modernity and an unmistakable focus on sensitivity towards the environment and contemporary cruising regulations.

Slated for release in autumn 2026, the first 34.5-metre unit of this high-velocity miracle is already in production at the Ferretti Group Superyacht Yard in the beautiful port-city of Ancona. The shipyard functionaries have also hinted at the in-build status of the second and third hulls of this astonishing model which are already booked, showcasing the high degree of anticipation and excitement this new model brings.

According to the shipyard’s ethos, the Navetta 35 prioritises 'comfort, liveability and aesthetic refinement', and has borrowed several intricate design featues from the larger Navetta 38 model, including the emphasis on promoting wellbeing on the water. Despite its slightly diminished size, this newcomer is generously endowed with over 300 square metres of spectacular interior and exterior spaces across three expansive decks offering an incomparable experiencing of luxury on water.

A striking feature of the Navetta 35 is the unique positioning of the exterior staircase. The design, which deviates from the traditional central positioning to aft, has been moved to amidships, generating additional space on the aft decks and running optimal functionality throughout the yacht. Complementing this, the staircase inside has also been shifted to a starboard position, ingeniously concealed behind a reflective surface, thereby giving rise to a spacious, well-lit corridor sans obstructions.

title: Sailing Rivers and Canals: An Expert's Advice on Inland Voyages
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Sailing Rivers and Canals: An Expert's Advice on Inland Voyages
summary: Sailing inland waterways demands exclusive skills and understanding. This piece unravels expert tips on navigating unique challenges of canals and rivers.
body: Inland sailing is a passion that comes its share of challenges. Rivers and canals each presenting a unique set of circumstances requiring extra attention whilst afloat. Man-made canals often have little or no water flow, and rely on locks to change water levels. Rivers, on the other hand, always witness a downstream flow which concludes at another river or perhaps a tidal location. They too rely on locks to accommodate boats when the water level change is too monumental. These structures are often accompanied by a weir and sluices to manage the level and flow of the navigable river.

Traffic during the peak of the boating season can test a sailor's patience, especially in commercial routes with additional regulations known as CEVNI. Additionally, the shoaling at river edges necessitates caution when mooring along banks or rounding river bends. The rivers' insides are often shallow, leading to potential congestion in tight spaces. Our expert suggests maintaining a position roughly in the centre, moving to starboard when required. Be aware of floating debris or hidden hazards, particularly after heavy rainfall and flooding. Overhanging branches could also pose problems during manoeuvring.

While we will delve into navigating locks in a future discussion, the principal hurdle you are likely to face on inland routes are bridges. Often, bridges cross at an angle due to the orientation of overhead roads, forcing a careful alignment of the vessel. The ideal method is to place your boat straight between the bridge's piers and engage minimum power, maintaining steerage. Too slow, and the swirling water can push you towards the piers; too fast, and any incorrect calculation might make for an expensive blunder.

In conclusion, inland cruising is an elevated art, a skill that is earned through observation, practice, and respect for the unique factors that rivers and canals present. Stay alert, obey signs, and remain mindful of conditions and obstacles. Happy cruising!

title: The 13th Monaco Energy Boat Challenge is Bursting with Ingenuity as 43 Teams from 21 Nations Unleash Their Marine Technologies
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The 13th Monaco Energy Boat Challenge is Bursting with Ingenuity as 43 Teams from 21 Nations Unleash Their Marine Technologies
summary: The waters off the coast of Monaco will bubble with innovation on 8-11th July 2026 as the 13th Monaco Energy Boat Challenge returns at the renowned Yacht Club de Monaco.
body: Coming to life in the scintillating waters off Monaco's coast is the Monaco Energy Boat Challenge. Marking its 13th edition, this annual event serves as an incubator of ideas and innovation for tomorrow's marine propulsion and fuel. Students, universities, technical colleges, and industry professionals from 21 nations have been drawn to this 'outdoor laboratory,' creating a platform for exploration and innovation for alternative propulsion systems and fuels in the boating sector. In an engaging competition, participants present an array of ingenious solutions; from advanced-stage optimisations to newly tested prototypes. The endeavors of these young inventors and experienced professionals have resulted in creations such as predictive energy management from HydroVinci in France, and bio-sourced materials from Team Sea Sakthi in India. With four unique categories to compete in, participants can push boundaries in dedicated areas. The AI Class, premiering in 2025, exists to drive artificial intelligence for boats. The Energy Class and SeaLab Class enable testing of electric, hybrid, and emerging energy sources. The Open Sea Class serves as an exhibition of the industry's zero-emission creations, with its wing open for entries until mid-May. Off water, participants engage in Tech Talks , the Corporate Mentoring Programme , and a Job Forum , valuable platforms for interacting with professionals in the maritime sector and gaining further industry insights. With this event, the bustling city-state of Monaco cements its commitment to a sustainable maritime sector, emphasizing ingenuity and collaboration in its drive to become the Capital of Advanced Yachting.

author: Old Sea Dogs

summary: Get set for a spectacular show as the Superyacht Cup Palma turns thirty, welcoming a thrilling new performance multihull class to the starting line.

Delivering high-seas excitement on a grander scale than ever before, this edition will inaugurate a thrilling performance multihull class, complementing the regatta’s traditional superyacht classes, J Class, Café Racer, and Corinthian categories. In 2025, the spectacular 24-metre Wally sailing yacht Rose made history, defending her title and becoming the first yacht to clinch three consecutive overall victories. This year's competition promises no less excitement, with formidable contenders ready to challenge her supremacy, including the Baltic 108 Win Win - a former Superyacht Cup Palma victor, and last year's Class A champion, the 35-metre Southern Wind Gelliceaux. Other promising entrants include the J Class yachts Rainbow and Svea, along with Baltic 68 Café Racers Ganesha and Scorpione di Mare. Adding further intrigue to this high-stakes contest, several newcomers will be joining the Palma regatta for the first time. They include the Wally 100 Inco, the Swan 90S Hummingbird (formerly Leonara), and performance multihulls Highland Fling 18 and Allegra. The competitive spirit of this revered regatta is matched only by its adaptability and commitment to enticing both returning and new competitors. In the words of event director, Kate Branagh, 'Superyacht Cup Palma has a long and remarkable history, balancing evolving with the superyacht racing world and consistently welcoming new and loyal yachts to Palma’s unique setting.' With such a distinguished lineup and the thrilling addition of the new class, this 30th edition of the Superyacht Cup Palma is already promising to be a regatta for the ages.

author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover Harken's High-tech ILCA Kicker: A Leap in Marine Racing Gear Unveiled at RYA Dinghy & Watersports Show 2026

This innovative piece of marine gear showcases the evolution of the ILCA kicker from its origin as a simplistic 3:1 purchase system to a highly sophisticated racing component.

Harken Professional, David Brown, delighted the audience with a tour around the advanced features of the new Harken ILCA (which is also referred to as a Laser kicker or vang system). One of the major highlights of the new system is the inclusion of Harken Zircon blocks - known as the most efficient, low-friction, and high-load racing blocks for small boats.

With its unveiling, the Harken ILCA kicker promises to revolutionize marine racing gear, pointing towards an exciting future of sailing marked by phenomenal technological advancement and superior performance on the water.

title: New Cycles, New Crews: The 49er, 49erFX and Nacra 17 Fleets Reset for LA 2028
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: New Cycles, New Crews: The 49er, 49erFX and Nacra 17 Fleets Reset for LA 2028
summary: From Olympic farewells to new partnerships, the skiff and multihull classes are already reshaping the road to Los Angeles The off-season rarely means downtime in the skiff and multihull world. As the new Olympic cycle gathers momentum, the 49er, 49erFX and Nacra 17 fleets are already in motion—closing chapters, forming new combinations and quietly laying the foundations for LA 2028.
body: Across the globe, programmes are evolving fast. Some of the sport’s most familiar names are stepping away from full-time Olympic life, others are re-emerging with new teammates, and training hubs are lighting up as teams chase sunshine, speed and rhythm. The next four-year story is being written now.

After a standout Paris 2024 campaign, silver medallists Isaac McHardie and Will McKenzie have stepped away from full-time Olympic campaigning. It marks the end of a hugely successful partnership—but not the end of New Zealand’s influence in the 49er class.

Life has moved quickly for both sailors. McKenzie is now based in Sydney, working full-time as an engineer, while McHardie has completed his building apprenticeship and is now a qualified carpenter. Away from the racecourse, both have also hit major personal milestones, with engagements announced and weddings on the horizon.

Yet neither has drifted far from performance sailing. McKenzie has joined the New Zealand Black Foils in a shoreside support role, working alongside former 49er coach Matt Steven. Combining engineering know-how with elite skiff experience, he’ll travel with the team contributing to performance analysis and race support.

Their legacy remains clear. A deep domestic fleet is already active, Nationals are approaching, and a new generation of Kiwi skiff sailors is stepping confidently into the space McHardie and McKenzie helped define.
With winter biting in the north, many teams have gone chasing sun—and the usual hotspots are buzzing.

Lanzarote is once again a focal point for the 49er fleet, hosting a strong mix of German, French and Polish teams. On the water are Paris Olympians Jakob Meggendorfer and Andreas Spranger (GER), alongside France’s Erwan Fischer and Clément Péquin, with Polish crews including Staniul and Sztorch adding depth and pressure.

Across the multihulls, several Nacra 17 teams are clocking serious mileage in Lanzarote, including world championship bronze medallists Scipio and Willemijn, joined by the Austrian Nacra squad as European programmes ramp up early.
In the 49erFX fleet, German teams have spread across Sicily, Cagliari, Vilamoura and New Zealand, deliberately rotating venues to build versatility in waves, chop and lighter Mediterranean airs.

Meanwhile, the wider foiling world overlaps constantly. Several Nacra 17 sailors are sharpening racecraft elsewhere, with the Liddell brothers currently leading a 66-boat fleet at the F18 World Championship—a reminder of how transferable foiling skills have become across classes.
A familiar name is back on the FX circuit. Rui Qi Cecilia Low has returned to 49erFX racing, teaming up with Elizabeth Lin.

Low brings deep experience: an Olympic campaign at Tokyo 2020, where she and Kimberly Lim became the first Singaporean sailors to qualify for an Olympic medal race, plus an Asian Games gold medal and multiple World Cup appearances. The new partnership has been years in the making, and both sailors are already eyeing major regional targets as the long LA 2028 road begins.
Her return adds maturity and momentum to a fleet that continues to deepen in both quality and global reach.

After five intense years together, Lara Granier and Amélie Riou have formally closed their Olympic campaign. Following a narrow miss on Paris selection and a period of reflection after Cagliari, the pair chose to end a project defined by growth, resilience and shared highs on and off the water.

But endings in this fleet are rarely final. Riou is already back on the start line, forming a new partnership with Manon Peyre. With the 49erFX World Championship in Quiberon in May as their first major milestone, the focus is firmly on building foundations—fast.

Early-cycle movement continues in the multihull fleet. Sarah Newberry-Moore has announced a new Nacra 17 partnership with Hoël Menard, officially launching their LA 2028 campaign. Training is already underway, underlining just how quickly new combinations are forming across the class.
Oceanbridge Sail Auckland Regatta: early signals

The Oceanbridge Sail Auckland Regatta delivered strong international racing across the 49er fleet. Overall victory went to Seb Menzies and George Lee Rush, with Swiss Olympians and SailGP sailors Sebastian Schneiter and Arno De Planta second. Mattias Coutts and Oscar Gunn completed the podium, while Americans Nevin Snow and Ian Macdiarmid placed fourth.
All are expected back on the line for the New Zealand 49er Nationals, before heading to the Trofeo Princesa Sofia in Palma this March—one of the first true measuring sticks of the new cycle.

And finally, a name that always draws attention. Ruggero Tita has been dropping hints about a potential return to the Nacra 17. Nothing official—yet. But in a fleet where combinations shift quickly and ambition never rests, the sailing world is watching closely to see what shape that next move might take.
