imageAlt: Under Wraps Until Now, Rossinavi's 53m Superyacht 'Heed' Finally Sees the Light of Day
summary: Italian shipyard Rossinavi has finally lifted the wraps on its highly secretive, state-of-the-art 52.7-metre superyacht 'Heed'.
body: The unveiling of a new custom-built superyacht on the market is always a momentous occasion, and this is certainly the case for 'Heed', born out of the Italian shipyard Rossinavi. The project, previously known only by its hull name FR052, has been kept closely under wraps throughout its construction since January 2024. But now, Rossinavi is ready to introduce the world to its newly completed, gleaming masterpiece. Augmented by a fast-displacement hull, the all-aluminium superyacht has been expertly designed by Alberto Mancini, with interiors by Achille Salvagni Architetti and naval architecture by Arrabito Naval Architects. It’s the result of a close and energetic partnership with the owner, who has worked tirelessly alongside Matty Zadnikar of SeaNet SuperYachts to bring 'Heed' to life. With stunning clean architectural lines and understated volumes, 'Heed' is designed to look both elegant at rest, and dynamic underway with a sleek, metallic grey hull completing the yacht's sophisticated geometric profile. 'Heed' is not just about her stylish exteriors, but also about the ultimate luxury lifestyle she offers on-board. The custom-build features an aft beach club with a pool and drop-down side platforms for an expansive social space, and a faultlessly designed look-out point on the observation deck. The yacht's interiors consist of a spacious, fully-glazed main saloon leading out to a panoramic dining area on the aft deck, perfect for an al fresco dining experience. What’s more, the entire upper deck is exclusively dedicated to the owner with a forward owner's suite, private outdoor lounge, and a forward pool with a counter-current. The superyacht’s metallic grey hull adds a touch of elegance, playing beautifully with the light and shadows throughout the day. Federico Rossi, Chief Operating Officer of Rossinavi, has shared his excitement about this stimulating project, which he believes will leave its mark on the yacht market. Heed also features an onboard battery system, enabling operation at anchor with the generators switched off, for a serene and quiet experience at sea. Amongst the key specifications are a 9.1-metre beam and a draught of 2.5 metres. 'Heed' stands as a testament to Rossinavi's commitment to functionality and style, solidifying the shipyard's leading position in the industry. In a world of superyachts, 'Heed' is a game-changer.

title: The Inaugural Antigua Racing Cup Arrives in 2026
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: The Inaugural Antigua Racing Cup Arrives in 2026
summary: Antigua, West Indies – The Caribbean sailing calendar is set for a thrilling new addition. As Antigua proudly prepares to launch its inaugural Regatta Month next year, the flagship event—the Antigua Racing Cup (ARC)—is already generating significant buzz, poised to redefine high-performance yacht racing in the region.
body: Scheduled to debut from April 9–12, 2026, the Antigua Racing Cup represents a bold vision. It’s where the spirit of pure, unadulterated competition and professional race management converges with the vibrant energy of Antigua’s sailing community and the island’s world-famous hospitality. This isn't just another regatta; it's a dedicated commitment to the core racing sailor.

A Strategic Vision for a Premier Sailing Destination In a strategic move to cement Antigua and Barbuda’s reputation as the marquee destination for Caribbean sailing, the Ministry of Tourism and the Antigua & Barbuda Tourism Authority, in collaboration with the National Parks Authority and a coalition of local marine stakeholders, is launching this innovative event. The Antigua Racing Cup is designed to build directly upon the legendary foundation of Antigua Sailing Week, creating a powerful, month-long focus on the sport that extends the island's sailing season and appeal.

By confidently steering into the wind, the ARC is crafted to complement its iconic predecessor while decisively carving out its own unique identity as a "sailors-first" regatta focused on high-level performance.
Positioned off Antigua’s spectacular south coast, with the historic Nelson’s Dockyard serving as both the operational base and social heart of the event, the ARC promises an unparalleled experience.

A Racing-Centric Format, Pure and Simple: The ARC is meticulously designed around the explicit needs of dedicated racing sailors. Every element—from the challenging course configurations and optimised scheduling to the world-class race management—is fine-tuned for performance, fairness, and competitive integrity. The South Coast’s Natural Amphitheater: Antigua’s south coast provides a stunning and strategic racetrack. Known for its reliable and steady trade winds, combined with dramatic coastal seascapes, it creates the perfect natural arena for intense, tactical duels.

A UNESCO World Heritage Hub: This iconic location doubles as the vibrant Regatta Village. It offers teams a historic and breathtaking setting for all logistics, fostering camaraderie and serving as the backdrop for unforgettable post-race celebrations. Social Energy Meets Maritime Heritage: While the on-water action is the priority, the ARC understands the social soul of sailing. The Dockyard ensures this spirit thrives with lively gatherings, prestigious prize-givings, and cultural showcases that authentically highlight Antigua’s rich maritime heritage.

The significance of this new regatta extends across the entire sailing ecosystem: For Competitive Sailors: This is a rare opportunity to compete in an event designed entirely around their passion. It promises challenging courses, top-tier race management, and a community of like-minded individuals. For Antigua & Barbuda: The ARC powerfully strengthens the nation’s identity not just as a scenic cruising ground, but as a serious, premier destination for international-level yacht racing. For the Caribbean Region: It adds crucial depth and prestige to the spring racing calendar, ensuring Antigua remains the undeniable central hub for the world’s best sailors and most advanced yachts.

The Antigua Racing Cup is engineered to deliver pure competition across multiple disciplines. For monohulls, racing will be scored under both CSA and IRC rules, seamlessly managed via Nautical Cloud regatta software. This dual-scoring approach ensures a level playing field for both regional and international competitors, providing almost immediate results and comprehensive fairness. The on-water experience is equally refined. Maxis and powerful offshore multihulls will have the opportunity to stretch their legs on longer, more expansive racetracks that test speed and endurance across a wide range of wind angles. Simultaneously, smaller boats will engage in tight, tactical battles with a mix of windward/leeward and reaching leg courses that demand strategic brilliance.

Adding a layer of precision competition, dedicated One-Design divisions will be featured, including the RS Elite and Petticrow Dragon fleets, with the potential for high-performance Diam trimarans. This brings the purest form of yacht racing—where boat-for-boat tactics reign supreme—to Antigua’s ideal trade wind conditions.

With the introduction of the Antigua Racing Cup, the island further solidifies its status as the beating heart of the Caribbean sailing world. From the epic ocean-going challenge of the RORC Caribbean 600 to the timeless elegance of Antigua Classics and the world-renowned spectacle of Antigua Sailing Week, the island is synonymous with phenomenal racing conditions, warm, genuine hospitality, and an unwavering passion for the sea. The ARC is the next exciting chapter in this storied maritime legacy.

title: Boost in International Visitors as boot Düsseldorf 2026 Unveils Elite 24m+ Yachts Amid Strengthening Demand
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Boost in International Visitors as boot Düsseldorf 2026 Unveils Elite 24m+ Yachts Amid Strengthening Demand
summary: The world's premier yacht and watersports expo, boot Düsseldorf 2026, witnesses burgeoning international interest and robust demand for luxury super yachts.
body: The illustrious yacht and watersports exhibition, boot Düsseldorf, once again transformed the 16 halls of Messe Düsseldorf into a breathtaking panorama of vanguard marine industry. Occurring from January 17 to 25, the 2026 edition drew an impressive array of over 200,000 visitors from more than 110 countries, indicating a slight year-on-year uptick in attendance. Organisers reported that roughly one quarter of these enthusiasts voyaged from European markets outside Germany and from international destinations, marking a notable surge in the event's 'internationality'.

The largest global first-time appearance in length was by Bluegame, which unveiled its premier 24-metre-plus model, the BGX83. Founder and head of product strategy at Bluegame, Luca Santella, described the event as an incisive launch platform, emphasising that boot Düsseldorf 'is a very good setting for a presentation because everybody is focused on your event.'

Furthermore, the event witnessed the inception of new model designs, including Pearl Yachts’ 22-metre Pearl 73 and Greenline Yachts’ 13.5-metre Greenline 42. These launches underscored the importance of boot Düsseldorf as a global springboard for the marine industry's most innovative offerings, setting a high bar for future expos.

title: Strong Sales, Global Energy and Record International Reach Mark a Breakout boot Düsseldorf 2026
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: boot Düsseldorf 2026: The Global Marine Industry Regains Its Momentum
summary: When boot Düsseldorf 2026 closed its doors on 25 January, the verdict from across the marine world was unusually clear — the industry has turned a corner. After several difficult seasons marked by cautious spending and delayed decisions, exhibitors reported strong business, meaningful conversations, and deals being signed on the show floor. The mood inside the Düsseldorf exhibition halls was not speculative optimism,
body: “After the challenging past few years, our exhibitors are back on track,” said Marius Berlemann, COO of Messe Düsseldorf. “boot 2026 once again proved itself as the international beacon and driving force of the maritime industry. The deals are made here in Düsseldorf.”

With more than 200,000 visitors from over 110 countries, boot Düsseldorf recorded a modest but significant increase in attendance — with international participation standing out as the defining feature. Nearly 25% of visitors travelled from outside Germany, many from other European markets and overseas, reinforcing boot’s position as the world’s most influential water sports and boating trade fair.

Crucially, visitor quality matched the numbers. Almost 95% of attendees reported achieving their objectives, underlining the fair’s reputation as a place where decisions are made, not just explored. The high proportion of trade visitors further cemented boot Düsseldorf’s role as the industry’s commercial nerve centre.

Interest in sailing yachts and boats rose noticeably in 2026, with 25 class associations represented and nearly every major global brand present. According to Petros Michelidakis, Director of boot Düsseldorf, the sailing halls were exceptionally strong.

“We were excellently positioned in the sailing boat and yacht sector this year,” Michelidakis said. “Almost all global players were present with boat premieres, alongside innovative new manufacturers launching models here in Düsseldorf for the first time.”

Motorboats across all sizes and categories also drew sustained attention, supported by a strong showing of engines, accessories, and technical innovations. Across the show, boat premieres, new propulsion technologies and refined onboard systems illustrated an industry investing again in product development and differentiation.

Beyond boats, visitors flocked to the Destinations & Boatlife Hall, where charter, holiday and cruising concepts struck a chord. From houseboats to sailing and motor yacht charters, many visitors moved from inspiration to booking — often directly at the stands.
“The diverse holiday regions whet the appetite for time on the water,” Michelidakis noted. “Many visitors made concrete bookings during the show.”
Water sports such as paddling, surfing and foiling also remained high on the agenda, highlighting boot’s broad appeal across experience levels and disciplines.

The diving halls once again proved a major draw, combining cutting-edge equipment, immersive presentations, and packed audiences at the Dive Centre and diving tower. The Dive Award, now firmly international in reach, added further profile to the sector.

Environmental engagement was equally prominent. The ‘love your ocean’ initiative — in cooperation with the German Ocean Foundation — attracted strong interest, alongside association stands and the presentation of the Ocean Tribute Award, now in its eighth year. The 2026 award went to Spain’s One Ocean Planet Foundation, recognising its contribution to marine conservation.

Sustainability discussions found a dedicated home at the blue innovation dock (bid) in Hall 10, organised with European Boating Industry (EBI). The forum hosted high-level exchanges between policymakers, researchers and industry leaders, outlining practical pathways toward a more sustainable and competitive maritime economy.
“What defines boot is not just the products,” Michelidakis reflected. “It’s an experience space, a dialogue platform and a community meeting place.”

That ethos was particularly visible in initiatives such as ‘boot for school’, where thousands of schoolchildren explored ocean literacy through the Maritime Classroom in cooperation with the Aquazoo Löbbecke Museum — while also trying sailing, paddling, surfing and diving firsthand.
Throughout the nine days, the atmosphere remained open, energetic and distinctly optimistic — perfectly aligned with the show’s long-standing motto: We love water.

boot Düsseldorf 2026 attracted 1,810 journalists and content creators from 49 countries, ensuring global coverage across print, digital and broadcast platforms. Nearly 1,500 manufacturers, dealers and destinations from 68 nations presented their products and ideas, reaffirming the event’s unmatched scale.
Henning Mittelmann, President of the German Maritime Industry Association (VMWD), described boot as “a perfect global marketplace” and a strong start to the 2026 financial year.
Beneteau Group highlighted the exceptional quality of international buyers and confirmed strong performance across both power and sail brands.
Bavaria Yachts reported a clear upward trend, strong customer engagement and renewed confidence.
HanseYachts AG noted stabilising market conditions and met expectations despite ongoing challenges.
Saxdor Yachts, Sea Ray, Boston Whaler, NAVAN, Cressi, and Bukh Bremen all reported high-quality leads, concrete deals and strong international interest.
boot Düsseldorf 2026 didn’t just reflect a recovering market — it helped drive it. As Berlemann put it, the show departs as “a powerful catalyst, international meeting place and emotional highlight.”
The next edition of boot Düsseldorf will take place from 23–31 January 2027. If 2026 is any guide, the industry will arrive not cautious — but ready.

title: Discover Four Luxury Motor Boats Offering Serious Value Right Now
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover Four Luxury Motor Boats Offering Serious Value Right Now
summary: Many dream about the glamour of the millionaire lifestyle that includes a palatial motor yacht. Discover how this dream can become an attainable reality with four affordable, yet luxurious motor boats currently on the market.
body: Societal conceptions of affluence often paint a picture of impossible wealth and grandeur; of sprawling estates with peacocks roaming free, the distinct scent of cash notes kindling a cigar, and the feeling of luxe interiors in a chauffeur-driven Rolls-Royce. Unmistakably, amongst these symbols of opulence, features the impressive form of a grand motor yacht.

However, these lofty dreams seem barely within the grasp of many, with a million barely covering the cost of a shiny new 40-footer, not to mention the accompanying threads of a high-end lifestyle. But, hope is not lost. There's untapped potential in the used boat market that could just make the high-life an achievable proposition, assuming a healthy six-figure budget.

First on this list is the spectacular Fairline Squadron 65. Built in 2010 and priced at £650,000, it stands as a testament to Fairline's longstanding tradition of top-tier boat building. The boat's impressively modern design is accentuated by vast amounts of natural light seeping in through generous glazing. With three spacious cabins, a sizeable owner's cabin with hull windows, and a galley positioned optimally for convenience, this is a vessel built for comfort.
Other features include a hydraulic high/low bathing platform for tender launch and storage, a lift-up section in the transom that reveals an overhead shower, and a large, well-equipped flybridge.

The remaining trio of possibilities includes the Trader 64 Sunliner, a model that veers towards the explorer yacht end of the spectrum. While it is designed for relaxed, long-range cruising rather than rapid dashes, its appeal is undeniable. Built by Tarquin and launched in 2007, this boat offers style and substance on top of affordability.

Regardless of the model, these boats all deliver a blend of luxury, practicality, and cost-effectiveness that could make even the most casual cruiser dream of adventure at sea. Worth noting is that these are not merely recreational vessels but tangible symbols of attainable dreams for the aspiring sea-lover with a taste for the finer things in life and a wise mind for value.

title: Foiling at Full Flight Beneath Sugarloaf
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: SailGP Lands in Rio: Foiling at Full Flight Beneath Sugarloaf
imageCaption: Sail GP ready for 2026 starts in Rio - Brazil
summary: Few cities feel built for spectacle quite like Rio de Janeiro — and in April 2026, SailGP finally brings its brand of edge-of-control foiling to South America for the first time.
body: Tickets for the 2026 Enel Rio Sail Grand Prix went on sale first to SailGP+ members on 19 January, before opening to the general public on 23 January via SailGP.com/Rio. Given the setting, the speed and the long-awaited arrival of the circuit in Brazil, demand is expected to be fierce.

Scheduled for 11–12 April 2026, the Rio event will mark the fourth stop of the 2026 Rolex SailGP Championship, dropping the world’s fastest racing fleet into the dramatic amphitheatre of Guanabara Bay, with Sugarloaf Mountain and Rio’s skyline forming one of the most jaw-dropping backdrops in modern sailing.
SailGP’s South American debut

For SailGP, Rio represents more than just another pin on the calendar. It is the championship’s first ever event in South America, a major milestone for a series built on global reach, stadium racing and fan accessibility.

Across two high-octane days, 13 national teams will go head-to-head in identical 50-foot foiling catamarans, capable of speeds exceeding 100 km/h, often sailing faster than the wind itself. The racing is short, brutal and unforgiving — tactical mistakes punished instantly, bravery rewarded just as quickly.

For Brazilian fans, the moment carries even more weight. The Mubadala Brazil SailGP Team will race at home for the first time, entering its second season in the championship after an eye-catching debut year that delivered race wins and proved Brazil belongs at the sharp end of foiling’s elite.
A homecoming for Brazilian sailing
Driving the Brazilian boat is Martine Grael, already a household name in Olympic sailing and now one of SailGP’s standout helms. For her and the team, Rio is not just another venue — it’s personal.
“Our first season in SailGP was incredibly special,” Grael said. “We grew a lot as a team and even secured two race wins, which showed the potential of this Brazilian project.”

“But now the excitement is even greater. Racing at home, in Rio, with our own fans behind us — that’s something we didn’t get to experience last season. Sailing in Guanabara Bay, surrounded by that energy, will be fantastic. We can’t wait to give our best on the water.”
For a league built on national identity and crowd connection, few scenes promise more atmosphere than a Brazilian team racing in front of a Brazilian shoreline.
Speed, spectacle — and a new way to watch
SailGP CEO and co-founder Sir Russell Coutts believes Rio will quickly become one of the series’ defining events.

“The 2026 Enel Rio Sail Grand Prix will deliver everything that makes SailGP the most exciting racing on water: incredible speed, tight competition and a backdrop you simply can’t find anywhere else,” Coutts said.

“Brazil’s fans bring extraordinary passion, and with the Mubadala Brazil SailGP Team racing at home — alongside the launch of our new VELA Beach Club — this will be one of our most vibrant and unforgettable events yet.”

Rio will also be the first location to offer tickets for VELA Beach Club, SailGP’s new premium hospitality concept. Designed as a chic, waterside social hub, VELA combines best-in-house race viewing with refined lounge spaces, premium food and drink, and a distinctly relaxed yet elevated atmosphere.
The name “VELA”, drawn from the Latin for sails, reflects freedom, movement and the pursuit of new horizons — a fitting ethos for foiling at full flight beneath Sugarloaf.
Ticket options for 2026
Two ticket tiers will be available for the Enel Rio Sail Grand Prix, with pricing announced closer to the on-sale dates:
Waterfront Grandstands Positioned in the heart of the race stadium, grandstand seating delivers elevated views, live expert commentary, big screens, and access to food and drink throughout the day.

VELA Beach Club A premium waterfront experience blending elite racing with a vibrant social scene, featuring top-tier race views, complimentary culinary offerings, premium beverages, and attentive service — SailGP, done in style.
Beyond the racecourse

The Rio announcement also coincides with the launch of “Born to Sail”, a five-episode documentary series following the Mubadala Brazil SailGP Team through its first season. Airing on Sportv2 and Globoplay, the series dives behind the scenes of a campaign shaped by extreme speed, strategic calls, near misses and victories decided by seconds.
It’s a reminder that SailGP’s appeal isn’t just the spectacle — it’s the human stories unfolding at 50 knots.
Come April 2026, those stories will play out against one of the most iconic shorelines on Earth.
Rio is ready. SailGP is coming.

title: Journey to the Unforgettable One Metre World Championships in Remote Queensland
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Journey to the Unforgettable One Metre World Championships in Remote Queensland
summary: A small Queensland club delivered an impressively high-profile International One Metre World Championships, earning global recognition and admiration.
body: When the International One Metre (IOM) World Championships were announced to be hosted by an eleven-member club in a remote corner of Queensland, eyebrows were understandably raised. No one could have predicted the grandeur of the event that was to come: a world championship delivered with such finesse, it rivalled major international competitions.

Complete with worldwide livestreaming, stadium-style viewing and sterling organization, this impressive feat found an apt stage in Australia’s ‘Gem’, Gladstone. This event proved that a small, closely knit community had the power to execute one of the most professionally managed world championships the class had ever seen.

Emirates' A380 business class softened the long journey, even though turbulence reminded the participants of the might of nature. The arrival was marked with a minor security incident involving a tiny screwdriver set and a backpack filled with batteries. Swift action, and a helpful airline representative helped avert a crisis, keeping the spirits undeterred.

Crowned as the 'engine room of Queensland', Gladstone is a hub of industry. Despite its industrious spirit, conversations with locals revealed a town proud of its heritage and thrilled to share its seafaring credentials with the visitors. Among the towering conveyor belts and bustling ports, a spectacular event took sailing sports to new heights.

title: Mark Your Calendar for the 21st Nautilus Marine Insurance Sydney Harbour Regatta 2026: Action-Packed Weekend Unfolds!
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Mark Your Calendar for the 21st Nautilus Marine Insurance Sydney Harbour Regatta 2026: Action-Packed Weekend Unfolds!
summary: Dive headfirst into the 2026 Nautilus Marine Insurance Sydney Harbour Regatta, a thrilling celebration of the event's 21st birthday offering unmatched nautical action over the weekend of 7 and 8 March.
body: The 21st Nautilus Marine Insurance Sydney Harbour Regatta, set to take place on 7 and 8 March 2026, is a much anticipated event that combines the excitement of competitive sailing with the vibrancy of Sydney's harbour. This regatta, the largest of its kind in New South Wales, continues to draw sailing enthusiasts and competitors from both NSW and interstate. A particularly special highlight of this 2026 edition is the newest addition- the Super Cruiser Racer Group, which will be featuring remarkable yachts like Caol Ila, Odin, Xanthus, Triton, Antipodes, Sydney, and Shearwater. These behemoths of the sea are set to intensify the competition and elevate the spectacle, with the first day featuring two inshore-offshore races tailored for them, and an offshore passage race in store for the closing day, in conjunction with the Super 50 fleet. The Sydney 38 class, continuing its tradition, will engage in the NSW Championship, bringing power-packed performance and tactical ruling through offshore windward/leeward races on the opening day, and three inshore windward/leewards on the second. After a roller-coaster of victories amongst Conspiracy, Challenge, Mondo and Gusto in recent years, expectations are high to see who finally clinches the anticipated confrontations. Also featuring in the regatta lineup is the Fareast 28R Australian Championship, the Super 30 Cup, the Cavalier 28 NSW Championship, and of course, the classic one-design classes in the Etchells, J/70, J/24, Adams 10, VX-One and Super 40 (MC38s and others of that ilk). The regatta also features an Open Class (IRC and ORC), a Performance Class (with Spinnaker and Non-Spinnaker divisions), Classic Keelboats, and the Historic 18' Skiffs. With a massive fleet expected, courtesy of the Middle Harbour Yacht Club (MHYC) and eight supporting clubs, the regatta promises to be an exciting venture. The racing spectacle will be split over seven course areas, under the watchful gaze of Principal Race Officer, Denis Thompson and a crew of passionate volunteers. Unfolding over two days and featuring an array of fierce competitions, the Sydney Harbour Regatta is set to provide an unforgettable 21st celebration that will captivate sailors and spectators alike.

title: AES Yacht and Cass Yacht Design Celebrate Collaboration with Groundbreaking 50m and 70m Superyacht Concepts
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: AES Yacht and Cass Yacht Design Celebrate Collaboration with Groundbreaking 50m and 70m Superyacht Concepts
summary: Turkey's Cass Yacht Design marries art with architecture in their unprecedented superyacht designs made for AES Yacht.
body: Turkey takes the bow as Cass Yacht Design steers the superyacht industry into uncharted waters with two avant-garde concepts for AES Yacht. These aren't your standard yachts. The first of the duo is a sub-500GT, 50-metre masterpiece, sporting a full-beam 'architectural approach.' To truly appreciate the design, picture floor-to-ceiling glazing, ample private balconies, and an irresistible allure of understated elegance. Bathed in natural light, the insides merge seamlessly with the outside, creating a tranquil yet chic ambience. The 50-metre yacht is poised to redefine calmness on the water.

The second of the pair is the 70-metre concept, standing at a considerable 1,500GT of interior volume, with an edgy, futuristic silhouette. The distinguishing factor of this design is at the aft, where opening platforms unravel forming a beach house-style space beside the water. Designers have braved the unusual, creating a cylindrical pool akin to an aquarium at the foredeck cylinder entwined by a round stairwell. But it doesn't stop there. The layout ensures ample space across decks, adaptable to varied owner lifestyles. Less is indeed more as the design favours simplicity, providing a distinct identity through stripped-back sophistication.

Yavuz Akyildiz of Cass Yacht Design believes these designs are projects completed in their own rights yet offer a myriad of customisation opportunities to prospective owners who, like them, believe 'a ship in harbour is safe, but that's not what ships are built for.' The designs not only reflect aesthetic brilliance but the possibility of where we could take artisanal creation within yachting if we dare to ride the wave.

title: A voyage through the 2025 boat season: Dazzling innovations, tugboat chic, and the rise of sociable cruising
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A voyage through the 2025 boat season: Dazzling innovations, tugboat chic, and the rise of sociable cruising
summary: Explore the standout launches and nautical novelties that defined the 2025 boating season, spotlighting the trends and triumphs of a year on the water.
body: The 2025 boating season was nothing short of an adventure, with engineers, designers, and boat enthusiasts travelling the globe, striving to sea trial the latest yacht launches and innovations. The motor yacht industry was abuzz as the international show circuit displayed a range of engaging, static yacht tours.

A particular type of anticipation filled the air during boat show premieres, introducing designs that either made waves or quietly sank. This year, the industry was split into two distinct camps: the maestros, who were champions of sociable, manageable efficiency, and the daring innovators, who sought to redefine the boundaries of custom engineering.

This commitment to volume was further illustrated at the Cannes Yachting Festival with the Absolute Navetta 62. The festival attendees hailed it as the epitome of modern grandeur, injected into a classic trawler style. Its distinct design - from cutaway bulwarks and glass balustrades in the cockpit, to the generous headroom and vertical windows of the open-plan saloon - was classically Absolute: voluminous, cruising-centric, yet refreshingly far from formulaic.

Meanwhile, some designers sought to push boundaries in other areas, turning their attention to innovative, efficient use of materials. The Delta 72 embodied this trend, utilising carbon fibre to shed significant weight. Weighing in at a mere 31 tonnes, this lightweight wonder cruised at an impressive 30 knots with a fuel burn of a measly 6.1 litres per nautical mile. This is an example of embracing lightness to foster speed and efficiency in ways traditional GRP cannot match.

In the multihull sector, Aquila 46 Yacht showcased the continuing reign of power catamarans. With the masterful use of its wide 23' 3'' beam, this nautical marvel offered an intermediate deck level for the owner's cabin—preserving precious sea views while providing luxurious cabinetry and double sinks. Configurable with three to five cabins, it remained a highly competitive contender.

All in all, the 2025 boating season was a testament to the ongoing evolution of the industry, defining cutting-edge designs, recognising the value of sociable spaces, and embracing intelligent materials to foster efficiency. Marvelling at this year's achievements, we excitedly anticipate what the forthcoming boating seasons will bring.

title: Discover the Bee Explorer: A Pocket-Sized Superyacht with Long-Range Cruising Capabilities
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover the Bee Explorer: A Pocket-Sized Superyacht with Long-Range Cruising Capabilities
summary: The Bee Explorer, a 35.4-metre motor yacht brandishing top-tier features, is up for sale, exuding elegance and efficiency.
body: Stepping at the pinnacle of modern marine innovation is the Bee Explorer, a compact yet power-packed superyacht. This 35.4-metre motor yacht, crafted by Turkish shipyard Bee Yachts, is a marvel of nautical engineering and design prowess. Branded by eminent designer Sergio Cutolo and engineered by Hydro Tec, this opulent ocean vehicle emerges as a ground-breaking prototype in yacht construction.

Representing grandeur in a compact format, the Bee Explorer offers the enticing combo of easy marina access and hull design calibrated for extensive sea expeditions. The asking price for this aquatic gem? A cool €15,250,000. Powering this price tag are its distinguished features including a high bow, bold lines, expansive glazing, full-displacement steel hull, and an aluminium superstructure. Its RINA class status and successful sea trials set the stage for its reliability.

Talking about accommodation, it houses five cabins designed to hold ten guests. An extravagant full-beam owner’s suite, two double cabins, and two twin cabins on the lower deck ensure comfortable lodgings. Additionally, there are quarters for a six-member crew.

Fuelled by a pair of Caterpillar engines, Bee Explorer guarantees 4,000 nautical miles of smooth sailing at 10 knots, with zero-speed stabilisers for added stability. Brimming with cutting-edge technology, brokers report it to be efficient and economical.

Currently berthed in Istanbul, the Bee Explorer maps an intriguing course for the future of yacht design and navigational prowess, establishing a fresh illustration of manageable luxury in the domain of private yachting.

title: Mastering the Art of Superyacht Refit: The Starry Tale of Amico & Co's Genoa Shipyards
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Mastering the Art of Superyacht Refit: The Starry Tale of Amico & Co's Genoa Shipyards
summary: In the competitive world of superyacht refit and repair, a Genoa-based family business stands out for its exceptional commitment to excellence. Discover the journey of Amico & Co.
body: Unfolding the pages of maritime history, one comes across the story of an unassuming shipyard in Genoa. Setting course in a world of superyachts that is continually growing in complexity, Amico & Co reveals a unique blend of craftsmanship and customer-centric service proving that the yard is not just about advanced technical ability.

This family-run shipyard, originating from the late 1700s, transcends over two centuries with the Amico family repairing boats since 1799. It began with Matteo Amico's first yard in Loano, and over time, father-to-son transitions ensured remarkable continuity of maritime wisdom, culminating in the establishment of the modern Amico & Co by Alberto Amico in 1991. Back then, the superyacht universe was relatively less bustling, with the global fleet merely brushing the 40-metre mark and a total of 800 to 900 superyachts vis-a-vis today's 14,000 plus. Not to mention, there were no dedicated refit infrastructures for superyachting.

Amico & Co's family-centric approach is a distinctive strength, ensuring a flexible chain of command while emphasising open exchange of information. Each refit project, with its unique operational scope, client expectations, and regulatory benchmarks, demands crucial and timely decision-making. A rigid hierarchy would hinder expedient decision-making, a hurdle effortlessly crossed by a short-chain, family-operated yard.

Amico & Co enjoys a sterling reputation for managing complex refits and rebuilds. Imbued with over 200 years of maritime knowledge, this family-run shipyard proficiently navigates the world of superyacht refit, proving that an unwavering commitment to precision, reliability, and exceptional customer service never goes out of style.

title: Discover the Innovations and Future Plans of Italian Custom Shipyard CRN
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover the Innovations and Future Plans of Italian Custom Shipyard CRN
summary: With its roots stemming from the 60s, Italian yard, CRN, is well-known for its blend of classic and modern designs. However, it holds a deeper history.
body: Costruzioni Riparazioni Navali (CRN), an Italian shipyard with roots dating back to the1960s, has made its mark within the Ferretti Group's portfolio of builders as a 'pure custom' shipyard. With a fleet now boasting 80 strong units, CRN has become renowned for its remarkable combination of classic and contemporary design aesthetics. Beyond this, what people may not know is that CRN has also been part of some of the yachting industry's most significant advancements.

CRN's commitment to innovation and its readiness to push boundaries is palpable when speaking with custom business unit sales director, Vittorio Blengini. This innovative spirit has led CRN to maintain a well-established place within the world of yachting, and its future plans promise even more revolutionary contributions to the sector.

As the industry proceeds into an exciting era of constant transformations, CRN's commitment to initiating change rather than merely adapting to it is a testament to their visionary approach. This continued dedication to innovation ensures a compelling outlook for the future for both CRN and the wider yachting industry.

title: Promising Excitement on the Water: The Much-Anticipated Euromarina Optimist Torrevieja 2026 Regatta
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Promising Excitement on the Water: The Much-Anticipated Euromarina Optimist Torrevieja 2026 Regatta
summary: Torrevieja's Real Club Náutico officially launched the Euromarina Optimist Torrevieja 2026, a riveting regatta event to be held at the end of January, promising a delightful gathering of the best Optimist sailors nationally and internationally.
body: A thrilling wave of competition is soon to hit the Spanish shores as Real Club Náutico de Torrevieja prepares to host the much-anticipated Euromarina Optimist Torrevieja 2026. The regatta, a children's sailing event, is scheduled from Thursday 29th January to Sunday 1st February. The gathering will bring together the crème-de-la-crème of Optimist sailors both on the national and international levels.

The event is expected to serve not only as a platform for high-level competition but also as a vibrant display of maritime spirit, hosting over 400 sailors from 28 different nations. To add to the excitement, Patricia Quesada, representing the luxury brand Euromarina, emphasized the significant visibility that the regatta will bring to the brand, being a showcase of the Costa Blanca's sport, gastronomy and lifestyle.

Club President, Carlos Carmona, closed the presentations by expressing gratitude to main sponsor Euromarina, as the Quesada family has supported the regatta for 12 long years. He acknowledged the event as the most significant one held at the club each year, reiterating the essence of what the Optimist regatta signifies for them: a celebration of the maritime life, a shared love for sailing and the spirit of sportsmanship it brings among everyone involved. As the days narrow down to the commencement of the regatta, anticipation runs high among the maritime community as the promise of excitement on the waves grows stronger.

title: Discover Blue Legend, the Super Yacht Born of an Ambitious Dream and Unbridled Enthusiasm for the Sea
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover Blue Legend, the Super Yacht Born of an Ambitious Dream and Unbridled Enthusiasm for the Sea
summary: Explore the captivating story of the Blue Legend, an unparalleled 80ft Nelson motor yacht that was custom-built out of sheer desire and aspiration.
body: In the world of boats, where size, power, and elegance often walk hand in hand, the Blue Legend, a custom Nelson 80 motor yacht, stands as a testament to the seemingly boundless human spirit of creation. Like a mythical sea giant conceived in the hearts of those who dared to dream big, the Blue Legend was born out of pure desire and aspiration. Conceived by a fervent yacht owner who had enjoyed voyaging on a Nelson 32 to a 45 and yearned to own one even larger. Suddenly, this aspiration led to the Blue Legend's birth, a larger-than-life, 80ft Nelson motor yacht. The handsome vessel was crafted by Arthur Mursell of TT Boat Designs with Richardson’s Yacht Services commissioned for the build. This maritime marvel evolved during its creation, eventually reaching lavish luxury yacht standards. Inside, visitors are greeted by an extravagant ensemble of limed oak woodwork, Connolly leather, and custom woven carpets. The vessel, powered by twin 1,000hp Caterpillar diesels, gleams with resplendence, living testament to the owner’s audacious vision. But the tale does not end here; a decade later, the Blue Legend was extended to 80ft to accommodate additional crew cabins and a grander layout, testament to the owner's penchant for enhanced luxury and space. As a result, the Blue Legend continues to be a sight to behold on any journey, from Mallorca to the south of France, Italy, Sardinia, and Corsica, always stealing the spotlight in harbours. So, here stands the Blue Legend, as a maritime embodiment of what human creativity, passion, and wealth can manifest when they fuse seamlessly.

title: Ground-breaking second hull in Heesen’s 'new class' of superyachts revealed - welcome aboard the Project Evita
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Ground-breaking second hull in Heesen’s 'new class' of superyachts revealed - welcome aboard the Project Evita
summary: Dutch shipbuilding industry giant Heesen take another bold step in yacht engineering with the unveiling of their second 'high speed' superyacht, the Project Evita.
body: In an eventful turn of marine technology, the hull and superstructure of the second instalment in Heesen's innovatively hewed 'high-speed' aluminium superyachts have been successfully conjoined. This paves the way for the grand arrival of Project Evita, the most colossal vessel ever spec-built by the Dutch titans of the shipbuilding industry. As per the projections, the well-appointed superyacht is set to be delivered in the third quarter of 2027.

However, what truly distinguishes Project Evita from the Santosha is a revitalised main deck aft - the social hub of the vessel. The design showcases a sprawling six square-metre infinity pool, which is flanked by inviting sunpads and complimented by a special lazarette for storing water toys. The sundeck features a segregated area divided into three zones equipped with sun loungers, a forward lounge, and fine al fresco dining under a solid hardtop bar.

This epitome of luxury has been designed to offer both seclusion and social interaction with over 780GT and 400 square metres of interior space. With the yacht's visual harmony maintained by rich woods set against a nautical cream and blue palette, the interior resonates a classy vibe.

The yacht boasts ample accommodation for up to 12 guests, with six opulent cabins including a luxurious 60-square-metre master suite. Furthermore, the quarters have space to accommodate a 13-member crew comfortably. A futuristic central glass elevator connects all the decks together. With a transatlantic range of 3,900 nautical miles at 13 knots, Project Evita makes for a perfect companion on high sea adventures while also aligning with IMO Tier III standards.

The revelation of Project Evita marks a vibrant period for the Dutch shipyard, which currently has six yachts under construction. Project Evita follows in the wake of the 50-metre Project Grace, another spec-built vessel by Heesen that achieved the same construction milestone previously.

title: Harnessing the Adventure of the Sea Safely: A Deep Dive into the International Safety at Sea Course
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Harnessing the Adventure of the Sea Safely: A Deep Dive into the International Safety at Sea Course
summary: When the whispers of adventure beckon from the vast ocean, safety should be an adventurer's top priority. US Sailing's International Safety at Sea course elevates the tides of nautical knowledge with a hands-on approach.
body: For those who find solace in the gentle lap of the waves and the dance of the sails, an ordinary day beckons extraordinary adventures. Yet, even the most seasoned sailor knows that safety in these seemingly serene surroundings is imperative. That's where the 'International Safety at Sea' course, meticulously designed by US Sailing, comes gallantly into the picture.

Remember the adage 'A smooth sea never made a skillful sailor'? This is the essence of this remarkable course. It is an intensive one-day program, scheduled for May 15, 2026, comfortable nested at the Milwaukee Yacht Club and Pulaski Indoor Pool. What's unique about this course is that it prepares participants for survival offshore during on-the-water emergencies. The course material lends a robust understanding of the sea's unpredictable nature and teaches how to remain steadfast and resilient during testing times.

Moreover, the course deserves applause for its race readiness, meeting the most recent requirements for the famous Race to Mackinac (Chicago-Mac). The path to certification entails completing an Offshore Safety at Sea online course within a year of taking the hands-on course. Its extensive curriculum comprises 14 diverse topics, covering everything offshore related and a certificate of completion must be produced before attending the hands-on program.

With limited space, early bird registrations are the safest bet to secure a spot in this revolutionary course. The knowledge you gain here might not only save your life but also the lives of others. It's about preparing for anything the sea may throw your way with utmost confidence, turning adverse situations into opportunities of growth, learning, and survival. So, anchors aweigh, ladies!

title: Day 1 & 2 of the Flying Dutchman Australian Championship 2026: A Rollercoaster of Skill, Strategy and Sailing!

body: The Flying Dutchman Australian Championship 2026, hosted on the beautiful waters of Lake King, Metung, set sail amidst an atmosphere of high energy and competition. Day one saw participants taking on an engaging triangular course, with 13 boats sailing for gold.

Four-time-world champions Peter Bevis and Ian McCrossin were among the leaders after the initial day. However, the competition was heating up with two races already completed on day one. Mark Henger and Matt Bismarck, the reigning Australian and New Zealand champions, managed to reach the windward gates first in race one. However, they faced stiff competition from McCrossin and Bevis in Lupicus 60 AUS33.

Despite the challenging conditions, the spirit of the competition and the drive to win were clearly evident among all participants. The promise of an exciting showdown in the forthcoming days hangs in the air, as the series board remains wide open.

Spectators watching the regatta are gripped by the thrill of the race, as they watch sailors navigate through strategy, quick decisions, and skill. An event not just for sailing enthusiasts but for those seeking a taste of excitement and adventure, the Flying Dutchman Australian Championship 2026 has proven to be a spectacular display of competitive sailing.

title: Breath-taking Struggles in the ILCA Under 21 World Championships 2026, Where Top Spots Are Fought Tooth and Nail
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Breath-taking Struggles in the ILCA Under 21 World Championships 2026, Where Top Spots Are Fought Tooth and Nail
summary: The penultimate day of the ILCA Under 21 World Championships 2026 thrilled spectators, as winds challenged participants, shaking up the contest in Lanzarote.
body: The Ilca Under 21 World Championships 2026 in Lanzarote has reached a taut crescendo on its penultimate day. Spine-chilling west-north-westerly winds bellowed and challenging conditions weighed heavily on the competitors, ensuring an exciting twist in the contest.

The top spot at the ILCA 7 class is now shared between Slovenia's Luka Zabukovec and Spain's Karol Krupski. The duo's heated contest has kept the audience on its toes. On the other hand, Italy's Ginevra Caracciolo has forged an impenetrable lead in the ILCA 6 class, disregarding the tumultuous weather conditions.

The race fragment of the championship was a demanding, yet enthralling test of tactics and endurance. A combination of surging strong winds and mental tenacity became the deciding factors of the day's contest.

However, the final race of the day was an absolute turning point, which rejigged the overall classification. With the perfect level played by Krupski and Zabukovec, they stand joint-first at 48 points. Also, Pulci's commendable feats solidified his third position, though trailing by 11 points behind the leaders. The languid windswept Canary Islands now anxiously await the conclusion of this under-21 championship. The players are poised and the stage is set for a thrilling finale.

title: Fierce Competition on Day Five: ILCA Under 21 World Championships 2026 in Lanzarote
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Fierce Competition on Day Five: ILCA Under 21 World Championships 2026 in Lanzarote
summary: Italy's Ginevra Caracciolo reinforces her position at the ILCA 6 Under 21 World Championships as competition intensifies.
body: Day five of the Under 21 World Championships in Lanzarote presented a daunting mix of strong west-north-westerly winds and demanding conditions, reshuffling the leaderboards and making for an adrenaline-fueled day of racing. In the ILCA 7 category, Spain's Karol Krupski and Slovenia's Luka Zabukovec remained tied, their tenacity inflamed by the challenging conditions. Meanwhile, in ILCA 6, Italy's Ginevra Caracciolo continued her reign, asserting control over her class while the fight for remaining podium places intensified.

The whirl of races took place by Marina Rubicón, Lanzarote, a perfect setting that greeted contestants with steady west-north-westerly winds from early morning. Gusts exceeded 20 knots, stretching the endurance and concentration of the fleets. The sea churned as several general recalls took place, especially within the men's gold fleet, forcing meticulous verification before the two scheduled races could commence.

The women were not to be outdone. Italy's Ginevra Caracciolo displayed a clear dominance in her class, holding a commendable lead of 45 points. The world title seems to be well within her grasp. However, a fierce fight unfolded for the remaining podium places, with the standings witnessing numerous position changes - bar Caracciolo and Greece's Hermione Ghicas. With such fierce competition, the conclusion of the Under 21 World Championships in Lanzarote is sure to offer a spellbinding display.

title: All Set for an Exciting Start: The Bacardi Winter Series Sailing Regatta Kicks Off
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: All Set for an Exciting Start: The Bacardi Winter Series Sailing Regatta Kicks Off
summary: The anticipation intensifies as the Bacardi Winter Series begins with the J/70 and Melges 24 fleets returning to Miami's Biscayne Bay.
body: As daybreak greets Biscayne Bay on January 23rd, the curtain will be raised on the 2026 Bacardi Winter Series, where nearly 60 boats will compete in the first event of the season. Hosted at Shake-A-Leg Miami, this three-day series is not only about unleashing top-tier sailing, but also about fostering camaraderie within an ambiance of Bacardi's renowned hospitality nestled in the heart of Coconut Grove. Eddie Cutillas of Bacardi USA encapsulates the spirit of the event succinctly, remarking that it serves as a momentum builder, igniting the spark for the season. He emphasizes that Bacardi's regattas are not just about fierce competition, but also about creating bonds that span across years. This year, the stakes are higher, attributing additional weight to the first regatta of the season; the event also doubles as the Melges 24 North American Championship. This has transformed the Bacardi Winter Series into a significant early-season litmus test, with all eyes on the fleets as many hopefuls aspire to claim the world championship returning to U.S waters later this year. Lizz Flowers, having previously led WallyCento maxi yacht Galateia to a world championship triumph, is all set to amplify her accolades with her debut sportboat appearance in her new Melges 24 program, Mini Gal. Coupled with this, the finale of the 2025 M24 North American Sailing Series is also culminating at the event, adding an extra layer of excitement. With the sailing stage meticulously set, all that's left is for the captains and their crews to grip their tillers, hoist their sails, and brace themselves for a winter sailing extravaganza like no other. One thing's for certain - the Bacardi Winter Series will certainly keep spectators glued to the water's edge. Buckle up, it’s time to ride the winds!

title: An Unforgettable Adventure Begins: Oyster Owners Embark on 16-month Circumnavigation in the 2026-2027 Oyster World Rally
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: An Unforgettable Adventure Begins: Oyster Owners Embark on 16-month Circumnavigation in the 2026-2027 Oyster World Rally
summary: The latest edition of the Oyster World Rally, an exciting, 16-month journey around the globe, recently kicked off in Antigua, marking the beginning of an incredible adventure for all participating Oyster boat owners.

The Oyster World Rally 2026-2027, a symbol of this longing for discovery, recently commenced in Antigua, embarking on a fully supported 16-month circumnavigation of the globe.

Sailing boat owners and enthusiasts congregated at the start line, excitement palpable in the air, as they prepared to delve into an incredible journey that would see them traverse the world's oceans. Among them, the owner of the Oyster 595 Viva candidly recounted his journey from being a casual boat enthusiast to embarking on a worldwide adventure. With humor and charm, he spoke of the initial interaction with an Oyster salesman that eventually led him to upgrade his vessel and, with the builder's support, prepare for this expansive voyage.

Minutes before they set sail, the group attentively sat through a briefing by weather forecaster Simon Rowell, absorbing information about the initial few days of the rally. As the crews busied themselves with final checks and preparations, laughter and camaraderie filled the air. The docks were abuzz with activities, as technical support staff in navy shirts addressed the last-minute issues, surrounded by Oyster Yachts' team documenting every moment as supplies made their way onto the boats.

This rally epitomizes the adventurous spirit of Oyster boat owners, providing them with a platform to realize their sailing dreams while demonstrating their seafaring skills. It offers participants a unique chance to experience the challenges and joys associated with circumnavigation, fostering a sense of unity within the sailing community. For these adventurers, the journey is not merely about the distance they traverse but the memories they amass and the camaraderie they forge in this celebrated rally tradition.

title: Immerse in a 5-Day Women-focused Sailing Camp at St. Thomas: A Perfect Blend of Learning, Racing, and Revelry
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Immerse in a 5-Day Women-focused Sailing Camp at St. Thomas: A Perfect Blend of Learning, Racing, and Revelry
summary: St. Thomas Yacht Club hosts the second annual Women's Regatta Camp from January 26-31, 2026. Sail, learn, and dazzle in the heart of the U.S. Virgin Islands.
body: For the second consecutive year, the St. Thomas Sailing Center (STSC) is hosting the Women's Regatta Camp amidst the captivating turquoise waters and steady tradewinds of the U.S. Virgin Islands, the 'Caribbean Yachting Destination of the Year' 2025. Scheduled from January 26-31, 2026, the camp promises to be more than a maritime event. It beckons individual sailors and full teams alike, offering an enticing blend of intense training by globally accomplished women sailors, match-racing in the sturdy IC24s—retrofitted J/24s designed for focused team coordination and maximizing race execution, and of course, the excitement of round-the-island racing.

The Women's Regatta Camp, however, is not just about sailing. Balancing instruction with island banter, it incorporates off-the-water activities like savoring lunch at the charming floating pizzeria near Christmas Cove, and an evening of convivial restaurant dining on neighboring St. John. Indeed, Bobby Brooks, the STSC executive director, captures the essence of the camp by emphasizing its focus on creating a platform where women sailors can learn, compete, and grow together as part of an extraordinary maritime community.

Whether you're a team trying to up your sailing game, an individual looking to delve into the world of sailing, or a seasoned sailor seeking new challenges, the Women's Regatta Camp at St. Thomas offers a wonderfully inclusive and experientially rich opportunity to sail, learn and make new connections.

title: Prestigious Navetta 37 Model Yacht Sokny Finds New Owner in Exclusive Sale
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Prestigious Navetta 37 Model Yacht Sokny Finds New Owner in Exclusive Sale
summary: The Cabernet-coloured jewel of the sea, motor yacht Sokny has been bought. This 37-metre nautical masterpiece is now sailing under new flag.
body: In an intriguing twirl of the marine world, the 37-metre motor yacht Sokny, elegantly built by Custom Line, has found a new place to call home. This fascinating legal tussle defines the sessions with Kevin Bonnie of IYC and Karma Yachting batting for the seller, while Jean Christophe Santarelli of Santarelli Marine Brokerage and Alexis Colin of Abys Yachting marked their expertise for the buyer.

Constructed in superior quality GRP, Sokny stands as a testament to the design brilliance of the Zuccon International Project alongside the Ferretti Engineering Department. The interior elegance was stitched together at the drawing boards of Odone International Design Studio. Sokny sails as one of the 15 highly sought-after yachts from the Navetta 37 line, which were gifted to the waves in 2022.

The yacht's generous accommodation spans across five cabins, each designed with a unique aesthetic flair. The layout includes a magnificent master suite, two cozy double cabins, and two delightful twin cabins, all adequately outfitted with their very own en suite. A respectable crew of seven ensures flawless service on board.

Sokny's decor marries monochrome elegance with splashes of colour, jazzy patterns, and abstract artwork, setting the mood for leisure, luxury, and la vida loca. The boat’s exterior areas are extensive and versatile, offering a myriad seating and dining options for owners and guests alike. From the sun deck with its own Jacuzzi to the comfortable lounge areas and removable awning, Sokny is truly a floating paradise worth every penny spent.

title: Italian Sea Group Responds to Press Reports Over Legal Proceedings Resulting from Bayesian Yacht Tragedy
author: Old Sea Dogs

summary: Reports suggest that The Italian Sea Group (TISG) has responded to news alleging it is seeking £400 million in damages from plaintiffs associated with the unlucky Bayesian sailing yacht.
body: In a recent development that has caught the attention of sailing enthusiasts and industry insiders alike, The Italian Sea Group (TISG), a major player in the marine world, has broken its silence about ongoing legal proceedings connected to the unfortunate Perini Navi sailing yacht, known as Bayesian. Word circulating in the media has suggested that TISG is pursuing £400 million in damages from individuals associated with the ill-fated vessel, a report that the marine group has now responded to. The journey of Bayesian yacht and its unfolding narrative continue to sail in stormy legal waters. This complex case involving one of the leading yachting firms has left onlookers speculating and waiting with anticipation for every tidbit of news about the lawsuit. The claim constitutes a procedural measure in connection to the reported damages, as per the statement shared with BOATPro by Perini Navi. Deciphering who is at fault in this series of unfortunate events will hinge on the findings of ongoing investigations - their outcome eagerly awaited by all interested parties. However, at this juncture, it's crucial to remember that the legal journey can often be as unpredictable as the sea itself. As the saga continues to unfold, industry observers, yacht enthusiasts and general public remain on tenterhooks, waiting for the next direction the tide will turn.

title: The Lavish Italian-built Sanlorenzo SL106 M/Y Piacere III Finds a New Home

summary: The ritzy 32.2-meter Sanlorenzo SL106 motor yacht Piacere III has found a new owner. This Italian masterpiece was previously selling at €6,400,000.

This transpired via a deal between Gabriele Bacci of Sanlorenzo S.p.A., representing the seller, and Stratos Korais of Atalanta Marine S.A., who introduced the buyer. The notable Alessandro D'Este and Riccardo Piasenti of International Yachts Srl also played a significant role in the transaction.

Crafted in the prominent Italian shipyard, and delivered in 2019, Piacere III boasts construction in GRP to a full design by the renowned Italian designer Francesco Paszkowski Design. The yacht is one of 21 vessels delivered to date from Sanlorenzo's illustrious SL106 line that reveals naval architecture developed in-house.

Numerous expansive windows and two sliding glass doors invite plenty of natural light into the main saloon. This area features a comfortable sofa space and a formal dining table seating 10. On the outside, Piacere III offers ample deck space for al fresco dining and lounging. The flybridge comes fitted with a sizeable 10-seater dining table, a bar, and a teppanyaki grill for open-air entertaining.

Twin MTU 2434hp engines power the luxury motor yacht to a top speed of 29 knots, while cruising is comfortably achieved at a speed of 24 knots. With its combination of high-performance and lavish design, the Sanlorenzo SL106 motor yacht Piacere III truly is the epitome of nautical indulgence.

title: Exploring the Impact of Environmental Regulations and Sustainability Goals on Yacht Refit Coatings
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Exploring the Impact of Environmental Regulations and Sustainability Goals on Yacht Refit Coatings
summary: The demand for sustainable coatings in yacht refits is on the rise, bringing a unique set of challenges and opportunities to the boating industry.
body: Picture the coat of paint on a luxury yacht. It's more than just aesthetics. It's where expectations, practical realities, and stringent regulations intersect. Historically, skilled labour for such intricate work has become increasingly elusive and costly, especially in the realm of high-profile yachts. On one hand, yacht owners now demand near-new-build standards with darker hull colours, even when dealing with limitations posed by existing substrates, restricted access, and pre-set timelines. On the other, environmental regulations are continuously reshaping the groundwork for paint projects.

However, the yachting industry is displaying resilience. Adopting sustainable materials and adjusting to new regulations, though it may initially require adaptation, is considered manageable. The industry is also tapping into technological solutions to abide by potential future guidelines. While these measures may have a bearing on the final cost of a paint refit, they promise improved efficiencies and superior performance. Moreover, advancements in paint-application systems promise to expedite refit timelines and trim associated costs.

Experience has shown that timely upgrades to include appropriate systems and procedures go a long way in future-proofing against changing regulations. Recognising trends in other industries such as automotive, where sustainability requisites have forced substantial product changes, can offer key insights for the yachting sector. Maximising on facilities, such as permanent, weather-proof, climate-controlled paint hangars can ensure optimal project execution, while also slashing gas consumption costs by up to 70%, further bolstering the sustainability aspect of yacht refits.

title: How Environmental Regulations and Sustainability Goals are Redefining Superyacht Paint Refits
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: How Environmental Regulations and Sustainability Goals are Redefining Superyacht Paint Refits
summary: The intricate dance of modern coating refits involves a delicate balance of expectations, regulations, and on-the-ground realities.
body: Once upon a time, the world of superyacht refitting was a simple affair, focused on presenting an aesthetically pleasing facade and ensuring the vessel's operational efficiency. However, the winds of change are gusting strongly through the marinas and dry docks that service these seafaring giants. Nowhere does this change manifest more visibly than in the painting stations, where the tussle between expectation, regulation, and harsh reality plays out brightly. The mounting pressures on the coatings market are not begotten of a single development. The dwindling availability of hard-to-find skills and the subsequent rise in labour costs have had a major impact, especially with large, more prestigious yachts. Parallel to this, customers' expectations for finish quality have risen precipitously, with demands for 'near-new-build standards' and darker hull colours becoming the modicum. Further complicating the scenario is the increase in stringent environmental regulations, forcing authorities to rethink how paint projects are organised and executed. These regulations, despite being generally accepted as manageable, can cause significant delays and increased work requirements when structures fail to comply. It is important to understand that paint in a refit does not operate independently. The mesh of these complex factors has made paint projects the most sensitive element in the refit matrix. And understanding how these pressures manifest on the ground demands insight from captains who manage these refits firsthand. Industry leaders have been invited to share their perspectives on how evolving environmental regulations and sustainability goals are changing their approach to planning, costing, and delivering paint projects. Their responses highlight the transformation sweeping across superyacht refits. These conversations highlight that navigating these new waters is far from simple. With environmental regulations demanding changes in product selection, application methods, and even the choice of yard, complexities in specifications and containment costs have soared while planning has become more meticulous. However, amidst this seeming upheaval, hope is rising on the horizon. Innovations in paint application systems offer potential solutions for future regulations and also promise efficiencies that may help to mitigate cost impact and reduce refitting timelines. These encouraging developments suggest a positive turn of the tide. While challenges and uncertainties lie ahead, industry captains seem prepared to embrace these in the pursuit of a more sustainable and eco-responsible future for superyacht refitting. The sea may be rough, but the winds are promising, and the destination - a future where beauty and performance do not have to come at the earth's expense - is worth every storm.

title: How Environmental Regulations and Sustainability Goals are Changing the Yacht Coatings Industry
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: How Environmental Regulations and Sustainability Goals are Changing the Yacht Coatings Industry
summary: The increasing focus on sustainability is significantly altering the yacht coatings sector, affecting cost, project planning, and delivery.
body: For superyachts, a sleek, well-presented exterior is not just about aesthetics. It portrays an unspoken promise of quality, luxury, and craftsmanship. But for that glossy, polished veneer to maintain its gleam, one crucial element is irreplaceable - paint. Not just any generic option picked up at a hardware store, but special marine-grade varieties, formulated for endurance, appeal and increasingly, sustainability.

Sustainability is steering the way for the coatings industry, as painted superyacht hulls catch the attention of regulators. Shaping the future of yacht maintenance, environmental regulations are shifting how paint refits are developed, specified and carried out. Growing issues of expertise scarcity and ballooning costs add to the strain, even as expectations continue to spiral upward for the calibre of finish and sustainability in the sector. Tricky factors such as operational substrates, fixed schedules, and access restrictions continue to contraindicate these lofty ambitions.

At Royal Huisman, General Manager Stefan Coronel shares a similar sentiment. He acknowledges the need for adaptation around regulations and the growth of more sustainable materials, but also recognises it as a manageable challenge. From GYG Ltd, CEO Remy Millott envisions the advent of technical solutions and innovations that will respond to these regulations, though acknowledging a likely impact on costs. Meanwhile, Manuel Di Tillio, Technical & Sales Director, Amico & Co, highlights the yet unrealised shift in product offerings due to sustainability requirements.

These insights offer only a snapshot of a broader change across industries brought on by an increasing emphasis on sustainability. It highlights the importance of proactively managing sustainability as an integral part of major refits, where its impact is particularisable rather than brushed aside.

title: Westport Yachts breaks from dock with the first yacht of its innovative 41-meter Raised Pilothouse series
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Westport Yachts breaks from dock with the first yacht of its innovative 41-meter Raised Pilothouse series
summary: One of America’s largest yacht builders, Westport Yachts has tasted the saltwater with its first magnificent 41-meter yacht from its new Raised Pilothouse series.
body: An important milestone in the tantalizing chronicles of yachting has been reached. Westport Yachts, a stalwart in the American shipbuilding industry, has officially launched its first yacht from the freshly minted 41-meter Raised Pilothouse (RPH) series. The construction of this groundbreaking motor yacht began back in 2024 in Westport's cutting-edge facilities located in the Olympic Peninsula, Washington. Alongside it started the construction of two other hulls, all part of the same riveting RPH series.

The maiden voyage for the showgirl of the Westport's RPH series is scheduled for completion following vigorous sea trials, following which she will take to the stage in all her grandeur at the 2026 Palm Beach International Boat Show. Donned as the 'enhanced Westport 125', this 41-meter semi-custom model is touted as the crown jewel of Westport's 'next-generation' of motor yachts.

The interior of this marine marvel is a combination of luxury and practicality. It boasts a sizeable salon and dining area on the main deck designed to foster an 'indoor-outdoor' flow. Forward of this, there is a homey country-style galley and a generous skylounge to provide guests with unparalleled relaxation. Let's not forget about the sun deck replete with a hot tub, bar, and a beach-club-style transom. Accommodation is lavishly provided for 10 guests in a five-cabin configuration which includes a full-beam owner’s suite on the main deck.

In yet another demonstration of Westport's popularity, hulls two and three have already been sold. With hull two scheduled for delivery in September this year, and hull three in early 2027, it's safe to say Westport's vision is in high demand!

Daryl Wakefield, president of Westport, couldn't hide his excitement. Nothing seals the deal better than market response. The early sales success of hulls two and three, he believes, is the seal of approval from the market for this newcomer to Westport's armada.

title: Excitement Builds as 34-Meter Yacht ‘50 Shades of Play’ Emerges for the First-Time in Brokerage Market
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Excitement Builds as 34-Meter Yacht ‘50 Shades of Play’ Emerges for the First-Time in Brokerage Market
summary: The 34-metre AB Yachts motor yacht '50 Shades of Play' makes her premier appearance on the brokerage market after clinching the under-40-metre category Neptune at the 2025 World Superyacht Awards.
body: A breath of fresh sea air to the brokerage market, the award-winning 34-metre motor yacht '50 Shades of Play' has finally surfaced for the discerning buyers. Drawing a sporty yet contemporary profile, this stunning superyacht beat the competition to bag a Neptune in the under-40-metre category at the 2025 World Superyacht Awards.

Developed by AB Yachts, a brand by the Next Yacht Group, with design inputs from Archea Associati, '50 Shades of Play' boasts of not just an unmistakable modern aesthetic but also carried a suite of cutting-edge technology, setting her apart from her competitors. The highlights include the yacht's Starlink connectivity and integrated NEXT AI system, lending the vessel a high tech appeal.

The interiors of the yacht are a testament to tasteful minimalism, presenting clean lines and a refined colour palette. Expansive windows wash the main saloon with an abundance of natural light, accentuating the modern appeal.

Equipped with three MAN 2000hp water jets and powered by Seakeeper stabilization, ‘50 Shades of Play’ promises high-speed performance with a cruising speed of 38 knots, coupled with the practicality of a 1.3-metre draught, making her ideal for both high-speed and shallow-water cruising. The yacht also comes with warranties active until November 2027.

Currently harbouring in The Bahamas, '50 Shades of Play' marks a dynamic addition to the Fraser boats for sale roster, present on request and bound by confidentiality. With her debut in the brokerage market for the first time since her delivery in 2025, ‘50 Shades of Play’ presents an opportunity for an unforgettable Caribbean sailing adventure for its next owner.

title: The Valetta Voyage - Embarking on a Dynamic Journey with Malta's Own Melita Marine Group
author: Old Sea Dogs
