It's famed not only for its enriching VAT schemes and the honour of its Flag of Registry but for a nautical heritage that's steeped in tradition and innovation. It is within this vibrant backdrop that the Melita Marine Group flourishes.

From a distance, one may be drawn to the splendid architecture and robust infrastructure of Valetta Harbour, but it's the charm of Melita’s Chairman, Pierre Balzan, that beckons a deeper exploration. Exceptionally passionate about his venture, Pierre is a beacon whose glowing charisma brightens up an entire room. His far-reaching vision for the sector, paired with enduring customer relationships, lays the foundation for Melita's success.

Melita's strength lies in its diverse team. From hardworking shipyard characters to office staff managing finance, marketing and projects, all play an integral role in defining Melita's unwavering dedication to delivering excellence.

From the dry dock to the shipyard and offices, Melita echoes with a resonating motto - 'Because we care'. This is a truth passionately upheld by every member of Melita, from the longest-serving employee to the newest recruit. This ethos of committed care is being passed down to future generations, as Pierre’s son, John Balzan, stands ready to carry forward this legacy.

Indeed, Melita Marine Group serves a wide array of sectors including power generation, military, energy, commercial marine, and yachting. The scale and scope of their facilities dispel any perception of this entity as anything less than significant. It is this commitment to quality service and their care approach that cements Melita’s place as a guided beacon within Malta's maritime landscape.

title: Right Off the Racks! First Model of the Sunseeker 134 Yacht Acquired by an American Aficionado
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Right Off the Racks! First Model of the Sunseeker 134 Yacht Acquired by an American Aficionado
summary: A notable event at boot Düsseldorf 2026 was the announcement by British builder Sunseeker of the sale of the inaugural unit of their Sunseeker 134 yacht model.
body: Sailing in with noteworthy news from boot Düsseldorf 2026, British builder Sunseeker seized the platform to announce the first-ever sale of their sparkling new Sunseeker 134 yacht model. The mammoth 40.5-metre marvel has found an owner in America and is all set to make waves in 2027.

Sneaking a peek at Sunseeker’s renewed Superyacht Range, the Sunseeker 134 was initially presented to the world at the 2025 Cannes Yachting Festival. Aiming to transcend the bar set by its original concept designs, this model showcases a revamp in design, both in technicality and experience. Credited as a 'bold step forward' in the luxury marine industry, it represents Sunseeker’s revamped superyacht ethos.

An enhancement to the exterior living spaces across the aft cockpit, upper deck, and flybridge is also noteworthy. These spaces are distinctly designable with add-on features like a spa tub, extended hardtop, and a flybridge helm station. Further amplifying the yacht's social spaces and solidifying its connection with the sea is the significantly extended beach club and swim platform.

On the inside, the 134 unit was created in collaboration with Design Unlimited. This collaboration grants owners the freedom to design their own yacht with bespoke materials, finishes, and details. The interiors, bathed in natural light thanks to expansive floor-to-ceiling windows, showcase a warm neutral colour palette. The accommodation is spacious enough for a 10-person party and a nine-member crew.

Propelling the Sunseeker 134 are twin MTU engines, capable of reaching top speeds of up to 20 knots and covering a range of more than 1,200 nautical miles at 10 knots. The engineering sophistication and enhanced stabilization systems promise serene cruising. Key numbers include a 7.9-metre beam and a draught of 2.4 metres.

This sale announcement is coupled with the news of Andrea Frabetti stepping down as CEO and board director recently. Currently, Sunseeker has 31 yachts that are either on order or under construction. The Sunseeker 134 yacht, a testament to style, luxury, and engineering wanderlust, is all set to redefine the high-end yachting experience.

title: Remembering Alan 'AJ' Johnson: Icon of UK Dinghy Racing Across Multiple Classes
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Remembering Alan 'AJ' Johnson: Icon of UK Dinghy Racing Across Multiple Classes
summary: The world of UK dinghy racing mourns the loss of Alan 'AJ' Johnson, a passionate racer over the past six decades.
body: Alan 'AJ' Johnson, a stalwart of the UK dinghy racing scene, has sailed into the sunset. With a sailing career that spanned over six decades, AJ left a significant impact in various classes of dinghy racing.

It all began in 1963, when at the tender age of 16, AJ made his mark by finishing 13th in the GP14 National Championships, a competition with over 250 contenders. This was just the start for AJ, who went on to build a reputation in the GP14 and Enterprise fleets. His successes included two-time victor of the Enterprise National Championships, three-time Inland Championships conqueror, and Masters Championships triumph.

AJ leaves behind his wife Jane, who crewed for him in the 70s, eight children and 13 grandchildren. It’s apparent that love for the sea runs in the family; four of his children have sailed across the Atlantic while others are involved in the sailing and watersports industry, with some already tasting championship success.

The legacy that AJ leaves behind is undeniably profound. As the sailing world says its final goodbyes at the funeral service to be held on February 2nd, his love for the sport and zest for life continues to ripple through generations.

title: Expert Advice: Master Your Boat’s Trim for a Smoother, Economical and Safer Sailing Experience
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Expert Advice: Master Your Boat’s Trim for a Smoother, Economical and Safer Sailing Experience
summary: Get the smoothest, most efficient, and ultimately safest ride when sailing. Learn the intricate technique of trimming your boat from expert sailor Jon Mendez.
body: Sailing purists know that the key to smooth, economic, and safe navigation lies in mastering the art of trimming your boat. Basic good hull design will usually mean you won't need to constantly trim from the helm to keep the ride comfortable. But having the ability to effectively adjust the trim both fore and aft, as well as side to side, is extraordinarily beneficial for altering your vessel’s attitude to the sea.

Imagine, in an ideal world, as you hit the gas on a perfectly balanced sailboat. As the speed increases, the hull’s shape naturally lifts the boat onto its planing speed, seemingly skimming over the water’s surface. However, reality checks in when the boat’s weight starts to fluctuate due to adding passengers, fuel, supplies or even kit, thus altering the initially perfect balance.

Most vessels, equipped with shaft and pod drives, do not have the ability to trim the propeller’s angle of attack. They usually come with trim tabs or interceptor plates on the transom's sides at the hull's base. Descending them into the water increases pressure, leading to lift. The more they're trimmed down, the greater the stern's lift, forcing the bow downwards.

Getting to grips with how your boat responds under different loads, wind and sea conditions', using available controls, can make your sea voyage as smooth as the one its designer initially envisioned. Steering a sailing boat is a science, and trimming is its most crucial experiment, one that needs to be mastered for safer, smoother, and more economic voyages.

title: The Clipper Round the World Yacht Race Participants Relish an Exhilarating Stopover in the Midst of Tropical Cyclone at Airlie Beach
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Clipper Round the World Yacht Race Participants Relish an Exhilarating Stopover in the Midst of Tropical Cyclone at Airlie Beach
summary: The Clipper Round the World Yacht Race's exceptional stopover at Airlie Beach demonstrates its reputation as a first-rate sailing destination, despite challenging tropical conditions.
body: Airlie Beach and Coral Sea Marina has once again solidified their reputation as a destination of choice for world-class sailing events. The beach was recently the gracious host of a lively stopover for the Clipper Round the World Yacht Race. The international fleet arrived at a time when a tropical low was brewing, setting the stage for an exhilarating showdown.\With the imminent threat of Tropical Cyclone Koji, the marina presented a dramatic backdrop for yachts making landfall amidst stormy, wet conditions, welcomed by eager race officials and adoring supporters.\Coral Sea Marina CEO, Kate Preston, highlighted how events like these cast a global spotlight on the Whitsundays' ability to deliver top-notch sailing experiences. This, she believes, lays the groundwork for the upcoming Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games sailing events.\As Cyclone Koji finally passed, the fleet found safe refuge at the port. Upon the storm's passage, sunshine returned, bestowing a warm welcome for the final arrivals at the Coral Sea Marina.\The Airlie Beach Stopover program then kicked off, lavishing yacht crew members with a plethora of exhilarating experiences, both at sea and onshore.\A memorable point was the Leg 4 Prizegiving Event. Hosted at Coral Sea Marina, the event was an outpour of camaraderie, celebrating the completion of the All-Australian leg of the race, with food, music, and fond reminiscing of sea voyages.\The event didn't just stop at celebrations; education and conservation projects were a significant portion of the stopover activities. Crew members got an insightful look into local restoration works, guided tours, and wildlife experiences, truly immersing them in Australia's rich coastal ecosystem and lifestyle.\In conclusion, this was more than just a race event. It was a complete ensemble of adventure, learning, and enjoyment, highlighting Australia's commitment to promoting top-tier sailing experiences and conserving its unique marine ecosystem.

title: Witness the Epoch of Turkish Yacht Building: Meet M/Y Angelique, the Nation's Largest Craft
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Witness the Epoch of Turkish Yacht Building: Meet M/Y Angelique, the Nation's Largest Craft
summary: Marking a historical moment in Turkish yacht building, Turquoise Yachts introduces M/Y Angelique, the largest yacht ever built in the country.
body: Turkey's illustrious shipbuilding name, Turquoise Yachts, has unveiled the crown jewel in the country's yacht-building history. Introducing M/Y Angelique, an 87-metre behemoth shattering records as the largest yacht ever constructed in Turkey, setting a new course for the nation's naval achievements. The superyacht marks the pinnacle of a 17-year collaboration between Turquoise and H2 Yacht Design, a partnership responsible for 12 stellar projects. "Vento is a remarkable achievement," expresses Burak Akgül, CEO of Turquoise Yachts, "reflecting the collective expertise, dedication and passion applied to designing, engineering and crafting yachts at Turquoise."

The interior design further impressively displays rich Art Deco influence. Jonny Horsfield, founder of H2, explains how the design, initially inspired by the 77m Go, another Turquoise and H2 collaboration, was morphed into something uniquely suited to the tastes and lifestyle of the owner, featuring blue accents throughout, deluxe guest accommodation and a private wellness suite.

The triumphant project is the result of intense cooperation between Turquoise Yachts, H2 Yacht Design and the owner's team, with Occam Marine providing owner’s representation. Co-founder of Occam Marine, Giles Frankal, applauds the unison, attributing the success to "transparency, shared commitment to excellence, and a genuine spirit of partnership." So it is, the M/Y Angelique becomes the grand testament to what can be achieved when a shipyard and owner's team work in harmonious synchrony. As the future unfolds, it's certain that the world will be watching what leaps of nautical glory come next from the Turquoise Yachts and H2 Yacht Design collaboration.

title: Unveiling the Pioneers of the Seas: Winners of the 2026 Motor Boat Awards
author: Old Sea Dogs

summary: Paying tribute to exceptional oceanic explorers, the 2026 Motor Boat Awards announced its winners at a grandiose ceremony held in Düsseldorf.

Hosted amidst the splendour of Düsseldorf, the gleaming awards celebrated outstanding designs, valiant performance, and inspiring maritime innovation. The meticulousness of the judging process that spanned months of testing, weeks of analysis, and days of cogitation was evident in the winners.

Each winner was selected from a cohort of ten categories, considering the stellar performance during rigorous sea trials as well the aligned requirements of its target market in terms of size, style, and price. Top performers were recognised in innovative ways, with a few contentious categories ending in a commendable second place.

In the fascinating world of weekenders, the Navan S30 ascended to the top in splendid style. Its predominant win in a market teeming with multi-purpose centre-console sports boats emphasises the outstanding design, laudable build quality, and pleasing layout of Navan S30.

As for family cruisers, the Norwegian native, Viknes 10, scooped the award. Its clever, well-specified design and meticulous detailing reflect the essence of seamless integration. Its rewarding design clarity, complemented by a reasonable price, positions it as a well-deserving winner in the family cruiser category.

In captivating a global audience with design, performance and innovation at its peak, the Motor Boat Awards provided a platform for maritime revolutionaries to shine, setting the course for future seafarers to steer their own inventions and adventures.

title: Amid Geopolitical Tensions and Corporate Strain, KKCG Maritime Ups the Ante in Ferretti's Quandary
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Amid Geopolitical Tensions and Corporate Strain, KKCG Maritime Ups the Ante in Ferretti's Quandary
summary: KKCG Maritime aims to increase its stake in Ferretti, marking a tipping point in the Italian yacht builder's turbulent shareholder climate.
body: KKCG Maritime, the ambitious maritime offshoot of Prague-based conglomerate KKCG, has gone all in on its quest for a near-blocking stake in the Italian luxury yacht maker, Ferretti. This savvy move comes as Ferretti finds itself mired in an increasingly complex and politically charged shareholder landscape. Ferretti's entanglement in the broader scrutiny of Chinese strategic ownership in Italy following recent allegations of espionage ramps up the stakes even further.

Strategically, KKCG Maritime aims to snap up to 52.1 million shares, roughly 15.4 percent of Ferretti’s total share capital. This tactical manoeuvre would nudge KKCG Maritime's stake from a healthy 14.5 percent to a commanding 29.9 percent, offering the company greater influence in the boardroom, all for a tidy sum of roughly €182.5 million. It's a high-risk bet that could pay off handsomely.

Interestingly, KKCG's proposition is just teetering below the 30 percent threshold that would necessitate a full takeover under Italian and Hong Kong regulations. This appears to be a strategic manoeuvre, as the company has no intentions of eliciting a delisting.

Upon successful completion of the offer, KKCG Maritime plans to wield its newfound clout to champion its nominees for Ferretti’s board at the forthcoming annual general meeting. As Karel Komárek, founder and chairman of KKCG, notes, 'This offer reflects our aim to build upon our long-standing investment in Ferretti and contribute to its future growth and prosperity, leveraging our proven expertise to bolster Ferretti’s organic and inorganic growth opportunities amid the prevailing global sector dynamics.'

The dynamic power play by KKCG Maritime symbolises a possible proxy contest at Ferretti with the potential to reshape the company's control dynamics. Previous squabbles with Weichai over capital allocation and a withdrawn share buyback program have already spotlighted the power struggles within the company. As such, KKCG's gambit arrives at a globally sensitive time, with boardroom tensions soaring owing to recent claims of surveillance on Weichai's representatives. This ensnares Ferretti in an international mesh of scrutiny and it's certain to be a tension-fraught journey on the horizon.

title: Steeler Yachts Hits the Waves with a Second Unit from Their Impressive Ocean Explorer 85 Yacht Series: Meet Moss
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Steeler Yachts Hits the Waves with a Second Unit from Their Impressive Ocean Explorer 85 Yacht Series: Meet Moss
summary: Steeler Yachts announces the launch of Moss, the second offering from its Ocean Explorer 85 yacht series—a testimonial to achievement at sea.
body: The Dutch shipyard Steeler Yachts unveils its latest manifestation of marine ingenuity–the Moss. This second yacht of its innovative Ocean Explorer 85 series is all set to embark on a fascinating voyage, proving once again the inimitable capabilities of the distinguished boat-maker.

Gently skimming the waters near the Steeler's facilities in Meppel, in the Netherlands, Moss anticipates a round of sea trials before marking its unstoppable presence in the world's seascapes. Its scheduled delivery soon follows, the next adventure being a maiden voyage to the Indian Ocean.

Steeler Yachts penchant for close collaboration with yacht owners was pivotal in fashioning Moss' signature style. Devised for 'hands-on, long-distance cruising', Moss personifies adventure on the open seas. The yacht's owner, who also serves as its captain, played a significant role in curating its bespoke design—each element symbolising a rendezvous of luxury and functionality. The full custom 148GT interior, masterminded by revered designer Kees Marcelis, fosters an ambiance of comfort for extended time spent on the open water. Moss can comfortably accommodate up to six guests across its three cabins in addition to providing quarters for a crew of two.

The launch came closely on the heels of the groundbreaking transatlantic crossing by Ocean Explorer 72 Two Bubbles. Having completed the voyage with flying colours, it exemplified the Ocean Explorer line’s prowess for both offshore and long-distance cruising. The Ocean Explorer catalogue thus flaunts three new builds to its credit, with an additional Ocean Explorer 72 in commission.

The new Moss boasts an impressive beam measuring 6.6 metres with a shallow draft of 1.7 metres. In compliance with CE-A standards, Moss meets the Malta sCYC 2024 flag requirements for an unrestricted navigation notation.

This second unit of the Ocean Explorer 85 series, with its trailblazing design and formidable functionality, not only furthers Steeler’s Yachts esteemed legacy but takes it to a stellar new level by redefining luxurious long-distance cruising.

title: Revolutionising the Yachting Sector: AV/IT Training Programme Empowers Crew with Essential Technical Skills
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Revolutionising the Yachting Sector: AV/IT Training Programme Empowers Crew with Essential Technical Skills
summary: The Professional Yachting Association introduces a unique AV/IT training initiative, bridging the gap between technological needs and crew capabilities on board yachts.
body: Charting a course to meet the increasing demand for skilled yacht crews, The Professional Yachting Association (PYA) unveils an avant-garde AV/IT training programme tailored to the evolving needs of the industry. Working in collaboration with key stakeholders, including equipment manufacturers, installation and maintenance specialists, and training providers, the initiative seeks to familiarise crews with the technological systems found on modern yachts. These are not just any system, but those that greatly influence on-board operations, guest experiences, and cyber-security. The courses chart a new destination, not leaning towards a degree-level certificate of competency in electrical systems, but rather a practical proficiency in audio-visual and IT systems – a requirement slowly gaining more traction.

Level one provides foundational insights into common AV/IT systems onboard superyachts. Level two, on the other hand, targets crew members keen on spearheading the role of an on-board AV/IT expert. It includes training on the types of data circulating within on-board networks, common terminologies, and the integration between the yacht's internal systems and external networks. Level three focusses on operational expertise around installation and integration of AV/IT systems during new builds and refitting projects. This pioneering initiative bridges the gap between the industry's increasing requirement of tech-proficient crews and presently unmet training needs, paving the way for a future where technology and yachting are not separate entities, but co-pilots in a harmonious journey.

title: Golden Opportunity: Britain's Youth America's Cup Team Kick-starts Selection Process Under Guidance of Hannah Mills
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Golden Opportunity: Britain's Youth America's Cup Team Kick-starts Selection Process Under Guidance of Hannah Mills
summary: Olympic gold medalist, Hannah Mills OBE, launches the selection process for Britain's Youth America's Cup Team, aiming at nurturing the next generation.
body: The sails are set and the selection process for Britain's Youth America's Cup Team is officially underway. The announcement comes from none other than Team Principal of Athena Pathway Programme (APP), Hannah Mills, at the America's Cup Partnership event in Naples.

This marks the initiation for the Youth Squad to compete in the exciting spectacle of the Youth America's Cup in Naples, slated for 2027. The programme, meritoriously backed by Cobham Ultra, nestles at the core of the team's high-performance development blueprint. It aims at identifying, assessing, and honing British talent with the aptitude to contend in the grand Youth America's Cup. It also nourishes progression into professional maritime careers.

Speaking about this blue ribbon event, Team Principal Hannah Mills expressed her thrill about the initiation of the selection process. Having almost reached the summit of the podium in the women's and youth categories previously, she feels this is a ripe opportunity to tie up loose ends.

The published selection policy frames a transparent eligibility criterion, assessment processes, and expectations from the athletes. Open to male and female young sailors compliant with World Sailing Regulation 19 and born between 1 July 2001 and 1 July 2008, the programme promises high-performance levels, primarily catering to sailors with national or international sailing experience or crucial foiling experience.
Promoting inclusivity, the Athena Pathway doesn't limit participation based on conventional pathways and encourages application from sailors who may have taken a nonlinear or unconventional route.

Their last campaign introduced several talents to the world including Matt Beck, Nick Robins, and Ellie Aldridge. Ellie Aldridge, an Olympic gold medallist, is now a full-time member of the APP Women's Team and the Emirates GBR SailGP Team.

The America's Cup's fresh commitment to Women's and Youth competitions shines a hopeful light, manifesting a future that is both inclusive and forward-focused. And it serves to inspire the next generation of exceptional sailors, a venture at which Athena Pathway Programme has been a driving force for the past five years.

title: Industry Initiative 'Superyacht Reality' Launches to Showcase the True Experience of Life at Sea
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Industry Initiative 'Superyacht Reality' Launches to Showcase the True Experience of Life at Sea
summary: Superyacht Reality, an initiative by the Professional Yachting Association, is set to correct common misconceptions about life on yachts by giving the public a first-hand, realistic view of this profession.
body: Superyacht Reality, the Professional Yachting Association's groundbreaking initiative launches in January 2026. Backed by acclaimed think tank, 'Raising The Bar', this global awareness campaign aims to shed light on the true realities of life on a yacht, dispelling common misconceptions and public misunderstandings about the industry.

The campaign encourages professional yacht crew members to provide an insider's view into their lives at sea, initiating a unique storytelling experience to the public. By sharing authentic photos and candid videos that portray everyday life and work onboard, they offer insights into skills, teamwork, and the routines that shape a career at sea. This initiative strives not only to present a realistic view of professional life on board but also to highlight the professionalism, skill, and responsibility that define the modern yachting industry.

The campaign is actively sharing this content with media outlets, extending its reach beyond the yachting community and into the general public and education sector. By prioritizing the true portrayal of life onboard, the campaign aims to promote yachting as an appealing career path to the upcoming generation.

The initiative is not just for the yacht crews, it presents a unique chance for the audiences to interact with daily Instagram themes, compete in supplementary competitions, and potentially win giveaways. The primary competition however, occurs through the PYA website, where submissions are awarded for the Best Photo – Life On Board, Best Video – Work & Skill and The Superyacht Reality Award – Most Authentic Moment.

Superyacht Reality stands as a beacon of truth in an industry often misconceived, shifting perceptions through a realistic depiction of career awareness, responsible recruitment and accurate public understanding of professional yachting. This campaign is testament of a collective commitment to upholding industry standards and promoting crew wellbeing.

title: Step Inside the Bold Evolution of Mediterranean Living Afloat: Aiata's Striking Flagship, the Sunfinder 50
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Step Inside the Bold Evolution of Mediterranean Living Afloat: Aiata's Striking Flagship, the Sunfinder 50
summary: One autumn after its initial endeavour, young Turkish boat-builder Aiata sails into Düsseldorf, breaching the surface with its newest admiration: the Sunfinder 50.
body: A year after debuting at boot Düsseldorf, Aiata surfaces to reveal its Dreamliner - the Sunfinder 50 - a bold evolution in the realm of Mediterranean style boating. Born from a collaborative process with Finnish designer Jarkko Jämsén, the Sunfinder 50 focuses on fast-paced, spacious, multipurpose family boating with modular versatility at its heart.

Embracing an expansive, open-deck lifestyle orientation, the Sunfinder 50 appeals to a unique class of mariners who savour that immersive connection to the sea, prioritizing a shared beach club vibe over all-weather protection.

Through an artistic reimagination that reduces the enclosed cabin to a sleeker T-top design, Aiata allows sea voyagers an unbarred transition from the vessel's helm to the swim platform. This aesthetic revolution morphs the boat from being a simple rugged commuter to an elegant Mediterranean day-boat, capable of sailing nimbly across weekend coastal journeys.

Despite introducing an innovative design concept, the Sunfinder 50 doesn't marginalize on essential comforts for any overnight voyage. The flared bow of the boat, equipped to function as a capacious dining station and convertible sunpad, will be further amplified in its new avatar.

The flagship from Aiata is an exemplar of exciting innovation, and it will dock alongside a 38ft model of the same Sunfinder lineage in Germany. This duo demonstrates Aiata's vision to construct a comprehensive, multi-tiered portfolio at an impressively brisk pace.

Will the Sunfinder series mark a new era in the boating industry? Renowned as the home of motoryacht enthusiasts, Motor Boat & Yachting is a fitting platform to make this brand's vision sail towards its shore of dreams. As they often say, a journey to the horizon begins with the unbraiding of the ropes.

title: Vaikobi Revolutionises Sailing Gloves with Launch of Gen2 V-Grip for Enhanced Protection
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Vaikobi Revolutionises Sailing Gloves with Launch of Gen2 V-Grip for Enhanced Protection
summary: Sailing gear giant Vaikobi introduces a game-changer in nautical attire: the revamped Gen2 V-Grip Gloves. Adaptable and protective, they promise to redefine on-deck wear.
body: Innovation and protection meet as Vaikobi, renowned ocean performance gear brand, unveils the sophisticated Gen2 V-Grip Gloves. A step above their predecessor, the Gen2 Gloves retain the durability and grip of Gen1 whilst stepping ahead in terms of protection and comfort.

Nothing less than revolutionary, these gloves are simultaneously robust and dexterous. Leveraging the proven grip of Gen1, the gloves have been upgraded with more hand and finger protection. In particular, the wrist cuffs have been lengthened, ensuring additional sun and abrasion coverage without adding unnecessary bulk to the wearer.

Specifically designed for on-deck usage, they are perfect for trimming heavy lines, loaded winches, or in the pit. For jobs requiring reactive or quick trimming of thin lines, or for those just seeking an extra layer of protection from the sun and abrasion while boating, the Gen2 V-Grip Gloves come through.

From skiffs to dinghies, big boats to personal cruisers, the Gen2 V-Grip Gloves prove a worthy addition to any sailor’s gear. With their proven grip and enhanced protection, they bear the potential to redefine the standard of nautical wear. Vaikobi clearly steps into the future, once again meeting the demands of the evolving world of ocean performance.

title: Enthusiasm grows as Round The Island Race 2026 draws near; substantial discounts for those who jump on board early
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Enthusiasm grows as Round The Island Race 2026 draws near; substantial discounts for those who jump on board early
summary: The iconic Round The Island Race is back for yet another year of enthralling and spectacular sailing competition. A call to skippers worldwide, seize early bird discounts that will make sailing enthusiasts swoon.
body: Skippers around the globe are bracing themselves in thrilled enthusiam for the globally-renowned Round The Island Race 2026, a 50-nautical mile championship around England's emerald isle, the Isle of Wight. The competition gears up for the launch event on Friday, January 23, extending a generous early bird discount to those ready to ride the wind for three weeks until race day on Saturday, July 11.

"The thrill is almost tangible. We can't wait to set free this sportive bird. The Round The Island Race 2026 is stepping into the spotlight," shares Dave Atkinson, Race Director. Ensuring every detail is perfectly in place, the Island Sailing Club has been laboring diligently behind the scenes. As the launch approaches, it's high time to build that pre-race momentum.

Set off from the infamous Royal Yacht Squadron Line at Cowes and set sail west to The Needles. Traverse around the isle, pass St Catherine's Point and Bembridge Ledge Buoy, voyage into the Solent and sail back to Cowes to finish. This is one unforgettable and thrilling journey worth every penny.
Take advantage of significantly discounted prices across boats of all sizes by signing up early. Entry fee prices that start from £140 will revert to standard prices from Friday, February 14.

In addition to the race, a dedicated Race Village on Cowes Parade will be open throughout the race weekend, supplying a plethora of entertainment over three days, from Friday, July 10. From live music to thrilling maritime activities for all family members, there won't be a dull moment.

title: Experience the Unparalleled Luxury and Superior Performance of the Beneteau FIRST 60
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Experience the Unparalleled Luxury and Superior Performance of the Beneteau FIRST 60
summary: The Beneteau FIRST 60, the grandest vessel from Beneteau Group, is a wonder of naval design and craftsmanship, promising exhilarating seafaring adventures and unprecedented opulence.
body: For close to five decades, the FIRST lineup from Beneteau Group has unveiled vessels of elegance and superior performance, specially crafted for sailors whose heartbeats align with the rhythm of the sea breeze and the gentle lapping of the waves. The Beneteau FIRST 60 marks a considerable milestone, as the largest First ever built, promising an undiluted sailing experience to those in pursuit of intensity and precision.

Adorned with a sleek profile and timeless lines, the FIRST 60 beautifully embodies the artistry and engineering brilliance of naval architect, Biscontini Yacht Design, and acclaimed designer Lorenzo Argento. Every element of this extraordinary yacht is meticulously honed to perfection - from the streamlined sailing systems that offer flawless interaction with the vessel, to the carefully arranged cockpit that affords breathtaking views of the surrounding water.

Unveiling unparalleled advancement in sail controls, the FIRST 60 introduces a captive mainsheet winch for effortless precision and an adaptive helm ergonomics shaped around the sailor's natural posture. All running rigging is centralized in the walk-around Winch Island for secure, seamless handling, while the Park Avenue boom simplifies the hoisting and lowering of the mainsail. This design not only ensures speed but also provides ample space, guaranteeing a thrilling yet confident sailing experience.

The FIRST 60 is an unabashed celebration of luxury, purpose, and performance. She offers distinctly designed cockpit zones for relaxation, dining, and sailing - seamlessly integrating comfort, safety, and ease of movement. This thoughtful segregation heightens the onboard experience, making every second at sea or anchor an immersive, luxurious journey.

title: The 2026 Chemical Riders Event: A Breakthrough Moment In Windsurfing, Setting A Course For A Future 4 Challenger World Cup
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The 2026 Chemical Riders Event: A Breakthrough Moment In Windsurfing, Setting A Course For A Future 4 Challenger World Cup
summary: The 2026 Chemical Riders event marks a bold step forward for Eastern Mediterranean windsurfing, setting the stage for a potential 4-Star Challenger World Cup.
body: The 2026 Chemical Riders event highlighted an exciting era for Eastern Mediterranean windsurfing, and is surfacing as a definitive turning point for the sport. Hosted in Haifa's raw, industrialised 'Tails' beach, the event boasted what many describe as the best competition conditions ever recorded in the region. These included powerful 4-metre wave faces coupled with 30-knot winds that created a challenging yet highly entertaining showdown of skills.

The event was masterfully orchestrated by Moran Tapiro and Arnon Dagan. Their efforts showcased the rare power and consistency of Mediterranean conditions, further hinting that Haifa could potentially rise to a 4-Star Challenger World Cup status by 2027.

The spectators were also treated to some heart-stopping manoeuvres during the event. Steep, fast-moving sections demanded late drops, vertical hits, and total control amidst punishing gusts. These exhilarating moments greatly separated those with genuine wave skills from mere survival.

The professional judging and the LiveHeats platform guaranteed world-class standards throughout the competition. 'Seeing Olympic champions, professional tour riders, and local talents all charging serious waves together shows just how far Israeli windsurfing has come - and where it can go,' stated producer Moran Tapiro.

The Chemical Riders Haifa, with its extreme conditions, seasoned operations team, and unique Mediterranean setting, has impressively carved its place beyond regional status. The 2026 edition, with its focus on conditions, credibility, and performance, echos the elevated potential of Haifa as a serious 4-Star Challenger candidate from 2027.

title: 2026 Chemical Riders Event Ushers New Era For Eastern Mediterranean Windsurfing; On Track For 4-Star Challenger World Cup Status
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: 2026 Chemical Riders Event Ushers New Era For Eastern Mediterranean Windsurfing; On Track For 4-Star Challenger World Cup Status
summary: The 2026 Chemical Riders historical event has brought Eastern Mediterranean windsurfing into the limelight, a game-changer that pushed Haifa towards a prospective 4-Star Challenger World Cup status by 2027.
body: The Chemical Riders Haifa 2026 has generated an electrifying shockwave in the windsurfing community, bringing a revolution in the Eastern Mediterranean windsurfing and marking a new era. The event, which unfolded under some of the most condusive competition conditions, showcased both Eastern Mediterranean's raw, industrial beauty and high-octane windsurfing power.

The fleet dazzled not only in its sheer size but also in the exceptional cross-disciplinary talent it brought together. Olympic heroes, world-tour sailors and proven international champions shared the same high-intensity arena, battling it out on powerful 4-metre wave faces combined with blistering 30-knot winds. These commendable conditions were unmatched, ramping up the excitement and lending a palpable exhilaration to the event, such that has never been seen in the region.

The competition standards were upheld, led by professional on-site judging and the use of the LiveHeats platform. Among those who rose triumphant were great luminaries such as Olympic Gold Medallist Tom Reuveny and Youth World Champion Yoav Cohen, contributing to the show of strength by Israel's windsurfing elite.

Looking beyond the regional status, Chemical Riders Haifa 2026 has demonstrated extreme conditions and a solidly capable operations team, which propels it towards the status of 4-Star Challenger candidate from 2027. This speaks volumes about the vibrant future of Israeli windsurfing and sets the stage for the upcoming 2026 Melges 24 World Championship in Harbor Springs, Michigan.

title: The Exhilarating 43.5m Tecnomar Catamaran 'This Is It' Debuts in the Brokerage Market
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Exhilarating 43.5m Tecnomar Catamaran 'This Is It' Debuts in the Brokerage Market
summary: For the first time, the breathtaking 43.5-metre Tecnomar catamaran 'This Is It' hits the brokerage market. Regionally known as the world's largest motor catamaran for charter.
body: There is a newcomer on the brokerage scene that's bound to cause quite a stir. The 43.5-metre Tecnomar catamaran, 'This Is It', listed for sale by IYC and Royal Yacht International, is a spectacle to behold. The first of its imagination-defying kind to ever grace the market since its creation in 2024, 'This Is It' stuns with its aluminium construction by the prominent Italian shipyard, The Italian Sea Group.

This audacious aquatic marvel's unveiling occurred at the 2023 Monaco Yacht Show, setting the industry abuzz with excitement. 'This Is It' soon joined the charter market as the world's largest motor catamaran for charter, a credential that is no small feat. Its unique design, elegantly encapsulating a 14.5-metre beam, and approximately 600 square metres of glass panelling, has seen the catamaran play host to celebrities like Rihanna and A$AP Rocky.

Unique floor-to-ceiling doors connect the saloon to the exterior which houses a bar, game area, swimming pool, and formal dining space. The upper deck doesn't lose any charm with a contained spa, complete with a dedicated treatment area and sauna. Even more impressive is the playroom that doubles as a guest room, adjacent to the spa. A swanky show-kitchen, designed with polarised glass, finishes off the amazing offerings of 'This Is It'.

A combination of inspiration from the automotive world, sea creatures, and residential architecture, all manifest in the life of this beautiful sea vessel, redefining traditional yachting norms and pushing yacht design boundaries ever further.

title: How The Uncertain Waves of Geopolitics and Insurance Transform the Yacht Chartering Industry: An Analysis
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: How The Uncertain Waves of Geopolitics and Insurance Transform the Yacht Chartering Industry: An Analysis
summary: A sudden closure of Caribbean airspace reveals glaring vulnerabilities in the yacht charter industry, sparking discussions about risk mitigation, insurance limitations, and effective contingency planning.
body: In the idyllic Caribbean—a prime destination for yacht charters—an unexpected airspace shutdown left guests adrift, forcing the industry to confront its vulnerabilities and limitations. More significantly, it emphasized the intertwined nature of geopolitical risks, insurance limits, and charter assumptions during the jet-set charter season.

This incident, seemingly a hindrance, served as a wake-up call, pushing the industry behemoths to reassess risk management strategies and contingency plans. Marine insurers, security specialists, and charter brokers engaged in serious dialogue to examine how the event has irrevocably shaped attitudes towards routing, coverage, and contingency planning.

The ripple effects of geopolitical instability are not confined to terrestrial domains and the airspace above; they expand into the maritime sphere, directly influencing the yacht charter industry. Acknowledging this, industry players have begun to critically examine insurance limits and scrutiny of Advance Provisioning Allowance (APA) assumptions.

The takeaway from this incident is clear—the yacht charter industry must navigate carefully through the turbulent waters of risk, while ensuring adequate insurance coverage and robust contingency plans. The Caribbean airspace closure serves as an instructive lesson in adaptability and preparedness, proving that unexpected obstacles are opportunities in disguise.

title: Experience Unmatched Luxury on the High Seas: Price Drop On The Esteemed 38m Sanlorenzo Motor Yacht Glory
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Experience Unmatched Luxury on the High Seas: Price Drop On The Esteemed 38m Sanlorenzo Motor Yacht Glory
summary: Attention, yacht admirers! The 38.4-metre Sanlorenzo motor yacht 'Glory' boasts a new price cut of a whopping $1.5M. Now own this opulent beauty for a riveting sea journey like no other.
body: Built to US spec and one of the stunning 18 units of the SD126 series by the Italian shipyard Sanlorenzo, the 38.4-metre motor yacht 'Glory' is far from stepping off the limelight. Delivered in 2022, it has received a massive $1.5M price reduction and is now up for grabs at $14,500,000, inclusive of US duty paid.

With its exterior lines designed by Francesco Paszkowski Design and interior styling by Marty Lowe, 'Glory' is the epitome of finesse. Since its delivery, the yacht has been meticulously maintained, boasting a new exterior ceramic hull coating, and bottom paint completed in October 2025. Further augmenting its appeal are the new exterior cushions, tables and loose furniture added in October 2024.

The upper deck skylounge, acting as the perfect hub for entertainment, houses a wet bar and lounge seating along with a television. Offering panoramic views is the aft deck, establishing itself as the go-to zone for al fresco dining and casual barbecues alongside additional lounge seating.

The flybridge, under the shelter of a louvred hardtop, comes equipped with overlooking bar stools and a Jacuzzi. A second Jacuzzi finds its place on the foredeck, with a swim platform offering easy water access.

'Glory' can comfortably house up to 12 guests, with an array of cabin configurations. The owner's suite spans the yacht's full 7.5-metre beam on the main deck, and it is further supplemented by a VIP cabin on the upper deck, three double cabins on the lower deck, and a twin bunk cabin on the lower deck guest foyer. The twin bunk cabin doubles up as the captain's cabin, providing extra flexibility.

The yacht is powered by twin CAT C32 1,600hp engines, allowing a cruising speed of 11 knots and a top speed of 16.5 knots. At present, 'Glory' is up for sale in Miami, Fort Lauderdale, awaiting its next owner who appreciates the art of sailing with unmatched luxury.

title: Azimut Peddles Luxury with Flagship Design Unveiling: An Insight on the Fly 82 Interior
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Azimut Peddles Luxury with Flagship Design Unveiling: An Insight on the Fly 82 Interior
summary: Azimut, the Italian shipyard, unveils remarkable interior designs for its latest flagship flybridge model, the Fly 82, redefining the look of luxury yachting.
body: Known for its innovative and remarkable designs, the Italian shipyard Azimut has taken the wraps off its most recent flybridge model, the Fly 82. This flagship model stretches 24.8 metres and adds a fresh aspect to Azimut's best-selling Fly series that features six different designs sailing between 16.8 and 23.6 metres. The exterior of the Fly 82, designed by long-standing collaborator Alberto Mancini, merges gentle curves with sharply defined lines, creating a look that somehow appears to be in motion even when at rest. The yacht's interiors are brought to life by Fabio Fantolino, marking his third successful project with Azimut.

Incorporating brand's signature DNA with innovative layout solutions, the Fly 82 models a significant advancement in Azimut's vision of outdoor living. It introduces the pioneering Deck2Deck terrace system, an additional social space at the stern, defined by an opening transom that seamlessly aligns with the aft edge of the main deck.

Mancini's design choice for the flagship model includes power from Triple Volvo Penta engines capable of a top speed of 32 knots and a cruising speed of 25 knots. The Fly 82 boasts an optimised hull designed by Pierluigi Ausonio Naval Architecture and the Azimut|Benetti Group R&D department, offering a 20 to 30 per cent decrease in CO2 emissions. Fitted with a WATCHIT Eye, the first collision avoidance system for yachts based on artificial intelligence, the model amalgamates luxury with safety.

Currently, Azimut has 79 superyachts undergoing construction or on order, each vying to redefine luxury yachting. The Fly 82 is not just another addition to Azimut's portfolio, but a leap forward in setting new standards in the world of luxury yachting.

title: Experience Marital History: Classic Feadship Superyachts for Future Custodians
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Experience Marital History: Classic Feadship Superyachts for Future Custodians
summary: Owning a classic Feadship superyacht means being custodian to a slice of maritime history. Several lovingly restored models await new owners on the brokerage market.
body: To be a custodian of a classic Feadship superyacht is akin to being designated the steward of a significant slice of maritime chronicles. Many of these grand dames forged by the revered Dutch yard await fresh starts and humming futures in the hands of new torchbearers in the bustling brokerage market.

Another classic ride on the waters, Calypso was conceived from steel and aluminium for the esteemed E. Clayton Gengras. Since her arrival, the Calypso has served to the needs of royalty and Hollywood luminaries alike and has seen a colorful life of charting remote expeditions. With multiple refits over the years, the Calypso retains the unmissable Feadship aesthetic, seamlessly meeting modern-day specifications. The recent refit of 2025 augmented it with new hull upgrades, fresh teak decks, and interior enhancements. The once forward main-deck dining room has been transformed into an opulent owner's suite, making room for a VIP suite. With additions like a Jacuzzi, alfresco dining, a redesigned bar, and an outdoor cinema on deck, Calypso promises an unforgettable step back in time.

Hailed as the priciest Feadship model during her 1963 launch, Santa Maria was constructed acting upon the commands of the automobile giant Henry Ford II. With chic interior designs resembling that of an old chateau, Santa Maria exudes a charm that ages like fine wine.

To own such a vintage Feadship superyacht promises not just the chance to experience an era of grandeur gone by - it also conveys the power of luxury sailing, where time-honored design elements interweave with the best of modern-day advancements.

title: The Greenline 42 Makes Waves with its Semi-custom Design and Advanced Solar Technology.
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Greenline 42 Makes Waves with its Semi-custom Design and Advanced Solar Technology.
summary: Slovenian firm Greenline makes a splash at Dusseldorf with the versatile and energy-efficient Greenline 42, offering semi-custom features and cutting-edge solar power technology.
body: The Greenline 42, unveiled at the Düsseldorf Boat Show, marks a new era in semi-custom boating design, offering innovative solar power technology for high-efficiency cruising. This innovative model from Slovenia’s Greenline shipyard exudes versatility with a dizzying array of customisable options that give future owners the freedom to design their dream vessel. Amidst these options, the base model itself comes festooned with a plethora of amenities which further enhance the vessel's appeal.

The boat’s aesthetic allure is equally praiseworthy. Graceful windows at the aft end of the superstructure, molded bulwark cut-outs, and low-level glazing present a sleek and modern silhouette. Further aesthetic delights include glass panels housed in the roof struts and an array of intricate angles in the hull, windows, and topsides that add a touch of contemporary flair.

As for its performance, the Greenline 42 comes equipped with twin Yanmar 4LV-250 diesels, enabling a top speed of 25 knots. However, it's not all about high speed. Greenline's focus on smoothness, stability, and optimised efficiency allows the installation of a 4.3kW solar array on the expansive roof structure, plus a Greenline H-Drive 6G system for silent electric maneuvering. All the above, combined with interior decadence and external charm, make the Greenline 42 a unique contender in the yachting world, redefining the landscape of versatile and sustainable cruising.

title: World Premiere of Greenline 42: A Solar Power Advanced Cruiser Offering Semi-Custom Approach
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: World Premiere of Greenline 42: A Solar Power Advanced Cruiser Offering Semi-Custom Approach
summary: Greenline, a Slovenian Shipyard, unveils its newest vessel - the Greenline 42, offering versatile customization options and superior energy efficiency with its advanced solar power setup.
body: Say hello to the latest marvel in the world of eco-conscious boating - the Greenline 42. Its unveiling marks an enormous stride in the direction of innovation, class and environmentally friendly voyaging. The boat, meticulously crafted at Greenline's Slovenian shipyard, is a testament to the company's commitment to versatility and efficiency.

Boasting a semi-custom approach, the Greenline 42 offers potential buyers the chance to tweak the interiors such as the cabins, bathrooms, furniture and appliances to a greater degree than any previous model. This approach caters to a broad range of preferences without undermining the meticulous attention to precision and craft. From fashionable facing benches to a fully naked deck, the vessel provides ample room and flexibility to accommodate any sort of furniture or application the owner finds fit.

Not only does this vessel offer distinguished aesthetics, but its performance also holds up to scrutiny. Equipped with twin Yanmar 4LV-250 diesels on straight shafts, this superdisplacement hull can reach a brisk top end of 25 knots. Matching the need for smooth sailing, stability, and efficiency, the Greenline 42 can also be outfitted with a 4.3kW solar array and a Greenline H-Drive 6G system for silent electric manoeuvring.

Overall, this debut from Greenline not only holds promise for dedicated mariners but proves a formidable choice for any luxury enthusiast. It is an excellent choice for those who are seeking to combine elegance with high energy efficiency. As an embodiment of modernity and practicality, the Greenline 42 is indeed an exciting addition to the world of boating.

title: An Era Begins: Turkey's Mengi Yay Sells Inaugural NL Plus 52 Luxury Yacht
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: An Era Begins: Turkey's Mengi Yay Sells Inaugural NL Plus 52 Luxury Yacht
summary: Turkey's prestigious Mengi Yay shipyard has proudly announced the sale of the premier unit of its groundbreaking NL Plus 52 yacht model.
body: Stirring waves in the world of luxury yachting, Turkey's renowned Mengi Yay shipyard has announced the sale of the first unit from its avant-garde NL Plus 52 yacht model. Currently under construction in Istanbul's high-end facilities, this sublime 52.6-metre superyacht, endearingly baptized as the project NB114, is set to chart new waters in 2027. Following this groundbreaking sale, the shipbuilder revealed that a second yacht from the same series is set to enter the construction stage, adding a thrilling sequel to this debut tale. The announcement comes less than a year after Mengi Yay showcased the concept interiors of their NL Plus 52 capsule collection, masterfully crafted by Italian designer Nuvolari Lenard.

The yacht's sundeck stands as a distinctive feature. Reputed as 'one of the largest in this category', it boasts a tailor-made heated spa pool and a fire pit, exuding a luxurious resort-like feel. Moreover, ample storage space onboard allows cabin for a seven-meter-tender and a variety of water play items.

The NL Plus 52 truly exemplifies waterfront living. The interiors, kept casual yet sophisticated, incorporate a warm color palette and minimalist lines, coupled with fine woodwork for a versatile ambiance. Offering a tribute to the vision of Nuvolari Lenard, the yacht's interiors replicate the vitality of Mediterranean life, with expansive glass surfaces ensuring abundant natural light and a seamless indoor-outdoor connection. The innovative sliding balcony, as described by Carlo Nuvolari, the naval architect and co-founder, has multiple modes. When closed, it affords a small open area that offers the joy of basking in the sea breeze or relishing the surrounding landscape. Day or night, a Mengi Yay NL Plus 52 yacht presents a one-of-a-kind experience of exclusivity and intimacy with the captivating seascapes.

title: Sea-Alliance Group Announces the Sale of a Prestigious Mangusta GranSport 34 Yacht to UK Owner
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Sea-Alliance Group Announces the Sale of a Prestigious Mangusta GranSport 34 Yacht to UK Owner
summary: Mangusta Yachts sells its third GranSport 34 unit to a UK owner, setting a delivery date for summer 2027.
body: Mangusta Yachts, renowned for its luxury sailing vessels, has successfully sold the third unit of its acclaimed Mangusta GranSport 34 model. The lucky owner hails from the UK, and the yacht is poised to make its grand delivery by summer 2027. The deal was expertly mediated by Sea-Alliance Group, a leading entity in the yacht charter sector. The Mangusta GranSport 34 is an artful evolution of the immensely successful Mangusta GranSport 33 series, already boasting 12 units on waters across the globe. The latest model not only inherits the predecessor's esteemed lineage but gets enhanced with improved performance and a refined design. The credit goes to the talented team at Overmarine's Engineering Department and the deft pen strokes from Alberto Mancini, a renowned Monaco-based designer. The new owner, a long-time enthusiast of yacht chartering, was fascinated by the unit's perfect balance of easy handling and ample space. The yacht beautifully merges the paradigms of power and comfort, exceedingly suitable for cruising the enchanting waters of the Mediterranean Sea. The Mangusta GranSport 34 stands out with its sporty outlook and flexible interiors, encouraging a fluid transition among cruising, unwinding and socializing. Large volumes and sea-facing features are complemented with lavish accommodation facilities such as a 40-square-metre main-deck master suite along with several guest and crew cabins on the lower deck. The auspicious news comes hot on the heels of the sale of the second Mangusta GranSport 34 unit just a month ago. According to Mangusta's sales manager Nicolò Strocco, the model's versatility, large volumes, and constant sea contact are increasingly appreciated by clients. The surprisingly nimble yacht boasts four Volvo Penta IPS engines, reducing fuel consumption, vibrations and noise, all the while enhancing manoeuvrability. Its maximum speed clocks at 24 knots, boasting an impressively extensive range. The Overmarine Group gears up with 24 yachts currently on order or under construction, including the first model in its proud flagship Oceano 52 line. As the excitement unfolds, one thing is certain - the waves of success show no signs of ebbing for the esteemed Italian shipyard.

title: A Thrilling Adventure on the High Seas: Sodebo Ultim 3 Keeps the Lead in Quest for the Jules Verne Trophy
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A Thrilling Adventure on the High Seas: Sodebo Ultim 3 Keeps the Lead in Quest for the Jules Verne Trophy
summary: In their daring pursuit of the Jules Verne Trophy, the distinguished team on board Sodebo Ultim 3 remains in the lead after a month.
body: The team aboard the Sodebo Ultim 3 has been relentlessly pursuing the coveted Jules Verne Trophy for a month now. With stalwarts like Thomas Coville, Benjamin Schwartz, Frédéric Denis, Pierre Leboucher, Léonard Legrand, Guillaume Pirouelle, and Nicolas Troussel on board, the team embarked on this audacious journey on December 15th. Their journey so far has been marked by record-breaking times and awe-inspiring moments.

Surpassing challenges in the form of the three daunting capes - Good Hope, Leeuwin, and Horn - they have made remarkable progress, consistently maintaining an impressive average speed of 30 knots (56 km/h). However, they remain steadfast and focussed on their ultimate goal - breaking the round-the-world record held by IDEC Sport since 2017.

Even as their journey intensifies, the crew remains dedicated and driven; every milestone has been met with grit and determination. While they may have a nerve-wrecking journey ahead, Thomas Coville voices the sentiment of the crew, asserting that the boat and the crew are performing at 100%.

As they make their way towards the equator, the goal is clear and in sight - to cross the finish line before January 25th. A testament to their skill, determination, and unwavering courage, the quest for the Jules Verne Trophy continues to inspire awe and admiration.

title: A New, Custom-Made Luxury: ISA Gran Turismo Yacht Sold to Fortunate American Patron
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A New, Custom-Made Luxury: ISA Gran Turismo Yacht Sold to Fortunate American Patron
summary: The renowned Italian boatbuilder ISA Yachts announces the sale of an exquisitely designed 68-metre superyacht for delivery in 2028.
body: ISA Yachts, a distinguished brand under the mantle of Palumbo Superyachts, is making waves in the nautical world with the recent sale of a luxurious, 68-metre ISA Gran Turismo superyacht. The lucky buyer, hailing from the United States, can expect to set sail on his new beauty in 2028. The design of the steel and aluminium vessel originates from the esteemed Studio Vallicelli, responsible for the striking exterior, while the inviting interiors are the creation of Team for Design – Enrico Gobbi.

Conceived to augment the connection to the sea, the yacht will boast a beach club devoted to wellness and socialising. With opening platforms that extend the area outwards, guests can enjoy a gym, an elegant lounge, and a spa. Additionally, a swimming pool accompanied by a cosy lounge will complete the outdoor experience.

Accommodation is planned for up to 14 guests, with a crew of the same number. The lower deck will host four guest cabins, three doubles and one twin, whereas the remaining three cabins, two doubles and the forward-positioned owner's suite, will be situated on the main deck. Engine power will come from twin MTU engines, expected to muster a top speed of 17.5 knots and an approximate range of 5,000 nautical miles at a 14-knot cruising speed.
With this new build, ISA Yachts add another feather to their cap, which currently boasts 14 yachts either under construction or on order.

title: Unexpected Valor: How Crew of Oyster Yacht 'Raven' Saved a Stranded Transatlantic Rower
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unexpected Valor: How Crew of Oyster Yacht 'Raven' Saved a Stranded Transatlantic Rower
summary: In an unexpected twist, the crew of the Oyster sailing yacht 'Raven' enacted a daring rescue of a solo transatlantic rower stranded in the Atlantic.
body: The owner of the Oyster 82 sailing yacht 'Raven', Philippe Goossens, received a distress call on 27 December while in Cape Town, notifying him of a distress signal from a boat of the same name. Alerted to an unfolding emergency, the 'Raven' swiftly responded in spite of their upcoming participation in the Oyster World Rally and navigational concerns being over 70 nautical miles away from the source of the distress beacon.

Despite the growing distance and logistical challenges, such as refit works and limited fuel reserves, the 'Raven' crew recalibrated their direction towards the beacon. On the morning of 28 December, their gallant efforts culminated in the discovery of Rebecca Ferry, a 47-year-old British solo rower whose namesake boat had been adrift, following the critical malfunction of its steering system and solar panels.

The crew's chief stewardess, Michelle Christie, documented the harrowing event as an incredibly emotional moment. At the helm, Captain Julien Orus braved rough waters to manoeuvre close enough to secure Ferry's rowing boat, affectionately dubbed 'Baby Raven', for towing.

Thanks to the 'Raven' team's focused effort, Ferry was returned safely to Cape Verde, sacrificing only two days of sea time. Despite the unplanned events and challenges faced at sea, Goossens refused a standard reimbursement for fuel expenses, further adding to the yarn spun of on-the-spot assistance and community spirit among seafarers.

In a surprising turn of events, Ferry is set to join the 'Raven' crew in their future Pacific crossing, adding an avant-garde twist to a profound partnership forged in the jaws of adversity. Truly, an inspiring and invigorating tale that encapsulates the unpredictability and potential for human connection on the open seas.

title: Navigating a Sea of Sparks: A Wake-Up Call for Fire Safety in the Yachting Sector
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Navigating a Sea of Sparks: A Wake-Up Call for Fire Safety in the Yachting Sector
summary: As fire incidents rock the yachting industry with alarming frequency, it's high time for a determined focus on prevention and safety measures.
body: High-profile fires have been making ominous waves in the yachting industry. These flame-induced shocks are distressingly commonplace, occurring aboard vessels or in shipyards with worrying regularity. Like the echo of Billy Joel’s hit song, 'We Didn't Start the Fire', these incidents have become a calling card for an industry desperate for immediate safety reforms.

Over the past five years, the world of yachting has been rocked by a series of significant instances of combustion, sparking off severe damages, operational disruptions, and in some cases, complete vessel loss. For instance, the July 2024 inferno at a northern European shipyard mirrors the tragic pattern of the Project Sassi blaze four years earlier. There's an eerie similarity in these chronicles of fire, with emergency responders battling ceaselessly to reign in the uncontrolled flames.

These heart-stopping instances of combustion serve as red flags, forcing the industry to take a long, hard look at its fire-safety protocols. It's not a question of looking back with regret, but rather, focusing on proactively preventing the next big blaze. Superyachts are consistently pushing the boundaries of design and technology, making the urgency for top-notch fire-prevention measures a clear and present priority.

Dan Robsham, a veteran hull and machinery surveyor, echoes this sentiment stating that shipyards are a potential hotbed for fires with the close proximity of fuel, oxygen, and heat. This underscores the need for enhanced disaster-management protocols, less they become ticking time bombs.

The key takeaway from these heated experiences is that the industry needs to swiftly shift focus from firefighting to fire prevention. After all, when it comes to flame-induced incidents, an ounce of prevention is certainly worth a pound of cure.

title: Pete Hill's Lifetime of Adventure and Rig Expertise Recognized with CCA's Prestigious Blue Water Medal
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Pete Hill's Lifetime of Adventure and Rig Expertise Recognized with CCA's Prestigious Blue Water Medal
summary: An exploration of the multi-faceted maritime adventures of Pete Hill, 2025's worthy recipient of the Blue Water Medal.
body: The Cruising Club of America's annual anticipation of their distinguished Blue Water Medal announcement has a purpose and that is to genuinely reward maritime audacity and skill. British sailor Pete Hill, the award's honored recipient for 2025, is someone who has turned seafaring into an art. In 1923, this medal first found hands of gallant wanderers of the sea. Since then, legendary sailors like Bernard Moitessier, Eric Tabarly, and Sir Francis Chichester have proudly owned it. Hill is the latest addition to that impressive list, applauded for his half-century devotion to sailing and exploring vast expanses of oceans.

Hill's journey did not stop there; he then designed and built 'Chin Moon', a 38-foot junk-rigged catamaran. Steering this vessel, Hill sailed high latitudes for half a decade, traversing the symbol of sailing challenges - Cape Horn. In the following years, Hill converted a Freedom 33 to a junk rig, created cruising guides, embarked on more journeys, and even persevered through personal tragedies.

Despite losing his wife Carly to a tragic accident at sea in 2015, Hill found solace in the waves, undertaking a solitary voyage across the Indian Ocean. During the pandemic, he built 'Kokachin', another junk-rigged schooner, with Linda Crew-Gee, charting new paths from the Caribbean to Greenland.

In a twist of fate, Hill reacquired his earlier creation, China Moon, in Tasmania and spent four months refitting it despite encountering challenges that only the high seas could conjure. As of now, Hill is blissfully marking his miles on the South Pacific aboard China Moon, basking in the hard-earned glory of the Blue Water Medal.

title: Sailing Towards a New Fiscal Horizon: A Proposed VAT Strategy to Boost Spain's Yachting Industry
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Sailing Towards a New Fiscal Horizon: A Proposed VAT Strategy to Boost Spain's Yachting Industry
summary: In the international yachting landscape, Spain could accelerate its competitiveness with a strategic update to its value-added tax (VAT) regulations.
body: Driving Spain's competitiveness in the yachting world relies on updating its fiscal framework, especially concerning Value Added Tax (VAT). This might include adopting technical measures that are fully aligned with EU regulations, thereby attracting specialist investment and consolidating a high-value economic activity nationwide.

One such technical measure could be incorporating into domestic legislation the faculty provided for in Article 59 bis of Directive 2006/112/EC. This regulation allows countries to exclude from VAT taxable income that portion of the charter fee that occurs (pro rata temporis) in international waters. This discretionary option has seen successful adoption by Spain's competitors, such as France and Italy, making it one of the distinctive elements in their yachting offerings.

The likely fiscal impact of such reform would arguably be limited. This is because most of the charter sailing in Spain happens within territorial waters. Yet, the positive impact on competitiveness could be substantial; it would align Spain's yachting offers with European standards, increasing confidence among international operators and driving a strategic industry known to generate qualified employment, bolster regional economies, and promote sustainable, high-value tourism.

In essence, adopting Article 59 bis of Directive 2006/112/EC would be a strategically necessary measure to advance Spain's consolidation as a leading destination in the international charter industry, particularly in the superyacht segment.

title: Master Lock Comanche and URM Group Dominate SOLAS Big Boat Challenge - 2025 Rolex Sydney Hobart Yacht Race
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Rolex Sydney Hobart Yacht Race
summary: Two of offshore racing’s biggest names laid down unmistakable markers ahead of the 2025 Rolex Sydney Hobart Yacht Race. Under blue skies and postcard conditions, Master Lock Comanche and URM Group delivered emphatic performances in the SOLAS Big Boat Challenge.
body: James Mayo and Matt Allen’s 100-foot Maxi Master Lock Comanche strengthened her position as favourite for Line Honours with a commanding victory over her most obvious rival, LawConnect, the two-time defending Line Honours champion owned by Christian Beck. It was a result that resonated well beyond the finishing line. Beating LawConnect decisively in pre-Hobart conditions is never routine, and on Sydney Harbour it sent a clear message: Comanche was fast, sharp, and very much back with unfinished business. The previous Sydney Hobart had ended in heartbreak for the Comanche camp, when a torn mainsail in the early hours abruptly ended a meticulously prepared campaign. Twelve months on, the scars remained — but so did the resolve. “As Victor Kovalenko would say, the greatest Olympic sailing coach of all time, we’re ready to race,” Mayo said at the time, summing up a campaign built on methodical preparation and collective belief. “We’d put a lot of work into this program over a number of training camps, and they’d been really successful. We had a tremendous team. Together, everyone achieves more — and that’s exactly what we’d built.”

Redemption drove the Comanche campaign Mayo did not shy away from revisiting the disappointment of the previous year, describing the moment when everything unravelled offshore. “It was brutal. We were incredibly well prepared, had a great team, and then suddenly — bang — it was all over in the middle of the night,” he said. “That hurt. But a year on, I genuinely felt we were in really good shape. It felt good. We just had to go out on the 26th and sail the best we possibly could.” While the rivalry with LawConnect was impossible to ignore, Mayo maintained that Comanche’s focus stayed firmly inward. “Competition’s great — the more, the better,” he said. “But our job was to look after our boat and our crew. If we put our best performance on the water, we were quietly confident.” By crossing the line first in the SOLAS Big Boat Challenge, Comanche also secured Line Honours in the Australian Maxi Championship, having won four of the five legs contested across an intense week of racing.

URM Group emerged as serious Tattersall Cup contenders If Comanche stamped authority at the front of the fleet, URM Group arguably did something even more significant — announcing themselves as genuine contenders for Overall honours in the Sydney Hobart. Owned by waste management magnates Anthony and David Johnston and skilfully skippered by Marcus Ashley-Jones, the Reichel/Pugh Maxi 72 dominated the Overall Division of the Australian Maxi Championship. Their performance was measured, consistent and relentless — exactly the qualities required to win the Tattersall Cup. With four consecutive Overall race wins, URM Group left no doubt about their credentials, finishing clear of the chasing pack, with No Limit and Moneypenny tied for second overall. Anthony Johnston was understandably buoyant as attention turned south. “Really, really happy,” he said. “Four wins in a row was a first for us, so we were absolutely stoked.” Timing it right for Hobart URM Group’s momentum was all the more impressive given the challenges faced earlier in the season. After losing their mast the previous year, the team opted for patience rather than rushing back into competition. “We started the season a bit slow,” Johnston explained. “We didn’t do the Sydney to Gold Coast race. We took time to get used to the new rig — and we started to come good at exactly the right time.” That timing proved crucial when the fleet turned left at Sydney Heads on Boxing Day. Adding a deeply personal dimension to the campaign, Johnston sailed to Hobart alongside his four brothers — David, Nick, Andrew and Nigel — a tradition that continued to define the spirit of the URM Group program. “I love doing Hobart with my brothers,” he said. “It’s a privilege to sail with them in the first place. To win together would have been something really special.”
With Master Lock Comanche firing on all cylinders and URM Group peaking at precisely the right moment, the narrative heading into the 2025 Rolex Sydney Hobart Yacht Race was already clear.

By the time the fleet reached Hobart, the picture was clear. LawConnect had taken Line Honours, turning early promise into hard miles offshore. Others took lessons, stories and scars south with them — reminders that Hobart is never just about who arrives first, but about how the ocean chooses to let you arrive at all.

title: ER Yacht Design Captivates with the Debut of Logos, a Superyacht Designed for Continuous Sea-Splashed Adventures

body: Adding another feather to its hat, ER Yacht Design presents its latest creation, the 61-metre superyacht, Logos. This innovative giant showcases an 'ultra-modern' personality that thrives on ambitiously bold proportions and sharp architectural lines, making a dynamic mark in the world of luxury yachting. The superyacht is a marvel of 'continuous motion' characters, where the sculptural hull and superstructure play catch with the light, transforming character with every ripple and wave.

The design ethos of Logos extends beyond aesthetics. The superyacht, built around an aluminium structure, features an efficient hull form and is adorned with carbon-fibre free-standing wing boards and a bimini-top arch to 'lift' the vessel's silhouette in a ceremoniously proud stance at sea. Complementing its striking design are elongated glazing and geometric shapes, enhancing Logos' modern appeal.

Presenting an inviting on-board layout, Logos makes it a mission to keep guests connected, be it at a full-throttle social gathering or a relaxed, intimate occasion. The lower deck saloon epitomises spaciousness, integrating dining within the main-deck superstructure. The yacht ensures its playfulness quotient isn't far behind, dedicating the bow to an array of toys; an eight-metre tender, jet skis and a rescue rigid inflatable boat, all available at one’s disposal via twin launching cranes. Logos boasts numbers hard to overlook - an extravagant volume of 850GT, a 10.5-metre beam and a three-metre draught.

The yacht's accommodation is set for a party of 12 guests across six double cabins on the main deck, and a full-beam owner's suite located on the upper deck, presenting panoramic views that can pull any seafarer's heartstrings.
