title: Unmasking the Navigator's Dilemma: Directions, Speed and Strategy in the Famed RORC Transatlantic Race
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unmasking the Navigator's Dilemma: Directions, Speed and Strategy in the Famed RORC Transatlantic Race
summary: The RORC transatlantic race sets the stage for a riveting narrative, unveiling the intricate decisions and strategies crafted by world-class sailing navigators.
body: In the complex dynamics of the RORC Transatlantic Race, both speed and navigation play vital roles. Spanning over three thousand nautical miles, strategic decisions made before the race are continuously refined as the fleet traverses from the Canary Islands into the trade winds.

Sailing wisdom suggests that victory often lies in determining when to stick to the rhumb line or when to deviate south towards the Cape Verde Islands. For Vila, navigating on James Neville's Carkeek 45 Ino Noir in the fiercely competitive IRC environment, the key lies in the difference of speed. He reveals the added challenge of taking a slower boat, compared to the maxis Vila has previously raced on, which required transitioning from one weather system to another.

In essence, the RORC Transatlantic Race is a test of mettle and wits, a thrilling display of mastering winds and waves. Only those with the keenest eyes, sharpest insights, and most precise calculations will find favour in this grandest carnival of maritime adventure.

title: The Unapologetically Futuristic Wallywhy200: Innovation Meets Luxury on the Waves
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Unapologetically Futuristic Wallywhy200: Innovation Meets Luxury on the Waves
summary: Transcending the conventions of yacht design, the Wallywhy200 motor yacht fused audacity with ingenuity, offering an enthralling maritime spectacle.
body: Standing out in the world of luxury yachting is no mean feat, yet the towering Wallywhy200 instantly grabs attention with its audacious and striking design. Angular, towering and unashamedly futuristic, the Wallywhy200 is a departure from the norm. But step inside this ‘why’ series flagship from Wally, and it's clear that beneath the surface of this radical exterior lies a luxury experience carefully crafted for its owners.

The Wallywhy200 introduces a new interpretation of hybrid, a term inherently associated with propulsion systems. However, the 'why' in this yacht's name stands for 'Wally Hybrid Yacht,’ denoting the seamless blend of speed, performance, and the lavish comfort typical of a displacement vessel. It's a design that merges the spaciousness of a catamaran with the speed and performance of a semi-displacement hull. This hybrid approach has resulted in a yacht that is not only visually impressive but also provides practical advantages.

The unique, aggressive design profile stems from a collaboration between Wally’s in-house team and the Ferretti Group Engineering Department, with naval architecture by Laurent Giles. Long bands of glazing slice across the metallic hull, whereas the 4.7-metre-high bow looms over the water, overall bearing a resemblance to a spaceship. The design is a deliberate venture from the traditional yacht norms, appealing to an adroit niche of yacht-owners with voracious innovation appetite.

Studio A. Vallicelli & C are the creative minds behind the open and sculptural interiors. The laminated carbon staircase encapsulated in class connects all three decks, making dividers redundant and creating a flowing, open-plan space. The natural palette, dominated by open-pore teak, seeps through the salon walkways and down the lower-deck corridor, imbuing the interiors with a tranquil aura - a testament to the brilliant execution of the design concept.

Defying expectations, the 37-square-metre master suite enjoys 270-degree panoramic views of the horizon. Owners have the freedom to personalize layouts, with liberty to reposition the bed or even convert the suite into a game room. A noise-free environment tops the priority, with crew quarters planned amidships effectively segregating the guest accommodations from the technical spaces.

True to their heritage, a futuristic glass-and-carbon dome crowns the upper deck, characteristic of the celebrated 'Wallypower' range. This dome encapsulates the skylounge, forging remarkable harmony between avant-garde innovation and opulent luxury, which is the essence of the groundbreaking Wallywhy200.

summary: The 2026 ILCA Nationals event is set to spotlight the world's superior ILCA sailors in the dazzling Bay of Islands, featuring intense racing sessions.
body: A thrilling event is on the horizon as the world's top ILCA sailors anchor their sights on the Bay of Islands, gearing up for the spectacle of the 2026 ILCA Nationals. The competition boasts of an undeniably upstanding lineup of personalities that are nothing short of sailing royalty.

In the rather magnetic attraction of the Bay of Island Yacht Club at Paihia, the 2026 NZ ILCA Nationals promises four electrifying days of high-quality sailing contests. The event, slated to run from the 14th to the 18th of January 2026, anticipates a robust turnout of nearly 100 boats with a comprehensive representation of the best ILCA athletes New Zealand has seen in many years.

The ILCA 6 Open division is no less sizzling. World-class athletes including Erika Reineke (USA) and Frances Beebe (AUS) bring their craft to the fore, challenging last NZ Olympic representative Greta Pilkington and former Men's ILCA 6 world champion George Lane, for an indispensable flavour of excitement.

A new generation of sailors, including the 2025 U17 Women's World ILCA 6 champion Chloe Turner and the recent NZ youth worlds representative Tom Pilkington, also grace the contest, adding an extra layer of intrigue.

In the Masters and ILCA 4 categories, seasoned sailor Phil Wild will be looking to protect his title, while Ellie Tapper and Kiera Dimock, fresh from the Oceania champs in Australia, carry the ILCA 4 torch.

The races are set to launch on Thursday, 15th January, with ten adrenaline-infused events slated to commence at 1 pm. For the first time in a NZ ILCA event, live tracking will be available, dishing out real-time stats and updates for zealous fans and followers.

title: Day 3 Drama at the 2025 World Match Racing Tour: The Race for Redemption in Shenzhen Heats Up.

summary: At the heart of Shenzhen, the 2025 World Match Racing Tour spins headlong into the knockout stages punctuated by a day of drama.
body: The third day of the 2025 World Match Racing Tour final saw the sailing fervor hit new highs in Shenzhen. Repechage racing under pressure in the city's heart, the stakes were at their peak, and every move carried weight. In the traditionally fickle and ultra-light winds of OH Bay, survival was the only goal, and any slip-ups were alarmingly expensive.

Amidst the intensity, two teams emerged undeterred, securing their places in the much-anticipated quarterfinals. New Zealand's Nick Egnot-Johnson, leading the Knots Racing, and Denmark's Jeppe Borch at the helm of Borch Match Race dazzled spectators with their strategic resilience in tackling the harsh sailing conditions. Their victories completed the elite eight-team lineup, now barreling into the decisive stage of the skirmish for the Match Racing World Championship.

The Danes, led by Borch, echoed this crackerjack intensity. They triumphed in six out of the seven starts, with their single setback inflicted by the invincible Kiwis. However, maintaining a consistent performance throughout the day underpinned their berth in the quarterfinals. Clash wind conditions imparted their unique challenge to both competitors and the race management, pushing each to the brink.

Eventually, what defined the day was the showdown between the two leaders in Flight 6, with a coveted quarterfinal slot hanging in the balance. Following contact in a fever-pitched pre-start, Borch's team received a penalty, granting the Kiwi crew an early advantage.

title: Legendary 55-Meter Feadship Motor Yacht Olympus Changes Hands After a $10,000,000 Refit
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Legendary 55-Meter Feadship Motor Yacht Olympus Changes Hands After a $10,000,000 Refit
summary: The opulent 55-meter Feadship motor yacht Olympus has found a new captain following an extensive $10 million refit.
body: Relaying tales of grandeur and sophistication, the Olympus, a 55-meter motor yacht from the renowned Feadship, has finally discovered fresh horizons to conquer. Brokers Alex Busher of Edmiston and Stuart Larsen of Fraser cemented the sale, with the buyer introduced by Simon Ting of SuperYachtsMonaco.

Born from the expertise of the renowned British design studio Winch Design, the Olympus graced the waters in 1996. The naval architecture bears a testimony to the legend of Frits De Voogt, keeping her steadiness over the ocean waves. The Olympus found herself under the same patronage for almost three decades before debuting in the market in 2022. She further underwent a grand refit, worth a staggering $10 million, and was taken care of by the folks at Monaco Marine in 2023. The Feadship's original Dutch builders also conducted a thorough winter maintenance, which entailed significant upgrades and enhancements to the tune of $5 million.

Featured on the main deck is a commodious master cabin, accessorized with a private observation lounge, a dedicated office, an en suite, along with a gym-cum-hairdressing salon. Meanwhile, guest accommodations comprise one VIP suite, two twin cabins, two doubles accompanied by pullman berths, and two singles. In addition, a well-equipped space is available for up to 16 diligent crew members.

Promising an exquisite culinary experience, an oval dining table awaits guests on the main deck, forward of the saloon. An open-air dining setup is also in place on the aft deck. Catering to social and private requirements, the bridge deck houses a skylounge functioning either as a VIP private lounge or a secondary social space.

The Lloyds-classified and MCA-compliant motor yacht is powered by twin 2,600hp Caterpillar diesels, ensuring a smooth voyage with a cruising speed of 12 knots and a maximum speed of 17.5 knots. With her multiple amenities and tailored luxuries, the Olympus offers an unmatched experience of living on board, promising beautiful memories on the ocean waves.

title: Cracking the Code: How the Right Shipyard Selection Can Make or Break Your Superyacht Refit Experience
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Cracking the Code: How the Right Shipyard Selection Can Make or Break Your Superyacht Refit Experience
summary: Just ahead of a major event, an expert marine consultant shares his wisdom on selecting the right shipyard for yacht refits, potentially saving owners from catastrophic errors.
body: When shaping the future of a superyacht, selecting the right shipyard for a refit or serious maintenance interval is a critical decision. This selection goes beyond creating a foreseen technical outcome; it governs the overall experience of the project, affecting time, cost and even crew contentment. However, care and planning behind this decision are something this industry often overlooks. One might wonder how far the restaurants and bars for the crew are, as the crew part of this industry is indeed a deciding factor. Every shipyard may be equipped to paint, weld, and pull shafts- but not all possess the same mindset or operational culture. The key lies in understanding the type of yard being dealt with and aligning its mentality to the task. Three main categories grace our world: the new-build yards, refit yards, and commercial yards. They each operate under a unique philosophy, posing various advantages and risks, depending on your vessel, scope, and expectations. The finest refit yards perceive a yacht under refurbishment as a living entity, requiring quick decision-making, clear communication, and utmost respect for the boat's operational life. Nevertheless, it's not all seamless- opting for a refit in a new-build yard or a yard designed for new vessels often leads to clashes with their rigid structures. New-build yards primarily focus on production efficiency, while refits need problem-solving skills. Unmanageable expectations could result in spiralling costs and timelines, which is something we frequently witness. Meanwhile, dedicated refit yards, which base their businesses on the principle of flexibility, deal explicitly with existing vessels needing maintenance upgrades and surveys. In short, the art of choosing the right yard for a yacht refit involves navigating a fascinating yet complex landscape of variables. Doing so correctly can save owners from disaster and steer them toward success.

title: Unveiling the Future of Superyachting: Europe's Defining Regulatory Landscape in 2026
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unveiling the Future of Superyachting: Europe's Defining Regulatory Landscape in 2026
summary: Major regulatory changes are coming quietly but steadily to the superyacht ecosystem in Europe by 2026, impacting every facet of the industry.
body: Like a rising tide, Europe's regulatory adjustments seldom come crashing but rather increase steadily until they've completely transformed the landscape. Such is the anticipated scenario for the superyacht industry in the year 2026. This changing tide brings a trio of significant climate measures, reshaping everyday superyacht operations. The EU's anti-money-laundering package solidifies compliance expectations for high-value yacht transactions. Simultaneously, factors around sustainability reporting have been chronologically arranged instead of entirely eliminated, marking a critical shift. Lastly, 2026 will witness Malta, a key player in European yachting, entering its first full year under an updated Commercial Yacht Code.

In tandem with the Emissions Trading System, FuelEU Maritime imposes progressive greenhouse-gas intensity standards. Fulfilling these more stringent requirements necessitates adjustments in fuel documentation and procurement, creating an additional compliance layer.

Another significant shift involves the adaptation of the 2024 anti-money-laundering package. Regulations regarding financial transactions related to high-value yachts have undergone drastic transformations, taking the sector closer to stringent scrutiny and transparency. This revamping includes a limit on Union-wide cash transactions, further tightening the regulatory perimeter.

Despite these mounting pressures, relief comes in the form of deferred corporate sustainability reporting. Instead of abandonment, obligations have been simplified and sequenced, providing room for industry players to adjust and adapt. Yet, such breather must not be misconstrued as a free pass. As obligations mount, so does the need for due diligence.

title: Discover the Boarncruiser Ocean 53 Sport: A Fusion of Toughness and Luxury Debuting at the Düsseldorf Boat Show
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover the Boarncruiser Ocean 53 Sport: A Fusion of Toughness and Luxury Debuting at the Düsseldorf Boat Show
summary: The Düsseldorf Boat Show has premiered the latest gem from Boarnstream Yachting, the Boarncruiser Ocean 53 Sport, offering the perfect blend of rugged durability and sheer opulence.
body: The Düsseldorf Boat Show was graced with an exquisite addition, as Boarnstream Yachting revealed their latest steel marvel, the Boarncruiser Ocean 53 Sport. With over 60 years of experience working tirelessly to perfect the art of steel yacht building, the Dutch firm presented a splendid spectacle with this fully steel, Category A, long-distance motor yacht that addresses the seemingly contradicting requirements of toughness and luxury with flair.

Sporting a semi-displacement hull crafted for comfort and efficiency, the Ocean 53 Sport is powered by twin Cummins QSB 6.7L engines, promising power levels between 305 and 480hp. The ingenious implementation of a Hull Vane, a submerged wing at the transom, incorporates a touch of lift at the aft end, reducing sea pitching, enhancing efficiency, decreasing wake size, and improving stability throughout the rev range. Not least, it helps propel the vessel to Boarnstream’s target speed of 16 knots.

The yacht's dynamism is balanced elegantly with practical deck layouts designed for sea enthusiasts. It features an L-shaped unit placed to the ship's port and linear cabinetry located at the starboard side, divided by a central walkway. An expansive U-shaped dinette adorns the cockpit, ideal for freestanding furniture. Descending the starboard staircase takes one to the lower decks, arranged around an owner’s cabin, a VIP chamber, a bunk room, and twin bathrooms.

However, more than just its appeal and functionality, the Ocean 53 Sport has been designed with attention to accessibility and customization. The focus is unmistakably on easy navigation and storage. But, while the hull and superstructure remain constant, practically everything else can be customized to the owner's preference, from interior layouts and materials to technical components.

The Boarncruiser Ocean 53 Sport demonstrates that the essence of yachting goes beyond pure extravagance. It is about the marriage of capability, comfort, and individuality, creating an unparalleled marine traveling experience.

title: Dutch Craftsmanship Meets the High Seas: The Steely Elegance of Boarncruiser Ocean 53 Sport

It also merits appreciation for how it leverages a Hull Vane (or submerged wing), leading to an admirable reduction in pitching at sea and boosting stability. Each of these design elements pushes the yacht closer to its impressive target speed of 16 knots. At an imposing 35 tonnes, the beauty of the Boarncruiser Ocean 53 is its ability to transform itself into a versatile performer. It promises an extensive range of approximately 2,500 nautical miles at a cruising speed of six knots. Moreover, the yacht ensures all journeys are as relaxing as they are adventurous, whether it's a sunny day-cruise or tackling the challenge of an exposed voyage. With its practical and innovative deck layouts, the Ocean 53 doesn't skimp on style or space. Featuring a sociable port dinette, a galley that straddles the central walkway, a U-shaped dinette in the cockpit, and ample room for relaxation, it epitomises luxury sailing. Within its spacious interiors, the lower deck houses an impressive full-beam owner's cabin, a VIP room fit for royalty, and a comfortable starboard bunk room. This exemplar yacht is not just about fixed exteriors. As a semi-custom yacht, it offers a plethora of options to be personalised to match distinct sensibilities, centred around comfort and accessibility. The interiors, catering to everything from storage to upgrades, can be tailored to match individual preferences. title: Yacht Management Software DeepBlue Earns DNV Approval, Emphasizing Digitalization of Maintenance Systems
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Yacht Management Software DeepBlue Earns DNV Approval, Emphasizing Digitalization of Maintenance Systems
summary: DeepBlue, the yacht management platform, has successfully secured type approval from DNV for its Planned Maintenance System module, a significant achievement in digital yacht operations.
body: In an exceptional milestone in digital yacht operations, the yacht management platform DeepBlue has garnered type approval from DNV for its Planned Maintenance System (PMS) module. This development brings the software within an internationally recognized classification framework, underscoring the growing role of digitalization in yacht maintenance and operations.

DNV's approval testifies to the ongoing efforts to standardize digital maintenance data and fortify connections between onboard systems and classification services. As Diego Zanco, DeepBlue's Chief Operating Officer, puts it, this certification goes beyond being a mere badge. Rather, it attests to the prowess of their technology to withstand the rigorous scrutiny that their customers contend with daily. DeepBlue's development strategy has always revolved around real operational conditions, and this approval is a significant affirmation of that approach.

DeepBlue's focus doesn't end with obtaining DNV's approval. Looking towards the future, they intend to expand this compliance further. DNV issued approval confirms the PMS's adherence to class requirements relating to onboard maintenance management's functionality, reliability, and compliance. As Erik Spieler from DNV articulates, the PMS module fulfils the stringent DNV specifications needed for standardizing maintenance data transfer. Indeed, this is a stride towards greater industry digitalization and the evolution of classification services.

The first day of the series greeted the sailors with a quintessential wintry scene — icy winds, sheets and sails ensnared by stubborn ice, but spirits undeterred by the chilly weather.

As the competitors launched, the hardy sailors battled against a substantial westerly breeze, navigating through long beats and encountering heart-pounding closeness at the mark roundings. A testament to the sailor's formidable skills and the gloriously unpredictable nature of sailing.

Dan O'Connell emerged triumphant in the ILCA 7 fleet, followed by Peter Hassett's victory in the ILCA 6 fleet. Daragh Sheridan, sailing on his RS Aero, led the PY fleet, chalking up an impressive win in Race 1 and a commendable second position in Race 2.

The Dinghy Frostbites Spring Series attests to the thriving sailing culture, fostering competition, championing skills, and sharing grand adventure tales that unfurl against the majestic backdrop of the open sea and, in this instance, the crunch of ice underfoot.

title: Viking Explorers Rally 2026 Sets New Departure Date in Response to Unfavourable Weather Conditions
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Viking Explorers Rally 2026 Sets New Departure Date in Response to Unfavourable Weather Conditions
summary: The Viking Explorers Rally 2026 announces a rescheduled departure date from Las Palmas de Gran Canaria in light of challenging weather conditions.
body: In winning the battle against the elements, the Viking Explorers Rally organisers and participating skippers showcase the epitome of seamanship by making the unanimous decision to reschedule their departure. The lure of the open sea can be dreamily compelling but the reality of Mother Nature’s whims brings the intrepid sailors of the Viking Explorers Rally 2026 back to the practical realities of ocean sailing. The original departure date, slated for the 6th of January, has been moved to the morning of the 8th. The change comes after a careful assessment of recent unfavourable weather conditions sweeping the departure locale of the Canary Islands.

The Canary Islands have recently been buffeted by significant storm systems, raising tumultuous seas and unwieldy winds across the departure zone. In light of the challenging conditions, organisers took the prudent decision to allow for improvement in weather before setting out. This move demonstrates the rally’s penchant for safety over rush.

The Viking Explorers Rally enjoys global recognition for it's unique blend of fellowship, expert guidance, and emphasis on safe, responsibly executed ocean crossings. The rally thrives as an exclusive fleet, limited to a maximum of 25 boats. Careful planning and stringent safety protocols are laid down at every step of the journey. The skippers enjoy benefits of detailed pre-voyage seminars, weather briefings, and continuous coordination throughout the crossing.

"Safety always takes precedence - for our crews, their yachts, and the wider maritime environment," reiterates managing director Oliver Solanas Heinrichs, underlining the ethos that has guided the decision to brave the wait rather than confront unfavourable conditions.

The rally’s schedule remains unaltered, with the revised plan still considering departure from Las Palmas towards Marina Mindelo in Cape Verde and then across the Atlantic to Port Louis Marina in Grenada. The organisers continue to monitor weather updates vigilantly and will circulate further advisories if the conditions mandate additional adjustments.

A flagship event since 2018, the Viking Explorers Rally is the go-to choice of blue-water sailors seeking a thrilling and memorable Atlantic sailing experience. The rally’s accent on camaraderie, safety, and adept support paves the way for a community of sailors ready to embark on a voyage of thousands of nautical miles, soaked in shared adventure and guided wisdom.

title: Charlie Dalin Awarded the 2025 Magnus “Mange” Olsson Prize
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Charlie Dalin Awarded the 2025 Magnus Mange Olsson Prize
imageCaption: French offshore sailing sensation Charlie Dalin
summary: In offshore sailing, true greatness is rarely defined by speed alone. It is shaped by endurance, judgement, innovation — and the ability to keep going when the ocean, the clock, and life itself begin to apply pressure. This year, the Magnus Olsson Foundation has recognised exactly that blend of qualities by naming Charlie Dalin as the recipient of the 2025 Magnus “Mange” Olsson Prize.
body: For those who follow offshore racing closely, Dalin’s name has long been synonymous with precision, intelligence and relentless competitiveness. But this award goes deeper than results. It honours a sailor who has quietly reshaped modern offshore racing — as a skipper, as a designer, and as a human being who refused to let adversity dictate the limits of his ambition.
From Childhood Curiosity to Offshore Obsession

Born and based in Le Havre, Dalin discovered sailing at the age of six — a familiar story that, in his case, became something far more serious. While many young sailors are content to race dinghies and dream, Dalin combined passion with study, eventually graduating as a naval architect from the University of Southampton in 2006.

That dual identity — engineer and racer — has defined his career ever since. Dalin does not merely sail fast boats; he understands them from the keel bolts up. He questions shapes, load paths, structures and compromises. In an era where offshore racing has become increasingly technical, that knowledge has proven decisive.
Learning at the Sharp End

Dalin’s early professional career placed him immediately at the heart of elite offshore racing. He joined the design and build team for Ericsson 4, the VO70 that went on to win the 2008–09 Volvo Ocean Race and set a 24-hour monohull speed record along the way. It was a baptism by fire — exposure to the pressures of round-the-world competition, cutting-edge design, and a culture where marginal gains matter.

But it was in the Figaro Beneteau class that Dalin truly announced himself as a sailor. Five consecutive podium finishes in the Solitaire du Figaro is an achievement that places him among the very best the class has ever produced. One-design, single-handed, brutally tactical — Figaro racing rewards no shortcuts. Dalin’s consistency there marked him out as a future star.
Mastering the IMOCA Circuit

Transitioning to the IMOCA class, Dalin quickly proved he could translate Figaro discipline into big-boat success. His résumé reads like a modern offshore highlights reel: victories in the Transat Jacques Vabre in 2015 (with Yann Eliès) and again in 2019 (with Paul Meilhat), the IMOCA Globe Series World Championship, and countless podium finishes across the most competitive fleet in ocean racing.

The 2020 Vendée Globe cemented his status. Dalin crossed the finish line first after 80 days alone at sea — only to be classified second after time redress for assisting a fellow competitor. The result stung, but it also revealed Dalin’s character. There was no public bitterness, no theatrics. Just a calm acceptance and a quiet resolve to come back stronger.
Redemption — and a Record for the Ages

That resolve culminated spectacularly in the 2024 Vendée Globe, sailed aboard MACIF Santé Prévoyance, a Guillaume Verdier-designed IMOCA in which Dalin was deeply involved from the earliest sketches through to launch. This was not simply a campaign; it was a full intellectual and physical commitment.

The outcome was historic. Dalin obliterated the existing Vendée Globe record by nine full days, finishing in 64 days, 19 hours, 22 minutes and 49 seconds — a time that redefined what was thought possible in solo, non-stop, unassisted circumnavigation.
It was one of the most complete performances the race has ever seen: relentless pace, measured risk management, and total command of boat and self.
Racing Through Adversity

What elevates Dalin’s achievement beyond pure sporting excellence is what emerged afterward. In a revelation that stunned the sailing world, Dalin disclosed that he had been diagnosed with a gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST) in late 2023 and had undergone targeted treatment throughout his Vendée Globe preparations — and during the race itself.

Solo ocean racing is already an exercise in isolation and mental resilience. To undertake it while managing serious illness requires a level of fortitude few can comprehend. Dalin did so without public drama, focusing instead on the race, his systems, and the discipline that has always underpinned his sailing.
It is this combination of courage, humility and professionalism that makes the Magnus Olsson Prize such a fitting recognition.
The Spirit of Mange Olsson

Established in memory of the legendary Swedish sailor Magnus “Mange” Olsson, the Magnus Olsson Prize honours individuals who embody excellence, innovation and sportsmanship at the highest level of sailing. Past recipients form a roll-call of modern greats: Franck Cammas, Torben Grael, Grant Dalton, Carolijn Brouwer, Stan Honey, Sir Ben Ainslie, Peter Burling, Martine Grael and Santiago Lange.
Dalin now joins that company — not just as a winner, but as a standard-bearer for the values the prize represents.

“Receiving the Magnus Olsson Prize is an honour that reflects not just my victories on the water, but also what we must overcome off the water,” Dalin said. “Magnus Olsson was a legend whose spirit of adventure inspired everyone he met. I am proud to accept this prize and carry on his legacy.”
Giving Back: Supporting the Next Generation

Alongside the main prize, the Magnus Olsson Foundation continues its vital work supporting young Swedish sailors through annual scholarships. More than 20 promising athletes have benefited so far, and this year’s recipients underline the programme’s impact.

Cornelia Baldock Frost, who finished fifth at the Youth World Championships in the double-handed 29er class, spoke of renewed motivation: “Having my drive and my sailing recognised like this gives me the energy to aim for even bigger goals.”

Erik Norlén, gold medallist at the Under-21 European Championships in the single-handed ILCA class, echoed that sentiment, calling the scholarship “a great honour” that means “a lot to me and my sailing.”
A Legacy Still Being Written

Dalin’s recently published book, La Force du Destin (The Force of Destiny), offers an unvarnished look at his journey — from childhood sailing to the mental and physical battles of racing solo around the world. It is not a victory lap, but a thoughtful exploration of purpose, resilience and the quiet determination that defines the very best offshore sailors.

Charlie Dalin, along with the scholarship winners, will be honoured in person at the 2026 Magnus Olsson Prize Ceremony in Stockholm — a fitting setting for a sailor whose career reflects both modern excellence and timeless seamanship.

In a sport increasingly driven by technology and data, Dalin reminds us that character still matters. Boats may be faster. Foils may lift higher. But the ocean still rewards those who combine intelligence, humility and courage — and who keep going when the horizon feels impossibly far away.

title: Stepping to the Fore: Polish Docklands Transformed from Industrial Shipyards to Luxury Yacht Builders
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Stepping to the Fore: Polish Docklands Transformed from Industrial Shipyards to Luxury Yacht Builders
summary: Defining old traditions and rubbishing stereotypes, Poland's shipbuilding industry is evolving from industrial shipyards to high-end yacht builders.
body: The Polish Investment and Trade Agency recently embarked on a tour that began in the historic city of Gdańsk, a location with a maritime story reaching back a thousand years. Monumental landmarks such as the centuries-old crane on the Motława River and the World War II Museum coexist in a brutal contrast that beautifully encapsulates the nation's past and present. In particular, this juxtaposition serves as a metaphorical representation of Poland's transition from a past steeped in engineering and politics to a future grounded in innovation and sophistication.

For a long time, Poland was perceived to be a fringe player in the world of European yacht building. However, a tour through the bustling workshops and rapid waterfront developments throughout the Tricity region, spanning Gdańsk, Gdynia, and Ostróda, paints a very different picture today. Local shipyards are displaying a promising potential, recently venturing into the exclusive market of high-end sailing and motor yachts.

Sunreef Yachts is leading the charge in this transformation, bestowing the industry with a unique Polish touch. Their key offering doesn't lie in the production of single luxury motor yachts; instead, they're concentrating their efforts on substantial catamarans that cater to a growing customer base. Recent advancements in solar power research and alternative propulsion options are marking the brand's path. After initial hurdles in persuading customers of the high quality of Polish-built luxury yachts, Sunreef Yachts has firmly established itself as a recognised player in the global yachting community.

A testament to this successful transition was Sunreef's introduction of a 65-metre Explorer catamaran concept at the Monaco Yacht Show. Despite being a conceptual project, it has demonstrated Poland's growing influence in a sector where size, range, and volume are emerging as crucial deciding factors for new buyers.

Only a few miles away, Conrad Shipyard is carving out a niche for itself by specialising in unique, one-off projects. Through the launch of the ACE in 2022, they made a statement about the potential and quality of the Polish shipbuilding industry.

title: Pole Position: How Poland is Transforming its Historic Shipyards into Global Superyacht and Luxury Catamaran Hubs
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Pole Position: How Poland is Transforming its Historic Shipyards into Global Superyacht and Luxury Catamaran Hubs
summary: Poland, a nation with an intricate maritime history stretching back a millennium, is making strides in the realm of luxury watercraft, becoming a new hub for superyachts and solar-powered catamarans.
body: From the historic city of Gdańsk to the modern shipyards of Ostróda, Poland's maritime story is a rich tapestry of potent history and innovative modernity. Its shipyards are treasured landmarks, reminders of the nation's enduring shipbuilding heritage and centres of industrial innovation. Today, these historical dockyards are transforming into beacons of luxury watercraft production, leaving behind their stale industrial image. Poland is rising as a leader in European yacht building, creating ripples in the realm of luxury watercraft.

At the recent Monaco Yacht Show, Sunreef unveiled a 65 metre Explorer catamaran concept, a pioneering design that challenged preconceptions about the size and range of multi-hull watercraft. The concept marked another step forward for the company and for Polish yacht production.

Not far away lies Conrad Shipyard, renowned for creating bespoke one-off projects for international clients. A trendsetter in the world of luxury watercraft, Conrad Shipyard is working on several large-scale projects, including a new 42-metre sailing yacht. Their course is a testament that Polish yards can compete in areas where craftsmanship matters as much as scale.

Lastly, Poland's competitive edge owes a lot to its technical universities that provide a reliable stream of specialised labour. As a result, it remains a strategic advantage that keeps Poland sailing ahead on this innovative journey.

title: Histonic Refurbishment for the 48m 'Mirabella' Trinity Motor Yacht is in Progress
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Histonic Refurbishment for the 48m 'Mirabella' Trinity Motor Yacht is in Progress
summary: Reviva Refit, a renowned Turkish shipyard brand, is conducting significant renovation work on the 48m motor yacht 'Mirabella'.
body: The bustling Turkish shipyard, Reviva Refit, has made waves with its announcement of substantial refit operations underway on the 47.9m motor yacht 'Mirabella'. This luxury vessel, which once commanded a staggering price tag of $12,400,000, was initially delivered back in 2004 by the esteemed US-based Trinity Yachts. Project R15, as dubbed by the shipyard, officially started in October 2025, with a delivery date penciled in for mid-April 2026. This significant refit comes in response to the sale of 'Mirabella' in May 2025, sparking a renewed interest in the vessel.

As the 15th major refit undertaken by the yard, the operation involves the implementation of a 'major modernization package'. Included in this package are full interior renewal, electrical, electronic, and lighting upgrades, and an exterior repaint in the ship's original splendor. The interior furnishing and woodwork will also undergo refurbishments or replacement, while the exterior deck lights will be enhanced for a stellar nautical experience.

The Mirabella is more than just a seafaring marvel. A multitude of lifestyle upgrades are slated to be a part of the overhaul. The super yacht will boast an extensively redesigned sundeck equipped with a new, bespoke Jacuzzi. It will also feature new exterior seating areas on all decks to improve guest flow and use. Further enhancing the yacht's versatility, a transformer will be integrated within the swim platform, accompanied by structural revisions and a dedicated watertight compartment.

A project of this magnitude requires astute technical expertise and robust management from dedicated owner’s representatives. For the Mirabella’s refit, these roles are being adeptly managed by Rob Dolling from Verpeka Dolling. In this grand symphony of renovation, Dolling is leading the charge and ensuring a seamless transition from old to new. Through this refit, the Mirabella will shine anew, encapsulating all the luxury, excitement, and adventure that come with the superyacht territory.

title: The Luxurious Debut: CL Yachts' First CLX96 Sold, Renamed as 'Reunion'
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Luxurious Debut: CL Yachts' First CLX96 Sold, Renamed as 'Reunion'
summary: The first hull of CL Yachts' groundbreaking 29.5-metre CLX96 motor yacht has been sold and renamed 'Reunion', a testament to sleek design and supreme luxury.
body: CL Yachts, a brand born from the esteemed Chinese shipyard Cheoy Lee in 2017, has made waves by selling its first 29.5-metre CLX96 motor yacht. The luxury yacht, now christened 'Reunion', symbolises a revolutionary shift in yachting design and a nod to the new age of luxury sea travel.

The sale was brokered with David Johnson from Denison Yachting representing the buyer, while Panu Virtanen of CL Yachts represented the seller. 'Reunion' was delivered in 2022 and showcases a wealth of grandeur and superior sea capabilities.

A trailblazer in his field, the boat's designer Jozeph Forakis is known for marrying functionality with artistic flair. In 'Reunion', his unique rugged profile combines with a commitment to versatility and high performance, all without compromising on style. It's an effect that truly redefines the idea of a luxury motor yacht.

Entering the saloon from the aft deck - considered the ultimate al fresco dining spot - the boat offers long sightlines through an open-plan dining area, a sleek galley, and a champagne lounge with stunning views ahead. The extensive use of carbon fibre in the yacht's construction allows for structural beams and window mullions minimising intrusion on natural light, creating a well-lit, elegant interior.

For those who relish their time in the sun, two distinct social areas - the 'Terrazza Portoghese' or Portuguese bridge, and the circular seating zone named 'Piazza del Sole' add a distinctive charm. The 'Piazza del Sole' easily converts into loungers for relaxation. Towards the boat's rear, twin stairs lead down to a significant swim platform, featuring a fold-out 'Z-lift' platform, all clad in teak and perfect for launching the tender.

Powered by twin 1,900hp Caterpillar diesel engines, 'Reunion' boasts a cruising speed of 22 knots and a maximum speed of 25 knots. Whether it's the unique design, the versatility of use, or the generous speed, 'Reunion' is undoubtedly setting a high bar for other creators in the industry. It gives a glimpse into the future of luxury yachting and sets a benchmark for what luxury can truly mean in the world of sailing.

title: Luxury Yacht FIVE WAVES: Luxury, Performance, and Timeless Elegance Up for Sale

summary: FIVE WAVES, the luxurious yacht cultivated by AB Yachts in 2010 and revamped in 2017, is now open for sale.
body: Known for its luxurious accommodations and timeless styling, FIVE WAVES is now up for grabs. Crafted by AB Yachts in 2010, this impressive yacht underwent a revamp in 2017. It boasts accommodations for up to 10 guests in 5 spacious cabins, including a master suite, a VIP cabin, and 3 twin cabins, two of which are convertible to queen-sized spaces. To uphold the luxury yacht experience, a professional crew of six is there to ensure utmost tranquility. The yacht's deep-V-planing hull and superstructure, constructed from a blend of advanced materials, endow FIVE WAVES with impressive strength and weight savings. This makes for optimum performance and stability, even when the yacht is at high speeds. FIVE WAVES is not only about high performance, but it also emanates an elegant and comfortable atmosphere, thanks to the timeless styling, beautiful furnishings, and generous seating throughout. Strikingly, FIVE WAVES champions the open-style yacht design, a design that emphasizes airy spaces and sunning areas. This design philosophy is perfect for those who love to entertain, as the yacht’s expansive deck areas can easily accommodate large gatherings and parties. With her minimal draft and impressive features, FIVE WAVES is the ideal yacht for cruising in the shallow Bahamas waters. The 2017 refurbishment saw the introduction of two new main engines, a fresh paint job, new teak, new generators, and a new air conditioning system. The yacht has been highly maintained, exhibiting an outstanding condition and includes a Nouvorania Diesel Jet tender and two Yamaha Wave Runners. General specifications of FIVE WAVES include: length overall: 35.99 meters, length at the waterline: 29.9 meters, a beam of 7.32 meters, and a max draft of 1.52 meters. The yacht has a gross tonnage of 218, a tops speed of 30 knots, cruising speed of 26 knots. It's also powered by an MTU engine with a total power of 7500hp.

The capacious aft cockpit merges both functionality and leisure, being equipped with dual helm stations, shaded lounge corners, and a generous open-air dining area.

MY STAR offers a true seaside living feel, thanks to a hydraulic swim platform and fold-out chaise lounges. These amenities ensure relaxed enjoyment while at anchor. Designed for long-range cruising, the yacht packs ample storage, a professional galley, and high-quality engineering, making it ideal for adventurous souls. This beautifully maintained gem is poised for her next voyage, bringing together the thrill of exploration with the luxury of top-tier sailing.

title: 40-Metre Christensen Motor Yacht 'Sweet Escape' Now in New Hands
author: Old Sea Dogs

summary: The prestigious American Shipyard-built 39.6-metre vessel Sweet Escape has found a new owner.
body: The 39.6-metre Christensen motor yacht christened Sweet Escape has exchanged hands. The prestigious vessel became a delight to a new owner, thanks to the broker team helmed by Jarrett Hiebert of Merle Wood & Associates, and Will Noftsinger and Paolo Ameglio of Denison Yachting.

Originated from the reputable US yard, The Sweet Escape was birthed into the aquatic world in 1993, having gone through a total refit in 2023. The asking price for this magnificent entity stood last at a cool $3,999,999.

The main saloon of the yacht gushes of comfort, adorned with a large sofa, cosy armchairs, a coffee table, a grand piano and a game table. A glass wine rack artistically separates the saloon from a large formal dining table that lies forward.

The aft deck finds shelter under the overhang of the deck situated above and exhibits built-in settees and a teak table, making it perfect for outdoor dining. The skylounge, beautified by large windows that pour in natural light, serves as an ideal lounging spot for relaxing, watching films, or socialising. The sun deck is fitted with a barbecue, Jacuzzi, sun pads, and optional shade, making it a crowd favourite.

Powered by Twin C32 Caterpillar 1,650hp engines, Sweet Escape comfortably cruises at a speed of 12 knots. It has a commendable range of 2,000 nautical miles, with a full throttle speed peaking at 17 knots.

title: Westport’s Enchanting 'Avalina' Finds a New Home: Semi-displacement Motor Yacht Changes Hands
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Westport’s Enchanting 'Avalina' Finds a New Home: Semi-displacement Motor Yacht Changes Hands
summary: The grandeur of the sea, the riveting Westport motor yacht 'Avalina', has now been successfully sold to a thrilled buyer.
body: Sharing the news that makes every sailing enthusiast's heart burst with thrill: the 39.6-metre Westport motor yacht Avalina has found its new possessor. Jeff Shaffer of Superyacht Sales and Charter represented the seller, showcasing an impressive sales acumen. Simultaneously, the buyer’s interests were well-courted by Chris Daves from Denison Yachting. It was a deal done in sailing heaven, truly fitting for a vessel as magnificent as Avalina.

This semi-displacement Westport 130 is a testament to the U.S. yard's craftsmanship and design prowess. Created in 2003 using Glass Reinforced Plastic (GRP), Avalina boasts a design planned and executed in-house. Credits go to the famed Naval Architect William Garden for the yacht's clean, contemporary exterior profile that simply stuns onlookers.

The interior is another chapter to fall in love with, featuring a cherry wood finish throughout, creating a homey ambiance of warmth and comfort. It accommodates ten guests across five cabins, a main deck master suite featuring a queen-sized bed and jacuzzi bathtub, two doubles, and two twins on the lower deck, and cabins for a crew of seven. Common areas abound, with the saloon a generous rendition of welcoming design and a separate formal dining room for exquisite dining. The sundeck is a whole other realm of luxury, with a jacuzzi and sunpads to enjoy the oceanic vista.

Beneath its understated elegance lies brute strength. Powered by a pair of 2,735hp MTU engines, this 298GT yacht can shred the waves at a top speed of 24 knots or coast leisurely at cruising speed of 13 knots. Avalina has certainly left an indelible mark on Fort Lauderdale, its last port before the sale, and will undoubtedly continue to make waves with its new owner.

title: Boating Champions of the Future: Young Sailors Excel in Draycote Water Youth Open Meeting
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Boating Champions of the Future: Young Sailors Excel in Draycote Water Youth Open Meeting
summary: Young sailing talents across the country showcased their skills at the Draycote Water Sailing Club Youth Open Meeting, with home-grown sailors staking their claim to top prizes.
body: December 30th, 2025 marked a major event in the world of youth sailing as a wave of young talent descended upon Draycote Water for a thrilling competition. The Draycote Water Sailing Club Youth Open Meeting saw over a hundred eager sailors, all showing an astounding level of skill and determination.

The enthralling one-day event, sponsored by Fernhurst Books, featured fierce competition across four single-handed classes. The classes included Optimist, RS Tera, Topper, and ILCA, with battle cries resonating across the water as youthful sailors went head-to-head.

With an ideal north-easterly breeze setting the stage, the competitors, each battling within different classes, immersed themselves in the heady thrill of a cold but enthralling day of back-to-back races. The event drew commendable entries, with the overall victory in the ILCA 4s being claimed by Callum Marshall from the east coast club Blackwater SC, while Draycote Water's own Toby Turner secured second place.

Club Manager Dave Rowe couldn't contain his joy while welcoming sailors from across the country to Draycote Water. Aside from being a fan of the sport, Dave was particularly thrilled by the success of the home sailors, congratulating his academy team and thanking the staff and volunteers who helped run the event.

Stepping into 2026, the club is gearing up for an eventful year ahead. The young sailors too, undeterred by winter's chill, look forward to rigorous training sessions in preparation for the upcoming season. With its glorious setting and an encouraging ambience, Draycote Water continues to serve as a nurturing platform for these burgeoning sailing talents, setting the scene for an exhilarating future of the sport.

title: Year Begins with a Bang as GLOBE40 Sailors Embark on Pacific Trek
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Year Begins with a Bang as GLOBE40 Sailors Embark on Pacific Trek
summary: Kicking off the New Year, competitors of the prestigious GLOBE40 set sail on a high-stakes oceanic journey from Sydney to Valparaiso, Chile.
body: The New Year's fireworks had barely faded when, on the first day of the year, the GLOBE40 competitors took to the sea. The fourth leg of their global race saw them launch from the iconic Sydney Harbour, bound for distant Valparaiso, Chile. This journey transports them from one legendary destination to another, spanning a staggering 6,400 nautical miles.

For these racers, the Pacific Ocean awaits, brimming with tales of powerful storms, heroic seafarers, and untold mysteries. Their route takes them from the Australian coastline to the Chilean shores, with New Zealand serving as the last sight of land before they dive headlong into the beckoning void of the deep ocean.

The midway point in Sydney provided a memorable break, with the charismatic city offering a warm welcome. This mix of a stunning cityscape revolving around the sea and a supportive public makes Sydney a sailor’s haven.

As they cast off for the New Year, the racers are set to chart their course between Sydney Harbour and Valparaiso Bay, navigating numerous obstacles such as Point Nemo, the reputed location furthest from land on Earth. This prestigious leg, featuring predominantly western to eastern oceanic crossing, is likely to be at least as challenging as its predecessors, posing a fresh test for the competitors.

The Pacific crossing commences with a sense of anticipation and novelty, merging the thrill of the unfamiliar with the adrenaline rush of competition. As the sailors' venture into the vastness, they not only push the limits of sailing ingenuity but remind us of the human capacity for adventure.

title: 2026 ILCA Oceania Solidarity Squad Aims for Fair, Safe, and Fun Competition in Upcoming Championship

Gathering from New Zealand and from various corners of Australia, the squad congregated in Hobart for their inaugural day of preparation for the 2026 Oceania and Australian Open and Youth Championships. Here, their primary directive was underlined: fair, safe and fun competition should guide every nautical mile they tackle.

The principal race officer, Colin Dods, impresses this ethos upon them, reminding that the squad's purpose goes beyond individual glory. He encourages them to invest in their collective sailing experience, forming lifelong friendships and fostering a love for sailing that transcends scores and titles.

Racing in boats with significant Olympic heritage on the River Derwent, each team member benefits from the equal playing field provided by identical ILCA dinghies. Recognizing that single-handed sailing is often a solitary endeavor, encouragement to communicate, learn from one another, and share the same experience, creates a team spirit that is rarely found in such events.

Within this inspiring context, the 2026 ILCA Oceania Solidarity Squad continues to prepare for the Championships. They do so reminding us that fair competition, safe practices, and above all, fun, constitute the backbone of sport at its finest.

title: Min River Declared Winner of the 2025 Rolex Sydney Hobart
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Min River Declared Winner of the 2025 Rolex Sydney Hobart
imageCredit: © Rolex Sydney Hobart Yacht Race - Cruising Yacht Club of Australia
summary: The Rolex Sydney Hobart Yacht Race has never been a contest that ends neatly at the finish line. For all its drama offshore, the race has a long history of decisions, disputes and fine margins being settled ashore — sometimes days later, when the salt has dried and the paperwork begins.
body: Min River Crowned Overall Winner After Protest Decision Shakes 2025 Rolex Sydney Hobart

Following a formal protest lodged by the Race Committee against BNC – my::NET / LEON, the International Jury has now delivered its verdict. The protest has been upheld, and a time penalty of one hour and five minutes has been applied to the yacht’s elapsed time.
The decision alters the final standings and confirms Min River as the Overall Winner of the 2025 Rolex Sydney Hobart Yacht Race.

For many crews, Hobart represents the end of the road — a line crossed, a watch stopped, and a quiet exhale after 628 demanding nautical miles. But in this case, the race remained unresolved long after the last sails were flaked and the dockside beers poured.

The Race Committee’s protest centred on a rule breach involving BNC – my::NET / LEON. While the specific technical details sit firmly in the domain of race management and the International Jury, the guiding principle behind the decision was clear: fairness, proportionality, and the preservation of competitive integrity.

In its ruling, the Jury stated that the penalty imposed ensured that any possible performance gains were fully accounted for, while also applying a sanction proportionate to the breach. In plain terms, this was not about punishment for punishment’s sake — it was about restoring the competitive balance of the race.

In offshore racing, an hour can be nothing — or everything. Over days at sea, boats may separate by hundreds of miles, only to converge again as weather systems compress the fleet. In IRC racing, where corrected time reigns supreme, even minutes can determine a winner.

A penalty of 1 hour and 5 minutes is therefore decisive, but not excessive. It reflects both the seriousness of the infringement and the Jury’s obligation to ensure that results genuinely reflect performance within the rules.

With that adjustment applied, Min River’s consistent, disciplined race is elevated to the top of the standings — a reminder that offshore success is built not just on speed, but on compliance, seamanship and attention to detail.

While much of the public spotlight inevitably focuses on supermaxis and line honours battles, the soul of the Sydney Hobart has always lived in the IRC fleet — where crews race boat-for-boat, rule-by-rule, and mile-by-mile.

Min River’s campaign exemplified that ethos. Clean sailing, smart decisions and steady pressure across the course delivered a result that stood up not only to the ocean’s scrutiny, but to the rulebook as well.
In a race defined by attrition, fatigue and relentless weather systems, Min River stayed in the game — and crucially, stayed on the right side of the rules.
This outcome will inevitably spark dockside debate. That, too, is part of the Sydney Hobart’s DNA. But the International Jury’s role is not to please the crowd — it is to protect the race.

The Rolex Sydney Hobart Yacht Race is not just a test of boats and crews; it is a test of discipline under pressure. Sail changes at 0300, navigation decisions made in exhaustion, and compliance with racing rules when the margin for error is thin. The standard expected is high because the race itself is unforgiving.
When penalties are applied, they reinforce a simple truth: offshore racing rewards those who combine speed with responsibility.

For Min River, the verdict delivers a well-earned overall victory — one that will stand the test of time in the official record. For BNC – my::NET / LEON, it is a harsh outcome, but one that reflects the reality of racing at the highest level.
And for the wider sailing world, it is a reminder that the Sydney Hobart is never truly over until the final ruling is signed.

From the spectacle of Sydney Harbour on Boxing Day to the sober deliberations of an International Jury, the 2025 Rolex Sydney Hobart has once again proven why it remains one of the most demanding and respected offshore races on the planet.
The ocean delivers the first judgement. The rulebook delivers the last.

title: The 2025 Memorial Winter Pursuit Race Echoes Legacy of Ashley Crawford at Plym Yacht Club
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The 2025 Memorial Winter Pursuit Race Echoes Legacy of Ashley Crawford at Plym Yacht Club
summary: Embodying the spirit of camaraderie at sea, the Ashley Crawford Memorial Pursuit Race 2025 celebrates the enduring legacy of its late patron.
body: The late winter chill of the sea breeze at Plym Yacht Club is pierced by the camaraderie and competitive spirit of local sailors. They annually congregate here not simply for the sport of sailing, but to honor the memory of a beloved member, Ashley Crawford. The Ashley Crawford Memorial Pursuit Race, dreamt up by Crawford himself years ago as a way to entice sailors from their Christmas-induced hibernation, has become a cherished tradition.

The 2025 winter edition of the event witnessed a robust turnout, a testament to Crawford's impact on the sailing community. The race admitted a diverse array of watercraft from yachts and dinghies to wingfoilers, straining against the moorings in anticipation. With the North Easterly breeze pushing against their sails, a bevy of seafarers embarked on a course from Deadman's Bay to North Drakes Island, navigating the famously unpredictable winds of Plymouth Sound.

After the racing was finished, all retreated to the warmth of the Plym, to share laughter, drinks, and stories of the day's events. The Ashley Crawford Memorial Pursuit Race proved once more that it is not just about racing, it is a gathering of the extended family that is the sailing community, united in memory of a cherished member, and in celebration of the joy of being on the water.

title: Rossinavi's Groundbreaking Explorer Yacht Akula Marks Its Premier Appearance on the Market
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Rossinavi's Groundbreaking Explorer Yacht Akula Marks Its Premier Appearance on the Market
summary: The impressive 59.4-metre Rossinavi explorer yacht Akula is making waves for the first time on the market, with David Legrand of Fraser acting as broker.
body: Rossinavi's explorer yacht Akula, frequently seen cruising the globe with its striking scarlet red profile, is now available on the market. Its audacious design, drawn from the innovative mind of Gian Paolo Nari, has stirred up much interest and praise since its delivery in 2024. This admiration testifies to the Italian shipyard's successful leap into explorer yacht construction.

The 59.4-metre Akula - designed for ventures anywhere on the globe - features an ice-class steel hull and a hybrid diesel-electric propulsion system. Offering a remarkable range of up to 8,000 nautical miles, the vessel not only prioritises efficiency but also environmental consciousness during its exploration.

More than a sophisticated space of leisure, the Akula is outfitted with various dedicated spaces, such as a full-fledged gym, sauna, massage room, heated pool, a 'man cave' adorned with nautical trinkets, and practical equipment such as inbuilt drying areas for outdoor gear on the bridge deck. A 'craft cave' and a lower-deck workshop, connected by an elevator that services all decks, lends a touch of whimsy and practicality. Akula features accommodation for ten guests, distributed between an owner's suite, three double cabins and one twin cabin with a convertible study, all located on the main deck. Additional quarters can host a crew of thirteen.

Yet, her luxury and comfort don't detract from her practicality and workabilty, as she also houses labs and workshops that add an avenue for scientific research on the vessel. Her exterior is as impressive, displaying vast open deck spaces, generous storage capable of housing up to nine-meter long tenders, and a crane designed to handle large equipment, including a mini-submarine. With stellar specifications such as an 11.3-metre beam, a draught of 3.5 metres, and a stealthy max speed of 15 knots, Akula is believed to be a breakthrough in the yacht market. The remarkable sailing credentials and the sophisticated design make Rossinavi's Akula an explorer yacht par excellence.

title: Experience the Thrill of Securing Europe’s First Schaefer V44: A Boating Adventure Shaped by Lifelong Passion
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Experience the Thrill of Securing Europe’s First Schaefer V44: A Boating Adventure Shaped by Lifelong Passion
summary: Embark on a fascinating journey with David Ross, as he navigates his way through the high seas of yacht ownership to finally secure Europe’s first Schaefer V44.
body: From daydreams of adventures with Jacques Cousteau, to the reality of sailing into the sunset on his very own Schaefer V44, David Ross's narrative is more than a tale of yacht ownership. It's intrinsic to his identity, to his deep love for the open ocean that has weathered throughout myriad life tides.

Ross's nautical journey begins with the acquisition of a Sessa Key Largo 30. Despite its superb seakeeping abilities and the fun it brings, it lacked one crucial element - ample sun protection. With a growing family to consider, Ross moves on to trade the Sessa Key Largo 30 for a handsome Sessa C52, 'Vamos II.' Its three cabins, large diesels, and open potential posed it as the perfect family boat. Despite some teething issues, the resilience of Vamos II mirrored Ross's spirit, leading them on countless picturesque endeavours around Denia and the Balearics.

The sleek design of the Schaefer V44, its futuristic helm station, their promise of quality – everything about it reeled Ross in, hook, line, and sinker. She might not have been everything he was looking for, but the Schaefer V44 sparked an unprecedented excitement in him. Two things powered the final decision - his wife's absence at the boat show, and an insuppressible desire that was hard to ignore.
Despite her considerable price and deviation from his brief, the Schaefer V44 became the boat Ross really, really wanted – an embodiment of his lifelong dream.

title: Revolutionary Design for Day Cruising: Invictus TT550 Dedicates Over 40% to External Relaxation Spaces
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Revolutionary Design for Day Cruising: Invictus TT550 Dedicates Over 40% to External Relaxation Spaces
summary: The Invictus TT550 luxury day boat turns boat building on its head, prioritising a connection with the sea through its unique design and layout.
body: With a reputation for innovation and design, Invictus's newest flagship offering, TT550, breaks away from the conventional with its trendsetting styling and luxurious detailing. The striking reverse bow and a sweeping carbon-fibre hardtop are just starters as the design amps up the charm with a long hull window mirroring an equally impressive bulwark cutaway.

Yet, what truly makes the Invictus TT550 a remarkable feat of design is its emphasis on creating a strong bond with the sea through its exterior layout. Over 40% of the boat is dedicated to an expansive aft beach club, boasting a spacious aft-facing dinette, a central sunbed with a reversible backrest, an open transom, dual drop-down terraces, and a submersible stern platform. This focus on 'day spaces' reinforces the underlying design philosophy of the boat - to help occupants connect with the sea.

As a luxury brand, Invictus leaves no stone unturned when it comes to providing personalisation options. The in-house 'Atelier Invictus' department assists in customising each boat with modular layouts and bespoke finishes. A choice of modern exterior tones and upholstery colors, coupled with a new water-resistant exterior fabric, further amplify the boat’s appeal.

In a world of high seas and higher styles, the Invictus TT550 stands out with its thoughtful blend of contemporary design, luxurious features, and synthesis with the sea. It's more than just a day boat; it's a testament to Invictus’s commitment to pushing the envelope of marine design.

title: New Year's Eve Turns St. Barths into Grand Display of Luxury Superyachts
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: New Year's Eve Turns St. Barths into Grand Display of Luxury Superyachts
summary: St. Barths, a Caribbean superyacht hub, once again plays host to a spectacle of unparalleled luxury as the world's most prestigious yachts dock in its waters to welcome 2026.

Welcome to New Year's Eve in St. Barths. A premier location known globally for its beach clubs and festive spirit, St. Barths is indisputably the heart of the Caribbean superyacht scene. As the calendar turns, the French island hosts an array of the globe’s most recognizable and majestic yachts, becoming an absolute must-see for maritime enthusiasts worldwide. Among the fleet is an impressive line-up of lavish heavyweights who have returned to partake in the jubilations. Lürssen's 122-metre marvel Kismet, Freire's 112-metre leviathan Renaissance, and Oceanco's 110-metre Kaos have taken their places, joined by Lürssen’s 138-metre Rising Sun, gracing the location with its appearance after its memorable appearance also marking the island’s waters in 2022. The deep blue sea serving as a picturesque backdrop to these stunning vessels is completed by a flotilla of newly delivered sleek models from 2025. This includes Feadship’s 101-meter stunner Moonrise, leading an imposing squadron of craft fresh off the construction docks. This crew includes gleaming new arrivals from distinguished builders such as Amels, Benetti, Baglietto, and Royal Huisman. According to maritime sources, approximately 135 yachts have already secured their spots around St. Barths for the grandeur of New Year's Eve, and more are projected to glide gracefully onto the scene in the ensuing days. As the grand countdown to 2026 begins, it becomes crystal clear that there’s no place quite like St. Barths for a nautical New Year extravaganza.

title: A Boxing Day institution where grit meets ocean
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Rolex Sydney Hobart Yacht Race 2025
summary: There are yacht races, and then there is the Rolex Sydney Hobart Yacht Race — a Boxing Day institution where grit meets ocean, and fortunes are won or lost on the cruel 628-mile highway south. This year’s 80th edition was no different: a brutal opening leg out of Sydney Harbour, a tactical slug-fest across Bass Strait, and a battle down the Tasmanian coast that proved once again why this is one of sport’s toughest of
body: The fleet — 129 boats of all sizes — carved a corridor through the swirling start line at Rushcutters Bay at 1300 on Boxing Day, bows pointed toward Hobart and hearts set on legend. From the outset it was clear this wouldn’t be a procession. Strong southerly winds, pounding swells and an unforgiving Bass Strait test meant the battle would be as much about staying in it as being fast. Nine

In classic Hobart fashion, the drama began even before the official gun. Yendys, a seasoned contender, broke her backstay and was forced to withdraw just minutes before the start — a reminder that this race respects no one. Live Sail Die

As the horn sounded, LawConnect — defending Line Honours champion — leapt into an early advantage, punching through Sydney Heads ahead of the pack and setting a daunting pace. But it wouldn’t stay that way for long. Reuters

By the first night out to sea, the heavyweight duel had formed: Master Lock Comanche and LawConnect trading tacks and miles, with SHK Scallywag 100 lurking just behind. These supermaxis — behemoths designed for speed — were in a three-way fight that would carry them deep into the Tasman Sea.

Bass Strait has a reputation as a place where races are won and lost, and 2025 delivered the usual tests in spades. Wind angles oscillated and seas kicked up under heavy pressure bands, forcing navigators to make calls that carried heavy consequences. The big boats led into the zone, but smaller boats in stronger breeze found themselves making up ground, skimming waves and chasing every fraction of apparent wind.

This was not a race for the faint of heart. More than 30 boats pulled out by the second night: rudder failures, rigging issues, and sheer crew exhaustion taking their toll. Wild Thing 100, a much-anticipated challenger with a fresh rig, succumbed to gear failure — a bitter blow in any Hobart. Kiwi entries V5 and Vixen also retired, adding to an early attrition toll that underscored Bass Strait’s volatility.

As the race clock ticked south, the leaderboard tightened. Master Lock Comanche, skippered by Matt Allen and James Mayo, had edged into the lead and held a narrow advantage over LawConnect, with SHK Scallywag 100 pressing hard in third. Just behind them sat Lucky, an American entry from the New York Yacht Club, and Palm Beach XI, the former Wild Oats XI with a storied Hobart history.
1st – Master Lock Comanche (NSW) — holding a slight edge in both pace and position.
2nd – LawConnect (NSW) — defending champion and perennial contender.
3rd – SHK Scallywag 100 — the Hong Kong-owned script-flipper in a classic chase.
4th – Lucky (USA) — a strong performance from the American fleet.
5th – Palm Beach XI — once the king of Sydney to Hobart, still mixing it at the sharp end.

Every one of those boats was posting double-figure speeds, but the Southern Ocean has a way of making even a small change in pressure feel vast. A late penalty turn for SHK Scallywag, executed to avoid future time penalties, demonstrated just how finely poised these battles were.

Offshore racing is as much about people as it is about hardware. Crews spent long watches steering into seas with 20–30 knot winds, hands raw and minds locked on every shift. Helm calls blended with tactical updates, and every squall brought a fresh tally of sweat and salt.

The Southern Ocean doesn’t roar every year, but when those swells lock in and the wind stiffens for days on end, sailors enter a kind of ordered survival mode: trims refined, risks assessed, and goals reduced to simple truths — stay upright, stay fast, stay alive.

Approaching Tasmania brings a mix of relief and anxiety. Scores are tallied, standing rigging inspected each watch, and every crew knows the story of Hobart’s final hurdle: the Derwent River. Like a trickster, its fickle afternoon breezes can make a leader a sitting duck or a straggler suddenly fast.
At the point of writing, the leading group was still racing south of Gabo Island, the finish line yet hours away and the Derwent wind pattern still a factor to be won or lost.
But no matter what the finish order becomes, the narrative has already been written across sunburned faces, shredded gloves and lines pulled taut in the dark.

This year’s Rolex Sydney Hobart Yacht Race wasn’t the easiest on record, but it was one of the most complete tests of offshore craft and crew. It brought together international challengers and local veterans, pedigree boats and hungry upstarts — all subjected to the harsh but fair judgement of ocean and wind.
More than 30 retirements, several gear failures and strategic call after call reminded everyone that Hobart remains a race where ‘because we could’ is never enough reason to finish.

And so, as these yachts dot the final miles toward the Tasmanian capital, and as Constitution Dock begins to fill with battle-scarred hulls and exhausted sailors, there’ll be stories — long, salty and unvarnished — of every tack, trade-off and survived squall.

For those on the rail this year — and those watching from shore — the 80th Sydney Hobart will be remembered not just for its leaders, but for the relentless push that nearly every competitor made from start to finish.

title: Exceptional Growth for the Melges 15 Winter Series as Sailors Register a Record 126 Boats
author: Old Sea Dogs

summary: In an unprecedented show of growth, the Melges 15 Winter Series sees an impressive register of 126 boats for its second event.

A record-smashing 126 boats were registered for participating in the second event of the Winter Series, a considerable leap from the preceding year when a still not-to-be-scoffed-at 109 vessels graced the waters. This fascinating episodic growth trajectory has firmly placed Melges 15 Winter Series on the map as one of the rapidly expanding one-design fleets in North America.
