The clinic, expected to see participation from over 30 teams, will be conducted under the aegis of the lauded three-time world champion and guest coach Steve Hunt alongside 2025's National Champion Madeline Baldridge. Across the years, the Melges 15 Winter Series has drawn enormous fleets to the sunlit shores on Florida, riding on the cusp of the winter break. Year after year, the Winter Series Event 2 has shattered attendance records, presenting a spectacle that has delighted attendees and participants equally. As the intensity of the race mounts on water, an equally vibrant scenery enscones spectators on land. Nail-biting races and thrilling culmination of events create an electric atmosphere, both off and on water. The event offers a wholesome family experience, peppered with loads of fun and camaraderie. The Winter Series has also evolved into a technical playground to test and showcase RaceSense, a proprietary technology by Vakaros, for enhancing the racing experience. The unprecedented scale of the fleet provides a real-world environment to assess and refine race management, ensuring a seamless experience. The Melges Watersports Center in Merritt Island has proven to be the perfect venue with its convenient location and efficient logistics support. Besides the efficient management of the event, the welcoming and enjoyable atmosphere created by the Melges Team plays a vital role in creating memorable experiences.

title: East Anglian Offshore Racing Association Debuts New Format for 2026: An Intriguing Coastal Regatta
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: East Anglian Offshore Racing Association Debuts New Format for 2026: An Intriguing Coastal Regatta
summary: The East Anglian Offshore Racing Association (EAORA) is set to launch the 2026 season with a refreshing new coastal regatta.
body: Prepare for a remarkable change of course in the sailing calendar as the East Anglian Offshore Racing Association (EAORA) gets ready to take the plunge in 2026, charting a new path with an innovative coastal regatta. Fueled by the desire to inspire sailors to explore beyond their usual local waters, EAORA has revamped the racing programme in 2026, kicking things off with a freshly minted coastal regatta during the first May Bank Holiday.

A meticulously planned itinerary includes races from Harwich to Medway on May 2, onward from Medway to Burnham on May 3, and finally setting sail from Burnham to West Mersea on May 4. This not only offers seasoned sailors a fabulous opportunity to test and calibrate their yachts, but it also provides a stunning prelude to the Royal Ocean Racing Club's (RORC’s) North Sea Race, scheduled on May 15, from Harwich to Scheveningen.

Carrying forward the exhilarating spirit of the new EAORA’s format, the 2026 itinerary includes an array of compelling races. Scheduled events include the Round the Goodwins Race on July 19, the HMS Halcyon Cup on August 15, followed by the Houghton Cup on September 5, culminating in the traditional season’s grand finale with The Buckley Goblets on September 18.

The 2026 sailing season beckons with its exciting revamped format, promising not just a race, but an adventure waiting to be experienced. Seafarers, it's time to embark upon the new-wave EAORA format in 2026 and sail into unexplored waters!

title: The 80th Sydney Hobart Yacht Race
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: The 80th Sydney Hobart Yacht Race
summary: Before the gun fires and the fleet charges south, the Rolex Sydney Hobart Yacht Race will pause this Boxing Day to look back — and do so in style. To mark the 80th edition of one of offshore sailing’s most revered contests, the Cruising Yacht Club of Australia will stage a Parade of Sail, celebrating the founding fathers, the early boats, and the stories that shaped a race first sailed in 1945.
body: Long before foils, canting keels and weather routers, just nine yachts set off on that inaugural voyage south. None of those sailors could have imagined that their modest adventure would grow into a 628-nautical-mile institution, watched by millions worldwide and drawing fleets as large as 371 starters, as seen in the race’s 50th anniversary year in 1994.

On Boxing Day morning, classic yachts will assemble in Rose Bay, before beginning the Parade of Sail from 10:30am to 11:30am. The fleet will sail north past Steele Point off Nielsen Park, continue to Sow and Pigs Reef at Watsons Bay, and return to finish at Obelisk Bay.
Resplendent with flags flying, these yachts — spanning the golden era and the more modern classic period — will transform Sydney Harbour into a living museum of offshore racing history.

Leading the procession will be the sail training ship Young Endeavour, operated by the Royal Australian Navy. For thousands of young Australians, Young Endeavour has offered life-shaping experiences at sea — and 2025 carries special poignancy, marking her final voyage as Flagship for the Sydney Hobart Yacht Race.
Every yacht in the Parade carries a story — and together they form the spine of the race’s history.

Defiance, launched in 1935, was the first Australian-designed and built 8-metre yacht constructed to the International 8 Metre Rule. She raced to Hobart in 1946, finishing second over the line and fourth overall. Today, she is proudly owned by Nicole Shrimpton, continuing her long life afloat.

Built in 1948, Margaret Rintoul was the boat to beat in her era. Campaigned five times by original owner A.W. Edwards, she narrowly missed Line Honours in 1949 before claiming it in 1950 and 1951, breaking the race record and holding it for six years. Now owned by Sydney Hobart veteran Bruce Gould, the elegant yawl remains a benchmark of her time.

Fidelis, a Knud Reimers design conceived in the mid-1930s but not built until 1964, etched her place in history in 1966. Sailed by James Davern, she became the first New Zealand yacht to win Line Honours — and did so by an astonishing 17 hours, 27 minutes and 3 seconds, a margin that still stands. Long-time owner Nigel Stoke has raced her to Hobart four times since 1994.

Maris, a Tasman Seabird design launched in 1958 for CYCA founding member and artist Jack Earl, carries deep family connections. Owned today by Earl’s granddaughter Tiare Tomaszewski, Maris has competed in seven Sydney Hobarts, always with one of Earl’s grandchildren aboard — a living bridge between generations.

Two iconic Halvorsen yachts also take their place. Solveig, built in 1950 by Lars Halvorsen & Sons for brothers Trygve and Magnus Halvorsen, claimed Line Honours in 1953 and Overall victory in 1954. She will be helmed this Boxing Day by Bob Allan.
Anitra V, launched in 1956, followed with Overall victory in 1957 under the same famous brothers and is now owned by Philip Brown.

They are joined by Caprice of Huon, owned by David Champtaloup, an Admiral’s Cup veteran that finished second overall in the 1972 Sydney Hobart, and Lolita, built in 1946 and boasting seven Hobart starts, now beautifully maintained by Gary Cassim.

From the modern classic era comes Sagacious V, one of the most formidable Farr 40 one-tonners of her generation. Sailed by Gary Appleby, she claimed Overall victory in the 1990 Sydney Hobart, following campaigns in the Admiral’s Cup, Southern Cross Cup and Kenwood Cup.
Now owned by David Hundt, Sagacious V remains in immaculate condition — a rare sight of a grand-prix racer preserved exactly as she once was.

As spectators line the harbour and cameras turn seaward, the Parade of Sail offers a moment to slow the clock — to remember that today’s spectacle rests on decades of ambition, heartbreak, innovation and seamanship.
Before the fleet heads south, Sydney Harbour will tell the race’s story the only way it knows how: under sail.

title: Exploring the Adventurous Journey of RS Sailing in 2025: Astonishing Boating Launches, Regattas, and Vibrant Youth Participation
author: Old Sea Dogs

The summer season announced a full schedule of international RS events. Standouts included the RS Aero World Championship in Quiberon, France, and the RS21 World Championship in Porto Rotondo, Italy, with over 200 sailors battling big waves and gusty winds.
Overall, 2025 was a year that reaffirmed RS Sailing's commitment to cultivating a sense of community, enthusiasm, and participation on global waters.

title: 80th Rolex Sydney Hobart Yacht Race has a new headline act
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: 80th Rolex Sydney Hobart Yacht Race has a new headline act
summary: Master Lock Comanche Fires a Warning Shot: Champions Poised for Overall Cabbage Tree Island Race Glory The road to the 80th Rolex Sydney Hobart Yacht Race has a new headline act — and it thunders in red, black, and carbon fibre. Master Lock Comanche, already one of the most feared Maxi yachts on the planet, has delivered a dominant statement victory in the Cabbage Tree Island Race, the traditional proving ground for
body: In classic east-coast conditions, Comanche powered her way up the NSW coastline and back, completing the 172-nautical-mile course in a provisional 14hrs 34mins 21secs. The final two miles, however, offered the sort of maddening calm that only ocean racing can produce — glassy water, postcard sunrise, absolutely zero wind. Comanche ghosted across the line, sails hanging limp but boat speed still good enough to secure another clinical Line Honours win.

This marks back-to-back victories for Matt Allen and James Mayo’s weapon of a yacht in the Audi Centre Sydney Blue Water Pointscore, following their Bird Island Race triumph. And if form counts for anything, Comanche is now the boat to beat heading into the historic 80th edition of the Sydney Hobart.
LawConnect Holds On, Thorpe Makes Offshore Debut

Chasing hard behind Comanche was LawConnect, with Olympic legend Ian Thorpe onboard making his offshore racing debut. Steering the ship was veteran skipper Tony Mutter, filling in for owner Christian Beck.

Despite a false start, a torn jib, and a chaotic scramble to regroup before exiting the Heads, LawConnect dug deep to limit the damage. They crossed the line 1hr 8mins 11secs behind Comanche — not the result they wanted, but a gritty performance all the same.
Thorpe’s first impressions of offshore life were delivered with trademark understatement:
“Ocean race means something completely different in my sport… In swimming it’s 15 or 25 kilometres. Today was a little bit further.”

The transition from pool tiles to carbon foils seems to have left a mark. Thorpe spoke candidly about the contrast between the unseen coaching worlds of elite swimming and the very visible choreography of a Maxi crew under pressure.
Scallywag Fights, Celestial V70 Poised for Overall Win
Hong Kong’s SHK Scallywag 100, owned by Seng Huang Lee and skippered by David Witt, finished a further 27 minutes behind LawConnect, coming home in third.
But the real storyline developing further down the fleet is the one the handicap tables love — Celestial V70.

The former winner of the 2024 Rolex Sydney Hobart Overall title has sailed herself into pole position to claim the Cabbage Tree Island Race Overall crown. But in true offshore fashion, the champagne must remain on ice: the slower boats still on course could reshuffle the leaderboard as the day unfolds.
The Cabbage Tree Island Race is only the beginning. Over the next three days the Australian Maxi Championship continues, before culminating in the iconic SOLAS Big Boat Challenge on Sydney Harbour.

Eight Maxis and Mini-Maxis — led by Master Lock Comanche, LawConnect, and SHK Scallywag 100 — will roar across the harbour in front of thousands of spectators. It’s the last big dress rehearsal before Boxing Day.
And make no mistake: Comanche’s performance in the Cabbage Tree Island Race has changed the temperature in the Maxi fleet.
She’s fast. She’s hungry. And she’s refusing to let anyone forget who the reigning giant truly is.
The stage for the 80th Rolex Sydney Hobart is set — and if this race is any indication, the battle for Line Honours will be nothing short of explosive.

title: Holiday Team Race Launches the Season in Style at Waldringfield Sailing Club
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Holiday Team Race Launches the Season in Style at Waldringfield Sailing Club
summary: Unexpectedly harsh weather set the stage for an exhilarating Christmas Eve team race at Waldringfield Sailing Club, bringing together seasoned sailors and rising talents alike.
body: A perfect storm of holiday cheer and ardent competition, Waldringfield Sailing Club's Christmas Eve team race erupted against a backdrop of rattling windows and gusty winds, as an obscenely brisk chill swept in from the Siberian wastelands. Yet, it was precisely this daunting weather that lent the event a particular twist, making it as exhilarating as unwrapping a coveted gift.

Despite the temptation to seek refuge under warm blankets, the fervor for sailing ran high. Ribs were launched amid shivering temperatures, all thanks to the raw enthusiasm and indomitable spirit of the sailors, particularly the younger participants. Youth racing member, Angus, declared the conditions 'more or less sailable', and so, wrapping their resilience around them like cloaks against the wind, the participants forged ahead.

On this frosty morning, 26 eager sailors—ranging from World Champions to budding sailing enthusiasts—participated in the race, strategic maneuvers and family rivalries taking precedence over freezing temperatures. Much like a festive game of Monopoly on water, the course was fraught with moments of playful confrontation and cutthroat competition.

And so, after a double-round robin race that culminated in four teams each facing off twice, some worthy winners emerged. But beyond the victories and defeats, it was the communal feeling of resilience and determination that truly took center stage. In the face of a winter chill that could deter even the bravest, the sailors of Waldringfield continued to find joy, camaraderie, and fulfillment on the rolling waves, marking yet another successful start to the holiday season.

title: Embarking on an Unforgettable Journey through the Solent: A Yorkshireman's Adventures at Buckler's Hard
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Embarking on an Unforgettable Journey through the Solent: A Yorkshireman's Adventures at Buckler's Hard
summary: A northern Britain recounting a remarkable sojourn. Travelling around the Solent and sharing his first-time rapture at Buckler's Hard. His joyride'll entice you to set your next sail toward the Solent.
body: Every seafarer has a tale to tell. For Ian Furby, a Yorkshireman who would launch his boat from Runswick Bay, his story leads us through a mystical journey navigating the waters of the Solent and anchoring at the marvelous Buckler's Hard. Despite his experiences sailing the northern seas, the Solent provided a new voyage of discovery.

Being at the helm of a Nordkapp Enduro 605 wasn't for the faint of heart, but Furby was eager, ready, and excited. The vast expanse of water, new adventures around every wave, sightings of minke whales, and glimpses of sun-dappled bottlenose dolphins solidified his fondness for marine life and deepened his passion for sailing.

With the desire to extend his boating season and the support of a quality road trailer, our refined Yorkshireman navigated the roughly 300 miles to Oban. After soaking in its exquisite beauty, he decided to round off his season a little differently, by steering the Six 0 Five 'down south' to the Southampton Boat Show. A clear vision, some meticulous planning and nothing but the open water ahead, the journey promised exciting days of sailing and several cherished memories.

Their Boat Show visit was an annual event, usually a chance for beers and conversation among the 'lads'. Yet, this trip offered a unique twist. His wife, Sheddy, was to join him, transforming it into an intimate couple's adventure. Thus, their berths were decided at the pristine Town Quay Marina, the ideal base, granting easy access to the show and located conveniently near a boat launch.

Prepared for his five-day journey, their Monday kick-off was welcomed by an ideal high-pressure system; bright blue skies, and lovely mid-20s temperatures. A northeast wind provided the only wrinkle, but nothing could deter our dauntless explorer. Hours away from Yorkshire, they landed at the Marina Office on the Solent and prepared for launch, having perfectly timed their arrival with the midpoint of the tide.

Their journey was fruitful. The array of sights, all bathed in the warmth of the afternoon sun, including the breathtaking landscape of Buckler's Hard in the Beaulieu River, etched a lasting memory in their hearts. This remarkable journey underscored Furby's burning passion for the sea, and Buckler's Hard will undoubtedly call him back for many more adventures.

title: Old Sea Dogs: One Year Afloat
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Old Sea Dogs - One Year Afloat
imageCaption: Happy Christmas from all at Old Sea Dogs
summary: Old Sea Dogs: One Year Afloat Earlier this year, OldSeaDogs.com slipped its lines and pointed its bow toward open water.
body: No grand launch fanfare. No corporate polish. Just a simple idea: tell boating stories properly — with salt still drying on the pages, with respect for tradition, and with curiosity for where the marine world is heading next. A place for sailors, powerboaters, dreamers, racers, refitters, dock-talk philosophers, and those who simply feel more at home when the horizon is visible. One year on, Old Sea Dogs has become a logbook of global boating life — stories gathered from harbours, racecourses, boatyards, show pontoons, and far-off seas. It’s been a year of wind shifts and learning curves, of long nights writing and longer days watching boats do what boats have always done: carry people toward something just beyond reach. This is that first year, written down before the wake fades.

One of the earliest realisations was simple: boating has no borders. Within weeks of launching, stories were flowing in from every corner of the map — Mediterranean, Atlantic crossings, Caribbean trade winds, Northern European boatyards, Australian marinas, American coastal towns. Different accents, different traditions, but the same language spoken fluently: tide, wind, hull, weather, risk, reward. Old Sea Dogs covered elite international racing and grassroots sailing with equal care. From team racing in light, fickle conditions to offshore classics that demand sleep deprivation, discipline and deep respect for the sea, the racing stories weren’t just about results — they were about why people keep turning up. Because racing sailors understand something early: the sea doesn’t care who you are. Whether it was Olympic-pathway sailors threading mark roundings in barely two knots, or offshore crews preparing for days of cold watches and wet decks, the common thread was commitment. Preparation. And that quiet moment before the start gun when everyone knows that once you leave the dock, excuses stay behind.

But Old Sea Dogs was never intended to be only about racing. Some of the most-read and most-shared pieces this year weren’t about podiums at all. They were about boats themselves — why they’re designed the way they are, how they behave when the conditions turn ugly, and what they offer the people who live with them day after day. Boat reviews became a core pillar early on, not as glossy brochure rewrites, but as honest conversations. The kind you’d overhear leaning on a pontoon rail with a mug of coffee in hand. What works offshore? What works at anchor? What looks clever on paper but proves awkward at sea? What boats earn loyalty — and which ones quietly get sold on? From practical cruisers to modern hardtops, from classic lines to contemporary design experiments, the underlying question stayed the same: would you trust this boat when the weather stops being polite? That perspective resonated. Because most readers don’t just want to admire boats — they want to understand them.

Early on, Old Sea Dogs leaned deliberately into something the boating world sometimes forgets: people matter more than vessels. The stories that linger are rarely about horsepower figures or sail area ratios. They’re about the decisions made at 3 a.m. The friendships forged over refits. The quiet pride of a well-sailed passage. The humility learned after getting it wrong. Throughout the year, the site explored the human stories behind the hardware: owners, sailors, designers, builders, dreamers, risk-takers, restorers, innovators. People who didn’t always start with perfect conditions or unlimited budgets — but who shared a stubborn pull toward water. Some stories were aspirational. Others deeply practical. A few were cautionary. All of them shared one thing: authenticity. No filters. No artificial drama. Just life afloat, as it really happens.

One of the strongest themes to emerge naturally was respect for maritime history — not as nostalgia, but as continuity. Historic yachts undergoing major rebuilds weren’t treated as museum pieces, but as living links between generations of sailors. Restorations weren’t framed as vanity projects, but as acts of stewardship — keeping knowledge, craftsmanship and design philosophy alive for those who come next. At the same time, Old Sea Dogs didn’t shy away from asking hard questions about where boating is going. Safety. Design assumptions. Environmental responsibility. Technology creeping onboard. Automation versus seamanship. The balance between innovation and over-complexity. When modern yachts fail, or when design choices deserve scrutiny, the site addressed it respectfully but honestly. Because the sea has always punished complacency — and always will.

Sailing may have deep roots in Old Sea Dogs’ DNA, but powerboating took its rightful place this year too. Fast boats. Offshore fishing machines. Long-range cruisers. Performance hulls designed for serious water. The site celebrated the joy of speed and control just as much as quiet passages under sail. Because the divide between sail and power has always been exaggerated dock-talk nonsense. At heart, it’s the same instinct: movement across water, mastery of conditions, and the satisfaction of arriving under your own command. Some readers come for the sails. Some come for the engines. Most appreciate both.

Perhaps the most important achievement of the first year wasn’t traffic numbers or article counts — it was tone. Old Sea Dogs never tried to be everything to everyone. It never chased clickbait or hollow outrage. It spoke to its readers, not at them. The comments, messages and shared stories reflected that. Readers didn’t just consume articles — they recognised themselves in them. They saw their own mistakes, ambitions, frustrations and triumphs mirrored back with honesty and humour. That sense of community — informal, opinionated, welcoming — is rare online. And it’s something Old Sea Dogs intends to protect fiercely.

Every first year afloat teaches lessons. That consistency matters more than perfection. That readers can spot authenticity instantly. That good stories take time. That the best pieces often start with a simple observation. That the sea always gives you more to write about than you have hours in the day. Most of all, the year reinforced why Old Sea Dogs exists at all: because boating deserves better storytelling. Not louder. Not flashier. Just truer.

As the calendar turns, Old Sea Dogs enters its second year with clearer purpose and broader horizons. More long-form features. Deeper event coverage. More marina and club profiles. More honest boat reviews. More global voices. More room for the kind of stories that don’t fit neatly into categories.
The ambition isn’t scale for its own sake — it’s depth. To become a place readers return to not because they have to, but because they want to.

And finally — because no proper logbook ends without gratitude. To every reader who clicked a link, shared a story, sent a message, or simply read quietly from afar: thank you. You are the reason this site exists. Wherever you are reading this — in a marina office, at home planning next season, on a night watch, or with a drink in hand remembering the last good sail — know that you are part of this story. From all of us at Old Sea Dogs, we wish you a wonderful Christmas and a happy, healthy New Year. May your anchors hold. May your weather windows open. May your charts be honest. And may the pub always be exactly where you left it. Here’s to another year of salt in the air, stories worth telling, and horizons worth chasing. — Old Sea Dogs

title: Unraveling the Mysteries of Isobars and Their Influence on the Sydney to Hobart Race
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unraveling the Mysteries of Isobars and Their Influence on the Sydney to Hobart Race
summary: Combine isobars' eloquent dance, that carves meteorological pathways, with sailing battles and a picnic perspective for an enticing read.
body: Picture this, you're on your way to a scenic picnic spot, possibly atop a gentle hill. The terrain's gradient subtly shifting under your feet as you ascend. Well, imagine these shifts, these gradients, now taking place in a two-dimensional scenario with our beloved yachting and sailing involved. The science behind it? Isobars.

Now the term 'isobars' might not commonly crop up in everyday conversations. You may ask, what's in a gradient-how does it affect the adrenaline-pumping Sydney to Hobart race? But for sailors who challenge the open seas, deciphering their dance is knowledge as crucial as the sails, the wind, and the sea. You see, topography uses contour lines to mark an area's elevation. The same can be applied theoretically for isobars that denote barometric pressure rather than physical height.

The Southern Hemisphere, where our Sydney to Hobart race takes place, introduces another dynamic actor to this meteorological play. Here, low-pressure systems whirl clockwise, growing in intensity the further south you venture, while high-pressure counterparts pirouette anticlockwise. Don't be mistaken; this atmospheric ballet has significant implications for our brave racers. Wind direction, sailing routes, even race strategy revolve around these subtle, barely perceptible pressure changes, turning meteorology into an indispensable compass when out on the ocean.

To sum up, the next time you get wind of a gradient or hear sailors talk about isobars, you'd appreciate how interwoven the art of sailing is with meteorological nuances. As the race from Sydney to Hobart unfolds, like mariners reading signs in the sky, you’d understand the invisible battle lines being drawn, the hidden pathways being tread. No doubt it adds depth to the joy we get from the nail-biting race, making the sailing adventure a bit more personal, a bit more thrilling.

title: The Rolex Sydney Hobart Yacht Race: An Epic Sea Battle Among the Supermaxis
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Rolex Sydney Hobart Yacht Race: An Epic Sea Battle Among the Supermaxis
summary: In the world of competitive sailing, the Rolex Sydney Hobart stands apart, bringing together multimillion-dollar yachts and the who's who of sailing.
body: In the exciting world of yacht racing, the Rolex Sydney Hobart race unfailingly serves a treat. A sparkling mix of aggressive competitiveness and a warm familiarity characterize the atmosphere among the elite fleet, home to world-class sailors and their yachts worth many millions. But, amidst the light-hearted jokes and banter, there's a unanimous understanding that unadulterated horsepower alone won't decide this year's winner. An unpredictable forecast can turn the table anytime, making the race all the more tactically challenging.

Two-time champ Christian Beck, with his yacht LawConnect, has surprised many with his persisting dominance, often defying odds against more formidable rivals. Beck admits with a chuckle, drawing both mirth and surprise, that his yacht is 'worse in every way' than its competitors.

Contrary to Beck's 'underdog' projections, Matt Allen, co-skipper of Master Lock Comanche, asserts their competitor's strength in upwind situations and lighter conditions. Beck's modest representations may well be a strategic move—after all, the best battles are unpredictable.

Another force to reckon with is the 88-foot powerhouse from the USA, Lucky. Even among spectator vessels, Lucky stands apart, impressing all with its quick deployment of a new North Sails A2 as it rushes past the iconic Bondi Beach. The sheer quickness and resulting acceleration of the crew posit them as a tough competitor in the upcoming race across Storm Bay. Indeed, the Rolex Sydney Hobart race promises a thrilling, nail-biting experience, affirming why it's such a spectacle in the world of sailing.

title: When the Titans Collide on Waves: Supermaxi Yachts Battle in the Rolex Sydney Hobart Race
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: When the Titans Collide on Waves: Supermaxi Yachts Battle in the Rolex Sydney Hobart Race
summary: In the world of high-stake yacht racing, the Rolex Sydney Hobart proves yet again to be a blend of old mate camaraderie and fierce rivalry.
body: The waves of the Rolex Sydney Hobart Race have seen the mighty collision of multimillion-dollar yachts and world-class sailors. The atmosphere is a remarkable blend of fierce competitive spirit and warm camaraderie between old-mate rivals. Below the surface of laid-back jests and light deprecations, however, lies a common understanding that this year's race might not just be a show of brute force. Instead, an unsettled, uneven, and highly tactical weather forecast might play the role of the true adjudicator.

Among the stellar competitors is the two-time defending champion, Christian Beck, who has astonishingly managed to triumph in recent races aboard LawConnect. Light-heartedly referring to it as a ‘s***box’, Beck's vessel has remarkably outperformed far superior yachts, despite his claim that it's 'worse in every way' compared to the notable rival, Master Lock Comanche.

This perspective is politely refuted by Master Lock Comanche co-skipper, Matt Allen, who suggests that Beck's modest proclamation is as much a tactical move as it is entertaining. Allen reminds that LawConnect is powerful upwind and may even perform better than Comanche in lighter stuff later in the race. The tension and excitement of this matchup set the stage for an electrifying competition in the waters of Sydney Hobart.

The battle Superyacht likewise extends to the awe-inspiring 88-foot American vessel, Lucky. With its impressive new North Sails A2, it managed to catapult into the third place at the outer turning mark. The success of these underdogs continues to thrill the spectators and keeps everyone guessing about the unpredictable nature of high-sea racing.

title: A New Era for Superyacht Sustainability: Leah Werner to Helm Water Revolution Foundation
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A New Era for Superyacht Sustainability: Leah Werner to Helm Water Revolution Foundation
summary: Leah Werner, an expert in environmental science and policy implementation, is slated to become the new executive director of the Water Revolution Foundation, effective from 1st January 2026.
body: The maritime world is set for a shot in the arm as Leah Werner steps up to the plate as the new executive director of the Water Revolution Foundation, effective from 1st January 2026. The foundation, a non-profit organisation squarely centered on fostering sustainable evolution within the superyacht industry, has given a nod to Werner's 13-year-old leadership history brimming with environmental science expertise, policy implementation, and a brilliant understanding of biological oceanography.

It's clear that Werner's robust ability to bridge the gap between complex scientific concepts and non-technical audiences will be harnessed to its maximum potential. Industry decision-makers and stakeholders alike stand to benefit from her unique ability to translate and repackage complex ideas into palatable directives, a skill that will be quintessential to the foundation's mission. Certainly, her appointment is expected to prompt fresh opportunities for the foundation's programme, sparking a trajectory of growth in reach and impact.

Werner's appointment follows a recent shakeup in the foundation's ranks, specifically the appointment of Aino Grapin as board chair, succeeding Henk de Vries. It's a time of change for the foundation, but with change comes revitalisation and the promise of a sustainable future for the superyacht industry.

title: Luxury Motor Yacht Sarabeth Sold and Emerges with a New Identity: Bella Vita
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Luxury Motor Yacht Sarabeth Sold and Emerges with a New Identity: Bella Vita
summary: The 39.6-metre Westport motor yacht Sarabeth has transitioned into a new era, rechristened as Bella Vita.
body: From now on, the 39.6 metre Westport motor yacht formerly named Sarabeth will navigate the high seas under the new and vibrant identity of Bella Vita. Orchestrated by broker Mark Elliott of IYC, this transition symbolises a new era of luxury and adventure for the renowned vessel. Originally manufactured by the prestigious American yard, Sarabeth was part of the esteemed Westport 130 series, boasting a striking design courtesy of Gregory Marshall. The most recent refit came to a culmination in 2022, further enhancing the yacht's grandeur and appeal. The stunning interior of Bella Vita, the work of Westport's in-house team, caters to the highest standards of comfort and luxury. As per the last records, Bella Vita was sold for $15,995,000. The yacht offers lavish accommodation for up to ten guests across five exquisite cabins. This includes a main deck king-sized master cabin, two VIP king-sized doubles, and two twin cabins situated on the lower deck. In addition, the yacht houses living quarters for a seven-member crew. Bella Vita also houses a commodious open-plan saloon and dining area, further complemented by a skylounge on the boat deck. The broker, heralding the yacht's many virtues, describes her as a stunning epitome of a classic Westport model laden with luxurious amenities, snug features, and expansive exterior deck spaces. Adding to its allure, Bella Vita's expansive aft deck houses a full-service bar and lounge seating, while the foredeck introduces additional seating areas poised on its teak decks. The yacht's flybridge sports a Jacuzzi, further seating options, and an open-air dining area. Bella Vita, with her overbearing 333GT, runs on twin 2,896hp MTU diesel engines. These engines empower her to cover a range of 3,000 nautical miles. With top-notch Naiad at-anchor stabilisers installed for enhanced comfort, Bella Vita cruises effortlessly at 20 knots and can reach top speeds of up to 23 knots. Housing an affluence of luxurious offerings, Bella Vita truly champions the ethos of sea-based escapades and high-end luxury living.

title: Step Aboard Sea La Vie: The Newly Renamed 30-metre Sunseeker Alina Is Ready to Soar the Seas
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Step Aboard Sea La Vie: The Newly Renamed 30-metre Sunseeker Alina Is Ready to Soar the Seas
summary: The magnificent 30-metre Sunseeker motor yacht, formerly known as Alina, starts a fresh chapter under the new name, 'Sea La Vie'.
body: The transformative journey of the elegantly built 30m Sunseeker motor yacht Alina offers an inspiring tale. Now sailing under her new name, Sea La Vie, this grandiose monument to seaworthiness is ready to etch memorable tales on the canvases of the sea. The deal was facilitated by Harry Bristow-Holmes of Bristow Holmes, representing the seller and Orieta Saraci of Est Yachting & Services, introducing the fortunate buyer. This magnificent vessel was immaculately conceived by the British yard with a design by Don Shead, and she took her maiden voyage in 2011. Boasting only two prior owners, Sea La Vie captures the imagination with her resplendent gloss black American walnut cabinetry. With five cabins, including a split-level master suite, two VIP suites, and twin rooms, she comfortably sleeps up to 12 guests. Each cabin offers entertainment centres, Samsung television screens and en suite bathrooms, vowing to keep luxury a constant companion of its guests. Embracing the allure of an open-plan concept, the living area and dining place form a seamless spectrum, basking in the warmth of convivial moments. The large gallery upfront pledges culinary delights with the option of a dedicated chef onboard. The flybridge, encapsulating the breathtaking undefined sea views, hosts flexible sunbathing lounges and dining spaces flanked by canopies offering an ambience perfect for any occasion. Adorned with twin MTU 16V 2000 M94 diesel engines, she cruises at a sprightly 22 knots, accelerating up to 29 knots at full throttle. Her previously known asking price was €2,999,500. Currently based in the vibrant South of France, Sea La Vie is not just a yacht, she is a testament to the joys and exhilarating experiences that life at sea can offer.

title: The Nautical World Witnesses a New Wave: Honouring the Pioneering 49er and 49erFX Rookie Teams of 2025
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Nautical World Witnesses a New Wave: Honouring the Pioneering 49er and 49erFX Rookie Teams of 2025
summary: In the sailing world, some waves usher in more than just tides: they birth a new generation of seafarers, steering the ship of innovation towards uncharted territories.
body: The open sea. A wave of change. The 2025 sailing season heralded a new generation of elite sailors, cementing their position within the admiring gaze of the 49er class of the sailing fold. Out of all the fresh-faced rookies, the ones who steered the sail of undeniable talent and clasped the helm of tenacity were Ben O'Shaughnessy and Ethan Spain.

This dynamic Irish duo deftly manoeuvred their way from a celebrated journey in the 29er, conquering National and European Championship titles along the way, before transitioning commendably into the senior 49er fleet. They whisked up the sea spray as they breezed past seasoned Olympians, showcasing flair and agility with their front-of-the-fleet speed. Amassing multiple top-three finishes, they crowned their progress with a resounding victory at the World Championship's Qualifying round in Cagliari, an achievement defying the depths of talents in the fleet.

On par with their progressive strides in the senior fleet, Ben & Ethan also laid claim to the Junior 49er European Championship title in Sferracavallo, Italy, underlining their dominance and showing the sailing world that they indeed were a force to reckon with.

The Hamm twins also garnered much attention in the sailing scene. Their impressive journey from the 49erFX to the 49er, punctuated by their win in the 29er European Title, demonstrates the enormous potential they have in the competitive sailing scene. Despite not having contested at a major 49er championship yet, they have already etched their burgeoning talent in the hearts and minds of sailing enthusiasts worldwide. As we hoist our sails and set our rudder towards the future, it's clear these new teams have marked their coordinates on the competitive sailing map, propelling the sport into a new era of intensity and innovation.

title: Embrace the Joys of Exploring Cornwall’s Secluded Harbours and Laurelled Waterbodies, on a maiden family cruise journey.
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Embrace the Joys of Exploring Cornwall’s Secluded Harbours and Laurelled Waterbodies, on a maiden family cruise journey.
summary: Experience the vivid saga of a family's adventurer spirit as they traverse Cornwall's concealed harbours on their new cruiser, post-weathering storm Betty.
body: The glorious end of October marked the arrival of the much awaited Iolar, the new family cruiser, coinciding with the last wisp of summer. Prior to its legal possession, two breathtaking weekends were joyously spent in sea trials on the enchanting coast of Pembrokeshire. These trials exemplified the interesting process of the handover by Dale, accompanied by 'rough-water tuition' from the illustrious Mike Reynolds. Resultantly, the winters and springs were a seesaw of short scale trips in the thrilling anticipation of a long tour.

Next on the agenda was the intricate task of topping up the fuel tanks in Falmouth. This posed as an important aspect of speccing the cruiser. Fueling up rode on largely diesel, contributing to generators and heating. Every other facet relied on electricity such as induction hob, electric oven and two fridges. The added lithium-ion batteries significant enough to run the boat silently for days, charging at the move or through generator. This maiden exploration was finely balanced with seasons of calm and storm, hobbies of sea explorations and experiences of onboard life, summing up into a delightful, adventurous sea journey.

title: Unparalleled Quality Meets Discretion in the Luxurious Motor Yacht 'KAISER', Now For Sale
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unparalleled Quality Meets Discretion in the Luxurious Motor Yacht 'KAISER', Now For Sale
summary: Rare opportunity to acquire the prestigious motor yacht 'KAISER', a symbol of Northern European pedigree, now on sale for the first time by the original owner.
body: Marking a remarkable inflection point in the world of maritime luxury, the magnificent 'KAISER' is a 60 metre, 196 foot motor yacht presented to the market for the first time by its original owner. This is a singular opportunity to own a yacht of unmatched excellence and timeless appeal, constructed by the renowned Northern European shipyard, Abeking & Rasmussen. The 'KAISER', having complimentary exterior features designed by Donald Starkey and a bespoke interior by Bannenberg & Rowell, was delivered in 2011.

Boasting a transatlantic range of 4,500 nautical miles at 14 knots, 'KAISER' adheres to Lloyd’s Commercial Class, LY2, and Cayman Flag standards. It mixes comfort with style, housing 12 guests in 6 plush staterooms. The Owner’s suite, found on the main deck, offers private lounging space, his-and-hers ensuites, and expansive views of the sapphire expanse. Four guest staterooms on the lower deck include a versatile full-beam VIP.

The main salon fluent merges into the formal dining beneath sculptural lighting. The sky lounge presents an intimate retreat for serene nights of cinema or relaxed sundowners. The yacht's smartly designed deck layout offers walkaround access and various lounging sections, with the sundeck and upper decks crafted for effortless outdoor living.

Tender storage, both discreet and broad, houses a complete set of aqua toys and support craft. Having been used privately for only one season since delivery, the 'KAISER' is in peerless condition, making it an exceptional value in terms of gross ton for a yacht of its magnitude, specs, and pedigree. Its quiet elegance is perfect for those who prefer discretion over display; the 'KAISER' is a collector’s yacht in every essence.

title: Italy Makes History at Inaugural EurILCA
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: EurILCA Team Racing European Champions in Athens
summary: The first chapter in European ILCA team racing history has been written — and it belongs to Italy. After a long, tactical and at times nerve-shredding final day on the water in Athens, Italy emerged as the inaugural EurILCA Team Racing European Champions, lifting the title at the close of the 2025 EurILCA Team Racing Championship. In doing so, they etched their names into the record books as the very first nation to
body: Racing got underway early, with the first start firing at 08:00, as sailors faced a classic Mediterranean test: light, patchy and highly variable winds, fluctuating between just 1 and 7 knots throughout the day. These were conditions that rewarded patience, communication and flawless teamwork — the very foundations of successful team racing.

With breeze lines constantly shifting across the course, every tack, mark trap and positioning decision carried extra weight. It was a day where mental sharpness mattered just as much as boat speed, and where teams had to adapt on the fly to survive.

The morning session was devoted to completing the round-robin qualification, gradually separating the contenders from the rest of the fleet. As the final results were tallied, four nations rose to the top and secured their places in the knockout stages:
Italy
Greece
Sweden 1
Sweden 2
With qualification complete, the fleet returned ashore while the Race Committee crunched the numbers — tension building as teams waited to learn their semifinal match-ups.

The first semifinal saw Italy take on Sweden 2 in a closely fought encounter that demanded precision and discipline. Italy executed their race plan with authority, controlling key moments and denying Sweden 2 the opportunity to break through, earning their place in the final.

The second semifinal delivered another gripping contest as Sweden 1 faced Greece. In a match defined by smart positioning and calm decision-making under pressure, Greece emerged victorious, booking their place in the championship decider.
Meanwhile, the third-place playoff provided its own drama, with Sweden 2 defeating Sweden 1 to secure the bronze medals.

The grand final brought together Italy and Greece, two teams that had shown consistency, adaptability and resilience throughout the regatta. With the first-ever EurILCA Team Racing European Championship title on the line, the racing tightened even further.

In another tactical battle shaped by light airs and strategic control, Italy held their nerve. Through disciplined teamwork and sharp execution at critical moments, they edged ahead and closed out the race — sealing a historic victory and becoming Europe’s first ILCA Team Racing champions.
Italy – Inaugural Champions
Greece
Sweden 2
4th – Sweden 1
Italy’s historic victory was delivered by a well-balanced and composed team:
Alberto Avanzini
Enrico Morina
Sofia Berteotti
Martina Corno
Their blend of tactical awareness, communication and calm under pressure proved decisive across the final stages.
The Greek team, who pushed Italy all the way in the final, consisted of:
Stefanos Samaras
Michail Akalestos
Fragkiski Kosma
Eleni Alchanati
Adele Ramm-Ericson
Oskar Annwall
Oskar Wetter
Lova Leringe

Beyond the medals and trophies, the 2025 EurILCA Team Racing Championship marked a significant milestone for European sailing. The event showcased the growing appetite for team racing within the ILCA class — a format that places equal emphasis on tactical intelligence, teamwork and adaptability.
Athens provided a fitting backdrop for this historic debut, delivering conditions that demanded the very best from sailors and race officials alike.

With the bar now set, EurILCA has confirmed that the EurILCA Team Racing European Championship will return in 2026, and all European nations are invited to take part. After a compelling inaugural edition, expectations are already high for an even bigger, more competitive fleet next year.
If this first championship is anything to go by, ILCA team racing in Europe has a very bright future indeed.

title: Ocean Independence Becomes New Central Agency for the Sale of the Magnificent 53m Oceanfast Motor Yacht Mizu
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Ocean Independence Becomes New Central Agency for the Sale of the Magnificent 53m Oceanfast Motor Yacht Mizu
summary: The splendid 53-metre Oceanfast motor yacht Mizu, now sails under a new central agency and is listed for sale by Ocean Independence.
body: Splendidly taking to the waters, the 53-metre Oceanfast motor yacht Mizu has changed her course towards a new central agency. Now gracefully listed for sale with Ocean Independence, she waits to embark on a new voyage with a passionate navigator. From the Land Down Under, Mizu was presented to the world in 2004 by Australian yard Oceanfast. The team chose 'Mizu', the Japanese word for water, articulating her elemental purpose. The genius behind her military-inspired design is Sam Sorgiovanni, who brought a unique structural integrity to this luxurious yacht. Austal Ship Design, the renowned Australian ship design company, was responsible for the naval architecture of Mizu. What makes Mizu extraordinary is her adaptive transformation. Originally birthed into the world as an Austal frigate, she underwent significant modifications by the Australian team, evolving into a true ocean-going vessel. With her asking price set at €11,400,000, the aluminium yacht has rejuvenated twice in her cruise through time — once in 2016 and again in 2023. Her recent refurbishments in 2024 featured the addition of zero-speed stabilisers, enhancing her stability and maximising the comfort of her esteemed guests. Designed in rich woods, the internal realm of Mizu mesmerises with its contemporary design. With the capacity to house a party of 10 in her five cabins, her owner can look forward to a dedicated deck featuring large picture-frame windows. In addition, Mizu provides separate accommodations for a fabulous crew of 10. The sundeck flaunts a luxurious 10-person Jacuzzi and bar, and a magnificent home theatre on the upper deck making her an epitome of entertainment. Her main deck aft further provides plenty of space for lounging and storing tenders or toys. Packed with twin MTU 3750hp diesel engines, Mizu can reach top speeds of 30 knots and cruises smoothly at 25 knots. With her transoceanic range, she can cross the vast expanses of both Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, with an impressive coverage of 5,300 nautical miles. Currently stationed in Athens, Greece, Mizu is ready to touch the farthest horizons of seas for a price of €11,400,000.

title: The 31.6-Metre Classic Motor Yacht, Sounion II, Swaps Hands in a Central Agency Shift
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The 31.6-Metre Classic Motor Yacht, Sounion II, Swaps Hands in a Central Agency Shift
summary: The Benetti motor yacht, Sounion II, has undergone a significant change in agency, now falling under the remit of Michel Chryssicopoulos at IYC.
body: A stunning embodiment of seafaring elegance, the 31.6-meter Sounion II has recently seen a fundamental change in its central agency. The motor yacht, known for its classic design sensibilities, is now listed under the aegis of the renowned Michel Chryssicopoulos at IYC. Constructed by Benetti in the pivotal year of 1969, the yacht boasts a sturdy amalgamation of steel and aluminium in its construction. Sounion II has been the subject of extensive refits in recent years, now featuring the stylings of the illustrious interior designer Anouska Hempel, who has instilled the vessel with a subtle Asian aesthetic.

A crew of six can feasibly be housed on the Sounion II, with quarters allocated specifically for this purpose. The yacht's three decks are testament to adept space optimisation. Here, the saloon leads through to a longitudinal dining area featuring two rectangular tables which can merge to form a single extended dining surface.

Sounion II further possesses an al fresco dining option at the aft of its saloon, neatly shaded by the overhanging sundeck. With a comfortable seating area also located in the canoe stern, the yacht is perfect for casual cocktail parties or simply savouring the pleasure of being at sea. Stylistically, the yacht successfully marries atemporal charm with modern amenities. The ingenuity behind its design is a testament to the allure of the modern superyacht lifestyle.

The engine configuration is impressive, powered by a duo of refurbished 750hp Volvo diesels. Sounion II can achieve a cruising speed of 11.5 knots, topping out at a maximum speed of 13 knots. With substantial fuel capacity, the yacht boasts a range of 2,900 nautical miles at a consistent cruising speed of 11 knots. The Sounion II embodies a bygone era of seafaring glamour, taking its place as one of the most delightful classic yachts currently up for sale. It is currently berthed in Athens, Greece, calling prospective new owners to experience the thrill of life on the water.

title: Scaling Mountaneous Challenges: Francesca Clapcich Charts Her Course Towards a Transformational 2025
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Scaling Mountaneous Challenges: Francesca Clapcich Charts Her Course Towards a Transformational 2025
summary: Get a unique glance into the life of sailing prodigy Francesca Clapcich as she uncovers her 2025 vision, sculpted by experiences and introspection.
body: Francesca Clapcich, a renowned sailor and star of the racing world, reflects upon her journey and future at the upcoming conclusion of the year. She offers not the numbers of her sailing stats or performance KPIs, but rather an open letter to inspire and encourage introspection.

Clapcich, who authored the reflection hours after the wrap-up of her first Mer Montagne Trophy, experienced an epiphany during a ski tour at a height of 3,000m. Amid the fatigue and the lack of abundant oxygen, she realised the significance of breathing, metaphorically and literally, and delving deeper into personal fears and emotions.

Looking further ahead, Clapcich figured that the subsequent year, 2026, would be the Year of the Horse, a year of energy, ambition, and momentum. She perceived the Lunar horse as a confident and expressive symbol that advocates for quick action over analysis. Indeed, these Horse years were seen as opportunities to bring to life the ideas nurtured during the introspective Snake years.
Francesca Clapcich offers us a unique lesson in time management and self-growth, her sailing journey acting as a portal to understanding the course of personal and professional progression.

title: Horizon Yachts Launches Fourteenth Hull of FD100 Series, Marrying Sophistication and Utility in the Sailing World
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Horizon Yachts Launches Fourteenth Hull of FD100 Series, Marrying Sophistication and Utility in the Sailing World
summary: Horizon Yachts, the renowned Taiwanese shipyard, has unveiled Hull 14 of its esteemed FD100 Tri-Deck motor yacht series - a hallmark of high-volume interiors and modern style.
body: "Sailing in luxury" takes on a whole new meaning with the latest release from Taiwanese shipyard Horizon Yachts. The company has launched the fourteenth hull from its eminent series - the Fast Displacement FD100 Tri-Deck yacht. Renowned for high-volume interiors wrapped in a cultivated style, the fourteenth addition to this lauded line is sure to stun the most discerning seafarer.

Conceived by Cor D. Rover, the FD100 line presents a model that boasts full-height windows that flood the yacht with natural light, generous deck areas for open-air lounging and a blend of natural dyed oak and Mikado Calacatta Fantasy quartz detailing. The hull is readily available for those in the US market, searching for an ultimate sailing experience with panache.

The yacht's cabin layout - consisting of a full-beam master suite, four en-suite cabins, and accommodations for a crew of five - is versatile, comfortable, and meticulously designed. Complementing the plethora of amenities is the yacht’s power from twin Caterpillar C32A engines offering a smooth and swift ride.

This elaborately designed masterpiece features an enclosed skylounge introduced as a 'private, climate-controlled retreat'. Coupled with a bar, convenient wet storage, and a rain shower, it culminates in a hybrid beach club experience, redefining the very essence of luxury sailing. The distinct craftsmanship, meticulous engineering, and sheer opulence, Horizon Yachts' latest FD100 release is setting a new standard in the maritime industry."

title: Step Aboard the Belt-and-Braces Luxury Experience of the 40m Trident Yacht ‘Package Deal’
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Step Aboard the Belt-and-Braces Luxury Experience of the 40m Trident Yacht ‘Package Deal’
summary: Recently added to the yacht market, discover high-seas luxury epitomised aboard the 40.2 metre Trident Yacht, Package Deal.
body: Listing recently for sale with Mark Elliott of IYC, the 40.2-metre Trident motor yacht ‘Package Deal’ carries an allure of crystalised seaworthiness; a testament to American craftsmanship. Delivered in 1999 and refurbished in 2023, she's a seasoned veteran of the seas, boasting a GRP design conceived by the creative mind of Wesley Carr.

Major selling points of ‘Package Deal’ derive from its unparalleled outdoor spaces – nautical playgrounds awash with striking features. The sundeck metamorphoses into a ‘resort-style’ spectacle, complete with a Jacuzzi, well-stocked bar, sunpads, and accommodate large umbrellas - essentials for basking in the panorama-abundant sunshine.

This majestic sea-farer embraces the al fresco life; her layout includes two outdoor dining setups. The main deck, at the aft, can transform into an all-weather space with full enclosure, while the bridge deck aft offers the privilege of shadow-play with an optional awning.

Boasting an internal volume of 383 Gross Tons, ‘Package Deal’ illustrates an ideal charter layout. Its main saloon, bathed in natural light, is a civic space with ample sofa seating teamed with a marble centre table. Forward, a dedicated dining area waits in anticipation for feasts and fêtes.

A crowning feature of the yacht is a fitness suite skilletted into the skylounge, a rare yet fitting amenity in a yacht of this calibre. This dual-purpose space houses an assortment of equipment, including a Peloton, treadmill, and rowing machine, while also functioning as a sophisticated lounge.

‘Package Deal’ can host up to 11 guests across her five well-appointed staterooms. The master suite stretching the full 8.7-metre beam on the main deck, featuring a decadent his-and-hers bathroom with Jacuzzi and large shower. Below deck, an additional four cabins push the envelope of comfort and luxury.

The yacht’s power originates from dual 720hp Caterpillar 3412-DITA diesel engines. She can cut through waves at a top speed of 12 knots, cruising serenely at 10 knots. Her 2.1-metre draught gives her friendly clearance for Bahamas cruising, casting the net wide for her future explorations.

title: Second Unit from the Mangusta GranSport 34 Series Snapped Up by Experienced Turkish Buyer
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Second Unit from the Mangusta GranSport 34 Series Snapped Up by Experienced Turkish Buyer
summary: Italian shipyard Mangusta Yachts announces the sale of another unit of their luxurious GranSport 34 model, acquired by an experienced Turkish owner.
body: The high seas are set to welcome another luxurious gem as Italian shipyard, Mangusta Yachts, a prestigious brand of the Overmarine Group, confirms the sale of the second unit of the Mangusta GranSport 34 series. The buzz around the latest in mangusta luxury resonates far and wide, reaching the shores of Turkey, where an experienced yacht owner has eagerly claimed the sophisticated vessel.

Expected to land in its new owner's arms in 2026, the sale was skillfully facilitated by BTWO Marine. The 33.9-metre yacht stands tall in the alignment of the brand's smaller, albeit successful Mangusta GranSport 33 series. Drawing from the success of its predecessor, the GranSport 34 raises the stakes with improved performance and a meticulously fine-tuned design, courtesy of Overmarine's Engineering Department and Monaco-based designer, Alberto Mancini.

BTWO Marine's Omer Balkan, the Mangusta sales representative for Turkey, reflected on the sale of the second Mangusta GranSport 34 as a testament to the yacht's value combining fast-displacement performance, refined comfort, and timeless beauty. Nicolò Strocco, Mangusta sales manager, voiced that the sale indicates the value and demand of the GranSport 34 in the Turkish market and the yachting industry at large.

Keeping up with the ripe appetite for luxury yachting, the motorized beauty is powered by four Volvo Penta 1,000hp engines and an IPS pod system, engineered to ensure easy manoeuvrability while efficiently reducing consumption, vibrations and noise. This sleek sea whisperer is expected to reach maximum speeds of 24 knots. The shipyard celebrated the sale of its first in-build unit earlier this year. As reported by BOATPro, Overmarine Group currently has 24 yachts under construction or on order.

title: Ferretti 800 Flybridge: The Majestic Finale of Ferretti's Renewal Process Initiated in 2018
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Ferretti 800 Flybridge: The Majestic Finale of Ferretti's Renewal Process Initiated in 2018
summary: The Ferretti Group leaves a striking imprint with the Ferretti 800 flybridge, the last chapter in a range renewal process started in 2018.
body: The Ferretti Group has succeeded in leaving a lasting impression with a series of launches stretching across the year, but it is the Ferretti 800 Flybridge that stands as the crown jewel, completing their range renewal process set in motion back in 2018.

The design of the 800 Flybridge is a tribute to the fine craftsmanship of naval architect Filippo Salvetti; bringing a fresh, sophisticated edge to Ferretti's characteristic stateliness. The yacht exhibits larger hull windows, glossy black stanchions, glazed flybridge supports and a glass cockpit transom, all attributing to its striking impression.

Undergirding their reputation for sound engineering and solid build quality, Ferretti accommodates impressively powerful MAN engines on straight shafts. Wrapping it all up, the Ferretti 800 encompasses these deluxe features within an efficiently organized, well-lit space. Despite not deviating significantly from its predecessors, the Ferretti 800 outshines them, excelling in every feature with grandeur.
After a refreshing journey since 2018, the arrival of the Ferretti 800 signifies the completion of an era, marking its existence as a seaworthy symphony of innovation and elegance.

title: The Accused Enginner Pleads Not Guilty: A Tragic Murder Aboard a Superyacht Ignites Conversations About Crew Safety
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Accused Enginner Pleads Not Guilty: A Tragic Murder Aboard a Superyacht Ignites Conversations About Crew Safety
summary: The tragic murder of a crew member aboard a superyacht has spurred a widespread conversation about crew safety in the yachting sector.
body: Docked at Harbour Island in the Bahamas, the 43.3-metre Far From It Richmond superyacht was unexpectedly thrust in the spotlight when its crew member was tragically murdered in July. The accused engineer found at the crime scene has recently pleaded not guilty in front of the Supreme Court of the Bahamas, which instantly rippled through the yachting industry and incited a fervent debate about the safety of those working on these luxurious vessels.

Brigido Munoz, the 39-year-old accused engineer was discovered alongside the body of 20-year-old South African stewardess, Paige Bell, igniting an industry-wide discourse on the need to prioritize the wellbeing of crew members. In the aftermath of the incident, the industry rallied together to support Paige Bell's family, raising a collective voice for the safekeeping of the males and females who dedicate their lives to the smooth operation of mega-vessels.
This incident has generated calls for more rigorous background checks for all crew members, which would inevitably assist in preventing such tragic incidents in the future.

Beyond the mourning and justice-seeking, a group from within the yachting community launched an initiative dubbed 'Protecting Crew Lives (PCL)'. This initiative is set to propagate a set of guidelines for the yachting industry ensuring transparency, safeguarding, and responsible engagement throughout the sector. The initiative aspires to make the care, safety, and ultimate wellbeing of the crew paramount over all else.

While the case is set to proceed, the yachting industry reflects soberly, rallying behind promises of better safety regulations and practices. A tragedy that serves as a vivid reminder of the importance of crew safety above all else; the waves of change are surely coming.

title: Turkish Shipyard AKYACHT Starts Construction on its Largest Superyacht Ever to Be Built on Turkish Soil
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Turkish Shipyard AKYACHT Starts Construction on its Largest Superyacht Ever to Be Built on Turkish Soil
summary: AKYACHT, a renowned Turkish shipyard, has commenced construction on a sprawling 125 to 130-metre superyacht, a first of its kind for the country.
body: AKYACHT, a leading Turkish shipyard has launched work on NB012, an innovative superyacht reaching from 125 to 130 metres. This project reflects a notable moment in the shipyard's history, as it signifies not only the most ambitious endeavour AKYACHT has undertaken but also the largest superyacht ever to be cultivated on Turkish soil. The highly anticipated delivery is set for 2030. This magnificently mammoth superyacht's beauty is matched only by the grandeur of its design team. Experienced designer Espen Øino is guiding the exterior design, whilst the interior design is championed by Sinot Yacht Architecture and Design and the naval architecture by Azure Yacht Design and Naval Architecture. Dölker + Voges, a Hamburg-based studio is responsible for the interior design of the crew areas. The NB012 project, first introduced in 2023, is being constructed from steel and aluminium. It promises to intermingle 'uncompromised luxury, technology, engineering and propulsion' as per the shipyard's assurance. The new superyacht’s gross tonnage is expected to weigh in the region of 8,000 to 10,000GT. NB012 is being assembled at AKYACHT’s recently standing locations in the Kocaeli Free Trade Zone. This upgraded workspace offers a footprint of over 100,000 square meters, suggesting AKYACHT as one of Turkey's most ambitious yacht constructors. Once completed, NB012 will pedestal past the current flagship, the 85-metre Victorious and will fully eclipse the existing largest Turkish superyacht, the 88-metre sailing yacht, Maltese Falcon.

title: Finnish Shipyard Baltic Yachts Makes Waves with Their Latest Sale: The First Unit of the Baltic 80 Café Racer Sailing Yacht Series
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Finnish Shipyard Baltic Yachts Makes Waves with Their Latest Sale: The First Unit of the Baltic 80 Café Racer Sailing Yacht Series
summary: The Finnish shipyard, Baltic Yachts, has broken new ground with the sale of its first unit in the Baltic 80 Café Racer sailing yacht series.
body: Responding to the ever-increasing market demand for high performance, lifestyle-centric sailing yachts, Baltic Yachts, a leading Finnish shipyard, has stepped up the game with their latest offering: The Baltic 80 Café Racer. In a significant development, the company has announced the sale of the first unit from this exemplary series, with construction set to kick off in April 2026 and delivery expected in June 2027.

The Café Racer name harks back to the 1960s London culture, where aesthetically minimalist motorbikes were fashioned for speed, attitude, and rebellion. The Baltic 80 Café Racer integrates this spirit in its very soul – projecting confidence, focus, and distinct uniqueness.

Further details on this exceptional yacht, which is elegantly penned to be enjoyable to sail, quick to set-up and easy to handle even by a small crew, are expected to be revealed sometime in the new year. Baltic Yachts, according to BOATPro, currently has two yachts under construction, one of which is a 37-metre custom cruising sloop anticipated for delivery next year.

title: Sunseeker’s 29m Motor Yacht Timeless C, a Masterpiece Built with a blend of Luxury and Power, Now Available for Sale
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Sunseeker’s 29m Motor Yacht Timeless C, a Masterpiece Built with a blend of Luxury and Power, Now Available for Sale
summary: The brokerage market welcomes a new star - the Sunseeker motor yacht Timeless C, a masterpiece for luxury sailing enthusiasts.
body: Built in 2002 with chic exterior designs by Don Shead and elegant interiors by Ken Freivokh Design, the 29-meter Sunseeker's Timeless C is a yacht that comfortably blurs the line between sports dynamism and luxury cruising. With its naval architecture seamlessly woven into the grand design, it is no wonder that this diamond, which sails under a UAE flag, is in impeccable mechanical shape.

Recently emerging from an extended maintenance stint in 2024, this yacht is more than ready to woo prospective buyers with its smooth performance and well-documented maintenance history. It holds elegant accommodation for eight guests across four stylish staterooms along with separate quarters for up to three crew members, the Timeless C is an embodiment of luxury for those who live to sail.

This handsome yacht operates from Dubai, set at a pretty price of $1,250,000. The price also includes a tender packaged within. Let the spirit of the Timeless C guide you to the best yacht purchase decision you could ever make.

title: An Ocean Titan Acquired: The Understated Elegance of the 44m CMN Motor Yacht De-De Unveiled
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: An Ocean Titan Acquired: The Understated Elegance of the 44m CMN Motor Yacht De-De Unveiled
summary: The exclusive 44-metre CMN motor yacht De-De, with its French elegance and sea-faring prowess, has a new owner to navigate the oceans.
body: Welcome to the most exclusive club on the seven seas. The 44-meter CMN superyacht De-De is now proudly owned by a new sea captain. The deal was brokered by Adam Levine of IYC representing the seller and Joao Kossmann of BYS International introducing the lucky buyer. This isn't just any yacht but a floating masterpiece designed by Stirling Design International and crafted with precision by the renowned French yard in 2002.

In 2020, De-De underwent a significant transformation, completely reinventing its look and feel. She received a multimillion-euro refit including a brand-new hull paint job, bringing new life to the yacht's exterior. Inside, guests will notice fresh carpets throughout, and those working behind the scenes will appreciate the upgraded crew areas. The majority of her technical systems were given an overhaul or service, enhancing her performance and longevity. All this for a last-known asking price of $7,990,000.

The common areas are equally impressive: the formal dining area adjacent to the main saloon seats 10, while the aft and upper decks are perfect for hosting larger parties. Fitted with potent 1,200hp Caterpillar engines, De-De offers a cruising speed of 12 knots and a range of 4,000 nautical miles at a relaxed pace of 11 knots. With Quantum zero-speed stabilisers also fitted, her promise of a smooth voyage is undoubted. So here's to the De-De—a testament to 21st-century design and seafaring elegance.
