title: Flying Fifteen's - Recounting Championships and Looking Forward to an Exciting 2026 Season
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Flying Fifteen's - Recounting Championships and Looking Forward to an Exciting 2026 Season
summary: Celebrating the triumphs of the Flying Fifteen season in 2025 while eagerly anticipating the events of 2026.
body: The 2025 UK Flying Fifteen season offered a thrilling spectacle for sailing enthusiasts, with boats duelling for victory across variable conditions. The season was characterised by laser-thin finish lines at all five major events, further intensifying the passion and competitiveness of this thrilling racing series. Overall, a fleet of 104 boats took part in at least one championship event, including a sturdy National Championship fleet with 65 participating boats.

This year’s victors deserve heartfelt applause, with Ben McGrane securing two major titles at the Inland Championship and National Championships. Elsewhere, Steve Goacher, a former world champion, won the Northern Championship held at Windermere. Meanwhile, the Southern Championship was claimed by racing sleuth Greg Wells at Hayling Island, and Mike Preston dominated the Scottish Championship at Loch Tummel.

The UK Flying Fifteen community has every reason to be buoyant, looking onwards to an exciting 2026! The upcoming season promises an enthralling journey through a variety of competitions, with the championship season curtain falling at the Europeans in Mallorca. We bank on the thrill as yet another year of spectacular racing draws closer. Let the winds fill in, and let the best mariner conquer the waves!

title: World Premiere of Riveting Yacht Race Documentary 'True South' Graces Sydney's Westpac OpenAir Cinema
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: World Premiere of Riveting Yacht Race Documentary 'True South' Graces Sydney's Westpac OpenAir Cinema
summary: The riveting documentary 'True South' garners attention as it commemorates 80 years of the Sydney to Hobart Yacht Race, premiering at the Westpac OpenAir Cinema in Sydney.
body: Marking the commencement of a new era in maritime storytelling, the momentous documentary 'True South' set its sails at the Westpac OpenAir Cinema in Sydney. The film vividly captures the roller coaster ride experienced by the participants of Sydney to Hobart Yacht Race over 80 years. An emotional testament to the resilience of Homo Sapiens, 'True South' not only superbly narrates an epic yacht race but unveils a deeply human story of grief, perseverance, and camaraderie. The film enters the canvas of the Winning and Dean families, whose roots intertwine, tested through rigorous and ruthless maritime challenges.

The documentary is the brainchild of Will Alexander, a childhood friend of the Winning and Dean families. His proximity and understanding of the families allowed him an unprecedented access, offering the film an unfiltered emotional authenticity.

'True South' is decidedly more than a sailing film. It's a timely tribute to familial resilience, bravery, and to the sailors whose voyage ended prematurely. Directed by Dave Klaiber and vocally carried by Sigrid Thornton AO with an evocative original score by Elena Kats-Chernin AO, 'True South' promises to leave a haunting echo in the chapters of the maritime history.

title: Magnificent 37m Posillipo Technema Yacht Reborn and Renamed – Discover Once More
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Magnificent 37m Posillipo Technema Yacht Reborn and Renamed – Discover Once More
summary: The notable Posillipo Technema motor yacht Peftasteri has undergone a significant change, taking on the refreshed moniker, Once More.
body: Every once in a while, a classic beauty emerges anew on the market, creating ripples in the yachting world. Such is the case with the 37m motor yacht formerly known as Peftasteri, which has recently been sold and rebranded with an exciting new name - Once More.

Brought into fruition with the extensive expertise of Michel Chryssicopoulos from the International Yacht Corporation who introduced the buyer, Once More radiates elegance, speed, and comfort. The Italian gem was originally built back in 2009, as part of the shipyard's Technema 120 series by Galeazzi Design. It features an exquisite GRP build and underwent a comprehensive, state-of-the-art refit in 2024.

One More not only looks the part but plays it magnificently too. Able to host a party of ten guests comfortably across five deluxe cabins, the yacht also houses separate quarters for a diligent crew of six. But, it's the beast beneath the beauty that truly sets Once More apart. MTU 3,750hp engines power the yacht, promising an adrenaline-inducing maximum speed of 28 knots and a comfortable cruising speed of 24 knots.

Significant measurements include a 7.5-meter beam, 2.8-meter draught, and a generous internal volume of 248GT. Underneath the refined facade and impressive figures, the renamed Once More speaks of meticulous craftsmanship and thoughtful redesign. Seamlessly unifying comfort, design, and performance, the rebirth of this vessel serves as a testament to the dynamic and ever-evolving world of yachting.

title: Luxurious 40m Sunseeker Motor Yacht Deseo Changes Central Agency, Now Up For Sale
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Luxurious 40m Sunseeker Motor Yacht Deseo Changes Central Agency, Now Up For Sale
summary: The exquisite Sunseeker Deseo, a 40-metre motor yacht, moves to a new central agency and now hits the market.
body: The captivating 40-metre Deseo, a motor yacht mastercrafted by Sunseeker, has shifted central agencies and now graces the market, awaiting its new owner. Currently listed for sale with William Burns of IYC, Deseo towers as a testament to the blend of unmatched engineering and trendsetting design, which are hallmarks of Sunseeker. Delivered in 2014, Deseo is one of the 14 magnificent 40-metre Sunseeker models and has been owned by only one owner throughout. EXCEPTIONAL FEATURES SET Deseo APART. Deseo has been impeccably maintained since its birth, most notably reflected in it successfully passing her 10-year RINA survey last winter. Along with its superior construction and upkeep, it's the modern interiors of Deseo that create a stirring impression. Tailored with fine woods and plush chocolate leathers, Deseo exhibits a warm ambience for guests to kick back and enjoy their marine sojourn to the fullest. White leather sofas joyfully coexist with avant-garde coffee tables at the heart, drawing a welcoming scene for casual conversations and evening merriment. Offering accommodations for up to 12 guests and nine crew, Deseo extends three decks of lavish living quarters. A plush owner’s suite takes centre stage on the main deck, with the additional en suite cabins distributed comfortably around. The lower deck houses the remaining guest accommodation, divided into three doubles and a twin cabin, each accompanied with a Pullman berth. Sample the joys of al fresco dining on the bridge deck aft, or climb up to the sundeck for a casual lunch, strategically designed for leisurely entertaining. Sunseeker Deseo sails swiftly on the power of her twin MTU 12V 4000 M93 diesel engines, which offer a top speed of 26 knots and a 1,500 nautical miles range at a comfortably economical speed of 10-12 knots. As for the price, Deseo is listed at €8,950,000, securely harbored in Livorno, Italy, waiting for her new voyage.

title: The 49-metre Royal Hakvoort Motor Yacht Olmida Finds a New Owner
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The 49-metre Royal Hakvoort Motor Yacht Olmida Finds a New Owner
summary: An iconic icon of nautical splendour, the 49m motor yacht 'Olmida', crafted by Dutch shipyard Royal Hakvoort, has been sold to a new owner.
body: Bearing the mark of Dutch shipyard excellence, Royal Hakvoort's motor yacht ‘Olmida’ has changed hands. With stature and grandeur embodied in its exquisite 49-metre length, the yacht was beautifully brought to life in 2010.

Acclaimed for its superior construction in steel and aluminium, Olmida is a tribute to the architectural brilliance of Glade Johnson and Diana Yacht Design. For the past decade, Olmida has been privately cherished by two owners, each contributing to the high-standards of maintenance that it proudly boasts.

In 2020, the superyacht benefitted from an essential maintenance update. This included a fresh paint coat for the hull and superstructure, alongside audio-visual and IT enhancements, ensuring guests can enjoy their voyages with the optimum in modern convenience. Olmida also passed a rigorous assessment for the RINA class certificate in 2024, further proof of its remarkable quality and preparation for sea adventures.

Additional guest spaces, convertible cabins for added flexibility, and staff quarters complete the composition. Welcoming social gatherings with an alfresco dining setting, bar and lounge, Olmida ensures a captivating charm and magnetic energy surround it.

At the heart of the yacht lies power and precision, with twin MTU engines capable of 13.2 knots maximum speed and boasting a cruising speed of 12.5 knots. From top-notch deck design to the versatility in culinary delights, Olmida continues to captivate sailors with its elegance and charm.

title: Revealed: How Naval Architects Turn the Volvo 70 into an Unstoppable 'Ratings Bandit'
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Revealed: How Naval Architects Turn the Volvo 70 into an Unstoppable 'Ratings Bandit'
summary: Discover how a premier design firm managed to turn the renowned Volvo 70 race-boat into a race-dominating 'Ratings Bandit'.
body: Since the earliest days of yacht racing, achieving a favourable rating for a race-boat has been a preoccupation, even an obsession, for owners, designers, and crew. The story of the Volvo Open 70 (VO 70) boat - a vessel that dominated three Volvo Round the World Races from 2005 to 2012 - provides a fascinating case study in this pursuit. This proud legacy was shaped by the Juan-K Design office, under the guidance of Philippe Oulhen.

Oulhen paints a vivid picture of relentless refinement and evolution. The first two races were won by boats designed by Juan Kouyoumdjian of the office, with his winning streak capped by a victory by Groupama IV in the 2011-2012 edition. These boats, rather than resting on their laurels, have since gone on to seize numerous ocean race victories and set race records. Indeed, five VO 70s still compete at the top of their class.

These boats have earned their position as benchmarks in offshore racing, their structures, deck layouts, rigs, sail plans, and systems finely honed into a stable, reliable package. This stability and reliability is an added bonus for potential buyers; they understand the IRC hull factor and rig, and are afforded a fair degree of flexibility in their sail selection to affect their rating, thanks in part to the dedication of the original sailors. These sailors, crucially, are drawn from a pool of sailors who participated in earlier Volvo campaigns and now affiliate with major sail lofts. In essence, the transformation of a Volvo 70 into a 'Ratings Bandit' is a story drenched in determination, collaboration, and an unwavering spirit of competitive maritime innovation.

title: Historic Yacht Sea Cloud Experiences New Dawn with Lavish Rebuild
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Historic Yacht Sea Cloud Experiences New Dawn with Lavish Rebuild
summary: The iconic Sea Cloud, once the world's largest private sailing yacht, is being revitalized with a multi-million-euro rebuild in Malta.
body: Once the world's largest private sailing yacht, the legendary Sea Cloud is currently experiencing a renaissance. Known for her impressive history, design, and engineering, the 1931 built ship is undergoing a comprehensive refit, breathing new life into this historic vessel. Sea Cloud has a rich lineage, conceived by American businesswoman and cereal heiress Marjorie Merriweather Post, and Wall Street financier, Edward Francis Hutton. Carefully designed by renowned architects at Cox & Stevens in New York, her launch in 1931 marked a milestone as the world's largest private sailing yacht. It was, by all means - a floating masterpiece. Now, the 110-meter yacht is going through a massive transformation, aiming to restore its original charm and majesty. After arriving in Malta in November 2025, the top-to-bottom overhaul was announced by Daniel Kũpfer, her current owner's representative. Over the decades, Sea Cloud has worn many faces. Besides her illustrious start, she served as a weather ship during World War II, before becoming a presidential ship named 'Angelita'. After a series of transitions, the splendid vessel, then experiencing a hardship at Panama, was rescued by a group of German entrepreneurs who brought it home and named it Sea Cloud once again. The ongoing refit represents more than pure aesthetics - it is an endeavor to restore Sea Cloud's authenticity. Her impressive history deserves nothing less. This detailed reconstruction, inspired by historical documents and Sea Cloud's original blueprints, brings back the grandeur whilst adhering to a meticulous craftsmanship. This period of rejuvenation also marks a significant shift in Sea Cloud's function. Once the world's most beautiful cruise ship, known for hosting 64 guests with a 60-person attentive crew, Sea Cloud will soon sail away from an extensive customer service era. The revamped yacht will house only 20 guests, reinstating the true vibe of this historic sailing vessel. It's a move that prioritizes the intimate and classic sailing experience, attracting people who don’t just wish to sail but want to revel in the yacht's breath-taking legacy. Breathing fresh air into a classic, the Sea Cloud is rising from the wake of time, her golden age still shimmering on the sea horizon. This isn't just ship restoration, it’s a resurrection of an era.

title: The Power of Sydney Hobart Yacht Race: Unveiling the Offshore Performance of LawConnect and Comanche
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Power of Sydney Hobart Yacht Race: Unveiling the Offshore Performance of LawConnect and Comanche
summary: The Sydney Hobart Yacht Race is a theatre of tradition, endurance, and high-stakes competition, where the most innovative sailing equipment is tested to the limit.
body: In the world of offshore yacht racing, the Sydney Hobart Yacht Race is far less a race and more an odyssey. Each year, it captivates the global audience, putting a spotlight on a relentless 628-nautical mile passage off the east coast of Australia. A race taking place through unpredictable weather systems and demanding ocean conditions, it's a seafaring ballet that demands flawless performance under extreme fatigue and potential consequences.

Navigating through such a daunting race demands more than just the best sailors. It necessitates the best sailing gear, created remarkably for these punishing conditions. Zhik proudly gears LawConnect and Comanche's crews with the most cutting-edge offshore equipment. From the striking resilience of the offshore OFS800 waterproof range to the high performing UVActive sun protection tops and award-winning Seaboots, every piece of gear assures maximum performance when conditions are the toughest.

The toughness of offshore yacht racing punctuates the need for absolute trust in equipment. As yachts take on the punishing conditions, every layer of gear must function seamlessly and without compromise. LawConnect and Comanche put their faith in Zhik's offshore gear, engineered supremely for durability, security, and adaptability, such that it remains comfortable and efficient from start to finish.

Sailing enthusiasts and seafarers are left in awe as they witness such formidable display of grit and determination. It's not just a race; it's a constant battle against time, where performance stands as the ultimate truth.

title: Dive into the Holiday Season with Ensign Yachts: Unveiling New Models and Unforgettable Adventures
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Dive into the Holiday Season with Ensign Yachts: Unveiling New Models and Unforgettable Adventures
summary: Ensign Yachts celebrates the holiday season with a joyful message, unveiling of new models and focus on exceptional adventures, both on and off the waters.

With a heartwarming holiday greeting, the renowned yacht brand is keeling the excitement afloat with announcements of enticing opportunities and sensational new arrivals.

This holiday season, Ensign Yachts unveils more than just a garland of bright red and green. They're showcasing new models from phenomenal brands, in addition to an introduction of an exciting new premium brand scheduled for next year. With a year that was nothing short of fantastically rewarding, the Ensign Yachts team is fascinated by the prospect of another year full of maritime adventures and memorable journeys.

The Mediterranean has never been more alluring, with Ensign Yachts offering irresistible yacht charter deals with discounts running up to 50%. What’s more, they're even throwing in a 10% discount for first-time charter customers booking this month, a perfect opportunity for those looking to experience the serene and captivating waters on a luxury yacht.

For those keen on making immediate plans and eager to start their journey, Ensign Yachts also has a range of used boats in excellent condition ready to set sail. These include the 2022 Tofinou 12, 2010 Bavaria Cruiser 45, 2024 Tesoro T40, 2022 Bavaria SR41, and a variety of lovingly-used Nautitechs in Australia, Europe, and the Pacific.

Moreover, Ensign Yachts paves the path for a stress-free sailing journey with European delivery services equipped for a seamless process. And just when you thought owning a yacht entails a lot of responsibilities, Ensign Yachts proves otherwise with yacht management services designed to take away the hassles of yacht ownership.

The upshot is a holiday season aglow with luxury, comfort, and versatility. Ensign Yachts not only delivers award-winning vessels but also provides exclusive and tailored experiences out on the open waters. Time and time again, the team manifests their inseparable bond with the sea and shares it with fellow enthusiasts. A message of good tidings shared with a wave of new opportunities and sailing adventures, it truly is a festive season like no other with Ensign Yachts.

title: Timeless Marine Icons, 'Seagull of Cayman' and 'Gin Tonic', Embark on New Chapters
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Timeless Marine Icons, 'Seagull of Cayman' and 'Gin Tonic', Embark on New Chapters
summary: Two acclaimed yachts, the 40-metre Feadship motor yacht 'Seagull of Cayman' and the 41.7-metre 'Gin Tonic' have recently changed ownership.
body: This old thread of maritime sophistication and luxury has found new shores to explore, with the acquisition of two classic Feadship motor yachts - the 40-metre 'Seagull of Cayman' and the 41.7 -metre 'Gin Tonic'. These timeless marine icons, with their illustrious lineage and unparalleled craftsmanship, have set off on new chapters in their seafaring chronicles./n/nThe revered 'Seagull of Cayman' was sold, with Kevin Bonnie of International Yacht Corporation (IYC) representing the seller and Yves Di Lena of YDL Yachting Corp championing the buyer. This quintessential Dutch-build, has been the symbol of maritime magnificence since her launch in 1980. Tasked with her creation were the maestros of De Voogt Naval Architects, who skillfully wielded steel and aluminium to shape this masterpiece. Following through the years, she underwent major refits in 2006 and 2015-2017 and was last asking price was a hefty €3,200,000 with VAT delivered. She's currently lying in the glamorous realm of Saint Tropez, France ready to unfurl her sails in pursuit of new horizons.

The other prized half of this transference rhapsody is the 'Gin Tonic'. The auspicious occasion of her sale found David Legrand of Fraser and Ian Sherwood of Burgess orchestrating the deal. Birthed at the Dutch yard of Feadship in 1981, she is the embodiment of classic charm and timeless functionality. Receving an update recently, her interiors showcase glossed woods, plush fabrics and rich textures. She was one of three distinguished Feadships commissioned by the same owner in the 1980s. Her last known asking price was a substantial €4,500,000 (VAT Paid) while laying in Viareggio, Italy.

In the pantheon of sailing royalty, these vessels hold a lofty position. Famed for their impeccable design and remarkable expedition capabilities, both yachts are geared for adventures. So, as they embark under new ownership, it is the dawn of fresh tales in their enduring legacy.

title: Ferretti's Masterpiece 'Étoile' Beckons Buyers with a €1,049,000 Price Drop
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Ferretti's Masterpiece 'Étoile' Beckons Buyers with a €1,049,000 Price Drop
summary: Italian yard Custom Line's 32.8-metre motor yacht, 'Étoile,' has seen a significant price reduction, making it an enticing offer for yacht enthusiasts.
body: The world of yacht trading has just been sent into a flurry with a massive €1,049,000 price drop on the Italian-made 'Étoile,' a 32.8-metre show-stopping beauty from high-profile shipbuilders Custom Line. Launched in July 2023, this motor yacht has been listed by broker Mark Seaton of Yacht & Villa, and has garnered attention from yacht enthusiasts around the globe.

An artistic creation wrapped in a veneer of practicality, Étoile was designed by Francesco Paszkowski, along with Margherita Casprini handling the interior. This CL106 beauty stands as the sixteenth model in the range, developed in collaboration with Ferretti Group Engineering. A testament to its flawless performance and exceptional build quality, 'Étoile' is still under the manufacturer's warranty, boasting less than 200 hours on her engines.

Living spaces within the yacht are designed with warmth and inviting decor. An open plan saloon and dining room form the centrepiece, affording ample space and creature comforts. Up on the sundeck, guests can drink in the sun or unwind in the Jacuzzi while enjoying an elevated view of the ocean. A commanding flybridge and two guest zones of seating and sun pads on the foredeck complete the elevated outdoor experience.

At the heart of 'Étoile' are twin 2,638hp MTU engines, driving the yacht to a cruising speed of 22 knots while capable of reaching 26 knots at full throttle. This RINA-classed, 210GT yacht also offers a comfortable 1,000 nautical miles range when cruising at 10 knots. Zero-speed stabilisers add to the comfort for those journeys at sea or when anchored up. Lying in Italy, this luxury yacht is now available for purchase at a much-reduced price, currently asking for €9,950,000.

title: Sailing Takes the Lead at Scottish Sports Awards with Duo of Honours
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Sailing Takes the Lead at Scottish Sports Awards with Duo of Honours
summary: The Scottish Sports Awards celebrated two sailing personalities, Andy Brown and Ann Roy, recognizing their impressive contributions to the world of sailing.
body: Scotland's sailing community reached a new pinnacle at this year's Scottish Sports Awards. Signals of joy and waves of applause filled the Old Fruitmarket in Glasgow on 15th December as two distinguished personalities of sailing, Andy Brown and Ann Roy, were honoured for their contributions.

Andy Brown, Glasgow’s windsurfing ace, was crowned the Athlete of the Year. Brown established himself as a global windsurfing icon after scoring Gold at the iQFOiL World Championships in July. This significant victory catapults his reputation, prepping him for a promising LA 2028 Olympic Games campaign.

Moreover, Brown has been a beacon of support for Scottish windsurfing's future development. As RYA Scotland's Head iQFOiL Coach and an active member of the Scottish Fin & Foil Association, Brown nurtures emerging talent, positioning Scotland as a thriving hub for water sports.

These recognitions emphasise the vital role sailing and windsurfing have come to play in Scotland's sporting lexicon, led by exceptional ambassadors and driven by boundless passion and the spirit of competition.

title: Announcing a fresh cycle of reinvention, France SailGP team introduces Phillippe Presti as the new team manager and reveals an invigorated line-up for 2026
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Announcing a fresh cycle of reinvention, France SailGP team introduces Phillippe Presti as the new team manager and reveals an invigorated line-up for 2026
summary: The France SailGP team is looking forward to a promising 2026 season, as they introduce their new team manager Philippe Presti, and announce an energetic line-up.
body: On the trail of a strong 2025 season, the France SailGP team has set its sights high for the forthcoming contests. Finishing in an impressive 5th place, the team is now gearing up for a fresh start, with a clear objective: to leverage the sturdy foundation they have laid and turn that into heftier wins in an ultra-competitive and professional championship.

The movement to sustain the sporting continuity is at play against a particularly vibrant transfer window in the SailGP Championship. Making a confident choice, the French team is pinning its hopes on a stable sporting foundation that assures both continuity and performance. Welcoming back Quentin Delapierre, Manon Audinet, Jason Saunders, Timothé Lapauw, and Olivier Herlédant to their respective positions, they bid adieu to Kevin Peponnet and Matthieu Vandame, expressing gratitude for their unwavering dedication.

Experienced hands McMillan and Mourniac bring added strength to the French project with their unique skills and excellent track records. Each of these members is renowned for their tenacity, versatility, and exceptional abilities. Additionally, young talent Enzo Balanger has been signed as a reserve athlete for the 2026 season, symbolising the team's ongoing commitment to youth and inclusion.

This transformation of the components of the France SailGP team is predicted as a game-changer. With the experienced Philippe Presti leading, a spectacular 2026 performance is expected. These changes are not just bringing a wave of freshness but also a calculated dialectic of stability and dynamism. Indeed, it's a new high-tide in the team's journey, and they're sailing straight into success.

title: Iconic 33m Gulf Craft Yacht Santosh Sells and is Rebranded as Gold Star
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Iconic 33m Gulf Craft Yacht Santosh Sells and is Rebranded as Gold Star
summary: The Dubai-built, 32.9-meter motor yacht Santosh has recently found a new owner, along with a new name—Gold Star.
body: It's a new era for the luxurious 32.9-meter Gulf Craft motor yacht Santosh, as it has recently changed hands and is primed for a quick rebranding. Soon, this vessel will be cutting through the ocean waves under a new moniker, Gold Star. Brokers from Worth Avenue Yachts and Next Generation Yachting played key roles in this notable transition. This yacht, which is valued at around $5,950,000, is a stunning member of the Majesty 100 series from the highly esteemed Dubai-based shipyard.

Crafted in 2020, this superyacht boasts a semi-displacement hull and a superstructure that's expertly crafted from fiber-reinforced plastics. Gold Star is commercially registered under the Cayman Flag and upholds the rigorous RINA Class classification standards. Stepping onboard, guests are welcomed by a light-drenched interior, thanks to floor-to-ceiling windows and expansive glass doors. The airy ambiance is perfect for social gatherings or tranquil relaxation.

The Gold Star comfortably accommodates 10 guests across five staterooms. The master stateroom, positioned conveniently on-deck, features grand windows and a king-sized bed. The en suite bathroom is designed with luxurious marble accents and a spacious waterfall shower. Four additional guest staterooms are available below deck.

Finally, making this remarkable vessel move is a pair of MAN V12-1900 engines, which provide imposing 1,874 horsepower, propelling the yacht to cruising speeds of 15.4 knots and a thrilling maximum speed of 20 knots.
The majestic vessel Santosh has indeed begun a new chapter as Gold Star, promising to deliver exceptional voyages in its future.

title: Legendary Motor Yacht Rena Finds a New Owner in a Remarkable 64 Days
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Legendary Motor Yacht Rena Finds a New Owner in a Remarkable 64 Days
summary: The magnificent 44.2-metre classic motor yacht Rena has found a new owner, a swift 64 days after hitting the market.
body: The embodiment of grandeur, speed, and stability, the legendary Rena motor yacht has found a new steward. Its sale, just 64 days after hitting the market, was completed by BR Marine Group. Brenda Roney, acting on behalf of the seller, with assistance from Ken Bracewell, and Rebecca Gormley, who introduced the buyer, successfully concluded the transaction. Design credits for Rena, conceived by the Australian yard NQEA in 1989, belong to extraordinary US naval architect Jack Hargrave. The creation of Rena not only served to debut a yacht 'that could do everything' but also showcased Hargrave’s exceptional talent for designing both the interior and exterior profiles of a yacht. A previous owner saw potential to enhance the yacht in 1994, adding 4.5 metres to Rena's length overall. Since then, the yacht has been maintained regularly, most recently receiving a new stabiliser system and Starlink connectivity. From 2023-2024, it also underwent a complete rebuild of main engines and transmission, including an electrical refit. Rena’s interior offers ample space for socialising and relaxation, with the main deck saloon featuring a U-shaped sofa and another row of couch seating. A formal dining table for 10 is situated further forward, separated by a wooden partition for clear demarcation of spaces. A nautical theme pervades the interior, marked by navy blue furnishings, embroidered with ocean insignia. The yacht boasts accommodation for 14 guests across five staterooms, which includes a full-beam (7.8 metre) master suite. The exterior spaces offer sublime panoramas from the main deck aft, bridge deck aft, and sundeck. Amenities include an outdoor gym, multiple tanning locations, and an assortment of water toys, from Yamaha WaveRunners to a catamaran landing tender. Twin 1500hp Caterpillar engines empower Rena's impressive speeds. title: New Training, Safety and Social Responsibility Standards Aiming to Mitigate Harassment and Violence at Sea
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: New Training, Safety and Social Responsibility Standards Aiming to Mitigate Harassment and Violence at Sea
summary: As we welcome 2026, an essential reform takes place in seafarer training modules focusing on safety and harassment prevention.
body: To kick off 2026 on a decisive note, a momentous shift is expected in the realm of the maritime industry. The compulsory update to the Personal Safety and Social Responsibility (PSSR) course reflects this evolution by introducing crucial amendments in the seafarer’s STCW basic training regime. Notably, these changes target violence and harassment at sea, setting new standards for both commercial vessels and private superyachts.

These amendments sprung forth from the International Maritime Organization’s Resolution MSC.560 (108), adopted in May 2024. The resolution laid ground for minimum competency standards for every PSSR course. Thereby, it strove to bolster safety and welfare standards across all vessels. Seafarers who have already completed the course will not be required to re-take the course. However, specialized training to align with these mandates might be necessary in some cases.

To keep up with these changes, yacht crew members are encouraged to familiarize themselves with newer requirements and deepen their understanding of harassment-related risks at sea. Evidently, awareness now forms the linchpin for professional competence, empowering crew members at all levels to combat harmful behaviors effectively.

By arming themselves with this enhanced understanding, crew members contribute to safer and more respectful sailing environments. In a field often fraught with significant pressure and close quarters, correct and timely responses can conserve professionalism and overall well-being. As these maritime sectors sail towards high accountability and transparency, crew members well-versed with these issues can uphold maritime standards, promoting a healthier on-board culture.

title: 2025 EurILCA Team Racing
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Italy and Sweden Set the Pace After a Testing Day Two at the EurILCA Team Racing Europeans
summary: 2025 EurILCA Team Racing European Championship delivered exactly what team racing does best: pressure, patience, and precision, all played out in marginal conditions that rewarded calm heads and disciplined tactics.
body: Sailors arrived dockside to a stubborn standstill. Heavy rain swept across the venue and the race area lay glassy and lifeless, forcing a prolonged postponement ashore. For team racing sailors, used to split-second decisions and aggressive manoeuvres, the wait was as much a mental test as the racing itself.

Eventually, persistence paid off. At 11:23 local time, the first group was released onto the water as a fragile breeze filled from the shore. Despite continued drizzle, the wind stabilised just enough to allow racing to begin, hovering around 5 knots and gradually building throughout the afternoon.

By the close of play, 13 races had been successfully completed in 5–10 knots of breeze, with flat water turning every match into a chess game of positioning, mark traps and boat-on-boat pressure. Then, just as the final flights were underway, heavy rain returned — a reminder that nothing comes easily at this level.
Light Winds, Flat Water, High Stakes

Conditions across Day Two demanded a disciplined approach. With limited leverage across the course and little margin for recovery, starts were decisive and penalties brutally costly. Every cross, every slow tack, every compromised overlap mattered.
This was classic ILCA team racing: no hiding places, no room for heroics, just relentless execution and teamwork.
Perfect Records at the Top: Italy and Sweden 2
When the spray settled and the scores were tallied, two teams stood clear.

Italy delivered a flawless performance, closing the day with six wins from six starts, demonstrating superb coordination and race control. Calm under pressure and ruthless when opportunities appeared, the Italian squad looked completely at home in the conditions.

Alongside them, Sweden 2 matched the intensity, posting five wins from five races to remain unbeaten. Their ability to convert small gains into race-winning positions marked them out as a serious title contender as the regatta moves into its decisive phase.
Together, Italy and Sweden 2 have established themselves as the teams to beat.
Greece Impresses on Home Waters

Hot on their heels, the Greek team produced one of the strongest performances of the day. With five wins from six races, the hosts used their local knowledge well, showing sharp boat handling and smart tactical awareness in the light air.
Their consistency kept them firmly in the hunt and ensured strong home representation near the top of the leaderboard.
Tight Battles Through the Fleet
Behind the leaders, the competition remains finely balanced:
France and Sweden 1 are tied for fourth, each posting three wins from five races
Bulgaria sits sixth with three wins from six
Germany 1 holds seventh
Ireland and Lithuania are tied for eighth, each with two wins from six
Further down the order, Germany 2 and Serbia 2 each managed a single victory from five starts, while Serbia 1 endured a difficult day, finishing without a win after six races.
Championship Poised on a Knife Edge

With conditions expected to remain changeable, adaptability will be key as the EurILCA Team Racing European Championship heads toward its conclusion. In light winds like these, momentum can swing rapidly, and a single strong flight can reshape the leaderboard.
Italy and Sweden 2 may lead for now, but nothing is settled. Team racing has a habit of punishing complacency, and with margins this tight, the championship remains wide open.

One thing is certain: the sailors who thrive over the coming days will be those who stay patient, communicate clearly, and keep executing when the pressure is highest — exactly what European team racing is all about.

title: Reliving 2025: A Shocking Year of Maritime Perilous Events
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Reliving 2025: A Shocking Year of Maritime Perilous Events
summary: A year in retrospect, 2025 witnessed several heartrending boat calamities worth noting from fires to unfortunate groundings.
body: If history must be retold, the nautical world of 2025 had its fair share of excitement skewed towards the unfortunate spectrum. The year showcased calamitous tides featuring some harrowing incidents quite unparalleled. The entire fraternity, however, remained hopeful despite the twist of events and arose stronger in spirit for navigating forward. Among the headlines that blew the sailor hats off, a chilling marina fire in Marseilles stood out, as well as the grounding of Sanlorenzo's flagship. Yet, nothing was more dramatic than the sinking of a newly built superyacht within moments of its virgin voyage. Indeed, these evidences narrate a tale of bravery, sorrow, and vigilance. The 24-meter superyacht from Medyılmaz Shipyard, Dolce Vento, capsized immediately post-launching owing to an alleged stabilization issue. The yacht sank to a depth of seven meters even before the celebratory champagne could dry! Swiftly following this episode was the sinking of the Tecnomar Lamborghini 63 sports yachts off Miami Beach. Too close for comfort, yet an event that shook the ethos of boating. The year saw its sharpest sting when the 41-meter superyacht Sea Lady II suffered severe damage due to a fire while docked cozily in St Tropez. Flames engulfed the boat causing it to partially sink, leaving but a haunting vision for many. Tale of woes continued when the 43-meter Custom Line motor yacht, Lady Dia ran aground near Bonifacio Marina, another incident that reaffirmed how we must never underestimate the sea's power. Also, the 29-meter Astondoa motor yacht Da Vinci caught fire off the coast of Formentera, Spain while carrying seven souls. It was also a year when a ferocious fire demolished the 30-meter Azimut yacht, Ramonda while it was calmly anchored in Portonovi, a resort marina in Montenegro. Taking a stroll back through these episodes from 2025, it is a stark yet powerful reminder of the importance of vigilance, safety, and preparedness. The sea, after all, is a call to adventure and thrill, but one which demands respect, caution, and wisdom along the ride.

Moonstone sailed out as a re-evolved Delta Marine flagship, majestic, yet faithful to her original DNA.

Preparations were afoot at Giacalone Shipyard for a complete overhaul and conversion of the 71.8-metre Snellius, a former Royal Dutch Navy build, into a luxury charter yacht designed for silent, smooth cruises. The refit was designed to encompass structural work, updated electrical and automation systems and a new, elegant interior.

Lastly, German yard Abeking & Rasmussen proudly unveiled the year-long transformation results of Lürssen superyacht Starfire. The makeover featured a swim platform extension, performance upgrades, a remodelled sundeck, and vibrantly nature-inspired interiors. Accompanied by increased headroom, an elevator on all levels, and a counter-current pool with a bar, Starfire emerged with a stunning profile and heightened appeal.

These 2025 refurbishments propagate a renewed spirit in refits worldwide, manifesting the possibilities of technological advancements, reconstruction and imaginative design in revitalising superyachts.

title: Deconstructing the Numbers: The Significance of Newton Measurements in Lifejackets and Buoyancy Aids
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Deconstructing the Numbers: The Significance of Newton Measurements in Lifejackets and Buoyancy Aids
summary: Delving into the deep, this article sheds light on the role of Newton measurements in the selection of reliable lifejackets and buoyancy aids.
body: Newton - a term that makes one feel back in Physics 101, yet holds significant importance when selecting secure lifejackets or buoyancy aids for seafaring. A Newton is a metric measurement of force, which, in the case of lifejackets and buoyancy aids, indicates its buoyancy potential. The numbers on a buoyancy cloak could range from 50N to a hefty 305N, each bearing its appropriate significance and applicability.

The ISO 12402 standards classify buoyancy aids into four categories, based on their level of performance - 275, 150, 100, and 50. Essentially, the number represents the force in Newtons that the jacket can exert to keep an individual afloat. The prized rule of 'higher the better' doesn't necessarily apply to these measurements. Allow us to guide you through these numbers.

Alternatively, inherent buoyant foam lifejackets, usually rated at 100N, come with an array of inflatable options. They are particularly tailored for children and are designed to turn an unconscious person onto their back in water. Lifejackets with Newtons up to 149.9N fit into this category.

Lastly, the 150N lifejackets are the default choice for those venturing out into sheltered and coastal waters. Mastering the nuances of these numbers and their implications would enable a more conscious and informed choice of life-saving gear.

title: The Achievements of the 2025 Superyacht Design Revolution: Luxurious Concepts Capturing Attention
author: Old Sea Dogs

summary: In 2025, the superyacht sector took an audacious leap towards a future marked by unrivalled grace, innovation and efficiency.

title: A Beautiful Juxtaposition: Apreamare Gozzo 48 Cabin Blends Classic and Contemporary with Ease
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A Beautiful Juxtaposition: Apreamare Gozzo 48 Cabin Blends Classic and Contemporary with Ease
summary: The Apreamare Gozzo 48 Cabin brings an exciting evolution to traditional Italian boating, combining modern features with age-old charm.
body: The Apreamare Gozzo 48 Cabin stands out in the Gozzo line as a testament to Apreamare's innovative interpretation of the classic Sorrentine fishing boat. Its modern twist leaves no room for subtlety; it captures the attention with its well-designed deckhouse serving as its focal point. Adorned with a dinette that encompasses the entire starboard side, the 48 Cabin maximises space utilisation, providing ample room for three cabins and two bathrooms. Creative inclusion of a reversible helm seat adds a delightful twist to the overall ensemble. A port galley of equal length complements the deckhouse. Flexibility lies at the heart of the vessel’s design. For those desiring a lower galley, a two-cabin configuration offers a perfect solution. Irrespective of the layout, an ensuite owner's cabin nestled in the bow always enhances the boat’s appeal, taking full advantage of the raised mouldings of the foredeck. External living spaces are no less remarkable. The bow houses a bench, flanked by seat pods on either side of the anchor winch, offering a comfortable alternative to aft zones. However, the prime spot for outdoor indulgence remains the cockpit. Encircled by a characteristic curved transom, a sun pad integrated with a bench seat fills the space, complete with a flush-mounted table at deck level. Apreamare Gozzo 48 Cabin's propulsion options do not disappoint. With twin IPS700 or 800s, or a pair of D8 600hp on straight shafts, you can achieve speeds of up to 30-31 knots. And, if more guest cabins are needed, you can add a compact aft crew cabin. While the Gozzo’s distinctive style is not for everyone, no one can resist the authentic vintage vibes given off by a boat produced by Apreamare, a company with a rich history dating back to 1869.

title: Unfaltering Tom Gillard Clinches Another Win in Sailjuice Winter Series, Despite Crew Change
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unfaltering Tom Gillard Clinches Another Win in Sailjuice Winter Series, Despite Crew Change
summary: Formidable sailor, Tom Gillard continues to dominate the Seldén Sailjuice Winter Series, securing his third consecutive victory, showcasing an uncanny level of consistency and skill.
body: Tom Gillard's mastery in sailing remains unrivalled as he secures his third straight victory at the Robline Polar Chase, despite experiencing a change in his racing crew. Event #3 of the Seldén Sailjuice Winter Series once again witnessed Gillard's fearsome prowess at the helm of his bright red Merlin Rocket.

Gillard and Arran Holman won both races of last Saturday's Robline UK Polar Chase, the third of eight events in this season's Seldén Sailjuice Winter Series. Even with his regular crew Rachael Gray's absence, and Holman stepping to the front of the construction, Gillard proved his mettle yet again.

Gillard's impact at the Chase Sailing Club was evident, winning the average-lap race and clocking a considerable lead over the Laser 3000 of local duo Emma Robertson and Bryn Abendstern. The venue in Birmingham hosted the Series for the second time, and once more, it was a hit among the sailors, thanks to its friendly atmosphere and conducive sailing conditions.

Making a sweeping score in the Series, Gillard and Holman outraced Andy 'Taxi' Davis in the pursuit race, who looked poised to steer his OK dinghy to victory but fell short in the final stages. Gillard's control and coordination with the Merlin were impeccable, highlighting his trained knack for sailing under varying pressures and conditions.

Sailing enthusiasts are now looking forward to the next event in the Series, the Yorkshire Dales Brass Monkey, set to take place on 27 December. This will be followed by the Grafham Grand Prix on 4 January 2026, contributing to an exciting winter of sailing-the perfect opportunity for other contenders to rise!

title: Italy Shines on Day One of the Exciting 2025 Youth Sailing World Championships in Vilamoura, Portugal
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Italy Shines on Day One of the Exciting 2025 Youth Sailing World Championships in Vilamoura, Portugal
summary: Italy stands out on the opening day of the 2025 Youth Sailing World Championships taking place in Vilamoura, Portugal, leading three of five events.
body: The 2025 Youth Sailing World Championships couldn't have begun on a more exciting note. Vilamoura, Portugal, the picturesque host city, saw teams from all over the world flocking in, ready to pit their best against the ocean and each other. Casting light on the Italian team's stunning performance, they managed to gain an impressive start, leading three out of the five events that were held on the opening day.

Alessandro Cirinei and Marina Murri, stole the limelight by snatching victories in the male and female ILCA 6 races respectively. But they weren't the only Italians on top form. Making an early impression in the male/mixed 29er races were Giuseppe Montesano and Enrico Coslevich, who presently enjoy the enviable position of being the early frontrunners.

On an equally thrilling note, the Nacra 15 races weren't without their share of drama. Four pairs mistook the course, leading to drastic misjudgments. Among them were reigning Youth World and Nacra 15 world champions Lorenzo Sirena and Alice Dessy, who despite crossing the line first, were later marked with an NSC (not sailed course).

However, the difficulties faced by some lead to opportunities for others, and Praud and Mansouri took full advantage, leading with only four points, ahead of both Dylan Tomko and Casey Small (USA), and Belgium's Lotte Meynen and Simon Jacobs.

In the 29er category, the Italian team held onto their slim lead, with Montesano and Coslevich finishing seventh in the first race and second in the following one. Close on their heels, the German and Australian duos also displayed commendable spirit.
Despite unfavorable winds causing a halt to the remaining six events, these promising early results have set an eager tone for the rest of the Championship.

imageAlt: Day of drama and excitement in the 33rd SEA Games: SSL kicks off in Thailand with promising action.
summary: The South-East Asian Games (SEA) proudly marked the commencement of the Star Sailors League (SSL) in the coastal city of Pattaya, Thailand.
body: The first day of the coveted SEA Games stirred the waters in Pattaya, unveiling a striking spectacle of the Star Sailors League (SSL). The docks woke up to a flurry of activity and anticipation as sailors diligently prepped their SSL47s under unblemished sky. A multitude of spectators convened along the shoreline, hearts charged with exhilaration and fists clenched in support. Regatta Director Paul Hutton Ashkenny emphasized the global essence of the SSL Gold Cup and its quintessential role in promoting participation from emerging nations. The incorporation of SSL47 into the SEA Games, he believed, communicated a statement of strength and unity. Ashkenny praised the warm welcome from the region and shared his thrill at the day's naval play. Day One saw the unfolding of three fleet races, where five nations matched skills on a windward leeward course. The offshore scene was a vibrant palette as the inaugural race lifted off under ideal sailing conditions. Small waves lapped against the hulls, while the sun painted the arena between tropical islands and the Pattaya skyline. As the race commenced, SSL Team Philippines led from the leeward end, while SSL Team Thailand trailed closely. The first upwind leg witnessed a tactical swap as Thailand inched ahead while Malaysia and Myanmar remained in the fray. Chasing dominance, the teams executed tight manoeuvres, on-board shouts resonating against the rhythmic percussion of the waves. As the adrenalin surged, Thailand rounded the windward mark and distanced themselves from the fleet, demonstrating perfect execution and strategy with a commanding win. Meanwhile, Vietnam and the Philippines grappled with tricky manoeuvres and wind pressure, exhibiting sportsmanship and skill even in adversity. SSL Team Thailand's trimmer, Dylan Whitcraft, reflected on their victory, attributing their success to the team's cohesive effort and strategic execution. Amplifying the anticipation and excitement, Day One of the SSL at the SEA Games has set the expectations sky-high for what promises to be an enthralling series of races in the coming days.

title: A Deep Dive into the Chase Sailing Club's Momentous 70th Anniversary Celebrations
author: Old Sea Dogs

summary: Join us as we recount the jubilant 70th-anniversary celebrations of the Chase Sailing Club, marked by camaraderie, merriment, and unwavering dedication.
body: The year 2025 stands out as a historic chapter in the Chase Sailing Club's illustrious history. It saw the Club mark its grand 70-year anniversary, a milestone that was honoured and celebrated thanks to the diligent planning, support, and tireless efforts of an exceptional committee. Truly, the year's achievements were an all-hands-on-deck affair, reflecting the spirit of teamwork that lies at the heart of sailing.

The Club inaugurated its celebration year by laying out carefully crafted plans aimed at celebrating its storied past, vibrant present, and promising future. The ensuing months were marked by spirited debates and in-depth discussions, and it was with the members at the very heart of these deliberations that an action plan was conceived.

It was an evening that truly encapsulated the spirit of the Club – jubilant, nostalgic, and forward looking, brimming with camaraderie and shared love for the sea.

title: The Risks and Flaws of Modern Maritime Design: An Analysis of Superyacht Safety
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Risks and Flaws of Modern Maritime Design: An Analysis of Superyacht Safety
summary: Boarding a superyacht in challenging sea conditions can be treacherous, given certain persistent design flaws.
body: Piloting a superyacht can be an invigorating experience. The feel of the salt air, the wind in the sails, and the stunning vistas can create the impression of conquering the seas. However, beneath this adventurous façade lurks the harsh reality of maritime safety. As any seasoned sailor will profess, being on the open water is not without risks, particularly when it comes to boarding a vessel under challenging sea conditions.

Recently, a case study from CHIRP Maritime’s Superyacht Feedback highlighted the risks associated with boarding a superyacht. This knowledge sharing program brought attention to several design flaws that could jeopardize the safety of both maritime pilots and crew members. Prompting this investigation were a series of unsuccessful boarding attempts under adverse weather conditions, along with the vessel's corresponding non-compliant safety protocols.

The following day, the pilot was to board near the vessel's stern, however, the resultant swell again set the stage for hazardous access with the potential risk of swamping the crew. As a somewhat desperate last resort, the crew opened a gate amidships - a decision that only amplified the existing danger due to the tumultuous seas rolling over the deck.

It was not until the third attempt in calmer weather that a successful boarding was made, but it did not come without its fair share of obstacles. The secured ladder against the ship's hull proved inadequate, with poor securing, gaps, and obstructions posing as significant trip and entangle hazards.

These potentially life-threatening experiences underscore the urgent need for a design overhaul. It is crucial that manufacturers address these issues, as neglected safety measures and improvised, non-compliant boarding methods expose pilots and crew to unacceptably high risks simply not worth the thrill of the high seas.

title: All-Female Crew of The Famous Project CIC Determined to Triumph Despite Difficulties on their Jules Verne Trophy Attempt
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: All-Female Crew of The Famous Project CIC Determined to Triumph Despite Difficulties on their Jules Verne Trophy Attempt
summary: The all-women crew of The Famous Project CIC continue their Jules Verne Trophy record attempt aboard the IDEC SPORT maxi trimaran, displaying unprecedented resilience.
body: "Adventure and passion on high seas". These aren't just words for the courageous all-women crew of The Famous Project CIC, undertaking the remarkable challenge of a nonstop, unaided circumnavigation of the world in the renowned Jules Verne Trophy challenge. Despite difficult circumstances, the women remain steadfast in their journey, refusing to abandon their dream of breaking a record and inscribing their names in the annals of nautical history. Aboard their battle-worn maxi trimaran, IDEC SPORT, the team encounters adversity, their mainsail blocked at the second reef, Cape town looming ahead. A stopover could mean the loss of their dream. Yet, the sturdy spirit of Alexia, Dee, Annemieke, Rebecca, Deborah, Molly, Tamara, and Stacey can hardly be subdued. Sisterhood, grit and an unwavering will keep them stubbornly pressing on. The problem lies with a stubborn hook, refusing to let the mainsail rise. Stuck and blocked, the hook, a clasp that relays the sail's tension to the mast's top, becomes a formidable adversary. With the spirit of their mission in mind, and the lyrics of Bruce Springsteen's The River reinforcing their resolve: 'Because a dream is a lie if it doesn't come true', they labour for hours, inside the boat's wing mast and out, attempting to repair the stubborn hook. Each crew member, with patience and diligence, contributes to the task. Undeterred by uncertainties and the unknown, the women of The Famous Project CIC stand resolute, committed to seeing their dream come to fruition. As they press ahead on their momentous journey, their resilience becomes a beacon of inspiration, a testament to the power of dreams, determination, and the indomitable spirit of women explorers. Their story continues to inspire countless others, a vivid reminder of the strength of human character when it is steeled by ambition and fortified by an unwavering belief in one's dreams.'

title: A NEW ERA FOR THE BRITISH VIRGIN ISLANDS’ PREMIER MARINE HUB
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: NANNY CAY MARINA BREAKS GROUND ON MAJOR $40 MILLION EXPANSION
imageCredit: © Alastair Abrehart/Broadsword PR, Alex Turnbull, Michael Winter Jr.
summary: TORTOLA, BRITISH VIRGIN ISLANDS – The Caribbean’s sailing capital is setting course for a bold new chapter. On Friday, October 31, 2025, Nanny Cay Marina — the beating heart of the BVI’s marine industry — officially broke ground on an ambitious $30–$40 million expansion project, ushering in the next era of yachting excellence in the British Virgin Islands.
body: The landmark ceremony, held on-site at Nanny Cay, marked the beginning of construction on a project that will transform the marina into one of the most advanced and versatile facilities in the entire Caribbean. The expansion includes 112 brand-new berths, an enormous custom-built Marine Travelift capable of handling the new generation of 60–80-foot catamarans, expanded boatyard space, and upgraded visitor amenities designed to rival the world’s finest resort marinas.

Government officials, industry leaders, and local dignitaries gathered to celebrate this milestone moment — one that signals both confidence in the BVI’s maritime future and recognition of Nanny Cay’s crucial role in it.
A Vision Anchored in Growth and Innovation

“This expansion reflects our ongoing commitment to improving facilities for the BVI’s marine community and strengthening Nanny Cay’s position as the heart of Caribbean yachting,” said Cameron McColl, Chairman of Nanny Cay.

“The new travelift and additional berthing will significantly increase our capacity and allow us to better serve both local and visiting vessels, particularly the growing number of large catamarans and superyachts operating in the region. This is more than a marina project — it’s a tangible step toward securing the BVI’s place as a premier global destination for sailing and yacht services.”
The new Travelift, one of the largest in the region, will handle vessels up to 165 feet — an essential step as the Caribbean continues to see a surge in multihull and superyacht traffic.

Miles Sutherland-Pilch, Nanny Cay’s General Manager, added: “We’ve seen increasing demand from larger multihulls and monohulls. This expansion was designed to meet that need head-on. The new lift and berths will enable us to manage more vessels efficiently and safely, all while maintaining the high standard of service that sailors associate with Nanny Cay. It’s an exciting evolution — not just for us, but for the entire BVI marine sector.”
Government Backing and Economic Confidence

Among the guests at the groundbreaking were Premier and Minister of Finance Dr. The Honourable Natalio D. Wheatley, His Excellency the Governor Mr. Daniel Pruce, and Deputy Premier and Minister of Environment, Natural Resources and Climate Change, Honourable Julian Fraser — reflecting the project’s national importance.
Premier Wheatley hailed the development as a cornerstone investment for the Virgin Islands’ future:

“We gather not only to break ground on this expansion, but to celebrate the beginning of an exciting new chapter for the Virgin Islands. This marina expansion represents the first of three phases in a broader transformation of the Nanny Cay Resort and Marina — a project that will create 91 new jobs and inject up to $40 million into our economy. It’s a declaration of confidence in our people, our maritime legacy, and the BVI’s position as a global yachting hub.”
Building a Future for the Next Generation

Beyond its world-class infrastructure, the expansion carries a strong focus on community development and education. Through a new partnership with H. Lavity Stoutt Community College, Nanny Cay will launch a marine training hub for local youth — providing hands-on education in marine engineering, operations, and hospitality.
Dedicated spaces within the expanded complex will also support the Royal BVI Yacht Club’s youth sailing and dinghy programs, nurturing the next generation of BVI sailors and maritime professionals.
Key Expansion Highlights
New 112-Slip Marina: Built to accommodate larger catamarans, luxury sailing yachts, and superyachts up to 165 feet.
Next-Generation Marine Travelift: Custom-engineered to service 60–80-foot multihulls and heavy displacement yachts.
Enhanced Boatyard Facilities: Upgraded infrastructure and expanded work areas to handle increased capacity.
Visitor Amenities: A new beachfront, upscale dining options, luxury pool, beach bar, and boutique retail village.
Education & Jobs: Partnership with H. Lavity Stoutt Community College to train young marine professionals; 91 new local jobs created.
A Legacy of Yachting Excellence

For decades, Nanny Cay has stood at the heart of the Caribbean sailing scene — a haven for cruisers, racers, and liveaboards alike. It’s home to the legendary BVI Spring Regatta and Sailing Festival, now approaching its 53rd edition in 2026, which draws yachts and sailors from across the world.
From hosting regattas and refitting round-the-world racers to serving as a hub for charter fleets and bluewater cruisers, Nanny Cay’s reputation for service, innovation, and community runs deep.

“The ongoing success of Nanny Cay became evident as our existing marinas outgrew capacity,” McColl said. “This third marina is essential to meeting demand — and ensuring the BVI remains the epicentre of Caribbean yachting.”
About Nanny Cay Marina

Located on Tortola’s south shore, Nanny Cay Marina is the British Virgin Islands’ premier marina, boatyard, and resort village. The property offers over 300 berths, full-service boatyard operations, a hotel, restaurants, and a vibrant village atmosphere that blends tourism, craftsmanship, and seafaring tradition.

Serving as a central hub for the Caribbean yachting community, Nanny Cay continues to drive innovation while staying true to its roots — providing safe harbour, expert service, and a welcoming spirit to sailors from around the world.

title: Last Week's Contest Unfurls: Decode the Thrilling Drama of the DF95 Autumn Series Week 9 at East Kent Radio Sailing Club
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Last Week's Contest Unfurls: Decode the Thrilling Drama of the DF95 Autumn Series Week 9 at East Kent Radio Sailing Club
summary: Experience the exhilarating thrills of the DF95 Autumn Series' ninth week held at East Kent Radio Sailing Club that was marked with audacious attempts and nail-biting finishes.
body: Week nine of the DF95 Autumn Series at the East Kent Radio Sailing Club ushered in a refreshing zest of fervent competition and undeniable skill. The sailing community reveled in the audacious spirit that rippled through the event, leaving spectators and participants alike with tales that will echo through the annals of sailing.

In Barton's Point Coastal Park, Kent, thirteen members navigated through temperamental gusts with eleven boats, quickly switching to B rigs after A rigs proved too tough to master in the weather. Experienced sailors Jim La Roche and Ralph Wilkinson took the helm as course setter and race officer respectively, sanctioning a day of unforgettable sailing experience.

The day's adventures unfolded with Rob Owens racing ahead to clinch victory in the fourth race, leaving Jim La Roche for second place in a see-saw battle with Dave Adams. Series leader Adrian Tomlinson had an uphill task fighting for positions in the middle until he turned the tide to snag the second place in the 5th and 7th races and besting his fellow sailors on the final race.

Highlighting the dynamic sailing landscape, Alan Hounsell and Spencer Pope sailed commendably, securing a series of fourth places and rounding off with a proud third for Alan. The day's events were punctuated with intermittent podium finishes, signaling the unpredictable and captivating nature of the sport.

Post the lunch break, sailing stalwarts, Dave, Adrian, and Rob maintained their commanding performances. Marking the climax of the series, Dave, in the dire need of victory to level off with Adrian, had four victorious finishes in the last six races, mostly with Adrian hot on his tail. Sum up this saga of brave sailors and thrilling race days, where every unpredictable twist became the stepping stone to glory.

title: A New Dawn for Foiling: WASZP North America Reveals Exciting 2026 Calendar
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A New Dawn for Foiling: WASZP North America Reveals Exciting 2026 Calendar
summary: WASZP North America breaks new ground in foiling with the launch of its ambitious 2026 calendar, heralding a bright future for foiling in the region.
body: WASZP North America is stirring attention in the foiling world by releasing an impressive 2026 calendar. With a pending World Sailing Certification, the launch of USFoil and the burgeoning activity in high school and college classes, North America is poised on the cusp of a golden era of foiling. The Official 2026 Calendar of WASZP North America is more than a lineup of events; it is a roadmap to an exhilarating journey that foiling enthusiasts can't afford to miss. The calendar unfolds an epic route from Florida to Canada, across the Pacific Northwest and California, onto Hawaii and rounding off the adventure back to Miami. The proposed season is filled with riveting excitement that surpasses anything the class has conceived before. The year kicks off to an energetic start in Jensen Beach, an emerging hub of North American foiling. The hub will serve as a winter training base for January and February which will see race teams gather and launch new high school and college programs. Steady winter breeze and an ever-expanding community make Jensen Beach an ideal location for early season training. According to Tyler Bjorn, North American Class Manager, this platform is where the journey truly begins. Fast forward to March, and the excitement shifts west along the Gulf Coast to Pensacola for a hallmark occasion - the International WASZP Games. This event promises to mobilize one of the largest foiling fleets ever assembled in the Americas, showcasing not only the abundant North American talent but also the seriousness of the pathways being carved out for regional sailors. Furthermore, the Games will help solidify the strategic partnership with America One Racing, bringing professional coaching, technical development, and athlete support to the forefront of the WASZP environment. As spring gives way to summer, the calendar unfolds a series of regattas and training opportunities, climaxing in Halifax, which has the honor of hosting the 2026 North American Championship.

title: Unveiling Hoshi: A Timeless Beauty in the Benetti Classic 115 Motor Yacht Series
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unveiling Hoshi: A Timeless Beauty in the Benetti Classic 115 Motor Yacht Series
summary: The esteemed 35.1-metre Benetti motor yacht Hoshi is making waves as it enters the market with generous volumes, graceful interiors, and a design that redefines expectations.
body: Unleashing the charm of its timeless profile, the 35.1-metre Benetti motor yacht Hoshi is up for grabs and it's sure to appease those with a penchant for luxury yachting. With a bewitching blend of design prowess and exceptional engineering, Hoshi, a part of the much-sought Benetti Classic 115 series, represents the epitome of comfort, style, and nautical competences.

Francois Zuretti and Marty Lowe were in charge of the yacht's interiors, bestowing the senses with light, elegant spaces. The main saloon is no doubt the yacht's place du jour, remarkable for its size on a 35-metre yacht. It is split into a lounge and dining area forward, with a bar interspersed between.

The crew quarters, built for six and with private access from the galley, ensure a discreet service. Another unique feature of the yacht is the sky lounge, which houses a large day head, making it possible for the area to double as an extra cabin should the need arise.

In the realm of outdoor spaces, Hoshi does not disappoint. The upper deck bestows a lavish social area with a bar and ample seating. The sundeck, completely refurbished recently, now boasts a Jacuzzi and expansive lounging areas. Both the upper deck aft and the main deck aft offer dedicated dining spaces, allowing guests to enjoy a varied ambience throughout the day and evening.

Over the years, Hoshi has seen substantial investment, including the installation of two new Zenoro generators in 2023, and an all-inclusive history of upgrades and refits, that add significantly to its value. The yacht features a major refit in 2014–15 valued at around €2,500,000, full engine and gearbox overhauls in 2017, Quantum stabiliser overhauls in 2018, and completion of her ABS A1 20-year class survey in 2020.

Hoshi is driven by twin 1350hp MTU diesel engines, giving a top speed of roughly 17 knots and cruising speed of 12 knots. Hoshi is currently docked in Italy, listed for sale at a compelling asking price of €4,500,000.
This yacht truly characterises a dream seafaring experience – offering a synthesis of grandiosity, comfort, and technical prowess.

title: Stunning Sanlorenzo Motor Yacht Anmax Sees Million-Dollar Price Reduction - A Winning Opportunity for Discerning Buyers
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Stunning Sanlorenzo Motor Yacht Anmax Sees Million-Dollar Price Reduction - A Winning Opportunity for Discerning Buyers
summary: The market is abuzz with news of a significant price cut on the 34m Sanlorenzo motor yacht Anmax, opening a window of opportunity for yacht aficionados.
body: The sleek and elegant 34m Sanlorenzo motor yacht Anmax has seen a massive $1M reduction from her sales listing, stirring up waves of excitement in the marine market. Now priced at an even more tempting $9,500,000, yacht enthusiasts are sure to find great value in this luxury vessel.

Anmax is proudly part of the illustrious Sanlorenzo SP110 series, a range cherished for its fusion of Italian flair, innovative design, and high-performance capabilities. The yacht's interior is expertly designed by Lissoni & Partners, while her streamlined and efficient exterior profile is courtesy of Zuccon International Project.

The yacht's living area demonstrates fluidity and thoughtfulness, revolving around a loft-style concept spread over two levels. This design masterstroke culminates in a spacious and comforting experience, reinforced by her impressive 8.2-metre beam - a feature that not only increases onboard space but also promotes stability while cruising.

No expense was spared when it came to ensuring Anmax's raw power and performance. Powered by three 2,000hp MAN diesel engines and sporting MJP water jets, Anmax reaches a top speed of around 37 knots and cruises comfortably at 27 knots. She boasts a fuel capacity of 12,000 litres, allowing an approximate range of 433 nautical miles – optimal for those extended trips out at sea.

Her Seakeeper 35 gyro stabilisers significantly boost comfort levels for guests during sail. Now, with her recent price reduction, Anmax stands as a star buy in the yachting world, promising unrivalled luxury, comfort, performance, and exclusivity.

title: 35.9-Metre Custom Yacht Jangada Embarks on Sea Trials; Delivery Slated for 2026
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: 35.9-Metre Custom Yacht Jangada Embarks on Sea Trials; Delivery Slated for 2026
summary: Van der Valk’s 36-meter custom yacht Jangada has started sea trials, bringing her a step closer to 2026 delivery.
body: Van der Valk, an industry-leading Dutch yard, has ushered in a new chapter in luxury seagoing, launching sea trials for the bespoke, 35.9-meter yacht Jangada. This grand vessel was launched from its prestigious Waalwijk facilities not long ago, catching the attention of enthusiasts and industry insiders alike. According to reports, she is on track for a 2026 delivery. With an owner famed for being a repeat client of the legendary Dutch shipyard, Jangada promises to join the sea’s elite ranks.

The majestic Jangada not only commands attention with its sheer size but also captivates with thoughtfully designed details. The owners requested an additional deck and higher levels of noise and vibration attenuation, prompting the shipyard to opt for a steel hull, aluminum superstructure, and extensive sound insulation throughout.

Interiors exude a contemporary charm with whitewashed wood details and boast of ‘architectural functionality’. The layout is family-centric; it features an owner's suite spreading across the width of the main deck and cabins on the lower deck, custom-built for the owner's children and grandchildren. Among Jangada's standout amenities are a dedicated gym, 2.6-meter-high ceilings, expansive windows and, notably, a flybridge positioned 4.5 meters long, 1.5 meters deep jet-stream pool.

Undoubtedly, Jangada, once fully complete and delivered, will become a true crown jewel of the high seas, demonstrating the innovative spirit and meticulous craftsmanship characteristic of Van der Valk. Meanwhile, BOATPro reports that Van der Valk has five more yachts in the pipeline — an assertion of the Dutch shipyard's dominance in the industry. Among these vessels is Project Zen, promising to be the yard’s largest custom superyacht to date. As the future unfolds, one can safely expect Van der Valk to continue crafting yachts that set precedence in impeccable design and luxurious sailing experiences.

title: Meet Numarine's New CEO, Patrik von Sydow, Pioneering the Turkish Shipyard towards Global Expansion
author: Old Sea Dogs
