As the new captain on deck, von Sydow will not only develop but also direct the vision, innovation, and execution of strategies at Numarine. The entire marine industry is abuzz with speculation and excitement about the new developments and advancements expected under the leadership of von Sydow.

Successful leadership is about setting a course, using the winds of change to help get there, and weathering any storm that may arise. This is what the new era of Numarine is all about, with von Sydow at the helm. The boat is ready, the crew is eager, and the seas of opportunity are vast. With von Sydow as the new CEO, it seems the only direction for Numarine is onwards and upwards.

title: An Exclusive Inside Look at the Impeccably Designed Admiral Yacht by Late Fashion Mogul, Giorgio Armani
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: An Exclusive Inside Look at the Impeccably Designed Admiral Yacht by Late Fashion Mogul, Giorgio Armani
summary: A 72-metre Admiral superyacht, the first ever designed by the late fashion icon Giorgio Armani, has recently been sold off-market, taking on the new moniker - No Rush.
body: An exemplar of nautical craftsmanship, the 72-metre Admiral yacht, initially christened 'Admiral Armani 72m' now goes by the name 'No Rush'. This sale occurred off-market, a testament to the luxury and exclusivity radiating from the vessel borne out of late fashion icon Giorgio Armani's discerning design brain. Both the seller and the shipyard were represented by Michel Chryssicopoulos from IYC, while the buyer was introduced by Royal Yacht International. Launched in May of the year, this nautical beauty made her official world debut at the 2025 Monaco Yacht Show, taking all attendees by storm. Commissioned by the dynamic collaboration between Giorgio Armani and Centro Stile of The Italian Sea Group (TISG), this spectacular yacht, comprised of steel and aluminium, showcases an ethereally satin gold profile, where geometric volumes alternate with curved surfaces in impeccable symmetry. Floor-to-ceiling windows punctuate the structure, allowing abundance of natural light to filter in and highlight the yacht’s grandiose aesthetic. The decor, strikingly minimalist in palette and finished by refined materials, is graced by hand-crafted finishes in a testimony to the designers' acute attention to detail. 'No Rush' is commendably spaced for up to 14 guests with a seven-cabin layout, each replete with creature comforts that cater to the guests' every whim. Each living area speaks volumes about Armani's flair for design, echoing in harmonious unison with the yacht's exclusive champagne theme. Relaxation and recreation spaces abound, with en suites decorated in exotic quartzites, private cinemas and lounges, bars, infinity pools, and sun loungers - all elements essential in crafting an unforgettable luxury sailing experience. Aesthetically pleasing and functionally state-of-the-art, the 'No Rush' is indeed a floating sanctuary, poised to traverse the vast oceanic expanse, leaving an indelible trail of elegance and serenity in its wake.

title: A Review of the 2025 Fireball Class: A Mashup of Innovation, Inspiration, and Intense Competition
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A Review of the 2025 Fireball Class: A Mashup of Innovation, Inspiration, and Intense Competition
summary: As the year 2025 wraps up, the Fireball Class has established itself as an incredibly exciting sailing class due to its innovative designs, heightened competition, and an exceptional community spirit.
body: As 2025 came to a close, a retrospective look at the Fireball Class season revealed an epic year marked by innovation, world-class competition, and the power of an energised community. Looking back, it was a year of renewed vitality, bolstered by the launch of a modernised Fireball design that redefined how the world saw this class. This updated design, which debuted in February at the Dinghy Show, retained the classic hull shape while incorporating enhancements to improve performance and overall accessibility. This revolutionary design fuelled renewed enthusiasm among fleets across the country and stoked growth and excitement throughout the season.

The National Championships, hosted in the picturesque Looe, Cornwall, confirmed the Fireball class’s status as a thrilling spectacle. The contest provided everything a sailor could wish for—testing conditions, tactical manoeuvring, and a vibrant social scene. Consistency and deft tactical moves allowed Tom Gillard and Andy Thompson to bag the National title, further highlighting the intense competition level within the Fireball world. Their victory was the culmination of an eventful championship that included last-minute sprints and nerve-wracking contests.

The crown jewel of the 2025 season was undeniably the World Championships at Lake Garda. The sheer magnificence of Garda offered an unrivalled sailing experience—thermal breezes, stunning mountain landscapes, and an atmosphere that resonated with the spirit of sailing. Stiff competition from 137 boats highlighted the championship's global appeal, but former Olympians Yves Mermod and Maja Siegenthaler proved superior. The duo provided a masterclass in precision, and their teamwork was impeccable. Their admirable performance sealed their World Title victory and earned them the respect of the Fireball community, rounding off what was an incredible season.

title: Discover How the Ainslie Family is Revolutionising the Future of American Sailing and SailGP
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover How the Ainslie Family is Revolutionising the Future of American Sailing and SailGP
summary: Nestled in the world of American Sailing and the notorious America’s Cup, Ben and Georgie Ainslie envisage a promising future for the sport.
body: An engrossing conversation ensues as Ben Ainslie, the esteemed founder and director of Athena Racing, delves into his aspirations for the future alongside his wife Georgie, former Sky Sports presenter and host of the podcast series 'Performance People'. Their lively exchange provides a rare glimpse of the behind-the-scenes action of the SailGP Grand Final series and the America's Cup teams. Despite bidding adieu to his CEO role at Athena Racing recently, Ainslie anticipates an exciting future.

With a no-nonsense approach, Ainslie remains committed to his teams, adhering to a simple principle - doing 'whatever is right for the team'. While he admits to the complexities of balancing his sporting career with the business side of things, the depth of his dedication is undeniable. He candidly shares his thoughts about his potential contribution, noting it's not singularly his choice, but rests on what is best for the team.

The Founding Partners, Ainslie enlightens, are groups who enrol during the America's Cup Entry period. However, late entries are subject to the unanimity of all board members. He proudly notes, “Ultimately, the teams, the Founding teams, will all own an equal share in that Partnership.”

The interview casts light on the desire amongst the 2024 America's Cup teams for a structural, befitting change in the Cup's organisation for the future. Ainslie recalls a thoughtful conversation in Barcelona, emphasising the need to deeply understand and harness the commercial potential of the sport. As they continue to ride the waves of incredible ventures, the Ainslies are undoubtedly steering American sailing into a buoyant future.

title: Aussie Sailors Turf: Clipper Race Fleet Overcomes World's Toughest Sailing Challenges to Dock in Fremantle
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Aussie Sailors Turf: Clipper Race Fleet Overcomes World's Toughest Sailing Challenges to Dock in Fremantle
summary: After one of the world's toughest sailing challenges, the Clipper Race fleet, carrying 15 Aussie sailors, docks at Fremantle, WA, to a grand welcome.
body: After an incredible 4,800nm race from Cape Town, South Africa, overcoming notorious winds of 50 knots, 'phenomenal' sea states, and frigid temperatures, the Clipper Race fleet has arrived at Fremantle, WA. Australia welcomed its heroes, including a Viictorian firefighter and a Perth doctor, among the 15 Australian nationals returning home.

The third leg of the Clipper Race circumnavigation is one of the most challenging routes taken on by sailors, sailing through the infamous Roaring Forties. This remote region remains an elusive voyage for many due to its extreme weather conditions and inherent perils.

Among the returning Aussies is Craig Head, a project manager from South Bunbury, Western Australia. As part of the winning team, GOSH, he spoke of the formidable yet exhilarating experience of racing the Roaring Forties. The sense of accomplishment echoing from his words, Craig exclaimed joyously about his well-deserved homecoming.

While not everyone can participate in this extreme sailing adventure, the Clipper Race offers an opportunity for the public to experience the thrill virtually by opening the hatches for free public tours of the yachts when docked.

A motley crew of engineers, directors, and paramedics from both Australia and overseas made up the victorious Clipper Race Fleet, demonstrating a wide swath of backgrounds converging over the love of sailing. Every sailor's journey paints a vivid picture of what it takes to overcome one of the world's most formidable races and to ultimately dock in familiar territory.

title: Turkish Wonder: The 30m Motor Yacht Ezgy Changes Hands in an Exciting Turn of Events
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Turkish Wonder: The 30m Motor Yacht Ezgy Changes Hands in an Exciting Turn of Events
summary: The sale of the bespoke 30-meter motor yacht Ezgy has been confirmed, showcasing the substantial appeal of bucket-list-worthy sea vehicles.
body: Injecting fresh impetus to the seafaring world, the 30-meter motor yacht Ezgy has changed hands, embodied the spirit of nautical adventure, and relished the thrill of the water. Notably, the transaction was navigated by Moravia's Sam Tucker, exhibiting his prowess in yacht brokerage. The contractual knot was tightly held by Marco Fodale of Fraser and Riza Cagdas Cakir of channel.R.

The yacht was born in the skilled hands of Turkish artisans at Blaundus Yachts. This sea behemoth, launched in 2021, has an extraordinary and angular look courtesy of Unique Yacht Design. Whether observed from afar or explored up-close, Ezgy boasts an innovative exterior that sets it apart in any marina. Its many visual highlights include a stunning master cabin on the deck bridge that opens aft to the deck, and a spacious 28-square-meter owner's cabin on the main deck.

This vessel’s standout features extend beyond its robust steel hull. The lower deck accommodates three separate double cabins, each more comfortable and private than the last. The full-beam cabin and transversely positioned bed cabins collectively allow for a grand party of 10, perfect for memorable voyages with family and friends. Supplementing the luxury are five additional crew members who ensure service excellence, alongside stabilizers that guarantee a steady and enjoyable trip.

Ezgy's interior, brought to life by Studio Urun Design, is a play in modernity and elegance. The layout flows seamlessly from the insides to the exterior decks. Complementing the vessel's contemporary feel are wood-planked floors in social spaces and soft carpets in cabins, with light streaming in from numerous windows.

One cannot overlook Ezgy's tremendous transom, which folds out to reveal a protected lounging area perfect for relaxation. This also serves as a deck for boarding water toys or swimming, approachable by convenient twin staircases from the aft deck.

Seafaring in Ezgy is an exercise in opulence, with the RINA-classed 290GT explorer yacht boasting a range of 4,050 nautical miles at 9 knots. The power is feasibly distributed via twin 650hp MAN diesel engines with only 200 utilized hours. Whether one prefers a leisurely cruise at 10 knots or pushing limits with a top speed of 13.5 knots, Ezgy performs commendably.

In conclusion, the sale of the Ezgy yacht underscores the tug-of-war in the yacht market that often leans towards premium sea vehicles. With its new owner, this awe-inspiring yacht will continue to chart water bodies, embarking on journeys that promise both thrill and tranquility.

title: Beat the Seasons with Four of the Best All-Weather Motor Yachts on the Market
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Beat the Seasons with Four of the Best All-Weather Motor Yachts on the Market
summary: Explore the versatility and practicality of four of the finest all-weather motor yachts available on the market today.
body: Savoring the joy of boating shouldn't be limited to sunny summer days. For seasoned and aspiring seafarers alike, there exists a range of all-weather motor yachts designed to withstand various conditions, extending the pleasure of boating beyond seasonal constraints. This article spotlights four of the finest:

The Hardy Mariner 25 is a classic choice. Built in 2001 and currently priced at £39,950, this compact motorboat illustrates how far boating as a sport and industry has evolved over the past few decades. Featuring a solid and practical interior design, coupled with a compact wheelhouse, the Hardy Mariner allows for excellent adaptability. With a convertible dinette, a galley, a head, and a quarter berth, the vessel offers compact comfort. It's equipped with a canvas for protection from unfavorable weather, making it a reliable all-weather option.

When it comes to performance, the powerful Yanmar 230hp diesel engine doesn't disappoint. Despite the potential option for a 170 hp Yanmar diesel, most boat users prefer the larger 230hp engine. This choice allows a comfortable 16-knot cruising speed and even attains over 20 knots.

Although the Hardy Mariner 25 might not be as spacious or luxurious as some other yachts, the blend of compact size, practical design, and a powerful engine make it a sturdy and efficient all-weather motorboat. It is the embodiment of the adage: 'good things come in small packages.'

title: Sailing Sensation Andrew Tarboton Conquers the Seas, Seals Stellar 2025 UK Skiff Circuit Win
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Sailing Sensation Andrew Tarboton Conquers the Seas, Seals Stellar 2025 UK Skiff Circuit Win
summary: Andrew Tarboton cements his standing as the reigning champion, dominates the dashing waves and wraps up a glorious victory at the 2025 Musto Skiff UK Circuit.
body: Andrew 'Turbo' Tarboton, the indomitable champion of the 2025 Musto Skiff World Championship, upheld his sterling performance, asserting his supremacy to secure the UK Circuit title. Adding another feather to his cap, Tarboton even snatched victory in the Southern Circuit, outpacing Robert Richardson in the final nail-biting event. Notably, Richardson, the second-place finisher at the Worlds, ended up bagging the silver in the UK Circuit, demonstrating the consistent performance of these top-tier sailors.

In the 2025 season, the exhilaration escalated across 14 events, featuring a blend of Southern and Northern series, the Inland Championship in March, and the UK National Championship at the renowned Hayling Island Sailing Club in September. To ensure excitement and fair competition, a weighted scoring system was employed, factoring in three circuit events as well as the unexcisable UK Nationals.

The season was testament to the sportsmanship and intensity that epitomizes the Musto Skiff UK Circuit, accommodating 62 competitors from 28 different sailing clubs across the UK. Though the turnout seemingly dipped from the previous year owing to the World Championship in Weymouth, the heightened competitiveness, embodied in seven separate winners across 14 events, reiterates the profound diversity and thriving spirit of the fleet.

As the curtains drop on a brilliant season of wave-riding and determined competition, it's time to gear up for another year of oceanic adventures and impassioned rivalry. 2026 holds promise of even greater thrills, embarking on the season with a flurry of exciting events and conclude at the grand UK Nationals at East Lothian Yacht Club, just outside Edinburgh, in September.

title: Breaking New Waters: How the 18 Foot Skiff Academy is Charting a Successful Course for Women in Sailing
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Breaking New Waters: How the 18 Foot Skiff Academy is Charting a Successful Course for Women in Sailing
summary: The Australian 18 Footers League is making waves with its innovative Skiff Academy program, leading to significant success for women in sailing.
body: The Australian 18 Footers League is to be commended for breaking down barriers and opportunities in sailing. Stepping away from tradition, the League made the groundbreaking decision in 2023 to launch an Academy, aiming to inspire more women to plug into the then 131-year-old skiff class. The first graduates, Emma Rankin and Bec Hancock, have since set their sails high, and are riding on the waves of success with the League's 2023-24 season fleet.

Rankin has carved her place in maritime history by becoming the maiden female skipper to clinch a victory in Race 2 of the NSW Championship. She prides herself on being a determined and skilled sportswoman rather than standing out on the strength of her gender. Both Rankin and Hancock have proven their talent, resolve, and dedication, cementing their standings as formidable contenders in a highly competitive field.

Before diving into the 18-footers, Rankin held an impressive track record, from being a national champion of NS14 in 2016 and 2017, the Australian Women's Match Racing National Champion in 2018, Formula 16 Catamaran National Champion in 2022 and 2023 to bagging the Hobie 16 Women's State and National Champion title in 2023. Despite her petite size and initial doubts, as she confessed in 2025, she never allowed any physical or mental hurdles to deter her objectives or cloud her determination.

Emma's transition from a successful past to a prosperous present in sailing 18 foot skiffs was made possible by the Academy's commitment to facilitate women's inclusion and, of course, her prowess in the field. As per her words, "The League has been a big driver in getting women into class. Without them providing the opportunity to get involved, I wouldn't be sailing an 18 today." Emma's story and her incredible success serves as a beacon of accomplishment, proving that the world of sailing is open to all. It's indeed a soaring symbol of determination, hard work, and the power of opportunity.

title: Experience the four elemental forces aboard Feadship's 76m Super Yacht Etherea: Rooted in Nature, Designed for the High Seas
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Experience the four elemental forces aboard Feadship's 76m Super Yacht Etherea: Rooted in Nature, Designed for the High Seas
summary: Feadship, the renowned Dutch shipyard, partners with FM Architettura and Studio de Voogt to unveil a 75.5-metre yacht concept named Etherea, echoing the symphony of earth.
body: Dutch shipbuilding powerhouse Feadship is on the industry's cutting edge once again with their unveiling of a fresh yacht concept - an epic 75.5-metre marvel dubbed Etherea. This design isn't solo work; it's cemented in a creative partnership between Feadship De Voogt Naval Architects and the Italian design masterminds at FM Architettura. The latter is a familiar name within Feadship's halls, having previously collaborated on several builds, including the Somnium, Zen and the newly minted Stella M. Etherea dances with the elemental - pulling inspiration not only from earth, fire, air and water, but also from the so-called 'fifth element' - ether. This cryptic force is often considered the thread that weaves through the other four elements, binding and connecting them. Etherea's design reflects this oneness, boasting a plumb bow, plenty of glass and sweeping lines. This results in a low profile, as eternal as the elements which influenced it, engineered to stand strong in the face of all seasons. In an evolution from previous designs, Etherea stands out as sharper, sleeker. Its split-level design makes for an open, bright sundeck not requiring a bridge deck, allowing generous living spaces within. The use of structural glass and skylights fill each deck with natural light, granting uninterrupted views. Etherea is a continuous flow between solitude and sociability, work and play. The designers took cues from California's natural beauty, adding a touch of muted, earthy tones and tactile materials. This fluid design harks back to the comfort of home, fostering an environment that doesn't feel temporary - it is a permanent residence at sea, 'a true residence on the water', as Feadship puts it. Finally, what's under the hood? Two Veth POD CR1250is aim to give Etherea a maximum speed of 14.5 knots and a cruising speed of 12 knots with an impressive range of 4500 nautical miles. Etherea is more than a concept, it's a vision. It's the spirit of voyage meeting the soul of home. It's Ethereal.

Returning for the fifth time, the Halls share a legacy steeped in deep kinship, tradition, and shared passion for the sea. This familial thread weaves through the 2026 RORC Transatlantic Race, reinforcing its stature as not merely a competition but rather a celebration of sailing.

title: The 2026 RORC Round Britain & Ireland Race
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: The 2026 RORC Round Britain & Ireland Race
summary: Fifty Years Around Britain: The 2026 RORC Round Britain & Ireland Race Announces Start Date and Open Entry An epic 1,805-mile circumnavigation returns — tougher, older, and more legendary than ever.
body: One of offshore sailing’s greatest odysseys is back. The Royal Ocean Racing Club (RORC) has officially released the Notice of Race for the 50th Anniversary edition of the Round Britain & Ireland Race, confirming that the 1,805-nautical-mile epic will set sail from Cowes, Isle of Wight, on Sunday, 9 August 2026.

Online entry opens 3 November 2025, inviting an international fleet of monohulls racing under IRC, multihulls, IMOCA 60s, and Class40 one-designs to take on one of the most demanding offshore courses in the world.

Half a century since its inaugural running in 1976, the Round Britain & Ireland remains the Everest of British ocean racing — a test of endurance, strategy, and raw seamanship that has forged legends for five decades.

The RORC Round Britain & Ireland Race is as brutal as it is beautiful. Spanning 1,805 nautical miles, the race circumnavigates the entire British Isles, leaving every headland, rock, and island — including the windswept Muckle Flugga at the northern tip of Shetland — to starboard.

Starting and finishing in Cowes, the route is a gauntlet of shifting weather systems, relentless tides, and narrow gates. Crews battle the Atlantic rollers off Ireland, the unpredictable North Sea, and the swirling eddies around the Channel’s iconic headlands — Land’s End, St Kilda, Fair Isle, and more.

Few offshore challenges combine this scale and complexity. From high-speed surfing off the west coast of Ireland to the bone-chilling fogs of the North Sea, every mile of the race demands endurance, precision, and nerves of steel.
The 2026 edition marks 50 years since the race’s creation — and half a century of daring campaigns that have defined the modern era of offshore competition.

First run in 1976, the Round Britain & Ireland Race has become a proving ground for both professional teams and Corinthian crews alike. It’s seen record-breaking multihulls, Olympic heroes, and determined double-handers take on the same wild, unpredictable course — united by the spirit of adventure that defines offshore sailing.

The current overall and outright record stands with Oman Sail – Musandam, the MOD70 trimaran skippered by Sidney Gavignet, who in 2014 completed the course in 3 days, 3 hours, 32 minutes, and 36 seconds. That benchmark still stands today — a breathtaking standard of speed and precision few have come close to matching.

Back in 2014, Ian Walker and Abu Dhabi Ocean Racing’s VO65 Azzam set the monohull record at 4 days, 13 hours, 10 minutes, 28 seconds — a performance that echoed all the way to their Volvo Ocean Race victory the following year.

“The opening 48 hours were brutal,” Walker recalled. “We were battered, blistered, and running on adrenaline. But the final twelve hours were even tougher — a drifting duel in dying breeze, knowing every inch counted. We didn’t tack once until the Solent — racing anti-clockwise because of an Atlantic storm. That race was extraordinary from start to finish.”
Richard Palmer – “The Pinnacle of Offshore Racing”

In 2022, Richard Palmer’s JPK 1010 Jangada, sailing double-handed with Rupert Holmes, claimed overall victory under IRC. “Just a full-on race with absolutely no let-up,” Palmer said. “You’re constantly on edge, mentally exhausted but completely alive. There’s nothing else like it. It’s the ultimate offshore test — tidal gates, weather systems, headlands — this race throws everything at you.”
RORC Racing Manager Steve Cole summed up the anticipation perfectly:

“The Round Britain & Ireland Race is one of the ultimate tests in offshore sailing. Its combination of coastal and ocean legs makes it unpredictable, tactical, and unforgettable. With the Notice of Race now out, we’re expecting a truly world-class fleet in 2026.”

The race is part of the RORC Season’s Points Championship, ensuring a mix of seasoned campaigners and new faces at the line — from fully-crewed maxis to adventurous two-handers, each with their own story to tell.
A Farewell to Sevenstar — and a Call for New Partners

Since 2006, the race has proudly carried the Sevenstar Yacht Transport title sponsorship, whose support has been instrumental in keeping this iconic challenge alive and thriving. That long and successful partnership has now run its course, and RORC is inviting new sponsors and partners to join the race’s next chapter.
For brands seeking to align with one of sailing’s most authentic, heroic events — one that combines heritage, endurance, and media reach — 2026 offers a rare opportunity.
Online Entry Opens: 3 November 2025
Official Website: www.roundbritainandireland.rorc.org
Start Date: Sunday, 9 August 2026 – Cowes, Isle of Wight
Course Length: 1,805 nautical miles
Eligibility: IRC Monohulls (Overall Trophy), Multihulls, IMOCA, Class40, and Double-Handed
Governing Rules: CAT 1 World Sailing Offshore Safety Requirements + Offshore Communications standards

The RORC Round Britain & Ireland Race is more than a competition — it’s a voyage through the soul of offshore sailing. It’s about the smell of salt spray at 3am, the whine of the winches, the constant hum of the keel through dark Atlantic waters. It’s the exhaustion, the exhilaration, and the quiet pride of rounding Muckle Flugga under a silver moon.
For fifty years, this race has defined the spirit of adventure. In August 2026, that legacy continues.

title: Discover the Delightful Eccentricity of the Sunseeker XS2000: A Bonkers Tale of a Novelty Powerboat
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover the Delightful Eccentricity of the Sunseeker XS2000: A Bonkers Tale of a Novelty Powerboat
summary: This is a voyage into the captivating history of the Sunseeker XS2000 - a powerboat that disrupted expectations and left a legacy in its wake.
body: Once upon a time, in the era of the 1990s, where Audi was known for its polite German saloon cars and hatchbacks, Sunseeker surprised the world by introducing the XS2000. With its origin rooted in the unexpected, this boat was a drastic departure from the builder's renowned fast, classy weekenders from the Hawk range, making it an entrancing case of delightful bafflement.

Designed by the famed Italian powerboat racer and designer, Fabio Buzzi, the Sunseeker XS2000 was nothing short of a wolf in sheep's clothing. Packed with up to 1,100hp and harboring a barely-civilized, outright racing mentality, this was not your ordinary weekend getaway vessel. Its functionality was so covertly tucked beneath its racing exterior that many would've been hard-pressed to guess Sunseeker as its manufacturer at the London Boat Show.

The Sunseeker XS2000, with its twin, hefty 420hp Yanmar diesel engines or a pair of 550hp Mercruiser petrols, proved its mettle by achieving 65 knots during the sea trial - and there was a potential for 5 knots more with fine-tuning! Imagine hitting the water in this stygian powerhouse, cutting through waves with an exhilarating rush.

Beneath its bonkers exterior and racing guise, the Sunseeker XS2000 nurtured a unique charm. Although its design could be polarizing, it is undeniable that it made a bold mark in Sunseeker's history. This extraordinary vessel was a tangible testament to the joy of risk-taking and the magnetic allure of audacity. The Sunseeker XS2000 was an oddity, an eccentricity, a wonderment - but above all, it was an adventure, and it's one that continues to captivate enthusiasts, pushing the boundaries of what a powerboat could be.

title: Antigua Bermuda Race 2026: The Return of the Atlantic Adventure
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Antigua Bermuda Race 2026: The Return of the Atlantic Adventure
summary: After a Two-Year Pause, the 935-Mile Ocean Classic Returns to the Western Atlantic Offshore sailors, start plotting your course. After a two-year hiatus, the Antigua Bermuda Race is officially set to return, with the fifth edition departing from Nelson’s Dockyard, Antigua, on April 29, 2026.
body: Timed perfectly to follow Antigua Sailing Week (April 22–26) and lead into SailGP Bermuda (May 9–10), this 935-nautical-mile blue-water challenge is ready to reclaim its place among the most thrilling ocean passages in the western Atlantic.

Run by the Royal Bermuda Yacht Club (RBYC) in partnership with Antigua Sailing Week, and proudly supported by the Bermuda Tourism Authority, Goslings Rum, and Fairhaven Shipyard, the 2026 edition promises to deliver everything the race has become known for — big seas, big miles, and even bigger stories.
From Caribbean Trade Winds to North Atlantic Swell

The course is pure offshore gold. Once the fleet clears English Harbour and slips past Barbuda, it’s nothing but open blue for nearly 1,000 nautical miles — a full week of ocean racing across trade-wind territory, then into the shifting systems of the subtropics.

Crews will trade the turquoise calm of the Caribbean for rolling Atlantic swells, long reaching legs, and nights lit only by stars and phosphorescence. It’s the kind of sailing that reminds competitors why they fell in love with the sport in the first place: self-reliance, endurance, and the quiet rhythm of a yacht surging through open water.
By the time they reach Bermuda, they’ll have experienced a complete ocean microcosm — from the warmth of the trade winds to the cool Atlantic air that greets them at the finish.
As one competitor put it: “This isn’t just a race. It’s a journey into the deep heart of the Atlantic.”
Voices from the Fleet: Hermes II and the Joy of Ocean Racing
Few boats capture the spirit of the race quite like Hermes II, a Canadian Pogo 12.50 that has now raced the Antigua Bermuda twice. Her skipper Meg Reilley summed it up perfectly in 2022:
“Every year I look forward to the Antigua Bermuda Race — and I think Hermes does too. She gets to stretch her legs and surf real ocean waves.

The first few days can be a sleigh ride — reaching in the trades, Hermes just coasts between waves, holding double-digit speeds with barely a sound. You set the trim, and she drives herself. You just sit back and enjoy the ride.”

That effortless rhythm — part power, part poetry — is what draws many to this race. Whether you’re a professional sailor or an adventurous cruiser, it offers a pure taste of long-distance ocean racing without the logistical demands of a full transatlantic.
One of the charms of the Antigua Bermuda Race is its inclusivity. It’s open to:
IRC and CSA Racing Yachts
Cruiser-Racers and Performance Cruisers
Superyachts
Multihulls
Classic Yachts
Double-Handed Teams

There’s even a CSA Motor Sailing Handicap Division, allowing yachts to use their engines for propulsion — with a time penalty applied — ensuring every boat, no matter her configuration, can enjoy the challenge and still post a result.
The race operates under World Sailing Offshore Safety Category 1, with additional offshore communications requirements — ensuring safety remains as much a part of the event as competition.
Race Chairman and RBYC Past Commodore Les Crane explained the strategic timing:
“The Antigua Bermuda Race is perfectly placed at the end of Antigua Sailing Week, when many yachts are preparing to head north to North America or east toward Europe.

With today’s high ocean freight costs, this race gives owners a safe, cost-effective, and highly enjoyable alternative to shipping their yachts. It’s a proper ocean passage — with competition and camaraderie built in.”

Originally revived as a feeder race for the 2017 America’s Cup in Bermuda, the course has become a natural migration route for yachts leaving the Caribbean at the close of the season. Its timing, distance, and festive start make it one of the most compelling offshore opportunities of the spring calendar.

No two Antigua Bermuda Races are ever the same. Some years deliver dream conditions, with powerful trade-wind surfs and record-breaking runs. Other editions serve up the opposite — long stretches of glassy calm where navigation, sail handling, and patience decide the winners.

Over its four previous editions, crews have faced it all — heavy squalls, smooth calms, tactical gambles, and moments of transcendent beauty. It’s that variety that keeps sailors coming back, year after year.
As Crane put it,
“The Antigua Bermuda Race delivers a true transatlantic experience, without the time, cost, or logistical burden of crossing the whole ocean.”
Finishing in Bermuda is its own reward. The Royal Bermuda Yacht Club transforms into a sailor’s paradise — a welcome sight of pink-hued sunsets, dark rum cocktails, and familiar faces.

There are dockside celebrations, awards ceremonies, and the kind of camaraderie that only comes after a week of shared ocean miles. Goslings Rum flows freely, tales grow taller, and the race’s unofficial motto — “Sail hard, arrive happy” — comes to life on the quays of Hamilton Harbour.

For many crews, the Antigua Bermuda Race 2026 will mark both a return to adventure and a bridge between seasons — the perfect conclusion to the Caribbean regatta circuit and a launching point for transatlantic ambitions.

Nine hundred and thirty-five nautical miles of open ocean, one of sailing’s most iconic routes, and the promise of both challenge and celebration — the race is back, and it’s ready to remind the world what blue-water racing is all about.

title: Debut of Galeon 620 Fly at Cannes: A Flybridge Decked with Features and a Vast Beach Terrace
author: Old Sea Dogs

summary: The Galeon 620 Fly, launched at the Cannes Yachting Show, boasts a unique feature set including three fold-down platforms and a vast beach terrace.
body: The Galeon 620 Fly premiered at the renowned Cannes Yachting Show, dazzling spectators with its remarkable features. Despite the distraction of the surprise reveal of its 430 Explorer sibling, the 620 Fly shone in its category. It is the first vessel of its size to offer three fold-down platforms, setting new standards for innovation in yachting design. One of these awe-inspiring platforms provides direct access from the owner’s full-beam cabin, promising an ease of on-board living that is incomparable. With two other platforms folding flush with the bathing platform, a beach terrace of substantial size is created. This transforming feature extends along the port side, merging seamlessly with a watertight door leading to the owner’s cabin, offering direct access for an invigorating morning swim. A third fold-down platform operates at main-deck level on the starboard side, doubling as an outside galley-counter bar, complete with plug-in stools for guests. The Galeon 620’s deck, both aft and fore, offers ample lounging space for guests and owners to enjoy the stunning vistas of the open sea. What sets the Galeon 620 Fly apart even more is its unquestionably spacious flybridge, which Galeon proudly claims to be the largest in its class. No doubt, its numerous seating areas, voluminous wet bar, and two-person helm affirm this claim convincingly. On-board comfort continues with three ensuite cabins, all accessible from a centrally located lobby. A VIP bow cabin offers a pleasing amount of natural light courtesy of large picture windows and a full-length skylight. Finally, the Galeon 620 Fly comes with an available crew cabin that is sizable and a separate single or double bunk cabin. With a top speed of 31 knots, the Galeon 620 Fly is an undeniable jewel among yachts and a dream come true for any yachting enthusiast.

title: Kai Marks-Dasent Outstandingly Seizes the Sylvester Simmons Young Sailor of the Year Award for the Second Time
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Kai Marks-Dasent Outstandingly Seizes the Sylvester Simmons Young Sailor of the Year Award for the Second Time
summary: Kai Marks-Dasent impressively claims the Sylvester Simmons Young Sailor of the Year award twice.
body: Kai Marks-Dasent, a rising star of the sailing world, has once again been awarded the prestigious Sylvester Simmons Young Sailor of the Year, courtesy of the SVG Sailing Association. This impressive accolade accentuates not only his extraordinary sailing ability but also his exceptional character, ingrained with service and leadership—core values that align exquisitely with the charitable Sylvester Simmons Foundation's mission.

Throughout the course of the year, Marks-Dasent emphatically represented his homeland, St. Vincent and the Grenadines, in numerous regional and international sailing events. These included prominent regattas such as the Barbados Youth Sailing Week, the Antigua ILCA Open, the UK ILCA Nationals and the Caribbean Dinghy Championships in his home waters of Antigua. Each performance was testament to his indomitable spirit and a clear statement of his desire to excel both for himself and his fellow countrymen.

In recognition of his growing influence within the youth sailing arena and his evident ambassadorial skills, Marks-Dasent was chosen to represent the national youth sailing community as a Baton Bearer when the King's Baton Relay landed in St. Vincent. Later in the year, he added another feather to his already impressive cap by being bestowed with the Prime Ministerial Youth Sailor of the Year Award, acknowledged for his substantial sailing accomplishments, commendable leadership, and lifelong devotion to excellence off the seas as much as on them.

Dr Kingsley Simmons, speaking for the Sylvester Simmons Foundation, praised Marks-Dasent's recent achievements as genuinely inspiring. He stated that Marks-Dasent indeed thoroughly embodies the virtues of service, bravery, and community leadership that were intrinsic to the late Sylvester 'Pepe' Simmons.

The Sylvester Simmons Foundation, established to continue Pepe Simmons' legacy of empowering young people across the Grenadines, recognises and rewards youths who not only excel in their chosen fields but also show a strong commitment to aiding others. Through initiatives like the Young Sailor of the Year Award, it continues to foster an enduring belief in opportunity, justice, courage and service to others.

title: Meet the Focus: An Icon of Seafaring Grandeur Finds a Distinguished New Owner
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Meet the Focus: An Icon of Seafaring Grandeur Finds a Distinguished New Owner
summary: The all-aluminium 46.6-metre Focus motor yacht has been bought, marking an exciting chapter for this buoyant example of aquatic elegance.
body: The purchase of the 46.6-metre marvel, the Focus, showcases a monumental triumph in the world of aquatic vessels. Known for its robust, cutting-edge motorboats and yachts, North American Yachts produced another masterstroke in seafaring technology and luxury. The all-aluminium Focus motor yacht sets the course for unmatched elegance and functionality.

In a sale facilitated by industry powerhouses Northrop & Johnson's Sean Doyle, Mike Finnegan, and Wes Sanford and Superyacht Sales and Charter's Neil Emmott, the exquisite vessel has found a new connoisseur to carry forward its legacy. The buyer, introduced by Burgess's Charles Jones, will now set sail on this beacon of design and functionality.

The Focus was meticulously designed to accommodate ten guests luxuriously. An upper-deck master suite offers bewitching elevated views, optimising the yacht's design. The remaining four cabins, a combination of queen and twin configurations, provide equally impressive vistas through their lower deck location. Each cabin comes equipped with its own ensuite, culminating in a hotel-like experience. And to host its ten-member crew, provisions have been thoughtfully made across the yacht.

The captivating narrative of luxury continues with the yacht's expansive partially enclosed sundeck. The forward section elegantly gifts occupants with a climate-controlled observation lounge offering 270-degree panoramic views. From hosting a bountiful Jacuzzi to a welcoming expanse for lounge seating, Focus is queen of outdoor living. Further enhancing the atmosphere, the aft deck acts as a perfect setting for dining under the stars.

Undergoing an extensive series of technical and cosmetic upgrades between 2023 and 2025, the Focus surely stands as a trendsetter in the world of long-range explorer vessels. With a 5,000-nautical-mile transoceanic range and hitting a top speed of 18 knots, Focus sails headfirst into the future of marine adventuring. And for those who have the privilege to step on board, it promises all the excitement of conquests on the high seas with a comfort akin to home.

title: A Burst of High-Value Sales and New Listings Energizes November Yacht Brokerage Markets
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A Burst of High-Value Sales and New Listings Energizes November Yacht Brokerage Markets
summary: November 2025 experienced a refreshing surge in brokerage yacht sales, marked by valued transactions and the introduction of fresh listings.
body: November 2025 witnessed a notable surge in brokerage yacht sales, driven in large part by high-value transactions and an influx of fresh listings. The presented data reveals 31 yachts were sold, with the combined going-total reaching an impressive €473.8 million—a remarkable increase from €329.7 million recorded from 29 sales in the same month in 2024.

The high-dollar deals included the sale of Lürssen's 55.5-metre Moon Sand for €65 million. The motor yacht, just out of a refit, was brokered by Edmiston and Cecil Wright, while Denison Yachting introduced the buyer. Among the 31 transactions, two were new-build yachts—the Maiora 42 Exuma and horizon FD80 yacht Hull 15, selling for €28 million and €6.5 million, respectively.

Additionally, 68 price drops were recorded in November, leading to a combined trim of €59.9 million off the marketplace. Notable price reductions included the 55-metre yacht Galene, which now stands at €35.5 million following a €4.3 million price drop, and the 49.8-metre Rocket, reduced by €4 million to a new asking price of €24 million.

title: Petros Michelidakis Reveals How boot Düsseldorf 2026 Aims to Attract New Comers, While Azimut|Benetti Group Enhances Owner Experience
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Petros Michelidakis Reveals How boot Düsseldorf 2026 Aims to Attract New Comers, While Azimut|Benetti Group Enhances Owner Experience
summary: Petros Michelidakis, director of boot Düsseldorf 2026, plans on reinvigorating the boating industry, while Azimut|Benetti Group unveils their new Service Division to bolster owner experience.
body: The director of boot Düsseldorf 2026, Petros Michelidakis, revealed his strategic plan to reinvent the love for boating. Thousands of potential buyers are evaporating from the boating industry each year, posing a significant concern that Michelidakis aims to address. His vision for boot Düsseldorf 2026 targets to open up the waters to new enthusiasts, thereby ensuring a continuous flow of newcomers into the exciting world of boating.

Meanwhile, the Azimut|Benetti Group is taking a massive step forward to enrich the owner's experience in yachting. The well-known company announced the launch of its new Service Division – a progressive move designed to support yacht owners in all aspects of their nautical journeys, from the boardwalk to the high seas. This initiative seeks not just to maintain but to strengthen the Group's commitment to providing unparalleled sailing experiences. Together, these strategic moves by industry leaders reflect an optimistic outlook for the future of boating, highlighting an enhanced experience for both newcomers and seasoned veterans.

title: The Majestic 27.7m Swan Sailing Yacht Strathisla Changes Hands
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Majestic 27.7m Swan Sailing Yacht Strathisla Changes Hands
summary: The grand 27.7m sailing yacht Strathisla, crafted by Nautor Swan, has found a new owner.
body: As the whispered news of a sailing giant's sale traverses through maritime circles, The 27.7m sailing yacht Strathisla has found a new guardian. The sale was managed by Thea Shaw of Nautor Swan on behalf of the seller, with Antonis Dimitrakopoulos of Praxis Yachts representing the new keeper. The yacht was claimed three months after its market is negotiated. The Strathisla is more than just a sailing yacht; it's a testament to unparalleled craftsmanship and luxury. Designed by the renown German Frers, she was constructed with carbon composite by the Finnish yard Nautor Swan and introduced to the open waters in 2009. It was part of the yard's regal Swan 90 series, marking another impressive addition to its legacy. Strathisla, till its last negotiation, was valued at a significant €3,300,000. The serene beauty of Strathisla doesn't stop at its exterior. The interiors are designed to accommodate up to eight guests in four cozy cabins, including a full-beam owner's suite, a VIP suite, and two twin cabins, all furnished with en-suite facilities. Additional accommodations are provided for a crew of four, ensuring a seamless sailing experience. The yacht doesn't stop impressing there; its saloon burgeons with natural light, adding an airiness to the dining area, amplifying the interior comforts. Geared for both cruising and regatta setups, Strathisla features an intriguing range of features including a hydraulically managed sailing and furling package, in-boom furling, South Spars EC6 rigging, and an extensive set of North Sails sails. Organized with a semi-raised saloon configuration, Strathisla is designed to cater to short-handed sailing. It also hosts a lift keel that brings down its draft to a manageable 3 metres, paired with twin rudders, and bow and stern thrusters to aid in navigation. Tucked away in Strathisla's hull is the powerful Volkswagen diesel engine and twin Northern Lights generators, enabling her to reach a top pace of 12.5 knots and cruise comfortably at 11 knots. Strathisla translates to a magnificently orchestrated blend of power, luxury, and design, clearly establishing why it's a prized jewel of the maritime domain.

title: Regaining the Glory of 'Windward', Supported by Barton Victory Blocks: A Dedicated Restorer's Journey
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Regaining the Glory of 'Windward', Supported by Barton Victory Blocks: A Dedicated Restorer's Journey
summary: The reappearance of 'Windward' is a majestic tale of a dedicated restorer using Barton Victory Blocks to bring a traditional lapstrake dinghy back to shipshape condition.
body: Every restoration journey has its own tapestry of intricate details and unwavering dedication. This is the same for Robert Starr, a celebrated author from the U.S.'s inland Northwest, who embarked on an overriding passion to restore his elegant lapstrake dinghy 'Windward'. Over the course of more than a year, the exclusive use of Classic Wooden Victory Blocks from Barton Marine, a trusted name in block manufacturing, was instrumental in actualizing his dream of refurbishing this classic watercraft.

A past life spent professionally racing cars around the globe found Robert longing for a more tranquil existence. As if aligning with this pursuit, he chose to introduce a 'wishbone sprit sail' into the new rig setup. The design logic allowed for one sprit arm to remain on the leeward side, ensuring a balanced performance in any wind direction.

Drawing inspiration from the Morbic 12 design, Robert envisages the addition of a removable bowsprit and a small jib to harness light winds effectively during his lake expeditions. Complementing this setup, Barton Victory 50030 Wooden Blocks will be employed to carry the load and retain the traditional restoration style.

The path to restoration is mainly defined by the gear one chooses. For Robert, the attraction towards Barton Victory Blocks was not limited to their functionality, but also the classical appeal they lent to his wooden dinghy.

It is gratifying for the Barton team to realise that their blocks played a crucial role in reviving a classic like Windward. Robert's boat restoration saga, filled with challenges and victories, represents the spirit of every mariner dreaming of taming the waters with a vessel they can proudly call their own.

title: Unleash the Power of Marine Radios with New Icom UK Knowledge Base Articles
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unleash the Power of Marine Radios with New Icom UK Knowledge Base Articles
summary: Icom UK expands its online Marine Knowledge Base, delivering three insightful articles to enhance marine communication.
body: Staying in tune with the aim of enhancing marine adventures, Icom UK has extended its online Marine Knowledge Base with a fresh batch of informative articles. Designed to deepen the understanding of mariners and organizations that utilize Icom VHF marine radios, these new pieces serve up a rich repository of vital information and tips.

First among the recent additions to the knowledge bank is an exhaustive exploration of the Squelch function on maritime VHF radios. It delves into the technicalities of how the function operates and offers useful advice on how to employ it optimally to ameliorate on-water communications. This piece will surely provide mariners an edge while navigating the waters.

The final piece of the trio helps unlock the full potential of Icom marine radios with the help of a Commandmic. This illuminating article unlocks the mystery of this accessory, shedding light on how it operates as an essential tool for managing and controlling the functions of an Icom fixed marine radio from secondary locations on a vessel.

Icom UK's marine VHF radio solutions are a beacon of hope in stormy weather, ensuring that no call for help goes unheard. Visit the Icom UK website to explore their full range of products and enrich your navigation and communication skills on the briny deep. The sea may be a harsh mistress, but with Icom UK, you're never alone in her embrace.

title: Heralding a New Reign: Lürssen Prepares to Debut its Grand 117m Superyacht, Boardwalk
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Heralding a New Reign: Lürssen Prepares to Debut its Grand 117m Superyacht, Boardwalk
summary: Luxury shipyard Lürssen unveils the 117-meter superyacht, Boardwalk. A majestic successor to previous projects, details of this vessel remain a tantalising mystery.
body: Upon the waters of Lemwerder, Germany, Lürssen, a renowned luxury shipyard, debuts the resplendent 117-meter superyacht, Boardwalk. Commissioned by an American owner in 2022, this ship's mysteries remain closely guarded from the public eye. However, the name provides a significant clue as it seems to be the successor to the 76.5-metre Feadship yacht called Boardwalk, which was marketed in the previous September. Before the Feadship, the owner possessed a Westport 164, also named Boardwalk, that has since been renamed Night Howl. The superyacht's initial images highlight its sleek white profile, a majestic sight on the water's surface. Boardwalk unfolds over six expansive decks that house two helipads, a generous beach club, and a large pool complemented by an adjacent spa pool on the aft deck - granting luxuries that ensure an exceptional on-water experience. Although the specifics of the new build are still under wraps, it is believed that the yacht prides itself on a colossal gross tonnage of 5,350GT and a sturdy suite of steel and aluminium construction. Boardwalk is set to rise in the ranks as the 20th largest yacht by length from the German shipyard, surpassing the renowned Ahpo by a mere 0.9 meters. According to BOATPro, we can anticipate Boardwalk's delivery to happen in early 2026. Despite the curtain of secrecy, one thing remains clear - great expectations are tied with the unveiling of Lürssen's 117-meter superyacht, Boardwalk. As the world waits with bated breath, a new era of luxury on the water seems to be on the horizon.

title: Another Impressive Sale for Mangusta as Second Oceano 52 Yacht Sees New Ownership
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Another Impressive Sale for Mangusta as Second Oceano 52 Yacht Sees New Ownership
summary: The enchanting Mangusta Oceano 52 yacht model has once again found a buyer, marking another dazzling sale for esteemed yacht-maker, Mangusta
body: The team at Camper & Nicholsons is all aglow with recent news of their sale of the second Mangusta Oceano 52, a deal brokered by the firm's new build sales manager, Francesca Ragnetti. This exquisite craft by Mangusta Yachts, seen as a beacon of Italian shipyard excellence, is docked for delivery in the year of 2028, with Camper & Nicholsons' New Build Division steering its construction.

Known primarily for their ultra-performing open yachts, Mangusta Yachts shocks and awes with the Oceano 52's curvaceous, long-range design. Promoting a sense of grandeur with open sightlines, artful glazing, glass gunwales and an assembly of technological adjustments, the yacht sails to new heights with enlivening exterior views. According to Mangusta, this waterside fortress emulates the atmosphere of a 60-metre yacht all within a 499GT, 9.2-metre-beam platform.

Overseeing the project to ensure its challenging goals are met, Camper & Nicholsons' New Build Division plays dual roles coordinating efforts from both contract to delivery and lending the prowess of its in-house technical and interior design teams.

Francesca Ragnetti, revealing the sale, gave voice to the firm's elation and commitment, recounting, 'We are delighted that the Mangusta Oceano 52 fully meets the client’s requirements. As always, we place client satisfaction at the helm of our operations and feel privileged to have built such a robust relationship offering a bespoke service to them. Our pursuit of perfection will aid in ensuring they savor each phase of the project'.

This celebratory occasion follows shortly after the first sale of the Oceano 52 line in October 2025, with delivery for the pioneer unit scheduled for spring 2027. With deals under their belt, Mangusta continues to navigate through nautical realms, setting the bar higher with every departure.

title: Step aboard the Lady Estey: The Grandeur of 67M Benetti B.Now Series Unveiled
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Step aboard the Lady Estey: The Grandeur of 67M Benetti B.Now Series Unveiled
summary: Get an exclusive first-look inside the second flagship of Benetti's B.Now 67M superyacht series, Lady Estey, a stunning vessel that combines opulence with innovation.
body: Congruent with its brand commitment to luxury and exclusivity, Benetti, the revered Italian shipyard, has recently unveiled an inside look at their latest masterpiece - Lady Estey. This astounding 67-metre model is the second in its highly-anticipated B.Now 67M superyacht series, known for their superior design and plush comforts.

Be it her bespoke, rectangular elevator, expansive guest corridors, marble and glass staircase or the two custom pools, Lady Estey sets herself apart from her predecessor with a host of personalized touches. Kudos to the British studio RWD for the exquisite exterior design and Sinot Yacht Architecture & Design for the sophisticated, Gatsby-style interiors.

The superyacht boasts of many standout features such as a full lower-deck gym, a wood-clad spa area replete with sauna, steam room, and treatment room for a perfect relaxation retreat. An opulent main deck saloon with an onyx-backlit bar sets the mood, while the upper deck dedicated entirely to the owner guarantees utmost privacy. The owner's suite offers panoramic views forward and direct access to a private terrace.

Two custom pools expand on the infinity pool concept, incorporated alongside unfolding gunwales on the lower deck, creating overwater balconies for a delightful experience. A spa pool on the hidden observation deck and a shallow reflecting pool at the bow on the owner's deck enhanced by a waterfall impress anyone on board.

In addition, the Lady Estey exhibits seven cabins, including two on the main deck. The guest suites maintain the same style and quality as the owner's suite, keeping the luxurious theme consistent throughout.

Benetti's sales director, Daniela Petrozzi, has noted Lady Estey as a significant representation of the shipyard capabilities, showcasing the possibilities for clients to realize their ultimate expression of the yachting lifestyle. Currently, Benetti impressively holds 43 superyacht projects on order or under construction including the custom 80-meter known as Project Iron Man.

title: Mazu Yachts Co-founder’s Tragic Loss: Legal Repercussions for Cargo Ship Captain and Crew
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Mazu Yachts Co-founder’s Tragic Loss: Legal Repercussions for Cargo Ship Captain and Crew
summary: Charges are brought against the captain and crew of cargo ship Arel 7 following the fatal collision with Mazu Yachts co-founder Halit Yukay.
body: A profound ripple has been sent through the maritime world, as Turkish prosecutors announce a potential sentence of up to nine years for the captain and crew of the cargo ship, Arel 7. This comes in the aftermath of a tragic collision with esteemed yacht designer Halit Yukay, co-founder of Mazu Yachts, which shocked the marine community earlier this year.

Yukay was reported missing by his family on August 4th during a voyage to Mykonos from Yalova, Turkey. Despite tireless search and rescue efforts, Yukay’s body was subsequently discovered at a depth of 68 metres, 19 days later. Arel 7 Towering at 92 metres, the Arel 7 was implicated in the incident, leading to an intensive investigation by maritime authorities. The ship's captain, Cemal Tokatlıoğlu, initially arrested in August, was charged with 'causing death by negligence’. However, he was later released in October, pending future court action.

More than just a successful enterprise, Mazu Yachts, co-founded by Yukay, is a name marked with passion, vision, and undying dedication to the sea. Founded in 2011, the yard swiftly gained recognition in producing seaworthy and economical chase boats. From the Mazu 82 to the flagship 132 DS, the entity carved a prestigious niche in the semi-custom yachting sector, winning numerous accolades for its innovation and design. A particularly notable achievement came for the 28.5-metre Waterlily, a finalist at the 2024 BOAT International Design & Innovation Awards.

Yukay’s untimely demise has incited heartfelt tributes pouring in. His deep-rooted passion for the sea, vision for design, and warm friendships left behind a legacy – reminding us all of the powerful human connection at the heart of the nautical world. The maritime community continues to wait for justice for Yukay and his family, even as his spirit sails on in the yachts he brought to life.

title: Exploring the Four Must-Buy Coupé Motor Yachts Lifting the Anchor in the Market
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Exploring the Four Must-Buy Coupé Motor Yachts Lifting the Anchor in the Market
summary: Experience luxury, versatility and impeccable engineering through this selection of top four coupé motor yachts, now available for purchase.
body: A stunning blend of aesthetic appeal and practical utility, the coupé motor yacht is a category of marine engineering treasures that has captured the fascination of sea lovers. But what distinguishes a coupé from any ordinary hard top sportscruiser? Simply put, it's all about the doors. A hard top sportscruiser, akin to an open sportscruiser with a built-in lid, offers a bit of refuge for the helm and cockpit. Conversely, a coupé upgrades this by enclosing the section below the hard top with aft doors, providing a flexible space that can be either heated or cooled.
To master the essence of the coupé, take a look at four remarkable models that are currently turning heads in the market.

Princess V55 (Built in 2021, Price: £1,399,000): This opulent coupé is a tribute to the evolution of Princess V models. A perfect exemplar of the lifestyle coupé, it ticks all the boxes when it comes to mixing day boating with longer cruising features.

With coupé yachts' blend of sophistication and seaworthiness, there's every reason to set sail on these motor yachts. If regardless of the weather, you'd wish to relish your cruising moments, or if you chase the thrill of seamless navigation and versatility, coupe yachts are the call of your adventure on the water.

title: Flagship Zeelander 8 Yacht Is Approaching End of Assembly, Set to Sail the Seas in February 2026
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Flagship Zeelander 8 Yacht Is Approaching End of Assembly, Set to Sail the Seas in February 2026
summary: The latest Zeelander yacht, a gem among the luxury yachts, is approaching the final stages of construction and due for delivery in early 2026.
body: On the precipice of completion and ready to make waves is the newest member of the respected Zeelander 8 yacht series hatched from the Dutch shipyard. Keeping high hopes for February 2026, the yard is punctual with the delivery time, reaffirming its commitment to perfection. This yacht, the brainchild of imaginative Cor D. Rover, is positioned to travel to the Mediterranean upon completion.

The fancy extends to the yacht's deck, featuring golden accents and glossy teak flooring. Devoted equipment for diving and other water amusement toys are also part of the package. This shows the commitment of the designers to the highest standards of luxury sailing.

Hailed as 'whisper-quiet' by its makers, the Zeelander 8 yacht holds an impressive record of producing less than 65dBA noise even when moving at its top speed of 30 knots. Powered by three sturdy Volvo IPS 1350 engines, it promises a sailing range of around 600 nautical miles at top speed and an astonishing 3,000 nautical miles when cruising leisurely at seven knots.

Accommodation is taken care of with five cosy cabins offering ample space for 10 occupants. A Porsche Design Seabob, diving gear sets for six, and a Williams Jet Tender 395 find a home within a dedicated tender garage on this innovative yacht, which exhibits a seamless combination of indoor-outdoor living through its 'targa' sunroof and retractable aft windows. The yacht enthusiasts are eagerly anticipating the arrival of this latest elite addition to the Zeelander family.

title: In-Build 60-Metre Alia Yachts Project Serenity: A Look Inside Its Striking Interiors By Vripack
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: In-Build 60-Metre Alia Yachts Project Serenity: A Look Inside Its Striking Interiors By Vripack
summary: Dutch design studio Vripack, in alliance with Alia Yachts, presents the impeccable interior designs of the in-build 60-meter yacht project, Serenity.
body: Design masterminds from the Dutch design studio, Vripack, have rolled out the initial interior renderings for Alia Yachts' 60-meter venture, Serenity. Now undergoing construction in the Turkish yard's facilities in Antalya, the cutting-edge yacht will be ready for the high seas in 2026, according to reports.

The project has summoned the esteemed team behind the 55-meter Al Waab, teaming up Vripack's genius minds with Alia Yachts and SF Yachts, the Dubai-based owner’s consultant. Crafted for an adept yachtsman, Serenity hails nearly two decades' worth of collaborative efforts and shared visions among the owner and SF Yachts .

In the words of SF Yachts' CEO Francesco Pitea, the working synergy between Vripack, SF Yachts, and Alia Yachts bring together 'craftsmanship, innovation, and family-centric design.' The result embodies a blend of technical prowess and warm familial sanctuary cut for multiple generations.

Vripack envisioned a high-gloss, highly tactile ambient space which holds true across the yacht., from the main saloon's polished Italian Calacatta marble flooring to the subtly embossed Middle Eastern patterns on the leather ceiling of the multifunctional sky lounge cinema. A series of transitional lights add a sophisticated twist: by day, natural light shines through full-height windows. By night, the bespoke lighting softens the atmosphere onboard.

Vripack’s interior design helps Serenity live up to her name, blending luxurious interiors that elicits warmth and a sense of belonging. The strategic use of materials like wood, leather, marble, and steel all combine to create a masterpiece, states Aykut Berhan, interior manager at Alia Yachts.

Berhan further expresses the efficient teamwork with Vripack, as their combined efforts deliver ingenious design solutions that combine elegance and functionality. Thus, Alia Yacht’s newest venture showcases the advocacy for high-quality team collaboration delivering precise, premium results.

title: 2026's Motor Boat Awards: Diverse Finalists and Cutting-Edge Innovation on the Horizon
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: 2026's Motor Boat Awards: Diverse Finalists and Cutting-Edge Innovation on the Horizon
summary: Nominations for the prestigious 2026 Motor Boat of the Year Awards have been unveiled, marking it as one of the most competitive line-ups in the event's history.
body: Hosting the spectacular Motor Boat Awards is esteemed magazine, Motor Boat & Yachting. With a judging process based purely on boat design, ability, and value for money, these awards have become an industry highlight for those itching to make a splash in the marine world.

The finalists for the 2026 awards have now been disclosed and, impressively, boats from as diverse locations as China, Turkey, Finland, Ukraine, Europe, and the UK have all made the cut. This compelling array reveals a fascinating snapshot of the global motor boating scene, revealing the innovative and distinctive efforts of manufacturers worldwide.

Adhering to a strict selection criteria, all boats are exhaustively sea tested by the seasoned judging team of Motor Boat & Yachting, and grouped into categories based on size and type, ranging from nimble sub-30ft sportboats up to grand custom yachts exceeding 80ft.

Headline sponsor Sleipner, a crucial player in enhancing maritime comfort, continue to champion these awards, with Garmin, Lumishore, and JL Audio sponsoring individual categories. Each finalist will soon be receiving an invitation to the glamorous awards ceremony in Dusseldorf, a night that promises an exciting reveal of the winners.

From sporty speedboats to luxurious custom yachts over 80ft, the variety and quality of the entries reflect the dynamism and creativity in the boating industry today. Unquestionably, the 2026 Motor Boat Awards bolsters the spirit of competition, celebrating the innovation and excellence that propels the boat making industry forward. Indeed, this gala is cause for keen anticipation among those drawn to the majesty of the open sea.

title: Historic Win for Borghesi’s All-Female Team at the Prestigious SB20 Middle East & UAE Championships
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Historic Win for Borghesi’s All-Female Team at the Prestigious SB20 Middle East & UAE Championships
summary: Charlotte Borghesi and her dynamic all-female crew claim victory in the renowned 2025 Wicked SB20 Middle East & UAE Championships, inspiring sailors worldwide.
body: Carving their own wave through history, Charlotte Borghesi and her all-women team snatched victory at the 2025 Wicked SB20 Middle East & UAE Championships in Dubai. Set against a backdrop of light to moderate wind conditions, the championship was hosted by the illustrious Dubai Offshore Sailing Club (DOSC), seeing 25 one-design SB20 sportsboats battling it out on the shimmering azure waters.

Borghesi, at the helm of Kidzink, led her crew of highly decorated sailors. Her team included double Italian 470 Olympic representative Federica Salvà, Lovisa Karlsson, the Swedish 470 Olympic bronze medalist of Paris 2024, and British Olympic gold medalist Pippa Kenton-Page from the Beijing 2008 Yngling class championships. Ranging from world champions to Olympic medalists, the impressive assembly of female talent was a testament to the prowess of women in the world of sailing.

title: The Unsuspected Relationship Between Acting and Leadership in the Nautical Realm
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Unsuspected Relationship Between Acting and Leadership in the Nautical Realm
summary: Exploring a unique perspective on leadership development, this article delves into how innovative learning experiences can transform one's approach in nautical leadership.
body: The journey of personal and professional development for many is often marked by a ceaseless quest for understanding of self and of limitless potential. We all yearn for peace, purpose, a clear direction. This is no different in the nautical realm, where leadership often takes center stage.

This thirst for wisdom and understanding often leads the relentless explorer off the beaten track. For instance, travelling, engaging with diverse cultures, dialoguing with individuals dissimilar from oneself - all serve to broaden perspectives. Expanding beyond the customary training offered in the fleet industry, these experiences can often bestow rich insights into one's leadership potential.

Interestingly, acting classes emerged for one individual as an unconventional, yet enlightening avenue to enhance leadership skills. Going to LA and exploring the realm of acting was less about becoming a thespian and more about embarking on an introspective journey of self-discovery, thus responding to a fresh challenge.

We often underexamine and over discuss the concept of leadership in the superyacht industry. The real essence of leadership, however, goes beyond just textbook knowledge and discussions. It's about the lived experiences, the subtle shifts in dynamics aboard a yacht under high pressure, and the quiet moments of reflection on the deck at dawn.

Challenging traditional methods of leadership development, and engaging in unconventional realms such as acting, can indeed offer valuable insights into more effective and enlightened leadership. Ultimately, it's about being a more awakened being, and the transformation begins there.

title: The SEA.AI Watchkeeper: Harnessing AI to Mitigate Navigation Risks in Boating
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The SEA.AI Watchkeeper: Harnessing AI to Mitigate Navigation Risks in Boating
summary: Introducing the SEA.AI Watchkeeper, an artificial intelligence-driven innovation designed to prevent catastrophic events at sea by spotting even the slightest potential threats.
body: For many seafarers, the most dreadful experiences involve collisions. Whether it's an unexpected encounter with another vessel, an unnoticed swimmer in the open water, or an encounter with a semi-submerged log, these nightmares can turn into reality with just a moment's distraction. Enter the SEA.AI Watchkeeper, an innovative and intuitive solution engineered to alleviate these fears.

The SEA.AI Watchkeeper, a virtual watchkeeper, never rests. Using cutting-edge artificial intelligence, it stays alert for any impending collision threats and issues timely alerts. Leveraging a robust combination of highly sensitive low-light and thermal vision cameras, it can detect objects that even advanced radar and AIS systems could overlook. It can identify potential hazards from a database housing over 18 million images of various identified items, notifying the skipper with both visual and audio alerts.

Yet, the size and affordability do not compromise upon functionality. The SEA.AI Watchkeeper sees further and with greater accuracy than human vision, even under varied conditions. Covering the area from just in front of the boat to the horizon with a 135-degree field of vision, it can flag potential obstacles as small as a pot marker or a human head. Even creatures as majestic as passing whales or inconspicuous pieces of semi-submerged driftwood do not escape its keen observation.

Furthermore, the Watchkeeper's performance is adaptable with the fitted camera's specifications. For instance, the basic Watchkeeper Lite model comes with a 3840 x 2160 pixel colour camera, capable of identifying a large ship, motor, or sailing boat and even smaller objects like jet skis or RIBs at significant distances.

Setting a new benchmark in safety, the SEA.AI Watchkeeper is more than just an upgrade. It's a game-changer bringing a newfound peace of mind to all boating enthusiasts, regardless of the nature of their voyage or the size of their vessel.

title: Breakthrough Victory at the 2025 SB20 Middle East Championships: Borghesi's All-Female Crew Seizes the Title
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Breakthrough Victory at the 2025 SB20 Middle East Championships: Borghesi's All-Female Crew Seizes the Title
summary: Charlotte Borghesi's all-women team steal the show at the 2025 Wicked SB20 Middle East & UAE Championships, enhancing the profile of women in the world of sailing.
body: Charlotte Borghesi’s all-female team made waves in the sailing world with an outright victory at the prestigious 2025 Wicked SB20 Middle East & UAE Championships. The event, which hosted a fleet of 25 one-design SB20 sportsboats, played out from the Dubai Offshore Sailing Club (DOSC) across three days that tested skillsets and adaptability in varying wind conditions.

Borghesi was joined by fellow sailing prodigies, including two-time Italian 470 Olympic representative Federica Salvà, Swedish 470 Olympic bronze medallist from Paris 2024, Lovisa Karlsson, and British Olympic gold medallist from Beijing 2008, Pippa Kenton-Page. This powerhouse line-up certainly helped the team's chances. But it wasn’t just about the impressive crew. The skipper’s strategic prowess and decisive moves significantly contributed to the decisive victory.

But it wasn't just the women of the Borghesi family gracing the winners' podium. Paolo Borghesi, Charlotte's husband, and their young son William both showed their own prowess in the water, finishing third and sixth overall respectively. The family's success cemented the Borghesi name as formidable competitors within the world of SB20 racing.

Such a significant result is not just a victory for Borghesi and her crew, but also a stride forward in furthering gender diversity within the realm of sailing. It is hoped that this will pave the way for more women to helm their own victories in the sport’s future.

title: Revealing the Best Practices and Potential Pitfalls of Risk Mitigation Measures on Superyachts
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Revealing the Best Practices and Potential Pitfalls of Risk Mitigation Measures on Superyachts
summary: The tragic loss of crew member Paige Bell on superyacht ‘Far From It’ has prompted a call for significant strategic and cultural changes within the superyacht industry.
body: The tragic demise of Paige Bell, a crew member on board the M/Y 'Far from It' has sparked an urgent examination of the safety practices within the superyacht sector. This incident should not simply be logged as history; instead it should catalyze essential changes to enhance crew safety and welfare on-board.

Notably, Captain Rod Hatch's commentary has been put under the microscope, revealing both its insights and biases. Captain Hatch's credentials lend gravity to his observations but the defensive tone may prevent the industry from assimilating the crucial lessons hidden in this tragedy.

Bridging the gap between pompous rhetoric and ground reality can propel the industry towards a secure, resilient environment for both its crew and its reputation. Citing systems vulnerabilities as a recognition of crisis and not criticism, will allow the yachting industry to address and rectify systemic shortcomings.

Captain Hatch, in his narrative, draws a halo around the superyacht industry, asserting the infrequency of violent crimes and the coveted nature of crew life. However, this 'exceptionalism' narrative potentially obscures inherent issues such as harassment, power imbalances, fear of dismissal for reporting incidents, and a rigid hierarchy within operations.

Additionally, framing legislative reforms as naive while calling for cultural and educational improvements oversimplifies the complex nature of safety issues on superyachts. Both strategies are mutually supportive—not contradictory. Establishing a robust safety culture demands enforcement of current regulations, adherence to best practices, secure pathways for incident reporting, real-time feedback on safety indicators, and an inherently ethical crew.

Moving forward, a more balanced viewpoint which reconciles the industry exceptionalism with its inherent issues is crucial. This tragedy provides a poignant reminder of the need for improvements in crew safety measures and a collective push for a resilient and stronger superyacht industry.

title: Journey of Mohammed Al Barwani: Selling Oceanco, Reviving Turquoise Yachts and Redefining Yachting in Turkey

body: Dr Mohammed Al Barwani is an influential figure in the superyacht industry, renowned for his strategic purchases and the revival of conglomerates. In 2014, Dr Barwani acquired a majority stake in Proteksan Turquoise and subsequently rebranded the company as Turquoise Yachts, marking his second foray into the realm of superyachts. This decision came on the heels of his acquisition of the esteemed Dutch shipyard, Oceanco, in 2010.

However, recent times witnessed a shift in his business strategy, marked by Oceanco's sale to American tech magnate Gabe Newell. This move serves to free Dr Barwani of his obligations at Oceanco and allows him to channel his energies to the operations and strategic direction of Turquoise Yachts.

The change in Dr Barwani's focus coincides with a critical juncture in the yachting industry and is likely to carve a distinctive path in the landscape of yachting. With a keen business acumen and innovative ideas, Dr Barwani's journey has just begun, despite his impressive yachting legacy. His ambition for the yachting sector in Oman is strongly felt, and is a testament to his dedication to not just the growth of a company or industry, but the passion for yachts themselves.

title: A Spectacular Conclusion to the Hamble Winter Series 2025; Sailing Grand Slam Unveils Planned Olympic-Class Series for 2026
