title: Grace Under Pressure: How the Port Phillip Women's Championship empowers female sailors and fosters unity on the high seas
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Grace Under Pressure: How the Port Phillip Women's Championship empowers female sailors and fosters unity on the high seas
summary: The Port Phillip Women's Championship Series 2025-2026 is setting sail to create opportunities for aspiring female keelboat sailors, fostering unity and competitive spirit in equal measure.
body: As summer kisses the horizon, excitement courses through the veins of every sailor, poised for the return of the thrilling Port Phillip Women's Championship Series 2025-2026. This championship serves as a beacon of opportunity and unity for all aspiring women keelboat sailors ready to take the helm. Harnessing the spirit of sisterhood, the championship embodies the essence of empowerment and competitive kinship.

Since 2013, this unique series brings together five keelboat clubs from the bay's apex, each putting their signature spin on race day events across the 10-race series. It is a platform for female sailors to marshal their crew and showcase their mettle against larger fleets. Leading the initial charge is Hobson's Bay Yacht Club (HBYC) with the famed Shirley Freeman Trophy event. As a century-old testimony to women's inclusion in sailing, HBYC's legacy continues to inspire and advance the cause of the series.

Through the lens of Burke's journey owning the Defiance 30 'Lanncoorie', we see the championship's power to create opportunities for women. Her strategy of building a team of greenhorn women sailors and practicing together in actual race conditions bore fruit, securing them runner-up and then victors in the Australian Women's Keelboat Regatta (AWKR) Div2 (Performance Handicap) in June 2025.

Through tales of camaraderie, spirit, and successful endeavours, the Port Phillip Women's Championship illustrates why it is seen as an avenue for females to sharpen their sailing skills while fostering unity. The Championship offers an experience that illuminates the resilience, talent, and passion of women sailors, compelling others to cast their sails and voyage ahead.

title: Young Sailors Brave Winter Conditions at IOCA Optimist Championships in Rutland
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Young Sailors Brave Winter Conditions at IOCA Optimist Championships in Rutland
summary: Enthusiasm and competitive spirit compelled 128 Optimists to take part in the IOCA Optimist Winter Championships, amid the challenging winter conditions at Rutland Sailing Club.
body: Overcoming the bracing chill of British winter, 128 young sailors gathered at Rutland Sailing Club for the IOCA Optimist Winter Championships. Despite the weather playing spoilsport, their tenacity and passion for sailing were anything but dampened. With winds between 10-15knots, the competitive sailors embarked onto the water, ready for an exciting weekend of 'snakes and ladders' racing.

A fleet of 93 boats made up the Main Fleet, with the racing committee headed by Nigel Biggs. Laszlo Drummond stood out on the first day with three 1st place finishes. The competition grew intense on the second day as racers struggled for dominance on the leaderboard. Jonny Rogers edged out Laszlo Drummond by 2 points to take the first overall spot, while Sean Di Salle secured the third. In separate categories, Lizzie Hudson was the top girl, Archie Dowling took the under-10, and Theo Fox the under-11 spots.

The smallest fleet, the Coached Regatta, comprised four enthusiastic sailors, combining training and racing. Coached by Lola Andrews, their determination was notable. Running on 'hot chocolate power', they persevered on the water even as the other fleets retired, keen on improving their racing skills. Fletch Sheely won this category, followed by William Zhang, Zoe Grundy and Amina Melhem.

Hats off to Rutland Sailing Club for providing excellent facilities and superb race management, ensuring fun and competitive races despite the wet weather. Contributions from parents, sailors, and the organising committee truly made this event a success. This competition serves as a testament to the resilience, dedication, and pure love for sailing embedded in each competitor.

title: BROC Gathers in Bermuda to Strategically Plan for Their Blockbuster 100th Anniversary Celebration
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: BROC Gathers in Bermuda to Strategically Plan for Their Blockbuster 100th Anniversary Celebration
summary: The Bermuda Race Organising Committee (BROC) convened in Hamilton, Bermuda for their annual meeting centred around planning the centenary of the iconic ocean race.
body: The Bermuda Race, a marquee event in the global sailing calendar, is turning a century old. In preparation for the grand celebration, the Bermuda Race Organising Committee (BROC) has held its annual meeting at the RBYC in Hamilton. This gathering served up a vibrant mixture of face-to-face and virtual brainstorming sessions, packed with energy and anticipation for the forthcoming anniversary.

"The Bermuda Race is always an extraordinary spectacle," enthused Race Chair, Andrew Kallfelz. "We are amplifying that resonance in 2026 to mark a century of partnership and camaraderie embodying the quintessence of yacht racing. Every BROC member came equipped with brilliant ideas and spirited fervour to make this race a crowd-puller for posterity."

As we sail towards the end of 2025, anticipation for the next Bermuda Race is heightening. The formidable fleet is now over 100 strong. Alongside the illustrious yachts, there is a mix of family and community-based teams. Registration is now open and set to increase from December 19, prompting enthusiasts to secure their spots early.

This anniversary race promises not only competitive adventure on the high seas but also a celebration of a century-old international partnership, camaraderie, and history-making moments - a true embodiment of the spirit of sailing.

title: Human Spirit Soars As Rolex Sydney Hobart Yacht Race Marks Its 80th Edition
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Human Spirit Soars As Rolex Sydney Hobart Yacht Race Marks Its 80th Edition
summary: The 80th edition of the Rolex Sydney Hobart Yacht Race celebrates a legacy of courage, endurance, and remarkable human achievement.
body: Marking its 80th edition, the Rolex Sydney Hobart Yacht Race is a testimony to human endurance, resilience and a proud milestone in sailing history. Since it first began in 1945, it has surpassed being just a sailing event to become a global icon imprinted in maritime and sporting history.

Rolex, the title sponsor since 2002, has forged a cornerstone partnership with the race organizer, the Cruising Yacht Club of Australia. This partnership is part of the Swiss watchmaker’s near 70-year proactive involvement with yachting.

The 2025 race boasts a lineup of over 130 yachts, including the world's leading maxi yachts and former race winners, creating one of the largest and most eagerly anticipated events this century. The race continues to draw international sailing talent to its irresistible appeal.

The story of the Rolex Sydney Hobart Yacht Race started from a humble invitation to a cruise to Hobart in 1945. A simple response from British Navy Captain John Illingworth, 'I will, if you make a race of it,' triggered a tradition that's lived on for 80 years.

title: Sail into Luxury: The 29m Ferretti Yacht ‘Together’ hits the Market!
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Sail into Luxury: The 29m Ferretti Yacht ‘Together’ hits the Market!
summary: The recently-delivered 29-metre Ferretti 940 motor yacht 'Together' is up for sale, promising superior comfort, design, and functionality with no wait time.
body: Say hello to 'Together', a 29-metre Ferretti 940 motor yacht, the latest to hit the market. Crafted at Ferretti’s Cattolica facility, 'Together' offers the prospective seafarer an opportunity to own a modern, state-of-the-art yacht without the customary rigmarole of new builds, refit decisions, or wait times.

This epitome of sea luxury was birthed into the world in June 2025, and has since floated majestically into the Cannes Yachting Festival, turning more than a few heads. Valued at a cool €8,990,000, the vessel comes with an extended warranty valid through July 2027.

Ferretti's classic yachts are renowned for their beautiful fusion of interior volume and practical layout, and 'Together' is no exception. Blessed with a gross tonnage of 120GT, she strikes the ideal balance between operational simplicity and the high degree of comfort expected of yachts in this size bracket.

The exterior spaces are designed with adaptability and comfort in mind. They offer lounging and dining options, a hydraulic swim platform that can serve as a jetski launch, and a garage equipped with a Williams SportJet 435 tender. Coupled with the yacht's superior engine capabilities, capable of top speeds of 29 knots, 'Together' harmoniously blends practicality, elegance, and next-level performance to offer a truly unique offering.

In a nutshell, 'Together' is the perfect choice for someone seeking the thrill of navigating diverse cruising regions with comfort, style, and elite functionality. Sail into the world of luxury yachting with 'Together'!

title: Thrilling Start to the J/70 Championship and Tenzor International Cup in Turkey: A Beacon of Sailing Excellence
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Thrilling Start to the J/70 Championship and Tenzor International Cup in Turkey: A Beacon of Sailing Excellence
summary: The J/70 Turkish Championship and the Tenzor International Cup have officially begun amid an atmosphere of electric anticipation and competitive spirit in Turgutreis, Turkey.
body: A buzzing energy swept across D Marine Turgutreis as the J/70 Turkish Championship and Tenzor International Cup officially set sail. The grand opening ceremony combined with the skipper briefing marked the final leg of the Turkey Tour and the launching pad for the Tenzor International Cup Winter Series. With the event growing annually, great teams gathered to contest one another in a battle of sailing prowess, technique, and teamwork.

An impressive fleet of 20 J/70s sprung into action on the first race day, with the Race Committee (RC) team swiftly setting up the race course. A major milestone was the debut of the Vakaros system in Turkey, utilised to establish the starting line – a pioneering step for sailing in the country. The Vakaros devices were seamlessly integrated with TAYK's robotic buoys, offering a smooth and successful boat race execution.

The Corinthian’s teams, led by the Ayaz Jr team, made a solid start with the initial win, MYSK and Eker Efsane Yogurt tailing close. The same course was prepared for the immediate inception of the second race, which also concluded without a hitch. The action was palpable as Bogatyrs maintained their lead against the fleet, going pole-to-pole with Tenzor Team who secured a second-place finish in a thrilling encounter.

The exhilarating start to this high-stakes tournament promises exciting days ahead. Each team's sterling exhibition of sailing acumen and the cutting-edge technology debut have set the tone for an unforgettable series, cementing Turkey's reputation as an international sailing hub.

title: Global Yacht Technology Debuts Iconic Trimaran Yacht Design Known as Anahita
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Global Yacht Technology Debuts Iconic Trimaran Yacht Design Known as Anahita
summary: Global Yacht Technology, French innovators in the yachting industry, proudly unveils Anahita - a groundbreaking 31-metre trimaran yacht.
body: French engineering pioneers, Global Yacht Technology continues breaking boundaries with the introduction of Anahita, their new 31-metre trimaran yacht model. The Brittany-based company took the stage at Metstrade to reveal their latest creation, adding that imminently, this limited-production masterpiece will sail the high seas with the first unit already under construction.

Onboard, Anahita boasts 123 square metres of fully customisable living space. Internal features include a panoramic owner's suite with direct deck access, crew quarters, and adaptable living areas tailored to clients' preferences. The exterior design incorporates a large cockpit, expansive decks, and forward trampolines, or the 'forward deck garden marine,' summing up to 160 square metres. The conception of the trimaran owes a significant inspiration to the water strider insect. VPLP's Yann Prummel elucidated that mirroring the speed, stability, and precision of the water strider gave Anahita her unique profile. As Prummel likened the yacht to a wind-driven vessel, his design aimed to capture the tension and fluidity characteristic of a Formula 1 or aviation fuselage. In the end, Anahita emerges victorious, balancing the sleekness of a racing yacht with the luxury of a cruising yacht, possessing a unique identity.

Anahita's performance expectations transpire an optimistic picture with cruising speeds projected at 25 knots, capable of conquering the Atlantic in just six days. Additionally, a shallow two-metre draft enables exploration of secluded, preserved anchorages. This triumphant unveiling of Anahita by Global Yacht Technology signifies a pivotal moment in the evolution of yacht design.

title: Palumbo Superyachts Announces Successful Sale of Second Unit of the Exquisite 28m X90 Fast Model
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Palumbo Superyachts Announces Successful Sale of Second Unit of the Exquisite 28m X90 Fast Model
summary: Palumbo Superyachts' brand, Extra Yachts, earns another feather in its cap with the sale of its second 28m X90 Fast model.
body: Extra Yachts, a subsidiary of the illustrious Palumbo Superyachts, has reported the successful sale of its second 28-metre X90 Fast yacht model. Upon its anticipated delivery, this sleek and magnificent yacht will find its place alongside 'Iva', the first unit from the X90 Fast series, launched in July. Built and styled by the revered Italian Agon Studio, the yacht showcases a harmonious blend of sporty lines and forward projecting design, delivered in a dark-toned Glass-Reinforced Plastic (GRP) model. The second unit was brokered by Alina Emerly of Aberton Yachts. Offered customers the choice of having the galley situated either amidships or aft, the onboard layout of the X90 Fast also presents an optional second helm station on the sundeck. While the layout of the first unit - 'Iva' – that made a splash at the Cannes Yachting Festival in September is known, the details of the second unit's layout is yet to be unveiled. The dazzling yacht offers a spacious and versatile sundeck with modular areas primed for luxurious lounging or fine dining. The yacht boasts a revolutionary three-tiered stern which provides flawless accessibility from the main deck aft to the swim platform. With an expansive aft sun pad, the yacht also features a garage ingeniously designed to house a four-meter jet tender. Below deck, the yacht offers sumptuous living quarters across four en suite cabins including a master cabin nestled amidships, which makes superb use of the yacht's 7.4-metre beam. An additional accommodation for a four-member crew is also provided. The interiors are oozing with warmth, contemporary refinement, and luminosity, crafted to promote a tranquil experience at sea. Propelled by a trio of 1,000 hp Volvo Penta engines, the yacht flies on water at a top speed of 26 knots and cruises comfortably at 21 knots. A range of approximately 1,000 nautical miles is attainable at 12 knots. In addition to the sale of the X90 Fast, Extra Yachts has three more units in the pipeline from its 30-metre Extra 100 Triplex series.

title: Unveiling the Next Chapter in Sailing Luxuries: Wally’s Updated Wallywind110 All-Carbon Sailing Yacht
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unveiling the Next Chapter in Sailing Luxuries: Wally’s Updated Wallywind110 All-Carbon Sailing Yacht
summary: Making waves this summer is Wally's second high-performance wallywind110 sailing yacht, pushing out the envelope further in space, comfort, and speed.
body: Making a splash this summer, the second iteration of the 33.4-metre wallywind110 set sail. Following the successful launch of Galma, the first hull of its range, attention turned to this offering's evolution at the Monaco Yacht Show 2025. Designed as a progression for seasoned owners transitioning from a 24 to 28-metre sailing yacht, the wallywind110 combines enhanced personal space, opulence, and potential without jeopardizing performance.

Vittorio Blengini, the Ferretti Group's custom business sales director, extols the yacht’s unique balance of form and function. Hull number two, like its predecessor, continues the tradition of passionate investment in design and construction, eschewing shortcuts. This vessel's ethos is rooted in authenticity, celebrating the love of sailing and upholding Wally's robust sailing heritage. The concept of the wallywind110 encapsulates the best of the sailing world; not only does she embody the elegance of a cruiser, she also matches the effervescence of a racer.

Built to celebrate the outdoors, the yacht’s deck features plentiful seating areas and sun pads for relaxation and social entertainment. The aft steps provide breathtaking views via the open transom. What sets this model apart in its category is its intelligent deck layout, offering numerous lounge areas without disrupting flow. The cockpit, while providing trouble-free access to multiple storage areas—a feature often neglected on sailing yachts—still maintains an intimate atmosphere amidst a fully open setting.

The decking exhibits painstaking safety considerations, and its conscientious routing of all lines beneath deck ensures an immaculate and arranged environment. Steps aboard are deliberately minimised for fluidity of movement. The designers wanted the cockpit to feel approachable for those desiring participation in the sailing process, so the helm station was designed for accessibility. Here, guests can engage with the captain or owner and experience the cadence of sailing first-hand. The yacht’s design invites engagement and participation, a seamless blend of performance and luxury.

title: Discover the heart of UK's Barton Marine through a personal tour conducted by CEO Suzanne Blaustone
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover the heart of UK's Barton Marine through a personal tour conducted by CEO Suzanne Blaustone
summary: Join us on a riveting tour through the Barton Marine factory in the UK, led by none other than CEO Suzanne Blaustone.
body: Step into the bustling world of Barton Marine at Whitstable, Kent, led by an insightful guide - the firm's CEO Suzanne Blaustone. This UK-based factory bears the legacy of Whitstable Shipwright and boat builder Ron Barton, who founded R.S.J. Barton in 1948. Barton was at the forefront of a sea of change in yachting manufacturing, being one of the pioneers in utilizing the fabric-based laminated plastic Tufnol and stainless steel. The result? Yachting blocks that were noticeably lighter and stronger than ever before. Today, these innovations form the backbone of Barton Marine as it continues to produce top-notch sailing and yachting fittings. Enjoyed by sailors around the globe, Barton Marine's contributions extend beyond its industry, with other hardware designs finding applications in various sectors. A walk around the factory introduces you to the dedicated team behind these impressive innovations. They share their roles, work experiences, and the unique joy they find in being part of the Barton Marine legacy. For those who breathe the sea and sail, the seafront factory of Barton Marine holds many more stories.

title: Transatlantic Triumph: Bauza and Pillain Celebrate Memorable Finish at Transat Café L'or Race
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Transatlantic Triumph: Bauza and Pillain Celebrate Memorable Finish at Transat Café L'or Race
summary: In a show of grit and determination, Aina Bauza and Axelle Pillain showcased their skill in sailing by finishing 20th in the 17th Transat Café L'or Class 40 race.
body: Sailing is not for the faint-hearted. It tests resilience and courage, seeks out the dreamers and adventurers, and, at times, tries to break them. But through this storm rises a beacon of camaraderie and triumph, as seen in the case of two exceptional sailors, Aina Bauza and Axelle Pillain. These indomitable women, undeterred by harsh weather or the vastness of the sea, carved their name in the annals of the 17th Transat Café L'or race, placing 20th in Class 40.

Their route planning was a testament to their nautical wisdom and adaptability. After debating a 'half-south, half-north' course, they opted for a southerly direction seeking the trade winds. Not wanting their maiden transatlantic crossing to turn into a relentless fight against the elements, they made a plan both rational and human. Day by day, they found their footing on their vessel, learning more about each other, and finding strength in their shared experiences.

In another story of exemplary prowess, the Coffee Route double-handed race from France to Martinique unfolded over nearly a month, from October 26th to November 24th. Categories were numerous and the race ultimately heralded four winning duos across four classes. Every participant displayed a formidable mastery of the sea, modelled on the strength of their commitment, skills, and strategic planning.

Indeed, the adventures of Bauza and Pillain, and all the participants of the Transat Café L'or, encapsulate the sheer force of spirit that drives every sailor. Their story stands as a testament to the raw, unyielding beauty of the sea and those who dare to master it.

title: Revealing the Azzurra 36: An Exciting New Chapter Begins for Tureddi Yachts as they Embark on their First Full-Custom Superyacht Build
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Revealing the Azzurra 36: An Exciting New Chapter Begins for Tureddi Yachts as they Embark on their First Full-Custom Superyacht Build
summary: Tureddi Yachts has officially begun construction of the Azzurra 36, marking its first venture into full-custom superyacht manufacturing.
body: Tureddi Yachts, a renowned Italian shipbuilder, is making waves as it launches its novel venture into the arena of personalised, full-custom superyachts with the Azzurra 36. The groundbreaking ceremony was marked with a classic coin ceremony at Tureddi's Pisa facilities, signifying the initiation of a new chapter in its illustrious yachting journey.

Although other details remain shrouded in mystery, one thing is clear: the Azzurra 36 is a testament to Tureddi's dedication to exceptional onboard comfort, generous living spaces, and dynamic functionality. With a wide beam, expansive volume, and superior finishing, this vessel is set to redefine the parameters of luxury seafaring. It will cater to the needs of up to 12 guests, tended to by a proficient crew of eight.

"We want to work together with Alessandro's team, Pininfarina, Giamboi, and Ruggiero to create something absolutely special - a new benchmark for Tureddi," said the proud owner of the new build. Discussing the future of the collaboration, he added, "perhaps we will build something even bigger, an even more glorious marvel in the very near future."

Alessandro Tureddi, president of Tureddi Yachts, expressed his gratitude to the owner for his trust, recognizing the Azzurra 36 as the symbol of Tureddi's evolution from a trusted manufacturer to a promising designer of custom superyachts. This significant milestone marks the Italian shipbuilder's emergence as a formidable independent yacht builder. Echoing Tureddi's excitement, Luciano Aglioni, sales director at Tureddi Yachts, acknowledged the project as a perfect blend of tradition, innovation, and family values, representing the best of Italian excellence.

Earlier this year, Tureddi unveiled two new models, the Hyper 50 and the Ultra 40, solidifying the yard's reputation as a hotbed for exciting designs and high-profile collaborations. The future looks grand and promising for Tureddi. As the shipyard rides the waves of improvement and expansion, seafaring enthusiasts can only wait with bated breath to see what lies ahead in this exciting journey.

title: Foiler Introduces Ghost, the Luxurious 'Flying' Yacht That's Set to Change the Course of Naval Architecture
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Foiler Introduces Ghost, the Luxurious 'Flying' Yacht That's Set to Change the Course of Naval Architecture
summary: Foiler, an innovative UAE-based brand, has unveiled Ghost, a groundbreaking private foiling yacht developed in partnership with Turkish design studio, Bozca.
body: A revolution in yacht design unfurls in the United Arab Emirates as Foiler unveils the world's first-ever private foiling yacht platform, Ghost. This revolutionary 28-meter yacht is the fruit of a collaboration with Bozca Design, Istanbul's leading design studio. Debuting at the prestigious Abu Dhabi International Boat Show, further revelations confirmed that Ghost's construction will commence within 12 to 18 months, expecting a grand voyage initiation in 2029.

Ghost showcases an architectural masterpiece enveloped in a semi-customisable design that symbolises a shift into a 'new era of performance, comfort and elegance at sea.' The UAE shipyard, ENATA, ensures the yacht's manifestation from design to reality, signifying the pioneering spirit and the innovative drive shared by Foiler and Bozca Design.

Timur Bozca, the creative director at Bozca Design, underlines Ghost's design philosophy, stating that each structural aesthetic decision serves functionality over decoration, emphasizing performance, reliability and clarity. Crafted meticulously using carbon fibre and titanium for a lightweight structure, Ghost is not your ordinary yacht, but a high-performance platform that can 'fly' about two meters above the water.

Masterfully engineered, Ghost boasts a beam of eight meters that expands to almost 20 meters with foils extended, propelling this sublime yacht to unprecedented speeds of over 40 knots, and cruising comfortably between 30-35 knots.

Ghost is a stark departure from conventional yachting experiences. To quote Alois Vieujot, CEO of ENATA Group, 'Foiling transforms yachting,' allowing passengers to experience a smooth, stable ride even at 40 knots. Its unparalleled serenity and comfort, along with its impressive performance, fortifies the proclamation of Ghost as the forerunner of the new age of 'flying' luxury yachts.

title: Latest Addition to Horizon FD85s Yacht Series Finds Distinctive Owner – An Exclusive Look Into The Structuring Process
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Latest Addition to Horizon FD85s Yacht Series Finds Distinctive Owner – An Exclusive Look Into The Structuring Process
summary: The 18th unit of Horizon FD85s yacht series has been sold, introduced by Pierre Badin, to a client who seeks a vessel tailored to nurturing their family’s unique lifestyle.
body: Emerging from the semi-custom Horizon FD85s yacht series, the 18th unit has sparked a wave of interest. With Pierre Badin of Denison Yachting Monaco personally introducing the new owner, we’re treated to a spectacle of unique customization that screams 'family lifestyle' from the hull up to the helipad.

The 26-meter vessel, currently under construction at a Taiwanese-based shipyard, promises an experience tailored to the buyer's preference with an intense focus on outdoor entertaining. The design genius, Cor D. Rover, devised this model to be 'open to interpretation', transforming the owner's vision into floating reality. The vessel, therefore, encapsulates spaces that evolve with the owner's desires, focusing on family-friendly facilities, extended al fresco entertaining, and modular spaces.

Yet, the ingenuity doesn't stop there. Among the yacht’s distinct features is a versatile cockpit designed for angling and leisure alike. Special, child-friendly adaptations include a fold-down transom for the owner’s grandchildren, as well as ample storage for water toys. The yacht also features a custom-built helipad and a hot tub located on the bow, further amplifying the yacht's grandeur.

Under the current layout, the vessel accommodates guests in four opulent staterooms, including an on-deck, full-beam master suite, two VIP cabins amidships below deck, a versatile forward VIP with a convertible V-berth, and two crew cabins placed efficiently aft of the engine room.

'This project is the epitome of the FD85s series' originality. A vessel that fuses volume, efficiency, and adaptability in a way that perfectly appeals to active families prioritizing life on water, without a hint of compromise,' raved Badin. Truly, this grand vessel redefines personalization in luxury yachting.

title: Entrepreneur Steve Rigby's All-new Superyacht: The Darwin 102 Series' Sixth Unit, Haze²
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Entrepreneur Steve Rigby's All-new Superyacht: The Darwin 102 Series' Sixth Unit, Haze²
summary: The Italian boatyard Cantiere delle Marche has revealed an adventurous new addition to its fleet - Haze², owned by UK entrepreneur Steve Rigby.
body: When it comes to capturing the spirit of unfettered oceanic adventure, few master it as mesmerizingly as Italian boatyard Cantiere delle Marche (CdM). Its latest innovation to grace the waters is Haze², the latest addition to the lauded Darwin 102 series.

The proud owner of this 30.8-meter spectacle is British entrepreneur Steve Rigby, an experienced sailor with a fondness for the tranquil waters. His relationship with CdM took root upon a captivating tour of the Darwin 106 at none other than the 2022 Cannes Yachting Festival. The enchanting expedition-ready spirit of the Darwin models combined with CdM's impeccable ability to tailor-make each vessel uniquely to the owner's desires earned the British businessman’s faith.

Italian studio Hydro Tec lent their expertise to the naval architecture and exterior design. Their effort, combined with the use of innovative technologies, culminated in the creation of an exceptional vessel that seamlessly balances style and substance. The result: a free-roaming and technologically advanced yacht embodying both luxurious comfort and the raw spirit of sea exploration.

Revving under Haze²'s hood are twin Caterpillar engines, offering a remarkable cruising range of over 5000 nautical miles at a cruising speed of 9 knots. This feature ensures that no corner of the world's waterways remains beyond reach for this brave beauty. Moreover, the yacht's dual-classification as a private and charter vessel speaks of its versatility and adaptability. The splendid sun deck, equipped with a Jacuzzi and sunpads, encourages lounging under the vast open skies while cruising the open waters.

Artistry and engineering find their breathtaking confluence in Haze², a striking manifestation of Rigby's quest for seamless harmony between opulence and exploration. And as CdM continues to break new grounds with its upcoming projects, including a peek into its newest flagship, RJ - unveiled at this year's Monaco Yacht Show - the future of luxury yachting looks set for yet even more exciting adventures.

title: Confronting Uncertainty: Sunseeker Sets the Record Straight About CEO's Position Amidst Speculation
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Confronting Uncertainty: Sunseeker Sets the Record Straight About CEO's Position Amidst Speculation
summary: British marine entity, Sunseeker International Ltd, clears murky waters surrounding the position of its chief executive, Andrea Frabetti.
body: Confusion had been the order of the day within the marine industry for some time. Whispers ran rife, harnessing the power to unsettle the mightiest of entities. Standing tall amongst these infallible entities was Sunseeker International Ltd, a dominant name in the world of British shipbuilding. However, recently the company found itself subject to whispers and speculations about its leadership. The muddle pertained to none other than the company's CEO, Andrea Frabetti, and his alleged departure from the company. Unsettled by these rumors and realizing the impact on its reputation, Sunseeker decided it was time to steer the narrative ship in a direction of clarity and truth. They made an official statement that Andrea Frabetti was still CEO, pushing false rumors overboard. In their pursuit of transparency, they hoped to eliminate the clouds of confusion hovering over the boardroom. Establishing a factual basis cleared the swirling doubts, restoring peace to the helm and its members. These proactive steps not only secured their position in the ship-building industry but also displayed bravery as they navigated through tempestuous rumor-seas. Sunseeker's journey that started as a struggle against damning rumors, ended with it anchoring its integrity and fortifying its credibility in the market.

title: Discover the Inspirational Journey of Krijn Van Den Brink,, the Visionary Behind FD Yachts
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover the Inspirational Journey of Krijn Van Den Brink,, the Visionary Behind FD Yachts
summary: Embark on an inspiring journey with Krijn Van Den Brink, the man who breathed life into FD Yachts, a global sailing yacht brand.
body: Hailing from a rich heritage of sea-faring in the Netherlands, Krijn Van Den Brink was hardly still in his nappies when he first experienced the thrill of the open water. Growing up briefly racing in Flits dinghies then moving onto 20'-40-foot keelboats, sailing became second nature for Krijn very early on. This ignited what would become a lifelong passion that led him all the way to the helm of his own international yacht brand.

Later, Krijn linked up with his family to venture into professional boatbuilding. Driven by his fervour for sailing and his talent in boat construction, Krijn Van Den Brink aimed to turn his passion into an accessible source of exhilaration for others by founding FD Yachts.

FD Yachts stands as the vibrant embodiment of Krijn's vision, merging Dutch craftsmanship, Swiss design finesse, and the practical efficiency of Chinese manufacturing. The product of this novel fusion is a fleet of high-performance sailing yachts that exemplify elegance and deluxe, while maintaining an accessible quality. As part of the brand's contribution to growing the sailing community, they've recently become the first member of Tall Ships America's Leadership Circle.

Krijn's commitment to connecting sailors across disciplines shines through in the design of the FD Future range. Designed with both youth and adult sailors in mind, the FD Future, FD Future 6.8, and FD Future X stand as a testament to Krijn’s drive to make performance sailing available to everyone.

title: Revolutionary Ocean PRO Sailing Gear: Henri-Lloyd's Game-Changing Innovation Unveiled at Metstrade2025
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Revolutionary Ocean PRO Sailing Gear: Henri-Lloyd's Game-Changing Innovation Unveiled at Metstrade2025
summary: Henri-Lloyd heralds a significant leap forward with the introduction of its Ocean PRO range, taking professional sailing apparel to brand new heights.
body: Henri-Lloyd, a trusted name in sailing gear, presents its newest innovation - the Ocean PRO range at Metstrade2025. This breakthrough offering raises the bar for professional sailing apparel. Harnessing modern technology and sustainability practices, Ocean PRO is crafted to heighten performance, strengthen comfort and support survival at sea.

Recognized as a finalist for the Dame Award 2025, Ocean PRO seeks to satisfy the expansive requirements of professional offshore racing crews, long-distance sailors, and dedicated sea adventurers. This sea gear is a testament to what modern technology can achieve in extreme-weather gear, fully reimagining offshore protection.

Developed over a span of three years in collaboration with some of the most reputable names in sailing, Ocean PRO introduces the world's pioneering 4-Layer Hybrid Membrane Stretch Fabric. The result is handheld protection with survival-grade waterproofness, exceptional breathability and a significant reduction in weight compared with conventional offshore gear.

The Ocean PRO collection features an offshore jacket for both genders; integrating optimum protection with freedom of movement due to its removable face mask and photoluminescent safety elements. Furthermore, the jacket comes with a removable inner neoprene skirt, adding an extra layer of prevention against wind and water in harsh conditions.

Unbeatable innovation continues with the hybrid smock; combining the protective seal of a smock with the accessibility of a jacket, removing the inconvenience of overhead removal. Lastly, the collection boasts hi-fit salopettes, reinforced for enhanced comfort on extended trips.

Beyond extraordinary features, the Ocean PRO range exhibits Henri-Lloyd's commitment to sustainability and superior functionality. The range utilizes 100% recycled Polyamide and PFOA-free and PFC-free membrane, ensuring enduring waterproofness and breathability. Finally, strategic placements of stretch reinforcements and foam cushioning guarantee durability and reduced fatigue.

In summary, Henri-Lloyd's Ocean PRO range is a triumph in sailing gear, presenting extraordinary resilience, comfort and commitment to sustainability. A bold testament to the evolution of professional sailing attire.

title: Melita Marine Group Breaks Ground in South of France, Boosting Mediterranean Technical Service Network
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Melita Marine Group Breaks Ground in South of France, Boosting Mediterranean Technical Service Network
summary: Melita Marine Group announces a significant leap in its Mediterranean expansion with its new outpost in the South of France.
body: Navigating the picturesque blue waters of the Mediterranean Sea just got more exhilarating, thanks to the ambitious expansion of the Melita Marine Group. Bursting onto the scene with the launch of ‘Melita Shipyard Services France’, the group strengthens its Mediterranean presence, casting its technical service coverage all the way from the glittering Monaco to the historic port city of Marseille. Set to unfurl officially in January 2026, the prestigious base will be located crisply between Biot and Antibes. Not just limited by geography, the new operation will be supported by mobile technical teams offering an impressive array of onboard competencies. The group’s aim is to deliver a smooth technical and refit support network within the central and western Mediterranean, effecting an easeful cruising experience for all yacht enthusiasts. A significant milestone for Melita Marine Group, this expansion heralds their inaugural permanent service in South France. The fresh operation augments their existing enterprise—a 100-meter-capacity, fully equipped shipyard situated in Malta, renowned in the industry for its excellence. The Group’s founder, Pierre Balzan, sees the expansion as a bridge connecting two key European yachting hubs— offering their high-quality services across the Côte d'Azur seamlessly. He states confidently that enlarging the outfit’s reach allows the group to serve their clients more effectively, across diverse locales and aboard their yachts. A further feather in their cap, the group is burgeoning its role as an MTU Partner Distributor, notching up its technical and spare-parts workshops bandwidth in Malta, Greece, and Cyprus. A crucial move keeping in line with their ambitious vision for an expansive service area. The announcement was made amid an official gathering at the globally recognised Monaco Yacht Show 2025, orchestrated jointly with AG Advisory. The latter used the platform to celebrate its establishment as a licensed advisor provider in Malta, unveiling its extensive service portfolio spanning across financial, corporate, and compliance sectors. Echoing the shared ethos of expansion, both companies have indicated robust growth plans for 2026. While Melita Marine Group intends to stretch its technical coverage across the Mediterranean, AG Advisory sets its eyes on client-centric expansion, steaming ahead from its freshly minted base.

title: Ockelbo's Ultimate All-Weather Family Cruiser: The New Flagship Taking the UK Sailing by Storm
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Ockelbo's Ultimate All-Weather Family Cruiser: The New Flagship Taking the UK Sailing by Storm
summary: The ultimate multi-purpose, year-round cruising experience steps into the UK shores. Meet the new flagship from Ockelbo, designed for all weathers and adventures.
body: The wave of fresh sea air carries with it a sense of anticipation stirred by the debut of Ockelbo's latest flagship – an all-weather, four-season cruising boat. Designed and built by the Swedish aluminium sportsboat specialist, Anytec, the vessel is an embodiment of robust craftsmanship entwined with luxurious comfort for an unforgettable sea adventure.

Engineered mainly from aluminium, the cruiser's unique design embraces the harsh environmental conditions while serving as a stylish and regal refuge on the water. Its sturdy aluminium shell reinforces the vessel's durability, promising seafarers an unwavering companion for all their sea ventures.

Functionality was not sacrificed for style. The cruiser brags of practical side decks, a swing-up table in the aft cockpit accompanied by a pair of seat boxes and an outboard motor that can push the boat to about 45 knots. Further, one can opt for a separate heads and replace three forward-facing seat pods with a full convertible U-shaped dining station big enough for six. Despite its impressive array of features, there's room for customization, allowing captains to tailor the vessel to match their specific needs.

This latest offering from Ockelbo, with its innovative design, high-quality build and competitive pricing, is an exciting proposition for year-round family boaters. It challenges previous notions of what an all-weather cruising boat can be, bringing a thrill of adventure and comfort wrapped up in a high-value package.

title: Ockelbo's Flagship Multi-Season Cruiser Makes its Debut in the UK - The Ultimate in Versatility and Performance
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Ockelbo's Flagship Multi-Season Cruiser Makes its Debut in the UK - The Ultimate in Versatility and Performance
summary: The long-awaited debut of Ockelbo's new flagship model, an all-weather family cruiser, finally took place in Southampton.
body: The renowned brand Ockelbo, under the aegis of seasoned Swedish aluminium sportsboat specialist, Anytec, has launched its latest marvel. With an all-aluminium construction, this new flagship model is the epitome of toughness, purposefulness, and flexibility, suited for year-round operation.

Sporting an 8ft 4in beam, its pilothouse—with its functional reverse screen—virtually fills the entire width, leaving just enough space for a pair of practical, grippy side decks. A feature-packed superstructure includes a pair of seat boxes, a swing-up table, and a 300hp outboard motor—a mix of functionality and high performance. Speed lovers, fret not! The model can be upgraded with a larger engine, potentially boosting the speed from 45 to 55 knots.

As for the pilothouse itself, users will be delighted with its top-notch headroom and the panoramic view offered by its large frameless windows. Of course, the sunroofs are standard. The furniture is equally clever and versatile, comprising tapering side benches, optional lift-up aft seats, and swivelling helm seats providing sitting for up to eight. In an innovative design move, the rear section can be transformed into a whopping 7ft bed.

The model does lack cooking facilities. However, it offers two heads solutions to choose from – installing a loo beneath the pilothouse access step or, for an extra £3,000, opting for a full heads compartment with a sink and a black waste tank.

Despite the need for speccing up, the model’s impressive build quality, innovative design, and competitive pricing make it a high-value offering for the family boating enthusiast who doesn't want to be confined to any specific season. So, brace yourself. Ockelbo's new flagship multi-purpose, all-weather family cruiser has arrived in the UK, and it's as versatile and vibrant as you have anticipated.

title: Championing Sailing Talent: An Inside Look at the 29er Awards & M32 World Championship
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Championing Sailing Talent: An Inside Look at the 29er Awards & M32 World Championship
summary: Two significant events are set to dazzle the world of sailing: the launch of the 29er Awards and the M32 World Championship.
body: One can never understate the thrill and passion awash in the world of sailing. This year, there's fresh excitement on the sea breeze with the introduction of the 29er Awards 2025. A global celebration of excellence and ingenuity, the 29er community salutes not just sporting prowess but the creativity, spirit, and culture peppered throughout its ranks. With categories that extend from performance to creativity and community, this awards ceremony aims to recognize sailors, teams, coaches, and creators that have made the 29er community a vibrant tapestry of talent and creativity. Nominations and voting procedures offer a fair and democratic process, ensuring that the all-round talent and efforts of the 29er community get to bask in the limelight.

In essence, both these events compel us to witness and appreciate the talent, skill, and artistry prevalent in the world of sailing. One is an affirmation of achievement throughout the community; the other, a nail-biting battle for dominance on the world stage. But both, undeniably, encapsulate the sense of adventure and commitment that gets each sailor's heart racing faster than their yacht cutting through a wave. They truly represent the modern, global, spirited sport that sailing has become.

title: Announcing the 2025 29er Awards and Thrills of the M32 World Championship 2025 Set to Begin in Miami
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Announcing the 2025 29er Awards and Thrills of the M32 World Championship 2025 Set to Begin in Miami
summary: The 29er Class announces the 2025 29er Awards to recognize sporting excellence and community spirit, while the M32 World Championship 2025 is ready to launch in Miami.
body: In a world of sailing that celebrates sporting victories, community spirit and awe-inspiring prowess at sea, the 29er Awards and the M32 World Championship stand out as much anticipated events. The 29er Class is ecstatic to unveil the 29er Awards 2025, a planetary gala celebrating the sailors, coaches and the myriad of stories that have made the current season truly unforgettable. With a unique blend of sporting excellence along with recognizing the spirit, creativity and unique culture that defines the 29er community, the awards promise a vibrant celebration of excellence. Performance-based accolades accord recognition to athletes and coaches who made a mark, including categories such as Crew of the Year, Most Improved Team, and Coach of the Year among others. Additionally, the idea of sportsmanship goes beyond just speed and is about panache, ideas and influence. The Community and Creativity awards celebrate sailors who add colour, creativity, and consciousness to the 29er community. In addition, a special Creative Sailor of the Year award by Kidzink introduces a unique angle, recognizing a sailor who expresses creativity, originality, and visual impact within the community, selected independently by Kidzink. Parallelly, the M32 World Championship 2025 stands ready to launch in Miami soon. Racing enthusiasts avidly speculate who will hoist the hardware: an all-Julien podium, a magical performance by McKillen, a steadfast Wilson or perhaps an unprecedented surprise. The claim to the World Championship remains open to all attendees, bound to be decided by superior communication, unmatched skills and the one who gets off the line. Predicting a winner will have to wait until the adrenaline-packed last moment of the final race. Be prepared for an eventful sailing season with owner-drivers and a crew list that reads like a who's who of sailing in a championship that promises to be the climax of the M32 season. Here's to 19 thrilling races and crowning a new World Champion!

title: Dive into the New Pardo 43: Discover Transformations in the Ultimate Walkaround Day Boat
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Dive into the New Pardo 43: Discover Transformations in the Ultimate Walkaround Day Boat
summary: The Pardo 43 takes its place in the spotlight, showcasing subtle but impactful changes and redefining the concept of an ultimate day boat.
body: The evolution of the Pardo 43 is both delicate and significant, straddling a subtle line where tradition meets innovation. It's a boat that immediately strikes the eye with its classic features – the distinct bow shape, clean lines, sunbathing-friendly decks, central dinette, aft sunbed, transverse galley, open-plan overnight space, and more. At first glance, these recognisable traits lull the onlooker into a sense of familiar comfort. But peer closer, and the revamped Pardo 43 gently nudges you towards a fresh perspective.

Additionally, the Pardo 43 has also thrown open its doors (quite literally) for better access to the cabins, along with increasing the size of the hull windows to invite more natural light to the lower deck. The overnight space on the lower deck has also been transformed into an irresistible open-plan layout that features a day head, convertible lounge, breakfast bar, and a pair of beds beneath the cockpit.

The Pardo 43, available with a range of engines (ips-500s, 600s or 650s), brings about a significant evolution in day boats and realizes itself as a supremely well-calibrated upgrade, ticking all the right boxes for both purists and novices alike. The boat, which subtly weaves together design innovation with timeless elegance, makes living the sea life a genuine pleasure, bathing every sailing moment in delight and comfort.

title: Navigating the Murky Waters of Gratuities: A Look at the Intricacies of Tipping in the Charter Yachting Industry
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Navigating the Murky Waters of Gratuities: A Look at the Intricacies of Tipping in the Charter Yachting Industry
summary: Yacht crews face uncertain traditions and potential injustices related to gratuities - a topic blurred by varied ethics and legalities in the charter sector.
body: In the lively world of charter yachting, a riddle floats through the air. It is an unsolved mystery, a buffet of various ethics, practices, and legalities - Gratuity. The hotly debated subject of gratuities within the industry raises several palpable questions and provokes myriad perspectives. These discussions find their way into every channel, from yachting journals to crew bars.

Most service industries, yachting, in particular, abide by an unwritten code - performance of service is followed by receipts of tips. However, it's not always clear-cut. Several factors can affect the manner and quantum of gratuity distribution, including the relationship among the charter broker, the client, and the captain; the service satisfaction level of the client, and the level of involvement of the broker in matters, post-signing the Charter Agreement. Often, the burden of managing gratuity negotiations falls on the captain, adding an arduous task to their plate.

What escalates the issue is the fact that there are no legal regulations regarding the accumulation and distribution of gratuities. It paves the way for potential exploitation as owners can potentially retain the entire gratuity without any justifiable reason. The industry is brimming with tales of unjust gratuity distribution, hinting at a pressing need for more transparent and reasonable systems. Hence, it is advised for the yacht crew to dissect their Seafarers Employment Agreement (SEA) with an eagle eye or have someone examine it thoroughly on their behalf before signing off.

Sailing the high seas as a yacht crew member is challenging and rewarding in more ways than one. And when done right, gratuity can serve as an added bonus. But navigating this landscape requires patience, understanding, and a clear view of the legal underpinning. As the industry continues to surge forwards, so too must the conversation around ethics and legality of gratuities.

title: Seldén Mast Revels in Triple DAME Nominations and Unveils Novel StB Rigging Screws at Metstrade 2025
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Seldén Mast Revels in Triple DAME Nominations and Unveils Novel StB Rigging Screws at Metstrade 2025
summary: Seldén Mast triumphs in innovation with its new product line, including the versatile StB Rigging Screws, and earns multiple nominations from the DAME Design Awards.
body: Never one to be outdone in the twists and turns of marine engineering, Seldén Mast sails full-speed ahead into Metstrade 2025 with a new range of products – most notably, the revolutionary StB Rigging Screws. This launch marks a gigantic wave in Seldén's hardware portfolio, offering an efficient, modern alternative to conventional turnbuckles. This fresh approach boosts the options for rigging upgrades and new builds, making every sailor's life easier – and arguably, more thrilling.

The versatile StB Rigging Screws, crafted from AISI 316 stainless steel and bronze, are designed for wire diameters ranging from 3-19mm. These screws, with their reduced friction, ensure smooth adjustments and reliable fittings. Along with a secure wrench grip and measurement slot, the system boasts polished, rounded locknuts, offering a neat finish and minimizing chafe.

Brimming with pride at this achievement, Steve Norbury, Managing Director of Seldén Mast, expresses, 'They're a robust, well-engineered evolution of a core piece of deck hardware, and they sit perfectly alongside the other new products we're introducing this year.'

But the winds of success don't stop there. Seldén Mast has also triumphed in securing three DAME Awards nominations, recognizing their functional engineering focused on multiple aspects of sail handling. These nominations include the Nail Terminal, the dual-direction Ratchet for Seldén's CXr Code Furler, and the Clew Block for furling mainsails.

Building on their DAME success, Seldén Mast will grace Metstrade 2025 with the world premiere of the CXr series. Developed to provide robust furling torque, seamless integration, and improved handling, the CXr series redefines furling equipment and is expected to start deliveries in spring 2026.
Striding into the future, Seldén Mast remains persistent in innovation and its dedication to enhancing the exhilarating journey of sailing.

title: Striking a Balance between Luxury and Sustainability: How Prestigious Yacht Builders are Pioneering Eco-friendly Teak Alternatives
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Striking a Balance between Luxury and Sustainability: How Prestigious Yacht Builders are Pioneering Eco-friendly Teak Alternatives
summary: When tradition meets change, innovation thrives. Prestigious yacht builders embrace the pursuit of sustainable alternatives to teak, steering the industry towards an eco-conscious future.
body: Sailing into a future where sustainability intersects with luxury, leading yacht builders Oceanco, Feadship, and Lürssen are working untiringly to develop sustainable alternatives to teak. Yet, when an ingrained tradition is challenged, the seeds of resistance are sure to sprout. Crafting a yacht from teak, a symbol of ultimate opulence in the industry, is a centuries-old practice, akin to the grandeur of the high seas themselves. But as the future beckons, it becomes clear that change is not merely advisable, but obligatory. Sensing the shifting seas ahead, Oceanco commenced research into teak alternatives nearly half a decade ago, anticipating the need for radical innovation. After all, 'If you can get it, you can use it' had begun to fade as a viable adage, as sourcing teak turned into a complicated ball game. Covering an array of domains from decking to interiors and exterior fixtures, the Dutch shipyard’s holistic approach gave teak a prominent role in their masterpieces. Therefore, shifting gears from this core material doesn't result merely in a ripple, but a tsunami of necessary shifts in established systems. When Alan Coleman, Head of Interior Design and Outfitting at Oceanco, and Wim Verhoeff, Head of Sales, reflect on the journey, they recount being cognisant that the days of teak's undisputed reign were numbered. The biggest hurdle, they explain, lies in replacing teak, a non-slip surface par excellence, with a substitute up to par, without forgoing the yacht's visual allure. Each new candidate brings its quirks, presenting a unique challenge in regard to its installation, maintenance, and time-tested performance. While the decking is the most apparent area teak adorns, its usage transcends to include cladding, interior elements, and even structural features, elevating them all to an emblem of luxury. The oft-repeated sentiment of Verhoeff is echoed across the industry: a yacht is not a yacht without teak. However, the winds of change are building momentum. As more people navigate away from the timeworn reliance on teak, sustainable alternatives are stepping into the limelight. Striking a chord between luxury and sustainability, yacht builders like Oceanco pave the way for a future where luxury yachting and sustainability sail hand in hand.

title: Australian Superyacht Conference 2026
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Australian Superyacht Conference Returns in 2026
summary: New Sydney Venue, Fresh Format, and a Renewed Industry Focus A new chapter begins for Australia’s premier superyacht industry event
body: After a brief hiatus, one of the Southern Hemisphere’s most significant gatherings of superyacht professionals is returning — refreshed, refocused, and ready to redefine the future of luxury yachting in the Asia-Pacific.

Superyacht Australia has officially announced the return of the Australian Superyacht Conference in 2026, with a bold new format and an all-new Sydney location. Traditionally hosted on the Gold Coast each May in the lead-up to the Sanctuary Cove International Boat Show, the event will now anchor itself in Sydney Harbour for the first time — taking place immediately after the inaugural Sydney Charter Show in February.

This strategic repositioning will create an unmissable week of superyacht activity for owners, captains, charter professionals, and investors — reinforcing Australia’s standing as a rising powerhouse in the global superyacht scene.

The 2026 Sydney Charter Show, scheduled for Sunday 22 and Monday 23 February at Jones Bay Superyacht Marina, will lead the charge. Over two days, the show will showcase Australia and the South Pacific’s charter potential, featuring an elite line-up of vessels, brokers, and luxury travel partners.

Then, on Tuesday 24 February, the spotlight shifts to the Australian Superyacht Conference — a full day of insight, discussion, and networking that will connect the dots between policy, operations, and opportunity across the superyacht ecosystem.

By aligning the two events, Superyacht Australia aims to strengthen the industry’s collective voice, streamline collaboration, and build new bridges between business, government, and tourism stakeholders.

“The goal is to unite the sector under one roof — or one skyline, in this case — to discuss the future of Australian and South Pacific superyachting from every perspective,” said a spokesperson for Superyacht Australia. “Sydney’s global profile and central role in luxury marine tourism make it the perfect platform for this next chapter.”
The 2026 conference will not just celebrate industry growth — it will confront the real-world challenges and opportunities shaping the next decade of superyacht operations in Australia and beyond.
Delegates can expect in-depth panels, workshops, and keynote sessions spanning a broad spectrum of key issues:
Charter legislation and reform – examining progress toward streamlined national charter laws.
Importation and taxation frameworks – exploring simplified processes for foreign-flagged vessels entering Australian waters.
Crew recruitment and training – addressing workforce shortages and evolving skill demands.
Maritime labour and compliance – navigating evolving international regulations under MLC and AMSA frameworks.
Flag registration and classification – analysing global trends and regional registration advantages.
Yacht migration and global fleet data – understanding how vessel movements and charter flows are shifting across the Indo-Pacific.
Tourism integration – unlocking the potential of the South Pacific’s growing luxury cruising circuit, from Tahiti to Tasmania.
This practical, data-driven focus represents a departure from the traditional conference model, offering real-world takeaways for captains, brokers, family offices, and service providers alike.

With the superyacht fleet in the Asia-Pacific region expanding faster than anywhere else on the planet, the 2026 Australian Superyacht Conference aims to cement Australia’s position as a regional hub for refit, charter, and expedition cruising.

Sydney’s Jones Bay Wharf offers a fitting backdrop — a harbourside location steeped in maritime heritage, minutes from Darling Harbour and Barangaroo, yet fully equipped for modern superyacht operations.

“The move to Sydney reflects where the industry is heading,” noted one local captain. “It’s not just about luxury anymore — it’s about logistics, crew, sustainability, and connection. This event will bring all those pieces together.”

Over the past ten years, Australia’s superyacht sector has undergone a transformation. Legislative reforms allowing foreign-flagged vessels to charter in Australian waters, new marina developments, and stronger collaboration with tourism bodies have all contributed to a surge in superyacht visitation.
Today, Australian yards and marinas are catering to vessels up to 120 metres, and local expertise — from crew training to refit engineering — is increasingly sought after worldwide.
The return of the Australian Superyacht Conference signals not just a revival, but a recalibration of industry ambition, setting the tone for the next decade of growth.

One of the conference’s defining features will be its focus on the broader South Pacific network — an interconnected cruising ground spanning Australia, New Zealand, Fiji, Tahiti, and Papua New Guinea.

With improved infrastructure, shared charter legislation, and a growing emphasis on environmental stewardship, the region is fast emerging as the world’s most sustainable and adventurous luxury cruising destination.

Delegates can expect special sessions exploring cross-border opportunities, from seasonal yacht migration patterns to charter logistics, refit planning, and crew rotation strategies across the wider Pacific basin.
A Date for Every Superyacht Calendar
Between the glamour of the Sydney Charter Show and the insight of the Australian Superyacht Conference, February 2026 will be the must-attend moment on the global yachting calendar.

Superyacht Australia’s bold new approach ensures that these twin events will not only attract the industry’s biggest names, but also foster collaboration across sectors that define the superyacht economy — from marine engineering and brokerage to high-end hospitality and destination marketing.
The conference’s return marks an important milestone — both for Australia’s maritime identity and for the region’s rapidly expanding luxury marine landscape.

The sundeck is a haven for relaxation with in-built Jacuzzi, lounge-enveloped sunpads and a fully-stocked bar. Other enticing features include a fold-out swimming platform, a skylounge functioning as an entertainment hub and spacious al fresco dining spaces aft.

title: Blaze at Zea Marina, Greece, Results in Sinking of Four Luxury Yachts
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Blaze at Zea Marina, Greece, Results in Sinking of Four Luxury Yachts
summary: A devastating blaze at Greece's Zea Marina leads to the tragic sinking of several extravagant yachts, leaving the boating community aghast.
body: In the early hours of a brisk November morning, the tranquil, azure harbor at Greece's Zea Marina was disrupted by an unforeseen tragedy. Four majestic vessels, including the renowned 43.1-metre Overmarine yacht Sanctuary and two others that spanned more than 24 meters, sunk under the weight of a disastrous blaze that invaded the marina. Alongside these luxury vessels was the 24.1-metre Azimut yacht Alkyone, anchored nearby when disaster struck. As per local sources, the calamity originated aboard the day-trip sailing boat Mirasol, but rapidly spread, engulfing and sinking numerous vessels in the immediate vicinity. Despite the prompt response of twenty firefighters from the Fire Department and the Coast Guard, the flames burned unhampered for over five deadly hours. The Sanctuary has a rich nautical lineage, being one of the four Mangusta Oceano 43 models. Birthed from the designs of an all-Italian team, inclusive of Alberto Mancini and Pierluigi Ausonio, the yacht was well-regarded as a lucrative charter vessel. The elegance of the yacht, with its foredeck swimming pool and phenomenal accommodation capacity for 12 guests, featured a full-beam owner's suite with a fold-down balcony. Unfortunately, these vessels are now lost to the depths of the harbor waters. Enigmatically, this incident was not the first encounter the Zea Marina had with such a catastrophe. Several years prior, in August 2024, a similar fire rampaged through the marina and caused destruction to three yachts, including the 42.3-metre Picchiotti motor yacht, Libra Y, designed by industry titans Don Shead and Jon Bannenberg. While no casualties have occurred, the cause of the fire remains shrouded in mystery and active investigation. Such high-profile incidents serve as a reminder of the inherent dangers that the serene maritime life can harbor.

title: Discover Antonini Navi and Nauta’s ‘Project Light 63M’: A Bold Yachting Concept Shaped by Rising Demand for Larger Vessels
author: Old Sea Dogs

summary: In a visionary collaboration, Italian maritime yard Antonini Navi merges with Milan-based studio Nauta to launch an awe-inspiring 63.5-metre yachting concept, Project Light 63M.

The new design, known as Project Light 63M, is a collaborative brainchild born out of their partnership with the skilled designers at Milan-based studio Nauta. The proposal was inspired by in-depth discussions with yachting brokers and seasoned yacht owners who highlighted the increasing market thirst for larger yachts exceeding 500GT.

Chosen for its far-ranging industry experience, including commendable work on iconic vessels such as Lürssen's 180.6-metre Azzam and 142.1-metre Dragonfly, as well as the 88.4-metre Feadship yacht Zen, Nauta embodies a synergy of expertise. The collaboration manifests a clear understanding of the yachting world and thus, the Project Light 63M is an affirmation of this mutual respect and transcontinental partnership.

The distinctive owner's apartment and the VIP cabin are augmented with private outdoor terraces, adding an extra layer of opulence. A well-positioned gym benefits from an influx of natural light thanks to skylights and triple-aspect windows. The interiors, inspired by a 'contemporary Mediterranean aesthetic', bring together warm tones, light-coloured surfaces, and natural materials.

According to maritime information platform BOATPro, Antonini Navi is currently supervising the construction of two new yachts: the first model of their semi-custom steel and aluminium series, the Seamore 34, and the EVO 31, a full-custom motor yacht, both nearing their launch date. title: Van der Valk Floats Out Magnificent 36m Custom Yacht Jangada
