title: Harken Unveils Superior Tide Changer – The Grip&Go Aluminum Winch Handle
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Harken Unveils Superior Tide Changer – The Grip&Go Aluminum Winch Handle
summary: Winch operation just got an upgrade with the advent of Harken's Grip&Go Aluminum Winch Handle, incredibly lightweight and swift to use.
body: Gone are the days of struggling with your winch as Harken revolutionises the nautical world with the advent of their Grip&Go Aluminum Winch Handle. Crafted to take convenience to a whole new level, the Grip&Go Handle ensures a faster, easier, and more efficient sailing journey. As strong as it is lightweight, the Grip&Go harbors the promise of making grinding winches feel as smooth as spreading butter on warm bread. Race enthusiasts and relaxed cruisers alike will find the Grip&Go a welcomed innovation, brilliantly transforming racing tactics and cruising confidence in equal measure. The heart of the design lies in the patented locking mechanism that facilitates effortless locking in and out of the winch. The ergonomically designed grab bar enables one-hand operation – a simple squeeze with the palm to unlock, and an easy release for a guaranteed lock. As if reinventing the winch handle wasn't enough, Harken expanded the reach of the Grip&Go by integrating their unique SpeedGrip handle technology. This allows independent swivel between the ball bearing knob and handgrip, which fosters rapid trimming during low loads, and compellingly powerful when the high waves necessitate two-handed grinding. And it's not just in functionality that it excels, tipping the scales at just 605 g (21.3 oz). The Grip&Go keeps your boat's pace high and its weight low. The future of winching has arrived, and it's lighter, more efficient, and swifter than ever. The Harken Grip&Go Aluminum Winch Handle is available for order from Harken's website and through various dealers.

title: Exquisite 52-Metre Schooner Dona Francisca Witnesses $2.8 Million Discount: Get the Ultimate Sailing Experience
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Exquisite 52-Metre Schooner Dona Francisca Witnesses $2.8 Million Discount: Get the Ultimate Sailing Experience
summary: The magnificent 52.4-metre schooner, Dona Francisca, branded as one of the grandest carbon fibre sailing yachts, receives a substantial price reduction of $2.8 million on its sales listing.
body: The exquisite schooner Dona Francisca, revered as one of the largest carbon fibre sailing yachts ever crafted, has witnessed a stellar price markdown of $2,800,000 on its sales listing with Jochen Brill of Northrop & Johnson. Launched in 2014 by Astilleros Buquebus in Uruguay, this classically styled spectacle was meticulously designed by Javier Soto Acebal for a seasoned owner with a deep-rooted passion for sailing.

Conceived as a vessel for not just leisure but comfortable long-distance cruising, Dona Francisca naturally couples traditional aesthetics with contemporary efficiency. Her owners committed to a comprehensive refit in 2024 that modernized her top-to-bottom—from aesthetic carpentry and rigging to a full paint job and in-depth maintenance.

As with everything on this remarkable yacht, the interior takes the skillful combination of traditional and modern to another level. Warm, sophisticated, and adorned with mahogany panelling—each element harmoniously contributes to its ambiance. Classically inspired features, including beautiful deck prisms for natural lighting and timeless lamps, illuminate the main saloon and formal dining area, fostering a homely atmosphere aboard.

Since its listing in February 2024, the yacht has had just one owner. The RINA classed sailing yacht for sale can accomplish speeds up to 17 knots under sail and cruises comfortably at 10 knots when powered up. She claims an impressive 6,700-nautical-mile passage from South America to the Mediterranean, reaffirming her range and adept handling capabilities. With manoeuvrability enhanced by a large rudder and two Maxpower R600 thrusters, the yacht proves her worth in navigating the open sea with consummate ease. Dona Francisca, currently berthed in Valencia, Spain awaits her next adventurous owner.

title: Modular Chaseboat Revolution: Introducing the Synthesis S.60 by SPARK Marine Projects
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Modular Chaseboat Revolution: Introducing the Synthesis S.60 by SPARK Marine Projects
summary: Get to know the ground-breaking Synthesis S.60 chaseboat - a modular marvel brought to life by SPARK Marine Projects.
body: In the luxurious world of yachts and superyachts, a new star has risen. Named the Synthesis S.60, this innovative chaseboat is the brainchild of design-savvy thinktank SPARK Marine Projects. Conceived in Monaco but built with help from New Zealand's Lloyd Stevenson Boatbuilders, the Synthesis S.60 made its grand debut at the recent Monaco Yacht Show, where it captured significant attention due to its distinct features. This creation isn't merely a boat; it's a carefully built platform designed to revolutionise yacht support operations.

Its primary attraction is a purpose-built, foil-assisted hull, which masterfully amalgamates seakeeping qualities, fuel efficiency, and range without compromising the staple aesthetic appeal and detailing that one would expect from the luxury yacht field. However, the magic of the Synthesis S.60 is not merely confined to its hull. The central cabin is fully climate-controlled and can comfortably accommodate up to twelve guests and two crew members.

This emphasis on adaptability allows the Synthesis S.60 to cater to various scenarios, from high-speed guest transfers and watersport activities to cargo-carrying support roles, rendering the chaseboat an indispensable asset to any superyacht owner. Each Synthesis S.60 model is intricately tailored to cater explicitly to the customer’s design preferences and operational requirements, providing a high degree of personalisation to each vessel.

title: Palm Beach Motor Yachts Presents Innovative Upgrades for Palm Beach XI Preceding 2025 RSHR
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Palm Beach Motor Yachts Presents Innovative Upgrades for Palm Beach XI Preceding 2025 RSHR
summary: Mark Richards helms an ambitious transformation of Palm Beach XI, showcasing state-of-the-art upgradations ahead of 2025 RSHR.
body: Artistry in the ocean - that's what Palm Beach Motor Yachts brings with its latest offering, the much-overhauled Palm Beach XI. Positioned swiftly on the cusp of the 2025 RSHR (Rolex Sydney Hobart Race), the yacht rises with newfound valor, boosted by an impressive sweep of upgrades and remodelings.

The vision behind this glamorous overhaul? Mark Richards, the founder and CEO of Palm Beach Motor Yachts, who weaves his rich tapestry of ocean-racing experience and yacht-building prowess into the heart of Palm Beach XI's transformation. And it's not just a one-man show either. Lending their skills alongside Richards is a cast of industry giants ranging from Juan Kouyoumdjian, of America's Cup and Volvo Ocean Race-winning glory, to the composite racing specialists, McConaghy Boats, and North Sails, gifting a state-of-the-art sail package.

But what's so exciting about the upgrades? The appendage package catches the eye: the new and deeper Keel Fin and Bulb to cut drag and maximize the righting moment; the advanced upwind Daggerboards for sharper pointing ability and reducing drag in all water conditions; and perhaps the show-stealer - the C-Foils! These radical additions are geared to escalate lift, limit drag, and enhance the righting moment for reaching and downwind sailing angles.

These tweaks aren't just to elevate Palm Beach XI's race performance, nor to simply reel viewers in with their high-tech sheen. The redesign serves as a living platform for the future, setting a new bar of expectation for luxury motor yachts. With such an ambitious transformation, Palm Beach XI aims not just to capture the front of the Rolex Sydney Hobart fleet, but also the imagination of audiences - thereby disrupting the industry with a vision of what's truly possible for yachting's future.

title: Revolutionary ALY501 Superyacht from Alia Yachts Combines Performance with Luxury in a Spectacular 'Aircraft-carrier' Built
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Revolutionary ALY501 Superyacht from Alia Yachts Combines Performance with Luxury in a Spectacular 'Aircraft-carrier' Built
summary: In a stunning innovation, Turkish yard Alia Yachts has unveiled its newest marvel: the custom-designed 50-metre superyacht ALY501.
body: Pioneering new standards in luxury sailing, Alia Yachts has launched its latest game-changer, the custom-built 50-metre superyacht ALY501. Constructed at its Antalya site in Turkey, this high-strength Alustar aluminium and full carbon superstructure are crafted to embody a remarkable blend of rigidity, efficiency, and extreme lightness, making it a notable step in maritime innovation.

Sporting a futuristic 'aircraft-carrier' bow, ALY501's design showcases a captivatingly modern profile. But this yacht is not just about looks. Fitted with three water jet propulsion units, she is engineered to deliver high speeds, making for an adventurous sailing experience.

Alia Yachts' commitment to precision, emotion, and innovation is apparent in the creation of ALY501. As Alia Yachts' president Gökhan Çelik eloquently puts it, 'She’s engineered to be light, fast, complex and fearless— a testament to the harmony of performance and luxury.'

As she gets ready for the final commissioning and sea trials, completion and delivery are expected by early 2026. Meanwhile, Alia Yachts continues its streak of innovation, with seven superyacht projects – including a new flagship – either on order or under construction.
In the world of luxury boating, Alia Yachts’ ALY501 is a noteworthy launch that sails into the future, making a powerful statement of design, speed, and luxury seafaring.

title: Pioneer initiative by RYA seeks to redefine UK sailing future through community-driven Landmark Survey
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Pioneer initiative by RYA seeks to redefine UK sailing future through community-driven Landmark Survey
summary: In efforts to steer UK's sailing community towards a brighter future, RYA has launched a landmark survey initiative aimed at gathering insights from the community.
body: Sailing and boating in the UK have met their watershed moment. Participation has been waning, making it imperative for industry stakeholders to coalesce towards revitalizing this cherished tradition. Taking up this monumental task, the Royal Yachting Association (RYA), the National Governing Body for the UK's sailing and boating community, has embarked on a landmark initiative — the Reflections on Water Survey.

Advertised as the RYA's largest open study to date, the survey is designed to encapsulate the most holistic picture of life on the water in the UK. From the grassroots level to professional pathways, it aims at comprehending aspects that are functioning optimally, facets that are teetering, and areas most in need of change.

Whether you're a seasoned sailor, a club member, a volunteer, or a marine industry professional, your experiences and insights will contribute towards shaping the future of sailing in the UK. It will enable RYA to support the sport better, strengthen career pathways across the maritime sector, and serve as a beacon, guiding the way towards open and welcoming waters for all pastime enthusiasts and professionals.

The Reflections on Water Survey, which will run until December 2021, will help shape future initiatives, opportunities, and investment. It's a testament to RYA’s belief that sailing and boating is a thread in the rich tapestry of the UK's national identity and a hopeful call-to-arms for a united maritime future.

Embedded in the midst of RYA's Reflections on Water campaign, the survey becomes the conduit for connecting nationwide voices to drive meaningful change. Steering towards a more accessible, inclusive, and open sailing and boating culture, it stands as testimony to RYA’s steadfast long-term commitment to the maritime community.

Tying up for the future, RS Sailing, an innovative small-sailing craft designer, has been announced as the official partner of the RYA's Connected series of events, webinars, and activities for 2025-2026. The partnership aims to enhance and empower leaders across the RYA's extensive affiliate network, including sailing clubs, class associations, and training centres. Demonstrating strong faith in partnership and progress, these collaborative efforts envision a bright future for sailing in the UK.

title: Pristine 27m Leopard Motor Yacht Principessa Matera Reduced to Waterline in Shocking Blaze at Capo Noli
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Pristine 27m Leopard Motor Yacht Principessa Matera Reduced to Waterline in Shocking Blaze at Capo Noli
summary: The Leopard motor yacht Principessa Matera, a gem of the Italian seas, suffered a devastating fire, leaving only ashes in its wake.
body: The world of luxury yachting was shaken when news broke out that the prestigious 26.9-meter Leopard motor yacht, Principessa Matera, has been destroyed by an indefatigable blaze off the coast of Capo Noli in Italy. Alarms were raised promptly at 2.00 pm on the 6th of November, with authorities intervening and successfully evacuating the three souls on board – a heartening tale in a saga of loss.

Photos released by Italy's fire and rescue service, the Vigili del Fuoco team, reveal the heart-wrenching extent of the damage. Principessa Matera, once a shining symbol of aquatic luxury, was burnt down to the waterline. Thick plumes of dark smoke bellowed into the air, casting a shadowy veil visible for miles.

The devastating lost yacht, Principessa Matera, hailed from the Leopard 27M series, known for fixed sunpads on the aft deck and bow, accommodation for seven guests, and an impressive top speed of 35 knots. The exterior design was the brainchild of the renowned Italian studio Paolo Caliari. Its fiery end was a tragic blow to not only its owners but also to aficionados of the Leopard design.

As we delve deeper into the catastrophe and the status quo of the investigation, we bid farewell to the Principessa Matera. Once a symbol of unmatched grandeur and speed, the yacht now sleeps in ashes and silence beneath the azure Italian waves.

title: Sydney International On-Water Boat Show Ushers Advent of Discover Boating Festival Hub - Explore Boating Delights Without Laying Down a Dime
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Sydney International On-Water Boat Show Ushers Advent of Discover Boating Festival Hub - Explore Boating Delights Without Laying Down a Dime
summary: Sydney International On-Water Boat Show casts its net further afield, launching a captivating, free 'Discover Boating Festival Hub' this November.
body: The maritime sphere is spreading its wings further this year. The Sydney International On-Water Boat Show, scheduled from 13 to 16 November, will bring a breath of fresh air to the expansive public areas of Darling Harbour. A new, crowd-pleasing event, the Discover Boating Festival Hub, will not require visitors to purchase tickets and is guaranteed to sweep visitors off their feet. For the first time, venues such as Palm Grove, Tumbalong Boulevard, and Tumbalong Park will pulsate with the energy of a bustling festival, inviting thousands of curious folk to probe the delights of life connected to water. This freely accessible zone offers an effortless chance for the public to plunge into the boating universe, featuring straightforward trailerable craft, essential equipment exhibitions, and appealing hospitality options. A staggering 87% of past year's participants concurred that the event does a stellar job of endorsing boating as a cherished social or family pastime. The boating industry, thus, is eager to underline the already validated benefits of getting afloat, which amplify health and wellbeing. The grand festival endeavours to demonstrate how boating embodies the "Blue Mind" phenomenon - the soothing, rejuvenating state of mind we experience when dwelling close to, in, or on water - presenting an idyllic remedy for our frantic and tension-filled modern lives. In addition to more than 160 larger vessels that will spearhead the paid on-water display in Cockle Bay, the shore-side festival will flaunt an assortment of well-liked trailerable craft, boating accessories, and innovative technology. Noteworthy highlights of the Discover Boating Festival Hub include the grand introduction of the recognised Smuggler range of Amphibious RIBs in Australia by Amphibious AU. These boats are uniquely designed to deliver superlative performance, exceptional craftsmanship, and state-of-the-art innovation. The Amphibious AU's RIBs are engineered for adaptability and convenience, smoothly shifting between land and water, and offering outstanding freedom to those wishing to explore without boundaries. Another attention grabber, Hunts Marine South Coast will be exhibiting the extraordinary Cruise Craft line-up, headlined by the brand-new E770HT, the versatile E695HT, and the fan-favourite Explorer 635 Hard Top. These boats - perfect for both offshore escapades and tranquil weekends on water - are applauded for their inventive design, stellar performance, and unrivalled comfort.

title: Historic 72-Meter Superyacht Argosy Undertakes a Three-Year Overhaul Journey at Renowned Dutch Shipyard Feadship
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Historic 72-Meter Superyacht Argosy Undertakes a Three-Year Overhaul Journey at Renowned Dutch Shipyard Feadship
summary: The esteemed classic yacht Argosy, after decades of illustrious service and numerous ownership hands, is set for a comprehensive three-year restoration at the Aalsmeer Feadship house.
body: The historic 71.5-metre classic superyacht Argosy has been ushered to a distinguished new chapter in her journey. The vessel made its way to Feadship's renowned facility in Aalsmeer, the Netherlands, for a grand, three-year rebuild project. The redelivery has been scheduled for September 2028, and is eagerly awaited by maritime enthusiasts around the globe.

The extraordinary blend of heritage and design in Argosy's architecture makes her rebuild a highly anticipated event. Her classic blueprint was devised by the New York studio Cox & Stevens and briefly entrusted to Italian designer Luca Dini for its interiors and restoration before the project was brought to a halt. Eventually, Argosy was auctioned in 2021.

The current owner, represented by Anton Foord at Ocean Independence, plans to restore the yacht to its full glory, with the esteemed brokerage firm also supervising the technical aspects. As of her last sailing, Argosy flaunted five en suite cabins, accompanied by accommodation for 17 crew members, as well as stores and a galley. However, the full scope of the new restoration project remains a secret, but undoubtedly many eyes will be following the project with interest.

title: Compass Tenders Unveils Exclusive Boats for Amels’ First 80 Model, the Glorious Superyacht Pangea
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Compass Tenders Unveils Exclusive Boats for Amels’ First 80 Model, the Glorious Superyacht Pangea
summary: Compass Tenders has proudly launched two uniquely patterned tender boats for the foremost Amels 80 model, Pangea.
body: Compass Tenders sure knows how to make waves – they've announced the release of two exceptional custom-made tenders for the first-ever Amels 80 model, the much-coveted superyacht Pangea. This magnificent sea marvel was delivered from the Damen Yachting's top-notch facilities in Vlissingen, the Netherlands, last month and is currently sailing the high seas on course for the splendid Caribbean island of Antigua. The first custom order fulfilled by Compass was an impressively sleek 11.7-metre Limousine tender. The buyer specified certain preferences that included ensuring enough clear headroom for a party of eight guests and to maximise exterior seating space.

Creating a perfect blend of style, comfort, and elegance, Compass joined forces with Sinot Architecture and Design to bring the interior spaces to life. The results are nothing short of dazzling – walnut panelling and chic leather seating, ambience-enhancing subtle lighting, a premium K-Array sound system, reliable Starlink WiFi, and two TVs for onboard entertainment.

Matching the versatility of Pangea, the second custom order was a DRIB, a model that can swiftly switch roles between a dive and fishing boat, or guest transporter. A unique feature of this tender is her 'pick-up truck inspired' engine box which allows for secure transportation of equipment cases. Keeping up with the fashion statement of the former, the DRIB also features two-tone seating and a clear coat carbon construction.

Both of these tenders were constructed to superyacht standards, with meticulous attention to detail, in a swift 15-month timeframe. When it comes to luxury, Compass Tenders certainly makes no compromises!

title: Discover the Delights of Britain's Most Remarkable Sailing Spots on the RYA 150 Podcast
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover the Delights of Britain's Most Remarkable Sailing Spots on the RYA 150 Podcast
summary: RYA 150’s latest podcast instalment lifts anchor on a vivacious discussion regarding Britain's most thrilling sailing destinations, hosted by British yachtswoman Dee Caffari.
body: The United Kingdom, with its bewitching coastlines, ancient lochs and tranquil inland waterways, is a veritable Edenesque playground for sailors and boating enthusiasts. The question as to which of these enticing locations holds the crown as the 'best' sailing destination in Britain becomes the vibrant heartbeat of RYA 150’s seventh podcast episode. This lively episode is led by British yachtswoman and host, Dee Caffari, who navigates a passionate debate among a panel teeming with comprehensive knowledge and personal experiences. With an array of geographically diverse participants, each providing a unique perspective, the audience is left spellbound by secrets of the British Isles' vast sailing spaces. Panelists hail from various corners and components of the British boating community, each reflecting a distinct maritime experience. Offshore racer Maggie Adamson, minimalistic sailor Roger Barnes, Shell Channel Pilot editor Rachel Sprot, Para sailor Rory McKinna, and liveaboard narrowboater Elizabeth Earle all bring their unique stories to the table. From battling tides in the Solent to uncovering hidden inlets in West Country, from refining tactics in a shifting Scottish loch to serene scenes in quiet inland waterways, the episode paints a rich canvas of the myriad face of British boating. The episode is a splendid paean to the multitude of thrilling, beautiful, and historically rich sailing experiences the UK has to offer, rather than boiling the discussion down to the singular 'best' spot. As the enlightening narratives of the panelists unfurl, it becomes apparent that there is an astounding wealth of sailing opportunities, each with its unique thrill and charm, waiting right at Britons' doorstep. The celebration of exciting domestic sailing adventures adds to the existing charm of the RYA 150 Podcast series that showcases 150 years of enriching British sailing heritage. Beyond serving as an educational platform, the podcast is a beacon of inspiration for prospective sailors, inviting them to embark on their maritime journey across the UK's charming landscapes.

title: 18 IMOCAs Blast Off..... its the Transat Café L’OR 2025
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: 18 IMOCAs Blast Off as the Transat Café L’OR 2025 Gets Underway From Le Havre to the Caribbean
summary: LE HAVRE, FRANCE | The final IMOCA race of the 2025 season has officially roared into life, as 18 of the world’s fastest foiling yachts crossed the start line of the Transat Café L’OR, bound for Fort-de-France, Martinique. Stretching 4,350 nautical miles across the North Atlantic, the race marks the dramatic finale to a year of relentless competition for the IMOCA fleet — and with conditions building out of the Engli
body: The Transat Café L’OR closes a five-event IMOCA programme that has seen 22 boats compete across Europe and the Atlantic in both fully-crewed and double-handed formats. It also sets the stage for an even bigger 2026 season, with 11 new IMOCAs currently under construction — the clearest sign yet that the Class continues to grow in power, pace, and prestige.

Few sailors approach the IMOCA game with the quiet precision of Yoann Richomme. Already a two-time transatlantic race winner, and runner-up in the 2024 Vendée Globe, Richomme is a man who knows both how to pace an ocean and when to strike. Now, sailing alongside Corentin Horeau aboard Paprec Arkéa, he’s back in contention — and firmly among the favourites to win the Transat Café L’OR 2025.

“We’ve got a fairly good chance,” Richomme told the IMOCA Class in the days before the start. “Our boat is well suited to the conditions — November storms, big downwind legs, rough seas — it’s what we love. It’s everything IMOCA racing is about.”

That confidence is not misplaced. Paprec Arkéa has enjoyed a steady upward curve all season, finishing third in the Rolex Fastnet Race and second in The Ocean Race Europe. Add in Richomme’s relentless drive and Horeau’s tactical brilliance, and the duo are a potent force — cool, methodical, and quietly determined to go one better than their second-place finish in this same race two years ago.

The course itself is a sailor’s riddle. From Le Havre, the fleet charges through the Channel, then dives southwest past Ushant and Cape Finisterre, slipping beneath the Canary Islands before catching the Trade Winds across the Atlantic to the Caribbean. On paper, it’s simple. In practice, it’s chaos.

“It’s going to be strong out of the Channel,” Richomme said before the start. “We’ll be flat-out early on, then hit a ridge of light air in Biscay. After that, there’s a low off Portugal, and everything depends on how that develops. It could make or break the race.”

With the boats capable of sustained speeds above 30 knots, the early stages will be brutal — long hours on deck, short bursts of sleep, and every decision magnified. Richomme and Horeau will need to balance aggression with caution as the fleet snakes its way toward the Trades, where the foilers will finally stretch their wings for a downwind drag race to the finish.
The 2025 Transat Café L’OR has drawn one of the strongest IMOCA line-ups of the decade. At the front of the pack, expect fierce competition from:
Sam Goodchild & Loïs Berrehar (MACIF Santé Prévoyance) – current IMOCA Globe Series leaders, consistent and fast in all conditions.
Ambrogio Beccaria & Thomas Ruyant (Allagrande Mapei Racing) – fresh from success in The Ocean Race Europe, combining Italian flair with northern grit.
Elodie Bonafous & Yann Eliès (Association Petits Princes–Quéguiner) – a mixed-crew powerhouse with serious Figaro and Vendée experience.
Jérémie Beyou & Morgan Lagravière (Charal) – the ultimate veterans of foiling IMOCA racing, always dangerous in big breeze.

Further down the fleet, the talent runs deep. Sam Davies & Violette Dorange (Initiatives-Cœur), Justine Mettraux & Xavier Macaire (Teamwork–Team SNEF), and Romain Attanasio & Maxime Sorel (Fortinet–Best Western) bring years of Vendée Globe and transatlantic pedigree.

Even the so-called “daggerboard division” — featuring Nico D’Estais & Simon Koster on Café Joyeux — promises close racing, with boats separated by only fractions of a knot in performance. Expect them to punch above their weight in the early going, before the foilers take off in the Trades.

Another storyline to watch is the newly-renamed 11th Hour Racing Team, co-skippered by Francesca Clapcich and Will Harris, sailing the ex-Malizia–Seaexplorer. For Harris, this will be the final outing on this battle-proven foiler before Team Malizia takes delivery of its new generation IMOCA next summer.

“We finished seventh last time with Boris (Herrmann),” Harris explained. “Now I’d like to beat that. There are eight big foiling boats capable of winning, so a top-five finish would be really satisfying.”

It’s this mix of fresh ambition and veteran know-how that makes IMOCA racing so intoxicating — and why the Transat Café L’OR has quickly earned its place as a must-win on the professional ocean racing calendar.

This year’s race doesn’t just mark the end of a season — it signals the dawn of a new era for IMOCA. With 11 new boats in build, the Class is entering a phase of unprecedented expansion, powered by growing fan engagement, advanced sustainability goals, and crossover attention from other major events like The Ocean Race and Vendée Globe.

From Paprec Arkéa to MACIF and Charal, the latest generation of IMOCA designs has pushed the limits of performance — bigger foils, lighter hulls, smarter energy systems, and next-generation autopilots that are redefining solo and double-handed ocean racing.

Each transatlantic race becomes a live testing ground for what will eventually appear on the Vendée Globe start line in 2028. And that’s what makes Le Havre’s dockside buzz electric — sailors, designers, and sponsors all watching every mile like it’s a laboratory in motion.

For Richomme, the Transat Café L’OR carries more than just the lure of another trophy. He currently sits third in the IMOCA Globe Series standings, just behind Paul Meilhat (Biotherm) and leader Sam Goodchild. A strong result could lift him to second, or even challenge for the top spot — depending on how MACIF fares.

“It’s probably a long shot to catch Sam unless he has a problem — and you never wish that on anyone,” Richomme said. “But I’ve never won the IMOCA Globe Series, and that’s something I’d love to change.”

With 18 boats on the start line, 4,350 miles to the Caribbean, and an Atlantic full of shifting weather systems, the 2025 Transat Café L’OR promises to be the most exhilarating finale the IMOCA Class has seen in years.
The northwesterly start will test nerves, the light-air ridge in Biscay will sort the tacticians from the gamblers, and the final 1,000-mile Trade Wind run to Martinique will be pure foiling poetry.
As ever in ocean racing, nothing is certain — except that the fleet will arrive salt-crusted, exhausted, and changed by the crossing.

And somewhere on the docks of Fort-de-France, a new transatlantic champion will lift the trophy — proof once again that the IMOCA Class remains sailing’s purest test of endurance, technology, and human will.

title: 2025 ILCA Under-21 European Titles Decided
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: 2025 ILCA Under-21 European Titles Decided After a Week of Thrills and Precision
summary: After six days of fast, fierce, and finely balanced racing, the curtain has come down on the 2025 ILCA Under-21 European Championships & Open European Trophy, hosted by the renowned JK Mornar Yacht Club in Split.
body: A fleet of the world’s most promising young sailors — representing over 35 nations — delivered a masterclass in determination, boat-handling, and strategy across the ILCA 6 (Women’s) and ILCA 7 (Men’s) fleets. Twelve scheduled races for the gold groups, 11 for the ILCA 7 Silver fleet, and a final day that could not have been scripted better — this was youth sailing at its finest.

Under golden Adriatic skies, with a breeze of 10 to 14 knots filling across the bay, the final two races brought the week to a spectacular close. As the gun fired for the last time, titles were still up for grabs, the points razor-thin, and the margins measured in seconds rather than meters.

When the spray settled, Ginevra Caracciolo (ITA) and Erik Norlén (SWE) stood atop the podium as the 2025 ILCA Under-21 European Champions — both showing nerves of steel and the kind of form that hints at future Olympic glory.
Italy Dominates the ILCA 6 Women’s Fleet
Women’s division, confirming Italy’s status as the powerhouse of European dinghy sailing.

Caracciolo’s campaign was a model of consistency — smooth starts, surgical mark roundings, and an almost unflappable composure under pressure. Her mastery of the variable conditions around Split Bay earned her not just the European Championship title, but also victory in the Open European Trophy, edging out American sailor Isabella Mendoza Cabezas (USA), who placed a strong third overall in the Open standings.

“Each race tested something different — from light-air patience to heavy-air endurance,” Caracciolo said after coming ashore. “To win here, you had to adapt instantly. I’m so proud of the whole Italian team — we pushed each other every single day.”
Behind her, Arseni and Mattivi traded punches throughout the week, both scoring podium finishes that underline Italy’s depth in the next generation of Olympic-class sailors.
Sweden’s Norlén Holds His Nerve in the ILCA 7
the final day was a tactical chess match in motion. Erik Norlén (SWE), who had led overnight, showed remarkable calm under mounting pressure to seal gold with 45 points after 12 races.
Bronze — Rem Pulci Magen (ISR) — 62 pts

Norlén’s performance showcased textbook upwind control and downwind confidence — the combination every ILCA sailor dreams of. “It’s been a long week with every kind of condition you can imagine,” he said. “I just tried to stay smart and keep the boat moving fast. It’s an incredible feeling to win here in Split.”

Behind him, Germany’s Ole Schweckendiek finished strong with a series of top-five results to claim silver, while Israel’s Rem Pulci Magen took a well-earned bronze — a result that confirms his growing reputation as one of the fleet’s rising stars.
U19 Brilliance: Greece Strikes Gold
If there was one moment that summed up the spirit of youth sailing, it came in the Under-19 ILCA 7 Championship, where Greece’s Adamantios Petrianos clinched gold in the very last race.
With the pressure on, Petrianos delivered a near-perfect final day, finishing second in the last race to overtake Spain’s Karol Krupski Teterycz by just a few points.
“It came down to the wire,” said Petrianos, still grinning on the dock. “I knew I had to keep calm and just sail my race — not think about the points. It’s amazing to bring this win home for Greece.”
Split Delivers: A Showcase of Skill and Sportsmanship

Across the six days of racing, Split delivered the full range of conditions — from gentle thermals to sharp gusts and rolling chop. Each race demanded total focus and endurance, testing both technical skill and mental resilience.
Coaches and spectators praised the level of professionalism on display, calling the event “a glimpse into the future of Olympic sailing.”
By the time the final gun fired, sailors were sunburned, exhausted, and smiling — the surest sign of a week well sailed.
A Word of Thanks — and a Glimpse Ahead
As the championship wrapped up, organizers from JK Mornar Yacht Club earned praise for their flawless management of a complex regatta featuring over 200 boats and multiple fleets.

“The energy here has been phenomenal,” said one official. “From sunrise rigging to the last finish, these young sailors showed the passion and precision that define the ILCA class. Split has once again proven it’s one of Europe’s great sailing venues.”

The 2025 ILCA Under-21 European Championships will be remembered not only for its close finishes but also for the spirit of fair play, the camaraderie between nations, and the emergence of names we’ll almost certainly see on future Olympic start lines.

As the sails come down and the boats are packed away, the Adriatic quiets once more — but for the sailors of the ILCA class, Split 2025 will forever mark a milestone in their journey from youth promise to professional greatness.

title: Bridging the Thrill of Sailing and Luxurious Motor Yachts: Unveiling The Elemental Project
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Bridging the Thrill of Sailing and Luxurious Motor Yachts: Unveiling The Elemental Project
summary: Introducing Project Elemental - an innovative sailing catamaran concept that beautifully blends the luxury of motor yachts with the exhilarating spirit of sailing.
body: Imagine capturing the thrill of sailing while luxuriating in the comfort of a motor yacht. Project Elemental, a groundbreaking collaboration by Tripp Design Naval Architecture and British studio Design Unlimited, expertly caters to both the zestful sailors and the lovers of serene voyages. This 50.4-metre sailing catamaran, with brokerage by Superyacht Partners, is not about its size - it’s about setting new benchmarks in large sailing yachts and their offerings. The idea was to design a yacht that doesn’t compromise on excitement while maintaining stable control even at 18 knots to ensure a sense of safety and luxury for the owner. To amplify the allure for potential yacht owners, the Elemental Project aims to eliminate the discomfort and unease often associated with sailing on a racing yacht. By offering spacious, versatile, and luxurious spaces intrinsic to motor yachts, it successfully combines the best of both sailing and motor-yachting worlds. The desirability of this catamaran doesn’t stop there. Renowned yacht broker, Will Bishop, affirms that hybrid and regenerative systems integrated into Elemental Project essentially offer a vast range, beating any motor yacht, while minimising fuel consumption. Safety is another notable advantage – its design asserting stability even under strong winds. Careful attention is given to the scale of the catamaran without compromising its sailing performance. The ample hull volume allows the creation of generous interiors that offer a balance of open social spaces and private cosy corners that meet various needs of yacht owners. Considering modern yacht owners’ lifestyle and extended stay aboard, the design focuses on their need for both lively shared spaces and private retreats. Crew considerations have been just as central for the design team - private cabins, a watersports room, tender stowage, and straightforward sailing systems ensure better living and working conditions for the crew while enhancing the overall guest experience. To achieve an optimal balance wherein neither performance is compromised nor sail plan becomes unmanageable, aluminium Alustar hulls and moderate displacement are central to the design. These features permit the owner to venture further, experience sizzling speed, and revel in the luxury - all while reducing the carbon footprint. A foray into the future of yacht sailing, the Elemental project is a testament to ingenious design, environmental initiatives, the interface of opulence, and performance. This blend of speed, luxury, and sustainability in design leaves no doubt that the future of sailing will be an elemental sail plan.

title: Gareth Ede Shines at the Grafham Catamaran Open: An Exhilarating Display of Nautical Dexterity
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Gareth Ede Shines at the Grafham Catamaran Open: An Exhilarating Display of Nautical Dexterity
summary: The Grafham Catamaran Open witnessed Gareth Ede sailing into glory, marking an unrivaled winning streak in the Jon Montgomery Travellers Trophy series.
body: Imagine a fine Sunday morning, the wisps of fog parting to reveal the perfectly calm waters of Grafham, rippled lightly by a gentle Force 2 to 3 breeze. It was on this photographic tableau that Gareth Ede reigned supreme at the Grafham Catamaran Open, commanding an electrifying performance with six straight wins and nearly a perfect score for the entire season. The waterways came alive as five valiant Catapult helms duked it out in the highly anticipated last event of their season, held the weekend of 18-19th October. The excitement on board reached fever pitch as the finale of both the Jon Montgomery Travellers Trophy and the Alastair Forrest Personal Handicap Trophy drew near.

The event was a celebration of strategy and speed, of split-second decisions and of the deep connection between a sailor and his vessel. Beyond the individual feats, it was a testament to the age-old allure of nautical racing, rekindling the timeless romance between humankind and the vast blue.

title: An Embodiment of Innovation: Palm Beach Motor Yachts Reveals Ambitious Rebuild of Wild Oat XI
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: An Embodiment of Innovation: Palm Beach Motor Yachts Reveals Ambitious Rebuild of Wild Oat XI
summary: Palm Beach Motor Yachts is ushering in a new era for the renowned regatta champion, Wild Oats XI, reimagining it as Palm Beach XI.
body: Equipped with expertise, innovative vision, and loads of tenacity, Palm Beach Motor Yachts has embarked on an ambitious journey: the revival and transformation of the iconic 30.5-metre McConaghy sailing yacht, Wild Oats XI. Emerging under a new guise as the Palm Beach XI, the vessel is destined to carry its legacy forward.

Palm Beach XI is set to undergo numerous transformations, the most significant of which includes a new appendage package designed to put her back at the forefront of the Rolex Sydney Hobart fleet. A deeper keel fin and bulb will reduce drag while advanced upwind daggerboards will optimize pointing ability. The radical C-Foils will optimize lift and provide enhanced righting moment for reaching and downwind sailing angles. A state-of-the-art sail package by North Sails completes the equation, promising stellar performance.

The vessel's legacy speaks volumes. In 2014, sailing as Wild Oats XI, the yacht clinched the Rolex Sydney Hobart Yacht Race line honours for the eighth time, setting an unmatched record of two days, two hours three minutes and 26 seconds. This experience gives the new Palm Beach XI a springboard for future victories.

Moreover, the richness of these rebuild learnings will be carried over to Palm Beach Motor Yachts' upcoming motor yacht range, the flagship of which, the 27.6-metre Falcon, is expected to launch this October. History, innovation, and vision are converging as a new legend takes shape, perfectly encapsulating the courage to reimagine, the consistency to excel, and the passion that fuels it all.

title: Experience the Riva Ferrari 32: A Remarkable Fusion between the Power of Ferrari and the Craftsmanship of Riva
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Experience the Riva Ferrari 32: A Remarkable Fusion between the Power of Ferrari and the Craftsmanship of Riva
summary: Venture into the story of the Riva Ferrari 32, a unique combination of Riva's phenomenal boatbuilding skills and Ferrari's unrivalled design prowess.
body: Manipulating the confines between land and sea, the Riva Ferrari 32 emerged as a high-end feat of engineering and design. A blend of Ferrari's design aesthetics derived from the inspiring Testarossa supercar and Riva's boatbuilding excellence, this luxury yacht showcased power, style, and rarity at its finest.

Historically, car manufacturers have often stumbled when transitioning their prowess from asphalt to sea. Encounters with the marine world have led to infeasible designs and unseaworthy contraptions, marked by the unsuccessful attempts of Mercedes, BMW, and Lexus, among others. However, this rule found its exception in Ferrari during the 1980s.

Powering the Riva Ferrari 32 were two 390hp BPM Vulcano V8 petrol engines linked to race-style surface drives with Rolla propellers, enabling it to achieve commendable speeds. But beyond the performance and the aesthetics, the rarity of these yachts - with only 40 units ever built - adds to the allure and desirability of these magnificent vessels.

Taking the helm of a Riva Ferrari 32 in Port Hercule, Monaco, would certainly establish your presence, with a grandeur and panache that few other vessels could muster. As such, the Riva Ferrari 32 yacht remains a testament to what can be achieved when two remarkable forces in their respective fields join hands, creating an extraordinary addition to the maritime world.

title: The Majestic 47.9-metre Christensen Motor Yacht Amore Now up for Sale
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Majestic 47.9-metre Christensen Motor Yacht Amore Now up for Sale
summary: The luxurious 47.9-metre motor yacht Amore, an in-house designed beauty from US yard Christensen, hits the brokerage market.
body: The 'Amore', an exquisite product of US yard Christensen, is now on the brokerage market. Built in 2005, this premium motor yacht offers an experience of a lifetime to its dwellers. Amore was constructed under the astute supervision of a well-versed yachtsman having close connections with the shipyard.

The magnificence of the yacht lay in her construction, an in-house design crafted in GRP and beautiful interiors by Carol Williamson & Associates. The cabin, featuring walnut walls, hosts world-class marble inlay and stonework. Recently, Amore claimed a price tag of $19,500,000.

In 2022, a radical refit costing $2.8 million was undertaken in Fort Lauderdale. The refit added a new paint job, overhauled the engine, and upgraded the galley. Accommodations were updated with the replacement of the interior and exterior soft furnishings in 2021. Further, she is certified fit, having successfully completed a 15-year ABS special survey in 2020.

The yacht's top deck, boasting a barbecue, shaded bar, and a lounge with a forward Jacuzzi, offers a mesmerizing view of the endless ocean. An open-plan lounge and a formal dining area that can entertain up to 12 guests amplify the elegance of the main deck. The yacht is powered by twin MTU 1,800hp diesel engines. It can attain a top speed of 17 knots and cruise up to 4,500 nautical miles at 12 knots. Further, key specs include a nine-metre beam and an interior volume of 499GT.
This Christensen masterstroke, evolving with time and meticulous maintenance by its current owner, continuously endures to uphold its grandeur on the high seas.

title: Experience the Luxury of the Seas: The Majestic 29m Sailing Yacht Thila Now for Sale
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Experience the Luxury of the Seas: The Majestic 29m Sailing Yacht Thila Now for Sale
summary: Unleash your inner adventurer as the coveted 29.1 metres Thila, an Australian-born sailing yacht, comes up for sale, offering an artistic blend of sustaining opulence and maritime performance.
body: Gaze upon the exquisite Thila, a grand 29-meter sailing yacht that blends seaborne elegance with high-performance craft. Delivered in 2009 by renowned Australian shipyard Steve Ward & Co, and designed by the esteemed Dubois Naval Architects, Thila's allure is now available for the discerning eye to purchase.

Thila's life began under the warm Australian sun. Commissioned by an acclaimed Olympic yachtsman, she was crafted in the lively city of Perth. The yacht's external design is an artefact from the prestigious studios of Dubois Naval Architects, notable for their fashioning of aquatic masterpieces. The inviting interiors, the ingenious work of British studio Rhoades Young Design, complement the grandeur of the exterior perfectly.

Constructed with aluminium under the stringent guidelines of Lloyd's class, Thila has received nothing but professional use and meticulous care. The pride of her halfway world journey, Thila stands tall at a stately €4,850,000 (VAT included).

A key specification in her design is the completely moulded bowsprit extension, fixed in 2016, accommodating one of her magnificent twin gennaker sails, delivered in 2025. Thila’s interior is well-appointed to comfortably house up to six guests in a three-cabin layout. It includes a full-beam owner's suite, a twin cabin to port, and a double cabin to starboard. All three connected en suite and equipped with pipe cots, providing additional flexibility.

The living quarters onboard Thila are a testament to opulence, seamlessly marrying elegance with comfort. Broad picture frame windows bathe the raised primary saloon in soothing natural light while offering panoramic marina views. Step below to the secondary saloon, offering seclusion with its calm TV lounge and versatile seating arrangements, allowing glimpses of the maritime surroundings.

The yacht's exterior, a creation of Dubois, is family-friendly with ample lounging space, and a significantly large swim platform facilitated by a fold-down transom. The cockpit lounge, devoid of lines, is equipped with two U-shaped sofas perfect for relishing the outdoor sea breeze. The majestic Thila, a blend of grandeur and performance, awaits her new owner for the ultimate seafaring experience.

title: 38.4 Metre Feadship Yacht Calypso Set to Rekindle Majesty on Sea Following In-depth Refit
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: 38.4 Metre Feadship Yacht Calypso Set to Rekindle Majesty on Sea Following In-depth Refit
summary: Making a grand re-entry into the brokerage market is the classic Feadship motor yacht Calypso, which is now listed for sale following a meticulous 12-month refurbishment.
body: The 38.4-metre classic Feadship motor yacht Calypso, a symbol of elegance and sophistication, is once again ready to bask under the blazing sun and indulge leisure-seekers who are passionate about the serene infinity of open water. Fresh from a twelve-month, multi-million-dollar refit, the yacht is now up for sale, once again promising to make waves with her charm and class.

The yacht was constructed in aluminium and steel back in 1978 by Feadship, with the iconic De Voogt Naval Architects at the helm of her design. Over her impressive, almost half-century run, Calypso has undergone numerous refurbishment periods, particularly between 2016 and 2017, each renewing its lustre and keeping the stunning vessel sailing high.

The Calypso, asking $9,995,000, was initially designed as a venue to host luxurious parties by automotive millionaire E. Clayton Gengras. From royal dignitaries to Hollywood hotshots, many have graced her decks, most notably during the era of Malcolm Forbes. The yacht, once a party paradise, was later converted into a family yacht. In the early 2000s, the vessel embarked on a new venture, teaming up with National Geographic to delve into remote corners of the world to facilitate scientific research.

The latest refurbishment effort reflects an elegant balance between maintaining the original Feadship aesthetics and integrating modern technology. The once forward main dining room now serves as a lavishly decorated master cabin, while the full-beam lower deck that used to house the master, is now a plush VIP suite. Accommodation has been revamped to comfortably house up to 11 guests. The living space is bright and airy, thanks to oversized windows, while the decoration is intentionally designed to create an idyllic space to unwind.

Calypso epitomises outdoor luxury; a new jacuzzi, complimented by sunpads, sun loungers, a barbecue and a 12-person alfresco dining table forms the expanse of her outdoor facilities. A state-of-the-art audiovisual system expands enjoyment capacity of the vessel, ensuring guests can relish entertainment across interior and exterior spaces.

The refurbished vessel is equipped with a pair of Caterpillar 600hp engines and capable of cruising at 10 knots, with a top speed of 13 knots. Importantly, she is fitted with zero-speed stabilisers for safety and comfort while traversing unfettered across her impressive cruising range of 3,200 nautical miles.

title: Experiencing Bliss on Water: The Story of an Aquador, a Yamarin, and the Delightful Duchy 25
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Experiencing Bliss on Water: The Story of an Aquador, a Yamarin, and the Delightful Duchy 25
summary: How does owning two outstanding sailboats sound? Dive into this discovery of aquatic experiences on an Aquador 32C, a Yamarin 59HT and the quirks of the Duchy 25.
body: Is there anything better than owning a great boat? Owning two, of course! Let's embark on the story of a unique couple who own a farm situated virtually as a peninsula in the Fal Estuary, an idyllic locale for boat lovers. Lips are parted in wonder as the tale unfolds, relating the experience of owning an Aquador 32C, Molly, and a Yamarin 59HT, Sula.

Molly was welcomed in early 2022, joining her esteemed sibling, Sula, a fantastic launch-and-retrieve sportsboat, perfect for quick and spontaneous adventures. With a keen sense for both leisure and practicality, this couple basks in the simple pleasure and freedom Sula offers, particularly during the months Molly is docked (May to September).

But the aquatic adventure does not end there! Enter the Duchy 25, a British-built compact cruiser that woos every visitor at the Southampton Boat Show. Facing off competition from numerous flashy mass-market sportsboats, this charming craft stands apart.

The Duchy 25 is based on the hull of its popular namesake, modified to accommodate an outboard motor and reconfigured for an open day boat/weekender concept. One of its most appealing aspects is its adjustability to accommodate anything from a silent electric outboard to a beefy 200hp petrol engine. With the heavy engine box removed to maximize cockpit space, it’s perfect for leisurely excursions. The u-shaped dinette in the cockpit, designed for six, can convert into a sunpad or overnight berth, making it an affordable, family-friendly, and highly desirable boat. Thus, the story of this nautical trio - an Aquador, a Yamarin, and a Duchy - is a delightful chronicle of the joys and adventures of life on water.

title: Clapcich and Harris Utilise Météo France Weather Buoy to Enhance Oceanographic Research During Transat Café L'OR
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Clapcich and Harris Utilise Météo France Weather Buoy to Enhance Oceanographic Research During Transat Café L'OR
summary: Francesca Clapcich and Will Harris, participating in the Transat Café L'OR race, have used their race boat to deploy a weather buoy for oceanographic research.
body: In the throes of the Transat Café L'OR race (spanning a remarkable 4,350 nautical miles from Le Havre, France, to Fort-de-France in Martinique), Francesca Clapcich and Will Harris have placed themselves in the spotlight not only for their racing prowess but also for their addition to the field of Oceanographic research. Their 60-foot foiling IMOCA race boat, named '11th Hour Racing', served as the deployment site for a Météo France Surface Velocity Program (SVP) drifting weather buoy. This buoy, introduced between the Canary Islands and Cape Verde, has been met with considerable enthusiasm as it enables the capture and transmission of essential climate data, including atmospheric pressure, sea surface temperature, and ocean current dynamics.

The Météo France weather buoy is not the pair's only contribution to the scientific sphere. They are also carrying along a small Argonautica beacon - a component of France's Space Agency's (CNES) educational program. This beacon, tracked by the Argos satellite, serves as a learning aid for over 200 classrooms across France involved in the Argonautica Project. The 'Régate & Satellites' program allows students to track the team's progress on the ArgOcéan platform, fostering a keen interest in satellite technology, data science, and oceanography.

At the heart of these initiatives is Clapcich's mission encapsulated by her campaign 'Believe, Belong, Achieve'. The campaign, in association with their team sponsor, 11th Hour Racing, seeks to usher in transformative changes within the realms of sailing and sports. It does so through advocacy, inciting collective action and promoting inclusivity. Pleasingly, the deployment of the weather buoy mirrors this mission perfectly, symbolising the role sports can play in fostering a greater understanding of our world and contributing positively towards it.

title: Introducing Four Winns' Newest Powercats: The Stellar TH33 and TH38, Fusing Style and Power
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Introducing Four Winns' Newest Powercats: The Stellar TH33 and TH38, Fusing Style and Power
summary: Four Winns latest addition to the powercat family is the fun, spacious, and stylish TH33, a boat commanding a top-tier price of €354,000.
body: Four Winns doesn't stop stunning the yachting world with its breath-taking designs. The recent launch of the TH33 and an update on the TH36 catamarans serve as the latest testament to the brand's genius and creativity. The TH33 strikes as an embodiment of fun, comfort, and aesthetic appeal, albeit for a cool price of €354,000. The updated 36-footer, now dubbed TH38, follows suit in impressive style.

At the boat's aft, a generous swim platform situates neatly between the duo of 300hp outboards. It forms a natural and welcoming passerelle facilitating easy stern-to embarkation. Additionally, the TH33 comes equipped with removable grab rails, handy during cruising for ensuring young passengers' safety in the cockpit.

The TH33's drive and cabin carry forward the equal streak of brilliance. The squared-off bow manages to retain a decent chunk of the 12ft 7in beam, allowing up to six passengers to enjoy the comfort of either several seats or long, sun-soaking lounge pads. The cabin, however, requires re-arranging the port side cushions to allow the aft seat to swing up and expose the internal steps.

The cabin interior is a mixed bag. Certain areas, like the forward space and the port side cut short by the heads, waste considerable room. They're further occupied by a water tank and pipework. On the flip side, the bed situated at the rear end of the starboard cabin is supremely accommodating.

Although minor details like lids, catches, and cushions could be better for a boat this premium, one cannot overlook the TH33's winning qualities. Speed, space, stability, and striking looks all combined to steal the show at the recent Cannes Yachting Festival, where the TH33 had all eyes on her, in spite of her rigorous price tag of €354,000.

Armed with exciting features and a design to leave the yachting community tongues wagging, there's no questioning the stellar reputation of Four Winns' newest powercats, the TH33. A prime example of nautical engineering at its best, the TH33 justifies every penny of its price tag.

title: Behold the Orca 58: RMK Yachts' Newly Unveiled Ultra-Luxurious 58m Superyacht, Available for Sale
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Behold the Orca 58: RMK Yachts' Newly Unveiled Ultra-Luxurious 58m Superyacht, Available for Sale
summary: Astonishingly grand, the Orca 58, has just been launched by Turkish yard, RMK Yachts. This spectacular superyacht is redefining the concept of comfort and luxury on water.
body: Out of the shipyards of RMK Yachts emerges a sight to behold, the Orca 58. A symbol of profound engineering prowess and future-forward vision, the Orca 58 recently graced the Fort Lauderdale International Boat Show with its grandeur. Conceived several years back, the 58-metre vessel has passed through a remarkable transforming process overseen by Monaco-based Lagaria Yacht Design & Architecture, leading to its market relaunch. || The vessel exudes class through its top-notch features; from the precision-built hull with 1000GT volume and 12-metre beam, to the ambiguous layout perfect for modern yacht owners, especially those from the US. This steel giant offers a striking 30% extra space compared with similar-sized yachts, which directly translates to higher comfort and flexibility. || The Orca 58 provides lavish accommodation for 12 guests and 13 crew members. Its unique highlights encompass a six-by-three-metre main deck aft pool, alfresco dining, a generous beach club, and fold-down bulwarks. Highlighting its customizability feature, it offers optional add-ons like a gym, sky lounge, cinema, or spa. The Orca 58 can also host an eight-metre tender. || Propelling at a maximum speed of 15 knots, this nautical spectacle ensures an extended cruise with a range of 5,000 nautical miles at 12 knots. For those keen to make a purchase, it is available for sale through United Yacht Sales. As reported by BOATPro, RMK Marine is currently also crafting a 65-metre explorer yacht and the 49.9-metre Aries, designed in partnership with Milanese studio Hot Lab.

title: High Stakes Afloat: The Singular Challenge of the Seldén Sailjuice Winter Series
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: High Stakes Afloat: The Singular Challenge of the Seldén Sailjuice Winter Series
summary: For the seventeenth time, the much-acclaimed Seldén Sailjuice Winter Series takes to UK waters, securing its spot on every water-pressed contender's calendar.
body: The Seldén Sailjuice Winter Series is back and better than ever. As it sails into its 17th edition, it promises to be yet another thrilling season for the travellers' circuit, thrilling not just UK's small boat classes but sailors from all parts of the globe. Hosting eight exciting events this season, the series pits competitors from nearly a hundred different types of boats against each other. To gain a shot at the fabled overall title, competitors must make their mark by garnering their four best scores. With title sponsorship from long-time supporter Seldén Mast, the heritage of the series promises to remain robust even in the years of challenging Covid lockdowns. 2015 champions Tom Gillard and Rachael Gray are testament to the greatness that the Series offers competitors. Their assertive performance in the 2024/25 season set them on a trajectory for spectacular success in the summer's variety of dinghy classes. Gillard's triumphs in the Fireball Australian Nationals, Fireball UK Nationals, Fireball Inlands, Salcombe Merlin Week, Merlin Nationals, Scorpion Nationals, Streaker Nationals and Lark Nationals speak volumes about his prowess and strategic drive. Although they missed the Fireball Worlds held in Lake Garda, Gillard still endorses the 'hiking class' and Fireball events as adrenaline-pumping opportunities to stay race-ready even during the colder months. Previous season's winner, Sam Pascoe, who cruised to victory in his Musto Skiff, attributes part of his world title success to the challenging winter training. He looks forward to the 25/26 series, where he intends to compete alongside his son, Benjamin. Their teaming up will be something to watch out for. With such high levels of competition and camaraderie, the 17th edition of the Seldén Sailjuice Winter Series promises to be a perfect storm of excitement and adventure.

title: Ocean Science Merges With Racing As Clapcich and Harris Deploy Weather Buoy Mid-Race
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Ocean Science Merges With Racing As Clapcich and Harris Deploy Weather Buoy Mid-Race
summary: Every sea journey tells a story; for Clapcich and Harris, it's a tale of sailing, science and environmental stewardship.
body: While setting sail across the vast ocean, braving the whims of the wind, waves, and weather, there leaps a thrilling strain of adventure. But for sailors Francesca Clapcich and Will Harris, another dash of excitement is added to their journey — they are bringing science into their courageous racing venture. Sailing their 60-foot foiling IMOCA raceboat, 11th Hour Racing, the duo were 2,300 nautical miles into the 4,350 nautical mile Transat Café L'OR race when they deployed a weather buoy. This is not merely a recreational sea jaunt. The deployed buoy, part of the Météo France Surface Velocity Program (SVP), is now adrift somewhere at 22 36o N 19 00o W between the Canary Islands and Cape Verde. It's not casually floating, but rather working, recording atmospheric pressure, sea surface temperature, and ocean current data. The buoy transmits these vital data real-time via satellite to help scientists improve understanding of the global climate situation, refine weather models and forecasts, and gather information on ocean health. But the scientific endeavor doesn't cease there. The sailors also carry a small Argonautica beacon, part of the French Space Agency's educational program. Hundreds of French classrooms follow the beacon's track via the Argos satellite system, all being part of an expansive learning program that combines satellite data, oceanography, and study of the Earth's systems. The wave of discovery and learning merges in a spectacular meeting of sport, science, and education. As the sailors race, they unveil the vital role of research in understanding the world's oceans, showcasing just how potency of science can infuse itself everywhere, even into the heart of a transatlantic race. The collaboration reflects the perfect synergy between professional sport and education, making every ocean crossing a quest for knowledge and stewardship of the marine environment. Every action, every mile sailed, every data packet transmitted from the drifting buoy contributes to a greater understanding, a healthier ocean, and a better world. As Clapcich puts it, 'Whether it's deploying a buoy, mentoring students, or changing how we race, we can all contribute to a healthier ocean and a better understanding of our world.'

title: Navigating Night Adventures: A Tale of Preparation Confronting the Unexpected
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Navigating Night Adventures: A Tale of Preparation Confronting the Unexpected
summary: Unveiling a fascinating tale of an unforeseen sea journey, merging careful preparation with unpredictable events and night-time oceans.
body: The vast and mighty ocean demands respect. It possesses an uncanny knack for presenting the most diligent sailors with unforeseen circumstances, even when they have meticulously prepared for their journey. Our tale takes us through a daring nocturnal odyssey, where detailed planning faced off with the unexpected vastness of the sea.

The night air was a siren song, creamy with salt-tinged mist. A chartered course set, sails trimmed to precision, the boat sliced through the black waters, an elegant sentinel against the infinite void of the star-studded night. Yet, the best-laid plans of sailors often come to naught beneath the whimsical yet capricious heavens. That night was no exception.

Technology faltered; the sea's unpredictable nature unleashed. The crew was left with nothing but the stars to navigate their path. Harsh winds and turbulent seas tested the mettle of even the most seasoned sailors on board.

Just as dawn broke, the unforgiving seas subsided, bearing silent witness to the victorious sailors. The unexpected turn of events had shaken but not broken them. They returned to shore, tested and tempered, a solid testament of their will and fortitude.

This eventful night teaches us that no amount of preplanning can entirely negate the element of surprise at sea. Anticipate the journey, plan for the unknown, but be prepared to adapt at a moment's notice. The sea is both a harsh mistress and wise tutor, teaching us resilience and strengthening our determination. Such adventures are a testament to sailors' indomitable spirit, proving once again that no matter how daunting the challenges, success lies in perseverance.

title: Creating Waves in Luxury Sailing: The Exclusive Maybach Ocean Club Reveals its Immersive 155m Superyacht Concept
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Creating Waves in Luxury Sailing: The Exclusive Maybach Ocean Club Reveals its Immersive 155m Superyacht Concept
summary: Splendid Sea, co-created by renowned superyacht captain Matthias Bosse and Michael Hehn, presents a revolutionary cruising concept redefining luxury yachting.
body: Honoring the spirit of innovation and redefining luxury yachting, the company 'Splendid Sea' forges a trailblazing path in the maritime industry. This visionary company, co-founded by the seasoned superyacht captain Matthias Bosse, and the entrepreneurial force Michael Hehn, made a grand unveil at the renowned Fort Lauderdale International Boat Show of a fresh cruising concept that set the stage abuzz. They proposed a brilliant 155-metre club model circling a stunning superyacht, in a remarkable alliance with Mercedes-Maybach. The germ of this groundbreaking idea sprung during the troubling times of the Covid pandemic, while Bosse was helming the iconic 104.9-metre Lady Moura. Lady Moura, though largely idle amidst the pandemic, sat royally in the heart of one of the global communities most proficient to board her and make the most of her magnificence. Bosse then sparked the ingenious thought of converting Lady Moura into a private club, a concept which promised attraction amongst the elites of Monaco. Upon consultation and brainstorming with the hospitality virtuoso Michael Hehn, the idea of a members-only sailing club began to take hold and mirrored untapped potential in the market, mixing exclusivity with the thrill of life at sea. The concept was so appealing that once Lady Moura was sold, the torchbearers of the unique idea didn't abandon it, but rather continued concieving it further. They saw an opportunity to open the gates of the finest cruising experiences to the younger generation, who could partake in the lavish lifestyle without concerning themselves with the upkeep. Lady Moura, although a cherished symbol, was conceived years prior for the Middle East region, and lacked contemporary open-air spaces. Profoundly inspired by this, Splendid Sea started sketching the blueprint for a truly sophisticated vessel, with open decks and up-to-date facilities including a beach club, guest cabins of equal comfort and size, aiming to create an immersive club experience on water. It required a brand with significant weight to carry the idea forward, and this eventually led to the alliance with Mercedes-Maybach. The globally recognized brand brings along undeniable credibility and trust. After several negotiations, the one-of-a-kind Maybach Ocean Club came to light. The luxury club endorses a members club model on an ultra-luxury, purpose-built vessel and its 70-metre shadow vessel, aiming to cater to and entertain the world's most privileged. title: Are Superyachts forgoing safety for style? A spotlight on pilot welfare when boarding and the importance of communication and collaboration
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Are Superyachts forgoing safety for style? A spotlight on pilot welfare when boarding and the importance of communication and collaboration
summary: Putting the spotlight on superyacht safety, a recent CHIRP Maritime report raises concerns about nonchalant attitudes towards pilot welfare during boarding.
body: It's no news that the world of superyachts carries an aura of luxury, but what happens when this glamour clouds safety norms? A recent report by CHIRP Maritime's Superyacht Feedback programme underpins this critical concern. Notably, a pilot raised red flags about a non-compliant boarding arrangement on a superyacht. In a distressing state of affairs, the pilot found himself amidst the crew’s apathy, highlighting a blatant disregard for his safety. The dubious boarding arrangement saw the pilot ladder hanging from the deckhead, failing to rest against the ship's side because of hull belting—an apparent violation of safety standards. While there was a viable, safer alternative via a small shell door, the vessel's crew had rigged large fenders on both sides. On voicing concerns and requesting removal of these obstructions, the master refused, prioritising potential paintwork damage over the pilot's well-being. The escalated situation saw the pilot insist on removal of the fenders, only after which he proceeded to go on board. Adding fuel to the already heated situation, the boarding from the shell door was filmed, significantly adding to the pressure and discomfort felt by the pilot. To add to the pilot's woes, he suffered a minor head injury during boarding — an incident the crew observed passively, without offering first aid or inquiring after his welfare. This unsettling narrative underscores the common design problem in superyachts: a lack of integrated thought encompassing all safety aspects. Designers, owners, flag authorities, crew, contractors, and pilots must pull resources together and partake in a collaborative conversation during the design phase. The incident serves as a reminder that pilots, albeit outsiders, play a critical role in maritime operations, and their safety cannot be compromised. Slated for a 2028 enforcement, the revision to ISO 799 presents new requirements for ship's pilot ladders. Until then, it is imperative for superyacht owners to insist on adherence to existing standards and comply with SOLAS. In the meantime, CHIRP Maritime gears up to raise concerns with flag states. Reflecting upon the incident, deficiencies stand out in three main areas: culture, communication, and alerting. Disregarding the pilot's safety reflects poorly on the on-board safety culture. An obstructing communication flow hampers shared situational awareness and decision making. Lastly, discarding critical safety alerts undermines the effectiveness of safety systems and discourages future voicing of concerns. The take-home message is unmistakable: safety cannot be compromised, collaboration is indispensable, and effective communication paramount.

title: Revamped Luxury Sailing Yacht Kokotea Gets Price Chop and Now Commands €6,450,000
author: Old Sea Dogs

body: Step onto the deck of the 40-metre Kokotea, a splendid superyacht styled by Dubois Naval Architects and perfected by New Zealand's renowned shipyard, Alloy Yachts. The sloop has a price cut of €500,000, making the luxury vessel priced now at €6,450,000.

Historically significant, the Kokotea was the fifth commissioned project by the original owner to the architects and the seventh Dubois-designed yacht constructed by the shipyard. The yacht now stands with a fresh hull thanks to a whole repaint carried out in the extensive refit in 2021.

Abound with luxury, aboard the Kokotea, you will find comfortable accommodation for eight people in its four cabins. Of these, one is the full-beam owner’s suite, complete with a private office and an en suite bathroom. The remaining cabins are two doubles and a smaller double cabin. Furthermore, this elegant yacht has additional quarters to accommodate a crew of six.

The expansive cockpit, just right for outdoor dining, is a masterpiece in its design. Covered and well-protected, it is apt for hosting small get-togethers or casual afternoon conversations. The deck also possesses twin helm stations with great visibility forward around the superstructure and of the soaring Doyle sails.

This marvel of a yacht is not only about looks and comfort; she is ABS-classed and boasts a robust C18 Caterpillar engine. It ensures a cruising speed of 10 knots and a top speed of 13 knots. Presently, the Kokotea is docked in Vilanova, Spain, awaiting her new commander. The astounding makeover and the tempting price cut make the Kokotea an option worth considering for any avid sailor or yacht enthusiast.
