title: Olly Murs to Headline the Mubadala Abu Dhabi Sail Grand Prix 2025 Season Grand Final
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Mubadala Abu Dhabi Sail Grand Prix 2025 Season Grand Final
imageCaption: USA SailGP Team in action during a practice session ahead of the Mubadala SailGP.
summary: The stage is set. Mubadala Abu Dhabi Sail Grand Prix 2025 Season Grand Final, presented by the Abu Dhabi Sports Council, will take place on November 29–30 2025 in Mina Zayed, and today the global sailing‑sport powerhouse SailGP has confirmed the addition of platinum‑selling pop sensation Olly Murs as the headline entertainer.
body: As the high‑speed foiling catamarans slice across the Arabian Gulf, thousands of fans will be treated to more than just elite sport. When racing concludes on the evening of Saturday, 29 November, the purpose‑built SailGP Race Stadium at Mina Zayed will transform into a full‑scale music and entertainment spectacle featuring Olly Murs. Olly arrives in Abu Dhabi just eight days after the release of his eighth studio album ‘Knees Up’ and will bring his full band to deliver hits such as Troublemaker and Dance With Me Tonight. With over 5.7 million monthly Spotify listeners and two‑million tour tickets sold, his performance promises to be unforgettable.

Off the water, the event’s entertainment line‑up continues to build. On Sunday, 30 November, popular radio and TV personality and DJ Mark Wright will take centre stage at Après‑Sail presented by Mastercard, rounding out the weekend with groove‑laden beats and a live broadcast of Saturday Breakfast with Mark Wright & Olly Murs. In partnership with Mastercard, luxury‑seeking guests will enjoy the waterfront Priceless Lounge situated within the Waterfront Premium Lounge and catered by Nobu by the Beach. Exclusive Priceless Experiences will include behind‑the‑scenes tech tours of SailGP’s F50 foiling catamarans. Across the weekend the Race Stadium and Waterfront Grandstand will pulse with live music, hype hosts, roaming performers and F50 fly‑bys that skim just metres from shore. This is the ultimate fusion of sport and celebration.

On the water the stakes are huge. A field of 12 national teams will square off in identical 50‑foot foiling catamarans, racing at speeds in excess of 100 km/h. At stake is the coveted Rolex SailGP Championship trophy and a winner‑takes‑all prize of US $2 million. With the Grand Final set for the dramatic backdrop of Abu Dhabi’s Arabian Gulf shores, Mina Zayed will host not just a race, but a celebration of extreme sport, lifestyle and live entertainment.

Olly Murs said: “I’m incredibly excited to perform in Abu Dhabi at SailGP’s Grand Final. Taking to the stage right after the world’s best athletes have raced for the championship will be so special. It’s also going to be such a laugh hosting Saturday Breakfast on Heart with Mark amongst it all. I can’t wait!”

Mark Wright added: “I am buzzing to be linking up with SailGP again. It was incredible to get a behind‑the‑scenes experience on‑board the team’s F50 in the UK this summer – and I’ve told Olly what to expect. Now to be back, entertaining fans at the final event of the season in Abu Dhabi – and broadcasting live on Heart with Olly – it’s going to be epic.”

Leah Davis, Chief Marketing Officer of SailGP, commented: “From the moment fans step into the Race Stadium in Abu Dhabi, the atmosphere will take over – the music, energy and spectacle, on and off the water. The Après‑Sail presented by Mastercard celebration will come alive with world‑class pop sensation Olly Murs creating a party that keeps the excitement going as the sun sets against the beautiful Abu Dhabi backdrop.”

By blending the high‑tech thrill of foiling catamarans, a $2 million championship prize and headline entertainment from global pop icons, the Mubadala Abu Dhabi Sail Grand Prix 2025 Grand Final elevates sailing into full mainstream entertainment. For the luxury yacht sector, coastal tourism and live performance markets, this is a convergence of three powerhouse verticals. Tickets and hospitality experiences are now available: from grandstand seating to premium lounges offering immersive hospitality and front‑row views of on‑water drama. Mark your calendars for 29–30 November 2025 and get ready to experience world‑class sport, pop‑music entertainment and an unforgettable lifestyle weekend in Abu Dhabi.

title: Safety Tethers: A Valuable and Potentially Life-Saving Addition to Every Motor Boater’s Essential Gear
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Safety Tethers: A Valuable and Potentially Life-Saving Addition to Every Motor Boater’s Essential Gear
summary: Discover the importance of safety tethers for motor boaters and why this overlooked piece of equipment should be on your boat safety checklist.
body: All too often, safety tethers are noticed in marine supply stores but disregarded by motor boaters. Prominent among sailors for their use during windy conditions or nighttime boating to prevent overboard accidents, they also have significant utility on motor boats.

Insights from a recent simulated 'man overboard' scenario emphasized their usage. The heavy, unresponsive dummy, intended to mimic an unconscious person, proved challenging to handle while maintaining one's balance on the boat. Attachment to the boat via a safety tether provided a tangible advantage, allowing for the use of both hands in recovery efforts.

Standard tethers often come with clips at both ends, with some variations featuring elasticity and multiple clips. This design allows the crew member to stay connected while moving across different attachment points on the boat, providing continuous security. For instance, it could be advantageous when dealing with a loose anchor on a rough sea day.

Preference and convenience dictate the manner of attaching the tether to oneself. Lifeline harnesses and lifejackets with dedicated clip points are available options. Motorboats, unlike sailboats, typically lack safety lines along the deck. Therefore, secure points to clip onto, which can prevent an overboard fall, should be identified and shared with the crew. In scenarios where guardrails or cleats fall short of preventing an overboard accident, they can still keep one connected to the boat.

The choice of tether attachments varies according to personal needs and boat specifications, spanning fixed-length ropes, elasticated cords with one-handed clips, and strops with overload strain indicators. Lifejacket clip points also come in different styles, including strap clips, metal rings, or reinforced fabric loops. Regardless of hand strength, ensure the clip can be released one-handed before purchasing. Lastly, always be ready to detach instantaneously when using a tether, by keeping a knife within easy reach.

Ultimately, safety tethers can boost practicality by proving invaluable in enhancing safety while motor boating. By giving them due consideration, motor boaters can ensure a safer, more enjoyable experience on the water.

This compact cruiser, based on the popular Duchy 27 hull but with practical modifications, presents itself as an affordable day boat or weekender. This versatile cruiser has a few distinct benefits to offer. Its compact dimensions and light weight allow for easy towing behind a family SUV. Moreover, it is customisable with a silent electric outboard or a powerful 200hp petrol engine, catering to both river and coastal cruising enthusiasts.

The Duchy 27 Outboard stole the show, equipped with a 140hp Suzuki engine, hitting top speeds of around 20 knots. In summary, the Duchy 27 Outboard is indeed a gem of a boat and the anticipation for its sea trial is palpable.

title: Experience the Thrill and Stability of Arksen Discovery 8 on Rough Waters

summary: The Arksen Discovery 8, the first RIB from British adventure brand, Arksen, makes its dynamic debut, showcasing unparalleled performance and innovative design.

Recently, an exclusive opportunity to put this magnificent marine creation through its paces in rough waters, showcased its impressive offshore capability while revealing the essence of its innovative design. Following in the footsteps of its prototype, the Discovery 8 has been refined over time into an enticing blend of rugged aesthetics reminiscent of an SUV and serious offshore capability. The striking hull and deck design signals its intent as a proper offshore vessel. It sports a deep V hull with a fine entry and sharp, cleanly resolved spray rails, expertly designed to deliver peerless performance in challenging conditions. The boat features a revolutionary deck layout, painstakingly designed with an effective solution for boarding from the water. The seating arrangement is notably tailored to boost security, integrate useful features such as armrests, drained cupholders, and wireless phone chargers. The versatile cockpit shines with several innovative features, including a vast locker and an optional grill removable wet bar. The helm, neatly offset to port, creates a convenient starboard walkway and keeps the throttle safe from traffic. This clever layout generates extra room for a spacious heads compartment within the console, featuring neat inclusions such as a sink, fabric shelving, and a proper electric loo with a holding tank. Tested with the maximum power option, twin 4.2L V6 250hp outboards, the Discovery 8 demonstrates outstanding stability and strength at sea, even in challenging conditions. Cruising at an efficient 30 knots sees the engines turning a relaxed 3,500 RPM, consuming approximately 60 L/hr— a testament to the boat's efficient and excellent design.

title: Activist Investor Donerail Intensifies Pressure on MarineMax for Leadership Overhaul and Business Sale
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Activist Investor Donerail Intensifies Pressure on MarineMax for Leadership Overhaul and Business Sale
summary: Activist investor, Donerail Group, is upping the ante on MarineMax, the US yacht retailer, urging for a complete leadership replacement and the exploration of a business sale.
body: MarineMax, a renowned US yacht retailer, is at the throes of mounting pressure led by activist investor Donerail Group. According to recent reports, Donerail Group, who owns approximately 4% of MarineMax's stock, is calling for a revamp of the senior leadership and possible sale of the business. This move follows perceived mismanagement and 'poor capital allocation and flawed execution' under the stewardship of current CEO Brett McGill, who replaced his father and company founder Bill McGill in 2018. Despite attempts to appease its investors through changes in its board members and the removal of the CFO from directorship, MarineMax has failed to meet the escalating expectations. Most notably, Donerail co-founder Will Wyatt has reportedly held several meetings with the MarineMax leadership team, advocating for a leadership reshuffle ahead of next year's board elections, putting Brett McGill and two other directors' positions at risk. This unanticipated move by Donerail is considered as an escalation in its engagement with McGill, who has been striving to transform the company from a boat retailer into a fully-fledged marine services group. The company’s efforts to diversify its portfolio, specifically its acquisition of Island Global Yachting (IGY) in 2022, have been faced with significant integration challenges and public scrutiny. Further heating up the situation, IGY's founder, Andrew Farkas, has initiated an open offer to buy back up to 100% of IGY, a deal that could potentially close within 60 days. Farkas argues that IGY has been 'losing its competitive edge' under MarineMax's ownership and has failed to expand its portfolio in the marine space since the buyout. Meanwhile, its competitors have been significantly expanding their asset base. Amid increasing shareholder discontentment towards MarineMax's direction of strategy, the company’s shares have seen a substantial drop from its 2021 peak of $57 to $27. Levin Capital has also argued that MarineMax's corporate structure, combining retail, brokerage and marina assets, now potentially hides value rather than highlighting it. OneWater Marine reportedly offered $40 per share in an all-cash proposal valuing the company at $2.5 billion, which the board rejected. As the waves of discord keep rising, it is imperative for MarineMax to seize the tide and quickly address the issues at hand – be it a leadership revamp, a strategic shift in business, or simply a capitulation to Donerail or any convinced investor.

This is not where Sentinel's utilities stop. As a support vessel, it accommodates submersibles, tenders, sportfishing crafts, and terrestrial security vehicles, including armored SUVs. If air travel is needed, the dual certified helipads are ready to allow simultaneous operations for transfer, support, or emergency extraction.

Ensuring that professional aid is always at hand, Sentinel's broad personnel complement accommodates teams of security and logistics professionals, technical pilots and medical professionals with high-end shore-based facility equivalent medical infrastructure.

In its design, Sentinel also accounts for protection. The vessel features reinforced compartments and stairwells for added security, cementing its value as a 'foresighted' vessel aimed at ensuring guest security. With Shadowcat's Sentinel, maritime security has undoubtedly struck a new high.

title: Revelatory Shifts in Data Governance: How the EU Data Act Recasts the Business Models of the Superyacht Industry
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Revelatory Shifts in Data Governance: How the EU Data Act Recasts the Business Models of the Superyacht Industry
summary: As digitalisation advances in the superyacht sector, the EU Data Act is set to prompt a major shuffle in business strategies, contracts, and governance procedures.
body: The superyacht industry, increasingly embracing connectivity, digitalisation, and data-driven services is about to experience a sea change as the EU Data Act takes effect. This legislation, officially termed Regulation (EU) 2023/2854, was unveiled in December 2023 and came into play in January 2024. The Act's stipulations gradually apply till 2027, leading to comprehensive alterations in contracts, business prototypes, and data governance throughout the superyacht sector.

The Act also establishes a fairness system for B2B contract terms that unjustly limit access to or use of data. It imposes new design responsibilities for connected products released from September 2026. Moreover, the Act completely forbids switching costs for cloud/data-processing services from January 2027 onward.

For the superyacht industry, heavily reliant on data from several connected systems, such as engine sensors, IoT systems, navigation and monitoring networks, the Data Act has crucial implications. Being a 'user' of a connected product under the new law allows you to access product and related service data upon request. This shift can potentially turn the tide for OEMs, platform providers and charter businesses. Therefore, it is indispensable to realign your business models, contracts, and data governance systems proactively to stay afloat in this new digital era.

title: High Impact Radio Sailing on Display: The Dragon TT Series Concludes at the Gosport Model Boat and Yacht Club
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: High Impact Radio Sailing on Display: The Dragon TT Series Concludes at the Gosport Model Boat and Yacht Club
summary: The Dragon TT Series, a global phenomenon in radio yacht racing concludes its final match at the historic Gosport Model Boat and Yacht Club.
body: In the world of radio sailing, the Dragon TT series marked an indelible dent. Beginning mid to late last decade, the Joysways Dragon boats, the DF65 and DF95, caused a significant transformative wave. Despite the numerous radio yacht classes, the limited availability of new boats often deterred the sailing fraternity from further expansion. Enter the Dragon boats, and suddenly, everything changed. The world embraced these low-cost, conveniently built Dragon classes, which came delivered in a box. Thousands of sailing enthusiasts happily took to racing them, affirming the series's universal appeal.

At the historic Gosport Model Boat and Yacht Club, which recently celebrated a centenary of consistent activity, the final series unfolded. With over 200 members and a variety of classes competing daily, the club was an apt conclusion to a fierce competition exclusive to one design racing. Despite changes in local landscape, altering wind patterns, the tricky wind shifts only added to the thrilling race sequences throughout the weekend.

The DF65 may be the smallest of the two DF's, but it is indeed challenging to navigate. The boat's lightweight structure and short waterline length demand constant focus on maintaining speed. One small slip in concentration could see one's boat spiraling backwards through the fleet. Nevertheless, achieving mastery over this elusive craft offered unexpected rewards. 33 skippers faced this challenge head-on at the opening race of the DF65 TT 13 at Gosport on 25 October.

title: Navigating into a Greener Future: Rolls-Royce Tests Its First Pure Methanol Marine Engine Successfully
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Navigating into a Greener Future: Rolls-Royce Tests Its First Pure Methanol Marine Engine Successfully
summary: In an industry-defining breakthrough, Rolls-Royce announces successful testing of the world's first exclusively methanol-fueled marine engine.
body: Building on its legacy of pioneering propulsion technology, Rolls-Royce has set another industry benchmark with the successful testing of their first high-speed marine engine powered solely by methanol. This groundbreaking accomplishment from the leading aero-engine manufacturer and propulsion specialist ushers in a new era of energy-efficient marine transportation.

This pioneering test took place at their research facility in Friedrichshafen, Germany and forms part of the meOHmare research project. It's an ambitious initiative the company is diligently working on along with partners in the domain.

Dr. Jörg Stratmann, CEO of Rolls-Royce Power Systems AG, proudly announced that this is indeed a 'world first'. His assertion emphasized that this performance isn't just a fleeting accomplishment, but a significant step towards revolutionizing marine propulsion systems as they venture to introduce 'future technologies' like methanol fuel in the market.

Methanol, a liquid alcohol, differs from traditional diesel in many ways and poses unique challenges. It requires an entirely new injection technology as it does not spontaneously ignite. Nevertheless, this success story exhibits Rolls-Royce's ingenuity in overcoming these challenges and innovatively redesigning the combustion process, turbocharging mechanisms, controlling systems and their test bench infrastructure. The initial test exhibits a smoothly functioning engine, awaiting some minor tuning.

Recognized as one of the most promising alternative fuels for shipping, green methanol offers straightforward storage, biodegradability, significantly fewer pollutants, and the prospect of CO2-neutral operation.

Senior Vice President Denise Kurtulus asserts that the victorious test run sends a clear message to the world that green methanol is indeed the fuel of the future and they have the technology for it. In addition to this, Rolls-Royce is also developing a dual-fuel concept that enables both methanol and diesel fuel usage until green methanol becomes prevalent, making this a versatile and adaptable solution for the shipping industry.

title: Youthful Prodigies Set Sail at the 17th Eastern Seaboard Regatta in Thailand
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Youthful Prodigies Set Sail at the 17th Eastern Seaboard Regatta in Thailand
summary: The Royal Varuna Yacht Club in Pattaya, Thailand, recently hosted the 17th Eastern Seaboard Youth Regatta, a thrilling showcase of youthful talent in the dynamic world of sailing.
body: The 17th Eastern Seaboard Youth Regatta undoubtedly kicked off the sailing season in spectacular fashion at the prestigious Royal Varuna Yacht Club. The club once again proved a perfect venue for showcasing international competition, delivering steady winds and open waters that welcomed 140 boats from 11 countries to compete in this youthful sailing rendezvous. Thrilling action started on day one with winds building up 12-17 knots, presenting an exciting challenge across all classes. The Optimist fleet garnered significant attention, with Thai and Australian sailors vying for top honors while engaging in a scintillating head-to-head. Thailand's sailors leveraged their local knowledge to dominate both the ILCA 4 and 6 fleets, and an intense competition unfolded in the 420 classes between Thai and Malaysian teams. Day two started with a calming 10-knot breeze. However, changing currents, swells, and light and tactical conditions put competitors' skills to the test. The day ended with Thai teams leading the 420 class and Ton Rattana extending his lead over formidable Chinese rivals in the ILCA 6 fleet. Day three greeted participants with light morning rains, transitioning to a soft breeze of 7-9 knots by noon. The day unfolded strategically amid lighter wind conditions. Yet again, Thai sailors demonstrated dominance in the ILCA 4 and 6 fleets. The day concluded with setting the stage for a riveting end to the regatta, promising a showdown that will decide the eventual champions.

title: As Traditional Teak Flounders, What's On the Horizon for Sustainable Sailing Decks?
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: As Traditional Teak Flounders, What's On the Horizon for Sustainable Sailing Decks?
summary: There's more to a yacht’s deck than meets the eye, especially when it comes to the environmental factors at play. But as concerns over teak get more intense, what are the emerging alternatives?
body: A deck is more than just a wooden surface on which one can lounge, sipping a cocktail while watching a sunset in the middle of the ocean. It's the living, breathing soul of a boat, projecting and encapsulating the essence of the maritime lifestyle. Traditionally, the unchallenged king of boat decking materials has been teak, thanks to its aesthetic appeal, endurance, and highly desired texture. But as concerns over the environmental implications of teak sourcing mount, the nautical world is being nudged towards a new frontier of sustainable alternatives. Suppliers like Teak Decking Systems, Wolz Nautic, and Amorim have been pioneering in this regard, exploring and testing different materials to replace or at least complement traditional teak. Plantation teak, a managed version of the classic material, 'green teak', produced from veneer and modified woods like Tesumo, are among the alternatives in discussion. Cork is another contender, thanks to its carbon-negative profile, recyclability attributes, easy maintenance, and pleasant feel underfoot. But the conversation is far from closed. Yacht builders like Feadship have been investing in research toward long-term sustainable teak alternatives. Navigating the narrow line between client aspirations, material performance, and environmental responsibility, these brands are breaking new ground and reshaping the face of decking for the future. However, even with innovations and new options, acceptance of alternatives to teak still faces resistance. Decking, for many, begins and ends with traditional teak, not just for its physical attributes but also the intangible values it carries - the colour, aroma, and the sensation it imparts when being worked with. Transforming such deep-seated preferences is a tall order, making the journey towards sustainable alternatives as exciting and unpredictable as an ocean sailing adventure.

title: A Close Contest at the DF95 Eastern District Championship Round 3, Reveals Skippers Pushing the Envelope of Precision

summary: The competition heaved up at the Huntingdon Radio Yacht Club, with a nail-biting finish at the 3rd round of the DF95 Eastern District Champion Skipper Series.
body: In the bright morning sunlight, seventeen skippers assembled at the Huntingdon Radio Yacht Club and were welcomed by the Club Commodore, Martin Brooking. Some competitors had completed round journeys of up to 350 miles, a testament to their dedication to the sport. title: Dutch Shipyard Kick-Starts Construction on Mega Custom Build: The 47.8 Metre Project Zen
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Dutch Shipyard Kick-Starts Construction on Mega Custom Build: The 47.8 Metre Project Zen
summary: Van der Valk, reputed Dutch shipyard, embarks on its most ambitious custom build, the monumental 47.8-meter motor yacht, Project Zen.
body: The landscape of custom yacht building takes on exciting new contours as Dutch giants Van der Valk dive into constructing their most grandiose project to date, the mighty Project Zen. Commissioned as a family yacht, it began as a modest 36-metre design, gradually evolving to its current impressive 47.8 metres. The crux was offering enough room while maintaining its intimate ambiance, explained Bram Kooltjes, technical director at the yard. The process entailed gradually extending the proposed length until everything fit to perfection. Featuring an awe-inspiring all-aluminium RPH model, Project Zen is set to flaunt a low-profile exterior with a full-metallic finish. Sporting cues from high-end sports cars, this mammoth yacht taps into the client's personal passion. The projected completion and delivery is slated for the second quarter of 2028.

This distinguished yacht is crafted with efficiency at its heart, according to designer Guido de Groot. The owner fancied a hull shape that facilitates smaller engines to enhance the vessel's range. As swiftness wasn't the prime interest, the design team focused on a long, sleek form to bolster the yacht’s elegant style. Onboard, a 6.25-meter Williams DieselJet and a Jet Ski will reside in a lower deck garage that features an easy-to-use side-opening ramp.

Every stage of this project factored in the owner's very particular requirements. The main deck aft cascades down to a spacious sea terrace designed to provide a picturesque panoramic view of the surrounding waters. Electric sliding doors lead to a fully equipped sports garage and toy store. The indoor area has been designed specifically with family living in mind, boasting a well-equipped country-style kitchen with a dining area and a show gallery fit for show cooking. In addition, a full-beam wellness area with a yoga room and gym mere steps away from the owner's suite brings in a taste of fitness luxury aboard this yacht.

The elaborate split-level sundeck splits into two parts with the aft portion allocated for sunbathing and casual get-togethers, whereas the front side offers an open-air lounge. 'Project Zen is not only our largest undertaking but a fine display of what Van der Valk stands for: custom design from scratch in complete harmony with the owner's vision', says Kooltjes about this monumental project.

title: Three Ocean Fifty Trimarans Capsize in Sudden Transat Café L'OR Turbulence - Skippers Safe Amidst Unpredicted Havoc
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Three Ocean Fifty Trimarans Capsize in Sudden Transat Café L'OR Turbulence - Skippers Safe Amidst Unpredicted Havoc
summary: The Transat Café L'OR witnessed dramatic scenes when three Ocean Fifty trimarans capsized in choppy conditions, rattling nerves across the nautical community.
body: Unpredictable weather caused a dramatic upheaval at the Transat Café L'OR as three Ocean Fifty trimarans met an untimely fate, capsizing in tempestuous seas. The notable vessels included the 'Lazare X Hellio', 'Ocean Fifty Koesio', and 'Ocean Fifty Inter Invest'. Despite this misfortune, every sailor on board these vessels found safety.

The 'Lazare X Hellio', with skippers Erwan Le Draoulec and Tanguy Le Turquais, was the first craft to capsize off La Hague, situated north of Cotentin. The pair were quickly airlifted to safety, leaving the technical team and race organizers to contend with the subverted yacht in 22 to 25-knot winds and three-meter waves.

'Matthieu Perraut and Jean-Baptiste Gellée', aboard the 'Ocean Fifty Inter Invest', were the last to succumb to the raging seas. Found capsizing off the tip of Brittany, the sailors were at a daunting 4,475 miles from their desired finish line. The dreadful circumstances caught the nautical community by surprise, serving as a stark reminder of the merciless and unpredictability of the open seas. The crews' survival underlines the importance of sailor resilience and safety protocols, as races like Transat Café L'OR continue to challenge sailing finesse and navigation skills in the face of Mother Nature's whims.

title: Three Trimarans Toppled: Wild Seas Capsize Trio of Ocean Fifty Entrants in Transat Café L'or Regatta
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Three Trimarans Toppled: Wild Seas Capsize Trio of Ocean Fifty Entrants in Transat Café L'or Regatta
summary: Adventurous sailing took a harrowing turn in the recent Transat Café L'or as three Ocean Fifty trimarans capsized in challenging weather conditions.
body: Ocean racing is as unpredictable as the sea itself, a fact nautical enthusiasts were reminded of recently during the Transat Café L'or. The regatta was marked by tumultuous weather which resulted in not one, but three Ocean Fifty trimarans capsize in rapid succession. Surrendering to the supreme might of the North Atlantic, these high-performance vessels found themselves battling against extreme natural elements instead of their fellow competitors. The drama unfolded testing the resilience of man, machine, and maritime mettle amidst the roaring surge of the ocean. At approximately 8:27 p.m. UTC, the distress beacon of Ocean Fifty Lazare X Hellio was activated. The trimaran, manned by skippers Erwan Le Draoulec and Tanguy Le Turquais, capsized just three miles shy of La Hague's northern coast. Winds were blowing steady at 22 to 25 knots with gusts reaching up to 30 knots and waves topping out at around 3 meters. Rescue efforts were swift, with both skippers safely airlifted by a search and rescue team. Not long after, at 00:25 UTC, the Ocean Fifty Koesio under the command of Erwan Leroux and Audrey Ogereau, mirrored a similar fate north of Guernsey. Amidst a gale of northerly winds averaging at 25 knots, the Koesio succumbed to the weather conditions and capsized, causing another swift aerial rescue operation to take place. Less than four hours later, the third incident struck. The Ocean Fifty Inter Invest encountered the same perilous fate as its predecessors while sailing off the Abers coastline, Brittany. Skippers Matthieu Perraut and Jean-Baptiste Gellée found themselves a distressing 4,475 miles from the finish line as their boat was hurled over by the relentless waves. Fortunately, despite the terror of the situation, all sailors were rescued and found in good health - an undeniable testament to the efficiency of the rescue teams and the impassive courage of the skippers themselves. As the boats drift, the focus now turns to the challenge of recovering the capsized vessels. The respective technical teams in conjunction with race management are proposing strategies to tow these valuable racing assets back to port. This incident serves as a stark reminder of the ever-present unpredictability of ocean racing. Not for the faint of heart, this sport combines the fierce, relentless power of Mother Nature with the willpower and determination of dedicated sailors. Events like Transat Café L'or highlight both the thrill and peril of this high-octane, adrenaline-charged sport.

title: Italian Shipyard Cantiere delle Marche Unleashes the First Unit in Acciaio 130 Series: The 'Presence'
author: Old Sea Dogs

summary: Italian shipyard Cantiere delle Marche (CDM) embarks on a new venture with the launch of its first ever Acciaio 130 yacht, known as the 'Presence'.

A product of experienced craftsmanship and technical prowess, 'Presence' marks a significant moment in CDM's diverse portfolio, adding another dimension to the shipbuilding industry.

Following the precedent set by its famed predecessors - Acciaio 105 Gatto and Acciaio 123 Astrum, 'Presence' emerges as the third, and largest, model in the Acciaio range. An exclusive ensemble of an all-Italian design team is the force behind its creation, resulting in a charming blend of aesthetic appeal and functionality.

Interior details, yet to be unravelled, invite curiosity and promise an engaging living environment. Designer Giorgio M. Cassetta describes the spaces within 'Presence' as rich in persona, veering towards playful rather than pretentious, promising comfortable areas for both relaxation and entertainment.

Collaboration is at the heart of this remarkable creation. Richard Kaye, project manager of Arcon Yachts, mirrors the sentiment of pride and satisfaction as he talks about the fruitful partnership between CDM and Arcon Yachts. Their combined efforts have borne fruit in the form of 'Presence', the third Acciaio model involving them both.

'Presence' offers not only an aesthetically refreshing design but also an efficient hull that keeps fuel consumption to a minimum. Powered by twin MAN D2862LE engines, it can cruise for an impressive range of 5,000 nautical miles at 10 knots. The launching of 'Presence' reaffirms CDM's longstanding reputation for quality, reliability, and durability while also shining a light on Italian craftsmanship in the global yachting industry.

title: MACIF Santé Prévoyance Wins
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Défi Azimut – Lorient Agglomération: MACIF Santé Prévoyance Wins with Sam Goodchild and Loïs Berrehar
summary: In the world of offshore sailing, some boats earn a reputation for being more than just fast—they become legends. This week at the Défi Azimut – Lorient Agglomération, that legend grew as British skipper Sam Goodchild, sailing with French co-skipper Loïs Berrehar, drove the IMOCA MACIF Santé Prévoyance to yet another victory.
body: For Goodchild, who had only just stepped off Biotherm after playing a key role in their overall win at The Ocean Race Europe, it was the perfect encore. Teaming up with Berrehar, he took on the light-wind, tactical Azimut 48 Hours and emerged with the win in Lorient, a city long known as the beating heart of French offshore racing.

The 307-nautical mile course may not sound long by IMOCA standards, but the conditions made it grueling. Winds rarely climbed above 10–12 knots, and for long stretches the fleet drifted through flat water with sails barely drawing. Concentration was everything—constant trimming, endless tweaks, and a battle of nerves.

Goodchild and Berrehar, sailing a boat already steeped in history—winner of the last Vendée Globe under Charlie Dalin—showed why MACIF Santé Prévoyance is widely considered one of the most finely tuned weapons in the IMOCA fleet. After an indifferent start, they clawed into the lead and never looked back.

“This boat is just an incredible weapon,” said Goodchild at the dock. “We’re still learning her, but every day we get stronger. Jean-Yves Gau, our boat captain, reminded us as we stepped ashore—this is the fifth consecutive race win for MACIF. That says it all.”

Second place went to Justine Mettraux and Xavier Macaire on Teamwork-Team SNEF. For Mettraux, one of Switzerland’s finest offshore sailors, the result was a welcome return to the front of the pack. They had led early before gear issues slowed their pace, but managed to hold off Charal, skippered by Jérémie Beyou and Morgan Lagravière, by just a single minute at the line.

“It was light, unstable, and you couldn’t switch off for a second,” Mettraux admitted. “We even had a tack line failure on the J0, so to hang onto second in those conditions feels fantastic. This race has given us confidence as we prepare for the Transat Café L’OR.”

One of the stories of the event was Café Joyeux, sailed by Nicolas D’Estais of France and Swiss co-skipper Simon Koster. Racing a veteran daggerboard IMOCA once campaigned by François Gabart, they pushed hard for the podium and eventually finished fourth.

“This boat is like a big Mini,” D’Estais laughed afterwards, reflecting on his roots in the Mini Transat. “Everything’s heavier—the sails, the ropes—but she just keeps moving in conditions where foilers stall. For us, this race was about proving the project works. We’ve only had six sails on her, so to be fighting at the front is a great start.”

While the Défi Azimut celebrated innovation and close racing in Brittany, the weekend also echoed with results from Montenegro. There, Paul Meilhat’s Biotherm—a team where Goodchild had sailed as navigator for most of the race—clinched overall victory in The Ocean Race Europe.

Behind them, Paprec Arkéa, skippered by Yoann Richomme, secured second overall, edging out Team Holcim-PRB skippered by Rosalin Kuiper. Team Malizia, under Boris Herrmann, took fourth, just ahead of Ambrogio Beccaria’s Allagrande Mapei Racing. The final places went to Canada Ocean Racing – Be Water Positive, led by Scott Shawyer, and Team Amaala, skippered by Alan Roura.

For IMOCA teams, the Défi Azimut – Lorient Agglomération is more than just another race. It’s a benchmark ahead of the Transat and the Vendée Globe, a chance to test boats, refine crew work, and measure up against rivals in conditions that demand skill rather than brute speed.

This year’s edition underlined what many already knew: MACIF Santé Prévoyance is the boat to beat. With Goodchild and Berrehar now fully integrated, and Dalin’s legacy of relentless performance behind them, the boat looks poised for more glory on the international stage.
As Goodchild put it, with a wry smile: “We’re just getting started.”

title: Unveiling Althea: An Admirable Display of Exceptional Design in the 48m Admiral Yacht
author: Old Sea Dogs

summary: Althea, an impressive 47.5-metre motor yacht, is a testament of ingenious design, blending modern elegance with matchless functionality."
body: When one navigates the realm of motor yachts, they will find a separation - those that are simply used, and those that are loved unconditionally. Among the latter is Althea, a 47.5-metre luxurious motor yacht crafted by Admiral in 2020. A shining addition to The Italian Sea Group's Atos 47 series, Althea's elite build quality, proactive maintenance, and intelligently structured layout distinguishes her as a unique proposition in the current yacht brokerage.

Bryan Somerset Mehut, the yacht's broker at Fraser, proclaimed Althea as 'one of the most compelling fully VAT-paid offerings in the 50-metre segment'. She sings a song of contemporary Italian design both inside and out, penned by the talented Gian Marco Campanino. Defined by sleek lines and a captivating sky-blue hull, Althea's exterior paints a modern silhouette. Her aluminium frame houses a vast 499GT volume skillfully accentuated with an airy, open ambiance. The yacht's tri-deck layout presents a variety-filled sailing experience where guests enjoy distinct areas to unwind, savour meals, or entertain to their heart's content.

On the onset, Althea emanates a strong, mesmerizing aura. As one steps into her, they find an inviting haven bathed in natural light flowing through full-length windows. The serene neutral shades, placid woods, and delicate textures of the décor invite a comforting warmth. An aptly chosen array of Minotti furniture and flowing layout bridges the lounge and formal dining area. Divided by a seamlessly sliding bar with a fitted television, this space caters equally for quiet family gatherings and grand entertainment.

title: Exquisite Christensen Motor Yacht Lady Elaine Goes Under the Hammer, Experiences Exceptional $1M Price Cut Just a Week before Major Boat Show
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Exquisite Christensen Motor Yacht Lady Elaine Goes Under the Hammer, Experiences Exceptional $1M Price Cut Just a Week before Major Boat Show
summary: In the world of luxury yachts, the latest talk of the town is the remarkable $1 million price reduction on the illustrious Lady Elaine, just before the prestigious Fort Lauderdale International Boat Show.
body: The mesmerising world of luxury yachting has been set abuzz with the recent announcement of a staggering $1 million price drop on the much-celebrated motor yacht, Lady Elaine. The garlanded yacht, listed with Bob Cury of RJC Yachts, has sparked a surge of renewed interest, especially as the sizeable discount comes just a week before its feature at the notable Fort Lauderdale International Boat Show. Here, Lady Elaine will take centre stage as one of the most expensive yachts on display. Originally delivered in 2008 by prominent American yacht builders Christensen, this exquisitely designed yacht boasts high-grade GRP construction and exceptional naval architecture, producing a vessel that exudes nautical elegance. Designed to cater to the world of luxe seafaring, Lady Elaine has maintained ABS and MCA Class and recently completed her 15-year ABS survey in 2023. But that's not all. This majestic beauty underwent considerable refit works in 2025 that saw her hull's complete ceramic coating along with a fresh 'bottom job' and new, plush exterior deck furnishings. Adding another feather to her cap is her accommodation capacity that accommodates an owner's party of up to 15 in six luxury cabins, additional quarters for a crew of 10, and an elevator servicing all four decks. This grandeur is heightened with a full-beam skylounge on the upper deck and a sundeck complete with a large Jacuzzi, wet bar, and ample space for relaxation and entertainment. Indeed, the Lady Elaine serves as a shining beacon of the boundless luxuries that can be found in the world of high-class yachting.

title: Ahead of the Prestigious Fort Lauderdale Boat Show, the Grand 50m Trinity Motor Yacht Impromptu Receives a Whopping $550k Price Cut
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Ahead of the Prestigious Fort Lauderdale Boat Show, the Grand 50m Trinity Motor Yacht Impromptu Receives a Whopping $550k Price Cut
summary: The sale of the 50-metre Trinity motor yacht Impromptu is becoming more enticing with a significant price drop. The announcement of a $550k reduction comes just ahead of her much-anticipated appearance at the upcoming Fort Lauderdale International Boat Show.
body: Be prepared for a delightful surprise on the high seas as the magnificent 50-metre Trinity motor yacht Impromptu sees its price slashed by a considerable $550,000. Kristen Klein and Kevin Merrigan, the worthy trustees handling the sale within the prestigious Northrop & Johnson frame, announced this staggering discount ahead of her much-awaited appearance at the Fort Lauderdale International Boat Show.

This custom-built maritime jewel was handed over by the acclaimed US-based Trinity Yachts back in 2011. Following the installation of a new ASEA shore power converter, a thorough upgrade of the A/V and Wi-Fi systems, and the completion of a full Awlgrip paint job as part of her 2022 refurbishment, the yacht stood as the zenith of maritime elegance. The quality and condition of the yacht received reaffirmation through the successful conclusion of her 15-year ABS survey, conducted earlier this year.

The versatility of her layout, boasting a split-level master cabin with sweeping 180-degree panoramic views, a bridge deck VIP cabin, three king cabins and a twin cabin on the lower deck, remains a significant contributor to her impressive charter history. The main salon, fashioned in an open-plan layout, houses 12 guests with dedicated dining and seating spaces and is accentuated by a centrally located spiral staircase topped with an exquisite wine cellar.

Impromptu further enraptures her guests with a luxurious sundeck comprising of a custom, elevated waterfall Jacuzzi, a well-stocked outdoor bar, an alfresco dining table and BBQ facility, and an array of sunpads and loungers accompanied by shady umbrellas. The impeccably designed skylounge, complete with an L-shaped sofa, bar, 60-inch screen and games table, ensures relentless entertainment for its guests.

The yacht's engine room, powered by twin CAT engines, allows the grand beauty to reach cruising speeds of up to 16.5 knots and a maximum speed of 18.5 knots. With such remarkable specifications, the Trinity motor yacht is now on sale for $23,950,000. As she preps to grace the Fort Lauderdale International Boat Show, the Impromptu stands as one of the priciest yachts for sale. Yet, her charisma continues to seduce potential buyers on the hunt for luxury and adventure on the high seas.

title: AES Yacht's Mereley I, a 35m 'Pocket Explorer', Gets Notable €500k Price Reduction
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: AES Yacht's Mereley I, a 35m 'Pocket Explorer', Gets Notable €500k Price Reduction
summary: The 34.6-metre explorer yacht Mereley I, from AES Yacht, now boasts a €500,000 price cut. This compact yet powerful expedition vessel is seeking a brave new owner to sail uncharted waters.
body: From the skilled shipbuilders at the Turkish AES Yacht shipyard comes the Mereley I, a 34.6-metre explorer yacht often affectionately known as the 'pocket explorer'. The vessel, expertly designed by the Italian studio Hot Lab, is finished to the nines with a breathtaking blue exterior, hiding a world of luxury within its deck. This powerful miniature expedition vessel is now even more desirable with the announcement of a substantial price reduction of €500,000. This pricing revision is set to result in an influx of interested buyers. Mereley I, originally constructed on speculation, has been seeking a new captain since she majestically hit the waters. She radiates an air of grandeur and practicality that few boats her size achieve. Being small does not mean the Mereley I is lacking in any way. This incredible pocket explorer comes equipped to house up to 12 guests comfortably. Inside the vessel, there's an owner's suite befitting a king with a central king-sized bed, a wall-mounted 55-inch TV, walk-in wardrobe, office space, extensive glazing, and a bath with a marble-detailed ceiling. Among the remaining cabins are two VIP sections and two twins, all located midship on the lower deck, complete with ensuite facilities. The vessel also offers accommodations for a crew of seven. The interior design is bathed in natural light thanks to some ingenious design choices. The lounge area commands stunning, panoramic views, and a sliding glass door offers direct deck access to a second dining space. This makes Mereley I an oasis of light and space. And that’s not all. One of the highlights of this vessel is its versatile aft swim platform. This multi-functional space, directly connected to a summery 'beach house', accommodates tenders or Waverunners. Her two powerful MAN engines guarantee a top cruising speed of 14 knots while ensuring a transatlantic range of 3,800 nautical miles when travelling at a comfortable 11.5 knots. With the new price tag of €12,750,000, Mereley I doesn't just offer a world of luxurious adventure at sea, but also represents excellent value. Now awaiting her new owner in Turkey, Mereley I is a superb testament to compact yet powerful yacht exploration designs. Potential buyers should take note - rarely has adventure been available at such a pleasing discount.

title: Embark on a Memorable Voyage: The Tale of a Three-Month Cruise from Poole to Isles of Scilly
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Embark on a Memorable Voyage: The Tale of a Three-Month Cruise from Poole to Isles of Scilly
summary: Embark on an unforgettable nautical odyssey from Poole to the Isles of Scilly. Experience the thrill, the tranquility and the occasional tribulations of coastal cruising in this delightful escapade.
body: Our intrepid adventurer, Simon Ellis, undertakes a maritime journey spanning three months, sailing from Poole to the Isles of Scilly. His voyage unfurls with the wake of his sail boat, taking him through the scenic locales. As Simon travels across Polperro, Fowey, Falmouth, Porthleven, and Mousehole, his journey is fraught with challenges that only serve to amplify the splendour of the entire adventure. Though the Atlantic swell and blocked toilets prove a challenge, they can't deter the spirit of a true sailor. As he takes refuge in the lee of the land, the tranquility of the anchored boat juxtaposes the surges he's battled. The landscapes create breath-taking views, an ample recompense to the occasional inconveniences of the trip. The journey is seasoned with memorable incidents like a trip to the Ferryboat Inn and an exploration on foot to Penzance harbour, each adding a unique flavour to the voyage. The trip culminates with a visit to the remarkable cliffside Minack Theatre, an architectural marvel commanding a majestic view of the sea. Despite the occasional doubts and residual swells, the spirit of exploration and love for the sea remain undeterred. As our voyager navigates past Land’s End and turns a corner towards home, his memorable journey remains a testament to the unfailing allure of the sea and the joy of life spent sailing on it.

title: Exclusive Look: Italian Yard Columbus Yachts Unveils Inner Majesty of its First Crossover 42, Big Naan
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Exclusive Look: Italian Yard Columbus Yachts Unveils Inner Majesty of its First Crossover 42, Big Naan
summary: Palumbo Superyachts' acclaimed Italian brand, Columbus Yachts, gives boating enthusiasts a tantalising glimpse of the exquisite interior of its game-changing Crossover 42 yacht, the Big Naan.
body: Columbus Yachts, a brand of Palumbo Superyachts, has allowed a sneak peek into the lavish interior of its first Crossover 42 model, famously known as the Big Naan. Following her much-anticipated debut at the 2025 Cannes Yachting Festival, expectations have been soaring for a closer look. Sailing alongside the likes of Singolare, Project T, and Juno's 7, she undoubtedly was one of the largest and luxurious yachts on display.

With design credits to the Italian studio Hydro Tec, the Crossover 42 exudes confidence with a 'modern and muscular' exterior. It incorporates a concentrated volume in the bow area, typical of explorers, and flat, tapered stern sections. The stunning yacht was sold to her fortunate American owner in 2023, thanks to Zarpo Yachts, with Trevor van Wyk acting as the owner's representative.

The interiors, a masterpiece crafted by the proficient Milanese study Hot Lab, are a balanced infusion of warm grey and beige tones, punctuated by bright pops of colours from designer furnishings and stunning artworks. Adding to its contemporary aura is the micro-perforated metal ceiling, artistically lit by sculptural light fixtures.

The yacht's 'extremely flexible dimensions' are apparent in its cockpit, designed to accommodate a large tender with a built-in stern crane. Adjoining it is a 10-square-metre swimming pool build with four glass walls, ingeniously filtering natural light into the beach club gym located below.

The sundeck is equipped with a bar, grill, and a 360-degree rotating television. It also features a table that can ingeniously convert into a sunlounger if necessary. With twin CAT C32 engines, the yacht achieves a maximum speed of over 14 knots and boasts a range of over 5,500 nautical miles.

The Big Naan is synonymous with sustainable luxury; a selective catalytic reduction system meeting IMO Tier III emission standards enables it to cruise within marine protected areas. With four superyacht projects underway, Columbus Yachts recently initiated the construction of Big Naan's larger sibling, the Crossover 47, promising more grandeur and luxury.

title: Champion Berntsson Takes Dramatic Charge in the 2025 Bermuda Gold Cup Amid Intriguing Tactics and Fierce Competition
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Champion Berntsson Takes Dramatic Charge in the 2025 Bermuda Gold Cup Amid Intriguing Tactics and Fierce Competition
summary: Rising tides in the 2025 Bermuda Gold Cup as defending champion Johnie Berntsson shows his mettle, battling out a sparklingly flawless second day.
body: This latest edition of the Bermuda Gold Cup sees a dramatic sea showdown between defending champion Johnie Berntsson from Sweden and USA's Chris Poole, climaxing in a flawless performance by Berntsson. In a race awash with penalties and drama, Berntsson navigated through the turbulent waters to emerge victorious. Victory was also tasted against opponents Garreta from France, former match racing world champion Nick Egnot-Johnson from New Zealand, and Great Britain's Ian Williams. Complemented by Swiss skipper Eric Monnin, Berntsson currently holds the yachting world in thrall as he ascends the leaderboard of the prestigious cup.

In the women's field, the Aspen Bermuda Women's Match Racing Regatta pits Sweden's Anna Östling against defending champion Pauline Courtois from France. It's turning out to be quite the epic duel, with Courtois managing to rebound from a disappointing opening day by securing wins in all three races.

After the stormy start, Berntsson was thrilled with the hard-fought victory. He said, 'It was two penalties each and good, fun racing.' Speaking about his duel with Poole, he said, 'We gained after the start, passed him, and they came back at the second upwind mark and locked us up. Then we overtook him, did a gybe and he got a penalty.' This tactical manoeuvre was pivotal in defining the race and ultimately shaped up an exciting competition - a testament to the spirit of yacht racing.

title: Bilgin Yachts Unveils Tamasha, The Pioneering Model of the Bilgin 170 Series: A Maritime Triumph
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Bilgin Yachts Unveils Tamasha, The Pioneering Model of the Bilgin 170 Series: A Maritime Triumph
summary: Turkish shipyard, Bilgin Yacht's premier unit of its Bilgin 170 series, Tamasha, has been presented to the world, encapsulating a blend of elegance and grandeur.
body: In a glamorous display of maritime excellence, Bilgin Yachts, the renowned Turkish shipyard, has unveiled the first ship in its Bilgin 170 series, deemed Tamasha. A collaborative blueprint by Unique Yacht Design and Hot Lab, Tamasha's design draws inspiration from the Bilgin 163 series, with a significant model being the 50-meter Eternal Spark launched last year.

Following the launch, Tamasha was transported to the West Istanbul Marina for the final outfitting processes. The event, beyond being a mere launch, marked a proud milestone for the Bilgin family and represented the commencement of Tamasha's legacy. Tamasha’s launch epitomised the grace, grandeur, and the iterative passion and diligence of the Bilgin team.

Tamasha can cater up to 12 guests and nine crew members, with the owner's cabin situated on the bridge deck. During the design course, the principal aim was to better the 50-meter models by achieving a more athletic and masculine look while seamlessly integrating the design to provide customers with the opportunity to utilise both open and enclosed spaces under 500 gross tons. This design integration for practicality and aesthetics has resulted in a yacht that truly stands out from the crowd.

According to maritime industry tracker BOATPro, a dozen other yachts, including three Bilgin 173s and three Bilgin 170s, are in production at the Turkish shipyard. This comes after the interior reveal of Camila, the second Bilgin 163, before her debut at the 2025 Monaco Yacht Show.

title: Raising the Wave of Foiling with Armstrong's Integration of Foil Drive in Carbon Masts
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Raising the Wave of Foiling with Armstrong's Integration of Foil Drive in Carbon Masts
summary: Armstrong Foils revolutionises the world of sailing with their latest creation - an integrated carbon mast supported by Foil Drive technology.
body: Armstrong Foils have taken a crucial stride forward in redefining the future of powered foiling, surging ahead of the curve with the introduction of their Foil Drive integrated carbon masts. The company continues to live up to its reputation for consistent innovation, unfurling a new chapter in powered foiling that aligns with the brand's ethos of constant progression.

The Armstrong carbon mast, reinforced by Foil Drive technology, aims to amplify the foiling experience, enabling longer stints on water and broadening the scope of what foiling can achieve. Armsie Armstrong, the founder of Armstrong Foils, emphasises that the prime objective of this inventive endeavour is to enable riders to spend more time on the water, raising their performance bar.

Armstrong Foils provides two configurations, meticulously crafted from premium Toray high-modulus carbon fiber and titanium hardware. The Foil Assist configuration focuses on enhancing foil riding experience for intermediate and advanced riders. The E-Foil configuration, on the other hand, is all about creating that quintessential Armstrong feeling. Ideal for flatwater rides and beginners, it ensures constant submersion and full-time motoring without the motor pod.

Significant features of these integrated masts lie in their internal cable routing, adding to a clutter-free appearance while maintaining optimal stiffness and strength. They are compatible with Armstrong’s A+ System forward and backward modularity, allowing usage of any front foil and stabilizer from the Armstrong range. Backed by Foil Drive Gen 2 Assist MAX and Slim systems (sold separately), Foil Assist and E-Foil take riding and foiling experiences to new heights.

Transformative in their conception and design, Armstrong's carbon masts have truly elevated the experience of powered foiling. Armstrong Foils invites us all to be a part of this thrilling journey and witness how this innovative technology shapes the future of foiling.

title: Discover the New Horizons with Mitan, the Second in Numarine's Flagship 40MXP Series
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover the New Horizons with Mitan, the Second in Numarine's Flagship 40MXP Series
summary: Sparking the curiosity of yacht enthusiasts, Turkish yard Numarine announces the delivery of their second 40MXP flagship, the exceptional Mitan.
body: The maritime world takes a fresh breath as the second hull of the flagship 40MXP series by Numarine, aptly christened Mitan, graces the waters. Designed with the South American owners' tastes in mind, Mitan, a spectacular 39.4-metre yacht, elegantly marries the practicality of long-range expedition capabilities with an irresistible ethos of outdoor living. The secret behind this unique blend lies in the natural evolution from Numarine's highly esteemed 37XP design.

Regarded as the distinguishing feature of this flagship series, the remarkable aft deck, a sheer epitome of meticulous design, intrigues the most discerning of yacht lovers. By extending the hull and shifting the aft sliding doors of the saloon just a bit forward, an entirely new spatial dimension has been created. Now, the aft deck accommodates a spacious al fresco dining space, a bar, a lounge and a wrap-around aft pool with a magnetic allure.

The awe-inspiring look of Mitan is credited to Can Yalman, a long-standing Numarine collaborator, while the naval architecture is the handiwork of the inimitable Umberto Tagliavini. Mitan outshines her sistership Miouch, delivered in August, with an exclusively tailored interior and exterior colour palette.

Performing as impressively as she appears, Mitan provides a staggering 6000-nautical-mile range at eight knots, thanks to her twin MAN 800hp engines. The yacht's performance can be further enhanced with an optional Tier III-compliant 900hp configuration.

Signalling an overwhelming interest, Numarine's 40MXP is rapidly growing in popularity, with a third model already been sold and is presently under construction, slated for a grand unveiling next year.

title: Meet P3 Marine, The Startup That's Taken Superyacht Finance By Storm In Just A Year
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Meet P3 Marine, The Startup That's Taken Superyacht Finance By Storm In Just A Year
summary: One year ago, P3 Marine embraced an ambitious mission to revolutionise financial management in the superyacht industry. Today, it’s astonishingly doing just that.
body: In the shimmering world of superyachts, a fresh breeze is stirring the sails — born from a pioneering start-up called P3 Marine. Just a year ago, the company was launched with a bold promise: to redefine financial management in the superyacht industry. Cofounded by a pair of enthusiasts, superyacht aficionado Reda Bedjaoui and former banker Philippe Werner, P3 Marine tackled the glaring issue that traditional financial operations for ultra-high-net-worth individuals in the yachting scene had not kept pace with technology.

Fast-forward to the present, P3 Marine is not only fulfilling its promise but impressively exceeding expectations. It has rapidly morphed into a widely trusted platform for yacht owners, captains, managers, brokers and family offices alike. Conceived as a purpose-built financial hub, P3 Marine aims to bring a sense of clarity, efficiency, and control to the usually cloudy world of superyacht finances.

The incredible success of P3 Marine, now a pillar in yacht financing, is largely thanks to its in-house development team. Their ability to quickly integrate client feedback allowed the platform to evolve at a dizzying pace within mere months of its conception.

A considerable turning point in P3 Marine's journey came with the achievement of becoming a Principal Member of Visa. This prestigious status allows it to issue cards directly to clients, providing an unprecedented level of control over yacht operations. Department-level spending limits can now be assigned to cards issued for crew, chefs or engineers, significantly facilitating large event planning and provisioning tasks.

This cherished accomplishment serves as a testament to the resilience and innovation that P3 Marine brings to the superyacht industry. Despite its remarkable first-year growth, the journey has only just begun for this resilient start-up. The waves they've created are undoubtedly making a splash, and the yachting world is all ears, eager to see what innovative solutions they will introduce next.

title: Ruthless Racing and Innovation at The International Moth Winter Championship 2025 Hosted by Rutland Sailing Club
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Ruthless Racing and Innovation at The International Moth Winter Championship 2025 Hosted by Rutland Sailing Club
summary: The International Moth Winter Championship 2025, held at Rutland Sailing Club, proved to be a thrilling two-day sailing spectacle, showcasing both fierce competition and innovatively designed vessels.
body: The last major event in the sailing calendar, the much-anticipated International Moth Winter Championship 2025, unfurled its sails at the Rutland Sailing Club. The line-up consisted of Exocet, Aerocet, and Exploder designs, adding more sparks to the thrilling weekend event.

Among the collection of skilfully designed vessels, Paul Gliddon's recently converted Exocet caught most of the attention, with solid wings and a reduced foredeck. The change in design stirred up conversation, acknowledging that improvement and innovation in the most unlikely areas often help in gaining a competitive edge.

While Saturday's weak breeze left much to be desired, patience paid off as the participants experienced an inspiring 15-Knot NE breeze on Sunday, kicking off an exhilarating round of races. Sailors deliberated preparations; choosing between big foils and sails for handling lulls and tackling, or smaller foils concentrated on straight-line speed.

Unsurprisingly, the races highlighted Paul Gliddon's superior expertise and rigging adaptations, though competitors Alex Adams and Jason Belben proved their worth by capitalizing on the scarce errors made. Behind them, the remaining fleet showcased an exhilarating battle at each level, creating a gripping spectacle for all involved.

The event was a vivid reminder of sailing's capacity to encourage innovation and competitiveness. Success at the International Moth Winter Championship showed that even an older design like the Exocet could come front and centre with the right adjustments. And with the favorable market for secondhand vessels, participants had proved once again that achieving high-speed foiling dinghy status is within everyone's reach.

title: Sanlorenzo's New Heritage Yacht SHE is Redefining the Luxury Sea Experience
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Sanlorenzo's New Heritage Yacht SHE is Redefining the Luxury Sea Experience
summary: In unveiling their latest luxury yacht concept, titled SHE, Sanlorenzo is setting a new benchmark in sea innovation.
body: Breaking new grounds in nautical innovation, Sanlorenzo's latest concept yacht, SHE, pays homage to the glory days of relaxed sea travel while incorporating cutting-edge features. The 25.5-meter beauty is sure to make waves in the world of luxury sea voyages. Not just a nod to the past, SHE brings a fresh perspective to the yachting experience, striving for a harmony others have yet to achieve.

Modern, yet timeless, SHE couples advanced features like a hybrid, silent mode with intimate creature comforts. However, what truly sets this yacht apart is its perfect proportions devoid of any unseemly elements - a sanctuary for the fortunate owner and a spectacle for the onlooker. Previously admired yachts, such as the Baltic Café Racer, the Sanlorenzo's SP110, even the Feadship's M/Y Faith or any Riva under 15 meters may fall short in the face of SHE's charm. SHE is your personal sanctuary, a sight for sore eyes, always ready to entertain, to be enjoyed.

Of course, as with any grand venture, SHE isn’t without its nuances. The upper sun deck can get breezy, making it a place to secure cushions safely. A minor hiccup in an otherwise perfect creation. As with any classic beauty, SHE draws attention for all the right reasons and leaves passers-by admiring without any hint of jealousy or envy. Aptly compared to a 1960s’ Aston Martin DB5 for its irresistible appeal and tastefulness, SHE signifies good taste and the enduring appeal of the quieter, more refined things in life.

Sanlorenzo's CEO, Massimo Perotti, describes the unveiling of SHE as a testament to seven decades of painstaking craftsmanship. A silent nod to elegant yachting of the past, SHE is the future. A testament to the potential for design and innovation to respect and enhance tradition rather than superseding it completely.

title: Setting new standards, Fairline F//Line 33 Shakes the World with its Exceptional Hull Construction and Design
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Setting new standards, Fairline F//Line 33 Shakes the World with its Exceptional Hull Construction and Design
summary: Outshining even the famed 'superboats', the Fairline F//Line 33 has gained global attention for its spectacular hull — one of the finest ever tested.
body: In 2019, the world witnessed the launch of the 'superboats' by three UK boat-builders. Aimed at bringing a sporty appeal to their range, these boats were designed as high-performance models mingled with impeccable style. From Sunseeker's Hawk 38, boasting a design by race boat driver and builder Fabio Buzzi and clocking a notable 70 mph, to The Princess R35, with its unique hydrofoiling technology, these 'superboats' were making waves.

Then, at the Monaco Yacht Show, Fairline stole the spotlight with the launch of the F//Line 33. Unlike its competitors, the F//Line 33 is still in production, a testament to its lasting appeal. More than just an eye-catching boat, the F//Line 33 also houses a remarkably brilliant hull. Powered by twin 430hp V8 petrol engines, it reached a top speed of nearly 50 knots during testing sessions. The boat’s exceptional seakeeping and handling have been regularly applauded in panel reviews.

Boasting features that many boat enthusiasts have yearned for in the past two decades, the F//Line 33 has truly become a standout in the world of motorboats. It’s not merely a recreational boat, the F//Line 33 is an enduring icon and testament to Fairline's dedication to blending style with performance on the high seas.

title: CL Yachts Breaks New Ground with 'Resort-style' C Series Catamaran Model
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: CL Yachts Breaks New Ground with 'Resort-style' C Series Catamaran Model
summary: Hong Kong-based shipyard, CL Yachts takes a bold leap into the catamaran market, revealing the environmentally conscious, tech-savvy, and luxurious CLC115.
body: No longer confined to monohulls, CL Yachts has taken a remarkable turn with the launch of their brand-new C Series, revealing the first model, CLC115, a 35-metre catamaran. Setting high standards in fiberglass hull construction, this lightweight build perfectly blends structural integrity with fuel efficiency. What truly sets the CLC115 apart is its commitment to sustainability, featuring optional solar panelling and eco-conscious interiors.

An advanced hybrid system fires the catamaran up to 18 knots. Complementing its eco-friendly design, a Smart Home module steps up energy efficiency by intuitively managing climate control, lighting, and other household systems. All credit to Incat Crowther for the naval architecture and exterior design, a catamaran design virtuoso renowned for his craft on Hodor and other Astilleros Armón builds.

Adorning the interiors are organic shapes, soft lines, and a neutral palette, conceived by Chinese designer Supertomato Studio. This resort-style aesthetic breathes tranquility into the space. The CLC115 is also certified to RINA Yacht Class standards.

Additional luxuries include a foredeck spa pool, a lifting beach platform, fold-down bulwarks, and generous storage for tenders and aquatic toys. The CLC115 represents an excellent fusion of sophisticated design with eco-friendly technology. Martin Lo, director of CL Yachts, highlights how every aspect of the CLC115 has been meticulously crafted to embrace nature, stimulate interaction, and promote well-being, setting a fresh benchmark for responsible yachting in the modern world.

title: Experience Unparalleled Luxury at Sea With the Highly Coveted FERRETTI 1000 Series Yacht 'SPICA' Now on the Market
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Experience Unparalleled Luxury at Sea With the Highly Coveted FERRETTI 1000 Series Yacht 'SPICA' Now on the Market
summary: Discover the pinnacle of seafaring luxury and sophisticated design in SPICA, the FERRETTI 1000 series yacht now for sale. Built for highly discerning owners, it represents the epitome of opulence and functionality at sea.
body: Showcasing the very best of the FERRETTI 1000 series, 'SPICA' is a motor yacht unrivalled in her elegance, sophistication and versatility. Built meticulously for discerning and experienced owners, she shines with a rich array of optional extras and upgrades that amplify her stately charm and operational efficiency. The distinct features collectively improve SPICA's charter ability and life on board, offering a smooth seafaring adventure, effortlessly blending luxury and practicality.

The innovative deck spaces on SPICA are an engineer's marvel, set to mesmerize any maritime aficionado. A large bow area, flying bridge, and aft beach deck flawlessly interlock to create an incredible outdoor space designed for relaxation, entertainment and soaking up the sun’s rays. Paired with a stunning, contemporary interior and generous windows, the yacht allows an ample flow of natural light, cultivating a relaxed, vibrant and refreshing aura throughout.

The boat is powered by a set of robust Caterpillar engines, delivering a total of 3446hp, cruising comfortably at 23 knots and maxing out near 28. Teeny details like a new design beach area, stunning deck spaces and a beautifully modern interior push the boundaries of aesthetics at sea. With spacious five-cabin layout, including a full-beam master cabin, it offers plenty of room for up to ten guests.
The SPICA is a true masterpiece of the sea, inviting seafarers to taste luxury the FERRETTI way, charting salty adventures in style.

title: An Extract on Superyachts: Addressing Safety Culture and the Well-being of Yacht Crew
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: An Extract on Superyachts: Addressing Safety Culture and the Well-being of Yacht Crew
summary: A crystal-clear perspective on the superyacht industry, focusing specifically on the pivotal aspects of safety and crew well-being.
body: Glistening on the glossy surface of the superyacht industry, luxury, precision, and flawless service are lined as the gold standards. However, trotting below this opulent façade is an arena of importance that cannot be watered down - safety culture and crew well-being. Maritime safety already receives a good thrust from evolving technology and regulations, but the real game-changer resides in shifting from compliance to empathy. A fresh perspective that knits humans into the centre of safety and operational efficiency. Moreover, it's not just textbook theory, as numerous high-profile incidents in the yacht community have hammered the need for microscopic focus on safety.

Waiting for tragedy to knock on the door before reacting to it isn't the go-to safety strategy anymore. The next-gen approach is proactive, fuelled by data that has passed the test of the time. Several instances in history like Titanic, Herald of Free Enterprise, and the Torrey Canyon exemplify the grave cost of inaction.

Yet, it's never too late to change the narrative. As a visionary, Lloyd's Register (LR) is pioneering a novel path that establishes a new safety culture benchmark in the yachting industry. This foresight takes the form of a holistic safety culture survey, executed across seagoing yachts and their management firms. In an attempt to unravel areas of improvement, this initiative quantifies safety practices, providing key insights to strength the safety framework. But a solo player can't rule the game, and industry participation becomes the heart of this operation.

The survey is an open invitation for yacht owners, crew members, operators, management corporations, to share their insights. An attempt to weave a safety culture that finds resonance with industry values while being robust. It is not a mere reactive step to increase safety standings, but a well-thought-out, united endeavour. The marathon to a safer, secure future begins at this very minute. The helm is in the hands of those who see beyond the horizon and change it for the better.

title: Meet Pegasus: The High-tech Electric Foiler Taking Yacht Toys to Dizzying 30-knot Speeds
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Meet Pegasus: The High-tech Electric Foiler Taking Yacht Toys to Dizzying 30-knot Speeds
summary: Step aside electric surfboards, the world of superyacht toys has a new speed demon. Meet Pegasus, a single-seating, all-electric foiling marvel styled after 1960's Formula One cars!
body: Superyacht toys have been taken to a new level with the innovation of Pegasus, an all-electric foiling craft that combines the thrill of high-performance sailing with the intuitive handling of a bicycle. Developed by Finnish start-up Foil.One, this impressive single-seater is constructed entirely of carbon fibre, capable of reaching incredible speeds up to 30 knots while gliding effortlessly above the water.

The secret behind its user-friendly design lies in a unique foiling set-up, integrating steering, balance, and ride height into one intuitive mechanism. Imagine handles like those on a bicycle - or, indeed, a rowing eight - and you've got the idea. This design makes steering as easy as biking, with balance quickly mastered.

But that's not all. The Pegasus is powered by a modest yet potent 10kW electric motor linked to a slender propeller-running shaft, promising silent propulsion through the water. The craft includes two 5kWh Torqeedo batteries, promising up to an hour of full-throttle fun.

In short, Pegasus redefines the realm of yacht toys, offering limitless fun punctuated with adrenaline-pumping speed. With just a few lessons, anyone can reach their 'need for speed' in a safe and exhilarating manner. So, grab your life jacket and hitch a ride on Pegasus' wings!

title: Unveiling the Distinct Reality of Safety Culture and Progressive Shifts in the Yachting Sector
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unveiling the Distinct Reality of Safety Culture and Progressive Shifts in the Yachting Sector
summary: The superyacht business, synonymous with luxury and precision, accentuates the critical importance of crew safety and their holistic wellbeing.
body: Beneath the shimmering world of superyachts is a crucial foundation - a robust safety culture and crew well-being. While the establishments and rapid advancements of technology contribute significantly to maritime safety, the real challenge bobs in the shift from a compliance-driven mindset to the one that embarks on a human-oriented approach. A handful of high-profile incidents have made safety a critical focal point in the yachting community. Though human error is loosely labelled for most of these accidents, a deeper examination unravels a more complex relationship between individuals, processes, and technology. With a plethora of yachts cruising through the sea's arteries, the number of serious incidents may seem relatively small. Yet, each accident unveils a lost chance to enrich knowledge, enhance techniques, and forestall future mishaps. The yachting industry urges a proactive, data-guided journey towards safety instead of waiting for a disaster to strike. History is impregnated with countless tales of how inaction results in loss of lives, like Titanic and Torrey Canyon. Lloyd’s Register (LR) presents a fresh course that sets an unprecedented benchmark for safety culture in the yachting sector. LR is spearheading a comprehensive safety culture survey across seagoing yachts and their management companies. The goal is to assess and benchmark safety practices, pinpoint areas in need of amelioration, and provide practical insights to bolster the industry’s safety framework. Such efforts are impossible without broad industry participation. An appeal goes out to yacht owners, operators, management companies and crew members to share their unique perspectives to shape a safety culture embodying the industry’s values. It's not just the regulations and safety procedures; the yachting sector also acknowledges the shifts that it has gone through over the years. Factors like comfort, seagoing capacity, range and size etc. have shown an upward trend making yachting more enjoyable. Yet with this growth, the depth, complexity and regulatory environment around yachting have become substantially intricate. The primary disciplines in yacht management and support remain the same amid various changes. However, the focus is now to ensure that safety standards are not just met but enhanced to craft a better future.

title: Thrilling Two-day Rooster ILCA 6 National Open Event at Weymouth & Portland Sailing Academy Dazzles Crowd
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Thrilling Two-day Rooster ILCA 6 National Open Event at Weymouth & Portland Sailing Academy Dazzles Crowd
summary: Rooster ILCA 6 National Open event culminated an action-packed two-day sailing spectacle at Weymouth & Portland National Sailing Academy, attracting international participants.
