body: It was an enthralling sight as nearly 186 sailboats from various countries swarmed the Weymouth & Portland National Sailing Academy for the Rooster ILCA 6 National Open event. The spirits were palpable as participants including half a dozen Irishmen and entries from France, Bermuda, and the Bahamas added to the International flavour of the contest.

The event faced some initial challenges due to a light forecast. However, the efficient race director, James Hynes, and the unwavering support of 60 volunteers ensured a flawless schedule of races over the weekend. The intense competition kept all on tenterhooks as the podium placements swung to the last wire.

Despite the tumultuous waves, challenges, and unexpected conditions, the sailors kept their spirits high. In the end, it was a thrilling weekend of sailing that brought racers from across the globe together. The adrenalin-filled event also provided crucial experience for sailors like Carys Attwell in advancing their skills before their upcoming Under 21 world championship.
Looking forwards, the buzz continues with National Open 5 scheduled at WPNSA, followed by Masters Inland Championships at Grafham Water and National Inland Championships at Draycote Water.

title: Which boat is right for you ?
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Setting Sail in Style: Which boat is right for you ?
imageCaption: Which boat is right for you ?
summary: There’s nothing quite like the moment your bow slices into open water. The hum of an engine or the snap of canvas in the breeze, a horizon that stretches forever, and the promise of adventure ahead. For some, a yacht is luxury. For others, it’s freedom itself. But whether you’re a veteran skipper or a newcomer to saltwater life, choosing the right yacht is a decision that shapes every mile of your voyage.
body: When it comes to luxury travel, few experiences can rival the sheer excitement of setting sail on your own yacht. Picture gliding over azure waters, with the wind in your hair and the horizon stretching endlessly before you. But before you embark on this unforgettable adventure, choosing the perfect yacht is essential. With so many options out there, selecting a vessel that perfectly aligns with your style, needs, and budget can be overwhelming. Fear not! This ultimate guide will navigate you through the intricate world of yachting, offering insights into various types of yachts, essential features to consider, and tips for ensuring a seamless experience on the water. Whether you’re a seasoned sailor or a first-time adventurer, we’ve got everything you need to make an informed choice and set sail in style. Get ready to chart your course toward an extraordinary journey, where every wave leads to new memories waiting to be made.

Embarking on your yachting adventure starts with understanding the different types of yachts available. Each type offers unique features and caters to various preferences and activities. Primarily, yachts can be classified into motor yachts, sailing yachts, catamarans, and mega yachts. Motor yachts are powered by engines and are known for their speed and ease of navigation. They are perfect for those who want to cover large distances quickly and enjoy a range of onboard amenities without relying on wind conditions. On the other hand, sailing yachts offer a more traditional and tranquil experience, allowing you to harness the power of the wind and enjoy a quieter journey. Sailing enthusiasts often prefer these for the sense of adventure and connection with nature they provide. Catamarans are another popular choice, featuring two hulls connected by a deck. They offer exceptional stability, ample space, and comfort, making them ideal for families or groups seeking a leisurely and spacious voyage. Catamarans are also known for their shallow draft, allowing them to navigate in shallower waters and access secluded spots that larger yachts cannot reach. Lastly, mega yachts, often referred to as luxury yachts, are the epitome of opulence. These colossal vessels come equipped with state-of-the-art facilities, including swimming pools, helipads, and expansive entertainment areas. Mega yachts are perfect for those seeking the ultimate luxury experience, complete with professional crew and personalised services. Selecting the right type of yacht depends on your personal preferences, planned activities, and the destinations you wish to explore. If speed and convenience are your priorities, a motor yacht may be the best choice. For those who cherish the art of sailing and the serenity of the sea, a sailing yacht is an excellent option. Families and groups looking for space and stability will find catamarans to be a perfect fit, while those desiring unparalleled luxury and amenities should consider mega yachts. Understanding these distinctions will help you take the first step in choosing the perfect yacht for your adventure.

Choosing the perfect yacht involves more than just picking a type; several factors must be taken into account to ensure your vessel meets all your needs. Start by considering the purpose of your trip. Are you planning a short coastal cruise, a long-term voyage, or a series of island hops? The intended duration of your trip will influence the size, range, and facilities you need. For instance, a long-term voyage may require a yacht with extensive storage, fuel capacity, and comfortable living quarters, while a short trip might prioritise speed and convenience. Another crucial factor is the number of guests and crew members. The size and layout of the yacht should accommodate everyone comfortably. Yachts come in various sizes, and larger vessels typically offer more space and amenities but also require more crew to operate and maintain. Make sure to choose a yacht that can comfortably house all passengers, with enough cabins, bathrooms, and communal spaces. Additionally, consider the level of privacy each guest requires, as some yachts offer more secluded quarters than others. Your budget will also play a significant role in your decision. Yachts vary widely in price, not only in terms of purchase or charter costs but also in maintenance, fuel, docking, and crew expenses. Determine your budget early on and be realistic about ongoing costs. It's essential to balance your desires with your financial limitations to avoid any unpleasant surprises. By carefully considering the purpose of your trip, the number of guests, and your budget, you can narrow down your options and choose a yacht that perfectly aligns with your needs.

Embarking on a yachting adventure requires careful financial planning. The cost of chartering or purchasing a yacht is just one part of the equation; there are several other expenses to consider to ensure a smooth and enjoyable journey. Start by setting a realistic budget that encompasses all aspects of your trip, including the initial costs and ongoing expenditures. Chartering a yacht is a popular option for many, as it provides the luxury of yachting without the long-term financial commitment. Charter fees vary based on the type of yacht, its size, age, and the season. High-demand seasons, such as summer in the Mediterranean, will typically have higher charter rates. When budgeting, don't forget to account for additional expenses such as crew salaries, fuel, docking fees, and provisions. Crew salaries can be a significant portion of your budget, especially if you require a full crew including a captain, chef, and deckhands. Fuel costs will depend on the type of yacht and your planned itinerary; motor yachts tend to consume more fuel compared to sailing yachts. Docking fees, which vary by location and the size of your yacht, should also be factored into your budget. Furthermore, provisioning costs for food, beverages, and other supplies must be considered to ensure a comfortable and enjoyable experience for all onboard. For those considering purchasing a yacht, the initial cost is just the beginning. Ownership comes with ongoing maintenance, insurance, registration, and storage costs. Regular maintenance is crucial to keep your yacht in top condition, and it can be costly depending on the size and complexity of the vessel. Insurance is another essential expense, protecting your investment against potential damages or accidents. Storage and docking fees, whether at a marina or a private dock, should also be included in your budget. By thoroughly understanding and planning for these expenses, you can ensure a financially sound and stress-free yachting adventure.

When selecting the perfect yacht, it's essential to consider the features that will enhance your overall experience. Comfort and functionality should be at the forefront of your decision-making process. Start by evaluating the layout and design of the yacht. A well-designed layout ensures that the space is used efficiently, providing ample room for relaxation and entertainment. Look for yachts with spacious cabins, comfortable living areas, and well-equipped kitchens. The number and arrangement of cabins are particularly important if you're traveling with a group, as everyone will need their own space to unwind. Another key feature to consider is the range of amenities offered onboard. Modern yachts come with a wide array of amenities designed to enhance your comfort and enjoyment. Consider amenities such as air conditioning, Wi-Fi, entertainment systems, and water sports equipment. Air conditioning is especially important if you plan to sail in warmer climates, ensuring a comfortable environment inside the yacht. Wi-Fi and entertainment systems keep you connected and entertained during your voyage. Additionally, having water sports equipment like snorkelling gear, kayaks, and paddle-boards can add an extra layer of fun to your adventure. Safety features should never be overlooked when choosing a yacht. Ensure that the yacht is equipped with all necessary safety equipment, including life jackets, life rafts, fire extinguishers, and first aid kits. Familiarise yourself with the yacht's navigation and communication systems, as well as any emergency procedures. It's also wise to check the yacht's maintenance history and ensure it's in good condition. By prioritising comfort, amenities, and safety features, you can select a yacht that provides a luxurious and secure environment for your journey.

The world of yachting is filled with renowned brands and models that have earned their reputation for quality, performance, and luxury. When choosing a yacht, it's helpful to be familiar with some of the most popular brands and their flagship models. One of the most esteemed names in the industry is Sunseeker. Known for their sleek design and high performance, Sunseeker yachts are a favourite among discerning yachting enthusiasts. Models like the Sunseeker Predator and Manhattan series offer a blend of speed, luxury, and cutting-edge technology, making them ideal for both short trips and longer voyages. Another prestigious brand is Azimut, which has been crafting exquisite yachts for over 50 years. Azimut yachts are celebrated for their elegant design, innovative features, and superior craftsmanship. The Azimut Grande and Flybridge series are particularly popular, offering spacious layouts, luxurious interiors, and advanced navigation systems. These yachts are perfect for those who seek a harmonious balance of style and functionality. Additionally, Azimut's commitment to sustainability and eco-friendly practices makes them a preferred choice for environmentally conscious travelers. For those who prioritise sailing, the Oyster and Beneteau brands are synonymous with excellence. Oyster Yachts are renowned for their robust construction, exceptional performance, and luxurious interiors. The Oyster 565 and 745 models are highly regarded in the sailing community, offering unparalleled comfort and reliability. Beneteau, on the other hand, is known for its wide range of sailing yachts that cater to different preferences and budgets. The Beneteau Oceanis and First series are popular choices, providing a perfect blend of performance, safety, and comfort. By exploring these esteemed brands and their models, you can find a yacht that aligns with your preferences and guarantees an exceptional yachting experience.

When selecting a yacht, the size and capacity of the vessel are critical factors that can significantly impact your experience. The size of the yacht determines the amount of space available for living, dining, and recreational activities. Larger yachts typically offer more amenities and greater comfort, making them suitable for longer voyages or larger groups. However, they also come with higher costs for fuel, docking, and maintenance. On the other hand, smaller yachts are easier to navigate and can access more secluded areas, but they may offer limited space and fewer amenities. The capacity of the yacht, in terms of both guests and crew, is equally important. Ensure that the yacht can comfortably accommodate all passengers, with enough cabins and bathrooms to provide privacy and convenience. Consider the layout of the yacht, as well as the availability of communal spaces such as lounges, dining areas, and outdoor decks. The number of crew members required will also depend on the size and complexity of the yacht. A larger yacht may need a full crew, including a captain, chef, and deckhands, while a smaller yacht might only require a captain and one or two additional crew members. It's also essential to consider the intended use of the yacht when determining the appropriate size and capacity. For example, if you plan to host parties or entertain guests frequently, a larger yacht with ample deck space and entertainment facilities would be ideal. Conversely, if your primary goal is to explore remote destinations and enjoy a peaceful retreat, a smaller yacht may be more suitable. By carefully evaluating the size and capacity requirements based on your needs and preferences, you can select a yacht that ensures a comfortable and enjoyable experience for everyone onboard.

One of the most significant decisions you'll face when planning your yachting adventure is whether to charter or buy a yacht. Both options have their advantages and drawbacks, and the right choice will depend on your lifestyle, budget, and long-term plans. Chartering a yacht is a popular choice for those who want to enjoy the luxury of yachting without the commitment of ownership. It offers flexibility, as you can choose different yachts for different trips and avoid the responsibilities of maintenance and storage. Chartering also allows you to experience yachting in various locations around the world without the need to relocate your vessel. This can be particularly appealing for those who enjoy exploring new destinations and prefer the convenience of having a fully-equipped yacht ready for their arrival. Additionally, chartering can be more cost-effective for occasional voyages, as you only pay for the time you spend on the yacht, without the ongoing expenses associated with ownership. However, it's essential to book your charters well in advance, especially during peak seasons, to secure your preferred yacht and itinerary. On the other hand, buying a yacht offers the advantage of having your own vessel at your disposal whenever you wish. Ownership provides a sense of pride and freedom, allowing you to customise the yacht to your preferences and enjoy spontaneous trips without the need for prior arrangements. However, owning a yacht comes with significant financial commitments, including the initial purchase price, ongoing maintenance, insurance, docking fees, and crew salaries. It's also a long-term investment that requires careful planning and budgeting. If you plan to spend a considerable amount of time on the water and are prepared for the responsibilities of ownership, buying a yacht can be a rewarding option. Ultimately, the decision between chartering and buying will depend on your personal preferences, budget, and yachting goals.

Preparing for a yacht adventure involves more than just choosing the right vessel; there are several essential steps to ensure a smooth and enjoyable journey. Start by planning your itinerary and researching your destinations. Familiarise yourself with the local weather conditions, navigational hazards, and customs regulations. It's also important to have a backup plan in case of unexpected changes in weather or other unforeseen circumstances. Creating a detailed itinerary will help you make the most of your time on the water and ensure you have all necessary permits and documentation. Packing for a yacht trip requires careful consideration of the limited space and the unique environment. Bring lightweight, breathable clothing suitable for the climate, as well as swimwear, hats, and sunglasses for protection from the sun. Don't forget to pack non-slip shoes for safety on deck. Essentials such as sunscreen, insect repellent, and any necessary medications should also be included. If you plan to engage in water sports or other activities, bring appropriate gear such as snorkelling equipment, fishing rods, or hiking boots. Additionally, consider bringing entertainment options such as books, games, or music to enjoy during downtime. Lastly, ensure that your yacht is well-provisioned with food, beverages, and other supplies. Plan your meals in advance and stock up on non-perishable items, as well as fresh produce and meats if storage allows. It's also wise to have a supply of bottled water and other beverages to stay hydrated. Coordinate with your crew to ensure they have everything they need to provide a comfortable and enjoyable experience. By thoroughly preparing and packing thoughtfully, you can set sail with confidence and focus on creating unforgettable memories on your yacht adventure.

Maintaining your yacht in top condition is essential for ensuring safety, performance, and longevity. Regular maintenance tasks should be performed to keep all systems and equipment functioning properly. Start with routine inspections, checking the hull, deck, and superstructure for any signs of damage or wear. Inspect and clean the propellers, rudders, and other underwater components to prevent the buildup of marine growth. Regularly wash and wax the exterior to protect the surfaces from saltwater and UV damage, preserving the yacht's appearance and value. The engine and mechanical systems require particular attention, as they are crucial for the yacht's operation. Follow the manufacturer's recommended maintenance schedule for oil changes, filter replacements, and other essential tasks. Monitor fluid levels, belts, hoses, and electrical connections for any signs of wear or leaks. Regularly test and service the navigation, communication, and safety equipment to ensure they are in working order. Keeping detailed records of all maintenance activities can help you stay on top of necessary tasks and provide valuable information for future servicing. Interior maintenance is equally important for ensuring comfort and hygiene. Clean and sanitise all living areas, including cabins, bathrooms, and kitchens. Check and maintain air conditioning, heating, and plumbing systems to ensure they are functioning correctly. Upholstery, carpets, and other soft furnishings should be regularly cleaned and inspected for damage. Proper ventilation is essential to prevent mold and mildew, so ensure that all hatches and vents are in good working order. By staying diligent with maintenance and care, you can keep your yacht in excellent condition, ensuring a safe and enjoyable experience every time you set sail.

Choosing the perfect yacht for your next adventure is a significant decision that requires careful consideration of various factors. By understanding the different types of yachts, evaluating essential features, and considering your budget and intended use, you can make an informed choice that aligns with your needs and preferences. Whether you decide to charter or buy, the key is to plan thoroughly and prepare for your journey to ensure a seamless and enjoyable experience on the water.

Embarking on a yacht adventure offers a unique opportunity to explore the world's most beautiful destinations in unparalleled luxury and comfort. From the tranquil experience of sailing yachts to the opulence of mega yachts, there is a vessel to suit every style and desire. By prioritising safety, comfort, and functionality, you can select a yacht that provides the perfect setting for creating unforgettable memories with family and friends. As you set sail on your yachting journey, remember that the adventure is not just about the destination but also the experiences and moments shared along the way. Whether you're navigating pristine waters, discovering secluded coves, or enjoying onboard festivities, every wave leads to new memories waiting to be made. With the right yacht and careful planning, you can embark on an extraordinary journey, setting sail with confidence and style. Happy yachting!

With so many designs, brands, and budgets in play, the world of yachts can feel like a fog-bound channel. This guide clears the course, from understanding types of yachts to knowing what features matter most, balancing budgets, and finally deciding whether to buy or charter. Whatever your heading, let’s plot the way forward so you can step aboard with confidence.
The first choice any sailor faces is simple: what sort of yacht suits you? Each has its own character, purpose, and quirks.

Motor yachts are the thoroughbreds of convenience. Push the throttles forward, and they’ll carry you swiftly from port to port, often bristling with creature comforts. Think speed, range, and indulgence at anchor.

Sailing yachts, on the other hand, offer romance and connection. Powered by wind alone, they demand patience, seamanship, and reward you with silence under canvas. For those who prize the journey as much as the destination, these are hard to beat.

Catamarans straddle the divide — literally. With twin hulls, they provide stability, deck space, and comfort, making them a popular choice for families and those who prefer less heel and more room to entertain.

And then there are mega yachts — floating palaces with pools, helipads, cinemas, and crews that outnumber the guests. For the few who can afford them, they’re not just yachts but statements of wealth and lifestyle.
Your choice depends on your appetite: speed or serenity, solitude or spectacle.
Selecting a yacht is less about falling in love with a gleaming hull and more about matching vessel to voyage.
Ask yourself: what’s the purpose of your trip? Short coastal hops? Ocean crossings? Island-hopping with friends? Each scenario demands a different blend of speed, storage, and seaworthiness.

Then comes capacity. How many souls will be aboard? A couple needs far less than a family of six or a charter group of ten. Privacy matters too — some layouts offer individual cabins, others cram bunks like hammocks on a frigate.

Finally, and inevitably, there’s budget. Yachting is never a cheap pastime, but the range is vast. Chartering costs vary with size, season, and crew. Buying brings not just the upfront price but ongoing mooring, maintenance, insurance, and fuel bills. Knowing what you’re prepared to spend avoids finding yourself becalmed financially before you’ve even set sail.

Many newcomers underestimate the running costs of a yacht. Chartering may seem expensive, but often it’s the smarter choice for occasional sailors. Charter fees cover the yacht, the crew, and a well-oiled machine ready to sail.

Ownership, however, is a different beast. Alongside fuel and docking fees come crew salaries, insurance, annual haul-outs, and constant maintenance. A simple truth of the sea: a yacht is happiest when it’s used. Leave her idle too long, and she’ll demand repairs.
Set a realistic budget — not just for the yacht itself but for everything that keeps her afloat, from provisioning to polishing stainless.

Not every yacht is created equal, and not every bell and whistle is worth chasing. Think first of layout and comfort. Are there enough cabins? Is the galley practical? Is there space to gather, eat, and relax?
Then look at amenities. Do you want air-con, Wi-Fi, or simply a good cockpit for sundowners? Are you planning to dive, fish, or paddleboard? The right gear can turn a voyage into an adventure.
Finally, never ignore safety. Lifejackets, rafts, radios, fire suppression — they’re not glamorous, but they’re the foundations of every safe return.

Certain names carry weight at the dock. Sunseeker and Azimut are the show ponies of motor yachts — sleek, fast, and packed with luxury. For sailing, Oyster and Beneteau remain stalwarts: one at the high-end bluewater bracket, the other delivering versatility and value across a broad fleet.
Know the reputations, study the models, and match them to your style. Whether you want understated reliability or headline-grabbing glamour, there’s a badge for you.

It’s the eternal question. Charter for freedom and variety, choosing different yachts in different waters without the hassle of upkeep. Or buy, if you crave ownership, customisation, and the ability to set off whenever you wish.

Chartering suits most, especially if you only sail a few weeks a year. Buying makes sense only if you’re ready to commit — in time, money, and passion. Both offer joy, but the wrong decision can sour the dream.

A yacht trip is only as good as the planning. Chart your route, study the weather, pack light but smart. Essentials like sunscreen, good deck shoes, and a sharp multitool matter more than extra luggage.
And remember: yachts demand love. Clean, check, and maintain her and she’ll reward you with safe passages. Neglect her, and she’ll repay you in breakdowns.

The right yacht is out there for everyone, from the humble sailor with a modest sloop to the billionaire in a 300-foot palace. What matters most isn’t the length of your boat but the richness of the experiences she delivers.

Choose wisely, prepare thoroughly, and you’ll discover what every old sea dog knows: that the real treasure isn’t found at the destination, but in the days and nights spent on the water, chasing horizons and making memories with those aboard.

There’s a saying among sailors: the best yacht is the one you use. Whether it’s a 10-foot dinghy or a 100-foot palace, the real value is in the memories it creates. But with so many choices afloat, how do you pick the right boat for you?

From the hum of a twin-diesel motor yacht to the whisper of canvas on a classic sloop, every type of yacht offers a different flavour of freedom. This guide cuts through the marketing gloss to show you what’s out there, how to match boat to budget, and which names at the dock are worth a closer look.
For those who want to point, push the throttles forward, and arrive in time for dinner reservations, motor yachts are the way to go. They’re all about convenience and comfort.
Entry level: Fairline Targa 38 – sleek, quick, and a favourite on the Solent.
Mid-range: Sunseeker Manhattan 52 – big enough for family cruising, small enough for weekend hops.
High-end: Azimut Grande 35 – Italian styling, walk-in wardrobes, and a crew to bring you cocktails.
Motor yachts gulp fuel, but for sheer glamour they remain unbeatable.
There’s nothing like the quiet thrill of a yacht under full sail. For some, the hiss of water along the hull is pure magic.
Entry level: Beneteau Oceanis 34 – perfect for learning and family coastal cruising.
Mid-range: Swan 48 – beautiful lines, bluewater capable, and a real sailor’s boat.
High-end: Oyster 745 – ocean-crossing pedigree with all the comforts of a floating manor.
Sailboats demand patience, but they repay you with poetry on the water.
Twin hulls mean twin benefits: loads of deck space and rock-solid stability. They’re the party platforms of the yacht world.
Entry level: Lagoon 380 – easy to handle, spacious, and ideal for family island-hopping.
Mid-range: Fountaine Pajot Saona 47 – plenty of cabins, perfect for charter income.
High-end: Gunboat 68 – carbon fibre, high performance, and the speed to outrun most monohulls.
Great for families and those who prefer sundowners without the heel.
If you’ve got the budget of a small country, there’s always the mega yacht. These aren’t just boats – they’re floating estates.
Modest by mega standards: Princess X95 – a long-range luxury explorer.
Serious statement: Feadship 70m Joy – helipad, gym, and cinema included.
Ultimate fantasy: Lürssen Dilbar – the world’s largest yacht by volume, with a 25m swimming pool onboard.
They’re not for everyone. But they do prove one thing: at sea, there’s always someone with a bigger boat.
Not everyone needs 12 crew in white polos. Here’s how dreams scale to reality:
Around £30k–£80k: Used Beneteau, Jeanneau, or Bavaria sailing yachts. Perfect for the Channel Islands or Mediterranean cruising.
£150k–£500k: Solid new motor yachts like the Princess V40 or Fairline Squadron. Practical, stylish, and manageable without a huge crew.
£1m–£5m: Luxury catamarans, mid-size Sunseekers, or small Oysters. Proper ocean capability with modern comforts.
£20m+: Superyachts with helipads, personal subs, and the sort of bills that make accountants cry.
For most sailors, charter is king. You avoid the hassle of mooring fees, insurance, and maintenance headaches. Want to cruise Greece one year and the Caribbean the next? Charter.
Buying only makes sense if the sea is your second home. And remember the golden rule: if you ask “how much does it cost to run?” you probably shouldn’t buy.
At the end of the day, the perfect yacht isn’t about the length overall or the brand stamped on the side. It’s about who you bring aboard and where you point her bow.
A young family exploring Devon creeks in a 20-foot day sailer.
A retired couple crossing oceans slowly on an Oyster.
A billionaire dropping anchor off Monaco in time for the Grand Prix.
Each is just as valid, just as rich in memory.

From dinghies to dream yachts, there’s a boat out there for every budget and ambition. Motor yachts offer ease, sailing yachts offer soul, cats offer comfort, and mega yachts… well, they offer bragging rights.

Whatever your choice, remember this: boats are meant to be used, not just polished. So choose the vessel that excites you, set a course, and get out there. Because the true luxury of yachting isn’t the teak deck or the champagne fridge – it’s the freedom to follow the horizon.

title: Sweden Launches Artemis SailGP Team for 2026 Season
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Artemis Racing Returns: Sweden Launches Artemis SailGP Team for 2026 Season
summary: A Swedish Powerhouse Returns to the Global Stage. The world of high-octane professional sailing has just received a seismic jolt. Sweden’s internationally acclaimed Artemis Racing has confirmed its long-anticipated comeback, officially entering the Rolex SailGP Championship 2026 Season as the newly rebranded Artemis SailGP Team.
body: For fans of speed, technology, and pure adrenaline on water, this marks the return of one of sailing’s most respected names. With a reputation forged in America’s Cup campaigns and global circuits, Artemis brings back a mix of experience, innovation, and Swedish competitive spirit that will raise the stakes in SailGP’s record-breaking sixth season.
The new season opens in January 2026 in Perth, Australia, and Artemis will be there, foils humming, ready to prove themselves against the fastest boats and sharpest minds in the sport.
The Leaders at the Helm: Percy and Outteridge Reunited

Guiding Artemis’ return is CEO Iain Percy, double Olympic gold medallist and long-time leader of Artemis Racing. Percy knows better than most how to build a team capable of going toe-to-toe with the very best. His role during Artemis Racing’s America’s Cup campaigns in 2013 and 2017 showcased not only his tactical brilliance but his ability to create a culture of relentless innovation.

Beside him on the water will be Nathan Outteridge, Olympic champion and one of SailGP’s most respected drivers. Outteridge is no stranger to SailGP success, having steered the Japan SailGP Team to multiple wins in Seasons 1 and 2 before lending his expertise across the fleet in interim roles.
Now, reunited with Percy and Artemis’ long-time backer Torbjörn Törnqvist, Outteridge is relishing the chance to bring Swedish sailing back to the cutting edge.

“Reuniting with Iain, Torbjörn and the Artemis team is incredibly exciting. We’ve shared huge moments together in the past, and bringing that experience into SailGP gives us a powerful foundation,” said Outteridge.
Sweden’s Sailing Legacy Meets SailGP’s New Era

Sweden has always punched above its weight in the world of offshore and grand prix racing. From classic offshore campaigns to high-tech foiling catamarans, Swedish sailors are known for grit, precision, and adaptability. With Artemis stepping into the SailGP arena, the nation now has a chance to showcase its talent and engineering expertise on sailing’s fastest stage.

Artemis Racing’s story began in 2007, quickly becoming synonymous with technological progress and competitive excellence. Their America’s Cup campaigns tested designs, data, and teamwork against the toughest in the sport. That DNA carries into SailGP, where speed and innovation define every race.

SailGP itself has transformed sailing since its launch in 2019 by Larry Ellison and Sir Russell Coutts. Built around identical F50 foiling catamarans capable of speeds over 50 knots, SailGP is a travelling global championship staged in iconic venues from Sydney to Saint-Tropez. Unlike traditional yacht racing, SailGP is designed for broadcast drama, fan engagement, and raw, edge-of-the-seat racing.
For Artemis SailGP Team, this is more than just a return. It’s a rebirth in the sport’s most exciting modern arena.
Innovation on Water: What Artemis Brings to SailGP
Artemis has always stood for pushing limits. In SailGP 2026, the team promises to bring:
Cutting-edge data use: Artemis has a history of leveraging simulation and analytics to sharpen race strategy.
Engineering pedigree: Backed by Sweden’s technology ecosystem, expect custom developments in training and performance management.
Talent depth: Outteridge at the helm is a proven winner, while Percy’s leadership ensures a steady hand.
Cultural pride: The return of a Swedish flag to SailGP will ignite local fans and inspire the next generation of sailors.
CEO Percy put it plainly:

“SailGP is redefining sailing with unmatched speed, innovation, and fan engagement. Bringing Sweden into this elite championship is a milestone we’re proud of. We’re determined to compete at the very highest level — pushing boundaries both on and off the water.”
A Growing League: Artemis Becomes SailGP’s 13th Team

By joining as the 13th international team, Artemis completes the 2026 line-up after a fiercely competitive global bid process. SailGP has grown rapidly, with Red Bull Italy and Mubadala Brazil joining in 2025, and high-profile acquisitions reshaping the championship’s landscape.
With Artemis on board, the Rolex SailGP Championship enters its sixth season stronger than ever — a mix of powerhouse teams, new challengers, and fierce rivalries across five continents.
SailGP CEO Russell Coutts welcomed Artemis with enthusiasm:
“We’re thrilled to have Artemis SailGP Team join the Championship. They bring remarkable depth of talent, experience, and professionalism. Expect them to be contenders from their very first race.”
What Fans Can Expect in 2026
The 2026 Rolex SailGP Championship promises more speed, more venues, and more drama. With Artemis back, the narrative gets even richer:
Rivalries reignited: Outteridge vs. the likes of Slingsby, Fletcher, and Burling adds spice to every start line.
New venues: Perth, Geneva, and Abu Dhabi add global variety.
Swedish pride: Expect a wave of yellow-and-blue in every fan zone.
For spectators, Artemis SailGP Team isn’t just another entry. It’s the return of a team with history, vision, and unfinished business.
Conclusion: A New Chapter in a Familiar Story

The return of Artemis Racing as Artemis SailGP Team is a reminder of why sailing captures the imagination: heritage meeting innovation, personalities colliding with technology, and national pride flying on wings of carbon fibre.

As the countdown to Perth 2026 begins, Artemis is not simply back to take part — they’re back to win. With Percy calling the shots and Outteridge driving, Sweden is set to make waves in the world’s fastest sailing league.
And for Old Sea Dogs like us, it’s a reminder that in this sport, legends never stay ashore for long.

title: Diving into RYA's 2026 University Sailing Sustainability Initiative Setting the Course for Green Boating
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Diving into RYA's 2026 University Sailing Sustainability Initiative Setting the Course for Green Boating
summary: The Royal Yachting Association (RYA) spearheads another year of sustainable sailing through its annual university challenge, as voyage towards 2026 commences.
body: In an epoch where the sea whispers of sustainability and the wind beckons towards green horizons, the Royal Yachting Association Green Blue University Sailing Sustainability Challenge stands as a beacon of environmental responsibility. Sponsored by the esteemed Royal Thames Yacht Club, this challenge shores up from the bustling universities of the UK, inspiring students towards eco-friendly sailing practices. Championed by the RYA's Green Blue initiative, the challenge celebrates university sailing environments that ingeniously intertwine day-to-day activities with sustainable measures.

The competition, running until February, gears towards a grand crescendo at the British Universities Sailing Association (BUSA) Championships where the winners will be applauded at a dedicated awards ceremony. Clubs participating in the challenge take up the mantle of sustainability across eight vital domains including water quality enhancement, biodiversity protection, engagement of young sailors, positive change advocacy, and event environmental sustainability.

The RYA Green Blue University Sailing Challenge leaps beyond merely raising environmental awareness and extends its virtuous ripples by empowering sailors with actionable means to preserve their much-loved playground. Thus, sailing clubs are called upon to bolster university sailors in rising to this challenge. The anticipation mounts as the universities set their sails for this significant journey, with hopes high for manifesting meaningful change towards a cleaner and healthier marine environment.

title: Saga of the Sea: The Intriguing Tale of Sanctioned Superyacht Amadea's Recent Sale
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Saga of the Sea: The Intriguing Tale of Sanctioned Superyacht Amadea's Recent Sale
summary: The US Government's sale of the 106-metre Amadea marks a turning point in the legal status of this superyacht.
body: In the world of luxury yachting, few tales echo louder than the intriguing saga of the Amadea, a 106-metre marvel that epitomizes the concept of a floating palace. But behind her sumptuous façade hides a voyage steeped in controversy, one that has now witnessed a pivotal turn with the vessel's sale by the US Government. The journey of the sanctioned superyacht, which boasts alleged links to Russian billionaire Suleiman Kerimov, weaves an intricate web of power, wealth and rarely seen complexity in the realm of maritime law.

Despite the sale, a cloud of legal uncertainty continues to veil the identity of her rightful owner. The backstory of Amadea is marked by a protracted legal battle commencing with the vessel's detainment by Fijian authorities at the behest of the US in May 2022. The vessel eventually found itself seized under asset-forfeiture provisions connected to sanctions on Kerimov, who is accused of concealing asset ownership via convoluted offshore structures. The battle over ownership of the Amadea reached a climax in March 2025, when Judge Dale Ho of the Southern District of New York pushed forward the government's motion to seize the vessel.

However, months following the auction, the battle over ownership of this grand vessel continues with an appeal pending, leaving potential buyers exposed to ongoing claims. Some pundits viewed the auction as politically driven and even labeled it as a 'theft', raising grave questions about due-process rights and the cost to US taxpayers. With legal proceedings still afoot, the saga of the Amadea may yet have chapters unwritten. Once the epitome of luxury at sea, this iconic superyacht now serves as a vivid illustration of the intersections of wealth, power, and the often nebulous pathways of global finance.

title: Luxury Yacht Chanticleer: A Drop in the Ocean at $500k Less
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Luxury Yacht Chanticleer: A Drop in the Ocean at $500k Less
summary: A reduction of half a million dollars has been announced on the magnificent 33-metre motor yacht, the Chanticleer, one of Burger Boat's timeless classics.
body: The motor yacht Chanticleer, a classic piece of nautical artistry from Burger Boat, has seen a significant reduction in its asking price. It is now listed for sale at $500k less, a deal brokered by Dominic Meredith Hardy of Classic Charters. Originally christened Buckpasser, the Chanticleer was commissioned by American stockbroker, philanthropist, and court tennis champion, Ogden Phipps. Delivered in 1973, it was the largest yacht ever built by its American crafters and the first to feature a helipad in the fleet. The yacht's design and naval architecture is a testament to the skill of Jack Hargrave.\ In 1986, the Chanticleer saw a new dawn when it was collected by the legendary singer, actress, and philanthropist, Frances Langford. A fervent yachting enthusiast, Langford modified the boat with a cockpit to cater to her love for fishing. Over the next two decades, the Chanticleer received stringent preventive maintenance and upgrades, embodying 'unwavering attention to detail'.\ Its 2006 makeover was nothing short of spectacular, a multimillion-dollar two-year-long rebuild. The most recent owner, who procured it in 2023, carried out extensive refurbishments to ensure it stands in an 'immaculate' condition today.\ The Chanticleer offers an indulgent experience for eight guests in its four boarding cabins while also accommodating three additional personnel quarters. The opulent ambiance is set by white-painted woods and light-coloured furniture, contrasted with dark mahogany. Paola D. Smith designed her interiors, laced with nautical blues. Multiple lounging areas, alfresco dining space, and a formal dining area nearby highlight the Chanticleer's desire to offer a space of relaxation while at sea. The current asking price? A mere $990,000.

title: A Thrilling Tale of the 46th Rolex Middle Sea Race: Athletic Offshore Adventurers Tackle Historic Voyage
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A Thrilling Tale of the 46th Rolex Middle Sea Race: Athletic Offshore Adventurers Tackle Historic Voyage
summary: The 46th iteration of the prestigious Rolex Middle Sea Race kick-started amid much fanfare, boasting an expansive and diverse fleet of 117 entries from 31 nations.
body: The iconic regatta set off from Valletta, the capital of the enchanting island of Malta, navigating the scenic 606-nautical mile course encompassing Sicily and two live volcanoes. The prestigious Rolex Middle Sea Trophy awaits the overall victor on corrected time. Over the years, a diverse array of yachts and crews has clinched this coveted title with the quickest vessels aiming for line honors. As it stands, the current monohull course record is a rapid-fire 40 hours, 17 minutes, and 50 seconds, set in 2021.

In 2025, the grandest yacht to traverse the ocean blue is the Black Jack 100, a 100-ft Maxi tipped as the front runner for monohull line honors. On the other end of the scale, the smallest yet equally fierce competitor is the 30.93m Farr 30 Calypso, skippered by Sebastian Ripard and Daniel Calascione.

The 5th day of the race brought its fair share of drama. With only 15 yachts securely moored, a staggering 85 out of the remaining 96 still battling the waves vie for the tournament's chief trophy. The Balthasar, who crossed the finish line early Tuesday morning, held a tight grip on the lead. Despite having survived a couple of nail-biting moments, the seasoned crew, led by Louis Balcaen, knows the competition is far from over.

Each new day offers fresh challenges and unpredictable weather patterns, but one thing is certain: these sailors won’t give up the chase until it becomes mathematically impossible to clinch the top spot.

title: The Lavish 37m Horizon Motor Yacht, Miss Michelle, Unveils an Astounding $1MPrice Dip
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Lavish 37m Horizon Motor Yacht, Miss Michelle, Unveils an Astounding $1MPrice Dip
summary: Luxury yacht Miss Michelle, a revelation in the 2025 Horizon fleet, has significantly reduced its price by a whopping $1M.
body: Steeped in luxury and designed for the high seas, Miss Michelle, the renowned 37.2-meter Horizon motor yacht made its majestic debut in 2025. A true gem of the expansive Horizon fleet, this beauty first graced the ocean tides in August 2024 as a shining addition to the yard's RP110 line-up. With an innovative design and a promise of luxury, she was eagerly awaited by boat enthusiasts worldwide. Now, with an incredible $1,000,000 price drop, this floating epitome of lavishness has become an even more irresistible proposition. Crafted with a meticulous touch and exceptional technology, Miss Michelle marvellously encapsulates all the charms of long-range cruising comfort. Its much-awaited markdown also succeeds in making the scale of its grandeur a touch more accessible. Chiseled and polished to dazzle, this remarkable yacht boasts a level of customization on par with much larger vessels, truly encapsulating the sophistication of a 'mega yacht'. The use of Horizon’s renowned SCRIMP™ resin-infusion technology is a testament to the model's innovation and quality and fills every inch of the vessel with progressive flair and performance efficiency. 'Miss Michelle' hosts an amalgamation of expertise from various industry leaders. The stately vessel is a product of Espinosa Yacht Design's intuitive engineering, fused with the striking naval architecture developed by Donald L. Blount. Graciously accepting eight guests in four opulent cabins, Miss Michelle does not compromise on space or luxury. Notably, it features two stylish master cabins: one is a sprawling full-beam king suite located on the main deck complete with a skylight, walk-in closet, pop-up coffee bar and rain shower. A second full-beam master-style cabin on the lower deck promises indulgence with a comfy seating area, vanity and outsized en suite. The interior design of Miss Michelle is a dreamy collaboration between Horizon's talented in-house team and the owners’ personally handpicked stylists. The overall vibe exudes calm luxury, from the big L-shape sofa, concealed wet bar to the articulated 75” LED TV that folds away seamlessly when not in use. Among the highlights is the customised ceiling treatment and a magnificent formal dining area with a capacity of seating ten. Nevertheless, the star of the yacht’s interior is the flybridge, a versatile zone to entertain guests. With features such as light-up bar, grill, alfresco dining for eight and a retractable projector screen, it effortlessly captures the spirit of luxury seafaring.

title: Dynamic Sails and Tense Waters as the 46th Rolex Middle Sea Race Thrills, Showcasing Elite Yachting Talent
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Dynamic Sails and Tense Waters as the 46th Rolex Middle Sea Race Thrills, Showcasing Elite Yachting Talent
summary: The 46th edition of the revered Rolex Middle Sea Race has set sail from Malta's capital, Valletta, drawing together a diverse fleet of international sailing craft.
body: The 46th edition of the Rolex Middle Sea Race commenced earlier today from the Maltese capital Valletta. This prestigious offshore racing event welcomes an impressive and diverse fleet—117 entrants from 31 nations this year—to compete in a challenging and scenic 606-nautical mile course around Sicily and two active volcanoes. The prize, the Rolex Middle Sea Race Trophy, is awarded to the overall winner on corrected time, recognising a diverse range of yachts and crews. The fastest boats aim for line honours, with the current monohull course record standing at a frugal 40 hours, 17 minutes, and 50 seconds set back in 2021.

The 2025 event sees the sleek 100-ft Maxi Black Jack 100 as the largest yacht competing, favourite to take monohull line honours, contrasting against the smallest, the 30.93m Farr 30 Calypso captained by Sebastian Ripard and Daniel Calascione. Founded in 1968 and organized by the Royal Malta Yacht Club, this epic 600-nautical mile offshore contest has received unwavering support from Rolex since 2002. The competition, far from reaching a halt, finds the crews with daggers drawn as they sail through the vast expanses of the Mediterranean Sea.

A few days into the contest, with only 15 yachts home and hosed, it is clear that the race is still wide open. Many participants are giving their all to clinch the first position and seize the sturdy symbol of maritime glory. As the clock ticks, the mathematic probability of emerging victorious phases out some competitors, but the unfading spirit of sportsmanship keeps the regatta as vibrant as ever until the very end.

title: Relive the Excitement of Sydney-Auckland and Ready Up for the 80th Rolex Sydney-Hobart Yacht Race
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Relive the Excitement of Sydney-Auckland and Ready Up for the 80th Rolex Sydney-Hobart Yacht Race
summary: Experience the thrill of ocean racing as we take you through the oaths of the Sydney to Auckland ocean race, followed by a peek into the upcoming Rolex Sydney-Hobart Yacht Race.
body: The ocean has always held a magnetic allure for the adventurous, swathing them in aquatic enchantments in return for braving its intimidating vastness. This tangible manifestation of the contest between mankind's adventurous spirit and Mother Nature's unpredictable temper engenders events like the Sydney to Auckland Ocean Race.

As the race concluded with an official presentation ceremony, two yachts remained at sea, resolute in their pursuit of the finish line and etching memories an onlooker can only imagine. The stalwarts, Wings and Cooloola, despite their torpid progress due to the lack of favourable winds, found joy in the companionship of oceanic fauna, bringing life to their challenge with dolphins and seals frolicking by their struggling yachts. Inspirational stories of their crew's resilience served as reminders of the sense of achievement inherent in completing the race.

This race brings back the previous winners along with new hopes, fostering intense competition among the participants. This year’s race has attracted an impressive fleet, all set to ride the waves over a 628-nautical mile journey. The lineup showcases a diverse mix of participants, featuring world class yachts and celebrated sailors from Germany, Hong Kong, the Netherlands, USA, New Caledonia, New Zealand, and Poland.

Through these races, sailors not only quench their thirst for adventure but also exhibit an admirable degree of resilience, strategic planning, and, most importantly, a steadfast spirit. It is these qualities that transform mere races into a celebration of human and maritime spirit, setting pulses racing on and off the waters.

title: Ocean Racing Explorer's Diary: Magical Experiences and a Clash of Titans in the Sydney to Auckland Race 2025
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Ocean Racing Explorer's Diary: Magical Experiences and a Clash of Titans in the Sydney to Auckland Race 2025
summary: As the Sydney to Auckland Ocean Race 2025 unfolds, participants encounter thrilling highlights, magical experiences, and intense rivalries - the elements of a true sea spectacle.
body: Witnessing the thrilling showdown in the Sydney to Auckland Ocean Race, two yachts remained adrift at sea, gracefully braving unpredictable weather patterns while the official awards ceremony proceeded at the race co-host, Royal Akarana Yacht Club (RAYC). Providing an element of suspense in the proceedings was the withholding of the next race's date until the announcement by illustrious Royal Prince Alfred Yacht Club (RPAYC) Commodore, Rob McClelland. In a moment that sent ripples of anticipation through the crowd, McClelland revealed, 'I'm delighted to confirm that the next Sydney to Auckland Ocean Race will start on October 10, 2027.' Meanwhile, the triumphant trio of Lucky, Frantic, and Antipodes, helmed by acclaimed skippers Bryon Ehrhart, Michael Martin, and Geoff Hill respectively, emerged victorious, lighting up the joyous atmosphere with their hearty celebrations. The yacht, Wings, and its competitor Cooloola, persevered in the expansive aqua arena with unwavering determination and robust skill, bearing testament to the race's spirit. A testament to the unpredictable dynamics of ocean sailing, Wings and Cooloola's endeared themselves as crowd favourites. Their tireless pursuit of the finish line, despite the yachts' challenging predicament and being marooned at sea, made the crowd's thunderous applause upon their arrival an unforgettable moment. The experiences narrated by the participants provided a unique perspective into the race. They spoke of encounters with playful seals and dancing dolphins who kept them company in the vast expanse, thus highlighting the race's enchanting allure. However, the defining moment for competitors on Cooloola was not a sprint to the finish line, but a magnificent encounter with a fin whale and her calf. As the journey's thrill continues, the anticipation for the 2027 event is growing, promising another unforgettable high-seas adventure in the arena of world-class yacht racing.

title: Minor Errors, Major Implications: Lessons from Superyacht Antenna Mislabeling Revealed in CHIRP Maritime Report
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Minor Errors, Major Implications: Lessons from Superyacht Antenna Mislabeling Revealed in CHIRP Maritime Report
summary: A revealing case study from CHIRP Maritime shines light on how minor errors in documentation can significantly impact the functionality and safety of superyachts.
body: Grappling with the unknown is a constant challenge for the maritime industry. The most unexpected things might go wrong, often highlighting long-overlooked areas requiring immediate attention. A case study from CHIRP Maritime’s Superyacht Feedback throws light on one such incident where something as elementary as incorrect labelling of antennas resulted in a potential crisis.

The GPS 1 and GPS 2 antennas were wrongly marked on both the bridge plan and the compass deck in the study’s specific case. Such incorrect markings could lead to costly errors, especially if technical issues arise and the crew attempts to resolve them based on the inaccurate plan. While the antennas were installed correctly, mismatches between their actual locations and the schematics posed a substantial risk.

Lessons from this incident underline the paramount importance of clear, accurate documentation and labelling. Any ambiguity can impede the correction of technical defects, potentially leading to significant onboard delays or even serious accidents. Imagine an erroneous location of a vital antenna leading your 60-metre yacht astray away from its navigable channel!

The takeaways from this event run deeper, spotlighting the crucial need for rigorous checks of new equipment installed during the vessel’s new build phase or at dry dock. Teams should ensure that all equipment locations are accurately marked and that the documentation is updated accordingly. The vessel’s management should also ensure that such practices extend to routine maintenance works and are not just limited to the installation phase.

In conclusion, this incident serves as a sobering reminder of the importance of stringent checks and cross-verification, alongside fostering effective collaboration across various departments on a vessel. These seemingly minor aspects of operational management can play a critical role in averting uncalculated risks and ensuring the smooth sailing of your prized superyacht.

title: Boys & Girls Clubs' Spectacular Yacht Event Features Grammy Nominee & BOAT International Sponsorship
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Boys & Girls Clubs' Spectacular Yacht Event Features Grammy Nominee & BOAT International Sponsorship
summary: BOAT International announces its media sponsorship for one of the biggest charity events in yachting: The 36th Annual Boys & Girls Clubs Yacht Rendezvous.
body: Charitable causes and the world of yachting may seem poles apart. However, BOAT International has brilliantly bridged the gap by announcing its media sponsorship for the 36th Annual Boys & Girls Clubs Yacht Rendezvous, a beneficial event in Fort Lauderdale. This annual convergence of generosity and glamour has been the epicentre of philanthropy in yachting for the better part of 37 years.

This year, the event is poised to sail into uncharted gusts of philanthropic success. With a lineup of yachts spanning 16.8 metres to a staggering 50 metres set to dock for the event, guests have much to anticipate. The Rendezvous will unfurl over two evenings of glamour and generosity, marked by a gala dinner and the traditional yacht hop.

Mike Busacca, COO of Fraser Yachts US, and event co-chair for 26 years said that this year's event will be 'the biggest yet'. Joining him in overseeing the event are his wife, Jessica, and philanthropist, Carla Taylor. The organizers expect a myriad of eminent international yacht builders and a significant line-up of sponsorships.

Apart from being a beacon of generosity, the Rendezvous will be honouring a legend of its own. Felix Sabates, a long-time supporter of the clubs and their mission, known for his illustrious career as a NASCAR and IndyCar team owner, will be recognized for his contributions.

But the event won't be all dockside talks, business, and big-hearted contributions. Enjoyment will be at full sail, particularly during Saturday night’s black-tie gala - a breath-taking concord of philanthropy and fine entertainment. On deck as headliner is five-time Grammy nominee, Robin Thicke, promising an unforgettable evening.

This rendezvous, the charity event of the year, not only fuels the love of yachting but also champions thousands of underprivileged children in the Broward County. Its impact extends beyond a glamorous night under the stars, ultimately offering these kids guidance, academic support, and security - crafting a more promising, resilient future, one sail at a time.
