title: Unleashing the Azimut 82 Fly: The Flagship Yacht that Embodies Innovative Design and Luxurious Comfort
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unleashing the Azimut 82 Fly: The Flagship Yacht that Embodies Innovative Design and Luxurious Comfort
summary: Let's raise the anchor and embark on a tour of the Azimut 82 Fly, the crowning gem of the rejuvenated Flybridge collection, guaranteeing an elegant amalgamation of boundary-pushing fittings with an opulently extravagant interior.
body: Commencing our voyage with the Azimut 82 Fly, this delightfully impressive addition to the shipyard's portfolio reaffirms their eminence in sculpting the most fashionable flybridge yachts. The brainchildren behind this masterpiece are Alberto Mancini, the exterior designer, and Fabio Fantalini, the interior designer, whose combined efforts have given rise to the epitome of avant-garde design and luxury.

Adorned with an exceptional semi-vertical bow, a striking feature pioneered by Azimut, the 82 Fly ensures pristine performance by ejecting water out efficiently. Complimenting the striking beauty of the hull are spacious, staggered windows bringing an abundance of natural light to the lower decks.

Devoted to leisure and recreation, the exterior spaces do not shy away from providing ultimate enjoyment. The cockpit gets a functional edge from the 'Deck-to-Deck' extension and incorporates seating arrangements that ensure a panoramic view for all on board. An inventive, integrated wet bar covertly harbours an auxiliary helm station under a teak cover.

The interior reflects a balanced blend of texture and contours mesmerisingly illuminated by the clever use of lighting. The main saloon's glass doors recede almost entirely into the deck, creating an uninterrupted flow from the cockpit. In a rare fusion of aesthetics with functionality, there is a hidden day-head tucked precisely between the saloon and the helm station.

The main helm, adorned with a sleek, three-screen Garmin setup, offers comfort with modifiable electronic seats and direct side deck access. Co-located with the helm is the excellently finished galley decked out with custom storage solution, adding an exclusive access to the crew quarters situated unusually at the yacht's front.

The Azimut 82 Fly is splendidly equipped with Azimut's proprietary 'Watch System.' This groundbreaking feature, powered by Artificial Intelligence, intelligently integrates AIS, depth sounder, GPS, charting, and a sophisticated radar system. This intuitive system processes all received data to ascertain immediate hazards and alerts the captain using clean, voice-activated announcements.

All in all, with the Azimut 82 Fly, the lovers of the sea are in for a luxurious treat wrapped in the elegance of Italian design, the efficiency of innovative technology, and the comfort of a truly world-class interior.

title: Exploring the Used Beneteau GT46: Is it the Wise Choice for a Family-ready Sports Cruiser?
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Exploring the Used Beneteau GT46: Is it the Wise Choice for a Family-ready Sports Cruiser?
summary: Nestled in the hotly contested 45-50ft sportscruiser market, the pre-owned Beneteau GT46 stands its ground as a family-friendly, middle-sized cruising boat. It brilliantly combines performance, styling, and comfort, offering excellent value for money.
body: In the world of motor boating, the 45-50ft sportscruiser sector offers intense competition, much to the delight of secondhand boat seekers in search of quality. From high-end models like the Sunseeker Portofino 47, Princess V48 and Fairline 47 GT to more modestly equipped vessels, there is an array of choices for those serious about a speedy and comfortable voyage on a mid-size cruising boat. Among these options stands a worthy contender – the Beneteau GT46. Compared to its rivals, such as Bavaria's Sport S45 and Jeanneau's Leader 46, the GT46 holds its own impressively with its combo of performance, style, comfort, and family-friendliness. Tax paid, the GT46 is available for around £324,950, quite in line with comparable Bavaria and Jeanneau models. A Princess V48 of identical age could easily incur a cost in excess of half a million – establishing GT46's distinct value proposition. Moreover, its modern and fresh design boasts a sporty profile with fascinating curves and angles, covered all year round by a vital hardtop. As part of Groupe Beneteau, the world's most significant leisure boat manufacturer dating back to 1884, the GT46 ensures a reliable build. Akin to other Beneteau products, an area of saving is the fixtures and fittings. For instance, the twin bi-fold doors separating the wheelhouse and cockpit don't take a straightforward line from one end to another. Instead, they follow an intricate path, both straight and curved. The resulting seal forms three sides of a hexagon projecting into the aft deck, a unique design that while practical, may require familiarisation. Notably, these doors accommodate the quirky extensions joining the saloon dining table's seats that can either face the table or extend the seats. One standout feature is the aft cockpit's reclining chairs. A touch of a button allows these to recline just like a dentist chair till they form a flat sunbathing area – a truly unique and enjoyable feature that kids are sure to love. Additionally, the ability to fold the saloon dining table in half, creating a passageway through the main deck, adds to the Beneteau GT46's versatility.

title: Biotherm Crowned in Boka Bay
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Biotherm Crowned in Boka Bay: A Dominant Finale to The Ocean Race Europe 2025
imageCredit: © © Lloyd Images / The Ocean Race Europe 2025
summary: The Boka Bay Coastal Race, sailed against the dramatic backdrop of Montenegro’s mountains and calm turquoise waters, was the perfect finale to this summer’s edition of The Ocean Race Europe 2025. It had everything: close-quarters duels, tactical brilliance, and one last show of dominance from Paul Meilhat’s Biotherm, who sealed overall victory with yet another flawless performance.
body: As they had done so many times over the six weeks of racing, Biotherm rose above the chaos to secure the win, confirming themselves as the benchmark of this year’s European tour. Paprec Arkéa crossed second to lock up runner-up overall, while Team Holcim-PRB, led by Rosalin Kuiper, completed both the day’s podium and the season’s top three.

Behind them, the fight raged on. Team Malizia edged out Allagrande Mapei Racing for fourth overall, thanks in part to a standout coastal performance from Canada Ocean Racing – Be Water Positive, who stunned many with a gritty fifth-place finish in Boka Bay.

The stage could not have been more spectacular. Boka Bay, a fjord-like harbour framed by steep cliffs and dotted with centuries-old stone towns, delivered a postcard-perfect setting for the finale. Seven IMOCA yachts lined up under blue skies and slightly stronger-than-forecast winds — around 10 knots — for the last dance of The Ocean Race Europe.

The atmosphere ashore was electric. Locals and visiting fans packed the waterfront as the fleet weaved tight mark roundings, foils slicing the water with precision. From the first moment, it was clear this would be no gentle parade.

At the gun, Yoann Richomme’s Paprec Arkéa made the most aggressive move, seizing control at the opening marks. With Mariana Lobato working the bow and the team drilling crisp manoeuvres, the French crew looked sharp and confident. For a moment, it seemed they might snatch both the coastal race win and second overall.

Behind them, Holcim-PRB faltered with an early messy manoeuvre, giving Biotherm space to stalk the leaders. Further back, Allagrande Mapei Racing and Team Malizia were locked in their own duel, every sail change critical in the marginal conditions.

The turning point came on the second lap. Biotherm, cool under pressure, closed in on Paprec Arkéa and pulled an audacious inside move at the mark. With the precision of a champion team, Meilhat’s crew seized the lead and never looked back.

Onboard, the celebration was visible as they powered toward the finish. Paul Meilhat, Amélie Grassi, Benjamin Ferré, and Carlos Manera embraced as they crossed the line — fists pumping, victory sealed. Four wins out of five legs, four scoring gates taken, and now the final flourish in Montenegro. Their points haul (55) crowned them undisputed champions of The Ocean Race Europe.

“We’re so happy,” grinned Meilhat. “For two months we’ve lived together with this goal in mind. To finish like this, with another win, it’s pure happiness. Every race, every leg, this team has been incredible.”
Paprec Arkéa and Holcim-PRB Round the Podium

Seconds later, Paprec Arkéa crossed in relief and satisfaction. Their consistency all season was rewarded with second place overall (40 points). “That was a really great race,” said skipper Yoann Richomme. “We didn’t expect such a strong start, but the foils worked beautifully. To finish behind Biotherm – that’s no shame at all. They’ve been almost impolite in their dominance!”
Crewmate Corentin Horeau added: “From the start we knew Holcim would be close, so we had to stay sharp. We executed cleanly and stuck to our game plan.”

For Rosalin Kuiper and Team Holcim-PRB, the third-place finish overall (38.5 points) capped a rollercoaster campaign that began with a damaging collision in Kiel. “Of course, we wanted more,” Kuiper admitted. “But looking back, I’m so proud of how far this team has come. We fought for every point, and we learned so much.”
Team Malizia, led by Boris Herrmann, finished fourth overall with 37 points — edging out Allagrande Mapei Racing, who had to settle for fifth (26 points).

But the story of the day belonged to Canada Ocean Racing – Be Water Positive. Scott Shawyer’s team delivered a gutsy fifth-place finish in Boka Bay, punching above their weight in a fleet stacked with IMOCA heavyweights. Their performance pushed Mapei down the order and earned respect across the dock.
At the tail end, Team Amaala crossed seventh, their campaign full of valuable lessons despite modest results.

As the sun dipped behind the Montenegrin hills, every sailor in the fleet could reflect on a campaign of fierce competition, new rivalries, and unforgettable moments. From Kiel to Nice, from Sardinia to Montenegro, The Ocean Race Europe once again proved itself one of offshore sailing’s most dynamic battlegrounds.

But the story doesn’t end here. The next chapter arrives in 2026 with The Ocean Race Atlantic — a transatlantic sprint like no other, connecting New York to Barcelona. A fresh challenge awaits, with the same promise: spectacular racing, dramatic stories, and the world’s fastest ocean-going yachts pushing human limits.

title: From Sailing Champions to Conservation Crusaders: Unveiling the Success Story of NZ's Hauraki Gulf Marine Protection
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: From Sailing Champions to Conservation Crusaders: Unveiling the Success Story of NZ's Hauraki Gulf Marine Protection
summary: Champion sailors, Peter Burling and Blair Tuke, brand NZ's Hauraki Gulf Marine Protection Bill's passage into law a momentous victory for marine conservation.
body: Peter Burling and Blair Tuke, both unrivalled sailors and co-founders of Live Ocean, salute the passage of the NZ's Hauraki Gulf Marine Protection Bill as a massive stride forward for the Gulf. This achievement has been central in the mission of these three-time America's Cup victors, multiple Olympic medallists, and distinguished SailGP sailors, who initiated the Live Ocean marine conservation entity half a decade ago. Since its establishment, Live Ocean has commendably infused $3.5 million to endorse 17 Marine conservation missions.

The Hauraki Gulf, celebrated for its richness in biodiversity, has always been under Live Ocean's spotlight. The spirited duo expresses their enthusiasm as this long-anticipated Bill will offer enhanced safeguarding to this treasured area. Blair Tuke, one half of the founding duo, commends the immense effort invoked by various community groups and individuals to realise this monumental achievement.

Live Ocean's commitment towards raising ecological consciousness is evident in their engaging initiatives such as 'Swim4TheGulf' in 2023. This event saw open-water swimmer Jono Ridler swimming non-stop for 33 hours, drawing attention to the declining health of the Gulf. In June of this year, Live Ocean united with the Black Foils, New Zealand SailGP team, on 'Foil4TheGulf', the country’s largest foiling event, urging the delayed Bill to advance.

The organisation also partners with scientists operating in the Gulf studying kelp forest restoration, innovators working on the Caulerpa response, and researchers striving to understand the unique population of oceanic manta. Live Ocean's proactive measures — informed by science, innovation, and outreach — ensure the future where the ocean teems with health and life. Hannah Prior, the Impact Director of Live Ocean, believes that this significant moment gives the Gulf its much-needed opportunity to restore the marine life that once flourished abundantly.

title: Revolution in Superyacht Ownership: How a Legal Ruling Reshaped the Landscape of Tax and Governance
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Revolution in Superyacht Ownership: How a Legal Ruling Reshaped the Landscape of Tax and Governance
summary: A fundamental shift in superyacht ownership is underway, the catalyst being a pivotal legal ruling by Germany's Federal Fiscal Court on tax and governance.
body: The winds of legislative change are billowing the sails of superyacht ownership. The epicentre of this revolution? A game-changing ruling from Germany's Federal Fiscal Court on tax and governance.

For years, yacht owners and their legal advisors have strived to construct robust yacht-holding structures in a complex and often cloudy legal landscape. However, the spring of 2025 brought new currents of clarity to assist superyacht owners in their navigation. The Court's landmark decision expands the protections and benefits of family foundations beyond EU's borders and validates them as legitimate channels for superyacht ownership. This ruling not only establishes a sturdier legal framework but also sharpens the requirements necessary to demonstrate genuine separation of ownership and control.

However, a clear understanding of VAT realities is crucial. Relief under Temporary Admission (TA), a scheme for non-EU yachts cruising the EU, hinges on the yacht being owned/used by persons living outside the EU customs territory. While welcoming, TA doesn't provide a free pass for EU-resident owners seeking private usage - the path to compliance demands import and VAT.

The veritable sea-change in tax and governance not only lessens uncertainties around tax laws but also aligns with Controlled Foreign Company regulations for operating incomes or passive cash flows. As superyacht owners adapt to the fresh breeze of transparency ushered in by this legal ruling, the future holds clearer waters and straighter sailing in the realm of superyacht ownership.

imageAlt: Custom Line Introduces Saetta: A Fresh Identity for Planing Line with Sporty Designs and Advanced Features
summary: Custom Line rebrands its planing line as Saetta, featuring sporty, fast-paced designs and state-of-the-art features, and debuts its 39.8-metre tri-deck yacht.
body: The Ferretti Group brand, Custom Line, recently took the stage at the Monaco Yacht Show to announce an exciting revamp. Their planing line now dons a fresh, invigorating identity - Saetta. The Italian term Saetta translates to 'arrow' or 'dart', aptly capturing the line’s sporty nature.

The makeover was not just limited to the name. Alongside the much-anticipated rebranding, the Italian yacht-makers showcased the newest addition to the series, the Saetta 128’. This stunning, 39.8-metre tri-deck yacht finds itself in impressive company, joining the already existing 106’, 120’ and 140’ models.

The reimagined Saetta line doesn't only score on looks and length. The chief commercial officer of Ferretti Group, Giordano Pellacani, revealed that the rebranding underscores their commitment to inject sizeable investments and innovative ideas to their offering.

The yacht further impresses with its 25 square metre foredeck, complete with a flexible seating area and a Jacuzzi. An extensive use of glazing on both decks ensures that the interiors are bathed in beautiful natural light. Five cabins, including a main deck owner’s suite with a walk-around bed, ensure comfort, complemented by the addition of four crew cabins.

Underneath its captivating exterior and luxurious interiors, the Saetta 128’ holds its own in the performance department. With a beam of 7.7 metres, a draught of 2.1 metres, it boasts a cruising speed of 19 knots, a top speed of 22 knots and a range of 1,000 nautical miles.

Even as Custom Line takes a bow for the Saetta 128’, the yacht-makers are far from done. BOATPro has announced that Custom Line has five more Saetta models on order, continuing to ride the wave of innovation and bring fresh options for yachting enthusiasts.

title: Get a First Glimpse of the Revitalized Naval Ship JeMaSa: An Over-the-top Luxury Charter with a Rich Naval Legacy
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Get a First Glimpse of the Revitalized Naval Ship JeMaSa: An Over-the-top Luxury Charter with a Rich Naval Legacy
summary: Dive into the heart of the revamped 52m luxury explorer yacht JeMaSa, rebirthed from a naval vessel into an awe-inspiring charter yacht.
body: The renowned brokerage firm Y.CO has ignited excitement in the yachting world, offering a detailed insight into the new face of the 52m luxury explorer yacht JeMaSa, formerly known as Plan B. The former naval ship has undergone a transformative metamorphosis, shedding its military sphere to don an opulent guise, boasting a magnificently refurbished interior, resplendent exterior, and high-end technical upgrades.

The pivotal focal point of JeMaSa's reinvigoration, a painstaking year-long project conducted at Gold Coast City Marina & Shipyard (GCCM) in Australia, included a complete redesign of the interior and exterior, along with extensive engineering work. This magnificent transformation extended to the addition of a modern swim platform, propelling the yacht's length overall from 49.9m to an impressive 52m.

Originally constructed as an Australian naval ship in 1973, JeMaSa has a steel hull and a steel superstructure, a vast beam of 10 metres, a draught of 3.2 metres and an expansive volume of 746GT. Misha Merzliakov was chosen to redesign both the interior and exterior, while Shaun Phelps of Periscope assumed responsibility for naval architecture.

The endeavour of transforming the battlescarred naval vessel into a five-star global cruising motor yacht involved extensive work. 'The project involved stripping the vessel back to bare metal, followed by a comprehensive redesign,' elaborated refit manager Juan Koegelenberg. The refit also included fresh upholstery, innovative wall and ceiling panels, custom beds, bespoke furniture, and marble-top bathrooms, breathing new life into the vessel.

With the all-new De Villiers-designed exterior featuring a subtle military-influenced profile nestled under the brilliance of a radiant white superstructure and a light-grey hull, JeMaSa's allure is hard to resist. Moreover, ample natural light filters through large-sized glazed windows, courtesy of Integ Marine Windows, enhancing the plush interiors with mesmerizing panoramic views.

Andrew Chapman, GCCM’s COO, expressed pride in collaborating again with Juan and his specialized companies, underscoring the immense experience they bring to the table in transforming capacious vessels.

JeMaSa's revamped interiors now radiate a modern, light aesthetic, incorporating organic materials. The luxury yacht also boasts seven adaptable cabins, two of which can be converted between twin and king configurations. In addition, a cinema room, sauna, and games room amplify the grandeur of the ship, promising enhanced experiences for guests onboard. This astonishing transformation underscores the tremendous potential hidden within aged naval vessels, waiting to be discovered, liberated, and converted into luxury haven on the seas.

title: Offshore Double Handed World Championships 2025: France Excels, as Young Talent and Nations Across Continents Battle it Out
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Offshore Double Handed World Championships 2025: France Excels, as Young Talent and Nations Across Continents Battle it Out
summary: At the enthralling Offshore Double Handed World Championships 2025 finale, France emerges victorious, showcasing the allure of offshore sailing.
body: With an electrifying atmosphere, the 2025 Offshore Double Handed World Championships reached its intriguing conclusion at Cowes. Organised by The Royal Ocean Racing Club in collaboration with Cap-Regatta and supported by LGL and Jeanneau, the tournament showcased the captivating sport of offshore sailing, attracting 21 teams, and displaying the prowess of 11 crews from four continents.

In the limelight stood France's Théa Khelif and Thomas André. In a masterful display of understanding the light and tactical conditions, the duo rode the shifting winds to become the crowned World Champions. GB's Willow Bland and Zeb Fellows, with Fellows being the youngest sailor at a tender age of 18, took up the thrilling runner-up spot. The third place was adorned by Domi Knuppel and Federico Waksman from Uruguay, marking it as Uruguay's debut podium finish on such a grand scale.
The championship, showcasing a broad spectrum of talents ranging from Olympians to offshore veterans and youth sailors, marked a new chapter in global competitive sailing.

title: Set Sail with Ensign Yachts! Dive into Exciting News, Astounding Reviews, and Amazing Picks

Hosted at the prestigious Royal Prince Alfred Yacht Club in Newport, this year's expo promises to be a happening marine extravaganza for all sailing enthusiasts, with Ensign unveiling their majestic J/Boats J/99, commanding Bavaria C46, and the elegantly graceful Tofinou 9.7.

At Ensign Yachts, luxury meets affordability. The award-winning Bavaria C46 now comes with an eyebrow-raising price reduction of over half a million dollars! This is an opportunity that no sailing enthusiast can allow to slip away. Furthermore, Ensign is proud to introduce a wide array of previously cherished yachts, all ready to embark on fresh adventures on the seas. Among them are the impeccable 2008 Amel 54, the powerful 2024 Tesoro T40, and the 2022 Bavaria SR41, the crowned Motorboat of the Year.

For those seeking to escape the cool Australian winter for the warm, inviting Mediterranean, Ensign Yachts has exclusive last-minute deals with discounts rocketing up to an impressive 50%. This provides the perfect opportunity to charter a yacht and immerse yourself in the Mediterranean's warm embrace.

Proudly partnered with award-winning brands, Ensign Yachts' dealer collection includes the likes of J/Boats J/40, the highly coveted European Yacht of the Year & Cruising World Boat of the Year 2025, Nautitech 44 Open, the glorious European Yacht of the Year & Best Boats Award winner of 2023, and Bavaria C46, another titanic figure in the European Yacht of the Year rosters.

The boating parade continues with the newly unveiled J/Boats J/36. Packed with a cruiser's style and comfort, it boasts the race-winning performance of the J/112E. At Ensign Yachts, they eagerly look forward to seeing the new J/36 perform both on racecourses and during leisurely cruises.
So, with all these fantastic offerings onboard, Ensign Yachts invites you to step aboard and sail into your next adventure.

title: Living the High Sea Life: Admiral's 48-Metre Althea is Now Up For Grabs
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Living the High Sea Life: Admiral's 48-Metre Althea is Now Up For Grabs
summary: Admiral's esteemed 48-metre motor yacht, Althea, is now listed for sale, boasting state-of-the-art features, extraordinary design and a wealth of luxuries.
body: In the world of luxury sea voyages, it doesn't get much better than the Althea, a 48-metre motor yacht by the iconic Admiral brand. Offering both style and substance, Althea has now been listed for purchase, making it a truly unique opportunity for aficionados of the sea.

Althea, delivered in 2021, is the largest yacht within The Italian Sea Group's acclaimed Atos 47 series. The superyacht is special for its exterior aesthetics, characterized by a sky-blue hull and defined architectural lines, work of the celebrated designer, Gian Marco Campanino.

In impeccable turnkey condition, the RINA-classed Althea recently went through an intensive refit under the care of Monaco Marine. Under warranty, her engines remain fully in class, adding to her potential as a worthwhile investment.

Floor-to-ceiling windows usher in a feeling of airiness and brightness to the living areas, which are adorned with high-quality materials like tropical ebony wood, statuario marble, and smooth alcantara. Althea has been astutely designed with separate spaces and routes for crew and guests, enhancing privacy while creating a natural flow within the yacht.

Neatly nestled under the elusive €30,000,000 line, Althea, lying in Golfe Juan, France, could well be considered a snip at €29,500,000, VAT paid, for the discerning buyer seeking unparalleled sea craftsmanship.

A shining gem among yachts of her class, Althea also offers lounge areas spread across her three decks, a 100-square-metre sundeck featuring a dry bar, and built-in television screens among its many luxuries. The yachts multiple communal spaces, including a spacious beach platform and a magnificent al fresco dining area, make socialising easy and enjoyable.
Althea is capable of touching a brisk maximum speed of 19 knots, thanks to her twin CAT C32 ACERT engines. Despite her speedy potential, the yacht maintains a comfortable cruising speed of 12 knots.
In sum, Althea is a symphony of design, comfort, and performance, a truly impressive superyacht that is as much about making a statement as it is about enjoying the pleasures of high oceanic living.

title: Renowned 43m ISA Motor Yacht Queen Alla Embraces a €1.5M Price Drop and Reflects a Change of Currency
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Renowned 43m ISA Motor Yacht Queen Alla Embraces a €1.5M Price Drop and Reflects a Change of Currency
summary: The unmistakable 43m motor yacht, Queen Alla, now listed for €13,000,000, has witnessed a significant price reduction and a shift in currency.
body: If striking yacht profiles and unparalleled luxury float your boat, ponder upon the Queen Alla. The 43m ISA motor yacht, notable for her vibrant, all-blue profile, has had a price reduction of circa €1.5M. More significantly, her exchange currency has also altered to Euros, with the yacht now listed for a tantalizing €13,000,000 for sale.

Constructed in steel and aluminium by the respected Italian yard, Andrea Vallicelli took charge of her design. More than just a pretty profile, the Queen Alla exudes a distinctive aura over the waves, making her an unforgettable marine presence. In 2019, she underwent a comprehensive overhaul prior to her appearance in the market in 2023.

Where luxury touches are concerned, Queen Alla does not disappoint. Swarovski crystal accents and contemporary design elements enhance her aesthetic charm. Gold tables and patterned leather seating grace the main saloon. The living space profits from generously sized panoramic windows, letting copious amounts of natural light flood in.

Befitting for a yacht of her caliber, Queen Alla has been used successfully as a charter yacht and has been meticulously maintained. For those perfect sunny days, her sundeck provides a Jacuzzi, bar, barbecue, al fresco dining options, and sunpads.

In terms of performance, Queen Alla is driven by two powerful 1320hp Caterpillar diesel engines. These allow for a top cruising speed of 16 knots and a maximum range of 3,100 nautical miles at a comfortable cruise of 12 knots. For added stability at anchor, she is equipped with zero-speed stabilisers. Her specs boast an impressive 8.6-metre beam and a 2.5m draft.

Now the Queen has put on her new tag of €13,000,000, she currently resides in the luxurious surroundings of Dubai. This vessel not only adds a touch of class to oceanic adventures, but her reduced price offers a more accessible opportunity to potential purchasers.

title: Discover the Majesty in the 32-Meter Gulf Craft Motor Yacht Big M, the Seventeenth Addition to the Series, Now For Sale
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover the Majesty in the 32-Meter Gulf Craft Motor Yacht Big M, the Seventeenth Addition to the Series, Now For Sale
summary: Presented 'as-new', the 31.7-meter Gulf Craft motor yacht, Big M, is the newest addition to the luxury yacht market.
body: The 31.7-meter Gulf Craft motor yacht, Big M, was delivered as the 17th hull of the renowned Majesty 100 series. Crafted from GRP in-house by the UAE-based shipyard, she personifies the epitome of sophistication. Now perfectly maintained and still under shipyard warranty, Big M is listed for sale for a modest €7,950,000.

Within the 194GT motor yacht, an aura of contemporary elegance prevails, underlined by neutral yet luxurious fabric choices. Designed to captivate both private owners and charter guests, a range of settings include an open-plan main saloon, a lounge area with a central television forward, and a more relaxed seating at the aft. A skylounge above provides another tastefully designed area, complete with an L-shaped sofa and fold-out tables.

Big M boasts an optional extended swim platform paired with the perfect accessory for water access - a Williams 505 tender. Further notable deck spaces include the elongated foredeck, perfect for al fresco dining or sunbathing with uninterrupted forward-facing views, and a sundeck accompanied by additional sofa seating under a protective awning.

At the heart of the yacht are twin 1,900hp MAN engines, offering a top speed of 19 knots and a cruising speed of 15 knots. This perfect blend of luxury, power, and carefully chosen detailing makes the Big M an irresistible acquisition for any luxury yacht enthusiast.

title: Unravelling the Story of Xwave: The Magnificent 32m Sanlorenzo SL106 Yacht Embarks on Her Next Voyage of Ownership
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unravelling the Story of Xwave: The Magnificent 32m Sanlorenzo SL106 Yacht Embarks on Her Next Voyage of Ownership
summary: Xwave, the stellar 32.3-metre Sanlorenzo SL106 motor yacht, starts a fresh course under a new owner; a testament to the enduring allure of sea conquest.
body: In the labyrinth of the luxury yacht market, deals sail in and out on a daily basis. One such captivating tale is the recent acquisition of the grand 32.3-metre Sanlorenzo motor yacht 'Xwave'. This sophisticated vessel has charted new horizons, embarking on a fresh ownership voyage. This successful transaction was navigated by the astute trio of Alex Dineen and Simon Goldsworthy from Edmiston, who stood representing the seller, and Dimitris Kyriazakos of Ekka Yachts, who welcomed the buyer into the scenic world of yachting. Xwave is a burgee of Sanlorenzo, built in 2019 as a proud member of the celebrated SL106 portfolio. This yacht, with her sleek shell drawn by the exceptional Francesco Paszkowski and contemporary interiors by Marty Lowe personifies the essence of private ownership. The vessel, pristinely maintained, has just concluded her five-year class survey at the Lauderdale Marine Centre, Florida, before traversing into the hands of her new owner. As one steps on board, Xwave's luxurious offering unravels — five elegantly tailored cabins that sleep up to ten guests, each with their en suite facilities, provide comfort for the tranquil sailing nights. An open-plan main saloon boasting a vibrant design scheme elegantly complements the dining section that exudes an aura of sophistication, perfectly completed by the natural light pouring in from the expansive windows. The exterior decks of the SL106 highlight the expansive flybridge with an equipped helm station, inviting for pleasurable lounging or alfresco dining. The aft deck doubles as another dining spot or a seashore-like lounging area. The swim platform links to the transom tender garage that houses a 4.5-metre tender and a Jet Ski — the perfect ingredients for water-based fun. Propelled by twin 2,400hp MTU diesel engines, she cruises effortlessly, reaching a top speed of 28 knots and a range of 400 nautical miles. Stabilisers guarantee the smoothest of voyages in all weather conditions, and her Americas Edition upgrade package makes her versatile and apt for both American and European waters. So, as Xwave charts her new course, the promise of enriching voyages and endless fun lies on the horizon.

title: Glimpse into the Extravagant World of AB 95 Yacht Model by AB Yachts
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Glimpse into the Extravagant World of AB 95 Yacht Model by AB Yachts
summary: Italian yard AB Yachts reveals the first look at its highly-anticipated AB 95 model, displaying impressive features and design.
body: AB Yachts has placed its first AB 95 model on the global stage, debuting at the celebrated Cannes Yachting Festival. Spanning a commanding 28.5 meters, the AB 95 design is available in two unique variations, showcasing visual elegance coupled with powerful performance poised at 50-knot top speeds. The yacht's most noteworthy area is the flybridge, characterized by an innovative reverse-glass windshield that shapes its external profile. This terrace-like space allows for an outstanding open-air viewpoint above the water, accessible via two carbon stairways extending from the aft cockpit. Inside, the yacht exhibits a minimalist, yet warm ambiance with premium materials such as teak parquet flooring and Italian leather, complemented by integrated LED strips and lightly colored ceilings. The saloon includes a black-lacquered galley that doubles as a cocktail bar, revolutionizing onboard experiences. Moreover, this design reallocates lower deck space to accommodate an extra guest cabin. The yacht provides luxurious arrangements across four cabins, with facilities for a four-person crew. The highlight of this level is the pair of teak staircases, beautifully complemented by bathrooms featuring ribbed wooden cabinetry. Additionally, the yacht boasts a beach area with direct sea access and a garage large enough for a 4.5-metre tender and a Jet Ski. The AB 95 is an embodiment of AB Yachts' thirty-year expertise in yachting, coupled with cutting-edge architectural and design projects, bringing forth a yacht that spotlights the most advanced engineering solutions with unparalleled materials and finishes. Further, the AB 95's key specs of a 6.8-metre beam and a draft of 1.35 metres, enable it to navigate in shallow waters with ease, offering flexibility in its maneuvering capabilities. Currently, AB Yachts has four yachts on order or under construction, among which the largest is the impressive 39.7-metre AB 130.

title: Echo of Sails and Roar of Waves: A Close Look at the 2025 Hobie 16 Open North American Championships
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Echo of Sails and Roar of Waves: A Close Look at the 2025 Hobie 16 Open North American Championships
summary: A riveting account of the 2025 Hobie 16 Open North American Championships, a thrilling competition under varying wind conditions and surging waves.
body: The fourth day of the 2025 Hobie 16 Open North American Championships at the Pensacola Yacht Club was, without a doubt, a day of surprises and challenges. It emphatically announced its start with boisterous winds and lively sea state. Indeed, the wind held its grip throughout the day, edging some teams to their limits.

After weathering the three-day spell of shifty winds, sailors onboard took on racing day 4, the first of the final series, with significant gusts of 22 knots. Four spirited races were completed under challenging waves, worthy of an adventurer's journal. However, as the day moved to its latter half, the winds started to fade. Yet again, the consistent winds morphed into breezy drafts, especially during the first three races. By the fourth race, the wind had calmed to a gentle breeze of 8-10 knots.

Each fleet progressed, bracing the waves and the wind that was to follow in the last day of the competition. Just like the previous days, gusty winds announced the daybreak, but later faded into serenity. The challenge on this day, after surviving the left-over waves from an overnight storm, was about staying in the breeze, and managing the favored shift. A suitable finish to an eventful championship.

After 16 nail-biting races spread over five days, the champions were declared. In the gold fleet, the Guatemalans, Jason HESS and Soniy PONCE, won the North American Championship. Coming after them were Venezuelan team Yamil SABA and Andrea SABA, and Puerto Rican team Enrique FIGUEROA and Irene FIGUEROA. The silver fleet was dominated by Miguel MILLET and Cipriano GONZALEX from Mexico. Jose Daniel MAYORGA and Juan Carlos CANIZALEZ from Guatemala, Bradley DAVIS and Erik VOLK from the USA filled the runner-up slots.
The excitement remains high as the upcoming competition is set to take place in Clear Lake, Iowa. May the upcoming showdown in the lake bring more unpredictable winds and high spirits.

title: Mangusta's Oceano 39 Series: An Affair of Luxury, Seakeeping and Design Excellence
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Mangusta's Oceano 39 Series: An Affair of Luxury, Seakeeping and Design Excellence
summary: A newcomer to the ocean waves, the eighth vessel of the stunning Mangusta Oceano 39 series, is set to sail in spring 2028.

The vessel's unparallel elegance and performance continue to uphold Mangusta Yachts' reputation in the yacht industry. With delivery set for spring 2028, this magnificent 39.2-metre motor yacht comes courtesy of the Italian yacht builders Mangusta Yachts, a brand under the Overmarine Group.

Spacious and alluring, the yacht boasts an impressive beam of 8.5 metres. This sophisticated vessel offers room for up to 12 guests across five exquisite cabins, paired with a dedicated crew contingent. Coupling generous interior space with contemporary design, it's no surprise this series continues to command respect in the yacht world.

The series indeed carries a standard of high performance, yet it does not skimp on aesthetics. The Oceano 39 line carries the stylish and sporty signature associated with the Mangusta brand. This aligns perfectly with the sophistication and elegance that one expects from such luxury vessels.

The sale of the eighth Oceano 39 vessel stands as a testament to the relentless dedication of the Mangusta team, including Americas president Stefano Arlunno. FGI Yacht Group, a Fort Lauderdale-based brokerage firm, has marked the sale their eight new-construction project with Mangusta, reinforcing their reputation as a leading enterprise for Mangusta builds globally.

title: A Thrilling Nautical Adventure Unfolds at the Welstead September Yawl Open - Blue Fleet
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A Thrilling Nautical Adventure Unfolds at the Welstead September Yawl Open - Blue Fleet
summary: The Welstead September Open - Blue Fleet held not in the choppy waves but in a serene yet unpredictable breeze, captured the hearts and minds of the sailing world.
body: The Welstead September Yawl Open – Blue Fleet was set to be a walk in the park; benign weather awaited the sailors after countless weeks of bitter winds and countless cancelled races. A sense of relief permeated the air. Expectations were as high as ever, with an event record of 18 boats lined up and ready to sail. There was no telling who would claim victory, it was anyone's game. Sunshine lit up the waters and the buoyant spirits amongst the sailors and spectators alike.

The first race was led by the exciting duo Mark and Phil on Y17, closely trailed by promising competitors on the loop around the harbour. A fiercely competitive tacking battle ensued, allowing 'The Commodores Barge' to extend its lead and take the first race. It was exciting, nail-biting, edge-of-your-seat style racing that hit all the right notes.

It was onto the third and fourth races which saw more stirring clashes and skills being put to the ultimate test. The unpredictable winds requiring on-the-spot decision making, a true testament to the sailing prowess and mettle of the participants. Amidst the ever changing tides and winds, every contestant fought hard, sailing the fine line between strategy and instinct, creating a truly unforgettable spectacle.

Indeed, the Welstead September Yawl Open - Blue Fleet turned out to be far more than just another sailing race. It was a thrilling nautical adventure that unfolded amidst placid yet unpredictable winds. With every gust and change of tide, it captivated the attendees and viewers, leaving an indelible mark. Amidst the calm waters, the true spirits of the sailors came to fore, but more than anything, it eulogised the idea that under serene exteriors, something incredible can exist. The tranquil waters of Welstead will continue to ripple with the echoes of this thrilling adventure for time to come.

title: Unveiling Safety Risks in Superyachts: Critical Learnings From Near Misses and Infestations
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unveiling Safety Risks in Superyachts: Critical Learnings From Near Misses and Infestations
summary: Examining the world of superyachts unequivocally exposes potential safety hazard points that can lead us towards creating safer waterways.
body: Navigating the tranquil expanse of the ocean on a superyacht is a sublime experience shrouded with numerous unseen safety threats. Uncovering these hazardous obstacles forms a crucial part in the journey to ensuring safer waters. Insightful case studies reported by the keen observers at CHIRP Maritime’s Superyacht Feedback program provide a glimpse into a few such situations.

During a routine inspection onboard a superyacht, a team found that an emergency escape hatch from the engine room to the deck was obstructed by turned-up mooring lines. The issue traced back to the superyacht’s design phase. While mooring arrangements and emergency escape routes were approved as compliant, no one had verified the practical operation of these systems. Just a few centimeters of rope blocked the emergency hatch, a small detail that could result in dramatic consequences in a critical situation.

These cases highlight the universal necessity of practical design considerations, rigorous inspections, and active communication among developers, designers, and operational staff. Emergency routes should be thoroughly familiarized and routinely inspected, a practice that should be ingrained in maritime operations. Silos between design and operational teams can lead to severe oversights, as demonstrated by the blocked escape hatch. Crew members, designers, and decision-makers need to work as a proficiently coordinated team, breaking down barriers that might hinder communication.

The critical incidents reported collectively emphasize the importance of integrating risk thinking across design, operational, and inspection stages. Safety measures should not only align with compliance but should also reflect the realities and nuances of onboard practices. An intricate understanding of these experiences paves the path to improved maritime safety, avoiding potential catastrophes in the shifting tides of the marine milieu.

title: Revel in Lavish Luxury: An Unveiling of Tankoa Yachts' Second 55 Sportiva Yacht, Loewe
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Revel in Lavish Luxury: An Unveiling of Tankoa Yachts' Second 55 Sportiva Yacht, Loewe
summary: Tankoa Yachts has gifted yacht enthusiasts a peek into its latest masterpiece in the 55 Sportiva series, named Loewe, a sistership to Rose.
body: Italy's premier yacht builder, Tankoa Yachts, presents a first look into the second jewel in its Sportiva 55 series. Following the successful launch of Rose, its new offspring, Loewe, splashed the waters at the Monaco Yacht Show this year. An exclusive soirée hailed its arrival, graced by the likes of Kylian Mbappé and hosted by audio specialists Loewe, celebrating their new limited edition range of headphones.

Crafted by renowned designer Luca Dini, Loewe boasts standout features harmonised into an under-500 GT model, with a highlight being a resort-style beach club. It includes a spa, an infinity pool, and a noteworthy 'sealine window', offering mesmerising underwater views. Dini aimed to amplify the charm of the Tankoa 55, fusing fluidity and character with the elegance and strength inherent in their design ethos. The result? An alluring yacht conveying dynamism and emotion.

Further adding to the luxury, the sundeck is fitted with another pool, a bar, and a sunbathing area, with the foredeck sporting another sunpad. The bow's intelligent design can accommodate tenders and toys, hidden in a forward bay. An elevator provides onboard transport across all decks, and a galley is situated on the primary deck.

Currently, the Italian shipyard is working on nine more yacht orders, the most extensive being the T650 Apache, measuring 56 meters. The unveiling of the new Loewe marks another significant milestone for Tankoa Yachts and is now available for charter with Ocean Independence across the Mediterranean, promising a voyaging experience of unmatched luxury and style.

title: High-Tech Bridge Refit Unveiled on the 97m Lürssen Superyacht Carinthia VII
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: High-Tech Bridge Refit Unveiled on the 97m Lürssen Superyacht Carinthia VII
summary: Lürssen's masterpiece, the 97.2-metre superyacht Carinthia VII, recently completed a comprehensive bridge refit, marking another significant upgrade in her illustrious journey.
body: One of the leading lights in the superyacht world, the 97.2-metre Lürssen vessel Carinthia VII, had recently added another feather to her extensively clad cap courtesy of a meticulous bridge refit. The process, undertaken at IGY Sète Marina in France, was expertly overseen by Ralph de Joode, founder of RYacht Monaco. With the invaluable assistance of Eekels Technology B.V., who chiefly contributed to the core systems installation, the bridge was given a swanky makeover featuring vital navigation and communication systems. Radio Zeeland facilitated the necessary package which boasted upgraded Furuno radars, ECDIS, an electronic logbook, AIS safety features, and seven 27-inch displays, among other modern amenities.

Bizzozero Cassina helmed the interior architecture of the bridge, beautifully aligning technical functionality with a crisp, contemporary aesthetic. The phenomenal Milan-based studio collaborated with the master crafters at Vedder to deliver the finished masterpiece; every tiny detail perfectly executed, from the carpentry to the console joinery and leather finishing.

This refit follows an ambitious transformation undertaken at the German yard Blohm + Voss, which lasted an impressive 300 days. The yacht's ravishing new look turned heads at the 2023 Monaco Yacht Show, yet another feather in Lürssen's cap.

The sophisticated hardware aside, Carinthia VII received some luxurious additions in this refit. An 11-metre pool was introduced on the aft deck, while a high-tech gym was installed on the bridge deck, surrounded by six tonnes of removable glass panels. Moreover, the interior was remodelled extensively, ensuring a fresh look and maintaining certain historical elements, like original pieces of furniture and the unique wooden floors. As a result, the already impressive superyacht now has an even finer blend of luxury and functionality.

An important aspect of this refit, however, was the technical modifications that transitioned the yacht from private to commercial usage. As explained by Lürssen's refit sales director, Alberto Perrone da Zara, such an endeavour requires proper understanding and review of regulations, followed by escalated negotiations with the class. Now, the grandeur of the Carinthia VII awaits her new commercial patrons, ready to offer an experience of a lifetime.

title: Epic Conclusion to the 2025 JOG Season at the Henri-Lloyd Cowes-Lymington Weekend
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Epic Conclusion to the 2025 JOG Season at the Henri-Lloyd Cowes-Lymington Weekend
summary: The 2025 JOG Season ended on a thrilling note at the Henri-Lloyd Cowes-Lymington weekend, challenging crews with shifting winds and testing tidal conditions.
body: The end of year racing spectacle, the Henri-Lloyd Cowes-Lymington Weekend, brought the 2025 JOG Season to a remarkable close. The event commenced under an unpredictable sky, dappled with both light and heavy airs that tested the grit and tenacity of the participating crews. The weekend reminded everyone of the exhilarating yet fine line that separates triumph from despair in tidal racing.

Saturday’s competition saw a relatively infrequent southerly breeze, allowing for an imposing 27-mile red flag course. The day concluded with every boat having finished by mid-afternoon, perfectly in time for a delightful pontoon party orchestrated by the JOG President Peter Rutter. The day's victors included Scream 2 (IRC 1), Bellino (IRC 2), Elaine Again (IRC 3) and SailFish (IRC 4), while Sanity bagged the double-handed division.

The racing season debuted in March, with the familiar Lonely Tower and Great Escape openers setting the tone for an exciting year ahead. The competitors navigated challenging routes to Weymouth, Eastbourne and across the Channel to St Vaast and Deauville. The season will fondly be remembered for its thrilling races where victory margins were often a matter of mere minutes.

Bellino, in particular, has had an exceptional season. The team, led by skippers Deb Fish and Rob Craigie, transitioned from a two-handed to a four-up coastal series. Despite the odds, their resilience and dedication culminated in unforgettable victories, redefining the spirit of the competition.

The grandeur and excitement of the entire season, with its highs and lows, all led up to this final weekend - a tribute to the unyielding spirit of every sailor who braved the challenges and savoured the victories.

title: Discover 'Outlier', where Lateral Naval Architects and Foster + Partners Redefine the 2,000 GT Yacht Compatibility
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover 'Outlier', where Lateral Naval Architects and Foster + Partners Redefine the 2,000 GT Yacht Compatibility
summary: Lateral Naval Architects and Foster + Partners revolutionise the yachting landscape with their disruptive 88.5-meter yachting platform design, 'Outlier'.
body: Lateral Naval Architects, creating waves of change in collaboration with the globally celebrated Foster + Partners, is set to challenge the classic designs of 2,000 GT yachts. Their groundbreaking creation, the 'Outlier', an 88.5-metre platform aims to upturn conventional norms with its inventive design, superior efficiency and user-friendly spaces. Lateral Naval Architects' Ollie Cooper describes the Outlier as a unique platform, calling upon yacht owners and designers to re-imagine yachts as more than mere boats on the sea, but as dynamic structures with unrestricted potential.

By moving the machinery forward, and integrating an electric-hybrid system supported by an expansive 4 Mwh battery, the Outlier opens up new possibilities for quiet, uninterrupted lower decks and enhanced comfort amidships. One of the primary design goals behind the Outlier was freedom; the power to create and re-imagine yachts without limitations. This extends to a staggering 40 per cent increase in exterior space, thanks to the extended hull and redistributed machinery.

Taking design liberties even further, the Outlier features an internal exhaust system routing, which offers flexibility in the yacht’s profile. To demonstrate the platform’s potential, Lateral called upon the design prowess of Foster + Partners, who conceptualised Outlier I. This design highlights how a 2,000 GT yacht can encompass attributes typical of much larger vessels, exceeding 5,000 GT. The suggestive design focuses on fluid connectivity between spaces and decks, uninterrupted exterior areas, and reimagined guest accommodation spaces designed to heighten both privacy and social interaction. Remarkably versatile, the Outlier model can also be scaled down to 1,500 or even 950 GT, providing the same core functional benefits.

Given the technology and design innovation of the Outlier, many question whether the traditional baseline concept remains relevant. As such, a scale model of this innovative design was presented at the Monaco Yacht Show, opening new discussions within the industry and spurring curiosity for the future of yachts.

title: A Revolutionary Approach to the 2,000 GT Yacht Rule: Lateral Naval Architects and Foster & Partners' Daring Innovation
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A Revolutionary Approach to the 2,000 GT Yacht Rule: Lateral Naval Architects and Foster & Partners' Daring Innovation
summary: Foster + Partners, in conjunction with Lateral Naval Architects, has revealed a groundbreaking 88.5-metre platform, Outlier, pledging to revolutionise the 2,000 GT yacht sector.
body: In a terrain known for its rigidity and conformity, Foster + Partners and Lateral Naval Architects are pushing the boundaries. Their latest innovation, the Outlier, aims to redefine the standards of the 2,000 GT yacht sector. Taking the reigns from existing norms, they promise a reimagined approach that goes far beyond the traditional blueprint. Senior naval architect at Lateral, Ollie Cooper, passionately believes in this cause, affirming that Outlier is not just a platform, but an invitation to reimagine yacht design from within.

Drawing from Lateral's Ultra-Efficient Hull series, the 88.5-metre Outlier platform vouches a 16 per cent escalation in length within the 85-metre load line limit, whilst using 20 per cent less power and attaining 17 per cent lower fuel consumption. By relocating the machinery to the front, facilitated by an electric-hybrid system with a 4.0 Mwh battery installation, Outlier promises quiet guest spaces, improved comfort amidships and seamless lower decks.

The redesigned platform also allows for up to 40 per cent more exterior space and increased flexibility with the yacht's profile courtesy of internal exhaust system routing. To showcase this, Foster + Partners have sculpted the Outlier I, embodying attributes usually seen only on larger superyachts over 5,000 GT with its strong emphasis on deck and space connectivity, revamped guest accommodations prioritising privacy and social interaction. Despite its innovation, the Outlier concept is not limited to the 2,000 GT range; the design could be applied to smaller yachts in the 1,500 GT or even 950 GT categories.

Presented at the Monaco Yacht Show, the Outlier is a testament to Foster + Partners and Lateral's commitment to challenging the norm and innovating in a sector often dominated by tradition. This bold step heralds the beginning of a new chapter for yacht design, where boundaries are actively pursued. It remains to be seen whether this will disrupt the longstanding baseline, and redefine what a yacht in the 2,000 GT bracket can be.

title: Unveiling the Transformed Luis Lima, a 45m Alpha Marine Motor Yacht, Post a Comprehensive Refit and Extension
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unveiling the Transformed Luis Lima, a 45m Alpha Marine Motor Yacht, Post a Comprehensive Refit and Extension
summary: After an extensive refit and extension, the first renderings of the 45m yacht Luis Lima, renovated from disuse, are now unveiled.
body: At a majestic 45 meters following seven-meter extension and inclusive of a thorough refit, the Alpha Marine yacht Luis Lima, resurfaces from her dormant state in Greece. Set to be relaunched from the Izmir site in late 2026, the yacht boasts a brand-new design by Baran Akalın, graced with an impressive 90-square-meter beach club - a prized feature in modern yachting. This space is outfitted with sizeable fold-down balconies, a Jacuzzi, lounge and dining areas, and a disappearing rotatable television.

A grand novelty for a 45-meter build, Luis Lima will house two commodious saloons, five guest cabins, and a full-service wellness center. You will traverse through a wine cellar on the lower deck before making it to the upper deck that serves as the owner's abode. The upper deck features a captain’s bridge at the bow and a Jacuzzi and seating area. A bar, digital gaming table, and a significant storage space adorn the owner's saloon. The suite includes a well-appointed bathroom with an integrated bathtub, a walk-in wardrobe, and access to a private garden terrace.

The fly deck has been reimagined with a third Jacuzzi, sun pads, lounge seating, a fully equipped service area midship, and an aft-facing bar. Whether you're looking to watch F1 races when docked in Monaco or enjoy an exclusive dinner by the sea, Luis Lima's redesigned, spacious, and versatile areas are ready to cater to your every need.
