imageAlt: Experience the Thrill of the 2025 Snipe North American Championship in San Diego Through the Lens of Bob Betancourt
summary: The 2025 Snipe North American Championship in San Diego welcomed spectacular conditions for sailing, as evident in the riveting photo gallery by Bob Betancourt.
body: On the waters off San Diego, on a warm Saturday in August 2025, Bob Betancourt set out on his boat, camera in hand. His mission? To capture the exciting moments from the second day of the Snipe North American Championship. San Diego Yacht Club played host to this prestigious event, providing a picturesque backdrop for a truly exciting regatta.

Betancourt's pictures captured the frenzy of the regatta with an artistic flair. Each flash of the camera immortalized a participant chasing victory on the glistening sea. Sailors dancing with the wind, sails full with anticipation and the kind of adrenaline only a regatta can inspire, came to life in his photos.

One can only appreciate the magnitude of such a race through Betancourt's lens. It reveals not just the physicality and technique, but also the strategy and emotion inherent in sailing at its highest level.

From start to finish, the Snipe sailors demonstrated their shoulder to the wheel dedication, coalescing their skill and wit to navigate through the demanding course. Betancourt's photographs encapsulated the spirit, the passion and the reverence everyone had for the sea - those onboard and spectators alike.

The 2025 Snipe North American Championship in San Diego will be remembered for its thrilling sailing and more so, through Betancourt's captivating images. These are not just photographs; they are stories of resilience, courage and jubilation, written on the canvas of the sea.

title: Team Holcim-PRB’s Setback Becomes Triumph as It Wins Redress at The Ocean Race Europe
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Team Holcim-PRB’s Setback Becomes Triumph as It Wins Redress at The Ocean Race Europe
summary: An unexpected twist in The Ocean Race Europe sees Team Holcim-PRB triumph via a redress ruling.
body: When we put ourselves at the mercy of the ocean’s vast expanse, we brace for every sudden gust and rogue wave. The race is rarely ever only against other boats, but also against circumstance and, if not careful, misfortune. Thus was the narrative set for Team Holcim-PRB at the start of The Ocean Race Europe in Kiel, Germany back in August 2025. A collision, not foreseen nor bargained for, compelled them to abandon the first leg of the race. Amid the salty splash of defeat, their hopes capsized.

'We're pleased with the Jury decision', said Alan Roberts, a crew member representing Team Holcim-PRB, 'This result fairly recognises our performance across the entire race. Proudly successful in Cartagena, we are back in full racing spirit, more determined than ever. Each hiccup is merely an opportunity for a stronger comeback.' Their spirits certainly were unphased, the sweet taste of redemption sowing seeds of resilient hope.

Two days later, they lined up again for the third leg from Cartagena to Nice. Though the unforgiving waters yet awaited, the team faced the challenging ocean expanse with their heads held high, ready to embrace their fortune-changing journey. Each crash of the wave was a reminder of their victory over adversity, the taste of success amidst the salty sprays. The Ocean Race Europe saw the tides tide change for Team Holcim-PRB, truly a triumph from tragedy. For in the seas of uncertainty, every setback may just be the start of a comeback.

title: Boats Group Faces Legal Battle Over Alleged Marketplace Monopoly
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Boats Group Faces Legal Battle Over Alleged Marketplace Monopoly
summary: An antitrust lawsuit has been filed against online boat listing conglomerate, Boats Group, in a bid to invigorate competition in the industry.
body: A storm is brewing in the world of boating, as a powerful force on the seas finds itself in choppy waters. Boats Group, the proprietor of illustrious online listing platforms Yacht World, Boat Trader, and boats.com, is being sued in a US federal court. For many, Boats Group represents a beacon in the world of marine trading, linking buyers and sellers across globe. However, a lawsuit has been filed alleging that the group is stifling competition in the marketplace, thus compromising the spirit of the sail.

The antitrust lawsuit, in this case, intends to break up an alleged monopoly held by the powerful entity, embarking on a legal tussle that could send ripples across the industry. By stimulating competition, it is hoped that a more dynamic, vibrant marketplace could emerge, providing customers with more options and vendors with a wider playing field.

Regardless of the outcome, this lawsuit exemplifies the importance of competition in any industry. The very essence of entrepreneurship is the approach to the market in a novel way, injecting fresh ideas and giving life to innovative products. When one player becomes too dominant, it not only stagnates the industry but also fuels resentment among other key players. This case will certainly keep the anchor of competition afloat in the landscape of the boating world.

title: Get Ready for Adventure: The 38-Metre Sea Axis by Heesen is Up for Grabs
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Get Ready for Adventure: The 38-Metre Sea Axis by Heesen is Up for Grabs
summary: Sea Axis, a 38.1-metre go-anywhere motor yacht by Heesen, is ready for a new owner, promising a life of luxury on the sea.
body: The grandeur of the Sea Axis, a 38.1-metre motor yacht crafted by Heesen, is poised for new horizons as it finds itself listed for sale. Constructed by the famed Dutch shipyard in 1987 with a captivating design by Frank Mulder, this aluminium marvel is a testament to timeless luxury. After a meticulous makeover, Sea Axis now boasts a contemporary interior that aligns effortlessly with its stature. In fact, it has just emerged from an exhaustive 40-year survey, leaving no stone unturned to ensure it retains its pristine condition. Fresh from its comprehensive revamp, it's ready to embark on its new voyage from day one of purchase, ensuring immediate enjoyment for its new owners.

The yacht's makeover wasn't a mere cosmetic endeavor. In 2011, Sea Axis underwent a massive two-year, $10 million refurbishment supervised closely by the original designer, undergoing extensive external and internal transformations, including a spruced-up sun deck, bridge and aft deck, and restructured exterior areas. As the Sea Axis sails towards a new chapter, it boasts a fresh paint job and all-new teak decks secured in 2022.

Boasting a pair of 1,250hp Deutz engines, the yacht ensures an exhilarating sea adventure with a top speed of 17 knots. With it's impressive range of 3000 nautical miles at a cruising speed of 12 knots, it offers both thrilling speed and stamina for long voyages. Priced at $4,499,000, the Sea Axis is a sumptuous testament to seafaring luxury. It waits, ready and gleaming, for its new owner in Newport, Rhode Island. The question remains, who will the lucky adventurer be to take the helm of this stunning vessel next?

title: Fleet storms away from the Solent as Ocean Race Europe Leg 2
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Ocean Race Europe Leg 2
imageCaption: Leg II starting line - The Ocean Race
summary: Portsmouth turned on the sunshine this evening as seven IMOCAs thundered off the Royal Yacht Squadron line at 17:00, launching the second leg of The Ocean Race Europe 2025. Ahead lies 1,400 nautical miles of hard running to Cartagena, Spain, with a midweek fly-by off Matosinhos-Porto to keep things lively.
body: The first prize came quickly — a scoring gate at The Needles. In sparkling downwind conditions, tide in their favour, the fleet tore past Cowes with spinnakers flying. Paprec Arkéa’s Yoann Richomme had grabbed the early spotlight, but once again it was Paul Meilhat and his Biotherm crew who bagged the maximum points, keeping their flawless scoring record intact. Paprec settled for second, while Holcim-PRB, freshly patched up and back from the brink, crossed third.

Holcim’s skipper Alan Roberts could hardly hide his pride. “It’s amazing we’re back. The shore team worked day and night — adversity bonded us tighter. We’re at 100% and hungry to race.” His words echoed the grit behind every sail change.

At the other end of the dock, Allagrande Mapei Racing arrived barely a day before the start, but skipper Ambrogio Beccaria shrugged it off. “Our boat’s made for strong winds,” he grinned. “Bring it on.”

Biotherm, still carrying the yellow jersey, are trying not to look too far ahead. “We’ve started well, but this leg will be brutal,” Meilhat admitted. “Transitions off Brittany, the Bay of Biscay, and finally the Med — there’s no let-up.”

Malizia, fresh from their bold Dover gamble, are thriving in tonight’s forecast. “These are our conditions,” said co-skipper Will Harris, now wearing the armband for Boris Herrmann. With new crew energy, Malizia smell opportunity.

Richomme’s Paprec Arkéa is relishing the opening blast but braced for tactical headaches down the line. “It’s going to be beautiful — spinnaker start, fast run — but tricky around Ouessant. Surprises always come.”

As the sun dropped over the Solent, the leaderboard read: Biotherm 11 points, Paprec Arkéa 7, Malizia 6, Canada Ocean Racing 4, Amaala 3, Holcim and Allagrande on zero. But numbers won’t tell the whole tale. Ahead lies Biscay, Portuguese trades, Gibraltar, and the Med — a sailor’s gauntlet.
By Wednesday, they’ll skim Porto. Soon after, Cartagena. And between now and then? Sails will rip, crews will curse, and fortunes will swing. Ocean racing at its finest.

title: Princess F58 - The Flybridge Yacht
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Princess F58: The Flybridge Yacht
summary: The Princess F58, the crown jewel of Princess Yachts’ F Class lineage, unveiled with style at Boot Düsseldorf 2025. This 59-foot-9-inch (18.2-meter) flybridge stunner, slotted sleekly between the F55 and F65, is the British brand’s latest ode to luxury living on the water. Launched this January in Plymouth, it’s tailored for the jet-set family or the ultimate entertainer, promising coastal chic from the Mediterranean
body: The Princess F58, the crown jewel of Princess Yachts’ F Class lineage, unveiled with style at Boot Düsseldorf 2025. This 59-foot-9-inch (18.2-meter) flybridge stunner, slotted sleekly between the F55 and F65, is the British brand’s latest ode to luxury living on the water. Launched this January in Plymouth, it’s tailored for the jet-set family or the ultimate entertainer, promising coastal chic from the Mediterranean to the British Virgin Islands.

Crafted from GRP (glass-reinforced plastic) with cutting-edge techniques, the F58’s hull and superstructure are a lightweight yet robust masterpiece, its elegant lines slicing through the waves with a 4.9-metre (16-foot-1-inch) beam and a 1.54-meter draft. Twin MAN V8 engines—your pick of 1,000 hp or the punchy 1,200 hp—propel it to a top speed of 34 knots, cruising at 25–28 knots with a vibe that turns heads. With a 2,200-litre (581-gallon) fuel tank and 630-litre (166-gallon) water reserve, plus a 73-litre hot water clarifier, it’s primed for a week-long Amalfi Coast escape or a Solent jaunt during Cowes Week (August 2–8, 2025).

The exterior is where the party lives. The flybridge is a social playground—think a sprawling dining table, an L-shaped wet bar with an electric barbecue, and convertible seating that flips into a sun pad for those wonderful hour in the sun. An optional hardtop keeps the vibe going rain or shine, while the central helm delivers panoramic views, a must for threading through Monaco’s yacht-choked harbour. The foredeck terrace, borrowed from Princess’s big-league designs, offers twin sun pads with storage and adjustable headrests—perfect for a chic deckside soirée. The cockpit flows into a “mini beach club” bathing platform, with optional toy storage and a waterside grill, making it the ultimate waterside hangout.

Inside, it’s a masterclass in understated elegance. Panoramic windows flood the saloon with light, framing a U-shaped sofa and a coffee-to-dining table that shifts from cozy chats to formal feasts. Below deck, three cabins dazzle: a forward VIP with a plush double, a starboard twin that converts to a double, and a full-beam owner’s stateroom with a superyacht-worthy en-suite and walk-in wardrobe. An optional aft crew cabin adds crew comfort. Customise with an Ash satin finish, and the north American versions come loaded with air conditioning, an 11.5 kW generator, and electric cooking—transatlantic luxury, sorted.

The F58 isn’t just pretty—it’s smart. A dedicated aft dinette expands dining options, while a silent-running battery pack lets you run AC and stabilisers at anchor without the diesel hum, a green nod for the eco-conscious elite. Princess Connect telemetry keeps tabs remotely, ensuring maintenance is a breeze whether you’re docked in Southampton or cruising the Caribbean.

title: From Toppers to Vintage: Battle for Prestigious Crossley Holland Trophy in Overy Staithe Regatta
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: From Toppers to Vintage: Battle for Prestigious Crossley Holland Trophy in Overy Staithe Regatta
summary: The Overy Staithe Regatta saw a spirited race for the 'Crossley Holland Trophy', with a mixed fleet of 40 boats sailing in pursuit.
body: In an extraordinary mix of expertise, technology, and sheer sailing spirit, the Overy Staithe Regatta unfolded, a canvas of 40 various boats, ranging from Toppers to vintage International 14 and local designs like Stiffkey Cockles to Twinkle Twelves, competing towards one goal, the 'Crossley Holland Trophy'. The trophy, sailed under pursuit principles, marks a key part of the club's annual regatta, setting the scene for a thrilling nautical experience.

This year, the Race Officers Bernard Clark and Will Worsley designed a challenging course which spread from marks C, E, D and A on a two-lap circuit. The race signaled off from the club line on the sea wall and concluded at the quay amidst cheers and eager anticipation.

The unexpected twist paved the way for Pete Turner, sailing on his 'OK'. His victory was closely followed by Alex Scoles and Spike Turner, claiming the second and third places respectively. Among the double handed boats, Alex Smith and Paul Beachell led the race, taking the 4th place. The junior category saw promising talent with Sam Worsley taking the 14th position.

All in all, the Overy Staithe Regatta, and particularly the race for the 'Crossley Holland Trophy', was a thrilling spectacle of mixed fleets, skilful sailing, and the unpredictability of the ocean waves, presenting a fantastic spectacle for any lover of the sea.

title: Diving into tales of seas and sails with Jack Macartney on 'Bulwarks and Bulldust’
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Diving into tales of seas and sails with Jack Macartney on 'Bulwarks and Bulldust’
summary: Immerse yourself in exhilarating maritime adventures as Episode Four of 'Bulwarks and Bulldust' Season Two sets sail, featuring renowned sailor Jack Macartney.
body: Prepare for a thrilling nautical journey as 'Bulwarks and Bulldust' unfurls its fourth episode in the second season! Adorned with legendary tales and hearty laughter, this episode invites sailing enthusiast Jack Macartney to helm the ship of conversation. Known for his exploits from the legendary 18-footers to supermaxis, TP52s, Volvo 70, J/70, and even Superfoiler, Jack offers unfiltered insights into his journey, without holding anything back. Every sailing tale ranging from the Hobart, Transpac, Fastnet, Caribbean 600, to Transat and the Volvo Ocean Race is dissected with keen detail. Laden with rich experiences and vivid storytelling, the potent combination of Jack's sea-faring anecdotes and the immersive nature of the 'Bulwarks and Bulldust' show guarantees an enthralling watch for viewers. The episode further navigates into the future, casting light on prospective sailing adventures on the horizon. It also applauds the commendable work done by the Sydney Bulldog Clinic, grounding the tales of sails with a touch of reality. The Cruising Yacht Club of Australia also earns a mention for the impressive additional footage of 'Celestial (70)', covering their overall win at the 2024 Hobart. Episode 4 of 'Bulwarks and Bulldust' applauds the steady support received from its Season Two sponsor, Pantaenius Sail and Motor Yacht Insurance. Thanks extend to The Boat Works Gold Coast, EspressoTwenty5, and Melfi Designs for their unwavering support. For copious intake of sea stories, iconic sea routes, and rich tales etched in the maritime world, 'Bulwarks and Bulldust' opens up a fascinating world for sailing enthusiasts, accessible on Spotify and YouTube. Jack Macartney's fascinating world of sails, 'Celestial' and 'Scallywag' make for riveting stories augmenting the allure of navigating uncharted waters.

title: Heralded Charter Yacht Sea Class Having Major Price Reduction, a Chance for the Fortunate to Sail the Seas
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Heralded Charter Yacht Sea Class Having Major Price Reduction, a Chance for the Fortunate to Sail the Seas
summary: The acclaimed 47.2-metre Christensen motor yacht Sea Class, constructed in 1997, witnesses a significant $500,000 price reduction.
body: Consider a life of glamour and excitement on the high seas. The magnificent 47.2-metre Christensen motor yacht, the Sea Class, boasts not only an illustrious history but a significant $500,000 price reduction. Constructed by the highly esteemed US shipyard in 1997, this grand vessel is represented by Kurt Bosshardt of Denison Yachting. Embellished with a distinct two-tone exterior design from the esteemed designer, Donald Starkey, the Sea Class is now available for a cool $12,495,000.

The Sea Class isn't just a marvel to behold, it's a testament to the luxury yachting industry. Her impressive charter record is a testament to her majesty. Astoundingly maintained to this day, she is regarded as a 'highly sought-after Christensen'.

Its passenger capacity is as impressive as its design. The yacht comfortably accommodates twelve guests in six cabins. It features a wide full-beam master suite on the main deck. This space is flanked by dual en suite bathrooms along with a special 'bonus' cabin, perfect for young children or a caregiver.
Common areas on the yacht are abundant with oversized seating, a wooden dining table that can accommodate ten guests, a sun deck with a four-person sunbed, BBQ, and Jacuzzi.

The American-built yacht speeds through the ocean with a top pace of 19 knots and a maximum cruising range of 3,500 nautical miles at a 12-knot cruising speed. Powering this sea beast are twin 2,200hp Deutz-MWM diesel engines, both of which were also rebuilt in 2024.
For those longing for the thrill of tackling the seven seas or simply seeking tranquility on the water, the Sea Class offers an extraordinary opportunity.

title: Magnificent Mangusta Yacht, Royale X, Returns to Market with a Whopping €2M Price Slash
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Magnificent Mangusta Yacht, Royale X, Returns to Market with a Whopping €2M Price Slash
summary: The acclaimed motor yacht, Royale X, has re-emerged on the market following an impressive €2,000,000 price drop.
body: The distinctively stylish Royale X, an impressive 49.9-metre yacht, sculpted by Italian talent, has made a triumphant re-entry into the brokerage market. Championing its return, she has undergone an exciting price slash of €2,000,000. This intriguing development comes as thrilling news for those seeking the self-indulgence and grandeur of superyacht lifestyle.

A vision of aesthetic grandeur, Royale X sports an aerodynamic profile subtly crafted by the capable hands of top Italian designer Stefano Righini. Infusing a contemporary touch with the classic, the interior is a marvel of bright, modern design, adorned by Valentina Balducci with the elegance of bleached teak wood, limed-oak panelling, complemented by cream soft furnishings and fittings.

Scaled for sheer comfort and opulence, Royale X’s accommodation caters to nine guests across four en-suite cabins. This includes a full-beam master suite, equipped with a tailored private office, redefining luxury at sea. Aside the deluxe personal spaces, the motor yacht further impresses with an inviting main saloon, featuring a well-stocked bar, tastefully appointed coffee table, along with a large U-shaped sofa and a dining table, perfect for socialising and relaxation. The forward section of the yacht houses a triple-seated helm station.

Stepping outside, the aft deck radiates with open, luxurious space, offering plush built-in seating and a grand dining table. Towards the fore of the windscreen, another expansive seating area and plush sunpads grace the foredeck, ideal for soaking in the excitement of speed when cruising, or relishing in private sunbathing when moored stern-to.

title: Marina Port Vell Raises the Bar in Luxury Yachting with Groundbreaking Partnership with Barcelona Port Heliport
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Marina Port Vell Raises the Bar in Luxury Yachting with Groundbreaking Partnership with Barcelona Port Heliport
summary: Marina Port Vell takes service to another level, inking a deal with Barcelona Port Heliport for direct helicopter transfers to the marina.
body: In a bold move, Marina Port Vell in Barcelona takes the yachting world by storm, entering into a pioneering agreement with Barcelona Port Heliport. This groundbreaking partnership offers a direct line of helicopter transfers to and from the luxurious marina, setting a high bar for other marinas around the world." "Never before has the world of yachting seen this level of service, convenience, and luxury in one package. By providing direct helicopter transfers from Barcelona Port Heliport, Marina Port Vell ensures that their clients can access their vessels in a quick, efficient, and supremely stylish way, taking the concept of nautical luxury to entirely new heights." "This move from Marina Port Vell not only showcases their dedication to client satisfaction and comfort, but also their ability to innovate in the marina service industry. By venturing beyond the traditional, they are setting a precedent for other marinas across the globe. With this unique service, clients of Marina Port Vell can now enjoy the pleasure of sailing combined with the thrill and convenience of helicopter travel." "This groundbreaking service is available immediately, providing boat owners with an unprecedented level of convenience and distinction. Marina Port Vell is ready to leave their mark on the world of luxury yachting, one helicopter transfer at a time. As always, their objective remains to provide superior service, aimed at enhancing the sailing experience for their clients."

title: Meet Mateo Majdalani: The New Forces Steering the Nacra 17 Class Towards a Promising Future
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Meet Mateo Majdalani: The New Forces Steering the Nacra 17 Class Towards a Promising Future
summary: Fresh winds are blowing in the Nacra 17 class as Mateo Majdalani takes the presidential helm, promising to elevate the sport to new heights.
body: In a significant transition of leadership, Mateo Majdalani has been appointed as the new President of the Nacra 17 class, succeeding Santiago Lange. This shift signifies not only a changing of the guard, but a recognition of the need for active sailors to have a louder voice in class representation.

Known for his achievements on the water, including a Silver medal won at the Paris Olympics alongside Eugenia Bosco, Majdalani is a well-rounded and fair figure. His active participation and dedication to the development and improvement of the Nacra 17 class, combined with an astute, thoughtful approach, makes him a popular choice for the helm.

As the Nacra 17 class sets sail under Majdalani's leadership, there's an atmosphere of excitement and anticipation. The promise lies not only within the continued growth and success of the class but also in the fresh perspectives and vibrant energy that Majdalani brings to the presidential post. The sailing community eagerly awaits the chapters yet to be written under his guidance.

title: Discover the Outer Reef 780 Adventure: The Ultimate Adventure yacht Bred in American Ingenuity
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover the Outer Reef 780 Adventure: The Ultimate Adventure yacht Bred in American Ingenuity
summary: Unveiling the newest gem in Outer Reef's fleet: the 780 Adventure. Fully equipped for off-grid adventures while offering superyacht-level luxury, it strikes an exquisite balance of capability and comfort.
body: There's a thrill that only a yacht owner can know – the ability to take luxury to the farthest corners of the world, in the boat they call their own. The Outer Reef 780 Adventure is the embodiment of that thrill. Conceived by the acclaimed American builder Outer Reef, renowned for its premium bluewater cruisers, the 780 Adventure is a thrilling addition to their fleet. Outfitted with top-notch facilities, it's designed for those who dare to chart their own course in ultimate comfort.

Underneath the glamorous shell of the 780 Adventure is a marine beast ready for the most daring of voyages. The boat is designed for those who live for the thrill of the journey. It boasts an enormous fuel capacity along with upgraded Caterpillar diesels, making transoceanic travel possible. Add to this a considerable storage capacity for expedition equipment, the yachting adventure-seekers have in their hands the perfect tool for charting new routes.

The 780 Adventure offers extensive customisation, making it perfect for owners with bespoke preferences. It features four guest cabins as standard, plus extra ensuite bunk cabins, accommodating up to 12 guests. For those looking for even more luxury, the yacht can be remodelled into a full-beam owner’s suite with an expansive bathroom.

Above deck, the 780 Adventure is an entertainer’s dream. The main deck is adorned with a sheltered aft cockpit perfect for social gatherings. The oversized aft ‘Sports Locker’ can function as a dive centre, while the bow has sufficient space for a crane, a 6m tender, and a pair of Jet Skis.

In a world where luxury often comes with concessions, the Outer Reef 780 Adventure is an exception, uncompromising on both opulence and functionality. It is a testament to the continuing thrill of voyaging the seas – the perfect harmony of comfort and adventure.

title: A 55-Year Odyssey of Unmatched Luxury and Tenacity: Exploring the Range Rover Legacy
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A 55-Year Odyssey of Unmatched Luxury and Tenacity: Exploring the Range Rover Legacy
summary: Unveiling the enduring allure of Range Rover, a trailblazing titan of the auto industry, celebrated for its unique blend of luxury and rugged off-road proficiency.
body: For over half a century, Range Rover has charted an unconventional course that’s been unswerving in its uniqueness and unexcelled in progressive innovation. The embodiment of a visionary concept, it emerged in 1970 as a groundbreaking invention - a luxurious SUV in an era when the term was still novel. For five decades it has reigned over the intersections of premium automotive design and audacious off-road dexterity.

Born from the imaginative mind of Charles Spencer King, Range Rover crafted a new norm in vehicular comfort and capability. Its inception marked the creation of a two-door 4x4, featherlight with a V8 engine, adopting a cutting-edge silhouette that soon set the blueprint for future generations of luxury SUVs.

Range Rover’s rich heritage lies in its uncanny ability to evolve continually. Each iteration redefines the meaning of a luxury off-road SUV, always pushing the thresholds of comfort, competency, and aesthetic design. With breakthrough suspension mechanisms and aluminium architecture, it transformed into next-generation personalisation and advanced electrified propulsion. It has been unwavering in its leadership, yet true to its inimitable character.

The fifth generation embodies the pinnacle of the modernist ideology – a testament to minimalistic grandeur. With clean surfaces, concealed lighting, signature silhouette and every proportion meticulously crafted, it exudes an elegance that is both eternal and innovative. The intentional lines and extensive detailing, from its laser-welded roof to the seamless waistline finisher, elevate its aura of tranquillity and power.

title: The Solent Gears Up for the Return of the Poker Run – A New 2025 Spectacle
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: The Return of the Poker Run – A New 2025 Spectacle
imageCaption: The UK Powerboating Club - Solent Poker Run
summary: After years in the wilderness, one of powerboating’s most entertaining traditions is roaring back to life on the South Coast. The UK Powerboating Club has confirmed that the inaugural Solent Powerboat Poker Run will be staged on 25 August 2025 — and already the buzz is spreading from Cowes to the Hamble.
body: The Solent Gears Up for the Return of the Poker Run – A New 2025 Spectacle

HAMPSHIRE, UK – After years in the wilderness, one of powerboating’s most entertaining traditions is roaring back to life on the South Coast. The UK Powerboating Club has confirmed that the inaugural Solent Powerboat Poker Run will be staged on 25 August 2025 — and already the buzz is spreading from Cowes to the Hamble.

For those new to the idea, a poker run is not about speed or horsepower alone. It’s a nautical treasure hunt, a test of navigation and seamanship laced with friendly rivalry and a good dose of fun. Crews steer their boats to a series of checkpoints scattered across the Solent, collecting a playing card at each stop. At the finish line, the best poker hand takes home the glory and prizes — but the real winners are those who savour the course, the camaraderie on the water, and the parties ashore.
This year’s event will wind through a carefully chosen route that blends classic Solent landmarks with hidden gems. Boats will check in at:
Yarmouth – the bustling harbour with its traditional waterfront pubs.
Buckler’s Hard – where a premium BBQ lunch will be laid out along the historic Beaulieu River.
Newtown Creek – the Solent’s serene backwater, a haven for wildlife and a spectacular checkpoint.
Lymington – with its lively marinas and salt marsh approaches.
The Needles – the Solent’s most iconic natural landmark and the dramatic turning mark for many a race.
the party continues afloat with a floating after-party at Hurst Castle, complete with a live DJ, sundowners, and views across the Solent that are as unbeatable as the soundtrack.

Entries are capped at just 25 boats, with around 125 participants expected. That means exclusivity, manageable logistics, and a chance to keep the atmosphere tight-knit. Whether you’re running a high-performance offshore beast or a more modest day cruiser, the emphasis is on participation and enjoyment, not sheer horsepower.

Beyond the spectacle, the Solent Poker Run has a serious purpose. Every pound raised will go directly to support the Royal National Lifeboat Institution (RNLI) and their life-saving work. Few organisations are held in such affection by the boating community, and the Poker Run provides the perfect blend of entertainment and fundraising for a cause that benefits everyone who takes to the water.
Event Director Pablo Portela summed up the mood:

“We’re thrilled to bring the poker run format back to the Solent. It’s a fantastic way to showcase our boating community, enjoy one of the UK’s best watersports playgrounds, and raise vital funds for the RNLI.”

Boat owners are urged to secure their spot early. With only 25 places available, demand is expected to outstrip supply. Registration is already open via ukpowerboatingclub.co.uk/pokerrun . So, on the August Bank Holiday weekend, expect the Solent to sparkle with spray, sound, and a festival atmosphere as the Poker Run tradition makes its long-awaited comeback. With cards to draw, checkpoints to reach, and stories to tell, this will be a day of powerboating where winning the hand is just part of the fun.
tags: The Return of the Poker Run

title: Embark on Water-borne Weekends: A Deep-dive Review of 2025’s Top-performing Weekend Motor Yachts
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Embark on Water-borne Weekends: A Deep-dive Review of 2025’s Top-performing Weekend Motor Yachts
summary: Ready for aquatic escapades? Discover, in this realistic appraisal, the best weekend motor yachts of 2025, combining comfort and speed to promise remarkable sea adventures.
body: Embracing motor yachts for weekend escapes is like introducing two old friends, speed and comfort, born separately in the realm of marine adventures, and broadening their horizons in a harmonious union. Such amalgamation unlocks a new level of freedom on the vast expanses of water, drafting the blueprint for ventures that are further, stays that are longer, invoking a unique taste of independence. However, in the vast sea of possibilities, determining the perfect harmony between performance and practicality can be like finding a needle in the proverbial haystack. But fret not, this year's comprehensive tests bring forth suitable contenders. Together, we navigate and explore family cruisers and sportscruisers alike, standing out in the fusion of design and innovation, reflected in the quality promising the best returns on investment. From the lush assembly of this year’s fleet, the Windy SR40 emerges as a game-changer. As a practically-minded weekender, it cleverly blends the thrill of Windy with sufficient protection embracing all seasons and climates. While trading-off a tad beauty and driving engagement vis-à-vis Windy's open sportsboats, SR40 compensates with versatility, especially with the neat sliding side doors. If your sea voyage is comfortable with a single cabin and slightly premium pricing, SR40 successfully delivers the best of both worlds. Then there is the Beneteau Antares 9, making its mark with versatility, despite lacking in size, speed, and glamour. Its winning move is not focusing on a single aspect, but doing a bit of everything. It caters to a crowd of ten and sleeps six - a family delight, with an array of indoor and outdoor seating options. Each coastal cruise promises manageability with a hint of sophistication, at an enticing starting price. Multiple add-ons align it with users’ needs, gravitating the actual cost towards €200,000. Mindful of the size constraints, the value this hard-working entry-level family boat extends is undeniably hard to match. The lengthy analysis concludes with the Fjord 39 XL, yet to be fully discovered, hinting at a promising blend of style, performance, and luxury. So revision your weekend escapes, as we reveal the finest seafaring vessels, promising unforgettable adventures on the aquatic horizon.

title: Flybridge yacht
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Flybridge yacht
summary: Flybridge yacht, often referred to as flying bridge yachts, are a standout category of motor yachts defined by their elevated upper deck—the flybridge—positioned above the main helm and living areas. This design, tracing its roots back to before World War II, has become a hallmark of luxury boating, particularly in warm climates where open-air cruising is a priority. The flybridge serves as a secondary helm station,
body: Driving a flybridge yacht is a unique experience, largely due to its elevated helm position, which provides exceptional visibility—a key advantage over other yacht designs like express cruisers or sport yachts. The flybridge helm, typically situated 10 to 20 feet above the waterline depending on the yacht’s size, offers a commanding 360-degree view of the surroundings. This height is particularly beneficial when navigating busy waters, such as during the Monaco Grand Prix in Port Hercule (happening this week, May 23–25, 2025 - https://oldseadogs.com/news/formula-1-monaco-grand-prix-2025/ ), where yachts crowd the harbour. The unobstructed sight lines allow captains to spot other vessels, buoys, and obstacles like floating debris far earlier than from a lower helm, reducing the risk of collisions and enhancing safety.

The elevated position also improves situational awareness during docking, a notoriously tricky manoeuvre in tight marinas. For example, docking a 50-foot flybridge yacht in a bustling spot like Wroxham on the Norfolk Broads becomes more manageable when you can see the entire length of the vessel and its proximity to the quay. The flybridge helm is often equipped with advanced navigation tools—think Raymarine chart-plotters, VHF radios, and bow thruster controls—mirroring the lower helm for seamless operation. On larger models, joystick controls, like those found on Azimut or Princess yachts, make handling a breeze, even for less experienced drivers, allowing precise movements in confined spaces.

Flybridge yachts also excel in handling and stability, thanks to their hull designs. Most feature planing or modified-V hulls, optimised for cruising speeds of 20–30 knots, with some models like the Ferretti 670 hitting 32 knots. The deep draft and wide beam—averaging 16 to 20 feet—provide a stable platform, reducing roll in choppy waters like the Solent during Cowes Week (August 2–8, 2025). Twin diesel engines, typically ranging from 800 to 2,000 horsepower, deliver the power needed for long-range cruising, while the weight distribution, despite the higher centre of gravity, is carefully balanced to maintain seaworthiness. However, smaller flybridge yachts under 40 feet can feel top-heavy in rough seas, so size and hull design are critical considerations.

Visibility is where flybridge yachts truly shine. The elevated helm offers an unparalleled vantage point, often likened to standing on a rooftop deck. From this height, a captain can see over smaller boats, spot distant hazards, and monitor the yacht’s wake, which is crucial for adjusting speed in no-wake zones or crowded anchorages like those near the Amalfi Coast during a summer charter. The 360-degree view also aids in spotting marine life—imagine cruising the Caribbean post-hurricane season (November to April) and catching sight of dolphins off Virgin Gorda from the flybridge.

The flybridge helm is typically designed with ergonomics in mind, featuring wraparound windshields or hardtops for weather protection, though smaller models may lack full enclosures, exposing drivers to the elements. On luxury models like the Princess F55, visibility is enhanced by large glass panels and minimal obstructions, with digital displays providing real-time data on wind speed, depth, and radar. For sport-fishing flybridge yachts, such as those from Grady-White, the elevated position doubles as a lookout for fish, with anglers using the height to scan for birds or baitfish schools—a tactic often employed during tournaments in the BVI.

However, visibility can have drawbacks. The height can make low bridges a challenge—yachts over 50 feet often have a 15- to 20-foot air draft, requiring careful route planning in areas like the Norfolk Broads, where Wroxham Bridge has a clearance of just 2.2 meters. Night driving also demands extra caution, as the elevated position can make it harder to judge distances to unlit objects, though modern LED lighting and thermal cameras on brands like Sunseeker mitigate this.
Several manufacturers dominate the flybridge yacht market, each bringing distinct strengths:
Known for sleek, modern designs, Azimut’s flybridge range, like the Azimut 60 (59 feet, 1,150 HP), combines Italian craftsmanship with tech like IoT dashboards. Prices start around $1.5 million.
Based in Plymouth, Princess offers luxury flybridge models like the F55 (57 feet, 1,800 HP), known for performance and elegance, costing $2–$3 million new.
Poole-based Sunseeker, a favourite at events like Cowes Week, produces flybridge yachts like the 76 Yacht (77 feet, 2,400 HP), blending speed (32 knots) and luxury, priced at $4 million.
Ferretti’s flybridge models, such as the Ferretti 670 (67 feet, 2,400 HP), emphasize opulent design and tech, with prices around $2.5 million.
Part of Groupe Beneteau, Prestige offers models like the 590 (61 feet, 1,200 HP), balancing affordability and luxury at $1.8 million.

Under Brunswick Boat Group, Sea Ray’s flybridge line, like the 520 Fly (52 feet, 1,200 HP), caters to the mass market, starting at $1.2 million. Flybridge yachts, with their superior visibility, versatile driving experience, and luxurious amenities, remain a top choice for those seeking to elevate their time on the water in 2025, whether cruising the Mediterranean or racing in the Solent.

title: Discover Hargrave's Future of Custom Yachting: The Dynamic New 36m Model
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover Hargrave's Future of Custom Yachting: The Dynamic New 36m Model
summary: Hargrave Custom Yachts breaks new ground with its innovative 36m model in the 120 Series, a masterpiece of contemporary Italian design.
body: Hargrave’s innovative approach has been taken to new levels with the unveiling of a stunning addition to their 120 Series. The 36.5-metre model is a true departure from the American shipbuilder's conventional portfolio and showcases their collaborative spirit through its partnership with Italy's renowned designer, Patrizio Facheris.

Facheris is synonymous with flowing lines and modern design aesthetics and his signature is evident in the yacht’s luxurious look. But, the yacht's charm is not all about aesthetics; it epitomises the future of custom yachting, setting the pace for fully bespoke models.

The yacht is constructed with carbon-reinforced E-glass epoxy composite for optimal resilience, with RINA Pleasure standards denoting the premium class. Exterior decks are hand-laid in Burmese teak, offering the choice of non-skid paint for rough sea conditions, while the hull and superstructure are coated with AWLGRIP and International treatments for durability.

Coupled with Hargrave Superyachts' launch of the 38-metre Hargrave 125 earlier this year in Antalya, Turkey, it’s clear that the future of custom yachting as envisaged by Hargrave is here. No longer are luxury yachts restricted to traditional designs, and buyers now have the chance of sailing in a yacht that not only meets their performance criteria, but also reflects their unique style.

title: William J. Healey, Co-founder and Past President of Viking Yachts, Leaves a Legacy in the Maritime Industry
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: William J. Healey, Co-founder and Past President of Viking Yachts, Leaves a Legacy in the Maritime Industry
summary: The nautical world mourns the passing of William 'Bill' J. Healey, former president and co-founder of renowned shipyard Viking Yachts, at age 97.
body: The sailing community is bidding farewell to one of its pioneering figures, William 'Bill' J. Healey. A titan in the shipbuilding sphere, Healey served as the past President of the esteemed American shipyard, Viking Yachts. His passion for boat-building and excellence in design are etched in the firm's successful history, and charges the future course for Viking Yachts.

William Healey passed away at the age of 97, on August 14, 2025. His demise was peaceful, surrounded by his loved ones in New Jersey. His departure was due to prolonged complications following a stroke. Yet, while he may no longer be present physically, his effusive spirit continues to helm Viking Yachts, a leading name in the industry that he remained ingrained throughout his life.

title: An Icon gets Reinvented: The Itama 54 Premieres at Cannes Yachting Festival, Promising Exceptional Seakeeping and Timeless Design
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: An Icon gets Reinvented: The Itama 54 Premieres at Cannes Yachting Festival, Promising Exceptional Seakeeping and Timeless Design
summary: Unveiled to breadths of awe at Cannes Yachting Festival, the brand new Itama 54 marks an exciting evolution in yachting design, blending traditional charm with nautical innovation.
body: Rare and precious, like an Italian blue moon, a brand-new addition to the Itama fleet arrived at this year's Cannes Yachting Festival –the Itama 54. The yacht bathed in an aura of intrigue, nestled between the popular Itama 45 and 62 models, and regularly attracting admirers keen to admire its enigmatic charm. The design of the Itama 54 pays homage to its esteemed founders, showcasing the classic, timeless aesthetic that has become a hallmark of the brand, while also sporting new innovative features.

Other firsts for the Itama brand include full-length side glazing in the topsides, a dynamic reverse-angled transom, and a new dual cockpit layout. This layout allows guests to bask in the shelter of the wraparound windscreen while sailing, and then sprawl out in the aft dinette and sun-pad when at anchor - an elegant blend of functionality and luxury.

Underneath the aesthetic charm, the hulking power of MAN engines propels the Itama 54. While these limit the top speed to 37 knots, potential owners can rest easy knowing that the focus for Itama has always been cruising comfort and imperious seakeeping. Backed with such robust engines, the Itama 54 can easily hold its head high against waves that would send most other yachts scurrying for the marina.

In summary, the Itama 54 is not just a yacht, it's a statement: testament to timeless design, robust power, and the joy of innovation. Debuting at the Cannes Yachting Festival, it already has boat enthusiasts vying for their piece of the prestige and charm that comes with the Itama name.

body: Stewart Campbell, an esteemed figure in the marine sphere, has taken on the reigns as the new Managing Director of BOAT International, in a step that underscores the ongoing advancement of Informa's luxury and lifestyle sector, Informa Prestige.

Taking his career up another notch, Campbell's appointment to the helm represents not just another job change, but a fresh chapter in the exciting narrative of BOAT International, a leading voice in the boating world for aficionados and professionals alike. Aligning strong leadership with an industry-renowned platform is likely to spark an era of sustained progress and success.

As Campbell sails into this new role, a sense of anticipation wafts in the sea air. It's a moment that foreshadows not just a change in leadership but an exciting evolution for BOAT International and everyone associated with this prestigious brand.

summary: Sailing enthusiasts recently rendezvoused at Hythe and Weecher Sailing Clubs, participating in spectacular championship races, showcasing their exceptional navigation skills and sportsmanship.
body: At the Hythe and Saltwood Sailing Club, the 7th round of the British Contender Association Travellers' Trophy took place amidst much anticipation and fervour. The participants, notably those who had recently returned from the breathtaking World Championship at Malcesine on Lake Garda, were treated to favourable sailing conditions, with an ideal breeze for launch and recovery.

Adrian Smith, Simon Mussell, and Ed Presley led the pack in the initial phase of the race which started under a slightly overcast sky. Compelling tussles for the lead ensued with potential infringements raising eyebrows. The race witnessed thrills and spills, with some sailors navigating the wrong way, but Smith managed to sail straight into second place. Though placings fluctuated, the skippers docking in the first five retained their positions until the end - culminating in an exhilarating finish.

title: SailGP locks in Sassnitz, Rio and Portsmouth for multi-year calendar shake-up
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: SailGP locks in Sassnitz, Rio and Portsmouth for multi-year calendar shake-up
summary: SailGP — the fastest show afloat — has confirmed a major three-season commitment for Germany, making Sassnitz a fixture in 2026 and 2027 after a sell-out debut where Deutsche Bank’s home team won race one and ROCKWOOL Denmark hit a record-breaking 103.93 km/h.
body: It’s a big statement. Germany now sits alongside a clutch of long-term calendar anchors as SailGP seeks stability, local connection, and repeat impact. Perth stays on the map through 2028, New York returns in 2026 and 2027, and Rio de Janeiro steps in as a new, multi-year stop — delivering foiling drama to one of the most iconic waterfronts in the world. Bermuda is locked through 2028, with May 2027 dates confirmed.

Closer to home, Portsmouth will roar again with 25-26 July 2026 and 24-25 July 2027 set in stone after 20,000 fans crammed the Solent shoreline this summer. Dubai and Abu Dhabi remain key pillars of the Middle East programme, strengthening the tour’s year-round global spread.

“We’re building legacy, not one-off spectacles,” said SailGP boss Sir Russell Coutts. “Sassnitz proves how a powerful debut can become a long-term story. These commitments give us depth, impact, and the chance to return year after year.”

Coutts points to Portsmouth as proof: nine in ten fans travelled from outside the city, half stayed three nights or more, and local hotels and restaurants cashed in. Add broadcast reach into 212 territories and it’s clear repeat venues gain more than epic racing — they gain global attention and lasting local value.

The 2026 calendar is now set: Perth, Sydney, Auckland, Rio, Bermuda, New York, Halifax, Portsmouth, Sassnitz, Saint-Tropez, Geneva, Spain, Dubai, and Abu Dhabi. The 2027 line-up already locks in Perth, Bermuda, New York, Portsmouth, Germany, Rio, and Dubai.
Meanwhile, the show rolls on: from Sassnitz to Saint-Tropez in September, then to Geneva for Switzerland’s first-ever SailGP stop. Tickets are already flying.
