title: Gladiator Joins the Fray as Flying Jenny Steals the Show
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Cowes week update 2025
summary: Big boats. Big stakes. Bigger delays. The Britannia Cup showdown saw Tony Langley’s Gladiator muscle into Class Zero, joining the heavyweight fleet on a day when patience proved the sailor’s greatest virtue.
body: Light airs forced hours of postponement across the board. Black Group finally got away at 1300. White Group? They sat. And sat. Not until 1415 did the Squadron cannon fire for the SB20s — a tight start and a recall for the over-eager. Sportsboats followed, with Jo Richards’ Tigger punching out first, chased by Annabel up the beat to Newtown East. Despite Tigger being dwarfed by her fleetmates, the RS21-CR held her own.

Out on Committee Vessel 1’s start line, the big guns in IRC Zero and Cape 31s surged west toward Tuakana Construction, Hamstead Ledge, and beyond — wind finally teasing out enough power to light up the course.

Gladiator stormed home first in IRC Zero, chased by Braveheart. But when the time corrections settled, it was the Cape 31 Flying Jenny that soared — besting 23 of the highest-rated boats in the regatta to lift the Britannia Cup. A mighty win for Sandy Askew and crew, with Amp Lifi second and Gladiator rounding out the podium.

In IRC2, youth and experience clashed bow-to-bow. Yes! skippered by Adam Gosling — and joined by 14-year-old son Leo — duelled hard with Jack Rabbit and Leon. It was Jack Rabbit that nailed the final hoist and claimed the win on corrected time. Leo’s helm skills, honed in the ILCA and at the Optimist Worlds, marked him as one to watch.

Youth Day at Cowes Everywhere, young sailors were proving their mettle. In the Sonars, 17-year-old Will Bradley and his all-under-20 crew sailed Cowes Match Racing Blue into second, keeping Bertie honest. The starts were sharp. The racing tighter still.

Jack Hartley helmed a Sunbeam keelboat for the first time aboard Osprey, describing the technical challenge of balancing heel and trim as “a big shift from dinghies — but brilliant.” His crew? Georgina Patterson and Luke Cross — young, smart, and unfazed.

In the XODs, familiar names led — Astralita’s John Tremlett, Tim Copsey, and Fraser Graham. But fresh faces were making waves, too. Racing XL under the Youth Bursary Scheme were Abby Hire, Alex Paton, and siblings Kate and Tom Whamby from Lymington. They finished 10th — top youth boat, and in light airs, it was their kind of day.
As Tom said: “We didn’t have a lane, so we tacked early into shore. Played the shifts. Rode the tide. Then the run to the finish — we were glad they shortened!”
Sailing the X? “You move the tiller and wait,” laughed Kate. “Then she says ‘fine, we’ll go’ — and off you go.”
Olympic hopeful Arthur Farley was campaigning in the J/70s mini-series. A mid-race collision cut short his Cowes, but he’s got bigger goals on the horizon.

Tomorrow brings stronger breeze and a return to classic Solent punch-ups. South-westerlies are set to gust into the high twenties. The XODs, Mermaids, and Victories head to the Committee Vessel. And for spectators ashore — a Royal Navy display at 7pm, featuring a helicopter and Fairey Swordfish flypast.

title: Centro Velico Punta Ala to Light Up with European Windsurfer Class Championships 2025
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Centro Velico Punta Ala to Light Up with European Windsurfer Class Championships 2025
summary: From 9 to 14 September 2025, Europe’s finest windsurfing talents will gather in Punta Ala, engaging in riveting competition and delivering a spectacular sporting event.
body: Windsurfing enthusiasts from around the globe are set to converge on Centro Velico Punta Ala for the Windsurfer Class European Championships 2025. This highly-anticipated event is ripe with promise, boasting registration of over 170 athletes from 16 nations. The Championship is more than a competition; it's a jubilant festival of shared passion, uniting generations of windsurfing devotees. The emerald Gulf of Follonica will quicken with the stirring hive of fluorescent sails, representing nations, families, and individuals unified by a love for the open water. The event promises a perfect blend of exhilaration, competition, and camaraderie in the stunning Tuscan coastal backdrop. The participating sporting legends will share the open water with budding talents, professionals, and amateurs. The event recognizes no hierarchy; every participant is jointly celebrated, enhancing the spirit of community and providing a rare, inspiring spectacle of dedication and skill on every level. This esteemed championship also signifies a critical juncture in windsurfing's international season, laying a pathway to the Windsurfer World Championships—a prime opportunity for contenders to challenge globally-renowned talents. The format comprises four disciplines: 8 course races, 1 slalom, 1 marathon, and a freestyle exhibition—the heart-pounding core of the event where consistency, strategy, and tactical prowess are tried and tested. The history of windsurfing echoes in this event, reminding of its birth in the late 1960s, its incredible upsurge in the 1980s, and the tradition carried forward today. At the heart of it stands the Windsurfer, the most iconic board in windsurfing history, its design and effectiveness perpetually preserved, signifying both tradition and innovation. This passion for the Windsurfer and the waterways will light up Punta Ala come September, delivering an unforgettable celebration of the sport.

title: Superyacht and Refit Giant MB92 Group Welcomes Remy Millott as Non-executive Board Member
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Superyacht and Refit Giant MB92 Group Welcomes Remy Millott as Non-executive Board Member
summary: Remy Millott, CEO of global superyacht painting and supply firm GYG Limited, has joined the board of MB92 Group, a leading superyacht refit and repair specialist.
body: MB92 Group, the esteemed specialist in the realm of superyacht refit and repair, recently made the notable addition of GYG Limited's CEO, Remy Millott, to its board of directors as a non-executive member. This move comes in the wake of MB92 Group's acquisition of GYG, a global leader in superyacht painting and supply, earlier this year.

This move signifies an enhanced collaboration between these two giants in the yachting industry. Despite the acquisition and the inclusion of GYG's CEO on MB92's board, both companies will continue operations as separate entities. This noteworthy addition can potentially pave the way for key strategic alliances and furthering the development and progress in the superyacht service industry.

While the companies continue to strengthen their respective footprints in the industry, the shared expertise promises potential growth and revolutionizing contributions in the superyacht service segment. They're redefining the business of blissful sailing, one board meeting at a time.

title: Sharp Form on Display as Dolan Prepares for Defending His Historic Title in the 2025 Solitaire du Figaro
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Sharp Form on Display as Dolan Prepares for Defending His Historic Title in the 2025 Solitaire du Figaro
summary: Irish offshore sailor Tom Dolan seizes the runner-up spot in the Fig'Armor, showcasing powerful precision as he prepares for the Solitaire du Figaro.
body: The Fig'Armor race, with its intense competition and challenging conditions, has established its landmark as the warm-up race for the Solitaire du Figaro. This year, Irish offshore sailor Tom Dolan has delivered an outstanding performance by securing second place. His achievement comes as an astute demonstration of readiness to defend his historic title in the Solitaire du Figaro, slated to commence on September 7. Teaming up with French sailor Gaston Morvan aboard the Figaro 3 Kingspan, Dolan purveyed exceptional form, completing a gruelling 200 nautical mile course in a blistering one day, 21 hours, and 3 minutes timeframe. He arrived a mere half an hour behind the victor, sending an uncompromising message of intent to his competition. Much more than a race, the Fig'Armor offers sailors a crucible to fine-tune boat handling, tactical decision-making, and onboard systems, putting them through their paces in anticipation of the major event. 'The Solitaire is a completely different beast, it's long, relentless, and solo,' Dolan commented, acknowledging the hard road ahead. 'This was a good final test. The learning never stops, especially after my few months in the IMOCA. Now, I'm poised to spend the upcoming weeks for further fine-tuning. I'm ready for the challenge.' Now, with support from Kingspan, Dolan's long-term partner in sustainable high-performance, the focus has shifted towards the final preparations. It's a step closer towards his anticipated return to what is widely considered the toughest proving ground in solo racing.

title: Engines Over Canvas – The Lymington Challenge Powers In
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Engines Over Canvas – The Lymington Challenge Powers In
summary: Sail takes a back seat this weekend as the offshore racers roll in for Round 4 of the 2025 UKOPRA Championship — and this one’s set to be a belter. The Lymington Challenge kicks off Saturday, August 9th, with a fleet of 15 boats battling it out in the fast-flowing waters of the Western Solent. Expect noise, speed, and a proper offshore showdown between Hamstead Ledge and the Needles.
body: Crews from across the UK, Sweden, and Spain are lining up in Classes 1, 1L, 2 and 3. The course loops the Solent’s finest backdrops — 78 and 62 nautical mile races, depending on class — with the start/finish line north of Newtown Creek. The racers will loop past coastal vantage points up to four times, giving fans multiple chances to watch the action thunder by.

Championship leaders Double Trouble (Eastwood Racing, with Gary Aldington at the helm) are looking to cement their position at the top, but they’ll have to fend off heavyweight challengers. Silverline, last year’s champ and multi-time Cowes-Torquay winner, is back with a point to prove. Sture Vodka are flying the Swedish flag, and Spanish outfit Smokin Aces are finally entering their first race of the year — father-and-son duo Chris and James Dodge behind the controls of their bright red Skater. And just when things couldn’t get hotter, Laa Laa Falcon - Multispark has dropped in late. Their ferocious yellow Fountain hull, always a crowd-pleaser, is known for its brutal engine growl and breakneck straight-line pace.
In Class 1L, Black Ball Racing and Piston Broke will be scrapping for points as the championship begins to tighten. With one eye on the final round at Portland Bill, every position counts.

It’s neck-and-neck here. Both lead teams are running identical XS Sunseeker hulls with matching muscle under the deck. Team 25 Sunseeker (Welham, Bontoft, Raven) claimed the flag on their race debut — and are clearly not here to make up numbers. But True Blue, the Scottish stalwarts, won’t go down quietly. Expect elbows out and throttles pinned.

Three sub-classes, six entries, and more stories than a boatyard pub. In 3C, New Kids on the Dock — a fresh pairing of Elliott Holman and Richard Watson — will debut their classic Mannerfelt. 3D sees Carpe Diem’s Winkworth and Flewin bringing the only rib in the field, looking to punch above their weight.

And in 3E? It’s all about Oblivion. The silver cat, steered by rally ace Marcus Dodd and Sean Girdler, is hunting its fourth straight win. Behind them, Renegade, Blast from the Past, and The Nicotine Machine — all still in the mix, especially if Oblivion finally flinches. Watch for Nicotine Machine, beautifully finished and testing well. If she holds together, driver Josh Warmington-Brown could upset the leaderboard in style.
Shamrock Quay, Southampton
12:00 – Boats depart Southampton for muster
13:00 – Green flag at Hamstead Ledge
17:00 – Podium at Shamrock Quay
Fort Victoria
Hurst Castle
Headon Warren
The Needles Battery

This one has all the ingredients: international boats, returning champions, late entries, and title hopes on the line. If you like your weekends loud, fast and covered in salt spray — The Lymington Challenge is where you need to be.

title: Tracing the Course of Women in Competitive Sailing: International Championships and Qualifying Races
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Honouring Feminine Sailing Excellence on the Global Stage
summary: An exhilarating narrative of women's ascent in competitive sailing, navigating two key events with some of the sport's most accomplished female skippers.
body: The waves ebb and surge, beckoning the resolute female skippers steering their yachts towards set goals in two noteworthy maritime events. We turn our introspective glass on New York Yacht Club International Women's Championship and the WASZP Games, highlighting the strides women have made in competitive sailing. The New York Yacht Club International Women's Championship, carving out a niche for femininity on the high seas, welcomes sailors from all nations. It’s here that Dominique Provoyeur, a seasoned representative from South Africa, plans to assemble an all-female, South African crew. Provoyeur, an Olympic veteran, completes her narrative with triumphant chapters in endurance racing, embodying the multifaceted strength of womanhood. The Championship, spanning from September 12 -19, 2026, uses a fleet of 20 sporty, powerful IC37s; a testament to the dynamic symbiosis of technical precision and athleticism. Switching seas, the SailGP WASZP Grand Final 2026 in Sydney stages an epic contest: The WASZP Women's Sprint Championship. Here, precision, boat handling, and tactics are the coveted triad, determining the fate of the sailors fighting for the top two spaces. The excitement is palpable as competitors launch shoulder to shoulder in the first race, skilfully harnessing the light winds for victory. This is more than a recounting of riveting races, it’s a narrative of transformation. It depicts a journey peppered with bronze and gold victories, showcasing talented females like Dominique Proyoveur and Lijia "Lily" Xu shaking up the traditionally male-dominated world of sailing. These platforms are instrumental in encouraging female sailors and enkindling their dreams of sailing at a higher level. Together, they chart the path for more women to command the helm, shaping an inclusive future for sailing.

title: Newcastle to Dominate Australian Maritime Scene with First Superyacht Marina
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Newcastle to Dominate Australian Maritime Scene with First Superyacht Marina
summary: Australia is set to upgrade its maritime landscape as Newcastle heralds the advent of its first superyacht marina.
body: Imagine an integrated hub of naval sophistication and luxury tourism, capable of generating significant economic proceeds and creating employment opportunities galore. The picture depicted isn't of Monte Carlo or Costa del Sol - instead, it's Australia's very own, Newcastle. This coastal city is set to be the toast of the Australian maritime world, with Newcastle Cruising Yacht Club (NCYC) announcing plans of constructing its first superyacht marina. This premier maritime venture comes to life courtesy of a substantial $5 million funding by the NSW Government through the Regional Economic Development and Community Infrastructure Program.

The superyacht marina stands as a symbol of Newcastle's progressive maritime economy, seamlessly aligning with its rich 200 years of seafaring history. However, the primary appeal is the economic ripple effect it triggers. Interestingly, less than 10% of superyacht expenditure is attributed to berthing, while the lion's share of over 90% is reinvested into local economies via marine services, luxury travel, dining, and accommodation. Extrapolating this, a single 55-meter superyacht contributes over $5.6 million annually in regional expenditure.

Venue convenience and the potential for generating high-skilled jobs are key factors driving this initiative. Growing congestion in Sydney's superyacht facilities grants Newcastle a significant strategic advantage. As a designated customs port of entry, the city is an enticing pick for vessels scouting for alternate bases. With the groundwork for the superyacht facility set to kickoff, Newcastle is all geared up to be the new favourite stop for the global superyacht fleet.

NCYC's audacious initiative could well be the dawn of a new chapter in Australia's maritime story. It positions the country's maritime industry at the vanguard of luxury maritime tourism. This could indeed position Newcastle as a stellar world-class destination for high-end maritime tourism and take the country’s maritime legacy up a notch. In the unfurling canvas of global maritime tourism, Australia is poised to be the artist, and Newcastle, its masterpiece.

title: Nía Suardíaz Fights to Defend Her Reign Against Mar de Arce in the Gran Canaria Wingfoil World Cup Showdown
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Nía Suardíaz Fights to Defend Her Reign Against Mar de Arce in the Gran Canaria Wingfoil World Cup Showdown
summary: As the Gran Canaria Wingfoil World Cup hits the water, it's an epic contest between Nía Suardíaz, the reigning champ, and her formidable rival Mar de Arce.
body: Gems of the beautiful east coast of Gran Canaria are setting the stage for a showdown of epic proportions in the realm of Wingfoil Freestyle. Who will snatch the title of the World Champion in the Gran Canaria GWA Wingfoil World Cup 2025? This prestigious event is poised to conclude a thrilling world tour after the unfortunate cancellation of the Brazil tour stop.

Pushing Suardíaz to defend her laurels is another Tarifa native, Mar de Arce. Fresh off a successful season including a critical victory at Fuerteventura, de Arce’s career is on a high tide. She stands firmly as the prime candidate to knock Suardíaz off the pedestal, promising an adrenaline-fuelled contest.

Adding to the suspense, 15-year-old German prodigy Marie Schlittenbauer stirred the waters with her first tour victory in Fuerteventura, making her a wildcard in the upcoming championship. Schlittenbauer could catapult her standings with another win, contingent on the performance of her prime rivals. France's Manon Dupé, currently third in line, is another potential titan ready to unleash a surprise.

In the lead up to the ultimate showdown in Gran Canaria, both Suardíaz and de Arce have proved their mettle, gaining 2,450 and 2,290 points respectively in the 2025 world tour. Whoever claims the top spot in Gran Canaria will indeed be able to write their name in the annals of Wingfoil Freestyle history.

title: Rum, Race, and Glory: Ninety-Nine Years of the Bacardi Cup
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: The Bacardi Cup
summary: There aren’t many sailing events that can claim near-century status with their class, culture, and charisma still fully intact. The Bacardi Cup does it all with a wink and a wedge of lime. Now entering its 99th year, the Bacardi Cup is one of the most iconic, enduring regattas in the world—and one of the very few where the drinks sponsor has been onboard since the start.
body: First staged in Havana, Cuba in 1927, the event was born out of sunshine, sailing, and Bacardi’s desire to blend sport with social connection. It’s been hosted in Miami since 1962, but the spirit—pun fully intended—remains true to its Caribbean roots: warm water, warm people, and razor-sharp racing.

This is Star Class country, and don’t let the elegant lines of those two-man keelboats fool you—the competition is fierce. Year after year, the world’s sailing elite converge on Biscayne Bay: America’s Cup legends, Olympic medallists, Volvo Ocean Race heroes, and world champions all line up alongside die-hard amateurs and weekend warriors. It’s that rare, magic mix where a Corinthian crew can cross tacks with Olympic royalty—and maybe even beat them to the top mark.

Winning the Bacardi Cup isn’t just about lifting silverware. The Bacardi Cup (for the helm) and Tito Bacardi Cup (for the crew) are among the most coveted awards in one-design sailing. They represent mastery of the Star Class, stamina over a demanding week-long series, and a place in the annals of one of sailing’s most prestigious traditions. The Bacardi Cup isn’t just a regatta—it’s a rite of passage.

And make no mistake: the level of racing is brutal. Biscayne Bay offers a challenging cocktail of flat water, building sea breeze, and tricky shifts off the shoreline. With a week-long format and no discard, there’s no room for error. Blow one race and you’re out of contention. Nail a consistent set and you’re in with a shout—but only if you can handle the pressure.
As the Bacardi Cup grew in popularity and prestige, a natural evolution occurred. Other high-performance fleets wanted in on the action. And so the Bacardi Invitational Regatta was born.

Now running alongside the Star Class each March, the Bacardi Invitational offers racing for J/70s, Melges 24s, VX-Ones, and Viper 640s. It’s fast, fun, and fiercely contested. With classes drawn from North America, Europe, and South America, the event has become one of the most international in the sport. The starting lines are thick with rock star tacticians, top-tier amateur helms, and boats bristling with talent.

But it’s not just about who wins. The beauty of the Bacardi Invitational is its atmosphere. There’s a relaxed camaraderie ashore, backed by seriously slick event management and world-class race committees on the water. And then there’s the post-race socials—open bars, Havana-style live music, impromptu dock parties, and endless tales of glory and disaster. The regatta has mastered the formula: world-class competition with a warm, rum-fuelled soul.

It’s hard to overstate just how good the conditions are. Biscayne Bay is a natural amphitheatre for racing: clear water, reliable sea breeze, and wide-open space without open ocean brutality. It's a bucket-list racecourse for a reason. Sailors love it not just for its beauty, but for the fair but tactical racing it produces.

Add to that the support of Miami’s yacht club scene and you’ve got something pretty special. The Coral Reef Yacht Club, Biscayne Bay Yacht Club, Coconut Grove Sailing Club, Shake a Leg Miami, and the US Sailing Center all throw open their doors and lend their facilities, giving the regatta a real sense of community. It’s a regatta where the city gets involved, and sailors from all over the world are treated like old friends.

There’s a reason sailors keep coming back. Whether you’re gunning for the podium or just happy to be on the start line, the Bacardi Cup and Bacardi Invitational Regatta are bucket-list events for good reason. You’ll race hard, laugh harder, and leave with more than just a suntan—you’ll leave with stories, friends, and maybe even a little hardware if the wind gods are kind.

So, mark your calendars. The 2026 Bacardi Invitational Regatta runs March 1–7, and promises all the thrills, breeze, and Bacardi-fuelled socials you can handle. Sail a Star, a J/70, or something in between—just don’t miss it.
Because at the Bacardi Cup, the race ends at the finish line—but the regatta never really stops.

title: Tenby Sailing Club Rings with Excitement as Sailors Battle it out in the 2025 GP14 National Championship
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Tenby Sailing Club Rings with Excitement as Sailors Battle it out in the 2025 GP14 National Championship
summary: An exhilarating day unfolded at the Tenby Sailing Club, the site of the gripping 2025 GP14 National Championship.
body: Day four of the Ripe Craftinsure GP14 National Championship 2025 at Tenby Sailing Club left a trail of adventure, drama, and an overwhelming sense of camaraderie in its wake. The 75th Anniversary National Championship powered into its penultimate day with a single race that welcomed a new wind direction - a steady 8-10 knots from the southwest to go against the tide.

The spirited team of Jasper Barnham and Graham Sexton demonstrated an awe-inspiring start right out of the middle of the line. Even though the fleet shifted towards the right to evade the tide, Team Barnham/Sexton held their ground. Through disciplined teamwork, they overtook the McGuinness team on the first run, with Fergus Barnham and Ellie Devereux seizing the third place.

On the final leg of the course, it was Barnham/Sexton who led the fleet, demonstrating superior strategy and skilful manoeuvring. Behind them, a fierce battle was brewing among the Cormacks, the Sinclairs, and Barnham/Devereux who sauntered sneakily into the Cormacks' spot at the gybe mark. The enthralling race drew to a close with Barnham/Sexton seizing victory, the McGuinness team landing at the second spot, and Barnham/Devereux closing the podium.

While the race on the fourth day was the highlight, the crew's race held its own charm. Although the Barnhams and Hayes/James returned to shore due to childminding duties, the remaining teams put up a gripping spectacle. The day wrapped up bringing a rich blend of relaxation and unrestrained fun as everyone relished the town's nightlife, celebrating an eventful day at the championship.

The final stretch of the racing week is poised to offer the pinnacles of sailing skill, high-stakes competition, and an infectious air of bonhomie among the participants. If the tainted sea state and the poor visibility of Thursday were a disappointment, Friday promises to bring cheer, with as many as three races being planned for the day.

title: Unveiling the First Viper 130: ISA Yachts Begins Outfitting of Innovative Superyacht
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unveiling the First Viper 130: ISA Yachts Begins Outfitting of Innovative Superyacht
summary: ISA Yachts takes major strides with the commencement of the Viper 130's outfitting process at its Italian facility.
body: In a landmark announcement, ISA Yachts, a revered subsidiary of Palumbo Superyachts, unveiled that the first build of its Viper 130 model has entered the outfitting phase at its Ancona facilities in Italy. This achievement arrives barely two months after the Viper line was launched in May 2024, reflecting a rapid momentum in the brand's operations.

Prominently, the Viper 130 model captured an American buyer's fascination, marking its first sale. The deal was facilitated by Zarpo Yachts, also credited for overseeing the sale of the Columbus Crossover model from ISA's sister brand.

Housing is spread across five cabins located on the lower deck. The owner's quarters feature a dual bathroom and can be arranged amidships to leverage the 7.9-metre beam or towards the bow for an expansive walk-in closet.

The main deck combines an extra bar-galley, a well-appointed saloon with semi-circular sofas, armchairs, and a ten-seater dining table. Maximising the interior, a unique, port-side walkway leads to the spectacular bow view, an additional balcony offers direct ocean vistas, and the main deck houses the wheelhouse. The sundrenched sundeck, on the other hand, features a secondary helm station, stern-planted sunpads, a lounge area, a 12-seater table, and a circular pool into the bow area.

From a functional standpoint, a garage suitable for a five-metre tender is positioned on the starboard. When it comes to performance, the Viper 130, integrated with three powerful MAN or MTU engines, aims to achieve a top speed of 33 knots and a cruising speed of 26 knots. The ISA Viper line consists of three models: the Viper 100, Viper 130, and Viper 140.

title: Numarine’s Second Hybrid 30XP Yacht Model ‘Tuccini’ takes the Centre Stage: A Look at the Craft’s Unsurpassed Flexibility and Class
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Numarine’s Second Hybrid 30XP Yacht Model ‘Tuccini’ takes the Centre Stage: A Look at the Craft’s Unsurpassed Flexibility and Class
summary: Numarine, the renowned yacht manufacturer, has launched Tuccini, its second 30XP series model, brimming with elegance and unprecedented functionality.
body: The seas are welcoming a new touch of class with Numarine's recent launch, christened ‘Tuccini'. This second yacht in the 30XP series, spanning an impressive 30.7 meters, carries an aura similar to its widely popular sistership ‘Minella’ which made its debut at last year's Cannes Yachting Festival. The striking similarity is beautifully contrasted with a classic, all-white paint scheme that pairs delightfully with interiors highlighting white and beige tones and some dark accents. Turkish studio Can Yalman, a master of marine design, is responsible for both the yacht's exterior and interior, with a special focus on the highly efficient raised pilothouse layout. Tuccini further sets sail toward environmental friendliness with a hybrid propulsion system. The yacht also boasts a substantial internal volume of 213 gross tons, offering an exemplary balance of flexibility for the owner and a delightful outdoor living experience. The spacious flybridge, rivaling those of larger yachts, and the expansive sunpad accommodating more than ten people are clear indicators of its outdoor prowess. There’s also a semi-open beach club at the stern, that dynamically expands to an area of 46 square meters, allowing extra room for various watersports and swimming. Offering plush dining options on the aft deck, a sundeck lounge, and a private balcony with exclusive access from the owner's suite, Tuccini is a true symbol of luxury and flexibility. Furthermore, the yacht is ready to cruise quietly across the waves at seven knots while maintaining a low noise level below 40 decibels in the guest cabins and a meremeasurementof 38.1 decibel in the master cabin. Propelled by a diesel-electric propulsion system, the yacht flies up to a maximum speed of 13 knots, and can cruise over a staggering range of 3,500 nautical miles at eight knots. One can also opt for solar panels to be added to the hardtop for additional support to onboard systems.

title: Trinity Motor Yacht Aquasition Undergoes $1 Million Price Cut, Reimagined Luxury Awaits at Sea
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Trinity Motor Yacht Aquasition Undergoes $1 Million Price Cut, Reimagined Luxury Awaits at Sea
summary: The opulent 43.3-metre motor yacht Aquasition welcomes potential owners with a fresh $1 million price drop, inviting luxurious voyages in a redefined style.
body: The unmistakably luxurious 43.3-metre Trinity Motor Yacht, Aquasition, is setting waves of excitement among seafaring enthusiasts. The yacht recently witnessed a $1 million reduction in its sales, making it an even more enticing opportunity for yacht connoisseurs. It is listed by RJC Yacht Sales with Bob Cury at the helm.

Delivered in 2010 by Trinity Yachts and refurbished in 2023, Aquasition is the epitome of elegance and class. The construction was brought to fruition in aluminum, conforming to ABS class specifications and MCA compliant standards. The most recent refurbishments are testament to the yacht's commitment to contemporary style, blending new furnishings with marble touches, enhanced lighting, updated audio/video systems, and LED television screens – an alluring cocktail of comfort and luxury.

The yacht's interiors are an invitation to indulgence. Cherry wood joinery wraps the traditionally-styled main saloon, accented by a dining table ready to accommodate 10 guests and a cosy lounge area. More than just a floating luxury, Aquasition also offers accommodations for 10 guests in four king-sized cabins and one twin cabin, staffed by a crew of nine. The main deck master suite takes luxury to a new level with an en suite with a marble bath and a sizable walk-in wardrobe.

The Aquasition's exterior is a realm of relaxation. A spacious alfresco dining area meets additional built-in seating while a lounge area waits ahead of the bridge with plush sofas and tables. The expansive sundeck is the epitome of sea relaxation, featuring a jacuzzi and bar.

Aquasition's last true owners set sail in 2020. Since being relisted for sale in October 2024,Aquasition's price has fallen by $2 million. Twin Caterpillar C-32A 1,800hp diesel engines power this beauty to a maximum speed of 17.5 knots and a cruising speed of 13 knots. A meeting point of style, speed, and luxury, the Aquasition is calling out to its next voyage companion.

title: Turn Heads with the new Aluminium Beauty: The Steeler Bronson 65
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Turn Heads with the new Aluminium Beauty: The Steeler Bronson 65
summary: The esteemed Dutch builder, Steeler Yachts, is set to wow the high-seas with its latest mastercraft, the Steeler Bronson 65. This cutting-edge, aluminium superstructure is designed to thrill both in performance and luxury.
body: Steeler Yachts, the renowned Dutch builders, introduced their new flagship model - the Steeler Bronson 65. Crafted entirely from aluminium and revved up by either a pair of Volvo Penta D11 IPS-950s or 1350s, this yacht is a perfect blend of power, speed, and luxury. The Bronson 65 dons a finesse aesthetic thanks to its sleek, single continuous hull window running unbroken from the forepeak to the engine room. The stylish coupé layout offers a practical day boating experience, enhancing the amicable social space that merges the intimate saloon interior with the openness of the aft cockpit. The saloon - a space dedicated to relaxation - boasts a wet bar, raised helm seats, comfortable settees, and moving seat pods. Overlooking the stern bench via the superstructure's open back end, one can unwind with delightful views, flanked by comfortable seat pods on the massive aft deck. A supplementary seating arrangement faces the hydraulic high-low platform, augmenting the yacht's capacity to accommodate increased gathering and festivities. Safety is paramount in Bronson 65's design. The yacht ensures this with deep, secure bulwarks and easy-to-navigate walkways, allowing you to enjoy the unique outdoor experience during sailing escapades. Essential amenities, including a roomy sunbed, tender garage, and a dining space for six in the forepeak, further enhance the yacht's charm and versatility. Yet, Bronson 65's alluring features extend beyond aesthetics and safety. It includes an electrically operated roof, creating an open ‘cabrio’ space or an entirely enclosed coupé structure, transforming the yacht to suit varying weather conditions and specific voyages. Integral to the layout is the open-plan galley – thoughtfully designed with a large dinette, big windows, an open stairwell, and transverse lighting engineered into the deckhead, making extended cruises blissful. While the yacht’s accommodation offering might appear modest with its two-cabin capacity, a spacious full-beam owner’s cabin and VIP guest cabin both with private ensuite settings make up for the limited space. Bronson 65 summarises the luxury yachting experience with its all-weather versatility, aesthetic exterior, and the possibility of customisation to match individual tastes. In conclusion, the Steeler Bronson 65 is a fine specimen of what it means to sail in unparalleled style. With its promise of an exceptional buildup, finish, and luxury living, this yacht will undeniably garner considerable attention in boating circles and beyond.

title: From the World of Gaming to Luxury Yachting: Tech Mogul Gabe Newell Buys Iconic Oceanco
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: From the World of Gaming to Luxury Yachting: Tech Mogul Gabe Newell Buys Iconic Oceanco
summary: The international yachting industry witnesses a thrilling development as tech billionaire Gabe Newell acquires the acclaimed shipyard, Oceanco.
body: Oceanco, a world-renowned yacht builder, is embarking on a new voyage. Born in South Africa in 1987, the company hopped on an intriguing odyssey, navigated by an array of visionaries, each contributing their unique touch to the company's evolution. Oceanco cruised the seas of innovation and prestige, a feat brilliantly embodied in

Their iconic Alfa Nero series, a worldwide recognized range that set sail in 2002 during the Angelopoulos Greek Era, forever etched in the annals of yacht design. Under the Omani investor Dr Mohammed Al Barwani, the shipyard raised anchor towards the 100-metre-plus luxury sector in 2010, continuing the Alfa Nero legacy while expanding the horizons further. Now, the renowned yacht builder prepares for another interesting chapter as American investor Gabe Newell steps aboard as the new owner.

Beyond his tech savvy and wealth, Newell boasts ownership of Inkfish, a marine research organisation, and an impressive flotilla of research vessels. Inkfish's fleet, which includes the substantial 68.3-metre Pressure Drop and the state-of-the-art R/V 6000, a 100-metre project currently under construction, represents Newell's deep-seated commitment to oceanic exploration and conservation.

Newell's vision for Oceanco intertwines his passions for technology, maritime exploits and the preservation of the oceanic ecosystem. With his extensive time spent onboard his vessels and his incredible west coast network, Newell's tenure promises to be a fascinating journey for Oceanco, one driven by technology, conservation and a fervent admiration for the high seas. Thus, Oceanco's future sails under Newell are certain to be watched with keen interest, propelling the shipyard into fascinating, uncharted waters.

title: Numarine Delivers Maiden 40MXP Model, A Redefinition Of Luxury With High-Volume And Low-Maintenance Features
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Numarine Delivers Maiden 40MXP Model, A Redefinition Of Luxury With High-Volume And Low-Maintenance Features
summary: Turkish shipyard Numarine raises the bar with the delivery of its first 40MXP model, a splendid superyacht named Miouch.
body: A game-changer in the world of luxury yachting, the 39.1-metre Miouch celebrates Numarine’s innovative ethos of high-volume, low-maintenance, and long-range functionality, pack tightly within a larger package. Single-handedly taking the market by storm, Miouch represents the evolution of the popular 37XP model, winning her an influx of interested boat owners. Before the first vessel hit the water, three 40MXP hulls were already sold, indicating the model’s commercial success. With a transatlantic range of 6,000 miles at eight knots, the 40MXP superyacht is a 'true global explorer', setting new standards for sea travel. The majestic vessel features a full-beam hydraulic swim platform, replacing the beach club and garage seen on the 37MXP. Moreover, Miouch is also two metres longer than her predecessor, channeling the extra space into the aft deck, housing large al fresco dining areas, a bar and a lounge with an aft pool featuring a glass transom. This fluid layout introduces a novel way of enjoying what the XPs offer and makes for a perfect chill spot to unwind with family and friends. In addition to comfort and luxury, Miouch successfully caters to adventure with ample space for a nine-meter tender, three Jet Skis, and more water sports gear. According to BOATPro, Numarine has 11 more yachts under construction or on order, furthering their mark on the world of luxury yachting.

title: Shattering the Illusions Around Yachting Trade Unions: In Defence of the Seafarers' Right
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Shattering the Illusions Around Yachting Trade Unions: In Defence of the Seafarers' Right
summary: Aiming to set the record straight, Nautilus International talks about modern yachting trade unions and their role in fortifying seafarers' rights.
body: Responding to recent claims that misrepresent the role of modern trade unions in the field of professional yachting, Nautilus International, with over 160 years of experience, aims to set the record straight. It underlies the commitment of its organization to ensure that yacht crew have an adequate representation and protection, which contradicts the depiction of trade unions as confrontational and public entities.

The Professional Yachting Association (PYA) serves as a trade association, primarily representing the professional interests to regulators and stakeholders. While recognizing the value of the PYA's pursuits, Nautilus International sublines a stark difference between unions and associations. The former engage in tasks aligning with their counterparts but do more by solely channelling efforts towards enhancing the conditions and lives of yacht crew without potential conflicts of interest.

The assertion that trade unions act on behalf of an individual only if benefiting the collective is an unjust portrayal. The power reinforced by a collective standing empowers the union to provide stout one-on-one support, defending the rights of every single member, without discrimination. Whether handling unfair dismissals, wage disputes, harassment, or contractual issues, the union's purpose remains to protect the individual. Hence, the existence of unions plays a pivotal role in supporting the yacht crew and upholding their rights.

title: Cowes Week began under a light north‑westerly breeze
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Cowes Week Opens
summary: Cowes Week began under a light north‑westerly breeze, with all eyes on the forecast: Storm Floris, emerging from Iceland, promised a dramatic shift in wind direction and intensity later in the day Due to the lighter airs and anticipated changes, race officials postponed the start for two hours and shifted larger Black‑Group yachts off the Royal Yacht Squadron (RYS) line to a committee‑boat start off Beaulieu, while s
body: At about 13:00, conditions began to improve, and by 13:24, the AP signal was dropped to launch racing

The 36‑boat J/70 fleet kicked off the action with a general recall, followed by individual recalls that left six boats OCS. Once away around 13:40, they raced a coastal course—Gurnard → Contessa 32 → Jane → Hill‑Head → East Knoll. Bruce Huber’s Endeavour led early, while Sardonyx ran aground. Endeavour claimed race one, followed by Lady Khumbu and Jelvis in third. Two further races ensued, both won by Jelvis, which capitalised on an OCS in race 1 by Casting Couch and established a comfortable overnight lead for the fleet

As the final one‑design class to start from the Squadron line, the XODs benefited from a steadier, building breeze. Racing got underway at 15:25 after another general recall; six boats went OCS on the second attempt. Their course sent them northward upshore to Polly’s Challenge, across to Hamble Yacht Services, then west via West Knoll, followed by North Ryde Middle before finishing at the Breakwater line. Astralita (skippered by John Tremlett, crewed by Fraser Graham) took the win, followed by Silhouette helmed by Tom Vernon. Adam Bowers on Silhouette reflected:

Larger boat classes—including IRC Zero and the Cape 31s, followed later by IRC 1, 2, 3, Performance Cruiser A, IRC 4, and J/109s—launched from Committee Vessel 1 at 14:25, with subsequent starts around 15:00. By then the breeze had built into a solid Solent blow, allowing for crisp and fast racing along the western Solent course: a long beat to Draycott Chartered Surveyors mark, downwind to Greenings Fintech, then finish. It was the Cape 31s that stole the show: Bullit (Julian Metherell) won the prestigious Queen’s Cup, ahead on IRC of Flying Jenny (Sandy Askew) and Swift Half (Ben Ward). When the breeze hardened to 18–20 knots, Bullit came alive—and Flying Jenny briefly surged but was defeated on corrected time by Bullit.

With Storm Floris approaching, day two presented more straightforward race management: steady breezes and on‑time starts across the board Notably, racing schedules progressed without delay, and action remained engaging on both water and shore.

The J/70s launched at 10:30, with strong, steadier offshore winds leading to a highly tactical and competitive pin‑end battle. Other one‑design classes followed with similar patterns. The XOD fleet experienced a minor drama when one crew member on Athena went overboard—but the team executed a textbook recovery and continued to finish 24th.

For the first time, Cape 31s raced independently off Committee Vessel 1. Three short windward–leeward races turned into a compelling showcase of surfing and tactical sailing across lively seas. Meanwhile, in Performance Cruiser A, Coco de Mer led the larger fleet, Flying Jenny topped the Cape 31s, and in IRC Zero Braveheart claimed both line‑honours and the class win

In IRC 3, Ziggy bounced back from Day 1 to win, with Whooper second and Njord third. Two boats—Malice and Full Circle—retired. Ed Mockridge’s Elaine Again took a safer, family crew approach aboard their JPK1010 (six adults and six under‑13s), describing the racing as long windward‑leeward legs and educational for the kids, who found thrills in watching dad get soaked on the foredeck.

The Etchells fleet lined up pin‑end off the Squadron and launched cleanly. No Dramas started conservatively and recovered well, though water ingress slowed them mid‑race and they ultimately finished fourth. Leading boats Tango, Palava, Desperate, and No Dramas rounded out the top four. Skipper Andy Beadsworth praised the shared experience sailing with his son Josh and crew, reflecting on the joy of mentoring young sailors while competing hard
Seventeen boats tackled the Redwing course, with the Gosling family—helmed alternately by sisters Serena and Rosie—well inshore. Rosie described their strategy and result:

The XODs battled again in the Captain’s Cup—a compact 3¼‑hour affair remembered for fierce starts and tight racing. After yesterday’s recall chaos, crews were cautious. Barry Dunning’s seasoned team nailed the pin‑end start, but streaking past them was Astralita (Graham, Tremlett, Copsey), sweeping for their second bullet. Gone Away placed second, with X Ray third after a demanding up‑Solent and Bramble Bank course. The fleet buzzed about the physical toll—metaphorically a “chipolata too many”—before the break for the storm tomorrow
Weather & Forecast

Storm Floris is due to strike on Monday, 4 August 2025, bringing strong gusty westerlies. Consequently, all racing has been cancelled for Day 3 on safety grounds. However, the shoreside scene remains lively: it’s Charity Day, featuring fundraising events and awareness efforts in support of the RNLI, Autism on the Water, Scaramouche Sailing Trust, and the Andrew Cassell Foundation

The first two days showcased classic Cowes Week traits: coastal race drama, changing breezes, fiercely packed one‑design fleets, and big‑boat elegant match racing. The Solent delivered both fickle inshore shifts and steady offshore pressure, creating dynamic conditions that rewarded strong boat handling and patience alike.
On Day 1 the slow start and postponed action built anticipation, culminating in standout performances from Bullit, Jelvis, Astralita, and others.
Day 2 confirmed the regatta’s depth: top‑level match‑ups, but also heartfelt family efforts, youth learning alongside season‑ed crew, and the enduring tradition of sailing as a generational sport.

title: Prominent Yachtsman and Mazu Yachts Owner, Halit Yukay, Disappears at Sea, Debris of his Yacht Found
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Prominent Yachtsman and Mazu Yachts Owner, Halit Yukay, Disappears at Sea, Debris of his Yacht Found
summary: A cloud of uncertainty looms as Halit Yukay, the renowned owner of Mazu Yachts, goes missing after his yacht wreckage was found.
body: An air of uncertainty hangs heavy as the search continues for a well-known yachtsman and owner of Mazu Yachts, Halit Yukay. All trace of Yakut was lost after authorities discovered the remains of his yacht, aptly named Graywolf, in the off coast of Marmara Island in Balikesir, Türkiye. The now missing 43-year-old Yukay reportedly set off on his sailing journey from Yalova to the idyllic Greek island of Mykonos, when the accident occurred. Mazu Yachts, founded by the adventurous seafaring architect, Yukay, in Yalova, Türkiye, back in 2011, quickly earned a name for itself in the yachting world for its superiorly designed carbon-composite and steel-hulled yachts, with superstructures that range from 11 to 40 metres. Yukay’s personal passion for nautical design began in childhood leading to his first major project, a 16-metre yacht, before he set the cornerstone of Mazu Yachts. The story takes a tragic turn on the fateful 4th of August, when relatives of Yukay reported him missing after all contacts were abruptly lost with the veteran sailor. He is said to have left Yalova Setur Marina that day on his private Turkish-flagged yacht, believed to be alone on his journey. The debris of the Graywolf was witnessed partially submerged in water by a commercial vessel operating off Turanköy, Kapıdağ Peninsula. Authorities were alerted at once and a dive team was promptly dispatched to the location. An intense search for Yukay ensued, but so far has yielded no evidence of his whereabouts. The search and rescue team continues their operations, with a helicopter, a dive team, and seven Coastguard vessels, not giving up hope. An investigation has been launched to study the circumstances leading to the tragic event. Early reports suggest deep cracks in the yacht’s hull, presumably resulting from an accident. The search operation, both underwater and aerial, continues in full throttle in hopes of finding the skilled sailor. Further updates on this developing story will be reported as more information becomes available. The boating world keeps its eyes firmly on the horizon, hoping for a safe return of the Mazu Yachts' champion, Mr Halit Yukay.

title: Changing Tides in the Maritime Industry: Why the Future of Yachting is Moving Away from Teak
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Changing Tides in the Maritime Industry: Why the Future of Yachting is Moving Away from Teak
summary: Change is afoot in the yachting industry. The sleek golden hue of teak, long seen as the hallmark of luxury maritime aesthetics, is falling out of favour due to increasing environmental concerns.
body: For the uninitiated, the link between teak, a golden honey-brown wood, and the majestic allure of yachts might seem faint. However, one walk on a teak-decked yacht, feeling the grain of the elegant and instantly recognisable wood underfoot, would be enough to uncover this link. Truth be said, for many yacht owners, the thought of a yacht without a teak deck is simply unthinkable.

Yet however timeless and elegant teak might be, the world is changing, and so are attitudes towards teak usage. It may have been a beloved standard for years, but teak's aesthetic legacy comes at a high environmental cost. Beyond its dwindling availability, the areas where teak is sourced — countries like Thailand, India, and Indonesia — are faced with rampant deforestation and illegal trade.

According to environmental research, about 75% of teak sourced from Myanmar is believed to be illegal, and around 40% of its exports go into yacht construction, highlighting the serious affect the industry has on deforestation issues. Large yachts, despite making up just 15% of the global fleet, contribute significantly to teak consumption, creating an unsustainable dependency and indicating the urgent need for alternatives.

The industry's addiction to teak needs to be curbed as it approaches an expected spike in demand by 2028 and a projected peak in 2048, with an almost double increase of today's requirement. In light of these facts, the once-revered teak is rapidly becoming a liability, and one that many in the industry can no longer afford to ignore.

In response to the mounting regulatory pressure and moral responsibility, the maritime industry must adapt and innovate. The burden of finding an alternative material that matches teak's undeniable appeal yet doesn't carry the heavy environmental price tag is undoubtedly challenging. However, if the industry is committed to a sustainable future, as it should be, it has to transition from teak to more eco-friendly materials.
The future of yachting may look different from the teak-decked dreams of yesteryears, but it promises to be just as elegant, only more responsible and kinder to our planet.

title: Yacht Club de Monaco triumphed in the 2025 Admiral’s Cup
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Yacht Club de Monaco triumphed in the 2025 Admiral’s Cup
imageCaption: Yacht Club de Monaco triumphed in the 2025 Admiral’s Cup
summary: ## A Principality Crowned: Monaco Wins the 2025 Admiral’s Cup The revived Admiral’s Cup, long considered the unofficial world championship of offshore sailing, returned in 2025 after a 22‑year absence. And in a watershed moment, the Yacht Club de Monaco (YCM)—making its very first appearance—secretly emerged as the 2025 Admiral’s Cup champions. Monaco’s debut was nothing short of sensational, combining precision sail
body: Monaco’s team sailed two boats:
Jolt 3, a TP52 skippered by Peter Harrison (competing in AC1, the larger-boat fleet), and
Jolt 6, a Carkeek 42 skippered by Pierre Casiraghi, vice‑president of YCM (racing in AC2, the smaller-boat division)
The event incorporated three key phases:
A RORC Channel Race (160 nm, coefficient ×2),
Six inshore races in the Solent, and
The Rolex Fastnet Race (695 nm, triple scoring, non‑discardable)

After mid‑event standings saw Royal Hong Kong briefly leading with 36 points to Monaco’s 44 and Italy at 59, the Fastnet transformed the leaderboard. Thanks to Monaco’s flawless execution, especially under high pressure, they surged to an overall margin of 16 points ahead of Hong Kong Yachting World

The Rolex Fastnet Race proved deciding. As dusk settled, both Jolt 3 and Jolt 6 arrived at Cherbourg nearly simultaneously with many rivals … and only hours to spare before protest deadlines. Jolt 6's navigator Will Harris played a pivotal role, expertly guiding his crew as they fended off fierce competition from Hong Kong’s Beau Ideal and New Zealand’s Callisto.

Casiraghi described the emotions vividly: “Honestly, I still can’t quite believe what we’ve achieved… we held the lead, fought off relentless pressure… it was truly a collective effort”—and later added: “At this point I’m exhausted… can’t imagine doing another offshore on a 42-footer any time soon”

Meanwhile, Harrison reflected on the campaign with humility and optimism: “This is the biggest result I’ve ever had in sailing… to help lead YCM to its first victory on our first attempt is extraordinary.” He praised the team chemistry, strategic management by Matt Adams, and vowed that YCM would already be planning to defend the trophy
Silver – Royal Hong Kong Yacht Club
Bronze – Yacht Club Costa Smeralda (Italy)
Royal New Zealand Yacht Squadron (4th),
Cruising Yacht Club of Australia (5th),
Royal Maas Yacht Club from the Netherlands (6th),
Royal Swedish Yacht Club, Royal Ocean Racing Club (two teams), Royal Irish YC, and New York Yacht Club among the 15‑team leaderboard

Historic debut victory: YCM entered and won on its first attempt. Flawless team execution: Success across multiple race formats, divisions, and pressure situations. Strategies matched to conditions: Solent singles sailed tight; Fastnet endurance and tactical nuance delivered the prize. Navigational excellence: Harris’s performance aboard Jolt 6 was singled out as “phenomenal” by Casiraghi.

The revival of the Admiral’s Cup after more than two decades was always a landmark moment for offshore sailing. Monaco’s triumph adds fresh significance—it symbolises the competitiveness of smaller nations, the power of first-time ambition, and the evolution of team‑based offshore racing.

With The Ocean Race Europe launching in August, YCM figures like Will Harris and Cole Brauer are set to transition to other high-profile events aboard Malizia‑Seaexplorer, the same platform that powered Greta Thunberg’s Atlantic crossing in 2019. Their performance in the Fastnet may have reinforced their confidence in offshore endurance racing.

Monaco’s 2025 Admiral’s Cup victory stands not just as a sailing achievement, but as a testament to ambition, precision, and the synergy of talent across disciplines. It’s the kind of story that lives on far beyond a leaderboard: a principality finds a place at the pinnacle of offshore legend.

The 2025 Admiral’s Cup didn’t just return. It returned with a twist. Monaco, a first‑timer, claimed glory on grit and guile. And knowing the principality as you do—you’ll feel it’s only the beginning.

title: In a Fascinating Twist, Investigation Reveals the Likely Culprit Behind the Sinking of the Lovebug Yacht
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: In a Fascinating Twist, Investigation Reveals the Likely Culprit Behind the Sinking of the Lovebug Yacht
summary: A riveting investigation into the sinking of 37.8-metre motor yacht Lovebug points towards an unexpected cause.
body: Set afloat on the tranquil waters of Chesapeake Bay, Maryland, the motor yacht Lovebug was seized by an unfortunate fate last year, sinking to the bottom with a heartbreaking end. The Lovebug, known for her grandiosity and elegant design, found herself in a nightmare scenario on that dark day of 27 July 2024. But the question remains what could have led to such a disaster? A revealing safety report by the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) provides some intriguing insights.

The Lovebug, in her ill-fated ordeal, sank in just 3.7 metres of water, with the total damage pegged at a staggering $8 million. To add to the woes, the recovery of the vessel was marred with delays. Scheduled to commence on 13 August, it was postponed due to a twist of fate in the form of Tropical Storm Debby inducing strong winds and high tides in the region. It was not until September that the yacht was finally salvaged, nearly two months after the sinking. The five souls on board were brought to safety by a good Samaritan and a tow boat.

The yacht, originally headed for Annapolis, Maryland's capital city, bore no reports of pollution, as per a statement by the US Coast Guard released shortly after the sinking. The NTSB report further confirmed the absence of pollution, stating the oil sheen around the vessel was kept contained. A beacon of luxury, Lovebug with her small swimming pool, bar and sunpads on the sundeck, accommodation for 11 guests, and a crew of seven, was a regular on the yacht charter circuit up until her fateful end.

title: Performance Racer and Luxury Cruiser: The Wally Sloop Sailing Yacht Galma Finds a New Home
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Performance Racer and Luxury Cruiser: The Wally Sloop Sailing Yacht Galma Finds a New Home
summary: The prestigious 28.6-metre Wally sloop sailing yacht Galma is embarking on a new voyage. The new home will be a place as timeless and adventurous as Galma herself.
body: A new chapter in nautical history begins as the 28.6-metre Wally sloop sailing yacht Galma transitions to new ownership. With a design penned by icons of the industry: Germán Frers, Luca Bassani, and Wally, the yacht models a delicate blend of performance and luxury.

Built in 2003, Galma was crafted in lightweight carbon fibre, furnished with a generous sail plan, and built as a performance racer. The prestigious yacht has an illustrious past, participating in prominent regattas such as the Loro Piana Superyacht Regatta in Porto Cervo, Italy, and has been prudently maintained ever since her substantial refit in 2008.

On the coveted deck, the yacht hosts a spacious guest cockpit offering a tranquil setting for enjoying cocktails or dining, shaded by a removable awning, while a section of the transom gracefully folds down to create a swim platform in the water. Her mast and both racing and cruising booms underwent a facelift in 2016-2017.

Driven by her 240hp Yanmar engine, Galma sails effortlessly at 10 knots with an impressive 800-nautical-mile range. The yacht flaunts a top speed of 12 knots, making her a perfect blend of luxury and performance.

Galma, with her rich history and impressive make, has finally found a new caretaker, signing off at a last asking price of €2,200,000. The new owner has not just acquired a yacht, but a piece of nautical history that will continue to leave a timeless impact in the world of sailing and luxury yachts.

title: An Intense Clash of Seasides: The 2025 Kestrel Nationals at Stone Week Garner High Anticipation
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: An Intense Clash of Seasides: The 2025 Kestrel Nationals at Stone Week Garner High Anticipation
summary: Battle lines are drawn as Stone's Sailing Club prepares to host the exhilarating Kestrel National Championship in August 2025.
body: Boat racing enthusiasts are in for a treat as Stone Sailing Club gears up to host the much-anticipated Kestrel National Championship 2025 between 4th and 8th of August as part of the renowned Stone Week. Sixteen boats have thrown their hat into the ring, with the championship looking set to be a fierce contest between nautical talents from England and Scotland. Current champions, Malcolm Worsley and Richard Harper, triumphant from their win at Royal Tay, are one team to watch. Malcolm, now paired with his daughter Danielle, are strong competitors aiming to retain the title. However, they face stiff competition from local heroes Howie Enkel and Danni Tebbutt from Maylandsea Bay who are setting their sights on the championship. Adding to the intrigue are Stewart Murdoch and Ken Scott-Brown, representing a potent Scottish contingent, ready to take on the waves and the competition. Early weather forecasts predict a strong westerly breeze, keeping the anticipation high for an enticing race. Particularly under watch are heavy weather specialists Rich and Liz Le Mare from Emsworth. On the other hand, Chris Grice from Maylandsea, a former national champion crewed by Kenny Hobbs, could be the dark horse of the competition. Adding an even more dynamic spin to the event, Chris's wife, Karin Grice, crewed by Katherine Wilkinson in boat 408, is another formidable presence. Mark Bollard from Starcross, onboard the newly-moulded and resin fresh 1652, could be the wildcard in the competition. The thrilling race week is set to be ablaze with riveting sporting spectacle as the title hangs in the balance, awaiting the most skilled and steadfast sailor!

title: Will Farnell Named ORCV Youth Sailor of the Year
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Youth, Grit, and a Taste for the Deep
imageCaption: Will (far right) with father Jason (far left) on 'Pa's'
summary: Will Farnell Named ORCV Youth Sailor of the Year The Ocean Racing Club of Victoria has named 16-year-old Will Farnell as its 2025 Youth Sailor of the Year — a fitting title for a young man who’s already logged more sea miles than many twice his age, and who carries the saltwater tradition in his bones.
body: It starts where many good sea stories do — with family and an old boat. His grandfather, Harry “Pa” Farnell, first caught the sailing bug in Bendigo. After moving to Geelong, Pa joined the Royal Geelong Yacht Club and passed the obsession down the line. First to Will’s dad, Jason. Then to Will and his sister.

“My first memory of sailing is Wednesday nights on Pa’s Van de Stadt 23,” Will says. “Just the two of us. Rigging it together after school. That’s where I started learning — not just sailing, but how everything worked.”

That early start gave him a head full of know-how and hands that already knew what winches were for while most kids were still learning to jibe a dinghy. Though he began in cadet dinghies in 2017, it was keelboats that got his full attention. Offshore was calling, and Will didn’t hang about.
Completed three Apollo Bay races with his dad on their Adams 10, Valiant
Raced offshore for the first time at 14
Delivered Iain Murray’s 37-footer Dark and Stormy to Sydney
Brought Chutzpah (Caprice 40) home from Hobart
Jumped aboard TP52 Smuggler after cheekily asking to crew at the dock—then raced and delivered her alongside Tim Davis
He’s not in it for the Instagram likes. Offshore sailing, he says, taught him real responsibility. “You have to stay dry, stay warm, and keep your head. Because other people are counting on you.”

Will’s already completed ORCV’s Foredeck Essentials Course with Peter Downey — “I learned heaps about dip-pole gybing,” he says — and works two years deep at DYSC Marine Supplies in Geelong, tightening his links with the boatbuilding and sailing community.

Talk to anyone who’s sailed with him and the same words come up: calm, curious, switched-on. Will doesn’t bang the drum or chase attention. He watches, listens, learns, and shows up. That’s how he ended up on some of the best boats in the fleet — by being quietly brilliant.
How did he feel about the award? In true Will style: “It’s something to be proud of. I’m grateful.”

What’s next? A race around the world, if he has anything to say about it. Europe, maybe. More deliveries. More offshore miles. “I don’t want to work inside,” he says, with that easy grin of someone who already knows where he belongs.
There’s even talk of a father-son double-handed Hobart campaign. But first, a likely tilt at the Devonport race aboard Dark and Stormy later this year.
From backyard boat sheds to TP52 cockpits, Will Farnell is quietly charting his own course — and ORCV is right to be proud. The ocean’s got a new name in the game.
And he’s just getting started.

Photos provided by Will Farnell Will (far right) with father Jason (far left) on 'Pa's' boat with fellow sailing friends Charley S and Josh G. Will helming on Smuggler with Tim Davis Will on the helm of his father's boat Valiant by Tom Smeaton About ORCV: A leading authority on ocean sailing, racing and training in Australia, the Club was formed so that ocean races in Victorian waters could be efficiently developed and run by an organisation focusing specifically on the needs of ocean racers.

title: Bolney Wine Estate Joins Cowes Week 2025
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Bolney Wine Estate Joins Cowes Week 2025
imageCaption: Bolney Wine Estate as the Official Sparkling Wine of Cowes Week 2025
summary: Bolney Wine Estate Joins Cowes Week 2025 as Official Sparkling Wine Partner Cowes Week Limited (CWL), organiser of the world’s most celebrated regatta, has announced a new partnership with Bolney Wine Estate — now the Official Sparkling Wine of Cowes Week 2025. The union brings together two British institutions known for craftsmanship, character, and quiet confidence.
body: Nestled in the rolling hills of Sussex, just north of Brighton, Bolney Wine Estate is one of the pioneers of English winemaking. Founded in 1972, the estate has spent over five decades mastering the art of cool-climate viticulture, producing elegant sparkling and still wines from their sandstone-rich soils. Bolney was among the first to grow Pinot Noir in the UK and remains one of the oldest commercial vineyards in England. Their philosophy combines traditional winemaking methods with sustainable farming, and their wines — particularly their Classic Cuvée and Pinot Noir Rosé — have scooped top international awards, including gold medals at the IWSC and Decanter World Wine Awards.

For Cowes Week 2025, Bolney brings more than just bubbles — they bring heritage and polish. As part of the partnership, their award-winning Bolney Cuvée Rosé will be poured at the iconic Cowes Week Cocktail Party at the Royal Yacht Squadron — a highlight of the regatta’s social calendar. Guests can expect refined, delicate fizz served against the grand backdrop of the Squadron lawn, where champagne flutes mingle with spinnaker talk.

Beyond the Squadron, Bolney will host their own presence on the lawn at Northwood House. The Bolney Bar promises to be a standout feature — a sanctuary of Sussex calm where sailors and spectators can unwind with a glass of sparkling or still wine and watch the racing unfold. Light, refreshing, and made for summer, their wines capture the spirit of the English coast.
Bob Trimble, Chair of Cowes Week Limited, commented:

"We’re delighted to welcome Bolney Wine Estate to Cowes Week. This is a regatta steeped in British tradition and style — values that mirror Bolney’s own. Their commitment to quality, provenance and craft make them the perfect sparkling wine partner.”
Samantha Cross, Marketing Controller at Bolney, echoed the sentiment:
"Partnering with Cowes Week gives us the perfect opportunity to showcase Bolney to an audience that appreciates refinement, legacy and attention to detail. It’s more than wine — it’s a lifestyle.”

As English sparkling wine continues to compete with the world’s best, Bolney stands tall among the leading lights of the industry. Their presence at Cowes Week 2025 cements the regatta’s position as a celebration not just of world-class sailing — but of British excellence, on land and at sea.

title: Celebrating Ivor Jones: The Legendary Co-founder of American Yacht Builder, Delta Marine
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Celebrating Ivor Jones: The Legendary Co-founder of American Yacht Builder, Delta Marine
summary: Delta Marine, famed American yacht manufacturer, pays homage to the legacy of its deceased co-founder, Ivor Jones.
body: Delta Marine's co-founder, Ivor Jones, was not just a boating enthusiast, but a visionary who dreamt of conquering the waters with his world-class vessels. Tracing his journey, Jones and his brother Jack founded the Seattle-based company in 1967. Inspired by the notorious Pacific Northwest's rough waters, they commenced by crafting fishing vessels sturdy enough to withstand the harsh conditions.

Their aspiration and unmatched craftsmanship led them to an unprecedented level of triumph, with more than 600 commercial vessels delivered during the company's early years. This success eventually led to Delta Marine's expansion into the luxury expedition yacht sector. These magnificent vessels were designed to navigate the icy waters of Alaska, find solace in the tranquil Pacific islands, or take adventurous souls around the globe.

Today, the company maintains its roots as a family-run enterprise and continues to uphold the principles set forth by Jones. In the heart of Seattle, the Delta Marine yard, spread over 25 acres along the Duwamish River, houses a remarkable 300,000 square foot manufacturing space. Several ambitious projects such as the 47.6-metre Project Ammo and the 44.2-metre Project Zembra stand as a testimony to the company's enduring commitment to quality and innovation.

Ivor Jones was more than a co-founder; he was an emblem of courage, dedication and an unfailing obligation to his craft, team and family. His indomitable spirit and drive for excellence have left an indelible mark on Delta Marine, as evident in the company's ethos. His vision, perseverance and integrity will continue to inspire the brand's endeavors in the years to come. Jones will be remembered with deep respect, profound gratitude and enduring admiration, a firmament in the vast sea of the yacht making industry.

title: Witness Penzance's Scorpion Nationals: The 80s themed sailing competition Blending Fierce Rivalries with Festive Cheer
author: Old Sea Dogs

body: As the Cornish coastline welcomes queues of vehicles, a common game ensues among the travellers. An alphabet-inspired guessing game swirls with an obvious letter of choice - 'S' for Scorpion. It's evident that the 55 shimmering Scorpion boats are making their way to the stunning waters of Mount’s Bay, ready to relish the hospitality of Penzance Sailing Club. The event harbours a convivial atmosphere, with each participant geared up to demonstrate their nautical prowess, wrapped in their best 80's attire. The dinghy park bustles with lively Scorpion sailors, a lot of them old hands who have stood the test of time, all vying to prove their supremacy in the waters ahead. The competition comprises four fleets: Platinum, Gold, Silver and Bronze. Unintimidated by the fiercest of competitions, the sailors eagerly anticipate showcasing their endurance when the sailing gets stern. Renowned to be a 'family fleet', the Scorpion Nationals allows families to unwind and relish their holidays. The weather gods have also decided to play fair, with the clear blue skies and warm sun setting a perfect stage for the participants. They are relishing every bit of the sunny days before they return to their routine lives post the event. Some more enthusiastic sailors made their way to the venue early in the week. These diligent participants practiced rigorously to present an exhilarating performance when the races commenced on Sunday. For the ones rolling in later, it was a matter of faith that their boats will effortlessly sail through the waters. However, the forecast of heavy winds on Monday promised a challenging scenario, spicing up the competition further. During Saturday night’s competitors briefing, participants were reminded to respect their competitors on water, easing the heat of the competition with a sense of sportsmanship. After the briefing, boats were inspected for optimal racing conditions, fostering a fair and exhilarating competition. Beyond the tense competition and athletic prowess, the Scorpion Nationals reflect hearty laughter, spirited conversations, and a true love for the sport among its participants. Unfazed by the obstacles mother nature may hurl their way, the competitors are united in their resolve not to back down. It's these final touches of friendly rivalry laced with camaraderie and an 80's spin that make the Scorpion Nationals a unique and unforgettable event.

title: Edgartown Race Weekend Transitions Back to July for its 89th Edition
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Edgartown Race Weekend Transitions Back to July for its 89th Edition
summary: In a bid to avoid conflicts with other regattas and uphold tradition, Edgartown Yacht Club recently announced the shift of the Edgartown Race Weekend's 'RTI Race' from June back to July.
body: Mark your calendars for July 25, 2026, as the Edgartown Race Weekend, with its top-billing 'Round-the-Island ('RTI) Race, makes a calendar shift from its recent June slot. This move, decided by the Edgartown Yacht Club, aims to minimize potential clashes with other regattas and to keep alive the longstanding tradition of holding the race in July.

The 'RTI Race, held at Martha's Vineyard, is widely distinguished as one of the oldest and most esteemed distance events in yacht racing. With 88 successful editions under its belt, the race is set to continue its proud legacy on its 89th run, planned for late July in 2026.

Not only is the 'RTI revered for its competitive spirit, but it is also known for its visually magnificent 55-mile route that wraps around the picturesque Martha's Vineyard. This potentially challenging yet rewarding course consistently captivates both seasoned sailors and offshore sailing novices.

Stakes in these races are high, with trophies such as the prestigious Venona Trophy up for grabs. This particular award traces its roots back to the very origins of the race in 1938, adding a touch of revered prestige to the event.

In an effort to build anticipation and ensure a strong turnout, the announcement of the date shift has been made well in advance. Event Co-Chair Cindy Alten-Delotto conveys the hope that all past participants will mark this important date in their calendars and spread the good news. Furthermore, she adds that the currents for this date are positive and if this July's winds are indicative of the winds during the race day, the participants can expect an exciting sail. All signs point towards an epic race come 2026. So, get prepping!
