Teams comprised of a large yacht (Class 1) and a smaller yacht (Class 2), encountering some of the most formidable courses in British waters. Pierre Casiraghi, YCM’s Vice President, relished the challenge, expressing how this unique blend of offshore and inshore racing heightened the complexity and the excitement.

Having maintained their resolve, the YCM repelled shifting breezes and accumulated fatigue, demonstrating impeccable sail changes, strategic decisions and unbroken focus. When the corrected times were confirmed in Cherbourg, the team catapulted to prime position. YCM’s triumphant campaign in Admiral’s Cup was a testament to their resilience, marking a deviation from the glamor and innovation usually synonymous with the club.

More than just a regatta, the Admiral's Cup 2025 was a breathtaking battle that united nations, clubs, and sailors in an exhilarating demonstration of maritime prowess. The event heralded a new dawn, with an arresting blend of inshore and offshore racing, reigniting its illustrious legacy infused with vitality and purpose.

title: Arcadia Soars to New Heights with the A80new: First-ever Raised-pilothouse Model in the Beacon of Innovation
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Arcadia Soars to New Heights with the A80new: First-ever Raised-pilothouse Model in the Beacon of Innovation
summary: Arcadia, the Italian yard renowned for its cutting-edge range of semi-custom cruisers, is set to escalate its innovation as they unwrap the A80new, the first-ever raised-pilothouse model.
body: Italian yard, Arcadia, revered for its semi-custom cruisers of the future, launches its first-ever raised-pilothouse model, the A80new. This 80ft yacht, the epitome of innovation and luxury, is already making waves with elements typically only found on considerably larger vessels. The pièce de résistance is the full-beam owner's cabin on the main deck, facilitated by an unusually tall, near-vertical bow and an elevated foredeck at the same height as the flybridge, leaving room underneath for a remarkably spacious, high-ceilinged owner's suite featuring outstanding views via oversized hull windows.

Traditional design seamlessly blends with progressive elements in the rest of the vessel. The flybridge extends forward from the raised pilothouse, offering multiple options for alfresco dining under a hard top or soaking up the sun in more exposed areas, with an outdoor helm station located on the starboard side. The elongated aft cockpit transitions seamlessly into the indoor saloon and dining area. An expansive hydraulic platform, when deployed, extends the beach club area and reveals a stairway to the sea, encapsulating the essence of relaxed open-air luxury.

Powered by twin Volvo Penta IPS drives, the A80new promises brisk cruises of 16 or 18 knots, with top speeds at a third load, cited as up to 21 knots. Starting at €6,200,000 (excluding taxes), it is an investment in luxury, comfort, and cutting-edge marine technology that pushes the boundaries of ultimate boating experience, truly rocking the foundations of the yachting world.

title: Transform Your Superyacht Experience: Unlocking the Full Potential of Maritime 5G Connectivity
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Transform Your Superyacht Experience: Unlocking the Full Potential of Maritime 5G Connectivity
summary: As we thrive on a powerful cellularly connected world, the maritime industry isn't left behind - 5G connectivity becomes fundamental to luxury superyacht operations.
body: From its boom in the 1980s, cellular technology has irreplaceably woven itself into many aspects of our daily lives. It's become difficult, nigh impossible, to imagine functioning without the power-packed, cellularly-connected devices that command our daily communication, information, education, business, health, and more. In this tech-driven world, high-performance connectivity isn't a luxury anymore - it's a vital expectation, and now more than ever with the wider accessibility of 5G networks, the demand intensifies.

However, sailing isn't always smooth. As these vessels dock in remote bays or cruise in international waters, they often find themselves at the brink of cellular coverage areas. This yacht proximity, though relying on 4G and 5G land-based cellular networks, poses service coverage challenges due to the boat's glass structure, steel hulls, and significant metal presence that rarely passes radio signals. These difficulties nosedive further into the yacht; the physical barriers, such as bulkheads, are more prevalent in areas like tank decks and engine rooms. Overcoming these challenges could involve hybrid solutions like a private 5G network backed by a satellite, enabling connectivity even when departing from the shore into areas unserved by standard land-based MNOs. Distributing the signal also warrants innovations such as a bi-directional amplifier connected to a pair of external antennas on the mast for service from onshore. This provides diversity, ensuring the coverage from onshore MNOs is received regardless of the superyacht's anchored position.

In all, the embrace of 5G technology in the maritime sector presents an opportunity to enhance the superyacht experience significantly, pivoting towards a future of enriched connectivity. The hurdles are there but with innovation and flexibility, 5G has the potential to create a sea change in maritime operations.

title: First Blind Sailor to Solo Round the Isle of Wight
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: First Blind Sailor to Solo Round the Isle of Wight
imageCaption: Dani Anglada Pich Sailing around the Isle of Wight
summary: Dani Anglada Pich Makes History: First Blind Sailor to Solo Round the Isle of Wight — In a Rudderless Catamaran Thursday 24 July 2025 will go down as a day of seamanship, stubborn grit, and something close to magic.
body: Catalan sailor Dani Anglada Pich, blind and utterly undaunted, became the first person to circumnavigate the Isle of Wight solo and unaided—without sight, without a rudder, without a boom, and without even a centreboard. Just one man and his Patí Català, the sleek but stubborn rudderless catamaran more often seen on Barcelona beaches than off the headlands of the Solent.

The start was straight from a naval novel: cannon fire from the Royal Yacht Squadron signalled the off, courtesy of RYS Secretary Patricia Lewington. With a tailwind and sheer will, Dani rocketed along the north shore, touching 12 knots to Lymington in under an hour. After a quick rendezvous with a support RIB helmed by Round the Island Race veteran Simon Rogers, he headed for the Needles. And that’s when the wind gave up.

From then on, it was hard-earned miles. With no steering gear, Dani had to shift body weight and play the sail to keep course—no small feat even in fair conditions, let alone offshore in a building sea. Eight miles offshore he searched for the gradient breeze, but approaching St. Catherine’s brought grief. The sea state turned ugly. “Every time I tried to gybe back towards land, the waves shoved the stern sideways—I nearly lost it,” Dani said.

By late afternoon, he’d passed the lighthouse and was aiming for Sandown Bay. Culver Down brought new breeze, but Bembridge Ledge brought chaos. Standing waves, rising wind, creaking ply. “That half hour was hell,” Dani admitted. “I could feel the boat twisting and flexing in a way I’ve never known. I didn’t know if I’d get through.”

A few yards behind, in a 4.8m RIB, Magnus Wheatley—himself a Round the Island winner aboard MOD70 PowerPlay Zoulou—was watching. “We’d drilled for this,” said Magnus. “He was tired, but his instincts were sharp. He nailed every tack on cue. I’ve rarely seen that kind of resolve.”

Once clear of the Ledge, Dani tacked past Bembridge Lifeboat Station, then cut out wide to dodge traffic off Seaview. He tiptoed over Ryde Sands with just enough pressure and a helpful tide to make the line before dark. The sun was setting, the wind dying. But the gods sent one last breath, and Dani ghosted back into Cowes, where the crowd on The Parade cheered him home. He collapsed, sobbing, on the deck. Job done.

Back at East Cowes Sailing Club, where the challenge had been planned and supported, Commodore Peter Ball called it “one of the finest moments in the club’s history.” The Mayor of East Cowes presented Dani with honorary citizenship, and the club gave him a trophy—he’d earned it ten times over.

Magnus Wheatley summed it up: “In 35 years of writing about sailing at every level, I’ve never seen anything quite like this. Ten minutes watching him and you forget he’s blind. He’s in a league of his own.”

The mission was bigger than one island. Dani sails to spotlight the push to get sailing reinstated in the Paralympics for Brisbane 2032. With support from Emirates Team New Zealand boss Grant Dalton and the YES WE SAIL Foundation, Dani’s not done yet. He’s now eyeing the Bol d’Or Mirabaud in 2026—one of Europe’s toughest inland races.
“From day one, the East Cowes Sailing Club saw me as a sailor first,” Dani said. “Not as someone with a disability. That made all the difference.”

You don’t plan to lose everything 500 miles off Hawaii. But that’s where Dani Anglada Pich’s story turns. A fire extinguisher explodes aboard a gas carrier. One moment he’s a sharp, young merchant navy officer with wings and sea miles under his belt. The next—face shattered, eyes gone, life off course.

For a while, the lights stayed out in every sense. The sea was far away. So was everything else. A degree in Nautical Studies, a master’s from ESADE, a pilot’s licence—none of it mattered much when the future looked like a closed door. “I went through a very dark tunnel,” Dani says. And he means it.
But some sailors are built different. The sea doesn’t forget them, and they don’t forget the sea.
Bit by bit, wave by wave, Dani made his way back. Not to the life he had—but to something harder, bolder, and arguably more important.
He founded YES WE SAIL to prove a point the world often needs reminding of: blind doesn’t mean broken. Disabled doesn’t mean done. Dreams don’t come with disclaimers.

And so this summer, he set out to do something no one had done before: sail solo around the Isle of Wight in a Patí Català—a crazy, rudderless, boomless, centreboard-less cat that’s usually sailed by the wildest Catalans on the Med. Except Dani’s is rigged with custom tech, stripped down for feel and instinct. He sailed 70 nautical miles without help, without vision—just guts, trim, and the unshakable will to push back at the world’s expectations.
Because Dani isn’t just chasing a sailing story. He’s showing us what’s possible when you throw the rulebook overboard. He’s showing us the only limits are the ones we let stay standing.

title: Hard Gains and Narrow Escapes – Admiral’s Cup Fleet Charges West
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Hard Gains and Narrow Escapes – Admiral’s Cup Fleet Charges West
imageCaption: Admirals Cup Race on it way
summary: As the Admiral’s Cup fleet thundered west toward Start Point, the gloves were off and the tactics got real. The leaders split north of the rhumb line—Black Pearl taking the high road, while Eric de Turckheim’s Teasing Machine dug in low and fast to the south. Black Pearl rounded Start Point with a boat length to spare over Jolt 3, both storming along at nine knots. Slightly offshore, Rán and Teasing Machine were push
body: From there, it was a raw offshore drag race to The Lizard. With breeze in the low teens and building, the front pack shifted up a gear. Double digits lit up on the speedos, and it was game on. Black Pearl still led on the water, but the offshore flyers—Zen and Teasing Machine—reeled in the margin, closing fast and hot.

Near the exclusion zones around the Isles of Scilly—those three traffic separation schemes that bite back if you mess with them—all the frontrunners played it safe and slipped east. No one wanted a penalty wrecking their race. Meanwhile, heartbreak struck for Ino Noir (James Neville, RORC Red), forced to retire with charging system failure. The crew are safe and ashore in Plymouth, but it was a bitter early exit.

By 1200 BST on Sunday, corrected time shuffled the pack again. Jolt 3 edged into the AC1 lead, twelve minutes clear of Beau Geste. Caro held third—just under an hour behind. Tight stuff in a long race.

AC2 – Currents, Calls, and a Battle of Boatspeed Down in AC2, the tactical roulette wheel spun around Portland Bill. By 1800 BST Saturday, most of the big players had made it through with the tide. But the smaller, lower-rated contenders—Ginkgo, Garm, Sunrise IV, and Edelweiss—got caught out, chewing the current instead of riding it. Valuable miles were lost.

It proved a turning point. The faster-rated boats got a free ride while the rest struggled to punch west. Whether the weather will repay the little guys later with lighter breeze is anyone’s guess. The Channel still has cards to play.
On Sunrise IV, navigator Tom Cheney checked in just after dawn on Day Two:

“We’re in good spirits aboard the good ship Sunrise. About two boat lengths from Garm—which is exciting and maddening all at once. We dodged Christchurch Bay and crossed swords with the other JPKs off Swanage. Got lined up for the Portland right shift but didn’t beat the tide. Since then it’s been a full-send drag race. We’ve clawed back half a mile, and Django isn’t far ahead. Expecting some funk near The Lizard. I’m already scratching my head at the nav table.”
At the front of the AC2 fleet on the water: Beau Ideal, Callisto, and Jolt 6, with Casiraghi’s crew holding a slight offshore lane. Pierre Casiraghi offered his own early Sunday thoughts:

“Our Solent exit was clean. In that mess of boats, it’s hard not to trade gelcoat or protest flags, but we stayed clear. We ground through multiple tacks and passed Callisto on current and guts. First night was solid—crew into rhythm, no dramas. We’re fighting for every inch now. Long way to go, but spirits are high.”

By Sunday midday, the numbers looked very good for the JPKs. After IRC correction, Django led AC2 by more than two hours. Garm and Sunrise IV were locked in a virtual draw for second. Jolt 6 is still in the game and pushing hard.
This is far from over. Long legs, long odds—and a fleet full of punchers still swinging.

title: JFA Yachts Marks Important Progress on Groundbreaking 51m Hybrid Aluminium Explorer Yacht
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: JFA Yachts Marks Important Progress on Groundbreaking 51m Hybrid Aluminium Explorer Yacht
summary: Progression on the inventive 51m hybrid explorer yacht by JFA, characterized by its impressive hybrid performance and spacious storage for water toys and tenders, has hit a significant milestone.
body: The French yacht builder, JFA Yachts, has achieved a notable milestone in the construction of their advanced 50.5-meter hybrid explorer yacht. Currently in the outfitting stage, the launch of this innovative vessel is eagerly anticipated for later this year. The exterior styling and naval architecture, conceived by Humphreys Yacht Design, lends the yacht a distinct presence on the high seas, while ensuring it packs powerful performance paired with eco-friendly operation. The aluminium explorer yacht, a brainchild of CEO Frédéric Jaouen, is being lauded for its substantial capacity for tenders and water toys. Installed with three high capacity cranes and an intelligent service area and guest social space configuration, this yacht aims to revolutionise luxury exploratory sailing. A davit, concealed foredeck crane and deck crane are to be installed for a 9.25-meter tender, rescue boats, jet skis, substantiating the explorer’s effort to be a supreme adventure vessel. The interiors, coming from Milanese studio m2atelier, are pitch-perfect for a yacht of this stature. The main deck houses the galley, dining area, and an inviting outdoor lounge replete with an integrated barbeque. Meanwhile, the owner's suite, comprising a personal lounge, office area, and outside lounge with a Jacuzzi, takes pride of place on the upper deck. Additional guest cabins are furnished below deck. An expansive array of solar panels and a high-capacity battery system outfits the yacht, enabling 'silent, emission-free operation' when anchored, in the harbour, or when cruising at low speeds. This facilitates an incredibly eco-friendly sailing experience. With a top speed of 20 knots achievable in hybrid boost mode and a range of over 5,000 nautical miles at 12 knots, this yacht indeed embodies a revolutionary step for the future of yachting. Partnering with the clients' team from A2B Marine Projects, JFA’s project team with Michel Siou at the helm, has ensured meticulous planning and expert execution of all aspects of this project. Signalling a milestone for JFA Yachts, this explorer is set to redefine luxury yachting with its blend of performance-, environment-, and leisure-oriented features.

title: Veteran Captain Brendan O'Shannassy Champions Sustainable Change in the Superyacht Industry
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Veteran Captain Brendan O'Shannassy Champions Sustainable Change in the Superyacht Industry
summary: With decades of experience steering iconic superyachts, Captain Brendan O'Shannassy offers his unique insights on the need for change in the industry.
body: Captain Brendan O'Shannassy has spent decades at the helm of iconic superyachts, developing a keen understanding of the complex dynamics of the industry. From his unique vantage point, he has identified a growing disquietude within the sector. With increased expectations from yacht designs and crews, O'Shannassy calls for a seismic shift in the service and manning model, recognising that the current practice is untenable in the long run. He notes a tenfold improvement in the onboard experience, lauding designers and builders, while pointing out the unchanged operational model of the past two decades.

O'Shannassy's remarkable journey from his beginnings in the coastal town of Fremantle, Australia, to operating ski apartments in the Austrian Alps and captaining leading charter yachts, gives him a unique perspective on the industry's workings. His experiences have led him to question the widening chasm between capability, culture, service and structure in yachting.

Furthermore, he emphasizes a pressing need for professional respect akin to the aviation industry. O'Shannassy points out a concerning double standard where owners treat their yachts as private bubbles, often pressurising yacht captains to overlook safety concerns, contrary to their usual adherence to corporate responsibility. He stresses that this practice undermines safety and morale, and calls for owners to uphold the same respect and rules they maintain elsewhere.
By voicing these perspectives, O'Shannassy is offering an invaluable beacon of change, seeking to steer the industry towards more sustainable and efficient waters.

title: Unfathoming 150 Years of Lürssen Yachts: From Modest Beginnings to Building the World's Most Impressive Superyachts
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unfathoming 150 Years of Lürssen Yachts: From Modest Beginnings to Building the World's Most Impressive Superyachts
summary: Travelling back in time, we unveil the arresting history of Lürssen and how it channelled its naval legacy to shape the superyacht industry.
body: The world of Lürssen is more than just a sea-faring tale. With a history spanning 150 years, the company has left its mark not just on the steel and wood of its majestic fleet, but also on the entire superyacht industry.

It all began with humble wooden rowboats, each carrying the touch of countless artisans whose craftsmanship has been handed down through the generations. Despite the transformations brought by two World Wars, the company resolutely glided towards its vision, and emerged as creators of some of the most breathtaking superyachts that rule the oceans today.

The numbers speak for themselves. Lürssen has delivered over 300,000 gross tons (GT) of luxury in the past 25 years, brought to life through a diverse fleet of 62 extraordinary superyachts. The scale at which the company operates is simply staggering. Putting that into perspective, it has created the equivalent of 200 x 30-metre Ferretti semi-custom yachts end to end or nearly 1,600 of the same 30-metre Ferretti’s in terms of GT volume. From marvelling at such a colossal project docked at the harbour to exploring the intricate interior passageways and stairwells onboard, the sheer scale of a Lürssen superyacht is enough to leave anyone awestruck.

The Lürssen legacy boats magnificent achievements in naval architecture and crafts. The gargantuan yachts synonymous with the Lürssen brand and family are a testament to the continuous strive for grandeur. Looking forward, it's nothing less than thrilling to anticipate what lies ahead in Lürssen's nautical narrative. As we continue to sail unfathomed waters of luxury, who knows what marvels of maritime architecture await on the horizon?

title: Experience Glamour Meet Adventure in the Mediterranean Aboard the Magnificent M/Y Larimar II
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Experience Glamour Meet Adventure in the Mediterranean Aboard the Magnificent M/Y Larimar II
summary: Embark on the adventure of a lifetime aboard the majestic M/Y Larimar II, a 25m Princess charter yacht cruising the glittering coasts of the Mediterranean.
body: Ever imagined sailing across the gorgeous Mediterranean seas on a luxurious yacht? It's time for this dream to come true aboard the magnificent M/Y Larimar II, now part of West Nautical's charter fleet. This sight of this 25m Princess flagship yacht, with her sleek design by Bernard Olesinski and interior styling by Princess Design Studio, is a showstopper. Launched in 2017, Larimar II offers an unrivalled experience, blending comfort, sophistication, and thrilling adventures.

From the expansive, sunbathed decks to the well-planned layout, prepare for relaxation and premium service, spiced up by an appropriate dose of adventure. The vessel lavishly accommodates eight guests in four spacious cabins, offering the epitome of a luxurious Eastern Mediterranean escape.

Entertainment continues below deck, where guests can enjoy the contemporary luxury and British refinement of the living space. With fully integrated audio-visual systems that link the flybridge and cockpit audio, and satellite TV, top-notch entertainment is merely a click away. The large double bed, spacious storage, and beautifully appointed en-suite bathroom in the master suite offer an oasis of calm and relaxation.

But this luxury yacht isn't simply about lazing around. Thanks to an impressive line-up of water toys — snorkelling gear, paddleboards, a SeaDoo jet ski, and more — guests are guaranteed an exhilarating adventure on the gleaming waters of the Mediterranean. A cruise aboard the M/Y Larimar II isn't just a holiday – it's a collection of magical moments and memories that will last a lifetime.

title: European Sailors Outclass International Competition, Dominating the ILCA 4 Youth World Championships 2025
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: European Sailors Outclass International Competition, Dominating the ILCA 4 Youth World Championships 2025
summary: European sailors showcased their prowess at the 2025 ILCA 4 Youth World Championships, claiming an incredible nine out of twelve possible podium spots.
body: The 2025 ILCA 4 Youth World Championships came to an exciting end off the Californian coast. The theatre of competitive sailing was on full display over six adventurous days where European sailors dominated the medal tally. Displaying tactical knowledge, perseverance, and superior skill, these athletes asserted Europe's status as a premier hub of youth sailing talent. With a tremendous record, European sailors won all four gold medals and secured an astounding nine of twelve available podium places across both age divisions and genders in this illustrious competition.

Portosalte's exhilaration was palpable as he reflected on his victory, "All the hard work from this year has paid off. I turned the disappointment of losing the European Championship in the last race into a resolve that fueled my performance here. My focus remained unshaken and led me to achieve the result I needed. I'm indebted to my coach, team, and family for their unwavering support. Today is a testament to the thrilling journey we've embarked on together."

In the Under 16 category, Turkey's Derin Bartan and France's Nathan Wehrle were imperious. Bartan also secured the commendable third place overall in the Girls’ fleet, while Wehrle ranked fifth among the Boys. This sterling achievement adds to the burgeoning list of European youth sailing stars who shine brightly on the international stage, extending the continent's impressive sailing legacy.

Europe's dominance in the competition underscores the region's deep and diverse talent pool. Athletes from Spain, Greece, Turkey, France, Italy, Sweden, Czech Republic, Great Britain, Switzerland, and Croatia exhibited splendid performances, each finding representation within the top ten. This European sweep reaffirms the continental supremacy in fostering sailing talent, and it promises great things for the future of the sport.

title: Thrilling Maneuvers and Tactical Decisions Shape the Second Day of Musto Lark National Championship 2025
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Thrilling Maneuvers and Tactical Decisions Shape the Second Day of Musto Lark National Championship 2025
summary: Well-executed strategies and heart-stopping moments punctuated Day 2 of the Musto Lark National Championship 2025, held at the South Caernarvonshire Yacht Club.
body: Day 2 of the Musto Lark National Championship 2025 proved a thrilling day of sailing at the South Caernarvonshire Yacht Club. With three races successfully completed, there were sharp strategies employed and impressive manoeuvres displayed along the course. Ed Bradburn and Holly Evans distinguished themselves in the first race, decisively holding their nerve amid a strong challenge from Tom Gillard and Rachael Gray, and capitalising on speed rather than distance to clinch their first win. Meanwhile, Gillard and Rachael Gray put a commendable effort trailing behind, securing the second position with Stuart and Nick Hydon taking up the third spot. The second race started in livelier breeze conditions, causing a scramble among the participants at the pin end due to tide fluctuations. It was racers Bradburn/Evans who took advantage and claimed the lead, displaying the skill and determination that sailing fans have come to have admire, and successfully led around the first marker. Gillard/Gray performed admirably yet again, battling through the fleet to finish second. Race 3 saw a repeat of Race 2 with many contenders struggling to overcome the tide and cross the line. Despite an initially promising lead by Fells/Allen, they ultimately lost out due to being Over Course Side (OCS). This allowed Gillard/Gray to resolutely sail through and snatch up their very first win of the championship. On the last day, spectators saw plenty of place changing before Jon and Vicky Brickwood pulled ahead, their triumph a testament to the power of holding the right corner. Day 2 of the Championship truly underlined the thrill and unpredictability of sailing, a sport where the combination of peak physical and mental abilities, as well as respect for the caprices of nature, can determine the winners and the also-rans.

title: Luxurious M/Y Milena Joins West Nautical's Fleet, Offering Exceptional Charter Ventures Across the Adriatic
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Luxurious M/Y Milena Joins West Nautical's Fleet, Offering Exceptional Charter Ventures Across the Adriatic
summary: Welcoming an extravagant addition, West Nautical is growing its CA fleet with the splendid M/Y Milena, an epitome of luxury at sea.
body: West Nautical celebrates the inclusion of yet another extraordinary yacht to their CA fleet, the exemplary M/Y Milena joining the ranks with her luxurious offerings and splendid sea experience. The stunning, 28.31m Custom Line Navetta 28 yacht, Milena, delivered by Ferretti in 2018, adds a new dimension of grandeur to the fleet. She has been crafted meticulously to spell opulence and comfort in every part of her build, from her expanse of 3 luxe decks to her stylish and spacious five cabin layouts. The yacht's exterior, designed by Zuccon International, is a sight to behold, enveloping guests in the comfortable embrace of top-notch amenities and luxurious milieu. Whether you envisage a leisurely family getaway in the sun or a thrilling Adriatic quest with close buddies, Milena never fails to exceed expectations. Her three exterior decks serve as sanctuaries isolated from the world's clamour. Ensconced in these heavenly outdoor spaces, guests can indulge in snug sunbathing, savour their morning coffee or evening drinks, or enjoy alfresco dining against the breathtaking panoramic ocean views. The main aft deck houses another grand social nucleus that transforms into an enchanting spot for starlit dinners. Adding to the charm is the yacht's fold-out beach club, tailor-made for morning swims or kick-starting an exciting water adventure. Stepping inside, Milena reveals an expansive salon that emanates serenity with its bright ambiance and neutral tones. High-class entertainment options include comfortable seating arrangements and a fold-down television. Her sleeping quarters are just as elegant, flaunting five commodious and well-equipped cabins, along with a full beam master cabin on the main deck. Regardless of your sailing conditions, Milena's zero-speed and underway stabilisers ensure a smooth, comforting sailing experience at her 10-knot cruising speed. Additionally, her fuel-efficient consumption provides economical voyaging for longer periods. With M/Y Milena, West Nautical promises an unparalleled sailing escapade, enveloped in luxury's plush embrace.

title: RMK Marine's Seven Seas Superyacht Gets a €2M Trim on Its Price Tag
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: RMK Marine's Seven Seas Superyacht Gets a €2M Trim on Its Price Tag
summary: The 36.9m explorer yacht ‘Seven Seas’, built by RMK Marine, has a new central agent and a €2 million price reduction ahead of sale.
body: A captivating blend of steel and aluminium, the 36.9metre explorer yacht ‘Seven Seas’ from RMK Marine has recently undergone a change of central agents. Consequently, this opportunity has been followed by a significant price drop of €2 million, fetching future owners a handsome deal.

Launched in July 2024, the naval architecture of ‘Seven Seas’ comes from Dutch studio Vripack. Their latest collaboration marks the sixth one so far with the Turkish yard. ‘Seven Seas’ holds the solitary model title from RMK Marine's 120 series, where Vripack's design had been imagined on a grand scale.

Functionality and aesthetics blend seamlessly in ‘Seven Seas’, which was crafted with an experienced yachtsman's vision. The design philosophy behind ‘Seven Seas’ revolved around world cruising. Consequently, the explorer yacht showcases a refined, masculine trawler-style exterior. The interior contrasted by a feminine, family-focused feel, for which Turkish design studio, Epikworks, took the helm.

But the true magic lies in the exteriors. The bridge deck's aft hosts a large lounge space shielded by the deck above. It allows for an enjoyable all-weather experience. Above this, the private top deck is replete with a Jacuzzi, a bar and sofa seating – perfect for luxury and relaxation. The main deck offers an al fresco dining space with aft-facing seats. The 55-square-metre dedicated tender deck carries two 7.5-metre tenders, and a significant lazarette furnishes further storage for water toys and RIBs.

‘Seven Seas’ is powered by Caterpillar C32 engines, promising a 14-knot maximum speed with a 10-knot cruising speed. With its new central agents, the explorer yacht ‘Seven Seas’ is awaiting a lucky owner to set sail across the high seas for a reduced price of €16,500,000.

title: Thrills and Antics at the Inspiring Lowestoft Sea Week 2025 in the Royal Norfolk & Suffolk Yacht Club
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Thrills and Antics at the Inspiring Lowestoft Sea Week 2025 in the Royal Norfolk & Suffolk Yacht Club
summary: Lowestoft Sea Week 2025 brought an exhilarating mix of competitive spirit and camaraderie, with unexpected weather conditions and high-stakes competition.
body: Lowestoft Sea Week 2025, hosted by the renowned Royal Norfolk & Suffolk Yacht Club, underwent a significant switch this year. The event, traditionally slated for August, sailed in during the neap tide week of July. This alteration spun out extraordinary racing competitions, albeit with fewer participants than usual.

This week-long oceanic extravaganza was orchestrated under the energetic guidance of Jenny and Bryan Riley as Race Officers. Their robust team was abetted by about 20 STARS (Support Team Aiding Racing at Sea) volunteers who provided vital on-the-water assistance.

The festivities commenced with the Inshore Challenge on the Saturday preceding the main event, which saw five boats racing against the currents. Among these challengers was Richard Fryer, the Commodore of the hosting yacht club. Veronica and Ben Falat's Squib, the Squffy, and the Custard, steered by Richard Fryer and David Houghton, emerged as two memorable entrants.
The following day, Sunday, was dominated by stirring and much-anticipated BODs and Squibs races, with Richard Sullivan and Sue Harper's Clever Dick clinching a spectacular Squib victory.

Monday's weather threw a wrench in proceedings with an odd mix of aggressive squalls complemented by an eerily calm afternoon. Competitors rushed to cover their boats before taking refuge at the bar, waiting for the weather to stabilise.

Tuesday was a testing day for the STARS team, as they organised two consecutive races amidst shifting off-shore winds. However, in true sailing fashion, they took it in stride, showing the resilience and adaptability that make the event such a captivating spectacle each year. The Lowestoft Sea Week 2025, with its twist of dates, turbulent weather, and thrilling sailing confrontations, proved once more why it is an event eagerly awaited and inscribed in the calendar by sailing enthusiasts worldwide.

title: Regal 2665 Commodore
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Regal 2665 Commodore
summary: A Classy Compact Cruiser That Goes the Distance For boaters who dream of escaping for a weekend on the water without sacrificing performance or comfort, the Regal 2665 Commodore has long stood as a well-balanced option. Built with Regal Boats’ signature attention to craftsmanship and detail, this mid-sized express cruiser packs big-boat features into a trailerable hull. Whether you're stepping up from a bowrider or d
body: First impressions count, and the 2665 doesn't disappoint. With a length overall of 27 feet 6 inches (including the extended swim platform) and an 8-foot-6-inch beam, it’s compact enough for trailering yet offers a surprising amount of onboard living space. The lines are sleek and modern, with a sporty, slightly aggressive stance that hints at the boat’s performance capabilities.

Construction is classic Regal—solid fiberglass hull, stainless steel fittings, and a thoughtfully laid-out deck. Notably, the 2665 features Regal’s innovative FasTrac hull, a stepped-hull design that reduces drag and improves speed, efficiency, and handling. The benefits are immediate and noticeable: quicker planing, tighter turns, and smoother cruising in choppy waters.

This hull innovation, paired with either a Volvo Penta or MerCruiser stern drive (typically in the 270–320 HP range), makes the 2665 agile and fun to drive. Depending on configuration and conditions, you can expect a top speed in the 35–40 knot range, with a comfortable and economical cruise speed around 24–28 knots.

The Regal 2665 handles beautifully underway. The helm is responsive and ergonomic, offering good sightlines and excellent feedback through the wheel. The twin bolster-equipped helm seat allows for standing or seated operation, and all instrumentation is within easy reach. Trim tabs and full engine controls give the skipper all the tools needed for confident navigation.

The FasTrac hull really shines when the sea state kicks up. While no 27-footer will glide through a heavy chop like a long-range cruiser, the 2665 performs admirably, with a soft, dry ride and a noticeable reduction in bow rise during acceleration. It’s a cruiser that feels nimble, not cumbersome—ideal for skippers who enjoy active driving.

One of the best things about the 2665 is how Regal uses every inch of space. The cockpit is smartly arranged for entertaining and relaxation. At the stern, a U-shaped lounge wraps around a removable table—perfect for evening drinks or a dockside lunch. A compact wet bar with sink is built into the port side, while the helm to starboard features a two-person seat that swivels to face the cockpit when socializing.

Storage is plentiful, including under-seat lockers, a transom locker, and access to the engine bay under the aft deck. The integrated swim platform is large enough for sunbathing or launching water toys, and includes a ladder and transom shower—great for rinsing off after a swim.
Optional extras on many models include a radar arch, full camper canvas, cockpit fridge, and upgraded sound systems. Add shore power and you’ve got a capable weekend home on the water.

Step below deck, and the 2665 reveals its real secret: it’s far roomier than its dimensions suggest. The cabin is finished with rich cherry cabinetry, easy-to-clean faux teak flooring, and quality upholstery. A combination of hull ports and an overhead hatch allow for decent natural light and ventilation.

At the bow, a convertible V-berth doubles as a dinette with a solid wood table. Aft is a true double berth, tucked under the helm deck, ideal for kids or a couple. It’s not quite standing headroom throughout (around 5'10"), but it's generous enough for most to move about comfortably.

The galley is compact but fully functional, with a single burner stove, microwave, refrigerator, stainless steel sink, and a Corian-style countertop. You can prepare basic meals or snacks easily without having to rely on shore facilities.
The enclosed head features a manual or electric toilet, vanity sink, and a pull-out shower. Hot water is standard on many models, and the head compartment is well-ventilated and cleanly finished.

With a 74-gallon fuel tank and 20 gallons of freshwater, the Regal 2665 is well-suited for overnight trips or long days on the water. It’s not a bluewater cruiser, but it excels in protected coastal waters, large lakes, and inland rivers. A VHF radio (typically Channel 16) and chartplotter make navigation safer, and many owners upgrade with radar and autopilot for extended cruising.
Because the beam is under 9 feet, it’s trailerable in many regions without a permit—offering flexibility for those who want to tow to new cruising grounds.

Owners consistently praise the 2665 for its thoughtful design, build quality, and performance. Many cite the luxurious feel of the interior and the solid ride as key reasons for purchase. It’s a boat that inspires confidence and pride of ownership.

However, some note that engine access can be tight, particularly for DIY maintenance, and the cabin headroom may feel snug for taller individuals. Like all older boats, used models may require updates to electronics or canvas, so a thorough survey is recommended.

In a crowded market of express cruisers, the Regal 2665 Commodore stands out as a well-executed blend of style, comfort, and seaworthiness. It’s a boat that punches above its weight, delivering a big-boat experience in a compact, manageable package. Whether you're watching the sunset from the cockpit, anchoring in a quiet bay, or cruising toward the next port, the 2665 offers everything you need for memorable weekends on the water.

If you're in the market for a used express cruiser in the 25–30 foot range, the Regal 2665 deserves a spot on your shortlist. It’s a stylish, seaworthy, and surprisingly spacious cruiser that still turns heads today.
