title: Ultim SVR Lazartigue Outraces the Opposition at Rolex Fastnet: Supermaxis Primed
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Ultim SVR Lazartigue Outraces the Opposition at Rolex Fastnet: Supermaxis Primed
summary: In a thrilling turn of events at the Rolex Fastnet race, French Ultim SVR Lazartigue beats Banque Populaire by an hour to round Fastnet Rock first.
body: It was a riveting day of racing at the Rolex Fastnet race on July 27, 2025, as four remarkable 100ft foiling trimarans rounded Fastnet Rock, putting on an exhilarating display of speed and skill. The French Ultim SVR Lazartigue, skippered by the impressive Tom Lapeche, stole the limelight by taking the lead at 1520hrs local time, an hour before the second yacht, Banque Populaire. Following closely behind were Actual Ultim 4 at 1706hrs, and Sudebo Ultim 3 at 1800hrs.

All four yachts are now racing downwind to round the Scilly Isles, before raising sails to set course for the finish line at the French port of Cherbourg. They are hitting speeds over 30kts, carving quite extreme angles to maintain apparent wind speed as they strive to reach the Scilly Isles, believed to be directly downwind from Fastnet Rock.

Behind these front runners, three supermaxi monohulls, SHK Scallywag, Black Jack 100, and Leopard, are on the prowl. Skippered by David Witt, the leader SHK Scallywag is clocking a speed of 13kts towards Fastnet Rock. While no rounding time is projected yet, it makes for an intriguing watch, setting stage for what promises to be a thrilling day of sailing ahead.

title: The 36.9-metre Seven Seas Explorer Yacht Drops Price Tag by €2M: An Alluring Deal on the Open Seas Now Within Grasp
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The 36.9-metre Seven Seas Explorer Yacht Drops Price Tag by €2M: An Alluring Deal on the Open Seas Now Within Grasp
summary: Negotiate the open waters with elegance and power as the striking 36.9-metre explorer yacht, the Seven Seas, receives a considerable €2,000,000 price drop.
body: Take the helm, dear mariner, and set your course for the prestigious Seven Seas explorer yacht, a paragon of maritime splendor, that’s just become more affordable. Created by RMK Marine, this 36.9-metre wonder recently shifted to fresh representation by Onur Erardag of Nautique Yachting, coinciding with a hefty €2,000,000 price reduction.

The Seven Seas was birthed into existence in July 2024, masterfully crafted with the robustness of steel and the agility of aluminium. It is the brainchild of Dutch studio Vripack's design and naval architecture, marking the sixth successful partnership with the Turkish yard. The one-of-a-kind luxury explorer boat is a unique gem in the crown of RMK Marine's 120 series. The design is a true embodiment of 'less is more' - a compact explorer yacht with all the grandeur you'd expect from a large-scaled model.

But it's not just about comfort; it's about connection. Centre the living spaces around streams of natural light pouring in through expansive windows, painting everyday aboard the Seven Seas in a breathtakingly cosy ambiance. Bask in the warmth of light-wood panelling, integrated lighting, and a soothing white-and-blue color palette that echoes the gentle rhythm of the surrounding seas.

The real pièce de résistance of this explorer yacht lies outside, where the magic truly unfolds. Suppose it's a lazy afternoon reading session or a round of spirited drinks. In that case, the large lounge space, at the aft of the bridge deck, lets you relax under the overhang of the deck above - a shelter for all seasons.

The ocean's whispers beckon you to the top deck, boasting a refreshing Jacuzzi, a fully-stocked bar, and comfortable sofa seating, making it the perfect venue for crisp leisure evenings or sun-lit morning brunches. If dining under the stars is more your style, the main deck offers an al fresco feast complete with aft-facing seating.

If you're a thrill-seeker, you'll find ample storage for water toys and RIBs, alongside a 55-square-metre dedicated tender deck that can house two 7.5-metre tenders. Let the Caterpillar C32 engines propel you through the waters with a maximum speed of 14 knots and a cruising speed of 10 knots. Fresh from the shipyard, the Seven Seas offers the exclusive opportunity to become the first owner of this extraordinary vessel – now available for €16,500,000.

Cast off with confidence aboard the Seven Seas, a prestigious jewel of the sea, now within your grasp less roughly 2 million euros. Seize this opportunity and embark on your next nautical adventure of a lifetime.

title: Stella M, A New Addition to the Feadship Fleet, Triumphantly Sets Sail on Sea Trials
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Stella M, A New Addition to the Feadship Fleet, Triumphantly Sets Sail on Sea Trials
summary: Stella M, the spectacular 71.8-meter Feadship superyacht has embarked on her sea trials after a successful launch.
body: They say luxury is in the detail, and with the 71.8-meter Feadship build Stella M, there is much luxurious detail to behold. Introduced as Project 827, construction began back in 2022. The lavish superyacht was snapped up by Burgess only six weeks after entering the market in July 2023, and its new, discerning owner is set to take delivery in August.

But what clinched the deal? According to Feadship's sales director, Maarten Janssen, it was a magnificent blend of timely delivery and the opportunity to bypass the waiting list, paired with the yacht's stunning exterior and interior design. The yacht resonated with the owner's preferences for a family-use layout.

The main deck comes with a seven-meter swimming pool and reveals a state-of-the-art wellness center at the heart of the vessel accessible via the beach club and main staircase. The unconventional cabin layout optimises natural light, with seven cabins including two VIP suites and four staterooms strategically placed on the main deck. Notably, the yacht houses an exclusive owner's deck with a master suite, private breakfast area, and hot tub framing panoramic views.

Additional deck areas are equally stunning. The sundeck holds a second pool with expansive sun pads. Meanwhile, a sizable aft deck offers a perfect spot for dining and relaxation. Balancing functionality and aesthetics, Stella M stands as testament to Feadship’s commitment and dedication to producing superyachts of exceptional quality and design.

The Dutch shipyard is currently busy with fifteen more projects of scale, one of which measures an impressive 132 meters and is scheduled for delivery in 2027. With the successful launch and sea trial of Stella M, they continue to set the benchmark in luxury superyacht design and construction.

title: Experiencing Sea-Splendour: Introducing the Eighth Unit of Amels 60 Superyacht, A Masterwork of Oceanic Opulence
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Experiencing Sea-Splendour: Introducing the Eighth Unit of Amels 60 Superyacht, A Masterwork of Oceanic Opulence
summary: Damen Yachting launches the eighth unit of grandiose Amels 60 series, taking the sea's luxury quotient up a notch.
body: In the city of Vlissingen, nestled snugly in the Netherlands, a masterpiece was born at Damen Yachting's shipyard. This diva, the eighth in the incredibly acclaimed Amels 60 series, is all set to make waves in the world of seafaring. The superyacht series first hit the maritime market in 2019, renowned for its geometric windows and grand exterior, hallmarks of a brilliant creation by Espen Øino.

Following closely in the successful wake of the seventh unit, Memories, the eighth child of Damen has generated soaring expectations and excitement. The illustrious tale of the series, from the first unit, 'Come Together', last sold at a staggering €59,950,000 to the Neptune reigning second unit 'Entourage', is itself a testament to triumph.

In terms of structural marvels, the yacht boasts a folding, 75-square-metre balcony within the owner's suite and a 162 square metre sundeck. Arranged typically with a 6-person Jacuzzi, a bar, and a sunbathing-friendly raised foredeck, it also doubles as a helicopter pad - truly, an adventurer's dream!

The yacht supports eco-friendly sailing with a hybrid propulsion package reaching a maximum speed of 15.5 knots on full power and 14 knots when 'eco-cruising'. On purely hybrid electrical motor propulsion, she can attain a speed of seven knots.

Damen Yachting's exciting work lineup includes three under-construction superyacht projects and a debut for its first Xplorer 60 model, After You, at the upcoming Monaco Yacht Show. With such a promising future, Damen Yachting continues to redefine the boundaries of luxury and comfort at sea. All sea-lovers should keep their binoculars focused on what Damen Yachting ventures next into the vast ocean of innovation.

title: Race Four of the Admiral’s Cup served up a proper Solent riddle
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Race 4 of the Admiral’s Cup served up a Solent riddle
summary: Beau Geste and Nola Strike as Light Airs Test the Best in the Solent Soft breeze, strong tide, and no margin for error. A classic light-wind shootout, where every shift mattered and boat speed had to be earned, not expected.
body: With the wind ghosting in from the north at 5 to 11 knots, and a west-going tide ripping across the course, PRO Stuart Childerley set up a windward-leeward challenge — 1.6nm for AC1 and 1.4nm for AC2 — well off the Hill Head shore. With the breeze flickering and the water still, it was brains over brawn from start to finish.

In AC1, it was Karl Kwok’s Beau Geste (TP52, RHKYC) that led the charge — at least on the water. They found early pace and punched ahead of Black Pearl and Jolt 3. But after IRC correction, it was Peter Harrison’s Jolt 3 (YCM) who snatched the win — by just three seconds. Behind them, Zen surged late for third, with Django WR51 roaring back from an OCS to finish just off the podium.

“We hadn’t seen a northerly in training,” said Beau Geste’s afterguard. “The call was to start hard right — even though the left looked favoured. We had a 50-degree header mid-leg. No warning. Just tack and survive. It was that kind of race — eyes out of the boat, constant decisions, no time to breathe. We sailed well, but Jolt had a blinder.”
Beau Geste’s consistency now puts the Royal Hong Kong Yacht Club in pole position overall — just one point ahead of Yacht Club de Monaco, with the Royal New Zealand Yacht Squadron in third.

In AC2, it was Nola (KSSS) that pulled off the upset. After a textbook pin-end start and early pressure call, tactician Juuso Roihu and navigator Aksel Magdahl rolled the dice — and nailed it. They held their lane, sailed clean, and on corrected time, won by over a minute. Beau Ideal (RHKYC) took line honours and second overall, with AMP-lifi (RORC White) rounding out the top three just seconds ahead of Abracadabra (NYYC).

“We knew it wasn’t a day to play safe,” said Magdahl. “The pressure was left, the call was there, and we committed. In a boat that doesn’t accelerate like some others, we have to out-think, not out-muscle. This crew — Estonian, Finnish, Swedish, Norwegian — is tight and tuned. Today we executed.”

Further down the fleet, Callisto (RNZYS) made a late surge but couldn’t claw past the frontrunners, while Garm and Edelweiss both struggled after early OCS calls. The front four broke away, but the real race was happening in the details — shifts, tide lines, clean manoeuvres. One poor tack and you were toast.

As the afternoon wore on, the wind faded and the race team stood down any further starts. With four races now in the books, and points from the offshore races carrying extra weight, it’s all to play for at the halfway mark. Hong Kong leads, but Monaco and New Zealand are breathing down their necks. Costa Smeralda isn’t out of it either.
The Solent reminded everyone why it’s such a difficult place to race. Light air doesn’t mean easy. Race 4 was proof that focus, finesse, and a bit of nerve can flip the leaderboard in an instant.

title: TEDx Forte dei Marmi: Shaping the Future of Sustainability in Yachting and Luxury Industries
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: TEDx Forte dei Marmi: Shaping the Future of Sustainability in Yachting and Luxury Industries
summary: The third TEDx Forte dei Marmi unfolds a stimulating discussion on sustainability, with a focus on Italy's influence in yachting, lifestyle, and design.
body: With the heart of Italy's shipbuilding hubs, Forte dei Marmi, as its stage, the third edition of TEDx Forte dei Marmi leaps onto the international scene on August 29. Held entirely on a beach, this one-of-a-kind event engages in thought-provoking discourses around the theme 'Designing Timeless Beauty'. Echoing the United Nations' 2030 Agenda, key speakers weave together themes of sustainability, yachting, fashion, tourism, and Italy's significant impact on them.

Renowned yacht designer Luca Dini, founder of LUCA DINI Design & Architecture, reveals insights into the convergence of yachting and architecture. This intriguing overlap has given birth to innovative, sustainable hybrid spaces, refining luxury, both ashore and afloat.

Joining them, founder of Formula Medicine, Dr. Riccardo Ceccarelli, unpacks the mental disciplines necessary to achieve peak performance. Top athletes, including Formula 1 drivers and tennis professionals, have benefited from his elite performance training programmes. Ceccarelli's insights resonate across high-pressure industries like yachting and luxury, providing strategies for maintaining performance under pressure.

In its remarkable role of fostering connection and sharing of transformative ideas, TEDx Forte dei Marmi, supported by generous sponsors like AB Yachts and Maiora, presents an extraordinary tribute to sustainable beauty blending tradition and innovation. Located in Forte dei Marmi, the audience can soak in the region's magical atmosphere, history, and rich cultural heritage, strengthening the global discourse on sustainability.

title: Unearthed Documents Reveal Efforts for a New Britannia: A Look into Palace Intrigue and Political Maneuvering
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unearthed Documents Reveal Efforts for a New Britannia: A Look into Palace Intrigue and Political Maneuvering
summary: Declassified government documents unveil behind-the-curtain bid to replace the iconic HMY Britannia during turbulent ’90s politics.
body: Deep within the labyrinthine folds of Britain's political and institutional history, secret whispers of ventures and objectives float through corridors of time, only to be flushed out years later. Such is the case with the quest for a successor to the HMY Britannia, as revealed by recently declassified UK government files. A silent campaign, shrouded in bureaucratic language and covert diplomacy, unrolled under the gaze of unexpectedly critical public eyes.

Delving into the files, one discovers a series of diplomatic gambits carried out in the 1990s by senior Buckingham Palace officials. Keen on ensuring a smooth transition, they discreetly engaged with Prime Minister John Major's administration to commission another royal sea bird to succeed the Britannia. Yet, the tightrope walk between constitutional neutrality and institutional giveaways was fraught with challenges.

The discussions centred around commissioning a new vessel, the cost of which was estimated at £50 million. Despite their cautious approach, attempts were made, behind carefully crumpled political memos, to frame the yacht as a diplomatic asset, accentuating its systemic value.

The urgency was borne of the period's political climate which was rife with public scepticism over taxpayer-funded repairs to Windsor Castle and the general decline in the Royal Family's popularity. The task was made more daunting given Labour’s general election victory under Tony Blair, which effectively overturned the Conservative promise of commissioning a replacement for Britannia.

Britannia was formally decommissioned after her final duty — making sure the last Governor of Hong Kong was safely returned to UK soil amidst the handover to China. Serving for 44 years, the Britannia had completed 696 foreign visits and 272 domestic voyages, commemorating herself as a pivotal diplomatic platform. However, subsequent plans for a successor yacht remained unrealised, and the dream of a new Britannia was once again cast adrift.

title: The 2025 Noakes Sydney Gold Coast Yacht Race Kicks Off Amid Perfect Sailing Conditions
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The 2025 Noakes Sydney Gold Coast Yacht Race Kicks Off Amid Perfect Sailing Conditions
summary: The eagerly-anticipated Noakes Sydney Gold Coast Yacht Race 2025 commenced amidst stunning winter weather, showcasing a thrilling, adrenaline-fuelled day on the waves.
body: On a picture-perfect winter day, the fleet for the 2025 Noakes Sydney Gold Coast Yacht Race set off at 1300hrs sharp. Under a brilliant winter sun, the yachts sailed north with a strong 13-15 knots, weaving through the light morning rain and evaporating clouds.

The conditions were near-perfect. As the yachts swiftly navigated the harbour, the larger boats showcased their prowess. There were two striking face-offs that held spectators' eyes captive: a nail-biting match between Wild Thing 100 and Moneypenny, and a fierce battle between Smuggler and Highly Sprung. Every second was a testament to tactical acumen, and every metre gained was a victory fiercely celebrated.

Smuggler, helmed by the adept Tim Davis and owned by Sebastian Bohm, was the first non-mini maxi to make its way out of Sydney Harbour. As the reigning champion of the 2024/25 Audi Centre Sydney Blue Water Pointscore, all eyes were on the Smuggler crew to repeat their sparkling performance. Frantic and Sticky, along with Highly Sprung, Koa, and Antipodes, closely followed behind.

Threading their way through the waves was a swarm of 40-foot range yachts, led by Daguet 2, Bushranger, and Minerva. With Division 1 and 2 packed with these formidable mid-sized yachts, onboard drama and high-seas action were practically guaranteed.

Among the 14 Double Handed teams, Avalanche emerged as the early leader. Co-skippers James Murchison and James Francis carried their wealth of experience from the Rolex Sydney Hobart Yacht Races into this competition, promising a fantastic contest in the days to come.

Every yacht race is a testament to the beauty of sailing, the synchronized dance of nature and machine, the thrill of competition, and the collective passion of sailors and spectators alike. And the 2025 Noakes Sydney Gold Coast Yacht race is set to be a sublime spectacle of this enduring saga.

title: TRANSPAC 2025: The Winners, The Legends, and the Long Blue Road
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: TRANSPAC 2025: The Winners, The Legends, and the Long Blue Road
imageCaption: Restless, winners of one of the race's top honors: the King Kalakaua Trophy
summary: Hawaiian sunshine, stories in the rigging, and rum in hand — the final Transpac 2025 prize-giving brought down the curtain in style on one of the world’s great ocean races. Held Saturday, July 19 at Kaneohe Yacht Club, the last of three awards ceremonies gave crews, skippers, and families a chance to celebrate not just the winners, but the sheer feat of making it across 2,225 miles of the Pacific Ocean.
body: Two earlier ceremonies took place at Waikiki Yacht Club (July 15) and Hawaii Yacht Club (July 17), but this was the big one — a gathering of salt-streaked legends and soaked heroes.

That honour, and the mighty Barn Door Trophy, went to Lucky, Bryon Ehrhart’s 88ft Juan K rocket sled. She did the job in 6 days, 6 hours, 23 minutes and 50 seconds — powered winches, movable ballast, and relentless pace.
That was Fast Exit II, John Raymont’s Ker 52, clocking in at 7 days, 15 hours, 39 minutes and 39 seconds — and earning the Merlin Trophy.

That went to Restless, Alli Bell’s Cal 40, with a corrected time of 8d 12h 5m 49s — and in doing so, Bell made history as the first woman skipper in Transpac’s 119-year run to win the overall handicap prize.

It didn’t stop there. Bell’s team also scooped the Aloha Class top prize, the Jensen-Lapworth Trophy (fastest Cal 40), and dominated Bridger Insurance Division 9. It was a masterclass from stem to stern.
Second overall corrected went to Jack Jennings’ Pied Piper, earning the Skip Warren Memorial, while Fast Exit II pocketed the Tureen Trophy for third.
Arsenal (J/125) took Garmin Division 6 and the Clark Sweet Trophy.
Macondo and Insoumise battled it out in Pasha Division 8.
BadPak won Boatswain’s Locker Division 1.
Fast Exit II cleaned up Mount Gay Division 2.
Pied Piper took Whittier Trust Division 3.
Aimant de Fille came out on top in Cal Maritime Division 4.
Westerly beat the SC52 fleet in Cabrillo Division 5.
Rahan, the stripped Beneteau First 36 doublehanded by Courouble and Devanneaux, took Suntex Division 7 — and also bagged the Jobson Leukemia Trophy for first doublehanded finisher.
Convexity2, Don Wilson’s Gunboat 68, dominated Division 10 and won the Rudy Choy Perpetual for fastest multihull.
Every division winner took home a Garmin quatix 7 Marine Smartwatch and a bottle of Mount Gay Black Barrel rum — not a bad way to toast the crossing.
Bolt earned the all-amateur crew prize, the Edmund Grant Trophy.
Zimmer, skippered by Samantha Gebb, took the Don Clothier Trophy for top under-49’ racer/cruiser.
Heroic Heart earned the Ilio Aukai Trophy for oldest crew average age.
Rhiannon, skippered by Stacy Sinclair, won both the Pacific High (furthest north) and Tail-End Charlie (last finisher) trophies.
Crusade, Groundhog Day, and Macondo formed Team MDR Fenders Out and took the Kenwood IOR Cup for top team performance.
Navigators weren’t forgotten either. Offshore strategy still matters in this satellite age:
Stan Honey (on Lucky) won the Ben Mitchell for fastest elapsed.
Graham Bell (on Restless) won the Chuck Ullman for fastest corrected.
Top divisional nav trophies went to Matt Wachowicz (Pied Piper), Randy Smith (Aimant de Fille), Chris Busch (Westerly), Ben Allen (Arsenal), and more.

And let’s raise a glass to Django Tomlinson, who claimed the prestigious Mark S. Rudiger Celestial Navigation Trophy — old-school stars and sextant navigation aboard Cal Maritime-Oaxaca. There’s still a place for dead reckoning in the digital age.
Best onboard media? That went to Andreas, a Norseman 447 skippered by Bernt Helgass, with standout video work from crewmember Lizzie Easter. The Ronald L. Burla Trophy never looked so deserved.
And finally, behind the scenes: Janet Kelley was honoured with the Clare Lang Trophy for outstanding service as part of the Honolulu Committee — proof that these races are won both at sea and ashore.

From brand-new maxis to ocean-worn cruisers, from sextants to Starlink, Transpac 2025 delivered classic drama and quiet triumph. Some crossed fast, some crossed last — but every boat that made it to Diamond Head did something extraordinary.
Now, it's back to the docks, the barstools, and the boatyards. But make no mistake — the Pacific will be calling again soon.

title: Escape the fast lane & relax on the Norfolk Broads in the UK
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Boating on the Norfolk Broads
summary: Boating on the Norfolk Broads in the UK offers a serene escape across over 125 miles of lock-free open waterways, a National Park formed from medieval peat diggings, now a haven of rivers, lakes, and wildlife-rich landscapes.
body: Spanning Norfolk and Suffolk, the Broads are ideal for exploring by boat—whether a traditional sailing yacht, a modern cruiser, or a day boat hired from key spots like Wroxham, often called the "Capital of the Broads." With its vast skies, rare birds like the bittern, and peaceful waters, the Broads are perfect for a relaxed 2025 adventure, whether for families, couples, or solo traveler's.

Wroxham, on the River Bure in the Northern Broads, is a bustling hub and a must-visit. Known as the heart of the Broads, it’s home to numerous boat hire companies like Norfolk Broads Direct, offering everything from day boats to week-long cruisers. Wroxham’s waterfront is lively with shops, cafes, and the historic Wroxham Bridge, a low medieval structure requiring careful navigation (air draft around 2.2 meters). The village also offers access to the Bure Valley Railway, a narrow-gauge steam train running to Aylsham, adding a nostalgic touch to your trip.

Moorings across the Broads cater to various needs. In Wroxham, you can moor at Norfolk Broads Direct or Hoveton St John, both providing easy access to local amenities like the Hotel Wroxham, which has a riverside restaurant. Horning, a picturesque village further along the Bure, offers moorings at The Ferry Inn or Horning Staithe, though spaces can fill quickly. For a quieter stop, Neatishead on the River Ant provides free moorings at Neatishead Staithe, a short walk from the White Horse Inn, known for its cozy atmosphere. Acle, also on the Bure, has moorings at the Acle Bridge Inn, a family-friendly spot with a large beer garden. In the Southern Broads, Reedham Quay offers free 24-hour Broads Authority moorings, perfect for a brief stop to explore the village’s historic railway swing bridge.

Waterside pubs enhance the Broads experience with hearty meals and scenic views. In Wroxham, the Hotel Wroxham’s restaurant serves modern British cuisine with river views, a great spot after mooring. In Horning, The Ferry Inn offers a warm welcome with moorings right outside, serving local ales and pub classics. The Acle Bridge Inn on the River Bure, with 12 moorings, is popular for its Suffolk cider, Norfolk ales, and gluten-free menu, ideal for families. In Coltishall, the King’s Head on the Bure provides top-notch food—reservations are wise as it’s a local favorite. For a rustic vibe, the White Horse Inn near Neatishead Staithe delivers a traditional pub experience with real ales. These pubs, easily accessible by boat, make for perfect stops, blending culinary delights with the Broads’ tranquil charm, ensuring a memorable journey.

title: Escapade, the Jewel of Fitzroy Yachts, Changes Hands in an In-House Deal
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Escapade, the Jewel of Fitzroy Yachts, Changes Hands in an In-House Deal
summary: The 37.5-meter sailing yacht Escapade, a marvel produced by Fitzroy Yachts, has been successfully sold in a private deal.
body: Escapade, the 37.5-meter sailing yacht constructed with precision and skill by the renowned Fitzroy Yachts in New Zealand, has been sold. The deal was an exclusive affair, involving Will Bishop and Matt Albert from Superyacht Partners. Delivered in 2014, Escapade is an exquisite long-range cruising yacht, embodying high performance and elegance.

The yacht's all-British design features an exterior crafted by the esteemed Dubois Naval Architects, with an interior styled by Design Unlimited. Escapade's previous owner kept her in immaculate condition, which played a significant role in upholding her allure in the market. The yacht underwent a comprehensive refit and completed her Lloyd's 10-year survey in 2024-2025, strengthening her appeal and usability.

Amenities on the yacht's vast exterior, including a jacuzzi, large sunpads, and an exercise bike that grandly emerges through a flush deck hatch offer a unique and indulgent experience for the guests aboard. Guests can enjoy the deck saloon boasting large double-glazed windows for awe-inspiring panoramic views and a suave lounge and bar.

Thanks to an impressive rig that stretches 50 meters above the waterline, Escapade stands tall in the water. She's powered by a singular Caterpillar engine which allows for a cruising speed of nine knots and a remarkable range of up to 3,900 nautical miles. This sailing gem, Escapade, was last asking €13,750,000.

title: Nautitech 40 Open Catamaran
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Nautitech 40 Open Catamaran
summary: The Nautitech 40 Open, a 39.4-foot catamaran that’s as much a lifestyle statement as it is a vessel, crafted for the modern sea lover. Built in Rochefort, France, by Nautitech Catamarans—now under the savvy umbrella of Capital Management Partners alongside Bavaria—this multihull marvel is a blend of Franco-German engineering and eco-conscious swagger.
body: Using VacuTec vacuum infusion, its resin-infused, foam-core hull cuts weight by 20% and slashes emissions by 80%, all while isophthalic acid resin wards off osmosis like a charm. At 11.98 meters long with a 6.91-meter beam, it’s a sleek, light contender at 8,500 kg, ready to glide through the waters of the Ionian, Amalfi Coast or the British Virgin Islands with effortless style. Marc Lombard, the design maestro behind this cat, pioneered the "Open" concept, and it’s a game-changer. The cockpit and saloon merge into one sprawling, indoor-outdoor living space, a tarpaulin system flexing to your mood—open for sun-soaked days, enclosed for stormy nights. It’s the ultimate setup for sipping rosé at anchor, whether you’re off Santorini or in the Whitsundays. The Mark 2 saloon’s aft-facing galley, decked with a double-drawer fridge, cockpit cooler, and freezer, ensures you’re stocked for the long haul, while the cockpit table seats eight with ease. Add coach roof loungers for sunset views, and you’ve got a floating penthouse vibe, amplified by hull windows and hatches that flood the space with light and sea breezes.

Performance? This cat’s got moves. A full batten mainsail, self-tacking jib, and roller furling make it a dream for short-handed sailing, with twin aft helms offering panoramic views of the sails and horizon. Lines lead to electric winches, and the high aspect sail plan lets you point 55 to 60 degrees upwind, especially with a Code 0 in lighter winds. Narrow, hydrodynamic hulls keep drag low, while hard-chined steps maximise cabin space without killing speed. Standard 30hp engines (50hp if you’re feeling extra) hit 7 knots at 2,000rpm, with zero slamming thanks to solid bridged deck clearance. Owners report 8–10 knots in moderate breezes, pushing 15 knots when the wind kicks up—a lively ride for its size.

Below deck, the Nautitech 40 Open caters to your crew’s vibe. Opt for the 4-cabin layout—four doubles, two heads with showers, plus a cockpit rinse—or the 3-cabin owner’s version with a sprawling master suite. Air conditioning, a B&G nav station with Triton displays, and a Zeus 9” chartplotter keep things luxe, whether you’re chartering in the Caribbean or cruising the Solent during Cowes Week (August 2–8, 2025 https://oldseadogs.com/boat-shows/the-199th-cowes-week-2025/ ). Light oak or walnut finishes add a modern edge, though some owners on the Nautitech Owners Facebook Group suggest more galley storage for extended trips.

The nautitech 40 pricing starts at €515,000, but load it up with a water maker, heating, and AIS, and you’re looking at €650,000–€665,000. Used models on YachtWorld span £183,173 for a 2014 to £563,944 for a 2025, or charter one for $5,000–$8,000 a week in the BVI or the Ionian. Early builds had hiccups—battery failures within 18 months and sun-damaged grey roofs (now white)—but the Generation 3 updates refine the helm and layout, keeping it fresh.

This catamaran isn’t just a boat; it’s a lifestyle. Stable, spacious, and built for the social sailor, the Nautitech 40 Open delivers the kind of effortless elegance that makes every voyage Instagram-worthy. Whether you’re chasing trade winds or hosting a floating dinner party, it’s your ticket to coastal chic. I have hired one of these 3 times and sailed around the Ionian / the greek islands. Its Ideal for family and friends. Plenty of space for them all to relax and sunbathe while I guide us to another island for dinner.

title: Record MOCRA Turnout for the Fastnet Centenary
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Record MOCRA Turnout for the Fastnet Centenary
summary: The 2025 Rolex Fastnet Race marks 100 years of hard offshore truth — and the multihull fleet has shown up in force. A record 20 boats are racing in the MOCRA class, all gunning for the coveted Crystal Trophy, a prize that’s older than some of the hulls — and certainly a few of the crews.
body: The Ultims and Ocean Fiftys may have their own sandbox, but the rest — cats, tris, cruisers and carbon flyers — are throwing down together in one of the most eclectic, unpredictable lineups in offshore sailing.

Leading the charge are the MOD70s — Argo (Jason Carroll, USA) and Zoulou (Erik Maris, FRA) — both turbocharged and loaded with offshore firepower. Loïck Peyron is on Zoulou, Brian Thompson on Argo. Their Channel Race showdown was a 30-knot drag race into the Solent, with Argo edging it by just three minutes. Not bad for boats nearly a decade old and now tricked out with custom foils.

Thompson helped push multihulls into the Fastnet in 1997 after an unofficial run on Lakota alongside the fleet. Peyron smashed the 1999 course record on Fujicolor. Now both are back, older, wiser, and still outrageously fast.

Beyond the MODs, it’s a proper feast. Among the standouts is the ORC 50 GDD, crewed by Halvard Mabire and Vendée vet Miranda Merron. Mabire first did this race in 1977 on a She 36. In ’97, he won both line honours and on CHS time — the last time anyone pulled off the double. Now, aged but undiminished, he’s back with a carbon cat and a freezer full of food.
“This boat is like what we used to race — cruiser-racers with guts,” Mabire said. “Built strong, fast enough, and practical. We can take passengers. We can live on it. And we can race hard.”

Then come the Dazcats — Britain’s homegrown fleet of fast cruising cats, all built at the Multihull Centre on the Cornish side of the Tamar. Simon Baker, MOCRA Vice Commodore, heads the charge aboard Hissy Fit, his fourth Dazcat and a class winner back in 2017. This year’s edition includes eight Dazcats ranging from 33ft to nearly 50, from refitted classics like Dazzle to the sharp new Minor Swing, skippered by French Figaro veteran Didier Bouillard.

Rupert Kidd, MOCRA Commodore, brings his Sueños — complete with washing machine and freezer, and crewed by one of the most seasoned offshore teams afloat. Bare Necessities, Easy Tiger, Slinky Malinki — the Dazcats bring depth, diversity, and British steel to a field full of French flair and foil.

Trimaran fans aren’t left wanting either. Paradox, a 63ft Nigel Irens design, is back under new ownership. Suerte, a grand prix 40-footer, now belongs to JFA Yachts’ Frédéric Jaouen, with Vendée Globe star Maxime Sorel aboard. Morpheus (Shuttleworth 39), Uno (Grainger 36), Rayon Vert (Pulsar 50) with Vincent Riou onboard — all fast, all built for the blue.

Even the smallest entries have teeth. Dogzhouse, an Excess 14 cruiser-cat, is the lowest-rated in the MOCRA class — but don’t count her out. And then there’s Tan 3, the brand new Dragonfly 40, fresh off wins at La Trinité–Cowes and the ArMen Race.

And just when you think you’ve seen it all, there’s Black Cap and Aile Bleue — two vintage Dick Newick tris with the iconic curves and low-slung frames that recall Olympus Photo and Mike Birch’s famous 1978 Route du Rhum upset.

Simon Baker sums it up: “The centenary brought them out — from pros to cruisers. Where else do you get to start with Ultims and IMOCAs blazing past you? It’s absolutely awesome. It’s why we race this.”

From carbon flyers to old school tris, from the Tamar to Concarneau, the MOCRA class has never looked stronger — or more varied. And as they line up off Cowes for the 2025 centenary start, one thing’s certain:
It’s going to be fast. It’s going to be wild. And the multihulls are here to put on a show.

title: Discover MASK architects' groundbreaking 85m superyacht concept, powered by eco-friendly 'Hydrogen Propulsion'
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover MASK architects' groundbreaking 85m superyacht concept, powered by eco-friendly 'Hydrogen Propulsion'
summary: Italian firm MASK architects delves into their hydrogen-powered superyacht concept, ONYX H2-B0 85, merging eco-conscious design with luxurious craftsmanship.
body: To embark on a journey of luxury while caring for the planet may soon be a reality, thanks to the ground-breaking vision of Italian studio, MASK architects. They lift the veil on their bold vision, code-named ONYX H2-B0 85, paving the way for an eco-conscious era of superyachting that's as luxurious as it is sustainable. This ambitious 85-metre project isn’t just another superyacht; it’s a flag bearer for an emerging future. Imagine, if you will, creating your fuel as you cruise the sea. By harnessing the transformative might of electrolysis and hydroelectric turbines, the ONYX H2-B0 85 could possibly produce hydrogen by tapping into the kinetic energy of the surrounding seawater. Principal designers Danilo Petta and Oznur Pinar Çer have engineered a mechanism that diminishes the requisite for vast fuel reserves, minimising reliance on fossil fuels. The hydrogen thus produced could power engines, generators, and fuel cells onboard or be stored to provide backing power. The design itself is reminiscent of sport yachts, with new renderings revealing an avant-garde living space encompassing eco-friendly and opulent materials. Leisure activities have been well-assumed, with ample space for sunbathing, alfresco dining, and even an aft deck swimming pool. A sophisticated seawater intake system is used to draw seawater, which is then treated to exclude harmful particles that could impede the electrolysis equipment. The water molecules are cleaved into hydrogen and oxygen gases via an electrical current, with the hydrogen being stored as fuel. The studio emphasises the necessity of marine engineering expertise and state-of-the-art equipment for the process. The concept of Hydrogen propulsion, while captivating, is receiving notable interest within the yachting sphere. Giants such as Port Vauban and the Port of Amsterdam are working towards incorporating hydrogen infrastructure. On a similar mission, the 118.8-metre superyacht Breakthrough, the world’s first hydrogen-powered superyacht by Feadship, will be making its debut at the Monaco Yacht Show this year. This move not only advocates for a more sustainable future but also propounds potential cost savings amid escalating fuel prices. MASK architects' daring vision is an invitation to embrace a future where luxury yachting is synonymous with ecological responsibility, made possible with the power of hydrogen.

title: 199th Cowes Week
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: The 199th Cowes Week 2025
summary: The 199th Cowes Week 2025, kicking off its 199th year, is set to be a jolly good time on the Solent waters near Cowes, Isle of Wight, from August 2 to August 8. Born in 1826, this grand old regatta, the longest-running sailing bash in the world, mixes fierce races with a great social vibe. Picture this: 1,000 boats, 8,000 sailors, and 100,000 happy spectators, all soaking up the fun. It’s now a summer must-do for eve
body: Cowes Week 2025, marking its 199th year, promises to be an exhilarating celebration of sailing excellence, set to unfold from Saturday, August 2, to Friday, August 8, on the iconic Solent waters off Cowes, Isle of Wight. Established in 1826, this prestigious regatta is the world’s longest-running sailing event, blending competitive racing with a vibrant social atmosphere, attracting around 1,000 boats, 8,000 competitors, and over 100,000 spectators. The event’s rich history and evolution from an elite pastime to an inclusive sport make it a cornerstone of the British sporting summer. The 2025 regatta will feature up to 40 races daily, accommodating a diverse fleet ranging from high-tech racing yachts to classic day boats, split into various handicap, one-design, and multihull classes. The renowned Royal Yacht Squadron line will host the rolling five-minute start sequence, a challenging and historic feature that enhances the event’s allure. Competitors, from Olympic professionals to weekend enthusiasts, will navigate the Solent’s tricky tides, showcasing skill and strategy. Notable classes like Dragons, Flying Fifteens, and Solent Sunbeams, raced for over 50 years, will join newer, popular designs, highlighting the regatta’s unique blend of tradition and innovation.

Beyond the water, Cowes Week 2025 will transform the town into a festival hub. Live music, open-air bars, market stalls, and black-tie balls will cater to all tastes, while the Musto Opening Party on August 2 will kick off the social calendar, supported by long-time sponsor Musto. Spectators can enjoy prime views from the Royal Ocean Racing Club or chartered yachts, with Garmin returning as the Official Weather Forecast Sponsor to provide real-time weather updates via the Cowes Week App and website. Entries opened in January 2025, offering Super Early Bird rates until February 16, Early Bird until May 4, and Standard Entry until July 20, with late entries accepted until the eve of the event.

Awards like the Queen’s Cup, Britannia Cup, and the Overall Winner Trophy will honour top performers, with the Young Skipper’s Trophy recognising talent under 25. As the 200th anniversary approaches in 2026, the event’s community spirit and sponsor support remain robust, ensuring a memorable 2025 regatta. Whether racing or spectating, Cowes Week offers an unmatched experience of sport and celebration.
So put it in your diary and join the fun if you can.

title: Melges Revolutionizes High-Speed Sailing with the US Debut of the Dynamic Switch One Design Foiling Dinghy
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Melges Revolutionizes High-Speed Sailing with the US Debut of the Dynamic Switch One Design Foiling Dinghy
summary: Melges Performance Sailboats makes waves as they announce the eagerly anticipated US launch of the Switch One Design, an innovative foiling dinghy.
body: With the captivating thrill of the ocean wave and the rush of wind in the sails, Melges Performance Sailboats proudly introduces the US launch of the Switch One Design Foiling Dinghy. This cutting-edge foiling dinghy is a game-changer in the sailing world, promising to blend stellar performance with accessibility, transforming the landscape of high-speed sailing. Tasked with national sales, support, and fostering growth for this quickly thriving global one-design class, Melges is ready to make a splash with the Switch.

Conceived by Element 6, the Switch is a high-performance, single-handed foiling dinghy that elevates the standards of sailing. It promises top-tier equipment and quality sailing in a package that is both moderately priced and widely available, aiming to attract sailors across the spectrum, worldwide.

"We're incredibly excited to bring the Switch to the U.S.", shared Louisa Nordstrom, the U.S. Dealer and representative for the class. "This boat is not only breaking records with top speeds over 30 knots, but it's also simplifying high-performance foiling racing, making it more accessible, and bringing the fun back into one-design sailing.”

Having stirred up a storm in Europe and Australia, the Switch class is now gaining rapid momentum in the U.S., with fleets budding in the UK, Italy, Sweden, Denmark, and Australia. It's no wonder it left a lasting impression at Foiling Week 2025 on Lake Garda, boasting 32 boats, 7 Olympic medals in Sailing, 25% of the fleet being women, and ages ranging from 19 to 64.

title: Adventurous Day Four at 2025 WASZP Games: Wind, Sunshine, and Racing before Torrential Rain
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Adventurous Day Four at 2025 WASZP Games: Wind, Sunshine, and Racing before Torrential Rain
summary: Day 4 of the WASZP Games 2025 was a dynamic mix of sunshine, wind, and racing cut short by rain. Get an inside look.
body: Day 4 of the much-anticipated WASZP Games 2025 turned out to be somewhat of a meteorological roulette. Launching into crisp sunshine and playful winds, sailors took to the water with animated gusto, eager to make the best of the day's promising conditions. The day's agenda: catching the delightful wind and radiant sun while they persisted. For a brief shining moment, there was a thrilling sense of unity as renowned sailor Mark Jardine captured the raw excitement with his magnificent photographs.

Jardine didn't just remain on the sidelines during this energetic day. Thanks to Dougal Henshall and his splendid launch, he was able to get a closer look, immersing himself in the thrills of the competitions and capturing the essence of the fleeting joy that filled the day before the rain put everything to a halt.

All in all, the fourth day of the WASZP Games 2025 was a beautiful testimony of sailing's unpredictable, wild spirit: at once becalming and testing, yet a source of ceaseless thrill. Even though it had to be cut short due to an unexpected rainfall, the spirit of sailing remained triumphant.

title: Yacht / Boat events and Regattas - Diary 2025
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Yacht / Boat events and Regattas - Diary 2025
summary: Several yacht and boat races, events, and regattas are scheduled over the next few months, based on available web information. These events span a variety of locations and formats, catering to classic yachts, modern racers, and even youth sailors. Here’s a rundown of what’s coming up through to August 2025.
body: The 52nd Trofeo de Vela Conde de Godó is happening now at the Real Club Náutico de Barcelona (RCN Barcelona). Announced via posts on X, this regatta features around 100 boats from 14 nations, including a Promoción class and the Godó Women’s Cup, emphasising inclusivity and competition. Also in May, the Melges 24 European Sailing Series is underway in Riva, Italy, as noted on X, drawing competitive sailors to this renowned series.

Moving into June, the 30th Les Voiles d’Antibes runs from June 4 to 8 on the Esplanade du Bastion Saint-Jaume in Antibes, France. This iconic Mediterranean regatta, celebrating its anniversary year, showcases classic yachts in a festive setting with races along the French Riviera. Also in June, the Finn World Masters takes place on the IJsselmeer near Medemblik, Netherlands, attracting seasoned sailors for a challenging competition in a vibrant Dutch sailing hub. Meanwhile, the Loro Piana Giraglia, connecting Saint-Tropez and Genoa, promises thrilling offshore racing with top-tier talent against stunning Mediterranean backdrops.

July brings the Rolex TP52 World Championship in Cascais, Portugal, where steady Atlantic breezes and tough seas set the stage for elite TP52 racing. This event, part of the 52 Super Series, highlights world-class competition. Also in July, the Trophée Bailli de Suffren sets sail from Saint-Tropez, offering a prestigious regatta with classic yachts, blending competitive racing with Mediterranean flair and rich maritime heritage.

August features Sneekweek 2025, Europe’s largest inland sailing event, held in early August on the Sneekermeer in the Netherlands. Known for daily regattas and lively onshore festivities, it draws sailors and visitors globally. Closer to the UK, the Cowes Week, one of the world’s most iconic regattas, runs from August 2 to 8 in the Solent. It’s a massive event with 8,000 competitors, from amateurs to pros, featuring races for classic yachts, modern fleets, and social events, as noted in historical context from web sources.

Looking slightly further ahead, the Ibiza Regatta 2025 is scheduled from September 20 to 27, offering yacht races against Ibiza’s stunning coastline, paired with vibrant social events. Also in September, the Porto Cervo Sailing Week marks the finale of the 52 Super Series in Sardinia, crowning the season’s champion amid intense competition. Les Voiles de Saint-Tropez 2025, another highlight, will bring classic and modern yachts to the French Riviera for races and festivities, a staple of the international sailing calendar.

Beyond racing, several boat shows are on the horizon. The Sausalito Boat Show, occurring on September 5–7 at Clipper Yacht Harbour, California, will showcase powerboats, sailboats, and luxury yachts, with local food, music, and educational seminars. The Newport International Boat Show in Rhode Island, spanning mid-September over 15 acres, is one of the largest in the U.S., featuring six connected sites. The United States Sailboat Show in Annapolis, Maryland, follows in October, recognised as the largest and oldest in-water sailboat show globally, drawing sailors worldwide.

For those interested in unique events, the Visit Qatar E1 Doha Grand Prix in February 2026 (just beyond the “few months” window but worth noting) at the Corinthia Yacht Club on The Pearl Island, Doha, is part of the UIM E1 World Championship, the first all-electric race boat series, featuring innovative RaceBird boats.
