Tom Slingsby, of the Bonds Flying Roos team, and Dylan Fletcher were among the distinguished sailors gracing the event. The latter, a guiding figure to sailing aspirants, generously allowed Jon Holt from the Greig City Academy a drive in the Emirates Team GBR F50.

The series, however, was not without its trials. The French team’s wingsail ran into a significant operational snag, breaking in half due to a mast compression issue. The mistake left sailing aficionados shocked, causing great anticipation to whether they could continue the race.

The event, though filled with trials and triumphs, stands as a testament to the tenacity and spirit of sailors worldwide. The buzz it has generated reinforces the charm and adventurous appeal of sailing, drawing fans and enthusiasts from all corners of the globe.

title: Thrilling one-design showdown as J/99s conquer the Noakes Sydney Gold Coast Yacht Race
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Thrilling one-design showdown as J/99s conquer the Noakes Sydney Gold Coast Yacht Race
summary: In the 2025 Noakes Sydney Gold Coast Yacht Race, a competitive field of J/99 yachts turns heads as they dominate the Double Handed Division.
body: The 2025 Noakes Sydney Gold Coast (NSGCYR) Yacht Race witnessed a thrilling spectacle. Among the fleet of 63 yachts racing down the mighty seas, a titanic contest emerged: a one-design showdown featuring the dominant J/99 yacht designs.

Of the 63, 14 gutsy Double Handed yachts engaged in a nail-biting 384-nautical mile race. The J/99s came to the fore with six intrepid yacht entries, delivering a captivating race within a race. These formidable vessels were the Balancing Act, Blue Planet, Jupiter, Rum Rebellion, The Gaffer, and Verite, helmed by experienced and ambitious pairs eager to outmaneuver one another.

Take, for instance, The Gaffer, co-skipped by Rob Frayne and Richard Dumas, a duo with a compelling narrative. Though unlisted in the previous year's entry, it sparked curiosity aboard as the first J/99 to reach Cabbage Tree Island during the 2024 Race. Their strategy? Gain vital offshore experience by artfully shadowing the fleet.

Another notable J/99, Jupiter, owned by Ian Smith, proved a picture of dogged determination and seasoned strategy. Smith's love for the discomfort the offshore challenges bring fueled his decision to stay in the game, and it paid off tremendously. Despite limited ocean racing experience, Smith bagged third place in the 2024 Rolex Sydney Hobart.

With an entire fleet of J/99s participating, this was more than a race; it was a veritable one-design spectacle. A tactical battleground where every yacht was closely watched and the slightest slip could change the game completely.

The J/99s' rise in this year's NSGCYR signals a changing tide in offshore racing. The thrill, elements of strategy, and sheer mastery of these yachts and their skippers underscore the boundless possibilities and ongoing evolution of the sport. As we look forward to more races, one thing is certain: the J/99s are here to stay.

title: Experience the Revitalisation of the 52.4-metre DB9 Palmer Johnson Yacht: Championing Elegance and Power in its New Avatar
author: Old Sea Dogs

Following an extended and rigorous refurbishment over 18 months at the Monaco Marine's facilities in La Seyne-sur-Mer, the revitalised DB9 stands proud and ready for a remarkable summer of sailing the South of France and Italy.

The transformational refurbishment has brought about a wave of significant modifications to this renowned yacht. Augmenting this exterior redesign is the updating of the exterior decks upholstery, providing a crisp and fresh feel to the overall outside space.

The superyacht isn't just about relaxation though - it caters to fitness enthusiasts as well. One of the few PJ170 Sport Yacht models, DB9 has always led the pack of luxury vessels with unique hallmark features. These include a sizeable swimming pool on the foredeck that smartly doubles as storage for a ultra-modern 6.5-meter tender and room for two Jet Skis on the foredeck.

Embodying elegance, power, and innovation, the remodelled DB9 is more than equipped to deliver the epitome of a luxurious maritime venture, making every journey a masterpiece of the seas. Let the adventure begin!

title: Admiral’s Cup Triumphant Return to Cowes in July 2025
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Admiral’s Cup Set to Make Triumphant Return to Cowes in July 2025
imageCredit: © Admirals Cup - Royal Ocean Racing Club (RORC)
summary: The Admiral’s Cup returns to Cowes from 17 July to 1 August 2025, reviving offshore sailing’s iconic team race. National teams will compete in inshore and offshore events, celebrating Corinthian spirit, tradition, and global competition on the Solent.
body: A New Chapter for the 'Unofficial World Championship of Offshore Sailing'

After a long hiatus, one of the most iconic and prestigious events in the world of sailing is set to make its dramatic return: the Admiral’s Cup. Known as the “unofficial world championship of offshore racing”, the Admiral’s Cup will re-launch in Cowes, England—the spiritual home of competitive yachting—on 17th July 2025, running through to 1st August. Hosted by the Royal Ocean Racing Club (RORC), the event marks a significant revival for international offshore sailing, rekindling rivalries, honouring tradition, and welcoming a new generation of elite sailors to the Solent.

First contested in 1957, the Admiral’s Cup quickly became the most coveted offshore trophy in the sport. Originally a biennial competition for national teams of three yachts, it attracted top sailors from across the globe and combined both inshore and offshore races in a demanding and highly tactical format. For decades, it served as a proving ground for technology, teamwork, and endurance.

The last official Admiral’s Cup was held in 2003. Its absence has left a void in the international offshore calendar—but no more. In 2025, the event will return with updated rules, modern racing formats, and a renewed commitment to excellence that honours its legendary past while embracing the future of the sport.

Cowes, on the Isle of Wight, has long been synonymous with yachting tradition. As the birthplace of the America’s Cup in 1851 and the home of the Royal Yacht Squadron and the Royal Ocean Racing Club, it is the ideal setting for the rebirth of the Admiral’s Cup.

The Solent, with its shifting tides, variable winds, and tight racecourses, offers both challenge and spectacle. During the two-week event, Cowes will transform into an international sailing village, welcoming spectators, competitors, and maritime enthusiasts from around the world.

The 2025 Admiral’s Cup will retain its national team structure, with each team consisting of two yachts—a move from the historic three-boat format. The aim is to strike a balance between accessibility and tradition. Teams may be entered by yacht clubs, federations, or national sailing authorities, and each will wear their national colours with pride.

The racing will be a mix of inshore and offshore disciplines, with courses designed to test navigation, strategy, and seamanship. RORC is expected to include: Short-course inshore racing in the Solent A medium-distance overnight race A long offshore race possibly extending into the English Channel or Celtic Sea A final showcase regatta near Cowes for spectators This mixed format pays tribute to the original spirit of the Cup, which was always more than a regatta—it was a test of complete sailing skill.

While official entries are still being finalised, expectations are high for the return of major sailing nations such as the United Kingdom, France, the United States, Germany, Australia, and Italy. Many top offshore teams and syndicates that typically compete in races like the Rolex Fastnet Race, Sydney Hobart, and RORC Caribbean 600 are lining up for a chance to etch their names into the Admiral’s Cup once again.
This year’s Cup also welcomes newcomer nations, with several emerging sailing programs expected to compete for the first time, reflecting the global growth of offshore racing.
The return of the Admiral’s Cup is not just about windward-leeward legs and waypoint navigation. It’s a cultural revival of one of the sport’s greatest traditions. The event will feature:

Opening and closing ceremonies at the Royal Yacht Squadron Dockside parties, forums, and technical briefings at RORC Cowes clubhouse Youth engagement and legacy programs, connecting the next generation to elite offshore sailing Live tracking and broadcast coverage, bringing the competition to global audiences Cowes itself will be buzzing with activity—yacht spotters, journalists, families, and fans will fill the High Street, and the marina will brim with national flags, team bases, and offshore thoroughbreds preparing for battle.

What sets the Admiral’s Cup apart from many high-tech, sponsor-heavy modern regattas is its Corinthian spirit. Though professional crews and high-performance yachts are expected, the focus remains on teamwork, national pride, and the complete sailor—traits that built the event’s legendary status in the 20th century.
In a world increasingly focused on foils and one-design formats, the Admiral’s Cup returns as a celebration of diverse yacht design, tactical nuance, and long-distance grit.

title: This weekend - HF50 Catamarans SailGP & Sir Ben Ainslie - Portsmouth Waterfront
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: HF50 Catamarans SailGP & Sir Ben Ainslie - Portsmouth Waterfront
summary: Don't forget this weekend the iconic Portsmouth Waterfront Grandstand will transform into the pulse of adrenaline‑fuelled sailing as SailGP’s high-tech F50 catamarans take centre stage. These cutting‑edge, foiling catamarans—each 50 feet long and capable of flying above water at nearly 100 km/h—are the pulse of the sport.
body: Sir Ben Ainslie, CEO & Co-owner of Emirates Great Britain SailGP Team, said: "It’s been three years since we last raced on British waters, so we’re delighted to be returning home — especially to a race track we know so well. The squad certainly caught the eye of the Waterloo crowds during rush hour today, and we can’t wait to capture the attention of the sell-out crowd in Portsmouth in just one month's time, as the most exciting racing on water returns to the UK. Don’t miss it!"

Adapted from America’s Cup AC50s and continually upgraded, F50s now boast the latest titanium T‑foils (introduced this season) for reduced drag, maximum lift, and blister‑fast speeds. In Portsmouth, the Great Britain Sail Grand Prix unfolds right on home waters. Fans will experience the raw power of identical, wing‑rigged F50s racing fleet‑style just meters offshore, making this one of the most immersive spectator events in sport. Expect dramatic manoeuvres, lightning‑quick tacks, and breathtaking fly‑bys—every bit of split‑second tactical brilliance visible from the grandstand or big screen.
Après‑Sail: Live Sets to Ignite the Evening Whether you came for the sails or stayed for the beats, SailGP brings an electrifying twist with its brand‑new Après‑Sail live music experience:

Multi‑platinum singer-songwriter Tom Grennan takes the stage, delivering powerful vocals and chart‑topping hits. Known for his energetic presence and soulful blends, Grennan is perfect backstage fuel after intense racing.

Legendary DJ Pete Tong spins a bespoke set post‑race. As a central figure in the global electronic dance scene, Pete’s infectious energy will transform the waterfront into a dance floor echoing with rhythm and cheers.
These performances are part of SailGP Portsmouth’s official Après‑Sail Party, exclusive to grandstand ticket holders—making the event not just a race day, but a full‑day entertainment experience.
SailGP isn’t just about speed—it’s a marriage of elite sport, sustainable innovation, and entertainment spectacle:
Waterfront Grandstand views put you amid the action—hear the wind roar, feel the spray, and witness tactical skirmishes played out at 60 mph.
After all the racing excitement there more …! Après‑Sail events with Tom Grennan and Pete Tong turn a day of racing into an evening festival of great music and fun.

* Saturday, 19 July: SailGP racing + Tom Grennan live set * Sunday, 20 July: Racing + Pete Tong DJ set Venue: Portsmouth Waterfront Grandstand—prime on‑water views, commentary, and big screens for in‑depth action. Tickets: Grandstand entry includes access to Après‑Sail. Premium options are available via official SailGP outlets.

In short, this weekend’s event is the perfect blend of high-stakes racing and after-dark celebration. Expect cutting-edge performance, fierce competition, and world-class entertainment—all unfolding by the sea.

title: Marine Weather Leader, PredictWind, Scores Official Supplier Role in Admiral's Cup 2025, Showcasing Commitment to Nautical Diversity
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Marine Weather Leader, PredictWind, Scores Official Supplier Role in Admiral's Cup 2025, Showcasing Commitment to Nautical Diversity
summary: PredictWind, the global weather forecasting giant, proudly announces its role as Official Weather Data Supplier and Race Day Sponsor for the Admiral’s Cup 2025.
body: PredictWind is setting the bar high, not just in meteorological advancements but also in its commitment towards promoting diversity in sailing. As the newly christened Official Weather Data Supplier and Race Day Sponsor for the prestigious Admiral’s Cup 2025, PredictWind ensures to provide superior weather insights which could prove crucial to participants. But the company doesn’t just stop at forecasts. On 21st July, it will host a distinctive women's reception at the esteemed RORC Yacht Club, demonstrating its commitment to fostering female talent and connectivity within the sport. This aligns with the Admiral's Cup's rule requiring every crew to include a female and a young member, effectively pushing for a diverse and inclusive sailing culture. PredictWind wholly supports this vision, seeing the inclusion of women as a significant enhancement to team dynamics and collective insight. Keryn McMaster, Support Team Manager at PredictWind and also a team member of the Australian Admiral’s Cup team, stresses the importance of providing opportunities to showcase female talent in enhancing team dynamics. Through this women's reception, there will be unique opportunities for networking, shared narratives and widened understanding of both the sport and weather forecasting. This initiative shines brightly under the 'Changing Tides' vision of the Admiral's Cup, which aims to uplift the visibility of women in offshore competitions. Owing to PredictWind's highly trusted prediction models, competitors of the 2025 Admiral's Cup will have valuable direction. The PredictWind team will also offer practical support at the event, providing an interactive experience with their first-rate products. To cap it all, Arnaud Monges, PredictWind’s resident meteorologist, will present the Fastnet Race 2025's much-looked-forward-to weather briefing at the RORC clubhouse. The Fastnet Race 2025 looks forward to its record-breaking event with the largest entries ever. PredictWind’s amplified presence at the Admiral's Cup is a testament to its dedication not just towards providing exceptional performance in elite racing but also fostering a sense of communal development within sailing, emphasising the promotion of diversity and women's participation.

title: Experience Elegance and Efficiency: Realm 45 Motor Yacht Offers 360° Views and Electric Power
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Experience Elegance and Efficiency: Realm 45 Motor Yacht Offers 360° Views and Electric Power
summary: Introducing the Realm 45 motor yacht by Rand. A luxurious and versatile choice, it promises an all-season experience, generously glazed for panoramic views and equipped with an electric powertrain.
body: The world of luxury yachting is set to be stirred up by Rand's ambitious new flagship — the Realm 45 motor yacht. Billed as a 'boat for all seasons', it combines elegance with versatility and sustainability in one indulgent package.

Its unique selling point is undoubtedly the stunning glass superstructure, virtually an all-glass ensemble that offers a truly immersive nautical experience, with 360° views and complete protection from the elements. This groundbreaking design enables guests to absorb the surrounding seascape in all its glory, irrespective of their position — be it at the helm, the roomy U-shaped dinette, or the amidships galley.

The lower deck is intelligently utilized, housing a double cabin with a uniquely placed bed, and two single berths tucked under the cockpit. Plus, the Realm 45 truly shines in offering a choice of powertrains. A standard all-electric system, two 300 kW E-drive motors powered by a hefty 440-kWh battery bank, ensures smooth sailing, boasting a serviceable range of 35-nautical miles at 25 knots. Solar panels on the coachroof aid in recharging during daylight hours.

If a more traditional thrust is preferred, the Realm 45 provides alternatives from leading manufacturers Volvo Penta, Mercury, and Yanmar. Configurations range from strongest twin Volvo Penta D6-440s giving a top speed of 41 knots, to powerful 600hp petrol Mercury V12 outboards capable of pushing the top speed to around 47 knots.
Join the new frontier of yachting, where luxury, innovation, and sustainability merge seamlessly with the Realm 45 by Rand. Charter a course to explore the joys and grandeur of nautical life.

title: Bilgin Yachts Announces the Technical Launch of the Fourth Unit in the Bilgin 170 Superyacht Series
author: Old Sea Dogs

summary: Turkish shipyard Bilgin Yachts has successfully executed the technical launch of the fourth unit in the Bilgin 170 superyacht series, setting its course for outfitting in Istanbul, with delivery scheduled for early 2026.
body: Bilgin Yachts, a prominent Turkish yard, is making waves in the superyacht arena by announcing the technical launch of the fourth yacht in the Bilgin 170 series. This news comes as a beacon of progress in the yacht building industry.

Designed under the watchful eyes of renowned Turkish studio Unique Yacht Design, the latest Bilgin 170, temporarily identified as NB85, draws inspiration from her "near sistership" Eternal Spark. The latter being another successful delivery by Bilgin Yachts, launched back in June 2024.

As with her predecessors, the same commitment to luxury and sophistication is evident. As evidenced by the full suite of interior renderings released by Fraser, the yacht brokerage firm handling her sale. The opulent master cabin includes an office, a full-height wardrobe, and floor-to-ceiling windows that offer spectacular sea views.

The yacht's exterior design presents a measured balance between elegance and functionality. It hosts a sophisticated range of open-air dining areas, lounge spaces, and a sweeping sundeck pool surrounded by sunpads. There's also a multi-purpose beach club that can be converted into a gym or lounge.
Moreover, the yacht stands out with its impressive specifications. Pivotal stats include a 9.3-meter beam, a draft deploying 2.6 meters in-depth, and a maximum achievable velocity of 16 knots.

The fourth Bilgin 170 joins a growing fleet. Bilgin Yachts currently houses ten yachts under construction, attesting to its commitment to enriching the luxury maritime community. The second Bilgin 170 unit recently touched base in Antalya, Turkey for outfitting, validating the series' remarkable success.

title: Italian Boatyard Baglietto Scores with Seventh Launch of its DOM 133 Series: Sui Generis
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Italian Boatyard Baglietto Scores with Seventh Launch of its DOM 133 Series: Sui Generis
summary: The renowned Italian shipyard, Baglietto raises the bar by successfully launching Sui Generis, the seventh superyacht from its lauded DOM 133 series.
body: Baglietto, the famed Italian shipyard, has successfully launched Sui Generis, the seventh hull from its esteemed 40.9-meter DOM 133 series. This iconic superyacht series has become the hallmark of Baglietto's pursuit of design innovation, superior performance, and exquisite craftsmanship. Launched at the yard’s La Spezia facilities, Sui Generis sports a uniquely striking cobalt blue hull and deck design that instantly sets it apart from its predecessors. Functionality blends seamlessly with aesthetics, as demonstrated by the extensive customisation potential of the interiors. Two VIP suites on the lower deck can be cleverly transformed into a second full-beam master cabin with a seamless sliding partition mechanism.

However, underneath its alluring design and expansive space is a beast of an engine. The Sui Generis houses twin Caterpillar C32 engines, capable of reaching a top speed of 17 knots. This unparalleled combination of power, luxury, and design is what sets Baglietto's DOM 133 series apart. The launch of Sui Generis not only marks Baglietto’s seventh successful launch this year but also underscores the shipyard's commitment to meeting the most specific needs of the discerning yacht owner. With two more DOM 133 units under construction, scheduled for delivery in 2026 and 2027, the future looks bright for Baglietto's innovative shipbuilding trajectory.

title: The Sea Shimmers with Moonrise: Feadship’s Majestic 101-meter Superyacht Embarks on its Nautical Journey
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Sea Shimmers with Moonrise: Feadship’s Majestic 101-meter Superyacht Embarks on its Nautical Journey
summary: Emerging from successful trials in the chilly North Sea, the 101-meter Feadship superyacht Moonrise, a marriage of innovation and style, has been delivered.
body: There is a beam of moonlight glittering on the horizon as Feadship’s latest brainchild, the 101-meter superyacht Moonrise, begins her maiden journey, having breezed through successful trials in the harsh North Sea. With Studio De Voogt at the helm of the sleek exterior design and the warm palette of Rémi Tessier adorning the interior, Moonrise pays homage to her predecessor's signature aesthetic while incorporating significant advancements.

Sharing more than a name with its forerunner, Moonrise carries the hallmark sleek exterior lines, the grey and snow-white colour scheme, and the signature 'powerful vertical bow'. However, she distinguishes herself with numerous technological enhancements and finer design nudges. An alteration is evident in the absence of the domes, traditionally housing VSAT and TVRO antennas. In their place, Moonrise boldly integrates Starlink satellite receivers into the superstructure, enhancing communication and streaming capabilities, and preserving the streamlined aesthetic.

Launched in March 2025, attention to Moonrise was fixated on noise reduction. Unique propellers and appendages, coupled with a first of its kind hyper-resilient anchor winch foundation, contribute to reducing underwater noise and minimizing sound pollution within the yacht. The secretive nature of this project allowed the world to catch its first glimpse of Moonrise only in late 2023. Since then, every new reveal - from shell doors on the lower deck to potential tender garages - have piqued interest and raised expectations.

As Moonrise sails away into the vast seas, the Dutch yard readies itself for a busy season, having recently celebrated the launch of Project 827 and the 79.9-meter Faith. The seascape is indeed shimmering under the radiant light of Moonrise.

title: Call for Entries: The Majestic 2025 Melges 24 U.S. National Championship at Pensacola Yacht Club Waits for You

title: Who Nailed the Breeze Call in the 2025 Transpac?
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Who Nailed the Breeze Call in the 2025 Transpac?
imageCredit: © The crew of Santa Cruz 52 Heroic Heart
imageCaption: The crew of Santa Cruz 52 Heroic Heart
summary: The 2025 Transpac is full steam ahead, and the fleet is chewing through the miles toward that sweet slice of volcanic paradise: the Diamond Head finish line off Honolulu. It’s the 53rd running of this epic 2,225-mile dash across the Pacific — and it hasn’t disappointed. A race born in 1906, Transpac is part marathon, part chess match, part saltwater soap opera. This year’s show kicked off with staggered starts over f
body: Gear failures, medical issues, bad luck. The remaining 49 boats, from sprightly 35-footers to ocean-stomping 88-foot sleds, are still punching westward across the big blue in 10 divisions, all chasing line honors and fastest elapsed time bragging rights.
Div 1 (Boatswain’s Locker/Yanmar): Bryon Ehrhart’s Lucky
Div 2 (Mount Gay): Thomas Akin’s Meanie
Div 3 (Whittier Trust): Dave Clark’s Grand Illusion
Div 4 (Cal Maritime): Rich Festa’s Groundhog Day
Div 5 (Cabrillo Boat Shop): Dave Moore’s Westerly
Div 6 (Garmin): Thomas Garnier’s Reinrag2
Div 7 (Suntex): Fred Courouble & Charles-Etieene Devanneaux’s Rahan
Div 8 (Pasha): Barry Clark’s Blackwing
Div 9 (Bridger Insurance): Alli Bell’s Restless
Div 10 (Multihull): Don Wilson’s Convexity2

TP52 Meanie, crushing it in Mount Gay Division 2. But it hasn’t all been smooth sailing. A rogue upper-level low swirled in the subtropical ridge, punching a hole in the tradewinds and splitting the fleet. “This was in the forecast,” said weather wizard Chris Bedford. “Some boats dove south to skirt it, others tried to leapfrog it — some just plain missed the mess altogether by starting early. But once past 135°W, it was back to being a tradewind drag race.”

Fans at home are glued to Transpac Onboard, a fresh-from-the-ocean six-part video series, and tracking every gybe on the Pasha YB Tracker — where position updates are zipping in near real-time. Why the improvement? No more four-hour delay. Thanks to Starlink, and a tweak in the AIS rules, nearly every boat is pinging hourly from the deep blue. The final 200 miles? That’ll speed up to 15-minute pings. The last five miles? Practically live at five-minute intervals. Sure, it's not the same as live AIS, but it’s close enough to light a fire under the nav table.

One man watching it all with a keen eye: Tom Garnier, skipper of Reinrag2. This is his eighth Transpac on the J/125, with three more J/125s nipping at his heels. “Rule one: be safe. Rule two: have fun. Rule three: do your best,” he said over sat-phone, sounding like a sea-sprayed monk of the Pacific. “But really — if you’re not doing your best, you’re probably not having much fun.”
And the Reinrag2 creed? “Accelerate to the finish.”

Speaking of finishes, the Nautical Cloud scoring system has added a juicy new feature: Time Sector Analysis. Five waypoints — Catalina, Halfway, 500nm to go, 100nm to go, and the Molokai Channel — are now mini finish lines, measuring how fast you cover each chunk. Green triangles mean you’re moving up. Red? You’ve got some explaining to do. Right now, Restless is riding high, followed by Rahan and Macondo.

And about Macondo — they kicked off strong. Zimmer, skippered by Samantha Gebb (third-gen Transpac sailor, first-gen boss), is hanging tough in Suntex Division 7. She’s out there with her dad crewing for her — proper family affair — using Pasha tracker data like a virtual telltale. “We were expecting a wind shift,” she said via Starlink. “So we used boats ahead to see when the header hit and plan accordingly.”

Smart stuff. And she’s not alone. The 2025 Transpac is making quiet history: over 10% of the fleet is skippered by women — and not just onboard for photos. These are full-blooded, watch-leading, kite-trimming, call-the-shots sailors.

Alli Bell (Restless) is leading by example — Rear Commodore of the Transpac YC, Comms Chair, Vice Commodore of San Diego YC, and still found time to boss the Cal 40 around the Pacific. She didn’t set out to run an all-woman fleet. “We didn’t aim to attract women skippers,” she said. “We aimed to attract sailors.”

Then there’s Heather Furey, skippering Mirage, a Santa Cruz 70. Third crossing, but this time, it feels different. “Before, I was lucky to have great mentors. Now, I feel like I own the role.” Her crew keeps teasing her: “You’re the owner, you’re not supposed to do that.” Her answer? “This is what we do. Together.”

Heather, Samantha, and Alli are also flying under the flag of “The Vixens,” a three-boat squad chasing the Storm Trysail Team Trophy. Seven other teams are in the hunt — but The Vixens are bringing the heat. “We’re cheering Samantha on live from the ocean,” said Heather. “And Alli? She’s smashing it.”

Maybe the best sign of progress came from one crew dad who told his daughter about Alli being in charge. “So… she’s the boss of you?” she asked. “Yep.” And her response? “Cool. I could do that someday.” Damn right you could.

July 5, 1800 PDT: GoodEnergy (Reichel/Pugh 63) out with rudder-bearing issues. July 5, 2134 PDT: Rock n’ Roll (Andrews 68) retired after a crew fall — medevac via Catalina and transferred to hospital. July 6, 1545 PDT: Ragtime (Spencer 65) retired — crew evacuated 230 miles offshore with help from USCG and USAF. Patient recovered; Ragtime safely returned to port.
The ocean, as always, doesn’t play favourites — but it does reward those who read it best. And right now, the Pacific’s picking winners.

title: High Drama on the Riviera: Famous Yacht Sea Lady II at Risk of Sinking After Fiery Incident in Saint-Tropez
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: High Drama on the Riviera: Famous Yacht Sea Lady II at Risk of Sinking After Fiery Incident in Saint-Tropez
summary: A catastrophic docking incident, engulfed Sea Lady II in flames at Saint-Tropez's Vieux-Port threatening to send it to a watery grave.
body: In a distressing turn of events, the esteemed Sea Lady II is precariously close to sinking. The mishap occurred shortly after the vessel docked at Quai de l’Épi in the Vieux-Port on an ill-fated summer evening. The blaze's cause remains a mystery, yet its consequences have been devastating, rendering the yacht with serious structural damage and a compulsion to take on water. This unfortunate incident required an intervention from approximately sixty firefighters, supplemented by two fireboats. In the process, they prompted an evacuation of about thirty nearby yachts as the flames proliferated through the forward hull and lower decks. It was a harrowing escape for the eight crew members and several passengers, with two crew members seeking treatment for smoke inhalation. Built in 1986 by British shipyard W.A. Souter & Sons and previously known as D'Angleterre II, the 277-tonne Sea Lady II is famed for her robust design by Don Shead Ltd. She had undergone an extensive refit in 2024, a testament to her durability. However, this incident has raised significant environmental alarms. A ruptured fuel tank containing approximately 27,000 litres of diesel aggravated the situation, fostering concerns about the surrounding marine environment. To mitigate the potential contamination, anti-pollution booms were deployed swiftly. The Vieux-Port, typically a bustling corner during peak summer, remains closed to navigation, impacting local operators and charter movements. Authorities are currently focusing on recovering the remaining fuel and preparing the hull for inspection and refloating. The recovery and structural assessment operations are being overseen by the municipality of Saint-Tropez, working closely with the Prefecture of Var and the Maritime Prefecture of the Mediterranean. As the Sea Lady II's future hangs in the balance, this incident serves as a reminder of the delicate interplay between human leisure and the vulnerability of nature's elements.

title: The Australian Commercial Marine Conference
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Australian Commercial Marine Conference
imageCaption: SeaLink's Starship Sydney - Australian Commercial Marine Conference
summary: The Australian Commercial Marine Conference returns to Sydney on Thursday, 31 July 2025 aboard the M/V Starship Sydney. Now in its second consecutive year, the event follows strong industry demand for a dedicated national forum to address sector challenges, explore insights from leading authorities and to strengthen connections across Australia’s commercial marine sector. Conceptualised by Nick Lester, General Manage
body: The one-day program will feature expert speakers, Q&A , panel discussions, and technical sessions addressing current concerns, future directions and relevant policy impacting the commercial marine industry. It also offers valuable opportunities for networking with a strong emphasis on exchanging ideas and informed decision-making.

Key speakers will include Arthur Fraccaro, Business Development Manager from AIRCAT Vessels, who will introduce Surface Effect Ship technology, a cutting-edge advancement in vessel design aimed at improving speed, efficiency and performance in commercial marine applications.

Kristina Agustin, the founder of Southern Sky AI will draw on her 20 years of experience in the global marine industry, specialising in maritime business, operations and regulatory compliance to explore how artificial intelligence is transforming the commercial marine industry by streamlining systems and enhancing service delivery. Offering insights into the U.S. marine market, Madeleine Simpson, Global Markets Representative from the U.S. Commercial Service and Duncan Archibald, Business Development Manager from the SelectUSA Program, will detail support available for Australian companies looking to expand into the United States, highlighting opportunities to connect Australian businesses with U.S. suppliers through platforms like the International WorkBoat Show. The developing Australian Commercial Marine Economic Impact Study (EIS) continues to gain momentum across the industry, drawing attention from both operators and regulators. Ashley Page, CEO of AEC Group, will provide to conference attendees a timely update on the EIS, outlining its focus and relevance to the commercial marine sector. Greg Newby, Director from the Sydney Maritime Institute will present solutions to address the growing shortage of qualified crew, showcasing traineeship programs and maritime career pathways. Whilst Peter Munckton, the Chief Economist at Bank of Queensland, arguably the best economist speaker in Australia will share an expert economic overview to help businesses steer confidently through the current uncertain economy. The newly introduced exhibition area will feature a showcase of industry expertise with dedicated information booths from Control Point Rescue, Logix Consulting, Marine Air Flow International and Spear Green Design. Offering the opportunity for delegates to engage directly with specialists in safety and emergency response , corrosion diagnostics and protection, ventilation systems and sustainable superyacht interior design. Additional exhibitors will be announced soon.

To further enhance cross-sector engagement, ACMG will host networking drinks at the conclusion of the conference in partnership with the Australian International Marine Export Group (AIMEX) and Superyacht Australia. Aligning these events provides a unique opportunity to connect professionals from across the broader marine industry. Registrations are now open via the ACMG website. ACMG Local Members receive one complimentary registration while Corporate Members receive four. Non-members and additional members are welcome to attend with registration available at $450+GST.

title: Discover the Thrills of Boating in Difficult Conditions with the Ockelbo B25 Cabin Boat
author: M
imageAlt: Discover the Thrills of Boating in Difficult Conditions with the Ockelbo B25 Cabin Boat
summary: Experience sea life like never before in the robust Ockelbo B25 Cabin boat, a unique blend of toughness and all-round performance from Swedish brand Ockelbo.
body: The search for an all-weather, all-condition boat is over. Ockelbo, a revered brand from Sweden, introduces the B25 Cabin boat, an indestructible offering constructed from marine grade aluminium. This unique material choice results in a lightweight yet strong structure that effortlessly withstands the brute force of all sea conditions.
The Ockelbo B25 Cabin boat's aesthetic has a charm of its own. Its simple design exudes a rugged elegance, on par with professional boats used in training facilities or comfortably docked at marinas.

A hallmark of the Ockelbo B25 is its fully equipped wheelhouse. It boasts of flush-fit windscreens and side windows, delivering unimpeded views of the sea, no matter the weather. A sizeable swing-up door connects to the spacious forward cockpit, replete with built-in seats and lockers. The aft cockpit, though compact, includes seating, making it a perfect spot to soak up the sun.

Relentless on functionality and quality, the Ockelbo B25 doesn't sacrifice speed or power. It comes with a wide range of high-performing Mercury Verrado engines and has a top speed of 42-48 knots, making it a worthy adversary for any boat in its class.

This formidable boat is making its mark in the UK thanks to Nordbalt, a new British importer, and Clipper Marine, its sub-dealer. With prices starting from £105,000 ex VAT, the Ockelbo B25 Cabin boat sets a new standard in providing high performance and durability, promising a boat-riding experience like no other.

Not only does the Ockelbo B25 fill the sails of seasoned sailors, but it also ignites the ambition of budding seafarers. Its low-maintenance and unparalleled resilience make it the ideal choice for those yearning to explore open waters all year round. So why wait any longer? It's time to set your sights on the horizon aboard the Ockelbo B25 Cabin boat.

title: Sneak Peek into the Elegance and Innovation of Alia Yacht's Striking Superyacht, Limerence
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Sneak Peek into the Elegance and Innovation of Alia Yacht's Striking Superyacht, Limerence
summary: Alia Yachts, the renowned Turkish shipyard, provides a rare glimpse into the exquisite Limerence, a powerhouse on the Mediterranean seas, pushing boundaries in luxury and performance.
body: Chartering across the glamorous Mediterranean is the breathtaking Limerence. A full-custom beauty from the lauded shipyard, Alia Yachts, she elegantly plies the azure waters with Christie Yachts. Her current anchorage graces the stunning coasts of Antibes, a jewel in the Mediterranean crown.

Designed by Azure Yacht Design and Naval Architecture, Limerence balloons with the heart of Alia Yachts' ingenuity and capabilities, as aptly stated by Gökhan Çelik, the shipyard's president. But the ultimate standout of this luxury liner is the raised aft deck. A spectacle in itself, it is both a fully certified helicopter deck and a giant hub for entertainment. Imagine a dance-floor on the high seas, or perhaps a volleyball, pickleball, or basketball court. The options are truly unlimited.

Originally envisaged as a support vessel, Limerence has morphed into a versatile superyacht armed with an arsenal of toys appropriate for indulgent sea lovers. This innovative approach led to a challenging yet gratifying build with the superyacht crafted in three unique parts – the hull, superstructure, and helideck, a design masterpiece of Dutch studio Diana Yacht Design.

Limerence, with interiors paralleling boutique hotels, showcases her roots as a support vessel with shell space for a 12.5-meter guest tender, 4.5-meter rescue tender, submarine, two wave-runners, two sailing dinghies, and two sailing catamarans. Coupled with a 50-square-meter storage equipped with 20 modular waterpark elements and additional space for small toys like diving equipment, surfboards, and electric bicycles, she is a treasure chest of adventure.

As Çelik aptly notes, 'A yacht of this pedigree is not destined to spend much time in harbour.' Indeed, Limerence is a vessel for those with a thirst for the sea’s thrills, promising to serve as a highly capable standalone yacht and an unparalleled support vessel swarming with amenities.

title: Laserfest 2025 Shines at Whitstable Yacht Club, Attracting a Stellar Fleet of 40 Laser/ILCA Sailboats
author: M
imageAlt: Laserfest 2025 Shines at Whitstable Yacht Club, Attracting a Stellar Fleet of 40 Laser/ILCA Sailboats
summary: Whitstable Yacht Club's annual celebration of Laser/ILCA racing, Laserfest 2025, saw a robust participation of 40 boats hailing from local and distant clubs.
body: The windy shores of Whitstable Yacht Club reverberated with spirited competition as it hosted Laserfest 2025, a celebration of Laser/ILCA racing. With an impressive line-up of 40 boats, the event not only boosted the sailing participation of Whitstable's local sailors, but also wooed entries from clubs as far-flung as Yorkshire.

The opening day saw an east-blowing F3 to F4/5 wind, accompanied by clear skies. These conditions were a boon for the race management team, steered by PRO Tom Bruton, who launched five consecutive sprint races of 20-30 minutes duration each. Competitors returned in time to catch the Wimbledon women's final.

Despite this, the series remained anything but predictable. Race four saw a bold move from Hythe sailor, Sebastian Robb, who daringly crossed the fleet on port, to everyone's astonishment. Though Finlay once more claimed victory, Robb held his own, securing a strong second place.

The day rounded off with the fifth race that felt like a tireless battle against a two-lap course and the day's strongest winds. Yet again, Finlay seized the win, creating a solid string of victories.

Beyond the competition, Laserfest lived up to its event tagline of 'Racing, Music, and Beer'. Sailors spent Saturday evening unwinding, indulging in Paella, beer, and lively music performed by the club band, The Dead Pelicans.

Sunday dawned more placid, however, with sore heads, light wind, and cloudy skies. Despite this, the excitement was still palpable as the next five back-to-back races were lined up, primed to decide the ultimate victor of Laserfest 2025.

title: InNORvation’25: Transforming the Maritime Industry in the Heart of Norway's Fjords
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: InNORvation’25: Transforming the Maritime Industry in the Heart of Norway's Fjords
summary: Imagine an exclusive convocation of industry experts brainstorming the future of maritime industry amidst the stunning Norwegian fjords. Welcome to InNORvation’25.
body: Immersing the best minds in the industry within the breathtaking Norwegian nature, The InNORvation’25 forum welcomed fifty specially chosen participants in May. Instead of conventional panel discussions and presentations, experts from the realms of shipbuilding, design, project management, and yacht management gathered in an inspiring, intimate setting to dive deep into the pivotal themes of today's maritime industry.

The event was supremely collaborative, with participants freely exchanging ideas and fostering 'blue-sky' thinking. Away from the routine commotion of shipyards, traditional event venues and yachting centers, the change of scene fostered new energy and elevated the freedom of thought. This unique experience was further amplified with the participants getting opportunities to escape into the fjords, allowing the serene surroundings to stimulate their minds and inspire dynamic thinking especially around waste, pollution, and sustainability.

Anchoring the industry's future in the present reality, with an eye on sustainability and progressive ideation, the InNORvation forums offer an unprecedented opportunity to steer the maritime industry towards sustainable and strategically sound waters. Future participants and industry enthusiasts are eagerly looked forward to at the upcoming InNORvation’26. This is a chance to contribute, learn, and witness the unfolding of the maritime industry's future.

title: Exciting One-Design Racing Action as Cape 31 Mediterranean Circuit Reaches Crucial Stage in Imperia
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Exciting One-Design Racing Action as Cape 31 Mediterranean Circuit Reaches Crucial Stage in Imperia
summary: The much-anticipated Round 4 of Cape 31 Mediterranean Circuit is about to usher in thrilling sailing action, as it berths in the vibrant coastal city of Imperia.
body: "The high-velocity thrill of sailing is heading to the Italian coast as Cape 31 Mediterranean Circuit gears up for its much-awaited fourth round in the charming city of Imperia. Taking place from 18 to 20 July, the competition is hosted by the renowned Porto Maurizio Yacht Club.

With just two more events left in the 2025 circuit, the pursuit for the prestigious race circuit champion title has elevated to fever pitch, and this round could well prove to be the game-changer. With 16 contesting teams from 13 nations, the pressure and anticipation are palpable.

As the contest stands, 'Give Me Five' has taken the lead in both the overall and Corinthian/1-Pro season standings, displaying an impressive succession of stellar performances. 'Shotgunn,' holding the second position, is another force to reckon with, and 'Adrenaline,' sitting third, has proven to be another strong competitor. The rivalry rippling throughout the fleet is fierce.

Imperia is anticipated to roll out a varied mix of conditions, spicing up the competition. Light and tactical racing is expected to set the tone for Friday, while by the time Sunday swings around, the winds might gear up for a full-throttle spectacular. The unique geography and local intricacies of Imperia present an invigorating challenge for the international fleet.

This is the final round in mainland Europe before the fleet sails for the shores of Palma de Mallorca for Round 5, which doubles as the stage for the Cape 31 European Championship. Imperia thus presents an exquisite battleground for the teams to fight for momentum, leaderboard position and bragging rights over this exhilarating 3-day tournament."

title: The Ocean Race will return to Itajaí
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: The Ocean Race will return to Itajaí
summary: The Ocean Race will return to Itajaí, Brazil during the 2027 and 2031 around the world races. Known for its enthusiastic fans who welcome the sailors and teams after weeks of racing through the challenging conditions of the Southern Ocean, Itajaí is always a welcome stop on the race calendar. This will mark the fifth time the race has been in Itajaí and the 11th visit to Brazilian shores.
body: Itajaí first joined the global sailing stage in the 2011-12 edition of The Ocean Race, becoming the race’s sole South American stopover that year. The city welcomed the fleet again in 2014-15 and 2017-18, and most recently hosted the 2022-23 edition, making 2027 its fifth consecutive appearance on the race route.
Together, these stopovers have attracted over one-million race fans, confirming Itajaí as a premiere destination for The Ocean Race and its teams, sailors and stakeholders.

Itajaí has long championed sustainability by hosting large-scale events while minimising environmental impact. With the support of The Ocean Race’s award-winning Racing for the Ocean programme, the city eliminated over 300,000 single-use plastics during the stopover during the 2023 edition of the Race and continues to apply these sustainable practices to other local events. In 2018, Itajaí became Brazil’s first city to join the United Nations #CleanSeas campaign, committing to reducing ocean plastic pollution. The Ocean Race will continue to work with local grassroots NGOs and other organisations to move policy forward.

Another legacy from prior editions of The Ocean Race is a donated fleet of small training boats which has evolved into a sailing school enabling young children to learn to sail and importantly get closer to nature and the sea. Each time the Race returns there is a visit to the sailing school for new activities and adventures.

The 2027 stopover will highlight these ongoing initiatives, showcasing a sustainable Ocean Live Park race village, along with education programmes for school children that promote ocean literacy and a passion for ocean health.

The 2027 edition of The Ocean Race will again feature the flying, foiling IMOCA yachts with their technical innovations and record-breaking speeds. The cutting-edge IMOCAs push the limits of offshore design, technology, and engineering and in the hands of the world’s best sailors, create an unforgettable race experience.

“Itajaí is always a very welcome stopover for The Ocean Race and our sailors, not least because it usually comes after the longest leg at sea,” said Johan Salen, Director of The Ocean Race. “The passion the people in Itajaí have for the Race and the leadership the team in Itajaí has demonstrated in sustainable event excellence makes it a natural fit for a fifth consecutive stopover.”

Beyond the Ocean Live Park race village, Itajaí always welcomes The Ocean Race with its rich cultural tapestry, spectacular beaches and inspired local gastronomy along with a genuine connection to the ocean.

“The Ocean Race in Itajaí is confirmed for 2027 and 2031. This is a partnership between this great event and the governments of Itajaí and the state of Santa Catarina. The City of Itajaí welcomes the visit and support of The Ocean Race team this week and now planning begins now to make this the biggest edition of The Ocean Race that Itajaí has ​​ever had,” said Robison Coelho, Mayor of Itajaí, Santa Catarina, Brazil.

"Here at The Ocean Race, we are truly happy to be coming back to Itajaí for a fifth consecutive visit and we look forward to working with Mayor Coelho and his team to ensure this is the best stopover yet!" concluded The Ocean Race's Salen.

title: Bilgin's Luxurious 45-Metre Motor Yacht, Elada, Returns to the Market in Impressive Fashion
author: M
imageAlt: Bilgin's Luxurious 45-Metre Motor Yacht, Elada, Returns to the Market in Impressive Fashion
summary: Elada, a 45-metre motor yacht, crafted by the esteemed Turkish shipbuilder Bilgin Yachts, has made an electrifying return to the market.
body: Built with a discerning eye for detail and finesse, Elada is a dazzling addition to the luxury yacht market. Constructed by Bilgin Yachts, a Turkish yard admired for its robust craftsmanship and timeless design, Elada exhibits all hallmarks of the shipbuilder's sterling reputation.

Crafted with fastidious attention by British studio H2 Yacht Design, Elada's aesthetic prowess is underscored by her metallic turquoise details and sharp reverse bow that make her a standout sight on waters. She was first unveiled to the world in 2014, and was bestowed her RINA class credentials after an extensive cold-moulding process.

A cavernous lounge serves as the main saloon, adorned with three honey-toned leather settees and a bar. The atmosphere resonates with warmth courtesy of ambient lighting, cream flooring, and wild woods. The yacht showcases its taste for grand entertainment with a grand piano and a large-screen television set.

Outdoor dining and entertainment find their home on the bridge deck, featuring alfresco seating, twin tables, sun pads, and an enclosed Jacuzzi spa. The flybridge offers built-in seating, an oval dining table, a bar, a barbecue, and yet another Jacuzzi tub.

Underneath the hood, Elada is fitted with two 1,900hp C32 Acert diesel engines provided by Caterpillar. The engines afford a cruising speed of 12 knots, peaking at 19 knots, and a range of 2,900 nautical miles at an 11.5 knots travel rate. Further enhancement of guest comfort comes in the form of ABT zero speed stabilisers.

Today, as the Elada lies anchored in Greece, a unique opportunity unfolds for luxury and convenience. With an asking price of €11,750,000, this offering represents an ideal chance to acquire a yacht that correctly implies the richness, elegance, and superior build that Bilgin Yachts is known for its worldwide.

title: Unveiling the Top-notch Skippers for 2026 New York Yacht Club International Women's Championship
author: M
imageAlt: Esteemed Skippers Invited to New York Yacht Club International Women's Championship 2026
summary: The New York Yacht Club has rolled out the third announcement of skippers for its International Women's Championship in 2026.
body: The countdown for the New York Yacht Club International Women's Championship in 2026 has begun, and with it comes the thrill of competition, teamwork, and the anticipation of great sailing races. A major milestone in the preparations for this exciting event is the unveiling of the invited skippers.

Among the notable names is South African sailor Dominique Provoyeur, an ardent competitor with a rich history of racing, having represented her country in the 2008 Olympics. The championship represents an open canvas, a platform where Provoyeur imagines to field an all South African team. For her, it’s not just about rallying the team, it's sharing the high seas experience with her countrywomen, showing them the opportunities the sailing world has to offer.

This showpiece event is set to take place from September 12 to 19 in 2026, at the prestigious New York Yacht Club Harbour Court in Newport, Rhode Island. The boats of the hour will be the Club's fleet of 20 IC37s. These 37-foot keelboats, designed by Mark Mills are perfect for the occasion, being powerful, sporty platforms that reward crew cohesiveness and athleticism.

One of the skippers to look out for is China's Lijia "Lily" Xu. She’s no stranger to breaking boundaries or setting precedents, having won the gold medal at the London 2012 Games which was a first for China in the Laser Radial Class. She's hoping to make a splash again with her team representing the Royal Hong Kong Yacht Club, thus exemplifying the global nature of this championship.
At its heart, the championship will be celebrating women's sailing and those paths tread by its participants while striving to ignite new interest in the sport for the future generations.

title: Discover 'Four Joys' - The Latest Innovation in Luxury Yachting Now on Sale for €8,200,000
author: M
imageAlt: Discover 'Four Joys' - The Latest Innovation in Luxury Yachting Now on Sale for €8,200,000
summary: Welcome aboard 'Four Joys', a 31m Maiora masterpiece, boasting an innovative flybridge and cutting-edge Italian design, now available for acquisition.
body: Fusing creativity and luxury, 'Four Joys', a 31m Maiora motor yacht is now up for grabs. Presented by Costas Dimopoulos of International Yacht Corporation (IYC), this vessel stands as the first unit from Maiora - Next Yacht Group's 30 Walkaround model series, captivating those who value matchless design as much as unforgettable voyages.

'Four Joys' accommodates up to 11 guests and six crew members, making it an ideal prospect for family vacations or corporate retreats. Its five spacious cabins, which include a large master suite with dual en suite facilities, ensure spectacular views and absolute privacy. Further, the guest cabins on the lower deck enhance the luxurious experience, promising comfort and tranquility.

But the true jewel in the crown is the yacht's rare walk-around flybridge, a feature that set it apart from its contemporaries. This unique design delivers unrestricted and seamless access from the aft to the foredeck. This creates a more expansive lounge area, perfect for enjoying the breathtaking views or basking in the sun. Post dusk, the place transforms into a personal alfresco dining spot.

'Four Joys' rooftop innovation has earned it notable recognition in the world of motor yachts, a proof of its status as a 'very successful charter yacht'. Besides, a suite of water toys, a large swim platform, and the promise of a cruising speed of 21 knots propels it even further in the race. Designed to conquer waters while ensuring utmost comfort, 'Four Joys' is available for €8,200,000. This vessel serves not just as a possession, but as a declaration of a lifestyle marked by adventure, sophistication, and the grandeur of the open seas.

title: Exceptional Sailing Performance and Thrilling Race at the 7th South West Travellers at Dittisham Sailing Club
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Exceptional Sailing Performance and Thrilling Race at the 7th South West Travellers at Dittisham Sailing Club
summary: The 7th South West Travellers set sail at Dittisham Sailing Club, presenting a day filled with bright sun, robust gusts, and riveting sailing competition.
body: Sunshine graced the marine canvas of Dittisham Sailing Club for the 7th South West Traveller of the year. Belying its outward serenity, gusty conditions and a restless tide added a thrilling unpredictability to the race which began with an extended beat, testing the mettle of all competitors.

In the closely fought competition, ten 5.3 rigs and two 4.2 rigs vied for dominance. In race 1, Harry MacLeod steered his way to victory, with Charlie Mackenzie and Edith Philips hot on his tail. The second race saw a fiercely competitive battle, returning the sailors to the harbour with the top three performers levelled on points. Edith edged out the competition for first place, with Charlie settling for second and Harry third.

In the third bout, Charlie Mackenzie claimed glory, trailed by Dittisham's Leo Kaneko. The final race was a triumphant one for Edith Philips, who navigated to her first traveller win, with Charlie a close runner-up.

Underpinning the intense competition was the immense appreciation for the volunteers and helpers, whose tireless efforts ensured a successful event. Over the weekend, Dittisham Sailing Club was home to a substantially competitive and excitingly strong racing fleet, yielding an impressive set of results.

Philips topped the leaderboard, followed closely by Mackenzie, with the top five rounded out by Harry MacLeod, Leo Kaneko, and Brooke Browning. All eyes now rest on the SW sailors as they prepare to battle the waves at the Worlds and Nationals.

title: An Exciting Review of the 2025 Lord Birkett Trophy from the Deck of a Vivid International 14
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: An Exciting Review of the 2025 Lord Birkett Trophy from the Deck of a Vivid International 14
summary: Experience the thrilling sailing journey of the radiant orange International 14, Zog, in the 2025 Lord Birkett Trophy.
body: The 2025 Lord Birkett Trophy held a majestic spectacle from the deck of an International 14 yacht. On the crystalline waters of Ullswater, home to legendary wind shifts and stunning scenery, half a dozen International 14s took part in this thrilling journey. Among these elegant maritime marvels was the freshly refurbished 'Zog'. Emerging from an intensive period of restoration and varnishing, Zog beamed with a bold shade of orange, stealing the limelight at the event with its festive hues.

Described as a work of art reminiscent of a traffic cone, it was a sight to behold on the water, earning the nickname from the fleet as 'Captain Tanny Danny's masterpiece. It evoked a visual of a floating sunburn gleaming under the sun, turning heads around.

Facing the rollercoaster of emotions and challenges, the race started amidst flags of frustration and shared perseverance. This account captures more than a sailing journey; it encapsulates an adventurous tale of camaraderie, endeavour and spirit in the face of trials at the 2025 Lord Birkett Trophy.

title: Monaco Yacht Show's First Wave of Blue Wake Sustainability Torchbearers Transforming the Superyacht Industry
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Monaco Yacht Show's First Wave of Blue Wake Sustainability Torchbearers Transforming the Superyacht Industry
summary: Monaco Yacht Show's novel environmental initiative, Blue Wake, unveils its first batch of officially validated exhibitors, marking a significant step towards sustainable yachting.
body: The Monaco Yacht Show has made waves in the industry, announcing the first validated exhibitors for its innovative sustainability project, Blue Wake. A roster of seventeen trailblazing companies, all remarkable actors in their respective areas, such as marine ecosystem protection, material circularity, emissions reduction, and eco-design, have earned top billing at the prestigious event.

Launched with the visionary aim of showcasing pioneering innovations, Blue Wake hopes to propel the superyacht industry's voyage towards sustainability. These exhibitors, verified by the Water Revolution Foundation, Blue Wake's official partner, will enjoy prime visibility during the Monaco Yacht Show. The initiative offers yacht owners, builders, investors, and industry leaders the unique opportunity to directly engage with the ground-breaking advancements spearheading sustainable yachting.

Robert van Tol, Water Revolution Foundation's executive director, emphasised the importance of such innovations across the yachting supply chain. Blue Wake gives them a platform while ensuring that recognition is backed by rigorous, transparent evaluation.

The initiative is still accepting proposals from interested companies for its 2025 exhibition until the 31st of July 2025. Strict standards of eligibility and comprehensive documentation are required to qualify. The first exhibitors include industry names such as Sanlorenzo, Rolls-Royce Power Systems AG, and Sunreef Yachts, among others, all part of this glorious leap towards a greener future for yachting.

title: ORCV Women's Helm Race
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Why the return of the ORCV Women's Helm Race Changes Everything
summary: Some people drift into sailing. Rachel Mcguigan charged in—eyes up, hands on, no time to waste. When she first spoke to Leo Cantwell, skipper of Aileron, he asked her straight: “What do you want to learn?” Her answer was clear and fearless: “I want to do a helming course. I want to learn bow. I want it all. I’m not mucking about.” And she wasn’t. Leo took her seriously—and from that moment, things started moving.
body: She’s now helming Duxelle, (X 362 sport) which is co-owned by Catherine North, in the upcoming ORCV Women’s Helm, Navigator & Radio Operator Race (WHNR), and it’s not luck that got her there. It’s work. “You don’t get much time on the helm unless you own the boat…” That’s the challenge when you're starting out. You can be determined, capable, full of potential—but unless someone gives you a shot at the wheel, you’re stuck trimming, grinding, or watching. Rachel’s lucky to have had skippers who invested in her, gave her time, and trusted her to take the lead.

She got her early miles and hands-on experience crewing on Magic Bullet and Aileron—learning the boat inside and out, doing deliveries, soaking it all up. But helming? That came slowly, outside of race mode, often on long, cold passages or casual sails. It was valuable, yes—but limited.

So, she doubled down. Dinghy courses. Helm time anywhere she could get it. She trained her eye to look outside the boat—to read wind, laylines, VMG and ladder runs. She started taking notes, replaying races in her head, and thinking deeply about her next step.
She's learning the helm, one honest mile at a time.

When Rachel races, she makes one thing clear to her crew: “Here’s what I’m good at. Here’s where I need to grow.” That honesty, she says, is non-negotiable. “It’s dangerous to overstate your skills. You have to be upfront and open to learning—otherwise no one can help you.”

What’s next? She’s training for the Melbourne to Hobart this year. She’s already done a stack of double-handed races with Leo on Aileron, soaking up every moment. Her dream is the big one: Melbourne to Osaka, double-handed. She’s studying Pip Hare’s videos, reading every tip she can find, and pushing herself to get comfortable in every role onboard.
“I live sailing,” she says. “It’s in everything. You have to drive yourself—be patient, speak up, and stay curious. When people see that, they’ll start trusting you. That’s when it clicks.”
Why the WHNR Race Matters

Some people ask, “Why do we need a women’s race?” Rachel answers without blinking: “Because we need to prompt opportunity. We need to create space for people to grow and that's exactly what both Catherine and Leo have provided me… I'll be eternally grateful…"

She’s right. The ORCV Women’s Helm, Navigator & Radio Operator Race, now back in 2025 as a standalone passage race, is more than just a race. It’s a chance for women to step into leadership roles—at the helm, on the bow, on the radio, in the nav seat—and show what they’re made of.
Because the future of sailing depends on fresh hands and hungry hearts. And Rachel? She’s leading from the front.
Ready to Race? Saturday 26th July is just around the corner.
If you're a boat owner or skipper, the WHNR needs you. Match your boat with a crew through the ORCV’s Expression of Interest form, or for more information on how to enter go to the ORCV race page.

If you're a female sailor looking to jump onboard—helm, nav, radio, or crew—this is your moment. You can also complete the ORCV’s Expression of Interest form and take part. The team will match you to a boat accordingly.
Let’s get more women on the water, more often.

title: This weekend its the UKOPRA Offshore Powerboat Championship
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Round 3 of the 2025 UKOPRA Offshore Powerboat Championship
summary: This weekend, the waters of the Solent will come alive with high-octane action as Round 3 of the 2025 UKOPRA Offshore Powerboat Championship roars into Haslar Marina for the much-anticipated Solent 80. Set for Saturday, 12 July, this event is shaping up to be a showcase of raw speed, adrenaline-fuelled competition, and technical mastery – all played out against the iconic backdrop of the south coast’s legendary boati
body: That’s this weekend
Haslar Marina, Gosport – boatfolk Solent 80 course in the Western Solent
High-speed offshore racing featuring multiple boat classes (e.g., Class 1L) Boats “flying” past Haslar and entering high-wind areas in the Solent

Organised by UKOPRA (United Kingdom Offshore Powerboat Racing Association), the Solent 80 promises to deliver one of the most thrilling fixtures on the 2025 championship calendar. Following the high drama of the Poole Bay 100 and the Round the Island Challenge earlier this year, anticipation is high as teams converge on Gosport’s Haslar Marina to battle it out for critical mid-season points.

The race format – named for its approximate 80-mile length – sends competitors hurtling through the Solent in a course designed to test every facet of offshore powerboat racing. Expect a mix of tight turns, open-water speed sections, and unpredictable wave patterns that will challenge even the most seasoned teams. Vessels across various classes, from nimble monohulls to monstrous catamarans, will take to the water, piloted by some of the best racers in the UK and beyond.

Leading the charge is a strong field of returning favourites and hungry newcomers. Teams such as Pippa Racing, Spirit of Inverclyde, and Silverline have made early statements this season, with standout performances in the opening rounds. All eyes will be on reigning Class 1L champion Tom Montgomery, who is expected to bring his twin-engine powerhouse back for another shot at glory. Also tipped to make a splash is the all-female team Venom Racing, who have been turning heads with their skill and precision this season.

Beyond the competition, the Solent 80 is also a celebration of the offshore powerboat racing community. Haslar Marina will be a hive of activity, with pre-race scrutineering, team meet-and-greets, and a chance for fans to get up close with the machines before they hit the water. Spectators are encouraged to arrive early to secure a good vantage point – prime viewing spots include the outer marina wall, nearby vantage points at Gilkicker Point and Lee-on-the-Solent, or from the water aboard spectator craft.

The racing is expected to start mid-afternoon, depending on conditions. With wind and tide always in play on the Solent, strategy and adaptability will be as important as engine power. Boats will be travelling at speeds exceeding 50 knots (around 60 mph), often just feet apart, as they battle through the chop and wake. Safety crews, marine observers, and race marshals will be in full force to ensure the event runs smoothly and to UKOPRA’s rigorous standards.

One of the key storylines this year is the increased focus on sustainable marine engineering. Several teams are experimenting with hybrid propulsion systems, low-emission fuel blends, and hull designs aimed at reducing drag and fuel consumption. UKOPRA has made it clear that the future of offshore racing must evolve alongside marine environmental priorities – a vision clearly taking shape in 2025’s innovations.

After the chequered flag drops, attention will turn to the social side of the championship. A post-race awards event will take place on-site, giving crews, sponsors, and fans a chance to celebrate, swap stories, and talk tactics ahead of the next round in Lymington this August.

Whether you’re a die-hard racing fan, a curious newcomer, or simply someone who loves to see powerful machines on the edge of control, the UKOPRA Solent 80 offers a weekend of unmissable action. With top-level competition, roaring engines, and the dramatic coastal beauty of the Solent as its backdrop, this is British offshore racing at its very best.
So pack your binoculars, grab your waterproofs, and head to Haslar Marina this Saturday – the powerboats are coming, and the Solent won’t know what hit it.

title: Luxury Superyacht Sea Lady II Severely Damaged in High-Profile Fire
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Luxury Superyacht Sea Lady II Severely Damaged in High-Profile Fire
summary: British superyacht Sea Lady II was engulfed in threatening flames while docked at the renowned Port de Saint Tropez.
body: A stunning drama unfolded in the glamorous town of St Tropez, as the revered 41.3-metre Sea Lady II superyacht succumbed to a raging inferno. Videos from the scene depicting the yacht enshrouded in flames and towering plumes of black smoke served as an ominous testament to the severity of the disaster.

According to data from BOATPro, Sea Lady II docked at the port around 6.00pm, with the fire breaking out approximately two hours later. Initial reports suggest the fire began in the bow of the yacht before rapidly spreading to the lower decks.

The superyacht, Sea Lady II, is a gem from 1986 and the eminent flagship of British yard W.A Souter & Son with an expertly crafted exterior design by Don Shead. Among its many luxury features are a semi-circular saloon bar, al fresco dining on the aft deck, and a spacious five-cabin configuration.
The cause of this grave accident now lies at the heart of an ongoing investigation. The fate of the historic vessel Sea Lady II remains uncertain, with further updates expected in due course.

title: Nautical Powerhouse Antonini Navi Unveils New 33.5-metre Sport Utility Yacht
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Nautical Powerhouse Antonini Navi Unveils New 33.5-metre Sport Utility Yacht
summary: Italian marine giant Antonini Navi reveals its latest addition to the formidable lineup - the 33.5m Sport Utility Yacht SUY110.
body: Another marvel has emerged from the renown Italian yard, Antonini Navi. Bringing innovation and an imposing character to the nautical stage, the company introduces its latest creation, the SUY110 - a 33.5m model yacht with distinctive lines penned by Fulvio de Simoni himself. Revealed with a flair of majesty in Monaco with CA Moravia Yachting, the SUY110 is the lesser, though no less ambitious, sibling to the under-construction SUY135.

Another innovative feature gracing the SUY110 model is the elevated beach club area, overlooking the impressive garage. With an easy access to the main deck, this space transforms into a 27m2 veranda lounge comprising dining and relaxation areas. A key factor for Antonini Navi in designing this superyacht was maneuverability, seen in the carefully crafted ramps that allow seamless movement between decks.

Inside, the SUY110 remains true to Navi's commitment to luxury and comfort, boasting five plush cabins, a master suite with private studio, and further accommodations decks below. The yacht is already anchored on an engineered platform, ensuring delivery 22 months post contract signing.

Crowning off these features are its twin CAT engines pushing its top speed to an impressive 14 knots, and cruising speed to a comfortable 12 knots. Antonini Navi deftly balances luxury and essence of the sea in their latest model, the SUY110, marking another milestone for the pioneering brand.

title: Blade II, the 44.7m MMGI Motor Yacht, Emerges as Masterpiece with 18-Month Overhaul
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Blade II, the 44.7m MMGI Motor Yacht, Emerges as Masterpiece with 18-Month Overhaul
summary: The 44.7-metre MMGI motor yacht Blade II has recently completed a massive 18-month refurbishment at the Arpeca Shipyard in Viareggio, Italy.
body: An exceptional feat in the world of luxury yachts has been achieved - the MMGI motor yacht, Blade II, has completed an extensive 18-month refit at the renowned Arpeca Shipyard in Viareggio, Italy. The meticulous refurbishment has not only maintained but considerably upgraded the yacht's status among its peers.

The Blade II has seen gifts of innovation in the form of notable technical and aesthetic modifications. For starters, full reconstruction of the crew quarters and pilothouse was undertaken, complemented by the addition of brand new galley, pantry and lift. The exterior has been refurbished to a state of modern allure, trading the original white superstructure for a dark blue, uniform veneer. Complete with a reflective bootstripe and matching outdoor furniture, the design denotes a contemporary, smooth feel.

On the technical front, the Blade II has seen widespread enhancements. All electronics — navigation, surveillance and entertainment systems have been modernised with the latest technology. Additionally, essential maintenance for propulsion, plumbing, and air conditioning systems was undertaken to ensure top-notch performance. Even the yacht's custom-made Castoldi tender has undergone a refit to stay in sync with the mother ship.

Delivered in 2010 as the flagship build for MMGI, Blade II showcases a trim, powerboat-inspired exterior crafted by the adept Italian studio Navirex. It's an impressive silhouette that boasts floor-to-ceiling windows, a top speed exceeding 30 knots, and a main deck that cleverly lowers to water level. With this unprecedented overhaul said and done, the yacht is now up for sale with Smart Yachts, and prospective owners can preview the masterpiece in Monaco.

title: Bidding Wars Get More Exciting with Two Online Auctions Slated for July 2025 by Marine Auctions
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Bidding Wars Get More Exciting with Two Online Auctions Slated for July 2025 by Marine Auctions
summary: Marine Auctions is set to turn up the heat this July 2025 with two special online auctions for marine enthusiasts.
body: July 2025 is set to be a thrilling month for sea-faring enthusiasts and marine vessel collectors. The well-established auction house, Marine Auctions, is staging two seperate online auctions. Each event promises an experience brimming with the charm of digital bidding and the prospect of securing an awe-inspiring boat.

The first auction commences on 20th July and wraps up on 22nd July, a swift and exhilarating affair that leaves no room for hesitation. The second auction, slightly longer in duration, starts on 24th July and concludes on 30th July. Both auctions encompass an impressive collection of marine vessels, including the much-anticipated 2012 Beneteau First 40 Sloop.

Looking to the future, Marine Auctions is calling for entries for their forthcoming online auction in August 2025. Bidding for this event is set to open on Friday 22nd August and close on Thursday 28th August, providing another round of intense bidding and breath-taking collections.

To add to these exciting offerings, Marine Auctions is on the hunt for a 45 to 50ft flybridge catamaran on behalf of a client. The desired vessel must be fully AMSA 2C survery accredited and not older than 2015 - owners looking to sell such a beauty are encouraged to reach out.

Whether you’re an avid collector, a hopeful sea-farer, or simply an admirer of marine beauty, keep a keen eye on Marine Auctions' bidding pages this July and August. Grab this opportunity to be part of the thrills and spills of an online auction and who knows, you might soon be sailing away on a dream vessel!

title: THIRD AND FINAL STARTERS DEPART LA FOR DIAMOND HEAD
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: TRANSPAC, THIRD AND FINAL STARTERS DEPART LA FOR DIAMOND HEAD
summary: The 20 biggest, fastest boats racing in the 2025 Transpac began their offshore sprint from Los Angeles, California, to Honolulu, Hawaii, today. Ranging in length from 51 to 88 feet, these boats are competing in four divisions and also aiming to win the race’s two most prestigious prizes. The Barn Door Trophy honours the boat with the fastest elapsed time across the 2,225 nautical mile racecourse, while the King Kalak
body: The third and final part of the 2025 Transpac’s get going. The biennial race is organised by the Transpacific Yacht Club and is considered one of the world’s greatest offshore events.

Under clear skies with flat seas and a light six-knot west-southwesterly, all 19 starting monohulls were across the line by 1301:07. John Raymont’s Ker 52 Fast Exit was OCS (“On Course Side,” or over early) but turned back to restart and exonerate herself. Don Wilson’s Convexity2, competing in the smithREgroup Multihull Division, began racing on schedule at 1330 in eight knots of southwesterly breeze, which was forecast to build throughout the afternoon.

At the time of this writing and according to the Pasha YB Tracker, today’s starters were on a southwesterly course and clear of the west end of Catalina Island, with Bryon Ehrhart’s 88ft Juan Kouyoumdjian-designed Lucky (née Rambler 88) around first. Andries Verder’s Marten 72 Aragon was leading the push in the Boatswain’s Locker/Yanmar Division 1; Thomas Furlong's Vitesse was frontrunner in the Mount Gay Division 2; and Jack Jennings’ Pied Piper was topping the leaderboard in the Whittier Trust Division 3.

While all 52 boats that are still racing in the 2025 Transpac (see below) are competing for the King Kalakaua Trophy, the Barn Door Trophy is a different matter. This coveted prize celebrates sheer speed and is pursued by the boats with the longest waterlines and the most polished crews, prepared to tackle the sometimes-mammoth loads generated by these boats’ towering rigs.

“We’re about half and half,” said Thomas Furlong, owner and skipper of the Reichel/Pugh 52 Vitesse, referring to his blend of amateur and professional crew members. On the amateur side, Furlong’s crew includes his niece, Sarah Young, who just graduated from Dartmouth, in addition to several friends who have raced with him for years. While all aboard are accomplished sailors, “Professionals are really good at helping us push,” he said. “It’s always good to have somebody say, ‘you know, it’s time to slow down’ or ‘you can go faster.’”

For Furlong, the 2025 Transpac was four years in the making. He raced it in 2019 and 2021, but just before the start of the 2023 event, his insurance company declined to issue an out-of-area waiver. While unfortunate news, the silver lining was a long lead-time to get organised for this year. “We’ve had a progression in our sail inventory that has been focused on reaching,” Furlong said, noting that things felt less frantic in the final push before today’s start. “We’ve been on that journey for over four years.”
