This impressive regatta has gained international recognition, drawing top-notch teams from across the globe and firmly establishing Valencia as a hub for high-performance sailing.

throughout the event, Varadero Valencia will run its own stand in the official village, playing host to customers, captains, crews and sailing enthusiasts. The stand will be a conduit for dialogue, shared experiences and celebrating the spirit of this spectacular sailing fiesta. The refit yard will seize the opportunity to share its latest advancements and services in the arena of refit and repair.

title: The Impressive 28.1-Metre Sunseeker 'New Edge' Yacht Changes Hands in a High-Profile Sale
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Impressive 28.1-Metre Sunseeker 'New Edge' Yacht Changes Hands in a High-Profile Sale
summary: The luxurious 28.1-metre Sunseeker motor yacht, 'New Edge', has been successfully sold, a testament to its sleek in-house design, top-notch maintenance, and successful charter record.
body: The exquisite 28.1-metre Sunseeker 'New Edge' yacht has found a new owner in a sale that exemplifies the boat's high reputation. Thanks to the collaborative efforts of Geoff Moore representing the seller and David Westwood introducing the buyer, the 'New Edge' will continue to reign the seas with its new owner.

Delivered in 2019 by the British yard, the 'New Edge' is a testament to excellent boat-crafting, illustrating top-notch, in-house design and construction in GRP. The luxurious yacht earned its sterling reputation under the maintenance of a dedicated captain since its build. It underwent a recent revamp in 2023, further ensuring its high-end status. The yacht is commercially registered and boasts an unmatched charter record throughout the glamorous Mediterranean, adding to its allure.

The main saloon of 'New Edge' offers an expansive lounge and cozy seating area, perfect for relaxation and socializing. The yacht also features a formal dining table for those high-profile maritime dinners. To heighten the maritime experience, a side balcony constructively brings guests closer to the breathtaking ocean views.

For those who enjoy al fresco dining and socializing under the stars, there's the flybridge area. This space features a wet bar and a fold-out table for ten. Complementing this setup is the 10-seater table on the aft deck, making it perfect for larger gatherings. An additional dining area on the foredeck provides a sense of privacy when docked stern-to in port.

Under its luxurious exterior, the 'New Edge' beholds power. The 101GT motor yacht relies on twin MTU diesels, offering a cruising speed of 18 knots and a top speed of 25 knots. Completing her inventory is the 2023 Williams SportJet 435 tender, just hinting at the yacht's knack for adrenaline and speed. Previously, the 'New Edge' was asking €5,400,000, but now, it's ready to weave tales of grandeur with its new owner.

title: Australian Sailing Team Continues Successful Partnership with B&G Through to Los Angeles 2028 Olympics
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Australian Sailing Team Continues Successful Partnership with B&G Through to Los Angeles 2028 Olympics
summary: The Australian Sailing Team (AST) has reinforced its bond with sailing navigation supremos B&G, extending a productive eight-year partnership.
body: When two powerhouses in their respective domains extend their collaboration, excitement runs high within the international sailing community. It's no different with the Australian Sailing Team (AST) unveiling the renewal of its high-yield partnership with sailing instrumentation specialist, B&G.

This collaboration, essential to AST's breathtaking triumphs over the past eight years, has now locked in a four-year extension, promising more medal rushes until, at least, the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics. The partnership thrives on mutual commitment to harness innovation, enhance performance, and pursue excellence on the global podium. Beyond a conventional supply agreement, the relationship arms AST coach boats with trailblazing B&G electronics and crucial technical support, often under stringent deadlines before headline international regattas.

A partnership that has birthed an array of World Championship and Olympic medals for team AST, while concurrently providing B&G with quintessential feedback to refine product development, holds promises of future glories. Lauding B&G as a trusted partner since 2016, Brad Verkerk, Navico Group's Marketing Manager, articulated the brand’s commitment to elite racing, youth development and broader maritime initiatives.

It's no surprise that every AST coach boat comes equipped with a B&G multifunction display and top-tier sensors that monitor wind, weather, and sea conditions in real time. This ensures uniform data and insights, no matter where the team dukes out its contests worldwide. Echoing this sentiment, Michael Blackburn, Olympic bronze medallist and Australian Sailing Technical Director, extolls the robustness of B&G's stellar support that holds firm under pressure in varying conditions. Interestingly, he sees the tools as not only important but game-changing, offering his endorsement for this enduring partnership.

title: Seasonal Shifts in Superyachting: Delving into the Differences Between the Mediterranean and the Caribbean Seasons
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Seasonal Shifts in Superyachting: Delving into the Differences Between the Mediterranean and the Caribbean Seasons
summary: Whether you're a newbie or a seasoned hand on deck, experiencing the Med and Caribbean seasons in superyachting gives two distinct tastes of luxury.
body: Navigating between the Med Season and Caribbean Season of superyachting unveils a luxury world split into two unique halves. While both share the lure of luxury yachting, the differences in their vibe, pace, and guest expectations cannot be understated.

The Med season, typically spanning from April through to October, after the completion of pre-season maintenance and preparatory tasks, is virtually synonymous with high glamour and intense energy. The journey traces an exciting route along the coastlines of France, Italy, Spain, Greece, Croatia and more, where yachts flit between indulgent Rivieras, serene island anchorages, and fashion-forward ports. Look forward to non-stop action, with meticulously planned itineraries, long lunches at exclusive locations like the Hotel du Cap-Eden-Roc, dinner at Michelin-starred restaurants, shopping sprees at premium designer boutiques, and amidst all these, the constant presence of VIPs and celebrities.

Come December, the yachting world sees a shift as many superyachts make the Atlantic crossing to usher in the Caribbean Season, which lasts till March. The pace slackens, the formal attire gives way to flip-flops, and the rhythm becomes more relaxed, reflecting the Caribbean soul. The guest itineraries shift focus to water sports, beach escapades, paddleboarding, and BBQs or a lobster feast now and then. Though the standards remain high, the environment tends to be less formal and more social.

Starting a yachting career with a Caribbean season could perhaps be an apt choice for those seeking to familiarize themselves with the world of luxury yachting at a slightly gentler pace. Once seasoned, the fast lane of the Med Season becomes a stimulating prospect. Remember to secure a B1/B2 visa if you're keen on crossing the ocean to live these contrasting yachting experiences.

title: Thrilling Results, Unpredictable Challenges at the Helly Hansen Merlin Rocket Week at Salcombe
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Thrilling Results, Unpredictable Challenges at the Helly Hansen Merlin Rocket Week at Salcombe
summary: At the Helly Hansen Merlin Rocket Week 2025, competitors were greeted with challenging weather and exhilarating races, making Day 4 a spectacle to remember.
body: On the fourth day of the Helly Hansen Salcombe Merlin Week 2025, unpredictable gusts of the dreaded Northwesterly wind ushered in an exciting and challenging day of competitive sailing. With the courses sending racers towards the upper regions of the Ria, the starting line proved especially tricky to navigate.

The day began with the Blue versus Black race. The combined forces of a flood tide and sudden gusts created a challenging environment not for the faint-hearted. A rush at the Watch House end caused a general recall with 12 numbers hitting the board of death, including event leaders Tom Gillard and Rachel Gray.

The final loop of the harbour brought an unforeseen twist, reshuffling the leaders and squeezing the leading pack. Despite this tumult, Stu and Katherine managed to stay ahead, clinching their premiere victory. Tim and Fran took advantage of the confusion to land themselves in second place, just in front of George and Mark.

The afternoon saw the Red versus Green race. As the ebb began to flow against the fleet, some teams found it increasingly difficult to press their advantage. Up front, frontrunners of the Helly Hansen Merlin Rocket Salcombe Week found themselves embroiled in heated discussions regarding the rules.

As chaos ensued, Ollie Meadowcroft and Pete Gray executed a brilliant maneuver at the less flooded Portlemouth end of the line. With stellar control, they led their team across the choppy waters towards Snapes Point and established a solid lead during the journey to Gerston. Throughout the race, they maintained a minute's lead over the Henderson family, eventually culminating in a well-deserved victory.

title: Perini Navi Delivers Fourth Hull of its 60m Series: The Elegant Katana Yacht
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Perini Navi Delivers Fourth Hull of its 60m Series: The Elegant Katana Yacht
summary: The Italian icon of sea craftsmanship, Perini Navi, has unveiled its fourth 60m sailing yacht, Katana.
body: The lofty arena of sailing yachts continues to be invigorated with breath-taking innovations and excellent craftsmanship. A prominent key player, leading the path of this industry's marvellous inventions, is the Italian seacraft maven, Perini Navi.

The revered shipyard, renowned for its exquisite sailing vessels, has recently introduced a new member into its esteemed fleet, the fourth hull of its 60-metre series, Katana. Secured at The Italian Sea Group's Marina di Carrara, the coveted yacht is armying up for its first sail towards Gibraltar. Following the helm of her sisterships Perseus 3, Seahawk, and Seven, the construction of Katana took off in 2016 and was acquired a year after by the owner of the Monaco-based Gamma Yachts. After a short pause, the beauty resumed its creation process in 2022, now finally gracing the waters.

In terms of onboard comfort, Katana astonishes with her interior arrangement that presents a master suite along with five stylish guest cabins. Her elegant interiors are the creation of renowned French designer Rémi Tessier. While the shipyard remains alluringly discreet about revealing full details, it promises 'refined' settings for voyagers, negating any need for excessive display to impress.

Echoing the resounding success of Katana’s delivery, Gianmaria Costantino, the Chief Commercial Officer of The Italian Sea Group, expressed that the launch marks another milestone for Perini Navi's grand relaunch project. He proudly affirmed the company's commitment to excellence and their ability to merge tradition with innovation harmoniously. His affirmation came in the wake of a successful financial report from the shipyard, which recorded a satisfactory €96.8 million revenue in the first quarter of 2025.

In the ocean of sailing vessels, the Katana yacht stands as a testament to Perini Navi's unwavering dedication to quality, innovation, and seaworthiness. As anticipation builds, sailing enthusiasts and fans eagerly await the day when Katana hits the water, confirming her place amongst the world's most impressive superyacht fleet.

title: Braving Seas of Time: Lürssen Celebrates a 150-Year Journey in Marine Excellence, From Modest Beginnings to Yachting Supremacy
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Braving Seas of Time: Lürssen Celebrates a 150-Year Journey in Marine Excellence, From Modest Beginnings to Yachting Supremacy
summary: The iconic German shipyard, Lürssen, commemorates an impressive journey of 150 years, underlining its evolution from humble roots to becoming a trailblazer in the global yachting scene.
body: Founded on a summer's day in 27 June 1875, the German shipbuilder, Lürssen, is raising a toast to its monumental legacy of 150 years of shipbuilding. This celebration is a nod to its spectacular ascent from humble beginnings to becoming an epitome of excellence in global yachting.

Over a century and a half, Lürssen has navigated the open seas of the marine industry, consistently setting standards and redefining the benchmarks in shipbuilding and yachting. It has carved a niche for itself, standing tall as one of the much-revered names in the maritime panorama.

The legendary shipyard's story remains an inspiration for the maritime world as it steps into the next century and a half, preparing to ride the tide of the future with the same undying spirit that had powered its inception 150 years ago.

title: Helly Hansen Merlin Rocket Week 2025: An Epic Display of Competitive Sailing at Salcombe Yacht Club
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Helly Hansen Merlin Rocket Week 2025: An Epic Display of Competitive Sailing at Salcombe Yacht Club
summary: The 2025 Helly Hansen Merlin Rocket Week showcases a breathtaking panorama of strategic maneuvers and sails ripping the wind at Salcombe Yacht Club.
body: Salcombe Yacht Club hums with excitement and competitive energy as the Helly Hansen Merlin Rocket Week 2025 sets sails on a new day. The weather, having passed the halfway point, serves up another unique layer of challenge as the dreaded Northwesterly winds blow, making the starting line one of the more daring tasks to conquer. Sailors deal with gusts from every direction, pushing their navigation skills to the limit.

Over the long stretch up to Gerston, the building breeze of 15 knots sees sailors Stu and Katherine cleverly navigate their way into a lead. They maintain their advantage over a 200-metre distance from William and Andy, who remain locked in a vicious battle for the second place with George Yeoman and Mark Oakey. Throughout the race, leaders exchange, suspense builds, and the day concludes with the afternoon race, featuring a tough start against the ebbing tide and an intense display of skillful navigation and knowledge of sailing rules.

The saga of the sailing competition does not end there. On the final day, under a beautiful blue sky, a light Southwester breathes life into the harbour, with the overall result still hanging in the balance. The morning race ensues with the flood tide making a challenging start. Yet, amid this dramatic scenario, Tom Gillard and Rachel Gray manage to take a commanding lead, providing an exciting climax to the eventful Helly Hansen Merlin Rocket Week at Salcombe Yacht Club.

title: Carbon Emission Rating System SEA Index Gets Region-Wide Adoption for Sustainable Boating
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Carbon Emission Rating System SEA Index Gets Region-Wide Adoption for Sustainable Boating
summary: The Superyacht Eco Association's emission rating tool, SEA Index, has been incorporated into the Agreements for a Sustainable Mediterranean.
body: A major stride forward has been taken in the realm of sustainable yachting. The Superyacht Eco Association's SEA Index, an initiative by the Yacht Club de Monaco, has been integrated into the Agreements for a Sustainable Mediterranean. This environmental plan of action is led by Région Sud (Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur), which underscores the commitment to environmental responsibility in the Mediterranean region.

The SEA Index presents an independent, verifiable, and effective framework for accurately measuring and reducing carbon emissions in yachts over 24 metres. The Lloyd’s Register-verified certification process is comprehensive, also addressing air and noise pollution. Moreover, it provides useful refit recommendations and access to a dynamic international network focused on sustainability.

It is an encouraging testament to the effectiveness of the SEA Index that it is now being adopted at a regional level, a leap from previous individual port adoptions. The aspiration is clear - to steer together towards a more responsible and sustainable future for yachting. The trust placed in the SEA Index is a beacon of hope that the yachting sector can sail in harmony with the preservation and conservation of our marine environment.

title: Bellini Astor 36: The Dazzling Revival of Bellini Yachts' After 50-Year Intermission
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Bellini Astor 36: The Dazzling Revival of Bellini Yachts' After 50-Year Intermission
summary: Bellini Yachts re-emerges in the boat market after a 50-year break, introducing the brand-new GRP sportscruiser, the Bellini Astor 36.
body: Half a century after their untimely exit from the boat market, Bellini Yachts is making a splash once more, re-establishing their roots with the launch of their new boat, the Bellini Astor 36. This family-owned Italian yard was once famous in the 1960s for creating wooden runabouts comparable in style and performance to Riva. Unfortunately, following the ill health of its founder Battista Bellini, production came to a halt in the early 1970s. The company then shifted focus to storage, sales, and restoration. Fast forward to 2023, a new generation of Bellinis is bringing the company back to its origins.

The Bellini Astor 36 does not offer any radical innovation in its layout, but it effectively strikes the right chords for an open Med-style sportscruiser. Included in the price are the folding balconies that extend the beam to over 6m when open. A functional looking T-top provides just enough shade to cover the helm and dinette.

The lower deck, while compact, appears well-resolved, with a generous amount of space around the island bed forward, and a subtle double mattress tucked behind the stairs. An assortment of petrol and diesel sterndrive engine options are available to buyers, and uniquely for a niche Italian brand, there's a UK dealer, Sebino Yachts, based in Christchurch, Dorset.
The Bellini Astor 36, blending the allure of the past with the sophistication of the present, is truly a triumphant return for Bellini Yachts' trademark glamour to the world of boating.

title: Adventurous UK Entrepreneur Steve Rigby Debuts 'Haze²', His Latest CDM Superyacht
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Adventurous UK Entrepreneur Steve Rigby Debuts 'Haze²', His Latest CDM Superyacht
summary: Steve Rigby, known for his daring ventures at sea, steps forth onto the world stage once again with his latest acquisition, Haze².
body: A well-known figure in the world of yachting, Steve Rigby's passion for the ocean is no secret. His latest addition, Haze², is a continuation of this love affair, marking his steady transition from land to sea. Haze² is the sixth unit in the Darwin 102 series by Italian yard Cantiere delle Marche (CDM), who Rigby has developed a strong relationship with. This led to the birth of his latest dream vessel, a successor of the much-lauded Extra Yachts' 26.2-metre Haze. Sporting a sharp metallic grey hull and bold blue superstructure, the yacht was launched after teasing eyes at the 2022 Cannes Yachting Festival. The construction of Haze² began that same year. A seasoned sailor with a history of both sailing and motor yachts, Rigby funnelled his clear vision of what he wanted his next yacht to be into the creation of Haze². The UK-based studio Lawson Robb is the brain behind Haze²'s riveting interiors. Known for their artistic discretion, they have also worked on its predecessor. George Wolstenholme, Lawson Robb's director and creative lead, noted that Rigby's vision had evolved from a 'fairweather craft' towards a design that could take him to more remote locations, aligning with his adventurous spirit. The enhanced features on Haze² reflect this evolution, including developed window systems for a wraparound glass feel, and a concealed tender crane in the yard's RJ line style. Hydro Tec is the talent behind the exterior design and naval architecture. Catering to Rigby’s lifestyle needs, the yacht comprises intimate areas tailored for entertaining and remote work. A soft, muted palette with sporadic bursts of vibrant colours, particularly reds and oranges, embellish the interiors. A sun deck Jacuzzi nestled between sun pads, along with an aft deck tender storage, are a few of its remarkable features. A private and charter yacht in essence, Haze² will be classed accordingly. As of now, CDM has eight yachts currently under construction according to BOATPro. Continuing to wow the marine world, the company launched its 46.9-metre flagship, the RJ. For the audacious traveller or the ardent sailor, Rigby's dynamic adventure with seafaring and yachts like Haze² drives home the joy and thrill of being one with the vast, captivating ocean.

title: An action packed day 1 at the 44Cup Marstrand.
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Tough Start for Lanzarote Calero Sailing Team
summary: Day 1 - 44Cup Marstrand, 25 June 2025: The Lanzarote Calero Sailing Team began their participation in the 44Cup Marstrand with an intense day on the water, marked by sunny conditions, gusty winds, and a series of incidents that impacted the day’s results.
body: Following a promising start and positive performance during training, the Spanish team's position was adversely affected by two significant penalties - one in the second race and another in the third—that directly impacted their standings. To top off an already complicated day, a broken line during the final race caused a crew member to fall overboard, forcing the team to slow down and ultimately finish the day in 12th position.

The team showed strong pace and good manoeuvres during segments of the first race, but gradually lost rhythm and positions due to the penalties, especially during tight mark roundings. In Race 3, despite a solid tactical start, protested decisions and a critical gear failure sealed their result. The day ended with the team in 12th place, highlighting the urgent need to climb back up the leaderboard in the coming races.

Tactician Alfredo González summed up the day: “We had a day with very strong points, such as the starts, and others that we are already working on, like boat speed. In races 2 and 3 we were in the top five group, but we were penalised at both gates. We’ll carefully review those situations so they don’t happen again.”

Wednesday’s weather report looks like its going to be tough as well with projected gusts of up to 23 knots and steady northwest winds (290–300º), demanding maximum focus on trimming and manoeuvres. While the day was visually stunning, the conditions punished every error and left no room for recovery.

title: Unveiling the Future of Exploratory Boating - Columbus Yachts' Groundbreaking Crossover 48
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unveiling the Future of Exploratory Boating - Columbus Yachts' Groundbreaking Crossover 48
summary: Pioneering a new chapter in luxury boating, Columbus Yachts has launched the revolutionary Crossover 48 explorer project.
body: Italian yard Columbus Yachts has ignited a frisson of anticipation in the nautical world with the announcement of its revolutionary new exploratory project, christened the 'Crossover 48'. Cementing its reputation as an industry trailblazer, the building of the new vessel is already underway at Palumbo Superyachts' shipyard, located in the picturesque port city of Savona, Italy.

Making a bold statement, Columbus Yachts marches ahead with the Crossover 48 project on-spec, a testament to its unwavering confidence buoyed by the success of its preceding models - 'Crossover 42' and 'Crossover 47'. Currently, Columbus Yachts has one unit each planned of the previous two models, with the Crossover 42 slated for delivery within the year.

Admirers of the new vessel can look forward to luxuriously appointed accommodations spread across six cabins, featuring one VIP cabin on the main deck and an indulgent owner's suite on the upper deck. The yacht also stands out with key specs like an 8.6-metre beam and a draft of 2.75 metres. As the build progresses, Columbus Yachts plans to keep the anticipation alive by revealing more details, slowly and steadily shaping the future of exploratory boating.

title: Chichester Yacht Club Hosts Thrilling 2000 Millenium Series with Simon and Katie Horsfield Dominating the Waters
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Chichester Yacht Club Hosts Thrilling 2000 Millenium Series with Simon and Katie Horsfield Dominating the Waters
summary: The 2000 Millenium Series 4 recently took place at the Chichester Yacht Club, with competitors experiencing superior sailing conditions and thrilling racing.
body: On the 29th of June, excitement ran wild at Chichester Yacht Club. An array of sixteen yachts sought to master the waves in the 2000 Millenium Series, an open event sponsored by West Country Boat Repairs. With brilliant sunshine, a rising breeze, and significantly less weed than last year, the stage was set for a day of remarkable sailing.

The first race took place with a promisingly shifty force 3/4 breeze and a rising tide. It was clear from the get-go that Simon and Katie Horsfield were going to be a force to be reckoned with. Excelling with their swift start, the Horsfields quickly took the lead, delivering a sailing masterclass throughout the day. Their first place position went uncontested over all three races of the event. Close behind were Rob and Gemma Burridge, securing a respectable second place followed by Jonathan and Louisa Ching in third.

The momentum of the event built as the day progressed. The second race saw a general recall and a black flag restart as the wind force escalated to 4. Struggling to adapt, the coastal teams sighed in relief as shifts dwindled. Though, this was a bitter pill to swallow for the landlocked sailors who thrive in the craft of negotiating sudden shifts. Nevertheless, at the conclusion of race two, Pete and Sophie secured second place, followed by Rob and Gemma and Jonathan and Louisa.

By race three, sailors were dealing with wind force 4/5, leading to intense competition and fatigued arms, especially with races two and three demanding five laps each. With the precious second spot up for grabs, Pete and Sophie finished the third race in second place, followed by Jonathan and Matthew. In the end, Katie and Simon Horsfield claimed the crown at the 2000 Millennium Series, with Pete and Sophie Vincent in second place and Rob and Gemma Burridge in third.
Such a delightful day of sailing once again proved that whether one is an experienced sailor or a newcomer, the thrill, camaraderie, and sheer joy of the sport are irresistible.

title: Diving into Sarah Diggle Whitlock's Extraordinary Career in West Nautical: From Cage Diving to Yacht Crewing
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Diving into Sarah Diggle Whitlock's Extraordinary Career in West Nautical: From Cage Diving to Yacht Crewing
summary: Explore the colourful career of Sarah Diggle Whitlock, West Nautical’s Captains and Head of Department Specialist and her journey from cage diving with great white sharks to shaping superyacht careers.
body: Sarah Diggle Whitlock, Captain and Head of Department Specialist for West Nautical, has a career as rich and colourful as the seas she's traversed. Incredible journeys into the depths with great white sharks have shaped her path, leading her to roles responsible for guiding and connecting the world of yacht crews. Having had her heart first stolen by her desire to save animals and a love for the open road in her early years, Sarah joined Greenpeace at age nine. However, she found her age restricitve in effecting the change she desired, ushering her towards her passion for travel worldwide. Her global trips led her to Byron Bay, where she became a dive instructor. Subsequently, her journey took her to Mallorca and later, South Africa where she practised great white shark cage diving - a definite standout in her career. A return to Mallorca saw her establishing connections with yacht captains and two globe-spanning journeys as a chief stewardess aboard sail and motoryachts. This series of well-suited roles helped her accomplish her childhood dream of traversing the seven seas. Sarah’s role at West Nautical, where she has now worked for 15 years, sees her using her experience and insights to pair yacht captains with crew candidates. Recognising the unique requirements of different yachts and yacht owners, Sarah thrives on the challenge of matching suitable crew members to each ship. Sarah also assists crew members in honing their industry CVs. The modesty of the individuals she works with often sees many sailing veterans downplaying their experiences - that's where she comes in. Sarah helps to highlight their accomplishments, character, and unique stories in order to stand out in the competitive arena of seafarers. In providing advice to individuals starting a career in yachting, Sarah stresses patience, positivity, and hard work. It's clear that her time as a chief stewardess continues to inform her outlook and strategies for success in this challenging, but deeply rewarding industry.

title: Meticulous Analysis of the 30 to 50-Metre Yacht Market Unearths Hidden Trends and Unmistakable Leaders
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Meticulous Analysis of the 30 to 50-Metre Yacht Market Unearths Hidden Trends and Unmistakable Leaders
summary: Dive deep into the performance of the 30 to 50-metre yacht market over the past decades, highlighting the dominating trends, players, and influences that shape the sector.
body: The 30 to 50-metre yacht market has seen dramatic shifts over the past two decades. Casting a discerning eye at the industry from a distance can give a distorted view. However, a more detailed analysis reveals critical patterns and leaderboards. There was a striking discovery when the spotlight was aimed at core builders in the 30 to 50-metre category. Bankruptcies and an uneven playing field skew the ranking and give a distorted view of the real titans of the sector. Consider Broward Marine that completed its last and final superyacht before bankruptcy while still ranking strong in many charts. Then there's Perini Navi, building only six yachts in the past decade, yet taking up notable space on the list of competitors. Insights only emerge when one segments the market, compares similar products, and considers time epochs intelligently. When looking at 20 years, 10 years and five-year spans, striking patterns emerge, narrating the story of success, competition, and changing market dynamics. These timelines demonstrate how shipyards' strategies, ownership changes, fiscal impacts, and other influences shaped the market. Sanlorenzo, steered by Max Perotti for 20 years, has established its position at the zenith when the recount is refined, with rivals like Sunseeker, Overmarine, and Azimut trailing behind. Nevertheless, the landscape can quickly shift if we factor in multi-brands like the Ferretti Group or the Azimut|Benetti Group. Through every shift and wave, the market bears witness to rise and fall, success and failure, carving stories into the hulls of these majestic oceanic beasts. The market awaits further insights as our team digs deeper into the histories and trends of the various shipyards. As we sail forward, we look ahead at the changing currents of the coming months.

title: Diving Deep with Sarah Diggle Whitlock: A Journey from Sharks to the Superyacht Industry & Sunseeker's Job Cut Insights
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Diving Deep with Sarah Diggle Whitlock: A Journey from Sharks to the Superyacht Industry & Sunseeker's Job Cut Insights
summary: Take a tour through Sarah Diggle Whitlock's extraordinary maritime career and unravel the impacts of Trump's tariffs on Sunseeker's staff reduction plan.
body: Embark on an unforgettable voyage with Sarah Diggle Whitlock, West Nautical's resident Captain and Head of Department (HOD) Specialist. Her trek from diving with great white sharks to honing superyacht careers is a saga that sparkles with maritime marvel. The captivating Cornish coastline, enchanting English Channel, and mesmerising Mallorca served as the backdrop for Sarah's vibrant voyage, which equips her masterfully in understanding and matching the crew to each yacht's unique environment.

Both Sarah's maritime journey and Sunseeker's workforce challenges offer two perspectives on the yachting industry – one that celebrates the sense of adventure nurtured by the sea, and another that sheds light on the economic realities seafarers must continuously navigate.

title: Lanzarote Calero Sailing Team aiming for the Podium
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Lanzarote Calero Sailing Team aiming for the Podium
summary: The Lanzarote Calero Sailing Team is heading into the third stage of the 2025 44Cup in Marstrand, Sweden, with a clear objective: to turn the season around and climb the overall rankings. The team returns to these waters with good memories, having claimed a remarkable third place the last time they raced in Marstrand back in 2011.
body: This regatta represents a turning point in the season, as the team seeks to regain momentum in one of the most competitive circuits in international sailing. Official practice will begin on 24th June, with racing scheduled from 25 to 28 June.

The team, led by Alfredo González, features a well-established crew and approaches this new challenge with greater preparation and experience. “We return to Marstrand with a clear mindset and strong motivation. This venue has always held something special for us, and we want to deliver a performance that takes us back to the top,” says the tactician.
Institutional support has also been expressed from their home island. Oswaldo Betancort, President of the Lanzarote Island Council, stated:

“Lanzarote wishes the Lanzarote Calero Sailing Team the greatest success. Like our island, they are unique, different, and full of talent and skill. A true benchmark in both sports and nautical excellence. Go team! You are pure Lanzarote DNA.”

The next stop for the Lanzarote Calero Sailing Team in the 44Cup is The Lanzarote Calero Sailing Team is supported by a strong group of partners that believe in the power of sport as a tool for global visibility. Their main backers include Turismo Lanzarote, the Centros de Arte, Cultura y Turismo (CACT), Calero Marinas, Calmar, Lanzarote Investment, and John Woods Real Estate. On the technical side, the team collaborates with Harken (via Equipyacht) and Gottifredi Maffioli, with Alegra Travel serving as their official travel partner.
With challenging wind conditions forecast for both training and racing days, the 44 Cup Marstrand promises to be an exciting and action-packed event, that I am looking forward to.

title: Meet Pegasus, the Electric Hydrofoil Set to Revolutionise Luxury Boating, Combining F1 Styling with Motorbike Handling Skills
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Meet Pegasus, the Electric Hydrofoil Set to Revolutionise Luxury Boating, Combining F1 Styling with Motorbike Handling Skills
summary: Introducing Pegasus, an innovative electric hydrofoil boat from Finnish company FoilOne, combining Formula 1 dazzle with motorbike handling in a cutting-edge design set to redefine luxury on water.
body: The inaugural presentation of the Pegasus, at The Foiling Week in Italy, was met with acclaim from the boating community. The distinctly novel electric hydrofoiling boat was crafted by Finnish company FoilOne and is aimed at redefining the high-end boating experience. The innovative design has already made a splash in the industry, earning the prestigious Foiling Motorboat of the year at the International Foiling Awards. Drawing inspiration from the characteristic charm of 1950’s Formula 1 cars, Pegasus becomes an F1 throwback on water, flaunting a wide grille-style bow and fuselage cockpit which are hard to miss. Yet, it fluidly combines this with a totally different dimension of handling reminiscent of motorbikes. The steering system, crafted in-house, was designed to simplify operation for those unfamiliar with boating, achieving a sense of familiarity with more widely driven motorbikes. The advanced hydrofoil featured on the Pegasus yields lower water resistance, enabling exceptional speeds and increased efficiency. This forward-thinking approach has allowed FoilOne to construct a craft that can journey faster and farther than any conventional electrically powered boat. Made of the lightweight, strong, and pricey material Carbon fibre, Pegasus maintains a minimum weight for efficient foiling, solidifying itself as a gamechanger in the world of luxury boating. An undoubtedly premium product targeting the superyacht market, the Pegasus comes with a hefty price tag, starting from €109,900, exclusive of the boat’s dual 5kWh Torqeedo electric batteries. However, the attention to detail, craftsmanship, and multitude of customisation options justifies the price tag for those seeking unmatched luxury and innovation in marine vessels.

title: Victory in DYSC Marine Supplies Winter Series Race 1
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Victory in DYSC Marine Supplies Winter Series Race 1
summary: Melbourne, VIC – Under crisp winter skies and a solid northerly breeze, the Ocean Racing Club of Victoria’s (ORCV) DYSC Marine Supplies Winter Series Race 1 delivered spectacular racing this weekend. With 36 boats lining up for the start, competitors were treated to classic Port Phillip conditions – shifting winds between 10 to 20 knots, flat seas, and plenty of tactical opportunities.
body: The day began with a rare and expertly coordinated on water practice distress flare drill session on the waters off Royal Brighton Yacht Club, offering sailors the chance to deploy a range of different types of flares under the supervision of CASA, Victoria Police, and the Port of Melbourne. It was a unique and valuable exercise in offshore safety training, reinforcing the ORCV’s commitment to both racing and safety preparedness.

Following the flare drill, race management set a dynamic course with a beat to the north of the bay, a long spinnaker run to Sandringham mark 5, and spinnaker finish to the finish line. With conditions varying across the course, smart navigation and tight teamwork were the keys to success.
The Botin Carkeek Gp 42 ‘Ambition’, skippered by Chris Dare, put on a commanding display from the outset and succeeded with an impressive line honours victory.

While competing in the Newport to Bermuda race this time last year, the J111 ‘Ginan’ Skippers Nigel Jones and Cam McKenzie missed out on taking part in the annual flare drill. This year, they achieved remarkable success, winning overall top honours (based on AMS). "Nigel gave us a nice start to the day, starting us off down the pin end, sitting behind Ambition and Salt we felt good about our position," McKenzie explained. "Later in the race we made a tactical call to stay out, and it paid off."

Meanwhile, Joel Matthews skippered Godzilla to 1st Place in Division 2 AMS, returning to the racecourse after a full hull respray and refit – and straight into the winner's circle. "None of the crew had sailed together before, or sailed on this boat," Matthews said. "While Godzilla prefers sub-8 knot conditions, the boat handled the brisk breeze…We were overpowered early, but made up serious ground on the downwind and final upwind legs," Matthews added.

Also putting in a strong performance was the Beneteau First 44.7 ‘Another Chapter’ skippered by Greg Clinnick, who missed AMS victory by a mere 14 seconds (based on corrected time) behind Ginan. The crew showed consistency, speed, and smart handling throughout, cementing their place as another boat to follow throughout the development of the DYSC winter series.

In the double handed category, veteran sailor Jock MacAdie skippered Alex-Team MacAdie to victory in the PHS division, making the most of the light start and building breeze. "It was one of those days where everything aligned," said MacAdie. "Flat water, a good working breeze, and a solid teammate who did most of the heavy lifting!" Jock's pedigree in short-handed sailing is well known – having won the 2007 Melbourne–Osaka race with his son Hamish. "We've been sailing this way for a long time. The boat's set up for it, but it takes time to get it right. Not just technically – you've got to race well, too."

Attention now turns to the popular Winter Series destination races to Geelong which is up next on July 5th where opportunities are given to Novice crews on July 6. Entries are open here https://www.orcv.org.au/winter-series
Full race results can be found here https://www.orcv.org.au/results/2024-25/2025MWS/series.htm?ty=78521

title: Rolex Fastnet Race Class40 top guns
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Class40 top guns Rolex Fastnet Race
summary: Now 20+ years old, the Class40 has proved itself one of the most successful genre of offshore race boat ever. Since Géry Trentesaux and class co-founder, round the world sailor and journalist Patrice Carpentier entered their first Pogo 40 in the 2005 edition, the Rolex Fastnet Race has included a strong entry from this French box rule class, providing it with its own class since 2009. Today the Rolex Fastnet Race fea
body: More than 200 Class 40s now exist. The latest hull number allocated by the class is #212 Luca Rosetti's Muso 40 Maccaferri Futura, which is one of the 24 so far entered in this year’s edition of the Royal Ocean Racing Club’s premier event, due to set sail from Cowes on 26 July.

Currently Italy is the rising star in the French short-handed classes. Like Ambrogio Beccharia who won the Mini Transat in 2019 then graduated up to a successful Class40 campaign, so Rosetti won the 2023 Mini Transat and his brand new Maccaferri Futura is the latest iteration of the Italian-designed and built Musa 40, of which Beccharia’s Alla Grande-Pirelli was the first.

The former Alla Grande-Pirelli will be raced in the Rolex Fastnet Race this year by Spaniard Pep Costa as VSF Sports. Since winning the last edition as crew on Everial, Costa has since won a competition to skipper for three years a Class40 backed by French automotive glazing company VSF. “Since I was a child, the Rolex Fastnet Race was for me an emblematic, mythical race, a race every sailor wants to do,” says Costa. “I was extremely happy to do it on Everial. Now I am looking forward to doing it on my own boat.” Since acquiring the boat Costa says they have upgraded the foils. His crew includes the successful Pablo Santurde, previously part of Gonzalo Botin's winning team on Tales II.

The second Muso40 Andrea Fornaro’s Influence2 is back having finished third in 2023. “It's an iconic race, a beautiful race to do, because everybody thinks of it as the pinnacle of offshore sailing, one of the most prestigious races, etc. We’ve got a new keel, new rudders and made some modifications.Last time we were third - this time we want first.”
Another Musa 40 is Les Invincibles of Frenchman William Mathelin-Moreaux, who finished second in 2023 with his previous boat Dekuple.

Making her race debut in Cowes will be the brand new Agité 40, Alex Le Gallais’ Trimcontrol. This has been conceived by Michel Desjoyeaux, having been developed by Desjoyeaux’s company CT Mer Forte and built by Mer Agitée. She will be a scow, although with a less extreme bow - for example, her chine will not extend to the bow. “The rule is simple, but the way to optimise around the rule is quite complex because there is a minimum weight but a minimum and maximum righting moment,” says Desjoyeaux. Having pioneered the enclosed IMOCA cockpit, the Agité 40’s cockpit can be fully enclosed with fabric walls and inflatable tubes providing stiffness. Also on board will be well-known RORC son Carlo Vroon (who raced with Le Gallais in 2023).

Other hot prosects include regular podium placer Legallais, the Lift V2 skippered by Figaro sailor/Volvo Ocean Race winner Fabien Delahaye, who finished second in last year’s Class 40 Championship. Pierre-Louis Attwell is back with his Mach 40.5 Vogue avec un Crohn, the 2024 Class 40 Championship winner. Also entered again is Nicolas Lemarchand and Matthieu Derenne's Lift 2 Weeecycling, previously Yoann Richomme’s 2018 Route du Rhum winner. Then there's Machouquette, Guillaume L'Hostis's 2023 vintage Mach 40.5, which was fifth in this year’s Normandy Channel Race and Thomas Jourdren’s Pogo S4 TNST Racing & Cabinet Z.

There are two British competitors: RORC regular and instructor Jonathan Tyrrell and Dan Jones' Pogo S4 Gambit, and Stuart Sawyer, two time IRC Nationals winner with his J/122 Black Dog, who is new to the class. He began racing shorthanded on a Sun Fast 3300 but then met Robin Elsey-Webb. A graduate of the Artemis Offshore Academy, Elsey-Webb nearly lost his life during an assault in 2023 and has since been on the slow road to recovery. The two conjured up two year program including the Rolex Fastnet Race and other RORC races culminating in Elsey-Webb competing in the 2026 Route du Rhum. Sawyer has acquired a Mach 40.4 (now with 40.5 appendages), previously Antoine Magré's 2021 Rolex Fastnet Race and Transatlantic Race winner E Leclerc Ville La Grand. “It is a highly competitive fleet and delivers the sheer thrills we all like,” says Sawyer of his Black Dog VI. Their Kernow Ocean Racing team raises money for and awareness about brain injury.

Other nations represented include Belgium in Jonas Gerckens’ Lift V2 Abeona (previously Marc Lepesqueux's Curium life forward) and Angolan Globe 40 round the world race competitor Jose Guilherme Caldas’ Barco Brasil-Mussulo, (highly successful over 2017-19 as Aymeric Chappellier’s AINA Enfance et avenir).

Other competitive boats of this vintage entered include Romain Van Enis' Max 40 Denti Aile, formerly Ian Lipinski's Credit Mutuel and sistership Gran Rhino, campaigned by the sole female Class40 competitor this year, Spain’s Aina Bauzà. Lawyer Renaud Courbon is back on the Cape Racing 40 The3Bros after failing to finish in 2023, while Italians Matteo Sericano and Francesco Rosati are campaigning the VPLP Clak40 Lucente, after finishing fourth in May's Paprec 600 Saint Tropez. Engineer Emmanuel Hamez, skipper of the Pogo S4 Viranga has been campaigning Class40s regularly since 2014 but returns for the first time since 2017.

While the modern example are all scows, a sub-set are the ‘sharp bowed’ Class40 - effectively hull #157 and older. Among these are German orthopaedic surgeon Sebastian Ropohl, back again on his Cantaloop40 and Nicolas Guibal’s Pogo S3 Moonpalace. “We’re entering the Rolex Fastnet Race with a clear goal: to be the first among the sharp-bowed Class40s,” comments Guibal.

title: AB Yachts Brings Automotive Inspiration to High Seas in Their New AB 110S Yacht
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: AB Yachts Brings Automotive Inspiration to High Seas in Their New AB 110S Yacht
summary: Italian shipyard AB Yachts unveils its sportiest model yet, the AB 110S, laden with innovative retractable technology and featuring collaborations with leading automotive industry design experts.
body: Italian luxury yacht builder, AB Yachts, part of Next Yacht Group, has just added another feather in its cap with the introduction of a new sporty model, AB 110S. This 33.7-metre model is a testament to cross-sector design collaboration, as it marks the brand's first partnership with automotive design specialist, EXE Design.

Taking inspiration from the automotive industry, the AB 110S isn't just a regular yacht. It stands out with a raked-back windshield and a narrow, lightweight profile that screams speed and sophistication. It also features dual decks and a flybridge, providing ample space for guests.

The main deck also exudes charm with an inviting cockpit sunbathing area and a tastefully designed bar unit that caters to both the yacht's interior and exterior. The bow also houses a 'flying couch', a raised, wrap-around sofa that offers panoramic sea views.
Not to be outdone by the glowing exterior features, the accommodation is for up to 10 guests in its four staterooms, all found on the lower deck.

In line with its sporty appeal, the AB 110S, powered by three MAN V12X-2200 engines, can reach a heart-racing speed of 48 knots, while ensuring a noise-free journey thanks to its total engine room soundproofing.

This launch reveals the ambition of AB Yachts to push the boundaries of design and technology. With nine yacht projects on order or under construction, this behemoth of the yachting industry proves its place at the forefront of innovative luxury yacht design.

title: Cowes Yacht Heaven
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Cowes Yacht Heaven
summary: Nestled in the heart of Cowes on the Isle of Wight, is a premier marina renowned as a hub for the sailing world. Offering 260 fully-serviced berths, it provides free Wi-Fi, on-site engineers, and a 50-ton hoist for lifting and launching boats, catering to both visiting yachts and local craft. A short walk from Cowes’ vibrant high street, it’s perfect for exploring pubs, shops, and the historic Royal Yacht Squadron. H
body: Nestled in the heart of Cowes on the Isle of Wight, is a premier marina renowned as a hub for the sailing world. Offering 260 fully-serviced berths, it provides free Wi-Fi, on-site engineers, and a 50-ton hoist for lifting and launching boats, catering to both visiting yachts and local craft. A short walk from Cowes’ vibrant high street, it’s perfect for exploring pubs, shops, and the historic Royal Yacht Squadron. Hosting major regattas like Cowes Week, it transforms into a bustling centre of entertainment with bars and events. Accessible at all tides, it’s a top destination for sailors year-round.

title: The Bayesian Tragedy: Seeking Answers and Ensuring Safety in Yachting
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Bayesian Tragedy: Seeking Answers and Ensuring Safety in Yachting
summary: The salvage of the wrecked yacht Bayesian off the Sicilian coast resurrects haunting questions about safety in the marine sector.
body: The silhouette of the sunken yacht Bayesian finally broke the surface off Porticello, Sicily, a sight made all the more tragic by the loss of lives it represents. It was an uncomfortable reminder of the unknowns that loom large in the marine industry. The Bayesian accident brought to light the hard truths of professional sailing. Even though she was managed and crewed by trained professionals, powerful in size at 60 meters, and equipped with stability documentation, she capsized - causing the loss of seven lives.

The sinking gained worldwide attention, resulting in a whirlpool of speculation, blame, and misinformation. It took the interim report from the Marine Accident Investigation Branch to provide a comprehensive picture of what transpired. The report pointed out operational and systematic failures that might have contributed to the tragedy, suggesting that the accident might have been prevented.

The Bayesian tragedy serves as a stark reminder of the need to continually evaluate and enhance safety protocols in the yachting world. It demonstrated the need for more transparency and a deeper understanding of maritime incidents. A unanimous question echoes in the aftermath - How can we prevent this from happening again? The Bayesian incident demands introspection and action from the marine industry to ensure the joy of sailing remains untainted by such heartbreaking tragedies.

title: Explore the XIMENA Yacht: A Fusion of Superior Technology, Sleek Design and Elite Comfort
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Explore the XIMENA Yacht: A Fusion of Superior Technology, Sleek Design and Elite Comfort
summary: Uncover the allure of the XIMENA, a luxury motor yacht boasting revolutionary engineering, award-winning design, and bespoke interiors.
body: Regarded for its exquisite design, robust performance, and state-of-the-art specifications, the luxury motor yacht XIMENA emerges as a true marvel in the yachting world. The exterior design stands as a testament to the talent and proficiency of Omega Architects, a multi-award-winning design team known for its stunning output. Furthermore, the yacht boasts a Van Oosanen-engineered Fast Displacement hull, a proof of XIMENA's focus on unrivalled performance at sea. At the helm, the yacht easily achieves a top speed of 22 knots and demonstrates an impressive range of 3,200 nautical miles cruising efficiently at 12 knots.

Making its mark with not just brilliant exterior design, the motor yacht's interiors equally stun, owing to Yodezeen's award-winning design. The aesthetic appeal is paired with functionality as seen in the layout that includes five elegant guest cabins. An added highlight of the yacht is its gym, offering a robust workout experience with a captivating view through full glass sliding doors. Designed diligently to accommodate ten guests with a master room, two double rooms, and two twin rooms, XIMENA embodies the pinnacle of luxury yachting.

title: A First Look at the Marex 390: Ample Spaces Encased in Expansive Windows
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A First Look at the Marex 390: Ample Spaces Encased in Expansive Windows
summary: Marex reveals the intricate details of its innovative beauty, the new Marex 390, focusing on expansive windows to illuminate the luxurious interior.
body: Marex has astounded the boating aficionados by unveiling the details of its latest sensation, the Marex 390. Positioned strategically between the much-admired 375 and 440 models, the 390 is a slight contradiction. While its length is a tad shorter than the 375, an increment of 6 inches in the beam and 9 inches in the height above water level make it a substantially larger alternative.

The essence of the 390 lies in the magnificently designed hull. Along with the heightened size, it has also gained an estimated weight of 2-3 tonnes. The result? An astonishingly larger vessel with an enhanced interior volume providing the ultimate luxury at sea. The added comforts ranging from expansive spaces to hatch designs do not compromise the practicality of the design.

As always, Marex has given particular prominence to practicality. The large bench lockers double up as aft-facing seating proving as a handy storage space for lines, fenders, and water toys. The cockpit can be seamlessly opened or closed thanks to Marex's signature sliding side curtains. The large retracting fabric sunroof overhead is sure to add a classy touch.

Traveling in groups won't compromise on the luxury either as bench seating on all sides will comfortably accommodate up to eight people. The layout allows unrestricted access to the saloon and the galley without affecting the ample dining space. The walkaround decks provide easy access from the bathing platform to the foredeck. A must-have feature for sunbathers is the adjustable backrests accompanied by the removable floating mattress.

The Marex 390 strikes a balance between luxury and practicality. The boat builder has not shied away from utilising the full potential of their design creativity. The cabins are well lit due to the elongated hull windows and contain plenty of storage options. Power choices range widely, starting from a single 480hp Volvo Penta D6 to twin 320hp D4s or 380hp D6s.

In conclusion, the new Marex 390 is a testament to Marex's commitment to innovate and enhance, offering boating enthusiasts a rewarding sailing experience. We're already eagerly waiting to get our hands on the wheel of this unique marvel.

title: The 2025 Squib Nationals Take Off at Torbay - Brace Yourselves for Ups, Downs, and Wins!
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The 2025 Squib Nationals Take Off at Torbay - Brace Yourselves for Ups, Downs, and Wins!
summary: The adrenaline-fuelled start to the Squib National Championship 2025 sees competitors facing severe wind shifts and teasing victories.
body: The buzz of anticipation filled the air as 46 Squibs launched on Day 1 of the Squib National Championship 2025, hosted by the prestigious Royal Torbay Yacht Club. The first day's racing kicked off with a Practice Race, followed by a tense Points Race, setting the thrilling stage of what's to come.

Competing in challenging conditions with cunning wind shifts of up to 40 degrees and erratic wind strength varying from 6 to 16 knots, the navigational prowess was put to the test. During the one-lap Practice Race, Richard Smith and Graham Reeve sealed the first victory with 'Flame', followed closely by 'Cariad Bach' helmed by Nick Whipp and James Budd. Rounding out the top trio was 'Atlanta', skippered by Nick Milton and Gavin Kemp.

Jack Grogan and Mike Banks sailing via 'Budgies Tongue' took an early lead at the windward mark, closely trailed by Nick Whipp. Last year's champions, Micky Wright and Alex Porteous, sailing 'Spoof' from RCYC held their positions at fifth. Despite a near-capsize scare, 'Budgies Tongue' held on to win the four-lap race.
As the fleet adjusts and strategizes against the unpredictable conditions, one must stay tuned for more dramatic turns and unexpected victories at the Squib National Championship 2025.

title: An Insightful Dive into Gulf Craft Under the Leadership of Chairman Mohammed Hussein Alshaali

title: Olympic Class Sailing in the Spotlight at 40th Hamilton Island Race Week
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Olympic Class Sailing in the Spotlight at 40th Hamilton Island Race Week
summary: The annual Hamilton Island Race Week celebration, entering its 40th year, introduces an exciting line-up of world-class Olympic sailors.
body: Nestled in the heart of the dazzling Whitsunday Islands, Hamilton Island Race Week readies for its 40th anniversary celebrations. This year, the annual carnival of sails is slated for 16-23 August, promising a spectacular weeklong feast of maritime competition and camaraderie. This year's spotlight shines on the Olympic class match racing, with teams from Australia and New Zealand firing up for a three-day exhibition series. New Zealand's men's 49er and Women's 49erFX teams will compete in earnest against their Australian counterparts. This Trans-Tasman clash, fondly known as the 'Wetisloe Cup', will take place from 17-19 August, seeing a total of 13 skiff teams duel on the adrenalin-filled waterways. The Palm Beach Motor Yachts Trans-Tasman 49er Series will be daily at the iconic Hamilton Island Yacht Club. Racing is scheduled for the afternoons, offering spectators a thrilling front-row seat as 49ers grace the water after the conclusion of the main fleet's schedule. As Brisbane prepares to host the 2032 Olympics, this event provides a golden opportunity to showcase Olympic class sailors at their best. Hamilton Island hopes to entice more people to the sport of high-performance sailing and offer a glimpse into the potential for Brisbane 2032's sailing venue. The Australian team, featuring Olympians Evie Haseldine and Shaun Connor, as well as Women's America's Cup sailors Laura Harding and Annie Wilmot, is enthusiastic about the chance to compete at one of the world's most iconic sailing locations. In front of a passionate sailing crowd, they'll display their skills and a day of camaraderie on the water. This Trans-Tasman sailing event is already creating waves of excitement. Yachting New Zealand High Performance Director, Ian Stewart, hails this as an initiative that showcases both the strength and depth of the Australian and New Zealand 49er fleets. A shared sentiment that the spectacular Hamilton Island provides perfect momentum towards the Brisbane 2032 Olympics. Meanwhile, New Zealand's top 49er duo, Isaac McHardie and William McKenzie, who boast a silver medal from the Paris 2024 Olympics, are gearing up to join their Kiwi crew at Hamilton Island. Elsewhere, activities such as the 'Speed and Tricks' wing foil afternoon on 16 August assure an action-packed outing with challenges like the fastest run, longest air, and highest jump.

title: Experience Openness at Sea: Nauta Design's New Wave in Luxury Yachting
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Experience Openness at Sea: Nauta Design's New Wave in Luxury Yachting
summary: Nauta Design has introduced a groundbreaking 75.1-metre superyacht concept, Project Velor, revolutionising seafaring and the luxury boat experience with its innovative design and functionality.
body: The titans of marine innovation at Nauta Design in Italy have ushered in a new era of seafaring elegance with their 75.1-meter superyacht concept: Project Velor. The streamlined four-deck structure, developed in collaboration with naval architect Francesco Rogantin of Studio Names, manages to encapsulate the comfort and functionality of a five-deck layout owing to its ingeniously utilised space.

Project Velor is a resplendent synthesis of clean horizontal lines, balanced organic and geometric forms – the epitome of Nauta's signature aesthetic. Prioritising functionality with a contemporary exterior profile, the project is a testament to future-proof yachting, centered on flexibility, liveability, and tasteful elegance.

Project Velor seeks to foster a strong connection with the sea. Its design philosophy emphasizes openness and flow between interior and exterior spaces, and this is realised in features like expansive decks, transparent platforms, and tiered architectural staircases which foster uninterrupted vistas.

Particularly impressive is the open-air beach club, or 'water patio'- a space designed for versatility with fold-out platforms and retractable glass doors. This area is transformed into a year-round lounge that flows seamlessly into a spa and wellness zone, making it perfect for any season. The ship also offers a sundae deck equipped for relaxation and recreation, featuring a children's nest, a pool, and designated areas for sunbathing or stargazing.

With a beam of 13 meters and a draft of 3.5 meters, Project Velor gets its immense power from a diesel-electric propulsion system comprising four generators. Clearly, this superyacht is not only paving the way for future sailing experiences but is also setting a high standard for upcoming creations in the superyacht industry.

title: Emerging Eco-Friendly Yachting Trends: Port Vauban Debuts Liquid Hydrogen Bunkering for Superyachts

body: In an era of renewed focus on climate action, the yachting industry is no exception to the rule. Embarking on an innovative environmental venture, Port Vauban, based in Antibes, France, is pioneering the use of liquid hydrogen (LH2) bunkering for luxury superyachts.

In a significant demonstration of its trailblazing refueling process, the port carried out the successful refuelling of the impressive 119-metre Feadship yacht Breakthrough. The arrival of the yacht, reported by BOATPro, marked a success for the integration of cleaner energy sources within industry operations.

In the grand milieu of yachting, the action of Port Vauban implies a future where luxury does not compromise the health of our oceans. As superyachts sail across global waters, they can now do so with a considerable reduction in carbon footprint, thanks to liquid hydrogen bunkering. This shift correlates closely with the global emphasis on sustainable living and the preservation of our natural worlds.

In summary, the introduction of liquid hydrogen bunkering at Port Vauban is more than just a new service. It is a testament to the willpower of the marine industry to adapt, innovate, and commit to a greener future. As we sail towards this horizon, we can expect a wave of similar eco-innovations in the future.

title: Assessing Salary and Benefits in the Yachting Industry: A Balanced Discussion on Compensation,Training and Retention
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Assessing Salary and Benefits in the Yachting Industry: A Balanced Discussion on Compensation,Training and Retention
summary: In the glamorous world of the yachting industry, a continuous tug of war regarding salary, benefits, and training is taking place behind the scenes.
body: Promoted by a LinkedIn post on the Human Capital Superyacht Sausage Factory, a comprehensive survey has been conducted, gathering insightful thoughts from crew members, captains, yacht managers, and recruitment professionals. The purpose was to gain industry-wide insights on rather elusive subjects such as salaries, benefits, training, and retention in the yachting industry. Unlike conventional business sectors, a compelling debate seems to linger around the adequacy or stagnation of crew salaries in this niche industry. While some are convinced that crew members are satisfactorily compensated, others highlight decades of unchanged entry-level pay despite the scale and complexity of operations increasing. They argue for improved financial incentives and believe that remuneration should reflect experience, leadership commitments, and actual responsibilities. Benefits, or the perceived lack thereof, are also a cornerstone of the controversy. Although health cover, pensions, structured time off, and mental health support are highlighted as areas for improvement, some yachts stand out, offering training budgets, rest days, global medical cover and even family-inclusive health plans. Nonetheless, majority participants agree that these are yet to become the industry norm. The training cost burden is another topic of heated discussion. While crew members generally bear the brunt of the expense in the early stages, anecdotal evidence suggests that owner-paid training fosters long-term loyalty. However, the consensus is that such supportive gestures are often undervalued. Alternate views suggest staggered reimbursements over time, structured training pathways, and bonus-linked development plans as preferred models. These findings underscore the complexity of compensation dynamics in the yachting industry, challenging the known narratives and paving the way for constructive dialogue and revolutionized practices.

title: Thrilling Encounters at the RS600 Rooster National Tour at Warsash; Sailors Deliver Remarkable Performances
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Thrilling Encounters at the RS600 Rooster National Tour at Warsash; Sailors Deliver Remarkable Performances
summary: Sailors of the RS600 fleet journeyed south and ignited the seas at the Warsash Sailing Club in an exciting regatta event.
body: The stage was set at the Warsash Sailing Club as the esteemed RS600 fleet sailed south for the first coastal event of the year. Fierce competition was laid bare even before the boats were afloat – a sudden surge in delayed traffic seemed to be the first daunting challenge. Will Russell experienced the brunt of the snarl-up, arriving late by a staggering 90 minutes. But the tide turned as the spirits in the RS600 fleet remained high – an extraordinary display of solidarity and efficiency was demonstrated when his boat was rigged in under 10 minutes.

The second race also did not lack in action. The tide started to slacken and a shift in its direction made unpredictable conditions towards the end of the race. This ignited a renewed vigor among the participants who then resumed the race with a defensive strategy. George Smith and Will Russell, who were leading at the time, embarked on their own course. As the tide turned, the rest of the fleet observed the shift and reclosed the gap, creating an engaging and dynamic race environment.

title: Under Arrest and Under Management: The Royal Romance Superyacht Shifts to Croatia for Essential Maintenance
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Under Arrest and Under Management: The Royal Romance Superyacht Shifts to Croatia for Essential Maintenance
summary: The seized superyacht, Royal Romance, is preparing for a voyage to Trogir, Croatia, all for mandatory technical maintenance.
body: In the world of grand seafaring vehicles, few vessels capture the imagination quite like a superyacht. One such floating spectacle, the 92.5-meter yacht named 'Royal Romance', seized in the maritime nation of Croatia in 2022, is set to make a temporary voyage to the historically rich port of Trogir. The purpose? Mandatory technical maintenance to ensure the vessel remains in peak condition. The impressive move was officially announced on 16 June by Ukraine's National Asset Recovery and Management Agency (ARMA), the authoritative entity that oversees the yacht's current disposition.

Once the Royal Romance is back in Split, ARMA plans to consult with the Prosecutor General's Office. The intention is to resurrect efforts to sell the valuable asset under Ukrainian law, as clearly outlined in an official statement by the agency. The statement also reiterated that the yacht's custody arrangement and its maintenance at a military facility will remain consistent. The message was straightforward - despite its change of scenery, the Royal Romance continues to remain 'under arrest and under the management of ARMA'.

title: Diving into the World of Boat Clubs: More Pleasure, Less Hassle for Boating Enthusiasts
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Diving into the World of Boat Clubs: More Pleasure, Less Hassle for Boating Enthusiasts
summary: Exploring a growing trend in the boating world: subscription-based boat clubs offering hassle-free sailing experiences to a growing legion of nautical enthusiasts.
body: There are several pearls of wisdom that suggest caution when dealing with things that fly or float, including the suggestion to rent rather than buy. But for the modern-day sailing enthusiast, there's a new choice emerging that brings a twist to the 'ownership versus rental' argument: subscription-based boat clubs. The rising popularity of these clubs indicates a trend where participation trumps possession. These clubs offer members easy access to a diverse fleet of boats without the burdens of ownership or rental, making this an optimal option in many boating enthusiasts' eyes. The premise is quite simple, you pay an annual or monthly subscription fee and gain access to a shared fleet of boats. Typically, these vessels are not just random, dated boats left to crumble in forgotten marinas, but thye are modern, well-maintained, and often nearly new boats based in convenient locations. Moreover, these boats are cleaned, fuelled and ready to set sail whenever a member needs them. Boat clubs also eliminate the financial risk and time-consuming chores associated with boat ownership. Making a large capital investment to purchase a boat and subsequent costs for berthing, insurance, maintenance, servicing and then potentially selling the boat are all taken care of by the club. Members are liberated to simply pay for fuel and embark on their sailing adventures. This contemporary boating avenue is especially appealing to the newer generations - Gen Zs and Millennials - who traditionally do not hold ownership close to their hearts. It has, however, also garnered interest from more mature boating enthusiasts who enjoy having a variety of boats to choose from, each offering a unique boating experience. Adding to the appeal, many boat clubs organise club social events, training courses and group cruises, all of which enhance the sense of community amongst the members. With sustainability becoming a global priority, shared boat usage makes a strong case for being an eco-friendlier choice. After all, who wouldn't love to boast about their eco-conscious boating decisions? Clearly, subscription-based boat clubs have managed to ride the current and are offering a winning proposition to a wide range of boating enthusiasts.

title: Unyielding Spirit Triumphs: A Solo Circumnavigation of the British Isles by a Charismatic Young Sailor
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unyielding Spirit Triumphs: A Solo Circumnavigation of the British Isles by a Charismatic Young Sailor
summary: Jazz Turner is making waves as she sails solo around the British Isles in a remarkable charity endeavor.
body: It's not every day a tale unfolds that combines wonder, bravery, and determination. This story revolves around the young and intrepid sailor, Jazz Turner, who is currently accomplishing the extraordinary feat of circumnavigating the British Isles single-handedly. Beyond the legacy of flaunting her navigation skills, Jazz's voyage seeks to shed light on the unexplored freedom and joy of sailing for those with disabilities.

This incredibly daring challenge is undertaken by Jazz not for her personal glory, but to raise funds for Sailability, a charity she holds dear. Her goal? To equip the charity with more boats and encourage more people to experience the exhilaration of being one with the sea. And her endeavors are bearing fruit - her voyage has so far raised an inspiring £35,883, and she isn't even finished yet!

Despite it all, some lighter moments grace Jazz's voyage. Like the joyous relief of washing her hair for the first time in 18 days, punctuated with an amusing anecdote of having to deal with an accidental gybe mid-shampoo! Though, as Jazz candidly admits, sailing brings its fair share of physical and mental exhaustion, with constant monitoring of sails, weather, and navigation.

As Jazz continues her brave journey, let's rally behind her and bring light to her cause. The more support Jazz receives, the more she can contribute towards her noble cause. Her voyage promises to represent a beacon of hope and resilience, and a beautiful exposition of the joy of sailing.

Amid thrilling waves and challenging times, Jazz Turner's story serves as a testament to formidable will and irrepressible spirit. Her journey is a reminder of the rewards that lie in overcoming challenges and venturing beyond our comfort zones.

title: Malizia Explorer: The Gripping Tale of a Private Yacht's Journey to Becoming a Sea-Loving Scientist
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Malizia Explorer: The Gripping Tale of a Private Yacht's Journey to Becoming a Sea-Loving Scientist
summary: One impeccable yacht's story of transformation - evolving from a high-end private vessel into an awe-inspiring climate research ship, the Malizia Explorer.
body: From private luxury to purposeful exploration, the transformation of the 26-metre Garcia-built private yacht into the Malizia Explorer, a futuristic climate research vessel, sets a new bar in yacht conversion. Celebrated at Yacht Club de Monaco after a comprehensive refit in Lorient, France, this aluminium yacht embraces its new calling with fervour. Now the flagbearer of Team Malizia, the intrepid sailing initiative, Malizia Explorer signifies a shift from thrilling ocean racing to groundbreaking climate research and observation.

Originally a private exploration yacht known as 'Beniguet', Malizia Explorer has successfully pivot while maintaining its sailing heritage. Now, it serves as a front-line platform for climate study, deploying advanced technologies that prioritize environmental sustainability. Its transition raised eyebrows in 2024 when the vessel was sold, marking the first steps towards its exciting new purpose.

The Malizia Explorer, now a beacon of hope and action. It embodies the commitment to lead change and protect our oceans. Alone, hope is impractical. By harnessing the combined powers of dedicated scientists and sailing enthusiasts, Malizia Explorer ensures that aspiring words get translated into impactful actions.

Selected for her sturdy aluminium hull, substantial volume, and range, Malizia Explorer now ventures on far-reaching expeditions fitted with an oceanic laboratory. Conducting continuous data collection on salinity, temperature, oxygen, and CO2 levels, the ship is also slated to include a CTD Rosette for deep water analysis. The vessel sails with the wind of responsibility, representing climate science in some of the most secluded ocean regions across the globe.

Dr. Sylvia Earle's christening of the Malizia Explorer in Monaco marks a major watershed moment, opening up a new chapter of unity and exploration. Steering away from personal luxury, this sea creature now swims with a noble purpose - to explore, understand, and protect the often-misunderstood marine environment.

title: New jewel in the sea: Hargrave Superyachts introduces the state-of-the-art Hargrave 125 at Turkish launch
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: New jewel in the sea: Hargrave Superyachts introduces the state-of-the-art Hargrave 125 at Turkish launch
summary: Iconic yacht builder Hargrave Superyachts recently marked another milestone with the launch of the Hargrave 125, a stunning tri-deck yacht, from Antalya, Turkey.
body: Hargrave Superyachts, the esteemed division of Hargrave Custom Yachts, has proudly announced the launch of the 38-metre Hargrave 125 superyacht at its shipyard in Antalya, Turkey. Known as Project 125, the striking tri-deck yacht is a notable addition to HSY Yachts' growing custom superyacht portfolio and is slated for a grand showcase at the 2025 Cannes Yachting Festival.

Boasting a generous beam of 7.92 metres and a draught of 1.95 metres, the Hargrave 125 has been explicitly designed for easy manoeuvring through the shallow waters of the Bahamas. The yacht features a specially engineered displacement hull for long-range cruising, providing steadfast and reliable performance even in adverse weather conditions. The on-board rest and underway stabilisation ensure optimal comfort for all aboard.

Power for the Hargrave 125 comes from two main engines; Caterpillar C32, coupled with two 75kW Caterpillar generators to deliver a solid cruising speed of 17 knots. She is supported by an ASEA power converter for global shore power compatibility. Furthermore, Hargrave stands behind its latest sea jewel with a generous 10-year structural warranty and a similar Platinum Warranty on her main engines and generators.

New owners will also enjoy a full yacht management package for the first six months of ownership. Currently available for inspection and sale, the Hargrave 125 is expected to attract considerable attention from both charter-focused buyers and private cruising enthusiasts.
