Indeed, the Benetti Oasis 34 motor yacht Y epitomizes the perfect blend of performance, luxury, and sea travel adventure that awaits its maiden voyage with its new owner.

title: Young Sailors Battle the Elements at the ILCA 4 Youth European Championships 2025 in Poland
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Young Sailors Battle the Elements at the ILCA 4 Youth European Championships 2025 in Poland
summary: Puck, Poland, becomes the playground for 440 determined young sailors, competing in the 2025 ILCA 4 Youth European Championships.
body: As the first foremost sail kissing the sky and the initial boat skipping across the water at the break of day, the air was thick with anticipation. Young sailors from 41 countries gathered in Puck, Poland, where the water beckoned 440 participants of the 2025 ILCA 4 Youth European Championships. A magnificent sight unfolded as rigging rattled, sails flapped, and hearts pounded at the beginning of the Day 2 races. The gusty winds with an average speed of 14 knots provided an exciting challenge. It was indeed a depiction of the sheer perseverance needed in the face of changing weather conditions. After two riveting races, everyone from the seven fleets returned to shore, their energy abating with the set of the sun, leaving them eager for the battles of the next day.

Day 3 of the Championships paid homage to the strength, strategy and heroic hearts of the young sailors. Despite the light winds of around 5 knots, the boys' first fleet commenced without delay. The fluctuating conditions in the girls' course led to a slight delay, symbolising a true test of patience and resilience. The light breeze, sunny skies and flat water set the tone for the day's competition, with everyone giving their best.

The Championships, organised by the Polish ILCA Class Association Team and co-financed by the Ministry of Sport and Tourism, served not just as a battleground but as a stage that unified young sailors globally. Puck, Poland, was more than just a host. It was a witness to burning passions, tremendous endurance and a showcase of future sailing stars.

title: Experience the Premiere Cannes-Malta Race: Where Cinema Meets Sailing
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Experience the Premiere Cannes-Malta Race: Where Cinema Meets Sailing
summary: Immerse yourself in the thrills of the first-ever exciting Cannes-Malta Race, a remarkable merger between prestigious sailing clubs and fascinating Mediterranean landscapes.
body: Excitement is in the air as the first-ever Cannes-Malta Race prepares to kick off. The product of a successful collaboration established last year between two distinguished sailing entities: The Yacht Club de Cannes (1860) led by Jean-François Cutugno, and the Royal Malta Yacht Club (1835) under the leadership of Mark Napier.
These esteemed institutions have teamed up to launch the inaugural Cannes-Malta Race, an offshore extravaganza in the Mediterranean set to commence in the glamorous city of Cannes on 8 October.

Fashioned along the lines of renowned races like the Fastnet, the Sydney-Hobart, the Paprec 600 Saint-Tropez and the Middle Sea Race, this event tests sailors over 600 miles (or 1100 kilometres) of azure sea.

The race's strategic charm lies in the fleet's need to explore the Strait of Bonifacio, south of Corsica, while leaving Sardinia and Sicily to the side, and navigating three gates before sprinting to the finish line in Valletta, the beautiful capital of the island of Malta.

At its core, this event aims to strengthen the bond between Malta, Cannes, the Côte d'Azur and all sailors at sea, while simultaneously enticing sailors to experience the enchanting off-season allure of Malta. Spearheaded by the bout of excitement and anticipation from Claude Zammit-Trevisan, the Director France of the Malta Tourist Board, this event promises to be a historic spectacle.

Participants are eagerly anticipating the inaugural Cannes-Malta Race, which also serves as a precursor to the Rolex Middle Sea Race. This also showcases the breath-taking sights of Sicily through the iconic Strait of Messina.

The Cannes-Malta Race is eagerly awaited and attended by Jérôme Nutte of the Yacht Club de Cannes, a well-respected figure in the racing community and a constant presence at the Olympic sailing events.

With three doors to monitor the boats, there's an ongoing buzz of anticipation among the sailors who are eagerly looking forward to this event. While the number of participants is not expected to break records, the thrill of unknown elements in a first-time event is creating much excitement.
When the first cannon fires on October 8th at the harbor of Cannes, history will be made, setting a precedent for future races.

title: Unveiling the Grandeur of Maximus III: 37 meters of Custom-Fitted Superyacht Luxury Ready for Sea Trials

Conceived with precision and a remarkable eye for detail by Canadian designer Gregory C. Marshall, the custom aluminium superyacht is a testament to the exceptional craftsmanship of the Canadian yard's Vancouver facility, further consolidating Canada's burgeoning reputation in the luxury superyacht sector.

This triple-deck spectacle is the outcome of a fruitful synergy between Marshall and a seasoned owner, who collaborated closely to create a yacht that perfectly echoes their opulent West Coast lifestyle. The yacht, which will make its home on the West Coast with a Californian owner post-delivery, features a substantial fishing cockpit at the aft – a nod to a preferred pastime.

Maximus III is not just a seafaring vessel, but also a social hub with an abundance of shared spaces. The California-style galley offers a convivial dining settee or a stone countertop setting for casual interactions. For guests desiring a breath of fresh sea air, the top deck furnishes a large sit-up bar, a spacious dining table, and a Jacuzzi complemented by a sun pad.

The interior aesthetic combines light woods, white onyx and off-white leather fabrics, sumptuously interspersed throughout the vessel. Additionally, the hull's base is surrounded by twenty-three underwater lights, illuminating the yacht's grandeur even further.

Upon delivery, Maximus III is prepared to be the star of yacht charters on the West Coast during the summer season, which includes a journey to the Pacific Northwest and Alaska. Embrace the adventure and explore the scenic treasures of the West Coast aboard this grandiose, superbly-appointed superyacht.

title: World-class Fleet Embarks on Thrilling Journey as the 2025 IMOCA Globe Series Championship Commences
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: World-class Fleet Embarks on Thrilling Journey as the 2025 IMOCA Globe Series Championship Commences
summary: Top-notch sailing teams are aligning their compasses for the start of the captivating Course des Caps, marking the beginning of the 2025 IMOCA Globe Series Championship.
body: Excitement is in the air as the 2025 IMOCA Globe Series Championship is set to begin this weekend, marking the very first step in the quadrennial journey to the 2028 Vendée Globe. The curtain raiser is no less than the enthralling Course des Caps, a non-stop sprint that sets the sailing enthusiasts off from Boulogne-sur-Mer, Pas-de-Calais on June 29th, and then circumnavigates the British Isles via the northern tip of the Shetland Islands.

Participating in such a significant event is a prestigious fleet comprising 11 IMOCAs, all helmed by a group of four sailing maestros, including at least one female sailor in each team. An Onboard Reporter, or OBR, is also onboard each IMOCA, responsible for documenting and broadcasting the thrilling narratives of their adventures.

The Course des Caps is renowned as one of the classic racetracks in world sailing, presenting a formidable 2,000-nautical mile challenge. With fluctuating coastal weather, headlands, and tidal gates for sailors and navigators to tackle, the route is perpetually engaging. The North Sea adds a daunting aspect to the competition, with oil and gas rigs, wind farms, commercial shipping traffic and exclusion zones at key headlands complicating pathways.

Brittany-based British sailor Sam Goodchild is making his debut as skipper on a fully crewed IMOCA during this race, taking over the Verdier-designed MACIF Santé Prévoyance from Vendée Globe winner Charlie Dalin who is presently on a health leave. Goodchild shares that what makes this race exhilarating is the ceaseless encounter of challenges be it tides, shifting winds or the course going over 60 degrees North.

In another notable story, Sam Davies is leading a team on Initiatives-Coeur that involves the emerging French star Violette Dorange. Davies, who has raced multiple times on this track and holds the record for a female crew when she led Team SCA in 2014, warns of heightened difficulties as the North Sea sees continuous wind farm construction.

title: High-End Yacht, Royal Romance, Relocated Amid Pivotal Legal Reforms in Ukraine
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: High-End Yacht, Royal Romance, Relocated Amid Pivotal Legal Reforms in Ukraine
summary: In conjunction with its active legal modifications, Ukraine has temporary relocated the multimillion-dollar yacht, Royal Romance, for maintenance, under stringent protection.
body: Ukraine's push to revamp its asset recovery program has led to the temporary relocation of the infamous Royal Romance yacht under armed escort for maintenance. This move is a part of Ukraine's progressive efforts to update and solidify its legal framework to effectively handle, and in due time, liquidate seized assets, despite certain persisting judicial hurdles. The 92.5-metre vessel, associated with Ukraine's sanctioned oligarch and pro-Russian politician, Viktor Medvedchuk, was moved from its mooring place at the naval base in Split, Croatia, to a shipyard in Trogir under the combined patrol of Croatian police and private security. The Ukrainian Asset Recovery and Management Agency (ARMA) has confirmed this repositioning. Soon after the completion of maintenance, the yacht is expected to return to Split and stay under arrest. ARMA is set to appeal to the Office of the Prosecutor General to commence the next stage of the asset realisation process under the current laws once the yacht is back in Split. Royal Romance's transfer reflects Kyiv’s all-encompassing endeavour to resurrect its asset recovery program amidst the growing discontent regarding the legal stagnation surrounding the yacht's final destiny. Medvedchuk, a former Member of Parliament and a close associate of Putin, dodged house arrest in February 2022 but was recaptured in April and handed to Russia in a prisoner exchange. He continues to face international sanctions imposed by Ukraine, EU, and the US. The yacht's relocation comes after formidable legal changes enacted by the Ukrainian parliament lately. The governing laws of ARMA have seen extensive amendments, broadening its authority further to oversee, monetise, and ultimately dispose off foreign-owned assets linked to Russia and Belarus. The reforms set explicit deadlines for prosecutors to transfer seized assets to ARMA, therefore facilitating a predictable legal framework for carrying out valuations, choosing external managers and readying assets for sale. The shift towards open public tenders via Ukraine's Prozorro procurement system for management appointments is intended to curtail the risk of non-transparent or politically-biased decisions. Coupled with full quarterly ARMA reports, an external audit mechanism, an independent public oversight council, and the establishment of a fund dedicated to directing the proceeds from sold assets into Ukraine’s reconstruction, these changes show a concerted effort to improve transparency and accountability. What the future holds regarding these matters is not clear yet. However, it can be deduced that Kyiv might target a swift offloading of the yacht. The cost of upkeeping the Royal Romance, which used to be covered personally by Medvedchuk until the vessel's seizure in 2022, has been taken up by the Ukrainian state via ARMA, reportedly amounting to more than €20 million annually. The expectation now is that the new legal framework will help offset these expenses with the proceeds from a potential sale.

title: Sail into Luxury with the 30.1m Aurora - Ferretti's Prized Motor Yacht Available for Purchase
author: Old Sea Dogs

summary: The 30.1-metre Ferretti motor yacht 'Aurora', with her sleek exteriors designed by Filippo Salvetti, has been listed for sale.
body: Sporting luxurious interiors and stunning exteriors, 'Aurora' - the 30.1 metre Ferretti Motor Yacht, is an epitome of elegance and sophistication on water. Designed by Filippo Salvetti, this elegant marine beauty was delivered in 2021. After undergoing a few name changes and finally stopping at 'Aurora', the yacht currently stands as a competitively priced asset, and is indeed, a delight for potential buyers looking for luxury and adventure combined.

Aurora's airy and contemporary interiors, a splendid creation of IdeaeITALIA, exudes refinement and grandeur. They feature panoramic windows and soft grey wood cabinetry, which are complemented by equally comfortable furnitures and navy and tan accents. A commodious main saloon seamlessly transitions to an elegant dining space that seats up to ten guests. Beyond this area, a middle deck fitted with loungers and the pathway to the beach club makes for an exquisite setting for relaxation.

The yacht's exteriors are no less impressive. There's an expansive flybridge and a spacious sundeck, offering scintillating views and plenty of space for entertaining. The direct access from stern to bow facilitated by the wrap-around side decks and the below sundeck comprising sun loungers and a spacious tender garage heightens its allure. With the comfort of guests in mind, Aurora comes fitted with dual stabilisation systems, ensuring ease while moving and anchoring. Powered by twin MTU M96L engines, the yacht cruises with ease at 24 knots and can reach top speeds of 27 knots.
With all the hallmarks of a perfect luxury getaway, 'Aurora' is uniquely positioned as a potential high-return investment for those looking to combine business with pleasure.

title: Heesen Celebrates the Grand Delivery of Their Largest Steel Superyacht 'Sparta'
author: Old Sea Dogs

summary: The 67-metre superyacht 'Sparta' by Heesen Yachts has been delivered to its owners, flaunting a sporty exterior and elemental-themed interiors.
body: Heesen Yachts, an esteemed brand in the yachting world, has successfully delivered their latest masterpiece, 'Sparta'. This 67-metre steel superyacht is the largest of its kind from the Heesen collection and stands as a testament to their dedication to innovation and design finesse.

'Sparta' boasts a sporty, low-profile exterior, courtesy of the British studio, Winch Design. The distinctive exterior features a sharp, reverse bow, underlining the yacht's seafaring prowess. This aspect is amplified by the contrasting hues of 'Venetian red' and metallic grey tones that adorn the yacht's sleek build.

The interiors of 'Sparta' hold a unique narrative. Winch Design has masterfully orchestrated an elemental theme throughout the yacht, with each deck embodying the qualities of earth, water, and air. This elemental harmony complements the owner's desire to cultivate an atmosphere of 'playfulness, activities and surprise'.

Heesen's 'Sparta' emphasizes the joys of togetherness and family living, manifested through an open-plan layout and shared spaces. Dual owner's suites, along with four additional cabins, comfortably accommodate a total of 12 guests and a crew of 15. Masterfully designed to represent the air element, the 56-square-metre master cabin presents a soothing sky-blue palette, punctuated by mother-of-pearl inlays and an abstract-patterned carpet.

The upper deck forward owner's cabin stands out even more, graced by abundant light from full-length windows, offering an unparalleled view of the seascape. Guests can enjoy the outdoor cinema screen or stargaze on the private owner's deck, truly immersing in the universe's grandeur. With dining chairs dressed in real palm leaf in the earth-themed main saloon and marine-themed VIP cabins, 'Sparta' truly offers a unique marine adventure tailored for luxury and comfort.

title: Introducing Bering’s Newest and Largest Powercat: A First Look at the BM50 SE
author: Old Sea Dogs

summary: Bering pushes frontiers with the launch of its largest multihull yet – the BM50 SE. A fusion of efficiency and practicality, this powercatamaran is reinventing expectations.
body: Bering is pushing boundaries with its latest creation – the Bering BM50 SE. This 50ft multihull stands as the jewel of Bering’s fleet, outstripping its siblings by 14ft and 20ft respectively.

Labelled as the Swift Explorer (SE), the BM50 SE brings together fluidity and practicality in one place. Its size provides ample space for comfortable living, while the reduced drag and enhanced efficiency of the hydrofoil make every voyage a pleasure. The manufacturer's projections, claiming a cruising range of 700 Nm at speeds of 25 to 35 knots and a peak speed of around 42 knots, paint a promising picture indeed.

Stepping inside, there's a peripheral galley opposite a diner with a raised cabinet. This carefully thought-out interior generates additional space for two bathrooms, while a raised bow deck means two forward cabins without reducing the bridge deck. The helm, positioned centrally on the deck, is complemented by an accommodating secondary helm on the flybridge with a nearby L-shaped diner.
In short, the Bering BM50 SE redefines boating by amalgamating efficiency, speed, and luxury, ensuring an unforgettable voyage every time you set sail.

title: Revolutionising Boating: Excellent Electric Outboard Motors Ushering in Zero-Emission Era
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Revolutionising Boating: Excellent Electric Outboard Motors Ushering in Zero-Emission Era
summary: With mounting environmental concerns, electric outboard motors are increasingly gaining traction. We examine an array of distinguished options on the market.
body: Innovation and sustainability are at the forefront of the boating industry, with electric outboard motors making significantly more appearances. Despite being in existence for some time, the past few years have seen a fresh batch of powerful and efficient models grace the market. These are not your everyday units; their capabilities range from energising a tender to propelling a 50-knot sportsboat. This advent of incredible technology is poised to alter the path towards a more sustainable future with all-electric boats. To help with your selection, we present a few standout models.

Next, we present the Mercury Avator 7.5e. As the first electric unit from the world's most considerable outboard engines builder, the Avator 7.5e introduced in early 2022, flaunts an easily removable battery and proclaimed remarkable range at 25% throttle.

The Remigo One, by a Slovenian company, boasts a smart design with the battery integrated into the shaft, reducing drag and enhancing steering power. Its features also include a waterproof casing and a two-year warranty, among others.

Lastly, the Thrustme Kicker, a lightweight Norwegian unit launched in 2021, excels in pushing one person from ship to shore and back, making it a perfect pick for those valuing weight and value over cruising range. These cutting-edge options point towards a future where one can enjoy a vibrant boating experience while leaving minimal environmental impact.

title: How to Blaze a Legal Trail in the Superyacht Community: Lessons from the Quarterdeck to the Courtroom
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: How to Blaze a Legal Trail in the Superyacht Community: Lessons from the Quarterdeck to the Courtroom
summary: In the world of commercial yachting, fine print matters. Yet, the implications often rock an owner’s balance sheet more than maritime hazards.
body: When you're signing on the dotted line of your next yacht contract, you might want to give those clauses another glance. Far from being "just boilerplate", these can resurface years later, turning gentle sea breezes into gales that could throw your balance sheet off course. Two landmark cases in recent years serve as timely reminders.

The English Commercial Court’s 2020 My Song ruling and the US Supreme Court’s 2024 decision in Great Lakes Insurance SE v. Raiders Retreat Realty, demonstrate why the superyacht community should not take the choice of law and choice of forum clauses lightly.

Turning high judicial drama into operational advantage requires understanding your contract from every angle. Ensure legal clauses are adequately scrutinized before signing and maintain clear evidence trails. My Song's case, for instance, involved sifting through WhatsApp messages and cradle-assembly photos, underlining the importance of keeping meticulous records over time.

Folks, every clause matters at sea, just like each drop in the vast ocean. These legal lessons ensure a smooth and prepared voyage, weathering the storms of maritime disputes and sailing towards a safe harbour.

title: ISA Yachts triumphs again with the sale of another Unica 45M Steel to a savvy European owner.

The exquisite design, intricately detailed by Enrico Gobbi’s Team for Design, bears the hallmark of ISA Yachts' naval architecture mastery. The Unica 45M Steel series boldly combines a robust steel hull with a lightweight aluminium superstructure, upping its game with an impressive fuel capacity of over 60,000 litres, enabling a transatlantic journey of 4,000 nautical miles effortlessly cruising at 10 knots. Characteristic of the Unica 45M Steel series is a uniquely slender silhouette. The yacht’s design bestows an opulent sunbathing space and an infinity cockpit encased in a glass balustrade, delivering uninterrupted sea views. A formal dining area, owner’s suite equipped with walk-in wardrobe, and the facility of an additional sixth cabin or office space further adorn the main deck. The sundeck – an astounding 16-metre outdoor paradise – accommodates a full array of al fresco living essentials: sun-pads, a bar, and a jacuzzi to name a few. Four additional guest cabins, as well as an accommodation for nine crew members, complete this floating mansion. Twin CAT C32 engines ensure a top speed of 15 knots and a cruising speed of 14 knots. The sale of the second Unica 45M Steel model catapults the count of ISA Yachts under construction to 11, diversifying their portfolio with models ranging from 40 to 80 meters. Their impressive projects include three 80-meter masterpieces and a newly announced Viper 120.

title: SailGP on its way to Sassnitz
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: SailGP heading to Sassnitz - Germany
summary: Hold onto your hats and tighten your lifejackets—SailGP is going to Germany for the very first time, and it promises to be an event for the ages. On August 16–17, the high-octane sailing series known for rewriting the rules of maritime racing will descend on the town of Sassnitz, nestled on the Baltic gem that is the island of Rügen. This isn’t your grandfather’s regatta—this is SailGP, where boats fly, and reputatio
body: For those unfamiliar, SailGP is the Formula One of the sea—only louder, faster, and wetter. Twelve national teams, helming identical F50 foiling catamarans, will be ripping across the waves at blistering speeds, often faster than the wind itself. It’s not just racing—it’s a full-blown aquatic spectacle. Think G-force turns, split-second tactics, and airborne hulls, all happening just metres off the shoreline.

But this stop on the 2025 Rolex SailGP calendar carries something extra: it’s home turf for Erik Heil and the Germany SailGP Team. For Heil—Olympian, thrill-seeker, and homegrown sailing hero—this is more than a race. It’s a coming-of-age for Germany on the world sailing stage, and Sassnitz will be flying the flag high.

Sassnitz and Rügen aren’t just names on a map—they’re places steeped in seafaring tradition. With its dramatic chalk cliffs and white-sand beaches, the coastline here offers a natural amphitheatre like no other. Fans won’t need binoculars or grandstand tickets to feel part of the action; the racecourse hugs the shore so tightly that the whoosh of foils and spray from the wakes will be impossible to miss. This is sailing, turned inside out—designed for spectators, made for adrenaline junkies.

The event marks the eighth leg of a global series that has already turned heads from Sydney to San Francisco, and now it’s Germany’s turn to play host to the world’s sailing elite. From seasoned skippers to daring young tacticians, each crew will be gunning for points as they charge toward the season finale. Mistakes will be punished, margins will be microscopic, and victory will be anything but easy.

For landlubbers and old seadogs alike, Sassnitz SailGP offers something irresistible—a unique blend of coastal charm and futuristic racing tech. And if you’ve never witnessed a catamaran flying above the water on carbon fibre wings, trust us: it’s the sort of sight that stays with you long after the race is run.

So whether you’re a Baltic local, a travelling yachtie, or just someone with salt in their blood, make your way to Sassnitz this August. Bring your camera, bring your earplugs—and bring your sense of awe.
The future of sailing is here, and it’s foiling fast !

title: Revel in the Massive Volume of the Cost-effective Cobra Campione 41 Fly: A Polish Marvel Redefining Yacht Value
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Revel in the Massive Volume of the Cost-effective Cobra Campione 41 Fly: A Polish Marvel Redefining Yacht Value
summary: Unraveling the mysteries of the Cobra Campione 41 Fly, a meticulously crafted vessel embodying extravagant volume in a remarkably budget-friendly package.
body: The lovechild of ingenious design and Polish craftsmanship, the Cobra Campione 41 Fly, paves new waters in the yacht industry by exceptionally tethering volume, quality, and cost-effectiveness. This marine marvel pours attractive specifications into a 42ft long boat, transforming space into an art form and challenging industry norms

Cobra Yachts, the renowned Polish builder, maximizes the generous volume of the Campione 41 Fly through inventive design. The vertical bow, full-beam saloon, and extended flybridge conjugate to offer impressive real estate onboard. A sensible upgrade in the engine power and inclusion of additional standard kit have led to a recent price rise. However, the base price incredibly holds at just over €360,000—marking a new high in value-for-money yacht offerings.

Access to truncated side decks is facilitated via two sliding doors adjacent to the helm and companionway entrance. They reach far enough back to hang midships fenders, providing easy access to the raised foredeck sunpad and anchor platform. The flybridge is truly a sight to behold, its tantalizing immensity as real as it appears, inviting the souls of water-lovers.

Below deck, two- and three-cabin layouts greet potential buyers. However, a lack of sophistication in design compared to more polished competitors starts to emerge here. The final price, complete with the two mightiest engines, comes close to rivals such as the Prestige F4.3. Still, it remains a cost-effective marine jewel reaffirming the age-old adage that size isn’t everything.

The groundbreaking Cobra Campione 41 Fly strikes marine enthusiasts with its enticing blend of volume, design, and cost-effectiveness. It is a testament that the beauty of the sea may indeed be captured and savored without draining one's purse, setting sail for new horizons in yacht value.

title: Unveiling the Best Boat Tubes of 2025: Exhilarating Journeys on the Water Await!
author: Old Sea Dogs

summary: Step into the world of thrilling watersports with the best boat tubes of 2025. Discover an unparalleled fun-filled experience with utmost comfort and versatility.

A perfect combination of thrill and skill, boat tubes provide a unique way of experiencing the magic of watersports. Unlike the more skills-intensive activities like wakeboarding and waterskiing, resorting to a boat tube equates to endless fun, irrespective of one's expertise level. And if the boat operator is seasoned enough, you're in for a secure as well as an exhilarating time.

Two-person boat tubes hold a great deal of appeal. Their size gives them a nippy and manageable feel, creating a delightful balance between fun and control. Alongside choosing an ideal boat tube, it's essential to read the safety instructions and consider the necessary accessories. However, you must also remember, due to the pendulum effect of the long tow rope, the tube is likely to speed up during turns, outpacing the boat.
Following the assessments, Boat tube 'Airhead Slice' emerged as the best option for beginners, 'Jobe Binar' aced the overall test, and 'O’Brien Sombrero' came out as the go-to choice for families.

For a beginner-friendly and stable riding experience, go for the 'Airhead Slice'. But do note its limited space might not work well for adults or for more experienced riders seeking a more thrilling ride. Alternatively, 'Jobe Binar' and 'O’Brien Sombrero' are also great options based on your specific needs.

In conclusion, picking up a boat tube for the high seas should be about matching the adventure quotient with just the right level of risk. Make sure to make a well-informed decision before hopping on board. With these tubes, your summer outings are bound to be unforgettable.

title: Charting the Course to Net-Zero: How Roadmap 2050 Paves the Way for a Sustainable Yachting Future
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Charting the Course to Net-Zero: How Roadmap 2050 Paves the Way for a Sustainable Yachting Future
summary: The Water Revolution Foundation sets sail towards a greener future with the unveiling of the game-changing Roadmap 2050, aimed at achieving net-zero emissions in yachting by 2050.
body: In a bold narrative of sustainable change, the Water Revolution Foundation has recently charted a course towards a greener future with the release of 'Roadmap 2050: Towards Regenerative Yachting'. This comprehensive plan aspires ambitious yet attainable goals aimed at achieving net-zero emissions within the yachting sector by 2050.

Developed through extensive collaboration and unique data exercise, this roadmap is widely embraced by the yachting community as a significant stride towards sustainability. It maps every stage of a yacht’s life cycle – from design and construction to operation and refit – and sets measurable, five-year targets. This represents a collective effort towards net-zero emissions, encompassing both product and processes.

The shift in focus towards implementing regenerative principles across the yachting value chain emerged prominently at this year's edition of the platform. Recognised environmental advocate Céline Cousteau's powerful keynote underscored the profound connection between humanity and the ocean, and emphasised the critical role the yachting industry can play in ocean conservation.

While the roadmap's ambitious targets surpass current regulatory thresholds, it remains largely voluntary and is aimed at sparking innovation, standardisation, and competition. Its sector-specific approach simplifies task allocation by setting priority targets for the four life-cycle stages. This strategy exhorts companies to go beyond 'wait and see' and seize the opportunity to transition towards net-zero emissions sooner rather than later.

This roadmap, developed with comprehensive data from designers, builders, operators and refit yards, marks the first step in a process that will become increasingly detailed with broader industry participation. It showcases the yachting industry's commitment to safeguarding the oceans, the very lifeblood of their operations, and underscores their role as proactive stewards of a sustainable future.

title: Experience the Uniting Force of the Sea at Rijeka's Vibrant Fiumanka Annual Race
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Experience the Uniting Force of the Sea at Rijeka's Vibrant Fiumanka Annual Race
summary: Rediscover the joys of sailing at the 26th annual Fiumanka Race, a celebration of seafaring traditions and communal unity in the picturesque city of Rijeka, Croatia.
body: For over 20 years, the Fiumanka Race has been an emblematic spectacle in Rijeka, demonstrating the unifying force of the sea and the spirit of yachting culture in Croatia. The 26th edition of the race unfolded on the 14th of June, seeing an exciting turnout of 153 boats painting the Kvarner Bay's canvas.

Organized in honor of Rijeka's City Day and the feast of Saint Vitus, the Fiumanka Race adheres to a philosophy that amalgamates tradition and freedom with an open invitation in racing - Free to Join. Free to Enjoy. The 26th year saw a diverse group of participants, including hardened sport crews, family teams, and recreational sailors, all soaking in and contributing to the thrilling atmosphere.

The principal regatta unfurled at noon, marking a display of exceptional seamanship across all racing categories. Once again, PROSECCO.DOC - SHOCKWAVE 3 proudly sailed their Maxi class, successfully defending their title, and claiming the overall win at Fiumanka's 26th race.

A unique aspect of this year's race was the Media Regatta, wherein representatives from Croatian and international media engaged in a friendly competition. The local newspaper, Novi list, claimed the victory, reinforcing the power of storytelling in yacht racing and the sailing community.

However, the Fiumanka Race is more than just a regatta. The event held at the Gat pier also featured live concerts, local food, sustainability-focused activities, and a spectacular performance by Daleka Obala, making the night come alive with merriment and music.

Underlining its commitment to environmental responsibility, the event promoted the BACKTOBLU initiative, indicating the growing consciousness of preserving maritime environments within the sailing community.

title: Lusben Embarks on Global Growth Strategy with Newly Opened Sales Office in Antibes, France
author: Old Sea Dogs

Lusben, famed for their exceptional refitting services and unique craftsmanship, continues their growth journey, with the Antibes outpost forming a part of their international expansion mission. Accelerating their global influence in the luxurious sailing sector, this move personifies Lusben's commitment to extend its refit expertise on an expansive platform.

The new office also stands as a testament to the thought leadership of the Azimut-Benetti Group, attesting to their future-forward approach and readiness to penetrate international markets. Continually improving their service deliverables through such progressive steps, they ensure a competitive edge and uncompromising customer satisfaction.

title: Breaking the Silence: Challenging the Superyacht Industry's Quiet Complicity in Discrimination
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Breaking the Silence: Challenging the Superyacht Industry's Quiet Complicity in Discrimination
summary: The superyacht industry is navigating choppy waters, with prolonged silence on poor conduct impeding its journey towards inclusion and diversity.
body: Set sail on a journey through the superyacht industry, and one is bound to encounter startlingly silent seas. This silence, however, isn't a mere absence of sound. It signifies a widespread complicity in discounting opinions, values, and ideas. The silent crowd, often choosing political correctness over unabashed truth, inadvertently confines the industry, causing a loss of potential advancement.

Beneath the serene surface of this tranquil silence lurks a more insidious issue – a palpable disrespect felt most prominently by women in the industry. Highly-successful, capable women have reported instances of being interrupted, overpowered and dismissed in public forums and events. Disconcertingly, this disruption doesn't come from fringe elements but from well-established members of this professional community.

This tacit acceptance exposes a concerning weakness in the superyacht industry's collective strength. The crowd's complacency stifles the robust exchange of ideas, inhibits diverse participation and ultimately, hampers the industry's growth. The real voyage for the industry lies not merely in cutting through the oceanic waves but in dismantling the barriers of silent acceptance. Gathering the winds of change in their sails, it's high time industry stakeholders steer their ships towards the shores of inclusivity and mutual respect.

title: Four Pristine, Affordable Motor Yachts Waiting to Embark on Your Next Adventure
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Four Pristine, Affordable Motor Yachts Waiting to Embark on Your Next Adventure
summary: Join the exclusive world of motor yacht ownership without breaking the bank. Discover four fantastic yachts that redefine affordability without compromising on luxury or performance.
body: While owning a motor yacht might present itself as an exclusive privilege of the super-wealthy, times are changing, and this luxury is becoming increasingly accessible. A tidy sum of £500,000 can now command a yacht that exudes glamour, sophistication and delivers exceptional performance at sea.

Among the proverbial stars in this segment are a sporty Windy sportscruiser, a dignified Princess flybridge, a resilient Aquastar, and a delightfully livable Beneteau Swift Trawler 41 Fly. These vessels are paradigms of craftsmanship and design, offering tantalising choices for prospective yacht owners with different preferences and needs.

The Swift Trawler 41 Fly takes pride in its hallmark features, including a convenient side access door by the helm, a sizeable vertical wheel, and a galley-aft layout – a first for the series. This layout provides easier, step-free movement on board, fulfilling the series' commitment to safety.

Advantageous features are not limited to the interior, as the exterior design exhibits a clever use of space for practicality. The cockpit seating can slide to either make room for more floor space or extend the bathing platform. As for performance, the twin Yanmar 8LV320 320hp motors equip the Swift Trawler 41 Fly with a top speed of about 20 knots.

Whether you're on the market for a swift sportscruiser, a luxurious flybridge, a steadfast Aquastar, or a cosy, well-rounded Beneteau Swift Trawler 41 Fly, there are enticing options out there. Embrace the sea breeze, the lapping waves, and the thrill of the open water – owning a motor yacht is now a dream within reach.

title: A Spirited Weekend Race at Bembridge Sailing Club Sees Keen Competition and A Surprise Winner
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A Spirited Weekend Race at Bembridge Sailing Club Sees Keen Competition and A Surprise Winner
summary: Revel in the nautical challenge of the Bembridge Sailing Club's mid-June Keelboat race. A lively weekend, defined by sunny skies, spirited competition and sailing camaraderie.
body: The weekend of the 14th and 15th of June, 2025 was a memorable one at the Bembridge Sailing Club, marking the mid-June Keelboat race. This event saw an eager group of sailors taking advantage of bright, sunny weather despite initially stiff southwesterly winds which had even the most ardent seafarers staying shore-bound on Saturday. However, the winds softened to a more manageable strength on Sunday, paving the way for keen competition.

As the race commenced, four stalwart Redwings and two One-Design boats navigated their way to the start area. Following a brief delay, a fifth Redwing, the Musicus helmed by Rosie Sym, arrived on the scene, joining the ranks of seafarers headed for the inflatable windward mark.

However, the fortunes of sea racing can ebb and flow like the tides. Harlequin, though confidently leading, was met with a misfortune when her main halyard broke, leaving the boat to complete the final leg under jib alone. This turn of events put Toucan helmed by Colin Samuelson in the leading position. Defying odds, Harlequin, although offered a tow, continued under jib, finishing only 10 minutes behind the leader.

Meanwhile, the One-Design race had its own share of equally tense moments. John Suffield, helming No 4 single-handed, had to retire due to a mainsail malfunction. Lavinia and Charles Perry in No 8, decided to practice their starting and enjoyed a splendid afternoon of sailing a full-length course.

Despite the trials and tribulations on the water, the mid-June Keelboat Weekend captured the very essence of sailing: adventure, competition, unpredictability, and camaraderie. At the end of the day, it was Toucan, who took home the coveted Evert de Kort Cup. The weekend was proof that sailing is not about the calm sea but about steering a steady ship amidst the stormy winds. Until next time, anchors aweigh!

title: Nasiba, the Third in the Outstanding Flexplorer 146 Series, Takes Sustainability and Adventure to New Heights
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Nasiba, the Third in the Outstanding Flexplorer 146 Series, Takes Sustainability and Adventure to New Heights
summary: Nasiba, the third installment in the renowned Flexplorer 146 yacht series, has been launched. This eco-friendly vessel redefines international adventure for a contemporary, environmentally aware generation.
body: Italian shipyard Cantiere delle Marche (CDM) has launched Nasiba, the third yacht in its stunning 44.3-meter Flexplorer 146 series. Named and commissioned by young and adventurous owners, Nasiba infuses high-seas exploration with sustainability and immense comfort. This yacht bears a striking similarity to Maverick, the series' maiden yacht, sharing an exterior profile by Sergio Cutolo and Hydro Tec, including an extended wheelhouse and a panoramic crow's nest. Unlike her previous sisterships, this model's interiors have been master-crafted by the British studio, Winch Design. The aim behind her design and construction was to create a yacht capable of taking its owners anywhere in the world, without compromising on comfort, privacy, or environmental responsibility, according to CDM's CEO Vasco Buonpensiere. Nasiba, therefore, stands as a testament to her owners’ lifestyle and mentality - an embodiment of daring and refined modern adventure on the seas. As described by William Yates of WSuperyachts, Nasiba's singular allure lies not only in her world-roaming navigation capabilities, but also in the distinctive interior designs and technical details. Some of these include mitigation of Electro-Motive Forces (EMF), an infra-red sauna, chilled plunge pool, and non-toxic, low VOC finishes applied throughout the interior. The result? A stunning yacht, underpinned by a can-do approach to accommodate the owner's detailed vision. Earthy hues, matte surfaces, and organic textures define Nasiba's interiors. Winch Design’s selection of eco-friendly materials such as recycled fishing nets, Foresso, woven grass, and Thames wood accentuates the yacht's commitment to sustainability. Special features include a 'green living wall' built from preserved moss and reclaimed seashell composites applied throughout the bathrooms. Carpets woven from recycled fishing nets and furniture adorned with palm leather highlight the same commitment. The layout caters to the owner’s every desire, with an active role being played in both creative and technical aspects of the project. A partnership was established with CDM and Hydro Tec design studio, to create a yacht perfectly suited for enduring living and worldwide exploration. The thoughtful arrangement spans across three decks, accommodating six cabins for guests and an additional six for the crew. An owner's deck houses the master suite, complete with a private stern terrace and a forward lounge area. This carefully crafted sailing vessel truly encapsulates the joy of exploration, the beauty of sustainability, and the luxury of supreme comfort.

title: Poole Bay 100: UKOPRA offshore powerboat championship
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Poole Bay 100: UKOPRA offshore powerboat championship
summary: There are days when the Solent feels like it’s holding its breath, and Saturday June 14th was one of them. With a pale blue sky above and the early morning mist still lingering like a sea ghost, Poole Quay slowly filled with the unmistakable growl of engines and the calm intensity of men and women who live for the roar of open water.
body: 'Double Trouble' (1-88) won the second round of the UKOPRA Offshore Powerboat Championships on Saturday, taking first place in the "Poole Bay 100."

Powerboats and competitors from the United States and Sweden encountered a tough course as the organizers opted for the Rough Weather Course. This choice was justified when the race was cut short after just four of the five scheduled laps. Early in the race, the Southampton-based team 'Falcon Multispark' (1-48), featuring former Formula 2 Grand Prix driver Dean Stoneman, took the lead in their eye-catching yellow Fountain monohull. However, the challenging conditions led to an engine overheating problem after a belt broke. Consequently, two groups of Class 1 teams, consisting of two and three boats, fiercely competed for the remainder of the race, creating an exciting show for the thousands of spectators along the Bournemouth seafront. Gary Aldington and Tom Gardner managed to hold off Rob Lockyer and Tim Linden in the popular 'Good Boy Vodka' (1-25) team to secure the Class 1 victory. The local favourite 'UNO Embassy' (1-717) finished the demanding course in a commendable third place in a highly competitive class, despite receiving a time penalty for incorrectly passing the Bournemouth Outfall buoy mark the wrong side..

In Class 1L, the uniquely coloured all-orange powerboat 'Black Ball Racing' (1L-8), featuring Martin McLaughlin, Rod Hawkins, and Darren Elliott, secured victory in their class which marked the team's first race in almost three years.

In the fiercely contested Class 3, Marcus Dodd and Sean Girdler navigated the challenging high seas in their silver Catamaran 'Oblivion,' (E-2) delivering an impressive performance despite the boat's preference for calmer waters in taking top honours. Meanwhile, Peter Hall and Terry Parsons continued to showcase determination with their classic Hunton hull 'Mango Crazy,' (E-8) finishing another race strongly and securing important points for the five-race series championship. Another Classic race hull took third place and their first podium in 2025 with 'Blast from the Past' (E-17) with Steven Tenant and Leslie Horner on-board. New team in a V24 racing hull ‘Team NEAFS’ (E-24) decided to retire early to preserve the boat for the next race in the series.
The fleet is set to move to Gosport and Haslar Marina on Saturday, July 14th, where they will navigate an offshore course around the Isle of Wight via the English Channel anticlockwise.

title: Emerging Insights on the Overhaul of the Polar Safety Code and Startling Reality of Superyacht Crew Living Conditions
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Emerging Insights on the Overhaul of the Polar Safety Code and Startling Reality of Superyacht Crew Living Conditions
summary: Fresh perspectives arise into a radical revamp of the polar safety code and conditions faced by superyacht crew members.
body: Revolutionary alterations to the Polar Safety Code by the Maritime and Coastguard Agency are gaining momentum. These are in a bid to uphold crew members', passengers' and vessels' safety in Polar waters, some of the planet's most dazzling yet volatile environments. The International Maritime Organization's changes to the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS) convention form the basis of these proposed modifications. Changes to the Merchant Shipping (Polar Code) (Safety) Regulations 2025 intend to apply stricter requisites for such hostile environments to a broader range of vessels, thereby elevating safety norms. Fishing vessels over 24 meters, cargo ships between 300gt and 500gt, and pleasure yachts of 300gt and above will now fall within the code's expanded scope. The goal is to safeguard passengers and crew amidst the harsh realities of the Polar regions and conserve fragile habitats from potential damage resulting from incidents such as pollution. Ship Construction and Equipment Lead Pete Rollason, endorsing the proposed changes, states that these common-sense, practical measures are in place on many vessels already. By expanding the code’s scope, an extra layer of protection for seafarers and some of the Earth's last great wilderness is anticipated. While safety measures advance, CHIRP Maritime’s Superyacht Feedback highlights grave concerns regarding superyacht crew’s living conditions. Reports indicate substantial safety and welfare issues as crew members were compelled to stay onboard during dry-docking periods when the vessel underwent considerable repairs. Living conditions became precarious with the presence of open fuel tanks in living areas, air conditioning, water and sewage services periodically shut down for extended times, and smoke detectors disconnected, compromising fire safety. Given the apathetic attitude of the management, the crew were forced to report the situation to CHIRP. These incidents underline the acute need for the maritime industry to not only enhance safety regulations but equally prioritize crew welfare and living conditions.

title: Thrilling Capers at Mid-June Bembridge and Medway Yacht Club Keelboat Regattas
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Thrilling Capers at Mid-June Bembridge and Medway Yacht Club Keelboat Regattas
summary: A spirited display unfolded on the waters as Bembridge and Medway Yacht Club hosted their mid-June sailing bonanzas, replete with high winds and impressive displays of seamanship.
body: The waves roared, the winds howled, and the sailing boats cut through, turning the sea into a grand arena. The mid-June weekend brought spectators and sailors to Bembridge Sailing Club and Medway Yacht Club for their eponymous keelboat regattas. Competitors patiently waited on Saturday for the strong southwesterly winds to subside at the Bembridge Sailing Club. The wind finally dropped to a more manageable strength for Sunday's races, with Redwings and One-Designs heading out to commence the vibrant race. After a thrilling competition, the Evert de Kort Cup was swept away by Toucan, despite an unexpected halyard break on Harlequin, initially leading the race.

title: BVI Spring Regatta & Sailing Festival 2026
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Change of date for 2026 BVI Spring Regatta & Sailing Festival
summary: For 2026, the BVI Spring Regatta & Sailing Festival has moved the event forward a week from previously published dates to March 23-29. Additionally, Scrub Island will now kick off the Sailing Festival, and the Nanny Cay Cup Round Tortola Race has moved to Wednesday (March 25, 2026).
body: Chris Haycraft, BVI Spring Regatta chairman explained: “Historically our competitors have run into a number of logistical obstacles with the event taking place over the Easter period. This move should make it easier to attend in terms of flight, accommodation, and boat availability.” He added, “Swapping the two races of the Sailing Festival gives competitors a shorter race for the first day, allowing them to shakedown their crew and hone their teamwork before the 36NM romp around Tortola.”

With over 60 islands and cays, and sheltered sailing waters, the British Virgin Islands are known as the ‘Sailing Capital of the World’. In five days of racing, the BVI Spring Regatta & Sailing Festival embraces its unique topography, setting courses that create a bucket list regatta using a combination of islands and buoys. This format provides a scenic tour of the BVI, matched with perfect courses for all classes. The racing is managed by a world-class race management team with two course areas, ensuring that the right classes get the right courses and racing for the day. The Regatta attracts a diverse fleet of international racing boats in addition to a strong bareboat fleet. Sailors can enjoy the two-day Sailing Festival, the three-day BVI Spring Regatta, or all five days of racing. While most sailors compete on their own boats, a sizeable number of the annual fleet compete on charter boats, and there are plenty of charter options available, from bareboat to performance race boats.

Nanny Cay Resort & Marina returns as host and presenting sponsor for the 24th year. The focal point of regatta social activities for the week is the Regatta Village at Nanny Cay which features the Big Top bar, satellite bars, food village, nightly DJs and live bands, tastings and demos, Moko Jumbies, art shows and more. “The BVI Spring Regatta is one of the most popular regattas in the Caribbean,” said Miles Sutherland Pilch, general manager of Nanny Cay. “At Nanny Cay we quite proudly feel that our staff, facilities and well-oiled regatta team play a big part in its continued growth and success. We’re very pleased to continue our support of this event that showcases the BVI and its spectacular sailing conditions.”

The Government of the Virgin Islands (GOVI) has increased its support of the event for 2026 and echoing Miles’ sentiments, Cayley Smit, BVI Spring Regatta organiser said: “Annually the BVI Spring Regatta brings sailors and spectators to the territory, and our year-round global marketing showcases the stunning scenery and boating life in the BVI. The ongoing development of art and culture displays and activities within the Regatta Village showcasing BVI culture, natural environment and maritime heritage is a new facet of the event that is supported by the Ministry of Tourism, Culture and Sustainability.”

Long-time Regatta partner, The Moorings has also already committed its support for 2026. Ian Pedersen, senior marketing manager at The Moorings & Sunsail, said: "The Moorings is proud to continue our sponsorship of the BVI Spring Regatta, one of the premier events on the Caribbean racing circuit, and one that is near and dear to our hearts. We look forward to working with the BVISR organising committee to host another incredible event, and once again welcome sailors from all over the world to experience this incomparable sailing ground."

title: Oceanco’s Masterpiece Y726: Embodying Bold Design Ambition and Robust Engineering
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Oceanco’s Masterpiece Y726: Embodying Bold Design Ambition and Robust Engineering
summary: Oceanco, the Dutch yacht manufacturer, has proudly launched Y726, an impressive 111-metre superyacht, embracing spectacular design ambition and superior engineering techniques.
body: In a formidable display of maritime artistry, Dutch yacht manufacturer, Oceanco, announced the launch of its latest masterpiece, the 111-metre superyacht, Y726. This is not just any launch; it's a testimony to design ambition, robust engineering, and collaboration. The Y726 promises to set new standards in the luxury maritime sector and transform how we perceive grandeur at sea.

Commissioned in 2022 by an experienced and returning client, the yacht rose from the depths of Oceanco's Alblasserdam facilities. It flaunts a 16-metre wide beam and a gross tonnage of 4,550GT, earning the title as one of the largest yachts by volume ever constructed by the shipyard. The yacht’s exterior, the creation of world-renowned designer Espen Øino, is complemented by an elegant, family-oriented interior from Mark Berryman. The intricacies of naval architecture have been meticulously planned and executed by the Lateral Naval Architects, in tandem with Oceanco's in-house team.

The yacht's beach club comes equipped with a bar that ushers directly onto the swimming platform, adding a cheerful wink to the yacht's luxurious exterior. The Y726 was last seen outfitted at Oceanco's Alblasserdam facilities in December 2023, wrapped in artwork by Rotterdam-based graffiti artist I AM EELCO.

Y726 reflects what is achievable when a shared vision is pursued by a team with aligned intentions and determined execution. Oceanco’s Y726 exemplifies an incredible feat of engineering prowess. As Lee Archer, programme director at Lateral, aptly described: 'Y726 stands as a testament not only to engineering enabling design at the highest level but also to the power of collaboration as a catalyst for excellence.'

title: Unfolding the Voyage of 'Memories': The Seventh Amels 60 Superyacht Ready for Charter Season
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unfolding the Voyage of 'Memories': The Seventh Amels 60 Superyacht Ready for Charter Season
summary: The Amels 60 lineage adds a new member to its fleet, dubbed 'Memories'. Preparing to make waves, this superyacht is ready for a lively charter season.
body: The latest jewel in the crown of the Amels 60 series, the vessel named 'Memories', embarks on a fresh journey with open horizons, poised to command the charter season. A private yacht naming ceremony that took place at the Dutch shipyard brought ancipation to a crescendo. The 60-meter marvel made its debut voyage from Damen Yachting's Vlissingen facility in the Netherlands, following rigorous sea trials held in April. Marking a landmark collaboration, this hull raises the curtain for the British studio Harrison Eidsgaard's exquisite design, with the superyacht flaunting a 'beach house' interior.

Even though the owner is expected to utilize this luxurious cruiser for personal voyages, charter exploitation stands as a formidable pillar. Changes were introduced to the beach club, owner's areas, and sundeck during its fabrication. 'Memories', beyond being a remarkable artifact of craftsmanship and innovation, encapsulates an indomitable shared passion for excellence. The living spaces are an aesthetic confluence of stainless steel, bronze, fluted details, and natural oak elements. Bren Harrison's design encapsulates the essence of a beach house luxury in an 'undeniably contemporary' vessel. With a full dive center, posh accommodation for 12 guests, and a luxurious beach club with a sauna and gym equipment, 'Memories' is all set to set course towards her first main destination in Ibiza.

title: Decoding the Art of Rigging: the Essentials of Load Pins in the World of Yacht Racing and Cruising
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Decoding the Art of Rigging: the Essentials of Load Pins in the World of Yacht Racing and Cruising
summary: Explore the pivotal role and versatility of load pins in achieving enhanced performance on both yacht racing and cruising vessels.
body: Load pins, ubiquitous and enduring tools gracing the world of sailboat racing since the 1980s, continue to prove their mettle onboard yachts, specifically those stretching beyond 50ft. While there's an array of load sensing contrivance present today, the kingpin - quite literally - is still the load pin, a frontrunner particularly where plug-and-play solutions like smarttune fall short.

Modern load pins offer enviable flexibility, connecting seamlessly with a wide spectrum of instrumentation brands and diverse apps and software platforms offering detailed analytics. Regardless of where they are fitted within a rig, their primary goal is to boost performance while ensuring safety and comfort. They offer various forms of data output — from analog and digital to wireless.

Yachts like X-Yachts' new XR-41 model feature Digital Direct Pins as optional upgrades, enabling operators to access real-time data, further strengthening the safety and performance of the vessels. Load pins’ versatility and practicality indeed make them an invaluable gear in the heart of any performance or cruising yacht.

title: Thrills and Solidarity Unfurl at Brindisi's Nastro Rosa Tour 2025 Regatta
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Thrills and Solidarity Unfurl at Brindisi's Nastro Rosa Tour 2025 Regatta
summary: Fierce competition under sail was the order of the day in Brindisi, the stage set for the Nastro Rosa Tour 2025.
body: The second day of the Marina Militare Nastro Rosa Tour 2025, held in the stunning Brindisi basin, offered up an adrenaline-filled spectacle of sailing competing. WASZP and WING classes lock-horns under the area's unique wind conditions, performing deft tacks and evolutions remarkable even to seasoned spectators. Drama was certainly not in short supply, drawing a hefty audience from both the city's residents and a legion of tourists.

Yet, the day transcended thrilling competition. A somber hush fell on the regatta village, cultural events and award ceremonies put on hold. The tragic and untimely death of Brigadier Chief Carlo Legrottaglie, occurring just a few kilometers from Brindisi, had shaken the athletes and organizers. A message of deep empathy and support was extended to the family of the soldier via the LED walls throughout the site and official social media channels, virtually enveloping the entire Defense family in a tangible camaraderie.

title: Sailor Ambrogio Beccaria, with Mapei, Takes Collective Strength into Prestigious IMOCA and The Ocean Race Europe
author: Old Sea Dogs

Beccaria's maiden voyage as the skipper of Allagrande Mapei begins in mid-July, quickly leading to a demanding challenge at The Ocean Race Europe, a prominent event in the IMOCA 2025 circuit. This race encompasses five culturally rich and geographically diverse stages, commencing from Kiel, Germany and concluding at Boka Bay, Montenegro.

While the course itself poses numerous strategic complications, Beccaria also anticipates rigorous competition. In the face of formidable opponents, who wield extensive sailing credentials, his team must quickly grasp their new environment, learn from the competition, and manage the diverse sailing conditions presented by this versatile European course. Their strategy relies on leveraging collective strength and maintaining the momentum to ensure a robust performance throughout the season.

title: Women sailors reflect on the Admiral’s Cup inclusion rule
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Women sailors reflect on the Admiral’s Cup inclusion rule
summary: The Royal Ocean Racing Club (RORC) has long acknowledged the slow but steady path toward gender inclusion in offshore sailing. For the forthcoming Admiral’s Cup, every boat must have at least one woman, as well as another sailor under 27. The goal is to expand access, broaden the talent pool, and create a more diverse and vibrant racing community.
body: Changing tides: Women sailors reflect on the Admiral’s Cup inclusion rule.

The RORC has seen pivotal milestones for women sailors over the one hundred years of the club’s existence, but there is still so much more to achieve. The inclusion rule for the 2025 Admiral’s Cup hopes to accelerate that change.

In 1929, Baroness André de Neufville became the first woman to join RORC after completing the Fastnet Race. In 1954, Hon. Ray Pitts Rivers broke new ground as the Club’s first female Rear Commodore. Another significant moment came in 1969 when Mary Pera captained Italy’s first Admiral’s Cup team - later going on to become RORC’s first female Secretary in 1972, raising visibility for women in offshore competition.

The identity of the first woman to compete in the Admiral’s Cup remains unclear, but Liz Watson sailed regularly on Cervantes IV, her father Bob Watson’s yacht, which helped Britain win the Cup in 1971. A decade later, Pam Saffery-Cooper raced aboard Dragon, part of the 1981 winning British team, alongside Victory of Burnham and Yeoman XXIII.

Despite these achievements, offshore sailing continues to be male-dominated. However, participation by women is growing. In a sign of changing tides, two of RORC’s senior Flag Officer roles are now held by women - Admiral Janet Grosvenor and Commodore Deb Fish - highlighting a shift toward a more inclusive and representative club culture.

This crew inclusion rule for the 2025 Admiral’s Cup is not just symbolic, it’s designed to spark real opportunity. By placing women and young sailors on the same starting line as elite professionals it offers a platform to gain experience, build confidence and challenge outdated assumptions about who belongs in high-level offshore racing.

As the sailing world watches the return of the Admiral’s Cup, this commitment to inclusion signals a bold step forward. It honours the achievements of trailblazers past, while creating new pathways for future generations, ensuring that offshore sailing is open to all who are ready to rise to the challenge.

Cole Brauer will be racing on the Monaco Yacht Club entry Jolt 6 for the Admiral’s Cup. Cole made history in 2024 as the first American woman to race solo nonstop around the world. Originally from Long Island, she didn’t grow up sailing but discovered her passion at the University of Hawaii where she quickly rose to lead the team. In a short period of time her journey from underdog to global record-setter has inspired thousands, both on and off the water.

“I’ll be honest, I wasn’t initially thrilled about the crew rule requiring one woman on board. It felt like the bare minimum, and I’ve often found myself as the only woman on the team. While I respect and enjoy sailing with the guys, I truly believe crews perform better with more women involved. Women are just as talented, just as driven, and they deserve the same opportunities to gain experience and grow. It’s not about filling a quota - it’s about recognising skill and building diverse, high-performing teams. I hope that in five or 10 years, we won’t need a rule like this, because the sailing world will naturally reflect the talent of both women and men equally.” - Cole Brauer (Carkeek 40 Jolt 6)

Joy Fitzgerald will be racing on the PAC 52 Final Final, representing the Royal Ocean Racing Club in the Admiral’s Cup. Fitzgerald has a background in physical strength and conditioning, as well as being an offshore and inshore professional sailor. She joined Team JAJO aboard their VO65 in the 2023 Ocean Race Sprint Cup. Fitzgerald got her big break racing with Niklas Zennstrom’s Team Rán and recently raced on the majestic J‑Class Svea. Her experience ranges from Maxi Yacht campaigns to the intensity of cutting-edge offshore teams, marking her as a true all-rounder.

“Honestly… my first reaction to the crew rule was a bit of an eye-roll - are we really still having to tell teams to include women? I’ve always sailed alongside inspiring women and never saw it as something that needed enforcing. But I also recognise that this rule has opened doors. For me, it led to joining the Final Final team and becoming part of something that goes beyond just one regatta. Offshore sailing is tough, physically and mentally, and I hope this rule helps redefine what strength looks like. Yes, it might start as tokenism for some, but it gives women the chance to prove their value and build a place in professional teams. Progress, to me, means that one day we won’t need a rule like this, we’ll just pick the best sailors for the job. But until then, if it helps shift mindsets and create real opportunities, then it’s a step worth taking.” - Joy Fitzgerald (PAC52 Final Final)

Abby Ehler will be racing on Black Pearl, representing the New York Yacht Club in the Admiral’s Cup. Ehler is a seasoned professional whose extensive career spans multiple round-the-world races and major global events. She first made waves as bowman and boat captain in the 2001‑02 Volvo Ocean Race aboard Amer Sports Too, and returned to the event in 2014‑15 with Team SCA and 2017‑18 with Team Brunel. Abby has also applied her logistical expertise shoreside at the America’s Cup and SailGP, and was part of Team Holcim‐PRB in the 2023 Ocean Race.

“When I first heard about the crew rule, I had mixed emotions. I was encouraged that a major event was prioritising inclusion, but I also worried it might lead to being seen as a quota rather than recognised for ability. That said, we’ve seen from SailGP and the Ocean Race that these rules can open doors and shift mindsets. If we want to normalise women in professional sailing, we need this kind of visible commitment. It’s not just about ticking boxes, it’s about changing culture. Inclusion leads to normalisation. The more women we see on the water, in key roles, the more natural it becomes. Five years from now, I hope we’re no longer asking, ‘Why is she here?’ but saying, ‘of course she is.’” - Abby Ehler (Botin 56 Black Pearl)

At 23 years of age, Anna Houtzager is one of the youngest sailors competing in the Admiral’s Cup. She is racing with the Rotterdam Offshore Sailing Team on Ker 46 ROST Van Uden. Her journey in sailing began at just six months old when her parents took her aboard a J/24 to Denmark, instilling a lifelong passion for the sport. Anna’s role on board is part of the pit crew for the young Dutch team.

“I think it’s a good thing this rule exists, it opens the door for women and younger sailors to be part of top-level racing. It’s not a shortcut, you still have to bring value to the team. But it does help teams notice potential they might have overlooked. In many crews, women are still seen as the exception, and this rule challenges that. I want to get to a point where no one’s surprised to see a woman on the crew list. If my presence helps shift that mindset, then that’s already progress.” - Anna Houtzager (Ker 46 ROST Van Uden)

Born in Lisbon, Mariana Lobato will be racing on Teasing Machine representing the Yacht Club de France for the Admiral’s Cup. Mariana has been on the water since infancy, racing Optimists by age eight. She quickly progressed through the 420 and 470 Classes before focusing on match racing where she represented Portugal at the 2012 London Olympics and clinched the 2013 Women’s Match Racing World Championship. Transitioning to high-performance multihulls and offshore boats, Mariana sailed GC32s, M32s, and Ocean Fifty trimarans. She joined the Mirpuri Foundation Racing Team, winning the 2021 Ocean Race Europe, and later competed as co-skipper on the IMOCA 60 Biotherm in the 2022–23 Ocean Race.

“This rule is a step forward - it gives women and young sailors a chance to get on board and grow. But ultimately, we want to be chosen for our skills, not just because of a rule. That shift in mindset is where real progress lies. Inclusion helps break down the outdated belief that women can’t be just as good as men. When we’re given equal opportunities to learn and gain experience, the difference shows. Five years from now, I hope we don’t need a rule to justify our place, we’ll be there because we’ve earned it.” - Mariana Lobato (NM54 Teasing Machine).

As the 2025 Admiral’s Cup approaches, the inclusion rule is doing more than shaping crew lists - it’s reshaping attitudes. From seasoned professionals like Abby Ehler, to emerging talents like Anna Houtzager, these women aren’t just filling a requirement, they’re redefining what excellence in offshore sailing looks like. Their voices underscore a shared desire not to be seen as exceptions, but as essential members of high-performing teams.

title: A Cool Million Off: The 34m Horizon Yacht Andrea VI Slashes Sale Price!

This included extensive upgrades conducted between 2022 and 2024 - a flawless and vibrant repaint job in 'Show White' and an upgrade to the yacht's Caterpillar engines.

The naval architecture is the handiwork of Donald L. Blount, while the exterior styling is accredited to Espinosa Yacht Design. Marty Lowe was the creative force behind the meticulously curated interior aesthetics of Andrea VI.

No space-dividing cabinets or partitions are present on-board the magnificent Andrea VI, allowing for an airy and comprehensive socialising area. title: Diego Botin’s Spain SailGP Team leads
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: DAY 1 - MUBADALA NEW YORK SAIL GRAND PRIX
summary: Diego Botin’s Spain SailGP Team leads the fleet after a stormy and tactical opening day of the Mubadala New York Sail Grand Prix. France, ROCKWOOL Denmark and New Zealand are all hot on his heels for all-important leaderboard points heading into Championship Sunday.
body: As the starting bell rang on the Hudson, SailGP’s fleet of international athletes took on multiple roles, with just three crew on board to reduce weight in light breeze. Straight across the startline, Diego Botin led the fleet to mark one, storming ahead to cross the finish line first.

Coming off the water, Botin remarked: “It was so hectic out there! The first race suddenly we were up – we didn’t know where we were within the fleet but we got a good start and then we managed to give it our all. Managing priorities on the boat in these kinds of conditions and in different formations onboard – that's the toughest thing. You cannot stop fighting until the end.”

Race two and a four-person crew meant an extra set of eyes and hands on board for teams navigating the flushing-out tides of the Hudson. Tom Slingsby – fresh off the hype of announcing a new Title Partner and co-owners, actors Hugh Jackman and Ryan Reynolds – tore through the startline and kept it up, sweeping across the line in first. Martine Grael’s Mubadala Brazil was close behind in second, with a consistent effort from Quentin Delapierre’s France taking Les Bleus into third.

Tom Slingsby, who sits sixth after the first three fleet races of the weekend, said: “We sort of had an up and down day. The race win was great – the boat was going really well and then the last race, unfortunately, we had a few issues and had a bad race. The forecast tomorrow looks great – we're going to focus on that.”

The third and final fleet race started with a drag race over the startline between Peter Burling’s Black Foils and Nicolai Sehested’s ROCKWOOL Denmark, as the Kiwis aimed to bounce back to the top after an 11th place finish in fleet race two. And boy, did it pay off as for the first time in SailGP racing history the New Zealand crew lapped the entire fleet, going three times the speed round the outside of the course and proving that once foiling, they were out of there…and across the finish.

Racing at home for the final time this season, the U.S. SailGP Team was buoyed by full grandstands of American racing fans. Driver Taylor Canfield said, “We could hear them cheering for us as we came by, and that's super cool. I'm so proud to represent our country and we're lucky to have this third event (Stateside).”

​​Prior to the racing beginning on Saturday, SailGP Chief Hype Officer, Grammy-Award winning music mogul DJ Khaled, hyped up the crowd. More than 10,000 fans are expected across the weekend, watching from the Governors Island Race Stadium and official spectator fleet.

The most exciting racing on water returns tomorrow (Sunday June 8) with a brighter forecast and shifty winds predicted, getting underway at 3:30 p.m. ET. Three fleet races will be followed by a winner-takes-all final. Limited tickets remain at SailGP.com/NY.

Spain (25 points) ROCKWOOL Denmark (20 points) France (20 points) New Zealand (19 points) Mubadala Brazil (17 points) BONDS Flying Roos (17 points) GER Deutsche Bank (11 points) Switzerland (10 points) Northstar Canada (10 points) Emirates Great Britain (7 points) Unites States (6 points) Red Bull Italy (3 points)

title: A Sea-Voyager's Guide to Successfully Cross the English Channel: A Deep-Dive Into Nautical Planning
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A Sea-Voyager's Guide to Successfully Cross the English Channel: A Deep-Dive Into Nautical Planning
summary: Venturing the vast waters of the English Channel can be quite a daunting task. Here's a definitive guide to help plan the perfect passage across this iconic waterway.
body: Sailing the English Channel is no small feat. Even for the most seasoned sailor, it presents a set of unique challenges which require meticulous planning. For instance, the use of the so-called APEM mnemonic (the acronym stands for: Appraise, Plan, Execute, and Monitor) is highly recommended. To start, one must prepare by assessing the desired route. If, say, the course is set from Poole to Honfleur, understanding the unique conditions and requirements of this route is paramount.

During the planning stage, the sailor must select waypoints and calculate tides and timings. Most sea-voyagers only resort to waypoints when a change of heading is mandatory. Still, these navigational tools can also serve as helpful reminders. For instance, one could designate waypoints to mark exiting UK waters, approaching a traffic separation zone, entering French waters, and making the necessary radio check-in at the port of entry in France.

Factoring in conditions is essential, as wind against tide can threaten comfort and safety during a seven-hour seafaring journey. Ideally, one should aim to make the passage when the forecast predicts a force less than 4 on the Beaufort scale. Final steps in the planning process include researching tidal limitations at the port of entry and using web-based tools such as webcams and digital tidal curves. These resources can provide live updates and a comprehensive visual understanding of the conditions on the ground, or rather, on the sea.

title: Diverging Interpretations of EU Customs Rules Leave Superyacht Operators in Troubled Waters
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Diverging Interpretations of EU Customs Rules Leave Superyacht Operators in Troubled Waters
summary: Incongruities in European Union customs enforcement present potential financial threats to superyacht owners and operators.
body: The intricacies of the European Union customs enforcement can prove to be a labyrinth for superyacht operators. A recent case surfaced the chilling inconsistencies that exist within this frame of lawmaking, potentially inflicting damage of millions of euros. The protagonist of this narrative is a non-EU flagged yacht benefiting from the Temporary Admission (TA) status, which faced a sequence of administrative events in Spain under the Inward Processing Relief (IPR) provision.

This view not only contradicts the transparent Article 215 of the UCC but also rejects the GPS data tracking that authenticated the yacht's departure and return beyond 12 nautical miles from Spanish territories. This observation strengthens the urgent need for uniformity among EU Member States regarding customs regulations. These discrepancies have hurled operators into a storm of uncertainty, triggering import VAT instantly if a vessel is seen to have overstayed its TA. To navigate these murky waters, yacht owners are now advised to reaffirm the inception of a new 18-month TA period by submitting an Annexe 71.01. Nonetheless, the overarching concern remains - the imperious need for harmonized customs enforcement within EU Member States.
