title: Evolving with the Waves: Quay Group Sails Beyond Yachting to Cater to Ultra-High-Net-Worth Clients
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Evolving with the Waves: Quay Group Sails Beyond Yachting to Cater to Ultra-High-Net-Worth Clients
summary: In response to growing demand from the wealthiest clientele, superyacht recruitment specialist Quay Crew has rebranded as Quay Group, promising high-calibre integrated staffing solutions across sea and shore.
body: Quay Crew, a renowned superyacht recruitment specialist, has broadened its horizons by transforming into Quay Group. The rebranding was initiated in response to a swelling demand from ultra-high-net-worth (UHNW) clients for talent solutions beyond the yachting industry. This move signifies a significant leap from being a single-focus recruiter to becoming a multi-division agency catering to a wider network of UHNW clientele and professionals. While the company's name has changed, the heart and soul of it remain unaltered; with the core values, commitment to quality, and expert team staying the same. The group's new structure introduces four specialist divisions, acknowledging the dynamic nature of internal workforce trends. Recognizing that most crew members eventually transition ashore, these expanded offerings open up new career pathways for those with maritime experience. Quay Crew has built a strong reputation in the superyacht industry since its inception in 2013. The company has had long-standing, diversified relationships with its clients and has expanded its service portfolio accordingly. Under the new group structure, Quay Crew will continue operating as the main division, placing global yachting industry professionals across all levels. Quay Group also aims to produce regular market insight reports and recruitment research, providing valuable touchpoints for clients and candidates in the sector. The new Quay Maritime Division will tackle operational, technical, and corporate roles, with special provisions set for land-based maritime positions. Next is the Quay Estates Division, dedicated to staffing solutions for UHNW-level private households, estates, and luxury residences. The latest addition is Quay Family Office which will cater to recruitment needs of family offices, investment organizations, and asset management firms. In essence, Quay Group's evolution signifies a thriving demand for unified recruitment across the entire UHNW lifestyle sector. From onboard positions in luxury hospitality to management roles ashore, the move taps into a wider trend where skilled professionals increasingly transition into multiple roles within the UHNW spectrum.

title: Discover the Windy SR40: An Innovative Family Boat with Unique Water Sports Capabilities

summary: The new Windy SR40, a thrilling multi-purpose family sports boat, is all set to charm the boating world with its diverse suite of cruising facilities and seagoing capabilities.
body: Debuting globally at this year’s Palma Boat Show was the Windy SR40, a vessel designed for the family that loves water and sports. More than just an in-between, this boat carves out its niche, blending elements of Windy's original Sports Cruiser Line and its SR Yacht Tenders in one mighty package. At the focus is the creation of a high-speed, go-anywhere, multi-purpose family sports boat that combines top-tier cruising facilities, a spacious day boating zone, and remarkable seagoing performance. Versatility is a key aspect of this boat, exemplified by its adaptable superstructure. It features a sliding roof, large 'disappearing' doors, and roof racks for paddleboards, fishing rods, and bikes. The aft bulkhead can be open or closed, providing an open boat or an enclosure for all-year-round recreation. In terms of accommodation, the SR40 offers a large sunbed at the bow and a range of other features, including joystick docking, a gyro stabiliser, sliding aft doors, lithium-ion battery bank, and extendable aft terraces. Its engine options, which include twin Volvo Penta D6-440s or triple Mercury V10 400s, offer a speed range of 42-52 knots. The Windy SR40 is a paradigm shift in family boating, showcasing the perfect balance between performance and luxury.

title: Revolutionising Sea Stability with Dometic DG3’s Cutting-Edge Boat Gyro Stabiliser
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Revolutionising Sea Stability with Dometic DG3’s Cutting-Edge Boat Gyro Stabiliser
summary: The innovative Dometic DG3 gyro stabiliser aims to redefine maritime equilibrium by conquering heavy-duty tasks without compromising functionality.
body: Sailors and yachting enthusiasts are no stranger to the challenge of managing stability at sea. Often referred to as the 'game of gyros', mastering this nautical balancing act can elevate cruising experiences from stressful to serene. Enter the Dometic DG3 — a gyro stabiliser that not only promises to offer the benefits of compact stabilisation systems but aims to eliminate known existing drawbacks within the maritime industry.

Until recently, the Seakeeper's compact model was the go-to gyro stabiliser for sub-40-foot boats. However, the market has positively ebbed and flowed, and we now find a veritable battleground of marine equipment manufacturers developing compact stabilisers. Italian company Quick and now Dometic have decided to join the fight, introducing their new models aiming to outperform the rest.

Another brilliant addition is the adoption of all-electric ‘roller screw’ technology. This simple yet functional change eliminates the need for high-pressure hoses and seals, thus minimising leak potential and abolishing the need for hydraulic fluid changes. The DG3 is also energy-efficient and helps to generate electrical current.

The 48V lithium-ion battery is a marvel of its own, powering the electric motor which enables rapid flywheel speed shifts. This reduces the time needed to reach maximum RPM and significantly lowers recover times post-action.

Furthermore, the DG3 model demonstrates concern for user compatibility by integrating with the boat’s main electrical system, running on 12V, 24V, and 48V systems with very little adaptation. This use of innovative technology encapsulates Dometic's commitment to accessible design and shows extreme promise for the future of gyro stabilisers.

The revolutionising Dometic DG3 seeks to embody the concept of cross-sea stability whilst maintaining a sense of affinity with its older siblings. With its groundbreaking performance, the DG3 gives a nod to modern yachting future, promising safer and more enjoyable sea adventures.

title: Discover the Wellcraft 38 T Top, A Maritime Marvel Blending High Performance With Sociable Entertaining
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover the Wellcraft 38 T Top, A Maritime Marvel Blending High Performance With Sociable Entertaining
summary: Unveiled at the Cannes Yachting Festival, the Wellcraft 38 T Top is a stellar addition to the company's celebrated 'Explorer' line, boasting an array of features designed for both adventure seekers and social butterflies.
body: Wellcraft continues to push the boundaries in yacht design with its latest offering - the Wellcraft 38 T Top. Featuring the familiar allure of the company's 'Explorer' line, this innovative vessel takes a step further by reflecting a clear emphasis on sociability and entertainment.

With the capacity to comfortably seat ten in its asymmetrical cockpit and six in the bow, the boat’s design underscores its social focus. An ingeniously designed terrace on the starboard side further enhances the environment, offering a perfect spot for relaxation and convivial gatherings.

But it's not all social bells and whistles. The boat retains classic maritime elements, with features such as a fold-away bench at the transom, and a hidden live bait well for the fishing enthusiasts. Drained storage spaces and conveniently integrated rod holders strategically dot the length and breadth of the yacht, giving a nod to its functional origin.

The Wellcraft 38 T Top demonstrates an intelligent and creative use of space. A decent cuddy cabin, complete with wet-room style heads, a separate sink and easy access from the port side deck, is found in the helm console. The design is rounded off with an invigorating bow design, new-age gas lockers, drained gunwale-top trays, flush-mount speakers and a smart table elegantly popping up from the deck at the push of a button.

In a world where boating designs can often feel repetitive, the Wellcraft 38 T Top manages to stand out. Not only has it won the European Powerboat of the Year, it's changing the narrative of boat designs, skillfully intertwining functionality with a refreshing, social element. And with more boats in this new series on the horizon, the future of boating might be sailing into more sociable waters.

title: The Dawn of a New Era for Classic Yacht Lady Esther following a Three-Year Refurbishment
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Dawn of a New Era for Classic Yacht Lady Esther following a Three-Year Refurbishment
summary: Reviving a classic, the 65-metre yacht Lady Esther is back on the water following an extensive three-year overhaul by Damen Maaskant.
body: Once a regal name among yachts, the 65-metre classic Lady Esther has triumphantly returned to the waves. After a comprehensive three-year refurbishment at the hands of the renowned Damen Maaskant, she took her maiden voyage last year from the Dutch yard's Stellendam site and is currently making waves along the eastern coast of Spain.

The significant refit not only repaired time's wear and tear but enhanced Lady Esther's stature considerably. Following the extensive works, she now enjoys a 10-metre extension, a rejuvenated interior layout, and the addition of two glass-walled decks and a luxurious new Jacuzzi. A glimpse at the refreshed Lady Esther reveals a remarkable transformation, as her previously faded grandeur is replaced with a robust masculinity typical of explorer yachts. The award-winning Dutch design studio, Vripack, applied their Midas touch to the redesign, both externally and internally, although the details of their craft are as of yet undisclosed.

Interestingly, the sundeck has long since held the title of the primary social hub onboard the Lady Esther. It is equipped with an array of features to promote leisure and relaxation, including a wet bar, Jacuzzi, sunpads, and even a selection of gym equipment, offering an inviting and versatile space for guests to unwind. Specific details of the changes to this area during the refit remain confidential for now.

Despite this refit marking a significant milestone in Lady Esther's well-travelled career, it is far from her first refurbishment. Over her 45 years of sailing, she has received several upgrades and refreshments. The most recent of these major upgrades, prior to the latest endeavour, occurred in 2004, when she received a 5.8-metre extension.
Celebrating the Lady Esther's storied past, the vessel embarks on the newest chapter of its adventure, bolstered by the timeless combination of classical elegance and powerful performance.

title: THE ‘BONDS FLYING ROOS"
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: THE ‘BONDS FLYING ROOS"
summary: BONDS Flying Roos Take Flight: Hugh Jackman and Ryan Reynolds Hop Aboard Australia’s SailGP Juggernaut
body: It’s all change in the antipodean fleet. The Aussie green-and-gold juggernaut that’s ruled the SailGP seas is now sailing under a new banner — and with two bonafide Hollywood heavyweights at the helm. Enter the BONDS Flying Roos, backed not just by Olympic gold medallist Tom Slingsby, but also by none other than Hugh Jackman and Ryan Reynolds, who’ve hopped aboard as co-owners and part-time mischief-makers.

That’s right — the Flying Roos have slipped their moorings with a bellyful of national pride, a new name, and a title partner stitched right into the sails. Thanks to Aussie icon BONDS, this flying marsupial of a racing team is kitted out and comfortable where it counts.

“It’s a perfect fit,” declared Jackman and Reynolds in a statement laced with their trademark charm, “Hugh brings the love of country and sailing. Ryan brings the clingy emotional support. And yes, we may be writing this in our undies. No further comment.”

SailGP, the global league where 50-foot catamarans tear around harbours faster than a southerly buster, was founded in 2019 by Sir Russell Coutts and Oracle’s Larry Ellison. Since then, Australia has become its top dogfish — three titles in four seasons and not a jib out of place. But now? Now the game’s changed. This isn’t just sailing — this is a movement in motion.

“This is a big moment — for our team and the sport,” said Tom Slingsby, who now wears three caps: Skipper, CEO, and Co-Owner. “With Hugh and Ryan on board, we’re bringing in big hearts, bigger laughs, and a global audience. The Flying Roos are built on grit, wit, and Aussie blood — and BONDS just makes it official.”

BONDS themselves, a household name from Byron to Broome, have never shied away from an adventure. “We’re known for comfort and spirit,” said Tanya Deans, BONDS Australia’s president, “and SailGP is full of both — especially when your bum’s glued to a trampoline doing 100 clicks an hour into a headwind.”

This multi-year partnership isn’t just about logos and laughs. It’s the first time an Aussie SailGP crew’s had a Title Partner, and it marks a new tack for BONDS — one of global ambition and sport-fuelled cool. Just months after their U.S. launch with Robert Irwin, they’re turning up the heat with foils, fame, and flying hulls.

The BONDS Flying Roos will debut their new name and look at the Mubadala New York Sail Grand Prix, June 7–8. If the wind gods smile, the Roos will not only hold their lead on the leaderboard but mark this new chapter with a splash of champagne and a standing ovation.

And to those watching from shore, a word of warning: don’t blink. The Aussies are fast, loud, and now backed by the only crew in the fleet who can brag about being both Olympic champions and action movie royalty. From front-stretch foil lifts to comfort-stretch waistbands — the BONDS Flying Roos are here to sail hard, laugh louder, and look damn good doing it.

title: Team Baam Emerges Victorious at Women's World Match Racing Tour 2025 Santa Maria Cup Event
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Team Baam Emerges Victorious at Women's World Match Racing Tour 2025 Santa Maria Cup Event
summary: The Women's World Match Racing Tour recently celebrated the impressive victory of Team Baam at the 2025 Santa Maria Cup Event in Annapolis, USA.
body: A major event on the competitive sailing calendar, the 2025 Santa Maria Cup, recently crowned Team Baam, a US women's match racing team, as its champions. The team, skippered by Allie Blecher alongside crew members Beka Schiff, Rose Edwards, and Ali Blumenthal Stokes, showed their mettle by defeating the Vela Racing Team skippered by Nicole Breault in a tense light-air final on the Severn River. Hosted by Eastport Yacht Club for over 20 years, the Santa Maria Cup is an essential women's match racing regatta on the Women's World Match Racing Tour. The tension mounted on the day of the race, as a long wait for the breeze preceded the crucial final matches. The competitors finally hit the water in front of the renowned U.S Naval Academy as the sea breeze arrived in the early afternoon. Luck didn't favor the defending Santa Maria Cup champions, Team Wings from Sweden, skippered by Anna Ostling, in their match against the determined Australian team, Easy Tiger Racing. Team Wings secured a hard-fought win against the Australians but their semi-final loss to Team Baam USA thwarted their comeback dreams. Similarly, Breault and her Vela Racing team had a tough day in the event final, outpaced by Team Baam in spite of challenging light-air conditions. Despite the rigorous competition and high stress levels, Team Baam emerged as the deserving champions. Skipper Allie Blecher attributed their success to the unity and competence of their crew, stating their ability to stay focused and maintain a steady level of performance under pressure was key. Reflecting on the showdown, Breault graciously congratulated Team Baam, acknowledging their incredible performance. The Santa Maria Cup event signalled the exciting second stage of the 2025 Women's World Match Racing Tour. Nicole Breault and Vela Racing sit atop the leaderboard owing to their accumulated 22 points, which includes their second-place standing at the initial event in San Francisco. Competition continues with the third stage of the tour soon to take place in Marstrand, Sweden. The Women's Tour Executive Director, James Pleasance, enthusiastically awaits the next leg of the championship, eager to see more powerful female athletes showcasing their sailing prowess.

title: Iconic Italian Shipyard Benetti Revels in the Launch of the Show-stopping Class 44M Superyacht ‘Fortitude1’
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Iconic Italian Shipyard Benetti Revels in the Launch of the Show-stopping Class 44M Superyacht ‘Fortitude1’
summary: Stealing the show, Benetti unveils its latest marvel, Fortitude1, the impressive newcomer in the Class 44M series.
body: Italy's premier shipyard, Benetti, has once again proven its supremacy in the yachting world with the launch of Fortitude1, the newest addition to their prestigious Class 44M series. This 44.1-meter fiberglass model is expected to make a grand delivery to her owner, a longstanding Benetti patron, this summer.

Renowned Italian studio Giorgio M. Cassetta has left his artistic imprint both inside and outside the yacht. The exterior design cleverly reinterprets the classic features of the Class series. Custom elements enhance its allure, including an expansive forward sunpad on the upper deck. Fortitude1 follows the legacy of the first unit, Juno's 7, which made its grand debut earlier this year.

The four-deck yacht encompasses accommodation for an intimate gathering of 12 guests spanning across six exquisite cabins, one of which includes a full-beam master suite. Low-profile bulwarks allow an uninterrupted view of the waters from the comfortable lounge on the main deck while the upper deck features a dining table seating ten.

Accompanying impressive aesthetics, Fortitude1 doesn’t falter in functionality. A clever layout, generous storage, and a cruising range of 4,100 nautical miles, make it an ideal vessel for long-range voyages.

Benetti, with a solid name equated to heritage, quality, and innovation, has consistently rewarded the unwavering faith that its clients place in them. This level of customer faith brings great pride, says Daniela Petrozzi, sales director at Benetti.
Notably, this launch comes during a period bustling with activity at Benetti, amidst the recent announcement of the 49.9-meter XWave and an astonishing 53 underway superyacht projects.

title: Experience the Excitement of Open Water Dinghy Racing at the Starcross Yacht Club's 2025 River Exe Regatta
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Experience the Excitement of Open Water Dinghy Racing at the Starcross Yacht Club's 2025 River Exe Regatta
summary: Embrace the opportunity to experience the thrill of open-water dinghy racing at the upcoming 2025 River Exe Regatta, hosted by Starcross Yacht Club.
body: Starcross Yacht Club serves up perhaps one of the most exhilarating sailing events of the year, hosting the River Exe Regatta of 2025. Bienvenu sailors of all skill levels! Open to all, this unmissable occasion promises two days of non-stop action on the 19th and 20th July. Participants are welcomed from boats with a PY from 790, like the swift RS800, to 1445, akin to the Tera Sport.

Adding to the sense of competition, separate prizes will be available for Juniors; anyone under 18 by the 1st of September will be keen to get their hands on these. Roll up, roll up, entries open on July 5th via the Regatta Website.

In the spirit of inclusivity, the Regatta is divided into three fleets; each run from two committee boats. So, whether you're a seasoned sailor or a novice with a passion for the sport, the River Exe Regatta is the beacon for all those who have their sights set on a stellar sailing experience in 2025.

title: Dive into the Exciting World of June Marine Auctions, Unmissable Oppurtunity for Boating Connoisseurs

summary: Witness the allure of the open sea with the upcoming June Marine Auctions. From breathtaking vessels to coveted marina berths, this auction has it all.
body: As the calendar flips to June, anticipation builds among the marine community. An event like no other—the June Marine Auction—is right around the corner. Bidding opens for this nautical extravaganza on the 20th of June, lasting until the 26th. The event holds particular appeal to boating enthusiasts with an array of vessels and marina berths up for bid.

Being an online event, the auction's reach is geographically boundless. Bidders from around the world can vie for their dream boat or secure a highly sought after marina berth. This extended bidding setup further enhances the experience, making it a must-attend for marine hobbyists and professionals alike.

Another exciting announcement of this forthcoming auction is the acceptance of entries for the July edition. So, whether you missed the opportunity to list your possession this time, or are already looking forward to the next, Marine Auctions are ready for your submissions.

There's more. The auction extends beyond the selling and buying of marine entities. Necessities such as boat insurance and vessel valuations come as added services. Certified professionals at Marine Valuations are ready to assist, ensuring you sail along smoothly.

In conclusion, the June Marine Auction is not just an event; it's an experience. Offering everything a mariner could wish for: dream vessels, coveted positions, and unwavering support. Make sure to mark your calendar and prepare to take part in this milestone marine event. Set sail towards your maritime dreams with the June Marine Auctions!

title: Round the Island Race 2025
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: Round the Island Race 2025
summary: Good luck to all taking part in today's the Round the Island Race 2025, 7th June. Organised by the Island Sailing Club, this annual spectacle draws over 1,700 boats and 16,000 sailors, making it one of the largest yacht races globally and the fourth largest mass participation sporting event in the UK.
body: Since its inception in 1931, the Round the Island Race has embraced a 'Race for All' ethos, welcoming a diverse fleet ranging from professional crews and Olympians to enthusiastic amateurs and family teams. This inclusivity fosters a unique camaraderie, with all participants navigating the same 50.1 nautical mile course around the Isle of Wight.

Starting from the Royal Yacht Squadron line in Cowes, the fleet sails westward, passing landmarks such as The Needles Lighthouse, St. Catherine’s Point, and Bembridge Ledge Buoy, before returning to Cowes. The course offers both challenges and breathtaking views, making it a favourite among sailors and spectators alike.
Spectator Highlights For those onshore, the race offers numerous vantage points:
Live updates and tracking will be available on the official website and social media channels, ensuring fans can follow the action in real-time .

Entries are open to all sailing enthusiasts. Whether you're a seasoned racer or a newcomer, the event offers an unparalleled experience. For registration details, visit the official Round the Island Race website.

Beyond the race, Cowes transforms into a vibrant hub of festivities, with events, music, and local cuisine celebrating the spirit of sailing. Whether you're competing or spectating, the Round the Island Race 2025 promises an unforgettable experience. For more information and updates, visit www.roundtheisland.org.uk

title: RYA Steps Up as Community Impact Partner for the Thrilling Emirates Great Britain Sail Grand Prix
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: RYA Steps Up as Community Impact Partner for the Thrilling Emirates Great Britain Sail Grand Prix
summary: The Royal Yachting Association (RYA) enhances its commitment to community engagement by partnering with the prestigious Emirates Great Britain Sail Grand Prix.
body: The build-up to the much-anticipated Emirates Great Britain Sail Grand Prix ignites with the announcement of the Royal Yachting Association (RYA) as its Official Community Impact Partner. This collaboration with SailGP represents a major partnership aimed at fostering connection with the local waters.

RYA’s energetic program is a celebration of community, inclusivity, and the belief that every young person, irrespective of their background, should get an opportunity to be stirred by the ocean experiences and grasp the opportunities that life on water offers. Alongside SailGP, they are creating various programs aimed at the local youth of Portsmouth as part of their ‘Better Sport’ initiative. This includes showcasing local young wing foilers, a STEM-based challenge and elements of engagement through sport in collaboration with the 1851 Trust.

RYA’s commitment is further exemplified through the launching of its Hampshire Virtual Impact League in association with Energise Me. By bringing marine-based STEM learning right into classrooms, this initiative leaves no stone unturned in stirring curiosity and creativity among students ahead of the big race weekend.

As the Emirates Great Britain Sail Grand Prix gears up and the excitement builds, the RYA stands ready to welcome the public in their stand at the heart of the SailGP Race Village. Here they offer interactive activities, expert guidance and, significantly, facilitate connections with local clubs and training centres, ensuring that the passion for boating is nurtured and sustained. They continue to demonstrate their commitment to sharing the joy of sailing experiences with each passing wave and each heave of the mainsail.

title: At the Cusp of Victory, American Magic Quantum Racing Shines on Day 4 of the Galicia 52 Super Series Royal Cup
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: At the Cusp of Victory, American Magic Quantum Racing Shines on Day 4 of the Galicia 52 Super Series Royal Cup
summary: Leaderboard spots shift as the winds pick up at the intense Galicia 52 Super Series Royal Cup, with American Magic Quantum Racing making a solid leap forward.
body: Day 4 of the Galicia 52 Super Series Royal Cup brought about thrilling turns on the blue waters as American Magic Quantum Racing leapt forward in the competition. Guided by Terry Hutchinson and helmed by Harry Melges IV, the US-flagged team capitalized on the 11-14kts winds to consolidate their leading position. Despite a slightly mixed performance, with a 7th and 3rd place finish, their sustained overall performance promises an imminent victory, their first 52 SUPER SERIES regatta win since 2022.

Meanwhile, the competition surged behind them. After a standout performance, boasting a 1st and 2nd place finish, Andrea Lacorte's Italian Alkedo Vitamina climbed to second overall. A fine example of the racing team's resilience and adaptability, Alkedo Vitamina capitalized on the rapidly changing wind and weather conditions, shaping the race-day landscape.

The first race saw the brilliance of Takashi Okura's Sled, closely followed by Alkedo and Paprec. Showing superior adaptability, Alkedo managed to lead at the leeward gate, leaving American Magic Quantum Racing grappling with Platoon Aviation for the seventh and eighth positions.

Provezza, helmed by John Cutler, shook up the second race. After getting the best of the first upwind; they managed to maintain a close lead against the surging Alkedo. Despite this, Provezza’s difficulty in capturing the shift and stronger breeze lost them their lead. This resulted in a riveting race, ultimately won by Provezza, their first race win of the season.

As they approach the final racing day, the American Magic Quantum Racing Team has the Royal Cup within their grasp with a modest performance being enough for them to secure victory. With just their second 52 Super Series under their belt, the second-place Italian team, Alkedo, also delivered a striking performance. This year’s Galicia 52 Super Series Royal Cup demonstrated the epitome of strategic sailing, where the slightest shift on the leaderboard was determined by seamless adaptation to every gust and wave.

title: Incident Analysis Sheds Light on Safety Protocols for Superyachts: A Case Study of a Fire on a Large Motoryacht
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Incident Analysis Sheds Light on Safety Protocols for Superyachts: A Case Study of a Fire on a Large Motoryacht
summary: An unfamiliar event on a large motoryacht brings to light the rigors of safety protocols in dry-docking and relocating maritime vessels.
body: A newly released case study from CHIRP Maritime's Superyacht Feedback, an industry-first superyacht-specific programme dedicated to improving safety, sheds light on a fire incident. The fire occurred aboard a large motoryacht after a dry-dock period, highlighting some crucial areas for improvement in the maritime domain. To ensure the safety of a vessel during a repair period where shore power isn't available, it is essential to employ specific measures which, unfortunately, were overlooked in this instance.

Other noticeable inadequacies included the challenge of operating the emergency fire pump, an inoperative emergency generator, the absence of smoke detectors and atmosphere testing equipment, and a faulty UPS battery of the fire system. All of these combined made it difficult for the emergency team to respond effectively. Moreover, both a lack of familiarity with the CO2 system's release procedure and difficulty accessing the CO2 cabinet resulted in incomplete CO2 system activation.

An exhaustive examination post-incident revealed that the fire resulted from exhaust gas accumulation due to a leak in the exhaust system and a malfunctioning exhaust valve. Restricted air circulation from the closed dampers exacerbated the situation. On top of it, a misconnected compressed air hose led to the failure of the CO2 system.

This incident emphasises the importance of effective communication, sound technical equipment, and thorough familiarity with safety procedures in safeguarding maritime vessels and their crews. Learning from such instances refines safety protocols, preparing us better for any such future unforeseen events. Averting potential hazards is a significant part of enhancing the experience of sea exploration.

title: Discover How a Yacht Miracle Worker Uses His Maritime Skills to Enrich the World of Bespoke Furniture Design
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover How a Yacht Miracle Worker Uses His Maritime Skills to Enrich the World of Bespoke Furniture Design
summary: Renowned shipwright Jonathan Minnebo is transforming the world of furniture design with his maritime touch, all made possible with West System epoxy.
body: After leaving a sparkling wave of awe at the 2025 Australian Wooden Boat Festival with his exquisitely restored Derwent-Class yacht, Gremlin, Jonathan Minnebo sought new waters to navigate. Applying his seasoned expertise in shipbuilding and a love for specialty timber, he plunged into the world of furniture and staircase design, establishing his own venture, Jonathan Minnebo Design, to grace Tasmanian and mainland clients with his unrivalled craftsmanship. His creation process marries the precise work ethic of a shipwright with the artistic flair of a bespoke furniture designer. Challenging the boundaries of these professions, he skillfully conjures exquisite pieces, from revitalising a deck damaged by freshwater ingress to crafting stylish record player cabinets out of Tasmanian Oak. With every project, whether it's designing a staircase for an under-construction house in Geeveston or creating deck hatches and butterfly skylight hatches from Queensland Maple, Minnebo redirects the sailing tide towards the shore. Securing the vitality of his creations is the impeccable West System epoxy from ATL Composites that he bases his trust on. When asked why he uses West System epoxy, the answer was obvious, 'dependability'. He elaborates on how he relies on its curing capabilities even during Tasmania's bracing months, offering comfort and trust for his clients, especially critical for mast construction and structural repair. Along with Epifanes' range of varnishes, particularly the Epifanes PP Extra, Minnebo adores his work's perfect finishing touch. Appreciating its ability to quickly build grain-filling coats, he emphasized the difference it makes in his work efficiency in Tasmania's climate and ultimate UV protection. In demonstrating the astonishing adaptability of his craft, Minnebo breathes life into the underappreciated connection between maritime pursuits and terrestrial creativity. Whether viewed from sea or land, the impressive applications of West System epoxy are indeed glaringly undeniable.

title: Northern Ireland's Ballyholme Yacht Club Hosts Enthralling Women on Water Festival 2025
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Northern Ireland's Ballyholme Yacht Club Hosts Enthralling Women on Water Festival 2025
summary: Northern Ireland's Ballyholme Yacht Club recently played host to the Women on Water Festival 2025, an event dedicated to encouraging female participation in sailing and other water-based activities.
body: Ballyholme Yacht Club in Northern Ireland recently became the setting for the Women on Water Festival 2025, a unique event aimed to inspire, equip and empower women and girls with the necessary confidence and skills to engage in sailing and other water-based pursuits. Hosted by RYA Northern Ireland, this event is designed chiefly for those with little to no sailing experience and offers a wealth of different water-based activities under professional guidance.

This festival is part and parcel of RYA Northern Ireland's Women On Water programme. This initiative, which has been running for more than a decade, was launched to stimulate an influx of women and girls into the realms of sailing and boating. Numerous studies have revealed that when women are provided with opportunities to hone their abilities in a supportive, positive environment, they are more likely to take part in a sport and stick with it.

In 2023, RYA Northern Ireland launched 'Navigating the Future', a bold five-year strategy aimed at enhancing diversity within the sport. Fast-forward to 2025, RBCA, a reputable chartered accountancy firm based in Belfast, proudly became the first-ever sponsor of the Women on Water programme. This pioneering partnership, set to provide support over an initial three years, will foster greater awareness of further events and foster the implementation of a broader range of Women On Water-focused programs at local sailing clubs throughout the region.

RYA Northern Ireland is on an unwavering quest to boost female participation across all clubs in the region. It is evident that such events are bridging gaps, breaking barriers, and crafting greater diversity in a sport that is enjoyed by all. They resonate with inspiring stories of empowerment, while winding integral threads of unity into the fabric of the broader sailing community.

title: Experience Unforgettable Mediterranean Getaways Aboard the Exquisite M/Y Omnia
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Experience Unforgettable Mediterranean Getaways Aboard the Exquisite M/Y Omnia
summary: Luxury meets comfort in M/Y Omnia, the 23.90m Pearl Yachts, waiting to take you on a quintessential Mediterranean voyage.
body: Step aboard the M/Y Omnia, a motor yacht that combines contemporary elegance with modern comfort. Designed to accommodate up to six guests, it offers the perfect setting for a memorable summer in the South of France or Italy. Built in 2018, by Pearl Yachts, the yacht is designed by Bill Dixon and features spectacular deck areas making it a sight to behold. From the outdoor dining area to the bar and waterfall jacuzzi, one can enjoy all the luxury ocean holidays have to offer.

The deck's generous space and sophisticated design make the yacht perfect for groups seeking the Mediterranean's allure. Sip cocktails at sea, savour meals in the alfresco dining area, or unwind on the spacious seating and sun pads. The retractable roof ensures shade whenever necessary, allowing guests to bask in panoramic views, sunbathe, or cool off as they please.

Providing endless entertainment options, Omnia is equipped with a Bang & Olufsen sound system and a rich movie and music library. The abundant onboard toys, like paddleboards, inflatables, fishing gear and a 3.9m Williams jet tender, enhance the on-water enjoyment. Added to all these is a jet ski, available for licensed guests.

M/Y Omnia sets new standards in luxury sailing, beckoning you to enjoy unforgettable ocean escapades. Starting from €44,000 per week, charters are available via West Nautical in the South of France or Italy.

title: Sea4All: Uplifting the Spirit of Inclusion with Thrilling Sea Sports Adventures in Lignano, Italy
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Sea4All: Uplifting the Spirit of Inclusion with Thrilling Sea Sports Adventures in Lignano, Italy
summary: Tiliaventum’s project, Sea4All, propels the inclusivity concept at sea, offering barrier-free water sports activities in Lignano, Italy.
body: Sea4All, the remarkable initiative brought to life by the Tiliaventum non-profit sports association in Lignano Sabbiadoro, Northeast Italy, is changing the way we view sea-based activities. Supremely excuse-free, the initiative provides a spectrum of sea sports experiences, from sailing, kite-surfing, fishing, to sea-side picnics, and welcomes everyone regardless of their physical, mental, or economic circumstances. The beauty lies in the fact that all activities are free of charge, made possible through community support and attention to accessible venues and equipment.

Through the year, the trained and dedicated team of Sea4All fosters engagement by organizing a cornucopia of sea-related events and activities that are even more appealing during the bright, sunny season, with the gentle afternoon breezes creating the ideal sailing condition for both novices and seasoned sailors.

Sea4All works with a variety of water craft. Their unique ‘Càpita,' a daysailer vessel, even allows individuals with disabilities to steer the helm, fill the sails, and participate in non-specific Paralympic regattas. They also have the ‘4All,' a motor-powered pontoon boat that opens up options for fishing outings or trials of Kite4All and Wake4All, or even SitPaddling, thanks to specially set-up equipment.

Sea4All is a proud participant in the epic Barcolana, the renowned regatta that draws more than 2,000 boats, adding further emphasis to their cornerstone of inclusivity. With regional support from entities like the Friuli Venezia Giulia region, Zampa Foundation, and many others who believe in the importance of inclusivity, Sea4All has charted new waters in adventure tourism, making waves that are set to ripple far beyond Italy's shores.

title: Aboard M/Y Orion: Discover the Refinement and Elegance of this Unique Van der Valk Masterpiece
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Aboard M/Y Orion: Discover the Refinement and Elegance of this Unique Van der Valk Masterpiece
summary: Step aboard and immerse yourself in the opulence of M/Y Orion, a modern embodiment of nautical craftsmanship, from its intricate detailing to her streamlined silhouette.
body: Picture this: You're adventuring across the open sea, swaying gently with the rhythmic dance of the waves while luxuriously ensconced within the elegant hull and streamlined contours of the 24.6m motor yacht, M/Y Orion. Her majestic frame, constructed by renowned Dutch builders Van der Valk, is a bespoke Continental Two model hallmarked by a widened beam and hardtop flybridge.

Outfitted with finesse and meticulous attention to detail, Orion is an exceptional yacht with a revered reputation. She flaunts an impressive pedigree, having undergone an extensive technical overhaul in early 2023, swiftly followed by an interior rejuvenation. Existing as a paradigm of opulence, Orion’s unique exterior and interior styling was penned by Van der Valk. Victorian-inspired accents intricately adorning her interiors elevate the vessel's grandeur, while plush fabrics and materials create an atmosphere of understated luxury.

In terms of technical design, Orion showcases extraordinary specifications. Her semi-displacement aluminium hull and superstructure are built to CE Category A classification society rules. She cruises comfortably at an impressive 21.5 knots, propelled by 3 Volvo Penta (D13-800) 800hp diesel engines, and can reach a top speed of 26.7 knots. The yacht also provides accommodation for two crew members onboard.

Now, M/Y Orion is listed for sale at €2,490,000 through West Nautical in Tivat, Montenegro. Those interested in the vessel are encouraged to visit the West Nautical website or contact the brokerage directly for further information.

title: Celebrating the Sale of the Seventh Moonen 122 Martinique to a Well-Versed American Enthusiast
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Celebrating the Sale of the Seventh Moonen 122 Martinique to a Well-Versed American Enthusiast
summary: Moonen Yachts is elated to announce the sale of its 37.4-metre Martinique series yacht, the Moonen 122 Martinique YN205.
body: Moonen Yachts proudly announced the sale of the seventh offering in its distinguished Martinique series, the 37.4-metre Moonen 122 Martinique YN205. The deal, the second in-house sale since the appointment of IYC as Moonen's global sales partner, was executed through Matthew Stone and Richard Gray, both of whom also act as global representatives for Moonen Yachts. An experienced, discerning American yachtsman, captivated by the model’s open-plan layout and harmonious relationship between indoor and outdoor living, acquired the under-construction yacht.

The Dutch yard's focus on craftsmanship and personalisation is eloquently mirrored through the interiors, conceived by Hollander Yacht Design. The vessel, a remarkable blend of steel and aluminium, boasts of exterior styling by René van der Velden and naval architecture by Diana Yacht Design. The client has sought several unique elements, one of them being a Jacuzzi.

Being powered by twin Caterpillar engines and promising a high speed of 17 knots and a cruising speed of 14.5 knots, the 345GT Moonen 122 Martinique will be delivered later this year. After the delivery, the motor yacht will leave the Netherlands to reach its homeport on the East Coast of the United States.

title: A Dive into Pearl 63 Luxury Yacht's Accommodations and Upgrades - The Epitome of Elegance for Eight
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A Dive into Pearl 63 Luxury Yacht's Accommodations and Upgrades - The Epitome of Elegance for Eight
summary: The Pearl 63 yacht, renowned for its comfort and deluxe accommodations, is introducing a sleek set of upgrades to its design, setting new benchmarks in luxury sailing.
body: For individuals who savour the joy and adventure of sailing, the Pearl 63 yacht offers an elevating experience with a perfect blend of comfort and luxury. This refined vessel carries the honour of being the smallest in modern Pearl fleet, yet it unarguably holds a grand accommodation capability, offering eight berths with the unique choice of a proper crew cabin.

This latest version of the Pearl 63 draws its inspiration from the successful and multi-award-winning predecessor, the Pearl 62. The new installment introduces several upgrades, most notably an enhanced aft cockpit featuring stunning dining tables, opening balconies on either side, and an innovatively designed L-shaped sofa. The sofa boasts a backrest that intriguingly flips over to face out over the balcony, a testament to the yacht's commitment to comfort and luxury.

The inside of the Pearl 63 is just as impressive as the outside. There's an upgraded, full-size dining table and a more social lounge area. All crafted in four appealing interior schemes: Modern, Luxury, Monochrome, and Indulgence. The full-beam owner's suite includes private staircase access and his-and-hers wardrobes. The Pearl 63 also ensures solid performance at sea, promising top speeds of around 27-33 knots, depending on the engine upgrade.

The Pearl 63 Yacht places itself among the pinnacles of luxury sailing with its enhanced upgrades, proving once again that Pearl has mastered the art of creating luxurious, practical and enduring vessels.

title: Thrilling Weekend Regattas at Staunton Harold and Draycote Water Sailing Clubs
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Thrilling Weekend Regattas at Staunton Harold and Draycote Water Sailing Clubs
summary: Experience the surge of adventure as we reflect on the sensational sailing competitions that recently swept Staunton Harold and Draycote Water Sailing Clubs.
body: The weekend was a slice of sailor's paradise at the Midlands where Staunton Harold and Draycote Water Sailing Clubs hosted their thrilling regattas.

Staunton Harold Sailing Club proudly kicked off the first Miracle class event of the year over the bank holiday weekend in late May, overcoming a challenging forecast. Despite the gusty winds, five determined boats, including one home team and four visiting teams, took to the water. The exciting races unfurled dynamically, with Miracle sailors setting sail after the Graduate Nationals' flotilla. Dave Turtle and Zara Frankton made their presence felt immediately with their superior downwind sailing skills, seizing the lead and securing a critical victory.

Both events encapsulated the heart and spirit of sailing - the tension of the starting line, the exhilaration of the race, and the satisfaction of crossing the finish line. These regattas serve as a reminder of why sailors brave the waves - for the camaraderie, the challenge, and, above all, the unrivalled thrill of racing on the open water.

title: Adventure and Resilience Shine at the Miracle Midlands Sailing Championship
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Adventure and Resilience Shine at the Miracle Midlands Sailing Championship
summary: The Miracle Midlands Championship brought a heady mix of endurance and camaraderie to the waters of Staunton Harold Sailing Club.
body: The Staunton Harold Sailing Club played host to the thrilling Miracle Midlands Championship over the Whit Bank Holiday weekend. David Turtle and Zara Frankton emerged as the formidable team to beat, leading the charge in a challenging environment. The blustery conditions cancelled the plans of at least three teams, leaving the waters open for five resilient boats, four visitors and one home team, to contest the championship.

Race 1 established the tone of the event. Graham Watts and Helen Jacks of the home team raised the anticipation by leading the fleet around the windward mark. However, Turtle and Frankton soon made their mark, overtaking the fleet with their formidable downwind prowess, leaving Watts and Jacks to fight pressure from the other competitors. Turtle and Frankton held on to clinch the first victory of the championship.

Sunday brought a similar forecast, but the teams agreed to sail only two back-to-back morning races. In Race 3, Watts and Helen's daring strategy of hard sailing right to the farmhouse bank saw them secure a comfortable lead. A wind shift later allowed Turtle and Frankton to pass by, while Watts and Jacks managed to grasp onto the second position. Despite the blustery conditions, the sailing championship brought out the best in resilience, competitiveness, and teamwork.

title: The Exquisite Luxury Superyacht Lady Azul, Now Available with a €1M Reduction in Asking Price
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Exquisite Luxury Superyacht Lady Azul, Now Available with a €1M Reduction in Asking Price
summary: The opulent Heesen-built superyacht, Lady Azul, sees million-euro discount, offering discerning buyers an elevated and adventurous sea experience.
body: The magnificent superyacht Lady Azul, crafted meticulously by the Dutch shipyard Heesen in 2001, sees a generous €1M price reduction. Co-listed for sale with Matthew Gusman of TWW yachts, this sea-treading beauty speaks volumes about luxury, superiority, and an unparalleled opulence. Purchased by her existing owner in 2019, Lady Azul instantly entered an eight-month refit period that saw her pump up with major technical and capital upgrades. The result was a remarkable odyssey spanning more than 20,000 nautical miles over five years en-route the captivating Southeast Asia.

Anchored currently in the enchanting Pattaya, Thailand, Lady Azul's reduced price tag stands at a competitive €6,950,000. Boasting a broad-beamed owner's suite situated on the main deck, two equally capacious VIP suites, and other luxurious rooms, she can easily make room for ten guests. A king-size bed, a private study, and a walk-in wardrobe further add to the grandeur of the owner's stateroom. The generous open-plan layout allows for seamless interaction among the crew of seven and the guests.

The sumptuous main saloon fuses comfort with sophistication, thanks to the plush seating, rich contemporary materials, and an advanced entertainment system. An extended warm space in the skylounge adds to the royal feel. Quite the crowning jewel of the yacht, the sundeck serves as a relaxation and entertainment hotspot, offering amenities for a perfect cruising experience. Look forward to lounging in the sun, dining al fresco, enjoying barbecues, or cool off in the netted lap pool. The beach club at the stern is an expedition into water sports, promoting activities like snorkelling, paddleboarding, wakeboarding, and more. A Williams Diesel Jet 5.5-metre tender ensures seamless shore excursions.

title: The Pristine Overmarine Motor Yacht, Sayonara, Heralds as a Perfect Turnkey Vessel for Discerning Buyers
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Pristine Overmarine Motor Yacht, Sayonara, Heralds as a Perfect Turnkey Vessel for Discerning Buyers
summary: Presenting a splendid opportunity for avid seafarers, the 28.7-metre Overmarine motor yacht Sayonara is now for sale.
body: Created in unobstructed detail by the renowned Italian yard and designed by Stefano Righini, the third part of the Mangusta 94 series yacht, Sayonara, offers untapped access to the charms of the sea. Since its delivery in 2015, it has been meticulously maintained and regularly upgraded, offering a satisfying experience to any owner looking for a ready-to-sail vessel. As of now, Sayonara is harboured in sunny Florida, listed at a reasonable price of $4,250,000, with US duty already paid. Comprising a double and a versatile twin, in addition to a full-beam master suite, Sayonara can comfortably accommodate six guests in its generously-sized cabins. Natural light is in abundance thanks to the large windows, whilst the en suite encompasses dual sinks and a spacious glass-enclosed shower, setting precedents in luxury and convenience. The yacht's main deck decor emphasises relaxation and social interaction, with a plush dining table, a wrap-around sofa and a bar set aft. The lower deck of the yacht stands as an intimate sanctuary for peaceful retreats, movie nights or relaxation after day-long water expeditions. Creating a perfect balance between luxury and practicality, Sayonara’s exterior layout seamlessly integrates bow to stern. Guests seeking an alfresco dining experience can enjoy leisurely meals outdoors, with the placement of sunpads allowing for unwinding under the sun. The spacious sunpad offers additional seating options and a large sunpad adds to the exterior aesthetics. The yacht's crowned gem, the flybridge, offers unobstructed 360-degree views, making it an ideal setting for socialising and taking in panoramic visions. Under the hood, Sayonara is powered by twin MTU M94 engines with water jet propulsion, and can glide at a cruising speed of 32 knots, with a top speed of 36 knots. Her draught of 1.6-metre ensures access to remote destinations, opening up options for island hopping and day trips to places like the Bahamas. The Overmarine Sayonara yacht thus combines state-of-the-art design with a bespoke sailing experience, presenting a prime investment opportunity for those drawn by the allure of the waves.

title: Betting a head of Mubadala New York Sail Grand Prix
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: SailGP Hits the Bookies as High-Speed Catamarans Return to New York
summary: SailGP Hits the Bookies as High-Speed Catamarans Return to New York. SailGP, the high-octane, data-fuelled racing league that’s turned sailing into a stadium sport, has dropped anchor in the world of sports betting. Just ahead of this weekend’s Mubadala New York Sail Grand Prix (June 7–8), the global series is now letting fans back their hunches with a wager or two.
body: That means you can now put your money where your mainsail is—DraftKings in the U.S. and Bet365 elsewhere will be taking bets on everything from fleet race winners to who’ll lift the championship silverware. Head-to-head showdowns? Finalists? Season champs? It’s all up for grabs, and it’s all powered by a swirling sea of data.

According to SailGP’s managing director, Andrew Thompson, the move is all about engagement: “We’re using the data that drives our sport to enhance how fans experience it—responsibly.” And when he says “data,” he’s not bluffing. The tech behind SailGP collects a wild 270,000 data points per second, creating live odds and probabilities faster than you can say “foiling gybe.”

Helping stitch this digital rigging together is Abelson Sports, with support from iGame Media, delivering low-latency broadcasts so punters and pundits alike can follow the action with barely a breath of delay.

Behind the spectacle is a fleet of identical 50-foot foiling catamarans, each representing one of 12 national teams, ripping along at over 60mph—yes, that’s faster than the wind itself. Add to that the tight, gladiatorial racecourses nestled close to shorelines, and you’ve got a new kind of regatta: part sailing, part motorsport, and part high-stakes chess match.

The next chapter unfolds in New York City this weekend, and the buzz is building. Tickets are moving fast—so whether you’re in the grandstands, glued to a screen, or quietly slipping a tenner on Team Australia to win the final, SailGP is offering more ways than ever to get in on the action.
Hold onto your hats. The sea’s never been this sharp. More info at: SailGP.com/betting

title: Under the Microscope: The Rise and Dip of the Multihull Market & Surging Yacht Sales Value
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Under the Microscope: The Rise and Dip of the Multihull Market & Surging Yacht Sales Value
summary: The yachting industry experiences dramatic shifts as multihull production faces a dip, and yacht sales value majestically rises.
body: As the world turns, so too does the boating industry. With multihulls becoming much admired since 2020, it has been surprising to witness a recent dip in their production levels. Despite continuous growth previously, experts are starting to question the long-term demand for these vessels.

On the other side of the aisle, the yacht brokerage sector is on a different trajectory. In comparison to the sibir,ging multihull sector, the may of yacht sales displayed a dramatic upturn. According to exclusive data, the sales for yachts of 24 metres or above reached a stunning €927.5 million.

title: A Look at the Futuristic Design of the Vibrant T57: An Unrivaled Luxury Motor Yacht Experience
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A Look at the Futuristic Design of the Vibrant T57: An Unrivaled Luxury Motor Yacht Experience
summary: Get a glimpse of the alluring T57, a trailblazer of luxury motor yachts. This treasure is peppered with premium amenities and high-tech solutions for an unmatched sailing experience.
body: Embark on a journey with the T57, a beacon of luxury motor yachts that is certain to turn heads. The 28.49-metre Argo 90 model showcases advanced design lines that are both progressive and dynamic, embodying the futuristic vision of its creators, Officina Italiana Design.

The interior of the T57 stands out with an array of esteemed Italian design pieces. This mesmerizing yacht comfortably accommodates eight in four ensuite cabins. The owner’s suite is conveniently situated on the main deck, alongside a full-beam VIP cabin, a double guest room, and a twin cabin.

The intricacies of the T57 are reflected in its performance as well. With a 26-knot top speed, the T57 is all set for high-speed island hopping or convenient coastal cruises. This epitome of luxury and quality has been on yachtsmen’s covet list for a while - as Riva, an esteemed name in the yachting industry, stands behind it. From cruising on the coastline with loved ones to a leisurely lunch at anchor, the Argo 90 indeed offers a superior experience.

title: Exploring Wild Thing 100's Innovative Updates Set to Challenge Sydney-Auckland Ocean Race Record
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Exploring Wild Thing 100's Innovative Updates Set to Challenge Sydney-Auckland Ocean Race Record
summary: The revamped Wild Thing 100, under the direction of Grant Wharington, is primed for a record-breaking attempt in the Sydney to Auckland Ocean Race.
body: Grant Wharington has revved up his vessel, Wild Thing 100, ready to challenge the best in the highly anticipated Sydney to Auckland Ocean Race. Keenly sponsoring the race on the 1250 nautical mile stretch globally recognised as a 'tough little piece of ocean', Wharington and his team are primed for an intense competition.

Stay tuned as Rodney Keenan, a well-known captain and owner of Evolution Sails in Auckland, joins the racing team. The Wild Thing 100 has been prepared meticulously with a new mast suited for her size, reassuring a promising performance in the race.

Wild Thing 100's boat manager, Patrick Lambourne, who is a strong advocate of the race and completed the inaugural S2A race on Mayfair, will also be aboard to support the challenge. While the Comanche 100 with larger gear might be the only competition in sight, Wharington explains that Wild Things possesses a little more righting moment than peers like Wild Oats and Black Jack.

As Wharington and his competent crew aim to set new benchmarks in the Sydney to Auckland Ocean Race, it means much more than just an adventure at sea. It's an iconic event in the offshore yachting scene that carries the excitement of true offshore sailing. From the young to the experienced, this race brings together a wide spectrum of sailors from across the world who carry the love for vast blue waters.

title: Azimut Yachts Furthers Ventures into Asia-Pacific Region with New Partnerships in Indonesia and Australia
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Azimut Yachts Furthers Ventures into Asia-Pacific Region with New Partnerships in Indonesia and Australia
summary: Azimut Yachts boost its presence in the Asia-Pacific region through partnerships with leading dealers Europa Yachts in Indonesia and Short Marine in Australia.
body: Azimut Yachts, a world-renowned Italian luxury motoryacht manufacturer, has recently widened its global reach by establishing two new strategic partnerships in the Asia-Pacific market. The company’s forward-thinking expansion strategy has led them to collaborate with Europa Yachts in Indonesia and Short Marine in Australia, leveraging their respective market strengths to boost Azimut's presence in these regions. By aligning with these established marine dealers, Azimut seeks not only to deliver its stunning yachts to new buyers in these markets but also to offer exceptional post-sale service through their partners' extensive networks. This ensures an enhanced ownership experience for their customers, reinforcing Azimut's commitment to customer satisfaction. This expansion into Australia and Indonesia is a strategic move for Azimut, opening up lucrative markets and connecting with new demographics of luxury yacht enthusiasts. As yachting gains popularity in the Asia Pacific region, Azimut caravan's quick response to this growing demand demonstrates their business acuity and unwavering commitment to lead the luxury yachting industry.

title: A Unique Blend of Networking, Innovation and Inspiration at The Superyacht Forum 2025 and InNORvation '25
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A Unique Blend of Networking, Innovation and Inspiration at The Superyacht Forum 2025 and InNORvation '25
summary: Get ready for an elevated experience at The Superyacht Forum 2025— a key gathering of industry leaders. Also, revisiting the memorable InNORvation '25 event.
body: In less than six months, a spectacle awaits as leaders of the superyacht market will descend on Amsterdam for the reimagined The Superyacht Forum. The forum, now under the capable helm of Amsterdam RAI, will undergo a significant transition presenting a vibrant, future-focused edition that will distinguish itself from other industry conferences.

The Superyacht Forum, with fresh branding and an invigorating programme, will be a crowd puller. Attendees will observe firsthand the transformative changes to this premier event. The two-day format promises ample time for networking with key decision makers in the superyacht industry.

Reflections also lead us to another unforgettable event — InNORvation ’25. This invite-only assembly brought together 50 visionaries who spent 48 hours in Norway, sharing groundbreaking ideas against the backdrop of breathtaking views. Consisting of shipyard technical teams, naval architects, captains, managers, owners’ representatives, and leading Norwegian energy experts, the event was unique, creating an unforgettable atmosphere.

InNORvation '25, far from traditional superyacht hubs, stands out for its authentic connection and energy. It combined serious conversations with blue-sky thinking, culminating in an experience that remains etched in memory. As we move forward, these gatherings signify promising advancements for the superyacht industry.

title: Invigorate Your Sea and Shore Adventures with Henri-Lloyd's Dynamic Range of Sailing Apparel
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Invigorate Your Sea and Shore Adventures with Henri-Lloyd's Dynamic Range of Sailing Apparel
summary: Enhance your sailing journey and onshore fun with the innovative Dynamic line of apparel, crafted by Henri-Lloyd, the legendary sailing gear specialist.
body: Packing for a sailing adventure or a relaxing weekend on the water has just become simpler and considerably more stylish, thanks to the trailblazing Dynamic range of sailing t-shirts and shorts by Henri-Lloyd. A name synonymous with sailing gear innovation, Henri-Lloyd, has outdone itself with this range, setting new industry standards for functionality and comfort. The seamlessness of these designs transforms the sailing experience, so much so that one may forget they're wearing anything at all.

The Dynamic range epitomises a perfect synthesis of technology and ergonomics, offering remarkable flexibility through its revolutionary stretch. Be it the Dri Fast short and long sleeve t-shirts, or the water-repellent shorts, both prove ideal for on-the-water action or for unwinding on the shore. The incorporation of an ergonomic cut with panel design using stretch fabric in the Dri Fast short sleeve t-shirt is a standout feature, enhancing its comfort quotient multifold.

Included in the collection is the indispensable Dynamic deck short, ideal for onboard and onshore wear. Crafted from durable double weave stretch recycled fabric, these breathable DWR shorts offer supreme comfort through their ergonomic design. With careful consideration to common sailing issues like snags and chaffing, these shorts include a hard-wearing Cordura seat.

In the words of Knut Frostad, Executive Chairman at Henri-Lloyd, 'Our whole Dynamic range is taking stretch and flexibility to a completely new level in sailing.' Such forward-thinking design focus on comfort and utility ensures that this range isn't just a fleeting trend, but an integral part of the future of sailing apparel.

title: Frank Hugelmeyer Takes Reins as New President of International Council of Marine Industry Associations
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Frank Hugelmeyer Takes Reins as New President of International Council of Marine Industry Associations
summary: Frank Hugelmeyer, residing president of NMMA, is now also heading the prestigious ICOMIA for a two-year term.
body: The marine world witnesses a significant turning point as Frank Hugelmeyer, the standing president and CEO of the National Marine Manufacturers Association (NMMA), assumes an influential new role. Elected as the new president of the International Council of Marine Industry Associations' (ICOMIA) board, Hugelmeyer is set to chart a new course for the association over a two-year term.

His pristine experience and leadership caliber, honed at NMMA, promise a progressive tenure ahead for ICOMIA. Born out of a passion for the marine industries, Hugelmeyer's appointment as ICOMIA president reflects his dedication to this buoyant sector. He is expected to spearhead initiatives that will further the global expansion of the marine industry and contribute to a sustainable boating future.

title: Discover How Italy’s Top Yacht Builders are Thriving Amidst Industry Shifts
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover How Italy’s Top Yacht Builders are Thriving Amidst Industry Shifts
summary: Three trailblazing Italian shipbuilders unveil steady Q1 2025 earnings, charting a course amidst shifting tides in the yachting industry.
body: Italy’s top shipbuilding yards, namely Sanlorenzo, Ferretti Group, and The Italian Sea Group, have painted a promising picture of the sector by posting unswerving growth in their Q1 2025 figures. This trend comes amidst rapidly evolving industry dynamics, which seem to favour larger, custom-made vessels over small-scale composite yachts.

Ferretti, Sanlorenzo, and The Italian Sea Group reported revenue augmentation, ranging from 1% to an impressive near 10% year-on-year growth for Q1 2025. Despite the prevailing macroeconomic uncertainty that subdued small craft sales in the European and US markets, these shipbuilders continue to flourish. The companies attribute their sustained performance to robust order books, supported by a burgeoning demand for high-value builds.

Despite a superficial 48% slump in the Superyacht sector, buoyant sales reveal a different reality. Ferretti Group attributes this apparent drop to an extraordinary one-off deal in the previous year, valued at €64 million. However, the segment's ledger shows a positive trend, with a backlog swelling by over 50% year-on-year, exemplifying a consistent demand for larger, custom vessels.

Sanlorenzo, another heavy-hitter in the luxury yacht market, witnessed a 9.6% escalation in revenues. Just like Ferretti, Sanlorenzo’s Superyacht division and its recently acquired Finnish sailing yacht brand, Nautor Swan, spearheaded this growth. However, a softened demand for smaller vessels under 30 metres indicates a shift in the consumer preference.

In the face of industry changes and economic fluctuations, these Italian shipbuilders have seized the opportunity to align the growth trajectory with their strategic initiatives and technological innovation, thereby continuing their legacy of excellence.

title: Turkish Maritime Giant, Numarine, Boosts Product Line with Latest 37XP and 26XP Explorer Yachts
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Turkish Maritime Giant, Numarine, Boosts Product Line with Latest 37XP and 26XP Explorer Yachts
summary: Numarine, a Turkish yacht manufacturer, has launched two new units from its esteemed XP explorer yacht series, showcasing practicality and luxury on the water.
body: Numarine, a premier Turkish yacht yard, recently raised the curtain on two brand new offerings from its XP explorer yacht range: the 37XP and the 26XP. Both yachts are the embodiment of elegance, versatility, and resilience, crafted meticulously to cater to the adventurous seaborn dweller who appreciates the fusion of practicality and luxury.

Touting a length of 37.2 metres, the 37XP sits proudly as the current flagship of the range. It flaunts a full-displacement build, merging a sturdy steel hull with a composite superstructure, promising exceptional handling and seafaring capabilities. The largest Numarine model so far, the yacht glamorously incorporates soaring windows in the main saloon and cabins, an 83-square-metre open-air living space, and accommodates up to 14 passengers.

The launch of these yachts underscores Numarine's commitment to the production of stylish, performance-driven, and comfortable yachts. According to Ömer Malaz, Nummarine's chairman, the XP Series reaffirms its position as one of the most coveted ranges in the superyacht industry, noted for their impressive design, spacious interiors, and superior noise reduction.

With these two new models gracing the waters and nine other superyacht projects in the pipeline, including three from its new flagship series, the 40MXP, Numarine's future in the yachting industry seems as infinite as the oceans it conquers.

title: Record-sized fleet
author: Michael Hodges
imageAlt: RORC Centenary Rolex Fastnet Race
summary: Less than two months now remain until the start of the 2025 Rolex Fastnet Race, this year coinciding with the Royal Ocean Racing Club's centenary. Another huge fleet has entered. While 2023’s 50th edition of the event, that back in 1925 caused the RORC to be founded, saw a record 430 boats set sail, the 2025 entry list indicates that even this figure may be exceeded when the race starts from Cowes on 26 July, bound f
body: Although some have yet to qualify and there will be inevitable attrition, at present 464 yachts are entered of which a record 407 are in the IRC fleet, compared with 358 IRC yachts from 430 starters in 2023. Currently, boats are registered from 33 countries, including Brazil, Hong Kong, Kazakhstan, Latvia, Australia, New Zealand and Turkey, but with the majority from the UK (160) and France (130). Their crews are even more international, from 41 countries, including French Polynesia, Rwanda and Zimbabwe, with competitors ranging in age from 14 to 81.

The RORC’s centenary year will see the return of the Admiral’s Cup taking place for the first time since 2003. This series will begin with the Channel Race on 19 July, with the Rolex Fastnet Race as its conclusion. The RORC’s revitalised grand prix yacht racing series looks set to be a considerable success: 15 yacht clubs from as far away as New Zealand and Australia are fielding two boat teams, with crews including world and Olympic champions, round the world racers and America’s Cup winners. They are approaching the event with the same professionalism, commitment, resource and attention to detail that teams employed during the event’s previous peak in the 1980s and 90s, with new boats having been built and optimised especially for the event.

Remon Vos’ Black Jack 100 is one of the highest rated boats in the fleet The top prize for the Rolex Fastnet Race is the Fastnet Challenge Cup, awarded to the top boat in the IRC fleet. This may well go to one of the hotshot Admiral’s Cuppers, but could go to any of the best sailed boats from across the fleet, for aside from being by far the world’s largest offshore yacht race, the Rolex Fastnet Race is also by far the largest IRC event. Scratch boats are the 100 footers; Seng Huang Lee’s SHK Scallywag (with an IRC TCC of 1.950) and Remon Vos’ Black Jack 100 (1.947), but they will also be challenged by past line honours winner Joost Schuijff’s Leopard 3 (1.793) and several former VO70s including Roy Disney's heavily turboed Pyewacket 70 (1.762) and Christian Zugel's Tschüss 2 (1.612).

The slowest yachts racing in IRC Four, where currently the lowest-rated is Gavin Lockhart-Miram’s Contessa 32 Musketeer II (0.860), plus the yellow Westerly Fulmar 32 Fulmar Fever (0.873) campaigned by a team from the Dunmore East Sea School in Ireland (and a past competitor in 2017 and 2023) led by Robert Marchant. They are followed by two Sigma 33s, father and son duo Andy and Pelham Etherington’s Magic Moments (0.897) and Andrew Laming’s Falmouth-based Afrita (0.905).

Gavin Lockhart-Miram’s Contessa 32 Musketeer II will compete in IRC Four Credit One of the toughest competitions, carrying almost as much prestige as winning the Rolex Fastnet Race overall, is to top any of the race’s seven principal IRC classes, ranging from the line honours contenders in IRC Super Zero to the slowest in IRC Four. Thanks to the IRC rating system, winners can be of any sizes. Over the last 25 years they have ranged in rating from at 0.913 - Iromiguy, Jean-Yves Chateau’s Nicholson 33 winner in 2005 – to 1.627 - the Askew brothers’ turboed VO70 Wizard in 2019. Over this period four 70-something footers have won the Fastnet Challenge Cup and five 30-something footers.

Equally important are the many ‘races-with-a-race’ that go on between the one designs and other genres taking part in IRC Two, Three and Four. The largest of these is the JPK 1010 fleet of which there are currently 18 entered - father and son doublehanded Pascal and Alexis Loison famously having won the 2013 Rolex Fastnet Race overall aboard theirs, Night and Day. Also entered are 17 examples of the newer JPK 1030, including Foggy Dew of Noel Racine, whose previous JPK 1010 and 960 have won class four times. There are also 17 First 40s, 16 Sun Fast 3600s and 3200s, 15 Sun Fast 3300 and 10 J/109s, all enjoying some of the most competitive racing across the fleet.

Benoit Rousselin's JPK 1010 Delnic - Boats of any size can take the overall win in the Rolex Fastnet Race © ROLEX/Kurt Arrigo Beyond the IRC fleet are the high profile French ‘pro’ classes including the fastest multihulls in the world – the Ultim 32/23 trimarans, which this year will feature Banque Populaire, skippered by Armel le Cléac’h and Thomas Coville’s Sodebo. The IMOCA flying monohulls of the Vendée Globe and Ocean Race are well represented with a line-up including Jeremie Beyou’s Charal, which finished fourth in last year’s Vendée Globe and Teamwork-Team SNEF of Switzerland’s Justine Mettraux, who was the top female finisher, having come home eighth. While the two MOD70s Argo and Zoulou are racing in the broader MOCRA multihull class, the Ocean 50 trimarans have their own class with five presently entered, while there is a strong turn-out of 21 boats in the ever-popular Class40.

title: Historic Yacht Maemere Sees New Life as Restoration Efforts Gather Speed
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Historic Yacht Maemere Sees New Life as Restoration Efforts Gather Speed
summary: The classic 34.1-metre Maemere, narrowly saved from demolition, is currently undergoing a painstaking restoration process led by McMillen Yachts.
body: Making her graceful return from the brink of demolition is the classic 34.1-metre Trumpy yacht, Maemere. The yacht, having arrived at McMillen Yachts for a thorough restoration in 2022, is currently being rebuilt from the keel up under the talented direction of Newport-based studio, Langan Design. The process has seen the interiors of the vessel removed, with attention now turned towards re-planking the bow.

"The work hasreally picked up pace over the last year," shares Thomas Degrémont, partner at Langan Design, noting that the yacht has been reworked to approximate her original lines as closely as possible. "The owner is eager to retain some of the yacht’s original elements, such as the cast iron tubs and mouldings, promoting a blend of heritage and modernity in the refurbished design."

Due to damage from iron rot, much of Maemere's original wood needed replacement. Likewise, the yacht now boasts a new keel, floors, frames, planking, decking, and steel structure. However, wherever possible, the original hardware will be recycled, and the steel bulkheads have been retained, albeit with bolstered strength.

Just whiskers away from being discarded, Maemere was fortunately reprieved by Earl McMillen III, the president of McMillen Yachts. By introducing a party interested in rescuing the vessel, he orchestrated the vessel’s transition from California to Rhode Island.

Subsequent to an adventurous cross-country journey involving repairs, salvage, and finally transport from Mexico to Philadelphia, Maemere arrived at her new home in Rhode Island. Fatefully, the yacht was offloaded in the river, a stone's throw away from where she was first constructed in Camden, New Jersey, 93 years prior.
The project proves to be more than just a restoration; it's a story of revival, bringing back to life a piece of maritime history, one plank at a time.

title: InMind Design's Interstellar: A Groundbreaking Superyacht Concept with a Futuristic VIP Cabin
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: InMind Design's Interstellar: A Groundbreaking Superyacht Concept with a Futuristic VIP Cabin
summary: Italian design maestro InMind has a new vision for the yachting world – the 49.9 metre superyacht Interstellar, characterised by its bold aesthetic and exploratory design.
body: In an adventurous step into the future of yachting, Italian studio InMind Design sets a new bar by introducing its latest brainchild - the luxurious 49.9-metre superyacht, Interstellar. Boasting sporty black and white lines, an expansive aft deck, and a daringly creative aesthetic, this yacht is envisioned for those who seek to embody distinctiveness and audacity. Lorenzo Squadrito, the founder of InMind envisions an owner with a keen aesthetic sensitivity who sees yachting as a cultural expression and a daring vision.

Taking a step inside, the futuristic VIP cabin disarms with its artistic use of floor-to-ceiling curved windows and mirrors, creating a sense of expansive space. Meanwhile, the upper levels offer a formal al fresco dining space for 14 guests and a sundeck adorned with an intimate coffee table lounge. Among other highlights are a complementary tender designed by the creative minds of InMind, and a full-scale gym, complete with rows of treadmills and weights.

Interstellar indeed appears to be a superyacht for the future, striving to create a truly evergreen design. The aim, as put forth by Squadrito, was to create a fluid and enduring design icon. The specs confirm this ambition, with a 9.5-metre beam and draft of 2.3 metres, powered by twin CAT engines, Interstellar can certainly stand tall among its peers. This spaceship of the seas serves to reflect that yachting is not just about navigating the seas, but also navigating one's own luxurious identity.

title: Cantieri di Pisa’s Custom Division Launches Construction of the First 40-Meter Yacht since its 2021 Acquisition
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Cantieri di Pisa’s Custom Division Launches Construction of the First 40-Meter Yacht since its 2021 Acquisition
summary: The custom division of Italian shipyard, Cantieri di Pisa, has kicked off the construction of a 40-metre motor yacht.
body: The creation of a 40-metre motor yacht marks a significant milestone for the newly formed custom division of Cantieri di Pisa since the shipyard's 2021 acquisition. This is the first 30-metre-plus yacht to commence construction under Enrico Gennasio's ownership, with the delivery expected in February 2027.

Innovative technology plays a big role in the development of the yacht.
