title: Decoding the Harmony Between Noise and Silence: Is it Art Or Science?
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Decoding the Harmony Between Noise and Silence: Is it Art Or Science?
summary: In the heart of NYE's clamour, an interesting thought might strike your intellect: Is noise, the art of chaos, the science of tranquility?
body: Amid the New Year's Eve hullabaloo, an intriguing thought swims against the tide of the mind: is the cacophony of sounds, dances of discord, and symphony of shrills - a hypnotic, abstract art? And does the cloak of silence, the essence of serenity and the gate-keeper of tranquillity, then not become a meticulously studied science? Is the pandemonium of noise the painting of a passionate artist, and is the placidity of silence the formula of an erudite scientist?

The dancer’s foot-thuds, the musician’s strumming, the crowd’s hubbub, and the sea waves’ lullabies – these are all parts of the beautiful mayhem we call noise. The poignant paradox lies in the fact that this perceived disorder is the very soundtrack of our lives, animating our existence and giving rhythm to our daily dance of reality.

Sublimely, there is a meditative quality in noise, and a melodic tune in silence, showcasing a captivating relationship between both of them. In the silence, we find respite and in noise, we find life. So, is it possible that they are, in essence, varied manifestations of the same reality?

Ultimately, the sound of the sea, the art of noise, murmurs across the waves, seemingly lost but not silent, raising a toast to this question: does noise, in all its beauty and chaos, not represent the imperfect art of existence? And does silence, the epitome of stillness, not symbolise the studied science of peace?

We may harp on this delicate balance of sound and quiet as the night matures. Perhaps, it's a symphony where chaos and calm, noise and silence, art and science not only intertwine but also harmoniously coexist.

Overlooked by many, it is a necessary piece of maritime equipment lurking on the decks of sailing boats and yachts, waiting for an opportunity to cause mayhem.

Predominantly, a bitt is a pair of short stout posts on the deck of a ship for mooring lines when the vessel docks. Harmonising toasty comfort with icy sea speed entails more than just throwing on an extra jumper. It's about understanding the science of cold air resistance, manipulating your boat's alignment to cut through frigid winds, and being avant-garde in your wintry wardrobe choices.

Cold winter air can thicken, making it more challenging for your vessel to push through. Knowing how to adjust your alignment can drastically improve your speed performance, enabling you to maintain your pace, even in chilly climates.

The goal is not just about pushing the speedometer. body: Imagine this—an azure expanse, the sun's golden rays dancing on the ocean's skin,and suddenly, a man is overboard. This confession unveils a commonly disregarded truth among sailors—the grit and daring of sailing the seven seas also requires intricate planning and reiterated rehearsal of emergencies. This mariner's experience serves as a strong reminder of the importance of preparing for the unexpected. title: Unleashing the Pilot Within: A Riveting Guide to Fire Safety on Your Beloved Marine Craft
author: Old Sea Dogs

summary: Breaking down your path to mastering fire safety on your luxury vessel: Enhancing experience, preserving tranquility, and ensuring everlasting adventures at sea.
body: The allure of shimmering waters under the exotic sun, lapping waves against the hull of your beloved craft, it's all part of the sea journey. However, ensuring a safe adventure means you have to be prepared for every possible setback, including fire threats.

While the thought of fire on a boat surrounded by a vast expanse of water may seem paradoxical, it remains a grave issue among seafarers. Not only can it lead to the loss of valuable marine property, but it also poses a significant risk to the precious lives on board.

It is important to conduct a thorough check of your boat periodically. Pay special attention to areas such as fuel lines, engine compartments, or any spot where electrical equipment is installed. These areas tend to be hotbeds for potential fire risks.

From a practical perspective, creating an evacuation plan and regularly briefing your crew and passengers about it can make a considerable difference in terms of fire safety. The plan should detail the locations of firefighting equipment, the sequence of actions to be taken in the event of a fire, and the evacuation route.

Don't forget that fire safety begins from basics like avoiding smoking indoors and following protocol while fuelling. Remember, prevention at all times is better than stepping up efforts when disaster strikes.

The command of the seas requires intense vigilance. Allow this guide to aid in your quest for a ceaselessly safe and thrilling voyage. Celebrate sailing epically while also saluting safety guidelines. Let us turn this seemingly intimidating task into a foundation for many victorious rides on the azure waves.

title: Clearing the Waters: Navigating the Murky World of Yachting Sustainability and Greenwashing
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Clearing the Waters: Navigating the Murky World of Yachting Sustainability and Greenwashing
summary: In the opulent universe of yachting, the term 'sustainability' can often get lost at sea. Here's setting the compass straight.
body: For those unacquainted with the term 'greenwashing', it refers to a practice where false or misleading information is disseminated about an entity's environmental practices or benefits. The super-swanky world of yachting has not been spared from this phenomenon. The reality is that the concept of a completely 'green' or 'sustainable' superyacht is presently elusive, primarily due to the significant impacts throughout its lifetime. In fact, the annual average carbon footprint of a superyacht can be shockingly equivalent to nearly nine centuries of emissions of the average person.

A note of caution here: It's crucial that these changes don't result in inadvertent trade-offs. For example, while recycled materials can be used for various products, they sometimes lack the durability of unrecycled items and hence, require more production. A more durable material, no matter how sustainable, will still have to be disposed of eventually in what might be an impactful manner. The trick, therefore, is to look for products that will genuinely reduce impact throughout their use.

This holds true for alternative fuels as well. While sources like methanol, hydrogen and HVO can reduce emissions, their overall impact relies heavily on their production methods or required resources. To ensure options result in a significantly lower impact than business-as-usual, adequate supporting data and third-party certified or accredited products should be sought.

In the coming years, the verification of eco-claims is likely to become more stringent, thanks to a new EU Directive on Green Claims set to be released later this year. The directive outlaws any misleading or unverifiable claims about product environmental impacts and calls for all such claims to be supported by verifiable sources. This step is sure to bring more accountability into the play and aid yachting enthusiasts and industry players alike in ensuring that the glorious waves they ride aren't tainted with greenwash. After all, in the course of charting the global waters, it's essential to acknowledge and respect the value of the true blue.

body: The world of 12ft skiff racing is an addictive rush of water and wind, where the unexpected can happen. However, there's one constant that rivals can't outrace – the Woof. Crafted to perfection in the mid-90s by Brendan Egan and Jim Walsh, this carbon composite design has been a game-changer.

For decades, the sailing field saw a torrent of self-designed timber boats, sprouted by ambitious designers aiming for a win. But the introduction of the Woof altered the scene dramatically. Not just any hull, this design reframed skiff dynamics with its blend of speed, cost, and undeniable longevity, putting an end to the era of home-grown timber boats.

Fast forward to the 2025 12 Foot skiff Interdominion, the Woof's influence was undeniable. Out of the 22 entries, a whopping 19 came out of the Woof mould or showed slight modifications of that design. And the winner? None other than Monkey Wrench, a 20-year-old Woof that, under the keen stewardship of its owner Jono Clough, still poses as a formidable competing presence despite its age.

The Woof’s continued supremacy denotes that, while the hull is a crucial component, it's far from being the whole package. Skiff racing is about adapting to waves and winds, harnessing the best of technology, and above all, the exhilaration and passion for sailing.

The 45M, designed for long-haul, epic ocean crossings, sports an intriguing stern configuration. A tiered 'relaxation zone', spread over three levels, features an enticing sunbathing area, a swimming pool and an infinity cockpit. Swimmers can enjoy panoramic seascape views framed by a glass balustrade, fusing safety with style.

A 16-metre long sundeck offers further opportunities for sunbathing, along with a well-appointed lounge, dining area, bar and jacuzzi. The lower deck houses more sleeping quarters, capable of accommodating four double cabins, with a dedicated area for the ship's crew.

Powered by twin CAT C32 engines, the Unica 45M will cruise at speeds of 14 knots, with a maximum speed of 15 knots and a range of 4,000 nautical miles at 10 knots. ISA Yachts anticipates a surging tide of orders, with the Viper 120 series next in line on the launching pad.

author: Old Sea Dogs

summary: Cantieri di Pisa reveals the internal renderings of their reimagined Akhir 44 model at the illustrious Dubai International Boat Show, fusing past glory with futuristic innovation.
body: Cantieri di Pisa, the renowned Italian shipyard, delivered a striking blow at the Dubai International Boat Show by unveiling the exquisite interiors of their redesigned Akhir 44 model. This revolutionary redesign was handed over to the capable hands of Italian designer Antonio Luxardo, tasked with a challenging balance of preserving the brand's historic legacy while steering it towards the future of nautical technology and environmental sustainability.

The pioneering Akhir line reached the zenith of its fame back in the 90s. The legacy returns with the Akhir 44, its carbon fibre composite structure crowned by an impressive 'wave-piercing' EHPH Power Fin hull. The lush interiors of this magnificent vessel owe their brilliance to a collaboration with Pulina Exclusive Interiors, a design studio also reputed for their work on the distinguished 38.2-metre K+ by Maori Yacht and the grand 62-meter CRN superyacht Rio.

This drive for innovation is reflected in their novel approach to space utilization. The spacious main deck prioritizes guests, introducing a retractable dining area with sliding panels that allow for an adaptable experience. The design renders two dining configurations; a reserved, formal setup and an open, interactive layout that enhances the onboard culinary experiences.

Design quirks like a floating staircase, made from metal and glass, act as the sculptural nucleus within the saloon. Accommodations include four plush guest cabins and an owner's suite, all strategically located on the lower deck.

The exterior design preserves key features from the earlier Akhir line such as narrow deckhouse lines, distinct strip windows, 'shark-like' bow decoration, horizontal-grid air intakes, and the striking black and white livery. Expected to cruise at a speed of 30 knots while capable of reaching a maximum speed of 35 knots, the Akhir 44 is outfitted with powered waterjets.

Currently, the Pisa facilities house two yachts under-construction, the 80 Veloce and a 37.5-metre custom model. With this introduction, Cantieri di Pisa reinstates its commitment to elevating design, combining heritage with a vision for the future.

summary: Take a dive into the world of extravagance as the stunningly luxurious 'Ulysses', a motor yacht from Mondomarine, hits the sales market.
body: Let's embark on a tour of the breath-taking 39.4-metre Mondomarine motor yacht, 'Ulysses'. Commissioned by the capable hands of Fraser Palma's Dennis Frederiksen and Matthew Lester, the 'Ulysses' is a masterstroke of marine engineering. Since its grand advent in 2009 from the Italian yard, it enjoys the distinction of both exterior and interior artisanship from the famed Italian studio, Luca Dini.

In 2012, the yacht underwent an extensive refit worth €1.5 million, which upgraded it with zero speed stabilisers among other additions. 'Ulysses', with her blend of immaculate Italian craftsmanship and high performance, stands as a symbol of grandeur at sea. Stunning 10 guests with its opulent facilities, it offers five spacious cabins, including a full-beam master suite, two VIP suites and generous quarters to host a crew of seven.

The main deck showcases a sizeable saloon and a formal dining area. The upper deck houses another large saloon which presents an embracing space for joyous interactions and leisure. Outdoors, the yacht flaunts sleek lines and extensive lounge areas, including a large aft deck with a dining location. The upper deck basks in the sun, with a tempting hot tub and sunbathing pads.

Driven by dual MTU engines, the yacht manoeuvres at a comfortable cruise speed of 15 knots and boasts a maximum speed of 17 knots. The semi-displacement hull amplifies her range to 2,600 nautical miles. Staying true to the name Ulysses and embodying the spirit of an adventurous voyage, the yacht invites connoisseurs to seize this magnificent seafaring wonder for a grand €2,800,000 (VAT paid). Let the sea mysteries unfold with the remarkable 'Ulysses'!

title: Experience the Thrill of Unveiled Boating Offers from Ovington at RYA Dinghy & Watersports Show 2025
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Experience the Thrill of Unveiled Boating Offers from Ovington at RYA Dinghy & Watersports Show 2025
summary: The esteemed Ovington Boats is set to star at the RYA Dinghy & Watersports Show 2025, dishing out scintillating deals of the year.
body: There's nothing quite like the anticipation that precedes a grand boating event. The moment is here – Ovington Boats strides with grandeur in the upcoming RYA Dinghy & Watersports Show, 2025. Occupying the eye-catching Stand 66, Ovington showcases the best of their fleet, along with irresistible bank on deals.

A glistening gem in the Ovington's exposition is the formidable Ovington ILCA, the sailboat that bore Matt Wearn to a triumphant Olympic Gold finish in Marseille, now available at a special boat show price of £7,990. Sporting complete with Paris Olympic graphics and a full Southeast Sailboats package, this showpiece also launches the all-new ILCA super stiff carbon tiller.

Ovington makes waves as they lift the veil off the newly announced VX2, a two-person hiking skiff. Eager sailors will be able to take this for a spin at the first demo sails in the UK, scheduled to happen at the Ovington Inland Championships on the 15th and 16th of March at Grafham Water.

The surprises don't end there. On the display is the new ILCA tiller, a product of imaginative collaboration with British Sailing Team sailors, available at a limited quantity for £229. Not to be overlooked, the stand will also feature the new Sailteck Race Compass, a superb design marvel from the creators of the original TackTick compass. Priced at £345.95, it boasts a massive dual-level display, cleverly offering both heading and countdown simultaneously.

None should miss the opportune chance to indulge in the thrill of sailing and the joy of owning a top-tier boat offered by Ovington Boats at the 2025 RYA Dinghy & Watersports Show. Time to weigh anchor, and set sail towards Stand 66.

title: Get the Best Deal: 29m Sanlorenzo Yacht 'Don't Tell Mom' Sees Further $500K Price Drop
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Get the Best Deal: 29m Sanlorenzo Yacht 'Don't Tell Mom' Sees Further $500K Price Drop
summary: Luxury just got more affordable. The 29.3-metre motor yacht 'Don't Tell Mom' sees another price slash of $500,000.
body: In a twist that whispers of luxury deals, Sanlorenzo's 29.3-metre yacht 'Don't Tell Mom' has become notably more affordable with a cool slash of $500,000 off its original price. Now listed for sale at $6,999,000 with Boomer Jousma of The Italian Yacht Group, the yacht flaunts its pedigree in every one of its fine lines and features. Constructed in the year 2021, this SD96 is not just another yacht—it's a masterstroke of customization, embodying the exquisite vision of an experienced owner with a discerning taste for high-quality design and unparalleled craftsmanship. 'Don't Tell Mom' bears a bold profile, its design proudly penned by Zuccon International Project. Its interiors, warmed by the inviting brilliance of Patricia Urquiola, boast a chic modern look that immediately captures attention. Currently basking in the waters of Fort Lauderdale, Florida, the yacht has the capacity to sleep eight guests across four snug cabins—a decadent exploration of comfort that includes two cabins etched on the lower deck and a sumptuous owner's cabin taking pride of place on the main deck. 'Don't Tell Mom' is brilliantly adaptable with living areas that transform as per your whims and requirements. The lower deck saloon, for instance, can double up as a VIP cabin with its own en suite, thanks to a nifty system of sliding panels. Quiet dinners or grand soirées? The yacht's dining table, which unfurls from a seemingly regular bench in front of the sofa, can comfortably seat 10 people. Notable features include a convertible coffee table up on the flybridge, upgraded skylounge side doors replacing standard fixed glass, and a host of cutting-edge electronics. Driven by two powerful diesel engines, the yacht can reach top speeds of up to 19 knots. Slowing down to a leisurely cruise, she comfortably travels at 14 knots—creating a perfect blend of speed and suave, just as her name 'Don't Tell Mom' suggests—silent strides of elegance that ought not to be whispered about, but widely celebrated. Take the helm, experience the luxury, and let the winds carry your whispers of delight across the ocean.

title: Get a Front-Row Seat as the Royal Yachting Association Makes Waves at the Dinghy & Watersports Show
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Get a Front-Row Seat as the Royal Yachting Association Makes Waves at the Dinghy & Watersports Show
summary: The Royal Yachting Association (RYA) is set to make a splash at the Dinghy & Watersports Show, offering ample guidance, advice, and expertise to sailing enthusiasts.
body: Dive into the upcoming Dinghy & Watersports Show and immerse yourself into the world of sailing. The Royal Yachting Association (RYA) anchors into the show, oozing with know-how and advice to upgrade your watercraft skills. Whether you're interested in racing, coaching, club membership, or the latest training courses, the RYA team will be on hand to offer a warm welcome. The RYA team doesn't just offer advice; it opens a door to a new adventure.

Whether you're a novice or a professional racer, the RYA team can help steer your journey. Enquire about the newly launched junior and youth 'Pathway Club' programme, race officiating, event volunteering, and club racing. Refresh your memory with the new Racing Rules of Sailing enforced recently and take home the latest editions of RYA’s Racing Rules. Also on offer are books or eBooks tailor-made for racing enthusiasts - you can even check out The Racing Rules of Sailing in audiobook format.

Last but not least, RYA membership has its perks. You can join the community of over 100,000 people at the show itself. A complimentary dry bag awaits new recruits. And if you're already its member, bring along a friend to join in, and you both can take home a dry bag as a token of appreciation. The RYA welcomes everyone onboard its journey to promote and celebrate the adventure that sailing offers!

title: Bask in Nautical Excellence at the 2025 RYA Dinghy and Watersports Show – Europe Class Steals the Spotlight
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Bask in Nautical Excellence at the 2025 RYA Dinghy and Watersports Show – Europe Class Steals the Spotlight
summary: Sailing enthusiasts and novices alike are all set for an extravaganza at the upcoming RYA Dinghy and Watersports Show 2025, with the Europe Class taking centre stage.
body: The upcoming RYA Dinghy and Watersports Show 2025 is set to be a sail lover's dream, especially for followers of the iconic Europe Class. The UK Europe Class Association is geared up to showcase its finest at the Farnborough International Exhibition Centre. The event promises not just to be a display of the class's rich history and a growing UK fleet, but also a much-anticipated gathering of sailing aficionados eager to explore the progress of this cherished class.

In the spotlight at this year's show is 'Skelf', the elegant wooden Europe boat constructed in the '80s by gifted boat builder, Gerry Ledger. Proudly owned and masterfully sailed by Luke Lazell, 'Skelf' has proven its mettle at every UK Europe National Championship since 2021, pitting its vintage charm against the might of modern marvels. Now, nestled in the scenic expanses of Swanage bay, 'Skelf' relishes the contrast of its rolling wave backdrop to the River Crouch where its journey began.

Not to be outdone, Allen Sailing, in collaboration with Synergy Marine, is presenting its latest generation Europe sailed by none other than Tom 'Mozzy' Morris, the reigning champion of the 2024 National Championships. Representing the epitome of British boat building and marine hardware, this vessel is set to impress. The diverse fleet, boasting of age-old wooden boats racing in parity with brand new ones, truly encapsulates the dynamic spirit of the Europe Class.

Join the spirited Europe Class community and discuss the nuances of sailing these unique vessels at the booth. With an all-inclusive racing schedule set for 2025, which commences at WPNSA in April, and culminates in the 2025 Youth & Masters European Championship at Hayling Island SC in July, now is the perfect time to dive into the enthralling world of Europe Class sailing. Revel in the legacy, explore the innovation, and get set to ride the waves of your dreams in the Europe Class adventure!

title: Discover the Art and Science of Laser-Precision Two-Boat Tuning with Cyclops Marine’s Innovative Devices
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover the Art and Science of Laser-Precision Two-Boat Tuning with Cyclops Marine’s Innovative Devices
summary: Imagine easily uncovering the secret behind your sailing buddy's knack for speed. With laser-precision two-boat tuning, this could be your reality.
body: Picture this: two chums, Tom and Ben, out sailing their Lasers. Tom, the speed demon upwind and Ben, the master downwind. Frustratingly, they haven't a clue why. Any seasoned coach would recommend two-boat tuning - an objective way to analyze and compare their techniques, and pinpoint areas for improvement.

But despite rigorous testing - lining up, swapping boats, tweaking settings - Tom's upwind advantage and Ben's downwind prowess remain enigmatic. The answer, as they soon discover, lies in hard, real-time data on their settings, which is precisely what Cyclops Marine’s smartlink Atto delivers.

Migrating the smartlink Atto load sensor to a new location on the rig allows for detailed inspection of various performance-critical loads. Once they've got a handle on their targets during onshore debriefs, they can start fine-tuning on water, repeating live target numbers until they become second nature. They're able to monitor how equipment selection, such as sails and rigging, affects dynamic loading on the water. Fusing different data sets, they can form a comprehensive, performance-enhancing strategy.

With this smarter approach to training, Tom and Ben are making tremendous strides in their sailing prowess, their eyes already set on Los Angeles 2028. This innovative solution explains why Olympic Federations across 14 countries including the GBR, GER, NOR, SWE, AUS, AUT, FRA, ITA, USA, ESP, NED, SUI, JAP & CAN all relied on Cyclops Marine devices in their Paris campaigns. In the competitive world of sailing, real-time, comparative data is a game-changer.

title: 2025 Lanzarote International Regatta Sets Sail: Jonatan Vadnai Shines with his ILCA Lead
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: 2025 Lanzarote International Regatta Sets Sail: Jonatan Vadnai Shines with his ILCA Lead
summary: The Lanzarote International Regatta of 2025 sees Hungarian sailor Jonatan Vadnai dominating the ILCA 7 racing, marking an early noteworthy lead.
body: The sun rose over the Atlantic, illuminating the Lanzarote waters as the 2025 International Regatta set sail, alive with the energetic anticipation of a thrilling race ahead. At the heart of the action was Hungarian sailor, Jonatan Vadnai, who showcased his skill in the physically challenging ILCA 7 racing series, securing two race wins and a second place. He deftly maneuvered through 12 to 17 knots of breeze, charging Atlantic waves, and abundant Canarian sunshine, to firmly set himself as the frontrunner. The Spanish team of Silvia Mas and Alex Marsans also made quite a splash, claiming the early lead in the 470 Mixed fleet. The spanking new team exhibited a prodigious partnership against veteran competitors such as Diogo Costa and Carolina Joao of Portugal and the Italian Olympian Elena Berta along with her crew-mate Giulio Calabro. Marsans hailed the day as a tough but encouraging testament to their nascent collaboration. They acknowledged their need to fine-tune certain aspects, but overall the team was confident about the progress they'd made in the short span of their training together. Among the younger participants in the event, there were several who boldly challenged the seasoned competitors, gaining invaluable experience on the waters where they are set to compete in the ILCA 7 Under-21 World Championship of 2026. As the day wound down, amidst the camaraderie and sea-spray, Marina Rubicón was abuzz with tales of extraordinary sailing conditions and unison in the joy of competition. All in all, the Lanzarote International Regatta of 2025 proved an exhilarating tableau of sailboat racing, setting an extraordinarily high bar for future matches.

title: Eternity, the Premier 65-metre Codecasa Motor Yacht, Makes its Market Debut
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Eternity, the Premier 65-metre Codecasa Motor Yacht, Makes its Market Debut
summary: Crafted by renowned Italian shipbuilder Codecasa, the elegant 65-metre motor yacht Eternity is now on sale.
body: Italian craftsmanship meets oceanic luxury in the form of the 65-metre Codecasa motor yacht, Eternity. Built as the first 65-metre yacht by the famed Italian yard, Eternity has made a name for itself in the world of luxurious seafaring vessels. Launched amidst great fanfare in April 2010, Eternity was followed by the likes of Joia the Crown Jewel and Regina D'Italia, forming an exclusive trifecta of elegantly crafted 65-metre ships by Codecasa. Crafted from steel and aluminium, Eternity underwent significant rework in 2022. This evolution saw her exteriors and interiors revamped to what can only be termed 'superlative standards'. This transformation was the brainchild of the renowned Suzanne Lovell. Further enhancements occurred in 2024, reinforcing her spot at the top of luxury yachting. Boasting a master suite, four doubles, and two twins, Eternity provides luxe accommodation for up to 14 guests. Exuding freshness and contemporary elegance, her interiors reflect an understated oceanic theme. The 'Bahamas-esque' aesthetics pay homage to her current location at Nassau, The Bahamas. Social space abounds on this stately vessel, with the main saloon divided only subtly into multiple seating areas and a chic bar. A formal dining room on the upper deck couples with versatile entertainment spaces, leading to an expansive al fresco dining area. Completing the package is a 6-meter exercise-cum-Jacuzzi pool, and a sundeck that houses a gym with a stunning view. In a league of its own, Eternity represents the pinnacle of luxurious seafaring, ready to meet its new owner at an asking price of €35,000,000.

title: Discover the Intriguing Innovation of Crow's Nest in the New Superyacht Concepts by Turquoise Yachts and Bannenberg & Rowell
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Discover the Intriguing Innovation of Crow's Nest in the New Superyacht Concepts by Turquoise Yachts and Bannenberg & Rowell
summary: Feast your senses on the stunning new superyacht concepts from Turquoise Yachts and British studio Bannenberg & Rowell, featuring inventive features like an elevator crow's nest.
body: Imagine embarking on an opulent adventure aboard a majestic superyacht, equipped with custom amenities and unconventional, yet innovative, design features. That's precisely the sort of marine escapade facilitated by Turquoise Yachts' recently unveiled series of superyacht concepts. Teaming up with the renowned British design house, Bannenberg & Rowell, Turquoise Yachts have turned traditional yacht design on its head with their 65m and 80m concepts, named Above + Beyond.

Sailing enthusiasts take note - these exceptional designs take an extraordinary design leap with the introduction of a crow's nest. Upon hearing 'crow's nest', one might imagine an elevated lookout post on traditional sailing vessels. However, these ingenious designers have taken it beyond conventional thought by revamping the crow's nest into a custom platform-cum-elevator, climbing to the top of the mast. With such a feature, one could enjoy an unparalleled view at the Monaco Grand Prix or when cruising the polar regions.

The upper deck houses the master suite, boasting a study, dressing room, ensuite, and promising a staggering 270-degree view. In contrast, the beach club embraces wellness with a sauna, steam shower, massage room, and a full gymnasium with a balcony. The service crew haven't been forgotten either. Every deck features an expansive pantry, with a commercial-grade galley, walk-in freezer, and pantry found below deck. Furthermore, the crew's comfort is ensured with laundry facilities, a gym, and a substantial mess area.

Above is expected to be built on a pre-existing hull platform by Turquoise Yachts, with a flexible final design and LOA to cater to the client's preferences. Turquoise Yachts continues to redefine luxury sailing, with these designs further cementing their place as pioneers in the industry.

title: Globally Inspired Albacore Stand Dazzles at the RYA Dinghy & Watersports Show 2025
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Globally Inspired Albacore Stand Dazzles at the RYA Dinghy & Watersports Show 2025
summary: The Albacore stand at the RYA Dinghy & Watersports Show 2025 promises an exciting mix of international appeal, featuring visitors from around the globe, fascinating sailing insights, and a stunning yacht showcase.
body: The 2025 RYA Dinghy & Watersports Show, hosted at the Farnborough International Exhibition Centre, offers attendees an engaging international experience, compliments of the Albacore Stand, standing tall at Stand A9. 2025 is special, as it plays host to the biannual Albacore Internationals at Hampton YC, Virginia, USA, in October, a drawcard event for sailing enthusiasts globally. The UK’s contribution to the affair promises to be vibrant, with their containers nearly filled to the brim. Among this assortment is a yacht earning its bragging rights, the immaculately presented, and aptly named, 'Uffa Fox Sake'. This phenomenal display is sure to leave sailing enthusiasts yearning for open waters. Adding a personalized touch to the stand is the yacht's owner, Matt Thompson, who will be available for interactions over the weekend. Thompson's role extends beyond ownership as he also shoulders responsibility as the chair of the International Albacore Association. For international visitors, the stand plays host to 'Mr. Albacore USA', Barney Harris, and Ralph Glass, adding a tasteful touch of overseas zest to the exhibit. Attendees can also treat themselves to a unique seminar by multiple International and National Albacore Champion Michael McNamara, presenting his sought-after sail tuning talk. Discounted membership offers and a demo boat for charter signal enticing opportunities for those hoping to join the Albacore fleet. For every sailing enthusiast, whether experienced or novice, the Albacore stand ensures an experience rich in sailing culture, international camaraderie, and the sheer thrill that is the open water.

This dynamic mix of sailors only conforms to the class's commitment to extend a supportive learning environment, promoting camaraderie and skill-building among novice and seasoned sailors.

title: Polish Masters Unveil Eco-friendly Marvel: The First Emission-Free 35m Sailing Catamaran by Sunreef Yachts
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Polish Masters Unveil Eco-friendly Marvel: The First Emission-Free 35m Sailing Catamaran by Sunreef Yachts
summary: The Polish shipyard, Sunreef Yachts, elevates the standard for eco-friendly travel with its latest innovation - the emission-free Sunreef 35M Eco series.
body: A silent revolution is stirring in the waters, and at the helm is Sunreef Yachts. The Polish shipyard is redefining luxury with an innovative nod toward sustainability in their latest release - the first unit of the Sunreef 35M Eco series. Sold to a client espoused by Y.CO in 2024, this sailing catamaran will make its debut in the charter market post-delivery. The model is a masterpiece of engineering, with its custom-built batteries, state-of-the-art electric engines, and solar panels seamlessly ensconced into the hull, superstructure, and Bimini. This ensures a graceful glide across the water's surface leaving no trail of emissions in its wake. The interior is as breathtaking as the technology is impressive. Custom 3D wood and leather panels meet an eco-leather ceiling, setting the stage for indulgent French bouclé fabric upholstery. At a generous 14.7-metre beam, the catamaran presents spacious interiors, housing a panoramic owner's cabin on the main deck with its access to the bow terrace. A super king-size bed, a dedicated seating area, a walk-in dressing room, and a limestone-effect bathroom with a bathtub forge an oasis of luxury inside. Meanwhile, the guests aboard will find their abodes ensconced within the hulls. The flybridge emerges as the chosen space for communal gatherings boasting a plunge pool, an inviting lounge space, and a bar. The 'Ocean Lounge' aft deck further augments the relaxation quotient with sofa seating and access to an array of toys stored in an unseen garage. As of June 2024, the market has 31 units of this eco-friendly wave-maker on order or under construction, the largest being the Sunreef 43M Eco. Sunreef Yachts continues to etch its name in the annals of maritime history, with its first unit in the Sunreef 43M Eco series nearing completion, poised to become the world's largest electric catamaran.

From this stunning revelation at the Dubai International Boat Show, it's clear that Sancrea Yachts isn't simply building boats, they're shaping the future of yachting luxury.
