The championship consists of ten adrenaline-fuelling races spread over five days under the keen oversight of PRO Sheela Lewis. title: Cruising Yacht Club of Australia Dominates in 2025 Helly Hansen International, Securing Joy Ride Perpetual Trophy for the Second Time

summary: The Cruising Yacht Club of Australia (CYCA) emerged victorious in the 2025 Helly Hansen International regatta, winning the prestigious Joy Ride Perpetual Trophy for the second consecutive time.
body: Australia's sailing stars shone brightly as the Cruising Yacht Club of Australia (CYCA) came out on top in the fiercely contested Helly Hansen International in 2025. The event saw them win the coveted Joy Ride Perpetual Trophy for the second time, outshining their American rivals led by Jeffrey Petersen.

The triumphant team, helmed by Cole Tapper, also included Max Brennan, Jack Frewin and Hamish Vass, showcased superior skill and tactical acumen, dominating the Final Series. Despite encountering spinnaker issues in one race causing them to sail without it momentarily, they held their ground. Their resilience was put on spectacular display when they bounced back swiftly, leaving their opponents in their wake.

Tapper's crew opened strong, winning the first race before Petersen levelled the series. Their intimate knowledge of the Elliott's came to bear in the proceeding races, as they displayed near-flawless handling, winning the next two starts and outpacing their American rivals to seize the Joy Ride Trophy.

The event marked the first time CYCA had the privilege to host since the World Sailing Youth Match Racing World Championship in 2023–a testament to the club's rising prestige on the global stage, where Tapper and Petersen had previously secured Silver and Bronze medals respectively.

The 2025 Helly Hansen International saw a broad age range with the category extended to under 25. It proved to be a wise decision, registering exceptional participation from five nations, with Canada making its debut, solidifying the event as Australia's premier match racing tournament and the country's sole World Sailing Grade 2 event.

Victory spirits high, many competitors including Tapper and Petersen, now gear up for a cross-country sailing bout in Perth, Western Australia. The Royal Freshwater Bay Yacht Club will host the 2025 Warren Jones Regatta on the Swan River, from Tuesday 27 to Friday 31 January, in what promises to be another stellar event.

title: A Deep Dive into the Impact of Spain's Matriculation Tax on Yacht Ownership
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A Deep Dive into the Impact of Spain's Matriculation Tax on Yacht Ownership
summary: From tax intricacies to exemptions, exploring Spain’s Matriculation (Mat) Tax and its ramifications on yacht ownership by Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBOs).
body: Spain's matriculation tax, often simply referred to as the 'mat tax', holds major implications for yacht owners and entities holding related interests, particularly UBOs. This tax, pegged at a staggering rate of 12% of the vessel's value, has been a source of intrigue and uncertainty since it was introduced.The Spanish Directorate General of Taxes (DGT) has made efforts to offer clearer guidance on who this tax affects and how. They've taken measures to clarify the confusing aspects surrounding yacht chartering by related persons, the tax implications for non-resident UBOs, and the potential exemption possibilities. In a notable progression, recent rulings have shed light on two critical stances. Firstly, pleasure boats and vessels used exclusively for charter in Spain may be exempt from mat tax - a significant boon for the charter industry. However, to benefit from this, exemption must be applied for and secured before the commencement of charter operations. Secondly, UBOs may not necessarily be bound by mat tax. If a UBO, despite their relationship to the owning entity, does not reside in Spain or have a direct 'establishment' in Spain, they're able to utilize the yacht under the above-mentioned conditions. In this case, they wouldn't stand to lose the recognition of exemption from Spanish mat tax. However, it's crucial to walk this fine line with care. Repeated or excessive yacht usage under 'market conditions' could raise red flags, hinting at an attempt to avoid accruing mat tax. Hence, proving a genuine business structure backing the yacht-owning entity is crucial. The Spanish mat tax continues to be an evolving space, warranting close attention from UBOs, yacht owning entities, and charter companies. Understanding its intricacies and limitations can open up advantageous avenues of tax exemption and legitimate usage. Keep a close eye, plan your moves carefully, sail the tax seas wisely and you could be charting a path to smoother sailing in Spanish waters.

title: Giancarlo Pedote Braces for the Last Stretch: Less than 1500 Miles from Vendée Globe Finish
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Giancarlo Pedote Braces for the Last Stretch: Less than 1500 Miles from Vendée Globe Finish
summary: Italian star sailor, Giancarlo Pedote, ventures towards the end of the Vendée Globe solo yacht race, with less than 1,500 miles to the finish line.
body: The relentless push towards the finish line is at full swing for renowned Italian sailor, Giancarlo Pedote. Navigating through an intense journey full of trials and tribulations, he is determined to finish the prestigious Vendée Globe solo yacht race on a high, aiming for at least a Top 15 place finish. As of now, he has approximately 1,500 miles remaining to Les Sables-d'Olonne. The race has been a rollercoaster ride for Pedote, punctuated by technical problems and strategic choices under often extreme weather conditions. The skipper of Prysmian found himself held back by regions of light winds within a high-pressure zone. Despite the pace-slowing conditions, Pedote’s commitment to his quest remains unshaken. He iterates the importance of keeping the boat moving in adverse situations but accepting the reality of his position lucidly. Assessing his current situation, Pedote says, 'A position out to the west looks more favourable and I'm over to the east. I've had to deal with what’s thrown at me.' He clarifies that his decision to stay the course stems from not wanting to stray off track with zigzagging. Despite these setbacks, he continues to fight and remains focused. His concentration now directed towards the final crucial steps of his journey. Pedote’s remaining voyage is expected to be swift, thanks to a depression set to propel his group to finish. Strategising his way through, he acknowledges a race against the clock in a literal drag race to the finish. Nonetheless, his undivided attention is on the here and now, refusing to let the anticipation of the finish line distract him. For him, the journey continues, as he once again gets ready to take on the challenges thrown by Mother Nature.

title: Inaugural Ronstan Junior Foiling Cup at McCrae Yacht Club Offers Thrilling Opportunity for Young Sailors

This sensational racing series, designed exclusively to instill passion and create a thrilling sailing experience for sailors aged 10 to 16, will unfurl its sails on the flawless flat waters of McCrae Yacht Club, off the stunning Mornington Peninsula, from March 1st through 2nd, 2025. This event serves as an idyllic platform for the young mariners to participate in exhilarating races, hone their sailing mettle, and savor the exhilarating speed of foiling boats. The registration is open to all junior sailors hailing from any class or club in Victoria for two days of heated round robin racing. However, the spaces are limited - so young seafarers, seize your chance to race high-speed foiling boats against the finest junior sailors from across all classes and clubs around Victoria. The inaugural Ronstan Junior Foiling Cup race at Bayview Racing Association in NSW was a notable success. Sailors traveled over 1000km, participating in nail-biting races and crossing the finish lines with remarkable speed. The chosen craft for the competition, the nimble and versatile Nikki foiling dinghy, is perfect for these enthusiastic young sailors to learn on while experiencing the thrill of both planing and foiling. Supported by major sailing brands like Ronstan, Australian Sailing and Forward WIP, clubs around the world can also get in touch to host such events, sharing in the pursuit to propel junior sailing to grand new heights. A foiling revolution awaits. Are you ready to ride the waves?

title: Journey to The RYA Dinghy & Watersports Show: Decoding Strategies to Land One's Ideal Boat

summary: Embark on a thrilling quest to find an ideal sailing setup at the upcoming RYA Dinghy & Watersports Show on 22-23 February 2025.

Keeping in tune with the competitive spirit of the sailors, Performance Sailcraft Europe has developed the ILCA Elite series. The Elite series boats, upgraded with Carbon Upper, Carbon Tiller and Extension and full Harken rigging, facilitates one in embarking on a unique, adventurous journey across the waves.

Among the exhibits, the Goat Marine's Topper, tailored for junior racers, also takes the limelight. Ensuring its visitors an immersive experience in the world of sailing, this event holds the keys to unravelling an unforgettable sailing journey.

title: Hardy Sea Dogs Brave Stormy Weather for Winter Time Trial at Rutland Sailing Club
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Hardy Sea Dogs Brave Stormy Weather for Winter Time Trial at Rutland Sailing Club
summary: Nine daring sailors stare down a squall for the thrill of the high-stakes Dart 15 Winter Time Trials at Rutland Sailing Club.
body: Bracing against a 35-knot gust, nine audacious sailors engaged in a thrilling face-off in the Dart 15 Winter Time Trials at Rutland Sailing Club. The rescheduled event, originally washed away by Storm Darragh, saw these seasoned waveriders tussle with the tempest, even as other parts of the country buckled under the weather's onslaught. Choosing to remain in the icy embrace of the sea over the warmth of their winter holidays, each sailor remained undaunted in the face of the impending storm.

The fleet, navigating towards the blustery start, was met with an expected hurdle in the form of a capsizing by sailer Charles Watson. His attempts at light humor, however, fell short when attributing the mishap to cleaning bird droppings off his boat. The sailors took off to a clean start post the incident. On the facing line, Jason Clarke and Jon Pearse lead, with the rest of the fleet in hot pursuit. The race under swirling conditions had begun. The fierce wind tutored the fleet in navigation, bending left as the seafarers progressed across the lake, pushing the majority to tack off midway through the crucial windward leg.

title: From a Humble Australian Boat Factory to Global Yachting Powerhouse: The Ascendancy of Palm Beach Motor Yachts
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: From a Humble Australian Boat Factory to Global Yachting Powerhouse: The Ascendancy of Palm Beach Motor Yachts
summary: Built on a passion for time at sea, Palm Beach Motor Yachts evolved from modest roots to a global luxury motor yacht brand.
body: When Palm Beach Motor Yachts planted its roots in Palm Beach, Australia in 1995, few could have anticipated the voyage they embarked upon—a 30-year odyssey to become internationally recognized luxury motor yacht brand.

Starting with a modest 100m2 factory crafting the original Palm Beach 38, the company grew at a steady clip. The business expanded, relocating to Mona Vale on Sydney's Northern Beaches peninsula to accommodate the demand for their superior vessels. The Palm Beach 50 quickly followed the 38, underscoring their reputation for beautifully engineered luxury motor yachts. Soon, the single factory became two, then four.

Barely a decade ago, Palm Beach Motor Yachts drew global attention when it was acquired by Grand Banks Yachts. This catapulted their operations to larger dimensions, relocating their molds to the Grand Banks Yacht shipyard in Malaysia where they are currently headquartered as part of the prestigious GB Marine Group.

With the announcement of the new Palm Beach 107, gears have shifted once more. It won't be surprising if further new models unveil between it and the Palm Beach 85. Motivated by the producing quality yachts for pleasure at sea, the brand continues to despise stagnation.

Emphasizing the upcoming successful year, the buoyant Richards announced the company's expansion plans with a whopping 110,000m2 factory space and a dedicated 1,200-person crew. He vowed his commitment to an all-inclusive, factory-direct model that not only sees through the sales but also comprehensive, top-notch service. His singular vision? A satisfied cadre of clients, every single one looked after by the experienced hands of Palm Beach and under the protective umbrella of the GB Marine Group.

title: Vendée Globe Participants Brave Harsh Seas in Determined Quest for Glory
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Vendée Globe Participants Brave Harsh Seas in Determined Quest for Glory
summary: In the world-renowned Vendée Globe sailing marathon, skippers battle through tough seas and fierce winds, on their thrilling race towards Les Sables d'Olonne.
body: The prestigious Vendée Globe race keeps global sailing enthusiasts on the precipice of their seats as two experienced skippers anthropomorphise their vessels, daring through daunting winds and towering waves. Boris Herrmann of Germany, sailing the Malizia Seaexplorer, maintains a cautious pace as he nears the finish line that he's targeting for a triumphant Wednesday finish, potentially securing a commendable 12th place. Hot on his heels is Britain's Sam Davies, aboard the Initiatives Coeur, closing the gap, lingering merely 78 miles behind Herrmann. Much like her rival, she's moderating her vessel’s walk in the face of compelling winds and gigantic waves.

Amidst this dramatic backdrop and a possible unlocking of the 'storm line', race direction is now in deliberation with Guyot Environnement - Water Family and L'Occitane en Provence regarding the arrival of Benjamin Dutreux and Clarisse Crémer at the iconic channel procession. Meanwhile, the top finishing IMOCAs MACIF Santé Prévoyance and Paprec Arkéa have their sights set on returning to their home ports, Concarneau and Lorient respectively, leaving Port Olona in their wake come Thursday.

Circa 1800 nautical miles southwest, a trail lined by the 15th placed Damien Seguin (Groupe Apicil) to Violette Dorange in the 26th position, aboard the Devenir, unfolds. Poised for a potentially longer itinerary west of the Azores, the sailors converge on an area of high pressure threatening to unleash light winds, escalating their routes and adding an unexpected hurdle in their journey. The Vendée Globe, truly the Olympics of the high seas, continues to offer trials, triumphs and tales worth narrating for generations to come.

title: In the Wake of Vendée Globe's Finish, the America's Cup Unfolds a Plot Twist: The Exit of Olympic Champion, Sir Ben Ainslie
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: In the Wake of Vendée Globe's Finish, the America's Cup Unfolds a Plot Twist: The Exit of Olympic Champion, Sir Ben Ainslie
summary: A fascinating turn of events has stirred the prestigious world of sailing as Sir Ben Ainslie departs the British-flagged INEOS Britannia team.
body: Shaking up the world of sailing, Sir Ben Ainslie, the most decorated Olympic sailor, has taken leave from the British-flagged INEOS Britannia team. Steering the British challenges in the past three races, Ainslie has triumphed over formidable competition, taking two significant wins from the Emirates Team New Zealand in the 37th America's Cup.

Yet, despite his impressive efforts, INEOS Britannia and Sir Ben have decided to sail separate courses following the conclusion of the competition in Barcelona. As per the official statement released by Sir Jim Ratcliffe and INEOS Britannia, plans are set to proceed without Ainslie, a decision that has succeeded in ruffling the waters.

This wave of uncertainty breaks at a critical time when the Defender, represented by Emirates Team New Zealand sailing team, was supposedly deep into discussions with the Challenger of Record about pressing details surrounding the next America's Cup match. To cap off the unpredictability, there's ambiguity regarding who between Ainslie and Ratcliffe, is operating as the Challenger of Record.

Hopes are high that circumventing the New York State Supreme Court and Court of Appeals, which governs the Deed of Gift of the America's Cup, could be possible. As the sailing world briskly adjusts its sails on the unfolding drama, the offshore sporting scene presents the completion of eight more skippers in the Vendée Globe.
What remains is to navigate the uncharted waters of the post-Ainslie era in the INEOS Britannia team and the unpredictable direction the America's Cup will take in this evolving climate.

title: Triumph Against Odds: Andrew Dolly Divola Conquers the Waves at 2025 Vaikobi Australian Windsurfer Nationals
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Triumph Against Odds: Andrew Dolly Divola Conquers the Waves at 2025 Vaikobi Australian Windsurfer Nationals
summary: Andrew 'Dolly' Divola, a living legend in the Australian Sailing Community, made waves at the 2025 Vaikobi Australian Windsurfer Class Nationals, undeterred by health struggles, and with pure aquatic finesse.
body: The 2025 Vaikobi Australian Windsurfer Class Regatta boasted a plethora of wave-riding, sail-harnessing talents, but among them, a singular figure stood out - Andrew 'Dolly' Divola. In true testament to the unprecedented spirit of Windsurfer Class competitions, Dolly secured a hard-fought third-place finish in the slalom division, providing a memorable highlight of the event.

His journey to the podium wasn't a smooth sail, rather a test of his resolve. He had to persist through multiple rounds of elimination to reach the final, often facing well-rested competitors, while Dolly himself had already endured numerous leg rounds. Yet, he prevailed - a testament to his notoriously resilient spirit and evident sailing prowess.

As Dolly came ashore, the exhaustion, pain, and raw, unfiltered emotion were palpable. More so, the elation. His triumphant beam, combined with the camaraderie shared with fellow sailors and spectators, was truly something to behold - visceral proof of what Windsurfer Class racing is truly about. To race not for the finish line, but for the love of the sport, the thrill of the ride, and the sheer joy of navigating the unpredictable ocean.

This is not just the story of Dolly; it is the essence of every sailor who has ever braced the gutsy wind in their sail and dared the waves beneath their boards. It is the testament and tribute to the indomitable spirit that defines the Windsurfer Class.

title: Clarisse Crémer's Triumphant Sea Voyage: An 11th Place Finish in Vendée Globe 2024
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Clarisse Crémer's Triumphant Sea Voyage: An 11th Place Finish in Vendée Globe 2024
summary: Showcasing remarkable prowess, determination, and resilience, Clarisse Crémer places 11th at the prestigious Vendée Globe 2024.
body: The waves of the prestigious Vendée Globe 2024 were determinedly quelled under the resilient bow of L'Occitane en Provence, an IMOCA that harboured an equally tenacious spirit, Clarisse Crémer. After 77 gruelling days of relentless sailing, she crossed the finish line, earning an impressive 11th position.

Her victory is striking given the limited preparation time, ridden with various challenges that could have easily unnerved even seasoned sailors. But the indomitable Crémer showcased her talent, grit, and years of experience in ocean racing, culminating in an incredibly strong performance.

Bad weather off the Vendée coast interfered with her arrival plans, forcing her to seek shelter and meet her technical team in La Rochelle. Once the storm subsided, Crémer’s sailing prowess truly shone as she maintained high velocities in her sleek vessel, rivalling Charlie Dalin, the runner-up of the previous Vendée Globe.

True to the spirit of the race, Crémer faced and overcame several technical challenges during the competition, from a broken gennaker to a foil cylinder failure and mainsail hook problem. Despite facing adversities head-on, she emerged stronger, more self-assured, and full of resolve.

The emotional tides of racing added another layer to her journey, from celebrating her daughter’s birthday remotely to rounding the Cape Horn on New Year's Day, which offered fleeting respite after battling rough southern conditions.

This race was yet another affirming chapter in Crémer’s life, a woman who found her calling in ocean racing rather late, leaving behind a promising business career. A 2nd place finish in the MiniTransat in 2017 hinted to her potential. With her 11th position in the Vendée Globe 2024, Crémer established herself as a force to be reckoned with in the world of sailing.

title: Rising Stars Prevail against Experienced Sailors in New Zealand's 2025 Flying 15 National Championship
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Rising Stars Prevail against Experienced Sailors in New Zealand's 2025 Flying 15 National Championship
summary: The prestigious 2025 New Zealand Flying 15 National Championship held at the Bay of Islands introduces new winners, after an adrenaline-packed sailing week.
body: New Zealand's largest keelboat regatta, the Bay of Islands Sailing Week, channeled riveting competition among a mix of local and international contestants in the 2025 Flying 15 National Championship. The penultimate week of January saw the racing world converge on the Bay of Islands. Despite initial gales and heavy rain, the weather mellowed sufficiently for a brief training session on Tuesday. Soon, the fleet began their journey to the course, heralding the official commencement of the championship. The first race saw Sarah Reynolds and Peter Macartney's smooth maneuvering in their newly renovated boat, Fflying Cloud. Their early lead was indeed a sight to behold. However, the winds of chance changed as four-time National Champions Murray Gilbert and Jonathon Burgess took the first victory on their boat, Ffrentic. Further excitement ensued during the second race when The Godffather, initially leading, was overtaken by FFantocini in a gripping duel during the race's finale. As the day continued, an unexpected sea breeze renewed the racecourse. Seizing upon this opportunity, Neil Easton from The Godffather crew secured an exhilarating win in the ultimate race of the day. The second day welcomed contestants with mild winds but gradually gave way to a burgeoning sea breeze. The fluctuating conditions brought out the best in Ffrentic, piloted by Gilbert and Burgess, showcasing their superior control and speed in light conditions that helped them clinch a hat-trick of victories. A taxing nine-hour journey home followed the day's races, punctuating the raw intensity and endurance required throughout the tournament. As the final day dawned, an enthralling spectacle was in store. Ben Lowe and Jonny Noakes, piloting Ffantoncini, showcased remarkable mettle, securing three back-to-back wins. This fascinating domination enabled them to clinch the regatta championship, marking them as the fifth new crew to secure the Flying 15 National Championships in as many years. Trailing them were Murray Gilbert and Jonathon Burgess of Ffrentic in the second spot and class President Sally Garrett alongside Neil Easton from The Godffather who clinched the last spot on the podium.

title: An Intrepid Duo's Breathtaking Nautical Journey from Spain to Australia's Shimmering Shores.
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: An Intrepid Duo's Breathtaking Nautical Journey from Spain to Australia's Shimmering Shores.
summary: Elizabeth Tucker and Cole Brauer navigate glistening waves, conquering the Southern Ocean on their Class 40 yacht, 'First Light'.
body: On their journey of almost 14,000 nautical miles across the globe, Elizabeth Tucker and Cole Brauer are turning maritime journeying into an art form. Back in November, they set sail from Spain aboard the spectacular Class 40 yacht, 'First Light', the destination – Sydney, where they are expected to arrive in the latter half of February.

The expedition isn’t void of action and suspense. Challenge after challenge, from food poisoning to minor damage on the yacht’s keel due to a collision, the duo has been resilient in the face of adversity. As they covered 9,000 nautical miles, they found themselves around 45 degrees South and 57 East, near the remote French-dominated Kerguelen Islands in the Southern Ocean.

Always looking on the bright side, Brauer and Tucker find joy in the smallest things, even during this demanding journey. Yearning for a simple cucumber sandwich, they take solace in the fact there's at least one cucumber aboard - a beautiful reminder that there's a thin line between luxury and the simple pleasures of life.

There’s a lot of water yet to cover before they dock at Sydney Harbour. The hardy seafarers will continue their adventurous journey, confronting the might of the seas, drifting towards realms where shimmering horizons dance in tandem with roaring waves.6 Their tale is one of resilience, tenacity, relishing life's simple pleasures, and most importantly, embracing the spirit of adventure.

title: Securing Triumph Amidst Stunning Weather and Challenging Conditions at Bacardi Winter Series
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Securing Triumph Amidst Stunning Weather and Challenging Conditions at Bacardi Winter Series
summary: Unfolding a perfect spectacle, Bacardi Winter Series Event 2 showcased three days of extraordinary sailing on Biscayne Bay.
body: The second event of the Bacardi Winter Series unfurled an unforgettable spectacle from January 24 to 26, 2025. Sailing enthusiasts witnessed three exhilarating days on Biscayne Bay, the stage meticulously poised to host the riveting competition. Miami's radiant weather and challenging conditions tested every performance nuance, pushing sailors to their absolute zenith. As proceedings culminated on a sunny, final day, three decisive races carved the event's victors amidst fluctuating 11-18 knot north-easterly knot breezes.

Emerging victorious from the fierce competition, Peter Duncan and his formidable two-time J/70 World Champion-winning team on 'Relative Obscurity', secured the sought-after J/70 series. Their consistency paid, as they continued their pole position domination from the inaugural day. Meanwhile, the 'Nefeli' team, under the aegis of Peter-David Karrié, advanced to secure a win in the Melges 24.

The second Bacardi Winter Series event culminated in the usual grand Bacardi style. The epic soirée and prize-giving celebration were held at Miami's Shake-A-Leg, a venue now synonymous with maritime triumphs. Adding to the suspense, J/70 and Melges 24 teams will incorporate their points from this event into their results at the Bacardi Cup Invitational Regatta (BCIR) to determine the overall series winner. The stage is set, the sailors poised, and the world watches as the saga of skill, strategy, and domination on the waters prepare for its next chapter.

title: Sporting Triumph at Düsseldorf's boot 2025: Defying the Elements in Sensational Indoor Windsurfing Show
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Sporting Triumph at Düsseldorf's boot 2025: Defying the Elements in Sensational Indoor Windsurfing Show
summary: Windsurfing leaps ahead of the curve, showcasing its fierce spirit in a riveting Indoor Tow-In World Series held at boot Düsseldorf 2025.
body: The world of windsurfing has carved its name into history. Boot Düsseldorf 2025 bore witness to an event that was every bit about skill, nerve, and the undeniable allure of pure sportsmanship. Staged with sublime flair and audacity, the first-ever Indoor Tow-In World Series literally made waves right where one would least expect - in a 65-meter indoor pool. Three electrifying days of battle, drama, stealth, and glory unfolded under the roof of the world's largest watersports trade fair.

As day one dawned, athletes plunged into the challenge, acclimatising to the unique trials of the indoor pool. Tactics, daring feats, and an edge-of-the-seat training session set the tone for spectacle that was yet to come.

However, the third day was the pinnacle moment when windsurfing history was penned. The finals rolled out like an about-to-burst adrenaline reservoir. Over five runs, the athletes conjured up unprecedented displays of freestyle windsurfing, each move stunning audiences into awed silence before erupting into thunderous applause.

In the women's division, after Elena Dominick took the early lead, it was reigning queen Maaike Huvermann who fired up the pool with her superb performance, claiming victory with a high-powered second run. French windsurfer Salome Fournier also displayed spectacular sportsmanship, sliding into third place with her innovative techniques.

The men's division, in comparison, was nothing short of combustive. As the competition evolved, shades of nerves smoothened into a palette of technical brilliance, closing with Lennart Neubauer's thrilling last-second triumph.
This event not just wrote history but also redefined the future of windsurfing and showed the resilience of a sport that can make waves, even indoors.

title: Lanzarote's Marina Rubicón Set to Blaze a Trail with First iQFOiL Games of the LA 2028 Olympic Cycle
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Lanzarote's Marina Rubicón Set to Blaze a Trail with First iQFOiL Games of the LA 2028 Olympic Cycle
summary: The inaugural iQFOiL International Games of the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic cycle are poised to make breakers at Marina Rubicón, Lanzarote.
body: An air of anticipation stirs the ocean at Marina Rubicón in Lanzarote as it braces to host the first iQFOiL International Games of the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Cycle. This world-class sailing destination, renowned for its contrasting volcanic landscapes, perennial sunshine, and steady trade winds, will stage five days of intensely thrilling racing from January 28 to February 2. Echoing the buzz and spirit of its successful past iterations, this marks the third year that Marina Rubicón has partnered seamlessly with the iQFOiL Class to host stellar global events.

The upcoming iQFOiL Games in Lanzarote will see a cadre of distinguished athletes race against the wind. The men's crew features eight competitors from the Paris 2024 Olympics, spotlighted by Kiran Badloe, the ex-Olympic champion. The lineup also boasts 2024 World Champion Nicolo Renna, European Champion Pawel Tarnowski, and U23 World Champion Finn Hawkins. These changes aim to reward consistency, champion inclusivity, and elevate the games to the next echelon, ensuring an adrenaline-packed spectacle for fans all over the world.

title: Notts County Sailing Club: Showing True Grit in 2025 County Cooler
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Notts County Sailing Club: Showing True Grit in 2025 County Cooler
summary: The 2025 County Cooler, hosted at Notts County Sailing Club, proves resilient in the face of a vicious storm, providing spectators with a thrilling sailboat race
body: The adventures on the high seas may have stories of heroism and courage, but the 2025 County Cooler held at the Notts County Sailing Club had its own tales of valour and tenacity. The annual sailing competition, held over two days, was preceded by the tumultuous Storm Eowyn spewing gusty wrath across the county. However, the tempest couldn't dampen everyone’s spirits. On the Saturday, the sun was shining bright, and thirty-four dinghies and seven windsurfers were bobbing along the starting line, ready for the challenge.

In attendance were the local clubs participating in the four-part Midlands series. With race officer Martin Hayhoe leading the charge, one would have found it difficult to believe the stormy turmoil from just a day ago. The events of the day included back-to-back races after a pause for lunch with congenial race conditions featuring warm sunshine and mild winds.

The severe conditions whittled the fleet, with only the boldest choosing to brave the final race. Among them were stalwarts Nigel Potter and Gerry Haninabus improving their overnight standing of 13th to finish 4th overall, and Rebecca Ogden in an Aero, who defied norms and stereotypes to claim the 1st lady position.

The windsurfing category saw Burton's Sam Birch and Joe Faulkner on equal points, but Birch took the trophy thanks to his performance in the final race. The 2025 County Cooler was a testament to the resolute spirit of competitors, who showcased extraordinary skill and camaraderie amidst challenging conditions. As all eyes turn to the next competition, one thing remains clear: the love for sailing and the joy of competition float ever high above the stormy waters.

title: An Inside Look into Navigational Safety and Risk Assessment in the World of Luxury Superyachts
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: An Inside Look into Navigational Safety and Risk Assessment in the World of Luxury Superyachts
summary: When two super-rich superyachts inadvertently dance too closely in the ocean, who's at the helm to avoid a grand nautical disaster?
body: In the glittering world of superyachts, luxury often overshadows the practicalities of sailing. However, behind the idyllic scenes of majestic yachts anchored peacefully in azure waters, safety procedures are of paramount importance. This importance is highlighted in a recent incident report which details a near-collision of two superyachts, caused by a wind shift that led to their overlapping swinging circles. One of the vessels managed to start its engines and attempt to manoeuvre away from the impending nautical disaster. Alas, the contact was inevitable. Interestingly, the second vessel's response came only after the collision, due to an unmanned bridge. Despite the lack of immediate human intervention, the damage was mercifully minimal.

As the narrative unfolds, it lays bare the complexities and challenges inherent in running a superyacht. It underscores the vital importance of having a culture of safety onboard, of making the difficult call to disappoint guest expectations for the sake of security, of carefully assessing and responding to weather conditions and collision risks even while at anchor, and of the delicate task of managing owner expectations. In a world where indulgence is expected, safety cannot be put aside, even against the most opulent of backdrops. The high seas may be a playground for superyachts but are, after all, fraught with unpredictability.

title: The 2025 Festival of Sails Crowns Twenty Division Champions Amid Thrilling Sea Spectacle
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The 2025 Festival of Sails Crowns Twenty Division Champions Amid Thrilling Sea Spectacle
summary: The famed Festival of Sails 2025 in Geelong, Australia, concluded in a spectacular display of seafaring prowess, crowning nearly twenty division champions.
body: The esteemed Festival of Sails 2025, held at the Royal Geelong Yacht Club, recently brought down the curtain on a breathtaking spectacle of sailing mastery. Featuring a staggering lineup of 246 boats, 1,100 sailors, and close to 100,000 onlooking visitors, this event was a remarkable display of maritime splendour. Upon its conclusion, almost twenty divisional champions were joyfully crowned. Raymond Roberts from Team Hollywood was among the victors, even graciously acknowledging his victory ahead of the final day of racing which was regrettably cut short due to storm threats.

Notably, the co-skippers of Clockwork, Andrew Lloyd and Mary Ann Harvey, clinched the overall win on IRC in Passage Rating Division 2. The ORC winner in this division was Wicked, co-skippered by the Welsh brothers, Mike and Mark. A splendid display was also put forth by Ginan, guided by sailing duo Nigel Jones and Cam Mckenzie, who impressively secured an almost flawless scorecard to clinch victory on AMS.

Notwithstanding the disappointment stemming from the early termination of the contest due to stormy weather, the participants and spectators alike savoured the ones-in-a-lifetime experience. The Geelong-based event, one of the highlight fixtures of the Australian yacht racing circuit, has continued to inspire generations of sailors with its unique blend of competition and camaraderie on the high seas.

title: Rough Waters Shift Vendée Globe Finishers Off Course: Unplanned Celebrations Ensue in La Rochelle
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Rough Waters Shift Vendée Globe Finishers Off Course: Unplanned Celebrations Ensue in La Rochelle
summary: In a twist of fate, stormy seas force the latest Vendée Globe finishers, Benjamin Dutreux and Clarisse Crémer, away from the exalted finish at Les Sables d'Olonne.
body: In a tussle with Mother Nature, the anticipated climax of the Vendée Globe race took an unexpected turn. Just when the solo skippers, Benjamin Dutreux and Clarisse Crémer, were about to bask in the glory of their victory, rough waters forced them to change course. The North Atlantic storm made Les Sables d'Olonne, the revered finish line, unsafe for the seafarers to venture into. Safety at sea is cardinal, and so they decided to divert their path towards La Rochelle. While the finish was different than they pictured, it was nonetheless filled with warmth and celebration. La Rochelle greeted the skilled mariners with open arms, making the unplanned detour a memorable occasion.

The tumultuous ordeal was not just limited to the top 10 finishers. The sweeping depression led to multiple sailors having to adapt their course of action. Among them, Boris Herrmann and Sam Davies had to slow down, letting the worst of the storm pass, putting their finishing attempts on hold. They are expected to be the next skippers to cross the finish line, adding to the growing list of Vendée Globe participants who embraced the unforeseen changes.

The thrilling episode underscores the fact that the sea remains unpredictable, no matter the circumstances. The hardened skippers who embark on the seafaring odyssey called Vendée Globe know this all well. The finish line, no matter where it lies, is an accomplishment in itself, and diverting to La Rochelle has allowed Dutreux and Crémer to bask in an unexpected celebration of their hard-fought victory.

title: The Latest Addition to the D-Class Fleet: Mermaid Shines in Hot Pink
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Latest Addition to the D-Class Fleet: Mermaid Shines in Hot Pink
summary: Making a dashing addition to the D-Class fleet, 'Mermaid' is a head-turner with her distinctive hot pink hull, ready to make waves in the yachting universe.
body: With a hue that's as stunning as the high seas she'll soon be sailing, Mermaid is far from your average D-Class yacht. Undergoing restoration by the proficient hands at Tasmanian Shipwrights & Co, she is the second D-Class family member for the owners of the Merlin D18. Making her debut in the regular twilight sessions in Kettering, her distinct hot pink hull is impossible to miss among the local fleet. Mermaid's restoration process was not just a lick of lively paint; the boat required comprehensive repair with a bevy of WEST SYSTEM epoxy products, E-fibreglass, Technifill R1160 and Epifanes gloss varnish from none other than ATL Composites. The result? A sight to behold. Mermaid's extravagant aesthetics aside, a considerable amount of work went into her six-month-long restoration endeavour, often involving long working days to ensure that she was ready for the relaunch at the Australian Wooden Boat Festival in February. Her imposing 36-foot mast enhances her grandness on the sea, which is unusual but fitting for her 24-foot size. Despite being intriguingly complex, the project turned out to be a fruitful one, with the end product being a unique blend of traditions and modern design choices. Matt Stevens, the director at Tasmanian Shipwrights & Co, praised the products used in the restoration process, particularly Epifanes' traditional varnish, for its ease of use and splendid results. With a successful restoration project under their belts, the team's gaze now turns towards several other projects, including the restoration of the 40-foot timber yacht, Tradition, and the 30-foot Cayzer motor yacht, Floki. To the owners' delight, Mermaid's striking pink outer shell stole the show, causing a stir around the yard and receiving mixed responses from the public. However, once they see the entire fleet line-up, with Nymph's yellow, Minerva's purple and Gremlin's dark forest green, Mermaid's hot pink will feel right at home. Anticipation builds for the official launch on February 5, where spectators can catch the stunning Mermaid gracing the waters along with her D-Class counterparts.

title: Exciting Finale to the Vaikobi Windsurfer Class Australian National Championships
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Exciting Finale to the Vaikobi Windsurfer Class Australian National Championships
summary: The highly anticipated conclusion of the 2025 Vaikobi Windsurfer Class Australian National Championships brought excitement and riveting competition.
body: The fifth and final day of the 2025 Vaikobi Windsurfer Class Australian National Championships at the Toronto Amateur Sailing Club was filled with electricity. Happening on the dates between the 22nd and 26th of January, the morning was graced by competitors performing dynamic freestyle routines to a pulsating soundtrack, providing a feast for the senses for the spectator assembly.

Complementing the enthralling spectacle, vibrant commentary was continuously driving amusement and keeping the spectators engaged. Upon the conclusion of the freestyle performances, the remainder of the Slalom knockout heats was held in an inviting 8-12 knot SSE breeze.

This thrilling spectacle was a smashing celebration of swirling winds, mighty waves, and remarkable agility. The participants showcased sheer determination and skills, while the audience fulfilled their roles as cheerful enthusiasts. It was indeed, a perfect demonstration of the lively, competitive, and adventurous spirit of the sailing community.

title: Ancasta Yachts Services Forges Alliance with Flexiteek UK to Offer Premium Decking Services
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Ancasta Yachts Services Forges Alliance with Flexiteek UK to Offer Premium Decking Services
summary: Ancasta Yachts Services has announced its collaboration with Flexiteek UK to deliver superior decking services to yachts spanning 35-75ft.
body: There's a fresh wind blowing in the world of yacht services. Ancasta Yachts Services, already a respected name in boat sales and maintenance, is joining forces with Flexiteek UK, the renowned supplier of synthetic teak decking products. This new alliance promises to set a new standard in yacht maintenance and aesthetics, delivering synthetic decking to yachts between 35-75 feet in length.

Under the agreement, Flexiteek UK will entrust its full range of synthetic teak decking products, inclusive of the award-nominated Flexiteek 3, to the expert craftsmen of Ancasta Yacht Services. With its highly experienced shipwright team and top-notch facilities, Ancasta is deemed the perfect partner to install Flexiteek’s product range along the South Coast.

Users have the option to choose from a wide selection of colour options, securing the possibility of a total deck transformation without sidelining their personal style. They can also avail themselves of the new Ash shade, a lighter colour for those seeking a fresher, brighter look.

The partnership doesn’t only spell a milestone for Ancasta and Flexiteek but also extends an exciting opportunity for owners to revamp their yachts or address any deck upgrades and repair needs from the previous season.

More than just a decking installer, Ancasta Yacht Services also provides a range of other marine products and services. It is an approved service agent for a list of leading marine brands, including Jet Thruster, Yanmar, Volvo Penta, Lewmar, and OceanLED, amongst others.

title: Bracing Winter Winds Drive Spirited Youth Race Training at Paignton Sailing Club
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Bracing Winter Winds Drive Spirited Youth Race Training at Paignton Sailing Club
summary: Avid young sailors at Paignton Sailing Club defied winter's chill in a captivating weekend filled with sailing strategies, camaraderie, and triumphant tacks.
body: In the crisp embrace of winter, Paignton Sailing Club burgeoned into a bustling haven for young sailing enthusiasts. The South West Youth Sailing Academy (SWYSA) masterminded an invigorating weekend of Race Coaching, held from Saturday, 11th to Sunday, 12th of January. Despite the winter chill, the conditions were surprisingly favourable, as the waves coursed rhythmically under the mellow gusts of an 8-15 knot wind.

Amidst the intense training and bouts of seafaring strivings, all sailors relished a hearty pasta lunch, courtesy of the host, Paignton Sailing Club’s diligent volunteers. The SWYSA's Winter Race Coaching sessions brought more than skills to the fore - a friendly, inclusive spirit burgeoned, as young sailors spent hours together, nurturing friendships and upholding the passion they share for the waters.
The success of the event owes much to the plentiful contributions from coaches and parents, those who animated the event's organisational efforts and navigated safety and coach boats on the water.

A hearty nod to Paignton Sailing Club for their warm reception and relentless commitment to hosting a successful event. The activities of the weekend have left our sailors eagerly anticipating the next training weekend, scheduled for 15-16 February, promising another exciting bout of maritime masterclasses.

title: Unseen Dangers Still Lurk on the Water: Luxury Yachts Devoured by Flames in Marseilles Marina
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unseen Dangers Still Lurk on the Water: Luxury Yachts Devoured by Flames in Marseilles Marina
summary: Recently, a marina fire in the Port de Lave in Marseille has sparked a crucial dialogue about safety measures in the boating world.
body: In a surreal scenario reminiscent of a classic rock hit, a dangerous fire danced upon the water at the Port de Lave in Marseille. The fire's insatiable appetite decimated three yachts, causing significant damage and raising unavoidable questions about safety on the water. Luckily, no lives were claimed, but with the destruction of valuable properties, the incident serves as a stern reminder of the importance of constant vigilance and fire prevention.

On the evening of January 9th, a massive force of 63 firefighters, 19 vehicles, three firefighting boats, and aerial reconnaissance drones were deployed to tackle the menacing blaze, signifying the scale of the challenge they were up against. A minor spark rapidly transformed into an uncontrollable force, leaping from one yacht to others moored nearby. In the chaos, two of the vessels broke away from their moorings, which further complicated the firefighting efforts.

While the cause of the fire remains unconfirmed, industry insiders suggest a likely culprit: lithium-ion batteries, commonly used in toys and tenders, could potentially be behind this and similar incidents. The batteries, though easy to use, might harbour unforeseen risks, serving as potential ticking time bombs.

The industry is at a critical juncture, forced to re-examine its guidelines to avoid such incidents. A comprehensive understanding of the risks and appropriate preventive measures are imperative. To achieve this, lessons must be learned from past incidents. This will entail data sharing and real investment of time in studying the root causes of these destructive fires. Safety is a collective responsibility and plays a vital role in preserving the reputation of the boating market.

Investigations into the Marseille fire are underway, but until the industry squarely faces the risks lithium-ion batteries may pose, doubts will be raised about current safety practices. Such incidents have wide-reaching implications on other aspects of the water world. It's time to face the music; the industry must act collectively and irrefutably to prevent fires in the marina and secure the future of sea-faring luxury.

title: British Luxury Goods Retailer Glancy Fawcett Expands Global Presence with Prestigious Abu Dhabi Showroom Opening
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: British Luxury Goods Retailer Glancy Fawcett Expands Global Presence with Prestigious Abu Dhabi Showroom Opening
summary: Renowned for their curated luxury items, Glancy Fawcett marks an innovative expansion with a prestigious showroom opening in Abu Dhabi.
body: Capping a decade of presence in the region, esteemed British luxury goods purveyor Glancy Fawcett has made a significant leap with the opening of a flagship showroom in Abu Dhabi. The new location provides an exclusive space for the brand's expanding clientele to peruse a curated assortment of the world's finest crystal, bed linen, dinnerware, table linen, towels, and silverware.

The bespoke showroom builds on the success of their Manchester boutique. The location allows clients to explore an extensive range of swatches, finishes, and materials, enabling them to truly personalise their interior dreams. The space will be stewarded by some of Glancy Fawcett's most experienced hands, exemplifying the brand's commitment to personalised service.

Elizabeth Quiligotti, Director at Glancy Fawcett, couldn't contain her enthusiasm about the launch. 'We are delighted to provide a space that represents our passion for luxury in Abu Dhabi. Our clients in the region have high expectations for service and personalisation. This showroom is a tangible epitome of these elements,' she stated.
The showroom offers a haven for those keen to immerse themselves in a realm of elegance, craftsmanship, and customised luxury, fully embodying the company's dedication to high-end service.

With the launch of the Abu Dhabi showroom, Glancy Fawcett has inarguably fortified its position within the luxury goods market – a true testament to their enduring commitment to delivering superior quality to their discerning patrons.

title: Majestic Innovation Underway: Italy Pushes Luxury to New Heights with Ground-breaking 100-Metre Superyacht
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Majestic Innovation Underway: Italy Pushes Luxury to New Heights with Ground-breaking 100-Metre Superyacht
summary: Setting all sails towards innovation, Italy's The Italian Sea Group is making remarkable progress on its largest superyacht construction.
body: The maritime landscape is about to welcome a gem of epic proportions. Italy's esteemed sea specialist, The Italian Sea Group (TISG), is living up to its reputation as a peddler of opulence and innovation. The pride of Italy, TISG's Admiral brand, has recorded an important step in the construction of its most ambitious project - a grandiose 100-meter hybrid superyacht, known as Hull 597.

Previously tongue-in-cheek referred to as Project Titanium, the build process has progressed into the outfitting phase at the shipyard's facility in Italy's Riviera hotspot, Marina di Carrara. The yacht is already turning heads as the largest of its kind under construction in Italy with a delivery date tantalizingly set for 2026.

Extravagance is the cornerstone of this floating palace. Boasting features such as a certified helicopter landing pad, an oversized swimming pool, a state-of-the-art spa, and a multi-level saloon beckon potential guests with luxury beyond imagination.

The involvement of the esteemed Magnitude Yachts as project managers highlights the project's prominence, marking their third joint venture with TISG. TISG's founder and CEO, Giovanni Costantino, expressed satisfaction with the yacht's production progress and the synergistic partnership with industry giants like Magnitude Yachts and Winch Design. The superyacht is not an isolated project within TISG's portfolio but part of a flourishing collection that includes the 82-meter Project Skyfall and 77-meter Project Blue Marlin - each scheduled for their grand reveal in 2025.

author: Old Sea Dogs

Led by accomplished sailor Alex Dare, the practise day saw a parade of young and experienced sailors from different backgrounds, united by their passion for the sport, and their shared vessel of choice: the increasingly popular J/70s.

It's evident that the sport of sailing continues to evolve with its competitors. This year's enthralling spectacle features five interstate teams, seven youth teams, and 14 teams of Corinthians, offering a flavourful mix of styles and strategies that keeps everyone on their toes. Nautical spectators and competitors can't help but get infused with an invigorating sense of anticipation and camaraderie.

Sailing these exhilarating boats is nothing short of a nuanced dance with wind and water, rewarding those who decipher its subtle cues. Chris magnifies this allure, revealing how the sport's heartening surge in youthful participants has accelerated the class's development via a fresh infusion of styles and ideas. Encouragingly, the stringent measurement rules and freedom to choose a preferred sailmaker allows each sailor to intricately tailor their boat according to their temperament and style.

The 2025 J/70 Australian Championship in Sandringham Yacht Club has certainly kicked off on a high. Stay tuned for more updates over the week as brave sailors continue to slice through Port Phillp Bay's mesmerising waters, their eyes set on the ultimate glory.

title: Online Tracking Technology Breaks Waves at the Euromarina Optimist Torrevieja Children's Regatta
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Online Tracking Technology Breaks Waves at the Euromarina Optimist Torrevieja Children's Regatta
summary: Emerging technology is transforming the world of sailing. The buzz? Online tracking at the Euromarina Optimist Torrevieja Children's Sailing Regatta.
body: The Euromarina Optimist Torrevieja Children's Sailing Regatta is setting the bar high within the competitive sailing scene. This well-renowned event is taking a quantum leap with a major technological partnership. They've recently teamed up with TracTrac, an online positioning company, to bring live tracking to the event's races for this edition and the following two. This mover-and-shaker approach places the regatta as the first of its kind to incorporate such technology at a national level.

This impactful upgrade is being introduced with less than three weeks to the official kick-off, slated from January 30th to February 2nd. The prestigious regatta, sponsored by Euromarina and organized by the Real Club Nautico de Torrevieja, will feature 430 sailors from 29 countries, including an intriguing entrant from Central Asia: Tajikistan.

As much as the competition is fierce and immersive, the social component of the event isn't overshadowed. A highlight includes a remarkable 'Welcome Party' set for Thursday, where Euromarina will host a lively parade spotlighting all the international teams alongside representatives of the Autonomous Communities of Spain.

As the regatta concludes, Sunday's trophy ceremony promises to be a grand spectacle, with the whole sailing family participating. Awaiting guests of honour are the Mayor of Torrevieja, the Regional Minister of Tourism, and authorities who enable this international event that promotes grassroots sports. This embracing party paints a beautiful picture of the integration of technology, fierce competition, and communal bond, all encapsulated in the love for sailing.

title: Southern Wind Strikes a High Note with Its Largest Sailing Yacht Yet
