This grand build is not just another ship in the fleet - it's considered a groundbreaking entity in the world of yachting, an "entirely new, customisable platform" built for performance and perfection.

The design anchors itself in the reliable partnership between esteemed collaborators, Farr Yacht Design and Nauta Design, imparting to the SW123 not only size but finesse and functionality. Constructed at the acclaimed yard's pristine facilities in Cape Town, the launch of this megayacht is set for February 2027.

The details that groom this yacht to perfection will be revealed as the build ambitiously sails towards its launch date. As per BOATPro reports, this is just one of the four yachts Southern Wind has on order; another mentionable build is the 35.4-metre Kiboko 4, which set sail for her sea trials in December 2024.

title: Second Wind: Yoann Richomme Makes Splash in His First Vendée Globe, Landing Coveted Runner-Up Position
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Second Wind: Yoann Richomme Makes Splash in His First Vendée Globe, Landing Coveted Runner-Up Position
summary: Yoann Richomme, a strategic maestro and audacious sailor, makes a phenomenal debut in the testing Vendée Globe race, sailing to a laudable second place finish.
body: When it comes to nautical mastery, Yoann Richomme is certainly making waves. This gifted sailor recently proved his mettle in the Vendée Globe, one of the most prestigious and rigorous yacht racing competitions across the globe. The solo round-the-world race, known for its treacherous conditions, saw Richomme fearlessly navigating his vessel to a commendable second place finish.

From the race's early days, Richomme's exceptional talent was evident. His subscription to a safe route around a perilous low-pressure system in the Indian Ocean, for instance, showcased his strategic acumen. While initially this decision appeared to put him at a disadvantage, his perseverance paid dividends in the end.

However, Richomme's unwavering spirit kept him firmly on course. It wasn't about claiming first place for him, but delivering his very best. This humble approach, coupled with his unparalleled talent, won him a revered spot among the leading figures of this legendary race, etching his name indelibly in Vendée Globe's annals.

In spite of the gruelling nature of the race, this sailing maverick expressed his astonishment at the voyage's swift conclusion. To him, it felt like they had departed merely two days prior—an indication of his unyielding passion for the sea and the thrill of competition. His relentless drive to hone his craft, build robust team dynamics, and pursue optimum results is a testament to his dedication.

Even in his triumph, Richomme remains grounded. Rather than chasing accolades, he's keen on the continuous pursuit of skill enhancement and enjoyment of the game. His approach personifies the spirit of fair play and good sportspersonship, offering an inspirational model to peak performers in any discipline.

By all accounts, Richomme's name is now engraved in the rich tapestry of sailing's history, and this audacious seafarer certainly has much more to offer in the wave-crested horizon. Yoann Richomme may have placed second in the Vendée Globe race this time, but he's off to a winning start in the arena of global maritime competitions.

title: Reviving Yesteryears: Royal Western Yacht Club Re-visits 1925 Fastnet Racecourse & Announces New Date for Round Iceland Race
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Reviving Yesteryears: Royal Western Yacht Club Re-visits 1925 Fastnet Racecourse & Announces New Date for Round Iceland Race
summary: Royal Western Yacht Club recreates maritime nostalgia, announcing a race along the 1925 Fastnet Course, while also shaking things up with a date change for the '25 Round Iceland Race.
body: In a breezy blend of nostalgia and ambition, the Royal Western Yacht Club invites sailing enthusiasts to partake in a celebration of a century. Recreating the original Fastnet race of 1925, the flotilla will trace the eastern path through the forts and perform a stately rotation around the Isle of Wight.

Marking the centenary of this legendary race, the club welcomes entries for this historic re-run. Notably, this will be only the second time that yachts have embarked on the original Fastnet Racecourse. The lap of honour setting out from Ryde Bank, heading due East out of the Solent and culminating in the same location as its namesake in 1925 - Plymouth Sound.

International entries are flooding in, pushing the starting lineup towards double figures. To add a bit of spice, many participants aim to rack up the qualifying miles for the World Star '26. Others, meanwhile, simply relish the challenge of this rigorous 2000-mile venture across some of the globe's harshest waters.

Open to a range of yacht classes, from solo to fully crewed, the race will start from Plymouth Sound National Marine Park. The challenge is to leave the Eddystone Lighthouse and Iceland to starboard, and finish on the Royal Western Yacht Club line.

Although the waves may be challenging, the camaraderie and spirit of maritime adventure unites competitors. Spectacular starts and nail-biting finishes are set to cement the Royal Western Yacht Club's place in yachting history once again.

title: Boris Herrmann Returns to Northern Hemisphere, Marks New Milestone in the Challenging Vendée Globe Race
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Boris Herrmann Returns to Northern Hemisphere, Marks New Milestone in the Challenging Vendée Globe Race
summary: German sailor Boris Herrmann has reached a significant milestone in the Vendée Globe race, crossing back over the equator and entering the Northern Hemisphere.
body: With the moon lighting his path, Boris Herrmann toasted to Neptune, marking his victory over the equatorial line and the tumultuous waters of the Southern Hemisphere. Herrmann has triumphed over some of the most challenging conditions in the Vendée Globe, the non-stop, unassisted, solo round-the-world race which has taken him on a remarkable nautical journey. Through the Cape of Good Hope, past the haunting Cape Leeuwin and the formidable Cape Horn, and beyond the solitude of Point Nemo, he has navigated vast oceans and lengthy solitude. After 64 thrilling days at sea, Herrmann stands tall at the 9th place, with 3,200 nautical miles beckoning him to the finish line at Les Sables d'Olonne. The journey has not been without its challenges - from lightning strikes that damaged crucial systems onboard, a broken J2 hook that left him without his most essential headsail, to an Arbalète issue. And yet, undeterred by setbacks and a fear of heights, he managed two mast climbs, swiftly mended his rigging issues, and resurrected vital systems. His spirit, as strong as the boat that they call Malizia - Seaexplorer, is far from broken; in fact, it's powered with an unflinching focus on the horizon ahead. The race may have seen a winner in Charlie Dalin, who impressively shattered the race record by over nine days, but Herrmann's journey isn't over. With his eyes firmly set on a top-five finish, this captain is steering his way into the final push. The Vendée Globe might be a race for some. Still, for Boris Herrmann, it's a testament to the mariner's spirit - a dance with the sea, a journey of perseverance and a celebration of adventure that resonates with the empowering crash of the northern waves.

title: Unrivaled Showdown at the 2025 Etchells World Championship Yields Victory for the Magpie Team
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unrivaled Showdown at the 2025 Etchells World Championship Yields Victory for the Magpie Team
summary: Winning is a habit for the Magpie skippered by Graeme Taylor, which recently defended their title at the 2025 Etchells World Championship.
body: When the ocean becomes a stage for a riveting battle of skills and strategy, it can only be a momentous sailing championship. The 2025 Etchells World Championship, hosted by the esteemed Royal Brighton Yacht Club, served as the theatre for a defining regatta saga, characterised by an unprecedented showdown between two highly-skilled teams.

The Magpie AUS1486 crew, led by the skillful Graeme Taylor, together with seasoned mariners, James Mayo and crew member Ben Lamb, raised their game to defend their title. This victory was a testament to their experience, dedication and remarkable teamwork, setting a remarkable standard for this prestigious competition.

Under the tactical guidance of 'Lamby', Ben Lamb, the team held firm their resolve, leveraging an advantageous mathematical standing on-tide to secure the championship. This showdown between the two contenders, trading blows on the open sea, offered an unforgettable spectacle for all present.

Despite their robust performance, DanEgerous was left in a vulnerable position with a higher worst discard compared to Magpie. Consequently, the Magpie crew seized the chance to reinforce their lead and ultimately emerged victorious. In the face of unpredictable winds and relentless opposition, they skillfully navigated their way to the podium.

The thrilling finale literally came down to what Graeme Taylor referred to as a 'boat on boat battle for the regatta title'. The spectator-lined coastline held its collective breath as the match kicked off with the hoist of the Orange Flag. The heart-stopping tussle between the two world-class teams ended only at the final gun.

Indeed, such a dynamite finale echoes the sentiments shared by sailing enthusiast, Bill Hardesty when he remarked, 'Well, sometimes you're the bug and sometimes you're the windshield.' The 2025 Etchells World Championship brought this wet and wild phrase to life and proved once again, that in the extraordinary theater of sailing, fortune favours the bold.

title: Thrilling Seas, Unseen Depths: An Unforgettable Dive into Charlie Dalin's Vendée Globe Triumph
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Thrilling Seas, Unseen Depths: An Unforgettable Dive into Charlie Dalin's Vendée Globe Triumph
summary: In a breathtaking demonstration of seamanship, Charlie Dalin claimed a resounding victory in the coveted Vendée Globe, leaving fans and competitors awestruck.
body: In the vast open waters that stretch beyond our familiar shores, unyielding skippers turn to the whispers of the winds and the pulsing tides, in an endeavour to conquer the formidable Vendée Globe race. Here, amid the breakwater roar and the thrilling skirl of sea birds, a new legend was crafted. Charlie Dalin, atop the magnificent MACIF Santé Prévoyance, did more than just win the Vendée Globe. He seized the race by its very nature, bending the very elements to his indomitable will, and wrote an unforgettable chapter in sailing history.

Dalins triumphant finish was a sight to behold - a sea-borne dance of man and vessel at the crack of dawn, with the ocean reflecting the heavenly hues. The record books will be rewritten, but the vistas of that awe-striking moment will forever remain etched in the memories of those fortunate enough to bear witness. His phenomenal performance is a beacon for aspiring sailors and a testament to human resilience.

Following closely behind Dalin were fierce competitors Yoann Richomme and Sébastien Simon, undaunted, pushing their boats and abilities to the limit, relentlessly pursuing the horizon. Their commendable efforts amplified the tenacity and level of skill that the Vendée Globe demands, setting a high bar for future contenders. A brilliant saga has come to a close, leaving an indelible impact on the soul of sailing. Dalin, on his victorious MACIF Santé Prévoyance, is more than just a champion of this Vendée Globe. He is a beacon of potential, skill, and unyielding inspiration, involved in a love affair with the open sea. Its wave-crested chaos and serene strength echo in his victory, a symphony that will sing of his triumph for generations.

So, as the salt spray settles, and the celebratory cheers fade to the ebbing music of the sea, Dalin's name will forever echo in the annals of sailing lore. A man and his yacht, together enduring the unforgiving ocean to claim victory. A testament to humanity's spirit, a beacon of our courage to dream, dare, and dominate. Through storm and calm, Charlie Dalin has sailed into history, and his legend, like the sea he commands, is unending.

title: Nico Lunven Recaptures Northern Hemisphere in Vendée Globe Race, Sails through Doldrums
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Nico Lunven Recaptures Northern Hemisphere in Vendée Globe Race, Sails through Doldrums
summary: Sailing magnate Nico Lunven brings his boat Holcim-PRB back to the Northern Hemisphere during the intense Vendée Globe competition.
body: Nicolas Lunven, the daredevil sailor, recently marked his triumphant return to the Northern Hemisphere during the thrilling Vendée Globe challenge. Having effectively traversed the notorious Doldrums, Lunven continues to stay the course and vie for contention in one of the world’s most gruelling yacht races. As the overall winner, Charlie Dalin, jubilantly disembarked in Les Sables d'Olonne, the race among the pursuers intensified. Lunven, navigating through the night, managed to conquer the Intertropical Convergence Zone, which is known to thwart even seasoned mariners. Lunven, however, dealt with it as though it was another day at the office. Since yesterday, he found merriment in navigating close to the Saint Peter and Saint Paul Islands marking his arrival in the Northern Hemisphere. Surviving the nerve-wracking Doldrums, Lunven attested to the vicissitudes, comparing it to someone toyishly tampering with a fan, adjusting the intensity, and setting it to spin in all directions. But the wind never lost strength, providing him with a persistent 10-12 knots of wind, demanding constant trimming and course adjusting, but always propelling him forward. Having cleared the erratic cloud zones, he still battles the ceaselessly fluctuating wind, making rest elusive. As the sun rose, he needed a brief pause to address an issue with his J2 tack. However, once resolved and back on his course, he contended with hard-hitting 28 knots of wind, shifting 50 degrees. The sudden chaos ensued, the boat heaving and plunging in the undulating waves. Lunven's adventure continues, demonstrating his undying spirit to sail in pursuit of glory in the Vendée Globe.

title: Sailing Prodigy Pollard Autographs the Waters of Singapore in the SB20 Championship: World Glory on Horizon
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Sailing Prodigy Pollard Autographs the Waters of Singapore in the SB20 Championship: World Glory on Horizon
summary: In an enticing prelude to the SB20 World Championships, sailor John Pollard steals the spotlight in Singapore, challenging the world's best with aplomb.
body: Riding the high tides of Sentosa Cove in Singapore, John Pollard, the British sailing maestro, gave a stellar performance at the SB20 Asian Continental Championship. This not only solidified his formidable reputation but also set up an exciting stage for the much-anticipated SB20 World Championships. The sportsboat fleet, steeped in talent and experience, witnessed a display of exceptional seamanship, strategy, and sportsmanship. All eyes are steadily trained on the upcoming World Championship, the first to be hosted in Southeast Asia, with an impressive international contingent of 45 fleets involved.

Adding flair to the competition, there's the French wunderkind Xavier Rohart, crewing for Ed Russo, the seasoned class loyalist, and Ukrainian sailor George Leonchuk, partnered with Paolo Borghesi. Not just relying on veterans, there is a wave of new talent with young sailors keen to take the prestigious SB20 podium.

Only three days of the SB20 Asian Continental Championship have now passed, yet they prove to be a valuable litmus test, offering glimpses into the form the main event could take. John Pollard shone brightly, pulling impressive leads, setting his boat, Xcellent, on a promising trajectory. Being a consistent high performer at the Worlds with 14 top ten finishes since 2009, Pollard's unwavering dedication and hard work have been crucial to his burgeoning success.

Stepping up to the plate, Pollard has well and truly laid down the challenge in Singapore. Capturing four victories out of five races in the Asian Champs, he has proved his unyielding desire to conquer the waters, symbolically discarding his 'worst' score, a stellar second place.

Singapore offers an opportunity for Pollard that may have seemed like a distant horizon in Ireland 2022, Netherlands 2023, and Dubai 2024. Will this be his time to outshine the competition and clinch the coveted title? Only the upcoming World Championship will tell. With the stage set for a thrilling showdown, all eyes are on Singapore as sailing’s most skilful seek World Championship glory.

title: Explore the Grandeur of Van der Valk's Custom 34.1-metre Superyacht 'One'
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Explore the Grandeur of Van der Valk's Custom 34.1-metre Superyacht 'One'
summary: Luxurious and unique, Van der Valk's 34.1-metre superyacht 'One' presents an exceptional fusion of functionality and aesthetics.
body: Hailing from the esteemed Dutch shipyard, Van der Valk's groundbreaking superyacht, One, rewrites the rule-books of luxury sea travel. Following upon its highly anticipated delivery at the end of last year, One emerges from the shadows of its initial alias, Project 111.11, into a world breathlessly awaiting its charm.

With design inputs from experienced owners, the 34.1-metre brain-child of Guido de Groot and Carla Guilhem depicts a vivid portrait of luxury. Naturally lit cabins, curving lines, and daringly large windows merge to form an unexpected symphony, driving a departure from organic designs to embracing the raw beauty of imperfect geometric forms.

The four-decked yacht comfortably houses up to ten people across five staterooms, despite the initial request for a larger space. Among the decadently adorned rooms, a full-beam master suite stands out, complete with a walk-in wardrobe and a unique recessed oval feature.

Making a bold statement are sculptural chairs, an impressive elliptical chandelier in the lounge, and a skin-smoothing monochrome look that highlights the neutral tones within the yacht. Yet, it maintains its formidable nature as a commercial charter class yacht, just under 300GT, and without needing a rescue tender or davit.

Powered by twin Volvo Penta 750hp engines, 'One' combines thrilling speed and unrivaled luxury, offering a peak velocity of up to 14.4 knots. In summary, Van der Valk's 'One' is a mingling of contrasting aesthetics and unyielding functionality, weaving an epic tale of maritime opulence.

title: Pulsating Rivalry and Breathtaking Speeds Ignite the 11th Royal Ocean Racing Club Transatlantic Race
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Pulsating Rivalry and Breathtaking Speeds Ignite the 11th Royal Ocean Racing Club Transatlantic Race
summary: The 2025 Royal Ocean Racing Club's Transatlantic Race builds intensity, marked by exhilarating speeds, neck-and-neck rivalry and atmospheric conditions dictating a strategic game.
body: Sea spray, the whispers of the wind, the scent of the salty open sea and the feeling of the deck moving beneath one's feet. There's nothing quite like the thrill and adventure of an offshore race, and the 2025 RORC Transatlantic Race delivers all these in spades.

Currently into its third day, Bryon Ehrhart’s Juan K 88 Lucky (USA) is carving a blazing trail, leading the monohull class. Trailing closely, with a gritty determination, Christian Zugel's Volvo 70 Tschüss 2 (USA) is posed for an electrifying challenge.

In the multihull class, the leader board is an intriguing puzzle. The huge fleet spread across 300 miles on either side of the rhumb line makes it hard to predict a definitive leader. However, Aldo Fumagalli's Rapido 53 Picomole (ITA) seems the closest to the finish line, situated outside the swanky Camper & Nicholsons Port Louis Marina, Grenada.

However, the competition remains incredibly fierce. Picomole, currently leading the multihull class, is cautiously defensive of its position. Further, despite a brief pit-stop, Hubert Wargny's Swan 78 Victoria (USA) is now back in the race, eager to assert its prowess on the rough open sea.

The Juan K 88 Lucky shines patriotically, leading the American charge across the Atlantic. It completes an impressive 400 miles every 24 hours since the start. In hot pursuit, the Volvo 70 Tschüss 2 is just 50 miles behind, pushing relentlessly. Both yachts have chosen a northern route past the Canary Islands, highlighting the labyrinthine strategising that this race demands.

Excitement, adrenaline, and the elemental beauty of the Atlantic. These are the promise of the 2025 RORC Transatlantic Race. This spectacle of maritime prowess is far from over, and the sea bares witness to a ballet of boats - a performance that exemplifies the true spirit of offshore racing.

title: Slower Boats Reign Supreme: The Pank Duo Triumph in the Infamous Bloody Mary Sailing Race
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Slower Boats Reign Supreme: The Pank Duo Triumph in the Infamous Bloody Mary Sailing Race
summary: Jono and Freddie Pank clinch victory in the iconic GJW Direct 49th Bloody Mary, outmanoeuvring faster boats and showcasing their savvy light-airs skills.
body: As the sails fluttered on a sleepy Saturday, the GJW Direct 49th Bloody Mary race hosted an unexpected spectacle. The Pank duo, Jono and Freddie, made the waves their playground, outsmarting faster vessels in a thrilling display of skill and strategy. In the world of sailing, this race holds a legendary status, renowned for its exhilarating pursuit race dynamic that tests the mettle of the UK's finest sailors. Jono Pank, a seasoned veteran, ignited his youthful spirit, laying out his strategy for this race after a 30-year hiatus. This time, he paired up with his 13-year-old son Freddie, forming an electrifying team. Their weapon of choice? The Firefly, a sailing dinghy well-suited for lighter airs. Defying the odds and proving that speed isn't the sole deciding factor, they emerged victorious against the fleet of 99 boats. As other faster boats struggled in the meager breeze, the Panks, aboard their Firefly, tactfully made their way to victory, crowning a new era for the slower boats. Spectators were left bewildered as the Panks strategically navigated through the fleet and ahead into the lead, a commendable feat given the tough competition. The duo's win gives rise to contemplation in a world traditionally spellbound by speed, magnifying the versatility and strategic nuances of sailing. In this battle of the boats, strategy, skill, and the fiery spirit of the Panks transformed the calm of the reservoir into a testimony of triumphant glory.

title: Historic Weather Bird Yacht, Exalted by Coco Chanel and Louis Armstrong, Destined for Auction
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Historic Weather Bird Yacht, Exalted by Coco Chanel and Louis Armstrong, Destined for Auction
summary: The Weather Bird, a legendary 1930s sailing yacht that once played host to icons like Coco Chanel and Louis Armstrong, is up for auction.
body: As far as nautical narratives go, few are as captivating as that of the Weather Bird. This 31-metre classic sailing yacht, now listed for auction by Boathouse Auctions, bears a history that resonates with glamour, legacy and an undeniable touch of regality. Bidding for the vessel kicks off at €1,000,000 and is set to unfurl virtually from 20th to 25th February.

Teeming with an allure that has magnetized luminaries and creatives since her inception in the 1930s, Weather Bird carries a legacy steeped in the grandeur of the Jazz Age. Crafted by the French yard Chantelot & Lemaistre to a design by Henri Rambaud, the yacht was commissioned by American expatriates Sarah and Gerald Murphy. The boat was often frequented by guests including the likes of Coco Chanel, Louis Armstrong, F. Scott Fitzgerald and Ernest Hemingway.

Despite the splendour that once surrounded her, Weather Bird's heydays encountered a sobering halt in 1933, with her owners soon forsaking their cherished vessel in the face of political turmoil and personal tragedy. After nearly a century, the gleaming schooner still embarks on new adventures, with several custodians maintaining her in pristine condition.

The yacht has undergone several updates, with the 2022 refit being particularly extensive. It rejuvenated her mechanical systems, automated her rigging systems and winches, and gave a fresh breath to the interiors, all while preserving her vintage elegance. It's a representation of yesteryears' glamour without compromising on modern functionalities.

From her Art Deco interior featuring a spacious saloon, U-shaped seating area, and bar, to the stylish outdoor lounging spaces complete with velveteen sunbeds, every corner of the Weather Bird is a testament to timeless style and grandeur. The yacht boasts four spacious guest cabins, including an owner's suite outfitted with a vanity desk.

Elevating Weather Bird beyond mere architecture is her unrivalled backstory - a narrative that sets one's imagination soaring to the golden days of yesteryears. As Broker Richard Callender points out, stepping onto the Weather Bird is a step into history, an era where exuberance, creativity and charm reigned supreme.

title: From Service Collaboration to Ownership: MB92 Group Welcomes GYG to Its Prestigious Fleet
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: From Service Collaboration to Ownership: MB92 Group Welcomes GYG to Its Prestigious Fleet
summary: Adding to its distinguished portfolio, MB92 Group has effectively acquired the reputable painting and supply firm, GYG, propelling its expansion aspirations.
body: With the arrival of the new year, MB92 Group commences an exciting phase of growth and dynamism. The esteemed institution has announced its effective acquisition of GYG, a distinguished painting, service and supply firm on the 31st of December, 2024. This acquisition aligns with MB92's aspirations of expansion through consolidation in light of evolving market demands. Moreover, it potentially solidifies MB92’s position, leveraging the collective expertise of both entities to present an enhanced repertoire of services to its wide client base.

Pepe García-Aubert, the chairman of MB92 Group, welcomes GYG warmly, emphasizing upon their shared trajectory rooted in mutual values, respect and an unwavering commitment to excellence, spanning a period of thirty years. The companies plan to further consolidate this strong foundation, by sharing their knowledge and expertise while propelling initiatives for sustainability and innovation for the benefit of the wider superyacht community.

Further consolidating its growth mandate, Squircle Capital, the private equity firm managing the fund that owns MB92 Group, also expressed support for this move. John Nery, the managing partner and head of investments at the firm, reaffirmed their unyielding commitment to fostering excellence and innovation in the superyacht sector. He also added that with the financial resources of MB92, GYG can enhance its operational and strategic capacities whilst planting the seeds for innovative growth opportunities.

MB92 affirms its client-centric approach and assures continued collaboration with a spectrum of providers. This promising approach ensures clients retain the flexibility to work in sync with their preferred partners while benefitting from the Group’s project management expertise. Meanwhile, joining the MB92 Group allows GYG to broaden its capabilities and continue delivering high-quality standards while exploring and manifesting growth opportunities.

title: Alfa Nero Superyacht Crew Nets a Staggering Payout: A Long-Fought Legal Battle Culminates in £890,000 in Unpaid Wages
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Alfa Nero Superyacht Crew Nets a Staggering Payout: A Long-Fought Legal Battle Culminates in £890,000 in Unpaid Wages
summary: Last on the saga of the luxury megayacht Alfa Nero - a six-figure windfall for the crew courtesy of relentless litigation and a tenacious union.
body: The once-bitten, twice-shy crew of the luxury superyacht Alfa Nero are, as of 9 January, 2025, exactly £890,000 wealthier. This staggering payday has been brought to fruition by virtue of dogged union representation, persisting through a labyrinthine legal battle. The process, described as long and gruelling by Charles Boyle, director of legal services at Nautilus International, tested the resolve of the crew who had not received the wages they had worked strenuously to earn. Their claim to settlement lay in Section 49(1) of the 2006 Merchant Shipping Act, which provides maritime lien rights, giving precedence to wages over other debts. The union's unyielding pursuit of justice had its genesis in a discord over outstanding payments to the superyacht's original crew, disagreements about abandonment, and disputes regarding skeleton crew replacements employed between March 2022 and April 2023. At the heart of the turmoil was a shockingly large sum of money – specifically, €2.2 million in unpaid wages, with a saucy 4 per cent interest rate. Parallel to the union's action, non-unionised crew members trod their path through the courts seeking payment of €439,494.40, escalating the total sum sought to roughly €2.7 million. The ultimate realization of these recompenses was hinged upon the sale of the not-so-modest vessel; at a tidy sum of $40 million to an undisclosed buyer, the sails were finally set for the crew to recover their unpaid dues. An elegant dance around maritime law later, and the crew are turning their glasses to the wind in an overdue toast for their hard-earned remuneration. Moreover, Nautilus, representing the best interests of the unionized crew, has further teased the court order for a claiming of an additional £331,000, a substantial cherry on the union's cake.

title: The Age of Sky Yachting: How Helicopter Hangars Enhance Superyachts and Secure Your Flying Asset
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Age of Sky Yachting: How Helicopter Hangars Enhance Superyachts and Secure Your Flying Asset
summary: In the realm of opulence, optimizing superyacht design with a helicopter hangar isn't just about luxury but a smart investment, delivering function and reliability on the high seas.
body: Diving into the world of superyachts, explorer yachts, and support vessels, one might discover that embedding a helicopter hangar into the mix is more than a display of extravagance. It's a shrewd investment that delivers unparalleled protection, superior performance, and indisputable peace of mind.

In an environment prone to elements such as salty ocean air and vexing humidity, designers have found well-designed, ventilated, and humidity-regulated hangars to be the perfect shield for helicopters. Corrosion, an unwelcome guest on many oceanic escapades, often threatens their integrity. Fortunately, these specialized hangars provide a highly secure and controlled setting—protecting the aircraft from high winds and rough seas, while simultaneously offering additional lashing points.

Hangars also serve as a boon for maintenance teams, offering optimal environments that allow them to perform at their best. Working in a clean, controlled space away from excessive heat, cold, or exposure to adverse weather conditions mitigates the risks of rushed maintenance, reducing errors while bolstering your aircraft's reliability.

Expedition yachts often serve as floating homes for operational equipment and spare aircraft parts, which necessitate proper environmental conditions. Adding to its growing list of purposes, a hangar also secures and properly houses these elements, ensuring they are in optimal condition when required.

Lastly, having a yacht equipped with a helicopter hangar is about ensuring mission success. In instances where environmental exposure might cause unexpected maintenance issues that could jeopardize the mission and leave the helicopter grounded, having this dedicated space mitigates the risk.

Designing your next maritime experience isn't just about staying ahead in the luxury race. It's about preserving adventure's essence—balancing elegance and practicality on the high seas while ensuring your helicopter is not just a toy but a reliable and enjoyable asset, ready to ascend into the azure when the time comes.

title: Encouraging Respect and Dignity at Sea: The Vital Mission to Stamp Out Sexual Harassment on Yachts
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Encouraging Respect and Dignity at Sea: The Vital Mission to Stamp Out Sexual Harassment on Yachts
summary: In the maritime realm, a pressing need exists to end the insidious issue of sexual harassment on yachts. This plays a key role in ensuring that every team member aboard experiences a safe and harmonious working environment.
body: Sexual harassment, as defined by English law, refers to any uninvited sexual conduct that infringes individual dignity or creates an intimidating or offensive environment for the victim. Unfortunately, this chronic problem respects no boundaries and can infiltrate all kinds of occupations and workplaces, including the sophisticated realm of yachting.

Despite various forms, be it explicit jokes, unsolicited touching, or inappropriate social media content, sexual harassment leaves victims feeling degraded and uncomfortable. Alarmingly, the problem often gets brushed under the carpet, leading to unsanctioned perpetrators, further victims, and a hostile environment that may push victims to resign.

So how do we combat these violating incidents at sea? The solution lies in proactive steps to prevent sexual harassment aboard. These include investing in training, support services and maintaining a positive, inclusive environment. Yachts managed in this manner can attract and retain proficient and motivated crew. For charter yachts, mechanisms to manage risks during charter and handling issues with onboard guests should be considered.

It's high time maritime workplaces, mirroring their terrestrial counterparts, confront this pressing issue head-on to create a secure, respectful environment where everyone can focus on the joys of being at sea.

title: Embark on a Voyage to Greener Horizons: Reimagining the Yachting World through Sustainable Resolutions
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Embark on a Voyage to Greener Horizons: Reimagining the Yachting World through Sustainable Resolutions
summary: In the pursuit of sustainable sailing, the Water Revolution Foundation extends an invitational guide packed with actionable resolutions - a blueprint for a healthier yachting future.
body: As the curtain falls on another year, in the wake of the majestic yachting realm, the wave of change is advancing. The trusty vessel navigating this transformation? The Water Revolution Foundation, trailblazing toward a sustainable future with an echo of new-age resolutions.

At the helm of these resolutions is an evaluation of the yacht's environmental performance through the Yacht Environmental Transparency Index (YETI). This pioneering industry tool lets owners examine their yacht's efficiency by measuring it up against a target reference line. Gathering insights into your yacht's environmental impact could become your compass, guiding you towards eco-conscious modifications.

Moulding an environmentally conscious culture on board your yacht is the second offering on the resolution blueprint. Empowering your operations team with comprehensive Environmental Crew Guidelines fosters green practices and promotes cost-efficiency.

Finally, the Foundation pitches the use of alternative fuels as a part of their yachting kite. A recommendable choice: hydro-treated vegetable oil (HVO) to replace fossil diesel. Such a shift in the wind can cut down your environmental impact significantly.

These four resolutions offer a voyage map toward a greener yachting legacy. Driven by the goal of becoming true vanguards of the sea, it's time to hoist the sails and navigate toward a sustainable yachting horizon.

title: Uncertainty Strikes the British Boatbuilding Industry as Sunseeker Announces Temporary Layoffs
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Uncertainty Strikes the British Boatbuilding Industry as Sunseeker Announces Temporary Layoffs
summary: Sunseeker International is stirring up waves in the British Boatbuilding sphere by temporarily laying off around 100 of its employees.
body: Where there was once smooth sailing, the boatbuilding industry now encounters rough seas, with Sunseeker International announcing temporary layoffs for approximately 100 staff members. The decision, the company ensures, is necessary due to 'operational issues' and is not permanent. A promise of return to work by the end of the month constitutes the company's balm to the abruptly cut-off employees. Yet, the news comes just a month after national competitor, Princess Yachts, executed similar cuts, clusters of dark clouds gather over the British boatbuilding sector. Despite these temporary layoffs, Sunseeker maintains its commitment to its staff, vowing no permanent employees have lost their jobs. The company’s recent ownership transition, moving from China’s Dalian Wanda Group to Lionheart Capital and Orienta Capital Partners, has been seen as a ray of hope in these turbulent times. Sunseeker’s headquarters and core production are expected to remain in Poole – its home, the heart of which roots back to the classic British brand. However, questions rise like tides as government officials demand more clarity about the motivations behind the layoffs. Criticism, especially from the likes of Neil Duncan-Jordan, Labour MP for Poole, emphasizes the need for transparency, especially when job security is on the line. Duncan-Jordan’s sentiment, relatable to many a modern workplace, is that employees deserve every shred of honesty a company can provide, particularly when the future of their livelihoods hang in the balance. While the critics voice concerns and questions, Sunseeker remains committed to its regaining course. The company acknowledges its recent lag behind competitors but sees the new investment as the crucial lifeline to steer them back into the right course. And though the water may be choppy now, Sunseeker sails on, with eyes fixed hopefully on the horizon.

title: Challenging the captain’s call: A vital peek into maritime safety practices on superyachts
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Challenging the captain’s call: A vital peek into maritime safety practices on superyachts
summary: Diving into the maritime world reveals a gaping hole in superyacht safety, with captains often skirting crucial protocols that ensure the welfare of all aboard.
body: The shimmering world of superyachts belies a lurking danger beneath the surface. A recent incident underscored this starkly, bolstering voices that demand a revamped safety culture within the maritime industry. Here's the story: A radio dropped into the waters off a small motor yacht’s stern, right under the propellers. The captain, evidently eager to retrieve the device, ordered a crew member to dive for it. The only hiccup? The process required a work permit— a protocol the captain dismissed with a wave of his hand, demanding evidence of such a law.

Consulting the COSWP or reaching out to a Designated Person Ashore (DPA) aren’t checkboxes to blindly tick but provide essential guidelines for efficient and secure operations. The stop-work authority represents a crucial tool for risk assessment and management, but without a robust safety culture, these mechanisms often go underutilized.

Diving at Work Regulations highlight the need for a risk assessment ahead of diving operations. A dive permit serves to ensure that all health and safety risks have been evaluated thoroughly and mitigation protocols are in place. This mandate isn’t based solely on preventing physical injury but forms part of the broader ethos of a safe and secure maritime industry.

While most superyacht crew members hold a Professional Association of Diving Instructors (PADI) certification, this in no way makes them immune to the risks present. It only underscores the pressing need for captains to acknowledge their responsibility in ensuring all onboard safety protocols are duly followed.

In the final analysis, the maritime industry finds itself at crossroads, balancing regulatory adherence with practical applications. Striking the right chord will require a mix of robust enforcement and cultivating a culture of safety, which begins at the top and gradually permeates down. While change may be slow, each step counts towards creating safer waters for all who navigate them.

title: Harnessing New Innovations for a Revitalised Superyacht Refit Sector
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Harnessing New Innovations for a Revitalised Superyacht Refit Sector
summary: A surge in demand is revolutionising the supervessel refit industry. This piece explores the innovation and ingenuity fuelling this transformation.
body: One cannot disagree that superyachts and luxury vessels represent not just a symbol of wealth and opulence but also the embodied spirit of human audacity and design celerity. As the industry scales new peaks and presents fresh challenges, stakeholders are turning to innovate solutions for a complete overhaul or 'refit' of their absolutist beauties. This exploration brings forth crucial insider insight from key decision-makers steering the course of the industry's future.

Leaders of prominent refit yards divulge their chief concerns and aspirations regarding the sector's evolution. Topping their agenda is the pressing need for improved refit conduct and bolstering of the shipyard's infrastructural framework, operations, and processes.

Highlighting another side of the issue, Ferdinando Pilli, General Manager of Lusben, outlines the firm's committed investment plan worth €12 million aimed at upgrading its facilities. The faith and focus of companies like Lusben and Lürssen on refining their infrastructures attest to the approach of reshaping the industry ground-up.

Coinciding with upward industry dynamics, the refit market resilience to economic downturns also speaks volumes about this sector's investment security. In contrast, the new-build sector saw a dramatic downturn during the 2008 financial crisis. Projections showcase an ever-increasing demand for refit services, making it a key player in the marine sector's future landscape.

In essence, the refit market is not just riding the waves but defining their contours. As long as there are more yachts, there will be a need for more places for their maintenance and upgrade, ensuring a long, prosperous voyage for the refit sector.

title: Sailing into the Spotlight: An Unveiling of Two Long Range Explorer Yachts on the Second-hand Market
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Sailing into the Spotlight: An Unveiling of Two Long Range Explorer Yachts on the Second-hand Market
summary: The exploration yacht industry is booming, with attention turning to two exceptional pre-owned yachts promising unrivalled journeys to prospective owners.
body: As the explorer yacht industry continues to sail full steam ahead, eyes turn to the thriving brokerage market. Here, amongst the ebb and flow, potential owners will find countless pre-owned yachts waiting for their next captain, ready to cruise into the heart of exploration yachting.

In the bustling field, two standout vessels have dropped anchor – go-to choices for those adventurers looking to embark on long-range journeys brimming with luxury and leisure. Falling under the dynamic sub-500GT category, these yachts come with far fewer regulatory constraints and an ideal balance of guests and crew, making them the gateway into the world of exploration yachting.

Among her improvements, you'll find state-of-the-art navigation systems, a relocated captain’s cabin, air-conditioned engine room, and subdued generator chamber for quiet operation. Bountiful storage space brands the Bravado ideal for extensive sea voyages, whisking owners off to secluded destinations around the globe.

Don’t let her sturdy exterior deceive you. Design luminaries Reymond Langton and Bizzozero/Cassina have given her an exterior of classic elegance and interior charm, beautifully accented with a blue hull and white superstructure. Her sundeck – a haven for sun-worshippers – boasts a Jacuzzi, bar, dining table and plenty of lounging space. Inside, large windows drench the living spaces with natural light, showcasing a stylish seating area and formal dining room that exude sophistication.

Accommodation echoes the vessel's overall opulence, welcoming up to 12 guests in its six staterooms. Among them, a full-beam master suite featuring a private gym on the bridge deck promises a stay nothing short of royal. A VIP stateroom on the main deck and double and twin cabins on the lower deck ensure every guest receives the luxurious voyage they deserve.

title: How Positive Leadership Can Transform a Yacht's Crew and Overall Performance in a Time of Crisis
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: How Positive Leadership Can Transform a Yacht's Crew and Overall Performance in a Time of Crisis
summary: Good leadership does more than simply keep a yacht afloat; it builds a happy, high-performing crew and a healthy working environment.
body: Navigating the high seas is not just about the nuts and bolts of a ship, but those who steer it. The term ‘trickle-down’ not uncommonly used in business to chuckle at the ultra-wealthy’s societal contributions. Yet, unbeknownst to some, it has a far more palpable footprint in the yachting industry, but with a cultural twist. Much like in any corporate setup, in sailing, it’s the leadership that sets the tone and course. The captain, heading a multi-million-euro vessel, plays a crucial role in influencing the performance, productivity, and wellbeing of the crew.

Indeed, there persists an argument in some corners of the industry advocating that crew members should just 'get on with it' and begrudgingly accept harsh working conditions. However, enlightened crew members are now more aware of their rights than ever before, longing for growth and due appreciate for their hard work. They seek work environments echoing these beliefs, like a seller’s market where their skills and experiences are treasured.

There’s a genuine competition brewing in the industry to secure quality crew, given the escalating demand with a surge in yachts. Disenchanted crew members are no longer bound to happily settle into any ship that sails along, knowing that their competence can land them a better gig.

The crew members do not merely represent the workforce; they are the face of the business, the 'service' in this tremendous service industry. A crew that feels valued well-rested, and motivated will operate with heightened efficiency, enhancing overall yacht performance. This calls for the yachting industry to earnestly address and resolve issues affecting crew welfare, capturing the essence of what the industry should stand for - the ultimate experience, powered by happy crews.

title: Albany Marina
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Albany Marina
summary: Located on the southwest coast of New Providence Island in The Bahamas, Albany Marina is one of the most luxurious and exclusive yacht harbours in the Caribbean. Part of the private, 600-acre Albany Resort, this world-class marina is a favourite among celebrities, super yacht owners, and high-net-worth individuals who seek privacy, elegance, and unmatched amenities. Backed by investors like Tiger Woods and Ernie Els,
body: Located on the southwest coast of New Providence Island in The Bahamas, Albany Marina is one of the most luxurious and exclusive yacht harbours in the Caribbean. Part of the private, 600-acre Albany Resort, this world-class marina is a favourite among celebrities, super yacht owners, and high-net-worth individuals who seek privacy, elegance, and unmatched amenities. Backed by investors like Tiger Woods and Ernie Els, Albany is more than just a marina—it’s a lifestyle enclave where the rich and famous unwind in style.

The marina itself is designed to accommodate the most discerning yachtsmen and women. With 71 slips, Albany Marina caters to a wide range of vessels, from 50-foot sport fishers to superyachts up to 300 feet (90+ meters) in length. The marina features deep-water access with depths of up to 16 feet, and offers stern-to and alongside berthing, with full-service dock assistance. The harbour is sheltered and secure, making it a year-round destination for yachting enthusiasts.

Each berth at Albany Marina is fully equipped with state-of-the-art amenities, including high-capacity electricity (100/200-amp), fresh water, high-speed internet, cable TV, and black/grey water pump-out services. The marina also provides fuel bunkering, 24/7 security, and concierge services that handle everything from provisioning and customs clearance to private chef bookings and ground transportation. But what truly sets Albany Marina apart is its integration into the ultra-luxury Albany Resort, which is designed to cater to every aspect of a high-end lifestyle. Yacht owners and guests enjoy access to private residences, luxury villas, and designer condominiums just steps from the dock. The resort features a wide range of amenities including an 18-hole championship golf course designed by Ernie Els, a mega-yacht-worthy fitness centre and spa, tennis and paddle courts, and a world-class equestrian centre.

Dining at Albany is equally exceptional, with multiple gourmet restaurants and bars, including fine dining, casual beachfront venues, and a private wine room. The resort also includes a boutique shopping plaza, a cinema, art gallery, and even a private school, making it a self-contained luxury community.

The social scene at Albany is exclusive and vibrant. The marina hosts elite events such as yacht shows, regattas, and private parties, attracting a clientele of global celebrities, entrepreneurs, and tastemakers. Yet despite its ultra-high-end appeal, Albany maintains a relaxed Bahamian vibe—casual elegance is the norm, and privacy is deeply respected.

Weather-wise, New Providence offers nearly perfect cruising conditions. The island enjoys tropical weather year-round, with average temperatures between 24–32°C (75–90°F). The sailing season peaks from November through May, with steady trade winds, calm seas, and minimal rainfall. The location also provides excellent access to the Exumas, Eleuthera, and the Out Islands, making Albany an ideal launch point for longer cruising adventures.

In summary, Albany Marina combines the best of high-end marina services with the unparalleled luxury of a private Caribbean resort. Whether you're mooring a super yacht or chartering for a weekend escape, Albany delivers world-class service, privacy, and sophistication in one of the most beautiful settings in the world.

title: Alimos Marina
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Alimos Marina
summary: Located just 15 kilometres southwest of central Athens, Alimos Marina (also known as Kalamaki Marina) is one of the largest marinas in Greece and one of the busiest in the Eastern Mediterranean. A vital hub for yacht charters, sailing enthusiasts, and cruising adventurers, it serves as the primary departure point for exploring the Saronic Gulf and the Cyclades islands—making it a cornerstone of Greece’s vibrant nauti
body: Located just 15 kilometres southwest of central Athens, Alimos Marina (also known as Kalamaki Marina) is one of the largest marinas in Greece and one of the busiest in the Eastern Mediterranean. A vital hub for yacht charters, sailing enthusiasts, and cruising adventurers, it serves as the primary departure point for exploring the Saronic Gulf and the Cyclades islands—making it a cornerstone of Greece’s vibrant nautical scene. With over 1,000 berths, Alimos Marina can accommodate a wide range of vessels, from modest sailing yachts to motor yachts up to 40 meters in length. The marina offers deep-water access and is well-protected, even in rough weather, making it a reliable home port or transit stop for boats of all sizes. The majority of the marina is dedicated to bareboat and skippered charters, and during the summer months, it buzzes with activity as fleets prepare to depart for nearby islands such as Aegina, Hydra, Poros, and beyond.

Alimos Marina is fully equipped to meet the needs of modern yachts and their crews. Each berth provides fresh water, 220V electricity, and waste collection. There are on-site fuel stations, a chandlery, and provisioning stores, along with technical support services ranging from engine repair to sail maintenance. The marina also features 24-hour security, car parking, and Wi-Fi access across much of the area. For more extensive maintenance or haul-outs, nearby facilities such as Perama or Lavrio offer full shipyard capabilities.

While Alimos Marina itself is more practical than picturesque, its strategic location is a major asset. It is easily reachable from Athens International Airport, just a 30-minute drive away, and well-connected by tram and taxi to Athens city centre, the Acropolis, and the cultural heartbeat of Greece. This makes it a perfect base for those combining sailing with city exploration. For yachters seeking luxury, Alimos is close to the Athenian Riviera, a glamorous coastal stretch dotted with upscale resorts, chic beach clubs, and high-end restaurants. Nearby neighbourhoods like Glyfada, Vouliagmeni, and Kavouri are known for their boutique shopping, fine dining, and elegant seaside promenades. The Four Seasons Astir Palace in Vouliagmeni is just a short ride from Alimos and is a favourite destination for those seeking the glitz and glamour of the Mediterranean lifestyle.

The weather in Athens and the surrounding waters is typically Greek—sunny, warm, and perfect for sailing. From May to October, sailors can expect long days of sunshine, calm seas, and average temperatures between 25–35°C (77–95°F). The Meltemi winds, which blow through the Aegean during July and August, offer exciting conditions for more experienced sailors, while the Saronic Gulf tends to remain more sheltered and predictable.

In summary, Alimos Marina is the beating heart of Athenian sailing. Whether you're launching a multi-island cruise, managing a charter fleet, or soaking up the lifestyle of the Aegean, Alimos offers a convenient and well-equipped base just steps away from both ancient wonders and modern luxury. It may not be the flashiest marina, but it’s undeniably one of the most important and functional in Greece.

title: Atlantis Marina
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Atlantis Marina
summary: Located within the iconic Atlantis Resort on Paradise Island in The Bahamas, Atlantis Marina is one of the most recognizable and vibrant marinas in the Caribbean. Known for its proximity to one of the world’s most famous resort destinations, the marina combines world-class yachting facilities with access to a spectacular range of amenities, entertainment, and leisure—making it a hotspot for yacht owners, charter gues
body: Located within the iconic Atlantis Resort on Paradise Island in The Bahamas, Atlantis Marina is one of the most recognizable and vibrant marinas in the Caribbean. Known for its proximity to one of the world’s most famous resort destinations, the marina combines world-class yachting facilities with access to a spectacular range of amenities, entertainment, and leisure—making it a hotspot for yacht owners, charter guests, and celebrities alike.

Situated in a protected lagoon on the north side of Paradise Island, Atlantis Marina features 63 deep-water slips that can accommodate yachts up to 220 feet (67 meters) in length. The harbour offers a depth of up to 12 feet and is easily accessible from the Nassau Harbour. Yacht owners can berth their vessels directly alongside a backdrop of luxury and fun, enjoying the unique blend of practicality and opulence that Atlantis is known for.

Each slip is fully serviced with 30, 50, and 100-amp shore power, fresh water, cable TV, and high-speed internet. In addition, the marina provides fuelling services, pump-out stations, and 24-hour dockside security. Customs and immigration clearance can also be handled on-site, making it a seamless entry point into the Bahamas. The staff is experienced, friendly, and available to assist with provisioning, deliveries, and concierge needs.

What sets Atlantis Marina apart is the unparalleled access to the Atlantis Resort and Casino. Docking at the marina grants you full access to the resort’s staggering array of luxury and entertainment offerings. This includes the Aquaventure water park, 14 pools, the world’s largest open-air marine habitat, world-class golf course, and the Atlantis Casino, which rivals those of Las Vegas in scale and spectacle. There's also a full-service Mandara Spa, a top-tier fitness centre, and tennis courts.

Dining options abound with over 20 restaurants and bars, ranging from celebrity-chef establishments like Nobu and Fish by José Andrés to casual beachfront grills and cocktail lounges. There’s also extensive high-end shopping, featuring designer labels and fine jewellery. For families, the Dolphin Cay experience and marine exhibits are world-class attractions. The social life at Atlantis Marina is glamorous and energetic. It’s a popular gathering point during major events and holidays, and the marina often hosts parties, yacht hop evenings, and informal gatherings where the global yachting elite mingle. It’s a destination that blends family-friendly fun with the high-society flair that defines much of Paradise Island.

As for the weather, Atlantis Marina benefits from the typical Bahamian tropical climate. The prime yachting season runs from November to May, with warm, dry weather and temperatures averaging 26–30°C (79–86°F). The waters are calm, clear, and ideal for cruising, snorkelling, or simply relaxing on the deck. With over 300 days of sunshine a year, it’s no surprise that the Bahamas are a magnet for yachters from around the world.

In short, Atlantis Marina offers more than just a place to dock—it offers an immersive resort experience. With high-end facilities, unbeatable resort access, and a reputation for fun and sophistication, it’s a must-stop for anyone cruising the Bahamas in style.

title: Brighton Marina
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Brighton Marina
summary: Nestled along the East Sussex coastline just half a mile east of the historic city of Brighton, stands as the UK’s largest marina, a vibrant hub for sailors and visitors alike. Opened by Queen Elizabeth II on May 31, 1979, this artificial marina boasts over 1,300 berths, a figure refined from its original 1,600 due to modern pontoon configurations favouring larger leisure boats. The marina’s two massive breakwaters—t
body: Nestled along the East Sussex coastline just half a mile east of the historic city of Brighton, stands as the UK’s largest marina, a vibrant hub for sailors and visitors alike. Opened by Queen Elizabeth II on May 31, 1979, this artificial marina boasts over 1,300 berths, a figure refined from its original 1,600 due to modern pontoon configurations favouring larger leisure boats. The marina’s two massive breakwaters—the Eastern and Western—provide secure shelter, making it an ideal haven for yachts, motorboats, and fishing craft up to 24 meters or 50 tonnes. Its strategic location offers easy access to open water, serving as a gateway for Channel hops to France or stopovers between Dover and the Solent.

For boat visitors, Brighton Marina offers a wealth of facilities to ensure a comfortable stay. The marina provides over 150 visitor berths. The entrance channel, dredged to 2 meters below chart datum, is buoyed with red and green markers, though depths can vary, especially in southwest winds above Force 5, requiring caution.

On-site, a full-service boatyard features a 60-tonne boat hoist, a static crane for mast and engine lifts, and a new mast rack, catering to maintenance needs year-round. A 24-hour fuel berth dispenses diesel and unleaded petrol, while a pump-out service on the East Jetty handles waste. Berth holders enjoy luxury shower rooms, a laundry with contactless payment, and dedicated car parks. The marina’s 24/7 security and RNLI lifeboat station on the west quay add safety. Beyond boating, visitors can explore a bustling waterfront with restaurants, a cinema, bowling alley, and water-sports like jet skiing or sailing lessons. Plus 1,500 free car parking spaces.

title: Coal Harbour Marina
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Coal Harbour Marina
summary: Set against the stunning backdrop of snow-capped mountains and glassy skyscrapers, Coal Harbour Marina is one of Canada’s most prestigious urban marinas—an oasis for yachtsmen in the heart of downtown Vancouver, British Columbia. It offers a rare combination of luxury, location, and accessibility, where the bustle of a world-class city meets the tranquillity of a Pacific inlet. Whether you’re staying overnight, layin
body: Set against the stunning backdrop of snow-capped mountains and glassy skyscrapers, Coal Harbour Marina is one of Canada’s most prestigious urban marinas—an oasis for yachtsmen in the heart of downtown Vancouver, British Columbia. It offers a rare combination of luxury, location, and accessibility, where the bustle of a world-class city meets the tranquillity of a Pacific inlet. Whether you’re staying overnight, laying up for the season, or beginning a voyage north to Alaska, Coal Harbour Marina is a top-tier gateway to the Pacific Northwest.

Coal Harbour lies at the foot of downtown Vancouver’s financial district, nestled between the world-renowned Stanley Park and the Vancouver Convention Centre. The marina is part of the Westin Bayshore complex and is managed by the Royal Vancouver Yacht Club. Its central location makes it the marina of choice for sailors who want immediate access to urban amenities without sacrificing the serenity and security of a well-maintained harbour.

Coal Harbour Marina boasts approximately 242 slips, accommodating vessels from 30 feet up to 330 feet in length. The marina is protected by a floating breakwater, and its inner basin remains calm even during the region’s winter storms. Average depths at low tide are approximately 4.5 to 5 meters, and access is available year-round. Larger yachts, including superyachts, will find ample space and professional handling on arrival, though advance booking is essential during peak months.
Coal Harbour Marina delivers a full complement of modern yachting services:
Shore Power: 30A, 50A, and 100A power is available at most slips.
Water Supply: Fresh potable water is supplied to all berths.
Wi-Fi: Complimentary Wi-Fi is provided, although many long-term users opt for their own connections due to occasional signal limitations.
Black and Grey Water Pump-Out: Dockside services are available on request.
Security: 24/7 gated access with CCTV surveillance, professional dock staff, and secure mooring.

Fuel & Maintenance: While the marina itself does not offer a fuelling dock or shipyard, these services are available nearby in False Creek or at North Vancouver’s shipyards. Minor repairs and provisioning can be arranged via marina management.

Additional services include laundry, showers, lockers, recycling, parking, and concierge assistance. The marina is pet-friendly and located adjacent to Vancouver’s extensive seawall, perfect for a morning run or dog walk.

What truly sets Coal Harbour Marina apart is its unbeatable location. Within minutes, guests can walk to fine dining, boutique shopping, theatres, museums, and high-end hotels. The marina is a short stroll from the Vancouver Aquarium, Canada Place, and Gastown, and just a 10-minute drive from the Vancouver International Airport (via seaplane or taxi).

Sailors often remark that the marina is not only a docking point but also an immersive city experience. Imagine sipping coffee from your cockpit as seaplanes take off across the water, cyclists roll by on the promenade, and the sun rises behind the Lions Gate Bridge.

Coal Harbour’s neighbouring cafés and bars—like the Lift Bar & Grill, Cardero’s Restaurant, and the waterfront TapShack—are popular haunts for crew and visitors alike. Whether you’re hosting guests or enjoying a quiet evening onboard, the surroundings offer a cosmopolitan charm rarely found in marinas.

Coal Harbour is not just a pretty face. It’s a strategic starting point for long-range cruisers heading to the Inside Passage, Desolation Sound, Haida Gwaii, or the remote coastlines of Alaska. Many yachts winter here before launching spring expeditions up Canada’s wild western seaboard. Charter captains and international cruisers alike use Coal Harbour as their North American base.

The customs clearance process is efficient, and the marina office is well-versed in supporting international arrivals. Provisioning is convenient, with grocers, wine merchants, and chandlers within walking distance or a short delivery drive away.

As a Royal Vancouver Yacht Club location, Coal Harbour Marina fosters a close-knit but welcoming atmosphere. Whether you're new in town or part of the regional cruising circuit, there’s a community feel among the resident boaters and marina staff.

While not as event-heavy as club-based marinas, Coal Harbour sees its fair share of visiting regattas, flotillas, and international yachts throughout the season. Social events, crew dinners, and impromptu dockside gatherings are common, particularly in the summer.

Coal Harbour Marina is not the cheapest marina in British Columbia—but it may well be the most rewarding. It offers the rare ability to moor your yacht in a truly world-class city without sacrificing tranquility, service, or security. From here, you can dine on sushi, hike a rainforest trail, ski in Whistler, or set sail to one of the world’s last great wilderness coastlines—all within a day. It’s a marina that understands what sailors need but delivers much more: convenience, class, and connection to one of North America’s most livable cities.
Whether you’re a circumnavigator, a seasonal cruiser, or a casual coastal explorer, Coal Harbour Marina is one of the finest berthing choices on the West Coast of Canada.

Whether you’re a superyacht owner, charter guest,
body: Situated in the tropical heart of Queensland, Coral Sea Marina (formerly Abell Point Marina) in Airlie Beach is a standout destination on Australia’s east coast. As the main access point to the stunning Whitsunday Islands and the Great Barrier Reef, Coral Sea Marina offers a seamless blend of professional yachting facilities, spectacular scenery, and laid-back luxury. Whether you’re a superyacht owner, charter guest, or coastal cruiser, this marina delivers a top-tier experience both on and off the water.

The marina features over 520 wet berths and accommodates vessels up to 80 meters (262 feet) in length. It is one of the largest marinas in the southern hemisphere and is designed to cater to a full spectrum of yachts, from monohulls and catamarans to motor yachts and superyachts. The marina is protected, secure, and offers deep-water access, making it ideal for vessels of all sizes, whether short-stay visitors or long-term berth holders.

Facilities at Coral Sea Marina are among the best in the region. Berths are equipped with power (single and three-phase up to 125 amps), potable water, high-speed Wi-Fi, and pump-out systems for grey and black water. The marina also provides refuelling services with high-capacity fuel docks for large vessels. There's 24/7 security with CCTV, a professional dockmaster team, and concierge services to assist with bookings, transportation, provisioning, and more.

Onshore amenities add to the appeal. The marina complex includes clean, modern shower and laundry facilities, a chandlery, and access to marine trades and technical services. There are also meeting and event spaces, ideal for yacht briefings, corporate functions, and social events. For crew, Coral Sea Marina is a comfortable and social-friendly stopover, with nearby fitness centres, cafes, and recreational areas. What truly elevates Coral Sea Marina is its location in Airlie Beach, a buzzing tropical town known for its easy going atmosphere and adventurous spirit. The marina sits at the heart of the Coral Sea Marina Resort Village, home to several stylish bars, restaurants, boutiques, tour operators, and the elegant Coral Sea Resort itself, which offers ocean-view suites and waterfront dining. It’s a great place to enjoy sunset cocktails, gourmet meals, and live music with stunning sea views.

Yachting from Coral Sea Marina opens up endless possibilities. The nearby Whitsunday Islands—like Whitehaven Beach, Hamilton Island, and Hayman Island—are among the most beautiful cruising grounds in the world, with turquoise waters, protected anchorages, and coral reefs perfect for snorkelling and diving. The marina is also a base for luxury charters, bareboat sailing holidays, and eco-tourism adventures to the Great Barrier Reef.

The weather is one of its biggest draws. Coral Sea Marina enjoys a tropical climate, with warm, sunny weather most of the year. The best boating season is from May to October, when temperatures range from 24–28°C (75–82°F) and rainfall is minimal. The wet season (November to April) brings occasional showers and warmer temperatures, but it also offers lush scenery and fewer crowds.

In short, Coral Sea Marina delivers the perfect balance of functionality, lifestyle, and natural beauty. For anyone looking to explore the Whitsundays in style, it offers a luxurious and fully supported base at the edge of one of the world’s most breathtaking marine environments.

title: Eden Island Marina
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Eden Island Marina
summary: Located just off the northeast coast of Mahé, the largest island in the Seychelles, Eden Island Marina is a luxurious and strategically positioned marina that has become a hub for yachts cruising the Indian Ocean. Set within the exclusive Eden Island residential and resort development, this modern marina offers state-of-the-art facilities, secure berthing, and a vibrant lifestyle—all within easy reach of pristine bea
body: Located just off the northeast coast of Mahé, the largest island in the Seychelles, Eden Island Marina is a luxurious and strategically positioned marina that has become a hub for yachts cruising the Indian Ocean. Set within the exclusive Eden Island residential and resort development, this modern marina offers state-of-the-art facilities, secure berthing, and a vibrant lifestyle—all within easy reach of pristine beaches, tropical cruising grounds, and the vibrant capital city of Victoria.

Eden Island Marina forms the nautical heart of the Eden Island complex, a reclaimed luxury island connected to Mahé by a short bridge. The marina features over 130 berths for private yachts and visitors, including dedicated superyacht berths that can accommodate vessels up to 115 meters (377 feet) in length. The marina basin is sheltered, with a depth of 3 to 5 meters, providing safe anchorage in all weather conditions. The approach to the marina is simple and well-marked, making it a convenient stop for yachts transiting the Indian Ocean or exploring East Africa and the Middle East.

The facilities at Eden Island Marina are world-class. Each berth is serviced with power (including 3-phase connections for large yachts), fresh water, high-speed internet, and pump-out systems for grey and black water. A fuel dock is available, offering both diesel and petrol, and the marina also provides customs and immigration clearance, making it an official port of entry into the Seychelles.

Onsite, the marina offers a range of support services and amenities. These include concierge assistance, chandlery supplies, provisioning services, and access to marine professionals for repairs, refits, and general maintenance. There is also 24/7 security and CCTV surveillance, ensuring peace of mind for owners and crew.

Eden Island itself is a world of luxury. The island features high-end residences, a resort hotel, private beaches, and a well-developed commercial precinct. Just steps from the marina, you’ll find fine dining restaurants, cafés, boutique shops, and an upscale supermarket stocked with international and local products. Popular spots like Boardwalk Bar & Grill and Bravo Restaurant offer stunning views over the water and are favourites for sundowners and evening gatherings.

The lifestyle here is exclusive yet relaxed. Yachters can enjoy the privacy of Eden Island while being minutes from Mahé’s international airport, the capital city’s markets and cultural attractions, and some of the world’s most stunning beaches and anchorages. Nearby cruising highlights include Praslin, La Digue, and the remote Aldabra Atoll, offering diverse opportunities for island-hopping, diving, fishing, and exploring protected marine reserves. The weather in the Seychelles is tropical and pleasant year-round. Temperatures average between 26–32°C (79–90°F), with the drier southeast trade wind season running from May to October, making it ideal for sailing. The wetter northwest monsoon from November to March brings more humidity and occasional showers but remains warm and inviting.

In summary, Eden Island Marina – Mahé is more than just a place to dock—it’s a gateway to paradise. With its top-tier facilities, stunning surroundings, and access to both luxury and adventure, it stands out as one of the finest marina destinations in the Indian Ocean. Whether you’re stopping over or staying for the season, Eden Island offers the perfect blend of sophistication and island escape.

author: Old Sea Dogs

As the primary base for yachting in the Ionian Sea, it serves as a launching point for charters and cruising adventures through the tranquil waters and verdant islands of western Greece. With its modern infrastructure, convenient location, and picturesque surr
body: Located on the northeastern coast of Corfu, just 6 kilometres from Corfu Town, Gouvia Marina is one of the most important and well-appointed marinas in Greece. As the primary base for yachting in the Ionian Sea, it serves as a launching point for charters and cruising adventures through the tranquil waters and verdant islands of western Greece. With its modern infrastructure, convenient location, and picturesque surroundings, Gouvia Marina is a top-tier destination for sailors and superyacht owners alike.

The marina boasts 1,235 berths, both permanent and for visitors, accommodating vessels up to 80 meters in length. The depth in the marina ranges from 2.5 to 5.5 meters, making it suitable for most yachts and catamarans. Berthing is available stern-to and alongside, with a helpful marina team providing 24/7 mooring assistance and security throughout the complex. Each berth is equipped with electricity (220V and 380V), fresh water, telephone lines, and Wi-Fi. On-site fuelling is available at the dedicated fuel dock, and there's a waste pump-out system for black and grey water, in keeping with international environmental standards. The marina also has a well-equipped boatyard with a travel lift (up to 65 tons), hard-standing areas for winter storage, and facilities for sail repairs, mechanical work, and hull maintenance.

Gouvia Marina is a self-contained village, with a wide range of services and amenities that make life easy for yacht crews and visitors. These include a supermarket, laundry, ATM, car and bike rentals, showers, and a medical centre. There are also several restaurants, tavernas, cafés, and bars on the marina premises, offering everything from casual Greek cuisine to upscale dining with sea views. Beyond its technical features, Gouvia offers access to a lifestyle that balances relaxed island charm with elements of luxury. Corfu is known for its lush, green hillsides, historic Venetian architecture, and a cosmopolitan feel that stems from centuries of international influence. Just a short taxi ride or bike trip from the marina is Corfu Old Town, a UNESCO World Heritage Site filled with narrow alleys, elegant squares, boutiques, and vibrant cafés. The island is also home to luxury resorts, golf courses, and pristine beaches.

For yachters, Gouvia Marina is the ideal base to explore the Ionian Islands. Destinations like Paxos, Lefkada, Kefalonia, and Ithaca are within easy reach, offering calm seas, sheltered anchorages, and charming harbours. The region is particularly popular with families and relaxed cruisers, thanks to its predictable weather and easy island-hopping routes.

Speaking of weather, Corfu enjoys a Mediterranean climate, with hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters. From May to October, sailing conditions are ideal, with temperatures ranging between 25–32°C (77–89°F) and gentle breezes from the northwest. The seas in this region are notably calm compared to the windier Aegean, making it perfect for smooth sailing and laid-back cruising.

In summary, Gouvia Marina blends exceptional yachting facilities with access to Corfu’s rich culture, natural beauty, and sophisticated charm. Whether you're provisioning for an Ionian voyage, wintering a yacht, or indulging in island life, Gouvia provides everything you need in a stylish, welcoming, and well-managed setting.

title: Gustavia Harbour
