Known for attracting superyachts, celebrities
body: Located on the ultra-luxurious island of Saint Barthélemy (St. Barths) in the French West Indies, Gustavia Harbor is one of the most exclusive and glamorous yacht destinations in the Caribbean. Tucked into a natural horseshoe bay and surrounded by red-roofed buildings, designer boutiques, and French cafés, the harbour is the beating heart of this small but stylish island. Known for attracting superyachts, celebrities, and international jet-setters, Gustavia is a place where maritime elegance meets Riviera-style indulgence in the tropics.

The harbour can accommodate around 60 yachts directly at the quay, including vessels up to 70 meters (230 feet) in length. During the high season, especially from December through March, berths are in exceptionally high demand—particularly around the holidays when St. Barths becomes the epicentre of New Year’s Eve celebrations. In addition to dockside berthing, the harbour offers anchorage for up to 100 vessels in the well-sheltered outer bay, with tender services available for larger yachts at anchor.

Facilities at Gustavia Harbor are modern and well-maintained, despite the harbour’s compact footprint. Each berth is equipped with electricity (110/220V), fresh water, fuel delivery, Wi-Fi, and black water pump-out services. The Port Authority of Saint Barthélemy provides 24-hour security and customs/immigration clearance, as well as a helpful marina team to assist with mooring and logistics. Provisioning services are available through local suppliers, and marine technicians, mechanics, and yacht support agencies are accessible through the island’s well-developed service network.

The real draw of Gustavia Harbour, however, is the lifestyle. Docking here places you steps away from Rue de la République, the town’s central promenade lined with high-end boutiques like Louis Vuitton, Cartier, Bulgari, and Hermès, along with charming art galleries and gourmet food markets. The harbour buzzes with activity day and night, from power breakfasts and boutique shopping to sunset cocktails and late-night parties. Dining in Gustavia is world-class. Whether it’s a beachfront lunch at Shellona, a sunset dinner at Bonito, or late-night drinks at Le Ti St. Barth, the island’s food scene is as refined as its clientele. With influences from French, Caribbean, and international cuisine, meals are more than nourishment—they're a social ritual.

The weather in St. Barths is ideal for yachting, particularly from November through May, when the climate is dry, breezy, and comfortably warm. Average temperatures hover between 26–30°C (79–86°F), and the trade winds offer smooth sailing and anchoring conditions. The surrounding waters are calm and clear, perfect for water sports, snorkelling, and beach-hopping. Iconic spots like Colombier Beach and Anse de Gouverneur are a short cruise away and offer stunning settings for private anchorages.

In summary, Gustavia Harbour is not just a marina—it’s a social hub and a symbol of Caribbean sophistication. With its top-tier facilities, postcard-perfect setting, and unmatched lifestyle appeal, it’s one of the most coveted berthing spots in the world. Whether you're arriving for a winter escape or to join the New Year’s festivities, Gustavia offers a slice of paradise wrapped in French elegance. Petite but posh. Yachts moor stern-to next to designer boutiques and cafés.

title: Hamilton Island Marina
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Hamilton Island Marina
summary: Located at the heart of Australia’s Whitsunday Islands, Hamilton Island Marina is a premier destination for luxury yachts, sailing enthusiasts, and adventurers exploring the spectacular waters of the Great Barrier Reef. As the main gateway to this world-renowned cruising ground, the marina combines modern marine facilities with upscale island living, offering a seamless experience that blends comfort, style, and adve
body: Located at the heart of Australia’s Whitsunday Islands, Hamilton Island Marina is a premier destination for luxury yachts, sailing enthusiasts, and adventurers exploring the spectacular waters of the Great Barrier Reef. As the main gateway to this world-renowned cruising ground, the marina combines modern marine facilities with upscale island living, offering a seamless experience that blends comfort, style, and adventure. Hamilton Island is the only island in the Whitsundays with its own commercial airport, making the marina exceptionally accessible by both sea and air. The marina boasts over 250 berths, including dedicated spaces for superyachts up to 60 meters (approximately 200 feet). The approach is well-marked and protected, with deep-water access and calm conditions in the sheltered harbour.

Facilities at Hamilton Island Marina are designed to meet the needs of yachts and their crews. Each berth is equipped with shore power (15, 32, and 63-amp), potable water, Wi-Fi, and waste pump-out services. The marina also provides 24-hour fuel access (diesel and unleaded), sewage pump-out, and grey water disposal. There’s a dedicated marina office offering assistance with bookings, customs and immigration (for international arrivals), and local information. Maintenance and support services are also available, including a shipwright, marine mechanic, electrician, and chandlery. Provisions can be delivered directly to the dock, and there are plenty of shore-based amenities for crew including laundry facilities, showers, and rest areas. Whether you’re staying for a few days or several weeks, the marina makes every aspect of your visit easy and enjoyable.

What sets Hamilton Island Marina apart is the glamorous lifestyle and amenities that surround it. Guests have full access to the island’s array of luxury accommodations, including qualia, one of Australia’s most exclusive five-star resorts, as well as the elegant Beach Club and family-friendly Reef View Hotel. Fine dining abounds, with waterfront restaurants like Bommie at the Hamilton Island Yacht Club, Coca Chu, and Manta Ray Café offering a mix of contemporary Australian, Asian, and Mediterranean cuisines.

The Hamilton Island Yacht Club, located at the edge of the marina, is an architectural showpiece and social hub for sailors. It hosts events like Audi Hamilton Island Race Week, one of Australia’s premier sailing regattas, which attracts top-tier yachts and global yachting enthusiasts each August.

Recreational activities are plentiful: from sailing and diving trips to the outer reef, to golf at the Hamilton Island Golf Club (on nearby Dent Island), or relaxing on Catseye Beach. There are also nature walks, spa services, art galleries, and boutique shopping, offering something for every type of traveller.

The climate is ideal for yachting year-round. The region enjoys a tropical climate, with the best cruising conditions during the dry season from May to October, featuring temperatures between 24–28°C (75–82°F) and low humidity. The wet season, from November to April, brings warmer weather and occasional showers, along with lush, green landscapes and quieter anchorages.

In summary, Hamilton Island Marina is not just a place to dock—it's a luxury destination in its own right. With top-tier facilities, stunning natural surroundings, and access to world-class accommodations and amenities, it’s the perfect base for exploring the Whitsundays and beyond.

title: Ibiza Marina
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Ibiza Marina
summary: Set against the dazzling backdrop of Ibiza Town’s iconic waterfront, Marina Ibiza is more than just a marina—it’s a statement. A symbol of Mediterranean glamour and elite lifestyle, this five-star destination combines the raw natural beauty of the Balearics with cutting-edge yachting facilities and vibrant cosmopolitan culture. Nestled on the southeastern edge of the island, Marina Ibiza is a magnet for the internati
body: Set against the dazzling backdrop of Ibiza Town’s iconic waterfront, Marina Ibiza is more than just a marina—it’s a statement. A symbol of Mediterranean glamour and elite lifestyle, this five-star destination combines the raw natural beauty of the Balearics with cutting-edge yachting facilities and vibrant cosmopolitan culture. Nestled on the southeastern edge of the island, Marina Ibiza is a magnet for the international yachting set, celebrities, and luxury travellers who crave sun-soaked days and unforgettable nights.

With over 400 berths, Marina Ibiza accommodates vessels ranging from nimble day boats to superyachts up to 110 metres (360 feet) in length. Its sheltered basin and deep-water access make docking safe and simple, even in challenging conditions. The marina’s layout ensures an easy approach and departure for large vessels, while private moorings and visitor slips offer flexible options for both long-term residents and cruising yachtsmen.

Each berth is fully serviced with high-capacity shore power (220V and 380V), fresh water, grey and black water pump-out, satellite TV, and fibre-optic Wi-Fi. The infrastructure is designed for performance and discretion, enabling yacht owners, captains, and crew to focus on enjoyment without compromise. The 24/7 harbour master team provides professional oversight, while concierge services can handle everything from provisioning and table bookings to private transfers and onboard entertainment.

Marina Ibiza isn’t just a place to dock—it’s a fully integrated luxury ecosystem. On-site fuelling services, a full-service shipyard, and technical assistance teams ensure that everything from engine overhauls to cosmetic touch-ups can be handled with minimal fuss. Whether it’s a last-minute repair or pre-season maintenance, the marina’s infrastructure and local partnerships make logistics seamless.

But it’s beyond the hardware that Marina Ibiza truly shines. The marina is a lifestyle hub, home to a curated selection of designer boutiques, fine-dining restaurants, art galleries, and wellness studios. This vibrant commercial zone wraps around the waterfront promenade, offering an effortless blend of style, convenience, and sensory indulgence.

Marina Ibiza’s social crown jewel is undoubtedly Lío Ibiza—a seductive fusion of fine dining, cabaret, and club. As night falls, Lío transforms from a waterfront restaurant into a lavish stage for live performances, drawing a mix of A-listers, yacht crews, and fashionistas. The energy is electric, the setting spectacular, and the dress code unapologetically chic.

Dining options throughout the marina cater to all tastes. Calma Bistro is famed for its panoramic views across the water to Dalt Vila, Ibiza’s UNESCO-listed old town, while Cappuccino Grand Café offers relaxed elegance with exceptional coffee, Mediterranean cuisine, and unbeatable people-watching.

Marina Ibiza’s location gives visiting yachts a strategic advantage. It’s within walking distance of Ibiza Town’s historic centre, where cobbled alleys and Moorish fortifications meet modern boutiques and buzzing tapas bars. And for those eager to escape to sea, the marina offers instant access to some of the Mediterranean’s most iconic cruising grounds.

Sail to Formentera for turquoise lagoons, Es Vedrà for mystical rockscapes, or Cala Jondal for barefoot beach clubs like Blue Marlin—all just a short hop away by tender or yacht. The area’s crystalline waters and consistent summer conditions make it ideal for both relaxed cruising and high-speed charter experiences.

From May through October, Ibiza basks in long days of sunshine, calm seas, and balmy evenings. With average highs between 26–32°C (79–90°F), the climate is perfect for deck lounging by day and dockside cocktails by night. The social calendar is equally radiant, featuring everything from high-end regattas to art openings and exclusive brand pop-ups within the marina.

In every sense, Marina Ibiza represents the evolution of yachting into lifestyle. With its fusion of world-class maritime infrastructure, luxury amenities, and proximity to culture, cuisine, and clubbing, it offers a singular experience that blends functionality with fantasy. Whether you arrive on a sleek 50-footer or a 100-metre megayacht, Marina Ibiza delivers the full package—nautical excellence wrapped in island hedonism.

title: Largs Yacht Haven
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Largs Yacht Haven
summary: Nestled on the scenic Ayrshire coast of Scotland, Largs Yacht Haven is a five-star marina that serves as a gateway to some of the finest cruising grounds in the UK. Overlooking the sheltered waters of the Firth of Clyde and within easy reach of the islands of Cumbrae, Bute, and Arran, it offers a superb blend of modern facilities, natural beauty, and seafaring heritage.
body: Nestled on the scenic Ayrshire coast of Scotland, Largs Yacht Haven is a five-star marina that serves as a gateway to some of the finest cruising grounds in the UK. Overlooking the sheltered waters of the Firth of Clyde and within easy reach of the islands of Cumbrae, Bute, and Arran, it offers a superb blend of modern facilities, natural beauty, and seafaring heritage.

Largs Yacht Haven boasts 750 fully serviced berths, accommodating everything from small sailing yachts to large motor cruisers. Berths are available for annual, seasonal, and short-term visitors, with generous pontoon space, deep-water access, and protection from prevailing weather conditions.

The marina is well-equipped with comprehensive facilities for visiting sailors. These include 24-hour access to luxury heated showers and toilets, free Wi-Fi across the site, a fuel berth supplying diesel and petrol, and secure car parking. There’s a fully stocked chandlery, a well-regarded boatyard with 50-ton hoist and hard standing for winter storage, and marine services ranging from rigging and engine work to electronics and hull maintenance. For those arriving by sea, the marina is easy to approach with deep access and helpful staff always on standby.

Onshore, Largs Yacht Haven is home to several excellent amenities including Scottish Chandlery, Bosun’s Table Café for breakfast and lunch, and the Largs Sailing Club, which regularly hosts regattas and sailing events such as the Largs Regatta Festival. The marina is also adjacent to the town of Largs, a short walk away, offering shops, restaurants, and rail links to Glasgow.

The surrounding cruising waters are ideal for both beginners and seasoned sailors, with abundant anchorages, wildlife, and breathtaking coastal scenery. The sheltered Clyde Estuary provides safe navigation year-round.

Whether you're passing through or planning a longer stay, Largs Yacht Haven offers an outstanding base for exploring the Clyde and beyond, combining top-tier facilities with a friendly and professional atmosphere.

title: Lymington Marina
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Lymington Marina
summary: Lymington Marina – The Gateway to the Solent Nestled on the western edge of the Solent, Lymington Marina stands as one of the most picturesque and popular berthing locations on the South Coast of England. With its scenic river setting, historic Georgian market town, and easy access to the Solent’s renowned sailing grounds, it’s no surprise that Lymington is a firm favourite among cruising yachtsmen, regatta crews, an
body: Lymington Marina – The Gateway to the Solent Nestled on the western edge of the Solent, Lymington Marina stands as one of the most picturesque and popular berthing locations on the South Coast of England. With its scenic river setting, historic Georgian market town, and easy access to the Solent’s renowned sailing grounds, it’s no surprise that Lymington is a firm favourite among cruising yachtsmen, regatta crews, and weekend sailors alike.

Operated by Berthon Marina, this modern facility blends high-quality infrastructure with centuries of maritime tradition. Whether you're preparing for an offshore passage, a family weekend on the water, or looking for a seasonal base, Lymington offers the perfect balance of charm, convenience, and capability.

Lymington has long been a hub of British seafaring. Historically known for shipbuilding and salt production, the town’s deep-water channel and protected harbour have drawn vessels for generations. Today, the marina maintains that legacy with over 280 deep-water berths available for yachts up to 45 metres (148 feet) in length.

The marina is located just upstream of the river mouth, with easy navigation and all-tide access. Berths are spacious and well-maintained, with both floating pontoons and fixed walkways designed to accommodate modern cruising yachts, motorboats, and bluewater cruisers alike.
Lymington Marina is more than just a safe harbour. It offers a comprehensive range of facilities that cater to the needs of visiting and resident yachts:
Electricity and fresh water to every berth (16–63 amp supply)
Free high-speed Wi-Fi across the marina
On-site fuel dock supplying diesel and petrol
Grey and black water pump-out facilities
Private washrooms, showers, and laundry areas
24/7 security and CCTV monitoring
Professional boatyard and full-service refit yard through Berthon Boat Company
Chandlery, marine electronics, rigging, and engineering services

The Berthon Boatyard, adjacent to the marina, is one of the UK’s most respected marine service providers, with over a century of expertise in yacht repair, refit, and brokerage. Whether you need a winter refit, emergency haul-out, or a full systems overhaul, skilled technicians are on hand to assist.

On land, Lymington Marina offers more than just maritime functionality. Its peaceful riverside setting is complemented by a selection of nearby dining options, including the Ship Inn and The Mayflower, both offering hearty fare and views over the harbour.

Just a short stroll from the marina, Lymington town centre offers a mix of boutique shops, traditional pubs, artisan bakeries, and a popular Saturday street market. The scenic Quay Hill winds up through cobbled streets and Georgian facades to a high street full of nautical charm and coastal hospitality.
Lymington’s location makes it an ideal starting point for adventures across the Solent and beyond. It’s just a short sail to iconic destinations such as:
Yarmouth on the Isle of Wight (just 4.5nm across the Solent)
Cowes, the home of British yachting
Newtown Creek, a peaceful anchorage and nature reserve
Beaulieu River, with its charming village and maritime museum
And for the more adventurous sailor, the English Channel and France lie just beyond the horizon, with the Channel Islands within reach for a long weekend cruise.

Lymington is also home to two prestigious yacht clubs: the Royal Lymington Yacht Club and the Lymington Town Sailing Club, both offering active racing programmes, training, and social events. The area has a vibrant sailing community, with regular regattas, youth sailing initiatives, and club racing throughout the season.

Whether you're looking for a long-term berth, a safe and welcoming stopover, or a vibrant home port with full facilities and timeless charm, Lymington Marina delivers on every front. With outstanding service, enviable access to the Solent, and a town steeped in nautical heritage, it’s easy to see why this marina remains a favourite among serious sailors and coastal cruisers.

title: Marina Coppola
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Marina Coppola
summary: Nestled against the dramatic cliffs of southern Italy’s most iconic coastline, Porto di Amalfi – Marina Coppola offers a stunning blend of traditional charm, exceptional service, and unrivalled Mediterranean scenery. Located in the historic town of Amalfi, this boutique marina is a gateway to the glamour, culture, and natural splendour of the Amalfi Coast, and a favoured stop for cruising yachts and luxury charters e
body: Nestled against the dramatic cliffs of southern Italy’s most iconic coastline, Porto di Amalfi – Marina Coppola offers a stunning blend of traditional charm, exceptional service, and unrivalled Mediterranean scenery. Located in the historic town of Amalfi, this boutique marina is a gateway to the glamour, culture, and natural splendour of the Amalfi Coast, and a favoured stop for cruising yachts and luxury charters exploring the Tyrrhenian Sea. While smaller than other Mediterranean ports, Porto di Amalfi is perfectly designed for the unique geography of the region. The marina offers about 100 berths and can accommodate yachts up to 35–40 meters (115–130 feet), depending on availability and weather. Though space is limited, the marina is well-organised and supported by an expert team that helps with mooring, lines, and logistics, especially during the busy high season. The facilities here are modern and tailored to yachters’ needs. Each berth provides access to fresh water, shore power, Wi-Fi, and waste collection, while the marina also offers fuel bunkering via nearby fuel services. There is 24-hour security, and although the marina lacks large-scale repair facilities, basic maintenance and provisioning support are available through local suppliers. Due to the compact layout and popularity of the area, advance booking is essential, particularly from May through September.

What truly sets Porto di Amalfi apart is its location—it sits just steps away from the historic centre of Amalfi, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the most picturesque coastal towns in Italy. Yachters stepping ashore are greeted by a maze of narrow alleys, medieval architecture, and lively piazzas. The 11th-century Amalfi Cathedral, with its grand staircase and striped façade, dominates the town square and offers a cultural anchor to this seafaring city.

Dining in Amalfi is an experience in itself. From family-run trattorias to upscale restaurants with terraces overlooking the sea, you’ll find plenty of spots to enjoy fresh seafood, handmade pasta, and local Limoncello. Popular dining destinations such as Eolo or Marina Grande Restaurant are within walking distance from the marina and known for combining culinary finesse with breathtaking views.

The glamorous lifestyle of the Amalfi Coast is less flashy than the French Riviera, but no less captivating. It’s all about understated elegance—sun-drenched days spent at sea, evening aperitifs on terraces, and boutique shopping in hillside villages like Ravello or Positano, both easily accessible by yacht or car.

The weather in Amalfi is typically Mediterranean and ideal for yachting. Summers are warm and dry, with temperatures averaging 26–31°C (79–88°F) and consistent sunshine. The spring and early autumn months are also fantastic for cruising, with calmer crowds and equally beautiful weather. The coastal cliffs help protect the marina from heavy seas, and the relatively short distances between towns make for leisurely sailing days. Porto di Amalfi – Marina Coppola is more than just a marina—it’s a boutique experience in one of Italy’s most romantic settings. With its prime location, excellent service, and connection to both natural beauty and Italian heritage, it’s a dream destination for yachters looking to immerse themselves in the soul of the Amalfi Coast.

title: Marina de Vilamoura
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Marina de Vilamoura
summary: Marina de Vilamoura – Portugal’s Crown Jewel on the Algarve Coast Sun-baked and impeccably stylish, Marina de Vilamoura is more than just Portugal’s largest marina—it’s the beating heart of the Algarve’s coastal lifestyle. Framed by terracotta-tiled promenades, palm-lined walkways, and a curved necklace of cafes, beach clubs, and boutiques, Vilamoura is where sailors, superyacht owners, and sunseekers drop anchor to
body: Marina de Vilamoura – Portugal’s Crown Jewel on the Algarve Coast Sun-baked and impeccably stylish, Marina de Vilamoura is more than just Portugal’s largest marina—it’s the beating heart of the Algarve’s coastal lifestyle. Framed by terracotta-tiled promenades, palm-lined walkways, and a curved necklace of cafes, beach clubs, and boutiques, Vilamoura is where sailors, superyacht owners, and sunseekers drop anchor to soak up the southern Portuguese charm.

Located between Faro and Albufeira, this award-winning marina blends full-service nautical facilities with a luxury resort vibe. From ocean racing yachts to sleek motor cruisers and globetrotting catamarans, Vilamoura welcomes them all with open arms, a Blue Flag, and a gin and tonic by the dock.

With over 825 berths, Marina de Vilamoura is Portugal’s largest marina and a serious player on the European cruising circuit. It can accommodate vessels from 6 to 60 metres, with dedicated slips for superyachts, deep-draft berths, and stern-to mooring options. The marina is dredged to a depth of 4 to 5 metres, making access safe and simple for even larger boats.

Mooring here means more than just tying up—it means plugging in to shore power, fresh water, and high-speed Wi-Fi. Waste disposal, black water pump-out, and fuel services are all available quayside, with marina staff always ready to assist on VHF Channel 09. The facilities are modern, well-maintained, and thoughtfully laid out with both short-term visitors and long-term residents in mind.

What sets Vilamoura apart isn’t just its glitz—it’s the professionalism. The marina offers a full suite of repair and maintenance services, including haul-outs via travel lift, antifouling, mechanical work, and hull polishing. On-site chandlers, marine engineers, electricians, and sailmakers are all within walking distance.

In addition to the marine side, the marina also supports the sailor’s shore life. There are clean shower and toilet facilities, laundry services, car hire, and concierge help for provisioning, excursions, and onward transport. Customs and immigration clearance is also available for international arrivals.

Vilamoura isn’t just about hardware—it’s a lifestyle. The marina’s elegant waterfront promenade is lined with restaurants, tapas bars, and seafood bistros where locals and visitors mix. Whether you’re tucking into octopus carpaccio, sipping espresso, or enjoying a cocktail at Purobeach, there’s no shortage of places to watch the boats roll in.

A short stroll leads to Vilamoura Beach, known for its golden sands and clear waters. To the west lies Praia da Falésia, regularly ranked among Europe’s top beaches. For sailors needing to work on their swing instead of their tack, several world-class golf courses are minutes away, including the Dom Pedro Victoria Course.

If you’re craving a little more action, Vilamoura Casino is right around the corner, hosting live shows, gaming, and late-night music. Families will enjoy boat tours, dolphin-watching trips, and even a nearby Roman archaeological site.

It’s this blend of nautical professionalism and leisure charm that makes Vilamoura a favourite among returning sailors. It’s not unusual for cruisers to come in for two nights and end up staying a month.

Whether you’re cruising down from Galicia, crossing over from the Med, or exploring Portugal’s southern coastline, Marina de Vilamoura is a perfect pit stop—or permanent base. With first-rate infrastructure, warm hospitality, and a luxurious atmosphere, it’s no wonder this marina regularly ranks as one of the best in Europe.
Drop the hook. Step ashore. And let the Algarve welcome you properly.

title: Marina del Rey – California
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Marina del Rey – California
summary: Marina del Rey, nestled on the coast of Los Angeles County, is the largest man-made small-craft harbour in the United States—and one of the most prestigious boating destinations on the West Coast. With over 4,600 boat slips spread across 19 marinas, it offers an unrivalled blend of urban convenience, marine services, and natural beauty, making it a favourite among both casual cruisers and seasoned sailors.
body: Marina del Rey, nestled on the coast of Los Angeles County, is the largest man-made small-craft harbour in the United States—and one of the most prestigious boating destinations on the West Coast. With over 4,600 boat slips spread across 19 marinas, it offers an unrivalled blend of urban convenience, marine services, and natural beauty, making it a favourite among both casual cruisers and seasoned sailors.

Originally developed in the 1960s, Marina del Rey has grown into a vibrant community that caters to vessels of all sizes—from modest sailing boats to luxury motor yachts up to 250 feet in length. The harbor is ideally located just four miles from Los Angeles International Airport (LAX), and within easy reach of Santa Monica, Venice Beach, and the open waters of the Pacific Ocean.

For visiting sailors, the facilities are extensive and world-class. The marina offers transient berthing, available through several operators including Burton Chace Park Guest Docks, which is managed by the Los Angeles County Department of Beaches and Harbours. These docks provide daily and overnight moorings with essential amenities such as shore power, water hookups, pump-out stations, and restroom/shower facilities.

Beyond the basics, Marina del Rey is packed with services tailored to boaters' needs: fuel docks, marine chandlers, boatyards, and repair yards are all within the harbor’s perimeter. Many marinas also feature Wi-Fi, security patrols, laundry rooms, and private lounges, creating a safe and convenient environment for long-term stays.

The harbour’s community vibe is enhanced by restaurants, cafes, and boutique shopping just steps from the docks. Dining ranges from casual eateries like The Cheesecake Factory and Killer Shrimp to elegant waterfront dining at SALT and Cast & Plow. During weekends, sailors can enjoy live music, farmers markets, and yacht club events, while the surrounding area offers access to biking trails, beaches, and water sports.

With its combination of luxury, accessibility, and comprehensive services, Marina del Rey stands out as the ultimate gateway to Southern California’s coastal lifestyle. Whether you're laying over during a coastal cruise or planning a long-term berth, it delivers the full package for visiting sailors.

title: Marina Grande - Capri
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Marina Grande - Capri
summary: Marina Grande – Capri: The Gateway to Italian Island Glamour
body: Marina Grande – Capri: The Gateway to Italian Island Glamour

Perched on the northern coast of the legendary island of Capri, Marina Grande is the island’s main port and a vibrant hub of Mediterranean charm, luxury, and nautical prestige. As one of the most iconic marinas in Italy, it is not only a practical point of entry to the island but also a window into the enchanting blend of natural beauty and jet-set glamour that Capri is famous for. Marina Grande welcomes a diverse range of vessels, from local fishing boats and ferries to elegant motor yachts and sailing cruisers. While relatively compact compared to larger Mediterranean ports, the marina provides approximately 300 berths, including around 40 slips reserved for visiting yachts, and can accommodate vessels up to 60 meters in length. Due to the marina’s popularity and limited space, it’s highly recommended to book in advance, especially during peak season (June to September), when the port is bustling with activity.

Despite its small size, the marina offers a solid range of facilities for yachts and their crews. Berths are supplied with fresh water, electricity (including 220V and 380V options), and dockside waste disposal. There are also fuelling services, 24-hour security, and assistance with mooring and provisioning. Though there’s no extensive repair yard onsite, nearby mainland facilities in Naples or Sorrento can handle more complex servicing needs. Port authorities are professional and used to handling a high volume of luxury traffic with efficiency and courtesy. Marina Grande isn’t just about the yachts—it’s a visual and cultural experience. Upon docking, visitors are greeted with a stunning panorama of colourful buildings rising up the cliffs, a lively waterfront, and an atmosphere that feels like a movie set. The piazzetta-style promenade is lined with gelato shops, upscale boutiques, and cafés where visitors sip espresso while watching tenders zip to and from superyachts anchored just offshore.

A short funicular ride or taxi from the marina brings you to Capri town, the island’s chic centre filled with designer fashion stores, historic villas, and elegant restaurants. Capri has long been a playground for the international elite, attracting stars from Hollywood to high society, and it still buzzes with a stylish, yet unpretentious energy. Iconic spots like La Fontelina beach club, Via Camerelle shopping street, and the glamorous Quisisana Hotel are all within reach for guests mooring at Marina Grande.

The natural beauty surrounding the marina is also breathtaking. Yachters use Marina Grande as a base to explore world-renowned sites like the Blue Grotto (Grotta Azzurra), Faraglioni sea stacks, and the crystal-clear coves around the island. Many choose to anchor offshore and visit the island by tender for a truly cinematic arrival. The weather in Capri is ideal for yachting, especially from late spring through early autumn. Summers are sunny and warm, with temperatures ranging between 26–32°C (79–89°F), and mild evenings perfect for alfresco dining. The Tyrrhenian Sea is generally calm, making it perfect for cruising, and the dramatic coastline offers plenty of scenic anchorages.

In essence, Marina Grande is more than just a place to dock—it's a destination in its own right. It offers a taste of Capri’s legendary lifestyle, where natural beauty, nautical charm, and Italian elegance come together in unforgettable harmony.

title: Montauk Yacht Club
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Montauk Yacht Club
summary: Located at the eastern tip of Long Island, the Montauk Yacht Club (now known as Gurney’s Star Island Marina) is one of the premier marina destinations on the U.S. East Coast. With its blend of luxury, nautical charm, and strategic location, this full-service marina offers both seasoned sailors and luxury cruisers an ideal base for exploring the waters of the Atlantic and Block Island Sound.
body: Located at the eastern tip of Long Island, the Montauk Yacht Club (now known as Gurney’s Star Island Marina) is one of the premier marina destinations on the U.S. East Coast. With its blend of luxury, nautical charm, and strategic location, this full-service marina offers both seasoned sailors and luxury cruisers an ideal base for exploring the waters of the Atlantic and Block Island Sound.

The marina boasts 232 deep-water slips, accommodating vessels up to 220 feet in length with a maximum draft of 12 feet. It’s one of the largest marinas in the Hamptons and welcomes both seasonal and transient guests. Many of the slips are equipped for large yachts, making it a popular summer stopover for super yachts and sport fishing fleets alike.
Facilities for Visiting Sailors Fuel: On-site high-speed fuelling stations offer both diesel and gasoline. In-slip fuelling is available for larger vessels upon arrangement.
Wi-Fi: Complimentary high-speed Wi-Fi is accessible throughout the marina, including slips, common areas, and the clubhouse.
Electricity: Shore power hookups include 30, 50, and 100 amp single- and three-phase service, suitable for yachts of all sizes.
Fresh Water: Clean, potable fresh water is available at every slip.
Waste Disposal: Pump-out services and environmentally compliant waste and oil disposal facilities are available dockside.
Food & Drink: The resort features on-site dining, including a waterfront restaurant and poolside bar. Gourmet provisioning and private catering are available upon request.
Maintenance Services: Full mechanical and marine repair services are available nearby. Staff can arrange emergency repairs, cleaning, diver services, and winterisation support.
Amenities: Visiting sailors also have access to luxury resort features including an outdoor pool, spa services, tennis courts, fire pits, fitness centre, and bicycle rentals.

title: Nanny-Cay-Marina

imageAlt: Nanny-Cay-Marina
summary: Located on the south coast of Tortola in the British Virgin Islands (BVI), Nanny Cay Marina is a premier full-service marina and resort that has become a favourite hub for cruising yachts, luxury charters, and liveaboards exploring the turquoise waters of the Caribbean. Blending top-tier facilities with a laid-back island vibe, it offers everything sailors need—whether they’re passing through, chartering, or staying
body: Located on the south coast of Tortola in the British Virgin Islands (BVI), Nanny Cay Marina is a premier full-service marina and resort that has become a favourite hub for cruising yachts, luxury charters, and liveaboards exploring the turquoise waters of the Caribbean. Blending top-tier facilities with a laid-back island vibe, it offers everything sailors need—whether they’re passing through, chartering, or staying long-term.

The marina is nestled within a protected lagoon, making it one of the most secure harbours in the region. It offers over 300 berths, including 110 slips in the outer marina and over 190 in the inner marina. The inner marina can accommodate the larger vessels up to 150 ft with deep draft access. All berths are equipped with electricity (30, 50, and 100-amp), potable water, Wi-Fi, and the marina has dockside pump-out services.

Nanny Cay is not just a place to dock—it’s a full yachting village. The marina is home to a comprehensive boatyard with a 50-ton and 70-ton travel lift, dry storage, and a full range of repair and maintenance services. Onsite professionals offer fibreglass work, engine servicing, sail repair, electronics, rigging, and more. It's also a designated hurricane shelter, with haul-out and storage services during storm season, making it popular among long-term cruisers. The amenities at Nanny Cay go beyond the technical. The marina is part of a resort that includes a hotel, beach bar, restaurants, swimming pool, laundry facilities, showers, provisioning market, and a dive shop. There’s even a small shopping plaza with a chandlery, gift shops, and marine supply stores. Yacht crews and guests can enjoy the beach, or hop on a snorkel trip right from the dock.

For those seeking the Caribbean yachting lifestyle, Nanny Cay is both vibrant and relaxing. It’s a hub of social activity, especially during regatta season. The marina hosts several popular sailing events including the BVI Spring Regatta and Round Tortola Race, which draw international competitors and boat lovers. With its friendly community and regular live music, happy hours, and cruising get-togethers, the marina cultivates a welcoming and social atmosphere. The climate in Tortola is ideal for yachting year-round. The BVI enjoys a tropical climate with warm temperatures averaging 28–31°C (82–88°F) and steady trade winds, particularly during the winter and spring months. The sheltered waters around Tortola and the proximity to dozens of nearby islands—like Jost Van Dyke, Virgin Gorda, and Anegada—make it one of the best cruising grounds in the world. Distances between anchorages are short, and the seas are generally calm, making it perfect for both experienced sailors and casual charters.

In short, Nanny Cay Marina offers an exceptional mix of professional services, resort-style comforts, and Caribbean charm. Whether you're starting a charter, docking for the season, or just sailing through, it's a perfect base to experience the magic of the British Virgin Islands from both a practical and lifestyle perspective.

title: Port Adriano
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Port Adriano
summary: On the sun-drenched southwest coast of Mallorca, Port Adriano stands as one of Europe’s most modern and luxurious marinas. Designed by the legendary French architect Philippe Starck, this sleek and elegant port blends cutting-edge infrastructure with refined aesthetics, creating a space where yachting excellence meets high-end living. Purpose-built to cater to superyachts and their discerning owners, Port Adriano is
body: On the sun-drenched southwest coast of Mallorca, Port Adriano stands as one of Europe’s most modern and luxurious marinas. Designed by the legendary French architect Philippe Starck, this sleek and elegant port blends cutting-edge infrastructure with refined aesthetics, creating a space where yachting excellence meets high-end living. Purpose-built to cater to superyachts and their discerning owners, Port Adriano is a true hub of Balearic luxury and one of the Mediterranean’s premier nautical destinations.

Located near El Toro, just 20 minutes from Palma de Mallorca and its international airport, Port Adriano offers 492 berths that accommodate yachts ranging from 6 meters to 80 meters (262 feet) in length. The marina features deep-water access with depths of up to 7 meters and wide fairways, ensuring easy manoeuvrability for large vessels. Its spacious layout and state-of-the-art facilities have made it a favourite stop for some of the world’s most impressive superyachts.

Every berth is fully equipped with high-amperage electricity (up to 600A), fresh water, Wi-Fi, satellite TV, and waste pump-out services. A dedicated fuel dock offers premium diesel with high-speed pumps suitable for large yachts. The marina also provides 24/7 security and video surveillance, customs clearance, and a comprehensive range of concierge services, including provisioning, transportation, and private event coordination. Onsite technical services include a full dry dock and boatyard for maintenance and repairs, with a 250-ton travel lift capable of handling large superyachts.

But what truly sets Port Adriano apart is its distinct ambiance—a mix of understated opulence and relaxed sophistication. The marina promenade is lined with designer boutiques, upscale cafés, and gourmet restaurants, each carefully curated to reflect the high standards of its clientele. From luxury fashion and fine jewellery to cutting-edge art galleries and home decor, the shopping experience is both refined and exclusive. Dining options at Port Adriano are equally impressive. Renowned restaurants such as Zhero Boathouse, Coast by East, and Bruno’s offer everything from Mediterranean seafood to sushi and cocktails, all with stunning views of the marina and sea. The port is also known for hosting high-profile events including fashion shows, classical concerts, regattas, car exhibitions, and lively summer festivals that attract visitors from across the globe. Port Adriano’s location makes it an ideal base for exploring the beautiful Balearic coast. Nearby attractions include the coves of Cala Fornells, the chic town of Andratx, and the UNESCO-listed Tramuntana mountains. The marina also provides easy access to Cabrera National Park and the other Balearic Islands—Ibiza, Menorca, and Formentera—making it a strategic starting point for longer cruising adventures.

The weather in Mallorca is quintessentially Mediterranean. Summers are hot and dry, with average temperatures between 28–34°C (82–93°F), and minimal rainfall. Spring and autumn offer mild conditions and clear skies, while winters remain relatively warm and pleasant, making Port Adriano a year-round destination for yachting and leisure.

In summary, Port Adriano is more than just a marina—it’s a luxury lifestyle destination. With its world-class berthing facilities, contemporary design, and vibrant social atmosphere, it caters to the elite yachting community while offering an unparalleled experience of Mallorca’s coastal charm and cosmopolitan flair.

title: Port de Saint-Tropez
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Port de Saint-Tropez
summary: Its more than just a marina—it’s a symbol of Mediterranean elegance, jet-set glamour, and maritime prestige. Situated in the heart of the iconic town of Saint-Tropez on the French Riviera, this small but legendary port is world-renowned for its vibrant atmosphere, picturesque setting, and as a favourite berth for celebrities, superyachts, and luxury travellers from around the globe.
body: Its more than just a marina—it’s a symbol of Mediterranean elegance, jet-set glamour, and maritime prestige. Situated in the heart of the iconic town of Saint-Tropez on the French Riviera, this small but legendary port is world-renowned for its vibrant atmosphere, picturesque setting, and as a favourite berth for celebrities, superyachts, and luxury travellers from around the globe.

With around 734 berths, Port de Saint-Tropez accommodates vessels of all sizes, from sleek day boats to yachts up to 70 meters in length. While it doesn’t offer the superyacht capacity of Port Vauban or Port Hercules, its prime location and prestige more than compensate. Berthing here is like getting a front-row seat at a catwalk of yachting style—right on the waterfront, in full view of bustling cafés, luxury boutiques, and vintage buildings with pastel facades. Despite its relatively compact size, the port offers excellent facilities for yachts and their crews. Each berth provides electricity (up to 600 amps for larger yachts), fresh water, Wi-Fi, and grey/black water disposal. The marina also includes a fuel dock, waste management services, and 24/7 security and mooring assistance. Onshore, yacht crews benefit from access to provisioning services, chandlers, laundry, maintenance support, and concierge-style service.

What makes this port so iconic is its location—right at the heart of the action. As soon as you step off your yacht, you’re in the centre of Saint-Tropez’s legendary harbour scene. The marina is surrounded by world-famous establishments such as Sénéquier Café, Le Quai, and Bar du Port, where yacht owners and visitors sip rosé and people-watch under the Provençal sun. Just a short walk away are high-end boutiques like Louis Vuitton, Hermès, Dior, and local designer labels, making the town a shopping paradise.

The glamour of Port de Saint-Tropez peaks during summer, particularly in July and August, when the town becomes a playground for billionaires, celebrities, artists, and fashion icons. Major events such as Les Voiles de Saint-Tropez, a prestigious sailing regatta held in late September, attract classic and modern sailing yachts from around the world, filling the harbour with polished hulls and colourful sails.

The weather in Saint-Tropez is textbook Mediterranean: long, sunny summers with average temperatures around 27–32°C (80–90°F) and mild, pleasant winters. The region enjoys over 300 days of sunshine per year, making it ideal for nearly year-round yachting. The famous Mistral wind can occasionally blow through, but it’s more common in the winter months and brings clear skies in its wake.

From a yachting perspective, Port de Saint-Tropez is not just a marina—it’s a statement. It offers high-end facilities with a front-row seat to one of the most glamorous seaside towns in the world. With its combination of service, setting, and style, it remains one of the most sought-after moorings on the Riviera, where life is lived alfresco, and every sunset is an event.

title: Port Denarau Marina
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Port Denarau Marina
summary: Port Denarau Marina – Fiji’s Nautical Welcome Mat If there’s a gateway to South Pacific cruising heaven, Port Denarau Marina is it. Not just a marina—it’s the marina. Tucked snugly on the western edge of Viti Levu, Fiji’s main island, and a short taxi hop from Nadi International Airport, this marina is the beating heart of Fiji’s yachting scene. body: Port Denarau Marina – Fiji’s Nautical Welcome Mat If there’s a gateway to South Pacific cruising heaven, Port Denarau Marina is it. Not just a marina—it’s the marina. Tucked snugly on the western edge of Viti Levu, Fiji’s main island, and a short taxi hop from Nadi International Airport, this marina is the beating heart of Fiji’s yachting scene. It's where palm trees meet provisioning, where you can stock up on diesel and dive gear with equal ease—and where more than a few voyages have started with an espresso and ended with a rum punch.

Arriving here by sea, the first thing you notice is how well laid out it all is. There’s room for 52 boats at fully serviced berths, with superyacht capacity up to 85 metres, and deep water that’s accessible even at low tide. For the bigger beasts, Jetty C is the star of the show—with fingers ready for yachts as long as 115m and enough elbow room to berth 20 superyachts side by side. Not many island marinas can boast that kind of muscle.

Port Denarau is more than just scale. It’s the polish that sets it apart. The marina is clean, modern, and efficient—an unusual trifecta in the South Pacific. It’s not just that everything works (and it does), it’s that it feels like it was built with proper cruisers in mind. High-capacity shore power? Check. Fresh water at every berth? Naturally. Pump-out? Of course. Fuel docks? Multiple, with high-flow pumps delivering up to 160 litres a minute. In a region where “island time” often rules, Denarau feels almost unnervingly Swiss.

But what really makes this place sing is the service. The harbour office team are seasoned pros—friendly, knowledgeable, and absolutely unflappable. Lost your customs paperwork? They’ll sort it. Need a mechanic on a Sunday? Give them ten minutes. Want a golf buggy ride to the chandlery with your diesel jerry cans? No problem. There’s a concierge-like energy here, but without the pretension.

Then there’s the backlot. Denarau isn’t just a marina—it’s a full-service ecosystem. A 30-ton travel lift stands ready for haul-outs, with dry storage for around 30 vessels. Need work done? On-site workshops cover every trade: rigging, sail repair, electrics, hydraulics, composites—you name it. There's also a serious chandlery, a marine electronics dealer, and even a diving contractor for hull scrubs or prop fouls. For bluewater cruisers arriving dusty and tired after an ocean crossing, it's like stumbling into an oasis.

When the day’s work is done, you can swap overalls for board shorts and explore the lively waterfront precinct that wraps around the docks. Port Denarau has grown into a commercial hub, with nine major hotels on the island, dozens of restaurants and cafés, a shopping complex with boutiques, supermarkets, a spa, banks, even a dentist (yes, really), and a bakery that does a croissant worth racing back from Musket Cove for.

And it’s not just facilities for owners—crews are treated like guests, not an afterthought. Free Wi-Fi zones, live music, regular crew parties, and a sociable vibe make this a favourite stop for delivery teams and liveaboards alike. There's a community here—well-fed, well-rested, and usually half-covered in suncream and salt.

From a cruising perspective, Denarau is the ideal jump-off point. Within a couple of hours’ sail you’ve got the coral wonderlands of the Mamanuca Islands, with turquoise bays, pristine reefs, and beach bars you’ll never want to leave. A day more and you're into the Yasawas—wilder, taller, and barely touched. Further afield, Fiji’s outer islands promise unspoiled anchorages, volcanic terrain, and the kind of remote anchor drops that old sea dogs live for.

The marina’s customs and biosecurity clearance setup is also top-tier. You can pre-arrange arrival, walk your documents to the office, and have your Q flag down in record time. This alone makes it the favoured port of entry for 80%+ of foreign-flagged yachts entering Fiji. The marina even offers agent support for more complex arrivals, charter permits, or yacht importation.

Now, lest we get too carried away, it’s worth mentioning a few minor caveats. During peak season (June–September), berths can be tight. Book well in advance, especially if you’re over 50 feet. And while the marina itself is protected, the outer basin can get choppy in big westerlies. But these are minor points in an otherwise superb offering.

Also worth applauding is the marina’s commitment to sustainability. Port Denarau is a certified Clean Marina and a founding member of the South Pacific Sustainable Yachting Network. They’ve invested in recycling, greywater handling, energy-efficient lighting, and local community programs. It's clear they're playing the long game—not just cashing in on passing yachts.

So, what’s the final word? Port Denarau Marina doesn’t just accommodate yachts—it welcomes them. It’s the kind of place that makes captains breathe easier and owners stay longer. Whether you’re provisioning for an island-hopping escape, fixing a leaky seal, or sipping espresso while waiting for your tender, this place delivers with quiet competence and tropical warmth.
Verdict? A five-star pit stop with a palm-fringed smile—and for many, the best marina in the South Pacific.

title: Port Royal
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Port Royal
summary: At the mouth of Kingston Harbour—one of the largest natural harbours in the world—lies Port Royal, once lauded as the “wickedest city on Earth.” Today, it serves as home to the Royal Jamaica Yacht Club (RJYC), the primary marina and anchorage for sailors arriving in Jamaica from the wider Caribbean or northern South America.
body: At the mouth of Kingston Harbour—one of the largest natural harbours in the world—lies Port Royal, once lauded as the “wickedest city on Earth.” Today, it serves as home to the Royal Jamaica Yacht Club (RJYC), the primary marina and anchorage for sailors arriving in Jamaica from the wider Caribbean or northern South America.

Port Royal is historically significant and strategically placed at the eastern entrance to Kingston Harbour—protected by the Palisadoes spit and guarded by colonial-era Fort Charles and the Plumb Point Lighthouse. The RJYC occupies the western tip of Port Royal, offering sheltered waters and convenient access to Kingston’s port authorities and capital city services.

The Royal Jamaica Yacht Club offers around 120 permanent berths, accommodating vessels up to 50 ft, plus a visitor dock designed for yachts as large as 150 ft. Berths are equipped with 110V / 220V shore power, metered water, well-lit docks, and services like showers and toilets. Many sailors opt to anchor in the mud-bottomed waters outside the marina, which Navily users say is “very quiet and perfectly protected,” with dinghy access to the docks for approximately USD 13/day to use yacht club amenities

RJYC provides more than just a berth—it delivers convenience in a relaxed setting. On-site facilities include: Clubhouse with bar & restaurant, offering lunch, snacks, and occasional dinner service, all with sweeping views of Kingston and the Blue Mountains Swimming pool, event spaces, and soft social activities for both sailors and members Light shop provisioning, booking assistance, occasional weekend races, and regattas organised through the Jamaica Yachting Association

Although RJYC lacks a full-service boatyard, cruisers may arrange haul-outs and technical repairs at Montego Bay Yacht Club or Errol Flynn Marina if needed—or rely on Kingston's limited workshop facilities nearby

Once a pirate republic and haven for privateers such as Henry Morgan, Port Royal’s fortunes changed on 7 June 1692 when a catastrophic earthquake liquefied the sandy spit and sank much of the city into the sea. Thousands died, and what remained was swiftly eclipsed by Kingston to the west.

Today, Port Royal is being redeveloped as a UNESCO World Heritage Site (as of mid-2025), with restored buildings, a floating cruise pier, the ruins of Fort Charles, and an underwater archaeology museum showcasing a submerged city frozen in time.
Fort Charles: Jamaica’s oldest fort, built in the 1650s—now open to the public.
Giddy House: A tilted building still standing, tilted by the 1907 quake.
The Port Royal Museum, housing artefacts discovered from underwater excavations.

Although Port Royal is tranquil and historical, Kingston—the capital—is just a short drive or taxi-boat ride away. Here you'll find galleries, music venues, the Bob Marley Museum, Devon House, vibrant street food, and a buzzing nightlife scene
Customs and immigration arrivals are typically processed via Kingston, although pilots often coordinate with RJYC to expedite clearance for vessels entering southern Jamaica

Kingston Harbour stretches 16 km by 3.2 km, making it properly marine-scaled but often impacted by agricultural runoff and industrial discharge at its northern and western edges. Approaching flows should avoid ammunition-laden areas near Rockfort or industrial docks. Anchor in the southern-mouth basin near Port Royal for clear water and scenic shelter
Visitor Fees: Approx USD 13/day for anchorage + yacht club access; berthing for yachts under 50 ft included in membership

For sailors navigating Jamaica’s southern coast, Royal Jamaica Yacht Club offers the perfect balance of history, service, and security. It’s not a glamorous superyacht hub, but it exceeds expectations as a friendly, protective, and culturally rich stopover.

Port Royal’s legacy and RJYC’s facilities elevate this anchorage from functional to fascinating. It’s where cruisers can anchor among pirate lore and colonial ruins, provision in a capital city, and slip into the storytelling spirit of the Caribbean—all anchored securely in one of the world’s grandest harbours.

title: Port St. Charles Marina – Barbados
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Port St. Charles Marina – Barbados
summary: Nestled along the tranquil northwest coast of Barbados in Saint Peter Parish, Port St. Charles Marina is widely regarded as the premier luxury marina on the island. With protected waters, a breakwater outfitted for megayachts, full port‑of-entry status, and an adjacent resort community, it offers a polished, well‑rounded stopover for sailors seeking both comfort and Caribbean charm.
body: Nestled along the tranquil northwest coast of Barbados in Saint Peter Parish, Port St. Charles Marina is widely regarded as the premier luxury marina on the island. With protected waters, a breakwater outfitted for megayachts, full port‑of-entry status, and an adjacent resort community, it offers a polished, well‑rounded stopover for sailors seeking both comfort and Caribbean charm.
Location & Coordinates
Port St. Charles sits in Heywoods, Saint Peter, just a short hop from Speightstown—a historic coastal town bustling with local culture.

Port St. Charles is built around a calm lagoon with an offshore breakwater that hosts six dedicated superyacht berths, capable of accommodating vessels 60 to 250 feet LOA. Within the lagoon itself, there are smaller berths for yachts from about 30 ft to 110 ft, and the inner lagoon is reserved for residents and marina guests. The lagoon depth at low tide is about 14 ft (~4.26 m), allowing moderate draft vessels to navigate safely. Beyond the breakwater, the marina also maintains a few offshore mooring buoys intended for larger yachts exceeding the breakwater berth lengths. On the offshore wall, superyachts tie alongside the breakwater, while the internal lagoon handles more sheltered dockage.
The recognised VHF channels for Port St. Charles are 77 and 16—common channels for routine marine communications.

In terms of customs and immigration, Port St. Charles stands as one of only two official sea-based ports of entry in Barbados (the other being Bridgetown’s Deep Water Harbour). Yachts approaching Barbados are instructed to call the Signal Station on VHF Channel 12 to request entry, as part of the national arrival procedures. barbadosport.com
Visitors must report directly to the seaport of entry (which might be the marina breakwater) and are generally not allowed to anchor or dinghy ashore before clearing immigration and customs. Noonsite
Port St. Charles offers a full suite of marina facilities designed to meet the expectations of discriminating yachts:
Electricity & Water: Available at most larger berths (30–110 ft and more) with metered systems. Marine Project
Cable TV / Telephony: Provided for qualifying berths.
Fuel (Dockside Bunkering): Fuel service is available to yachts.
Sewage / Waste: Pump-out and disposal services are supported.
WiFi / Internet: Provided as a marina amenity.
Security: Routine 24/7 marina security, gate access, and oversight.
Marine Support: While Port St. Charles is not known as a heavy-duty shipyard, light repair work, provisioning, and dockside services are available and coordinated through marina staff. Marine Project
Customs / Immigration / Police / Coast Guard: All these regulatory bodies maintain offices or facilities on or near the offshore breakwater, making arrivals and clearances relatively streamlined.
Heliport: The marina boasts a helipad for fast transfers to/from Grantley Adams International Airport or Bridgetown.
Resort Integration: Port St. Charles is part of a larger luxury resort community with villas, condos, amenities like swimming pools, spa, beach access, and dining venues (e.g. Pier One).
The resort side ensures that yacht crews and guests can enjoy a full island-stay experience without needing to leave the marina environment.
Strengths:
Luxury & integration – A rare blend of elite marina services and upscale resort infrastructure.
Port of Entry – Makes customs/immigration easier when arriving by sea.
Protected anchorage – The breakwater offers good shelter from prevailing seas.
Superyacht ready – Berths and mooring buoys suitable for large yachts.
Amenities ashore – Resort lifestyle, dining, villas, and services all part of the marina complex.
Challenges:
Book early – With only six megayacht berths and limited staff, demand in high season can stretch availability.
Draft limitations – The lagoon and inner slips have modest depths; deeper-draft yachts must negotiate carefully.
Service constraints – While offering light repairs and provisioning, major haul-outs or full refits require external yards.
VHF clarity – Always call ahead on the proper VHF (77 or 16) to coordinate entry; marina staff expect prior contact.
User Notes & Advice
Incoming calls: Call VHF 77 or 16 well in advance of reaching Port St. Charles.
Arrival procedure: As part of Barbados’ arrival rules, early communication with the Signal Station on VHF 12 is also standard. barbadosport.com
Stay inside the breakwater if possible—anchor outside only if instructed or authorised.
Access lagoon slips only if you are a resort guest or have marina permission.
Request assistance with docking—crew and staff at Port St. Charles are known to be very helpful.

title: Port Vauban
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Port Vauban
summary: Port Vauban, located in the charming town of Antibes on France’s Côte d’Azur, is one of the largest and most prestigious marinas in the Mediterranean. With its rich maritime history, world-class facilities, and stunning setting between Nice and Cannes, Port Vauban is a true icon of the French Riviera yachting scene. It seamlessly blends heritage, functionality, and luxury, attracting everyone from serious yacht owner
body: Port Vauban, located in the charming town of Antibes on France’s Côte d’Azur, is one of the largest and most prestigious marinas in the Mediterranean. With its rich maritime history, world-class facilities, and stunning setting between Nice and Cannes, Port Vauban is a true icon of the French Riviera yachting scene. It seamlessly blends heritage, functionality, and luxury, attracting everyone from serious yacht owners to globe-trotting celebrities.

At its core, Port Vauban is built to accommodate yachts of all shapes and sizes. With more than 1,500 berths, including around 19 dedicated spaces for superyachts over 70 meters in the exclusive “Quai des Milliardaires” (Billionaires’ Quay), it is a playground for the world’s most impressive vessels. Its sheltered harbour and deep draft make it a natural choice for large yachts, offering calm waters and direct access to the sparkling Mediterranean Sea. The marina offers extensive facilities tailored to the needs of both professional crew and discerning yacht owners. Berths come fully serviced with power (up to 600A), fresh water, Wi-Fi, black water disposal, and round-the-clock security. There are fuel stations, concierge services, and access to the IYCA (International Yacht Club of Antibes), which provides exclusive facilities and a vibrant social calendar for the elite yachting community.

For yacht maintenance, Port Vauban boasts a dedicated shipyard area with travel lifts and technical services for everything from routine checks to complex repairs. It’s also home to many yacht management, brokerage, and charter companies, making it a hub of Mediterranean maritime business. Antibes itself is steeped in old-world charm and modern Riviera luxury. Just steps from the marina, the Vieille Ville (Old Town) enchants with its cobbled streets, Provençal markets, and cozy cafés. The Picasso Museum, located in the old Château Grimaldi, is a cultural gem overlooking the sea. For fine dining, Antibes offers a mix of authentic French bistros and upscale restaurants, many of which have views of the port and the Alps in the distance.

Despite its quieter, more local charm compared to flashier neighbours like Monaco or Saint-Tropez, Antibes has long attracted the international jet set. The presence of the superyacht crowd gives the town a cosmopolitan buzz, especially during events like the Antibes Yacht Show and summer regattas.

The climate is another highlight. Antibes enjoys a typical Mediterranean climate, with hot, dry summers and mild winters. Expect long sunny days from May to September, with temperatures ranging from 25–30°C (77–86°F), and plenty of sailing opportunities well into autumn. The nearby Cap d’Antibes offers idyllic anchorages and stunning coastal views. Port Vauban isn’t just a place to dock a yacht—it’s a lifestyle. From high-end yachting facilities to the historic charm of Antibes and the glamour of the French Riviera, it offers a unique combination of function and flair. Whether you're provisioning for a charter, preparing for a summer cruise, or simply soaking up Riviera sophistication, Port Vauban delivers the ultimate Mediterranean yachting experience.

A purpose-built haven for sailors, jet-setters, and sun-seekers alike, it stands as the undisputed capital of the Costa Smeralda – the Emerald Coast – famous for its turquoise waters, unspoiled beaches, and luxurious Mediterranean lifestyle.
