title: Why the Increasing Complexity of Yachting Demands Greater Investment in Crew Competency
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Why the Increasing Complexity of Yachting Demands Greater Investment in Crew Competency
summary: The growth in sophistication of contemporary yachting is arguably outpacing the competency of its crews; an issue demanding immediate attention, for the implications are multifold and severe.
body: As the yachting industry continues to evolve, investing in crew education has become increasingly significant. The tragic outcomes of substandard competency are all-too-visible in our society. Incidents like the Grenfell Tower inferno and the subsequent findings underscore the danger of sacrificing safety for cost-cutting. Similarly, recent yachting accidents highlight these risks. While these events may differ in context, they share an uncanny similarity in their root cause: deficient responsibility. Numerous disasters could have been prevented if correct protocol was adhered to and crew proficiency was at a higher level. This should not be viewed as a criticism towards the crew; it's simply addressing the unavoidable fact that yachting has become more intricate. Larger yachts, more complex technology, and tighter regulations, require highly trained crews. The failure to prioritize such training endangers more than just safety. It also impacts broader issues, from influencing perception and insurance rates, to crew wellbeing and the industry's reputation. An industry, after all, is mirrored in the competence of its people. Therefore, it becomes incumbent for owners, both private and commercial, to invest in their crew, even if that means loosening their purse strings a bit. Even though this might seem an expensive proposition, in the long run, it might turn out to be a financially sound decision. Ignoring safety measures and crew training will eventually attract consequences that could demonstrably impact their financial status and the overall reputation of the yachting industry.

title: The Sea Change in Maritime Connectivity as Yachting Season Ends: The Starlink Revolution
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The Sea Change in Maritime Connectivity as Yachting Season Ends: The Starlink Revolution
summary: As the Mediterranean yachting season of 2024 wraps up, the maritime community delves into the transformative impact of SpaceX’s Starlink Maritime on leisure yachting.
body: As yachts sail off into the sunset, marking the end of the 2024 season, the maritime spews forth stories of change, innovation, and one name that drenched every deck and hull, Starlink Maritime. A brainchild of SpaceX, Starlink Maritime altered the course of connectivity at sea, sparked intrigue ship-wide, and turned conventional satellite installations on their heads, all within the sunny cruise of one season.

From the helm to the hold, no luxury leisure vessel was too large or too small to ask about the Low Earth Orbit (LEO) service by Starlink. A task typically spanning two to six months for a single ship was condensed into a spectacle where, in 2024, a service provider installed Starlink on over 40 vessels in the same timeframe. The waves of change were certainly felt as the industry transformed from a one-on-one match to a grand melee of installations, services, and action.

As sailors peer elusively into the horizon of 2025, a few changes stand out to be potential game-changers. It seems Starlink may tighten geofencing rules for ships sailing away from shore. Notably, early independent boat owners who smartly used land RV data packages, cheap alternatives to maritime plans, might sail towards stormy weather. Starlink brings in place location-based contract rules restricting data access based on the 'time out of their home port'. However, loopholes exist and ROAM can still be used up to 22 kilometers from shore. Nonetheless, Starlink's geofencing applications note some inconsistencies - as vessels can access services in unlicensed areas like Macedonia's waters.

The 2024 yachting season is but a port in the grand journey of maritime connectivity. As service providers review the year that was, they navigate changing tides, swirling winds, and a future brimming with exploration and possibilities.

title: On the Rise: First-ever Yacht Chartering Licences Issued by Saudi Red Sea Authority
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: On the Rise: First-ever Yacht Chartering Licences Issued by Saudi Red Sea Authority
summary: The Saudi Red Sea Authority (SRSA) launches into a new era, awarding its first set of yacht chartering licences.
body: A new vista has dawned upon the marine world as the Saudi Red Sea Authority (SRSA) has granted its first three yacht chartering licences. This groundbreaking move comes in anticipation of a surge in demand fuelled by the commencement of Sindalah and the advancement of other developments in the initiative. The chosen few to hold the maiden licences are Hill Robinson Saudi, Faisal M. Higgi & Associates, and JLS Yachts. These prestigious entities now have the authority to transform the Kingdom's Red Sea region into a paradise for yachting enthusiasts, operating under the Large Yacht Chartering Regulation formulated by the SRSA.

Treading more milestones, the authority has recently granted marina operator licences for the first time to Al-Ahlam Marine to enrich the seas of Yanbu and Al-Lith. The Jeddah Yacht Club and Marina, sporting the proud insignia of Sela, a Public Investment Fund company, has been crowned as the first international marina in Saudi Arabia to claim an operator licence.

However, the SRSA stands tall with its moral duties towards Mother Nature, as it claims that environmental protection plays a key role while the region transforms into a hub for superyachts. Backing its statement, it has inked a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the National Centre for Environmental Compliance with a prospective dream of developing technologies to monitor and reduce pollution, efficiently manage surrounding marine ecosystems, and streamline the environmental permitting process. This joined venture is not only aimed to preserve the marine environment but also significantly reduce pollution caused by yachts. Additionally, it paves the way for collaboration on research, disaster readiness planning, capacity enhancement, training, and public awareness programmes to sustain long-term environmental protection.

title: Masterful Aquarius II Gears Up to Dazzle the Superyacht Scene
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Masterful Aquarius II Gears Up to Dazzle the Superyacht Scene
summary: The remarkable Aquarius II is a breath away from gracing the high seas, setting a new standard in yachting excellence.
body: Tantalizingly close to its unveiling, the illustrious Aquarius II is waltzing through the endgame of production, assertively punctuating Royal Huisman's dedication to perfection. Aided by the same talent house that brought the remarkable Aquarius (now titled Apsara) to fruition, the Aquarius II readies to enrich the currents with its dignified silhouette.

CEO of Royal Huisman, Jan Timmerman shares his anticipation with palpable enthusiasm, appreciating the trust placed by the owners in their shipbuilding finesse. Aquarius II pays rich testament to the shipbuilder's commitment to innovation, client-centric solutions, and their adeptness with both sailing and motor yacht projects. Every superyacht that emerges from the shipyard is a meticulous manifestation of a dream, expertly tailored to align with the owner's vision.

Specifically engineered as a larger version of Aquarius, Aquarius II brandishes a 45% increase in volume, enlarged social and crew areas, refined integrated sail-handling systems, and a lift-fin keel for optimized performance. The semi-hybrid propulsion and lightweight Alustar aluminum hull bear the promise of unparalleled performance and immersive voyages.

Following a meticulously orchestrated transport to Amsterdam, all eyes are on the nearing launch and delivery of this remarkable superyacht. Aquarius II is not just a boat; it is an embodiment of aesthetic excellence, the fruits of years-long effort, and the vanguard of luxury sea accommodation.

title: Taking the Helm on Dry Land: Leveraging Superyacht Experience for Shore-Based Success
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Taking the Helm on Dry Land: Leveraging Superyacht Experience for Shore-Based Success
summary: When the lure of the land becomes too strong, former superyacht crew members often find themselves eyeing shore-based careers. Utilising skills honed at sea can see them riding the wave of success on land.
body: A superyacht experience offers a rare blend of arduous challenges and opulent rewards, making it a magnet for those harbouring a penchant for unique adventures. While the rush of the sea and the idyllic beauty of remote locations can be immensely endearing, some crew members may be enticed to swap their flip-flops for work boots. Bringing with them a wealth of exotic experiences and a set of transferable skills par excellence, former crew members are equipped to embark on a range of shore-based careers that are teeming with promise.

One such career is a household or estate manager. This role often naturally attracts chief stewards and stewardesses, due to the striking parallels in overseeing the operations of colossal private residences and yachts, managing teams, and providing high-end service.

A different direction could lead ex-crew to the role of a marketing manager for yachting brands. With an intimate knowledge of the lifestyle, audience, and trends within the yachting world, they have the unique ability to effectively promote products and services geared towards this niche market.

title: Exploring Life at Sea: West Nautical’s Superyacht Captain’s Course Commands Resilience and Confidence
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Exploring Life at Sea: West Nautical’s Superyacht Captain’s Course Commands Resilience and Confidence
summary: West Nautical's annual Captain’s Command and Control Course for superyacht captains isn't just an alias to the greatest captains. It's the modern-day educator for the maritime industry.
body: Every October, skippers from across the globe converge on Newcastle upon Tyne in anticipation of West Nautical's distinguished Captain’s Command and Control Course. A staple in West Nautical's event calendar, this course has secured Newcastle upon Tyne and South Shields Marine School's global reputation for excellence in maritime training, traditionally associated with the glamorously luxurious hubs of the South of France or Bahamas.

Designed exclusively for captains possessing a STCW Reg A-II/2 Master (Yacht) 3000GT or higher, this course never fails to exceed the expectations. It collaboratively integrates the sophisticated bridge simulator at South Shields Marine School and a series of emergency scenarios to test the participants' decision-making and communication skills. The ultimate goal here is not just to navigate the high seas but one's mind too. It instills confidence and prepares captains for high-pressure situations inherent in their jobs.

Incidents such as fires, collisions, and sinkings, while rare, do cast a shadow over the superyacht industry. To manage these effectively, West Nautical initiated this command and control course in 2015. The course’s simulated scenarios are specifically curated to be superyacht-centric, providing realistic experiences that are invaluable.

Over the years, the city of Newcastle upon Tyne, renowned for its shipbuilding legacy, has reshaped itself into a hub of maritime learning, courtesy of the South Shields Marine School. This transformative institution not only revived the city's dwindling maritime pulse but continues to fuel it by fostering skilled maritime professionals, reminiscent of the bygone shipbuilding era. As we glance into the future of marine training, it's safe to say that the helm is in good hands, steering steadily towards excellence.

title: The 82 metre Oceanco Alfa Nero Makes Tumultuous Re-entry Into The Boating World After Long-awaited Refit
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: The 82 metre Oceanco Alfa Nero Makes Tumultuous Re-entry Into The Boating World After Long-awaited Refit
summary: The Oceanco Alfa Nero, an iconic name in the yachting world, is back following a controversial hiatus and an impressive refit.
body: The return of the Oceanco Alfa Nero has been marked by high drama. Known for its notable history of controversy, the infamous yacht has now emerged from its tumultuous past, sailing into fresh horizons. The yacht's owner faced sanctions tied to Russia's invasion of Ukraine, sparking a chain of legal tussles and its subsequent stasis. However, a refit carried out by Martinique Shipyard, contrived to mark the end of the vessel’s infamous saga. Now, sleeker and more robust than ever, the yacht is available for charter, staking its claim in the sector once again.

The Alfa Nero’s reintegration into the market followed a month-long intensive refit. This included a series of high-intensity upgrades and replacements such as propeller polishing and a new water heater. A complete hull repaint, reconditioned antifouling and anodes, and minor deck repairs added the finishing touches.

The yacht’s revival hasn't been without controversy. It was mired in international sanctions due to its links to Russian billionaire Andrey Guryev. After being abandoned in Antigua’s Falmouth Harbour, stayed idle, piled up maintenance costs while legal disputes chained it from being sold. Its sale was made possible due to an unconventional legal framework enacted by the Antiguan government, naming it a wreck and an environmental hazard – a strategic move to expedite the sale. The government also retains any remaining sale proceeds to fund after reimbursing debtors, raising a few eyebrows.

While the measures may seem harsh, the yacht posed a potential environmental threat to Antigua, a nation reliant on nautical tourism and vulnerable to seasonal hurricanes. Nevertheless, the comeback of the Alfa Nero is an event marked by its capacity to weather storms, both literal and metaphorical, as it embarks on its new journey in the charter market.

title: Transform Your Open-Air Superyacht Dining Experience in Both Tropical and Frosty Settings
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Transform Your Open-Air Superyacht Dining Experience in Both Tropical and Frosty Settings
summary: For superyacht owners traversing both tropical paradises and icy realms, ensuring unbeatable al fresco dining experiences becomes a priority. This particularly holds true under any weather circumstances.
body: The superyacht owner is possibly the most autonomous individual to set sail, maneuvering through breathtaking waters and accessing remote beaches, fjords, and islets off-limits to ordinary folks. However, like everyone else, they fall victim to one out-of-control element - weather. An unseasonably cold morning in the Mediterranean or an explorer yacht unable to appreciate Scandinavia's frosty, rough terrain can dampen the guest experience. Enter Bromic Heating, the solution to all these dilemmas. Bromic Heating, a world leader in outdoor heating, has developed the first and only Lloyd’s Register-approved outdoor heater designed for high salt-air marine environments. Constructed with top-notch AISI316 marine-grade stainless steel, the Platinum Marine heater showcases a fully sealed body that shields its internal components. The heater, seamlessly recessed within vessel ceilings, assures easy cleaning and maintenance for the crew. Uniquely, it warms objects instead of just air, fitting perfectly with the al fresco lifestyle. Notable features that set it apart include compatibility with home automation systems, no light emission, and complementary design support ensuring optimal heater placement. Owners of famed builds from Lürssen, Rossinavi, and Van der Valk are already beneficiaries of Bromic Heating's innovation. From Coral Ocean's even heat emission with fewer cold spots to Lel's comfort enhancement in bar, lounge, and dining areas, and Lady Lene's praise for Bromic’s aesthetics, usability, and efficient heat output, these high-profile users provide robust testimonials to the brand. With the outdoor dining experience on superyachts now a worthy match for their mesmerizing environs, owners can truly enjoy their freedom on the high seas, regardless of the weather.

title: Setting Sail: Echo Yachts Kick-starts Production of Record-breaking Sailing Catamaran
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Setting Sail: Echo Yachts Kick-starts Production of Record-breaking Sailing Catamaran
summary: Echo Yachts has launched construction of the planet's largest sailing catamaran, the ASC57, charting new waters in the world of luxury seafaring.
body: There's a new titan on the horizon, and its name is ASC57. Echo Yachts, the famed Australian shipbuilders, have broken ground on what is poised to be the pinnacle of the sailing catamaran world. Nestled in their Western Australian facility, the 57-meter multihull marks a bold leap into the large-scale sailing yacht market for the venture.

The firm's new monument to seafaring luxury draws heavily on the design aesthetics of their earlier 56-meter marvel, Charley 2, but sets its own course with an array of cutting-edge features. In partnership with One2Three Naval Architects, a specialist firm in crafting aluminium multihulls, Echo Yachts aspires to navigate the seas with a vessel that is lightweight, user-friendly, and equipped for extensive cruising.

Convenience merges with grandeur as the vessel includes a helicopter landing pad on board, much like its inspiration, Charley 2. Not to mention its ingenious regenerative power system complete with twin shaft generators and battery storage, enabling it to function silently under sail, and thanks to a controllable pitch propeller (CPP) driveline, to run effectively whilst motoring.

Designed with aluminium hulls for enhanced hydrodynamic efficiency, the shipyard is touting a reduced environmental impact for the ASC57, placing it a bow ahead of conventional motor yachts on the sustainability front.

Historically, large multihulls have seen measured growth, despite their benefits of higher gross tonnage, fuel efficiency, and improved stability. Yet, Echo Yachts has been sailing ahead, pioneering developments in this sector with impressive projects such as Charley 2 and White Rabbit. As the firm ventures into the creation of the ASC57, they promise yet another jewel in the superyacht market.

title: Emerging from the Shadows: How Yacht Interiors Craft Functionality and Opulence into a Masterpiece
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Emerging from the Shadows: How Yacht Interiors Craft Functionality and Opulence into a Masterpiece
summary: Unveiling the complexities of boat interior design, two experts steer us through the intricacies of crafting immaculate spaces on the open sea.
body: When it comes to excellence in luxury design, the yachting world effortlessly sets the stage. Nestled within these floating embodiments of opulence are interiors carefully curated to be functional, practical and impossibly chic, a delicate dance between realities of the open sea and the love of refined living. Delving into the craft, utters the names Natalie Fogelström of Koja Design Studio and Anja Carlsson of Acoya Design House, the key distinguishers between yacht and terrestrial designs crystallizing effortlessly under their expert gaze.

Aboard a yacht, space is a commodity, every precious inch maximized for aesthetic charm and practicality. Built-in storage spots are cunningly integrated into the panels, floors and furniture, ensuring a balance of minimalistic grace with naval pragmatism. Contrary to the art of maximizing small urban apartments, land-based design deals with spatial generosity, offering a playground for stylistic freedom, lofted by larger square footage.

Weight is another metric critical in yacht design, playing a pivotal role in performance, fuel efficiency, and stability. Although lighter materials are predominantly employed, achieving sumptuous interiors without sacrificing yacht performance becomes the interior designer's pivotal challenge.

Effortlessly sailing between these nuances is how luxury yacht design constructs these mobile paradises, a testament to the art of intricate balance between functionality, durability, and splendor of visuals.

title: Unleashing the Majestic Marine Beast: US Lifts Sanctions on Eminent 'Flying Fox' Yacht
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Unleashing the Majestic Marine Beast: US Lifts Sanctions on Eminent 'Flying Fox' Yacht
summary: In a resolute development, the mighty 'Flying Fox' has been disentangled from the web of international sanctions, amplifying its grandeur and restoring its legacy.
body: Purity and precision, exquisitely crafted by Espen Øino and Mark Berryman, form the essence of a grandeur seafaring marvel. The 'Flying Fox,' a majestic Lürssen beauty spanning 136 metres, awes spectators with its gargantuan 9,022 gross tonnage. This man-made wonder first graced the international waters in 2019, proud and imposing, through the realms of Imperial Yachts. However, the stage wasn't set for an uninterrupted reign. The affecting tremors of the Russia-Ukraine conflict in 2022 besmirched the vessel's splendour, reducing it to a pawn in the geopolitical chessboard. The US Department of Treasury, clouded by allegations of Imperial Yachts' links to Russian interests, cast the Flying Fox and its CEO into the mire of sanctions. Consequently, an air of restriction consumed the yacht, limiting its interactions with US citizens and barring it from US waters. The onset of 2022, however, rekindled the light at the end of the tunnel. Bluewater Yachting Dubai cast the net of opportunity wide open by making the Flying Fox accessible to the UK and EU citizens. Yet, the scent of liberty was not entirely sweet, with restrictions trembling in the background. But change is inevitable. In a monumental comeback, the US Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) set the Flying Fox free from its nightmare, shedding the label of 'Specially Designated Nationals' (SDN). Metaphorically untied from its sanctions, the yacht is fortifying its sails, ready to glide in the global charter market once again. With a promise of unencumbered access to international waters, the majestic Flying Fox stands tall nonpareil, awaiting its long overdue rendezvous with the sea.

title: A Glittering Review: The Monaco Yacht Show's Impact on the Future of Luxury Yachting
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A Glittering Review: The Monaco Yacht Show's Impact on the Future of Luxury Yachting
summary: The Monaco Yacht Show once again proved to be the highlight of the yachting calendar, showcasing industry-defining designs, sustainability initiatives, and headline-making launches.
body: Despite the drizzling Monte-Carlo weather, the Monaco Yacht Show unfurled its sails to another year of extraordinary luxury and innovation on water. A perennial hotspot on the yachting calendar, this year's spectacle was crowned with launch announcements, philanthropic recognitions, and ambitious sustainability initiatives set to steer the future of the industry. Lighting up the event, The Honours 2024 celebrated three individuals championing extraordinary projects. Frédéric Jousset, founder of the Art Explora Foundation, received accolades for crafting the world’s largest floating art museum. Nick Entwisle, the visionary behind Yachting Gives Back, won plaudits for his remarkable efforts on tackling hunger and poverty in one of Spain's most popular sailing destinations, Mallorca. Then there was Mike Horn, the explorer behind the awe-inspiring Pangaea X project, celebrated for engaging the youth in global environmental and social powerhouse initiatives. Shifting gears to design and engineering, Ferretti Group made grand splashes with two world premieres. The audience witnessed the debut of the wallywind110 – GALMA, a carbon fibre sailing yacht, alongside the Custom Line 50 Asante, boasting the distinction of being the first all-aluminium yacht in their under-500GT range. In an impressive industry move, the construction of the Riva 70 Metri was also announced, set to be the largest vessel ever built by Riva. A captivating discourse between industry bigwigs Giovanni Pomati, CEO of Nautor Swan, and Massimo Perotti, CEO of Sanlorenzo, created quite a stir as they highlighted their collective future plans centred on innovation, sustainability and shared goals. Heesen's presentation of the 62-metre Project Monte-Carlo swivelled heads. Owing to its aluminium superstructure, steel hull, and state-of-the-art serial hybrid propulsion system, the Project Monte-Carlo captured the very essence of innovation in yachting. Heesen did emblemise bullish market trends, forecasting a record-breaking revenue of €230 million with their clutch of 12 yachts under construction. The Mishi 102, a 31-metre sailing yacht, raised eyebrows at the show, as it beautifully emulsified practical design elements with proficient sailing performance. From its harmonious sail-flow to its aerodynamic hull, this yacht proved to be an icon for future sailing masterpieces.

title: Summit Furniture's game-changing superyacht collection: eco-friendly teak meets award-winning design
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Summit Furniture's game-changing superyacht collection: eco-friendly teak meets award-winning design
summary: Summit Furniture has made its mark as a leader in sustainable, premium teak furniture for superyachts. Take a closer look at what sets them apart.
body: Superyachts are synonymous with luxury and grandeur, and the furnishings onboard are no exception. However, the staple wood of the superyacht world, teak, is known for its harsh environmental impact. One company strives to change that - Summit Furniture. With a commitment since 1979 to create high-quality furniture with a conscience, this US-based manufacturer has been leading a teak revolution for over four decades.

Summit Furniture is renowned worldwide for its premium, responsible approach to furniture production, utilising plantation-grown teak in its award-winning designs. Its collections grace several globally celebrated superyachts, residences, and resorts with a particular fan-favourite being the Sundeck line.

The real difference-maker, however, is how Summit Furniture approaches teak production. The company puts a high premium on environmental sustainability with its practice of sourcing teak from monitored plantations in Indonesia. This eco-minded approach ensures that for every teak tree harvested, two or more are planted, effectively kick-starting the growth cycle again. This process not only provides secure supply but also grants benefits to the local economy and the environment. It results in a furniture brand endorsed with full certification from the Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) assuring clients of responsible sourcing and production.

Summit leverages the expertise of globally celebrated designers like the UK-based yacht designer John Munford for its collections. The result is a truly innovative blend of functionality, style, renowned design, and a firm commitment to sustainability, that's pushing the boundaries of what it means to be 'luxury' in the superyacht world.

title: Modernising the Superyacht Industry: A Glimpse Inside the Groundbreaking Digital Platform for UHNWI
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Modernising the Superyacht Industry: A Glimpse Inside the Groundbreaking Digital Platform for UHNWI
summary: Welcome to the future of yacht management: A cutting-edge digital platform designed explicitly for ultra-high-net-worth individuals (UHNWI) disrupting traditional private banking.
body: In a world where digitalisation is rapidly reshaping numerous industries, the realm of wealth management is undergoing an evolution to cater to a bold new generation of ultra-high-net-worth individuals (UHNWI). These affluent seafarers demand services as elevated as their assets, and a new champion has arisen to meet this demand: Privat 3 Money or P3, a company established in 2018 and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority in 2020. Pioneering a modern approach to financial services, P3 has made waves with their revolutionary product, P3 Marine.

In the bustling world of family offices, often tasked with managing the finances of multiple yachts, P3 Marine proves invaluable. Its centralised expense tracking, real-time reporting and treasury management features simplify the complex financial management associated with high-value maritime assets. Yacht managers can also enjoy a newfound level of transparency and optimisation, as the platform offers an overview of a yacht's financial activities.

For the stakeholders involved in yacht sales or charters, P3 Marine offers another level of convenience. It aids the management of charter accounts, streamlining reporting and serving as a robust payment infrastructure. Operated on a secure, cloud-based banking platform, P3 Marine prioritises security and integrates advanced protection features such as facial recognition, electronic ID verification, and AI-powered anti fraud technology.

In the realm of traditional private banking, P3 Marine is sailing innovative waters. Offering a modern solution designed to enhance efficacy and reduce costs, P3 Marine is the buoy in the choppy waters of superyacht management, navigating its users toward a smoother, more secure financial future.

title: Ocean Alexander Unleashes The 28L, Its Latest Showpiece Yacht With Classic Touches
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Ocean Alexander Unleashes The 28L, Its Latest Showpiece Yacht With Classic Touches
summary: Evan K. Marshall, the maestro behind Ocean Alexander's newest yacht model, the 28L, unveils its classic charm and innovative design features.
body: Hot on the heels of its recent launch, the Ocean Alexander 28L is rapidly making waves in the world of luxury yachting. Its arrival offers an impressive blend of classic design and exciting new features, enabling a new category of yacht lovers to embark on their own Ocean Alexander journey. Design wizard Evan K. Marshall is the creative force behind the 28L, continuing his long-time collaboration with the Taiwanese yacht builder.

Sprawling across 28 metres, this superyacht embraces the core philosophy of the Legend series with its exquisite design. However, Marshall didn’t just stop there. The 28L incorporates contemporary elements tailored perfectly to meet the needs and wishes of modern yacht enthusiasts. One can enjoy the plush and generous social spaces on board, staying true to the designer's signature.

With room for eight guests across four deluxe cabins, the 28L is a compact but elegant beast. It elegantly fuses the best features of the venerable 32L and 37L models of the Legend series. The 28L’s upper deck offers 360-degree views, providing unhindered visual access to your surrounding seascape. This yacht provides an exceptional al fresco dining area, a buffet bar with barbecue, and sun loungers on the sizeable exterior aft deck. The main saloon, a relaxation oasis, equipped with a state-of-the-art bar, ensures that your experiences remain as indulgent and memorable as possible.

title: Sophia's Splendour: Exploring the Design Marvel of Heesen's 50-metre Speedy Cruiser
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Sophia's Splendour: Exploring the Design Marvel of Heesen's 50-metre Speedy Cruiser
summary: Project Sophia, the sensational new construction from Heesen, is making waves for exceptional design and deft craftsmanship, promising unparalleled cruising experience.
body: Gone are the days of waiting anxiously for a brand-new yacht. Heesen, the renowned shipbuilder, is setting a new standard with their latest offering - Project Sophia - a meticulously crafted fast cruising yacht, demonstrating once again their prowess in building enviable yachts on speculation. The 50-metre cruiser, fourth of its class, emerges with promise and prestige, its hull and superstructure now flawlessly merged in Heesen's bustling production facility.

Drawing your attention at first glance is Sophia's bold, sporty exterior. Bearing the creativity of Frank Laupman from Omega Architects, the yacht dons a stylish, curvy look, producing an elongated profile upheld by a downward-pointing bow. This isn't merely for aesthetics, though they are striking. It enhances onboard functionality, giving an unhampered line of sight from the bridge and presenting guests with ample views of the ever-changing maritime landscape.

Sophia impeccably balances style and functionality. A multi-purpose tender garage with a full-height beach club graces the lower deck, made possible by the elevated main deck. Folding transoms and generous headroom amplify the yacht's usability and comfort.
Sophia is much more than a high-speed cruiser; it's a work of art, breathing elegance and functionality, leaving an indelible mark on the yachting world.

title: Redefining Luxury: Baglietto's DOM Line of Superyachts – Your On-Water Home Away from Home
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Redefining Luxury: Baglietto's DOM Line of Superyachts – Your On-Water Home Away from Home
summary: Baglietto's DOM line introduces a fresh dimension to sailing extravagance: conceptualising superyachts as second homes. Dive in to discover more.
body: Every superyacht owner has unique expectations towards their maritime marvel, shaped by various factors including personal needs and intended usage. Some might view it solely as a ritzy escape, a floating oasis, or even an avenue for endless adventure. Baglietto’s DOM superyacht line, however, might be redefining the game, carving out a niche for themselves as a 'home away from home'. Lofty ambitions indeed, but a statement supported by their thoughtful design. Baglietto offers the DOM115 and DOM133 models as part of their line-up, featuring sleek exteriors inspired by the automobile industry and designed by Italian maestro Stefano Vafiadis. The sporty, mid-sized aluminium displacement cruisers, born out of a desire to blend lifestyle requirements and performance, are far from being just aesthetically fascinating. In words of Fabio Ermetto, CCO of Baglietto, aluminium as a choice of construction material over fibreglass for the DOM133 added not only to its superlative quality and onboard comfort, but also allowed for greater flexibility and modifications, resulting in unique and personalised interior and exterior layouts. Flagship of the line, the DOM133 - a 40-metre model, first launched in 2022 with the latest Barbara Anne model making its debut in 2024. Baglietto didn't stop there, spreading its wings to encompass a broader clientele, the shipyard introduced the smaller, entry-level DOM115 in 2023. The new addition brought numerous requests from admirers of the DOM133 who desired a more compact vessel. Despite their size, both models are designed as ocean-going passage makers. The robust DOM133 cruises at a top speed of 17 knots and a 3,500-nautical-mile range, while the efficient DOM115 provides a 3,700-nautical-mile range at a steady pace of 10 knots. Add to it a convenient shallow draught, making it a breeze to traverse the sun-kissed waters of the Caribbean and the Bahamas. The standout feature, however, is the exceptional interior volume and the array of customisation options: The DOM133 boasts an 8.7-metre beam while the DOM115 stretches impressively to 7.8 metres. Greater dimensions equate to higher comfort levels, transforming these superyachts into idyllic floating homes. Revel in the opulence of the sea and never compromise on comfort with Baglietto’s DOM line.

title: Behind the Scenes at Sirena Yachts: The Emergence of their First 42-metre Superyacht
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Behind the Scenes at Sirena Yachts: The Emergence of their First 42-metre Superyacht
summary: Sirena Yachts is swiftly carving out its first 42-metre luxury superyacht, anticipated to grace waters in 2026 -an epitome of elegance and sporty refinement.
body: Sirena Yachts, the prodigious marine industry player, is on a zestful journey of creating its first 42-metre superyacht, a project announced only six months ago. This maritime marvel, featuring five spacious staterooms to host ten guests including a personalised suite for the owner, is anticipated to be ready for her maiden journey in 2026. Sirena's CEO, Çağın Genç, offers a promising progress report, reflecting the timely progression and high-quality standards adopted in the construction. Steered by a diligent workforce exceeding thirty members, the yacht's hull and superstructure are expected to take form soon, with the final metalwork aimed to be ready at the start of the new year. The expected launch, keeping with Sirena’s consistency, is aptly scheduled for 2026. The Sirena 42M, the brainchild of Sirena’s evolution over six years, is the icon of the brand's ambition to conquer the superyacht sector. Building on the production expertise and client trust fostered through the range of 58 to 88-feet yachts, the creation of the 42M bears the brand's imprint of spacious interiors, attention to detail, seaworthiness and client-centric approach. The Sirena 42M also represents a gentle shift in Sirena’s focus towards a younger demographic—those within the 40 to 50 age bracket, who seek a marked difference in yacht features. This cohort, inclined towards soaking in aquatic beauty, relaxation, and entertainment on the water, has influenced the design and amenities of the superyacht, beautifully curated to serve the new generation of owners. Sirena's partnership with brokerage firms Northrop & Johnson for the US and Ocean Independence for Europe plays a crucial role in understanding and incorporating these needs. The Sirena 42M, with its sporty and polished charm, is pierced with features catering to the demands of these young owners. While rendering the signature Sirena elegance, it is an homage to the brand's lineage, while embracing the fresh waves of the customer's aspirations.

title: A Deep Dive Into the Game-Changing Stabilisation System Elevating Onboard Yacht Comfort
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: A Deep Dive Into the Game-Changing Stabilisation System Elevating Onboard Yacht Comfort
summary: Prioritizing onboard comfort leads yacht owners to seek top-shelf stabilisation systems, such as MC2 Quick Gyro stabilisers.
body: For connoisseurs of luxury yachting, onboard comfort is non-negotiable. The remarkable MC2 Quick Gyro stabilisers, emerging as a strong contender in the yachting world, are instrumental in achieving this elusive ideal. A stabilisation system that promises to mitigate the impacts of other boats’ wakes and sudden rough seas, these units can chop down a yacht’s roll by a near-staggering 95 per cent, whether underway or at anchor. To get a complete lowdown on these game-changing stabilisers, a tete-a-tete with Quick Group’s CCO, Andreas Karlsen, comes in handy. Ease of installation is a core feature of the MC2 Quick Gyro stabilisers. Fitting these units is plain sailing, even when the boat is bobbing in the water, provided there's ample space in the engine or technical room. Karlsen explains how the simplicity of the units alleviates maintenance and service issues. Design-wise, these stabilizers are 20% tinier than the majority of their market counterparts, affording more flexibility when deciding their placement. They can be installed amidships or aft, depending on the available space. Acknowledging the strong partnership between the shipyard and Quick right from the initial boat planning phase, Lion Yachts’ technical manager Antonio Acconcia commends Quick’s technical department’s steady support. Another striking feature of the MC2 Quick Gyro stabilisers is the naturally dissipated, air-cooled system. These standalone systems circumvent potential issues by forgoing reliance on secondary systems like water pumps or seawater intakes, common to water-cooled systems. Karlsen speaks about how the gyroscope flywheel's horizontal axis movement evenly distributes weight on the bearings, reducing pressure, and promoting quicker stabilisation. Such innovative tweaks make the MC2 Quick Gyro stabilisers an ideal piece of sailing equipment, combining practicality and adventure.

title: Carlo Nuvolari's Innovative Step Forward: The Future of Superyacht Interior Design is 'Holistic'
author: Old Sea Dogs
imageAlt: Carlo Nuvolari's Innovative Step Forward: The Future of Superyacht Interior Design is 'Holistic'
summary: Carlo Nuvolari introduces an immersive, aesthetics-meets-comfort philosophy that's set to redefine superyacht interior design.
body: Change is not only anticipated, it's desired, according to Carlo Nuvolari and Dan Lenard, co-founders of Italian design powerhouse Nuvolari Lenard. While their words echo the pulse of the vibrant yachting market, the unveiling of their 'holistic' approach to superyacht interior design actualises it. In the words of Nuvolari, it’s about jettisoning the typical emphasis on look and instead creating a sensory milieu that not only pleases the eyes but also nurtures the owner’s comfort and wellbeing.

In his designs, Nuvolari is steadfast in intersecting environment protection, a pertinent concern given the yacht industry's ecological footprint. He re-draws the lines of 'sustainability', challenging tradition-distorted information. It’s not about merely mimicking sustainable designs, but also about educated material use, underscoring this ambitious and comprehensive design revolution.
